english_verse: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
translation_verse: Durnya be sososo na, esoso nɛ kasawule nɛ Ebɔrɛ to.

english_verse: The earth was barren, with no form of life; it was under a roaring ocean covered with darkness. But the Spirit of God was moving over the water. The First Day
translation_verse: Loŋ be saŋɛ na shɛŋ shɛŋ daa maŋ wɔ kasawule so, amoso k daa du nna le muntuluŋ. Kumo be jemanɛ na so nchu e daa la kaplɛkama nɛ tentembiri daŋ sɔ kakpa kikɛ le mina nɛ Ebɔrɛ be Kiyoyu daa lɛa a lɛa nchuana na so.

english_verse: God said, “I command light to shine!” And light started shining.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ: “Shin nɛ kefulto e lar n fulto.” Epul na to nɛ kaboŋ fulto par.

english_verse: God looked at the light and saw that it was good. He separated light from darkness
translation_verse: Nɛ Ebɔrɛ wu fanɛ kefulto na walɛ, nɛ e barga kefulto na be saŋɛ ashi tentembiri be saŋɛ to.

english_verse: and named the light “Day” and the darkness “Night.” Evening came, then morning—that was the first day. The Second Day
translation_verse: E ka wora loŋ na nɛ e nase kefulto be saŋɛ na kapa nseŋ nase tentembiri be saŋɛ na malɛ kanyɛ. Ndoŋ nna nɛ kanyɛ biri nɛ kare chɛ ŋ ki kachɛ lelemu juŋkparso na.

english_verse: God said, “I command a dome to separate the water above it from the water below it.”
translation_verse: Kachɛ juŋkparso na be kaman nɛ Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ: “Shin nɛ kunji e barga nchuana na to nɛ ako e baa wɔ esoso nɛ ako malɛ e baa wɔ kaseto.” Nɛ loŋ wora.

english_verse: and named it “Sky.” Evening came, then morning—that was the second day. The Third Day
translation_verse: Nɛ Ebɔrɛ nase kunji na awɔlpa. Ndoŋ nna nɛ kanyɛ biri nɛ kare chɛ ŋ ki kachɛ lelemu nyɔsopo na.

english_verse: God said, “I command the water under the sky to come together in one place, so there will be dry ground.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Kachɛ nyɔsopo na be kaman nɛ Ebɔrɛ naŋ kaŋɛ: “Shin nɛ nchu nɛ a wɔ awɔlpa be kaseto na e gama abar so kaboŋ koŋwule n shin nɛ kasawule malɛ e di efuli.” Nɛ loŋ wora.

english_verse: God named the dry ground “Land,” and he named the water “Ocean.” God looked at what he had done and saw that it was good.
translation_verse: Loŋ ka wora na nɛ Ebɔrɛ nase kaboŋ wɔlso nɛ k di efuli na kasawule nseŋ nase nchuana nɛ a ba abar so na eteku. E ka wora loŋ na nɛ e wu fanɛ k walɛ.

english_verse: The earth produced all kinds of vegetation. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ asɔduuso be yiri yiri fanɛ ayu be yiri to nɛ asɔrso be yiri to kikɛ kɔr nɛ kekama sɔr kumo be yiri to be asɔrso be bibi. Nɛ Ebɔrɛ wu fanɛ a walɛ.

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the third day. The Fourth Day
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ kanyɛ biri nɛ kare chɛ ŋ ki kachɛ lelemu sasopo na.

english_verse: God said, “I command lights to appear in the sky and to separate day from night and to show the time for seasons, special days, and years.
translation_verse: Kachɛ sasopo na be kaman nɛ Ebɔrɛ naŋ kaŋɛ: “Shin nɛ kefulto e lar awɔlpa to m barga kapa ashi kanyɛ to nseŋ shin nɛ a baa ŋini jemanɛ nɛ saŋɛ nɛ nchɛ nɛ nfɛ bee fara.

english_verse: I command them to shine on the earth.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Shin nɛ a baa la afulbi nɛ a wɔ awɔlpa to a nyaŋɛ kefulto a yuu kasawule so.” Nɛ loŋ wora.

english_verse: God made two powerful lights, the brighter one to rule the day and the other to rule the night. He also made the stars.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Ebɔrɛ to asɔ fultoso anyɔ n shin nɛ kegboŋi na bee ji eleŋ kapaso nɛ kekakarbi na malɛ bee ji eleŋ kanyɛso. Loŋ be saŋɛ na nɛ e daŋ to achɛkpabi gba n ti so.

english_verse: Then God put these lights in the sky to shine on the earth,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ebɔrɛ shin nɛ amo kikɛ wɔ awɔlpa to a nyaŋɛ a yuu kasawule so

english_verse: to rule day and night, and to separate light from darkness. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: a ji kapa nɛ kanyɛ kikɛ so eleŋ nsaa barga kefulto ashi tentembiri to. Loŋ ka wora na nɛ Ebɔrɛ wu fanɛ k walɛ.

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the fourth day. The Fifth Day
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ kanyɛ biri nɛ kare chɛ ŋ ki kachɛ lelemu nasopo na.

english_verse: God said, “I command the ocean to be full of living creatures, and I command birds to fly above the earth.”
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Ebɔrɛ naŋ kaŋɛ: “Shin nɛ asɔ futeso be yiri yiri e sɔ nchuana na to nseŋ shin nɛ mbuibiana malɛ e sɔ esoso a firgi.”

english_verse: So God made the giant sea monsters and all the living creatures that swim in the ocean. He also made every kind of bird. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: E ka kaŋɛ loŋ na nɛ e to nchu to be asɔ futeso gboŋgboŋiana be yiri yiri kikɛ nɛ kusɔ futeso be yiri kama nyam nɛ k wɔ nchu to nseŋ naŋ to mbuibi be yiri yiriana kikɛ verr. Loŋ ka wora na nɛ Ebɔrɛ wu fanɛ k walɛ.

english_verse: Then he gave the living creatures his blessing—he told the ocean creatures to increase and live everywhere in the ocean and the birds to increase everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ebɔrɛ nɛfa asɔ na kikɛ nyam nseŋ kaŋɛ: “Men baa wɔtɔ a kurge nsaa to a bure bibi n salga to n sɔ nchuana to nɛ mbuibiana na malɛ gba e salga to n sɔ durnya to kikɛ verr.”

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the fifth day. The Sixth Day
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ kanyɛ biri nɛ kare chɛ ŋ ki kachɛ lelemu nusopo na.

english_verse: God said, “I command the earth to give life to all kinds of tame animals, wild animals, and reptiles.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ebɔrɛ naŋ kaŋɛ: “Shin nɛ asɔbɔya be yiri yiri e lar a wɔ kasawule so, amo nɛ baa bela nɛ amo nɛ a wɔ kupuŋ to, begboŋi nɛ bewurbi kikɛ nyam.” Nɛ loŋ wora.

english_verse: God made every one of them. Then he looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ ka to amo kikɛ na nɛ e wu fanɛ kusɔ kama walɛ.

english_verse: God said, “Now we will make humans, and they will be like us. We will let them rule the fish, the birds, and all other living creatures.”
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ Ebɔrɛ naŋ kaŋɛ: “Men shin nɛ an to edimɛdi nɛ b baa du fanɛ anyi, nsaa ji eleŋ ashi ekɔrɔtɔ so nɛ mbuibi so nɛ asɔ gbeyesoana so nɛ asɔ belaso na kikɛ so nɛ kasawule kikɛ nyam so.”

english_verse: So God created humans to be like himself; he made men and women.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Ebɔrɛ to dimɛdi fanɛ mo gbagba be kumu nɛ mo gbagba be kaduli. Enyɛn nɛ eche nɛ e daŋ to bumo.

english_verse: God gave them his blessing and said: Have a lot of children! Fill the earth with people and bring it under your control. Rule over the fish in the ocean, the birds in the sky, and every animal on the earth.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ebɔrɛ nɛfa bumo nseŋ kaŋɛ bumo le: “Men kurge n wora keshi n salga to n sɔ kasawule so kikɛ nsaa ji eleŋ kumo so. Men baa ji eleŋ ekɔrɔtɔ so nɛ mbuibi so nɛ asɔ gbeyeso kikɛ nyam so.”

english_verse: And I have given the green plants as food for everything else that breathes, including animals, both wild and tame, and birds. And so it was.
translation_verse: Ama kasawule ere so be asɔbɔya bre kikɛ nɛ mbuibi be yiri yiri kikɛ nɛ asɔ gbeyeso be yiri yiri kikɛ nɛ kusɔ futeso kikɛ nyam bre afitiri nɛ afantaŋ bumbuŋ nɛ n sa amo nɛ a baa la amo be ajibi.” Nɛ loŋ wora.

english_verse: God looked at what he had done. All of it was very good! Evening came, then morning—that was the sixth day.
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ ka keni asɔ nɛ e wora na kikɛ nɛ e wu fanɛ amo kikɛ walɛ ga. Ndoŋ nna nɛ kanyɛ biri nɛ kare chɛ ŋ ki kachɛ lelemu shesopo na.

english_verse: So the heavens and the earth and everything else were created. The Seventh Day
translation_verse: To, kananɛ Ebɔrɛ daŋ to esoso nɛ kasawule nɛ kusɔ kama, kebɛso kebɛso loŋ n ya loge nyam nna na.

english_verse: That's how God created the heavens and the earth. The Garden of Eden When the Lord God made the heavens and the earth,
translation_verse: To, kananɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ daŋ to esoso nɛ kasawule nna na. E ka daŋ to amo na,

english_verse: no grass or plants were growing anywhere. God had not yet sent any rain, and there was no one to work the land.
translation_verse: kedibi kama nɛ keduuso jiso kama daa maŋ naŋ kɔr kasawule so. Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ malɛ daa maŋ naŋ shin nɛ bɔrɛ ba kasawule so. Dimɛdi kikɛ malɛ daa maŋ wɔtɔ a dɔ kasawule so.

english_verse: But streams came up from the ground and watered the earth.
translation_verse: Saŋɛ nɛ bɔrɛ daa maŋ naŋ ba na, nchu daa shi kasawule to nna a bul a wushi kasawule na kikɛ nyam.

english_verse: The Lord God took some soil from the ground and made a man. God breathed life into the man, and the man started breathing.
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ka daa shin nɛ e to dimɛdi na, e daŋ ta shishɛr nna ashi kasawule so m pɔr enyɛn nseŋ fute ŋkpa be efute n wɔtɔ mbe kamuna to nɛ enyɛn na ki kusɔ futeso.

english_verse: The Lord God filled the garden with all kinds of beautiful trees and fruit trees. Two other trees were in the middle of the garden. One of these gave life—the other gave the wisdom to know the difference between right and wrong.
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ daŋ shin nna nɛ ndibi lela be yiri yiri kɔr n daŋ ashi ndoŋ. Ndibi na nɛ amo be asɔrso malɛ daa walɛ keji nna. Ama ndibi anyɔ ko malɛ daa yil kudɔbi na be nferinto. Loŋ be ndibi na be kuko be asɔrso daa sa ŋkpa nna nɛ kuko malɛ peya daa sa kanyiasheŋ nɛ k bee shin nɛ esa bee pin kelela nɛ kulubi.

english_verse: The first one is the Pishon River that flows through the land of Havilah,
translation_verse: Loŋ be eboŋ ana na be kumo nɛ k juŋkpar be ketre e daa la Pishon. K daa shile nna a kulti Havila be efuli.

english_verse: The second is the Gihon River that winds through Ethiopia.
translation_verse: Eboŋ nyɔsopo na be ketre e daa la Gihɔn. K daa shile nna a kulti Kush be efuli.

english_verse: The Tigris River that flows east of Assyria is the third, and the fourth is the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: Eboŋ sasopo na be ketre e daa la Tigris. K daa wɔ Asiriya be efuli so be epeŋipetekpa be kaba so nna. Eboŋ nasopo na malɛ be ketre e daa la Yufreetes.

english_verse: The Lord God put the man in the Garden of Eden to take care of it and to look after it.
translation_verse: To, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ daŋ ta enyɛn na nna n wɔtɔ kudɔbi nɛ baa tre Iden na to fanɛ e baa dɔ ndoŋ nsaa keni kumo so.

english_verse: except the one that has the power to let you know the difference between right and wrong. If you eat any fruit from that tree, you will die before the day is over!”
translation_verse: ama sa maŋ kaŋ ji kedibi nɛ k bee sa kelela nɛ kulubi be kanyiasheŋ na bre be asɔrso, ŋkpal manɛ so, kachɛ kama so nɛ fo baŋ ji loŋ be kedibi na be asɔrso, shɛŋ maaŋ mɔlga fo ashi luwu to. Abaanaaworasheŋ feeŋ wu.”

english_verse: The Lord God said, “It isn't good for the man to live alone. I will make a suitable partner for him.”
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ: “K maŋ daga fanɛ enyɛn na nawule e baa wɔtɔ. Meeŋ pɔr echɛtopo nɛ e beeŋ kukwe mo n sa mo.”

english_verse: So the Lord took some soil and made animals and birds. He brought them to the man to see what names he would give each of them. Then the man named the tame animals and the birds and the wild animals. That's how they got their names. None of these was the right kind of partner for the man.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ enyɛn na sa n sa asɔyigeso kikɛ nɛ mbuibi kikɛ nɛ kupuŋ to be asɔbɔya kikɛ amo be atre. Ama echɛtopo nɛ e daa beeŋ kukwe mo ere kanyɛn na bre gbagba, daa maŋ wɔ asɔ na to.

english_verse: So the Lord God made him fall into a deep sleep, and he took out one of the man's ribs. Then after closing the man's side,
translation_verse: Amoso Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ daŋ shin nna nɛ edigboŋ ko pɛ enyɛn na nɛ e di n chul nɛ Ebɔrɛ lara mbe kekentibi ko nseŋ shin nɛ ndoŋ chɛ n ti.

english_verse: the Lord made a woman out of the rib. The Lord God brought her to the man,
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ta kekentibi nɛ e lara enyɛn na to na n wora eche nseŋ ta mo m ba sa enyɛn na.

english_verse: and the man exclaimed, “Here is someone like me! She is part of my body, my own flesh and bones. She came from me, a man. So I will name her Woman!”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ enyɛn na kaŋɛ: “Too, naniere bre esa nɛ mbe awibi shi ma awibi to nɛ mbe eyur malɛ gba shi ma eyur to nde. Baaŋ baa tre mo eche, ŋkpal manɛ so, ma to nɛ e shi.”

english_verse: That's why a man will leave his own father and mother. He marries a woman, and the two of them become like one person.
translation_verse: Amoso nɛ enyɛn baŋ ta eche, a daga fanɛ e yige mo tuto nɛ mo nio nseŋ ya far n chɛ mbe eche nɛ b ki eyur koŋwule.

english_verse: Although the man and his wife were both naked, they were not ashamed.
translation_verse: Enyɛn na nɛ mbe eche kikɛ daŋ baa wɔtɔ kayurkpaŋ nna, ama anishinyɔr malɛ daa maŋ kɔ bumo.

english_verse: The snake was sneakier than any of the other wild animals that the Lord God had made. One day it came to the woman and asked, “Did God tell you not to eat fruit from any tree in the garden?”
translation_verse: Asɔbɔya nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ daŋ to na kikɛ to, kusɔkpaŋ e daa du fanɛ kanansabi a chɔ bumo nɛ b ka na kikɛ. Kachako nɛ kusɔkpaŋ na ba eche na kutɔ m ba bishi mo le: “Ama kashenteŋ nɛ Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ fanɛ men sa maŋ kaŋ ji kedibi kama be asɔrso nɛ a wɔ kudɔbi ere to a?”

english_verse: The woman answered, “God said we could eat fruit from any tree in the garden,
translation_verse: Nɛ eche na kaŋɛ kusɔkpaŋ na: “Ayai, Ebɔrɛ maŋ kaŋɛ loŋ, e yɛ anyeeŋ tiŋ n ji nfe be kedibi kama be asɔrso,

english_verse: except the one in the middle. He told us not to eat fruit from that tree or even to touch it. If we do, we will die.”
translation_verse: ama e yɛ an sa maŋ kaŋ ji kedibi nɛ k yil kakpa ere be nferinto ere bre be asɔrso. E yɛ an sa maŋ beta amo gba kuraa. Nɛ mannɛ aloŋ anyeeŋ wu.”

english_verse: “No, you won't!” the snake replied.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ kusɔkpaŋ na kaŋɛ eche na: “Abaa, men maaŋ wu.

english_verse: “God understands what will happen on the day you eat fruit from that tree. You will see what you have done, and you will know the difference between right and wrong, just as God does.”
translation_verse: Keni, Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ loŋ nna ŋkpal e ka nyi fanɛ men baŋ ji kumo be asɔrso na menyeeŋ baa pin asheŋ to nsaa du fanɛ Ebɔrɛ gbagba, a nyi kelela nɛ kulubi.”

english_verse: The woman stared at the fruit. It looked beautiful and tasty. She wanted the wisdom that it would give her, and she ate some of the fruit. Her husband was there with her, so she gave some to him, and he ate it too.
translation_verse: Kusɔkpaŋ na ka kaŋɛ loŋ na nɛ eche na wu fanɛ kedibi na be asɔrso walɛ kenishiso kashenteŋto nseŋ duli asɔ nɛ a beeŋ baa wɔ ebel, amo alɛ naŋ duli asɔ nɛ esa beeŋ ji nseŋ nya kanyiasheŋ. Nɛ amo be kayɛlga ba mo to nɛ e chuge kedibi na be asɔrso na n ji nseŋ ta n sa mo kul nɛ e daa wɔ mo kutɔ na nɛ mo alɛ gba ji.

english_verse: At once they saw what they had done, and they realized they were naked. Then they sewed fig leaves together to cover themselves.
translation_verse: B ka ji kusɔrso na nɛ bumo benyɔ kikɛ be anishi bugi nɛ b pin fanɛ b na kayurkpaŋ nna. Ndoŋ nna nɛ b chuge kedibi nɛ baa tre figi na be afantaŋ m ba m mata abar n dela.

english_verse: Late in the afternoon, when the breeze began to blow, the man and woman heard the Lord God walking in the garden. So they hid behind some trees. Sin Brings a Curse
translation_verse: Kumo be kamɔnchɛ kaboŋ ka ya kaa wushito nɛ enyɛn na nɛ mbe eche nu Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be aya be egbri kudɔbi na to nseŋ luri ndoŋ be ndibi to ŋ ŋana mo so.

english_verse: The Lord God called out to the man and asked, “Where are you?”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ tre enyɛn na m bishi mo le: “Fo wɔ nnɛ?”

english_verse: The man answered, “I was naked, and when I heard you walking through the garden, I was frightened and hid!”
translation_verse: Nɛ enyɛn na shuli ŋ kaŋɛ: “N nu fo ka na kudɔbi na to nna nɛ kufu pɛ ma ŋkpal ŋ ka maŋ dela shɛŋ so, amoso nɛ n ya ŋana.”

english_verse: “How did you know you were naked?” God asked. “Did you eat any fruit from that tree in the middle of the garden?”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ bishi mo: “Wanɛ e kaŋɛ fo fanɛ fo maŋ dela shɛŋ? Fo ji kedibi mo nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ fo sa maŋ ji kumo be asɔrso na nna a?”

english_verse: “It was the woman you put here with me,” the man said. “She gave me some of the fruit, and I ate it.”
translation_verse: Nɛ enyɛn na kaŋɛ: “Eche mo nɛ fo ta n wɔtɔ ŋ kutɔ nfe na e sa ma kedibi na be kusɔrso nɛ n ji.”

english_verse: The Lord God then asked the woman, “What have you done?” “The snake tricked me,” she answered, “and I ate some of that fruit.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ bishi eche na: “Manɛ be kushuŋ nɛ fo shuŋ loŋ?” Nɛ eche na kaŋɛ: “Kusɔkpaŋ na e fule ma nɛ n ji kusɔrso na.”

english_verse: So the Lord God said to the snake: “Because of what you have done, you will be the only animal to suffer this curse— For as long as you live, you will crawl on your stomach and eat dirt.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ kusɔkpaŋ na le: “Ŋkpal fo ka wora le ere so, fo nawule e naŋ nya kɔnɔsho asɔ belaso nɛ kupuŋ to be asɔbɔya kikɛ to! Fo epun so nɛ feeŋ baa gbeye nsaa ji shishɛr fo kebaawɔtɔ to kikɛ.

english_verse: You and this woman will hate each other; your descendants and hers will always be enemies. One of hers will strike you on the head, and you will strike him on the heel.”
translation_verse: Ma alɛ beeŋ ta kedoŋ n wɔtɔ fo nɛ eche na be nferinto nseŋ naŋ ta kedoŋ n wɔtɔ fo pibi nɛ eche na be kebia to. Eche na be kebia na beeŋ baa bɛa fo kumu to nɛ fo alɛ e baa duŋ mbe kenaŋkuŋ.”

english_verse: The Lord said to the man, “You listened to your wife and ate the fruit I told you not to eat. And so, the ground will be under a curse because of what you did. As long as you live, you will have to struggle to grow enough food.
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ka malga n sa eche na n loge nɛ e kilgi ŋ kaŋɛ enyɛn na malɛ le: “Ŋkpal fo ka nu n sa fo eche n ji kusɔrso nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ fo sa maŋ kaŋ ji na so so, meeŋ sho kasawule ere kɔnɔ ŋkpal fo so. Pɔɛŋ nɛ fo nya n ji, feeŋ baa wɔtɔ nna a ji awurfoŋ a nyɛa kebleŋ ashi fo kebaawɔtɔ to kikɛ.

english_verse: Your food will be plants, but the ground will produce thorns and thistles.
translation_verse: Kasawule na beeŋ baa kɔr ewi nɛ afitiri kpaŋ ŋkpal fo so; kasawule na malɛ so nɛ feeŋ baa dɔ a ji.

english_verse: You will sweat all your life to earn a living; you were made out of soil, and you will once again turn into soil.”
translation_verse: Kashenteŋto feeŋ baa nyɛa kebleŋ damta nna pɔɛŋ nsaa ji, hale loŋ nɛ fo naŋ ya bɛta n yɔ shishɛr to, ŋkpal manɛ so, shishɛr na nɛ b ta n pɔr fo. Fo la shishɛr nna, amo alɛ to nɛ feeŋ naŋ bɛta n yɔ.”

english_verse: The man Adam named his wife Eve because she would become the mother of all who live.
translation_verse: Enyɛn na be ketre e daa la Adam nɛ mo alɛ nase mbe eche Hawa, ŋkpal manɛ so, mo e naaŋ ba ki bomin kikɛ mo nio.

english_verse: Then the Lord God made clothes out of animal skins for the man and his wife.
translation_verse: Asheŋ na ka ba loŋ na nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ta asɔbɔya be nwɔl n wora asɔbuuso n sa Adam nɛ mbe eche nɛ b baa buu.

english_verse: The Lord said, “They now know the difference between right and wrong, just as we do. But they must not be allowed to eat fruit from the tree that lets them live forever.”
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ mbe kumu le: “Ŋkpal kanyɛn ere ka ji kusɔrso na so, naniere e ki fanɛ anyi to be eko nna a nyi kelela nɛ kulubi to, amoso a maŋ daga fanɛ e naŋ nya ekpa n chuge kedibi mo nɛ k bee sa ŋkpa na malɛ be kusɔrso n ji ŋkaa maaŋ naŋ wu kikɛ.”

english_verse: So the Lord God sent them out of the Garden of Eden, where they would have to work the ground from which the man had been made.
translation_verse: Amoso Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ daŋ ju mo ashi Iden be kudɔbi na to nna fanɛ e ya kaa shuŋ kasawule mo nɛ b daŋ ta m pɔr na so.

english_verse: Adam and Eve had a son. Then Eve said, “I'll name him Cain because I got him with the help of the Lord.”
translation_verse: Kachako nɛ Adam nɛ mbe eche Hawa di keche nɛ kenyɛn nɛ eche na di kedampo ŋ kurge ebinyɛn nɛ b nase mo ketre Keen. Ŋkpal manɛ so, Hawa yɛ: “Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e chɛ ma to nɛ ŋ kurge ebinyɛn.”

english_verse: Later she had another son and named him Abel. Abel became a sheep farmer, but Cain farmed the land.
translation_verse: B wɔtɔ loŋ nɛ e naŋ ba kurge Keen mo sipo nɛ baa tre mo Eebel. Mbia na ka daŋ nɛ Eebel bee bela mbolpɔ nɛ Keen malɛ bee dɔ.

english_verse: One day, Cain gave part of his harvest to the Lord,
translation_verse: Kachako nɛ Keen ya bar mbe adɔjibi ko m ba kɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na

english_verse: and Abel also gave an offering to the Lord. He killed the first-born lamb from one of his sheep and gave the Lord the best parts of it. The Lord was pleased with Abel and his offering,
translation_verse: nɛ Eebel malɛ bar mbe asɔbɔya to be ewurkoŋfɔlbiana na be eko m ba mɔ nseŋ lara kumo be ebɛaŋ n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na. Ndoŋ nna nɛ Eebel nɛ mbe kakɛ na be asheŋ bɔlɔ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kenishi.

english_verse: but not with Cain and his offering. This made Cain so angry that he could not hide his feelings.
translation_verse: Ama Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na daŋ kini Keen bre nɛ mbe kakɛ na nna. Keen ka wu loŋ na nɛ e nya agbo n tiŋ to.

english_verse: The Lord said to Cain: What's wrong with you? Why do you look so angry?
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na bishi Keen le: “Manɛ e ba nɛ fo nya agbo n tiŋ to loŋ?

english_verse: If you had done the right thing, you would be smiling. But you did the wrong thing, and now sin is waiting to attack you like a lion. Sin wants to destroy you, but don't let it!
translation_verse: Fo maŋ nyi fanɛ fo daŋ wora nɛnɛ nna asheŋ daŋ beeŋ nyalɛ n sa fo a? Ama ŋkpal fo ka maŋ wora nɛnɛ so, kulubi du fanɛ buluŋ nna a tɛ fo nɛ k jija fo, amoso wora ania m pɔɔ kumo so.”

english_verse: Cain said to his brother Abel, “Let's go for a walk.” And when they were out in a field, Cain attacked and killed him.
translation_verse: Kachako nɛ Keen kaŋɛ mo sipo Eebel fanɛ b yɔ kupuŋ to. Ndoŋ nna nɛ Eebel shuli nɛ mo nɛ Keen yɔ kupuŋ na to. B ka ya fo ndoŋ nɛ Keen tɛ n yuu mo sipo Eebel so m bri mo m mɔ.

english_verse: Afterwards the Lord asked Cain, “Where is Abel?” “How should I know?” he answered. “Am I supposed to look after my brother?”
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na bishi Keen: “Fo sipo Eebel wɔ nnɛ?” Nɛ Keen kaŋɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na le: “M maŋ nyi. Ma e naa keni n sipo so a?”

english_verse: Then the Lord said: Why have you done this terrible thing? You killed your own brother, and his blood flowed onto the ground. Now his blood is calling out for me to punish you.
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ naŋ bishi Keen le: “Manɛ be kushuŋ nɛ fo shuŋ le ere? Keni, n wu kananɛ fo mɔ fo sipo nɛ mbe ŋklaŋ nɛ a wurge kasawule du fanɛ dimɛdi a shu a ŋini ma fanɛ m bishi kuwule n sa mo.

english_verse: And so, I'll put you under a curse. Because you killed Abel and made his blood run out on the ground, you will never be able to farm it again.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal fo ka mɔ fo sipo so n sho fo kɔnɔ nsaa ju fo ashi kasawule nɛ k nuu fo sipo na be ŋklaŋ na so.

english_verse: When you try to farm the land, it won't produce anything for you. From now on, you'll be without a home, and you'll spend the rest of your life wandering from place to place.
translation_verse: Fo naŋ dɔ kumo so gba, fo maaŋ nya shɛŋ. Yili kabre a yɔ fo maaŋ baa kɔ epe, feeŋ baa la efɔ nna a na chamcham durnya ere to.”

english_verse: “You're making me leave my home and live far from you. I will have to wander about without a home, and just anyone could kill me.”
translation_verse: Keni, naniere fo ju ma ashi kasawule ere so nɛ e na durnya ere to chamcham. Ma alɛ maaŋ naŋ tiŋ m ba fo anishito gba. Amoso esa kama nɛ e tu ma kaplɛkama beeŋ mɔ ma.”

english_verse: “No!” the Lord answered. “Anyone who kills you will be punished seven times worse than I am punishing you.” So the Lord put a mark on Cain to warn everyone not to kill him.
translation_verse: N doŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ Keen: “Ayai, mannɛ aloŋ nna, esa kama nɛ e mɔ fo, meeŋ bishi amodoŋwura kumo be kuwule ale shunu.” Kede be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na dulgi Keen, saŋɛ na so esa kama nɛ e tu mo kaplɛkama maaŋ mɔ mo.

english_verse: But Cain had to go far from the Lord and live in the Land of Wandering, which is east of Eden. More and More People
translation_verse: Ndulgi na be kaman nɛ Keen lar Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kutɔ n ya kaa wɔ Nɔd be kasawule so. Ndoŋ daa wɔ Iden be epeŋipetekpa be kaba so nna.

english_verse: Later, Cain and his wife had a son named Enoch. At the time Cain was building a town, and so he named it Enoch after his son.
translation_verse: Keen ka ta eche nɛ mo nɛ mo di kenyɛn nɛ keche nɛ eche na di kedampo ŋ kurge ebinyɛn n nase mbe ketre Inɔk. Kakurge na be kaman nɛ Keen fara kade nseŋ ta mbe kebia na be ketre n nase kade na.

english_verse: Then Enoch had a son named Irad, who had a son named Mehujael, who had a son named Methushael, who had a son named Lamech.
translation_verse: Inɔk ka daŋ nɛ e ta eche ŋ kurge Irad nɛ Irad malɛ koso ŋ kurge Mehujaɛl nɛ Mehujaɛl malɛ kurge Metushaɛl nɛ Metushaɛl malɛ kurge Lamɛk.

english_verse: Lamech and Adah had two sons, Jabal and Jubal. Their son Jabal was the first to live in tents and raise sheep and goats. Jubal was the first to play harps and flutes.
translation_verse: Mo sipo be ketre e daa la Jubal. Jubal ere e daŋ fara a laŋ alaŋsɔ fanɛ keklaŋ nɛ kalopi.

english_verse: Lamech and Zillah had a son named Tubal Cain who made tools out of bronze and iron. They also had a daughter, whose name was Naamah.
translation_verse: Lamɛk be eche nyɔsopo nɛ b daa tre Zila na malɛ e daŋ kurge Tubalkeen. Mo alɛ daa la bɔyɛpo nna nɛ esa nɛ e daŋ fara n ta epal nɛ abɛlso be yiri yiri n lɔŋɛ ashuŋsɔ. Tubalkeen mo sipoche nɛ b daa tre Naama.

english_verse: Anyone who tries to get even with me will be punished ten times more than anyone who tries to get even with Cain.”
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ fanɛ esa kama nɛ e mɔ Keen, amodoŋwura beeŋ nya loŋ be kulubi na be kuwule be kebishi ale shunu so. Ama nɛ esa mɔ ma ere Lamɛk, kumo be kuwule beeŋ baa la ela adushunu nɛ ashunu nna.”

english_verse: Adam and his wife had another son. They named him Seth, because they said, “God has given us a son to take the place of Abel, who was killed by his brother Cain.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Adam nɛ mbe eche naŋ di keche nɛ kenyɛn nɛ eche na di kedampo ŋ kurge ebinyɛn nɛ b nase mo ketre Sɛt. Nɛ Adam be eche yɛ: “N nase mo loŋ nna, ŋkpal manɛ so, Ebɔrɛ naŋ sa ma ebinyɛn nna n tal Eebel nɛ Keen mɔ na to.”

english_verse: Later, Seth had a son and named him Enosh. About this time people started worshiping the Lord.
translation_verse: Sɛt malɛ ka daŋ nɛ e ta eche ŋ kurge ebinyɛn nseŋ nase mo ketre Inɔsh. Kumo be jemanɛ so nɛ basa fara a shuŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nsaa bunyaŋ mo.

english_verse: Lamech said, “I'll name him Noah because he will give us comfort, as we struggle hard to make a living on this land that the Lord has put under a curse.”
translation_verse: E daŋ nase ebinyɛn na ketre Nowa nna. E yɛ: “N nase mo loŋ nna, ŋkpal manɛ so, mo e naaŋ baa kaa leŋ anyi to ashi anyi be ashuŋ nɛ kegben damta nɛ anyee gben ashi kasawule mo nɛ Ebɔrɛ sho kɔnɔ ere so.”

english_verse: More and more people were born, until finally they spread all over the earth. Some of their daughters were so beautiful that supernatural beings came down and married the ones they wanted.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ebɔrɛso be asɔtoso nyɛnsoana ko wu edimɛdi be bibichesobiana na nɛ bumo be kebita par bumo nɛ b ta bumo nɛ baa sha a kil.

english_verse: The children of the supernatural beings who had married these women became famous heroes and warriors. They were called Nephilim and lived on the earth at that time and even later.
translation_verse: Jemanɛ na so nɛ kumo be kaman nɛ basa ko nɛ b daa tre Nefilebi nɛ b la basa tenteŋ nsaa kɔ eleŋ a kɔ kena ga nɛ basa kikɛ bee sa bumo bunyaŋ ga na daa wɔ durnya to. Le be saŋɛ ere nɛ Ebɔrɛso be asɔtoso nyɛnsoana daa ta edimɛdi be bibichesobiana a kurge mbia na.

english_verse: The Lord saw how bad the people on earth were and that everything they thought and planned was evil.
translation_verse: Kumo be jemanɛ na so nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ wu fanɛ basa be alubi bee wora keshi durnya to a ti so nɛ bumo be ŋgbene to be nfɛra fɛso kikɛ la asheŋ lubi.

english_verse: and he said, “I'm going to destroy every person on earth! I'll even wipe out animals, birds, and reptiles. I'm sorry I ever made them.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ e kaŋɛ mbe kumu: “Meeŋ mur basa nɛ n to durnya ere to kikɛ nyam, bumo nɛ asɔbɔya nɛ asɔ gbeyeso nɛ mbuibi firgisoana kikɛ nyam, ŋkpal manɛ so, ma kagbene jija ga ŋkpal ŋ ka to dimɛdi nɛ loŋ be asɔ na kikɛ so.”

english_verse: But the Lord was pleased with Noah,
translation_verse: Ama Nowa bre be asheŋ daŋ bɔlɔ Ebɔrɛ kenishi ga.

english_verse: He had three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
translation_verse: Nowa daa kɔ bibinyɛnsobi asa nna nɛ baa tre bumo Shɛm nɛ Ham nɛ Jafɛf.

english_verse: Get some good lumber and build a boat. Put rooms in it and cover it with tar inside and out.
translation_verse: Amoso, kuya ndibi kpakpaso n lɔŋɛ kuloŋ gboŋgboŋi nseŋ wora ebu wurbiana kumo to n ta kootal n laa kumo be epun to nɛ kaman to kikɛ nyam.

english_verse: I'm going to send a flood that will destroy everything that breathes! Nothing will be left alive.
translation_verse: Lɔŋɛ kuloŋ na, ŋkpal manɛ so, meeŋ shin nɛ bɔrɛ e ba durnya to nɛ nchu e sɔ kaplɛkama n ji kusɔ futeso kikɛ nyam. Kashenteŋto, durnya to be kusɔ kama nyam beeŋ mur.

english_verse: But I solemnly promise that you, your wife, your sons, and your daughters-in-law will be kept safe in the boat.
translation_verse: Ama ma ere nɛ fo beeŋ wora kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre, nɛ fo nɛ fo eche nɛ fo bibinyɛnsobiana na nɛ bumo be beche na e luri kuloŋ na to.

english_verse: Take into the boat with you a male and a female of every kind of animal and bird, as well as a male and a female of every reptile. I don't want them to be destroyed.
translation_verse: Ta mbuibi be yiri yiri nɛ asɔbɔya be yiri yiri nɛ asɔ gbeyeso be yiri yiri benyɔnyɔ nɛ a ba kaa wɔ ŋkpa to ashi kuloŋ na to.

english_verse: The Lord told Noah: Take your whole family with you into the boat, because you are the only one on this earth who pleases me.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe na kaŋɛ Nowa le: “Fo nɛ fo kanaŋ kikɛ e luri kuloŋgboŋ na to, ŋkpal manɛ so, n wu fanɛ fo jemanɛ ere so ebi to fo e la esa nɛ e niŋi ma anishito.

english_verse: Also take seven pairs of every kind of bird with you. Do this so there will always be animals and birds on the earth.
translation_verse: nɛ mbuibi be yiri yiri to malɛ kikɛ be kenyɛnso nɛ kecheso be ntuŋ ashunushunu. Saŋɛ na so kekama be yiri to maaŋ mur kasawule ere so kikɛ.

english_verse: He obeyed God and took a male and a female of each kind of animal and bird into the boat with him.
translation_verse: Asɔ nɛ a daŋ tu Nowa n luri kuloŋgboŋ na to na be kekama daa la kecheso nɛ kenyɛnso nna fanɛ kananɛ Ebɔrɛ daŋ kaŋɛ mo fanɛ e wora na.

english_verse: Seven days later a flood began to cover the earth.
translation_verse: Nchɛ ashunu na be kaman nɛ nchu fara a sɔ kasawule so kikɛ.

english_verse: The water under the earth started gushing out everywhere, the sky opened like windows, and rain poured down for
translation_verse: Bɔrɛ na daŋ ba kapa nɛ kanyɛ kikɛ, a maa teŋ hale n ya fo nchɛ adena.

english_verse: On that day Noah and his wife went into the boat with their three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth, and their wives.
translation_verse: Kachɛ nɛ bɔrɛ na fara a ba na gbagba nɛ Nowa nɛ mbe eche nɛ bibinyɛn nɛ baa tre Shɛm nɛ Ham nɛ Jafɛf na nɛ bumo be beche luri kuloŋgboŋ na to.

english_verse: Noah took a male and a female of every living creature with him,
translation_verse: Asɔ futeso kama to be benyɔnyɔ e daŋ tu Nowa n luri kuloŋgboŋ na to.

english_verse: Finally, the mighty flood was so deep that even the highest mountain peaks were about seven meters below the surface of the water.
translation_verse: Nchu na daŋ wora keshi loŋ hale n ya dii m muni abee na kikɛ so n fo fanɛ ayadra adunyɔ.

english_verse: A hundred fifty days later, the water started going down.
translation_verse: Nchu na daa wɔ kasawule so nchɛ kalfa nɛ adunu nna.

english_verse: God did not forget about Noah and the animals with him in the boat. So God made a wind blow, and the water started going down.
translation_verse: Saŋɛ nɛ kuloŋgboŋ na daa deŋ nchu na so na Ebɔrɛ daa maŋ teŋ Nowa nɛ asɔbɔya nɛ b wɔ kuloŋgboŋ na to na so kikɛ. E daŋ shin nna nɛ afu fara a chela kasawule so nɛ nchu na fara a gberge.

english_verse: God stopped up the places where the water had been gushing out from under the earth. He also closed up the sky, and the rain stopped.
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ daŋ ti kasawule to be nchuana nɛ a daa lar na nna nseŋ shin nɛ bɔrɛ nɛ k daa ba fanɛ awɔlpa be mbuna ka bugi na ku kuraa.

english_verse: Then on the seventeenth day of the seventh month of the year, the boat came to rest somewhere in the Ararat mountains.
translation_verse: Kufɔl shunusopo to be kachɛ kuduashunusopo nɛ kuloŋgboŋ na ya yili kebee nɛ baa tre Ararat na so.

english_verse: The water kept going down, and the mountain tops could be seen on the first day of the tenth month.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nɛ k daa yil nɛ nchu na bee gberge loŋ n ya fo kufɔl kudusopo to. Kufɔl kudusopo na to be kachɛ juŋkparso na nɛ kebee na be awɔltoana lar efuli.

english_verse: Forty days later Noah opened a window to send out a raven, but it kept flying around until the water had dried up.
translation_verse: nseŋ lara nyiŋgbeŋ ashi kuloŋgboŋ na to n lɛ kowu nɛ k baa wɔtɔ a lɛa a lɛa a jo saŋɛ nɛ nchu na kikɛ nyam beeŋ feeto kasawule so kuraa.

english_verse: Noah wanted to find out if the water had gone down, so he sent out a dove.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e lara keli malɛ n lɛ to nɛ e keni nchu na loge kasawule so a.

english_verse: Deep water was still everywhere, and when the dove could not find a place to land, it flew back to the boat. Then Noah held out his hand and helped it back in.
translation_verse: Ama keli na daa maŋ nya kaplɛkama nɛ k jɔŋɛ ŋkpal nchu na ka daŋ kraa wɔ kasawule so kikɛ so, amoso keli na daŋ naŋ bɛta nna m ba Nowa kutɔ ashi kuloŋgboŋ na to. Nɛ Nowa teŋi enɔ m pɛ keli na n wɔtɔ kuloŋgboŋ na to.

english_verse: It returned in the evening, holding in its beak a green leaf from an olive tree. Noah knew the water was finally going down.
translation_verse: Kumo be kase ka ya ka fo nɛ keli na bɛta m ba nɛ kedibi nɛ baa tre Ɔlif na be kefantaŋ popɔrbi fɛa kumo be kɔnɔ. Ndoŋ nna nɛ Nowa pin fanɛ nchu na kraa feeto nna.

english_verse: He waited seven more days before sending the dove out again, and this time it did not return.
translation_verse: Nɛ e naŋ jo bɔkwe koŋwule nseŋ naŋ lara keli na kuloŋgboŋ na to n lɛ kowu. Kede bre to, keli na maŋ naŋ bɛta m ba.

english_verse: By the twenty-seventh day of the second month, the earth was completely dry.
translation_verse: Kufɔl nyɔsopo na ka ya fo nchɛ adunyɔ nɛ ashunu nɛ kasawule na kikɛ wɔl nyam.

english_verse: God said to Noah,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Nowa le:

english_verse: “You, your wife, your sons, and your daughters-in-law may now leave the boat.
translation_verse: “To, naniere fo nɛ fo eche nɛ fo bibinyɛn na nɛ bumo be becheana e lar kuloŋgboŋ na to.

english_verse: Noah built an altar where he could offer sacrifices to the Lord. Then he offered on the altar one of each kind of animal and bird that could be used for a sacrifice.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Nowa gbare ajembu n deŋi abar so nseŋ pɛ m pɛ asɔbɔya nɛ a maŋ kɔ eyurpi n daga keta n lara sarga na be ako nɛ mbuibi nɛ a maŋ kɔ eyurpi n daga keta n lara sarga na be ako m mɔ n deŋi ajembu na so n chɔɔ n lara sarga n sa Ebɔrɛ.

english_verse: The smell of the burning offering pleased the Lord, and he said: Never again will I punish the earth for the sinful things its people do. All of them have evil thoughts from the time they are young, but I will never destroy everything that breathes, as I did this time.
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe na ka nu sarga na be efɛa belbelso na nɛ e kaŋɛ mbe kumu le: “N nyi fanɛ dimɛdi be kebia to kikɛ mbe nfɛra fɛso lubi, ama m maaŋ naŋ kpal dimɛdi so n sho kasawule ere kɔnɔ kikɛ. Ma alɛ maaŋ naŋ mur asɔ futeso fanɛ kananɛ n wora ere kikɛ.

english_verse: God said to Noah and his sons: I am giving you my blessing. Have a lot of children and grandchildren, so people will live everywhere on this earth.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ebɔrɛ nɛfa Nowa nɛ mbe mbia na nseŋ kaŋɛ bumo le: “Men kurge n wora keshi n sɔ kasawule so kikɛ.

english_verse: All animals, birds, reptiles, and fish will be afraid of you. I have placed them under your control,
translation_verse: Asɔbɔyaana kikɛ nɛ mbuibiana kikɛ nɛ asɔ gbeyesoana kikɛ nɛ ekɔrɔtɔana kikɛ beeŋ baa ŋana menyi nsaa ta kufu a shile menyi kutɔ. Ma alɛ ta amo kikɛ m bɔɔ menyi enɔ.

english_verse: and I have given them to you for food. From now on, you may eat them, as well as the green plants that you have always eaten.
translation_verse: Kusɔ kama nɛ k kɔ ŋkpa beeŋ baa la kusɔ jiso a sa menyi. Kananɛ n daŋ ta asɔ duuso kikɛ n sa menyi na, loŋ koŋwule na nɛ naniere mee ta kusɔ kama nyam nɛ k kɔ ŋkpa a sa menyi.

english_verse: But life is in the blood, and you must not eat any meat that still has blood in it.
translation_verse: Ama men sa maŋ kaŋ we eblaŋ kama nɛ kumo be ŋklaŋ maŋ lar kumo to, ŋkpal manɛ so, ŋklaŋ na to nɛ ŋkpa wɔ.

english_verse: I created humans to be like me, and I will punish any animal or person that takes a human life. If an animal kills someone, that animal must die. And if a person takes the life of another, that person must be put to death.
translation_verse: Esa kama nɛ e mɔ dimɛdi, baaŋ mɔ amodoŋwura gba n tal to, ŋkpal manɛ so, Ebɔrɛ pɔr dimɛdi nna fanɛ mbe kaduli.

english_verse: I want you and your descendants to have many children, so people will live everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Menyi ere e baa kurge n wora keshi n ti so n salga to n sɔ kasawule ere so kikɛ.”

english_verse: Again, God said to Noah and his sons:
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Ebɔrɛ naŋ kaŋɛ Nowa nɛ mbe bibinyɛnana na le:

english_verse: I am going to make a solemn promise to you and to everyone who will live after you.
translation_verse: “Yili kabre a yɔ, mee nase kɔnɔ nna a sa menyi nɛ men be kanaŋ to ebi

english_verse: I promise every living creature that the earth and those living on it will never again be destroyed by a flood.
translation_verse: Ma nɛ menyi be kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre nɛ mee nase a sa menyi nde, fanɛ m maaŋ naŋ ta nchu m mur durnya to be kusɔ futeso kikɛ. M maaŋ naŋ shin nɛ nchu e jija durnya ere kikɛ.”

english_verse: The rainbow that I have put in the sky will be my sign to you and to every living creature on earth. It will remind you that I will keep this promise forever.
translation_verse: Mee ta ma kabɔrɛnyaŋgelambi nna a wɔtɔ awɔlpa to nɛ k baa la ma nɛ durnya kikɛ be kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre na be kanyiŋi.

english_verse: When I send clouds over the earth, and a rainbow appears in the sky,
translation_verse: Saŋkama nɛ m baŋ shin nɛ bɔrɛwɔlpa deŋi nɛ kabɔrɛnyaŋgelambi lar awɔlpa na to,

english_verse: I will remember my promise to you and to all other living creatures. Never again will I let floodwaters destroy all life.
translation_verse: meeŋ nyiŋi ma nɛ menyi nɛ asɔ futeso kikɛ be kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre na. Kumo e la fanɛ m maaŋ naŋ shin nɛ nchu e bɔlɔ m mur kusɔ futeso kikɛ.

english_verse: When I see the rainbow in the sky, I will always remember the promise that I have made to every living creature.
translation_verse: Saŋkama nɛ kabɔrɛnyaŋgelambi na lar awɔlpa to, meeŋ wu kumo nseŋ nyiŋi ma nɛ menyi nɛ asɔ futeso kikɛ be kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre na.”

english_verse: Noah and his sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth, left the boat. Ham later had a son named Canaan.
translation_verse: Nowa be bibinyɛnsobi nɛ mo nɛ bumo daŋ shi kuloŋgboŋ na to n lar na e daa la Shɛm nɛ Ham nɛ Jafɛf. [Ham pibi e daa la Keenan.]

english_verse: Noah farmed the land and was the first to plant a vineyard.
translation_verse: Nowa e daa la edɔpo nɛ e fara a dɔ asɔrso nɛ baa ta a wora nsa nɛ baa tre wain na.

english_verse: Ham entered the tent and saw him naked, then went back outside and told his brothers.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ham nɛ e daa la Keenan mo tuto na ya wu mo tuto nɛ e dese eyurkpaŋ nɛ e lar n ya kaŋɛ mo daana benyɔ na.

english_verse: Shem and Japheth put a robe over their shoulders and walked backwards into the tent. Without looking at their father, they placed it over his body.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ mo daana Shɛm nɛ Jafɛf ta wajɛ m parga to n deŋi bumo be abatimu so nseŋ laŋɛ kaman loŋ n ta kumo n ya buu bumo tuto so. B daŋ pal kaman nna n ya wora loŋ, saŋɛ na so b maaŋ wu bumo tuto be eyurkpaŋ.

english_verse: he said, “I now put a curse on Canaan! He will be the lowest slave of his brothers.
translation_verse: “Kɔnɔsho e baa wɔ Keenan so. E beeŋ baa la mo daana be kenya.”

english_verse: I pray God will give Japheth more and more land and let him take over the territory of Shem. May Canaan be his slave.”
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ beeŋ shin nɛ Jafɛf be kasawule e kpalga to n ti so, nɛ mo nanabiana nɛ Shɛm e ba kaa wɔ abar be ewajɛbu to kɔnɔkoŋwuleso. Ama Keenan bre beeŋ ba ki Jafɛf be kenya.”

english_verse: Japheth's descendants had their own languages, tribes, and land. They were Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras. Gomer was the ancestor of Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah. Javan was the ancestor of Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim, who settled along the coast. The Descendants of Ham
translation_verse: Basa nɛ b daŋ n chena n chena teku be kɔnɔ na daŋ shi le be basa ere to nna. Bumo be ekama malɛ nɛ mbe kanaŋ e daa la nɛ bumo be ŋgbarana kɔr abar to. Basa nɛ b daŋ lar Ham be kanaŋ to be asheŋ

english_verse: but after some of them moved from the east and settled in Babylonia,
translation_verse: Basa daŋ sɔ epeŋipetekpa nna a yɔ nseŋ ya tu kaboŋ fultoso ko ashi Babilɔn be efuli so n ta ndoŋ ŋ ki bumo be kade.

english_verse: they said: Let's build a city with a tower that reaches to the sky! We'll use hard bricks and tar instead of stone and mortar. We'll become famous, and we won't be scattered all over the world.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ b kaŋɛ le: “Naniere bre men shin nɛ an pɔr kadegboŋ n sa anyi be amu nseŋ pɔr ketempreŋ jeŋgreŋ n ya chute awɔlpa, saŋɛ na so, anyi be ketre beeŋ dii nɛ anyi maaŋ naŋ pesaŋ to a wɔ kasawule so kikɛ.”

english_verse: But when the Lord came down to look at the city and the tower,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ba wu kadegboŋ na nɛ ketempreŋ jeŋgreŋ nɛ basa na daa pɔr na

english_verse: he said: These people are working together because they all speak the same language. This is just the beginning. Soon they will be able to do anything they want.
translation_verse: nseŋ kaŋɛ le: “Ŋkpal basa ere ka la basa koŋwule a gbar ŋgbar koŋwule nseŋ fara a wora kusɔ nɛ baa wora ere, kumo ere kusɔ kama nɛ baa fɛ kewora, baaŋ tiŋ n wora kumo.

english_verse: Let's go down and confuse them! We'll make them speak different languages, and they won't be able to understand each other.
translation_verse: Amoso men shin nɛ an yɔ n ya wea bumo be ŋgbar na to, saŋɛ na so b maaŋ naa nu abar be ŋgbar.”

english_verse: So the people had to stop building the city, because the Lord confused their language and scattered them all over the earth. That's how the city of Babel got its name. The Descendants of Shem
translation_verse: Loŋ be kade na nɛ b daa tre Babilɔn, ŋkpal manɛ so, ndoŋ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na daŋ wea basa kikɛ be ŋgbar to nseŋ pesaŋ bumo to nɛ b sɔ kasawule so kikɛ. Shɛm be kanaŋ to ebi be asheŋ

english_verse: Terah decided to move from Ur to the land of Canaan. He took along Abram and Sarai and his grandson Lot, the son of Haran. But when they came to the city of Haran, they settled there instead.
translation_verse: Nɛ Tɛra keta mo pibinyɛn Eebram nɛ mo nanabi Lɔt nɛ e daa la Haran pibinyɛn na nɛ mo shache Sɛɛrai, Eebram be eche, n ti mbe kumu so nɛ b lar Ur ashi Babilɔnia n yɔ Keenan be kasawule so. B ka bee yɔ Keenan n ya fo Haran nɛ b chena ndoŋ.

english_verse: The Lord said to Abram: Leave your country, your family, and your relatives and go to the land that I will show you.
translation_verse: Kachako nɛ Enyɛnpetale na kaŋɛ Eebram: “Lar fo efuli so nɛ fo basa to nɛ fo tuto be kowu to nseŋ yɔ kasawule nɛ mee sha keŋini fo ere so.

english_verse: I will bless you and make your descendants into a great nation. You will become famous and be a blessing to others.
translation_verse: Meeŋ shin nɛ fo ki kanaŋgboŋwura nsaa kɔ efuligboŋ. Meeŋ nɛfa fo n shin nɛ fo ketre e dii, nɛ fo ki nɛfa n sa basa kikɛ.

english_verse: I will bless those who bless you, but I will put a curse on anyone who puts a curse on you. Everyone on earth will be blessed because of you.
translation_verse: Bekama malɛ nɛ b nɛfa fo, ma alɛ gba beeŋ nɛfa bumo. Ama ekama nɛ e sho fo kɔnɔ, ma alɛ gba beeŋ sho amodoŋwura kɔnɔ. Fo so nɛ meeŋ bɔla n nɛfa durnya to ebi kikɛ.”

english_verse: Abram went as far as the sacred tree of Moreh in a place called Shechem. The Canaanites were still living in the land at that time,
translation_verse: B ka ya fo Keenan nɛ Eebram nite ŋ kulti kasawule na so hale n ya fo More be kedibigboŋ na ase, ashi Shɛkɛm. Kumo be saŋɛ malɛ nɛ Keenanebi kraa tase kasawule na so.

english_verse: but the Lord appeared to Abram and promised, “I will give this land to your family forever.” Abram then built an altar there for the Lord.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nɛ Enyɛnpe na lar Eebram so ŋ kaŋɛ mo: “Meeŋ ta kasawule ere n sa fo kanaŋ to ebi.” Kumo be kaman nɛ Eebram yuu bɔrɛsure ndoŋ n lara sarga n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ e lar mo so ndoŋ na.

english_verse: Abram traveled to the hill country east of Bethel and camped between Bethel and Ai, where he built another altar and worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e yɔ abee nɛ a wɔ Bɛtɛl be epeŋipetekpa be kaba so na n ya yuu mbe ewajɛbu Bɛtɛl nɛ Ai be kefɛato. Ndoŋ nɛ Eebram naŋ yuu bɔrɛsure m bunyaŋ Enyɛnpe na pɔɛŋ

english_verse: The crops failed, and there was no food anywhere in Canaan. So Abram and his wife Sarai went to live in Egypt for a while. But just before they got there, Abram said, “Sarai, you are really beautiful!
translation_verse: Mo nɛ mbe eche Sɛɛrai ka ta loŋ n ya kaa taga to Ijipt nɛ e kaŋɛ mo le: “Sɛɛrai, n nyi fo ka walɛ kebita ga.

english_verse: When the Egyptians see you, they will murder me because I am your husband. But they won't kill you.
translation_verse: Amoso Ijiptebi ere baŋ wu fo, baaŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ ma eche e la fo, nseŋ kpal loŋ so m mɔ ma ŋ ka fo.

english_verse: As soon as Abram and Sarai arrived in Egypt, the Egyptians noticed how beautiful she was.
translation_verse: Kashenteŋto malɛ, Eebram nɛ Sɛɛrai ka luri Ijipt nɛ Ijiptebi na wu fanɛ Sɛɛrai walɛ kebita pasaa.

english_verse: The king was good to Abram because of Sarai, and Abram was given sheep, cattle, donkeys, slaves, and camels.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal Sɛɛrai so, ewura Fɛɛro daŋ keni Eebram so nna nɛnɛ nseŋ daŋ sa mo mbolpɔ nɛ ana nɛ ekurma nyɛnso nɛ becheso nɛ anya nyɛnso nɛ becheso n ta enyɔma n ti so.

english_verse: Finally, the king sent for Abram and said to him, “What have you done to me? Why didn't you tell me Sarai was your wife?
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura na shuŋi nɛ b ya tre Eebram m ba nɛ e bishi mo: “Manɛ e ba nɛ fo wora ma loŋ? Nuso nɛ a ji nɛ fo maŋ kaŋɛ ma fanɛ Sɛɛrai la fo eche nna?

english_verse: Why did you make me believe she was your sister? Now I've married her. Take her and go! She's your wife.”
translation_verse: Manɛ so nɛ fo kaŋɛ fanɛ e la fo sipoche nna nseŋ shin nɛ n ta mo fanɛ ma eche? To, fo eche nde. Keta fo kusɔ a yɔ.”

english_verse: So the king told his men to let Abram and Sarai take their possessions and leave.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura Fɛɛro lara basa ŋ kaŋɛ bumo fanɛ b keta Eebram nɛ mbe eche nɛ asɔ nɛ b kɔ na kikɛ n lar kasawule na so.

english_verse: Abram was very rich. He owned many cattle, sheep, and goats, and had a lot of silver and gold.
translation_verse: Eebram daa la damawura nna kashenteŋto nseŋ daa kɔ mbolpɔ nɛ mboe nɛ ana nɛ shuwa nɛ gbiti.

english_verse: Abram moved from place to place in the Southern Desert. And finally, he went north and set up his tents between Bethel and Ai,
translation_verse: K maŋ chɛr nɛ Eebram naŋ lar ndoŋ a na a kilgi to hale n ya kaa taga to Bɛtɛl. E ka fo Ai nɛ Bɛtɛl be kefɛato, kakpa nɛ e daŋ yuu mbe ewajɛbu na

english_verse: where he had earlier camped and built an altar. There he worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: nɛ kakpa nɛ e daŋ yuu bɔrɛsure na, nɛ e naŋ bunyaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be ketre.

english_verse: Lot, who was traveling with him, also had sheep, goats, and cattle, as well as his own family and slaves.
translation_verse: Lɔt gba daŋ keta mbe mbolpɔ nɛ mboe nɛ ana nɛ mbe kanaŋ nna n tu Eebram n yɔ.

english_verse: At this time the Canaanites and the Perizzites were still living in the same area, and so there wasn't enough pastureland left for Abram and Lot with all of their animals. Besides this, the men who took care of Abram's animals and the ones who took care of Lot's animals started quarreling.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman Keenanebi na nɛ Pɛrizebi na gba daa wɔ kasawule na so nna n ti so. Amoso kolu daŋ tɔr Eebram nɛ Lɔt be asɔbɔyakpapoana so nna ŋkpal asɔbɔya be ejikpa so.

english_verse: Abram said to Lot, “We are close relatives. We shouldn't argue, and our men shouldn't be fighting one another.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Eebram kaŋɛ Lɔt le: “An la basa koŋwule nna, k maŋ daga kamalga ka wɔ ma nɛ fo be nferinto ŋko fo basa nɛ ma basa ka bee bile ŋkpal kasawule so.

english_verse: There is plenty of land for you to choose from. Let's separate. If you go north, I'll go south; if you go south, I'll go north.”
translation_verse: Mannɛ kasawule e dese ere a? Amoso shin nɛ an barga to n chena. Nɛ fo yɔ benaso, ma alɛ beeŋ yɔ jisoso nɛ fo alɛ naŋ yɔ jiso so, ma alɛ beeŋ yɔ benaso.”

english_verse: This happened before the Lord had destroyed the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah. And when Lot looked around, he saw there was plenty of water in the Jordan Valley. All the way to Zoar the valley was as green as the garden of the Lord or the land of Egypt.
translation_verse: Nɛ Lɔt maŋ mbe kumu so ŋ keni n wu Jɔɔdan be ketaŋɛ ka dese n ya fo Zowar, a kɔ nchu nseŋ daa du fanɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be kudɔbi nɛ baa tre Iden na, ŋko Ijipt be kasawule. [Ade kikɛ daŋ wora nna pɔɛŋ nɛ Enyɛnpe mur Sodɔm nɛ Gomɔra be ndegboŋ na.]

english_verse: So Lot chose the whole Jordan Valley for himself, and as he started out toward the east, he and Abram separated.
translation_verse: Eebram ka daŋ kaŋɛ loŋ na nɛ Lɔt lara Jɔɔdan be ketaŋɛ na be kaba so kikɛ n sa mbe kumu nseŋ barga n ya chena epeŋipetekpa be kaba so. To, kananɛ bumo benyɔ na daŋ barga abar nna na:

english_verse: Abram stayed in the land of Canaan. But Lot settled near the cities of the valley and put up his tents not far from Sodom,
translation_verse: Eebram daŋ chena Keenan be kasawule so nna nɛ Lɔt malɛ daŋ chena nde nɛ a wɔ Jɔɔdan be ketaŋɛ na be nferinto nseŋ yuu mbe ewajɛbu m mata Sodɔm.

english_verse: where the people were evil and sinned terribly against the Lord. Abram Moves to Hebron
translation_verse: Sodɔmebi malɛ daa la dalubiwuraana nna nseŋ daa wora alubi ga a gbiti Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na. Eebram ka yɔ Hibrɔn be asheŋ

english_verse: After Abram and Lot had gone their separate ways, the Lord said to Abram: Look around to the north, south, east, and west.
translation_verse: Eebram nɛ Lɔt ka daŋ barga abar na be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ Eebram le: “Yili kaboŋ nɛ fo wɔ ere m maŋ fo kumu so ŋ keni ŋ kulti kakpa nɛ fo wɔ ere kikɛ.

english_verse: I will give you and your family all the land you can see. It will be theirs forever!
translation_verse: Meeŋ ta kasawule nɛ fo wu ere kikɛ n sa fo nɛ fo kaman to ebi nɛ k baa la menyeya nna hale mbaanaayɔ.

english_verse: I will give you more descendants than there are specks of dust on the earth, and someday it will be easier to count those specks of dust than to count your descendants.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman, meeŋ shin nɛ fo kaman to ebi e wora keshi fanɛ kasawule so be shishɛr. Amoso nɛ esa baŋ tiŋ ŋ karga kasawule so be shishɛr, kumo ere e beeŋ tiŋ ŋ karga fo kaman to ebi gba.

english_verse: Now walk back and forth across the land, because I am going to give it to you.
translation_verse: Koso n nite kasawule na be nteŋ to nɛ mparto kikɛ, ŋkpal manɛ so, fo nɛ meeŋ ta kumo n sa.”

english_verse: Abram took down his tents and went to live near the sacred trees of Mamre at Hebron, where he built an altar in honor of the Lord.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Eebram tia mbe wajɛbu ŋ kaa n ya chena m mata Mamre be ndibigboŋ na ashi Hibrɔn nseŋ yuu bɔrɛsure a bunyaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ.

english_verse: About this time, King Amraphel of Babylonia, King Arioch of Ellasar, King Chedorlaomer of Elam, and King Tidal of Goiim
translation_verse: Jemanɛ nɛ Lɔt nɛ Eebram barga to nna nɛ Babilɔn be efuli so be ewura Amrafɛl nɛ Ɛlasa be ewura Ariɔk nɛ Ilam be ewura Kedɔrlawomer nɛ Goyiim be ewura Taidal kre kena m ba kɔ

english_verse: attacked King Bera of Sodom, King Birsha of Gomorrah, King Shinab of Admah, King Shemeber of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela, a city also known as Zoar.
translation_verse: Sodɔm be ewura Bɛra nɛ Gomɔra be ewura Birsha nɛ Adnab be ewura Shinab nɛ Zeboyim be ewura Shemeber nɛ Bela nɛ baa tre Zowar na be ewura na.

english_verse: King Chedorlaomer and his allies had ruled these last five kings for twelve years, but in the thirteenth year the kings rebelled and joined forces in Siddim Valley, which is now covered by the southern part of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Nfɛ kuduanyɔ nɛ b daŋ shuŋ ewura Kedɔrlawomer, ama kafɛ kuduasasopo to, nɛ b nyaŋɛ to ŋ kini fanɛ b maaŋ naŋ shuŋ mo.

english_verse: A year later King Chedorlaomer and his allies attacked and defeated the Rephaites in Ashteroth-Karnaim, the Zuzites in Ham, and the Emites in Shaveh-Kiriathaim.
translation_verse: Kafɛ kuduanasopo na to nɛ ewura Kedɔrlawomer nɛ bewura asa nɛ b daŋ ti mo so na nɛ bumo be benapo yɔ n ya kɔ m pɔɔ Refayebi nɛ b wɔ Ashterɔf Karnaya na nɛ Zuzebi ashi Ham nɛ Emiebi ashi Shaivaa Kiryatayim be kepreŋ so

english_verse: They also defeated the Horites in the hill country of Edom, as far as El-Paran, near the desert.
translation_verse: nɛ Horebi ashi Edɔm be efuli so be abee to na so nseŋ bɛ bumo so n yɔ kufɔ n ya fo Ɛl Paran be kiyi na be ekar.

english_verse: They went back to the city of Enmishpat, better known as Kadesh. Then they captured all the land that belonged to the Amalekites, and they defeated the Amorites who were living in Hazazon-Tamar.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ b bɛta kaman m ba Ɛn Mishpat. Ndoŋ nna nɛ b naŋ ya kɔ n sɔ Amalɛkebi be nsawule kikɛ nseŋ naŋ kɔ m pɔɔ so Amɔriebi nɛ b daa wɔ Hazazɔn Tamaa na malɛ so.

english_verse: At Siddim Valley, the armies of the kings of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, Zeboiim, and Bela fought the armies of King Chedorlaomer of Elam, King Tidal of Goiim, King Amraphel of Babylonia, and King Arioch of Ellasar. The valley
translation_verse: m ba kaa kɔ Ilam be bewura nɛ baa tre Kedɔrlawomer na nɛ Goyiim be ewura nɛ baa tre Taidal na nɛ Babilɔn be ewura nɛ baa tre Amrafɛl na nɛ Ɛlasa be ewura nɛ baa tre Ariɔk na kena nɛ k ki fanɛ bewura anu e daŋ kɔ bewura ana na. Bewura ana na be atre e daa la Kedɔrlawomer nɛ Taidal nɛ Amrafɛl nɛ Ariɔk.

english_verse: Their enemies took everything of value from Sodom and Gomorrah, including their food supplies.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ bewura ana na ya bela Sodɔm nɛ Gomɔra be asɔ nɛ ajibi kikɛ kuraa n choŋ.

english_verse: They also captured Abram's nephew Lot, who lived in Sodom. They took him and his possessions and then left.
translation_verse: Eebram mo sipo pibi Lɔt malɛ daa wɔ Sodɔm nna, amoso b daŋ ta mo alɛ gba nɛ mbe asɔ nɛ e kɔ kikɛ nna n ti so n yɔ.

english_verse: At this time Abram the Hebrew was living near the oaks that belonged to Mamre the Amorite. Mamre and his brothers Eshcol and Aner were Abram's friends. Someone who had escaped from the battle told Abram
translation_verse: Ama kanyɛn ko bre daŋ nya mbe kumu n shile nseŋ ya kaŋɛ Eebram, Hibruw be esa na, asheŋ nɛ a daŋ wora na kikɛ. Eebram malɛ daŋ chena m mata ndibigboŋ ko nɛ a daa la Amɔriebi be esa ko nɛ baa tre Mamre na peya. Mamre nɛ mo sipoana Ɛshkɔl nɛ Anɛr nɛ Eebram daŋ yili kumo nna fanɛ baaŋ baa chɛ abar to.

english_verse: that his nephew Lot had been taken away. Three hundred and eighteen of Abram's servants were fighting men, so he took them and followed the enemy as far north as the city of Dan.
translation_verse: Eebram ka nu fanɛ b pɛ mo sipo pibi na nɛ e tre benapo nɛ b kurge mbe laŋ to kikɛ m ba shɛr. Bumo kikɛ daa wɔ basa alfa asa nɛ kuduaburwa, nɛ b ju m buu bewura ana na so hale n ya fo kade nɛ baa tre Dan na.

english_verse: That night, Abram divided up his troops, attacked from all sides, and won a great victory. But some of the enemy escaped to the town of Hobah north of Damascus,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nɛ e ya barga mbe benapo to ntuŋ ntuŋ so nɛ b kɔ bumo doŋana na kena kanyɛso m pɔɔ bumo so cheche nseŋ ju m bɛ bumo so loŋ n ya fo Hobab nɛ k daa wɔ Damaskɔs be kelargato be esoso be kaba so na.

english_verse: and Abram went after them. He brought back his nephew Lot, together with Lot's possessions and the women and everyone else who had been captured. Abram Is Blessed by Melchizedek
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nɛ Eebram ya suge asɔ nɛ b daŋ ta na nseŋ bɛta mo sipo pibi Lɔt nɛ mbe asɔ nɛ ana nɛ beche nɛ basa pɔtɛ nɛ b daŋ ti so na kikɛ nyam m ba. Mɛlkizedɛk ka nɛfa Eebram be asheŋ

english_verse: Abram returned after he had defeated King Chedorlaomer and the other kings. Then the king of Sodom went to meet Abram in Shaveh Valley, which is also known as King's Valley.
translation_verse: Eebram ka daŋ ya kɔ m pɔɔ Kedɔrlawomer nɛ bewura nɛ b daŋ chɛ mo to a kɔ na so, nseŋ bɛta a ba na, nɛ Sodɔm be ewura daŋ ya shɛr mo to ashi Shave be Ketaŋɛ nɛ baa tre Bewura be Ketaŋɛ na to.

english_verse: King Melchizedek of Salem was a priest of God Most High. He brought out some bread and wine
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mɛlkizedɛk nɛ e daa la Salɛm be ewura nseŋ naa la Ebɔrɛ Ewurgboŋ na be bɔrɛmatapo na, ta bodobodo nɛ nsa ko m bar Eebram

english_verse: and said to Abram: “I bless you in the name of God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth.
translation_verse: nseŋ nɛfa mo ŋ kaŋɛ: “Ebɔrɛ Ewurgboŋ nɛ e to esoso nɛ kasawule na e nɛfa fo Eebram.

english_verse: All praise belongs to God Most High for helping you defeat your enemies.” Then Abram gave Melchizedek a tenth of everything.
translation_verse: Kemaŋkura e baa la Ebɔrɛ Ewurgboŋ nɛ e sa fo eleŋ nɛ fo kɔ m pɔɔ fo doŋana so na peya.” Nɛ Eebram sa Mɛlkizedɛk asɔ nɛ e ya nya kena na to na kikɛ be kudukudusopo.

english_verse: The king of Sodom said to Abram, “All I want are my people. You can keep everything else.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Sodɔm be ewura malɛ kaŋɛ Eebram: “Ta asɔ na bre nseŋ laŋɛ ma basa kikɛ n sa ma.”

english_verse: Abram answered: The Lord God Most High made the heavens and the earth. And I have promised him
translation_verse: Nɛ Eebram kaŋɛ: “M bɔ ntaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ Ewurgboŋ nɛ e to esoso nɛ kasawule na be anishito

english_verse: that I won't keep anything of yours, not even a sandal strap or a piece of thread. Then you can never say that you are the one who made me rich.
translation_verse: fanɛ m maaŋ ta fo kusɔ kama, hale kajesebi ŋko kesebeta be kawɔlbi gba, saŋɛ na so fo maaŋ nya ŋ kaŋɛ le: ‘Ma e shin nɛ Eebram ki damawura.’

english_verse: Let my share be the food that my men have eaten. But Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre went with me, so give them their share of what we brought back.
translation_verse: Ŋ gbagba maaŋ ta fo shɛŋ ama kusɔ nɛ mbrantiɛ na ji kena na to na nawule. Ama shin nɛ n teriana Anɛr nɛ Eshkɔl nɛ Mamre e ta asɔ nɛ an bar na be ako.”

english_verse: Later the Lord spoke to Abram in a vision, “Abram, don't be afraid! I will protect you and reward you greatly.”
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ Eebram ku bɔrɛdare nseŋ nu Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ka kaŋɛ mo: “Eebram, sa maa lɔ kufu. Ma e la fo ekumpo meeŋ ka fo kukɔ gboŋgboŋi.”

english_verse: But Abram answered, “Lord All-Powerful, you have given me everything I could ask for, except children. And when I die, Eliezer of Damascus will get all I own.
translation_verse: Nɛ Eebram kaŋɛ: “Enyɛnpe lela, ŋ ka baa maŋ kɔ mbia ere, manɛ be kelela nɛ fo kakɔka ere beeŋ wora ma? Damaskɔs be Eliaza ere e naaŋ ji ma kapetɛ na.

english_verse: You have not given me any children, and this servant of mine will inherit everything.”
translation_verse: Fo maŋ sa ma mbia, amoso ma anya ere be eko e naaŋ ji ma kapetɛ na.”

english_verse: The Lord replied, “No, he won't! You will have a son of your own, and everything you have will be his.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Eebram naŋ nu Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ka naŋ malga mo kutɔ ŋ kaŋɛ: “Mannɛ fo kenya Eliaza e naaŋ ji fo kapetɛ. Fo gbagba pibinyɛn kurgeso e naaŋ ki fo asɔ be kumuwura.”

english_verse: Then the Lord took Abram outside and said, “Look at the sky and see if you can count the stars. That's how many descendants you will have.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ shin nɛ Eebram lar kowu nɛ e kaŋɛ mo: “Keni esoso ŋ keni, feeŋ tiŋ ŋ karga achɛkpabi ere a? To, nɛ fo maaŋ tiŋ ŋ karga amo bre, kumo ere loŋ nɛ fo kanaŋ to ebi beeŋ ba kaa sa na.”

english_verse: Abram believed the Lord, so the Lord was pleased with him and accepted him. The Lord Makes Another Promise to Abram
translation_verse: Nɛ Eebram yirda Enyɛnpe be kamalga na. Nɛ Enyɛnpe na malɛ kpal loŋ so n nase kumo fanɛ e la esa nɛ e niŋi nna ashi mbe anishi to.

english_verse: Abram asked, “Lord God, how can I know the land will be mine?”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Eebram kaŋɛ: “Enyɛnpetale lela, manɛ e naaŋ baa la tɔɔnɛ fanɛ kasawule ere beeŋ baa la meya?”

english_verse: Then the Lord told him, “Bring me a three-year-old cow, a three-year-old female goat, a three-year-old ram, a dove, and a young pigeon.”
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ mo: “Bar ma nache fɔlbi nɛ kaboelote nɛ kpakpa, nɛ b fo nfɛ asasa, n ta lepɔ nɛ keli fɔlbi gba n ti so.”

english_verse: Abram obeyed the Lord. Then he cut the animals in half and laid the two halves of each animal opposite each other on the ground. But he did not cut the doves and pigeons in half.
translation_verse: Nɛ Eebram bar loŋ be asɔ na Ebɔrɛ be anishito nseŋ ku ŋ ku asɔbɔya na bre to anyɔnyɔ n ta kaba kama n nase m mata kumo barkasa kasawule. Ama e daa maŋ ku mbuibi na bre to.

english_verse: And when birds came down to eat the animals, Abram chased them away.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ejita ba kaa jɔŋɛ eblaŋ na so nɛ Eebram ju bumo.

english_verse: As the sun was setting, Abram fell into a deep sleep, and everything became dark and frightening.
translation_verse: Saŋɛ nɛ epeŋi bee sha ketɔr na nɛ Eebram di m mel nɛ tentembiri plɔtɔ ba buu mo so.

english_verse: Then the Lord said: Abram, you will live to an old age and die in peace. But I solemnly promise that your descendants will live as foreigners in a land that doesn't belong to them. They will be forced into slavery and abused for
translation_verse: Ama fo ere beeŋ ji kasawule ere so n ya bel n fuli kumu nseŋ wu kagbenewushi be luwu nɛ b puli fo.

english_verse: Four generations later, your descendants will return here and take this land, because only then will the people who live here be so sinful that they deserve to be punished.
translation_verse: Fo kenanagbiramuli be jemanɛ to nɛ baaŋ naŋ bɛta m ba kasawule ere so. Loŋ be saŋɛ na nɛ Amɔriebi be alubi wora keshi ga nseŋ daga kasogberge.”

english_verse: Sometime after sunset, when it was very dark, a smoking cooking pot and a flaming fire passed between the two halves of each animal.
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman epeŋi ka tɔr nɛ kaboŋ biri to nɛ kapuliya nɛ edishi bee lar kumo to nɛ kabulpi suseso ko ba choŋ n lar epul na to m ba bɔla eblaŋ na be nfɛato n choŋ.

english_verse: At that time the Lord made an agreement with Abram and told him: I will give your descendants the land east of the Shihor River on the border of Egypt as far as the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: To, kumo be kachɛ na nɛ Enyɛnpe nɛ Eebram wora kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre nɛ Enyɛnpe kaŋɛ mo: “Kɔnɔ nɛ mee nase a sa fo e la fanɛ meeŋ ta kasawule nɛ k yili lɔr nɛ k wɔ Ijipt be kasawule be ekar n ya fo lɔrgboŋ nɛ baa tre Yufreetes na kikɛ n sa fo kaman to ebi,

english_verse: They will possess the land of the Kenites, the Kenizzites, the Kadmonites,
translation_verse: n ta Kenebi nɛ Kenizebi nɛ Kadmɔnebi

english_verse: the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Rephaites,
translation_verse: nɛ Hitebi nɛ Pɛrizebi nɛ Refayebi

english_verse: the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Girgashites, and the Jebusites.
translation_verse: nɛ Amɔriebi nɛ Keenanebi nɛ Girgasebi nɛ Jebusiebi be nsawule kikɛ n ti so.”

english_verse: Abram's wife Sarai had not been able to have any children. But she owned a young Egyptian slave woman named Hagar,
translation_verse: Saŋɛ ere so kikɛ nɛ Eebram be eche Sɛɛrai daa maŋ naŋ kurge mbia n sa mo. Sɛɛrai malɛ daa kɔ Ijipt be kebita ko nɛ baa tre mo Heega.

english_verse: and Sarai said to Abram, “The Lord has not given me any children. Sleep with my slave, and if she has a child, it will be mine.” Abram agreed,
translation_verse: Kachako nɛ Sɛɛrai kaŋɛ Eebram: “Keni, Enyɛnpe maŋ sa ma kakurge nna na, nɛ manɛ nna nɛ fo maaŋ tu ma kebita ere n di? Ashere e beeŋ kurge mbia n sa ma.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ Eebram shuli n sa Sɛɛrai.

english_verse: and Sarai gave him Hagar to be his wife. This happened after Abram had lived in the land of Canaan for ten years.
translation_verse: Nɛ Sɛɛrai ta mbe Ijipt be kebita Heega na n sa Eebram fanɛ e ki mbe eche. Eebram daŋ chena Keenan beeŋ wora nfɛ kudu be kaman nna pɔɛŋ nɛ loŋ be kesheŋ na wora.

english_verse: Later, when Hagar knew she was going to have a baby, she became proud and treated Sarai hatefully.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Eebram nɛ Heega gama keche nɛ kenyɛn nɛ e di kedampo. Heega ka baŋ pin fanɛ e di kedampo na nɛ e nya kamoowu nseŋ daa maŋ naa keni Sɛɛrai a bɔlɔ kenishi.

english_verse: Then Sarai said to Abram, “It's all your fault! I gave you my slave woman, but she has been hateful to me ever since she found out she was pregnant. You have done me wrong, and you will have to answer to the Lord for this.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Sɛɛrai kaŋɛ Eebram: “Fo e shin nɛ Heega bee keni ma jiga na. Ma alɛ gbagba e ta mo n sa fo, ama yili saŋɛ nɛ e wu fanɛ e kɔ kedampo na kikɛ e maŋ naa tre ma ere shɛŋ. Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na malɛ e naaŋ ji ma nɛ fo demu n wu emo nɛ e kɔ kashenteŋ, fo ŋko ma.”

english_verse: Abram said, “All right! She's your slave—do whatever you want with her.” Then Sarai began treating Hagar so harshly that she finally ran away.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Eebram kaŋɛ: “To, Heega la fo kebita nna, nsaa wɔ fo kaseto, amoso, wora mo kusɔ kama nɛ fee sha.” Ŋkpal loŋ so nɛ Sɛɛrai fara a wora Heega asheŋ nɛ a maŋ daga, nɛ e shile.

english_verse: Hagar stopped to rest at a spring in the desert on the road to Shur. While she was there, the angel of the Lord came to her
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be malaika ya tu Heega ketirbu ko ase ashi keshishɛrsawule ko so ashi Shur be ekpa to,

english_verse: and asked, “Hagar, where have you come from, and where are you going?” She answered, “I'm running away from Sarai, my owner.”
translation_verse: nseŋ bishi mo: “Heega, Sɛɛrai be kebita, nnɛ nɛ fo shi m ba nfe nɛ nnɛ malɛ nɛ fee yɔ?” Nɛ e kaŋɛ: “Mee shile ashi n chepe Sɛɛrai kutɔ nna.”

english_verse: The angel said, “Go back to Sarai and be her slave.
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe be malaika na kaŋɛ mo: “Bɛta n yɔ mo kutɔ n ya ka la mbe kebita.”

english_verse: I will give you a son, who will be called Ishmael, because I have heard your cry for help. And someday I will give you so many descendants that no one will be able to count them all.
translation_verse: Feeŋ kurge ebinyɛn fo kedampo ere to nseŋ nase mo ketre Ishmaɛl, ŋkpal manɛ so, Enyɛnpe na nu fo awurfoŋ be kushu na.

english_verse: But your son will live far from his relatives; he will be like a wild donkey, fighting everyone, and everyone fighting him.”
translation_verse: Ama fo pibinyɛn na beeŋ ba ki fanɛ kurma nɛ k kpeŋ n luri kupuŋ to nna. Mo nɛ basa kikɛ beeŋ kɔ abar kena. Mo nɛ mo niopibiana beeŋ ba barga abar a wɔtɔ.”

english_verse: Hagar thought, “Have I really seen God and lived to tell about it?” So from then on she called him, “The God Who Sees Me.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Heega bishi mbe kumu le: “Ma alɛ e wu Ebɔrɛ nseŋ kraa wɔ ŋkpa to ere a?” Kumo be kaman nɛ e nase Enyɛnpe nɛ e daŋ malga mo kutɔ na ketre fanɛ “Ebɔrɛ nɛ e bee wu asheŋ.”

english_verse: That's why people call the well between Kadesh and Bered, “The Well of the Living One Who Sees Me.”
translation_verse: Amoso nɛ basa bee tre ketirbu nɛ Heega daa wɔ kumo ase nɛ k wɔ Kadɛsh nɛ Berɛd be nferinto na Beer Laha Roi na. Loŋ be ketirbu na malɛ kraa wɔtɔ hale nɛ mbre.

english_verse: I will keep my solemn promise to you and give you more descendants than can be counted.”
translation_verse: Saŋɛ na so ma nɛ fo be kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre fanɛ meeŋ shin nɛ fo kanaŋ to ebi e wora keshi ga na, beeŋ bɔlɔ so.”

english_verse: Abram bowed with his face to the ground, and God said:
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Eebram gbir ŋ kurgi kumu n yuu. E ka wora loŋ na nɛ Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ le:

english_verse: I promise that you will be the father of many nations. So now I'm changing your name from Abram to Abraham.
translation_verse: Fo ketre malɛ maŋ naa la Eebram. K beeŋ ki Eebraham, ŋkpal manɛ so, n ta fo ŋ ki efuli damtaana be basa bumo tuto nna.

english_verse: I will give you a lot of descendants, and they will become great nations. Some of them will even be kings.
translation_verse: Meeŋ shin nɛ fo mbia e wora keshi nɛ efuli damtaana nɛ bewuraana e shi bumo to n lar.

english_verse: I will always keep the promise I have made to you and your descendants, because I am your God and their God.
translation_verse: Meeŋ nase ma kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre n sa fo nɛ fo kaman to ebi nɛ bumo alɛ be kaman to ebi mbaanaayɔ. Meeŋ baa la fo nɛ fo kaman to ebi kikɛ be Ebɔrɛ.

english_verse: I will give you and them the land in which you are now a foreigner. I will give the whole land of Canaan to your family forever, and I will be their God.
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman, meeŋ ta Keenan be kasawule mo nɛ men la befɔ ashi kumo so naniere ere n sa fo nɛ k ki fo nɛ fo kaman to ebi be kapetɛ mbaanaayɔ nɛ ma alɛ e baa la bumo be Ebɔrɛ.”

english_verse: As the sign that you are keeping this promise, you must circumcise every man and boy in your family.
translation_verse: Men be katutuku na e naaŋ ki kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre na be tɔɔnɛ a wɔ ma nɛ menyi be kefɛato.

english_verse: Any man who isn't circumcised hasn't kept his part of the promise and cannot be one of my people.
translation_verse: Amoso enyɛn kama nɛ e maŋ ku kututu daga b ka lara mo ashi ma basa to, ŋkpal manɛ so, e maŋ bɛ ma kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre be kɔnɔ naseso na so nna na.”

english_verse: I will bless her, and you will have a son by her. She will become the mother of nations, and some of her descendants will even be kings.
translation_verse: Meeŋ nɛfa mo nseŋ shin nɛ e kurge ebinyɛn n sa fo. Meeŋ nɛfa mo n shin nɛ mbe mbia e ki efuli damta be bewura.”

english_verse: But God answered: No! You and Sarah will have a son. His name will be Isaac, and I will make an everlasting promise to him and his descendants.
translation_verse: Nɛ Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ: “Ayai, loŋ maaŋ wora, fo eche Sɛɛra e naaŋ kurge ebinyɛn n sa fo nɛ fo nase mo ketre Aizek. Meeŋ shin nɛ ma kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre na e baa wɔ mo ere nɛ mbe kaman to ebi so mbaanaayɔ.

english_verse: However, I have heard what you asked me to do for Ishmael, and so I will also bless him with many descendants. He will be the father of twelve princes, and I will make his family a great nation.
translation_verse: N nu kusɔ nɛ fo kule a yɔ Ishmaɛl be kaplɛa so na, amoso meeŋ nɛfa mo alɛ gba nseŋ sa mo mbia damta nɛ kaman to ebi damta. Ade kikɛ be kaman e beeŋ ki bewurbi kuduanyɔ bumo tuto nɛ n shin nɛ mbe efuli e ki efuli lempo gboŋgboŋi.

english_verse: But your son Isaac will be born about this time next year, and the promise I am making to you and your family will be for him and his descendants forever.
translation_verse: Ama meeŋ shin nɛ ma kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre na bre e baa wɔ fo pibinyɛn Aizek nɛ Sɛɛra beeŋ kurge kafɛ a ba saŋɛ ere so na so.”

english_verse: God finished speaking to Abraham and then left.
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ ka malga Eebraham kutɔ n loge nɛ e yɔ ŋ ka mo.

english_verse: On that same day Abraham obeyed God by circumcising Ishmael. Abraham was also circumcised, and so were all the other men and boys in his household, including his servants and slaves. He was
translation_verse: Loŋ be kachɛ na gbagba nɛ b daŋ ku Eebraham be laŋ to be enyɛn kama, bumo nɛ b kurge mbe laŋ to nɛ bumo nɛ b daŋ tɔ na kikɛ.

english_verse: One hot summer afternoon while Abraham was sitting by the entrance to his tent near the sacred trees of Mamre, the Lord appeared to him.
translation_verse: Kachako nɛ Enyɛnpe na naŋ lar Eebraham so ashi Mamre be ndibigboŋ na ase. Loŋ be kachɛ na K daa la kapaso nna nɛ kaboŋ bel edɛ nɛ Eebraham tase mbe wajɛbu be kabuna to.

english_verse: Abraham looked up and saw three men standing nearby. He quickly ran to meet them, bowed with his face to the ground,
translation_verse: Eebraham daa baŋ maŋ kumu so nna nɛ e keni nseŋ wu benyɛn asa ko kaa yil. E ka wu bumo, epul na to nɛ e shile n lar kowu n ya shɛr bumo to ŋ jɔŋɛ bumo ase

english_verse: and said, “Please come to my home where I can serve you.
translation_verse: ŋ kaŋɛ: “Men maaŋ yili ma kutɔ gbrɛbi pɔɛŋ nsaa yɔ a?

english_verse: I'll have some water brought, so you can wash your feet, then you can rest under a tree.
translation_verse: Men shin nɛ b bar menyi nchu nɛ men fɔr menyi be aya so. Men chena kedibi ere be kifito a wushi

english_verse: Let me get you some food to give you strength before you leave. I would be honored to serve you.” “Thank you very much,” they answered. “We accept your offer.”
translation_verse: nɛ n fin kusɔ ko n sa menyi nɛ men ji nseŋ nya eleŋ n naa yɔ menyi be enite to. Men maŋkura ma nna so nɛ men ba ma pe na, amoso men shin nɛ n wora kusɔ ko n sa menyi nɛ men ji.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ b shuli so nseŋ kaŋɛ: “To, an nu.”

english_verse: Abraham went quickly to his tent and said to Sarah, “Hurry! Get a large sack of flour and make some bread.”
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Eebraham wora manaŋ n luri mbe wajɛbu to n ya kaŋɛ Sɛɛra le: “Jɔ fo nyifu lela na manaŋ kananɛ a beeŋ fo basa asa ere ŋ gbiti amo n wora bodobodo.”

english_verse: After saying this, he rushed off to his herd of cattle and picked out one of the best calves, which his servant quickly prepared.
translation_verse: Eebraham ka malga loŋ n loge nɛ e shile n yɔ kenalu to n ya pɛ kena fɔlbi danso nɛ e maŋ naŋ shinto m ba sa mbe kenya nɛ e lɔŋɛ mo manaŋ.

english_verse: He then served his guests some yogurt and milk together with the meat. While they were eating, he stood near them under the tree,
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e ta kenyipo ko nɛ wagashi n ti eblaŋ nɛ b daŋɛ na so n ya yili bumo be anishito nseŋ kilgi a yil bumo kutɔ kedibi na be kifito nɛ b ji ajibi na.

english_verse: and they asked, “Where's your wife Sarah?” “She is right there in the tent,” Abraham answered.
translation_verse: B ka ji n loge nɛ b bishi mo le: “Nnɛ nɛ fo eche Sɛɛra wɔ?” Nɛ Eebraham kaŋɛ: “E wɔ wajɛbu ere to.”

english_verse: Abraham and Sarah were very old, and Sarah was well past the age for having children.
translation_verse: Saŋɛ na so malɛ nɛ Eebraham nɛ Sɛɛra kikɛ daŋ bel nna hale Sɛɛra daa maŋ naa fɔr gba.

english_verse: So she laughed and said to herself, “Now that I am worn out and my husband is old, will I really know such happiness?”
translation_verse: Nɛ Sɛɛra mushe nseŋ kaŋɛ mbe kagbene to le: “Kananɛ m bel ŋ ki ere, kanyɛndi beeŋ naaŋ yɛlga ma bre a? Kumo be kaman, ŋ kul malɛ gba bel.”

english_verse: The Lord asked Abraham, “Why did Sarah laugh? Does she doubt that she can have a child in her old age?
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe na bishi Eebraham le: “Manɛ nna nɛ Sɛɛra mushe nseŋ kaŋɛ mbe kumu fanɛ e maaŋ naŋ tiŋ n nya ebi saŋɛ nɛ e bel ere?

english_verse: I am the Lord! There is nothing too difficult for me. I'll come back next year at the time I promised, and Sarah will already have a son.”
translation_verse: Kusɔ ko malɛ wɔtɔ nna a du kpakpa n sa Enyɛnpe na a? Kafɛ a ba saŋɛ ere so, meeŋ naŋ bɛta m ba fanɛ kananɛ ŋ kaŋɛ na nɛ Sɛɛra nya kebia na.”

english_verse: Sarah was so frightened that she lied and said, “I didn't laugh.” “Yes, you did!” he answered. Abraham Prays for Sodom

english_verse: “This is the first I've heard about it,” Abimelech replied. “Why haven't you said something before? I don't have any idea who did it.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Abimelɛk kaŋɛ Eebraham le: “Ma ere maŋ nyi esa nɛ e wora loŋ. Naniere nɛ m baa nu kumo be asheŋ na, ŋkpal manɛ so, fo maŋ wule ŋ kaŋɛ ma.”

english_verse: Abraham separated seven female lambs from his flock of sheep,
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Eebraham lara mbolpɔ cheso fɔlbi ashunu ashi mbe mbolpɔ to n yili ŋ kɔr.

english_verse: Abraham replied, “I want you to accept these seven lambs as proof that I dug this well.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Eebraham kaŋɛ mo: “Jande, sɔ mbolpɔ cheso fɔlbi ashunu ere nɛ k baa la shɛda a ŋini fanɛ ma e kur ketirbu nɛ fo nyɛrbi suge na.”

english_verse: So they called the place Beersheba, because they made a treaty there.
translation_verse: Kede so nɛ kaboŋ na nya ketre Bɛshiba na a ŋini fanɛ ndoŋ nɛ basa anyɔ na nase kɔnɔ n sa abar.

english_verse: When the treaty was completed, Abimelech and his army commander Phicol went back to the land of the Philistines.
translation_verse: Eebraham nɛ Abimelɛk ka nase kɔnɔ ashi Bɛshiba n loge na nɛ Abimelɛk nɛ mbe benapo be enimu nɛ baa tre Fikɔl na bɛta n yɔ Filistiebi be kasawule so.

english_verse: Then Abraham lived a long time as a foreigner in the land of the Philistines.
translation_verse: Eebraham daŋ chena Filistiebi be kasawule na so n chɛr ga.

english_verse: Some years later God decided to test Abraham, so he spoke to him. Abraham answered, “Here I am, Lord.”
translation_verse: Eebraham wɔtɔ loŋ nɛ kachako Ebɔrɛ ba nɛ e ba wora mo ŋ keni, nseŋ tre mo: “Eebraham!” Nɛ Eebraham shuli ŋ kaŋɛ: “Ma nde.”

english_verse: The Lord said, “Go get Isaac, your only son, the one you dearly love! Take him to the land of Moriah, and I will show you a mountain where you must sacrifice him to me on the fires of an altar.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ mo: “Ta fo pibinyɛn koŋwule Aizek nɛ fee sha ga na n yɔ Moriya be kasawule so n ya mɔ mo n chɔɔ n lara sarga n sa ma ashi abee na be kumo nɛ meeŋ ŋini fo na so.”

english_verse: So Abraham got up early the next morning and chopped wood for the fire. He put a saddle on his donkey and set out with Isaac and two servants for the place where God had told him to go.
