translation_verse: Kumo be ŋklade chipurdidi nɛ Eebraham kil ndibi nɛ e beeŋ ta n ya chɔɔ sarga na n sulɔ mbe kurma nseŋ keta mo pibi Aizek nɛ nyɛrbi anyɔ n ti so m pɛ kakpa nɛ Ebɔrɛ daŋ malga kumo be asheŋ na be ekpa.

english_verse: Three days later Abraham looked off in the distance and saw the place.
translation_verse: B nite loŋ nchɛnsa. Kachɛ sasopo na nɛ Eebraham wu kaboŋ na kufɔ kufɔ.

english_verse: He told his servants, “Stay here with the donkey, while my son and I go over there to worship. We will come back.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ e kaŋɛ mbe nyɛrbi na le: “Menyi nɛ kurma ere e baa wɔ nfe nɛ ma nɛ kebia ere e yɔ anishito n ya bunyaŋ Ebɔrɛ nseŋ bɛta m ba menyi kutɔ nfe.”

english_verse: Abraham put the wood on Isaac's shoulder, but he carried the hot coals and the knife. As the two of them walked along,
translation_verse: E ka malga loŋ na nɛ e ta ndibi nɛ e beeŋ ta n lara sarga na n sulɔ mo pibinyɛn Aizek nseŋ ta edɛ nɛ kasaŋɛbi ŋ keta. Bumo basa anyɔ na ka bee yɔ na nɛ

english_verse: Isaac said, “Father, we have the coals and the wood, but where is the lamb for the sacrifice?” “My son,” Abraham answered, “God will provide the lamb.” The two of them walked on, and
translation_verse: Nɛ Eebraham kaŋɛ mo: “M pibi, Ebɔrɛ gbagba e naaŋ sa kubɔlpo fɔlbi nɛ anyeeŋ mɔ n chɔɔ n lara sarga na.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ b naŋ kilgi m pɛ bumo be ekpa.

english_verse: when they reached the place that God had told him about, Abraham built an altar and placed the wood on it. Next, he tied up his son and put him on the wood.
translation_verse: B ka ya fo kakpa nɛ Ebɔrɛ ŋini Eebraham fanɛ e lara sarga na nɛ Eebraham yuu bɔrɛsure ndoŋ nseŋ bela ndibi na n deŋi bɔrɛsure na so. Kumo be kaman nɛ e pɛ mbe kebia na ŋ kre mo n ya deŋi bɔrɛsure na nɛ ndibi na so,

english_verse: He then took the knife and got ready to kill his son.
translation_verse: nseŋ ta kasaŋɛ na nɛ e mɔ mbe kebia na.

english_verse: But the Lord's angel shouted from heaven, “Abraham! Abraham!” “Here I am!” he answered.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe be malaika shi ebɔrɛso m ponte n tre: “Eebraham, Eebraham!” Nɛ Eebraham shuli so: “Ma nde.”

english_verse: “Don't hurt the boy or harm him in any way!” the angel said. “Now I know that you truly obey God, because you were willing to offer him your only son.”
translation_verse: Nɛ malaika na kaŋɛ: “Sa maŋ kaŋ mɔ kebia na. Naniere m pin fo ka bee sha ma Ebɔrɛ, ŋkpal manɛ so, fo maŋ mɔn ma fo pibinyɛn koŋwule nɛ fee sha ga na.”

english_verse: Abraham looked up and saw a ram caught by its horns in the bushes. So he took the ram and sacrificed it instead of his son.
translation_verse: Malaika na ka kaŋɛ loŋ na nɛ Eebraham maŋ kumo so ŋ keni nɛ asɔ ko fanɛ chakpaŋare kre kpakpa ko n yili, nɛ e yɔ n ya saŋɛ kpakpa na m ba mɔ n chɔɔ n lara sarga n sa Ebɔrɛ, nseŋ yige mbe kebia na.

english_verse: Abraham named that place “The Lord Will Provide.” And even now people say, “On the mountain of the Lord it will be provided.”
translation_verse: Sarga ere be kaman nɛ Eebraham nase kaboŋ na ketre: “Enyɛnpe beeŋ sa.”

english_verse: The Lord's angel called out from heaven a second time:
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe be malaika na naŋ yili ebɔrɛso n tre Eebraham kela nyɔsopo ŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ

english_verse: You were willing to offer your only son to the Lord, and so he makes you this solemn promise,
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe yɛ: “M bɔ ŋ gbagba be kumu fanɛ ŋkpal fo ka maŋ mɔn ma fo pibinyɛn koŋwule Aizek nseŋ daa shin nɛ fo ta mo n lara sarga n sa ma so so,

english_verse: “I will bless you and give you such a large family, that someday your descendants will be more numerous than the stars in the sky or the grains of sand along the seashore. They will defeat their enemies and take over the cities where their enemies live.
translation_verse: meeŋ nɛfa fo kashenteŋto nseŋ shin nɛ fo kaman to ebi e baa shi fanɛ awɔlpa to be achɛkpabi nɛ teku ase be shishɛr na. Fo kaman to ebi beeŋ ba koso m pɔɔ bumo doŋana so n sɔ bumo be ndeana.

english_verse: You have obeyed me, and so you and your descendants will be a blessing to all nations on earth.”
translation_verse: Fo kaman to ebi so nɛ durnya to ebi kikɛ beeŋ bɔla n nya nɛfa ŋkpal fo ka wora ma kasonu ere so.”

english_verse: Abraham and Isaac went back to the servants who had come with him, and they returned to Abraham's home in Beersheba. The Children of Nahor
translation_verse: B ka wora kusɔ kama nyam n loge kebee na so na nɛ Eebraham nɛ mbe kebia na bɛta n yɔ mbe nyɛrbi na kutɔ nɛ bumo kikɛ ta n yɔ Bɛshiba, kakpa nɛ Eebraham daa wɔ na. Nahɔɔ be mbia be asheŋ

english_verse: Nahor also had another wife. Her name was Reumah, and she had four sons: Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah.
translation_verse: Nahɔɔ mo jipoche nɛ b daa tre Rɔima na gba daŋ kurge bibinyɛn nna n sa mo. Bumo be atre nde: Teba nɛ Gaham nɛ Tahash, nɛ Maaka.

english_verse: “I live as a foreigner in your land, and I don't own any property where I can bury my wife. Please let me buy a piece of land.”
translation_verse: “N la efɔ nɛ enitepo nna a wɔ menyi to nfe, amoso men jande, men fa kasawule ko nfe n sa ma nɛ m baa puli ma basa ndoŋ.”

english_verse: “Sir,” they answered, “you are an important man. Choose the best place to bury your wife. None of us would refuse you a resting place for your dead.”
translation_verse: “Keni, ebunyampo, nu nfe. Fo la esagboŋ nna a wɔ anyi to nfe. Kaplɛkama nɛ k par fo, feeŋ tiŋ a puli fo basa ndoŋ. Anyi be ekama maaŋ tiŋ m mɔn fo mbe kasawule nɛ feeŋ baa puli fo basa.”

english_verse: and replied, “If you are willing to let me bury my wife here, please ask Zohar's son Ephron
translation_verse: ŋ kaŋɛ bumo le: “To, nɛ men shuli fanɛ m baa puli ma basa nfe bre, kumo ere men jande, men kule Zohar pibinyɛn Efrɔn n sa ma

english_verse: “Sir, the whole field, including the cave, is yours. With my own people as witnesses, I freely give it to you as a burial place for your dead.”
translation_verse: “Ayai, n nyɛnpe, nu nfe. M maaŋ fa kumo n sa fo. N ta kebeelaŋ na nɛ kasawule na kikɛ ŋ kɛ fo ashi m peebi nɛ b wɔ nfe ere kikɛ be anishito. Baa puli fo basa ndoŋ.”

english_verse: and said to Ephron, “In front of these witnesses, I offer you the full price, so I can bury my wife. Please accept my offer.”
translation_verse: nseŋ kilgi ŋ kaŋɛ Efrɔn le ashi basa na kikɛ be anishito: “Jande nu n sa ma. Meeŋ ka kasawule na be kukɔ, amoso wora ania n sɔ loŋ be kakɔka na, saŋɛ na so meeŋ baa puli ma basa ndoŋ.”

english_verse: So Abraham buried his wife Sarah in Machpelah Cave that was in the field
translation_verse: Kesheŋ na ka nya eyilikpa na nɛ Eebraham puli mbe eche Sɛɛra kebeelaŋ na to ashi Hibrɔn nɛ k wɔ Keenan be kasawule so na.

english_verse: Abraham was now a very old man. The Lord had made him rich, and he was successful in everything he did.
translation_verse: Naniere Eebraham nya nfɛ damta nseŋ bel ga nɛ Enyɛnpe malɛ nɛfa mo ashi ekpa kama so nyam.

english_verse: in the name of the Lord, who rules heaven and earth, that you won't choose a wife for my son Isaac from the people here in the land of Canaan.
translation_verse: ashi Enyɛnpe nɛ e la esoso nɛ kasawule so kikɛ be Ebɔrɛ na be ketre to fanɛ fo maaŋ ta eche ashi Keenanebi nɛ n wɔ bumo to nfe ere n sa m pibinyɛn Aizek.

english_verse: Instead, go back to the land where I was born and find a wife for him from among my relatives.”
translation_verse: Ama feeŋ yɔ ma efuli so, ma basa gbagba kutɔ n ya fin eche m ba sa m pibinyɛn Aizek.”

english_verse: But the servant asked, “What if the young woman I choose refuses to leave home and come here with me? Should I send Isaac there to look for a wife?”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Eebraham be kayɛrbi na bishi mo nyɛnpe le: “To, nɛ k kaŋ ba fanɛ eche na maa sha ketu ma m ba efuli ere so nfe, kumo ere ŋ keta fo kebia na n yɔ fo efuli so ndoŋ n ya ta eche na n sa mo a?”

english_verse: “No!” Abraham answered. “Don't ever do that, no matter what.
translation_verse: Nɛ Eebraham kaŋɛ kayɛrbi na le: “Ayai, sa maŋ kaŋ bɛta ma kebia na n yɔ ndoŋ kuraa.

english_verse: The Lord who rules heaven brought me here from the land where I was born and promised that he would give this land to my descendants forever. When you go back there, the Lord will send his angel ahead of you to help you find a wife for my son.
translation_verse: M baa nyi fanɛ Enyɛnpe nɛ e wɔ ebɔrɛso nsaa la esa nɛ e lara ma ashi n tuto pe nɛ ma efuli so nseŋ malga ŋ kutɔ n nase kɔnɔ n sa ma fanɛ e beeŋ ta efuli ere n sa ma kaman to ebi na beeŋ shuŋi mbe malaika nɛ e juŋkpar fo n shin nɛ fo nya eche m ba sa m pibi ere.

english_verse: If the woman refuses to come along, you don't have to keep this promise. But don't ever take my son back there.”
translation_verse: Nɛ eche na kaŋ kini ketu fo m ba nfe, kumo ere ntaŋ nɛ fo bɔ n sa ma ere be kɔnɔsho maaŋ naa deŋ fo so. Ama sa maŋ kaŋ keta ma kebia na bre n naŋ bɛta n yɔ ndoŋ kuraa.”

english_verse: So the servant gave Abraham his word that he would do everything he had been told to do.
translation_verse: Eebraham ka malga le n loge na nɛ mbe kayɛrbi na ta enɔ n wɔtɔ mo nyɛnpe Eebraham be kebembi be kaseto m bɔ ntaŋ n sa mo a yɔ kesheŋ na be kaplɛa so.

english_verse: Soon after that, the servant loaded ten of Abraham's camels with valuable gifts. Then he set out for the city in northern Syria, where Abraham's brother Nahor lived.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ kayɛrbi na lara mo nyɛnpe be enyɔma kudu nseŋ ta ŋkɛ lela be yiri yiri ashi mo nyɛnpe kutɔ m pɛ ekpa a yɔ Nahɔɔ be kade nɛ k wɔ Mɛsopoteemia na.

english_verse: When he got there, he let the camels rest near the well outside the city. It was late afternoon, the time when the women came out for water.
translation_verse: Kaaseso, saŋɛ nɛ beche bee yɔ eboŋ to na nɛ b fo ndoŋ. Ndoŋ nna nɛ e shin nɛ enyɔma na gbir ŋ gbir ketirbu ko ase ashi kade na be ekarso.

english_verse: The servant prayed: You, Lord, are the God my master Abraham worships. Please keep your promise to him and let me find a wife for Isaac today.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e kule Ebɔrɛ ŋ kaŋɛ: “O, Enyɛnpe, n nyɛnpe Eebraham be Ebɔrɛ, sa ma kumulela kabre n wora n nyɛnpe Eebraham kelela.

english_verse: The young women of the city will soon come to this well for water,
translation_verse: N yil ketirbu ere akpa nfe nna a keni nɛ kade ere to be mbichebi e ba kaa jɔ nchu.

english_verse: and I'll ask one of them for a drink. If she gives me a drink and then offers to get some water for my camels, I'll know she is the one you have chosen and that you have kept your promise to my master.
translation_verse: Shin nɛ bumo be ekama nɛ ŋ kaŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ e sa ma nchu nɛ n nuu nɛ e shuli ŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ n sɔ n nuu nɛ e ya jɔ ako m ba sa ma enyɔma ere gba e baa la eche nɛ fo lara a sa fo kenya Aizek na. Nɛ loŋ wora, meeŋ pin fanɛ fo e wora n nyɛnpe Eebraham kelela kashenteŋto.”

english_verse: Abraham's servant ran to her and said, “Please let me have a drink of water.”
translation_verse: nɛ Eebraham be kayɛrbi na nya manaŋ n shile n ya kaŋɛ mo le: “Jande, sa ma fo nchu ere gbrɛbi nɛ n nuu.”

english_verse: “I'll be glad to,” she answered. Then she quickly took the jar from her shoulder and held it while he drank.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ e suge lɔŋkɔŋ na nɛ nchu na manaŋ nseŋ kaŋɛ: “N nyɛnpe, sɔ n nuu.”

english_verse: After he had finished, she said, “Now I'll give your camels all the water they want.” She quickly poured out water for them, and she kept going back for more, until his camels had drunk all they wanted.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e chulgi mbe lɔŋkɔŋ na to be nchu epul to n wɔtɔ asɔbɔya be kusɔ nuunchu ko nɛ k daa wɔ ndoŋ na to nseŋ bɛta n shile n yɔ ketirbu na akpa n ya jɔ nchu m ba sa enyɔma na. Loŋ nɛ e wora nɛ enyɔma na kikɛ ba nuu m moɛ.

english_verse: Abraham's servant did not say a word, but he watched everything Rebekah did, because he wanted to know for certain if this was the woman the Lord had chosen.
translation_verse: Rebɛka ka bee wora le ere kikɛ nɛ Eebraham be kayɛrbi na lo to boeŋ a dara mo a keni, ama Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nu mbe kekule na nna ere a!

english_verse: The servant had brought along an expensive gold ring and two large gold bracelets. When Rebekah had finished bringing the water, he gave her the ring for her nose and the bracelets for her arms.
translation_verse: Enyɔma na kikɛ ka nuu n loge nɛ kanyɛn na lara kamuna so be shuwa be kepinibi nɛ shuwa be enɔ to be mpinibi anyɔ n sa Rebɛka.

english_verse: Then he said, “Please tell me who your father is. Does he have room in his house for me and my men to spend the night?”
translation_verse: Eebraham be kayɛrbi na ka sa mo asɔ na n loge nɛ e bishi mo: “Jande, wanɛ pibiche e la fo? Meeŋ nya kakpa fo tuto pe n di ŋklade a?”

english_verse: She answered, “My father is Bethuel, the son of Nahor and Milcah.
translation_verse: Nɛ Rebɛka kaŋɛ mo: “N tuto e la Bɛtuwɛl nɛ e la Nahɔɔ nɛ Milka pibi na.”

english_verse: We have a place where you and your men can stay, and we also have enough straw and feed for your camels.”
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e naŋ kaŋɛ le: “An kɔ asɔbɔya be ajibi damta nɛ befɔ be ebu anyi pe.”

english_verse: Then the servant bowed his head and prayed,
translation_verse: Kanyɛn na ka nu loŋ na nɛ e gbir m bunyaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na

english_verse: Rebekah ran straight home and told her family everything.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Rebɛka shile n ya kaŋɛ mo nio be laŋ to ebi asheŋ na kikɛ nyam.

english_verse: Her brother Laban heard her tell what the servant had said, and he saw the ring and the bracelets she was wearing. So Laban ran out to Abraham's servant, who was standing by his camels at the well.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal Leeban ka wu kamuna so be kepinibi na nɛ enɔ to be mpinibi nɛ a daa wɔ mo sipoche be enɔ to na nseŋ naŋ nu asɔ nɛ e kaŋɛ fanɛ kanyɛn na kaŋɛ na so nɛ e nya manaŋ n lar n yɔ kanyɛn na kutɔ ashi ketirbu na ase n ya tu mo nɛ e yil mbe enyɔma ase.

english_verse: Then Laban said, “The Lord has brought you safely here. Come home with me. There's no need for you to keep on standing outside. I have a room ready for you in our house, and there's also a place for your camels.”
translation_verse: E ka ya tu kanyɛn na nɛ e kaŋɛ mo le: “Fo nɛ Ebɔrɛ nɛfa ere, manɛ nɛ fo yil nfe a wora? Baa ba epe. N lɔŋɛ ebu nɛ enyɔma ere gba be kakpa n yili.”

english_verse: Abraham's servant went home with Laban, where Laban's servants unloaded his camels and gave them straw and feed. Then they brought water into the house, so Abraham's servant and his men could wash their feet.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Eebraham kayɛrbi na tu Leeban n yɔ epe nɛ b saŋɛ n saŋɛ enyɔma na be esulɔ nseŋ sa bumo ajibi. Kumo be kaman nɛ b sa kanyɛn na nchu nɛ e fɔr aya so.

english_verse: After that, they brought in food. But the servant said, “Before I eat, I must tell you why I have come.” “Go ahead and tell us,” Laban answered.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ b ta ajibi m ba yili mo. Nɛ kanyɛn na kaŋɛ: “M baŋ maŋ lara ma kubɔya pɔɛŋ, m maaŋ ji ajibi.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ Leeban kaŋɛ mo: “Kumo ere lara fo kubɔya ai!”

english_verse: The servant explained: I am Abraham's servant.
translation_verse: Nɛ kanyɛn na kaŋɛ: “Eebraham be kayɛrbi e la ma.

english_verse: The Lord has been good to my master and has made him very rich. He has given him many sheep, goats, cattle, camels, and donkeys, as well as a lot of silver and gold, and many slaves.
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ malɛ nɛfa n nyɛnpe Eebraham ga nɛ e dii dama. E sa mo mbolpɔ nɛ ana nɛ shuwa nɛ gbiti nɛ anya nyɛnso nɛ becheso nɛ enyɔma nɛ ekurma.

english_verse: Sarah, my master's wife, didn't have any children until she was very old. Then she had a son, and my master has given him everything.
translation_verse: N nyɛnpe be eche Sɛɛra bel nna pɔɛŋ nseŋ kurge ebinyɛn n sa mo nɛ n nyɛnpe ta kusɔ kama nɛ e kɔ n sa mo pibi na.

english_verse: I solemnly promised my master that I would do what he said. And he told me, “Don't choose a wife for my son from the women in this land of Canaan.
translation_verse: Nchɛnnyɔ ere to nɛ n nyɛnpe shin nɛ m bɔ ntaŋ n sa mo fanɛ m maaŋ ta eche ashi Keenanebi nɛ e wɔ bumo be kasawule so na n sa mo pibi na,

english_verse: Instead, go back to the land where I was born and find a wife for my son from among my relatives.”
translation_verse: ama meeŋ yɔ mo tuto be basa to, mbe kanaŋ gbagba to ebi to n ya ta eche m ba sa mo pibi na.

english_verse: I asked my master, “What if the young woman refuses to come with me?”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ m bishi n nyɛnpe Eebraham le: ‘Nɛ ŋ kaŋ yɔ nɛ eche na kini ketu ma m ba ai?’

english_verse: My master answered, “I have always obeyed the Lord, and he will send his angel to help you find my son a wife from among my own relatives.
translation_verse: Nɛ e kaŋɛ ma fanɛ Enyɛnpe nɛ e bee bɛ mo so na beeŋ shin nɛ mbe malaika e juŋkpar ma n yɔ n ya shin nɛ n nya kumulela n nya eche ashi mbe kanaŋ to nɛ mo tuto pe m ba sa mo pibi na.

english_verse: But if they refuse to let her come back with you, then you are freed from your promise.”
translation_verse: E yɛ m baŋ yɔ mbe kanaŋ to, nɛ b ya kini keta eche na n sa ma kumo ere ntaŋ na be kɔnɔsho na maaŋ naa bɛ ma so.

english_verse: When I came to the well today, I silently prayed, “You, Lord, are the God my master Abraham worships, so please lead me to a wife for his son
translation_verse: Ma alɛ ka ba menyi be ketirbu na ase kabre, le nɛ ŋ kule: ‘O Enyɛnpe, n nyɛnpe Eebraham be Ebɔrɛ, nɛ k par fo, fo shin nɛ n nya kumulela ashi ma enite ere to.

english_verse: while I am here at the well. When a young woman comes out to get water, I'll ask her to give me a drink.
translation_verse: Shin nɛ kebichebi kama nɛ e ba nɛ e ba jɔ nchu nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ mo fanɛ e sa ma nchu nɛ n nuu nɛ e shuli n sa nchu nɛ n nuu

english_verse: If she gives me a drink and offers to get some water for my camels, I'll know she is the one you have chosen.”
translation_verse: nseŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ, nuu, nɛ n jɔ ako m ba sa fo enyɔma ere gba, e baa la eche nɛ fo, Enyɛnpe na lara a sa n nyɛnpe pibi na.’

english_verse: Even before I had finished praying, Rebekah came by with a water jar on her shoulder. When she had filled the jar, I asked her for a drink.
translation_verse: Ŋ kraa kule Ebɔrɛ ma kagbene to nna nɛ Rebɛka sulɔ lɔŋkɔŋ mbe kebatemu so n ya jɔ nchu ketirbu na to. Ndoŋ nna nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ mo le: ‘Jande, sa ma nchu nɛ n nuu.’

english_verse: She quickly lowered the jar from her shoulder and said, “Have a drink. Then I'll get water for your camels.” So I drank, and after that she got some water for my camels.
translation_verse: Ŋ ka kaŋɛ mo loŋ na nɛ e suge mbe lɔŋkɔŋ na manaŋ ashi mbe kebatemu so nseŋ kaŋɛ: ‘Nuu nɛ n jɔ ako n sa fo enyɔma gba.’

english_verse: I asked her who her father was, and she answered, “My father is Bethuel the son of Nahor and Milcah.” At once I put the ring in her nose and the bracelets on her arms.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ m bishi mo fanɛ wanɛ pibiche e la mo. Nɛ e yɛ, mo tuto e la Bɛtuwɛl nɛ e la Nahɔɔ nɛ Milka pibinyɛn na. E ka kaŋɛ ma loŋ na nɛ n ta kamuna so be kepinibi n wɔtɔ mbe kamuna to nseŋ ta enɔ to be mpinibi na malɛ n wɔtɔ mbe enɔ to.

english_verse: Then I bowed my head and gave thanks to the God my master Abraham worships. The Lord had led me straight to my master's relatives, and I had found a wife for his son.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ ŋ gbir m bunyaŋ nseŋ di n nyɛnpe Eebraham be Ebɔrɛ na epaŋ, ŋkpal e ka juŋkpar ma nɛ m ba nya n nyɛnpe Eebraham mo sipo Nahɔɔ mo nanabi nɛ n ya sa mo pibinyɛn na so.

english_verse: Now please tell me if you are willing to do the right thing for my master. Will you treat him fairly, or do I have to look for another young woman?
translation_verse: Amoso naniere, men jande, men kaŋɛ ma, Menyeeŋ wora n nyɛnpe na kelela ŋko men maaŋ wora loŋ? Nɛ menyeeŋ wora loŋ, men kaŋɛ ma, nɛ men maaŋ wora loŋ malɛ, men kaŋɛ ma, saŋɛ na so meeŋ pin kakpa nɛ meeŋ naŋ sɔ to.”

english_verse: Laban and Bethuel answered, “The Lord has done this. We have no choice in the matter.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Leeban nɛ Bɛtuwɛl kaŋɛ: “Asheŋ na kikɛ shi Ebɔrɛ kutɔ nna, amoso anyi ere maŋ naa kɔ shɛŋ nɛ an kaŋɛ.

english_verse: Take Rebekah with you; she can marry your master's son, just as the Lord has said.”
translation_verse: An shuli. Rebɛka nde. Keta mo a yɔ n ya shin nɛ e ki fo nyɛnpe pibi na be eche fanɛ kananɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ baŋ yili kumo na.”

english_verse: Then he gave clothing, as well as silver and gold jewelry, to Rebekah. He also gave expensive gifts to her brother and her mother.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e lara shuwa nɛ gbiti be abitasɔ nɛ asɔbuusoana ko n sa Rebɛka nseŋ naŋ sa Rebɛka mo da Leeban nɛ mo nio gba yawu kpakpaso be ŋkɛ.

english_verse: Abraham's servant and the men with him ate and drank, then spent the night there. The next morning they got up, and the servant told Rebekah's mother and brother, “I would like to go back to my master now.”
translation_verse: E ka wora ade kikɛ n loge na nɛ mo nɛ basa nɛ b daa wɔ mo kutɔ na kikɛ ji ajibi nseŋ di ndoŋ ŋklade. Kare ka chɛ chipurso nɛ Eebraham be kayɛrbi na kaŋɛ bumo le: “To, mee kule ekpa nɛ n yɔ n nyɛnpe kutɔ.”

english_verse: “Let Rebekah stay with us for a week or ten days,” they answered. “Then she may go.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Rebɛka mo nio nɛ mo da Leeban kaŋɛ: “Fo ere beeŋ tiŋ a yɔ, ama shin nɛ kebichebi na bre e ji anyi kutɔ nchɛ kudu pɔɛŋ.”

english_verse: But he said, “Don't make me stay any longer. The Lord has already helped me find a wife for my master's son. Now let us return.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Eebraham be kayɛrbi na kaŋɛ bumo le: “Men sa maŋ shin nɛ n chɛr nfe, ŋkpal manɛ so, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na teŋ sa ma kumulela ashi ma enite ere to. Men sa ma ekpa nɛ n yɔ n nyɛnpe kutɔ.”

english_verse: They called her and asked, “Are you willing to leave with this man at once?” “Yes,” she answered.
translation_verse: Nɛ b tre Rebɛka m bishi mo: “Rebɛka, feeŋ tu kanyɛn ere a yɔ a?” Nɛ e kaŋɛ: “Mm, meeŋ yɔ.”

english_verse: So they agreed to let Rebekah and an old family servant woman leave immediately with Abraham's servant and his men.
translation_verse: Rebɛka ka shuli na nɛ b sa mo nɛ Eebraham be kayɛrbi na nɛ mbe basa ekpa fanɛ b baa yɔ nseŋ shin nɛ kebita nɛ e daa keni Rebɛka so kebia to na tu mo n yɔ.

english_verse: They gave Rebekah their blessing and said, “We pray that God will give you many children and grandchildren and that he will help them defeat their enemies.”
translation_verse: Le be mmalga nɛ b daŋ ta ŋ kela mo. B yɛ: “Esipoche, Ebɔrɛ e nɛfa fo n shin nɛ fo mbia e wora keshi n fo ŋgboŋto ŋgboŋto nɛ fo kanaŋ to ebi kikɛ e pɔɔ bumo doŋana so n sɔ bumo be mboŋ a wɔtɔ.”

english_verse: Afterwards, Rebekah and the young women who were to travel with her prepared to leave. Then they got on camels and left with Abraham's servant and his men.
translation_verse: Mmalga ere be kaman nɛ Rebɛka nɛ mbe mbita bela ase n dii n dii bumo be enyɔma n tu kanyɛn na nɛ e keta Rebɛka n yɔ.

english_verse: At that time Isaac was living in the southern part of Canaan near a place called “The Well of the Living One Who Sees Me.”
translation_verse: Aizek malɛ daŋ shi Beer Lahai Rɔi n ya kaa wɔ keshishɛrsawule nɛ baa tre Negɛf na.

english_verse: One evening he was walking out in the fields, when suddenly he saw a group of people approaching on camels. So he started toward them. Rebekah saw him coming; she got down from her camel, and asked, “Who is that man?” “He is my master Isaac,” the servant answered. Then Rebekah covered her face with her veil.
translation_verse: nseŋ bishi Eebraham be kayɛrbi na le: “Kanyɛn mo e ya kaa wɔ ndoŋ ere a ba anyi kutɔ ere?” Nɛ kayɛrbi na kaŋɛ: “N nyɛnpe nna.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ Rebɛka ta mbe shata m buu mbe kumu so.

english_verse: and they had six sons: Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.
translation_verse: Mbia mo nɛ Ketura nɛ Eebraham daŋ kurge e daa la Zimran nɛ Jɔkshan nɛ Medan nɛ Midian nɛ Ishbak nɛ Shuwa.

english_verse: Later, Jokshan became the father of Sheba and Dedan, and when Dedan grew up, he had three sons: Asshurim, Letushim, and Leummim.
translation_verse: Jɔkshan e daŋ koso ŋ kurge Sheba nɛ Dedan. Dedan be kanaŋ to ebi e daa la Ashuurebi nɛ Letushebi nɛ Leyumebi.

english_verse: While Abraham was still alive, he gave gifts to the sons of Hagar and Keturah. He also sent their sons to live in the east far from his son Isaac, and when Abraham died, he left everything to Isaac. The Death of Abraham
translation_verse: Ama e ka daa wɔ ŋkpa to na e daŋ kɛ mo jipocheana be mbia na asɔ nna pɔɛŋ nseŋ n shin nɛ b lar Aizek kutɔ n ya ka wɔ epeŋipetekpa.

english_verse: Abraham died at the ripe old age of
translation_verse: Nfɛ kalfa nɛ adushunu nɛ anu nɛ Eebraham daŋ ji kasawule ere so.

english_verse: His sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him east of Hebron in Machpelah Cave that was part of the field Abraham had bought from Ephron son of Zohar the Hittite. Abraham was buried there beside his wife Sarah.
translation_verse: Kumo nɛ Eebraham daŋ tɔ ashi Hitebi kutɔ na. Ndoŋ nɛ b daŋ ŋana mo m mata mbe eche Sɛɛra.

english_verse: God blessed Isaac after this, and Isaac moved to a place called “The Well of the Living One Who Sees Me.” Ishmael's Descendants
translation_verse: Eebraham ka wu nɛ Ebɔrɛ nɛfa mo pibinyɛn Aizek nɛ e daŋ ya kaa wɔ a mata Beer Lahai Roi na. Ishmaɛl be kanaŋ to ebi be asheŋ

english_verse: Mishma, Dumah, Massa,
translation_verse: Mishma nɛ Duma nɛ Masa

english_verse: Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.
translation_verse: nɛ Hadad nɛ Tema nɛ Jetur nɛ Nafish nɛ Kedema.

english_verse: Each of Ishmael's sons was a tribal chief, and a village was named after each of them.
translation_verse: Bumo e ki nnaŋ kuduanyɔ be amuwuraana na nseŋ ta bumo be atre n nase bumo be ndeana na.

english_verse: Ishmael had settled in the land east of his brothers, and his sons settled everywhere from Havilah to Shur, east of Egypt on the way to Asshur. Ishmael was
translation_verse: Ishmaɛl be kaman to ebi daa tase kakpa nɛ k wɔ Havila nɛ Shur be kefɛato ashi Ijipt be efuli so be ekarso a yɔ Asiriya be efuli so be kaba so nna. Bumo nɛ bumo kurgepoana daa maŋ chena abar so. Jeekɔb nɛ Isɔɔ be asheŋ

english_verse: Rebekah still had no children. So Isaac asked the Lord to let her have a child, and the Lord answered his prayer.
translation_verse: Aizek nɛ Rebɛka ka ta abar Rebɛka daa maa kurge nɛ Aizek kule Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na n sa mo nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nu mbe kabɔrɛkule na n shin nɛ Rebɛka di kedampo.

english_verse: Before Rebekah gave birth, she knew she was going to have twins, because she could feel them inside her, fighting each other. She thought, “Why is this happening to me?” Finally, she asked the Lord why her twins were fighting,
translation_verse: Mborobi be kedampo nɛ Rebɛka daŋ di nɛ mbia na fara a ŋin a ŋin abar bumo nio be epun to. Nɛ Rebɛka fɛ mbe kumu to le: “Manɛ e ba nɛ le be kesheŋ ere bee wora ma ere?” Kumo be kaman nɛ e ya bishi Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kusɔ nɛ k ba nɛ loŋ be kesheŋ na bee wora mo na.

english_verse: and he told her: “Your two sons will become two separate nations. The younger of the two will be stronger, and the older son will be his servant.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ mo le: “Mbia anyɔ nɛ baaŋ ba ki efuli anyɔ be bejuŋkparpo anyɔ a wɔ fo epun to. Bumo alɛ beeŋ ba barga to a wɔtɔ. Eko beeŋ ba kaa kɔ eleŋ a chɔ mo barkasa, nɛ enimuso na e ba kaa shuŋ ekekarso so na.”

english_verse: As Jacob and Esau grew older, Esau liked the outdoors and became a good hunter, while Jacob lived the quiet life of a shepherd.
translation_verse: Mbia na ka daŋ nɛ Isɔɔ ki ekpampo a nyi kekpaŋ to ga nsaa sha kupuŋ to be kebaawɔtɔ, nɛ Jeekɔb malɛ du boeŋ nsaa sha laŋ to be kebaawɔtɔ.

english_verse: Esau would take the meat of wild animals to his father Isaac, so Isaac loved him more, but Jacob was his mother's favorite son.
translation_verse: Isɔɔ be asheŋ nɛ Aizek daa sha a chɔ Jeekɔb ŋkpal e ka bee ji kupuŋ a bar mo eblaŋ so. Rebɛka malɛ daa sha Jeekɔb nna a chɔ Isɔɔ.

english_verse: One day, when Jacob was cooking some stew, Esau came home hungry
translation_verse: Kachako nɛ Isɔɔ ta akoŋ n shi kupuŋ to m ba to nɛ Jeekɔb bee daŋɛ epo belbelso ko.

english_verse: and said, “I'm starving to death! Here and now give me some of that red stew!” That's how Esau got the name “Edom.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Isɔɔ kaŋɛ Jeekɔb le: “Jande sa ma fo epo peper ere be ako, nɛ mannɛ aloŋ, akoŋ beeŋ mɔ ma.” Amoso nɛ b daa tre mo Edɔm na.

english_verse: “I'm about to die,” Esau answered. “What good will those rights do me?”
translation_verse: Nɛ Isɔɔ kaŋɛ: “Keni, akoŋ bee shin nɛ k mɔ ma nna na, nɛ manɛ be tɔnɔ nɛ kekurge to be kenimu kɔ n sa ma?”

english_verse: Jacob then gave Esau some bread and some of the bean stew, and when Esau had finished eating and drinking, he just got up and left, showing how little he thought of his rights as the first-born.
translation_verse: Isɔɔ ka wora loŋ na nɛ Jeekɔb sa mo bodobodo nɛ mbe epo belbelso na be ako nɛ e ji nseŋ koso n choŋ. To, kananɛ Isɔɔ daŋ keni mbe kekurge to be kenimu jiga nna na.

english_verse: Once during Abraham's lifetime, the fields had not produced enough grain, and now the same thing happened. So Isaac went to King Abimelech of the Philistines in the land of Gerar,
translation_verse: Jemanɛ ko nɛ akoŋ tɔr efuli na so, ama mannɛ kumo nɛ k daŋ ba Eebraham be jemanɛ so na. Kede daa kɔr. Akoŋ na be jemanɛ na so nɛ Aizek koso n yɔ Filistiebi be ewura Abimelɛk kutɔ ashi Gerar.

english_verse: because the Lord had appeared to Isaac and said: Isaac, stay away from Egypt! I will show you where I want you to go.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe lar Aizek so ŋ kaŋɛ mo le: “Sa maŋ kaŋ yɔ Ijipt, baa wɔ kasawule mo nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ fo baa wɔ so ere so.

english_verse: You will live there as a foreigner, but I will be with you and bless you. I will keep my promise to your father Abraham by giving this land to you and your descendants.
translation_verse: Baa wɔ nfe n wora nchɛnnyɔ nɛ m baa wɔ fo kutɔ a nɛfa fo. Meeŋ bɛ kɔnɔ nɛ n nase n sa fo tuto Eebraham na so nseŋ ta kasawule ere kikɛ n sa fo nɛ fo kaman to ebi.

english_verse: I will give you as many descendants as there are stars in the sky, and I will give your descendants all of this land. They will be a blessing to every nation on earth,
translation_verse: Meeŋ shin nɛ fo kaman to ebi e wora keshi a sa fanɛ awɔlpa to be achɛkpabi nɛ n ta nsawule ere kikɛ n sa bumo nseŋ bɔla bumo so n nɛfa efuli kama so ebi durnya to.

english_verse: After Isaac had been there a long time, King Abimelech looked out a window and saw Isaac hugging and kissing Rebekah.
translation_verse: Aizek daa wɔ ndoŋ loŋ n chɛr nɛ kachako Filistiebi be ewura nɛ baa tre Abimelɛk na keni tokuro to n wu Aizek ka bee chɔlta mbe eche Rebɛka.

english_verse: Abimelech called him in and said, “Rebekah must be your wife! Why did you say she is your sister?” “Because I thought someone would kill me,” Isaac answered.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Abimelɛk shin nɛ b tre Aizek nɛ e bishi mo le: “Kajaa, fo eche e la mo nɛ fo kaŋɛ fanɛ fo sipoche e la mo a.” Nɛ Aizek kaŋɛ mo: “N daŋ fɛ nna fanɛ nɛ m maŋ kaŋɛ loŋ, baaŋ mɔ ma nseŋ ta mo.”

english_verse: “Don't you know what you've done?” Abimelech exclaimed. “If someone had slept with her, you would have made our whole nation guilty!”
translation_verse: Nɛ ewura Abimelɛk bishi mo: “To, manɛ be kushuŋ nɛ fo shuŋ anyi loŋ? Ndafanɛ fo maŋ shin nɛ nfe be enyɛn ko di fo eche nɛ kumo be loŋ e shin nɛ kɔnɔsho e ba anyi so a?”

english_verse: Then Abimelech warned his people that anyone who even touched Isaac or Rebekah would be put to death.
translation_verse: Kamalga ere be kaman nɛ ewura Abimelɛk fiɛ basa na kikɛ so ŋ kaŋɛ: “Meeŋ shin nɛ b mɔ esa kama nɛ e tɔrɔ kanyɛn ere ŋko mbe eche.”

english_verse: Isaac planted grain and had a good harvest that same year. The Lord blessed him,
translation_verse: Aizek ka dɔ n duu asɔ kasawule na so nɛ e nya adɔjibi ga loŋ be kafɛ na ŋkpal Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ka nɛfa mo so so.

english_verse: In fact, the Philistines were jealous of the large number of sheep, goats, and slaves that Isaac owned,
translation_verse: E daa kɔ asɔyigeso damta nɛ nyɛrbi damta nɛ Filistiebi na fara a besa mo eyur

english_verse: and they stopped up the wells that Abraham's servants had dug before his death.
translation_verse: nseŋ ya fara a kur shishɛr a ti a ti atirbu nɛ mo tuto Eebraham be nyɛrbi daŋ kur na kikɛ.

english_verse: Finally, Abimelech said, “Isaac, I want you to leave our country. You have become too powerful to stay here.”
translation_verse: Kachako nɛ ewura Abimelɛk kaŋɛ Aizek le: “Koso anyi kutɔ, ŋkpal manɛ so, naniere fo eleŋ pɔɔ anyi so nfe.”

english_verse: where he cleaned out those wells that the Philistines had stopped up. Isaac also gave each of the wells the same name that Abraham had given to them.
translation_verse: E ka yɔ ndoŋ na nɛ e naŋ ya shin nɛ b kur ŋ kur atirbu nɛ b daŋ kur Eebraham be jemanɛ to nɛ Filistiebi na daŋ ti amo na to nɛ e naŋ bɛta n ta atre mo nɛ mo tuto daŋ nase amo na gbagba n nase amo.

english_verse: While his servants were digging in the valley, they found a spring-fed well.
translation_verse: Kachako nɛ Aizek be nyɛrbi kur Gerar be ketaŋɛ to n nya nchu lela ko ndoŋ.

english_verse: But the shepherds of Gerar Valley quarreled with Isaac's shepherds and claimed the water belonged to them. So this well was named “Quarrel,” because they had quarreled with Isaac.
translation_verse: Ama k maŋ chɛr ko nɛ Gerar be asɔbɔya kpapoana nɛ Aizek be asɔbɔya kpapoana fara a dii abar so. Gerarebi be asɔbɔyakpapoana na daa kaŋɛ nna fanɛ nchu na la bumoya nna. Ndoŋ nna nɛ Aizek nase kaboŋ na Esɛk ŋkpal kɔnɔgberge nɛ b daŋ nya ndoŋ na so so.

english_verse: Isaac's servants dug another well, and the shepherds also quarreled about it. So that well was named “Jealous.”
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Aizek be nyɛrbi naŋ ya kur ketirbu ko nɛ bumo nɛ Gerarebi be asɔbɔya kpapoana na naŋ nya kɔnɔgberge ŋkpal kumo alɛ gba so nɛ Aizek naŋ sa kumo alɛ ketre Sitna.

english_verse: Finally, they dug one more well. There was no quarreling this time, and the well was named “Lots of Room,” because the Lord had given them room and would make them very successful.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal kɔnɔgberge na so, nɛ Aizek naŋ lar ndoŋ gba n yɔ kaboŋ pɔtɛ. Ndoŋ bre kɔnɔgberge kama daa maŋ naŋ ba, nɛ e nase kumo Rehobɔt ŋkpal manɛ so, e yɛ: “Naniere bre, Enyɛnpe na shin nɛ an nya anyi be amu nɛ an chena kasawule ere so n nya kanya.”

english_verse: Isaac went on to Beersheba,
translation_verse: Ade be kaman nɛ e yɔ Bɛshiba.

english_verse: where the Lord appeared to him that night and told him, “Don't be afraid! I am the God who was worshiped by your father Abraham, my servant. I will be with you and bless you, and because of Abraham I will give you many descendants.”
translation_verse: Kumo be kamɔnchɛ be kanyɛso nɛ Enyɛnpe na lar mo so ŋ kaŋɛ mo: “Ma e la fo tuto Eebraham be Ebɔrɛ na, sa maa lɔ kufu, ŋkpal manɛ so, n wɔ fo kutɔ. Meeŋ nɛfa fo nseŋ shin nɛ fo kaman to ebi e wora keshi ŋkpal ma kenya Eebraham so.”

english_verse: Isaac built an altar there and worshiped the Lord. Then he set up camp, and his servants started digging a well.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Aizek yuu bɔrɛsure ndoŋ m bunyaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na. Kumo be kaman nɛ e yuu mbe wajɛbu n chena ndoŋ nɛ mbe nyɛrbi kur ketirbu.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Abimelech had left Gerar and was taking his advisor Ahuzzath and his army commander Phicol to see Isaac.
translation_verse: Kachako nɛ ewura Abimelɛk nɛ mbe jinatopo nɛ baa tre Ahusal na nɛ Fikɔl nɛ e la mbe benapo be enimu na shi Gerar m ba Aizek kutɔ.

english_verse: When they arrived, Isaac asked, “Why are you here? Didn't you send me away because you hated me?”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Aizek bishi bumo: “Manɛ nɛ men naa ba ŋ kutɔ nɛ men ba wora, ŋkpal manɛ so, ŋ ka daa wɔ men kutɔ men ŋini ma da lubi nna n ju ma.”

english_verse: They answered, “We now know for certain that the Lord is with you, and we have decided there needs to be a peace treaty between you and us. So let's make a solemn agreement
translation_verse: Nɛ b kaŋɛ mo: “K baŋ di efuli nna fanɛ Enyɛnpetale na wɔ fo kutɔ, amoso nɛ an fɛ fanɛ fo shin nɛ anyi nɛ fo e bɔ ntaŋ n nase kɔnɔ n sa abar. Shin nɛ an wora kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre

english_verse: not to harm each other. Remember, we have never hurt you, and when we sent you away, we let you go in peace. The Lord has truly blessed you.”
translation_verse: fanɛ fo maaŋ wora anyi shɛŋ fanɛ kananɛ fo daa wɔ anyi kutɔ nɛ an maŋ tɔrɔ fo nseŋ daa kɔ fo to a wora fo kelela loŋ n ya lara fo ndoŋ kagbenewushiso boeŋ na. Naniere an wu fanɛ Enyɛnpetale nɛfa fo, amoso nɛ an ba na.”

english_verse: Isaac gave a big feast for them, and everyone ate and drank.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Aizek wora kejigboŋ n sa bumo nɛ b ji gbetɛɛ.

english_verse: Early the next morning Isaac and the others made a solemn agreement, then he let them go in peace.
translation_verse: Kumo be ŋklade chipurdidi nɛ Aizek nɛ basa na kre kɔnɔ naseso be ŋkre kpakpaso n sa abar pɔɛŋ nɛ Aizek sa bumo ekpa nɛ b ta kagbenewushi m bɛta n yɔ epe.

english_verse: Later that same day Isaac's servants came and said, “We've struck water!”
translation_verse: Kumo be kamɔnchɛ na gbagba nɛ Aizek be nyɛrbi ba kaŋɛ mo ketirbu ko nɛ b kur be asheŋ. B yɛ: “An nya nchu.”

english_verse: So Isaac named the well Shibah, and the town is still called Beersheba. Esau's Foreign Wives
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Aizek nase kumo be ketre Shiba. Kumo e ba ki kade na be ketre Bɛshiba hale nɛ mbre na.

english_verse: But these two women brought a lot of grief to Esau's parents Isaac and Rebekah.
translation_verse: Beche na daŋ shin nɛ kebaawɔtɔ daŋ ki nyaŋgraŋ nna n sa Aizek nɛ mbe eche Rebɛka.

english_verse: Isaac was old and almost blind, when he called in his first-born son Esau, who asked him, “Father, what can I do for you?”
translation_verse: Aizek ka bel nsaa maŋ naa wu nɛnɛ nɛ e tre mo pibinyɛn nimuso Isɔɔ kachako ŋ kaŋɛ mo: “M pibi.” Nɛ Isɔɔ shuli ŋ kaŋɛ: “Ma nde.”

english_verse: Isaac replied, “I am old and might die at any time.
translation_verse: Nɛ Aizek kaŋɛ mo: “To, naniere ŋ ki enyɛn nimu nna na a maŋ nyi kachɛ nɛ meeŋ wu.

english_verse: So go hunting with your bow and arrows and kill a wild animal.
translation_verse: Amoso koso n ta fo akpansɔ, fo keta nɛ kumo be atanyembi n yɔ kupuŋ to n ya mɔ eblaŋ ko m bar ma.

english_verse: Cook some of that tasty food that I love so much and bring it to me. I want to eat it once more and give you my blessing before I die.”
translation_verse: Fo kaŋ bar loŋ be eblaŋ na fo ta kumo n daŋɛ ajibi belbelso mo nɛ mee sha ga na m ba sa ma nɛ n ji n nɛfa fo pɔɛŋ nseŋ wu.”

english_verse: to kill a wild animal and cook some tasty food for him before he dies. Your father said this because he wants to bless your brother with the Lord as his witness.
translation_verse: nɛ Rebɛka kaŋɛ mo pibinyɛn Jeekɔb le: “Keni, n nu fo tuto ka bee kaŋɛ fo da Isɔɔ fanɛ e ya mɔ eblaŋ ko m ba wora ajibi belbelso ko n sa mo nɛ e ji nseŋ nɛfa mo Enyɛnpe na be anishito pɔɛŋ nseŋ wu.

english_verse: Now, my son, listen carefully to what I want you to do.
translation_verse: Amoso, m pibi, bugi asoe n nu nfe nseŋ ya wora kusɔ nɛ mee shin nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ fo ere:

english_verse: Go and kill two of your best young goats and bring them to me. I'll cook the tasty food that your father loves so much.
translation_verse: Lar ketaman n yɔ asɔbɔya na to n ya pɛ mboefɔlbi lelabi anyɔ m bar ma nɛ n wora ajibi belbelso nɛ fo tuto bee sha ga na,

english_verse: Then you can take it to him, so he can eat it and give you his blessing before he dies.”
translation_verse: ŋseŋ ta amo n ya sa mo nɛ e ji n nɛfa fo pɔɛŋ nseŋ wu.”

english_verse: “My brother Esau is a hairy man,” Jacob reminded her. “And I am not.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Jeekɔb bishi mo nio Rebɛka le: “Nɛ n da Isɔɔ be eyur so kikɛ ka kɔ afuibi nɛ ma alɛ peya maŋ kɔ ere a?

english_verse: If my father touches me and realizes I am trying to trick him, he will put a curse on me instead of giving me a blessing.”
translation_verse: Nɛ ŋ kaŋ wora loŋ nɛ n tuto beta ma a? Nɛ k ba loŋ k beeŋ wora fanɛ mee fule mo nna nɛ nɛfa na e ki kɔnɔsho n sa ma.”

english_verse: Rebekah insisted, “Let his curse fall on me! Just do what I say and bring me the meat.”
translation_verse: Nɛ mo nio kaŋɛ mo: “M pibi, shin nɛ loŋ be kɔnɔsho na e baa la meya. Fo ere e wora kusɔ nɛ mee kaŋɛ ere de. Ya pɛ kaboe na m bar ma.”

english_verse: So Jacob brought the meat to his mother, and she cooked the tasty food that his father liked.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Jeekɔb ya pɛ mboe na m ba sa mo nio nɛ e wora ajibi belbelso mo nɛ Jeekɔb mo tuto bee sha ga n yili

english_verse: and gave him some bread and the tasty food she had cooked.
translation_verse: E ka loge ade kikɛ na nɛ e ta ajibi belbelso na nɛ bodobodo nɛ e wora na n sa Jeekɔb.

english_verse: Jacob went to his father and said, “Father, here I am.” “Which one of my sons are you?” his father asked.
translation_verse: Nɛ Jeekɔb ta ajibi na n yɔ mo tuto kutɔ n ya tre mo ŋ kaŋɛ: “N tuto.” Nɛ mo tuto shuli nseŋ bishi: “M pibi mo nna?”

english_verse: Jacob replied, “I am Esau, your first-born, and I have done what you told me. Please sit up and eat the meat I have brought. Then you can give me your blessing.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Jeekɔb kaŋɛ mo tuto le: “Ma, fo wurkoŋ Isɔɔ nna. N wora kusɔ nɛ fo yɛ n ya wora na nna. Amoso jande, niŋi to n chena n ji kusɔ nɛ n ya nya kekpaŋ to m ba ere pɔɛŋ nseŋ nɛfa ma.”

english_verse: Isaac asked, “My son, how did you find an animal so quickly?” “The Lord your God was kind to me,” Jacob answered.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Aizek bishi mo: “Nuso nɛ fo wora n ya nya eblaŋ na m ba manaŋ loŋ?” Nɛ Jeekɔb kaŋɛ mo: “Enyɛnpe fo Ebɔrɛ na e chɛ ma to.”

english_verse: “My son,” Isaac said, “come closer, where I can touch you and find out if you really are Esau.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Aizek kaŋɛ mo: “Firgi n taga to nfe, m pibi nɛ m beta fo ŋ keni m pibi Isɔɔ gbagba e la fo ŋko mannɛ mo nna.”

english_verse: Jacob went closer. His father touched him and said, “You sound like Jacob, but your hands feel hairy like Esau's.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Jeekɔb yɔ mo tuto Aizek kutɔ nɛ e beta mo ŋ keni nseŋ kaŋɛ: “To, ebɔl ere la Jeekɔb be ebɔl nna, ama fo enɔana ere bre la Isɔɔ peya nna.”

english_verse: So Isaac told him, “Serve me the wild meat, and I can give you my blessing.” Jacob gave him some meat, and he ate it. He also gave him some wine, and he drank it.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Aizek kaŋɛ mo: “Kumo ere m pibi, ta kusɔ nɛ fo ya nya ashi fo kekpaŋ to m ba daŋɛ na m bar ma nɛ n ji nseŋ nɛfa fo.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ Jeekɔb ta ajibi na n sa mo nɛ e ji. Kumo be kaman nɛ e sa mo yabra belbelso nɛ e nuu.

english_verse: Then Isaac said, “Son, come over here and kiss me.”
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ mo tuto Aizek kaŋɛ mo le: “M pibi ba nfe nɛ n lala fo so.”

english_verse: While Jacob was kissing him, Isaac caught the smell of his clothes and said: “The smell of my son is like a field the Lord has blessed.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Jeekɔb yɔ nɛ mo tuto e lala mo so. Aizek ka nu mbe asɔbuuso na be efɛa nɛ e nɛfa mo nseŋ kaŋɛ le: “Cha, ma kebia ere be efɛa baa du fanɛ kasawule mo nɛ Enyɛnpe nɛfa nna.

english_verse: Nations will be your servants and bow down to you. You will rule over your brothers, and they will kneel at your feet. Anyone who curses you will be cursed; anyone who blesses you will be blessed.”
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ e shin nɛ efuli pɔtɛana be basa e ba kaa bunyaŋ fo nɛ basa be nnanto e baa gbir fo kumuli. Baa la fo sipoana kikɛ be ewura n shin nɛ fo nio be bibinyɛn kikɛ e ba kaa gbir fo kumuli. Ebɔrɛ e shin nɛ bekama nɛ baaŋ sho fo kɔnɔ e nya kɔnɔsho nɛ bekama malɛ nɛ b nɛfa fo e nya nɛfa.”

english_verse: Right after Isaac had given Jacob his blessing and Jacob had gone, Esau came back from hunting.
translation_verse: Aizek ka baŋ nɛfa Jeekɔb n loge nɛ e baa lar mo kutɔ nɛ mo da Isɔɔ malɛ shi mbe kekpaŋ na to m ba kaa luri.

english_verse: He cooked the tasty food, brought it to his father, and said, “Father, please sit up and eat the meat I have brought you, so you can give me your blessing.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Isɔɔ gba ya wora ajibi m bar mo tuto m ba kaŋɛ le: “N tuto, niŋi to n chena n ji kusɔ nɛ n ya nya kekpaŋ to m ba ere pɔɛŋ nseŋ nɛfa ma.”

english_verse: “Who are you?” Isaac asked. “I am Esau, your first-born son.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ mo tuto Aizek bishi mo: “Fo wanɛ nna?” Nɛ Isɔɔ kaŋɛ mo: “Ma, fo wurkoŋ nna.”

english_verse: Isaac started trembling and said, “Then who brought me some wild meat right before you came in? I ate it and gave him a blessing that cannot be taken back.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Aizek be eyur kikɛ chicha mo nɛ e bishi: “To, nɛ wanɛ malɛ e ya ji kekpaŋ n daŋɛ m bar ma na? M baŋ ji kumo nna pɔɛŋ nɛ fo ba na. Ma alɛ teŋ nɛfa amodoŋwura. Kashenteŋto malɛ, m maaŋ naŋ tiŋ n laŋɛ nɛfa na.”

english_verse: Isaac answered, “Your brother tricked me and stole your blessing.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Aizek kaŋɛ mo: “Keni, fo sipo teŋ ba m ba fule ma n sɔ fo nɛfa na.”

english_verse: Esau replied, “My brother deserves the name Jacob, because he has already cheated me twice. The first time he cheated me out of my rights as the first-born son, and now he has cheated me out of my blessing.” Then Esau asked his father, “Don't you have any blessing left for me?”
translation_verse: Nɛ Isɔɔ kaŋɛ mo tuto: “Mbe kela nyɔsopo nna na e ka puni ma. E daŋ kesɔ ma kekurge to be kenimu nseŋ naŋ sɔ ma nɛfa ere na. Alawude e ka bee ji Jeekɔb.” Kamalga ere be kaman nɛ Isɔɔ bishi mo tuto: “Ama fo maŋ yige nɛfa kaman yili ma a?”

english_verse: “My son,” Isaac answered, “I have made Jacob the ruler over you and your brothers, and all of you will be his servants. I have also promised him all the grain and grapes that he needs. There's nothing left that I can do for you.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Aizek kaŋɛ mo pibi Isɔɔ: “N teŋ ta mo ŋ ki fo nyɛnpe nseŋ ta mo niopibiana kikɛ ŋ ki mbe nyɛrbi. N ta ayu be yiri to be asɔ duuso kikɛ be kanya nɛ yabra belbelso kikɛ be kanya n sa mo. Amoso m pibi shɛŋ maŋ naa wɔtɔ nɛ meeŋ naŋ tiŋ n wora n sa fo.”

english_verse: “Father,” Esau asked, “don't you have more than one blessing? You can surely give me a blessing too!” Then Esau started crying again.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Isɔɔ bishi mo tuto: “N tuto nɛfa koŋwule nɛ fo kɔ a? Jande nɛfa ma alɛ gba.” Kumo be kaman nɛ e fara a shu awɔrso.

english_verse: So his father said: “Your home will be far from that fertile land, where dew comes down from the heavens.
translation_verse: Nɛ mo tuto Aizek kaŋɛ mo: “Bunyaŋ maaŋ shi ebɔrɛso m ba wushi fo kasawule; fo echenakpa nɛ kasawule lela malɛ beeŋ baa wɔ kufɔ.

english_verse: You will live by the power of your sword and be your brother's slave. But when you decide to be free, you will break loose.”
translation_verse: Fo tokobi so nɛ feeŋ baa bɔla a ji; fo alɛ beeŋ baa la fo sipo be kayɛrbi nna. Ama kachɛ nɛ fo ba diewu bre, feeŋ sɔ fo kumu ashi mbe enɔ to.” Jeekɔb ka shile n yɔ Leeban kutɔ be asheŋ

english_verse: Esau hated his brother Jacob because he had stolen the blessing that was supposed to be his. So he said to himself, “Just as soon as my father dies, I'll kill Jacob.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Isɔɔ fara a kishi Jeekɔb ŋkpal nɛfa nɛ mo tuto daŋ sa mo na so nseŋ fɛ mbe kumu to le: “K maaŋ naŋ chɛr nɛ n tuto e wu nɛ an shu mbe keeli. Keeli na be kaman meeŋ mɔ n sipo Jeekɔb.”

english_verse: When Rebekah found out what Esau planned to do, she sent for Jacob and told him, “Son, your brother Esau is just waiting for a chance to kill you.
translation_verse: Rebɛka ka pin kesheŋ nɛ Isɔɔ kre na nɛ e shuŋi n tre mo pibinyɛn kekarkarso Jeekɔb ŋ kaŋɛ mo le: “Keni, fo da Isɔɔ bee kre kemɔ fo nna m bishi kuwule.

english_verse: Now listen carefully and do what I say. Go to the home of my brother Laban in Haran
translation_verse: Amoso, m pibi, nu nfe nseŋ wora kusɔ nɛ mee sha kekaŋɛ fo ere. Lar nfe manaŋ n shile n yɔ n siponyɛn Leeban kutɔ ashi Haran.

english_verse: and stay with him for a while. When Esau stops being angry
translation_verse: Ya kaa wɔ mo kutɔ gbrɛ nɛ fo da be agbo e yɔɔ nɛ mbe kagbene e wushi

english_verse: and forgets what you have done to him, I'll send for you to come home. Why should I lose both of my sons on the same day?”
translation_verse: nɛ e teŋ kusɔ nɛ fo wora mo ere so pɔɛŋ nɛ n shuŋi n tre fo. Ŋkpal manɛ so m maa sha fanɛ m paŋ menyi benyɔ kikɛ kachɛ koŋwule.”

english_verse: Rebekah later told Isaac, “Those Hittite wives of Esau are making my life miserable! If Jacob marries a Hittite woman, I'd be better off dead.”
translation_verse: Rebɛka ka malga le ere be kaman nɛ e naŋ kaŋɛ Aizek le: “Ma ere, Hitebi to be mbichebi nɛ Isɔɔ ta ere be asheŋ baŋ lar ma ebɔl nna. Nɛ Jeekɔb malɛ naŋ ta Hitebi ere to be eche ko, kumo ere ŋ ka wu bɔ.”

english_verse: Isaac called in Jacob, then gave him a blessing, and said: Don't marry any of those Canaanite women.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Aizek tre Jeekɔb n nɛfa mo nseŋ fiɛ mo so ŋ kaŋɛ: “Sa maŋ kaŋ ta Keenan be efuli so nfe be eche kikɛ.

english_verse: Go at once to your mother's father Bethuel in northern Syria and choose a wife from one of the daughters of Laban, your mother's brother.
translation_verse: Kusɔ nɛ k daga fanɛ fo wora e la fanɛ fo yɔ fo nananyɛn Bɛtuwɛl pe ashi Mɛsopoteemia epul ere to n ya fin fo wɔpa Leeban be mbichebiana na be eko n ta ŋ ki fo eche.

english_verse: I pray that God All-Powerful will bless you with many descendants and let you become a great nation.
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ Enyɛnpetale na e nɛfa fo nseŋ sa fo mbia be kanya nɛ fo ba ki basa damta bumo tuto.

english_verse: May he bless you with the land he promised Abraham, so that you will take over this land where we now live as foreigners.
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ koŋwule na e sa fo nɛ fo kaman to ebi nɛfa mo nɛ e daŋ sa Eebraham na saŋɛ na so kasawule mo nɛ fo wɔ kumo so fanɛ efɔ naniere ere beeŋ ki feya. Kumo e la kasawule nɛ Ebɔrɛ ta n sa Eebraham na.”

english_verse: Esau found out that his father Isaac had blessed Jacob and had warned him not to marry any of the Canaanite women. He also learned that Jacob had been sent to find a wife in northern Syria
translation_verse: Isɔɔ daŋ ba nu fanɛ mo tuto daŋ nɛfa Jeekɔb nna nseŋ fiɛ mo so ŋ kaŋɛ mo fanɛ e sa maŋ kaŋ ta Keenanche kikɛ, nseŋ shin nɛ e yɔ Mɛsopoteemia nɛ e ya ta eche ndoŋ.

english_verse: Esau already had several wives, but he now realized how much his father hated the Canaanite women.
translation_verse: Loŋ be asheŋ na kikɛ e daŋ shin nɛ Isɔɔ pin mo tuto Aizek ka daa maa sha Keenancheana na be keta be asheŋ.

english_verse: So he married Ishmael's daughter Mahalath, who was the sister of Nebaioth and the granddaughter of Abraham. Jacob's Dream at Bethel
translation_verse: Nɛ e kpal loŋ so n yɔ Eebraham pibinyɛn Ishmaɛl pe n ya ta mo pibiche Mahalat nɛ e daa la Nabaiɔt mo sipoche na n ti mbe beche so. Jeekɔb ka daŋ ku edare ashi Bɛtɛl be asheŋ

english_verse: Jacob left the town of Beersheba and started out for Haran.
translation_verse: Jeekɔb daŋ lar Bɛshiba nna m pɛ Haran be ekpa.

english_verse: At sunset he stopped for the night and went to sleep, resting his head on a large rock.
translation_verse: E nite loŋ m ba fo kakpa ko nɛ epeŋi tɔr mo nɛ e ta kejembu ko ndoŋ n nase ŋ ŋele kumo a dese a di.

english_verse: In a dream he saw a ladder that reached from earth to heaven, and God's angels were going up and down on it.
translation_verse: Edi na to nɛ e ku edare n wu kasakpar ka yili kasawule n ya fo ebɔrɛso nɛ Ebɔrɛ be emalaika wɔtɔ a dii kumo a gbelge.

english_verse: The Lord was standing beside the ladder and said: I am the Lord God who was worshiped by Abraham and Isaac. I will give to you and your family the land on which you are now sleeping.
translation_verse: E daŋ wu fanɛ Enyɛnpe na e daa yil kumo be kumu so gbagba na. Ndoŋ nɛ Enyɛnpe na daa yil nseŋ kaŋɛ mo le: “Ma e la Enyɛnpetale, fo nananyɛn Eebraham be Ebɔrɛ nɛ Aizek be Ebɔrɛ na. Meeŋ ta kasawule mo nɛ fo dese so ere n sa fo nɛ fo kaman to ebi.

english_verse: Your descendants will spread over the earth in all directions and will become as numerous as the specks of dust. Your family will be a blessing to all people.
translation_verse: Fo kaman to ebi beeŋ ba kaa shi fanɛ kasawule so be shishɛr nseŋ sɔ durnya be abonfu ana ere kikɛ so nɛ m bɔla fo nɛ fo kanaŋ to ebi so n nɛfa durnya ere be efuli kama so ebi.

english_verse: Wherever you go, I will watch over you, then later I will bring you back to this land. I won't leave you—I will do all I have promised.
translation_verse: Amoso kaplɛkama nɛ fo yɔ, meeŋ baa wɔ fo kutɔ a keni fo so nseŋ bɛta fo m ba kasawule ere so. M maaŋ yige fo kikɛ ama m baŋ wora kusɔ nɛ n nase kɔnɔ fanɛ meeŋ wora ere nna.”

english_verse: Jacob woke up suddenly and thought, “The Lord is in this place, and I didn't even know it.”
translation_verse: Jeekɔb ka tiŋi mbe edi na to nɛ e fɛ mbe kumu to le: “Kajaa, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na wɔ kaboŋ ere nna nɛ n daa maŋ nyi!”

english_verse: When Jacob got up early the next morning, he took the rock that he had used for a pillow and stood it up as a place of worship. Then he poured olive oil on the rock to dedicate it to God,
translation_verse: Kare ka chɛ chipurdidi nɛ Jeekɔb ta kejembu nɛ e daŋ ŋele na n yuu fanɛ kanyiŋi be kejembu na nseŋ duga ŋku n wurge kumo be kumu so.

english_verse: Jacob solemnly promised God, “If you go with me and watch over me as I travel, and if you give me food and clothes
translation_verse: Asheŋ ere be kaman nɛ Jeekɔb nase kɔnɔ ŋ kaŋɛ le: “Nɛ Ebɔrɛ beeŋ baa wɔ ma kutɔ nsaa keni ma so ashi ma enite ere to nsaa sa ma ajibi nɛ asɔbuuso loŋ

english_verse: This rock will be your house, and I will give back to you a tenth of everything you give me.”
translation_verse: Amoso nɛ n yuu kejembu ere n dulgi ndoŋ nɛ k baa la fo Ebɔrɛ pe na. Kusɔ kama malɛ nɛ fo sa ma, meeŋ lara kumo be kudusopo n sa fo.”

english_verse: As Jacob continued on his way to the east,
translation_verse: Jeekɔb ka lar Bɛtɛl nɛ e ta kumu n sɔ epeŋipetekpa be kaba so ebi be efuli so.

english_verse: he looked out in a field and saw a well where shepherds took their sheep for water. Three flocks of sheep were lying around the well, which was covered with a large rock.
translation_verse: E ka bee yɔ nɛ e ya tu ketirbu ko kudɔsawule ko so nɛ mbolpɔ dese kumo ase ntuŋsaso, ŋkpal manɛ so, ketirbu na to nɛ b daa jɔ nchu a sa bumo. Kejembu gboŋgboŋi ko malɛ nɛ b daŋ ta m buu ketirbu na be kɔnɔ so.

english_verse: Shepherds would roll the rock away when all their sheep had gathered there. Then after the sheep had been watered, the shepherds would roll the rock back over the mouth of the well.
translation_verse: Mbolpɔkpapo ko daa jo nna nɛ bumo braana kikɛ e gama pɔɛŋ nɛ b gbelti loŋ be kejembu na ashi to nseŋ jɔ nchu n sa bumo be mbolpɔ. Kumo be kaman nɛ b naŋ gbelti kejembu na m buu ketirbu na so.

english_verse: Jacob asked the shepherds, “Where are you from?” “We're from Haran,” they answered.
translation_verse: Jeekɔb ka fo ndoŋ nseŋ wu mbolpɔkpapoana na nɛ e bishi bumo: “Ŋkurgepoana, nnɛ nɛ men shi?” Nɛ b kaŋɛ mo fanɛ b shi Haran nna.

english_verse: Then he asked, “Do you know Nahor's grandson Laban?” “Yes we do,” they replied.
translation_verse: Nɛ Jeekɔb bishi bumo fanɛ b nyi Nahɔɔ mo nanabi Leeban a? Nɛ b shuli ŋ kaŋɛ: “Mm, an nyi mo.”

english_verse: “How is he?” Jacob asked. “He's fine,” they answered. “And here comes his daughter Rachel with the sheep.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Jeekɔb naŋ bishi bumo fanɛ e kɔ alenfia a? Nɛ b naŋ shuli ŋ kaŋɛ: “Mm, e kɔ alenfia, mo pibiche Reechel gba e ya keta bumo be mbolpɔ a ba na.”

english_verse: Jacob told them, “Look, the sun is still high up in the sky, and it's too early to bring in the rest of the flocks. Water your sheep and take them back to the pasture.”
translation_verse: B ka malga loŋ na be kaman nɛ Jeekɔb kaŋɛ bumo le: “Epeŋi maŋ naŋ wora shɛŋ nɛ men gama mbolpɔ ere nfe na, amoso men jɔ nchu n sa bumo nɛ b nuu nɛ men naŋ keta bumo n yɔ keji to.”

english_verse: But they replied, “We can't do that until they all get here, and the rock has been rolled away from the well.”
translation_verse: Nɛ b kaŋɛ mo: “Anyi maaŋ tiŋ n wora shɛŋ ama an braana kikɛ gama nna nɛ an gbelti kejembu ere ashi to pɔɛŋ nseŋ nya n jɔ nchu n sa anyi be asɔbɔya.”

english_verse: While Jacob was still talking with the men, his cousin Rachel came up with her father's sheep.
translation_verse: Jeekɔb kraa malga bumo kutɔ nna nɛ Reechel keta mo tuto be mbolpɔ m ba, ŋkpal manɛ so, e daa la eche nɛ e bee kpa mbolpɔ nna.

english_verse: When Jacob saw her and his uncle's sheep, he rolled the rock away and watered the sheep.
translation_verse: Jeekɔb ka wu mo wɔpa Leeban pibiche Reechel nɛ mbolpɔ na nɛ e ya gbelti kejembu na ashi to nseŋ jɔ nchu n sa mo wɔpa be mbolpɔ na.

english_verse: He then kissed Rachel and started crying because he was so happy.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Jeekɔb ya ber Reechel to n chɔrɔ mo kashaso nseŋ fara a shu awɔrso

english_verse: He told her that he was the son of her aunt Rebekah, and she ran and told her father about him.
translation_verse: ŋ kaŋɛ Reechel fanɛ mo tuto Leeban mo sipoche Rebɛka pibinyɛn e la mo. Reechel ka nu loŋ na nɛ e shile n ya kaŋɛ mo tuto.

english_verse: As soon as Laban heard the news, he ran out to meet Jacob. He hugged and kissed him and brought him to his home, where Jacob told him everything that had happened.
translation_verse: Leeban malɛ ka baŋ nu mo sipoche pibi Jeekɔb be asheŋ nɛ e lar manaŋ n yɔ nɛ e ya shɛr mo to. E ka ya wu mo nɛ e ya ber mo to n chɔrɔ mo kashaso nseŋ keta mo n yɔ mo pe nɛ Jeekɔb ya kaŋɛ mo asheŋ nɛ a wora kikɛ nyam.

english_verse: Laban said, “You are my nephew, and you are like one of my own family.” Jacob Marries Leah and Rachel After Jacob had been there for a month,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Leeban kaŋɛ mo: “Ma ŋklaŋ e baa la fo.” Kede be kaman nɛ Jeekɔb chena ndoŋ kufɔl koŋwule. Jeekɔb ka ta Lia nɛ Reechel be asheŋ

english_verse: Laban said to him, “You shouldn't have to work without pay, just because you are a relative of mine. What do you want me to give you?”
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Leeban kaŋɛ mo le: “M maaŋ kpal fo ka la ma esa so nɛ fo baa shuŋ ma jiga. Amoso, kaŋɛ ma kananɛ meeŋ baa ka fo.”

english_verse: Laban had two daughters. Leah was older than Rachel, but her eyes didn't sparkle, while Rachel was beautiful and had a good figure.
translation_verse: Lia daa lɔ anishi nna, ama Reechel bre daŋ pɔr nɛnɛ nsaa walɛ kebita nna.

english_verse: Since Jacob was in love with Rachel, he answered, “If you will let me marry Rachel, I'll work seven years for you.”
translation_verse: Amoso Jeekɔb be kagbene daŋ pɛ Reechel nna nɛ e kaŋɛ Leeban le: “Meeŋ shuŋ nfɛnshunu n sa fo nɛ fo ta fo pibiche kekarkarso Reechel n sa ma.”

english_verse: Laban replied, “It's better for me to let you marry Rachel than for someone else to have her. So stay and work for me.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Leeban kaŋɛ mo: “Kumo ere, baa wɔ ŋ kutɔ nfe a shuŋ, ŋkpal manɛ so, ŋ ka ta mo n sa fo bɔ ŋ ka ta mo n sa enyɛn pɔtɛ.”

english_verse: Jacob worked seven years for Laban, but the time seemed like only a few days, because he loved Rachel so much.
translation_verse: Amoso nfɛnshunu nɛ Jeekɔb daŋ shuŋ ŋkpal Reechel so, ama nfɛnshunu na daa du fanɛ nchɛ gbrɛbi ko nna ŋkpal kasha nɛ e daa kɔ n sa Reechel na so.

english_verse: Jacob said to Laban, “The time is up, and I want to marry Rachel now!”
translation_verse: Nfɛnshunu na be kaman nɛ Jeekɔb kaŋɛ Leeban: “To, naniere saŋɛ fo nɛ n ta ma eche, amoso ta fo kebia na n sa ma nɛ e ki ma eche.”

english_verse: So Laban gave a big feast and invited all their neighbors.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Leeban shɛr ndoŋ be basa kikɛ n wora kejigboŋ n sa bumo.

english_verse: But that evening he brought Leah to Jacob, who married her and spent the night with her.
translation_verse: Ama kanyɛ ka biri nɛ e kini keta Reechel n sa Jeekɔb nseŋ keta Lia n ya sa mo nɛ Jeekɔb nɛ mo di keche nɛ kenyɛn.

english_verse: The next morning Jacob found out that he had married Leah, and he asked Laban, “Why did you do this to me? Didn't I work to get Rachel? Why did you trick me?”
translation_verse: Jeekɔb nɛ Lia ka di ŋklade nɛ Jeekɔb keni nɛ Lia nna, mannɛ Reechel. Ndoŋ nna nɛ e bishi Leeban le: “Manɛ be kushuŋ nɛ fo shuŋ ma loŋ? Reechel so nɛ n shuŋ fo ŋko mannɛ aloŋ nna? Nɛ manɛ e ba nɛ fo fule ma loŋ?”

english_verse: Laban replied, “In our country the older daughter must get married first.
translation_verse: Nɛ Leeban kaŋɛ mo fanɛ bumo ere be daŋkare to kebia maa kil nɛ mo da maŋ naŋ kil.

english_verse: After you spend this week with Leah, you may also marry Rachel. But you will have to work for me another seven years.”
translation_verse: Amoso e jo nɛ kejafɔ be aworbi na e loge bɔkwe na to pɔɛŋ nɛ e ta Reechel n sa mo nɛ e naŋ shuŋ nfɛnshunu n ti so.

english_verse: At the end of the week of celebration, Laban let Jacob marry Rachel, and he gave her his servant woman Bilhah. Jacob loved Rachel more than he did Leah, but he had to work another seven years for Laban.
translation_verse: Jeekɔb nɛ Reechel ka di keche nɛ kenyɛn nɛ Jeekɔb sha Reechel a chɔ Lia. Kede be kaman nɛ Jeekɔb naŋ shuŋ nfɛnshunu n sa Leeban. Jeekɔb be mbia be asheŋ

english_verse: The Lord knew that Jacob loved Rachel more than he did Leah, and so he gave children to Leah, but not to Rachel.
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ka wu fanɛ Jeekɔb maa sha Lia nɛnɛ nɛ e sa mo kakurge, ama Reechel bre daa la egbentepo nna.

english_verse: Leah gave birth to a son and named him Reuben. Then she said, “The Lord has taken away my sorrow. Now my husband will love me more than he does Rachel.”
translation_verse: Amoso Lia daŋ di kedampo nna ŋ kurge ebinyɛn nseŋ kaŋɛ le: “Enyɛnpe na wu ma kagbenejija nseŋ chɛ ma to, amoso naniere bre ŋ kul beeŋ baa sha ma.” Ŋkpal loŋ so nɛ e nase kebia na Ruben.

english_verse: Rachel was very jealous of Leah for having children, and she said to Jacob, “I'll die if you don't give me some children!”
translation_verse: Jemanɛ ere so kikɛ nɛ Reechel bre maŋ naŋ nya mbia n sa Jeekɔb, amoso e daa kɔ mo da Lia kukɔrkɔ nna nseŋ kaŋɛ Jeekɔb le: “Sa ma alɛ gba mbia, nɛ mannɛ aloŋ, meeŋ wu.”

english_verse: But Jacob became upset with Rachel and answered, “Don't blame me! I'm not God.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Jeekɔb nya agbo n wora Reechel nseŋ bishi mo: “N la Ebɔrɛ nna a? Mo nawule e naŋ teŋ shin nɛ fo kurge, mannɛ ma.”

english_verse: “Here, take my servant Bilhah,” Rachel told him. “Have children by her, and I'll let them be born on my knees to show that they are mine.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Reechel kaŋɛ mo: “Ma kebita Bilha e wɔtɔ na. To, ta mo n di nɛ e kurge mbia n sa ma, saŋɛ na so ma alɛ beeŋ bɔla mo so ŋ ki ebinio.”

english_verse: and they had a son.
translation_verse: Nɛ Bilha di kedampo ŋ kurge ebinyɛn n sa Jeekɔb.

english_verse: Rachel named him Dan, because she said, “God has answered my prayers. He judged in my favor and has given me a son.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Reechel kaŋɛ: “Naniere bre, Ebɔrɛ ji n chɛ ma to n nu ma kabɔrɛkule nseŋ sa ma ebinyɛn.” Amoso ketre nɛ e daŋ sa mo e daa la Dan.

english_verse: Rachel said, “I've struggled hard with my sister, and I've won!” So she named the boy Naphtali.
translation_verse: Nɛ Reechel naŋ kaŋɛ: “Ma nɛ n da Lia gberge abar to n chɛr ga, ama naniere bre m pɔɔ mo so.” Amoso ketre nɛ e daŋ sa kebia na e daa la Naftali.

english_verse: When Leah realized she could not have any more children, she let Jacob marry her servant Zilpah,
translation_verse: Lia malɛ ka wu fanɛ e maŋ naa kurge nɛ mo alɛ gba ta mbe kebita Zilpa n sa mo kul fanɛ e ta mo ŋ ki mbe eche.

english_verse: “I'm really lucky,” Leah said, and she named the boy Gad.
translation_verse: Nɛ Lia kaŋɛ: “Kumulela nde pasaa!” Amoso ketre nɛ e daŋ sa kebia na e daa la Gad.

english_verse: Leah exclaimed, “I'm happy now, and all the women will say how happy I am.” So she named him Asher. Love Flowers
translation_verse: Nɛ Lia kaŋɛ: “Ma kagbene fuli ma paa. Kede to bre, nfe be beche kikɛ beeŋ fara a tre ma kagbenefuliwura.” Amoso ketre nɛ e sa kebia na e la Ashɛr.

english_verse: During the time of the wheat harvest, Reuben found some love flowers and took them to his mother Leah. Rachel asked Leah for some of them,
translation_verse: Kachako kasɔteŋi be jemanɛ so nɛ Ruben yɔ kupuŋ to n ya wu asɔ duuso ko nɛ baa tre amo mandreek na nɛ e tia amo m ba sa mo nio Lia. Ndoŋ nna nɛ Reechel kaŋɛ Lia: “Jande, sa ma fo pibi be mandreek ere be ako.”

english_verse: but Leah said, “It's bad enough that you stole my husband! Now you want my son's love flowers too.” “All right,” Rachel answered. “Let me have the flowers, and you can sleep with Jacob tonight.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Lia bishi Reechel le: “Ama fo ka suge ŋ kul ŋ ka ma ere bre maŋ kukwe fo a? Nɛ fo naa sha kesɔ ma kebia be emandreek gba n ti so a?” Nɛ Reechel kaŋɛ mo: “To, kumo ere sa ma fo pibinyɛn be emandreek ere be ako nɛ n shin nɛ fo nɛ mo e di kanyɛ ere.”

english_verse: That evening when Jacob came in from the fields, Leah told him, “You're sleeping with me tonight. I hired you with my son's love flowers.” They slept together that night,
translation_verse: Kamɔnchɛ be kaaseso Jeekɔb ka shi ndɔ to m ba nɛ Lia ya kaŋɛ mo le: “Kanyɛ ere ma nɛ fo e wɔ kedi ŋkpal manɛ so, n ta ma kebia be emandreek nna n chɛr kedi ashi fo eche kutɔ.” Amoso Lia nɛ Jeekɔb e daŋ di kumo be kanyɛ na.

english_verse: Leah shouted, “God has rewarded me for letting Jacob marry my servant,” and she named the boy Issachar.
translation_verse: Lia ka kurge nɛ kaŋɛ: “Ebɔrɛ ka ma kukɔ ŋkpal ŋ ka ta ma kebita n sa ŋ kul so.” Amoso ketre nɛ e daŋ sa kebia na e daa la Isakar.

english_verse: she exclaimed, “God has given me a wonderful gift, and my husband will praise me for giving him six sons.” So she named the boy Zebulun.
translation_verse: Kede to nɛ Lia kaŋɛ: “Kashenteŋto, Ebɔrɛ kɛ ma kakɛ lela, amoso m baa nyi fanɛ kede to ŋ kul beeŋ bunyaŋ ma ŋkpal ŋ ka kurge bibinyɛn ashe n sa mo so.” Amoso ketre nɛ e daŋ sa kebia na e daa la Zɛbyulɔn.

english_verse: Later, Leah had a daughter and named her Dinah.
translation_verse: Zɛbyulɔn be kaman nɛ Lia kurge ebiche n nase mo Daina.

english_verse: Finally, God remembered Rachel—he answered her prayer by giving her a son. “God has taken away my disgrace,” she said.
translation_verse: nɛ e di kedampo ŋ kurge ebinyɛn nseŋ kaŋɛ: “Naniere bre, Ebɔrɛ lara ma anishinyɔr to.”

english_verse: “I'll name the boy Joseph, and I'll pray that the Lord will give me another son.” Jacob and Laban
translation_verse: Amoso ketre nɛ e daŋ sa kebia na e daa la Josɛf, ŋkpal manɛ so, le nɛ e daŋ kaŋɛ: “Ebɔrɛ naaŋ sa ma ebinyɛn ko n ti so.” Jeekɔb nɛ Leeban be asɔbɔya be asheŋ

english_verse: After Joseph was born, Jacob said to Laban, “Release me from our agreement and let me return to my own country.
translation_verse: Reechel ka kurge Josɛf na be kaman nɛ Jeekɔb kaŋɛ Leeban: “Sa ma ekpa nɛ m bɛta n yɔ ma efuli so.

english_verse: You know how hard I've worked for you, so let me take my wives and children and leave.”
translation_verse: Ta ma, ma beche nɛ mbia nɛ n shuŋ fo n nya na n sa ma nɛ n ta a yɔ. Fo alɛ gba nyi kushuŋ mo nɛ n shuŋ n sa fo.”

english_verse: Jacob answered: You've seen how hard I've worked for you, and you know how your flocks and herds have grown under my care.
translation_verse: Nɛ Jeekɔb kaŋɛ mo: “Fo gbagba baa nyi kananɛ n shuŋ n sa fo. Fo alɛ nseŋ naa nyi kananɛ fo asɔbɔya salga ashi ma enɔ to.

english_verse: You didn't have much before I came, but the Lord has blessed everything I have ever done for you. Now it's time for me to start looking out for my own family.
translation_verse: Asɔbɔya gbrɛbi nɛ fo daa kɔ pɔɛŋ nɛ m ba, ama naniere b salga n sɔ kakpa, nɛ Enyɛnpe na bɔla ma so n nɛfa fo ekpa kama so. To saŋɛ mo nɛ ma alɛ beeŋ wora kusɔ ko n sa ŋ gbagba be laŋ to ebi?”

english_verse: “How much do you want me to pay you?” Laban asked. Then Jacob told him: I don't want you to pay me anything. Just do one thing, and I'll take care of your sheep and goats.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Leeban bishi mo: “To, nɛ manɛ nɛ meeŋ ta ŋ ka fo kukɔ?” Nɛ Jeekɔb kaŋɛ mo: “Sa maŋ ka ma shɛŋ. Nɛ feeŋ shuli n wora kusɔ nɛ meeŋ kaŋɛ fo ere bre, meeŋ baa kraa keni fo asɔbɔya na so.

english_verse: Let me go through your flocks and herds and take the sheep and goats that are either spotted or speckled and the black lambs. That's all you need to give me.
translation_verse: Shin nɛ n luri fo asɔbɔya to kabre n lara mbolpɔ muchɛr muchɛr ŋko bechɛchɛrɛ na kikɛ nɛ bumo be befɔlbi nɛ b biri na kikɛ nɛ mboe chɛchɛrɛ ŋko bemuchɛr muchɛr na kikɛ ŋ ki ma kakɔka.

english_verse: In the future you can easily find out if I've been honest. Just look and see if my animals are either spotted or speckled, or if the lambs are black. If they aren't, they've been stolen from you.
translation_verse: Nɛ fo shin nɛ n wora loŋ, kumo ere echefoso feeŋ tiŋ m pin fanɛ mee ji kashenteŋ ŋko m maa ji kashenteŋ. Saŋɛ na so saŋkikɛ nɛ fee sha kekeni ma kakɔka be asheŋ to nseŋ wu kaboe kama nɛ e maŋ du muchɛr muchɛr ŋko chɛchɛrɛ ŋko kubolpɔbi kama nɛ e maŋ biri, kumo ere feeŋ tiŋ ŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ n yuri kumo nna.”

english_verse: Before the end of the day, Laban had separated his spotted and speckled animals and the black lambs from the others and had put his sons in charge of them.
translation_verse: Ama kumo be kamɔnchɛ kikɛ Leeban ya lara mboe nyɛnsoana nɛ b daa du muchɛr muchɛr ŋko chɛchɛrɛ na kikɛ nɛ mboe chesoana nɛ b daa du muchɛr muchɛr ŋko chɛchɛrɛ na nɛ mbolpɔfɔlbi lembirana na kikɛ n ta bumo n sa mbe mbia fanɛ b baa keni so.

english_verse: Then Laban made Jacob keep the rest of the sheep and goats at a distance of three days' journey.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e shin nɛ b ta loŋ be asɔbɔya na m barga Jeekɔb n nite nchɛ asa n ya chena, saŋɛ na so Jeekɔb malɛ beeŋ baa keni asɔbɔya nɛ b ka na so.

english_verse: Jacob cut branches from some poplar trees and from some almond and evergreen trees. He peeled off part of the bark and made the branches look spotted and speckled.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Jeekɔb ku kedibi ko nɛ baa tre pɔpla na nɛ kedibi nɛ baa tre amand na be ayabi nɛ kedibi nɛ baa tre pleen na be ayabi nseŋ marga m marga amo be afɔfɔ na be ako nɛ a fuli n weato.

english_verse: Then he put the branches where the sheep and goats would see them while they were drinking from the water trough. The goats mated there
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e ta loŋ be ayabi na n nase asɔbɔyaana na be asɔnuunchu akpa, saŋɛ na so asɔbɔya na ya kaa nuu nchu nsaa dii abar baaŋ baa wu ndibi weato na.

english_verse: Some of the sheep that Jacob was keeping for Laban were already spotted. And when the others were ready to mate, he made sure that they faced in the direction of the spotted and black ones. In this way, Jacob built up a flock of sheep for himself and did not put them with the other sheep.
translation_verse: Ade be kaman nɛ Jeekɔb barga asɔbɔya fɔlbiana na ashi begboŋi na to nseŋ shin nɛ begboŋi na bee keni Leeban be asɔbɔya weatoana na nɛ belembirana na be kaba so. Loŋ nɛ e daŋ wora n nya mo gbagba be asɔbɔya nseŋ barga bumo ashi Leeban peya to.

english_verse: But he would not put out the branches when the weaker animals were mating. So Jacob got all of the healthy animals, and Laban got what was left.
translation_verse: Ama asɔbɔya kama nɛ b daa maŋ kɔ eleŋ na bre baa dii e daa maa wora loŋ. Amoso asɔbɔya pɔsoana na e ki Leeban peya nɛ belempoana na malɛ ki Jeekɔb peya.

english_verse: Jacob soon became rich and successful. He owned many sheep, goats, camels, and donkeys, as well as a lot of slaves.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal loŋ so Jeekɔb daŋ ba ki damawura gboŋgboŋi nna a kɔ asɔbɔya damta nɛ nyɛrbi nɛ mbita nɛ enyɔma nɛ ekurma ga.

english_verse: Jacob heard that Laban's sons were complaining, “Jacob is now a rich man, and he got everything he owns from our father.”
translation_verse: Kachako nɛ Jeekɔb nu Leeban be mbia ka bee malga le: “Jeekɔb ta an tuto be kanya kikɛ ŋ ki mo peya, nseŋ bɔla amo so n dii dama.”

english_verse: Jacob also noticed that Laban was not as friendly as he had been before.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Jeekɔb wu fanɛ Leeban be asheŋ woraso maŋ naa du fanɛ kananɛ k daa du na.

english_verse: One day the Lord said, “Jacob, go back to your relatives in the land of your ancestors, and I will be with you.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Jeekɔb le: “Bɛta n yɔ fo basa pe ashi fo nanaana be kasawule so. Meeŋ baa wɔ fo kutɔ.”

english_verse: Jacob sent for Rachel and Leah to meet him in the pasture where he kept his sheep,
translation_verse: Jeekɔb ka nu loŋ na nɛ e shuŋi ŋ kaŋɛ Reechel nɛ Lia fanɛ b ba mo kutɔ kakpa nɛ mo nɛ mbe asɔbɔya wɔ na.

english_verse: and he told them: Your father isn't as friendly with me as he used to be, but the God my ancestors worshiped has been on my side.
translation_verse: B ka ba nɛ e kaŋɛ bumo le: “N wu fanɛ ma nɛ men tuto be kefɛato maŋ naa du fanɛ kananɛ k daa du na, ama n tuto be Ebɔrɛ na malɛ wɔ ma kutɔ.

english_verse: years to buy your sheep and goats. During that time you kept changing my wages.
translation_verse: Menyi alɛ kikɛ nyi kananɛ m bugi kagbene n shuŋ men tuto.

english_verse: and that he keeps cheating me by changing my wages time after time. But God has protected me.
translation_verse: Ama men tuto puni ma nseŋ chɛrga ma kakɔka ale kudu. Ama Ebɔrɛ maŋ shin nɛ e nya ma n doro bre.

english_verse: That's how God has taken sheep and goats from your father and given them to me.
translation_verse: Amoso fo keni a, Ebɔrɛ ta men tuto be asɔbɔya nna n sa ma.

english_verse: and I am the God you worshiped at Bethel, when you poured olive oil on a rock and made a promise to me. Leave here at once and return to the land where you were born.”
translation_verse: Ma alɛ e la Ebɔrɛ mo nɛ e daŋ lar fo so ashi Bɛtɛl na. Ndoŋ nɛ fo daŋ duga ŋku n wurge ndulgi be kejembu nɛ fo yuu na so nseŋ nase kɔnɔ n sa ma na. Naniere, lar kasawule ere so nfe epul ere to m bɛta n yɔ kasawule mo nɛ b kurge fo na so.’ ”

english_verse: He treats us like foreigners and has even cheated us out of the bride price that should have been ours.
translation_verse: Fo maŋ nyi fanɛ e bee keni anyi nna fanɛ befɔ a? E fa anyi nseŋ ta anyi be keshaji be asɔ n ji.

english_verse: So do whatever God tells you to do. Even the property God took from our father and gave to you really belongs to us and our children.
translation_verse: Amoso kanya kama nɛ Ebɔrɛ sɔ ashi an tuto kutɔ n sa fo ere e la anyi nɛ anyi be mbia peya na. Ŋkpal loŋ so, wora kusɔ kama nɛ Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ fo fanɛ fo wora na.”

english_verse: Then Jacob, his wives, and his children got on camels and left
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Jeekɔb ta mbe beche nɛ mbia n chena n chena enyɔma so

english_verse: northern Syria for the home of his father Isaac in Canaan. Jacob took along all his flocks, herds, and other property.
translation_verse: nseŋ kpa mbe asɔbɔya kikɛ n juŋkpar n ta asɔ nɛ e daŋ nya ashi Mɛsopoteemia na kikɛ n ti so a yɔ mo tuto Aizek kutɔ ashi Keenan be efuli so.

english_verse: Before Rachel left, she stole the household idols while Laban was out shearing his sheep.
translation_verse: Pɔɛŋ nɛ b lar na Leeban ka yɔ nɛ e ya kuya mbe mbolpɔ be afuibi nɛ Reechel ya yuri mo tuto Leeban be laŋ to be agbir.

english_verse: When Jacob crossed the Euphrates River and headed for the hill country of Gilead, he took with him everything he owned. Laban Catches Up with Jacob
translation_verse: Amoso, Jeekɔb daŋ ta mbe asɔ kikɛ nna n shile n ya dii lɔr nɛ baa tre Yufreetes na n ta n sɔ Gilead be efuli so, kakpa nɛ abee wɔ ga na. Leeban ka ju m bɛ Jeekɔb so be asheŋ

english_verse: Three days later Laban found out that Jacob had gone.
translation_verse: Jeekɔb ka shile na be kachɛ sasopo pɔɛŋ nɛ Leeban nu fanɛ e shile.

english_verse: So he took some of his relatives along and chased after Jacob for seven days, before catching up with him in the hill country of Gilead.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Leeban keta mbe basa n ju m bɛ Jeekɔb so nchɛnshunu pɔɛŋ nseŋ ya tu mo ashi Gilead be efuli so be kakpa nɛ abee damta wɔ na.

english_verse: But God appeared to Laban in a dream that night and warned, “Don't say a word to Jacob. Don't make a threat or a promise.”
translation_verse: Kumo be kanyɛso nɛ Ebɔrɛ lar Leeban so edare to ŋ kaŋɛ mo le: “Baa da so nsaa maŋ kaŋ malga kamalga lubi kikɛ ŋ gbiti Jeekɔb.”

english_verse: Jacob had set up camp in the hill country of Gilead, when Laban and his relatives came and set up camp in another part of the hill country. Laban went to Jacob
translation_verse: Jeekɔb daŋ ya yuu mbe wajɛbu abee to nna ashi Gilead be efuli so. Ndoŋ koŋwule na nɛ Leeban nɛ mbe basa gba daŋ ya yuu bumo be ewajɛbu.

english_verse: and said: Look what you've done! You've tricked me and run off with my daughters like a kidnapper.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Leeban bishi Jeekɔb le: “Manɛ be kushuŋ nɛ fo shuŋ ma loŋ? Fo fule ma nseŋ ta ma mbia n shile fanɛ anya nɛ b pɛ ashi kena to.

english_verse: Why did you sneak away without telling me? I would have given you a going-away party with singing and with music on tambourines and harps.
translation_verse: Manɛ e ba nɛ fo ŋana ma so n shile? Manɛ e ba nɛ fo daa maŋ kaŋɛ ma nɛ n shin nɛ an ta kagbenefuli nɛ alaŋsɔ m boŋ nshɛ n cha n shuŋi fo ekpa?

english_verse: You didn't even give me a chance to kiss my own grandchildren and daughters goodbye. That was really foolish.
translation_verse: Fo maŋ tiŋ n shin nɛ n lala n nanabiana so ŋ kela bumo nɛ bumo nioana kashaso gba. Fo wora kawulisheŋ ga.

english_verse: I could easily hurt you, but the God your father worshiped has warned me not to make any threats or promises.
translation_verse: Ŋ kɔ ekpa nɛ n daŋ shin nɛ b tɔrɔ fo, ama ndre kanyɛso, fo tuto be Ebɔrɛ na ba kaŋɛ ma fanɛ m baa da so nsaa maŋ kaŋ malga kamalga lubi kikɛ ŋ gbiti fo.

english_verse: I can understand why you were eager to return to your father, but why did you have to steal my idols?
translation_verse: N nyi fo ka shile ŋkpal kenaŋ bɛta n yɔ fo tuto pe be asheŋ ka pere fo kenishi ga so so, ama manɛ e ba nɛ fo naa yuri ma agbir malɛ a shile?”

english_verse: Jacob answered, “I left secretly because I was afraid you would take your daughters from me by force.
translation_verse: Nɛ Jeekɔb kaŋɛ Leeban: “N daa lɔ kufu nna fanɛ nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ fo, feeŋ suge fo mbia eleŋso ashi ŋ kutɔ.

english_verse: If you find that any one of us has taken your idols, I'll have that person killed. Let your relatives be witnesses. Show me what belongs to you, and you can take it back.” Jacob did not realize that Rachel had stolen the household idols.
translation_verse: Ama anyi to be ekama kutɔ nɛ fo wu fo agbir na, amodoŋwura maŋ daga e ka ji efute. Keni ma asɔ ere kikɛ to ashi an kurgepoana ere kikɛ be anishito ŋ keni fo asɔ ko wɔ amo to a. Nɛ fo kaŋ wu fo kusɔ kama amo to fo ta fo kusɔ.” Jeekɔb daa maŋ nyi fanɛ Reechel e yuri mo tuto be agbir na.

english_verse: Laban searched the tents of Jacob, Leah, and the two servant women, but did not find the idols. Then he went to Rachel's tent.
translation_verse: Jeekɔb ka kaŋɛ loŋ na nɛ Leeban luri mo ere Jeekɔb be wajɛbu to nɛ Lia nɛ bumo be mbita anyɔ na be ewajɛbu to ŋ keni ama e daa maŋ wu shɛŋ. Kumo be kaman nɛ e ya luri Reechel malɛ peya to.

english_verse: She had already hidden them in the cushion she used as a saddle and was sitting on it. Laban searched everywhere and did not find them.
translation_verse: Reechel malɛ daŋ ta mo tuto be agbir na nna n wɔtɔ mbe nyɔma be gaare be kaseto n chena so. Ndoŋ nna nɛ Leeban keni wajɛbu na to be asɔ kikɛ to nyam e maŋ wu shɛŋ.
