english_verse: Jacob became very angry and said to Laban: What have I done wrong? Have I committed some crime? Is that why you hunted me down?
translation_verse: Nɛ Jeekɔb kpal loŋ so n nya agbo n wɔtɔ Leeban nseŋ bishi mo: “Manɛ be kulubi nɛ n wora, nɛ fo kpal kumo so n ju a bɛ ma so?

english_verse: After searching through everything I have, did you find anything of yours? If so, put it here, where your relatives and mine can see it. Then we can decide what to do.
translation_verse: To, fo ka keni ma asɔ ere kikɛ to ere, manɛ nɛ fo wu nɛ k la fo laŋ to peya? Kusɔ kama nɛ fo wu, fo ta kumo n nase ma basa nɛ fo basa be anishito nɛ b keni esa nɛ e wora kulubi.

english_verse: If a wild animal killed one of your sheep or goats, I paid for it myself. In fact, you demanded the full price, whether the animal was killed during the day or at night.
translation_verse: Ma alɛ maŋ naŋ ta kusɔbɔya jiŋka kama nɛ kupuŋ to be kusɔbɔya kama pɛ n ji ŋ ka m bar fo. Kekama gba nɛ k daŋ wu, ma e daŋ ta kumo be kukɔ. Fo alɛ be kusɔbɔya kama nɛ b daŋ yuri kapaso ŋko kanyɛso fo daa shin nna nɛ mee ka loŋ be kusɔbɔya na be kukɔ.

english_verse: If the fearsome God worshiped by Abraham and my father Isaac had not been on my side, you would have sent me away without a thing. But God saw my hard work, and he knew the trouble I was in, so he helped me. Then last night he told you how wrong you were. Jacob and Laban Make an Agreement
translation_verse: Nɛ Ebɔrɛ nɛ n tuto Aizek bee bunyaŋ nɛ e la Eebraham gba be Ebɔrɛ na daa maŋ wɔ ma kutɔ nna, fo daa beeŋ ju ma fo laŋ to nɛ enɔfuloŋ. Ama Ebɔrɛ wu ma awurfoŋ nɛ kegben nɛ ŋ gben na kikɛ nna nseŋ fiɛ fo so edare na to.”

translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Leeban kaŋɛ Jeekɔb le: “Fo beche Lia nɛ Reechel ere la ma mbia nna nɛ fo mbia ere malɛ gba la n nanabiana nɛ asɔbɔya nɛ fo kɔ ere gba la meya. english_verse: So I am ready to make an agreement with you, and we will pile up some large rocks here to remind us of the agreement.”
translation_verse: Amoso shin nɛ ma nɛ fo e nase kɔnɔ n sa abar nɛ k baa la shɛda be kusɔ a wɔ anyi be kefɛato.”

english_verse: After Jacob had set up a large rock,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Jeekɔb ta kejembu ko n yuu n dulgi ndoŋ.

english_verse: he told his men to get some more rocks and pile them up next to it. Then Jacob and Laban ate a meal together beside the rocks.
translation_verse: E ka wora loŋ n loge nɛ e kaŋɛ mbe laŋ to ebi na: “Men gama ajembu n deŋi abar so.” Nɛ b gama ajembu n deŋi abar so nseŋ chena amo ekpa n ji.

english_verse: Laban named the pile of rocks Jegar Sahadutha. But Jacob named it Galeed.
translation_verse: Leeban daŋ tre loŋ be kaboŋ na Jega Sahaduta nna nɛ Jeekɔb malɛ tre ndoŋ Galeed.

english_verse: Laban said to Jacob, “This pile of rocks will remind us of our agreement.” That's why the place was named Galeed.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Leeban kaŋɛ: “Ajembu nɛ a deŋ abar so ere e la anyi be kɔnɔ naseso ere be shɛda kabre.” Loŋ so nɛ b daŋ nase ndoŋ Galeed na.

english_verse: Laban also said, “This pile of rocks means that the Lord will watch us both while we are apart from each other.” So the place was also named Mizpah.
translation_verse: Kumo be ketre ko gba e daa la Mispa, ŋkpal manɛ so, le nɛ e daŋ kaŋɛ: “Ebɔrɛ e baa keni ma nɛ fo kikɛ so saŋɛ nɛ anyee barga abar ere.

english_verse: Then Laban said: If you mistreat my daughters or marry other women, I may not know about it, but remember, God is watching us!
translation_verse: Nɛ fo baŋ tɔrɔ ma mbichebi ere be ekama ŋko n ta eche kama n ti bumo so, hale an ka bee shin nɛ an barga abar ŋkaa maaŋ naŋ wu abar ere gba, baa nyiŋi fanɛ Ebɔrɛ bee keni anyi.”

english_verse: Both this pile of rocks and this large rock have been set up between us as a reminder. I must never go past them to attack you, and you must never come past them to attack me.
translation_verse: Amoso m maaŋ baŋ amo so m ba tɔrɔ fo. Fo alɛ e sa maŋ baŋ amo so m ba tɔrɔ ma.

english_verse: My father Nahor, your grandfather Abraham, and their ancestors all worshiped the same God, and he will make sure that we each keep the agreement. Then Jacob made a promise in the name of the fearsome God his father Isaac had worshiped.
translation_verse: Eebraham nɛ Nahɔɔ nɛ bumo tuto be Ebɔrɛ na e gberge ekama nɛ e maŋ bɛ kɔnɔ naseso ere so kusoe.” Ndoŋ nɛ Jeekɔb yili Ebɔrɛ nɛ mo tuto Aizek daa bunyaŋ na be ketre so m bɔ ntaŋ fanɛ e beeŋ bɛ bumo be kɔnɔ naseso na so.

english_verse: Jacob killed an animal and offered it as a sacrifice there on the mountain, and he invited his men to eat with him. After the meal they spent the night on the mountain.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e lara sarga abee be efuli na so ndoŋ nseŋ tre basa nɛ b wɔ ndoŋ na kikɛ nɛ b ba ji. B ka ji n loge nɛ b di ndoŋ ŋklade.

english_verse: Early the next morning, Laban kissed his daughters and his grandchildren goodbye, then he left to go back home.
translation_verse: Kumo be ŋklade chipurdidi nɛ Leeban koso n lala mo nanabiana na nɛ mbe bibicheana na so n nɛfa bumo nseŋ bɛta n yɔ mo pe.

english_verse: As Jacob was on his way back home, some of God's angels came and met him.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Jeekɔb malɛ pɛ mbe ekpa a yɔ nɛ Ebɔrɛ be emalaika ba tu mo.

english_verse: When Jacob saw them, he said, “This is God's camp.” So he named the place Mahanaim.
translation_verse: Jeekɔb ka wu bumo nɛ e kaŋɛ: “Ebɔrɛ be benapo be echenakpa nde.” Kumo be kaman nɛ e nase kaboŋ na Mahanayim.

english_verse: Jacob told them to say to Esau, “Master, I am your servant! I have lived with Laban all this time,
translation_verse: Kamalga nɛ e daŋ ta n sa mbɔ na fanɛ b ya sa mo da Isɔɔ e la: “Fo kayɛrbi Jeekɔb yɛ: ‘N daŋ ya kaa wɔ Leeban pe nna m ba fo mbre.

translation_verse: Mbɔ na ka bɛta m ba Jeekɔb kutɔ nɛ b kaŋɛ mo le: “An yɔ fo da Isɔɔ kutɔ, amoso e ta basa alfa ana a shɛr fo to.”

english_verse: Jacob was so frightened that he divided his people, sheep, cattle, and camels into two groups.

english_verse: Please rescue me from my brother. I am afraid he will come and attack not only me, but my wives and children as well.

english_verse: But you have promised that I would be a success and that someday it will be as hard to count my descendants as it is to count the grains of sand along the seashore.

english_verse: And Jacob told them to be sure to say that he was right behind them. Jacob hoped the gifts would make Esau friendly, so Esau would be glad to see him when they met.

translation_verse: E ka ta bumo n dii eboŋ na n loge nɛ e ta mbe kanya malɛ kikɛ n dii.

english_verse: The man said, “From now on, your name will no longer be Jacob. You will be called Israel, because you have wrestled with God and with men, and you have won.”

translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Jeekɔb kule mo fanɛ e ti mbe ketre ŋ ŋini mo. Nɛ kanyɛn na kaŋɛ: “Manɛ nɛ fee sha ma ketre nɛ fo wora?” Kumo be kaman nɛ e nɛfa Jeekɔb.

english_verse: Then he said to the servant in charge of the first herd, “When Esau meets you, he will ask whose servant you are. He will want to know where you are going and who owns those animals in front of you.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e kaŋɛ anya na to be emo nɛ e daŋ juŋkpar na fanɛ mo da Isɔɔ baŋ tu mo nseŋ bishi mo fanɛ, “Wanɛ be esa e la fo? Nnɛ nɛ fee yɔ? Wanɛ e wɔ asɔbɔya damta nɛ b juŋkpar fo ere kikɛ?”

english_verse: So tell him, ‘They belong to your servant Jacob, who is coming this way. He is sending them as a gift to his master Esau.’ ”
translation_verse: Nɛ e kaŋɛ mo: “B la fo Isɔɔ be kenya Jeekɔb peya nna nɛ e kaŋɛ fanɛ an ta m bar fo. Ama mo ere wɔ kaman a ba.”

english_verse: Jacob also told the men in charge of the second and third herds and those who followed to say the same thing when they met Esau.
translation_verse: Loŋ koŋwule nɛ Jeekɔb daŋ kaŋɛ nyɛrbi nɛ b bɛ so na kikɛ fanɛ b kaŋɛ Isɔɔ.

english_verse: Jacob's men took the gifts on ahead of him, but he spent the night in camp. Jacob's Name Is Changed to Israel
translation_verse: Amoso Jeekɔb daŋ shin nna nɛ mbe kakɛ na juŋkpar mo nɛ mo ere naŋ shir echenakpa na n di ŋklade. Jeekɔb nɛ Ebɔrɛ ka kɔ emaŋ be asheŋ

english_verse: Jacob got up in the middle of the night and took his wives, his eleven children, and everything he owned across to the other side of the Jabbok River for safety.
translation_verse: E ka ta bumo n dii eboŋ na n loge nɛ e ta mbe kanya malɛ kikɛ n dii.

english_verse: Afterwards, Jacob went back and spent the rest of the night alone. A man came and fought with Jacob until just before daybreak.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Jeekɔb nawule bɛta n yɔ bumo be echenakpa na nɛ kanyɛn ko ba tu mo ŋ kɔ emaŋ hale nɛ kare ya chɛ.

english_verse: When the man saw that he could not win, he struck Jacob on the hip and threw it out of joint.
translation_verse: Kanyɛn na ka wu fanɛ e maa tiŋ a pɔɔ Jeekɔb so nɛ e beta Jeekɔb be kebembi nɛ mbe keleŋ kpekpel.

english_verse: They kept on wrestling until the man said, “Let go of me! It's almost daylight.” “You can't go until you bless me,” Jacob replied.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ kanyɛn na kaŋɛ Jeekɔb le: “Shin nɛ n yɔ, ŋkpal manɛ so, kare chɛ.” Nɛ Jeekɔb kaŋɛ mo: “M maaŋ shin nɛ fo yɔ ama fo baŋ nɛfa ma nna.”

english_verse: Then the man asked, “What is your name?” “Jacob,” he answered.
translation_verse: Nɛ kanyɛn na bishi Jeekɔb: “Fo ketre?” Nɛ Jeekɔb kaŋɛ: “Ma ketre e la Jeekɔb.”

english_verse: The man said, “From now on, your name will no longer be Jacob. You will be called Israel, because you have wrestled with God and with men, and you have won.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ kanyɛn na kaŋɛ Jeekɔb le: “Yili kabre mbaanaayɔ fo ketre maaŋ naŋ ji Jeekɔb, k ki Israɛl, ŋkpal fo nɛ Ebɔrɛ nɛ edimɛdi ka kɔ nɛ fo pɔɔ so so.”

english_verse: Jacob said, “Now tell me your name.” “Don't you know who I am?” he asked. And he blessed Jacob.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Jeekɔb kule mo fanɛ e ti mbe ketre ŋ ŋini mo. Nɛ kanyɛn na kaŋɛ: “Manɛ nɛ fee sha ma ketre nɛ fo wora?” Kumo be kaman nɛ e nɛfa Jeekɔb.

english_verse: The sun was coming up as Jacob was leaving Peniel. He was limping because he had been struck on the hip,
translation_verse: Epeŋi maŋ so nna pɔɛŋ nɛ e lar Peniyɛl a tɔr keleŋ so a yɔ.

english_verse: and the muscle on his hip joint had been injured. That's why even today the people of Israel don't eat the hip muscle of any animal.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal kesheŋ ere so nɛ Israɛlebi maa ji eblaŋ nɛ k mar kusɔbɔya be kebembi be echɛkpa na. Ŋkpal Ebɔrɛ ka daŋ beta Jeekɔb be kebembi nɛ k kpekpel na so e daa tɔr keleŋ so nna.

english_verse: As Jacob was on his way back home, some of God's angels came and met him.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Jeekɔb malɛ pɛ mbe ekpa a yɔ nɛ Ebɔrɛ be emalaika ba tu mo.

english_verse: When Jacob saw them, he said, “This is God's camp.” So he named the place Mahanaim.
translation_verse: Jeekɔb ka wu bumo nɛ e kaŋɛ: “Ebɔrɛ be benapo be echenakpa nde.” Kumo be kaman nɛ e nase kaboŋ na Mahanayim.

english_verse: Jacob sent messengers on ahead to Esau, who lived in the land of Seir, also known as Edom.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nɛ Jeekɔb yili n shuŋi mbɔ nɛ b juŋkpar mo a yɔ mo da Isɔɔ kutɔ ashi Seyir nɛ k wɔ Edɔm be efuli so na.

english_verse: Jacob told them to say to Esau, “Master, I am your servant! I have lived with Laban all this time,
translation_verse: Kamalga nɛ e daŋ ta n sa mbɔ na fanɛ b ya sa mo da Isɔɔ e la: “Fo kayɛrbi Jeekɔb yɛ: ‘N daŋ ya kaa wɔ Leeban pe nna m ba fo mbre.

english_verse: and now I own cattle, donkeys, and sheep, as well as many slaves. Master, I am sending these messengers in the hope that you will be kind to me.”
translation_verse: Ŋ kɔ ana nɛ ekurma nɛ mbolpɔ nɛ mboe, benyanyɛn nɛ benyache a ba nsaa kule fo n nyɛnpe fanɛ fo wu ma kuwɔr.’ ”

english_verse: When the messengers returned, they told Jacob, “We went to your brother Esau, and now he is heading this way with
translation_verse: Mbɔ na ka bɛta m ba Jeekɔb kutɔ nɛ b kaŋɛ mo le: “An yɔ fo da Isɔɔ kutɔ, amoso e ta basa alfa ana a shɛr fo to.”

english_verse: Jacob was so frightened that he divided his people, sheep, cattle, and camels into two groups.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ kufu nɛ kagbenejija damta tɔr Jeekɔb so nɛ e barga mbe basa nɛ mbe ana nɛ ekurma nɛ mbolpɔ nɛ mboe nɛ b wɔ mo kutɔ na to ntuŋnyɔ.

english_verse: Then Jacob prayed: You, Lord, are the God who was worshiped by my grandfather Abraham and by my father Isaac. You told me to return home to my family, and you promised to be with me and make me successful.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Jeekɔb kule Ebɔrɛ ŋ kaŋɛ: “N tuto Eebraham nɛ Aizek be Ebɔrɛ, n Nyɛnpe, fo e kaŋɛ ma fanɛ m bɛta n yɔ ma efuli so nɛ ma basa pe nɛ fo shin nɛ ŋ ki asɔwura.

english_verse: Please rescue me from my brother. I am afraid he will come and attack not only me, but my wives and children as well.
translation_verse: Amoso mee kule fo nna fanɛ fo mɔlga ma ashi n da Isɔɔ be enɔ to, ŋkpal manɛ so, mee lɔ kufu nna fanɛ e bee ba nna nɛ e ba kɔ ma nɛ ma beche nɛ mbia kena.

english_verse: But you have promised that I would be a success and that someday it will be as hard to count my descendants as it is to count the grains of sand along the seashore.
translation_verse: Ama fo alɛ kaŋɛ fanɛ feeŋ shin nɛ ŋ ki asɔwura nseŋ shin nɛ ma kanaŋ e salga fanɛ teku ase be leele nɛ esa maaŋ tiŋ ŋ karga na.”

english_verse: And Jacob told them to be sure to say that he was right behind them. Jacob hoped the gifts would make Esau friendly, so Esau would be glad to see him when they met.
translation_verse: E yɛ: “Men sa maŋ teŋ so kekaŋɛ Isɔɔ fanɛ mbe kenya Jeekɔb wɔ kaman a ba.” Jeekɔb daa fɛ nna fanɛ nɛ e ta le be ŋkɛ ere n juŋkpar n ya sa Isɔɔ, a beeŋ wushi mo kagbene nɛ e sɔ mo nɛ enɔ anyɔ.

english_verse: Jacob said, “I have seen God face to face, and I am still alive.” So he named the place Peniel.
translation_verse: Amoso nɛ Jeekɔb daŋ nase kaboŋ na be ketre Peniyɛl na, ŋkpal manɛ so, e yɛ: “N wu Ebɔrɛ kenishiso nfe nna, ma alɛ maŋ wu.”

english_verse: The two servant women, Zilpah and Bilhah, together with their children went first, followed by Leah and her children, then by Rachel and Joseph.
translation_verse: E daŋ ta mbita na nɛ bumo be mbia nna n juŋkpar nseŋ ta Lia nɛ mbe mbia m bɛ so n ta Reechel nɛ Josɛf m bɛ so lalaloge.

english_verse: Jacob himself walked in front of them all, bowing to the ground seven times as he came near his brother.
translation_verse: Jeekɔb ka wora loŋ na nɛ mo gbagba juŋkpar bumo kikɛ a jɔŋɛ a jɔŋɛ mo da Isɔɔ ase. E daŋ jɔŋɛ mo ase ale shunu nna pɔɛŋ nseŋ tu mo.

english_verse: But Esau ran toward Jacob and hugged and kissed him. Then the two brothers started crying.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Isɔɔ malɛ shile n ya ber Jeekɔb to n far n chɛ mo n lɛ mbe enɔ n deŋi mbe abatimu so nɛ bumo benyɔ na kikɛ shu ga.

english_verse: When Esau noticed the women and children he asked, “Whose children are these?” Jacob answered, “These are the children the Lord has been kind enough to give to me, your servant.”
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Isɔɔ ki ŋ keni n wu beche na nɛ bumo be mbia na nseŋ bishi Jeekɔb le: “Fo nɛ basa mo malɛ nna?” Nɛ Jeekɔb kaŋɛ: “Mbia nɛ Ebɔrɛ wu ma kuwɔr n sa ma, fo kenya nna.”

english_verse: Then the two servant women and their children came and bowed down to Esau.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ mbita na nɛ bumo be mbia ba jɔŋɛ m bunyaŋ Isɔɔ nɛ mbe basa na.

english_verse: Next, Leah and her children came and bowed down; finally, Joseph and Rachel also came and bowed down.
translation_verse: Nɛ Lia nɛ mbe mbia bɛ so n ta Reechel nɛ Josɛf malɛ m bɛ so lalaloge, nɛ bumo kikɛ jɔŋɛ m bunyaŋ Isɔɔ.

english_verse: Esau asked Jacob, “Why did you send those herds I met along the road?” “Master,” Jacob answered, “I sent them so you would be friendly to me.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Isɔɔ bishi Jeekɔb le: “Nɛ asɔbɔya damta nɛ n shɛr to na malɛ a?” Nɛ Jeekɔb kaŋɛ mo: “N ta bumo nna n sa fo nɛ fo wu ma kuwɔr n sɔ ma, n nyɛnpe.”

english_verse: “But, brother, I already have plenty,” Esau replied. “Keep them for yourself.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Isɔɔ kaŋɛ: “Bumo nɛ ma alɛ gba kɔ shi ga, amoso baa kɔ feya.”

english_verse: “No!” Jacob said. “Please accept them as a sign of your friendship for me. When you welcomed me and I saw your face, it was like seeing the face of God.
translation_verse: Nɛ Jeekɔb kaŋɛ mo: “Ayai, nɛ ma asheŋ baŋ bɔlɔ fo kenishi bre, kumo ere fo sɔ le be kakɛ nɛ mee sa fo ere, ŋkpal manɛ so, ŋ kaŋ baŋ wu fo anishito ere gba baa du nna fanɛ ŋ ka wu Ebɔrɛ be anishito na, fɔŋfɔŋ kananɛ fo sɔ ma nɛ enɔ anyɔ ere so.

english_verse: Please accept these as gifts I brought to you. God has been good to me, and I have everything I need.” Jacob kept insisting until Esau agreed.
translation_verse: Amoso, jande sɔ kakɛ nɛ n ta n shuŋi a sa fo ere, ŋkpal manɛ so, Ebɔrɛ wu ma kuwɔr ga n sa ma kusɔ kama nɛ k daga ma.” Ŋkpal Jeekɔb ka mata Isɔɔ so ga so nɛ e sɔ kakɛ na.

english_verse: “Let's get ready to travel,” Esau said. “I'll go along with you.”
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Isɔɔ kaŋɛ mo: “Shin nɛ n shuŋi fo n yɔ a!”

english_verse: But Jacob answered, “Master, you know traveling is hard on children, and I have to look after the sheep and goats that are nursing their young. If my animals travel too much in one day, they will all die.
translation_verse: Nɛ Jeekɔb kaŋɛ mo: “N nyɛnpe, fo nyi mbia ka maŋ kɔ eleŋ nɛ kumo alɛ naŋ daga fanɛ ŋ keni mbolpɔ cheso nɛ ana nɛ b kɔ bibi na so. B kpa bumo eleŋso kachɛ koŋwule n yɔ, asɔbɔya na kikɛ beeŋ wu.

english_verse: Why don't you go on ahead and let me travel along slowly with the children, the herds, and the flocks. We can meet again in the country of Edom.”
translation_verse: Amoso n nyɛnpe, juŋkpar ma a yɔ, nɛ ma alɛ e bɛ asɔbɔya na nɛ mbia na so a ba gbrɛgbrɛbi, hale nɛ an ba fo fo kutɔ ashi Edɔm be efuli so.”

english_verse: Esau replied, “Let me leave some of my men with you.” “You don't have to do that,” Jacob answered. “I am happy, simply knowing that you are friendly to me.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Isɔɔ kaŋɛ: “Kumo ere shin nɛ n yige ma basa ere be beko fo kutɔ.” Nɛ Jeekɔb bishi mo: “Manɛ nna nɛ fee sha nɛ fo wora loŋ, n nyɛnpe? Kananɛ fo sɔ ma ere gba kukwe.”

english_verse: But Jacob went to Succoth, where he built a house for himself and set up shelters for his animals. That's why the place is called Succoth. Jacob Arrives at Shechem
translation_verse: Ama Jeekɔb bre daŋ yɔ Sukɔf nna n ya pɔr kaboŋ ndoŋ n chena nseŋ yuu kuluu n sa mbe asɔbɔya malɛ. Sukɔf be kefito e la abuu to.

english_verse: After leaving northern Syria, Jacob arrived safely at Shechem in Canaan and set up camp outside the city.
translation_verse: Jeekɔb ka shi Mɛsopoteemia be efuli so m ba nɛ alenfia nɛ ya chena m mata kadegboŋ nɛ baa tre Shɛkɛm nɛ k wɔ Keenan be kasawule so na.

english_verse: The land where he camped was owned by the descendants of Hamor, the father of Shechem. So Jacob paid them
translation_verse: Gbiti be ndarbi kalfa nɛ Jeekɔb daŋ ta n tɔ kasawule nɛ e chena so na ashi Hamar be mbia kutɔ. Hamar ere e daa la Shɛkɛm mo tuto na.

english_verse: then he set up his tents and built an altar there to honor the God of Israel.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nɛ e pɔr bɔrɛsure m bunyaŋ Israɛl be Ebɔrɛ na nseŋ nase kumo Ɛl Elohi Israɛl.

english_verse: Dinah, the daughter of Jacob and Leah, went to visit some of the women who lived nearby.
translation_verse: Kachako nɛ Daina, Lia pibiche nɛ e daŋ kurge n sa Jeekɔb na lar n yɔ nɛ e ya bɔ Shɛkɛm be beche so.

english_verse: She was seen by Hamor's son Shechem, the leader of the Hivites, and he grabbed her and raped her.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Shɛkɛm, Hamar nɛ e daa la Hivebi nɛ efuli na so be ewura na pibinyɛn wu Daina nseŋ pur mo.

english_verse: But Shechem was attracted to Dinah, so he told her how much he loved her.
translation_verse: E ka pur mo na nɛ mbe kagbene kilgi Jeekɔb pibiche Daina na so ga nɛ mbe kasha ba kebichebi na so nɛ e malga mo kutɔ kashaso.

english_verse: Shechem even asked his father to arrange for him to marry her.
translation_verse: Kesheŋ ere be kaman nɛ Shɛkɛm kaŋɛ mo tuto Hamar fanɛ e ya sha kebichebi na n sa mo nɛ e ki mbe eche.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Jacob heard what had happened. But his sons were out in the fields with the cattle, so he did not do anything at the time.
translation_verse: Saŋɛ nɛ Jeekɔb nu fanɛ b jija mo pibiche Daina na nɛ mbe bibinyɛn daa wɔ kupuŋ to a keni bumo be asɔbɔya so. Nɛ e loto boeŋ hale nɛ mbe mbrantiɛ na ya shi kupuŋ to ŋ keta bumo be asɔbɔya m ba.

english_verse: just as Jacob's sons were coming in from work. When they learned that their sister had been raped, they became furiously angry, because nothing is more disgraceful than rape, and it must not be tolerated.
translation_verse: Kumo be jemanɛ malɛ nɛ Jeekɔb be mbinyɛnbi na shi kupuŋ to m ba. B ka nu kusɔ nɛ k wora bumo sipoche Daina na nɛ kagbenejija bumo nɛ agbo pɛ bumo ŋkpal Shɛkɛm ka wora Jeekɔb pibiche anishinyɔr be kusɔ nɛ k maŋ daga ashi Israɛl be efuli so so.

english_verse: Hamor said to Jacob and his sons: My son Shechem really loves Dinah. Please let him marry her.
translation_verse: Ama le nɛ Hamar bre daŋ kaŋɛ bumo: “Ma kebia Shɛkɛm be kayɛlga wɔ men pibiche Daina so nna. Amoso, jande men ta mo n sa mo nɛ e ki mbe eche.

english_verse: You can share this land with us. Move freely about until you find the property you want; then buy it and settle down here.
translation_verse: Menyeeŋ tiŋ n chena anyi be efuli ere be kaplɛkama nɛ menyee sha. Men baa wɔ kumo so a ji yawu nsaa fin kanya a sa menyi be amu.”

english_verse: Jacob's sons wanted to get even with Shechem and his father because of what had happened to their sister.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal Shɛkɛm ka jija bumo sipoche Daina so, Jeekɔb be bibinyɛn na daŋ fule nna n shuli n sa Shɛkɛm nɛ mo tuto Hamar.

english_verse: So they tricked them by saying: You're not circumcised! It would be a disgrace for us to let you marry Dinah now.
translation_verse: Le nɛ b daŋ kaŋɛ bumo: “Anyi maaŋ tiŋ n wora le be kesheŋ ere, anyi maaŋ tiŋ n ta an sipoche n sa esa nɛ e maŋ ku kututu. K beeŋ baa la anishinyɔr be kusɔ nna n sa anyi.

english_verse: But we will let you marry her, if you and the other men in your tribe agree to be circumcised.
translation_verse: Ekpa koŋwule so nawule nɛ anyeeŋ shuli n sa fo. Kumo e la fanɛ menyeeŋ ki fanɛ anyi nna, nseŋ ku menyi be benyɛn kikɛ atutu.

english_verse: Then your families can marry into ours, and ours can marry into yours, and we can live together like one nation.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ an baa ta abar be mbichebi a kil. Loŋ nɛ anyeeŋ chena menyi to nɛ anyi nɛ menyi e ki basa koŋwule.

english_verse: But if you don't agree to be circumcised, we'll take Dinah and leave this place.
translation_verse: Ama nɛ menyi maaŋ shuli ŋ ku menyi be atutu bre, anyeeŋ sɔ an sipoche nseŋ koso menyi be efuli so.”

english_verse: Shechem was the most respected person in his family, and he was so in love with Dinah that he hurried off to get everything done.
translation_verse: Shɛkɛm nɛ e daa la kabrantiɛbia nɛ ekama daa sa mo bunyaŋ ga ashi mo tuto be laŋ to na, daŋ maŋ naŋ jo kikɛ nseŋ wora kusɔ nɛ Jeekɔb be mbia daŋ kaŋɛ bumo na. Ŋkpal manɛ so, mbe kagbene daŋ pɛ Daina ga.

english_verse: These people really are friendly. Why not let them move freely about until they find the property they want? There's enough land here for them and for us. Then our families can marry into theirs, and theirs can marry into ours.
translation_verse: B yɛ: “Basa ere bee sha anyi be asheŋ ga. Men shin nɛ b chena anyi be kasawule ere so a ji yawu. Kasawule na shi ga nsaa beeŋ fo anyi nɛ bumo kikɛ. Anyeeŋ tiŋ n ta bumo be mbichebi nɛ bumo alɛ gba e tiŋ n ta anyeya.

english_verse: We have to do only one thing before they will agree to stay here and become one nation with us. Our men will have to be circumcised just like theirs.
translation_verse: Ama basa na be kechena anyi be kasawule ere so beeŋ shi kananɛ anyeeŋ baa shuli a ku atutu fanɛ bumo nna.

english_verse: Just think! We'll get their property, as well as their flocks and herds. All we have to do is to agree, and they will live here with us.
translation_verse: Nɛ an wora loŋ, basa ere be asɔbɔya ere nɛ bumo be kusɔ kama nɛ b kɔ ere kikɛ maaŋ ba ki anyeya a? Loŋ so, men shin nɛ an shuli kusɔ nɛ b kaŋɛ na nseŋ shin nɛ b chena anyi be kasawule ere so.”

english_verse: Three days later the men who had been circumcised were still weak from pain. So Simeon and Levi, two of Dinah's brothers, attacked with their swords and killed every man in the town,
translation_verse: B ka ku atutu na be nchɛ asa be kefɛato, saŋɛ nɛ b kraa wɔ bumo be katutuku be ebesa to na nɛ Jeekɔb be bibinyɛn anyɔ, Simiɔn nɛ Livai, Daina mo siponyɛnana gbagba na, ta bumo be etokobi n ya gboŋ bumo m mɔ bumo be benyɛn na kikɛ, ŋkpal manɛ so, b daŋ maŋ bela ase.

english_verse: Jacob's other sons came and took everything they wanted. All this was done because of the horrible thing that had happened to their sister.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Jeekɔb be mbia nɛ b ka na malɛ luri n sensaŋ kade nɛ b daŋ jija bumo sipoche kumo to na be asɔ kikɛ.

english_verse: They took sheep, goats, donkeys, and everything else that was in the town or the countryside.
translation_verse: B daŋ pɛ bumo be mbolpɔ nɛ ana nɛ ekurma nna, nseŋ ta bumo be asɔ kama nɛ b kɔ epe nɛ ndɔana to kikɛ.

english_verse: After taking everything of value from the houses, they dragged away the wives and children of their victims.
translation_verse: B daŋ ta basa na be kanya kikɛ nɛ bumo be beche nɛ mbia kikɛ nna.

english_verse: Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, “Look what you've done! Now I'm in real trouble with the Canaanites and Perizzites who live around here. There aren't many of us, and if they attack, they'll kill everyone in my household.”
translation_verse: Le be asheŋ ere ka wora na be kaman nɛ Jeekɔb kaŋɛ Simiɔn nɛ Livai le: “Men bar ma tɔrɔ nna na. Naniere Keenanebi nɛ Pɛrizebi, nɛ b wɔ efuli ere so ere beeŋ kishi ma. Anyi alɛ be basa maŋ shi. Nɛ basa ere kikɛ wora kɔnɔkoŋwule, baaŋ mur ma nɛ ma laŋ to ebi ere kikɛ.”

english_verse: They answered, “Was it right to let our own sister be treated that way?”
translation_verse: Nɛ mbe mbia na kaŋɛ mo le: “Anyi alɛ gba maaŋ shuli nɛ b ta an sipoche ŋ ki fanɛ bojuache.”

english_verse: Afterwards, we'll go to Bethel. I will build an altar there for God, who answered my prayers when I was in trouble and who has always been at my side.
translation_verse: nseŋ ba nɛ an yɔ Bɛtɛl n ya yuu bɔrɛsure n sa Ebɔrɛ nɛ e nu n sa ma nsaa wɔ ma kutɔ kaplɛkama nɛ n yɔ saŋɛ nɛ n wɔ awurfoŋ to na.”

english_verse: So everyone gave Jacob their idols and their earrings, and he buried them under the oak tree near Shechem.
translation_verse: Jeekɔb ka malga loŋ n loge nɛ b ta bumo be agbirana na kikɛ nɛ bumo be akondeana kikɛ n sa mo nɛ e ta amo m puli Shɛkɛm be kedibigboŋ na ase.

english_verse: While Jacob and his family were traveling through Canaan, God terrified the people in the towns so much that no one dared bother them.
translation_verse: Jeekɔb nɛ mbe kanaŋ ka lar Shɛkɛm a yɔ nɛ Ebɔrɛ shin nɛ kufu pɛ nde nɛ b bɔla amo ase a choŋ na be basa. Amoso b daŋ maŋ tiŋ n wora Jeekɔb nɛ mbe basa shɛŋ.

english_verse: Jacob built an altar there and called it “God of Bethel,” because that was the place where God had appeared to him when he was running from Esau.
translation_verse: Nɛ Jeekɔb pɔr bɔrɛsure ndoŋ n sa Ebɔrɛ nseŋ tre kaboŋ na Ɛl Bɛtɛl, ŋkpal manɛ so, ndoŋ nɛ Ebɔrɛ daŋ lara mbe kumu ŋ ŋini mo saŋɛ nɛ e daa shile a ŋana mo da Isɔɔ so na.

english_verse: While they were there, Rebekah's personal servant Deborah died. They buried her under an oak tree and called it “Weeping Oak.” God Blesses Jacob at Bethel
translation_verse: Loŋ be saŋɛ na nɛ Dɛbora, nɛ e daa la kebita a keni Rebɛka so kebiato na wu nɛ b puli mo Bɛtɛl be kedibigboŋ na ase. Loŋ so b daa tre ndoŋ Alɔn Bakut nna.

english_verse: After Jacob came back to the land of Canaan, God appeared to him again. This time he gave Jacob a new name and blessed him by saying: I am God All-Powerful, and from now on your name will be Israel instead of Jacob. You will have many children. Your descendants will become nations, and some of the men in your family will even be kings.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Ebɔrɛ naŋ kaŋɛ mo: “Ma e la Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na. Meeŋ shin nɛ fo mbia e ba kaa shi ŋ ki efuli damtaana be amuwuraana nɛ bumo be beko e ki bewura.

english_verse: I will give you the land that I promised Abraham and Isaac, and it will belong to your family forever.
translation_verse: N ta kasawule nɛ n daŋ ta n sa Eebraham nɛ Aizek na, n sa fo alɛ gba nɛ fo kaman to ebi.”

english_verse: Jacob set up a large rock, so that he would remember what had happened there. Then he poured wine and olive oil on the rock to show that it was dedicated to God,
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ ka yige mo n choŋ na nɛ Jeekɔb yuu ndulgi be kejembu ndoŋ nseŋ chulgi asɔnuuso ko nɛ ŋku n wurge kumo so fanɛ sarga na n sa Ebɔrɛ.

english_verse: and he named the place Bethel. Benjamin Is Born
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Jeekɔb nase ndoŋ be ketre Bɛtɛl. Reechel nɛ Aizek be luwu be asheŋ

english_verse: Jacob and his family had left Bethel and were still a long way from Ephrath, when the time came for Rachel's baby to be born.
translation_verse: Jeekɔb nɛ mbe kanaŋ ka lar Bɛtɛl a yɔ Efraf na nɛ kakurge ta Reechel. Kumo alɛ daa du kpakpa n sa mo.

english_verse: She was having a rough time, but the woman who was helping her said, “Don't worry! It's a boy.”
translation_verse: Mbe kakurge na be asheŋ ka bee ki kpakpa a ti so na nɛ kache nɛ e daa keta mo kurge na kaŋɛ mo: “Reechel, sa maa lɔ kufu, ebinyɛn nɛ fo naŋ nya.”

english_verse: Rachel was at the point of death, and right before dying, she said, “I'll name him Benoni.” But Jacob called him Benjamin.
translation_verse: Kajaa Reechel malɛ daa kɔ luwu nna, ama pɔɛŋ nɛ e wu nɛ e nase mbe kebia na Bɛn Oni. Ama kebia na mo tuto bre daŋ naŋ nase mo Bɛnjamin nna.

english_verse: Rachel was buried beside the road to Ephrath, which is also called Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Reechel ka wu nɛ b puli mo ashi Efraf be ekpa to. Ndoŋ koŋwule na e la Bɛtlɛhɛm na.

english_verse: Jacob, also known as Israel, traveled to the south of Eder Tower, where he set up camp.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Jeekɔb naŋ lar ndoŋ a yɔ n ya choŋ Mikdal Eder so n yɔ anishito n ya yuu mbe wajɛbu. Jeekɔb be mbia be asheŋ (

english_verse: During their time there, Jacob's oldest son Reuben slept with Bilhah, who was one of Jacob's other wives. And Jacob found out about it. Jacob's Twelve Sons
translation_verse: Saŋɛ nɛ Jeekɔb daa wɔ ndoŋ na nɛ Ruben ya tu mo tuto Jeekɔb mo jipoche Bilha n di nɛ Jeekɔb nu kumo be asheŋ. Jeekɔb daa kɔ mbinyɛnbi kuduanyɔ nna.

english_verse: Jacob had twelve sons while living in northern Syria. His first-born Reuben was the son of Leah, who later gave birth to Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun. Leah's servant Zilpah had two sons: Gad and Asher. Jacob and his wife Rachel had Joseph and Benjamin. Rachel's servant woman Bilhah had two more sons: Dan and Naphtali. Isaac Dies
translation_verse: Lia be kebita Zilpa be mbia e daa la, Gad nɛ Ashɛr. Jeekɔb be mbinyɛnbi nɛ b daŋ kurge n sa mo ashi Mɛsopoteemia be efuli so nna na. Aizek be luwu be asheŋ

english_verse: Jacob went to his father Isaac at Hebron, also called Mamre or Kiriath-Arba, where Isaac's father Abraham had lived as a foreigner.
translation_verse: Jeekɔb nite loŋ m ba fo mo tuto Aizek pe ashi Mamre nɛ k daŋ taga Kiriaf Aba na. Kumo koŋwule na e la Hibrɔn na. Ndoŋ nɛ Aizek nɛ Eebraham daŋ chena na.

english_verse: Isaac died at the ripe old age of
translation_verse: Nfɛ ere be kaman nɛ e wu nɛ mbe mbia Isɔɔ nɛ Jeekɔb puli mo.

english_verse: Esau, also known as Edom, had many descendants.
translation_verse: Isɔɔ nɛ mo koŋwule na la Edɔm na be kaman to ebi nde.

english_verse: He married three Canaanite women: The first was Adah, the daughter of Elon the Hittite; the second was Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah and the granddaughter of Zibeon the Hivite;
translation_verse: Isɔɔ daŋ ta beche nna ashi Keenanebi na to. Bumo e daa la Ada, Ilɔn nɛ e la Hitebi be esa na pibi, nɛ Oholibama, Ana pibi, mo alɛ nseŋ naa la Zibiɔn mo nɛ e la Hivebi be esa na mo nanabi.

english_verse: the third was Basemath, who was Ishmael's daughter and Nebaioth's sister.
translation_verse: Isɔɔ be eche sasopo malɛ e daa la Basemat nɛ mo sipo la Nabaiɔt nɛ bumo tuto la Ishmaɛl na.

english_verse: Esau and his three wives had five sons while in Canaan. Adah's son was Eliphaz; Basemath's son was Reuel; Oholibamah's three sons were Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
translation_verse: Nɛ Oholibama malɛ be mbia daa la Jewush nɛ Jalam nɛ Koora. Isɔɔ be bibinyɛn nɛ b daŋ kurge n sa mo Keenan be efuli so nna na.

english_verse: Esau took his children and wives, his relatives and servants, his animals and possessions he had acquired while in Canaan, and moved far from Jacob.
translation_verse: Isɔɔ daŋ keta mbe beche nɛ mbe bibinyɛn nɛ mbe bibiche nɛ mbe laŋ to ebi kikɛ nɛ mbe asɔbɔya nɛ mbe kanya nɛ e nya ashi Keenan be efuli so na kikɛ nna m barga Jeekɔb n ya chena kasawule ko so.

english_verse: That's why Esau made his home in the hill country of Seir.
translation_verse: Amoso Isɔɔ nɛ mo koŋwule na la Edɔm na, daŋ ya chena Edɔm be efuli so be abee to nna.

english_verse: Esau and Adah's oldest son was Eliphaz, and the clans that descended from him were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Kenaz,
translation_verse: Bewura nɛ b daa shi Isɔɔ be kanaŋ to nde. Bewura nɛ b daŋ shi Elifas nɛ e la Isɔɔ be wurkoŋ be mbinyɛnbiana to be eko daa la Teman nɛ Omaa nɛ Zefo nɛ Kenas

english_verse: Seir was from the Horite tribe that had lived in Edom before the time of Esau. The clans that had descended from him were Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
translation_verse: Seyir nɛ e la Horaiebi be esa na be mbinyɛnbi nɛ b daa wɔ efuli na so nde. Lotan nɛ Shobal nɛ Zibiɔn nɛ Ana,

english_verse: Lotan's sons were Hori and Heman; his sister was Timna.
translation_verse: Lotan be mbinyɛnbi e daa la Horai nɛ Homam. Timna malɛ daa la Lotan mo sipoche nna.

english_verse: Shobal's sons were Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.
translation_verse: Shobal be mbia e daa la Alvan nɛ Manahaf nɛ Ebal nɛ Shefo nɛ Onam.

english_verse: Zibeon's sons were Aiah and Anah—the same Anah who found an oasis in the desert while taking the donkeys of his father out to pasture.
translation_verse: Zibiɔn malɛ be mbia e daa la Aya nɛ Ana. Le be Ana ere e daŋ fara n wu kabombi tushiso na ashi kiyi to saŋɛ nɛ e daa kpa mo tuto Zibiɔn be ekurma na.

english_verse: Dishon's sons were Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.
translation_verse: Dishɔn malɛ be mbia e daa la Hemdan nɛ Eshban nɛ Itran nɛ Keran.

english_verse: Ezer's sons were Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.
translation_verse: Ezaa malɛ be mbia e daa la Bilhan, Zafan nɛ Akan.

english_verse: Dishan's sons were Uz and Aran.
translation_verse: Dishan malɛ be mbia e daa la Uz nɛ Aran.

english_verse: The clans of the Horites were Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
translation_verse: Le be basa ere malɛ e daa la Horaiebi na be bewura: Lotan nɛ Shobal nɛ Zibiɔn nɛ Ana

english_verse: Before there were kings in Israel, the following kings ruled Edom one after another: Bela son of Beor from Dinhabah; Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah; Husham from the land of Teman; Hadad son of Bedad from Avith ; Samlah from Masrekah; Shaul from the city of Rehoboth on the Euphrates River; Baalhanan son of Achbor; Hadar from the city of Pau .
translation_verse: Baalhanan, Akbɔ pibi ka wu nɛ Hadad ta kuwura na. Mbe kadegboŋ e daa la Pawu nɛ mbe eche malɛ be ketre daa la Mehetabel nɛ e la Matrɛd pibiche nsaa la Mezahab mo nanabi na.

english_verse: The clans that descended from Esau took their names from their families and the places where they lived. They are Timna, Alvah, Jetheth,
translation_verse: Bewura nɛ b daŋ lar Isɔɔ be kanaŋ to ashi ntuŋ so be atre nde: Timna nɛ Alvan nɛ Jetɛt

english_verse: Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon,
translation_verse: nɛ Oholibama nɛ Ila nɛ Pinɔn

english_verse: Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar,
translation_verse: nɛ Kenaz nɛ Teman nɛ Mibza

english_verse: Magdiel, and Iram. These clans descended from Esau, who was known as Edom, the father of the Edomites. They took their names from the places where they settled.
translation_verse: nɛ Magdiel nɛ Iram. Bewura nɛ b daŋ ji kuwura kakpa nɛ b chena ashi Edɔm be kasawule so nna na. Kananɛ Isɔɔ, nɛ e la Edɔmebi bumo tuto, na be kaman to ebi be kuwurji be asheŋ nite nna na. Kananɛ Edɔmebi nɛ b la Isɔɔ na be kaman to ebi lar nna na.

english_verse: Jacob lived in the land of Canaan, where his father Isaac had lived,
translation_verse: Jeekɔb daŋ chena Keenan be kaboŋ nɛ mo tuto daa wɔ fanɛ efɔ na nna.

english_verse: “They're not here anymore,” the man replied. “I overheard them say they were going to Dothan.” Joseph left and found his brothers in Dothan.
translation_verse: Nɛ kanyɛn na kaŋɛ mo: “B maŋ naa wɔ nfe. N daŋ nu b ka kaŋɛ abar fanɛ b yɔ Dotan.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ Josɛf ju mo daana na be kebɔr n ya tu bumo Dotan.

english_verse: Jacob loved Joseph more than he did any of his other sons, because Joseph was born when Jacob was very old. Jacob had even given Joseph a fancy coat
translation_verse: Jeekɔb malɛ daa sha Josɛf nna ga a chɔ mbe mbia na be ekama ŋkpal e ka daa la mbe mbel to be kebia so. Amoso e daŋ baa piŋi tenteŋ muchɛr muchɛr nna n sa Josɛf.

english_verse: which showed that Joseph was his favorite son, and so Joseph's brothers hated him and would not be friendly to him.
translation_verse: Mo daana ka wu fanɛ bumo tuto bee sha Josɛf a chɔ bumo na nɛ b kishi mo nsaa maŋ naa malga mo kutɔ kashaso.

english_verse: One day, Joseph told his brothers what he had dreamed, and they hated him even more.
translation_verse: Kachako nɛ Josɛf ku edare ko. E ka kaŋɛ mo daana edare na nɛ b kpal kumo so ŋ kishi mo ga n ti so.

english_verse: Joseph said, “Let me tell you about my dream.
translation_verse: Le nɛ e daŋ kaŋɛ bumo: “Men nu edare mo nɛ ŋ ku ere.

english_verse: We were out in the field, tying up bundles of wheat. Suddenly my bundle stood up, and your bundles gathered around and bowed down to it.”
translation_verse: Edare na to n wu fanɛ an yɔ ndɔ to nna n ya teŋi ayu a kre to a nase nɛ ma kuyu pati niŋi to n yili nɛ menyeyaana ba gama ŋ kulti meya na nsaa jɔŋɛ kumo ase.”

english_verse: His brothers asked, “Do you really think you are going to be king and rule over us?” Now they hated Joseph more than ever because of what he had said about his dream.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ mo daana na bishi mo: “Ama fee fɛ nna fanɛ feeŋ ba ji anyi so kuwura ŋko feeŋ ba kaa kɔ eleŋ anyi so a?” Nɛ b naŋ kpal edare na nɛ mbe mmalga so ŋ kishi mo ga n ti so.

english_verse: Joseph later had another dream, and he told his brothers, “Listen to what else I dreamed. The sun, the moon, and eleven stars bowed down to me.”
translation_verse: Kachako nɛ Josɛf naŋ ku edare ko nseŋ naŋ kute kumo ŋ ŋini mo daana na. E yɛ: “Men nu nfe, n yaŋ ku edare ko nna n wu epeŋi nɛ kufɔl nɛ achɛkpabi kudukako ka bee jɔŋɛ ma ase.”

english_verse: When he told his father about this dream, his father became angry and said, “What's that supposed to mean? Are your mother and I and your brothers all going to come and bow down to you?”
translation_verse: E ka kaŋɛ mo tuto edare na nɛ mo tuto ponte mo so ŋ kaŋɛ: “Nuso be edare nɛ fo ku loŋ? Fee fɛ fanɛ ma nɛ fo nio nɛ fo daana beeŋ ba kaa jɔŋɛ fo ase kashenteŋto nna a?”

english_verse: Joseph's brothers were jealous of him, but his father kept wondering about the dream. Joseph Is Sold and Taken to Egypt
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ mo daana na fara a kɔ mo kukɔrkɔ ŋko a besa mo eyur ashi bumo be ŋgbene to, ama mo tuto bre daa maŋ teŋ kesheŋ na so. Josɛf mo daana ka fa mo be asheŋ

english_verse: One day when Joseph's brothers had taken the sheep to a pasture near Shechem,
translation_verse: Kachako nɛ mo daana na kpa bumo tuto be mbolpɔ a yɔ Shɛkɛm,

english_verse: his father Jacob said to him, “I want you to go to your brothers. They are with the sheep near Shechem.” “Yes, sir,” Joseph answered.
translation_verse: nɛ bumo tuto Jeekɔb kaŋɛ Josɛf le: “Fo daana wɔ Shɛkɛm a keni mbolpɔ so, amoso shin nɛ n shuŋi fo bumo kutɔ.” Nɛ Josɛf shuli ŋ kaŋɛ: “To.”

english_verse: His father said, “Go and find out how your brothers and the sheep are doing. Then come back and let me know.” So he sent him from Hebron Valley. Joseph was near Shechem
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ mo tuto kaŋɛ mo: “Keni, yɔ naniere n ya keni kananɛ fo daana nɛ asɔbɔya na du. Fo kaŋ wu bumo, fo naŋ ba kaŋɛ ma kusɔ nɛ k wɔtɔ.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ e shin nɛ Josɛf bɔla Hibrɔn be ketaŋɛ to a yɔ Shɛkɛm.

english_verse: and wandering through the fields, when a man asked, “What are you looking for?”
translation_verse: E ka ya fo Shɛkɛm nɛ kanyɛn ko wu mo nɛ e na ndoŋ a kilgi to nɛ e bishi mo: “Manɛ nɛ fee fin?”

english_verse: Joseph answered, “I'm looking for my brothers who are watching the sheep. Can you tell me where they are?”
translation_verse: Nɛ Josɛf kaŋɛ mo: “N daana nɛ mee fin. Jande nɛ fo nyi kakpa nɛ b wɔ a keni anyi be mbolpɔ so, fo ŋini ma ndoŋ.”

english_verse: But before he got there, they saw him coming and made plans to kill him.
translation_verse: E kraa wɔ kufɔ nna a ba nɛ mo daana na wu mo nseŋ wora kɔnɔkoŋwule fanɛ e baŋ ba, b mɔ mo.

english_verse: They said to one another, “Look, here comes the hero of those dreams!
translation_verse: Le nɛ b daŋ kaŋɛ abar: “Men keni, edarekupo na e ya kaa ba na.

english_verse: “Don't murder him or even harm him. Just throw him into a well out here in the desert.” Reuben planned to rescue Joseph later and take him back to his father.
translation_verse: Men sa maŋ wora mo shɛŋ. Men shin nɛ an ta mo n lɛ ketirbu ere to ashi kiyi ere to nfe. Ama men sa maŋ shin nɛ an teŋi enɔ m beta mo.” E daŋ kaŋɛ loŋ nna, saŋɛ na so e beeŋ sɔ kebia na bumo be enɔ to n ya sa mo tuto.

english_verse: When Joseph came to his brothers, they pulled off his fancy coat
translation_verse: Josɛf ka ba fo mo daana na kutɔ nɛ b gbaŋ mbe piŋi tenteŋ muchɛr muchɛr nɛ e daŋ buu na

english_verse: and threw him into a dry well.
translation_verse: nseŋ ta mo n lɛ ketirbu nɛ k maŋ kɔ nchu to.

english_verse: As Joseph's brothers sat down to eat, they looked up and saw a caravan of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead. Their camels were loaded with all kinds of spices that they were taking to Egypt.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ b ya chena nɛ b ji ajibi nseŋ wu Ishmaɛlebi be eyawujipoana ko ka shi Giliad a yɔ Ijipt. Eyawujipoana na be enyɔma daŋ sulɔ tulale nɛ duwu nɛ asɔ warabi damta nna.

english_verse: When Reuben returned to the well and did not find Joseph there, he tore his clothes in sorrow.
translation_verse: Ruben ka laŋɛ m ba ketirbu na ase m ba wu fanɛ Josɛf maŋ naa wɔtɔ nɛ e kpɛa mbe asɔbuuso to ŋkpal kagbenejijaso

english_verse: Then he went back to his brothers and said, “The boy is gone! What am I going to do?”
translation_verse: nseŋ yɔ mo sipoana na kutɔ n ya bishi bumo le: “Kebia ere ka maŋ naa wɔtɔ ere, manɛ nɛ meeŋ ya kaŋɛ mo tuto?”

english_verse: Joseph's brothers killed a goat and dipped Joseph's fancy coat in its blood.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ b mɔ kaboe nseŋ ta Josɛf be piŋi tenteŋ muchɛr muchɛr na m melti m melti kumo be ŋklaŋ

english_verse: After this, they took the coat to their father and said, “We found this! Look at it carefully and see if it belongs to your son.”
translation_verse: nseŋ ta kale na n ya ŋini bumo tuto m bishi mo le: “Keni kusɔ nɛ an wu, fo kebia be piŋi na nde ŋko mannɛ kumo nna?”

english_verse: Jacob knew it was Joseph's coat and said, “It's my son's coat! Joseph has been torn to pieces and eaten by some wild animal.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ e pin kumo nseŋ kaŋɛ: “Ma kebia be piŋi nna. Kupuŋ to be kusɔbɔya lubi ko e pɛ mo na. K maŋ naa kɔ emɔrɔ fanɛ kusɔbɔya ko e kpɛa mo to n we.”

english_verse: Jacob mourned for Joseph a long time, and to show his sorrow he tore his clothes and wore sackcloth.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ e kpɛa mbe asɔbuuso to nseŋ ta kusɔbuuso ko nɛ kumo be kapɔr du sesaga fanɛ bɔtɛ m buu n ta nchɛ damta n shu mbe kebia na be keeli ga.

english_verse: All of Jacob's children came to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted. “No,” he said, “I will go to my grave, mourning for my son.” So Jacob kept on grieving.
translation_verse: Mbe bibinyɛn nɛ bibiche kikɛ daŋ wushi mo kagbene ŋ gben nɛ e yɛ: “Ayai, m maaŋ tiŋ n yige. Ma nɛ kushu ere e naaŋ yɔ ma nchaŋ to, kakpa nɛ ma kebia na wɔ na.” Kashenteŋto, e daŋ shu ga ŋkpal Josɛf so.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Midianites had sold Joseph in Egypt to a man named Potiphar, who was the king's official in charge of the palace guard.
translation_verse: Loŋ be saŋɛ malɛ nɛ Ishmaɛlebi nɛ b daŋ tɔ Josɛf na malɛ ta mo n ya fa n sa kanyɛn ko nɛ baa tre Potifa ashi Ijipt be efuli so. Potifa e daa la ewura Fɛɛro be esoji nɛ baa kuŋ mo na be enimu.

english_verse: About that time Judah left his brothers in the hill country and went to live near his friend Hirah in the town of Adullam.
translation_verse: Loŋ be jemanɛ na so nɛ Juda lar mo daana nɛ mo sipoana to n ya tu Adulam be kanyɛn ko nɛ b daa tre Haira na n chena.

english_verse: While there he met the daughter of Shua, a Canaanite man. Judah married her,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nɛ Juda daŋ wu Keenan be kanyɛn ko nɛ baa tre mo Shuwa na pibicheso nseŋ n ta mo

english_verse: and they had three sons. He named the first one Er;
translation_verse: nɛ e di kedampo n kurge ebinyɛn nɛ e nase mo ketre Ɛra.

english_verse: The third one was born when Judah was in Chezib, and she named him Shelah.
translation_verse: Onan be kaman nɛ eche na naŋ di kedampo ŋ kurge ebinyɛn n nase mo ketre Shela. Kade nɛ baa tre Kezib na nɛ Juda daa wɔ nseŋ kurge mo.

english_verse: But Er was very evil, and the Lord took his life.
translation_verse: Ama Ɛra daa la esa lubi nna ashi Enyɛnpe be anishito nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ shin nɛ wu.

english_verse: The Lord wasn't pleased with Onan and took his life too.
translation_verse: Kusɔ nɛ Onan daa wora na daa la kusɔ lubi nna Ebɔrɛ be anishito nɛ Ebɔrɛ shin nɛ mo alɛ gba wu.

english_verse: Judah did not want the same thing to happen to his son Shelah, and he told Tamar, “Go home to your father and live there as a widow until my son Shelah is grown.” So Tamar went to live with her father.
translation_verse: Onan malɛ ka wu na be kaman nɛ Juda kaŋɛ mo shache Taama le: “To, baa yɔ fo tuto pe n yaa ka la ekulpoche loŋ n ya fo saŋɛ nɛ n pibinyɛn Shela beeŋ daŋ n fo eche.” Juda daŋ kaŋɛ loŋ nna ŋkpal e ka daa lɔ kufu fanɛ nɛ Shela ta mo, mo alɛ gba beeŋ wu fanɛ kananɛ mo daana na wu n wu na. Ndoŋ nna nɛ Taama yɔ mo tuto pe n ya kaa wɔtɔ.

english_verse: Some years later Judah's wife died, and he mourned for her. He then went with his friend Hirah to the town of Timnah, where his sheep were being sheared.
translation_verse: B wɔtɔ loŋ nɛ Juda be eche nɛ e la Shuwa pibiche na ba wu. Juda ka shu mbe keeli loŋ n ya fo saŋɛ nɛ kagbene wushi mo nɛ mo nɛ mo teri Haira nɛ e shi Adulam na yɔ Timna, kakpa nɛ baa kuya mbe mbolpɔ be afuibi so na.

english_verse: Tamar found out that her father-in-law Judah was going to Timnah to shear his sheep.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ esa ko ya kaŋɛ Taama le: “Fo shanyɛn bee yɔ Timna nna nɛ e ya kuya mbe mbolpɔ be afuibi so.”

english_verse: She also realized that Shelah was now a grown man, but she had not been allowed to marry him. So she decided to dress in something other than her widow's clothes and to cover her face with a veil. After this, she sat outside the town of Enaim on the road to Timnah.
translation_verse: Taama ka nu loŋ nɛ e delge mbe kukulwu be asɔbuuso nɛ e daŋ buu na n nase nseŋ ta asɔ pɔtɛ m buu n ta shata n deŋi kumu nɛ k baa buu mbe anishiakpa so. Kumo be kaman nɛ e ya chena kade nɛ baa tre Enayim na be ekarso. E daŋ wora loŋ nna ŋkpal e kaa nyi Juda pibinyɛn Shela ka daŋ ŋ ki enyɛn nɛ bumo alɛ daa maŋ shin nɛ e ya kil mo na so.

english_verse: When Judah came along, he did not recognize her because of the veil. He thought she was a prostitute
translation_verse: Juda ka ba fo kakpa nɛ Taama tase na nseŋ wu mo nɛ e fɛ fanɛ sakaleche ko e la mo ŋkpal e ka ta shata m buu anishi so so.

english_verse: “What do you want?” he asked in return. “The ring on that cord around your neck,” was her reply. “I also want the special walking stick you have with you.” He gave them to her, they slept together, and she became pregnant.
translation_verse: Nɛ Juda malɛ bishi mo: “To, manɛ nɛ fee sha fanɛ n ta n wora tarma n sa fo n ya fo saŋɛ nɛ kaboe na beeŋ ba?” Nɛ kache na kaŋɛ mo: “Ta fo kemaŋkanibi nɛ fo ketre deŋ so nɛ fo di ere nɛ fo kekpabi nɛ fo keta ere n sa ma.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ Juda ta asɔ na n sa kache na nɛ mo nɛ mo di keche nɛ kenyɛn nɛ e luri kedampo.

english_verse: After returning home, Tamar took off the veil and dressed in her widow's clothes again.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ kache na bɛta n yɔ epe n ya deŋi shata na n nase nseŋ naŋ ta mbe ekulpoche be asɔbuuso na m mɛa to.

english_verse: Judah asked his friend Hirah take a goat to the woman, so he could get back the ring and walking stick, but she wasn't there.
translation_verse: Juda ka ya ta kaboefɔlbi na n shuŋi mo teri Haira nɛ e shi Adulam na fanɛ e ta n ya sa kache na nseŋ sɔ mbe asɔ na m ba, nɛ kache na maŋ naa wɔ kakpa nɛ b daŋ tu mo na.

english_verse: Hirah asked the people of Enaim, “Where is the prostitute who sat along the road outside your town?” “There's never been one here,” they answered.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ e bishi benyɛn mo nɛ e ya tu ndoŋ na le: “Nnɛ nɛ sakaleche nɛ e daa wɔ Enayim be ekpakar na wɔ?” Nɛ b kaŋɛ mo: “Sakaleche kama maŋ wɔ nfe.”

english_verse: Hirah went back and told Judah, “I couldn't find the woman, and the people of Enaim said no prostitute had ever been there.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ e bɛta n ya kaŋɛ Juda: “M maŋ ya wu kache na. Benyɛn nɛ b wɔ ndoŋ na malɛ gba kaŋɛ fanɛ sakaleche kama maŋ wɔ ndoŋ.”

english_verse: “If you couldn't find her, we'll just let her keep the things I gave her,” Judah answered. “And we'd better forget about the goat, or else we'll look like fools.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Juda kaŋɛ mo teri: “Shin nɛ e baa kɔ asɔ na, anyi maaŋ fin mo nɛ anyi be wulo e bugi. Ma ere wora ania nɛ ŋ ka mo kaboefɔlbi na, fo maŋ ya tu mo nna.”

english_verse: About three months later someone told Judah, “Your daughter-in-law Tamar has behaved like a prostitute, and now she's pregnant!” “Drag her out of town and burn her to death!” Judah shouted.
translation_verse: Kumo be afɔl asa be kaman nɛ esa ko ba kaŋɛ Juda le: “Fo shache Taama ji kubojua n di kedampo.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ Juda kaŋɛ: “Men ta mo n lar ekarso n chɔɔ mo edɛ m mɔ.”

english_verse: As Tamar was being dragged off, she sent someone to tell her father-in-law, “The man who gave me this ring, this cord, and this walking stick is the one who got me pregnant.”
translation_verse: B ka yaa keta mo a lar nɛ b ya chɔɔ m mɔ nɛ e ta le be kubɔya ere n shoŋi mo shanyɛn Juda: “Sɔ kemaŋkanibi nɛ kumo be efɔl ere nɛ kekpabi ere ŋ keni. Esa nɛ e di ma kedampo na be asɔ nna na.”

english_verse: “Those are mine!” Judah admitted. “She's a better person than I am, because I broke my promise to let her marry my son Shelah.” After this, Judah never slept with her again.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Juda pin asɔ na nseŋ kaŋɛ: “Alelasheŋ be kaplɛa so, kache na bɔ ma. A daŋ daga fanɛ n ta mo n sa m pibinyɛn Shela nna, ama ma alɛ maŋ wora loŋ.” Kumo be kaman Juda maŋ naŋ tu kache na n di keche nɛ kenyɛn kikɛ.

english_verse: Tamar later gave birth to twins. But before either of them was born, one of them stuck a hand out of her womb. The woman who was helping tied a red thread around the baby's hand and explained, “This one came out first.”
translation_verse: E kaa bee kekurge nɛ mbia na be eko be enɔ juŋkpar n lar nɛ esa nɛ e bee keta beche nɛ baa kurge na ta jese peper n chɛ enɔ na nseŋ kaŋɛ: “Ede e daŋ kelar na.” Ama k maŋ chɛr nɛ enɔ na naŋ bɛta n luri nɛ kebia nyɔsopo na ba choŋ n lar. Nɛ esa nɛ e bee keta beche nɛ baa kurge na kaŋɛ: “Ama kananɛ fee sha nɛ fo bugi ekpa n lar nde ŋko?”

english_verse: When the brother with the red thread was born, they named him Zerah.
translation_verse: Mo da na ka chɛ efɔl peper n shir kaman m ba lar nɛ b nase mo ketre Zera.

english_verse: So Joseph lived in the home of Potiphar, his Egyptian owner. Soon Potiphar realized that the Lord was helping Joseph to be successful in whatever he did.
translation_verse: Josɛf mo nyɛnpe Potifa ka wu fanɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na wɔ Josɛf kutɔ nsaa nɛfa kusɔ kama nɛ e bee wora na

english_verse: Potiphar liked Joseph and made him his personal assistant, putting him in charge of his house and all of his property.
translation_verse: nɛ Josɛf be asheŋ bɔlɔ mo kenishi ga. Ndoŋ nna nɛ e ta mo ŋ ki esa nɛ e bee shuŋ mbe ashuŋ nsaa keni mbe laŋ so.

english_verse: Potiphar left everything up to Joseph, and with Joseph there, the only decision he had to make was what he wanted to eat. Joseph was well-built and handsome,
translation_verse: Josɛf ka daŋ baa juŋkpar kusɔ kama ashi mbe laŋ to so, Potifa daŋ maŋ naa fɔŋ shɛŋ so ama ajibi nɛ e beeŋ ji nawule. Josɛf malɛ daŋ pɔr nɛnɛ nna a walɛ kayɛrbi.

english_verse: but he refused and said, “My master isn't worried about anything in his house, because he has placed me in charge of everything he owns.
translation_verse: Nɛ Josɛf kini nseŋ kaŋɛ kache na: “Ŋ ka bee ji kejuŋkpar laŋ ere to ere, n nyɛnpe maŋ naa fɔŋ shɛŋ so, kusɔ kama nɛ e kɔ e ta kumo nna m bɔɔ ma enɔ.

english_verse: No one in my master's house is more important than I am. The only thing he hasn't given me is you, and that's because you are his wife. I won't sin against God by doing such a terrible thing as this.”
translation_verse: Kenimu be kaplɛa so, esa kama maŋ chɔ ma laŋ ere to. N nyɛnpe maa mɔn ma shɛŋ shɛŋ laŋ ere to ama fo nawule nɛ e maŋ ta m bɔɔ ma enɔ, ŋkpal manɛ so, mbe eche e la fo. To, nɛ nuso nɛ meeŋ tiŋ n nya kagbene kpakpaso n wora le be kulubi ŋ gbiti Ebɔrɛ?”

english_verse: She kept begging Joseph day after day, but he refused to do what she wanted or even to go near her.
translation_verse: Asheŋ nɛ Josɛf daŋ malga na kikɛ daa maŋ luri kache na to, amoso saŋkikɛ e daa kaŋɛ Josɛf kesheŋ koŋwule na nna, nɛ Josɛf malɛ daa maa nu a sa mo nsaa gelge mo.

english_verse: One day, Joseph went to Potiphar's house to do his work, and none of the other servants were there.
translation_verse: Kachako nɛ Josɛf yɔ laŋ to nɛ e ya shuŋ nɛ laŋ na to be beshumpo na be ekama maŋ wɔtɔ.

english_verse: Potiphar's wife grabbed hold of his coat and said, “Make love to me!” Joseph ran out of the house, leaving his coat there in her hands.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ kache na ya pɛ Josɛf be kale to a gberge a kaŋɛ mo le: “Shin nɛ an di! Shin nɛ an di!” Ndoŋ nna nɛ Josɛf gbaŋ mbe kale n wɔtɔ kache na be enɔ to nseŋ shile n lar laŋ na to.

english_verse: she called in her servants and said, “Look! This Hebrew has come just to make fools of us. He tried to rape me, but I screamed for help.
translation_verse: nɛ e tre mbe laŋ na to be beshumpo na ŋ kaŋɛ bumo: “Men keni, ŋ kul bar Hibruw ere nna nɛ e ba tege anyi. Men keni, e ba ma ebu to nna nɛ e ba pur ma nɛ m boŋ to awɔrso ga.

english_verse: And when he heard me scream, he ran out of the house, leaving his coat with me.”
translation_verse: E ka nu kananɛ m boŋ to na nɛ e yige mbe kale n wɔtɔ ma enɔ to nseŋ shile n lar kowu.”

english_verse: But when I screamed for help, he left his coat and ran out of the house.”
translation_verse: Ama ŋ ka baŋ boŋ to n shu awɔrso nɛ e gbaŋ mbe kale n wɔtɔ ma enɔ to nseŋ shile n lar kowu.”

english_verse: and threw Joseph in the same prison where the king's prisoners were kept. While Joseph was in prison,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Josɛf mo nyɛnpe na pɛ mo n ti ebu, kaboŋ nɛ baa ti ewura Fɛɛro be basa lubi ebu na.

english_verse: the Lord helped him and was good to him. He even made the jailer like Joseph so much that
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na daa wɔ Josɛf kutɔ ashi kabuti na to gba nna a ŋini mo mbe kasha nseŋ shin nɛ Josɛf be asheŋ bee bɔlɔ kabutikenipo na kenishi.

english_verse: he put him in charge of the other prisoners and of everything that was done in the jail.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ kabutikenipo na ta basa nɛ b daa wɔ kabuti na to kikɛ nɛ kusɔ kama nyam nɛ k daa wora ndoŋ na m bɔɔ Josɛf enɔ nɛ e bee keni so.

english_verse: The jailer did not worry about anything, because the Lord was with Joseph and made him successful in all that he did.
translation_verse: Kabutikenipo na be lakal daa maŋ naa deŋ kusɔ kama nɛ Josɛf daa wora so, ŋkpal manɛ so, Enyɛnpe na daa wɔ mo kutɔ nna a nɛfa kusɔ kama nɛ k daa wɔ mbe enɔ to nɛ k bee wora nɛnɛ.

english_verse: While Joseph was in prison, both the king's personal servant and his chief cook made the king angry. So he had them thrown into the same prison with Joseph.
translation_verse: Amoso e daŋ shin nɛ b ti bumo ebu ashi kakpa nɛ Josɛf gba daa wɔ kabuti to na nna.

english_verse: They spent a long time in prison, and the official in charge of the palace guard, made Joseph their servant.
translation_verse: B ka wɔ kabuti na to na nɛ bekumpo be enimu na ta bumo m bɔɔ Josɛf enɔ nɛ e bee keni so.

english_verse: One night each of the two men had a dream, but their dreams had different meanings.
translation_verse: Kachako nɛ bumo basa anyɔ be ekama ku edare kanyɛ koŋwule na. Bumo be edareana na malɛ be kekama daa ŋini kusɔ ko nna.

english_verse: The next morning, when Joseph went to see the men, he could tell they were upset,
translation_verse: B ka ku edareana na ŋklade chipurso nɛ Josɛf wu fanɛ bumo be ŋgbene maŋ fuli bumo.

english_verse: and he asked, “Why are you so worried today?”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ e bishi bumo le: “Manɛ e ba nɛ men gbir anishito kabre loŋ?”

english_verse: “We each had a dream last night,” they answered, “and there is no one to tell us what they mean.” Joseph replied, “Doesn't God know the meaning of dreams? Now tell me what you dreamed.”
translation_verse: Nɛ b kaŋɛ mo le: “Anyi benyɔ kikɛ ku edareana nna, anyi alɛ maŋ nya esa kama nɛ e kute amo be afito n sa anyi.” Nɛ Josɛf kaŋɛ bumo: “Edareana be afito be kekute kikɛ wɔ Ebɔrɛ kutɔ nna, amoso, men kaŋɛ ma men be edareana na.”

english_verse: with three branches. As soon as it budded, it blossomed, and its grapes became ripe.
translation_verse: Epul na to nɛ k futi n sɔr asɔrso nɛ baa tre greep na nɛ a chɛ gbi gbi nseŋ daŋ m bel.

english_verse: I held the king's cup and squeezed the grapes into it, then I gave the cup to the king.”
translation_verse: Jemanɛ na so nɛ ewura Fɛɛro be kusɔnuuasɔ wɔ ma enɔ to nɛ n ya chuge egreep na n nyaŋ amo be nchu n wɔtɔ kumo to n ya sa mo.”

english_verse: Joseph said: This is the meaning of your dream. The three branches stand for three days,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Josɛf kaŋɛ mo: “Fo edare na be kifito nde. Ayabi asa na la nchɛ asa nna.

english_verse: and in three days the king will pardon you. He will make you his personal servant again, and you will serve him his wine, just as you used to do.
translation_verse: Ta a ba nchɛ asa to, Fɛɛro beeŋ lara fo kabuti ere to n shin nɛ fo naŋ ya kaa yil eyilikpa nɛ fo daa yil na a ta kusɔnuuasɔ nɛ kumo be asɔ a sa mo Fɛɛro fanɛ kananɛ fo daa wora na.

english_verse: But when these good things happen, please don't forget to tell the king about me, so I can get out of this place.
translation_verse: Ama mee kule fo nna fanɛ nɛ kusɔ kama kaŋ nyalɛ n sa fo, fo nyiŋi ma nseŋ wora ma kelela. Kaŋɛ Fɛɛro ma asheŋ n lara ma ashi kabuti ere to.

english_verse: I was kidnapped from the land of the Hebrews, and here in Egypt I haven't done anything to deserve being thrown in jail.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal manɛ so, b daŋ pɛ ma eleŋso nna ashi Hibruwebi be kasawule so m ba nfe. Ma alɛ ka ba nfe ere gba, m maŋ wora shɛŋ n daga kabuti.”

english_verse: When the chief cook saw that Joseph had given a good meaning to the dream, he told Joseph, “I also had a dream. In it I was carrying three breadbaskets stacked on top of my head.
translation_verse: Ewura Fɛɛro be bodobodo worapo nimuso na ka nu kananɛ Josɛf sa edare na be kifito nɛ k wɔ bel na nɛ e kaŋɛ Josɛf: “Ma alɛ gba ku edare nna n wu ŋ ka sulɔ bodobodo be alantaŋɛ asa ma kumu so.

english_verse: Joseph said: This is the meaning of your dream. The three baskets are three days,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Josɛf kaŋɛ mo: “Fo edare na be kifito nde. Alantaŋɛ asa na la nchɛ asa nna.

english_verse: and in three days the king will cut off your head. He will hang your body on a pole, and birds will come and peck at it.
translation_verse: Ta a ba nchɛ asa to Fɛɛro beeŋ lara fo kabuti ere to n shin nɛ b chɛ fo efɔl n shiga kedibi so m mɔ nɛ mbuibi e ba ji fo kebuni.”

english_verse: Three days later, while the king was celebrating his birthday with a dinner for his officials, he sent for his personal servant and the chief cook.
translation_verse: Edareana na be kaman be kachɛ sasopo na daa la Fɛɛro be kakurgeachɛ nna nɛ e wora kejigboŋ n sa mbe benimu kikɛ nseŋ lara asɔnuuso kenipo nimuso na nɛ bodobodo worapo nimuso na ashi kabuti to m ba benimu kikɛ be anishito.

english_verse: and had the cook put to death. Everything happened just as Joseph had said it would,
translation_verse: Ama bodobodo worapo nimuso na bre e daŋ shin nna nɛ b chɛ mo efɔl n shiga fanɛ kananɛ Josɛf daŋ kute bumo be edareana na be afito n sa bumo na.

english_verse: Suddenly, seven fat, healthy cows came up from the river and started eating grass along the bank.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ e wu ana danso ashunu nɛ b walɛ eyurto ga ka lar lɔr na to n yɔ kumo be ekarso n ya kaa ji afitiri.

english_verse: The king went back to sleep and had another dream. This time seven full heads of grain were growing on a single stalk.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e naŋ laŋɛ n di n naŋ ku edare nyɔsopo n wu ayu be amu lela lempo ashunu ko ka wɔ kuyudibi koŋwule so a daŋ.

english_verse: Later, seven other heads of grain appeared, but they were thin and scorched by a wind from the desert.
translation_verse: Le be ayu ere be kaman nɛ ayu be amu ashunu pɔsampɔsambi ko malɛ naŋ lar a du fanɛ ewule kpakpaso be epeŋi nɛ afu tushiso nɛ a shi epeŋipetekpa ka chɔ amo na

english_verse: The thin heads of grain swallowed the seven full heads. Again the king woke up, and it had only been a dream.
translation_verse: ta ayu lela lempo ashunu na m min. Kumo be kaman nɛ Fɛɛro tiŋi n wu fanɛ edare nɛ e ku.

english_verse: The next morning the king was upset. So he called in his magicians and wise men and told them what he had dreamed. None of them could tell him what the dreams meant.
translation_verse: Kare ka chɛ nɛ mbe kagbene jija mo ga nɛ e shuŋi n tre mbe efuli so be belejipoana kikɛ nɛ Ijipt be benyiashempo kikɛ m ba kaŋɛ bumo mbe edareana na, ama bumo be ekama daa maŋ tiŋ ŋ kaŋɛ mo edareana na be afito.

english_verse: The king's personal servant said: Now I remember what I was supposed to do.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Fɛɛro be asɔnuuso kenipo nimuso na kaŋɛ mo le: “Kabre nɛ n nyiŋi ŋ ka wora kusɔ ko n da so.

english_verse: When you were angry with me and your chief cook, you threw us both in jail in the house of the captain of the guard.
translation_verse: Saŋko nɛ fo ewura Fɛɛro daŋ nya agbo n wɔtɔ ma nɛ bodobodo worapo nimuso na nseŋ daŋ shin nɛ b ti anyi ebu ashi bekumpo be enimu pe na nɛ

english_verse: One night we both had dreams, and each dream had a different meaning.
translation_verse: anyi benyɔ na kikɛ daŋ ku edareana kanyɛ koŋwule nɛ amo be kekama daa kɔ kumo be kifito.

english_verse: A young Hebrew, who was a servant of the captain of the guard, was there with us at the time. When we told him our dreams, he explained what each of them meant,
translation_verse: Loŋ be saŋɛ na so nɛ anyi nɛ Hibruw be kabrantiɛbia ko nɛ e la ekumpo nimuso be kenya na daa wɔ kabuti na to. Ndoŋ nna nɛ an kaŋɛ mo anyi be edareana na nɛ e kute ŋ kute amo be afito n sa anyi. Ekama be edare nɛ kumo be kifito.

english_verse: and everything happened just as he said it would. I got my job back, and the cook was put to death.
translation_verse: Kananɛ mo alɛ daŋ baŋ kute amo n sa anyi na gbagba chap e daŋ wora. B daŋ bɛta ma nna m ba yili ma eyilikpa nseŋ daŋ chɛ emo na malɛ efɔl.”

english_verse: The king sent for Joseph, who was quickly brought out of jail. He shaved, changed his clothes, and went to the king.
translation_verse: Epul na to nɛ Fɛɛro shuŋi fanɛ b ya lara Josɛf kabuti na to m ba. Nɛ b ya bar mo manaŋ manaŋ. E daŋ she mbe kumu nna nseŋ chɛrga mbe asɔbuuso pɔɛŋ nseŋ ba Fɛɛro be anishito.

english_verse: The king said to him, “I had a dream, yet no one can explain what it means. I am told that you can interpret dreams.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Fɛɛro kaŋɛ Josɛf le: “Ŋ ku edare nna nɛ ekama pin kumo be kifito ŋ gben. Ma alɛ nu b ka kaŋɛ fanɛ fee tiŋ a kute edare be afito.”

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” Joseph answered, “I can't do it myself, but God can give a good meaning to your dreams.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Josɛf kaŋɛ mo: “Ewura Fɛɛro, ŋ gbagba maaŋ tiŋ n wora loŋ, ama Ebɔrɛ beeŋ chɛ ma to nɛ n sa fo edare na be kifito kananɛ k daga.”

english_verse: The king told Joseph: I dreamed I was standing on the bank of the Nile River.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Fɛɛro kaŋɛ Josɛf: “Ma edare na to n daa yil Nail be lɔrkar nna

english_verse: I saw seven fat, healthy cows come up out of the river, and they began feeding on the grass.
translation_verse: nseŋ wu ana danso ashunu nɛ a walɛ eyurto ka lar lɔr na to n ya kaa mur a ji afitiri kumo be ekarso.

english_verse: Next, seven skinny, bony cows came up out of the river. I have never seen such terrible looking cows anywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: Loŋ be ana na be kaman nɛ ana beeso kɔŋkrɔŋ wɔlsobi ashunu ko malɛ gba choŋ n lar lɔr na to. M maŋ naŋ wu loŋ be ana wɔlsobi kikɛ ashi Ijipt be kasawule so kikɛ.

english_verse: I also dreamed that I saw seven heads of grain growing on one stalk. The heads were full and ripe.
translation_verse: Ma edareana na to n daŋ wu ayu be amu lempo lela ashunu ko ka wɔ kuyudibi koŋwule so a daŋ.

english_verse: Then seven other heads of grain came up. They were thin and scorched by a wind from the desert.
translation_verse: Le be ayu ere be kaman nɛ ayu be amu ashunu ko malɛ naŋ lar, a du pɔsampɔsambi fanɛ ewule kpakpaso be epeŋi nɛ afu tushiso nɛ a shi epeŋipetekpa ka chɔ amo na.

english_verse: These heads of grain swallowed the full ones. I told my dreams to the magicians, but none of them could tell me the meaning of the dreams.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ayu pɔsampɔsambi na ta ayu amu lela ashunu na m min. Ŋ kute edareana ere ŋ ŋini efuli ere so be belejipo kikɛ, ama bumo be ekama maŋ tiŋ ŋ kute amo be kifito n sa ma.”

english_verse: Joseph replied: Your Majesty, both of your dreams mean the same thing, and in them God has shown what he is going to do.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Josɛf kaŋɛ Fɛɛro le: “Fo edareana na be afito la kukoŋwule nna a maŋ kɔr abar to. Ewura Fɛɛro, Ebɔrɛ lara kusɔ nɛ e bee shin nɛ e wora nna ŋ ŋini fo.

english_verse: The seven good cows stand for seven years, and so do the seven good heads of grain.
translation_verse: Ana lela ashunu na la nfɛnshunu nna nɛ ayu be amu ashunu na malɛ gba la nfɛnshunu. Amo be afito la kukoŋwule nna, a maŋ kɔr abar to.

english_verse: The seven skinny, ugly cows that came up later also stand for seven years, as do the seven bad heads of grain that were scorched by the desert wind. The dreams mean there will be seven years when there won't be enough grain.
translation_verse: Ana beeso wɔlsobi ashunu nɛ b daŋ bɛ kaman to n lar na gba la nfɛnshunu nna nɛ ayumu pɔsampɔsambi ashunu nɛ a du fanɛ ewule kpakpaso be epeŋi nɛ afu tushiso nɛ a shi epeŋipetekpa ka chɔ amo na malɛ gba la nfɛnshunu. Loŋ be nfɛnshunu na la nfɛ nɛ akoŋgboŋ beeŋ tɔr nna.

english_verse: It is just as I said—God has shown what he intends to do.
translation_verse: Ewura Fɛɛro, kumo nɛ n teŋ kaŋɛ fo na fanɛ kusɔ nɛ Ebɔrɛ bee shin nɛ e wora nɛ e lara ŋ ŋini fo na.

english_verse: For seven years Egypt will have more than enough grain,
translation_verse: Adɔjibi beeŋ wora ga ashi Ijipt be kasawule ere kikɛ so nfɛnshunu,

english_verse: The famine will be so bad that no one will remember that once there had been plenty.
translation_verse: Baaŋ teŋ kanya damta na so, ŋkpal manɛ so, akoŋ nɛ k beeŋ bɛ loŋ be saŋɛ na so be tɔrɔ maaŋ ba kaa walɛ kuraa.

english_verse: God has given you two dreams to let you know that he has definitely decided to do this and that he will do it soon.
translation_verse: Ewura Fɛɛro, kusɔ nɛ k ba nɛ edare anyɔ na duli abar m ba fo kutɔ na e la fanɛ Ebɔrɛ yili kumo nna fanɛ abaanaaworasheŋ, e beeŋ wora kumo. K maaŋ chɛr gba.

english_verse: Your Majesty, you should find someone who is wise and will know what to do, so that you can put him in charge of all Egypt.
translation_verse: To, amoso, naniere a daga fanɛ fo fin esa nɛ e nyi asheŋ nsaa tiŋ a wora kusɔ nɛ k daga saŋkikɛ n shin nɛ e baa keni Ijipt be efuli ere be asheŋ so.

english_verse: Give them the power to collect the grain during those good years and to store it in your cities.
translation_verse: A daga fanɛ fo shin nɛ loŋ be basa na e chala ajibi nɛ baaŋ sɔ nfɛ lela ashunu na kikɛ n yili nɛ fo enɔ e baa deŋ amoso a jo saŋɛ lubi na.

english_verse: It can be stored until it is needed during the seven years when there won't be enough grain in Egypt. This will keep the country from being destroyed because of the lack of food. Joseph Is Made Governor over Egypt
translation_verse: A daga fanɛ loŋ be ajibi na e baa la efuli ere peya a dese a jo nfɛnshunu lubi be akoŋ be jemanɛ nɛ k beeŋ ba na, saŋɛ na so akoŋ na maaŋ mur efuli ere so ebi.”

english_verse: The king and his officials liked this plan.
translation_verse: Kusɔ nɛ Josɛf kaŋɛ na daŋ par Fɛɛro nɛ mbe benimu kikɛ.

english_verse: So the king said to them, “Who could possibly handle this better than Joseph? After all, the Spirit of God is with him.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Fɛɛro bishi mbe benimu na: “Anyeeŋ naŋ tiŋ n nya esa ko n naŋ baŋ kanyɛn nɛ Ebɔrɛ be kiyoyu wɔ mo to ere so a?”

english_verse: The king told Joseph, “God is the one who has shown you these things. No one else is as wise as you are or knows as much as you do.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Fɛɛro kaŋɛ Josɛf: “Ebɔrɛ ka baŋ lara le be asheŋ ere kikɛ ŋ ŋini fo ere, esa kama maŋ naa wɔtɔ a pin asheŋ to nsaa nyi asheŋ fanɛ fo.”

english_verse: Then the king took off his royal ring and put it on Joseph's finger. He gave him fine clothes to wear and placed a gold chain around his neck.
translation_verse: Fɛɛro ka kaŋɛ loŋ na be kaman nɛ e lara mbe kuwurji be eleŋ be kepinibi mbe keshilbi to n ta n wɔtɔ Josɛf peya to. Kumo be kaman nɛ e shin nɛ b ta asɔbuuso lela ko m buu mo nseŋ ta shuwa be gbelge n di mo.

english_verse: The king told Joseph, “Although I'm king, no one in Egypt is to do anything without your permission.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Fɛɛro kaŋɛ Josɛf: “Ma e la ewura Fɛɛro, ama esa kama maaŋ tiŋ n wora shɛŋ Ijipt be efuli so nɛ fo maŋ sa mo ekpa fanɛ e wora loŋ.”

english_verse: He gave Joseph the Egyptian name Zaphenath Paneah. And he let him marry Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera, a priest in the city of Heliopolis. Joseph traveled all over Egypt.
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ Fɛɛro sa Josɛf ketre Zafenat Panea nseŋ ta On be kegbirwura Potifera pibiche nɛ baa tre Asenat na n sa mo fanɛ e baa la mbe eche. Josɛf ka nya loŋ be eyilikpa na nɛ e fara a nite Ijipt be efuli na kikɛ so.

english_verse: For seven years there were big harvests of grain.
translation_verse: Nfɛnshunu lela na to kasawule na kikɛ daŋ wora ajibi nna ga

english_verse: In fact, there was so much grain that they stopped keeping record, because it was like counting the grains of sand along the beach.
translation_verse: Ajibi na be keshi na daŋ ba wora kebanso ga nna nɛ e gben n yige amo be kekarga, ŋkpal manɛ so, esa daa maaŋ naŋ tiŋ ŋ karga amo.

english_verse: Their first son was named Manasseh, which means, “God has let me forget all my troubles and my family back home.”
translation_verse: Josɛf daŋ nase mbe wurkoŋ ketre Manase nseŋ kaŋɛ: “N nase mo loŋ nna, ŋkpal manɛ so, Ebɔrɛ shin nɛ n teŋ ma tɔrɔ kikɛ so nseŋ naŋ teŋ n tuto be kowu to ebi be asheŋ so.”

english_verse: Egypt's seven years of plenty came to an end,
translation_verse: B wɔtɔ loŋ nɛ Ijipt be kanya damta be nfɛnshunu na be jemanɛ ba choŋ

english_verse: and the seven years of famine began, just as Joseph had said. There was not enough food in other countries, but all over Egypt there was plenty.
translation_verse: nɛ nfɛnshunu be akoŋ be jemanɛ na malɛ ba fara fanɛ kananɛ Josɛf daŋ kaŋɛ na. Efuli kama so akoŋ na daŋ tɔr nna, ama Ijipt bre be kasawule so kikɛ ajibi daa wɔtɔ nna.

english_verse: When the famine finally struck Egypt, the people asked the king for food, but he said, “Go to Joseph and do what he tells you to do.”
translation_verse: Akoŋ na ka ba koso Ijipt be efuli so kikɛ nɛ efuli na so ebi kikɛ fara a shu a ŋini ewura Fɛɛro a fin ajibi. Nɛ Fɛɛro malɛ kaŋɛ Ijiptebi na kikɛ le: “Men baa yɔ Josɛf kutɔ n ya kaa wora kusɔ kama nɛ e yili menyi.”

english_verse: People from all over the world came to Egypt to buy grain, because the famine was so severe in their countries.
translation_verse: Basa daa shi efuli kama so nna gba a ba Josɛf kutɔ m ba kaa tɔ ayu, ŋkpal manɛ so, akoŋ na daa shi ga nna ashi kaplɛkama.

english_verse: When Jacob found out there was grain in Egypt, he said to his sons, “Why are you just sitting here, staring at one another?
translation_verse: Jeekɔb ka nu fanɛ ajibi wɔ Ijipt be efuli so nɛ e bishi mbe bibinyɛn na le: “Manɛ nna nɛ men tase a maa wora shɛŋ?

english_verse: I have heard there is grain in Egypt. Go down and buy some, so we won't starve to death.”
translation_verse: N nu fanɛ ajibi wɔ Ijipt, amoso men yɔ ndoŋ n ya tɔ ako m ba, saŋɛ na so akoŋ maaŋ mɔ anyi.”

english_verse: Ten of Joseph's brothers went to Egypt to buy grain.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Josɛf mo daana kudu yɔ Ijipt nɛ b ya tɔ ajibi na.

english_verse: But Jacob did not send Joseph's younger brother Benjamin with them; he was afraid that something might happen to him.
translation_verse: Ama Jeekɔb daa maŋ shin nɛ Josɛf mo sipo Bɛnjamin bre tu bumo n yɔ, ŋkpal e kaa daa lɔ kufu fanɛ Bɛnjamin beeŋ ya ji awurfoŋ so.

english_verse: Since Joseph was governor of Egypt and in charge of selling grain, his brothers came to him and bowed with their faces to the ground.
translation_verse: To, jemanɛ na so malɛ nɛ Josɛf e daa la Ijipt be kasawule na so be gomena. Mo e daa fa ajibi na a sa kasawule na so ebi kikɛ. Amoso mo daana na ka fo Ijipt, b daŋ jɔŋɛ mo ase nna ŋ kurgi amu n yuu to bunyanso.

english_verse: “No sir,” they replied. “We're your servants, and we have only come to buy grain.
translation_verse: Nɛ b kaŋɛ mo: “Ayai, enyɛnpe, mannɛ aloŋ nna. Fo anya ba nna nɛ an ba tɔ ajibi.

english_verse: “That isn't so!” Joseph insisted. “You've come here to find out where our country is weak.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Josɛf kaŋɛ bumo: “Ayai, mannɛ aloŋ nna, men ba nna nɛ men ba dara m pin efuli ere so be kakpa nɛ bekumpo maŋ wɔ.”

english_verse: But they explained, “Sir, we come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and one of our brothers is dead.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ b kaŋɛ mo: “Anyi, fo anya daa la enyɛn koŋwule be bibinyɛn kuduanyɔ nna. Ekoŋwule maŋ naa wɔtɔ nɛ kaluge na malɛ wɔ an tuto kutɔ.”

english_verse: and I'm going to find out the truth. I swear by the life of the king that you won't leave this place until your youngest brother comes here.
translation_verse: Kananɛ anyi alɛ beeŋ wora m pin fanɛ kashenteŋ nɛ menyee ji nde: M bɔ ewura Fɛɛro be kuwurputi nɛ e tase so ere fanɛ men maaŋ lar nfe ama men be kaluge na baŋ ba nfe nna pɔɛŋ.

english_verse: Choose one of you to go after your brother, while the rest of you stay here in jail. That will show whether you are telling the truth. But if you are lying, I swear by the life of the king that you are spies!
translation_verse: Amoso men shuŋi menyi to be eko nɛ e ya bar men sipobi na, ama baaŋ ti menyi nɛ men ka na ebu, saŋɛ na so anyeeŋ bɔla men gbagba be mmalga so ŋ keni, kashenteŋ nɛ menyee ji ere a? Nɛ k kaŋ ba fanɛ mannɛ kashenteŋ nɛ menyee ji, kumo ere m bɔ ewura Fɛɛro be kuwurputi fanɛ men ba nna nɛ men ba dara anyi be efuli nna.”

english_verse: before saying to them: Since I respect God, I'll give you a chance to save your lives.
translation_verse: Kumo be kachɛ sasopo nɛ Josɛf kaŋɛ bumo le: “Mee ŋana Ebɔrɛ nna, amoso men wora kesheŋ nɛ mee shin nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ menyi ere nseŋ nya men be amu.

english_verse: If you are honest men, one of you must stay here in jail, and the rest of you can take the grain back to your starving families.
translation_verse: Nɛ men baa la beshenteŋjipo bre men shin nɛ menyi to be ekoŋwule e shir a wɔ kabuti ere to nfe nɛ bumo nɛ b ka na e ta ajibi m bɛta n ya sa men be kowu to ebi nɛ akoŋ bee mɔ na.

english_verse: But you must bring your youngest brother to me. Then I'll know that you are telling the truth, and you won't be put to death. Joseph's brothers agreed
translation_verse: Ama men keta men sipobi na m bar ma nfe nɛ n yili men gbagba be mmalga so m pin fanɛ kashenteŋ nɛ menyee ji, saŋɛ na so, men maaŋ wu.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ b shuli fanɛ baaŋ wora loŋ

english_verse: and said to one another, “We're being punished because of Joseph. We saw the trouble he was in, but we refused to help him when he begged us. That's why these terrible things are happening.”
translation_verse: nseŋ kaŋɛ abar le: “K baŋ fuli nna fanɛ kusɔ nɛ an daŋ wora an sipo Josɛf na so so nɛ anyee nya le be kasogberge ere na. An daŋ wu kananɛ mbe kagbene kikɛ daŋ jija mo nɛ e daa yila kenishito fanɛ an wu mo kuwɔr nɛ an kini kenu. Kumo so nɛ le be kagbenejija ere ba anyi alɛ gba so na.”

english_verse: Reuben spoke up, “Didn't I tell you not to harm the boy? But you wouldn't listen, and now we have to pay the price for killing him.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Ruben bishi bumo: “N daa maŋ kaŋɛ menyi fanɛ men sa maŋ wora kebinyɛnbi na shɛŋ nɛ men kini kenu n sa ma? To, naniere kusɔ nɛ an wora mo na be kuwule e naa bishi anyi na.”

english_verse: They did not know that Joseph could understand them, since he was speaking through an interpreter.
translation_verse: B daa maŋ nyi fanɛ Josɛf daa nu bumo be mmalga na, ŋkpal manɛ so, esa ko e daa sɔ mo so a kilgi mmalga na a sa bumo.

english_verse: Joseph turned away from them and cried, but soon he turned back and spoke to them again. Then he had Simeon tied up and taken away while they watched. Joseph's Brothers Return to Canaan
translation_verse: B kaa bee malga na nɛ Josɛf pal kaman n sa bumo n shu ga. Kumo be kaman nɛ e naŋ kilgi m malga bumo kutɔ. E daŋ shin nna nɛ b lara Simiɔn ŋ kre mo bumo kikɛ be anishito.

english_verse: Joseph gave orders for his brothers' grain sacks to be filled with grain and for their money to be put in their sacks. He also gave orders for them to be given food for their journey home. After this was done,
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Josɛf shin nɛ b jɔ ayu m bɔlɔ m bɔla bumo be ebɔtɛ na nseŋ shin nɛ b ta ekama be amansherbi m bɛta n wɔtɔ mbe bɔtɛ to nseŋ shin nɛ b sa bumo ekpa to be kusɔ jiso n ti so. B ka wora asheŋ ere kikɛ n sa bumo n loge na

english_verse: When they stopped for the night, one of them opened his sack to get some grain for his donkey, and at once he saw his moneybag.
translation_verse: B ka ya fo kakpa nɛ baaŋ suge n di ŋklade na nɛ bumo be eko bugi mbe bɔtɛ nɛ e jɔ ajibi n sa mbe kurma nseŋ wu mbe amansherbi ashi mbe bɔtɛ be kɔnɔ to.
