english_verse: “Here's my money!” he told his brothers. “Right here in my sack.” They were trembling with fear as they stared at one another and asked themselves, “What has God done to us?”
translation_verse: Nɛ e kaŋɛ mo niopibiana na: “B bɛta ma amansherbi nna n wɔtɔ ma bɔtɛ to. Keni, amo e wɔ kumo to na.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ bumo be ŋgbene jija bumo nɛ b kilgi ŋ keni ŋ keni abar a chicha nseŋ bishi abar le: “Manɛ be kesheŋ nɛ Ebɔrɛ wora anyi loŋ?”

english_verse: When they returned to the land of Canaan, they told their father Jacob everything that had happened to them:
translation_verse: B ka ba bumo tuto Jeekɔb nɛ e daa wɔ Keenan na kutɔ nɛ b kaŋɛ mo asheŋ nɛ a daŋ ya tu bumo na kikɛ nyam.

english_verse: But we told him, “We're honest men, not spies.
translation_verse: Ama le nɛ an daŋ kaŋɛ mo: ‘An la beshenteŋjipo nna, anyi maŋ la efuli be bedarapo.’

english_verse: We come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and the other is dead.”
translation_verse: An kaŋɛ mo fanɛ an la esa koŋwule be bibinyɛn kuduanyɔ nna nɛ ekoŋwule maŋ naa wɔtɔ nɛ kaluge na malɛ wɔ an tuto kutɔ ashi Keenan.

english_verse: Then the governor of Egypt told us, “I'll find out if you really are honest. Leave one of your brothers here with me, while you take the grain to your starving families.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ kanyɛn nɛ e la efuli na so be gomena na kaŋɛ anyi le: ‘Kananɛ meeŋ wora m pin fanɛ men la beshenteŋjipo nde: Men yige men niopibi ko ŋ kutɔ nfe nseŋ ta ajibi n ya sa men be basa nɛ b wɔ epe nɛ akoŋ kɔ bumo a mɔ na.

english_verse: But bring your youngest brother to me, so I can be certain that you are honest men and not spies. After that, I'll let your other brother go free, and you can stay here and trade.”
translation_verse: Ama men keta men be kaluge na m ba ŋini ma, saŋɛ na so meeŋ pin men ka la beshenteŋjipo ŋkaa maŋ la bedarapo. Aloŋ nɛ meeŋ bɛta men niopibi ere n sa menyi nɛ men tiŋ n nya ekpa a ji yawu kasawule ere so.’ ”

english_verse: When the brothers started emptying their sacks of grain, they found their moneybags in them. They were frightened, and so was their father Jacob,
translation_verse: B ka ya kaa chulgi ayu na ashi bumo be ebɔtɛana na to nɛ ekama wu mbe amansherbi ka wɔ amo be lɔkɔ to ashi mbe bɔtɛ to! Bumo nɛ bumo tuto ka wu bumo be amansherbiana na nɛ kufu pɛ bumo ga.

english_verse: who said, “You have already taken my sons Joseph and Simeon from me. And now you want to take away Benjamin! Everything is against me.”
translation_verse: Nɛ bumo tuto Jeekɔb kaŋɛ bumo le: “Men shin nɛ m paŋ ma mbia. Josɛf maŋ naa wɔtɔ, Simiɔn gba maŋ naa wɔtɔ nɛ men naa sha keta Bɛnjamin malɛ ere, kumo ere menyeeŋ ta tɔrɔ ŋ deŋ ma so pasaa!”

english_verse: Reuben spoke up, “Father, if I don't bring Benjamin back, you can kill both of my sons. Trust me with him, and I'll bring him back.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ruben kaŋɛ mo tuto le: “Ta Bɛnjamin m bɔɔ ma enɔ, meeŋ ya bɛta mo m ba. Nɛ m maŋ ya bɛta mo m bar fo, fo mɔ ma bibinyɛn anyɔ.”

english_verse: But Jacob said, “I won't let my son Benjamin go down to Egypt with the rest of you. His brother is already dead, and he is the only son I have left. I am an old man, and if anything happens to him on the way, I'll die from sorrow, and all of you will be to blame.”
translation_verse: Ama le nɛ Jeekɔb daŋ kaŋɛ: “Ayai, ma kebia ere maaŋ tu menyi n yɔ ndoŋ. Mo da wu, mo nawule e baŋ ka na. Nɛ menyee yɔ nɛ tɔrɔ ko ya tu mo enite na to, menyeeŋ shin nɛ kagbenejija e mɔ ma ashi ma mbel to.”

english_verse: until finally, Jacob's family had eaten all the grain they had bought in Egypt. So Jacob said to his sons, “Go back and buy some more grain.”
translation_verse: Saŋɛ na so nɛ Jeekɔb nɛ mbe basa malɛ ji bumo be ajibi nɛ b daŋ ya tɔ Ijipt na n loge nɛ mbia na bumo tuto Jeekɔb kaŋɛ bumo: “Men naŋ bɛta n yɔ Ijipt n naŋ ya tɔ ajibi gbrɛbi m ba.”

english_verse: Judah replied, “The governor strictly warned us that we would not be allowed to see him unless we brought our youngest brother with us. If you let us take Benjamin along, we will go and buy grain. But we won't go without him!”
translation_verse: Ama nɛ fo maaŋ shuli n wora loŋ bre, anyi maaŋ yɔ ŋkpal kanyɛn na ka kaŋɛ anyi fanɛ: ‘Men naŋ ba nfe ŋkaa maŋ bar men sipo na, men sa maŋ shin nɛ n wu menyi so so.’ ”

english_verse: Jacob asked, “Why did you cause me so much trouble by telling the governor you had another brother?”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Jeekɔb bishi bumo: “Manɛ bre e ba nɛ men kaŋɛ kanyɛn nna fanɛ men kraa kɔ esipo n ta le be tɔrɔ ere a ba ma so?”

english_verse: They answered, “He asked a lot of questions about us and our family. He wanted to know if you were still alive and if we had any more brothers. All we could do was answer his questions. How could we know he would tell us to bring along our brother?”
translation_verse: Nɛ b kaŋɛ mo: “Kanyɛn na gbagba e lege anyi to m bishi anyi, anyi gbagba nɛ anyi be kanaŋ to ebi be asheŋ. E yɛ: ‘Men tuto kraa wɔtɔ a? Men kraa kɔ esipo nyɛnso a?’ Amoso mo ere be asheŋ bishiso na be afito nɛ anyi ere daŋ baa sa. Kumo be kaman nuso nɛ an daa wora a pin fanɛ e beeŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ: ‘Men naa ba, men keta men sipo na a ba?’ ”

english_verse: Then Judah said to his father, “Let Benjamin go with me, and we will leave at once, so that none of us will starve to death.
translation_verse: Kamalga ere be kaman nɛ Juda kaŋɛ mo tuto Jeekɔb: “Ta kebia na m bɔɔ na enɔ nɛ an yɔ epul ere to, saŋɛ na so anyi nɛ fo nɛ anyi be mbia beeŋ baa wɔtɔ ŋkaa maaŋ wu.

english_verse: I promise to bring him back safely, and if I don't, you can blame me as long as I live.
translation_verse: Ma ere beeŋ keni mo so nɛ shɛŋ maaŋ wora mo. Nɛ kusɔ kama wora mo nɛ m maŋ tiŋ m bar mo nfe m ba sa fo, meeŋ sɔ kumo be turju ma ŋkpa to kikɛ mbaanaayɔ.

english_verse: If we had not wasted all this time, we could already have been there and back twice.”
translation_verse: Keni, nɛ an daa maŋ jija saŋɛ nna m ba fo mbre, n dafanɛ an yɔ ndoŋ m bɛta m ba ale anyɔ gba.”

english_verse: Their father said: If Benjamin must go with you, take the governor a gift of some of the best things from our own country, such as perfume, honey, spices, pistachio nuts, and almonds.
translation_verse: Nɛ bumo tuto Jeekɔb kaŋɛ bumo: “To, nɛ k nya a du loŋ bre, men bela ase n ta kasawule ere so be asɔrso lelaana ko n wɔtɔ men be adiiku to n ya sa kanyɛn na. Men ta tulale nɛ duwu nɛ asɔ warabi nɛ mushoŋ gbrɛ ya sa mo.

english_verse: Also take along twice the amount of money for the grain, because there must have been some mistake when the money was put back in your sacks.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman, men ta amansherbi ko n naŋ ti amo nɛ men daŋ wu men be ebɔtɛ to na so n yɔ, ŋkpal manɛ so, shere b wora nna n foe.

english_verse: Take Benjamin with you and leave at once.
translation_verse: Men ta men sipo gba n ti so n yɔ naniere.

english_verse: When you go in to see the governor, I pray that God All-Powerful will be good to you and that the governor will let your other brother and Benjamin come back home with you. But if I must lose my children, I suppose I must.
translation_verse: Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na malɛ e ya shin nɛ kanyɛn na e wu menyi kuwɔr n shin nɛ men da nɛ e ka ndoŋ na nɛ Bɛnjamin e tu menyi m ba. Nɛ k ba fanɛ meeŋ paŋ ma mbia gba nna meeŋ paŋ bumo nna.”

english_verse: he saw Benjamin and told the servant in charge of his house, “Take these men to my house. Slaughter an animal and cook it, so they can eat with me at noon.”
translation_verse: Josɛf ka wu Bɛnjamin nɛ mo daana na nɛ e kaŋɛ mbe laŋ to be nyɛrbi be enimu le: “Keta basa ere n yɔ ma pe n ya mɔ kusɔbɔya n wora ajibi nɛ ma nɛ bumo e ji kapa ere.”

english_verse: The servant did as he was told and took the brothers to Joseph's house.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ nyɛrbi be enimu na keta bumo n yɔ Josɛf pe fanɛ kananɛ e kaŋɛ mo na.

english_verse: But on the way they got worried and started thinking, “We are being taken there because of the money that was put back in our sacks last time. He will arrest us, make us his slaves, and take our donkeys.”
translation_verse: B ka fo Josɛf pe na, kufu daŋ pɛ bumo nna, ŋkpal manɛ so, b daa fɛ nna fanɛ amansherbi nɛ b daŋ bɛta n wɔtɔ bumo be ebɔtɛ to saŋɛ nɛ b fara m ba ndoŋ na so nɛ b bar bumo laŋ na to. B daa fɛ fanɛ e beeŋ pɛ bumo ŋ ki mbe anya nseŋ suge bumo be ekurma nna.

english_verse: So when they arrived at Joseph's house, they said to the servant in charge,
translation_verse: Ŋkpal le be nfɛra ere so, b ka fo Josɛf be laŋ to nɛ b kaŋɛ mbe nyɛrbi be enimu na le:

english_verse: “Sir, we came to Egypt once before to buy grain.
translation_verse: “Ebunyampo, an daŋ keba nfe nna m ba tɔ ajibi.

english_verse: together with enough money to buy more grain. We don't know who put the money in our sacks.”
translation_verse: Amo alɛ be buushi, an naŋ bar amansherbi ko nɛ an naŋ ba tɔ ajibi. Ama hale mbre anyi maŋ nyi esa nɛ e ta amansherbi na n wɔtɔ anyi be ebɔtɛ na to.”

english_verse: The servant took them into Joseph's house and gave them water to wash their feet. He also tended their donkeys.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ kayɛrbi nimuso na keta bumo n luri Josɛf be kowu to n ya sa bumo nchu nɛ b fɔr bumo be aya so nseŋ sa bumo be ekurma ajibi.

english_verse: The brothers got their gifts ready to give to Joseph at noon, since they had heard they were going to eat there.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Jeekɔb be mbia na lara bumo be ŋkɛ mo nɛ b bar Josɛf na n yili a jo mo, ŋkpal manɛ so, b daŋ nu fanɛ bumo nɛ mo e naa shin nɛ b ji kapaso be ajibi kamɔnchɛ na.

english_verse: When Joseph came home, they gave him the gifts they had brought, and they bowed down to him.
translation_verse: Josɛf ka ba epe nɛ b jɔŋɛ mo ase bunyanso nseŋ ta bumo be ŋkɛ nɛ b bar mo na n sa mo.

english_verse: After Joseph had asked how they were, he said, “What about your elderly father? Is he still alive?”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ e chɔrɔ bumo nseŋ bishi bumo kananɛ kebaawɔtɔ du n sa bumo nɛ kananɛ bumo tuto du. E yɛ: “Men tuto kraa wɔtɔ a?”

english_verse: They answered, “Your servant our father is still alive and well.” And again they bowed down to Joseph.
translation_verse: Nɛ b naŋ jɔŋɛ mo ase nseŋ shuli ŋ kaŋɛ: “Mm, an tuto fo kenya kraa wɔtɔ a kɔ alenfia.”

english_verse: When Joseph looked around and saw his brother Benjamin, he said, “This must be your youngest brother, the one you told me about. God bless you, my son.”
translation_verse: E ka maŋ kumu so ŋ keni n wu mo sipo Bɛnjamin nɛ e la mo nio pibi gbagba na nɛ e bishi bumo: “Men sipobi nɛ men kaŋɛ ma mbe asheŋ na nde a?” Kumo be kaman nɛ e kaŋɛ: “M pibi, Ebɔrɛ e nɛfa fo.”

english_verse: After washing his face and returning, he was able to control himself and said, “Serve the meal!”
translation_verse: E ka shu n loge nseŋ fɔr mbe anishito nɛ e lar a wora ania a pɛ mbe kumu nseŋ kaŋɛ mbe nyɛrbi fanɛ b chige ajibi na to.

english_verse: Joseph was served at a table by himself, and his brothers were served at another. The Egyptians sat at yet another table, because Egyptians felt it was disgusting to eat with Hebrews.
translation_verse: B daŋ ta Josɛf be ajibi nna n yili mo kakpa ko nseŋ ta mo daana na malɛ n chena kakpa ko nseŋ ta Ijipt be basa nɛ b daa wɔ ndoŋ na peya n yili kakpa ko. B daŋ wora loŋ nna, ŋkpal manɛ so, k daa la ekishi nna fanɛ Ijipt be esa e tu Hibruw be esa n chena a ji.

english_verse: To the surprise of Joseph's brothers, they were seated in front of him according to their ages, from the oldest to the youngest.
translation_verse: B daŋ shin nna nɛ Josɛf mo daana na chena n chena m bɛ abar so kenimu kenimuso loŋ n ya fo bumo be ekekarso. Nɛ kumo be loŋ chinchiŋ bumo nɛ b keni ŋ keni abar.

english_verse: They were served food from Joseph's table, and Benjamin was given five times as much as each of the others. So Joseph's brothers ate and drank with him and had a good time.
translation_verse: Josɛf be echenakpa na nɛ b daŋ yili n chige ajibi na n sa bumo. Bɛnjamin malɛ peya daa chɔ ekama peya ale anu. Ama bumo kikɛ daŋ ji kejigboŋ nna nseŋ tu Josɛf n nuu asɔnuuso yɛlyɛla so.

english_verse: Later, Joseph told the servant in charge of his house, “Fill the men's grain sacks with as much as they can hold and put their money in the sacks. Also put my silver cup in the sack of the youngest brother.” The servant did as he was told.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ fo ta ma gbiti be kusɔ nuunchu na n ti mbe ayu be amansherbi so n wɔtɔ bumo be kaluge na be bɔtɛ to.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ kayɛrbi nimuso na wora asɔ nɛ Josɛf kaŋɛ fanɛ e wora na kikɛ.

english_verse: Early the next morning, the men were sent on their way with their donkeys.
translation_verse: Kumo be ŋklade, kaboŋ ka bee kpaŋɛ to nɛ Josɛf mo daana nɛ bumo be ekurma pɛ epe be ekpa.

english_verse: But they had not gone far from the city when Joseph told the servant, “Go after those men! When you catch them, say, ‘My master has been good to you. So why have you stolen his silver cup?
translation_verse: B ka lar kade na to b daa maŋ naŋ fo kufɔ nɛ Josɛf kaŋɛ mbe kayɛrbi nimuso le: “Ju m bɛ basa na so epul ere to. Nɛ fo ya tu bumo fo bishi bumo le: ‘Manɛ e ba nɛ menyee ta kulubi a ka kelela be kukɔ?

english_verse: Not only does he drink from his cup, but he also uses it to learn about the future. You have done a terrible thing.’ ”
translation_verse: Manɛ e ba nɛ men yuri n nyɛnpe be gbiti be kusɔnuunchu? To, kumo nɛ e kɔ a nuu asɔ nseŋ naa kɔ kumo a bishi so. Kusɔ nɛ men wora ere maŋ walɛ kuraa!’ ”

english_verse: When the servant caught up with them, he said exactly what Joseph had told him to say.
translation_verse: Kayɛrbi na ka ya tu bumo nɛ e ta asheŋ nɛ mo nyɛnpe kaŋɛ na kikɛ chap ŋ kaŋɛ bumo.

english_verse: But they replied, “Sir, why do you say such things? We would never do anything like that!
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ b bishi mo le: “Manɛ e ba nɛ fo, an nyɛnpe bee malga le ere? Kaarɛ gba nɛ anyi, fo anya e wora loŋ!

english_verse: We even returned the money we found in our grain sacks when we got back to Canaan. So why would we want to steal any silver or gold from your master's house?
translation_verse: An ka daŋ ya wu amansherbi anyi be ebɔtɛ be nnɔ to gba an daŋ shi Keenan m bɛta amo m ba. Nɛ manɛ so nɛ anyee yuri fo nyɛnpe be gbiti ŋko mbe shuwa ashi mo pe?

english_verse: If you find that one of us has the cup, then kill him, and the rest of us will become your slaves.”
translation_verse: Nɛ fo kaŋ keni n wu kumo anyi be ekama be bɔtɛ to, amodoŋwura na beeŋ wu nɛ bumo nɛ b ka na malɛ kikɛ e ki fo enyɛnpe na be anya.”

english_verse: “Good!” the man replied, “I'll do what you have said. But only the one who has the cup will become my slave. The rest of you can go free.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Josɛf be kayɛrbi na kaŋɛ bumo: “To, n shuli, anyeeŋ wora kusɔ nɛ men kaŋɛ ere. Ekama nɛ k wɔ mo kutɔ beeŋ ki ma kenya nɛ bumo nɛ b ka na bre e baa wɔ bumo be amu.”

english_verse: Each of the brothers quickly put his sack on the ground and opened it.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ bumo be ekama nya manaŋ n suge mbe bɔtɛ n yili m bugi kumo so.

english_verse: Joseph's servant started searching the sacks, beginning with the one that belonged to the oldest brother. When he came to Benjamin's sack, he found the cup.
translation_verse: Nɛ Josɛf be kayɛrbi na fara a keni bumo be asɔ na to. Bumo kikɛ be enimuso peya to nɛ e fara ŋ keni kebɛso, kebɛso loŋ n ya fo bumo kikɛ to be kebia peya. E keni to loŋ n ya wu gbiti be kusɔnuunchu na Bɛnjamin be bɔtɛ to.

english_verse: This upset the brothers so much that they began tearing their clothes in sorrow. Then they loaded their donkeys and returned to the city.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ b kpɛa bumo be asɔbuusoana to ŋkpal kagbenejijaso nseŋ naŋ bɛta ŋ kre bumo be esulɔana n deŋi bumo be ekurma so m bɛta n yɔ kade na to.

english_verse: When Judah and his brothers got there, Joseph was still at home. So they bowed down to Joseph,
translation_verse: Josɛf daa maŋ naŋ lar epe nɛ Juda nɛ mo sipoana na ba m ba dese kekil mbe anishito.

english_verse: “Sir, what can we say?” Judah replied. “How can we say we are innocent, when God has shown we are guilty? And now all of us are your slaves, especially the one who had the cup.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Juda kaŋɛ: “To, naniere, manɛ nɛ an naa kɔ nɛ an kaŋɛ fo, an nyɛnpe? Manɛ nɛ anyeeŋ naŋ tiŋ ŋ kaŋɛ ŋko manɛ nɛ anyeeŋ naŋ tiŋ n wora ŋ ŋini fanɛ anyi maŋ tɔr kapɔŋ? Ebɔrɛ shin nɛ fo anya be alubi di efuli, amoso naniere an ki fo anya, anyi nɛ emo nɛ b wu kusɔnuunchu na mbe kusɔ to na kikɛ.”

english_verse: Joseph told them, “I would never punish all of you. Only the one who was caught with the cup will become my slave. The rest of you are free to go home to your father.” Judah Pleads for Benjamin
translation_verse: Nɛ Josɛf kaŋɛ: “Cha, kaarɛ gba nɛ n wora loŋ. Esa nɛ b wu ma kusɔnuunchu na nawule e naaŋ ki ma kenya. Menyi nɛ men ka na e bɛta a yɔ epe men tuto kutɔ nɛ kagbenewushi.”

english_verse: Judah went over to Joseph and said: Sir, you have as much power as the king himself, and I am only your slave. Please don't get angry if I speak.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Juda yɔ mo kutɔ n ya kaŋɛ mo: “N nyɛnpe jande, shin nɛ fo kenya e malga kamalgabi ko n sa fo, n nyɛnpe. N nyi fo nɛ ewura Fɛɛro ka sasa, ama jande, sa maŋ nya agbo n wora ma.

english_verse: You asked us if our father was still alive and if we had any more brothers.
translation_verse: Fo, n nyɛnpe e daŋ bishi anyi fo anya le: ‘Men kɔ etuto ŋko esipobi a?’

english_verse: So we told you, “Our father is a very old man. In fact, he was already old when Benjamin was born. Benjamin's brother is dead. Now Benjamin is the only one of the two brothers who is still alive, and our father loves him very much.”
translation_verse: Nɛ an shuli ŋ kaŋɛ fo: ‘An kɔ etuto nɛ e bel a kɔ kebinyɛnsobi nɛ e kurge mbe mbel to. Kebia na mo da wu nɛ e ki mo nawule ashi mo nio be mbia to nɛ mo tuto bee sha mo ga.’

english_verse: You ordered us to bring him here, so you could see him for yourself.
translation_verse: An ka kaŋɛ fo loŋ na nɛ fo kaŋɛ anyi, fo anya le: ‘Men ya bar mo nɛ ma alɛ gba e wu mo.’

english_verse: But you warned us that we could never see you again, unless our youngest brother came with us.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ fo kaŋɛ anyi, fo anya le: ‘Nɛ men sipobi na baa maŋ tu menyi m ba, ma nɛ menyi maaŋ wu abar.’

english_verse: But we told him, “We can't go back to Egypt without our youngest brother. We will never be let in to see the governor, unless he is with us.”
translation_verse: Nɛ an kaŋɛ mo: ‘Ayai, an sipobi ere baa maŋ tu anyi n yɔ, anyi maaŋ tiŋ n yɔ, ŋkpal manɛ so, an maaŋ ya tiŋ n wu kanyɛn na, ama an sipobi ere baa wɔtɔ nna.’

english_verse: Sir, our father then reminded us that his favorite wife had given birth to two sons.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ an tuto, fo kenya kaŋɛ anyi: ‘Men nyi ma eche ka kurge bibinyɛnsobi anyɔ nawule.’

english_verse: One of them was already missing and had not been seen for a long time. My father thinks the boy was torn to pieces by some wild animal,
translation_verse: Eko maŋ naa wɔ ma kutɔ nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ le: ‘Kashenteŋto kupuŋ to be kusɔ ko e kpɛa mo to n we na.’ Yili kumo be jemanɛ na so malɛ kikɛ m ba fo mbre, m maŋ naŋ wu mo kikɛ.

english_verse: and he said, “I am an old man. If you take Benjamin from me, and something happens to him, I will die of a broken heart.”
translation_verse: Nɛ men naŋ ta ede malɛ ŋ kutɔ naniere n yɔ nɛ kusɔ ko naŋ ya nya mo alɛ, kagbenejija beeŋ mɔ ma ashi ma mbel ere to.

english_verse: That's why Benjamin must be with us when I go back to my father. He loves him so much
translation_verse: Amoso nɛ m baŋ bɛta n yɔ n tuto, fo kenya na kutɔ ŋkaa maŋ keta kebia na n yɔ

english_verse: I promised my father that I would bring him safely home. If I don't, I told my father he could blame me the rest of my life.
translation_verse: Amoso pɔɛŋ nɛ an ba nfe ere, ma fo kenya nase kɔnɔ nna fanɛ kebia na beeŋ naŋ bɛta n fo n tuto nɛ eyur be alenfia. Ŋ kaŋɛ n tuto nna fanɛ nɛ kebia na baa maŋ bɛta m ba epe, meeŋ sɔ mbe turju ma ŋkpa to mbaanaayɔ!

english_verse: Sir, I am your slave. Please let me stay here in place of Benjamin and let him return home with his brothers.
translation_verse: Amoso, jande, shin nɛ ma fo kenya e sɔ kebia na so n shir a wɔ nfe ŋ ki fo kenya nɛ kebia na e tu mo daana ere m bɛta n yɔ epe.

english_verse: How can I face my father if Benjamin isn't with me? I couldn't bear to see my father in such sorrow.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal manɛ so, nɛ kebia na maŋ tu ma n yɔ epe, nuso nɛ meeŋ wora n yɔ n tuto kutɔ? Ayai, jande, sa maŋ shin nɛ n ya wu kagbenejija nɛ k beeŋ ba n tuto so na.”

english_verse: Since Joseph could no longer control his feelings in front of his servants, he sent them out of the room. When he was alone with his brothers, he told them, “I am Joseph.”
translation_verse: K ka fo le na, Josɛf daa maŋ naŋ tiŋ nɛ e keta mbe kumu nseŋ kaŋɛ basa pɔtɛ nɛ b daa wɔ ndoŋ na le: “Ekama e lar nfe ŋ ka anyi.” Amoso esa pɔtɛ kama daa maŋ naa wɔ Josɛf kutɔ saŋɛ nɛ e lara mbe kumu ŋ ŋini mo daana

english_verse: Then he cried so loudly that the Egyptians heard him and told about it in the king's palace.
translation_verse: nseŋ shu awɔrso ga hale nɛ Ijiptebi nɛ b daa wɔ kowu na nu e ka bee shu. Ewura Fɛɛro be laŋ to ebi gba nu mbe kushu na be asheŋ.

english_verse: Joseph told them to come closer to him, and when they did, he said: Yes, I am your brother Joseph, the one you sold into Egypt.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Josɛf kaŋɛ mo daana na: “Men firgi a ba ma kutɔ nfe.” B ka firgi n taga mo to nɛ e kaŋɛ bumo: “Ma, men sipo Josɛf nɛ men daŋ fa n sa Ijiptebi na nna na.

english_verse: There has already been a famine for two years, and for five more years no one will plow fields or harvest grain.
translation_verse: Akoŋ ere ka tɔr kumo be nfɛ anyɔ e kraa la na, kumo alɛ kraŋ ka nfɛ anu. Nfɛ anu na be jemanɛ so basa maaŋ tiŋ n dɔ, a bishi nɛ b duu asɔ ŋko a teŋi.

english_verse: But God sent me on ahead of you to keep your families alive and to save you in this wonderful way.
translation_verse: Ama Ebɔrɛ shin nna nɛ n juŋkpar menyi m ba nfe nɛ m ba bɔla le be ekpa ere so m mɔlga menyi, saŋɛ na so, menyi nɛ men be kanaŋ to ebi maaŋ mur.

english_verse: To his father he sent ten donkeys loaded with the best things in Egypt, and ten other donkeys loaded with grain and bread and other food for the return trip.
translation_verse: Mo tuto malɛ le be asɔ ere nɛ e daŋ ta n chise mo: Ekurma kudu e daŋ sulɔ Ijipt be kasawule so be asɔ lela be yiri yiri nɛ ekurma cheso kudu malɛ sulɔ ayu nɛ bodobodo nɛ asɔ jiso ko n ti so fanɛ a baa la mbe keba be ekpa to be ajibi.

translation_verse: E ka malga loŋ n loge na nɛ Josɛf maŋ mbia na so ashi mbe aya so nseŋ gbir mbe anishito ndoŋ ŋ kurgi kumu n yuu to.

english_verse: After Joseph got up, he brought his two sons over to Jacob again. He led his younger son Ephraim to the left side of Jacob and his older son Manasseh to the right.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Josɛf shin nɛ Efreim yili Jeekɔb be enɔ benaso nɛ Manase malɛ yili mbe jiso so.

english_verse: But before Jacob gave them his blessing, he crossed his arms, putting his right hand on the head of Ephraim and his left hand on the head of Manasseh.
translation_verse: Ama Jeekɔb daŋ bal mbe enɔana nna n deŋi mbia na so n shin nɛ mbe jiso yɔ Efreim nɛ e la ekekarso na so nseŋ shin nɛ mbe bena malɛ yɔ Manase nɛ e la enimuso na be kumu so.

english_verse: Then he gave Joseph his blessing and said: My grandfather Abraham and my father Isaac worshiped the Lord God. He has been with me all my life,
translation_verse: E ka wora loŋ na be kaman nɛ e nɛfa Josɛf nseŋ kaŋɛ: “Ebɔrɛ mo nɛ n nananyɛn Eebraham nɛ n tuto Aizek daŋ shuŋ na e nɛfa fo mbia ere. Mo, Ebɔrɛ koŋwule mo nɛ e juŋkpar ma a keni ma so fanɛ asɔbɔyakpapo na e nɛfa bumo.

english_verse: and his angel has kept me safe. Now I pray that he will bless these boys and that my name and the names of Abraham and Isaac will live on because of them. I ask God to give them many children and many descendants as well.
translation_verse: Malaika mo nɛ e tu ma ŋ kɔ emaŋ na e nɛfa bumo. Ebɔrɛ e shin nɛ ma ketre nɛ n tuto Aizek be ketre nɛ n nananyɛn Eebraham be ketre e bɔla mbia ere so a wɔtɔ mbaanaayɔ. Ebɔrɛ e sa bumo mbia damta nɛ kanaŋ to ebi damta durnya to.”

english_verse: Joseph did not like it when he saw his father place his right hand on the head of the younger son. So he tried to move his father's right hand from Ephraim's head and place it on Manasseh.
translation_verse: Josɛf ka wu mo tuto ka ta mbe jiso n deŋi Efreim so na k maŋ par mo nɛ e ya deŋi mo tuto be enɔ na ashi Efreim be kumu so n ta n deŋi Manase peya so,

english_verse: Joseph said, “Father, you have made a mistake. This is the older boy. Put your right hand on him.”
translation_verse: nseŋ kaŋɛ mo tuto: “N tuto, mannɛ aloŋ nna, ede e la enimuso, amoso mo e daga fanɛ fo ta fo jiso n deŋi mo so.”

english_verse: But his father said, “Son, I know what I am doing. It's true that Manasseh's family will someday become a great nation. But Ephraim will be even greater than Manasseh, because his descendants will become many great nations.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ mo tuto kini nseŋ kaŋɛ: “N nyi, m pibi n nyi. Mo alɛ gba beeŋ ki basa ko be kumuwura, mo alɛ gba beeŋ ba ki esagboŋ, ama mo sipo e naaŋ ba kaa chɔ mo eleŋ nɛ mbe kanaŋ to ebi e ba ki efuli damtaana be basa.”

english_verse: Jacob told him that in the future the people of Israel would ask God's blessings on one another by saying, “I pray for God to bless you as much as he blessed Ephraim and Manasseh.” Jacob put Ephraim's name first to show that he would be greater than Manasseh.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Jeekɔb nɛfa bumo kamɔnchɛ na ŋ kaŋɛ: “Israɛlebi beeŋ ba kaa kɔ men be atre a nɛfa bumo braana a kaŋɛ: ‘Ebɔrɛ e shin nɛ fo baa du fanɛ Efreim nɛ Manase.’ ” E ka wora loŋ na e daŋ ta Efreim nna n juŋkpar Manase.

english_verse: After that, Jacob said, “Joseph, you can see that I won't live much longer. But God will be with you and will lead you back to the land he promised our family long ago.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Jeekɔb kaŋɛ Josɛf: “M maaŋ naŋ chɛr nseŋ wu, ama Ebɔrɛ beeŋ baa wɔ menyi kutɔ n naŋ yɛr menyi men nananyɛnana be kasawule so.

english_verse: Jacob called his sons together and said: My sons, I am Jacob, your father Israel.
translation_verse: Kachako nɛ Jeekɔb kaŋɛ mbe bibinyɛnana na le: “Men gbargbar abar m ba ma anishito nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ menyi kusɔ nɛ k beeŋ nya menyi echefoso be asheŋ.

english_verse: Uncontrollable as a flood, you slept with my wife and disgraced my bed. And so you no longer deserve the place of honor.
translation_verse: Fo daa du fanɛ ketiligboŋ nna, ama fo maaŋ naa la esagboŋ ŋkpal fo ka di ma kowurche keche nɛ kenyɛn n wora ma, fo tuto be edesekpa eyurpi na so so.

english_verse: Simeon and Levi, you are brothers, each a gruesome sword.
translation_verse: Simiɔn nɛ Livai, la esa nɛ mo sipo nna, a kɔ bumo be etokobi a ŋini eleŋ a jija asɔ.

english_verse: I never want to take part in your plans or deeds. You slaughtered people in your anger, and you crippled cattle for no reason.
translation_verse: M maaŋ ta ma kɔnɔ n wɔtɔ bumo be wulo be mmalga to, ma alɛ nɛ bumo maaŋ shɛr ŋ kre asheŋ kikɛ. Ŋkpal manɛ so, b kaa agbo m mɔ basa nseŋ tuge asɔbɔya be aya be achin kenyaŋnyaŋɛso nɛ a ki ebobi.

english_verse: Judah, you will be praised by your brothers; they will bow down to you, as you defeat your enemies.
translation_verse: Juda, fo sipoana nɛ fo daana beeŋ chɔrɔ fo. Feeŋ pɔɔ fo doŋana so. Fo sipoana nɛ fo daana beeŋ jɔŋɛ fo ase.

english_verse: My son, you are a lion ready to eat your victim! You are terribly fierce; no one will bother you.
translation_verse: Juda, fo du fanɛ buluŋ nna, mo e naa pɔɔ mo braana asɔbɔya so a mɔ bumo, nsaa bɛta a yɔ mbe eŋanakpa n ya kaa teŋi to a dese na. Wanɛ e naaŋ tiŋ n tɔrɔ mo?

english_verse: Your eyes are darker than wine, your teeth whiter than milk.
translation_verse: Mbe anishi beeŋ ba pere fanɛ nsa nɛ baa tre wain na, nɛ mbe anyii malɛ e fuli parr fanɛ kenyipochu na.

english_verse: Zebulun, you will settle along the seashore and provide safe harbors as far north as Sidon.
translation_verse: Zɛbyulɔn beeŋ ba kaa wɔ teku ase nɛ mbe echenakpa e ki nchu so be ekuloŋgboŋana be eyilikpa. Mbe kasawule beeŋ dese loŋ n ya taga to Sidɔn.

english_verse: Issachar, you are a strong donkey resting in the meadows.
translation_verse: Isakar, fo du fanɛ kurma lempo nɛ e teŋi to a dese mbe esulɔ gbɛgbɛso be nferinto nna.

english_verse: You found them so pleasant that you worked too hard and became a slave.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal kananɛ fo ewushikpa walɛ nɛ kananɛ kasawule na so wɔ ebel so feeŋ yɔɔ m barase n sɔ kenyaya be kushuŋ gbɛgbɛso n shuŋ.

english_verse: Dan, you are the tribe that will bring justice to Israel.
translation_verse: Dan, feeŋ ji fo basa demu nɛ kumo be ekpa so ashi Israɛl be nnaŋ na to.

english_verse: Our Lord, I am waiting for you to save us.
translation_verse: O, Enyɛnpe, mee jo fo kenya be kesɔnyige nna.

english_verse: Asher, you will eat food fancy enough for a king.
translation_verse: Ashɛr, fo adɔsawule beeŋ wora ajibi lela damta, ajibi nɛ feeŋ nya na beeŋ baa walɛ nna n sa ewura.

english_verse: Your help came from the God your father worshiped, from God All-Powerful. God will bless you with rain and streams from the earth; he will bless you with many descendants.
translation_verse: Fo tuto be Ebɔrɛ na e naa chɛ fo to. Enyɛnpetale na e naa nɛfa fo, a sa fo bɔrɛchu nɛ nchu nɛ a bee bul kasawule to nɛ asɔbɔya nɛ mbia nɛ kenyipochu damta nɛ mbia na e baa nuu.

english_verse: My son, the blessings I give are better than the promise of ancient mountains or eternal hills. Joseph, I pray these blessings will come to you, because you are the leader of your brothers.
translation_verse: Fo tuto be nɛfa nɛ e sa fo ere beeŋ ba shi a chɔ bedarapo na peya nɛ asɔ lela nɛ a shi a chɔɔ abeebi, nsaa wɔtɔ mbaanaayɔ na. Le be nɛfa ere kikɛ e baa wɔ Josɛf so ŋkpal e ka ki enimu ashi mo daana kikɛ so so.

english_verse: Benjamin, you are a fierce wolf, destroying your enemies morning and evening.
translation_verse: Bɛnjamin, fo du fanɛ jiŋkaamu lubi nɛ e bee kaa mɔ asɔbɔya chipurso nsaa kpɛa bumo to a we kanyɛso na nna.”

english_verse: Both the cave and the land that goes with it were bought from the Hittites.
translation_verse: B daŋ tɔ kasawule na nɛ kebeelaŋ nɛ k wɔ ndoŋ na ashi Hitebi kutɔ nna. Men puli ma ndoŋ.”

english_verse: When Jacob had finished giving these instructions to his sons, he lay down on his bed and died.
translation_verse: Jeekɔb ka ta le be mmalga ere kikɛ m bɔɔ mbe mbia na enɔ n loge nɛ e lɔŋɛ n dese nseŋ fute mbe lalaloge be efute n wu.

english_verse: Joseph started crying, then leaned over to hug and kiss his father.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Josɛf kilgi n tɔr mo tuto so n shu ga nseŋ lala mo so kashaso.

english_verse: When the time of mourning was over, Joseph said to the Egyptian leaders, “If you consider me your friend, please speak to the king for me.
translation_verse: Keeliwora na be jemanɛ ka choŋ nɛ Josɛf kaŋɛ ewura Fɛɛro be benimu le: “Nɛ menyee sha ma asheŋ, men ta le be kubɔya ere n ya sa ewura n sa ma.

english_verse: Just before my father died, he made me promise to bury him in his burial cave in Canaan. If the king will give me permission to go, I will come back here.”
translation_verse: Men kaŋɛ mo fanɛ n tuto ka daa shin nɛ e wu, e daŋ shin nna nɛ n nase kɔnɔ n sa mo fanɛ nɛ e kaŋ wu, meeŋ ya puli mo nchaŋ nɛ e wora n nase Keenan na to. Amoso e jande, e sa ma ekpa nɛ n yɔ ndoŋ n ya puli mo nseŋ naa ba.”

english_verse: The king answered, “Go to Canaan and keep your promise to your father.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura Fɛɛro kaŋɛ mo: “Bɛ kɔnɔ nɛ fo nase na so n ya puli fo tuto.”

english_verse: When Joseph left Goshen with his brothers, his relatives, and his father's relatives to bury Jacob, many of the king's highest officials and even his military chariots and cavalry went along. The Israelites left behind only their children, their cattle, and their sheep and goats.
translation_verse: Basa nɛ b daŋ tu mo n yɔ na to be beko daa wɔ egbaŋɛturko to nna nɛ bede dii egbaŋɛ. Kashenteŋto jimaŋ damta e daa la bumo.

english_verse: After crossing the Jordan River, Joseph stopped at Atad's threshing place, where they all mourned and wept seven days for Jacob.
translation_verse: B daŋ ta loŋ m ba fo Atad nɛ k wɔ Jɔɔdan be epeŋipetekpa be kugooro nɛ b daa bri asɔ ndoŋ na m ba shu awɔrso ndoŋ ga nɛ Josɛf ta bɔkwe n wora keeliwora be edaŋkaresheŋ ndoŋ.

english_verse: After Jacob died, Joseph's brothers said to each other, “What if Joseph still hates us and wants to get even with us for all the cruel things we did to him?”
translation_verse: Jeekɔb be luwu na be kaman nɛ Josɛf mo daana na kaŋɛ abar le: “Shere an tuto ka wu ere, Josɛf beeŋ kishi anyi nseŋ wora anyi n tal alubi nɛ an daŋ wora mo na kikɛ nyam to.”

english_verse: he told us, “You did some cruel and terrible things to Joseph, but you must ask him to forgive you.” Now we ask you to please forgive the terrible things we did. After all, we serve the same God that your father worshiped. When Joseph heard this, he started crying.
translation_verse: ‘Men kaŋ wora, men kule Josɛf alubi be ketampaŋ ŋ kaŋɛ: Jande, ta fo daana be alubi nɛ b wora fo na kikɛ m paŋ bumo.’ Amoso, anyee kule fo nna fanɛ fo ta m paŋ anyi nɛ an la fo tuto be Ebɔrɛ be anya na.” Josɛf ka nu bumo be kubɔya na nɛ e shu.

english_verse: Right then, Joseph's brothers came and bowed down to the ground in front of him and said, “We are your slaves.”
translation_verse: Ama kubɔya na be kaman, mo daana na gba daŋ naŋ ba mo kutɔ nna m ba gbir mbe anishito ŋ kurgi amu n yuu to ŋ kaŋɛ mo: “Anyi, fo anya nde!”

english_verse: But Joseph told them, “Don't be afraid! I have no right to change what God has decided.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Josɛf kaŋɛ bumo: “Men sa maa lɔ kufu, mannɛ ma e la Ebɔrɛ.

english_verse: You tried to harm me, but God made it turn out for the best, so that he could save all these people, as he is now doing.
translation_verse: Menyi ere daŋ kre ma kulubi nna, ama Ebɔrɛ malɛ ta kumo ŋ ki kelela, saŋɛ na so e beeŋ sɔ basa damta nɛ b wɔ ŋkpa to kabre ere n yige ŋkpal kusɔ nɛ k daŋ wora na so.

english_verse: Don't be afraid! I will take care of you and your children.” After Joseph said this, his brothers felt much better. Joseph's Death
translation_verse: Amoso, men sa maŋ shin nɛ kufu kama e baa kɔ menyi. Meeŋ baa keni menyi nɛ men be mbia so.” E daŋ leŋ bumo to nna m malga mmalga lela n sa bumo. Josɛf be luwu be asheŋ

english_verse: Joseph lived in Egypt with his brothers until he died at the age of
translation_verse: Josɛf nɛ mo tuto be basa na kikɛ daŋ shir a wɔ Ijipt nna. Josɛf daŋ ji nfɛ kalfa nɛ kudu nna pɔɛŋ nseŋ wu.

english_verse: Joseph lived long enough to see Ephraim's children and grandchildren. He also lived to see the children of Manasseh's son Machir, and he welcomed them into his family.
translation_verse: E daŋ wu Efreim be mbia nɛ bumo alɛ be mbia nna pɔɛŋ nseŋ wu. E daŋ wu Manase pibinyɛn Makiir gba be mbia. B ka baŋ kurge bumo na nɛ e ta bumo n ti mbe kanaŋ so.

english_verse: Before Joseph died, he told his brothers, “I won't live much longer. But God will take care of you and lead you out of Egypt to the land he promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
translation_verse: Kachako nɛ e kaŋɛ mo daana na le: “To, k maaŋ naŋ chɛr ko nɛ n wu, ama abaanaaworasheŋ Ebɔrɛ maaŋ yige menyi n to, e beeŋ keni menyi so nseŋ juŋkpar menyi, n lara menyi kasawule ere so n ta menyi n yɔ kakpa nɛ e daŋ nase kɔnɔ n sa Eebraham nɛ Aizek nɛ Jeekɔb fanɛ e beeŋ sa na.”

english_verse: Now promise me that you will take my body with you when God leads you to that land.”
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Josɛf kaŋɛ mo daana na le: “Ama, men nase kɔnɔ n sa ma fanɛ ŋ kaŋ wu nɛ Ebɔrɛ lara menyi nfe, menyeeŋ ta ma eyur n ti so n yɔ.”

english_verse: When Jacob went to Egypt, his son Joseph was already there. So Jacob took his eleven other sons and their families. They were: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun, Benjamin, Dan, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher. Altogether, Jacob had
translation_verse: Saŋɛ nɛ b yɔ Ijipt na nɛ Jeekɔb be kanaŋ to ebi kikɛ daa wɔ basa adushunu. Kumo be saŋɛ so nɛ Josɛf bre tea wɔ Ijipt.

english_verse: After Joseph, his brothers, and everyone else in that generation had died,
translation_verse: B wɔtɔ loŋ nɛ Josɛf nɛ mo daana nɛ bumo be jemanɛ to ebi kikɛ wu n loge.

english_verse: the people of Israel became so numerous that the whole region of Goshen was full of them.
translation_verse: Ama bumo be kaman to ebi, Israɛlebi na, daa kurge nna ga n wora keshi n sɔ kasawule na so kikɛ.

english_verse: Many years later a new king came to power. He did not know what Joseph had done for Egypt,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ esa popɔr ko nɛ e daa maŋ nyi Josɛf ba ji Ijipt be efuli so be kuwura.

english_verse: and he told the Egyptians: There are too many of those Israelites in our country, and they are becoming more powerful than we are.
translation_verse: Kachako nɛ e kaŋɛ mbe basa le: “Men keni, naniere Israɛlebi ere wora keshi ga nsaa kɔ eleŋ ga a chɔ anyi.

english_verse: If we don't outsmart them, their families will keep growing larger. And if our country goes to war, they could easily fight on the side of our enemies and escape from Egypt.
translation_verse: Amoso men shin nɛ an bɔla kanyiasheŋ be ekpa so n wora kusɔ ko ŋ kuŋ anyi be amu. Mannɛ aloŋ, baaŋ baa kraa wora keshi a ti so, nɛ k ya ba fanɛ kena koso anyi nɛ basa ko so, baaŋ chɛ an doŋana na to ŋ kɔ anyi nseŋ shile anyi be efuli ere so kuraa.”

english_verse: The Egyptians put slave bosses in charge of the people of Israel and tried to wear them down with hard work. Those bosses forced them to build the cities of Pithom and Rameses, where the king could store his supplies.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ijiptebi na lara basa fanɛ benyɛnpe nɛ baaŋ baa keni Israɛlebi na so fanɛ anya. Ndoŋ nna nɛ b ta kanyaŋ be kushuŋ a tɔrɔ Israɛlebi na nseŋ shin nɛ b pɔr nde nɛ baa tre Pitɔm nɛ Rameses na n sa ewura Fɛɛro nɛ e baa ta mbe asɔ a yili to ndoŋ.

english_verse: But even though the Israelites were mistreated, their families grew larger, and they took over more land. Because of this, the Egyptians feared them worse than before
translation_verse: Ama kanaŋkama nɛ b daŋ baa tɔrɔ Israɛlebi na, bumo alɛ daŋ baŋ kraa wora keshi nna a ti so nseŋ sɔ kasawule na so kikɛ nɛ Ijiptebi na fara a ŋana Israɛlebi na alegaiso.

english_verse: that their lives were miserable. The Egyptians were cruel to the people of Israel and forced them to make bricks and to mix mortar and to work in the fields.
translation_verse: nɛ kebaawɔtɔ ki nyaŋnyaŋ n sa bumo ŋkpal loŋ so. B daa shin nɛ baa baga eshii a kuya ebirkesi a pɔr nwu nsaa shuŋ ndɔana to nna. Bumo alɛ daa maa wu Israɛlebi na kuwɔr kikɛ.

english_verse: Finally, the king called in Shiphrah and Puah, the two women who helped the Hebrew mothers when they gave birth.
translation_verse: Kachako nɛ Ijipt be ewura Fɛɛro na kaŋɛ Hibruw be beche nɛ baa tre Shifra nɛ Puwa nɛ b daa keta beche nɛ baa kurge na le:

english_verse: He told them, “If a Hebrew woman gives birth to a girl, let the child live. If the baby is a boy, kill him!”
translation_verse: “Saŋkama nɛ men baŋ ya kaa keta Hibruwche kama kakurge nseŋ wu fanɛ ebinyɛn nɛ e kurge, men mɔ kebia na. Ama nɛ fanɛ kebia na la ebiche bre, men yige mo.”

english_verse: But the two women were faithful to God and did not kill the boys, even though the king had told them to.
translation_verse: Ama beche nɛ b daa keta kakurge na daa kɔ kabɔrɛŋana nna, amoso b daŋ kini kewora kusɔ nɛ Ijipt be ewura na kaŋɛ bumo na nna, nseŋ daa yige mbinyɛnsobi na gba.

english_verse: God was good to the two women because they truly respected him, and he blessed them with children of their own. The Hebrews kept increasing
translation_verse: Beche nɛ baa sɔ kakurge na ka daa ŋana Ebɔrɛ so so e daŋ nɛfa bumo nna n sa bumo be ekama mo gbagba be mbia.

english_verse: until finally, the king gave a command to everyone in the nation, “As soon as a Hebrew boy is born, throw him into the Nile River! But you can let the girls live.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura Fɛɛro sa mbe basa kikɛ ebɔl kenishipereso ŋ kaŋɛ le: “Hibruwebi na baŋ kurge ebinyɛn kikɛ, men ta mo n ya lɛ lɔr nɛ baa tre Nail na to, ama becheso na bre, men yige bumo kikɛ nɛ b baa wɔtɔ.”

english_verse: A man from the Levi tribe married a woman from the same tribe,
translation_verse: Loŋ be jemanɛ na malɛ nɛ kanyɛn ko nɛ e daŋ shi Livai be kanaŋ to daŋ ta livaiebi ko a kil

english_verse: and she later had a baby boy. He was a beautiful child, and she kept him inside for three months.
translation_verse: nɛ kache na di kedampo ŋ kurge ebinyɛn. E ka wu kananɛ kebia na daa walɛ keyɛrbi na nɛ e ta mo ŋ ŋana afɔl asa.

english_verse: But when she could no longer keep him hidden, she made a basket out of reeds and covered it with tar. She put him in the basket and placed it in the tall grass along the edge of the Nile River.
translation_verse: Ama saŋɛ nɛ e wu fanɛ e maaŋ naŋ tiŋ n ta kebia na ŋ ŋana na nɛ e ta kootal n laa kelantaŋɛ nɛ b ta agasa n lue nseŋ ta kebia na n wɔtɔ kumo to. Kumo be kaman nɛ e ta kelantaŋɛ na nɛ kebia na kikɛ n ya yili nchu to ashi lɔrkar be afitiri jeŋgreŋ ko nɛ a du fanɛ agasa na to.

english_verse: The baby's older sister stood off at a distance to see what would happen to him.
translation_verse: Nɛ kebia na mo dache malɛ ya feŋ n yili a keni kusɔ nɛ k beeŋ wora mo.

english_verse: About that time one of the king's daughters came down to take a bath in the river, while her servant women walked along the river bank. She saw the basket in the tall grass and sent one of them to pull it out of the water.
translation_verse: K maŋ chɛr ko nɛ ewura Fɛɛro pibiche ba lɔr na to nɛ e ba bɛr nɛ mbe mbita malɛ na lɔr na be ekarso. Nɛ ewura Fɛɛro pibiche na wu kelantaŋɛ na ka yil nchu to ashi afitiri jeŋgreŋ na to nɛ e shuŋi mbe kenyache fanɛ e ya ta kumo m ba.

english_verse: When the king's daughter opened the basket, she saw the baby crying and felt sorry for him. She said, “This must be one of the Hebrew babies.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura Fɛɛro pibiche na bugi kelantaŋɛ na so n wu kebia nyɛnsobi kumo to nɛ e bee shu. Nɛ mbe asheŋ pɛ mo kuwɔr nɛ e kaŋɛ: “Hibruwebi be mbi popɔrbi ere be eko nde.”

english_verse: At once the baby's older sister came up and asked, “Do you want me to get a Hebrew woman to take care of the baby for you?”
translation_verse: Epul na to nɛ kebi popɔrbi na mo dache na ba bishi ewura Fɛɛro pibiche na le: “N ya tre Hibruw be eche ko m ba nɛ e ba sɔ mo n ya kaa nyipo a sa fo a?”

english_verse: “Yes,” the king's daughter answered. So the girl brought the baby's mother,
translation_verse: Nɛ ewura Fɛɛro pibiche na kaŋɛ mo: “Mm, yɔ.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ kebia na mo dache na ya bar kebia na mo nio gbagba.

english_verse: and the king's daughter told her, “Take care of this child, and I will pay you.” The baby's mother carried him home and took care of him.
translation_verse: Kache na ka ba nɛ ewura Fɛɛro pibiche na kaŋɛ mo le: “Ta kebia ere n ya kaa keni so a sa ma nɛ ŋ ka fo kukɔ.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ keche na ta kebia na n ya kaa bela.

english_verse: And when he was old enough, she took him to the king's daughter, who adopted him. She named him Moses because she said, “I pulled him out of the water.” Moses Escapes from Egypt
translation_verse: Kebia na ka daŋ gbrɛbi nɛ kache na ta mo n ya sa ewura Fɛɛro pibiche na, nɛ e ta mo ŋ ki mo gbagba pibinyɛn nseŋ nase mo Mosis. Ŋkpal e ka nya mo ashi nchu to so. Mosis ka shile n yɔ Midian be asheŋ

english_verse: Moses looked around to see if anyone was watching, then he killed the Egyptian and hid his body in the sand.
translation_verse: Mosis ka gbɛ ŋ keni nfe ŋ gbɛ ŋ keni nfe nsaa maŋ wu esa kikɛ ka da mo so nɛ e mɔ Ijipt be esa na nseŋ ta mo m puli eshishɛr to.

english_verse: When Moses went out the next day, he saw two Hebrews fighting. So he went to the man who had started the fight and asked, “Why are you beating up one of your own people?”
translation_verse: Kumo be ŋklade Mosis ka naŋ lar nɛ e ya tu Hibruw be basa anyɔ ko nɛ baa bile. Ndoŋ nna nɛ e bishi emo nɛ e daŋ fara kolu na le: “Manɛ e ba nɛ fee ŋmɛa fo barkasa Hibruw be esa loŋ?”

english_verse: The man answered, “Who put you in charge of us and made you our judge? Are you planning to kill me, just like you killed that Egyptian?” This frightened Moses because he was sure that people must have found out what had happened.
translation_verse: Nɛ emo nɛ e daŋ fara kolu na bishi Mosis le: “Wanɛ e ta fo ŋ ki anyi be enimu nɛ anyi be demujipo? Ŋko, fee sha kemɔ ma alɛ gba nna fanɛ kananɛ fo daŋ mɔ Ijipt be esa na a?” Ndoŋ nna nɛ kufu pɛ Mosis nɛ e kaŋɛ mbe kumu: “To, k baŋ di efuli nna na fanɛ basa pin kusɔ nɛ n wora na.”

english_verse: When the king heard what Moses had done, he wanted to kill him. But Moses escaped and went to the land of Midian. One day, when Moses was sitting by a well,
translation_verse: Ewura Fɛɛro ka nu kesheŋ na nɛ e bee fin kemɔ Mosis. Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis shile n yɔ Midian be kasawule so n ya chena ketirbu ko ase.

english_verse: the seven daughters of Jethro, the priest of Midian, came up to water their father's sheep and goats.
translation_verse: Nɛ Jetro nɛ e daa la bɔrɛmatapo ashi Midian na be mbichebi ashunu ba nɛ b ba jɔ nchu ketirbu na to n wɔtɔ asɔbɔya be asɔnuunchu to n sa bumo tuto be mbolpɔ nɛ mboe.

english_verse: Some shepherds tried to chase them away, but Moses came to their rescue and watered their animals.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ asɔbɔyakpapoana ko ba kaa ju Jetro be mbichesobi na. Nɛ Mosis koso n ya mɔlga mbichesobi na nseŋ chɛ bumo to n jɔ nchu n sa bumo be asɔbɔya na.

english_verse: When Jethro's daughters returned home, their father asked, “Why have you come back so early today?”
translation_verse: Mbichesobi na ka bɛta n yɔ bumo tuto Jetro kutɔ nɛ e bishi bumo: “Manɛ nna nɛ men bɛta m ba manaŋ kabre loŋ?”

english_verse: They answered, “An Egyptian rescued us from the shepherds, and he even watered our sheep and goats.”
translation_verse: Nɛ b kaŋɛ mo: “Ijipt be kanyɛn ko e mɔlga anyi ashi asɔbɔyakpapoana na kutɔ nseŋ jɔ nchu n sa anyi be asɔbɔya gba.”

english_verse: “Where is he?” Jethro asked. “Why did you leave him out there? Invite him to eat with us.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ mbichebi na bumo tuto bishi bumo le: “Nɛ nnɛ nɛ e wɔ? Manɛ nna nɛ men yige mo ndoŋ? Men ya tre mo nɛ e ba ji kusɔ ko.”

english_verse: Moses agreed to stay on with Jethro, who later let his daughter Zipporah marry Moses.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Mosis shuli n chena Midian. Mosis nɛ bumo wɔtɔ loŋ nɛ Jetro ta mo pibiche Zipora n sa mo nɛ e ki mbe eche.

english_verse: And when she had a son, Moses said, “I will name him Gershom, since I am a foreigner in this country.”
translation_verse: Zipora ka kurge ebinyɛn nɛ Mosis nase mo Gɛshɔn, ŋkpal e ka daa fɛ le so: “N la efɔ nna ashi efuli pɔtɛ ere so, kumo so, meeŋ nase ma kebia ere loŋ be ketre na.”

english_verse: After the death of the king of Egypt, the Israelites still complained because they were forced to be slaves. They cried out for help,
translation_verse: Kumo be nfɛ damta ka ba choŋ nɛ Ijipt be ewura na wu, ama amo nɛ amo kikɛ nɛ Israɛlebi na kraa wɔ kenyaya to nna a ji awurfoŋ nsaa shu a tre Ebɔrɛ fanɛ e chɛ bumo to.

english_verse: and God heard their loud cries. He did not forget the promise he had made to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob,
translation_verse: Nɛ Ebɔrɛ nu bumo be nfubel na nseŋ nyiŋi mbe kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre nɛ k wɔ mo nɛ bumo nananyɛnana Eebraham nɛ Aizek nɛ Jeekɔb be kefɛato na.

english_verse: and because he knew what was happening to his people, he felt sorry for them.
translation_verse: Israɛlebi na be asheŋ daŋ tir mo ga m pɛ mo kuwɔr ŋkpal kenyaya nɛ b daa wɔ to na so.

english_verse: One day, Moses was taking care of the sheep and goats of his father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian, and Moses decided to lead them across the desert to Sinai, the holy mountain.
translation_verse: Mosis daa kpa mo shanyɛn Jetro nɛ e daa la Midian be bɔrɛmatapo na be mbolpɔ nna. Kachako nɛ e kpa bumo m bɔla kiyi to n ya fo Ebɔrɛ be kebeegboŋ nɛ baa tre Sainai na ase.

english_verse: There an angel of the Lord appeared to him from a burning bush. Moses saw that the bush was on fire, but it was not burning up.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be malaika lar mo so fanɛ edɛ be adondulombi na ashi kupumbi ko to. Mosis daŋ wu kupumbi na ka bee suse edɛ ama kumo alɛ daa maa chɔɔ a mur.

english_verse: When the Lord saw Moses coming near, he called him by name from the bush, and Moses answered, “Here I am.”
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ka wu fanɛ Mosis firgi n taga to nɛ e keni na nɛ e tre mo ashi kupumbi na to ŋ kaŋɛ: “Mosis, Mosis!” Nɛ Mosis shuli ŋ kaŋɛ le: “Ma nde.”

english_verse: God replied, “Don't come any closer. Take off your sandals—the ground where you are standing is holy.
translation_verse: Nɛ Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ mo: “Sa maŋ kaŋ naŋ firgi m ba n ti so. Lara fo asɛbta na, ŋkpal manɛ so, kasawule cheembi so nɛ fo yil na.

english_verse: I am the God who was worshiped by your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.” Moses was afraid to look at God, and so he hid his face.
translation_verse: Ma e la fo tutoana, Eebraham nɛ Aizek nɛ Jeekɔb be Ebɔrɛ na.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis kurgi kumu n yuu to, ŋkpal e ka daa ŋana kekeni Ebɔrɛ na so.

english_verse: The Lord said: I have seen how my people are suffering as slaves in Egypt, and I have heard them beg for my help because of the way they are being mistreated. I feel sorry for them,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ mo le: “N wu tɔrɔ mo nɛ ma basa bee ji ashi Ijipt be efuli so, ma alɛ nseŋ naŋ nu b ka bee shu ŋkpal awurfoŋ nɛ baa ji ashi anyakenipoana be enɔ to na so. Bumo be asheŋ tir ma ga.

english_verse: and I have come down to rescue them from the Egyptians. I will bring my people out of Egypt into a country where there is a lot of good land, rich with milk and honey. I will give them the land where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal loŋ so, nɛ ŋ gbelge m ba nɛ m ba mɔlga bumo ashi Ijiptebi na be enɔ to nseŋ lara bumo ashi Ijipt be kasawule so n yɛr bumo kasawule lela nɛ k shi so. Kasawule mo nɛ k kɔ kanya alegaiso nsaa wora ajibi nɛnɛ. Loŋ be kasawule na so nɛ Keenanebi nɛ Hitebi nɛ Amɔriebi nɛ Pɛrizebi nɛ Hivebi nɛ Jebusiebi tase so na.

english_verse: My people have begged for my help, and I have seen how cruel the Egyptians are to them.
translation_verse: N nu ma basa Israɛlebi be kushu kashenteŋto, ma alɛ nseŋ naŋ wu kananɛ Ijiptebi bee tɔrɔ bumo.

english_verse: Now go to the king! I am sending you to lead my people out of his country.
translation_verse: Amoso mee shuŋi fo Ijipt be ewura Fɛɛro kutɔ nna naniere nɛ fo ya lara ma basa Israɛlebi ashi efuli na so.”

english_verse: But Moses said, “Who am I to go to the king and lead your people out of Egypt?”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis kaŋɛ Ebɔrɛ le: “Ma alɛ e la wanɛ nɛ n tiŋ n yɔ Ijipt be ewura Fɛɛro be anishito, hale n ya lara Israɛlebi na ashi Ijipt be efuli so!”

english_verse: God replied, “I will be with you. And you will know that I am the one who sent you, when you worship me on this mountain after you have led my people out of Egypt.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ mo le: “Meeŋ baa wɔ fo kutɔ. Fo kaŋ ya lara basa na ashi Ijipt be efuli so m ba kebee ere so nfe m ba bunyaŋ ma na nɛ feeŋ pin fanɛ ma e shin nɛ loŋ wora.”

english_verse: Moses answered, “I will tell the people of Israel that the God their ancestors worshiped has sent me to them. But what should I say, if they ask me your name?”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis naŋ kaŋɛ: “Nɛ ŋ kaŋ yɔ Israɛlebi na kutɔ n ya kaŋɛ bumo le: ‘Men nananyɛnana be Ebɔrɛ e shuŋi ma menyi kutɔ.’ Nɛ b kaŋ bishi ma fanɛ: ‘Mbe ketre e la nuso?’ Nuso nɛ meeŋ kaŋɛ bumo?”

english_verse: God said to Moses: I am the eternal God. So tell them that the Lord, whose name is “I Am,” has sent you. This is my name forever, and it is the name that people must use from now on.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Ebɔrɛ naŋ kaŋɛ Mosis fanɛ e kaŋɛ Israɛlebi na le: “Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ e la men nananyɛnana Eebraham nɛ Aizek nɛ Jeekɔb be Ebɔrɛ na e shuŋi ma menyi kutɔ. Ketre ere malɛ e naaŋ baa la ma ketre hale mbaanaayɔ. Loŋ nɛ men be kaman to ebi kikɛ gba beeŋ ba kaa tre ma.

english_verse: Call together the leaders of Israel and tell them that the God who was worshiped by Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob has appeared to you. Tell them I have seen how terribly they are being treated in Egypt,
translation_verse: Yɔ n ya tre Israɛlebi na be bejuŋkparpo kikɛ n shɛr ŋ kaŋɛ bumo fanɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ e la men nananyɛnana, Eebraham nɛ Aizek nɛ Jeekɔb be Ebɔrɛ na e lar ma so ŋ kaŋɛ: ‘Ŋ keni n wu kusɔ nɛ baa wora menyi ashi Ijipt be efuli so nɛ menyi be asheŋ tir ma ga.’

english_verse: and I promise to lead them out of their troubles. I will give them a land rich with milk and honey, where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
translation_verse: Ma alɛ yili kumo fanɛ meeŋ lara menyi ashi tɔrɔ nɛ menyee ji ashi Ijipt be efuli so na to n yɔ Keenanebi nɛ Hitebi nɛ Amɔriebi nɛ Pɛrizebi nɛ Hivebi nɛ Jebusiebi be nsawuleana so. Loŋ be nsawule na e kɔ kanya alegaiso nsaa wora ajibi nɛnɛ.”

english_verse: The leaders of Israel will listen to you. Then you must take them to the king of Egypt and say, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Let us walk three days into the desert, where we can offer a sacrifice to him.”
translation_verse: “Nɛ fo wora loŋ, Israɛl be benimu na beeŋ nu n sa fo nɛ fo keta bumo n yɔ Ijipt be ewura Fɛɛro kutɔ n ya kaŋɛ mo le: ‘Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ e la Israɛlebi be Ebɔrɛ na e lara mbe kumu ŋ ŋini anyi, amoso jande, sa anyi ekpa naniere nɛ an ta nchɛ asa n nite n yɔ keshishɛrsawule na so n ya lara sarga n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ anyi be Ebɔrɛ na.’

english_verse: But I know that the king of Egypt won't let you go unless something forces him to.
translation_verse: Ama n nyi Ijipt be ewura na ka maaŋ shin nɛ men yɔ, ama m baŋ ki mbe enɔ to nna pɔɛŋ nɛ e shuli.

english_verse: So I will use my mighty power to perform all kinds of miracles and strike down the Egyptians. Then the king will send you away.
translation_verse: Amoso meeŋ ŋini ma eleŋ nseŋ wora emamachisheŋ ŋ gberge Ijiptebi kusoe ndoŋ nɛ kufu e pɛ bumo ga. Kumo be kaman nɛ e shin nɛ men yɔ.

english_verse: After I punish the Egyptians, they will be so afraid of you that they will give you anything you want. You are my people, and I will let you take many things with you when you leave the land of Egypt.
translation_verse: Ma alɛ beeŋ shin nɛ Ijiptebi na e bugi ŋgbene n chɛ Israɛlebi na to saŋɛ na so men kaa lar ndoŋ men maaŋ ta enɔfuloŋ n lar.

english_verse: Every Israelite woman will go to her Egyptian neighbors or to any Egyptian woman living with them and ask them for gold and silver jewelry and for their finest clothes. The Egyptians will give them to you, and you will put these fine things on your sons and daughters. Carry all this away when you leave Egypt.
translation_verse: Amoso Israɛl be eche kama beeŋ ya kule mbe bechenashapoana nɛ b la Ijipt be beche na asɔbuuso nɛ shuwa nɛ gbiti be abitasɔ lelaana. Nɛ menyi Israɛlebi na e ta loŋ be asɔana na n wɔtɔ men be mbinyɛnso nɛ men be mbicheso, saŋɛ na so, menyeeŋ nya Ijiptebi be asɔ n yɔ.”

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord, “Suppose everyone refuses to listen to my message, and no one believes that you really appeared to me?”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis kaŋɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ le: “To, nɛ b ka maŋ yirda ma ŋko n nu n sa kusɔ nɛ meeŋ kaŋɛ bumo na nseŋ kaŋɛ le: ‘Enyɛnpe maŋ lar fo so a?’ ”

english_verse: The Lord answered, “What's that in your hand?” “A walking stick,” Moses replied.
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na bishi mo: “Manɛ e wɔ fo enɔ to ere?” Nɛ Mosis kaŋɛ mo: “Kekpabi nna.”

english_verse: “Throw it down!” the Lord commanded. So Moses threw the stick on the ground. It immediately turned into a snake, and Moses jumped back.
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ mo: “Ta kumo n lɛ kasawule!” Mosis ka wora loŋ nɛ kekpabi na kilgi kuwɔ nɛ Mosis shile ashi kumo ase.

english_verse: “Pick it up by the tail!” the Lord told him. And when Moses did this, the snake turned back into a walking stick.
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ mo: “Murgi m pɛ kumo be kodu to n ta kumo.” Nɛ Mosis murgi m pɛ kuwɔ na be kodu to nɛ k naŋ kilgi kekpabi n wɔtɔ mbe enɔ to.

english_verse: “Do this,” the Lord said, “and the Israelites will believe that you have seen me, the God who was worshiped by their ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Mosis: “Fo baŋ wora loŋ, baaŋ yirda fanɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, bumo nananyɛnana Eebraham nɛ Aizek nɛ Jeekɔb be Ebɔrɛ na e lar fo so.”

english_verse: Next, the Lord commanded Moses, “Put your hand inside your shirt.” Moses obeyed, and when he took it out, his hand had turned white as snow—like someone with leprosy.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ naŋ kaŋɛ mo: “Ta fo enɔ n wɔtɔ fo piŋi to.” Nɛ Mosis ta mbe enɔ n wɔtɔ mbe piŋi to. E ka lara kumo nɛ keboti pɛ kumo nɛ kumo kikɛ fuli parr fanɛ ateebi.

english_verse: “Put your hand back inside your shirt,” the Lord told him. Moses did so, and when he took it out again, it was as healthy as the rest of his body.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ naŋ kaŋɛ mo: “Naŋ ta fo enɔ n wɔtɔ fo piŋi to.” Nɛ Mosis naŋ ta mbe enɔ n wɔtɔ mbe piŋi na to. E ka naŋ lara kumo nɛ k naŋ nyalɛ so ŋ ki mbe kayurwule gbagba.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “If no one believes either of these miracles, take some water from the Nile River and pour it on the ground. The water will immediately turn into blood.”
translation_verse: Nɛ k ba fanɛ b maŋ yirda amo anyɔ na kikɛ ŋko nɛ b kini kenu n sa fo kamalga na fo jɔ lɔr nɛ baa tre Nail na be nchu n wurge kasawule. Loŋ be nchu na beeŋ kilgi ŋklaŋ kasawule na so.”

english_verse: Moses replied, “I have never been a good speaker. I wasn't one before you spoke to me, and I'm not one now. I am slow at speaking, and I can never think of what to say.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis kaŋɛ le: “O, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, jande, sa maŋ shuŋi ma! Ŋkpal manɛ so m maŋ nyi kamalga to. Nɛ mannɛ fo ka bee malga ma fo kenya kutɔ nfe ere so, ma nɛ esa kikɛ maŋ naŋ malga le kikɛ. N la esa nɛ m maa tiŋ kamalga nna.”

english_verse: But the Lord answered, “Who makes people able to speak or makes them deaf or unable to speak? Who gives them sight or makes them blind? Don't you know that I am the one who does these things?
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ bishi mo: “Wanɛ e wora dimɛdi be kɔnɔ? Wanɛ e naaŋ tiŋ n shin nɛ esa e ki kpawu ŋko neemu ŋko wanɛ e naa sa esa anishi ŋko a shin nɛ esa bee ki tanpo? Mannɛ ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ a?

english_verse: Now go! When you speak, I will be with you and give you the words to say.”
translation_verse: Amoso baa yɔ! Meeŋ ya bugi fo kɔnɔ nseŋ ŋini fo kusɔ nɛ feeŋ kaŋɛ bumo.”

english_verse: Moses begged, “Lord, please send someone else to do it.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Mosis naŋ kaŋɛ: “O n Nyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, jande shuŋi esa pɔtɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord became angry with Moses and said: What about your brother Aaron, the Levite? I know he is a good speaker. He is already on his way here to visit you, and he will be happy to see you again.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ agbo pɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ e bishi Mosis le: “Nɛ fo da Ɛɛrɔn nɛ e la Livainyɛn na malɛ? N nyi mo ere ka bee tiŋ a malga nɛnɛ ga. Mo alɛ tea wɔ ekpa to a ba nɛ e ba tu fo. E kaŋ ba wu fo mbe kagbene beeŋ fuli mo ga.

english_verse: Aaron will speak to the people for you, and you will be like me, telling Aaron what to say. I will be with both of you as you speak, and I will tell each of you what to do.
translation_verse: Ɛɛrɔn beeŋ ki dɔɔtɛ m malga n sa basa na n sa fo. Nɛ fo alɛ e baa kaŋɛ mo asɔ nɛ Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ fo na.

english_verse: Now take this walking stick and use it to perform miracles. Moses Returns to Egypt
translation_verse: Ama ta kekpabi ere ŋ keta a yɔ ŋkpal manɛ so, kumo nɛ feeŋ ta a wora emamachisheŋ na.” Mosis ka bɛta a yɔ Ijipt be asheŋ

english_verse: Moses went to his father-in-law Jethro and asked, “Please let me return to Egypt to see if any of my people are still alive.” “All right,” Jethro replied. “I hope all goes well.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis bɛta n yɔ mo shanyɛn Jetro kutɔ n ya kaŋɛ mo le: “Jande, sa ma ekpa nɛ m bɛta n yɔ ma basa kutɔ ashi Ijipt n ya keni b kraa wɔ ŋkpa to a.” Nɛ Jetro kaŋɛ Mosis le: “Ebɔrɛ e yɛr fo nɛ alenfia.”

english_verse: But even before this, the Lord had told Moses, “Leave the land of Midian and return to Egypt. Everyone who wanted to kill you is now dead.”
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ naŋ kaŋɛ Mosis ashi Midian: “Bɛta n yɔ Ijipt be efuli so, ŋkpal manɛ so, basa nɛ b daa fin fo nɛ b mɔ na kikɛ kuraa wu.”

english_verse: So Moses put his wife and sons on donkeys and headed for Egypt, holding the walking stick that had the power of God.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis keta mbe eche nɛ mbe mbinyɛnsobi n chena kurma so nseŋ ta kekpabi nɛ k kɔ Ebɔrɛ be eleŋ na ŋ keta m bɛta a yɔ Ijipt be kasawule so.

english_verse: On the way the Lord said to Moses: When you get to Egypt, go to the king and work the miracles I have shown you. But I will make him so stubborn that he will refuse to let my people go.
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ naŋ kaŋɛ Mosis: “Fo kaŋ fo Ijipt, fo nyiŋi n wora emamachisheŋ nɛ n sa fo amo be eleŋ na kikɛ ashi ewura Fɛɛro be anishito. Ama meeŋ shin nɛ e wora mbe kagbene kpakpa ŋ kini fanɛ e maaŋ shin nɛ basa na e yɔ.

english_verse: Then tell him that I have said, “Israel is my first-born son,
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ fo kaŋɛ ewura Fɛɛro fanɛ ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e kaŋɛ le na: ‘Israɛlebi du fanɛ ma wurkoŋnyɛn nna.

english_verse: and I commanded you to release him, so he could worship me. But you refused, and now I will kill your first-born son.” Zipporah's Son Is Circumcised
translation_verse: Amoso nɛ n yɛ fo shin nɛ ma basa e yɔ n ya bunyaŋ ma na. Nɛ fo baŋ kini, kumo ere, meeŋ mɔ fo wurkoŋnyɛn.’ ”

english_verse: One night while Moses was in camp, the Lord was about to kill him.
translation_verse: B ka bee yɔ Ijipt nseŋ ya fo kakpa ko n dese ŋklade nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ lar Mosis so ndoŋ a shin nɛ e mɔ mo.

english_verse: But Zipporah circumcised her son with a flint knife. She touched his legs with the skin she had cut off and said, “My dear son, this blood will protect you.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ mbe eche Zipora ta kefalta jiso ko ŋ ku mo pibinyɛn be kututu nseŋ ta kumo be kawɔl na m beta Mosis be ayadra ŋ kaŋɛ mo le: “Kashenteŋto naniere fo ki ŋ kul nna, amoso fo maaŋ naŋ wu.”

english_verse: So the Lord did not harm Moses. Then Zipporah said, “Yes, my dear, you are safe because of this circumcision.” Aaron Is Sent To Meet Moses
translation_verse: Ŋkpal ŋklaŋ mo nɛ a daŋ lar katutuku na to so nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ daŋ maŋ mɔ Mosis na.

english_verse: The Lord sent Aaron to meet Moses in the desert. So Aaron met Moses at Mount Sinai and greeted him with a kiss.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Ɛɛrɔn: “Yɔ keshishɛrsawule na ase n ya tu Mosis ndoŋ.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ɛɛrɔn yɔ n ya tu Mosis ashi Sainai be kebeegboŋ na so nseŋ ya ber mo to n chɔrɔ mo kashaso.

english_verse: Moses told Aaron what God had sent him to say; he also told him about the miracles God had given him the power to perform.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nɛ Mosis malɛ kaŋɛ Ɛɛrɔn Enyɛnpe be mmalga nɛ e ta n shuŋi mo na kikɛ nseŋ naŋ kaŋɛ mo emamachisheŋ nɛ Ebɔrɛ ŋini mo fanɛ e ya wora na kikɛ be asheŋ.

english_verse: and Aaron told them what the Lord had sent Moses to say. Then Moses worked the miracles for the people,
translation_verse: Nɛ Ɛɛrɔn kaŋɛ bumo kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ daŋ kaŋɛ Mosis na kikɛ nseŋ naŋ wora emamachisheŋ na basa na be anishito

english_verse: and everyone believed. They bowed down and worshiped the Lord because they knew that he had seen their suffering and was going to help them.
translation_verse: nɛ b yirda kusɔ nɛ e kaŋɛ na. Kumo be buushi, Israɛlebi na ka nu fanɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ wu kananɛ baa tɔrɔ bumo na nsaa shin nɛ e chɛ bumo to nɛ b gbir m bunyaŋ mo.

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king of Egypt and told him, “The Lord God says, ‘Let my people go into the desert, so they can honor me with a celebration there.’ ”
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn yɔ Ijipt be ewura Fɛɛro kutɔ n ya kaŋɛ mo le: “Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ e la Israɛlebi be Ebɔrɛ na yɛ: ‘Shin nɛ ma basa e yɔ n ya wora kejigboŋ m bunyaŋ ma ashi keshishɛrsawule na so.’ ”

english_verse: They answered, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Please let us walk three days into the desert where we can offer sacrifices to him. If you don't, he may strike us down with terrible troubles or with war.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn kaŋɛ: “Israɛlebi be Ebɔrɛ na e lara mbe kumu ŋ ŋini anyi. Amoso sa anyi ekpa nɛ an ta nchɛ asa n nite n yɔ keshishɛrsawule na so n ya lara sarga ndoŋ n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ e la anyi be Ebɔrɛ na. Nɛ mannɛ aloŋ e beeŋ shin nɛ alɔ ŋko kena e ba mɔ anyi.”

english_verse: The king said, “Moses and Aaron, why are you keeping these people from working? Look how many you are keeping from doing their work. Now everyone get back to work!”
translation_verse: Ŋkpal manɛ so, Israɛlebi na e shi ga a chɔ anyi, nɛ menyee sha kelara bumo ashi kushuŋ ere to na!”

english_verse: That same day the king gave orders to his Egyptian slave bosses and to the Israelite men directly in charge of the Israelite slaves. He told them:
translation_verse: Kumo be kamɔnchɛ kikɛ nɛ ewura Fɛɛro kaŋɛ basa nɛ baa keni anya na so na nɛ kushuŋ na be bejuŋkparpoana na le:

english_verse: Don't give the slaves any more straw to put in their bricks. Force them to find their own straw wherever they can,
translation_verse: “Men sa maŋ naa fin afitiri nɛ baa ta a wɔtɔ eshii to a baga a kuya ebirkesi na a sa basa na. Men shin nɛ bumo gbagba e baa yɔ n ya kaa fin amo.

english_verse: but they must make the same number of bricks as before. They are lazy, or else they would not beg me to let them go and sacrifice to their God.
translation_verse: Ama men shin nɛ b baa kraa kuya ebirkesi na nɛ a baa fo kananɛ b chɛr a kuya amo na. Men sa maŋ shin nɛ kukoŋwule gba e duga so. Ntɔl e kɔ bumo so so nɛ baa kaŋɛ le: ‘Shin nɛ an ya lara esarga n sa anyi be Ebɔrɛ.’

english_verse: Make them work so hard that they won't have time to listen to these lies.
translation_verse: Men sa bumo kushuŋ kpakpaso n ti so nɛ b baa shuŋ, saŋɛ na so b maaŋ naa nya dama a nu efɛ be mmalga fuloŋ ere.”

english_verse: The slave bosses and the men in charge of the slaves went out and told them, “The king says he will not give you any more straw.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ basa nɛ baa keni anya na so na nɛ kushuŋ na be bejuŋkparpoana yɔ n ya kaŋɛ Israɛlebi na le: “Ewura Fɛɛro yɛ e maaŋ naŋ sa menyi afitiri nɛ baa ta a wɔtɔ eshii to a kuya ebirkesi na kikɛ.

english_verse: But the slave bosses were hard on them and kept saying, “Each day you have to make as many bricks as you did when you were given straw.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Ijipt be basa nɛ baa keni anya na so na malɛ bɛ so a nyaŋ bumo fanɛ b kuya ebirkesi na nɛ a fo kananɛ a chɛr a fo saŋɛ nɛ b daa sa bumo afitiri na.

english_verse: The bosses beat the men in charge of the slaves and said, “Why didn't you force the slaves to make as many bricks yesterday and today as they did before?”
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ Ijipt be basa nɛ baa keni anya na so na wɔtɔ a bri Israɛlebi na be bejuŋkparpo nɛ b daa juŋkpar bumo kushuŋ na to na nsaa bishi bumo le: “Manɛ so nɛ menyi maa kuya ebirkesi na nɛ a bee fo kananɛ men chɛr a kuya amo saŋkama na?”

english_verse: Finally, the men in charge of the slaves went to the king and said, “Why are you treating us like this?
translation_verse: Ŋkpal loŋ so nɛ Israɛlebi na be bejuŋkparpoana na yɔ ewura Fɛɛro kutɔ n ya fubel ŋ ŋini mo ŋ kaŋɛ le: “Yiramu, mannɛ nna nɛ fo wora fo anya loŋ?

english_verse: No one brings us any straw, but we are still ordered to make the same number of bricks. We are beaten with whips, and your own people are to blame.”
translation_verse: B maŋ naa sa anyi afitiri nɛ anyee ta a wɔtɔ eshii to a kuya ebirkesi na, ama bumo alɛ kraa kaŋɛ fanɛ an baa kuya amo nɛ a baa fo kananɛ an chɛr a kuya amo na. Hale ŋkpal loŋ so a bri anyi. Mannɛ anyi alɛ e bar kuko, fo basa na gbagba e maŋ wora n nyalɛ.”

english_verse: The king replied, “You are lazy—nothing but lazy! That's why you keep asking me to let you go and sacrifice to your Lord.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura Fɛɛro kaŋɛ bumo le: “Betɔlpo e la menyi kashenteŋto, amoso nɛ men ba kaa kaŋɛ ma fanɛ n shin nɛ men yɔ n ya lara sarga n sa men ‘Nyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.’

english_verse: Get back to work! You won't be given straw, but you must still make the same number of bricks.”
translation_verse: Men bɛta epul ere to n ya kaa shuŋ men be ashuŋ! B maaŋ sa menyi afitiri na kuraa. Menyi alɛ kraa beeŋ baa kuya ebirkesi na nɛ a baa fo kananɛ men chɛr a kuya amo na.”

english_verse: The men knew they were in deep trouble when they were ordered to make the same number of bricks each day.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Israɛlebi na be bejuŋkparpoana na pin fanɛ awurfoŋ tu bumo kashenteŋto ŋkpal b ka kaŋɛ bumo fanɛ karechɛ kama be ebirkesi nɛ baaŋ baa kuya na maaŋ duga so kikɛ na so.

english_verse: After they left the king, they went to see Moses and Aaron, who had been waiting for them.
translation_verse: B ka baŋ lar ewura Fɛɛro kutɔ nɛ b ba tu Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn nɛ b yil a jo bumo.

english_verse: Then the men said, “We hope the Lord will punish both of you for making the king and his officials hate us. Now they even have an excuse to kill us.” The Lord's Promise to Moses
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ b kaŋɛ bumo le: “Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ gbagba wu kusɔ nɛ men wora anyi nna na. Mo alɛ beeŋ gberge menyi kusoe, ŋkpal men ka shin nɛ ewura Fɛɛro nɛ mbe basa nya agbo n wora anyi nseŋ sa bumo ekpa fanɛ b mɔ anyi na so.”

english_verse: Moses left them and prayed, “Our Lord, why have you brought so much trouble on your people? Is that why you sent me here?
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis naŋ lɔŋɛ m bishi Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ le: “Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, manɛ e ba nɛ fo ta tɔrɔ m ba fo basa ere so le? Ama le so nɛ fo shuŋi ma nfe a?

english_verse: Ever since you told me to speak to the king, he has caused nothing but trouble for these people. And you haven't done a thing to help.”
translation_verse: Yili saŋɛ nɛ fo shuŋi ma fanɛ m ba yili fo katelamu to m malga n sa ewura Fɛɛro na kikɛ nɛ e baa wɔtɔ a tɔrɔ Israɛlebi ere, ama fo alɛ maŋ wora shɛŋ n chɛ fo basa to kuraa.”

english_verse: The Lord God told Moses: Soon you will see what I will do to the king. Because of my mighty power, he will let my people go, and he will even chase them out of his country.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Mosis le: “Naniere bre feeŋ wu kusɔ nɛ meeŋ wora ewura Fɛɛro. Ŋkpal ma eleŋ nɛ ŋ kɔ na so, e beeŋ shin nɛ ma basa e yɔ. Kashenteŋ nɛ mee kaŋɛ fo na fanɛ meeŋ tintiŋ mo hale nɛ e ju bumo nɛ b lar mbe kasawule ere so.” Ebɔrɛ ka naŋ tre Mosis be asheŋ

english_verse: But when I appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, I came as God All-Powerful and did not use my name.
translation_verse: N daŋ lar men nananyɛnana Eebraham nɛ Aizek nɛ Jeekɔb so fanɛ Ebɔrɛ Elempo nna, ama n daa maŋ shin nɛ b pin fanɛ ma e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.

english_verse: Now I have seen how the people of Israel are suffering because of the Egyptians, and I will keep my promise.
translation_verse: Kede malɛ be buushi naniere bre n nu Israɛl be basa nɛ Ijiptebi nyaŋ n wɔtɔ a tɔrɔ fanɛ anya na be kushu nseŋ nyiŋi ma kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre be kɔnɔ naseso na.

english_verse: I will accept you as my people, and I will be your God. Then you will know that I was the one who rescued you from the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Menyeeŋ ba kraa la ŋ gbagba be basa nɛ ma alɛ e baa la menyi be Ebɔrɛ. Saŋɛ na so nɛ menyeeŋ pin fanɛ ma e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ e la menyi be Ebɔrɛ nɛ e lara menyi kenyaya to ashi Ijiptebi be enɔ to.

english_verse: I will bring you into the land that I solemnly promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and it will be yours. I am the Lord!”
translation_verse: Meeŋ yɛr menyi kasawule nɛ n nase kɔnɔ fanɛ meeŋ ta n sa Eebraham nɛ Aizek nɛ Jeekɔb na so. Ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na beeŋ ta kumo n sa menyi nɛ k baa la menyeya.’ ”

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Mosis:

english_verse: But Moses replied, “I'm not a powerful speaker. If the Israelites won't listen to me, why should the king of Egypt?”
translation_verse: Nɛ Mosis kaŋɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ: “Keni, Israɛlebi na gba e kini kenu n sa ma na nɛ nuso nɛ ewura Fɛɛro bre beeŋ nu n sa ma nɛ m maŋ nyi kamalga ere?”

english_verse: But the Lord sent Aaron and Moses with a message for the Israelites and for the king. He also ordered Aaron and Moses to free the people from Egypt. Family Record of Aaron and Moses
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn fanɛ b ya kaŋɛ Israɛlebi na nɛ Ijipt be ewura Fɛɛro, kenishipereso fanɛ e shin nɛ Israɛlebi na e lar ashi Ijipt be efuli so.

english_verse: The following men were the heads of their ancestral clans: The sons of Reuben, Jacob's oldest son, were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
translation_verse: Ruben nɛ e daa la Jeekɔb pibinyɛn wurkoŋ na be mbinyɛnsoana be atre e daa la Hanɔk nɛ Pallu nɛ Hesron nɛ Karmi. Bumo e ki Ruben be kanaŋ be mbunana na.

english_verse: Gershon's sons were Libni and Shimei.
translation_verse: Gɛshɔn be mbinyɛnsobi nde: Libni nɛ Shimei.

english_verse: Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. All of the above were from the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Mɛrari be mbinyɛnsobi malɛ be atre e daa la Maali nɛ Mushi. Bumo alɛ e ki Livaiebi be kanaŋ to be mbuna na.

english_verse: Izhar's sons were Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri.
translation_verse: Ishar be mbinyɛnsobi be atre e daa la Koora nɛ Nefeg nɛ Zikri.

english_verse: Uzziel's sons were Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri.
translation_verse: Uziɛl malɛ be mbinyɛnsobi be atre e daa la Mishaal nɛ Elzafan nɛ Sitri.

english_verse: Aaron married Elisheba. She was the daughter of Amminadab and the sister of Nahshon; they had four sons, Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
translation_verse: Nɛ Ɛɛrɔn malɛ ta Elisheba nɛ e daa la Aminadab pibiche nsaa la Nashɔn malɛ mo sipoche na ŋ ki mbe eche nɛ mo nɛ mo kurge Nadab nɛ Abihu nɛ Eleazar nɛ Itama.

english_verse: Aaron's son Eleazar married one of Putiel's daughters, and their son was Phinehas. This ends the list of those who were the heads of clans in the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ɛɛrɔn pibinyɛn Eleazar malɛ ta Putiɛl pibiche ko ŋ ki mbe eche nɛ mo nɛ mo kurge Finihas. To, bumo e daa la Livai be kanaŋ to be mbuna be benimu.

english_verse: The Lord had commanded Aaron and Moses to lead every family and tribe of Israel out of Egypt,
translation_verse: To, loŋ be Ɛɛrɔn ere gbagba nɛ Mosis e daa la basa nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ daŋ kaŋɛ le na: “Men ya lara Israɛl be basa kanaŋ kanaŋ so ashi Ijipt be kasawule so.”

english_verse: and so they told the king of Egypt to set the people of Israel free. The Lord Commands Moses and Aaron To Speak to the King
translation_verse: Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn ere e daŋ malga n sa Ijipt be ewura Fɛɛro fanɛ e sa Israɛl be basa ekpa nɛ b lar ashi Ijipt na. Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ka sa Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn kamalga be asheŋ

english_verse: When the Lord spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt,
translation_verse: To, kachɛ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ daŋ malga n sa Mosis ashi Ijipt be kasawule so na,

english_verse: he said, “I am the Lord. Tell the king of Egypt everything I say to you.”
translation_verse: le nɛ e kaŋɛ: “Ma e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na. Amoso, kaŋɛ Ijipt be ewura Fɛɛro asheŋ nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ fo ere kikɛ.”

english_verse: But Moses answered, “You know I am a very poor speaker, and the king will never listen to me.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Mosis kaŋɛ mo le: “Enyɛnpe, fo nyi ŋ ka maa tiŋ kamalga nɛ nuso nɛ meeŋ wora m malga nɛ Fɛɛro e nu n sa ma?”

english_verse: The Lord said: I am going to let your brother Aaron speak for you. He will tell your message to the king, just as a prophet speaks my message to the people.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Mosis le: “Keni meeŋ shin nɛ fo yili ma katelamu to n yɔ ewura Fɛɛro be anishito, nɛ fo da Ɛɛrɔn malɛ e malga n sa mo fanɛ anebi.

english_verse: Tell Aaron everything I say to you, and he will order the king to let my people leave his country.
translation_verse: Fo e naaŋ baa malga asheŋ nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ fo na kikɛ a sa Ɛɛrɔn nɛ mo alɛ e kaŋɛ Fɛɛro fanɛ e shin nɛ Israɛl be basa na e lar mbe kasawule so.

english_verse: But I will make the king so stubborn that he won't listen to you. He won't listen even when I do many terrible things to him and his nation. Then I will bring a final punishment on Egypt, and the king will let Israel's families and tribes go.
translation_verse: Fɛɛro kraa maaŋ nu n sa fo. Kumo be kaman meeŋ shin nɛ b wu ma eleŋ, nɛ m bar kasogberge kpakpaso damta Ijiptebi so pɔɛŋ nseŋ juŋkpar ma basa Israɛlebi be nnaŋana na n lar Ijipt be kasawule na so.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Moses, when the king asks you and Aaron to perform a miracle, command Aaron to throw his walking stick down in front of the king, and it will turn into a snake.”
translation_verse: “Nɛ ewura Fɛɛro ka baŋ kaŋɛ menyi le: ‘Men wora kemamachisheŋ ko nɛ k ŋini fanɛ kusɔ nɛ men kaŋɛ ere la kashenteŋ nna.’ Fo kaŋɛ Ɛɛrɔn le: ‘Ta fo kekpabi na n lɛ Fɛɛro be anishito, k beeŋ kilgi kuwɔ.’ ”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king and his officials and did exactly as the Lord had commanded—Aaron threw the stick down, and it turned into a snake.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn yɔ ewura Fɛɛro kutɔ n ya wora kananɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ŋini bumo na. Ɛɛrɔn daŋ ta kekpabi na nna n lɛ Fɛɛro nɛ mbe benimu be anishito nɛ k kilgi kuwɔ.

english_verse: Then the king called in the wise men and the magicians, who used their secret powers to do the same thing—
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Fɛɛro malɛ tre mbe benyiashempo nɛ ŋkilgiwuraana nɛ bumo alɛ gba ba ta bumo be ŋkilgi n wora loŋ gbagba chap.

english_verse: The king behaved just as the Lord had said and stubbornly refused to listen. The Nile River Turns into Blood
translation_verse: Ama ade kikɛ be kaman Fɛɛro kraŋ wora kagbene kpakpaso nna nseŋ kini kenu n sa Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn fanɛ kananɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ na. Nchuana ka kilgi ŋklaŋ be asheŋ

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: The Egyptian king stubbornly refuses to change his mind and let the people go.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ naŋ kaŋɛ Mosis le: “Fɛɛro be kagbene du kpakpa ga, kumo so nɛ e kini fanɛ e maaŋ shin nɛ basa na e yɔ na.

english_verse: Tomorrow morning take the stick that turned into a snake, then wait beside the Nile River for the king.
translation_verse: Amoso wule n yɔ Fɛɛro kutɔ kachipurso, saŋɛ nɛ e lar a yɔ Nail be lɔr to na. Ta kekpabi nɛ k daŋ kilgi kuwɔ na ŋ keta n ya kaa jo mo lɔrkar.

english_verse: Tell him, “The Lord God of the Hebrews sent me to order you to release his people, so they can worship him in the desert. But until now, you have paid no attention.
translation_verse: E kaŋ ba nɛ fo kaŋɛ mo le: ‘Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, Israɛlebi be Ebɔrɛ na e shuŋi ma fo kutɔ fanɛ ŋ kaŋɛ fo fanɛ fo shin nɛ mbe basa e yɔ keshishɛrsawule so n ya bunyaŋ mo’, ama hale mbre fo maŋ naŋ nu n sa ma.
