english_verse: “The Lord is going to do something to show you that he really is the Lord. I will strike the Nile with this stick, and the water will turn into blood.
translation_verse: Amoso Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na yɛ: ‘Kesheŋ nɛ mee sha kewora ere e naaŋ shin nɛ fo pin fanɛ ma e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.’ Keni, meeŋ ta kekpabi nɛ k wɔ ma enɔ to ere ŋ ŋmɛa Nail be nchu ere so nɛ a kilgi ŋklaŋ.

english_verse: The fish will die, the river will stink, and none of you Egyptians will be able to drink the water.”
translation_verse: Meeŋ wora loŋ nɛ lɔr na to be ekɔrɔtɔ kikɛ e wu m bɛ a dufɛ nɛ Ijiptebi e nuu kumo to be nchu ŋ gben.”

english_verse: Moses, then command Aaron to hold his stick over the water. And when he does, every drop of water in Egypt will turn into blood, including rivers, canals, ponds, and even the water in buckets and jars.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Mosis le: “Kaŋɛ Ɛɛrɔn le: ‘Teŋi fo kekpabi na n shoŋi Ijipt be nchuana fanɛ eboŋana nɛ nchu be abɔr kursoana nɛ apaana nɛ edampuana nɛ atirbuana kikɛ nɛ a ki ŋklaŋ.’ Ijiptebi be asɔ nɛ baa saŋ nchu a wɔtɔ kikɛ fanɛ mpuya nɛ eboketi nɛ echeenshigboŋ nɛ egarwa kikɛ to be nchu beeŋ ki ŋklaŋ.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron obeyed the Lord. Aaron held out his stick, then struck the Nile, as the king and his officials watched. The river turned into blood,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn wora kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ŋini bumo na. Ɛɛrɔn daŋ maŋ mbe kekpabi so ashi Fɛɛro nɛ mbe beyaasepoana na be anishito nna ŋ ŋmɛa Nail be nchu so nɛ nchu na kikɛ kilgi ŋklaŋ.

english_verse: the fish died, and the water smelled so bad that none of the Egyptians could drink it. Blood was everywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: Nɛ ekɔrɔtɔ nɛ a daa wɔ Nail be lɔr na to kikɛ wu nɛ nchu na fara a dufɛ puŋ puŋ puŋ nɛ Ijiptebi na nuu amo ŋ gben. Ŋklaŋ e daa la kaplɛkama ashi Ijipt to.

english_verse: But the Egyptian magicians used their secret powers to do the same thing. The king did just as the Lord had said—he stubbornly refused to listen.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ijipt be ŋkilgiwuraana malɛ gba ta bumo be ademansheŋ be ŋkilgi n wora loŋ koŋwule na nɛ Fɛɛro be kagbene naŋ ki kpakpa n ti so nɛ e kini kenu n sa Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn fanɛ kananɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ na.

english_verse: Then he went back to his palace and never gave it a second thought.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Fɛɛro kilgi n choŋ mbe laŋ to nɛ k maŋ tir mo gba kuraa.

english_verse: The Egyptians had to dig holes along the banks of the Nile for drinking water, because water from the river was unfit to drink. Frogs
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ijiptebi na kikɛ fara a kur a kur Nail be lɔr na be ekarso kikɛ a fin nchu nuuso ŋkpal b ka daa maŋ naa tiŋ a nuu lɔr na to be nchu so so.

english_verse: Seven days after the Lord had struck the Nile,
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ka jija nchu na be nchɛnshunu.

english_verse: he said to Moses: Go to the palace and tell the king of Egypt that I order him to let my people go, so they can worship me.
translation_verse: Nɛ e kaŋɛ Mosis le: “Yɔ Fɛɛro kutɔ n ya kaŋɛ mo: ‘Kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ e la fanɛ fo shin nɛ mbe basa e yɔ, saŋɛ na so baaŋ ya bunyaŋ mo.’

english_verse: If he refuses, I will cover his entire country with frogs.
translation_verse: Nɛ fo baŋ kini keshin nɛ b yɔ, meeŋ shin nɛ epulo e ba sɔ fo efuli ere kikɛ so.

english_verse: Warn the king that the Nile will be full of frogs, and from there they will spread into the royal palace, including the king's bedroom and even his bed. Frogs will enter the homes of his officials and will find their way into ovens and into the bowls of bread dough.
translation_verse: Nail be lɔr ere kikɛ beeŋ bɔlɔ epulo nɛ b lar m ba fo laŋ to m ba luri fo ebu deseto to n dii n sɔ fo gedo so. A beeŋ luri fo beyaasepoana nɛ fo basa kikɛ be elaŋana to. Epulo beeŋ ba kaa wɔ men be bodobodo be etɔkpaana nɛ men be asɔ nɛ menyee gbiti ebodobodo kikɛ to.

english_verse: Frogs will be crawling on everyone—the king, his officials, and every citizen of Egypt.
translation_verse: Epulo na beeŋ ba kaa dii fo nɛ fo basa nɛ beyaasepo kikɛ so.”

english_verse: Moses, now command Aaron to hold his stick over the water. Then frogs will come from all rivers, canals, and ponds in Egypt, and they will cover the land.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ naŋ kaŋɛ Mosis le: “Kaŋɛ Ɛɛrɔn nɛ e teŋi mbe kekpabi na n shoŋi mbombi nɛ nchu be abɔr kurso nɛ apa kikɛ so n shin nɛ epulo e ba Ijipt be kasawule so kikɛ.”

english_verse: But the magicians used their secret powers to do the same thing.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ŋkilgiwuraana na gba ta bumo be ŋkilgi n wora bumo be ewulosheŋ, nɛ epulo ba Ijipt be kasawule na so.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “If you ask the Lord to take these frogs away from me and my people, I will let your people go and offer sacrifices to him.”
translation_verse: Ama ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ Fɛɛro naŋ tre Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn ŋ kaŋɛ bumo: “Men kule Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ e ta epulo ere ashi ma nɛ ma basa so nɛ n shin nɛ basa na e yɔ n ya lara esarga n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.”

english_verse: “All right,” Moses answered. “You choose the time when I am to pray for the frogs to stop bothering you, your officials, and your people, and for them to leave your houses and be found only in the river.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Mosis kaŋɛ Fɛɛro le: “Kaŋɛ ma saŋɛ nɛ fee sha fanɛ ŋ kule Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ n sa fo nɛ fo beyaasepo nɛ fo basa nɛ epulo na e lar menyi be elaŋana to n ya ka wɔ Nail be lɔr na to nawule?”

english_verse: After Moses and Aaron left the palace, Moses begged the Lord to do something about the frogs he had sent as punishment for the king.
translation_verse: Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn ka lar Fɛɛro kutɔ nɛ Mosis ya kule Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ a laŋɛ epulo nɛ mo ere Ebɔrɛ daŋ bar nɛ e ba gberge Fɛɛro kusoe na be kaplɛa so.

english_verse: The dead frogs were placed in piles, and the whole country began to stink.
translation_verse: Nɛ Ijiptebi na bela epulo wuso na n deŋi n deŋi abar so le kululu nɛ b bɛ a dufɛ puŋ puŋ puŋ kasawule na so kikɛ.

english_verse: But when the king saw that things were now better, he again did just as the Lord had said he would and stubbornly refused to listen to Moses and Aaron. Gnats
translation_verse: Fɛɛro ka wu fanɛ epulo na be tɔrɔ na loge nɛ e naŋ wora mbe kagbene kpakpa nseŋ kini kenu n sa Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn fanɛ kananɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ na. Asɔ firgisobi duŋso ko be asheŋ

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Command Aaron to strike the ground with his walking stick, and everywhere in Egypt the dust will turn into gnats.”
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ naŋ kaŋɛ Mosis: “Kaŋɛ Ɛɛrɔn fanɛ e ta mbe kekpabi na ŋ ŋmɛa kasawule be shishɛr so nɛ a kilgi asɔ firgisobi duŋso ko n sɔ Ijipt be kasawule so kikɛ.”

english_verse: They obeyed, and when Aaron struck the ground with the stick, gnats started swarming on people and animals. In fact, every speck of dust in Egypt turned into a gnat.
translation_verse: Nɛ loŋ wora. Ɛɛrɔn daŋ teŋi mbe kekpabi na nna ŋ ŋmɛa kasawule na be shishɛr so nɛ eshishɛr na kilgi asɔ firgiso duŋso ko m mel edimɛdi nɛ asɔbɔya kikɛ so. Ijipt be kasawule so be eshishɛr kikɛ daŋ kilgi asɔ firgiso duŋso na nna n sɔ Ijipt be kaplɛkama.

english_verse: The magicians told the king, “God has done this.” But, as the Lord had said, the king was too stubborn to listen. Flies
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ŋkilgiwuraana kaŋɛ Fɛɛro le: “Ebɔrɛ ko be eleŋ be aworbi nde.” Ama Fɛɛro daŋ kraŋ wora kagbene kpakpaso nna ŋ kini kewora kasonu fanɛ kananɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ na. Ashushombi be tɔrɔ be asheŋ

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: Early tomorrow morning, while the king is on his way to the river, go and say to him, “The Lord commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him.
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ naŋ kaŋɛ Mosis: “Wule ŋ koso echefo chipurso n ya tu Fɛɛro saŋɛ nɛ e bee yɔ lɔr ase na ŋ kaŋɛ mo fanɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ yɛ: ‘Shin nɛ ma basa e yɔ n ya bunyaŋ ma.

english_verse: If you don't, he will send swarms of flies to attack you, your officials, and every citizen of your country. Your houses will be full of flies, and the ground will crawl with them.
translation_verse: Nɛ fo baŋ maŋ shin nɛ ma basa yɔ, meeŋ shin nɛ ashushombi damta e buu fo nɛ fo beyaasepoana nɛ fo basa kikɛ so nseŋ luri m bɔlɔ menyi be ebuana gba to hale n ya lar elaŋ to kikɛ.

english_verse: The Lord kept his promise—the palace and the homes of the royal officials swarmed with flies, and the rest of the country was infested with them as well.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ wora loŋ n shin nɛ ashushombi damta ba m ba bɔlɔ Fɛɛro be kowu kikɛ to nɛ beko malɛ yɔ mbe beyaasepoana be elaŋana to nɛ Ijipt be kasawule so kikɛ a sha kejija kasawule na kikɛ kuraa.

english_verse: Then the king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Go ahead and sacrifice to your God, but stay here in Egypt.”
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Fɛɛro shuŋi n tre Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn ŋ kaŋɛ bumo le: “Men yɔ n ya lara sarga na n sa menyi be Ebɔrɛ ashi Ijipt be kasawule ere so nfe.”

english_verse: No indeed! The Lord has ordered us to walk three days into the desert before offering sacrifices to him, and that's what we have to do.”
translation_verse: K daga fanɛ an ta nchɛ asa n nite n yɔ keshishɛrsawule na so n ya lara sarga na n sa Enyɛnpe anyi be Ebɔrɛ na fanɛ kananɛ mo gbagba yili anyi na.”

english_verse: Then the king told him, “I'll let you go into the desert to offer sacrifices, if you don't go very far. But in the meantime, pray for me.”
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ Fɛɛro kaŋɛ: “To, n nu, meeŋ shin nɛ men yɔ keshishɛrsawule na so ya lara sarga n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ e la men be Ebɔrɛ na, ama men sa maŋ yɔ kufɔ ga bre. Ama pɔɛŋ nɛ men yɔ men kule Ebɔrɛ nɛ ashushombi ere e yɔ ŋ ka anyi.”

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” Moses replied, “I'll pray for you as soon as I leave, and by tomorrow the flies will stop bothering you, your officials, and the citizens of your country. Only make sure that you're telling the truth this time and that you really intend to let our people offer sacrifices to the Lord.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis kaŋɛ mo le: “M baŋ lar fo kutɔ meeŋ ya kule Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ ashushombi na e lar fo nɛ fo beyaasepo nɛ fo basa so echefo kikɛ. Ama sa maŋ fule anyi nseŋ naŋ kini keshin nɛ basa na e yɔ.”

english_verse: and the Lord answered his prayer. Not a fly was left to pester the king, his officials, or anyone else in Egypt.
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nu Mosis be kekule na nseŋ shin nɛ ashushombi na shile ewura Fɛɛro nɛ mbe beyaasepo nɛ mbe basa kikɛ so nɛ ekoŋwule gba maŋ naŋ ka kasawule na so.

english_verse: But the king turned stubborn again and would not let the people go.
translation_verse: Ama kumo alɛ gba be kaman, ewura Fɛɛro daŋ wora kagbene kpakpaso nna ŋ kini fanɛ e maŋ shin nɛ basa na e yɔ.

english_verse: The Lord sent Moses with this message for the king of Egypt: The Lord God of the Hebrews commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him.
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ naŋ kaŋɛ Mosis: “Yɔ Fɛɛro kutɔ n ya kaŋɛ mo fanɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, Israɛlebi be Ebɔrɛ na yɛ: ‘Shin nɛ ma basa e yɔ, saŋɛ na so baaŋ ya bunyaŋ ma.

english_verse: he will bring a terrible disease on your horses and donkeys, your camels and cattle, and your sheep and goats.
translation_verse: meeŋ ta kulɔ lubi n lɛ men be asɔbɔya, fanɛ egbaŋɛ nɛ ekurma nɛ enyɔma nɛ ana nɛ mbolpɔ nɛ mboe kikɛ so.

english_verse: But the Lord will protect the animals that belong to the people of Israel, and none of theirs will die.
translation_verse: Ama ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na beeŋ barga Israɛlebi be asɔbɔya nɛ Ijiptebi be asɔbɔya to nseŋ shin nɛ Israɛl be basa bre be asɔbɔya e sa maŋ wu.’ ”

english_verse: Tomorrow is the day the Lord has set to do this.
translation_verse: Ade be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ: “Echefo nɛ ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ beeŋ wora le be kesheŋ ashi kasawule ere so.”

english_verse: It happened the next day—all of the animals belonging to the Egyptians died, but the Israelites did not lose even one.
translation_verse: Kumo be ŋklade nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ wora loŋ be kesheŋ na fanɛ kananɛ e kaŋɛ na nɛ Ijiptebi be asɔbɔya kikɛ kuraa wu, ama Israɛlebi na bre be kusɔbɔya koŋwule gba daa maŋ wu.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses and Aaron: Take a few handfuls of ashes from a stove and you, Moses, throw them into the air. Be sure the king is watching.
translation_verse: Kede malɛ be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ naŋ kaŋɛ Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn le: “Men jɔ nsunɔ ashi kakpa nɛ edɛ gboŋ chɔɔ m bɔlɔ menyi be enɔana, nseŋ shin nɛ Mosis e ta amo ŋ kpa awɔlto ashi ewura Fɛɛro be anishito.

english_verse: The ashes will blow across the land of Egypt, causing sores to break out on people and animals.
translation_verse: Saŋɛ na so nsunɔ na beeŋ ki shishɛr mushimushibi n sɔ Ijipt be kasawule so kikɛ nɛ alɔbi e pɛ edimɛdi nɛ asɔbɔya kikɛ nyam ashi kasawule na kikɛ nyam so.”

english_verse: So they took a few handfuls of ashes and went to the king. Moses threw them into the air, and sores immediately broke out on the Egyptians and their animals.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ b jɔ nsunɔ na n ya yili ewura Fɛɛro be anishito nɛ Mosis ta amo ŋ kpa awɔlto nɛ a kilgi alɔbi m pɛ edimɛdi nɛ asɔbɔya kikɛ nyam.

english_verse: The magicians were suffering so much from the sores, that they could not even come to Moses.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal loŋ be alɔbi na ka daŋ pɛ ŋkilgiwuraana na gba so b daa maŋ naŋ tiŋ n yili Mosis be anishito.

english_verse: Everything happened just as the Lord had told Moses—he made the king too stubborn to listen to Moses and Aaron. Hailstones
translation_verse: Ama ade kikɛ gba be kaman, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kraŋ shin nɛ ewura Fɛɛro wora kagbene kpakpaso nseŋ kini kenu n sa Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn fanɛ kananɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ baŋ kaŋɛ na.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to get up early the next morning and say to the king: The Lord God of the Hebrews commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him!
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ naŋ kaŋɛ Mosis le: “Echefo kachipurdidi, fo wule ŋ koso n ya tu ewura Fɛɛro ŋ kaŋɛ mo fanɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ Israɛlebi be Ebɔrɛ na yɛ: ‘Shin nɛ ma basa e yɔ, saŋɛ na so baaŋ ya bunyaŋ ma.

english_verse: If you don't, he will send his worst plagues to strike you, your officials, and everyone else in your country. Then you will find out that no one can oppose the Lord.
translation_verse: Nɛ mannɛ aloŋ, meeŋ shin nɛ kulɔ lubi nɛ k chɔ etɔrɔana ere kikɛ e tu fo nɛ fo beyaasepo nɛ fo basa kikɛ nɛ fo pin fanɛ esa kikɛ maŋ naa wɔtɔ a du fanɛ ma ashi durnya ere to kikɛ.

english_verse: In fact, he could already have sent a terrible disease and wiped you from the face of the earth.
translation_verse: Kashenteŋto, nɛ n daa sha nna n dafanɛ n shin nɛ kulɔ lubi mo nɛ k daa beeŋ tiŋ m mur fo nɛ fo basa kikɛ ashi kasawule ere so ba menyi so n chɛr.

english_verse: But he has kept you alive, just to show you his power and to bring honor to himself everywhere in the world.
translation_verse: Ama ŋkpal ŋ ka bee sha fanɛ ŋ ŋini fo ma eleŋ so nɛ n shin nɛ fo kraa wɔtɔ na, saŋɛ na so durnya ere be esa kama beeŋ pin esa nɛ e la ma.

english_verse: You are still determined not to let the Lord's people go.
translation_verse: Ŋkeshin nɛ fo alɛ kraa wɔtɔ nna a ŋini ma basa fo eleŋ nsaa kini keshin nɛ b yɔ.

english_verse: Some of the king's officials were frightened by what the Lord had said, and they hurried off to make sure their slaves and animals were safe.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Fɛɛro be beyaasepo nɛ b daŋ yirda Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be kamalga na nya manaŋ n shin nɛ bumo be anya nɛ asɔbɔya kikɛ shile n luri ebu to.

english_verse: But others paid no attention to his threats and left their slaves and animals out in the open.
translation_verse: Ama bekama nɛ b daŋ kplaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be kamalga na so na bre daŋ shin nna nɛ bumo be anya nɛ asɔbɔya na a kilgi to.

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sky, so that hailstones will fall on people, animals, and crops in the land of Egypt.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Mosis le: “Teŋi fo enɔ ŋ ŋini awɔlto nɛ abɔrɛjembubi gbɛgbɛso na e tɔr edimɛdi nɛ asɔbɔya nɛ asɔ duuso nɛ a wɔ Ijipt be kasawule so na kikɛ so.”

english_verse: Moses pointed his walking stick toward the sky, and hailstones started falling everywhere. Thunder roared, and lightning flashed back and forth, striking the ground. This was the worst storm in the history of Egypt.
translation_verse: Ijipt ka fara kikɛ loŋ be abɔrɛjembubi be bɔrɛ na be kaduli maŋ naŋ ba kumo be kasawule so kikɛ.

english_verse: Only Goshen, where the Israelites lived, was safe from the storm.
translation_verse: Kakpa nɛ Israɛlebi na daa wɔ nɛ baa tre ndoŋ Goshen na nawule nɛ abɔrɛjembubi be bɔrɛgboŋ na daa maŋ yɔ.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Now I have really sinned! My people and I are guilty, and the Lord is right.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Fɛɛro naŋ shuŋi n tre Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn m ba kaŋɛ bumo le: “Kede bre to, m pin fanɛ n wora kulubi. Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e kɔ akpa. Ma nɛ ma basa kikɛ wora alubi.

english_verse: We can't stand any more of this thunder and hail. Please ask the Lord to make it stop. Your people can go—you don't have to stay in Egypt any longer.”
translation_verse: Amoso kule Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ n sa anyi, ŋkpal manɛ so, bɔrɛ na be keponte nɛ abɔrɛjembubi na wora kebanso. Naniere bre n sa menyi ekpa fanɛ men baa yɔ. A maŋ naŋ daga fanɛ men baa kraa wɔ nfe.”

english_verse: Moses answered, “As soon as I leave the city, I will lift my arms in prayer. When the thunder and hail stop, you will know that the earth belongs to the Lord.
translation_verse: Nɛ Mosis malɛ kaŋɛ mo: “Ŋ kaŋ baŋ lar kade ere to na nɛ meeŋ maŋ ma enɔana so ŋ kule Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ e shin nɛ bɔrɛ na be keponte nɛ abɔrɛjembubi gbɛgbɛso na kikɛ e ku nɛ fo pin fanɛ durnya ere la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na peya nna.

english_verse: But I am certain that neither you nor your officials really fear the Lord God.”
translation_verse: Ama n nyi fo nɛ fo beyaasepo ka maa ŋana Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, the flax and barley crops had been destroyed by the storm because they were ready to ripen.
translation_verse: Bɔrɛ na tiŋ n jija aboyu nɛ ayu bre, ŋkpal amo ere ka bee wora manaŋ manaŋ so.

english_verse: But the wheat crops ripen later, and they were not damaged.
translation_verse: Ama enyaŋkpaŋ nɛ adurbi bre be kekama daa maŋ jija, ŋkpal amo ere ka maa wule a wora so.

english_verse: After Moses left the royal palace and the city, he lifted his arms in prayer to the Lord, and the thunder, hail, and drenching rain stopped.
translation_verse: Ade be kaman nɛ Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn lar ewura Fɛɛro kutɔ nɛ kade na to nɛ Mosis maŋ mbe enɔana so ŋ kule Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ bɔrɛ na be keponte na nɛ abɔrɛjembubi gbɛgbɛso na kikɛ nɛ bɔrɛchu nɛ k daa chulgi kasawule na so na kikɛ ku kuraa.

english_verse: When the king realized that the storm was over, he disobeyed once more. He and his officials were so stubborn
translation_verse: Ama Fɛɛro ka wu fanɛ bɔrɛchu na nɛ abɔrɛjembubi gbɛgbɛso na nɛ bɔrɛ be keponte na kikɛ yige nɛ mo nɛ mbe beyaasepo naaŋ wora ŋgbene kpakpaso.

english_verse: that he refused to let the Israelites go. This was exactly what the Lord had said would happen.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura Fɛɛro naŋ kini keshin nɛ Israɛl be basa na e yɔ fanɛ kananɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ daŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ e beeŋ shin nɛ e wora na.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: Go back to the king. I have made him and his officials stubborn, so that I could work these miracles.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ naŋ kaŋɛ Mosis le: “Naŋ yɔ ewura Fɛɛro kutɔ n ya shin nɛ mo nɛ mbe beyaasepo kikɛ be ŋgbene e ki kpakpa, saŋɛ na so meeŋ wora ma emamachisheŋ ere nɛ b wu amo.

english_verse: I did this because I want you to tell your children and your grandchildren about my miracles and about my harsh treatment of the Egyptians. Then all of you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Kumo be loŋ beeŋ shin nɛ menyi alɛ gba e kaŋɛ men be mbia nɛ men nanabiana kananɛ n daŋ wora emamachisheŋ ashi Ijiptebi be anishito, saŋɛ na so menyi kikɛ beeŋ pin fanɛ ma e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king and told him that the Lord God of the Hebrews had said: How long will you stubbornly refuse to obey? Release my people so they can worship me.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn naŋ yɔ Fɛɛro kutɔ n ya kaŋɛ mo fanɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, Israɛlebi be Ebɔrɛ na yɛ: “Shin nɛ ma basa e yɔ, saŋɛ na so, baaŋ ya bunyaŋ ma.

english_verse: Do this by tomorrow, or I will cover your country with so many locusts
translation_verse: Nɛ fo baŋ kini keshin nɛ ma basa yɔ, meeŋ shin nɛ elotɔr e ba fo efuli ere so echefo.

english_verse: that you won't be able to see the ground. Most of your crops were ruined by the hailstones, but these locusts will destroy what little is left, including the trees.
translation_verse: Baaŋ ba mel kasawule so kikɛ nna gbi nɛ esa kama maŋ naŋ tiŋ n wu kasawule gbagba kenishiso. Baaŋ ji kusɔ kama nɛ abɔrɛjembubi na jija ŋ ka na kikɛ nyam n ta kedibi kama nɛ k wɔ men be adɔana to n ti so.

english_verse: Your palace, the homes of your officials, and all the other houses in Egypt will overflow with more locusts than have ever been seen in this country. After Moses left the palace,
translation_verse: Baaŋ luri m bɔlɔ fo nɛ fo beyaasepo nɛ Ijiptebi kikɛ be elaŋana to. K beeŋ baa la kusɔ nɛ men tutoana na ŋko men nanaana gba maŋ naŋ wu ŋ ku so, yili saŋɛ nɛ b ba kasawule ere so kikɛ m ba fo nɛ mbre.” Kumo be kaman nɛ Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn lar ewura Fɛɛro kutɔ.

english_verse: the king's officials asked, “Your Majesty, how much longer is this man going to be a troublemaker? Why don't you let the people leave, so they can worship the Lord their God? Don't you know that Egypt is a disaster?”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura Fɛɛro be beyaasepo na kaŋɛ mo le: “Shin nɛ basa na e yɔ n ya bunyaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, bumo be Ebɔrɛ na, ŋkpal manɛ so, fo maŋ nyi fanɛ Ijipt bee mur nna ere a?”

english_verse: The king had Moses and Aaron brought back, and he said, “All right, you may go and worship the Lord your God. But first tell me who will be going.”
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ b naŋ ya bar Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn ewura Fɛɛro kutɔ nɛ e kaŋɛ bumo: “Menyeeŋ tiŋ n ya bunyaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, men be Ebɔrɛ na. Ama menyi to be bumo bre nɛ fee sha fanɛ b yɔ ere?”

english_verse: “Everyone, young and old,” Moses answered. “We will even take our sheep, goats, and cattle, because we want to hold a celebration in honor of the Lord.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Mosis kaŋɛ mo: “Anyi nɛ anyi be mbia nɛ anyi be mbolpɔ kikɛ e naa yɔ, ŋkpal manɛ so, anyee sha keya wora kejigboŋ nna n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.”

english_verse: The king replied, “The Lord had better watch over you on the day I let you leave with your families! You're up to no good.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura Fɛɛro kaŋɛ bumo: “Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e nɛfa menyi, ama men sa maŋ keta men be beche nɛ mbia bre n yɔ! Kashenteŋto, nɛ men wora loŋ kumo ere, nfɛra lubi ko e wɔ menyi to na.

english_verse: Do you want to worship the Lord? All right, take only the men and go.” Then Moses and Aaron were chased out of the palace.
translation_verse: Amoso, shin nɛ menyi to be benyɛn na nawule e yɔ n ya bunyaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na, ŋkpal manɛ so, aloŋ nɛ men chɛr a kule ma fanɛ n wora gba.” Kumo be kaman nɛ b ju Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn ashi ewura Fɛɛro kutɔ.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward Egypt. Swarms of locusts will come and eat everything left by the hail.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Mosis: “Teŋi fo enɔ n shoŋi Ijipt be kasawule so nɛ elotɔr e ba ji asɔ kama nɛ abɔrɛjembubi na jija ŋ ka na nɛ a wɔ ndɔana to nɛ kasawule na kikɛ so na.”

english_verse: were swarming everywhere. Never before had there been so many locusts in Egypt, and never again will there be so many.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ elotɔr na ba sensaŋ Ijipt be kasawule kikɛ to nseŋ buu efuli na so kikɛ. Bumo be keshi nɛ kulubi be kaduli maŋ naŋ ba kasawule so kikɛ. Bumo alɛ maaŋ naŋ ba kasawule so loŋ kikɛ.

english_verse: At once the king sent for Moses and Aaron. He told them, “I have sinned against the Lord your God and against you.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Fɛɛro shuŋi n tre Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn manaŋ nseŋ kaŋɛ bumo le: “N wora kulubi ŋ gbiti Enyɛnpe, men be Ebɔrɛ na nseŋ wora ŋ gbiti menyi alɛ gba.

english_verse: Forgive me one more time and ask the Lord to stop these insects from killing every living plant.”
translation_verse: Amoso men ta ma alubi nɛ n wora na m paŋ ma nseŋ kule Enyɛnpe, men be Ebɔrɛ na nɛ e lara le be aleblawu lubi ere ma so.”

english_verse: Then the Lord sent a strong west wind that swept the locusts into the Red Sea. Not one locust was left anywhere in Egypt,
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ shin nɛ epeŋitɔrkpa be afugboŋ ko malɛ kilgi m ber m ba eleŋso m ba gbare elotɔr na kikɛ nyam n ya wɔtɔ teku peper na to nɛ ekoŋwule gba daa maŋ naŋ ka ashi Ijipt be efuli na kikɛ so.

english_verse: but the Lord made the king so stubborn that he still refused to let the Israelites go. Darkness
translation_verse: Ama ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ naŋ shin nɛ Fɛɛro be kagbene naŋ ki kpakpa nɛ e naŋ kini keshin nɛ Israɛlebi na e yɔ. Tentembiri be tɔrɔ be asheŋ

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sky, and everything will be covered with darkness thick enough to touch.”
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ naŋ kaŋɛ Mosis le: “Teŋi fo enɔ ŋ ŋini awɔlto nɛ ketentembiri e ba buu Ijipt be kasawule so kikɛ, k beeŋ baa la ketentembirigboŋ nna nɛ k beeŋ ba du mina kashenteŋto.”

english_verse: Moses stretched his arm toward the sky, and Egypt was covered with darkness for three days.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis maŋ mbe enɔ so ŋ ŋini awɔlto nɛ ketentembirigboŋ le plɔ ba Ijipt be efuli so kikɛ nchɛnsa.

english_verse: During that time, the Egyptians could not see each other or leave their homes, but there was light where the Israelites lived.
translation_verse: Basa daa maŋ naa wu abar kumo be saŋɛ. Ekama malɛ daa maŋ yɔ kaplɛkama nchɛ asa na to. Ama amo be saŋɛ na kikɛ so nɛ kefulto wɔ kakpa nɛ Israɛlebi na bre daa wɔ na.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and told him, “Go worship the Lord! And take your families with you. Just leave your sheep, goats, and cattle.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Fɛɛro naŋ tre Mosis ŋ kaŋɛ mo: “Men baa yɔ n ya bunyaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na. Men be beche nɛ mbia gba beeŋ tiŋ a yɔ, ama menyi be asɔbɔya bre beeŋ shir nfe.”

english_verse: This time the Lord made the king so stubborn
translation_verse: Ama Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ daŋ shin nɛ Fɛɛro naŋ wora kagbene kpakpaso ŋ kini keshin nɛ b yɔ.

english_verse: “Have it your way,” Moses answered. “You won't see me again.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis kaŋɛ mo: “To, k nyalɛ. Fo ka baŋ kaŋɛ le ere, m maaŋ naŋ ba fo anishito kikɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: I am going to punish the king of Egypt and his people one more time. Then the king will gladly let you leave his land. In fact, he will even chase you out.
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Mosis le: “Ŋ kraa beeŋ bar aleblawu koŋwule ewura Fɛɛro nɛ Ijiptebi so. Kumo ere be kaman e beeŋ shin nɛ men yɔ. E beeŋ ju menyi gba kuraa n lar mbe efuli so.

english_verse: Now go and tell my people to ask their Egyptian neighbors for gold and silver jewelry.
translation_verse: Amoso naniere ya malga n sa Israɛl be beche nɛ benyɛn fanɛ b kule ŋ kule bumo be bechenashapoana shuwa nɛ gbiti be abitasɔ.”

english_verse: So the Lord made the Egyptians greatly respect the Israelites, and everyone, including the king's officials, considered Moses an important leader.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ shin nɛ Ijiptebi na be ŋgbene pɛ Israɛlebi na ga nɛ ewura Fɛɛro be beyaasepo gba nɛ Ijipt be basa kikɛ fara a keni Mosis a bɔlɔ kenishi.

english_verse: Moses went to the king and said: I have come to let you know what the Lord is going to do. About midnight he will go through the land of Egypt,
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Mosis kaŋɛ ewura Fɛɛro le: “Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ fanɛ ta a ba kiidiso e beeŋ nite Ijipt kikɛ to.

english_verse: and wherever he goes, the first-born son in every family will die. Your own son will die, and so will the son of the lowest slave woman. Even the first-born males of your cattle will die.
translation_verse: Kaplɛkama malɛ nɛ e yɔ be ewurkoŋ nyɛnso beeŋ wu. Yili ewura Fɛɛro n ya fo kenyache nɛ e bee kɔr ayu be ewurkoŋ nyɛnso beeŋ wu, nɛ asɔbɔya na gba peya e wu.

english_verse: Everywhere in Egypt there will be loud crying. Nothing like this has ever happened before or will ever happen again.
translation_verse: Ijipt be kaba so kikɛ nyam, basa beeŋ baa boŋ to a shu. B maŋ naŋ shu loŋ be kushu ashi Ijipt be kasawule so kikɛ, bumo alɛ maaŋ naŋ shu loŋ be kushu kikɛ.

english_verse: But there won't be any need for the Israelites to cry. Things will be so quiet that not even a dog will be heard barking. Then you Egyptians will know that the Lord is good to the Israelites, even while he punishes you.
translation_verse: Ama kakpa nɛ Israɛlebi na bre wɔ, basa maaŋ shu, hale jɔnɔ gba maaŋ gbu. Saŋɛ na so menyi, Ijiptebi beeŋ pin fanɛ Israɛlebi na kɔr menyi to ashi ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kutɔ.

english_verse: Your leaders will come and bow down, begging me to take my people and leave your country. Then we will leave. Moses was very angry; he turned and left the king.
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman fo beyaasepo ere kikɛ beeŋ ba ma kutɔ m ba gbir ma anishito ŋ kule ma ŋ kaŋɛ le: ‘Fo nɛ basa nɛ baa bɛ fo so na kikɛ, e baa yɔ.’ Kumo be kaman nɛ an lar.” Mosis ka malga le n loge nɛ e nya agbo ga nseŋ lar ewura Fɛɛro kutɔ.

english_verse: What the Lord had earlier said to Moses came true. He had said, “The king of Egypt won't listen. Then I will perform even more miracles.”
translation_verse: Ama Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ teŋ kaŋɛ Mosis fanɛ ewura Fɛɛro maaŋ nu n sa mo, saŋɛ na so, mo ere Ebɔrɛ be emamachisheŋ beeŋ wora keshi Ijipt to.

english_verse: So the king of Egypt saw Moses and Aaron work miracles, but the Lord made him stubbornly refuse to let the Israelites leave his country.
translation_verse: Kashenteŋ nɛ Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn daŋ wora emamachisheŋ damta ere kikɛ ewura Fɛɛro be anishito, ama Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ daŋ shin nna nɛ Fɛɛro wora kagbene kpakpaso ŋ kini keshin nɛ Israɛl be basa na e lar mbe efuli so.

english_verse: Some time later the Lord said to Moses and Aaron:
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn le ashi Ijipt be efuli so:

english_verse: This month is to be the first month of the year for you.
translation_verse: “Yili kabre a yɔ kufɔl ere e naaŋ baa la kafɛ to be kufɔl juŋkparso n sa menyi Israɛlebi.

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel that on the tenth day of this month the head of each family must choose a lamb or a young goat for his family to eat.
translation_verse: Amoso kaŋɛ Israɛl be basa na kikɛ le be kesheŋ ere fanɛ kufɔl ere be kachɛ kudusopo, kowurnyɛn kama e lara kpakpafɔlbi ŋko kaboelotebi n sa mbe kanaŋ nɛ b mɔ n ji. A daga fanɛ laŋ kama to ebi e nya kusɔbɔya koŋwule.

english_verse: If any family is too small to eat the whole animal, they must share it with their next-door neighbors. Choose either a sheep or a goat, but it must be a one-year-old male that has nothing wrong with it. And it must be large enough for everyone to have some of the meat.
translation_verse: Laŋ kama to be kusɔbɔya e baa la kusɔbɔyanyɛnso nɛ k ji kafɛ koŋwule nsaa maa kɔ ndulgi kikɛ. Baaŋ tiŋ n lara kumo ashi mbolpɔ to ŋko mboe to.

english_verse: Each family must take care of its animal until the evening of the fourteenth day of the month, when the animals are to be killed.
translation_verse: Men lara loŋ be asɔbɔya na n yili hale n ya fo kufɔl ere be kachɛ kuduanasopo na be kaaseso. Saŋɛ nɛ kaboŋ bee biri to na nɛ men mɔ amo.

english_verse: Some of the blood must be put on the two doorposts and above the door of each house where the animals are to be eaten.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ men ta amo be ŋklaŋ na be ako ŋ gbiti ŋ gbiti men be ebuana nɛ menyeeŋ chena to n we n we eblaŋ na be akuloŋ be mbuna be akel to nɛ amo be awɔlto.

english_verse: That night the animals are to be roasted and eaten, together with bitter herbs and thin bread made without yeast.
translation_verse: K daga fanɛ b tɔ eblaŋ na edɛ to nna nseŋ ta amo nɛ bodobodo nɛ a maŋ kɔ yiisi nɛ epofantaŋ kekra n wea abar to n we.

english_verse: Don't eat the meat raw or boiled. The entire animal, including its head, legs, and insides, must be roasted.
translation_verse: Men saŋ maŋ kaŋ we eblaŋ na abumbuŋ ŋko n ta nchu n daŋɛ amo. Men tɔ amo nɛ amo be amu nɛ ayawɔrta nɛ apuntosɔ kikɛ edɛ to.

english_verse: Eat what you want that night, and the next morning burn whatever is left.
translation_verse: Men sa maŋ kaŋ shin nɛ kare e chɛ eblaŋ na be kekama so. Men chɔɔ ekama nɛ meeŋ we ŋ ka.

english_verse: When you eat the meal, be dressed and ready to travel. Have your sandals on, carry your walking stick in your hand, and eat quickly. This is the Passover Festival in honor of me, your Lord.
translation_verse: Kusɔ nɛ menyeeŋ wora nde: Men ta men be asɔbuusoana m buu nseŋ kre to kpakpa n ta men be asɛbtaana n wɔtɔ, nseŋ ta men be akpabi malɛ ŋ keta. Men we eblaŋ na malɛ manaŋ manaŋ, ŋkpal manɛ so, k la kebansonchoŋ be kejigboŋ nɛ k bee maŋkura ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nna.

english_verse: That same night I will pass through Egypt and kill the first-born son in every family and the first-born male of all animals. I am the Lord, and I will punish the gods of Egypt.
translation_verse: Kumo be kanyɛ na meeŋ ba Ijipt be efuli so m ba mɔ ewurkoŋnyɛn kikɛ, meeŋ mɔ edimɛdi nɛ asɔbɔya kikɛ peya. Ma alɛ beeŋ gberge Ijipt be efuli so be agbirana kikɛ kusoe. Ma e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.

english_verse: The blood on the houses will show me where you live, and when I see the blood, I will pass over you. Then you won't be bothered by the terrible disasters I will bring on Egypt.
translation_verse: Ŋklaŋ nɛ menyeeŋ ta ŋ gbiti men be nwu nɛ men wɔtɔ ere be mbuna na beeŋ baa la ndulgi nna n sa menyi ere. Saŋɛ na so nɛ m baŋ ta luwu be aleblawu lubi a ba Ijiptebi so saŋ wu ŋklaŋ na, meeŋ baŋ menyi so n choŋ nɛ shɛŋ maaŋ wora menyi.” Bodobodo nɛ k maŋ kɔ yiisi na be kejigboŋ be asheŋ

english_verse: For seven days you must eat bread made without yeast. And on the first of these seven days, you must remove all yeast from your homes. If you eat anything made with yeast during this festival, you will no longer be part of Israel.
translation_verse: Yili loŋ be kachɛ na n ya fo bɔkwe men be ekama e sa maŋ kaŋ ji bodobodo nɛ b ta yiisi n wora. Bɔkwe na to be kachɛ sososo na ekama e lara yiisi kikɛ ashi mbe laŋ to. Esa kama nɛ e baŋ ji bodobodo nɛ b ta yiisi n wora nchɛnshunu na to, meeŋ lara mo ashi ma basa to.

english_verse: Meet together for worship on the first and seventh days of the festival. The only work you are allowed to do on either of these two days is that of preparing the bread.
translation_verse: Men ta kachɛ sososo na nɛ kachɛ shunusopo na n shɛr n shuŋ Ebɔrɛ. Loŋ be nchɛ na, ekama e sa maŋ kaŋ shuŋ kushuŋ kikɛ, ama menyeeŋ tiŋ n daŋɛ ajibi bre kanaŋkamaso nɛ ekama beeŋ tiŋ n ji.

english_verse: Begin on the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month by eating bread made without yeast. Then continue this celebration until the evening of the twenty-first day.
translation_verse: Kufɔl juŋkparso na be kachɛ kuduanasopo be kaaseso nɛ menyeeŋ fara a ji bodobodo nɛ k maŋ kɔ yiisi na hale n ya fo kumo be nchɛ adunyɔ nɛ kakosopo be kaaseso.

english_verse: During these seven days no yeast is allowed in anyone's home, whether they are native Israelites or not. If you are caught eating anything made with yeast, you will no longer be part of Israel.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal loŋ so kumo be nchɛnshunu na bre to k maŋ daga menyi be ekama kaa kɔ yiisi ashi mbe laŋ to kikɛ. Ekama, kadetobia ŋko efɔ, nɛ e baŋ ji ajibi kama nɛ a kɔ yiisi, meeŋ lara mo ashi Israɛl be basa to.

english_verse: Stay away from yeast, no matter where you live. No one is allowed to eat anything made with yeast!
translation_verse: Amoso men be ekama e sa maŋ kaŋ ji kusɔ kama nɛ k kɔ yiisi nchɛnshunu na to.” Kebansonchoŋ be asheŋ

english_verse: Make a brush from a few small branches of a hyssop plant and dip the brush in the bowl that has the blood of the animal in it. Then brush some of the blood above the door and on the posts at each side of the door of your house. After this, everyone is to stay inside until morning.
translation_verse: Men ta echeenshi n suse n suse ŋklaŋ na nseŋ ta keche n nyɔ amo to ŋ gbiti ŋ gbiti menyi be mbuna be akel to nɛ esoso kikɛ. Kumo be kaman ekama e sa maŋ kaŋ naŋ lar kowu kikɛ hale nɛ kare e ya chɛ kachipurso.

english_verse: During that night the Lord will go through the country of Egypt and kill the first-born son in every Egyptian family. He will see where you have put the blood, and he will not come into your house. His angel that brings death will pass over and not kill your first-born sons.
translation_verse: Saŋɛ na so Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na baŋ luri Ijipt to nɛ e mɔ ewurkoŋnyɛn nseŋ wu ŋklaŋ ka gbiti menyi be akuloŋ be esoso nɛ akel to, e beeŋ baŋ amo so n choŋ nɛ emɔpo na maaŋ luri menyi be elaŋ to m mɔ menyi be ewurkoŋnyɛn.

english_verse: After you have entered the country promised to you by the Lord, you and your children must continue to celebrate Passover each year.
translation_verse: Men kaŋ yɔ kasawule mo nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nase kɔnɔ fanɛ e beeŋ sa menyi na gba so, men baa kraa nyiŋi a wora le be kesheŋ ere.

english_verse: Your children will ask you, “What are we celebrating?”
translation_verse: Nɛ men be mbia kaŋ bishi menyi fanɛ: ‘Le be kesheŋ ere be kifito bre e la nuso?’

english_verse: And you will answer, “The Passover animal is killed to honor the Lord. We do these things because on that night long ago the Lord passed over the homes of our people in Egypt. He killed the first-born sons of the Egyptians, but he spared our children from death.” After Moses finished speaking, the people of Israel knelt down and worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Men kaŋɛ bumo fanɛ: ‘K la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be kebansonchoŋ be sarga nna. E daŋ baŋ anyi Israɛlebi be nwu so nna ashi Ijipt be efuli so nseŋ ya mɔ Ijiptebi be ewurkoŋnyɛnana, ama shɛŋ daa maŋ wora anyi ere be basa.’ ” Ndoŋ nna nɛ Israɛlebi gbir m bunyaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.

english_verse: Then they left and did what Moses and Aaron had told them to do. Death for the First-Born Sons
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Israɛlebi na yɔ n ya wora asɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ daŋ kaŋɛ Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn na kikɛ chap. Ewurkoŋ be luwu be asheŋ

english_verse: At midnight the Lord killed the first-born son of every Egyptian family, from the son of the king to the son of every prisoner in jail. He also killed the first-born male of every animal that belonged to the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Kumo be kamɔnchɛ kiidiso nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ luri Ijipt to m mɔ ewurkoŋnyɛn kikɛ ashi Ijipt be kasawule so. Yili Fɛɛro n ya fo esa nɛ e wɔ kabuti to be wurkoŋ nyɛnso nɛ asɔbɔya kikɛ peya nɛ e daŋ mɔ.

english_verse: That night the king, his officials, and everyone else in Egypt got up and started crying bitterly. In every Egyptian home, someone was dead. The People of Israel Escape from Egypt
translation_verse: Kumo be kanyɛ na nɛ ewura Fɛɛro nɛ mbe beyaasepo nɛ Ijipt be basa kikɛ koso a boŋ to a shu awɔrso kaplɛkama, ŋkpal manɛ so, laŋ kama daa maŋ wɔ Ijipt to nɛ esa maŋ wu kumo to. Israɛlebi ka lar Ijipt to be asheŋ

english_verse: During the night the king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Get your people out of my country and leave us alone! Go and worship the Lord, as you have asked.
translation_verse: Epul na to nɛ Fɛɛro shuŋi n tre Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn kanyɛso na kikɛ nseŋ kaŋɛ bumo: “Men bela n lar ma efuli so, menyi nɛ Israɛlebi nɛ b wɔ nfe na kikɛ. Men baa yɔ n ya bunyaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na fanɛ kananɛ men kule ma na.

english_verse: Take your sheep, goats, and cattle, and get out. But ask your God to be kind to me.”
translation_verse: Men ta men be mbolpɔ nɛ mboe nɛ ana kikɛ a yɔ fanɛ kananɛ men kule na, ama men kaŋ yɔ, men kule Ebɔrɛ be nɛfa n sa ma ere gba!”

english_verse: The Egyptians did everything they could to get the Israelites to leave their country as quickly as possible. They said, “Please hurry and leave. If you don't, we will all be dead.”
translation_verse: Kede be kaman Ijiptebi na daŋ fuge Israɛlebi na be aya ase kenishipereso nna fanɛ b lar bumo be kasawule so manaŋ. B yɛ: “Nɛ mannɛ aloŋ, anyi Ijiptebi kikɛ beeŋ wu n loge.”

english_verse: So the Israelites quickly made some bread dough and put it in pans. But they did not mix any yeast in the dough to make it rise. They wrapped cloth around the pans and carried them on their shoulders.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Israɛlebi na ta bodobodo nɛ a maŋ kɔ yiisi na be kubuu nɛ b gbiti m bɔlɔ bumo be ntishaŋana nɛ b kɔ a wora bodobodo na nseŋ ta ewajɛ ŋ kre amo so n ta amo n deŋi bumo be abatimuana so m pɛ ekpa.

english_verse: The Israelites had already done what Moses had told them to do. They had gone to their Egyptian neighbors and asked for gold and silver and for clothes.
translation_verse: Kusɔ kama nɛ Mosis daŋ kaŋɛ Israɛlebi na, bumo alɛ wora. B daŋ kule ŋ kule Ijiptebi na shuwa nɛ gbiti be abitasɔ nɛ asɔbuuso nna.

english_verse: The Lord had made the Egyptians friendly toward the people of Israel, and they gave them whatever they asked for. In this way they carried away the wealth of the Egyptians when they left Egypt.
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ daŋ shin nɛ Israɛlebi na be asheŋ bɔlɔ Ijiptebi na kenishi nna nɛ b sa bumo kusɔ kama nɛ b daŋ kule bumo kikɛ. Loŋ be ekpa na so nɛ Israɛlebi na daŋ bɔla n sulɔ Ijiptebi na be asɔ damta n yɔ.

english_verse: Many other people went with them as well, and there were also a lot of sheep, goats, and cattle.
translation_verse: Basa pɔtɛ damta gba daŋ ti bumo so n yɔ. B daŋ keta asɔbɔya fanɛ mbolpɔ nɛ mboe nɛ ana kikɛ n ti so n yɔ.

english_verse: They left Egypt in such a hurry that they did not have time to prepare any food except the bread dough made without yeast. So they baked it and made thin bread.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ b ta bodobodo nɛ a maŋ kɔ yiisi be kubuu nɛ b gbiti n shi Ijipt na n wora bodobodo. Ŋkpal b ka daŋ ju bumo fanɛ b lar Ijipt to manaŋ na so, b daa maŋ naŋ nya saŋɛ nɛ b wɔtɔ amo yiisi ŋko n naŋ wora ajibi kama n ti so.

english_verse: On that night the Lord kept watch for them, and on this same night each year Israel will always keep watch in honor of the Lord. Instructions for Passover
translation_verse: Loŋ be kanyɛ na Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be anishi daŋ baa yuu Israɛlebi na so nna nɛ b lar Ijipt to. Amoso kafɛ kama nɛ loŋ be kanyɛ baŋ fo, Israɛlebi nɛ bumo be kaman to ebi kikɛ bee gal edi nna a chena kanyiŋiso a bunyaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na a klade. Kebansonchoŋ be kejigboŋ be mbraana be asheŋ

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following instructions for celebrating Passover: Only Israelites may eat the Passover meal.
translation_verse: Kamalga ere be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn le: “Kebansonchoŋ be kejigboŋ na be mbraana nde: K maŋ daga efɔ kikɛ ka ji kumo.

english_verse: Your slaves may eat the meal if they have been circumcised,
translation_verse: Ama kenya kikɛ nɛ men tɔ nseŋ ku mo kututu bre beeŋ tiŋ n ji kumo.

english_verse: And all Israelites must take part in the meal.
translation_verse: Israɛlebi kikɛ daga fanɛ b baa ji le be kejigboŋ ere nna.

english_verse: If anyone who isn't an Israelite wants to celebrate Passover with you, every man and boy in that family must first be circumcised. Then they may join in the meal, just like native Israelites. No uncircumcised man or boy may eat the Passover meal!
translation_verse: Efɔ kama nɛ e ba tu menyi n chena nsaa sha fanɛ e ti menyi so n ji kumo m maŋkura Enyɛnpe na, k daga fanɛ mbe laŋ to be benyɛn kikɛ e ku atutu. Kumo be kaman pɔɛŋ nɛ loŋ be efɔ na e tiŋ n tu menyi n wora kejigboŋ na be aworbi fanɛ Israɛl be kadetobia, a daga fanɛ e ku kututu.

english_verse: The Israelites obeyed everything the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron to tell them.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Israɛlebi na kikɛ wora kasonu nseŋ wora asɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ yili n sa Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn na kikɛ.

english_verse: And on that same day the Lord brought Israel's families and tribes out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Kumo be kamɔnchɛ malɛ kikɛ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ lara Israɛl be basa kanaŋ kanaŋ so nɛ mbuna mbuna so ashi Ijipt to.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Mosis le:

english_verse: “Dedicate to me the first-born son of every family and the first-born males of your flocks and herds. These belong to me.” The Festival of Thin Bread
translation_verse: “Lara wurkoŋnyɛn kikɛ ashi Israɛlebi ere to nɛ e baa du cheembi a la meya. Dimɛdi ŋko kusɔbɔya be wurkoŋnyɛn, la meya nna.”

english_verse: The Lord promised your ancestors that he would bring you into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites, and Jebusites. It is a land rich with milk and honey. Each year during the month of Abib, celebrate these events in the following way:
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋ baŋ yɛr menyi basa nɛ baa tre Keenanebi nɛ Hitebi nɛ Amɔriebi nɛ Hivebi nɛ Jebusiebi be kasawule nɛ e nase kumo be kɔnɔ n sa men nananyɛnana fanɛ e beeŋ ta n sa menyi na so, men baa kraa wora le be kesheŋ ere kufɔl ere to.

english_verse: For seven days you are to eat bread made without yeast, and on the seventh day you are to celebrate a festival in honor of the Lord.
translation_verse: Menyeeŋ ji bodobodo nɛ a maŋ kɔ yiisi bɔkwe na nseŋ wora kejigboŋ kumo be kachɛ shunusopo na n nyiŋi kananɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na lara menyi ashi Ijipt be efuli so.

english_verse: During those seven days, you must not eat anything made with yeast or even have yeast anywhere near your homes.
translation_verse: Men ji bodobodo nɛ a maŋ kɔ yiisi na nchɛnshunu. K maŋ daga b ka wu yiisi ŋko ajibi kama nɛ a kɔ yiisi gba menyi be elaŋ to.

english_verse: Then on the seventh day you must explain to your children that you do this because the Lord brought you out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Kachɛ shunusopo na nɛ ekama e kaŋɛ mbe mbia fanɛ e bee wora le be kesheŋ ere nna a nyiŋi kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ wora n sa mo, saŋɛ nɛ e lar Ijipt to na.

english_verse: This celebration will be like wearing a sign on your hand or on your forehead, because then you will pass on to others the teaching of the Lord, whose mighty power brought you out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Kesheŋ ere beeŋ baa la kanyiŋi nna nsaa du fanɛ b ka kre mbra na m mata menyi be enɔana so ŋko menyi be nsɔto nɛ men baa ŋini beko kumo be asheŋ. Saŋɛ na so, k beeŋ baa nyiŋi menyi kananɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be mbra na bɔlɔ menyi to kpal manɛ so, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ta mbe eleŋgboŋ nna n lara menyi ashi Ijipt be kasawule so.

english_verse: The Lord will give you the land of the Canaanites, just as he promised you and your ancestors.
translation_verse: Ama saŋkama nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋ yɛr menyi Keenanebi be kasawule na so fanɛ kananɛ e nase kɔnɔ n sa menyi nɛ men tutoana fanɛ e beeŋ ta kumo n sa menyi na,

english_verse: From then on, you must give him every first-born son from your families and every first-born male from your animals, because these belong to him.
translation_verse: men ta men be ewurkoŋnyɛn nɛ men be asɔbɔya be bibinyɛn nɛ baaŋ fara ŋ kurge ashi ndoŋ na kikɛ n sa ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.

english_verse: You can spare the life of a first-born donkey by sacrificing a lamb; if you don't, you must break the donkey's neck. You must spare every first-born son.
translation_verse: Ama men ta kubolpɔ fɔlbi n chɛr kurma bre pibinyɛn juŋkparso. Nɛ fanɛ men maaŋ ta kubolpɔ n chɛr kumo malɛ, kumo ere men bu kumo be kubɔ. Men shin nɛ menyi be ewurkoŋnyɛn na bre e baa du cheembi a la Enyɛnpe na peya.

english_verse: In the future your children will ask what this ceremony means. Explain it to them by saying, “The Lord used his mighty power to rescue us from slavery in Egypt.
translation_verse: Ama saŋko nɛ menyi be mbia kaŋ bishi menyi kejigboŋ ere be kifito, men kaŋɛ bumo le: ‘Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ daŋ ta mbe eleŋgboŋ nna n lara anyi kenyaya to ashi Ijipt be kasawule so.

english_verse: The king stubbornly refused to set us free, so the Lord killed the first-born male of every animal and the first-born son of every Egyptian family. This is why we sacrifice to the Lord every first-born male of every animal and save every first-born son.”
translation_verse: Ama saŋɛ nɛ Fɛɛro daŋ wora kagbene kpakpaso ŋ kini keshin nɛ an yɔ na, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ daŋ mɔ Ijipt be kasawule so be ewurkoŋnyɛn kikɛ nna, edimɛdi nɛ asɔbɔya kikɛ peya. Ŋkpal loŋ so nɛ an ta asɔbɔya be bibinyɛn juŋkparso kikɛ a lara sarga a sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nsaa shin nɛ anyi be ewurkoŋnyɛn malɛ kikɛ bee ki cheembi a wɔtɔ a sa mo na.

english_verse: This ceremony will serve the same purpose as a sign on your hand or on your forehead to tell how the Lord's mighty power rescued us from Egypt. The Lord Leads His People
translation_verse: Le be kejigboŋ ere malɛ beeŋ baa du fanɛ tɔɔnɛ be asɔ nɛ anyee kre a mata enɔ so ŋko nsɔto nna a nyiŋi anyi kananɛ Enyɛnpe ŋini eleŋ n lara anyi ashi Ijipt be efuli so.’ ” Kananɛ Enyɛnpe juŋkpar mbe basa be asheŋ

english_verse: After the king had finally let the people go, the Lord did not lead them through Philistine territory, though that was the shortest way. God had said, “If they are attacked, they may decide to return to Egypt.”
translation_verse: Saŋɛ nɛ ewura Fɛɛro daŋ sa Israɛl be basa ekpa fanɛ b yɔ na, Ebɔrɛ daa maŋ juŋkpar bumo m bɔla ekpa shiimbi ashi Filistiebi be kasawule so, ŋkpal manɛ so, le nɛ Ebɔrɛ daŋ fɛ: “Nɛ Filistiebi kaŋ ya kre kena n tu bumo, baaŋ chɛrga bumo be nfɛra m bɛta n yɔ Ijipt.”

english_verse: So he led them around through the desert and toward the Red Sea. The Israelites left Egypt, prepared for battle.
translation_verse: Amoso Ebɔrɛ daŋ juŋkpar bumo nna ŋ gelge m bɔla teku peper na be kaba so ashi keshishɛrsawule ko so. Israɛlebi na daŋ wora kena be shiriya nna pɔɛŋ nseŋ lar Ijipt.

english_verse: The people of Israel left Succoth and camped at Etham at the border of Egypt near the desert.
translation_verse: Israɛlebi ka lar Sukɔf nɛ b yɔ Etam ashi keshishɛrsawule na be ekarso n ya yuu ewajɛbu n wora bumo be keeyi to ndoŋ.

english_verse: During the day the Lord went ahead of his people in a thick cloud, and during the night he went ahead of them in a flaming fire. That way the Lord could lead them at all times, whether day or night.
translation_verse: Karechɛ kikɛ kuwɔlpa nɛ k bee juŋkpar bumo na maa barga bumo kikɛ. Loŋ nɛ edɛ be kabulpi na malɛ gba maa barga bumo kanyɛso kikɛ.

english_verse: At Etham the Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ naŋ kaŋɛ Mosis le:

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel to turn back and camp across from Pi-Hahiroth near Baal-Zephon, between Migdol and the Red Sea.
translation_verse: “Kaŋɛ Israɛlebi na fanɛ b bɛta kaman n ya yuu bumo be ewajɛbu Migdɔl nɛ teku na be kefɛato m mata Pihahirɔf ashi Baal Zefon be kaba ndoŋ dede.

english_verse: The king will think you were afraid to cross the desert and that you are wandering around, trying to find another way to leave the country.
translation_verse: Saŋɛ na so ewura Fɛɛro beeŋ fɛ mbe kumu to ŋ kaŋɛ: ‘Men keni Israɛlebi na e ya shir a wɔ keshishɛrsawule na so a kulti a maŋ nyi kakpa nɛ baaŋ bɔla n lar na.’

english_verse: I will make the king stubborn again, and he will try to catch you. Then I will destroy him and his army. People everywhere will praise me for my victory, and the Egyptians will know that I really am the Lord. The Israelites obeyed the Lord and camped where he told them.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ n naŋ shin nɛ Fɛɛro be kagbene e ki kpakpa nɛ e ju m buu menyi so, saŋɛ na so meeŋ mur Fɛɛro nɛ mbe beyaasepo kikɛ nɛ Ijiptebi e pin fanɛ ma e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ kemaŋkura bɔlɔ ma to na.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ Israɛlebi na wora kusɔ nɛ Mosis kaŋɛ bumo na.

english_verse: When the king of Egypt heard that the Israelites had finally left, he and his officials changed their minds and said, “Look what we have done! We let them get away, and they will no longer be our slaves.”
translation_verse: Amoso b ka daŋ ya kaŋɛ Ijipt be ewura fanɛ Israɛl be basa na shile n choŋ nɛ mo nɛ mbe basa kikɛ chɛrga bumo be nfɛra nseŋ bishi bumo be amu le: “Manɛ so bre nɛ an wora le be kesheŋ ere? Manɛ nna nɛ an shin nɛ Israɛlebi na yɔ nsaa maaŋ naa shuŋ anyi ere?”

english_verse: But the king's horses and chariots and soldiers caught up with them while they were camping by the Red Sea near Pi-Hahiroth and Baal-Zephon.
translation_verse: Fɛɛro nɛ mbe benapo kikɛ daŋ ju nna m buu Israɛlebi na so, hale n ya kaa taga bumo to ashi kakpa nɛ b yuu bumo be ewajɛbu m mata teku na ashi Pihahirɔf nɛ k wɔ Baal Zefon be kaba ndoŋ na.

english_verse: They also complained to Moses, “Wasn't there enough room in Egypt to bury us? Is that why you brought us out here to die in the desert? Why did you bring us out of Egypt anyway?
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ b kilgi m bishi Mosis le: “Nchaŋana ka maŋ wɔ Ijipt to bre so nɛ fo keta anyi m ba keshishɛrsawule ere so fanɛ an baa wu ere a? Manɛ so nɛ fo wora anyi loŋ n lara anyi ashi Ijipt to ere?

english_verse: While we were there, didn't we tell you to leave us alone? We'd rather be slaves in Egypt than die in this desert!”
translation_verse: Mannɛ kusɔ nɛ an teŋ kaŋɛ fo Ijipt na nde a? An yɛ fo yige anyi boeŋ nɛ an baa wɔ Ijipt a shuŋ bumo. Nɛ an daa wɔ Ijipt a shuŋ bumo, k daa beeŋ baa bɔ an ka wu keshishɛrsawule ere so.”

english_verse: But Moses answered, “Don't be afraid! Be brave, and you will see the Lord save you today. These Egyptians will never bother you again.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis kaŋɛ basa na: “Men sa maa lɔ kufu, men leŋ men be amu to. Menyeeŋ wu kumɔlga nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ beeŋ bar menyi kabre. Ijiptebi mo nɛ men wu kabre ere, men maaŋ naŋ wu bumo kikɛ.

english_verse: The Lord will fight for you, and you won't have to do a thing.”
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na beeŋ kɔ bumo kena n sa menyi. Menyi ere e yige a keni mo de.”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Why do you keep calling out to me for help? Tell the Israelites to move forward.
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ Mosis le: “Manɛ e ba nɛ fee shu a tre ma? Meeŋ mɔlga menyi, amoso kaŋɛ Israɛlebi na fanɛ b baa yɔ anishito.

english_verse: Then hold your walking stick over the sea. The water will open up and make a road where they can walk through on dry ground.
translation_verse: Teŋi fo kekpabi na n shoŋi teku na nɛ k ku to nɛ Israɛlebi na e nite kasawule wɔlso so m bɔla kumo to n choŋ.

english_verse: I will make the Egyptians so stubborn that they will go after you. Then I will be praised because of what happens to the king and his chariots and cavalry.
translation_verse: Meeŋ naŋ shin nɛ Ijiptebi na be ŋgbene e ki kpakpa nɛ b yuu teku na to m bɛ bumo so, saŋɛ na so nɛ n nya kemaŋkura ŋkpal kusɔ nɛ meeŋ wora ewura Fɛɛro nɛ mbe benapo so so.

english_verse: All this time God's angel had gone ahead of Israel's army, but now he moved behind them. A large cloud had also gone ahead of them,
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ Ebɔrɛ be malaika mo nɛ e daa wɔ kuwɔlpa to a juŋkpar Israɛlebi na bɛta n ya kaa bɛ bumo be kaman.

english_verse: but now it moved between the Egyptians and the Israelites. The cloud gave light to the Israelites, but made it dark for the Egyptians, and during the night they could not come any closer.
translation_verse: Malaika na daa wɔ Ijipt be benapo na nɛ Israɛlebi na be nferinto nna. Kuwɔlpa na daŋ shin nna nɛ ketentembiri buu Ijipt be benapo na so nseŋ sa Israɛlebi na bre kefulto. Amoso kanyɛ na kikɛ Ijiptebi be benapo na daa maŋ tiŋ n tu Israɛlebi be benapo be katuŋ na.

english_verse: Moses stretched his arm over the sea, and the Lord sent a strong east wind that blew all night until there was dry land where the water had been. The sea opened up,
translation_verse: Le be asheŋ ere kikɛ ka wora n choŋ nɛ Mosis teŋi mbe kekpabi na n shoŋi teku na so. Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ shin nɛ kebɔrɛfito be afu lempo ko chala kanyɛ na kikɛ n shin nɛ teku na ku to anyɔ.

english_verse: But before daylight the Lord looked down at the Egyptian army from the fiery cloud and made them panic.
translation_verse: Kaboŋ ka ba kaa kpaŋɛ to nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ yili edɛ be kabulpi nɛ kuwɔlpa na to n wu Ijipt be benapo na nseŋ ta kebagato n lɛ bumo so.

english_verse: Their chariot wheels got stuck, and it was hard for them to move. So the Egyptians said to one another, “Let's leave these people alone! The Lord is on their side and is fighting against us.”
translation_verse: E daŋ shin nna nɛ bumo be egbaŋɛturkoana na be aya gbaŋ n lar n lar nɛ eturko na be kefar ki bumo so kpakpa. Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ijipt be benapo na kaŋɛ abar le: “Men shin nɛ an bɛta nfe, ŋkpal manɛ so Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ bee kɔ anyi kena a chɛ Israɛlebi to nna na.”

english_verse: The Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sea—the water will cover the Egyptians and their cavalry and chariots.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Mosis le: “Teŋi fo kekpabi n shoŋi teku na nɛ nchu na e bɛta m ba buu Ijipt be benapo na nɛ bumo be egbaŋɛturkoana kikɛ so.”

english_verse: Moses stretched out his arm, and at daybreak the water rushed toward the Egyptians. They tried to run away, but the Lord drowned them in the sea.
translation_verse: Kare ka bee chɛ na nɛ Mosis teŋi mbe kekpabi n shoŋi teku na nɛ k naŋ bɔlɔ fanɛ kananɛ k daa du na. Nɛ Ijipt be benapo na wora ania fanɛ baaŋ shile n lar nchu na to nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ shin nɛ nchu na ji bumo kikɛ.

english_verse: The water came and covered the chariots, the cavalry, and the whole Egyptian army that had followed the Israelites into the sea. Not one of them was left alive.
translation_verse: Nchu na daŋ bɔlɔ m bɛta kaman nna n ya muni Fɛɛro be benapo nɛ b daŋ ta egbaŋɛturkoana nɛ mbe egbaŋɛdiipoana m bɔla kasawule wɔlso so ashi teku na be nferinto n ju a buu Israɛlebi na so nɛ bumo kikɛ nyam mur.

english_verse: But the sea had made a wall of water on each side of the Israelites, so they walked through on dry land.
translation_verse: Ama Israɛlebi na bre daŋ nite kasawule wɔlso so nna m bɔla teku nɛ k ki fanɛ egbalana a wɔ bumo be jisa so nɛ bena so n dii pɔɛŋ nɛ nchu na ji Ijipt be benapo na.

english_verse: On that day, when the Israelites saw the bodies of the Egyptians washed up on the shore, they knew that the Lord had saved them.
translation_verse: Kumo be kamɔnchɛ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ mɔlga Israɛlebi na ashi Ijiptebi na be enɔ to nɛ b wu Ijiptebi na ka wu a deŋ a deŋ teku na be ekarso.

english_verse: Because of the mighty power he had used against the Egyptians, the Israelites worshiped him and trusted him and his servant Moses.
translation_verse: Israɛlebi na ka wu eleŋgboŋ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ŋini ŋ kɔ m pɔɔ Ijiptebi na so na nɛ b bunyaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nseŋ yirda mo nɛ mbe kayɛrbi Mosis.

english_verse: Moses and the Israelites sang this song in praise of the Lord: I sing praises to the Lord for his great victory! He has thrown the horses and their riders into the sea.
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ Mosis nɛ Israɛlebi na kikɛ boŋ le be kashɛ ere n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ a kaŋɛ: “Meeŋ boŋ kashɛ n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na, ŋkpal manɛ so e kɔ m pɔɔ so kemaŋkuragboŋ so. Mo e shin nɛ egbaŋɛ nɛ bumo be bediipoana mur ashi teku to na.

english_verse: The Lord is my strength, the reason for my song, because he has saved me. I praise and honor the Lord— he is my God and the God of my ancestors.
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e la ma elempo nɛ ma emɔlgapo. Meeŋ boŋ kashɛ ŋ dele mo. Mo e la ma Ebɔrɛ, amoso meeŋ di mo epaŋ. N tuto be Ebɔrɛ e la mo, amoso meeŋ fur mo.

english_verse: The Lord is his name, and he is a warrior!
translation_verse: Mbe ketre e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na. Mo e la enakɔpo na.

english_verse: He threw the chariots and army of Egypt's king into the Red Sea, and he drowned the best of the king's officers.
translation_verse: Mo e shin nɛ Fɛɛro be egbaŋɛturkoana nɛ mbe benapo kikɛ mur ashi teku to na. E shin nɛ Fɛɛro be benapo be benimu nɛ e yirda ga na kikɛ mur ashi Teku Peper na to.

english_verse: With the tremendous force of your right arm, our Lord, you crushed your enemies.
translation_verse: O, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, fo enɔ jisa so nɛ kumo be eleŋ kɔ kufu ga na nɛ fo ta m buri fo doŋana to cheche.

english_verse: What a great victory was yours, when you defeated everyone who opposed you. Your fiery anger wiped them out, as though they were straw.
translation_verse: Fo kemaŋkura nɛ eleŋgboŋ wɔ kumo to na nɛ fo ta m pɔɔ bumo nɛ b kishi fo na so. Fo agbogboŋ nɛ k bee ji fanɛ edɛ be kuwuloŋ na a chɔɔ bumo burburbi fanɛ atuweklaŋ na m mur.

english_verse: You were so furious that the sea piled up like a wall, and the ocean depths curdled like cheese.
translation_verse: Fo kamuna to be efutegboŋ nawule e shin nɛ nchu nɛ a daŋ ber abar so na kikɛ barga to n niŋi to n yili fanɛ egbal na, nɛ teku na be kechimbi to ki kasawule wɔlso.

english_verse: Your enemies boasted that they would pursue and capture us, divide up our possessions, treat us as they wished, then take out their swords and kill us right there.
translation_verse: Edompo na daŋ ji njɔŋ nna ŋ kaŋɛ: ‘Meeŋ ju m buu bumo so n ya pɛ bumo nseŋ barga bumo be asɔ to n ta amo nɛ mee sha kikɛ. Meeŋ pee ma tokobi m mɔ bumo.’

english_verse: When you signaled with your right hand, your enemies were swallowed deep into the earth.
translation_verse: Fo e teŋi fo enɔ jisa nɛ kasawule ta fo doŋana kikɛ m min na.

english_verse: The leaders of Edom and of Moab were terrified. Everyone in Canaan fainted,
translation_verse: Kufu beeŋ pɛ Edɔm be bewuraana nɛ Mowab be bejuŋkparpoana ga ŋkpal loŋ so. Keenan be basa kikɛ beeŋ pɔ aba,

english_verse: struck down by fear. Our Lord, your powerful arm kept them still as a rock until the people you rescued to be your very own had marched by.
translation_verse: nɛ kufu nɛ kechichachicha e tɔr bumo so. Ŋkpal eleŋ nɛ k beeŋ lar fo enɔ to na so, baaŋ wora shruum fanɛ kejembu na n ya fo saŋɛ nɛ fo basa nɛ fo lara ashi kenyaya to na choŋ na pɔɛŋ.

english_verse: You will let your people settle on your own mountain, where you chose to live and to be worshiped.
translation_verse: Fo e naaŋ yɛr fo basa n ya chena fo gbagba be kebee so, kaboŋ nɛ fo, Enyɛnpe lara fanɛ k baa la fo pe nsaa la ebu cheembi nɛ fo gbagba pɔr na.

english_verse: Our Lord, you will rule forever! The Song of Miriam
translation_verse: Fo Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e naaŋ baa ji kuwura hale mbaanaayɔ.” Miriam be kashɛ be asheŋ

english_verse: The Lord covered the royal Egyptian cavalry and chariots with the sea, after the Israelites had walked safely through on dry ground.
translation_verse: Israɛlebi na daŋ bɔla teku na to nna n nite kasawule wɔlso so n choŋ. Ama Fɛɛro be egbaŋɛturkoana nɛ egbaŋɛdiipoana na bre ka bɔla teku na to nɛ b choŋ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ shin nɛ nchu na bɛta m ba mur bumo kikɛ.

english_verse: Miriam the sister of Aaron was a prophet. So she took her tambourine and led the other women out to play their tambourines and to dance.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ anebi cheso Miriam, nɛ e la Ɛɛrɔn mo da cheso na, ta mbe chakachaka, nɛ beche nɛ b ka na malɛ ta echakachaka m bɛ mo so nɛ baa laŋ nsaa cha.

english_verse: Then she sang to them: “Sing praises to the Lord for his great victory! He has thrown the horses and their riders into the sea.” Bitter Water at Marah
translation_verse: Nɛ Miriam bee boŋ kashɛ a wɔtɔ bumo to a kaŋɛ: “Men boŋ kashɛ n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na, ŋkpal mbe kekɔmpɔɔso be eleŋ nɛ kemaŋkura ka shi ga so. Mo e shin nɛ egbaŋɛturko nɛ amo be bediipo mur teku to na.” Nchu kekra na be asheŋ

english_verse: After the Israelites left the Red Sea, Moses led them through the Shur Desert for three days, before finding water.
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ Mosis juŋkpar Israɛlebi na ŋ koso teku peper na ase n nite n ya luri Shur be keshishɛrsawule so. B daŋ nite keshishɛrsawule na so nchɛ asa nɛ b maŋ nya nchu nɛ b nuu.

english_verse: They did find water at Marah, but it was bitter, which is how that place got its name.
translation_verse: B ka ya fo kaboŋ ko nɛ baa tre Mara, b daa maŋ tiŋ nɛ b nuu ndoŋ be nchu na, ŋkpal a ka daa du kekra so, amoso nɛ b daŋ nase ndoŋ Mara nna.

english_verse: The people complained and said, “Moses, what are we going to drink?”
translation_verse: Nɛ basa na naŋ fara a fubel a kaŋɛ Mosis le: “To, nnɛ nɛ anyeeŋ nya nchu n nuu?”

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord for help, and the Lord told him to throw a certain piece of wood into the water. Moses did so, and the water became fit to drink. At Marah the Lord tested his people and also gave them some laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis shu n tre Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ŋini mo kedibi ko nɛ e ta kumo n lɛ nchu na to, nɛ a kilgi nchu belbelso. Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ka wora bumo ŋ keni na nɛ e sa bumo mbra

english_verse: Then he said, “I am the Lord your God, and I cure your diseases. If you obey me by doing right and by following my laws and teachings, I won't punish you with the diseases I sent on the Egyptians.”
translation_verse: nseŋ ŋini bumo ŋ kaŋɛ le: “Men baŋ bugi asoe nɛnɛ n nu ma, men Nyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be ebɔl nseŋ wora kusɔ nɛ k niŋi ashi ma anishito, nseŋ bɛ ma mbraana so bre, menyeeŋ baa kɔ eleŋ. Ma alɛ maaŋ ta alɔ wurbi be aleblawu nɛ n daŋ ta n lɛ ljiptebi so na n lɛ menyi so.”

english_verse: On the fifteenth day of the second month after the Israelites had escaped from Egypt, they left Elim and started through the western edge of the Sinai Desert in the direction of Mount Sinai.
translation_verse: B ka lar ljipt be kasawule so na be kufɔl nyɔsopo be kachɛ kuduanusopo na nɛ b lar Elim m pɛ kebee nɛ baa tre Sainai na be ekpa m ba fo Sin be keshishɛrsawule na so.

english_verse: There in the desert they started complaining to Moses and Aaron,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Israɛlebi na kikɛ naŋ fara a fubel a malga a gbiti Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn

english_verse: “We wish the Lord had killed us in Egypt. When we lived there, we could at least sit down and eat all the bread and meat we wanted. But you have brought us out here into this desert, where we are going to starve.”
translation_verse: a kaŋɛ le: “Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ daŋ shin nɛ an wu ashi ljipt be kasawule so gba, k daa bɔ, ŋkpal manɛ so, an ka daa wɔ ndoŋ, an daa nya eblaŋ nɛ ajibi kanaŋkamaso nɛ anyee sha a ji. Ama kumo nɛ men bar anyi keshishɛrsawule ere so m ba ka shin nɛ men ta akoŋ m mɔ anyi kikɛ na.”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “I will send bread down from heaven like rain. Tell the people to go out each day and gather only enough for that day. That's how I will see if they obey me.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Mosis: “Keni meeŋ shin nɛ ajibi e shi esoso n wurge fanɛ bɔrɛ na n sa menyi nɛ basa na e baa lar n ya kaa muu amo kananɛ baaŋ tiŋ n ji karechɛ kama. Loŋ nɛ meeŋ wora bumo ŋ keni baa bɛ ma keŋini so a?

english_verse: But on the sixth day of each week they must gather and cook twice as much.”
translation_verse: Ama kachɛ shesopo na bre, b muu nchɛnnyɔ be ajibi n daŋɛ amo m barga amo to ntuŋ anyɔ ŋkpal b ka maaŋ muu amo kachɛ shunusopo na so.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron told the people, “This evening you will know that the Lord was the one who rescued you from Egypt.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn kaŋɛ Israɛlebi na kikɛ le: “Ta a ba kaaseso menyeeŋ pin fanɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na gbagba e lara menyi ashi ljipt be kasawule so.

english_verse: And in the morning you will see his glorious power, because he has heard your complaints against him. Why should you grumble to us? Who are we?”
translation_verse: Echefo chipurso menyeeŋ wu Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be kemaŋkura, ŋkpal manɛ so, e nu menyi be mmalga nɛ menyee malga a gbiti mo na kikɛ. Mo nɛ men daa malga ŋ gbiti na, mannɛ anyi.”

english_verse: Then Moses continued, “You will know it is the Lord when he gives you meat each evening and more than enough bread each morning. He is really the one you are complaining about, not us—we are nobodies—but the Lord has heard your complaints.”
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ Mosis naŋ kaŋɛ bumo le: “Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e la esa mo nɛ e beeŋ baa sa menyi eblaŋ kaaseso nɛ men baa we, nseŋ naa sa menyi ajibi malɛ chipurso kanaŋkamaso nɛ k daga. Ŋkpal manɛ so, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nu menyi be nfubel, manɛ e la anyi nɛ menyee malga gbiti anyi? Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ menyee malga a gbiti, mannɛ anyi.”

english_verse: Moses turned to Aaron and said, “Bring the people together, because the Lord has heard their complaints.”
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Mosis kaŋɛ Ɛɛrɔn: “Kaŋɛ Israɛlebi na kikɛ fanɛ b ba Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be anishito, ŋkpal manɛ so, e nu bumo be nfubel.”

english_verse: Aaron was speaking to them, when everyone looked out toward the desert and saw the bright glory of the Lord in a cloud.
translation_verse: Ɛɛrɔn ka bee malga a sa Israɛlebi na nɛ b keni keshishɛrsawule na be kaba so n wu Enyɛnpe be kemaŋkura ka bee nyaŋɛ kuwɔlpa to epul na to.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Mosis:

english_verse: “I have heard my people complain. Now tell them that each evening they will have meat and each morning they will have more than enough bread. Then they will know that I am the Lord their God.”
translation_verse: “N nu nfubel damta ashi Israɛlebi na kutɔ, amoso kaŋɛ bumo le: ‘Ta a ba kaaseso saŋɛ nɛ kaboŋ bee jija to na menyeeŋ we eblaŋ. Kachipurso malɛ nɛ men nya ajibi n ji kananɛ menyee sha nseŋ pin fanɛ ma e la Enyɛnpe, menyi be Ebɔrɛ na.’ ”

english_verse: That evening a lot of quails came and landed everywhere in the camp, and the next morning dew covered the ground.
translation_verse: Kaase ka fo nɛ mbuibi nɛ baa tre kweels na baŋ ba chase bumo be echenakpa na kikɛ. Kachipurso malɛ nɛ bunyaŋ tɔr ŋ kulti bumo be echenakpa na kikɛ.

english_verse: After the dew had gone, the desert was covered with thin flakes that looked like frost.
translation_verse: Bunyaŋ na ka yɔ nɛ asɔ fufulbi patapatabi ko malɛ ba keshishɛrsawule kikɛ nyam so.

english_verse: The people had never seen anything like this, and they started asking each other, “What is it?” Moses answered, “This is the bread that the Lord has given you to eat.
translation_verse: Israɛlebi na ka wu amo nɛ b bishi abar: “Manɛ nna?” Ŋkpal manɛ so, b daa maŋ nyi kusɔ nɛ k daa la asɔ na. Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis kaŋɛ bumo le: “Ajibi nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ sa menyi fanɛ men baa ji nna na.

english_verse: And he orders you to gather about two liters for each person in your family—that should be more than enough.”
translation_verse: Ama mbra nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ sa e la fanɛ ekama e muu kanaŋkamaso nɛ e beeŋ tiŋ n ji nseŋ muu kurwa kurwa n sa esa kama nɛ e wɔ mbe wajɛbu to.”

english_verse: They did as they were told. Some gathered more and some gathered less.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Israɛlebi na wora kusɔ nɛ Mosis kaŋɛ bumo na, beko daŋ muu ga ga nna nɛ beko malɛ muu gbrɛgbrɛ.

english_verse: Some of them disobeyed, but the next morning what they kept was stinking and full of worms, and Moses was angry.
translation_verse: Ama bumo be beko daa maŋ wora kasonu n sa Mosis nseŋ ta amo be ako n yili ŋklade. Kare ka chɛ nɛ a bɛ a dufɛ nɛ ashushombi bɔlɔ amo to nɛ Mosis nya agbo n wora Israɛlebi na.

english_verse: Each morning everyone gathered as much as they needed, and in the heat of the day the rest melted.
translation_verse: Kare baŋ naŋ chɛ kachipurso esa kama bee muu kananɛ e beeŋ tiŋ n ji nna. Epeŋi baŋ bel na nɛ amo nɛ a ka kasawule so na kikɛ e ŋalga.

english_verse: However, on the sixth day of the week, everyone gathered enough to have four liters, instead of two. When the leaders reported this to Moses,
translation_verse: Kachɛ shesopo na bre ekama daa muu kananɛ e bee muu karechɛ kikɛ be ntuŋnyɔso nna. Kumo be kaman nɛ Israɛlebi na be bejuŋkparpo kikɛ e yɔ Mosis kutɔ n ya kaa kaŋɛ mo amo be asheŋ.

english_verse: he told them that the Lord had said, “Tomorrow is the Sabbath, a sacred day of rest in honor of me. So gather all you want to bake or boil, and make sure you save enough for tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Mosis kaŋɛ bumo: “Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nase mbra nna fanɛ echefo la mo gbagba be kachɛ cheembi nɛ e lara nɛ k baa la ewushi be kachɛ nna. Amoso, men tɔ amo nɛ menyee sha ketɔ edɛ to n ji nseŋ daŋɛ amo nɛ menyee sha kedaŋɛ n ji malɛ nseŋ ta amo nɛ a ka na n yili echefo.”

english_verse: The people obeyed, and the next morning the food smelled fine and had no worms.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ b ta amo nɛ a ka na n yili ŋklade fanɛ kananɛ Mosis kaŋɛ bumo na. Amo alɛ daa maŋ bure ashushombi ŋko m bɛ a dufɛ.

english_verse: “You may eat the food,” Moses said. “Today is the Sabbath in honor of the Lord, and there won't be any of this food on the ground today.
translation_verse: Nɛ Mosis kaŋɛ bumo: “Men ji ade kabre, ŋkpal kabre ka la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be kewushiachɛ so, men maaŋ nya ako m muu kasawule.

english_verse: You will find it there for the first six days of the week, but not on the Sabbath.”
translation_verse: Nchɛnshe she nɛ menyeeŋ baa muu amo, ama kachɛ shunusopo nɛ k la kewushiachɛ na bre men maaŋ nya amo m muu.”

english_verse: A few of the Israelites did go out to look for some, but there was none.
translation_verse: Amo nɛ amo kikɛ basa na be beko daŋ naŋ yɔ nna nɛ b ya muu amo kachɛ shunusopo na, bumo alɛ maŋ wu amo.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “Moses, how long will you people keep disobeying my laws and teachings?
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ bishi Mosis: “Manɛ nna nɛ men wɔtɔ a kini kebɛ ma mbraana so?

english_verse: Remember that I was the one who gave you the Sabbath. That's why on the sixth day I provide enough bread for two days. Everyone is to stay home and rest on the Sabbath.”
translation_verse: Keni! Men nyiŋi fanɛ ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e sa menyi kewushiachɛ na, amoso nɛ kachɛ shesopo na mee sa menyi be ekama nchɛnnyɔ be ajibi na. Kachɛ shunusopo na, ekama e shir a wɔ mbe laŋ to. Esa kama e sa maŋ lar kowu kikɛ.”

english_verse: And so they rested on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Amoso basa na daa wushi kachɛ shunusopo na nna.

english_verse: The Israelites called the bread manna. It was white like coriander seed and delicious as wafers made with honey.
translation_verse: Israɛl be basa daa tre loŋ be ajibi na ‘manna’ nna. Amo alɛ daa du wurwurbi n fuli fanɛ ateebi nsaa du belbel fanɛ mushoŋ nna.

english_verse: Moses told the people that the Lord had said, “Store up two liters of this manna, because I want future generations to see the food I gave you during the time you were in the desert after I rescued you from Egypt.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis kaŋɛ bumo le: “To, kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ta n sa anyi a yɔ ajibi na be kaplɛa so nde. E yɛ: ‘Men ta manna na fanɛ kurwa n yili menyi be kaman to ebi, saŋɛ na so baaŋ ba wu ajibi nɛ ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na daa sa menyi keshishɛrsawule so, saŋɛ nɛ n lara menyi ashi ljipt be kasawule so na.’ ”

english_verse: Then Moses told Aaron, “Put some manna in a jar and store it in the place of worship for future generations to see.”
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Mosis kaŋɛ Ɛɛrɔn le: “Jɔ manna na be kurwa be bɔlɔ n wɔtɔ kɔlba to n yili kakpa nɛ menyee bunyaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nɛ a baa yil anyi be kaman to ebi kikɛ.”

english_verse: Aaron followed the Lord's instructions and put the manna in front of the sacred chest for safekeeping.
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ka baŋ kaŋɛ Mosis na, nɛ e shin nɛ Ɛɛrɔn ta amo n yili kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre be deka na be anishito, nɛ a baa yil ndoŋ.

english_verse: The Israelites left the desert and moved from one place to another each time the Lord ordered them to. Once they camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for them to drink.
translation_verse: Israɛlebi na kikɛ daŋ naŋ koso Sin be keshishɛrsawule na so nna a na a bɛ kananɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ daŋ ŋini bumo na so n ya yuu bumo be ewajɛbu ashi Refidim. Ndoŋ malɛ daa maŋ kɔ nchu nɛ b nuu.

english_verse: The people started complaining to Moses, “Give us some water!” Moses replied, “Why are you complaining to me and trying to put the Lord to the test?”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ baa fubel a kaŋɛ Mosis le: “Sa anyi nchu nɛ an nuu.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis bishi bumo: “Manɛ nna nɛ menyee fubel loŋ? Manɛ nna nɛ menyee wora Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na a keni?”

english_verse: But the people were thirsty and kept on complaining, “Moses, did you bring us out of Egypt just to let us and our families and our animals die of thirst?”
translation_verse: Ama ŋkpal achukoŋ ka daa kɔ basa na ga so b baa bile asheŋ nna nsaa malga a gbiti Mosis a bishi mo: “Manɛ nna bre nɛ fo lara anyi ashi Ijipt m ba kaa shin nɛ fo ta achukoŋ m mɔ anyi nɛ an be mbia nɛ asɔbɔya kikɛ ere?”

english_verse: Then Moses prayed to the Lord, “What am I going to do with these people? They are about to stone me to death!”
translation_verse: Asheŋ na ka daŋ ki loŋ na nɛ Mosis shu n tre Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ m bishi mo: “Nuso nɛ meeŋ wora basa ere? A ka gbrɛbi nɛ b kpa ma ajembu m mɔ nna na.”

english_verse: The Lord answered, “Take some of the leaders with you and go ahead of the rest of the people. Also take along the walking stick with which you struck the Nile River.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Mosis le: “Ta fo kekpabi nɛ fo daŋ ta ŋ ŋmɛa Nail be lɔr na so na nseŋ keta Israɛlebi be benimu na be beko n ti fo kumu so n choŋ basa na so n yɔ anishito.

english_verse: When you get to the rock at Mount Sinai, I will be there with you. Strike the rock with the stick, and water will pour out for the people to drink.” Moses did this while the leaders watched.

english_verse: These judges can handle the ordinary cases and bring the more difficult ones to you. Having them to share the load will make your work easier.

english_verse: This is the way God wants it done. You won't be under nearly as much stress, and everyone else will return home feeling satisfied.
translation_verse: Kananɛ Ebɔrɛ bee sha fanɛ asheŋ e baa du nna na. Saŋɛ na so fo maaŋ naa gben ga nɛ basa ere malɛ e baa ta ŋgbenefuli a yɔ epe.”

english_verse: After Moses and his father-in-law Jethro had said goodbye to each other, Jethro returned home.
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ Mosis shuŋi mo shanyɛn Jetro ekpa nɛ e bɛta n yɔ mbe efuli so.

english_verse: You saw what I did in Egypt, and you know how I brought you here to me, just as a mighty eagle carries its young.
translation_verse: ‘Men wu kusɔ nɛ n daŋ wora Ijiptebi na nɛ kananɛ n daŋ ta menyi fanɛ kusore ka ta mo pibi a firgi na, m bar menyi ma kutɔ nfe.

translation_verse: Menyi alɛ beeŋ baa la kanaŋ cheembi to ebi nɛ bɔrɛmatapoana nɛ b shi kuwurji be kanaŋ cheembi to.’ Kusɔ nɛ mee sha fanɛ fo kaŋɛ Israɛlebi nna na.”

english_verse: and they all promised, “We will do everything the Lord has commanded.” So Moses told the Lord about this.
translation_verse: Nɛ basa na kikɛ chɛ abar n shuli so ŋ kaŋɛ: “Anyeeŋ wora asheŋ nɛ Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ na kikɛ.” Kumo be kaman nɛ Mosis ya kaŋɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kusɔ nɛ basa na malɛ kaŋɛ na.

translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Mosis: “Keni, meeŋ bɔla kuwɔlpagboŋ ko to a malga fo kutɔ, saŋɛ na so basa na beeŋ nu ŋ ka bee malga fo kutɔ nsaa yirda fo saŋkama.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis naŋ kaŋɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ asheŋ nɛ bejuŋkparpoana na malɛ malga kikɛ.
