translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Mosis: “Bɛta n yɔ basa na kutɔ n ya kaŋɛ bumo nɛ b ta kabre nɛ echefo n lara alubi ashi bumo be ŋgbene to nseŋ ki cheembi. K daga fanɛ b fɔr bumo be asɔbuuso gba

english_verse: On the morning of the third day there was thunder and lightning. A thick cloud covered the mountain, a loud trumpet blast was heard, and everyone in camp trembled with fear.
translation_verse: Kumo be kachɛ na be kachipurdidi nɛ bɔrɛ nyɛkpɛ nseŋ ponte nɛ kuwɔlpagboŋ ko ba kebeegboŋ na be awɔlto nɛ kabel ponte awɔrso nɛ basa mo nɛ b daa wɔ kaboŋ na chicha kufuso.

translation_verse: Kumo be kachɛ na, Sainai be kebeegboŋ na so kikɛ daŋ baa la edishi nna, ŋkpal manɛ so, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ daŋ bɔla edɛ to nna m ba kumo so. Nɛ kumo be edishi na daŋ yɔ awɔlto fanɛ edishi nɛ a shi edɛ nɛ baa chɔɔ nɛ a shi ga na nɛ kebeegboŋ na kikɛ gbuŋgbuŋ to eleŋso.

translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ mo le: “Yɔ n ya kpele basa na kusoe fanɛ b sa maŋ kaŋ temba egbaŋ na a fin kewu ma kenishiso. B kaŋ baŋ wora loŋ, bumo be bedamta beeŋ wu.

translation_verse: Basa na kikɛ daŋ ya kaa yil kufɔ kufɔ nna nɛ Mosis bre firgi n taga ketentembirigboŋ na to ashi kakpa nɛ Ebɔrɛ daa wɔ na. Bɔrɛsure be mbraana be asheŋ

translation_verse: Ŋkpal manɛ so, nchɛ ashe nɛ ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ta n to esoso nɛ kasawule nɛ teku nɛ asɔ nɛ a wɔ amo to kikɛ nseŋ wushi kachɛ shunusopo na, amoso ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nɛfa kewushiachɛ na nna nseŋ ta kumo ŋ ki kachɛ cheembi.

translation_verse: Men sa maa yɛlga men baraana be nwu ŋko bumo be beche ŋko bumo be anya ŋko bumo be ana ŋko ekurma ŋko kusɔ kama nɛ k la men braana peya.” Kufu ka daŋ pɛ basa na be asheŋ (Ditɛronɔmi

translation_verse: Basa na ka daŋ wu bɔrɛ ka nyɛkpɛ m ponte nɛ kabel ponte awɔrso nɛ b wu edishi ka sɔ kebeegboŋ na kikɛ so na nɛ kufu pɛ bumo nɛ b chicha kufuso nseŋ bɛta n yɔ kufɔ n ya yili.

translation_verse: Kede be kaman, men sa maŋ kaŋ pɔr bɔrɛsure nɛ menyeeŋ baa ta kasakpar a dii so. Ŋkpal manɛ so, men baa dii kasakpar na baaŋ baa wu men be mboŋ gela.”

english_verse: Death is the punishment for attacking your father or mother.
translation_verse: Esa kama malɛ nɛ e ŋmɛa mo tuto ŋko mo nio, k daga fanɛ b mɔ mo.

english_verse: Suppose two of you are arguing, and you hit the other with either a rock or your fist, without causing a fatal injury. If the victim has to stay in bed,
translation_verse: Basa anyɔ malɛ baa bile nɛ eko ŋmɛa mo barkasa kejembu ŋko m bɔ kuluŋguntuŋ ŋ ŋmɛa mo nɛ e maŋ wu, nseŋ nu ebesa a dese ebu to ŋkpal keŋmɛa na so,

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses the following laws for his people:
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ebɔrɛ naŋ kaŋɛ Mosis le: “Naŋ ta le be mbraana ere n sa Israɛlebi na.

english_verse: If you buy a Hebrew slave, he must remain your slave for six years. But in the seventh year you must set him free, without cost to him.
translation_verse: Fo baŋ tɔ kenya nɛ e la Israɛl be esa, nfɛnshe e daga e ka shuŋ fo, ama kafɛ shunusopo bre to, k daga fanɛ fo shin nɛ e nya mbe kumu nsaa maŋ ka shɛŋ.

english_verse: If he was single at the time you bought him, he alone must be set free. But if he was married at the time, both he and his wife must be given their freedom.
translation_verse: Nɛ k la fanɛ kenya na nawule e ba mo nyɛnpe na be enɔ to, k daga fanɛ mo nawule e baa yɔ. Ama nɛ mo nɛ mbe eche e ba bre, kumo ere k daga fanɛ mo nɛ mbe eche na kikɛ e baa yɔ.

english_verse: If you give him a wife, and they have children, only the man himself must be set free; his wife and children remain the property of his owner.
translation_verse: Nɛ fanɛ mo nyɛnpe e sa mo eche nɛ mo nɛ eche na kurge mbinyɛnso ŋko mbicheso, kumo ere k daga fanɛ eche na nɛ mbe mbia kikɛ ka ki mo nyɛnpe na peya nɛ mo nawule e nya mbe kumu a yɔ.

english_verse: But suppose the slave loves his wife and children and his owner so much that he won't leave them.
translation_verse: Ama nɛ fanɛ kenya na bugi to ŋ kaŋɛ le: ‘Mee sha n nyɛnpe nɛ ma eche nɛ ma mbia ga, amoso m maaŋ sɔ ma kumu’,

english_verse: Then he must stand beside either the door or the doorpost at the place of worship, while his owner punches a small hole through one of his ears with a sharp metal rod. This makes him a slave for life.
translation_verse: kumo ere a daga fanɛ mo nyɛnpe na ka keta mo n yɔ kakpa nɛ baa shuŋ Ebɔrɛ na n ya shin nɛ e yili m mata kukuloŋ ŋko kabuna to nɛ e futi mbe kusoe, a ŋini fanɛ e beeŋ baa la mo nyɛnpe be kenya hale nɛ e ya wu.

english_verse: A young woman who was sold by her father doesn't gain her freedom in the same way that a man does.
translation_verse: Nɛ enyɛn kama baŋ fa mo pibiche fanɛ kenya, mo ere maaŋ tiŋ n nya mbe kumu fanɛ anya nyɛnso na.

english_verse: If she doesn't please the man who bought her to be his wife, he must let her be bought back. He cannot sell her to foreigners; this would break the contract he made with her.
translation_verse: Ama nɛ b fa mo n sa enyɛn nɛ e ta mo ŋ ki mbe eche nseŋ naŋ kini mo, kumo ere e naŋ bɛta n fa mo n sa mbe basa, ŋkpal manɛ so esa nɛ e kini mo na maŋ kɔ ekpa nɛ e fa mo n sa esa pɔtɛ kama ŋkpal kananɛ e ŋaba mo na so so.

english_verse: If he selects her as a wife for his son, he must treat her as his own daughter.
translation_verse: Nɛ esa tɔ kenyache n sa mo pibinyɛn fanɛ e ta a kil, a daga fanɛ e keni mo so fanɛ mo gbagba pibiche.

english_verse: If the man later marries another woman, he must continue to provide food and clothing for the one he bought and to treat her as a wife.
translation_verse: Enyɛn kama malɛ nɛ e ta eche n ti mbe kenyache so, k daga nna fanɛ e baa kraa sa mbe eche juŋkparso na ajibi nɛ asɔbuuso nɛ keche nɛ kenyɛn be kedi be kasha nɛ k daga mo ashi mbe kakil to.

english_verse: If he fails to do any of these things, she must be given her freedom without paying for it. Murder and Other Violent Crimes The Lord said:
translation_verse: Nɛ enyɛn na baa maŋ wora le be asɔ asa ere m bɔlɔ so, kumo ere eche na kɔ ekpa nɛ e lar mbe enɔ to nsaa maŋ ka shɛŋ. Eleŋ be keŋini be mbra be asheŋ

english_verse: But if you did not intend to kill someone, and I, the Lord, let it happen anyway, you may run for safety to a place that I have set aside.
translation_verse: Ama nɛ k ba fanɛ e maŋ kute nna n wora loŋ, kumo ere Ebɔrɛ be kushuŋ nna, amoso e beeŋ tiŋ n shile n yɔ kakpa nɛ meeŋ ŋini menyi na n ya nya mbe kumu.

english_verse: If you plan in advance to murder someone, there's no escape, not even by holding on to my altar. You will be dragged off and killed.
translation_verse: Ama nɛ esa baŋ kute m mɔ mo barkasa bre, hale nɛ e shile n yɔ ma bɔrɛsure na ase gba, k daga fanɛ b mɔ mo.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for kidnapping. If you sell the person you kidnapped, or if you are caught with that person, the penalty is death.
translation_verse: Esa kama nɛ e yuri dimɛdi n fa ŋko n ta mo a kɔ fanɛ kenya, amodoŋwura gba daga luwu.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for cursing your father or mother.
translation_verse: Esa kama malɛ nɛ e sho mo tuto ŋko mo nio kɔnɔ daga luwu.

english_verse: and later has to use a stick when walking outside, you must pay for the loss of time and do what you can to help until the injury is completely healed. That's your only responsibility.
translation_verse: kachɛ nɛ e baŋ niŋi to n ta kekpabi n lar kowu, k daga fanɛ esa nɛ e ŋmɛa mo na ka ka nchɛ nɛ esa na dese na kikɛ be kukɔ. Kumo be kaman k daga e ka keni elɔpo na so nɛ e nya alenfia.

english_verse: However, if the slave lives a few days after the beating, you are not to be punished. After all, you have already lost the services of that slave who was your property.
translation_verse: Ama nɛ kenya na ji kachɛ koŋwule ŋko nchɛnnyɔ pɔɛŋ nseŋ wu bre, kumo ere mo nyɛnpe maŋ daga kasogberge, ŋkpal manɛ so, e paŋ mbe kapetɛ nna na.

english_verse: Suppose a pregnant woman suffers a miscarriage as the result of an injury caused by someone who is fighting. If she isn't badly hurt, the one who injured her must pay whatever fine her husband demands and the judges approve.
translation_verse: Nɛ basa anyɔ malɛ bee bile nseŋ nu edampoche ko ebesa nɛ mbe kedampo na gbeŋi, nɛ shɛŋ maŋ naŋ wora mo, k daga esa nɛ e nu mo ebesa na ka ka amansherbi kanaŋkamaso nɛ edampoche na mo kul beeŋ ku n sa mo. Kumo alɛ daga fanɛ k bɛ kananɛ ndoŋ be demujipoana bee yili asheŋ so.

english_verse: If you hit one of your slaves and cause the loss of an eye, the slave must be set free.
translation_verse: Nɛ esa baŋ ŋmɛa mbe kenyache ŋko mbe kenyanyɛn be kenishi m bure, k daga fanɛ e shin nɛ kenya na e baa yɔ nsaa maŋ ka shɛŋ ŋkpal kenishi na so.

english_verse: A bull that kills someone with its horns must be killed and its meat destroyed, but the owner of the bull isn't responsible for the death.
translation_verse: Esa kama nɛ mbe gbolu pur enyɛn ŋko eche, nɛ e wu, b kpa gbolu na ajembu m mɔ, ama b sa maŋ kaŋ we gbolu na be eblaŋ. Kumo be kaman k maŋ daga fanɛ b naŋ gberge gboluwura na kusoe.

english_verse: Suppose you own a bull that has been in the habit of attacking people, but you have refused to keep it fenced in. If that bull kills someone, both you and the bull must be put to death by stoning.
translation_verse: Ama nɛ k la fanɛ gbolu na chɛr a tɔrɔ basa nna nɛ b kpele mo nawura kusoe nɛ e yige nɛ k ya chute esa m mɔ, kumo ere k daga fanɛ b kpa gbolu na ajembu m mɔ nseŋ mɔ mo nawura na gba.

english_verse: pieces of silver for the loss of the slave, and the bull must be killed by stoning.
translation_verse: Ama nɛ gboluwura na shuli fanɛ e beeŋ ka kukɔ n sɔ mbe ŋkpa n yige, kumo ere k daga e ka kanaŋkamaso nɛ baaŋ ku kukɔ na n sa mo.

english_verse: This same law applies if the bull gores someone's son or daughter.
translation_verse: Nɛ fanɛ gbolu na pur esa ko pibinyɛn ŋko ebiche nna, loŋ koŋwule na e daga fanɛ b yili kumo.

english_verse: Suppose someone's ox or donkey is killed by falling into an open pit that you dug or left uncovered on your property.
translation_verse: Nɛ esa baaŋ bugi kemaŋ so ŋkoŋ kur kumo mo gbagba nsaa maŋ buu kumo so nɛ esa ko be kena ŋko kurma tɔr kumo to,

english_verse: You must pay for the dead animal, and it becomes yours.
translation_verse: k daga fanɛ kemaŋ na wura ka ka kusɔbɔya na be kukɔ nseŋ ta kusɔbɔya wuso na.

english_verse: If your bull kills someone else's, yours must be sold. Then the money from your bull and the meat from the dead bull must be divided equally between you and the other owner.
translation_verse: Nɛ fanɛ esa ko be gbolu mɔ mo barkasa be gbolu malɛ nna, k daga fanɛ b fa gbolu keniso na nseŋ barga kumo be amansherbi to n sa abar.

english_verse: If you refuse to fence in a bull that is known to attack others, you must replace any animal it kills, but the dead animal will belong to you.
translation_verse: Ama nɛ fanɛ gbolu na chɛr a pur nna nɛ mo nawura nyi nsaa maŋ chɛ kumo m muni, kumo ere k daga fanɛ e ta gbolu keniso n tal mo barkasa na to nseŋ ta gbolu wuso na.”

english_verse: If you steal an ox and slaughter or sell it, you must replace it with five oxen; if you steal a sheep and slaughter it or sell it, you must replace it with four sheep.
translation_verse: Esa baŋ yuri kena m mɔ ŋko n fa, k daga fanɛ e ka ana anu, nɛ kubolpɔ malɛ nna, a daga e ka mbolpɔ ana n tal to.

english_verse: But if you cannot afford to replace the animals, you must be sold as a slave to pay for what you have stolen. If you steal an ox, donkey, or sheep, and are caught with it still alive, you must pay the owner double. If you happen to kill a burglar who breaks into your home after dark, you are not guilty. But if you kill someone who breaks in during the day, you are guilty of murder.
translation_verse: K daga fanɛ esa e ka kusɔ kama nɛ e yuri be kukɔ. Nɛ e maŋ kɔ nɛ e ka malɛ, b fa mo fanɛ kenya ŋ ka kusɔ nɛ e yuri na be kukɔ. Nɛ esa yuri kena ŋko kurma ŋko kubolpɔ nɛ b ya wu kumo amodoŋwura kutɔ nɛ k kraa keni, k daga fanɛ e ka loŋ be asɔbɔya anyɔ n sa kusɔbɔyawura. Nɛ esa bee kɔ a fin keluri esa be laŋ to n yuri kanyɛso, nɛ b ŋmɛa mo m mɔ, esa nɛ e mɔ mo na maŋ wora kulubi, ama nɛ k la kapaso bre, esa nɛ e mɔ mo na wora kulubi ŋkpal e ka mɔ mo na so.

english_verse: If you allow any of your animals to stray from your property and graze in someone else's field or vineyard, you must repay the damage from the best part of your own harvest of grapes and grain.
translation_verse: Nɛ fanɛ esa baŋ yige mbe asɔbɔya nɛ b luri mo barkasa be ndɔ to n ji mbe asɔ, k daga fanɛ asɔbɔyawura na e lara mbe adɔjibi nɛ a walɛ ga na n ya tal mo barkasa na to.

english_verse: If you carelessly let a fire spread from your property to someone else's, you must pay the owner for any crops or fields destroyed by the fire.
translation_verse: Nɛ esa puga edɛ nɛ a chɔɔ m bɔla afitiriwurbi so n ya luri mo barkasa be ndɔ to n chɔɔ mbe adɔjibi, esa nɛ e puga edɛ na daga fanɛ e ka mo barkasa na be adɔjibi nɛ a chɔɔ na be kukɔ.

english_verse: Suppose a neighbor asks you to keep some silver or other valuables, and they are stolen from your house. If the thief is caught, the thief must repay double.
translation_verse: Nɛ esa ta amansherbi ŋko asɔ n sa mo barkasa nɛ e yili nɛ eyu ya yuri amo ashi mbe ebu to nɛ b pɛ eyu na nna, k daga fanɛ eyu na e ka loŋ be asɔ be ale anyɔ.

english_verse: Suppose two people claim to own the same ox or donkey or sheep or piece of clothing. Then the judges must decide the case, and the guilty person will pay the owner double.
translation_verse: Nɛ basa anyɔ bee kɔ a mɔlga kusɔ foeso fanɛ kusɔbɔya ŋko kusɔbuuso, nɛ k ki bumo emɔrɔ, k daga fanɛ b ta demu na n yɔ Ebɔrɛ be anishito demujipoana kutɔ nɛ b mige to. Kumo be kaman nɛ b shin nɛ emo nɛ e bee puni kumo na e ka kusɔ nɛ e bee puni na be ntuŋ anyɔ n sa mo barkasa na.

english_verse: Suppose a neighbor who is going to be away asks you to keep a donkey or an ox or a sheep or some other animal, and it dies or gets injured or is stolen while no one is looking.
translation_verse: Nɛ esa ta mbe kusɔbɔya n sa mo barkasa fanɛ e baa keni so nɛ kusɔbɔya na wu ŋko n nya doro ŋko n foe nɛ esa kama maŋ wu kumo,

english_verse: But if the animal was stolen while in your care, you must replace it.
translation_verse: Ama nɛ fanɛ b yuri kusɔbɔya na nna ashi esa nɛ e bee keni kumo so kutɔ, k daga fanɛ e ka kumo be kukɔ n tal to.

english_verse: If the animal was attacked and killed by a wild animal, and you can show the remains of the dead animal to its owner, you do not have to replace it.
translation_verse: Nɛ k ba fanɛ kupuŋ to be kusɔbɔya e mɔ kumo n ji, k daga fanɛ esa nɛ e bee keni kusɔbɔya na so ka ta kusɔbɔya jiŋka na m ba ŋini shɛdaso, saŋɛ na so, e maaŋ ka kumo be kukɔ n tal to.

english_verse: Suppose you borrow an animal from a neighbor, and it gets injured or dies while the neighbor isn't around. Then you must replace it.
translation_verse: Nɛ esa malɛ kule mo barkasa be kusɔbɔya nɛ k ya nya doro ŋko n wu, saŋɛ nɛ kusɔbɔya na wura maŋ wɔtɔ, k daga fanɛ e ka kusɔbɔya na be kukɔ.

english_verse: But if something happens to the animal while the owner is present, you do not have to replace it. If you had leased the animal, the money you paid the owner will cover any harm done to it. Laws for Everyday Life The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ama nɛ fanɛ kusɔbɔya na wu saŋɛ nɛ kumowura wɔtɔ bre, k maŋ daga esa na ka ka kukɔ kikɛ. Nɛ e haya kusɔbɔya na nna bre, kumo ere haya na be kukɔ nɛ e beeŋ ka. Kachɛ kama be kebaawɔtɔ be mbra be asheŋ

english_verse: Suppose a young woman has never had sex and isn't engaged. If a man talks her into having sex, he must pay the bride price and marry her.
translation_verse: Esa kama nɛ e fule kasuŋgurbia nɛ e maŋ nyi enyɛn nɛ b maa chɔlta ŋ kil mo tumba, k daga fanɛ enyɛn na e ka keshaji be kukɔ n sa kasuŋgurbia na nseŋ ta mo ŋ ki mbe eche.

english_verse: But if her father refuses to let her marry the man, the bride price must still be paid.
translation_verse: Hale nɛ eche na mo tuto kini kasha na gba, k daga fanɛ enyɛn na e ka kasuŋgurbia na be tumba be kukɔ.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for witchcraft.
translation_verse: Eche kikɛ nɛ e kɔ kegba be ŋkilgisheŋ, b mɔ mo.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for having sex with an animal.
translation_verse: Enyɛn kama nɛ e tu kusɔbɔya n di keche nɛ kenyɛn, k daga fanɛ b mɔ mo.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for offering sacrifices to any god except me.
translation_verse: Esa kama nɛ e lara sarga n sa kegbir kama m baŋ ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ so, b mɔ mo.

english_verse: Do not mistreat widows or orphans.
translation_verse: Men saa maa mɛaŋ bekulpoche ŋko amunibi,

english_verse: If you do, they will beg for my help, and I will come to their rescue.
translation_verse: nɛ mannɛ aloŋ nɛ b shu n tre ma, Enyɛnpetale na, ma nɛ n nu bumo kushu na kashenteŋto

english_verse: In fact, I will get so angry that I will kill your men and make widows of their wives and orphans of their children.
translation_verse: nɛ ma agbo e koso nɛ n shin nɛ b ta tokobi m mɔ menyi nɛ menyi alɛ gba be beche e ki bekulpoche nɛ men be mbia e ki amunibi.

english_verse: Don't charge interest when you lend money to any of my people who are in need.
translation_verse: Ma basa to be etirpo baŋ paŋ ekama amansherbi, e sa maŋ wɔtɔ mo nchu.

english_verse: Before sunset you must return any coat taken as security for a loan,
translation_verse: Ekama nɛ e sɔ mo barkasa be wajɛ buuso n nase tarma, k daga fanɛ e bɛta kumo n sa mo pɔɛŋ nɛ epeŋi e tɔr,

english_verse: because that is the only cover the poor have when they sleep at night. I am a merciful God, and when they call out to me, I will come to help them.
translation_verse: ŋkpal manɛ so, kumo nawule e la mbe kusɔbuuso nɛ e bee buu a dese. Nɛ fo maŋ bɛta kumo n sa mo, manɛ nɛ e beeŋ buu n dese? Mannɛ aloŋ, nɛ kumodoŋwura baŋ shu n tre ma, meeŋ nu mbe kushu, ŋkpal ŋ ka la ewɔrwupo so.

english_verse: Don't speak evil of me or of the ruler of your people.
translation_verse: Ekama e sa maŋ kaŋ malga ŋ gbiti Ebɔrɛ ŋko n shoduu menyi to be ejuŋkparpo.

english_verse: Don't fail to give me the offerings of grain and wine that belong to me. Dedicate to me your first-born sons
translation_verse: Men sa maŋ kaŋ kini kesa ma men be adɔjibi nɛ asɔrso be asɔnuuso. Men ta men be ewurkoŋ nyɛnso

english_verse: and the first-born of your cattle and sheep. Let the animals stay with their mothers for seven days, then on the eighth day give them to me, your God.
translation_verse: nɛ men be ana nɛ mbolpɔ gba peya m bɔɔ ma enɔ. Asɔbɔya na bre daga fanɛ b baa wɔ bumo nioana kutɔ nchɛnshunu nna, kachɛ burwasopo na nɛ b ta amo m bɔɔ ma enɔ.

english_verse: You are my chosen people, so don't eat the meat of any of your livestock that was killed by a wild animal. Instead, feed the meat to dogs.
translation_verse: Men la ma basa cheembi nna, amoso men sa maa ji eblaŋ nɛ kupuŋ to be asɔbɔya jiŋka. Men baa ta amo a lɛ njɔnɔ.

english_verse: Always tell the truth in court, even if everyone else is dishonest and stands in the way of justice.
translation_verse: Men sa maa bɛ jimaŋ so a wora alubi ŋko a ji efɛ be shɛda ashi demujikpa.

english_verse: And don't favor the poor, simply because they are poor.
translation_verse: Men sa maa ji a chɛ esa to ŋkpal e ka la etirpo so.

english_verse: If you find an ox or a donkey that has wandered off, take it back where it belongs, even if the owner is your enemy.
translation_verse: Nɛ fo doŋ be kena ŋko kurma saŋɛ n shile n luri to a yɔ, k daga fanɛ fo kuŋ mo m bɛta m ba sa mo.

english_verse: If a donkey is overloaded and falls down, you must do what you can to help, even if it belongs to someone who doesn't like you.
translation_verse: Nɛ fo ya tu fo doŋ nɛ mbe kurma tɔr nɛ esulɔ deŋ mo so, k daga fanɛ fo chɛ mo to n niŋi kurma na to, sa maŋ kaŋ baŋ mo so n choŋ.

english_verse: Make sure that the poor are given equal justice in court.
translation_verse: Men sa maa mɔn betirpo kashenteŋ ashi demujikpa ŋkpal b ka la betirpo so.

english_verse: Don't bring false charges against anyone or sentence an innocent person to death. I won't forgive you if you do.
translation_verse: Men sa maa ku efɛ a deŋi basa so, ŋko a ji demu a kaŋɛ fanɛ basa nɛ b maŋ wora n jija daga luwu. Esa kama nɛ e wora loŋ maaŋ ji n lar ma anishito kikɛ.

english_verse: Don't accept bribes. Judges are blinded and justice is twisted by bribes.
translation_verse: Men sa maa sɔ brɔbu, ŋkpal manɛ so, brɔbu bee tan esa nna nɛ e maa wu kashenteŋ a ji.

english_verse: Don't mistreat foreigners. You were foreigners in Egypt, and you know what it is like. Laws for the Sabbath The Lord said:
translation_verse: Men sa maa mɛaŋ befɔ, ŋkpal manɛ so men nyi kananɛ kebaala efɔ du. Menyi alɛ gba daa la befɔ nna ashi Ijipt be kasawule so. Kewushiachɛ be mbra be asheŋ

english_verse: Plant and harvest your crops for six years,
translation_verse: “Men dɔ kudɔsawule kama so nfɛnshe

english_verse: but let the land rest during the seventh year. The poor are to eat what they want from your fields, vineyards, and olive trees during that year, and when they have all they want from your fields, leave the rest for wild animals.
translation_verse: nseŋ yige kumo nɛ k wushi kafɛ shunusopo na bre to. english_verse: Work the first six days of the week, but rest and relax on the seventh day. This law is not only for you, but for your oxen, donkeys, and slaves, as well as for any foreigners among you.
translation_verse: Men ta nchɛ ashe n shuŋ, nseŋ wushi kachɛ shunusopo na, saŋɛ na so men be ana dɔso nɛ ekurma gba beeŋ wushi. Nɛ men be elaŋ to be anya nɛ befɔ gba e wushi.

english_verse: Make certain that you obey everything I have said. Don't pray to other gods or even mention their names. Three Annual Festivals (Exodus
translation_verse: Men wora kasonu n sa kusɔ kama nɛ ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ menyi ere kikɛ. Menyi alɛ e sa maŋ kaŋ shuŋ kegbir kama ŋko a ti kegbir kama be ketre.” Nchɛgboŋ asa na be asheŋ (Ɛksodɔs

english_verse: Do not offer bread made with yeast when you sacrifice an animal to me. And make sure that the fat of the animal is burned that same day.
translation_verse: Men sa maŋ shin nɛ asɔbɔya nɛ men ta n lara sarga n sa ma na be ŋklaŋ nɛ kusɔ kama nɛ k kɔ yiisi e wea abar to. Menyi alɛ e sa maŋ shin nɛ kare e chɛ asɔbɔya nɛ men ta n lara sarga n sa ma kejigboŋana na to na be nfɔ so.

english_verse: Your women will give birth to healthy children, and everyone will live a long life.
translation_verse: Eche kikɛ be kedampo maaŋ gboŋi, ekama malɛ maaŋ ki egbentepo ashi men be kasawule so. Ma alɛ beeŋ sa menyi ŋkpa tenteŋ.

english_verse: Celebrate the Harvest Festival each spring when you start harvesting your wheat, and celebrate the Festival of Shelters each autumn when you pick your fruit.
translation_verse: Kasɔteŋi be jemanɛ baa fo, men wora Kasɔteŋi be Kejigboŋ. Kafɛ na ya kaa loge be saŋɛ nɛ menyee chala men be adɔjibi abar so na, men wora Kechala Abarso be Kejigboŋ na.

english_verse: Your men must come to these three festivals each year to worship me.
translation_verse: Kafɛ kikɛ to, a daga fanɛ menyi to be benyɛn kikɛ ka shɛr Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na be anishito ale asa.

english_verse: Celebrate three festivals each year in my honor.
translation_verse: Kafɛ kikɛ to men baa wora kejigboŋ be yiri yiri asa a bunyaŋ ma.

english_verse: Celebrate the Festival of Thin Bread by eating bread made without yeast, just as I have commanded. Do this at the proper time during the month of Abib, because it is the month when you left Egypt. And make certain that everyone brings the proper offerings.
translation_verse: Men baa wora bodobodo nɛ a maŋ kɔ yiisi na be kejigboŋ nchɛ ashunu kananɛ ŋ ŋini menyi na, Abib be kufɔl nɛ men daŋ lar kumo to ashi Ijipt be kasawule so na to. Loŋ be nchɛnshunu na to ekama e sa maŋ kaŋ ji bodobodo nɛ b ta yiisi n wora. Ekama malɛ e sa maŋ kaŋ ta enɔfuloŋ m ba ma anishito, ama e bar kusɔ ko m ba lara sarga n sa ma.

english_verse: Each year bring the best part of your first harvest to the place of worship. Don't boil a young goat in its mother's milk. A Promise and a Warning The Lord said:
translation_verse: Kafɛ kikɛ men baa ta men be adɔjibi juŋkparso lelaana a bar ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, ashi kakpa nɛ menyee bunyaŋ ma na. Men sa maŋ kaŋ daŋɛ kaboe fɔlbi kumo nio be kenyipochu to. Nnɔ naseso be asheŋ

english_verse: I am sending an angel to protect you and to lead you into the land I have ready for you.
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ bumo le: “Meeŋ shin nɛ malaika ko e baa juŋkpar menyi ŋ kuŋ menyi ekpa to loŋ n ya fo kaboŋ nɛ n lɔŋɛ n yili menyi na.

english_verse: My angel will lead you into the land of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites, and I will wipe them out.
translation_verse: Nɛ ma malaika na e juŋkpar menyi n yɔ Amɔriebi nɛ Hitebi nɛ Pɛrizebi nɛ Keenanebi nɛ Hivebi nɛ Jebusiebi be nsawule so nɛ m mur bumo kikɛ.

english_verse: Don't worship their gods or follow their customs. Instead, destroy their idols and shatter their stone images.
translation_verse: Men sa maŋ kaŋ bunyaŋ bumo be agbir na ŋko n shuŋ amo ŋko m bɛ bumo be edaŋkaresheŋ so. Men jija bumo agbirana na cheche nseŋ bure bumo be agbirjembu na to burburbi.

english_verse: Worship only me, the Lord your God! I will bless you with plenty of food and water and keep you strong.
translation_verse: Nɛ men baa shuŋ ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, men be Ebɔrɛ na, ma alɛ beeŋ nɛfa men be ajibi nɛ men be nchu nseŋ lara alɔana kikɛ ashi menyi to.

english_verse: I will terrify those nations and make your enemies so confused that they will run from you.
translation_verse: Meeŋ shin nɛ kufu nɛ keyeŋiyeŋi e tɔr basa nɛ menyee tu na so. Meeŋ shin nɛ men doŋana e kilgi n shile menyi.

english_verse: I will make the Hivites, Canaanites, and Hittites panic as you approach.
translation_verse: Meeŋ shin nɛ edundumbɔfo e juŋkpar n ya ju Hivebi nɛ Keenanebi nɛ Hitebi.

english_verse: But I won't do all this in the first year, because the land would become poor, and wild animals would be everywhere.
translation_verse: Ama m maaŋ ju bumo kafɛ koŋwule to, ŋkpal manɛ so, nɛ n wora loŋ, kasawule na beeŋ ki kiyitokpaŋ nɛ asɔbɔya lubi e wora keshi n sɔ kumo be kaplɛkama.

english_verse: Instead, I will force out your enemies little by little and give your nation time to grow strong enough to take over the land.
translation_verse: Amoso, gbrɛgbrɛ nɛ meeŋ baa ju bumo loŋ n ya fo saŋɛ nɛ menyeeŋ wora keshi nseŋ tiŋ n suge kasawule na kikɛ na.

english_verse: I will see that your borders reach from the Red Sea to the Euphrates River and from the Mediterranean Sea to the desert. I will let you defeat the people who live there, and you will force them out of the land.
translation_verse: Meeŋ shin nɛ men be ekar e yili teku peper na n ya fo Filistiebi be teku na nseŋ naŋ yili keshishɛrsawule na so n ya fo Yufreetes be lɔr na to. Meeŋ ta nsawule na so ebi m bɔɔ menyi enɔ nɛ men ju bumo ashi to.

english_verse: But you must not make any agreements with them or with their gods.
translation_verse: Men sa maŋ kaŋ shin nɛ menyi nɛ bumo nɛ bumo be agbirana e wora kɔnɔkoŋwule kikɛ.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Come up to me on this mountain. Bring along Aaron, as well as his two sons Nadab and Abihu, and
translation_verse: Kachako nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Mosis le: “Fo nɛ Ɛɛrɔn nɛ Nadab nɛ Abihu nɛ Israɛlebi be bejuŋkparpo adushunu e ba ma kutɔ ashi kebee ere ase nfe. Ama pɔɛŋ nɛ men fo kumo men feŋ n yili m bunyaŋ ma.

english_verse: Then Moses wrote down what the Lord had said. The next morning Moses got up early. He built an altar at the foot of the mountain and set up a large stone for each of the twelve tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis sibɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be mmalga na kikɛ n nase. Kare ka chɛ kachipurdidi nɛ e wule ŋ koso n ya yuu bɔrɛsure ashi kebee na be kaseto nseŋ ta ajembu tenteŋ kuduanyɔ n yuu nɛ a yili n sa Israɛlebi be eyiri kuduanyɔ na.

english_verse: He also sent some young men to burn offerings and to sacrifice bulls as special offerings to the Lord.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Mosis lara Israɛl be basa na to be mbrantiɛbia nɛ b ya lara sarga chɔɔso nseŋ ta ana n lara kɔnɔkoŋwuleso be esarga n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.

english_verse: Moses put half of the blood from the animals into bowls and sprinkled the rest on the altar.
translation_verse: Nɛ Mosis ta loŋ be asɔbɔya na be ŋklaŋ be bargato n wɔtɔ ntishaŋ to nseŋ ta bargato nɛ a ka na malɛ ŋ ŋmenyaŋ bɔrɛsure na so.

english_verse: Then he read aloud the Lord's commands and promises, and the people shouted, “We will obey the Lord and do everything he has commanded!”
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ e ta kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre be kawɔl na ŋ kraŋ kumo awɔrso nɛ basa na nu nseŋ kaŋɛ le: “Mmalga nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na malga na kikɛ, anyeeŋ bɛ amo so nseŋ wora kasonu n sa amo.”

english_verse: Moses took the blood from the bowls and sprinkled it on the people. Next, he told them, “With this blood the Lord makes his agreement with you.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis ta ŋklaŋ na be amo nɛ a wɔ ntishaŋ to na malɛ ŋ ŋmenyaŋ basa na so nseŋ kaŋɛ le: “Men keni kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre nɛ menyi nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ bɔla mmalga ere kikɛ so n nase na be ŋklaŋ nna na.”

english_verse: and saw the God of Israel. Under his feet was something that looked like a pavement made out of sapphire, and it was as bright as the sky.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nɛ b wu Israɛl be Ebɔrɛ na, nɛ kaboŋ dɛdɛso nɛ k du fanɛ yawukpakpaso be kejembu nɛ baa tre safiri na nseŋ fulto parr fanɛ awɔlpa na, ka wɔ mbe aya be kaseto.

english_verse: Even though these leaders of Israel saw God, he did not punish them. So they ate and drank. Moses on Mount Sinai
translation_verse: Ama Ebɔrɛ daa maŋ teŋi mbe enɔ m bar tɔrɔ Israɛl be bejuŋkparpo na be ekama so. B daŋ wu mo kenishiso nseŋ kraa wɔtɔ a ji a nuu. Mosis ka dii n yɔ Sainai be kebee na so be asheŋ

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Come up on the mountain and stay here for a while. I will give you the two flat stones on which I have written the laws that my people must obey.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Mosis: “Dii m ba kaa jo ma kebee ere be esoso nɛ n sa fo ajembu pantraŋ pantrambi nɛ n sibɛ mbra nɛ ma mmalga n deŋi so nɛ a baa ŋini Israɛlebi kananɛ baaŋ ba wora asheŋ.”

english_verse: Moses and Joshua his assistant got ready, then Moses started up the mountain to meet with God.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis nɛ mbe kayɛrbi Joshuwa wora shiriya nɛ Mosis dii n yɔ Ebɔrɛ be kebee na so.

english_verse: When Moses went up on Mount Sinai, a cloud covered it,
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Mosis yɔ kebee na so nɛ kuwɔlpa buu kebee na kikɛ so.

english_verse: and the bright glory of the Lord came down and stayed there. The cloud covered the mountain for six days, and on the seventh day the Lord told Moses to come into the cloud.
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be kemaŋkura gbelge m ba Sainai be kebee na so nɛ kuwɔlpa na buu kumo so hale n ya fo nchɛnshe. Kachɛ shunusopo na nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ shi kuwɔlpa na be nferinto n tre Mosis.

english_verse: Tell everyone in Israel who wants to give gifts that they must bring them to you.
translation_verse: “Kaŋɛ Israɛlebi na fanɛ b bar ma ŋkɛ ashi bumo be kagbene to nɛ fo sɔ amo n sa ma.

english_verse: Here is a list of what you are to collect: Gold, silver, and bronze;
translation_verse: Ŋkɛ nɛ a daga fanɛ fo sɔ bumo kutɔ e la shuwa nɛ gbiti nɛ danyaŋ

english_verse: olive oil for the lamp; sweet-smelling spices to mix with the incense and with the oil for dedicating the tent and ordaining the priests;
translation_verse: nɛ ɔlif be ŋku nɛ baaŋ baa ta a wɔtɔ efitila to nɛ efɛa belbelso be asɔ nɛ b kɔ a wɔtɔ ŋku nɛfaso to nɛ asɔ nɛ baa ta a wora duwu nɛ amo be efɛa wɔ ebel na

english_verse: I also want them to build a special place where I can live among my people.
translation_verse: Ade be kaman nɛ fo shin nɛ basa na e yuu wajɛbu cheembi n sa ma, saŋɛ na so, meeŋ ba kaa wɔ bumo to.

english_verse: The lamp on the top and those at the end of each of its six branches must be made so as to shine toward the front of the lampstand.
translation_verse: Men ta shuwa gbagba n lɔŋɛ efitila wurbi ashunu nɛ baaŋ baa chɔɔ a yili kefitilatɔl na so nɛ k baa fulto anishito na kikɛ.

english_verse: Cover it inside and out with pure gold and put a gold edging around the lid.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ b ŋalga shuwa gbagba m mata deka na be epunto nɛ kaman kikɛ nseŋ lɔŋɛ shuwa be kekrande m mata ŋ kulti kumo

english_verse: Make four gold rings and attach one of them to each of the four legs of the chest.
translation_verse: nseŋ naŋ bɛl shuwa be mpinibi ana n wɔtɔ kumo be aya ana na to nɛ anyɔ e baa wɔ kaba ko so nɛ anyɔ malɛ e baa wɔ kaba ko so.

english_verse: Don't ever remove the poles from the rings.
translation_verse: A daga fanɛ loŋ be ndibi tenteŋ na e baa wɔ mpinibi na to saŋkikɛ.

english_verse: Inside it place the two flat stones with the Ten Commandments on them and put the gold lid on top of the chest.
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ b ta ajembu pantraŋ pantrambi anyɔ nɛ ma mbraana deŋi so na n wɔtɔ deka na to nseŋ ta buuso nɛ baa tre kuwɔr be kakpa na m buu so.

english_verse: I will meet you there between the two creatures and tell you what my people must do and what they must not do. The Table for the Sacred Bread (Exodus
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nɛ ma nɛ menyi beeŋ baa shɛr nɛ m baa bɔla chɛrubim anyɔ na be nferinto ashi buuso na so a ta ma mbra nɛ ma mmalga a sa fo nɛ fo alɛ e baa ta amo a sa Israɛlebi na. Sarga be bodobodo be teebɔl be asheŋ (Ɛksodɔs

english_verse: Cover it with pure gold and put a gold edging around it with a border
translation_verse: nseŋ ta shuwa n wora kekrande nɛ kumo be mpar sa fanɛ enɔ be mparto ŋ kulti kumo be ekarso kikɛ.

english_verse: near the edging. The poles for carrying the table are to be placed through these rings and are to be made of acacia wood covered with gold.
translation_verse: Men ta akasiadibi n shɛl ndibi nɛ baaŋ pɛ to a maŋ teebɔl na so a keta na nseŋ ŋalga shuwa n wurge amo kikɛ so.

english_verse: The table is to be kept in the holy place, and the sacred loaves of bread must always be on it. All bowls, plates, jars, and cups for wine offerings are to be made of pure gold and set on this table. The Lampstand (Exodus
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ men ta teebɔl na n yili kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre be deka na be anishito nsaa ta bodobodo nɛ b kɔ a lara sarga a sa ma na a deŋi kumo so saŋkikɛ.” Kefitilatɔl na be asheŋ (Ɛksodɔs

english_verse: Make a lampstand of pure gold. The whole lampstand, including its decorative flowers, must be made from a single piece of hammered gold
translation_verse: “Shin nɛ b ta shuwa gbagba m bɛl kefitilatɔl, nɛ kumo be ayabi nɛ a kɔ asɔ ko fanɛ atoto be alambu na nɛ amo kikɛ e baa la kukoŋwule.

english_verse: There are to be three decorative almond blossoms on each branch
translation_verse: Ayabi ashe na be kekama daga fanɛ k baa kɔ asɔ ko nɛ a du fanɛ atoto be alambu na be asa.

english_verse: The lampstand, including its branches and decorative flowers, must be made from a single piece of hammered pure gold.
translation_verse: B ŋalga shuwa gbagba n lɔŋɛ kefitilatɔl na nɛ kumo be ayabi na, nɛ amo kikɛ e baa la kukoŋwule.

english_verse: The tongs and trays for taking care of the lamps are to be made of pure gold.
translation_verse: Men ta shuwa m bɛl asɔ nɛ b kɔ a lɔŋɛ efitila na be achɛbi so nɛ eprete nɛ b kɔ a suse amo be nsunɔ na gba.

english_verse: and they must be made according to the pattern I showed you on the mountain.
translation_verse: Shin nɛ b wora amo kananɛ ŋ ŋini fo ashi kebee na so na gbagba chap.”

english_verse: For the entrance to the tent, use a piece of fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool and embroidered with fancy needlework.
translation_verse: Men shin nɛ esa nɛ e nyi kajɔ e ta ejese buru nɛ apeper kpaw nɛ ago nɛ ago be ejese lela mɔlmɔlbi n lue Ebɔrɛ be wajɛbu na be kabuna be epatisa.

english_verse: As the material for protecting the tent, use goat hair to weave eleven sections of cloth
translation_verse: Men shin nɛ amo kikɛ e baa sasa nɛ amo be kekama be nteŋ e baa la ayadra adena nɛ anu nɛ amo be mpar malɛ e baa la ayadra ashe.

english_verse: The top of the sacred tent must be made from ten pieces of the finest linen, woven with blue, purple, and red wool and embroidered with figures of winged creatures.
translation_verse: “Le e daga fanɛ men lɔŋɛ Ebɔrɛ be wajɛbu na, men ta ago be ejese lela mɔlmɔlbi nɛ ejese nɛ a la buru nɛ kepeper kpaw n lue epatisa kudu nseŋ shin nɛ esa nɛ e nyi kajɔ e ta kebasibi nɛ jese n jɔ chɛrubim be kaduli n deŋi n deŋi epatisa na so.

english_verse: Sew five of the sections together to make one panel. Then sew the other six together to make a second panel, and fold the sixth section double over the front of the tent.
translation_verse: Nɛ men baa ewajɛ na be anu n chɛ abar so nɛ a ki patisagboŋ koŋwule nseŋ baa ashe nɛ a ka na malɛ nɛ a ki patisagboŋ koŋwule nɛ men bɔɔ kenyɔsopo na be wajɛ shesopo na to nɛ kumo be kaba e chulgi Ebɔrɛ be wajɛbu na be anishito.

english_verse: Make two more coverings—one with tanned ram skins and the other with fine leather. The Framework for the Sacred Tent (Exodus
translation_verse: Ade be kaman nɛ men ta ekpakpa be nwɔl nɛ b nyɔɔ m pere n naŋ lɔŋɛ wajɛbu na be buuso nyɔsopo, nseŋ ta echuru be nwɔl nɛ b gbiti nɛnɛ ŋ ki lalaloge be buuso.

english_verse: Inside the most holy place, put the sacred chest that has the place of mercy on its lid.
translation_verse: n ta buuso nɛ baa tre kuwɔr be kakpa na m buu deka na so ashi acheembiana to be kakpa cheembi na to.

english_verse: Build a framework of acacia wood for the walls of the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Kede malɛ be kaman, men ta akasiadibi niŋiso ŋ ki Ebɔrɛ be wajɛbu na be ndibi yuuso.

english_verse: Place two silver stands under each frame with sockets for the pegs, so the frames can be joined together. Put
translation_verse: nseŋ naŋ ta gbiti n lɔŋɛ amo be atɔl adena n shin nɛ atɔl anyɔ e baa wɔ kedibi yuuso kama be kaseto.

english_verse: For the back wall along the west side use six frames
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ men wora Ebɔrɛ be wajɛbu na be epeŋitɔrkpa be kaba so malɛ be ndibi yuuso ashe

english_verse: with two more at the southwest and northwest corners. Make certain that these corner frames are joined from top to bottom.
translation_verse: Men wora amo be kekama anyɔnyɔ n shin nɛ ndibi anyɔ kama e fara kaseto m mata abar n ya fo esoso nseŋ ta kepinibi n wɔtɔ amo to be esoso

english_verse: Altogether, this back wall will have eight frames with two silver stands under each one.
translation_verse: nɛ ndibi yuuso na e wora aburwa nɛ amo be gbiti be atɔl malɛ e wora kuduashe.

english_verse: Make five crossbars for each of the wooden frames,
translation_verse: nseŋ ta anu malɛ ŋ deŋi kumo be epeŋitɔrkpa be kaba so be ndibi yuuso so.

english_verse: Then set up the tent in the way I showed you on the mountain. The Curtain inside the Sacred Tent (Exodus
translation_verse: Men lɔŋɛ Ebɔrɛ be wajɛbu nɛ k baa kɔ ebu anyɔ fanɛ kananɛ ŋ ŋini fo ashi kebee na so na gbagba chap.

english_verse: Outside the most holy place, as you face the curtain, put the table for the sacred bread on the right side and the gold lampstand on the left.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ men ta sarga be bodobodo be teebɔl na n yili kakpa cheembi na to ashi Ebɔrɛ be wajɛbu na be kelargato be esoso be kaba so, nseŋ ta kefitilatɔl na malɛ n yili a laŋɛ kumo be kelargato be kaseto be kaba so.

english_verse: Make a curtain to separate the holy place from the most holy place. Use fine linen woven with blue, purple, and red wool, and embroidered with figures of winged creatures. Cover four acacia wood posts with gold and set them each on a silver stand. Then fasten gold hooks to the posts and hang the curtain there.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ men ta patisa na ŋ kuŋ to nɛ k barga acheembiana to be kakpa cheembi na ashi kakpa cheembi na to nseŋ ta kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre be deka na n yili patisa na be kaman

english_verse: Cover five acacia wood posts with gold and set them each on a bronze stand. Then put gold hooks on the posts and hang the curtain there.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ men ta patisa na n shiga akasiadibi yuuso anu nɛ b ta shuwa m mata amo nɛ a kɔ shuwa be akɔltobi nɛ danyaŋ be atɔl anu na so.

english_verse: Cover two acacia wood poles with bronze and put them through the rings for carrying the altar.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ men ta amo n yisi n wɔtɔ bɔrɛsure na be akel to be mpinibi anyɔ na to a pɛ amo to a ta kumo.

english_verse: All the equipment for the altar must also be made of bronze—the pans for the hot ashes, the shovels, the sprinkling bowls, the meat forks, and the fire pans.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ men ta danyaŋ n lɔŋɛ asɔ nɛ b kɔ a shuŋ kumo so fanɛ nsunɔ be mpuliya nɛ eshabɔl nɛ ntishaŋgboŋ, nɛ kusɔ nɛ baa ta a chule eblaŋ nɛ kusɔ chɔ edɛ.

english_verse: Construct the altar in the shape of an open box, just as you were shown on the mountain. The Courtyard around the Sacred Tent (Exodus
translation_verse: Men ta ndibi peŋgeleŋ peŋgeleŋ n lɔŋɛ bɔrɛsure na nɛ k baa kɔ kelaŋ kumo to fanɛ kananɛ ŋ ŋini menyi ashi kebee na so na gbagba chap. Wajɛbu na be kelɔnɛ be asheŋ (Ɛksodɔs

english_verse: Command the people of Israel to supply you with the purest olive oil. Do this so the lamp will keep burning
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman kaŋɛ Israɛlebi na kenishipereso fanɛ b baa bar fo ɔlif be ŋku nɛ a maŋ kɔ eyurpi nɛ fo baa ta a chɔɔ efitiliana na so a yili saŋkikɛ.

english_verse: Use four more of these posts for the entrance way, then hang on them an embroidered curtain of fine linen nine meters long and woven with blue, purple, and red wool.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman, men shin nɛ esa nɛ e nyi kajɔ e ta ejese nɛ a la buru nɛ apeper kpaw nɛ ago be ejese lela mɔlmɔlbi n lue Ebɔrɛ be wajɛbu na be kelɔnɛ so be kabuna to gbagba be patisa nɛ kumo be nteŋ to e baa la ayadra adesa, nsaa kɔ ndibi yuuso ana nɛ amo be atɔl ana.

english_verse: Make the rest of the equipment for the sacred tent of bronze, including the pegs for the tent and for the curtain surrounding the courtyard. The Oil for the Lamp in the Holy Place (Leviticus
translation_verse: nɛ asɔ nɛ b kɔ a shuŋ Ebɔrɛ be wajɛbu na to nɛ kelɔnɛ na so nɛ ayir nɛ b yuu ŋ kulti kumo na kikɛ nyam. Kefitilatɔl na be kekeniso be asheŋ (Levitikɔs

english_verse: in front of the curtain that separates the holy place from the most holy place, where the sacred chest is kept. Aaron and his sons are responsible for keeping the lamp burning every night in the sacred tent. The Israelites must always obey this command.
translation_verse: Ɛɛrɔn nɛ mbe mbinyɛnso e daga fanɛ b baa chɔɔ efitila na so a yili patisa nɛ k kuŋ kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre be deka na be anishito na. B baa chɔɔ efitila na so kaaseso kikɛ nɛ a baa fuli to ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be wajɛbu na to a klade. A daga fanɛ Israɛlebi nɛ bumo be kaman to ebi kikɛ e baa bɛ mbra ere so mbaanaayɔ.

english_verse: Send for your brother Aaron and his sons Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar. They are the ones I have chosen from Israel to serve as my priests.
translation_verse: Naniere shin nɛ fo da Ɛɛrɔn nɛ mbe mbinyɛnso Nadab nɛ Abihu nɛ Eliazaa nɛ Itama e lar Israɛlebi na to m ba fo kutɔ, saŋɛ na so baaŋ ba kaa la bɔrɛmatapoana a shuŋ ma.

english_verse: Aaron is to be dedicated as my high priest, and his clothes must be made only by persons who possess skills that I have given them.
translation_verse: Shin nɛ basa nɛ ma ere Ebɔrɛ sa bumo enɔ to be kushuŋ be kenyi na, e lɔŋɛ Ɛɛrɔn be epiŋi na. Kumo be kaman nɛ b ta Ɛɛrɔn m bɔɔ ma Ebɔrɛ enɔ nɛ e shuŋ ma fanɛ bɔrɛmatapo.

english_verse: Here are the items that need to be made: a breastpiece, a priestly vest, a robe, an embroidered shirt, a turban, and a sash. These sacred clothes are to be made for your brother Aaron and his sons who will be my priests.
translation_verse: Shin nɛ b lɔŋɛ kusɔ kuŋ kagbeneso fanɛ kɔlgu, nɛ kale nɛ k maŋ kɔ mbre nɛ baa tre ɛfɔd na nɛ piŋi tenteŋ nɛ k bee fo aya so nɛ danshiki nɛ b ta jese n lue nɛnɛ nɛ neemu nɛ kreso peŋgeleŋ. Loŋ be asɔbuuso na e daga fanɛ b lɔŋɛ n sa fo da Ɛɛrɔn nɛ mbe mbinyɛnso, a ŋini fanɛ b la bɔrɛmatapoana nna a shuŋ ma.

english_verse: Use only gold and fine linen, woven with blue, purple, and red wool, for making these clothes. The Vest for the High Priest (Exodus
translation_verse: Shin nɛ enyipo e chaŋɛ shuwa fanɛ ejese n wea ejese buru nɛ apeper kpaw nɛ apeper kunɔkunɔ nɛ ago be ejese lela mɔlmɔlbi to n lue m baa asɔbuuso na.

english_verse: Attach two gold settings to the shoulder straps and fasten them with two braided chains of pure gold. The Breastpiece for the High Priest (Exodus
translation_verse: Shin nɛ b naŋ ta shuwa n lɔŋɛ ŋgbɛlɛbi wurbi lela anyɔ ŋ kɔl shuwa be mpinibi anyɔ na to. Demuji be kɔlgu be asheŋ (Ɛksodɔs

english_verse: and engrave on each of them the name of one of the twelve tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: A daga fanɛ b chaŋ n chaŋ Israɛlebi be nnaŋ kuduanyɔ na be ketre kama n deŋi ajembu kuduanyɔ na be kekama so.

english_verse: From the same costly material make a breastpiece for the high priest to use in finding out what I want my people to do.
translation_verse: Men lɔŋɛ kagbeneso be kɔlgu n sa bɔrɛmatapo nimuso na nɛ k baa la kusɔ nɛ e beeŋ baa ta a pin Ebɔrɛ be aparsheŋ. Men ta ejese be yiri ana nɛ men daŋ ta n lɔŋɛ ɛfɔd na n lue wajɛ nseŋ jɔ kumo.

english_verse: in the second row a turquoise, a sapphire, and a diamond;
translation_verse: Gbaŋ nyɔsopo na malɛ be ajembu e baa la ɛmeraldi nɛ safaya nɛ daimɔnd na.

english_verse: in the third row a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst;
translation_verse: Gbaŋ sasopo malɛ be ajembu e baa la amo nɛ baa tre turkoyis nɛ agate nɛ ametiste na.

english_verse: Attach two gold rings to the upper front corners of the breastpiece and fasten them with two braided gold chains to gold settings on the shoulder straps.
translation_verse: nseŋ ta nnɔso anyɔ nɛ a ka na malɛ n wɔtɔ piŋi na be mpinibi anyɔ na to.

english_verse: Then take a blue cord and tie the two lower rings on the breastpiece to those on the vest. This will keep the breastpiece in place.
translation_verse: Ade be kaman nɛ men ta efɔl farso nɛ k la buru ŋ kɔl kɔlgu na be mpinibi na nɛ piŋi na be mpinibi na to, n chɛ m mata abar nɛ kɔlgu na e sa maa filito.

english_verse: with an opening in the center for his head. Be sure to bind the material around the collar to keep it from wearing out.
translation_verse: nɛ k baa kɔ kubɔ. Men ta kechɛbi lueso m muya kubɔ na ŋ kulti nɛ k baa kɔ eleŋ ga.

english_verse: Along the hem of the robe weave pomegranates of blue, purple, and red wool with a gold bell between each of them.
translation_verse: Men shin nɛ a bɛ abar so ŋ kulti piŋi na kikɛ n chambɔ.

english_verse: If Aaron wears these clothes when he enters the holy place as my high priest, the sound of the bells will be heard, and his life will not be in danger.
translation_verse: A daga fanɛ Ɛɛrɔn e baa buu piŋi na saŋkama nɛ e bee yɔ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be anishito ashi acheembiana to be kakpa cheembi na to, saŋɛ na so adulombi na beeŋ baa shu a ŋini fanɛ e maŋ wu.

english_verse: On a narrow strip of pure gold engrave the words: “Dedicated to the Lord.”
translation_verse: Men ta shuwa lela n lɔŋɛ kusɔ paŋgelambi nseŋ chaŋ le be nsibɛ n deŋ kumo so: ‘Cheembi n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na’

english_verse: Fasten it to the front of Aaron's turban with a blue cord,
translation_verse: nseŋ ta jese nɛ k la buru m baa kumo m mata neemu na be anishito.

english_verse: so he can wear it on his forehead. This will show that he will take on himself the guilt for any sins the people of Israel commit in offering their gifts to me, and I will forgive them.
translation_verse: A daga fanɛ Ɛɛrɔn e baa chɛ neemu na nɛ kasibɛ na e baa wɔ mbe kasɔto so saŋkama a ŋini fanɛ e ta Israɛlebi be alubi nɛ b wora saŋɛ nɛ baa lara sarga a sa ma na n deŋi mbe kumu so nɛ ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e baa sɔ bumo be esarga na.

english_verse: Since Aaron's sons are priests, they should also look dignified. So make robes, sashes, and special caps for them.
translation_verse: Men baa nle nɛ ekreso nɛ eneemu n sa Ɛɛrɔn be bibinyɛn na malɛ nɛ a shin nɛ b baa kɔ bunyaŋ nsaa walɛ ayɛrbi.

english_verse: Make linen shorts for them that reach from the waist down to the thigh, so they won't expose themselves.
translation_verse: Men ta ago be wajɛ m ba ewondoŋshiimbi n sa bumo nɛ b baa dela a buu bumo be wulo so. Men shin nɛ amo be nteŋ to e yili kashɛr to m ba fo amuli to.

english_verse: Whenever they enter the sacred tent or serve at the altar or enter the holy place, they must wear these shorts, or else they will be guilty and die. This same rule applies to any of their descendants who serve as priests.
translation_verse: A daga fanɛ Ɛɛrɔn nɛ mbe mbinyɛnso na e baa wɔtɔ loŋ be ewondoŋshiimbi ere saŋkama nɛ baa luri Enyɛnpe be wajɛbu na to ŋko saŋkama nɛ baa ba bɔrɛsure na ase nɛ b ba shuŋ ma ashi kakpa cheembi na to, saŋɛ na so b maaŋ wu ŋkpal b ka na kayurkpaŋ so. Le be mbra ere beeŋ baa dese n sa Ɛɛrɔn nɛ mbe kaman to ebi hale mbaanaayɔ.

english_verse: Each day you must offer a bull as a sacrifice for sin and as a way of purifying the altar. In addition, you must smear the altar with olive oil to make it completely holy.
translation_verse: Nchɛnshunu na be karechɛ kama malɛ, men ta gbolu n lara alubi be ketampaŋ nɛ bɔrɛsure na be kefɔrso be sarga. Kumo be kaman nɛ men ta ɔlif be ŋku ŋ gbiti bɔrɛsure na so nɛ k ki cheembi.

english_verse: Then from your finest flour make three batches of dough without yeast. Shape some of it into larger loaves, some into smaller loaves mixed with olive oil, and the rest into thin wafers brushed with oil.
translation_verse: Men ta ayunyifu nɛ a pe nɛnɛ n wora bodobodo nɛ a maŋ kɔ yiisi. Men ta ɔlif be ŋku n wora bodobodo na be ako nseŋ wora ako malɛ loŋ, nseŋ ta nyifu na be ako malɛ n wora ekrakashi n ta ɔlif be ŋku n wurge amo so.

english_verse: Put all of this bread in a basket and bring it when you come to sacrifice the three animals to me.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ men ta amo n wɔtɔ kelantaŋɛ n ti gbolu fɔlbi na nɛ ekpakpa anyɔ na so m ba lara sarga n sa ma.

english_verse: Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the sacred tent and tell them to wash themselves.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ men shin nɛ Ɛɛrɔn nɛ mbe bibinyɛn na e ba Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be wajɛbu na be kabuna to m ba bɛr daŋkare be ekpa so.

english_verse: Lead the bull to the entrance of the sacred tent, where Aaron and his sons will lay their hands on its head.
translation_verse: Men baŋ mɛa bumo to n loge, a daga fanɛ men ta gbolu na m ba Enyɛnpe be wajɛbu na be kabuna to m ba shin nɛ Ɛɛrɔn nɛ mbe bibinyɛn na e ta bumo be enɔana n deŋi kumo be kumu so.

english_verse: Kill the bull near my altar in front of the tent.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ men mɔ gbolu na ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be anishito ndoŋ

english_verse: Use a finger to smear some of its blood on each of the four corners of the altar and pour out the rest of the blood on the ground next to the altar.
translation_verse: nɛ fo ta keshilbi n nyɔ gbolu fɔlbi na be ŋklaŋ na to n do n do bɔrɛsure na be alambɛ na so nseŋ chulgi ŋklaŋ na be amo nɛ a ka na malɛ kikɛ n wurge bɔrɛsure na be kaseto.

english_verse: But the meat, the skin, and the food still in the bull's stomach must be burned outside the camp as an offering to ask forgiveness for the sins of the priests.
translation_verse: Ama men yɛr gbolu na be eblaŋ nɛ kawɔl nɛ apumbi bre keeyi na be ekarso n ya chɔɔ. Loŋ be sarga na e naa bar bɔrɛmatapoana be alubi be ketampaŋ na.

english_verse: Bring one of the rams to Aaron and his sons and tell them to lay their hands on its head.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ men shin nɛ Ɛɛrɔn nɛ mbe bibinyɛn na e ta bumo be enɔana n deŋi kpakpa nɛ baaŋ mɔ na be kumu so

english_verse: Kill the ram and splatter its blood against all four sides of the altar.
translation_verse: nɛ men mɔ kumo nseŋ suse ŋklaŋ na ŋ ŋmenyaŋ ŋ ŋmenyaŋ bɔrɛsure na be mba ana na kikɛ so.

english_verse: Cut up the ram, wash its insides and legs, and lay all of its parts on the altar, including the head.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ men kuya kpakpa na to wurwurbi nseŋ fɔr kumo be apuntosɔ nɛ ayawɔrta so nseŋ ta amo n deŋi kumu na nɛ eblaŋ kuyatoso na so

english_verse: Then make sure that the whole animal goes up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_verse: n chɔɔ bɔrɛsure na so n lara sarga n sa ma. Loŋ be sarga chɔɔso na be efɛa bee par ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nna.

english_verse: Bring the other ram to Aaron and his sons and tell them to lay their hands on its head.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ men shin nɛ Ɛɛrɔn nɛ mbe bibinyɛn e naŋ ta bumo enɔana n deŋi kpakpa nɛ k ka na be kumu so

english_verse: Kill the ram and place some of its blood on Aaron's right ear lobe, his right thumb, and the big toe of his right foot. Do the same for each of his sons and splatter the rest of the blood against the four sides of the altar.
translation_verse: nɛ men mɔ kumo nseŋ suse ŋklaŋ na be ako n do n do Ɛɛrɔn nɛ mbe bibinyɛnana na be jisa so be asoe be nseto nɛ bumo be enɔjisaana be ashilbinio so nɛ bumo be ayajiso be anashibinio so nseŋ ta ŋklaŋ nɛ a ka na malɛ kikɛ ŋ ŋmenyaŋ ŋ ŋmenyaŋ bɔrɛsure na be mba ana na kikɛ so.

english_verse: Then take some of the blood from the altar, mix it with the oil used for ordination, and sprinkle it on Aaron and his clothes, and also on his sons and their clothes. This will show that they and their clothes have been dedicated to me.
translation_verse: Kede malɛ be kaman nɛ men nyia bɔrɛsure na so be ŋklaŋ na be ako n wea ŋku nɛfaso na be ako to ŋ ŋmenyaŋ Ɛɛrɔn nɛ bibinyɛn na nɛ bumo be asɔbuusoana kikɛ so. Saŋɛ na so Ɛɛrɔn nɛ mbe bibinyɛnana na beeŋ ki ma, Ebɔrɛ be basa laraso nɛ bumo be asɔbuuso e ki asɔ cheembi ashi ma anishito.

english_verse: This ram is part of the ordination service. So remove its right hind leg, its fat tail, the fat on its insides, as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal kpakpa ere ka la keta m bɔɔ Ebɔrɛ enɔ be kewora be kusɔbɔya na so, men lara kumo be kpandu nɛ k kɔ nfɔ nɛ apuntosɔ be nfɔ nɛ kegberche na be kaseto be kaba nɛ achɛbi anyɔ na nɛ amo be nfɔ nɛ kumo be jisa be kebɛaŋ

english_verse: and put this bread, together with the meat, into the hands of Aaron and his sons. Then they will lift it all up to show that it is dedicated to me.
translation_verse: Men shin nɛ Ɛɛrɔn nɛ mbe bibinyɛn na e maŋ amo so ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be anishito fanɛ kakɛ cheembi be sarga.

english_verse: After this, put the meat and bread on the altar and send them up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ men sɔ amo bumo kutɔ n chɔɔ bɔrɛsure na so ashi kakpa nɛ baa chɔɔ sarga chɔɔso na. Loŋ be sarga be efɛa bee par ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nna.

english_verse: You may eat the choice ribs from this second ram, but you must first lift them up to show that this meat is dedicated to me.
translation_verse: Kumo alɛ be kaman nɛ fo maŋ kpakpa nɛ b ta n lara Ɛɛrɔn be keta m bɔɔ Ebɔrɛ enɔ be sarga na be kagbene so ashi ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be anishito. Kusɔbɔya na be kagbene na la fo kachige nna.

english_verse: After Aaron's death, his priestly clothes are to be handed down to each descendant who succeeds him as high priest, and these clothes must be worn during the seven-day ceremony of ordination.
translation_verse: Emo nɛ e sɔ mo so ŋ ki bɔrɛmatapo nimuso a luri Enyɛnpe be wajɛbu na to be kakpa cheembi na, daga fanɛ e buu kabɔrɛmata be piŋi na saŋkama nɛ e bee luri ndoŋ hale n ya fo nchɛnshunu.

english_verse: then Aaron and his sons are to eat it together with the three kinds of bread at the entrance to the sacred tent.
translation_verse: nɛ Ɛɛrɔn nɛ mbe bibinyɛn na e yili nshɛr be wajɛbu na be kabuna to n we eblaŋ na nɛ bodobodo nɛ a ka a wɔ kelantaŋɛ na to na.

english_verse: If any of the sacred food is left until morning, it must be completely burned.
translation_verse: Ama nɛ fanɛ amo be ako ka nseŋ di ŋklade, men chɔɔ amo nɛ esa kama e sa maŋ kaŋ ji amo, ŋkpal manɛ so, a la asɔ cheembi nna.

english_verse: Repeat this ordination ceremony for Aaron and his sons seven days in a row, just as I have instructed you.
translation_verse: Ta nchɛnshunu dede n wora Ɛɛrɔn nɛ mbe bibinyɛn be keta m bɔɔ Ebɔrɛ enɔ be kasheŋwora na fanɛ kananɛ ŋ kaŋɛ fo na gbagba chap.

english_verse: Do this for seven days, and the altar will become so holy that anyone who touches it will become holy. Daily Sacrifices (Leviticus
translation_verse: Nchɛnshunu na be karechɛ kama men lara alubi be ketampaŋ be sarga bɔrɛsure na so, saŋɛ na so, bɔrɛsure na beeŋ baa du cheembi nɛ kusɔ kama nɛ k beta kumo gba e baa du cheembi. Karechɛ kikɛ be sarga be asheŋ (Nɔmbɛs

english_verse: Each day you must sacrifice two lambs a year old,
translation_verse: Karechɛ kikɛ men baa ta nfɛ koko be ekpakpafɔlbi anyɔ anyɔ a lara sarga bɔrɛsure na so.

english_verse: With each lamb offer one kilogram of your finest flour mixed with a liter of pure olive oil, and also pour out a liter of wine as an offering. The smell of this sacrifice on the fires of the altar will be pleasing to me.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ men naŋ ta kpakpafɔlbi nyɔsopo na nɛ asɔ nɛ men daŋ ta n ti chipurso peya na so na gbagba chap n ti so n chɔɔ n lara sarga kaaseso n sa ma. Loŋ be sarga chɔɔso na be efɛa bee wora ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ebel ga.

english_verse: You and your descendants must always offer this sacrifice on the altar at the entrance to the sacred tent. People of Israel, I will meet and speak with you there, and my shining glory will make the place holy.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nɛ ma nɛ Israɛl be basa beeŋ baa shɛr nɛ ma kemaŋkura e shin nɛ ndoŋ e ki ma kakpa cheembi.

english_verse: Because of who I am, the tent will become sacred, and Aaron and his sons will become worthy to serve as my priests.
translation_verse: Ma alɛ beeŋ shin nɛ Enyɛnpe be wajɛbu na nɛ bɔrɛsure na e ki ma asɔ cheembi. Nseŋ naŋ shin nɛ Ɛɛrɔn nɛ mbe bibinyɛn na malɛ gba e ki basa laraso cheembi a shuŋ ma fanɛ bɔrɛmatapoana.

english_verse: and you will know that I am the Lord your God, the one who rescued you from Egypt, so that I could live among you.
translation_verse: Aloŋ nɛ baaŋ ba pin fanɛ ma e la Enyɛnpe bumo be Ebɔrɛ nɛ n lara bumo ashi Ijipt nsaa wɔ bumo to na. Ma e la Enyɛnpe bumo be Ebɔrɛ na.”

english_verse: Build an altar of acacia wood where you can burn incense.
translation_verse: “Men ta akasiadibi n lɔŋɛ bɔrɛsure nɛ menyeeŋ baa chɔɔ duwu kumo so

english_verse: Then below the edging on opposite sides attach two gold rings through which you can put the poles for carrying the altar.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ men ta shuwa n lɔŋɛ mpinibi anyɔ n chɔga kumo be akel to, shuwa gbuntelin na be kaseto nsaa yisi ndibi tentembi a wɔtɔ amo to a maŋ kumo so.

english_verse: These poles are also to be made of acacia wood covered with gold.
translation_verse: Men ta akasiadibi n wora loŋ be ndibi tentembi na nseŋ ta shuwa m mata amo kikɛ so.

english_verse: Put the altar in front of the inside curtain of the sacred tent. The chest with the place of mercy is kept behind that curtain, and I will talk with you there.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ men ta bɔrɛsure na n yili kakpa nɛ ma nɛ fo beeŋ baa shɛr na be patisa nɛ k kuŋ kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre be deka na nɛ kumo be buuso nɛ baa tre kuwɔr be kakpa na be anishito na.

english_verse: Burn only the proper incense on the altar and never use it for grain sacrifices or animal sacrifices or drink offerings.
translation_verse: Men sa maŋ kaŋ chɔɔ duwu kama nɛ a maŋ daga ashi loŋ be bɔrɛsure na so, ŋko n lara kusɔbɔya ŋko ayu ŋko asɔnuuso nɛ a maŋ daga be sarga kikɛ kumo so.

english_verse: Once a year Aaron must purify the altar by smearing on its four corners the blood of an animal sacrificed for sin, and this practice must always be followed. The altar is sacred because it is dedicated to me. The Money for the Sacred Tent
translation_verse: Kafɛ kikɛ malɛ a daga fanɛ Ɛɛrɔn e ta asɔbɔya nɛ b ta n lara kulubi be sarga na be ŋklaŋ n do bɔrɛsure na so kela koŋwule nɛ k ki cheembi. Le be kesheŋ ere la kusɔ nɛ menyi nɛ menyi be kaman to ebi beeŋ baa wora nna hale mbaanaayɔ. Bɔrɛsure ere la kusɔ cheembi nna n sa ma, Eyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.” Enyɛnpe be wajɛbu be toto be asheŋ

english_verse: Find out how many grown men there are in Israel and require each of them to pay me to keep him safe from danger while you are counting them.
translation_verse: “Fo kaa karga Israɛl be basa nɛ fo pin bumo be kɔnɔ, fo shin nɛ bumo be ekama e ka kusɔ ko ŋkpal mbe ŋkpa so, saŋɛ na so kulubi kama maaŋ tu mo kekarga na to.

english_verse: , whether rich or poor, must pay me the same amount of money, weighed according to the official standards.
translation_verse: Loŋ be nchu na nɛ Ɛɛrɔn nɛ mbe bibinyɛn na beeŋ baa kɔ a fɔr bumo be enɔ nɛ aya so.

english_verse: This money is to be used for the upkeep of the sacred tent, and because of it, I will never forget my people. The Large Bronze Bowl (Exodus
translation_verse: Sɔ le be amansherbi ere ashi Israɛlebi na kutɔ nɛ a baa la alubi be ketampaŋ be sarga nɛ b ta amo a shuŋ Enyɛnpe be wajɛbu na to be kushuŋ.” Danyaŋ be katishaŋgboŋ be asheŋ

english_verse: If you ever make any of it to use as perfume, you will no longer belong to my people.
translation_verse: Esa kama nɛ e kpal amo be efɛa belbelso so n wora amo be kaduli, daga fanɛ b lara mo ashi mbe basa to.”

english_verse: Make a large bronze bowl and a bronze stand for it. english_verse: Then Moses replied, “If you aren't going with us, please don't make us leave this place.
translation_verse: Nɛ Mosis malɛ kaŋɛ mo: “Nɛ fo baa maaŋ tu anyi n yɔ, kumo ere, fo sa maŋ kaŋ shin nɛ an lar nfe.

english_verse: But if you do go with us, everyone will know that you are pleased with your people and with me. That way, we will be different from the rest of the people on earth.”
translation_verse: Nɛ fo maŋ tu anyi n yɔ, nuso nɛ esa beeŋ wora m pin ma nɛ fo basa be asheŋ ka bee par fo? Fo kebaawɔ anyi kutɔ e naaŋ shin nɛ an baa kɔr bomin kikɛ to ashi durnya ere to.”

english_verse: So the Lord told him, “I will do what you have asked, because I am your friend and I am pleased with you.”

english_verse: Then Moses said, “I pray that you will let me see you in all of your glory.”
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Mosis kaŋɛ: “Kumo ere, jande, shin nɛ n wu fo kemaŋkura.”

english_verse: The Lord answered: All right. I am the Lord, and I show mercy and kindness to anyone I choose. I will let you see my glory and hear my holy name,
translation_verse: Nɛ e kaŋɛ Mosis: “Meeŋ shin nɛ ma kemankura kikɛ e bɔla fo anishito n choŋ nɛ n ti ma ketre ŋ ŋini fo. Ma e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ mee wu kuwɔr nsaa lara ma kasha a ŋini bekama nɛ n lara na.

english_verse: The Lord said: I promise to perform miracles for you that have never been seen anywhere on earth. Neighboring nations will stand in fear and know that I was the one who did these marvelous things.

english_verse: Don't fail to observe the Festival of Thin Bread in the month of Abib. Obey me and eat bread without yeast for seven days during Abib, because that is the month you left Egypt.

english_verse: When you sacrifice an animal on the altar, don't offer bread made with yeast. And don't save any part of the Passover meal for the next day.

english_verse: I am the Lord your God, and you must bring the first part of your harvest to the place of worship. Don't boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
