translation_verse: nɛ mo nɛ Ɛɛrɔn nɛ Ɛɛrɔn be bibinyɛn e ta amo a fɔr bumo be enɔ nɛ aya so.

english_verse: In fact, they washed each time before entering the tent or offering sacrifices at the altar. These things were done exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.
translation_verse: Saŋkama nɛ baa luri Enyɛnpe be wajɛbu na to ŋko a yɔ bɔrɛsure na ase, baa fɔr bumo be aya nɛ enɔana so nna fanɛ kananɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Mosis na.

english_verse: Suddenly the sacred tent was covered by a thick cloud and filled with the glory of the Lord.
translation_verse: Nɛ kuwɔlpa ba buu Enyɛnpe be wajɛbu na so nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be kemaŋkura ba bɔlɔ kumo to.

english_verse: Whenever the cloud moved from the tent, the people would break camp and follow;
translation_verse: Israɛlebi na ka wɔ enite to na, saŋkama nɛ kuwɔlpa na baŋ tia ashi Ebɔrɛ be wajɛbu na so, bumo alɛ bee kaa nna.

english_verse: then they would set up camp and stay there, until it moved again.
translation_verse: Nɛ kuwɔlpa na baa maŋ tia bre, b maa kaa.

english_verse: No matter where the people traveled, the Lord was with them. Each day his cloud was over the tent, and each night a fire could be seen in the cloud.
translation_verse: Amoso saŋɛ nɛ Israɛlebi na daa wɔ bumo be enite to na, Ebɔrɛ be kuwɔlpa na daa buu Ebɔrɛ be wajɛbu na so kapaso kikɛ nna nsaa fulto edɛ kanyɛso malɛ kikɛ.

english_verse: The Lord spoke to Moses from the sacred tent and gave him instructions for the community of Israel to follow when they offered sacrifices. Sacrifices To Please the Lord The Lord said: Sacrifices to please me must be completely burned on the bronze altar. Bulls or rams or goats are the animals to be used for these sacrifices. If the animal is a bull, it must not have anything wrong with it. Lead it to the entrance of the sacred tent, and I will let you know if it is acceptable to me.
translation_verse: “Nɛ fanɛ kena nɛ e bee ta a lara sarga chɔɔso na, a daga k baa la gbolu nɛ e maŋ kɔ ndulgi kikɛ kumo be eyur so. Amodoŋwura malɛ beeŋ bar kumo wajɛbu na be kabuna ase, saŋɛ na so Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na beeŋ sɔ sarga na.

english_verse: Lay your hand on its head, and I will accept the animal as a sacrifice for taking away your sins.
translation_verse: Esa nɛ e lara sarga na beeŋ ta mbe enɔ n deŋi gbolu na be kumu so, saŋɛ na so, k beeŋ baa la alubi be ketampaŋ be sarga n sa mo.

english_verse: After the bull is killed in my presence, some priests from Aaron's family will offer its blood to me by splattering it against the four sides of the altar.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e mɔ kumo Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be anishito nɛ Ɛɛrɔn be mbinyɛnsobi nɛ b la bɔrɛmatapoana na be beko e suse kumo be ŋklaŋ ŋ ŋmenyaŋ bɔrɛsure nɛ k wɔ Enyɛnpe be wajɛbu na be kabuna to na be mba ana na kikɛ so ŋ kulti.

english_verse: Skin the bull and cut it up,
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e bɛ kusɔbɔya na nseŋ kuya kumo to.

english_verse: while the priests pile wood on the altar fire to make it start blazing.
translation_verse: Kumo alɛ be kaman nɛ bɔrɛmatapoana na malɛ e bela ndibi n deŋi bɔrɛsure na so n nya edɛ n wɔtɔ amo to

english_verse: Wash the bull's insides and hind legs, so the priests can lay them on the altar with the head, the fat, and the rest of the animal. A priest will then send all of it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_verse: Nɛ esa nɛ e bee lara sarga na e fɔr kusɔbɔya na be apuntosɔ nɛ kaman to be aya kikɛ so nɛ bɔrɛmatapoana na e chɔɔ amo kikɛ bɔrɛsure na so m mur. Ŋkpal manɛ so, sarga na la sarga chɔɔso nɛ kumo be efɛa bee par Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nna.

english_verse: If you sacrifice a ram or a goat, it must not have anything wrong with it.
translation_verse: Nɛ fanɛ esa na bee lara kubolpɔ ŋko kaboe nna, a daga k baa la kenyɛnso nɛ k maŋ kɔ ndulgi kikɛ kumo be eyur so.

english_verse: Lead the animal to the north side of the altar, where it is to be killed in my presence. Then some of the priests will splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
translation_verse: E beeŋ mɔ kusɔbɔya na bɔrɛsure na be kelargato be esoso ase, ashi Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be anishito, nɛ bɔrɛmatapo na e suse ŋklaŋ na ŋ ŋmanyaŋ bɔrɛsure na be mba ana na so ŋ kulti.

english_verse: Cut up the animal and wash its insides and hind legs. A priest will put these parts on the altar with the head, the fat, and the rest of the animal. Then he will send all of it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_verse: A daga e fɔr apuntosɔ nɛ kaman to be aya na so nɛ bɔrɛmatapo na e chɔɔ amo alɛ gba bɔrɛsure na so. Ŋkpal manɛ so, sarga na la sarga chɔɔso nɛ kumo be efɛa bee par Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nna.

english_verse: If you offer a bird for this kind of sacrifice, it must be a dove or a pigeon.
translation_verse: Nɛ fanɛ kabuibi nɛ esa na kɔ a lara sarga na, a daga k baa la lepɔ ŋko keli.

english_verse: A priest will take the bird to the bronze altar, where he will wring its neck and put its head on the fire. Then he will drain out its blood on one side of the altar,
translation_verse: Bɔrɛmatapo na beeŋ bar lepɔ ŋko keli na bɔrɛsure na ase nseŋ ba kii kumo be kubɔ to m mɔ. Kumo be kaman nɛ e chɔɔ kumo be kumu na bɔrɛsure na so nseŋ chise ŋklaŋ na malɛ n wurge bɔrɛsure na be kaba koŋwule so

english_verse: remove the bird's craw with what is in it, and throw them on the ash heap at the east side of the altar.
translation_verse: nseŋ lara kumo be kepe nɛ asɔ nɛ a wɔ kumo to kikɛ n lɛ ashi bɔrɛsure na be kaba nɛ k bee laŋɛ epeŋilarkpa be kaba so, kakpa nɛ baa lɛ nsunɔ na.

english_verse: Finally, he will take the bird by its wings, tear it partially open, and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e pɛ kabuibi na be aba to m baŋɛ kumo to nsaa maŋ chuge aba na to, nseŋ chɔɔ kumo kikɛ bɔrɛsure na so. Ŋkpal manɛ so, k la sarga chɔɔso nɛ kumo be efɛa bee par Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nna.”

english_verse: When you offer sacrifices to give thanks to me, you must use only your finest flour. Put it in a dish, sprinkle olive oil and incense on the flour,
translation_verse: Nɛ esa ta ayu nɛ e ba lara sarga n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na, a daga e kɔr amo nɛ a pe nɛnɛ. Kumo be kaman e ta ɔlif be ŋku m baga amo nseŋ ta duwu n ti so

english_verse: and take it to the priests from Aaron's family. One of them will scoop up the incense together with a handful of the flour and oil. Then, to show that the whole offering belongs to me, the priest will lay this part on the bronze altar and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_verse: m ba sa Ɛɛrɔn be mbinyɛnsobi nɛ b la bɔrɛmatapoana na. Nɛ bumo be ekoŋwule e jɔ nyifu nɛ ɔlif be ŋku be wea to na enɔ be bɔlɔ nseŋ ta duwu na n ti so n chɔɔ bɔrɛsure na so a ŋini fanɛ amo kikɛ la sarga chɔɔso nɛ amo be efɛa bee par Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nna.

english_verse: If you bake bread in an oven for this sacrifice, use only your finest flour, but without any yeast. You may make the flour into a loaf mixed with olive oil, or you may make it into thin wafers and brush them with oil.
translation_verse: Nɛ fanɛ b ta ayu na n wora bodobodo nna, kumo ere a sa maa kɔ yiisi amo to. Ama a beeŋ tiŋ a la bodobodo nɛ b ta nyifu nɛ a pe nɛnɛ nseŋ ta ɔlif be ŋku n wea amo to n wora, ŋko ekrakashi nɛ b ta ɔlif be ŋku m baga amo.

english_verse: If you cook bread in a shallow pan for this sacrifice, use only your finest flour. Mix it with olive oil, but do not use any yeast.
translation_verse: Nɛ fanɛ b ta ayu na a wora abuibi nna, kumo ere b ta nyifu nɛ a pe nɛnɛ nseŋ ta ɔlif be ŋku n wea amo to n wora nɛ e sa maa kɔ yiisi.

english_verse: Then break the bread into small pieces and sprinkle them with oil.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ b pupur amo to nseŋ n chulgi ɔlif be ŋku n wurge amo so n ta n lara sarga na.

english_verse: If you cook your bread in a pan with a lid on it, you must also use the finest flour mixed with oil.
translation_verse: Nɛ fanɛ b ta ayu na a wora akare nna, kumo ere b ta nyifu nɛ e pe nɛnɛ nseŋ ta ɔlif be ŋku n wea amo to n wora.

english_verse: You may prepare sacrifices to give thanks in any of these three ways. Bring your sacrifice to a priest, and he will take it to the bronze altar.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ b ta amo m ba sa bɔrɛmatapo na fanɛ sarga n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nɛ bɔrɛmatapo na e ta amo n yɔ bɔrɛsure na ase.

english_verse: Then, to show that the whole offering belongs to me, the priest will lay part of it on the altar and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_verse: E beeŋ ta amo be ako shɛda so n chɔɔ bɔrɛsure na so a ŋini fanɛ sarga na la sarga chɔɔso nɛ kumo be efɛa bee par Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nna.

english_verse: You may offer either of them separately, when you present the first part of your harvest to me, but they must never be burned on the altar.
translation_verse: A daga fanɛ men jɔ ayu nɛ menyeeŋ juŋkpar n teŋi kafɛ to n lara sarga n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na, ama men sa maŋ chɔɔ amo bɔrɛsure so.

english_verse: Salt is offered when you make an agreement with me, so sprinkle salt on these sacrifices.
translation_verse: A daga men baa wɔtɔ men be ayu be sargajibi kikɛ to nfɔl, ŋkpal manɛ so, nfɔl yili nna n sa menyi nɛ Ebɔrɛ be kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre na.

english_verse: Freshly cut grain, either roasted or coarsely ground, must be used when you offer the first part of your grain harvest.
translation_verse: Kafɛ to be ayu nɛ menyeeŋ juŋkpar n teŋi nseŋ jɔ amo m ba lara sarga n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na daga a baa la ayu nɛ b ke ŋko n yarga nna.

english_verse: You must mix in some olive oil and put incense on top, because this is a grain sacrifice.
translation_verse: Menyi alɛ beeŋ ta ɔlif be ŋku n wea amo to nseŋ ta duwu n ti so m ba, ŋkpal manɛ so, e la ayu be sargajibi nna.

english_verse: A priest will sprinkle all of the incense and some of the grain and oil on the altar and send them up in smoke to show that the whole offering belongs to me.
translation_verse: Bɔrɛmatapo na beeŋ jɔ nyifu nɛ b baga amo ɔlif be ŋku na shɛda so nseŋ ta duwu na kikɛ n ti so n chɔɔ bɔrɛsure na so fanɛ ayu be sargajibi n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.

english_verse: When you offer sacrifices to ask my blessing, you may offer either a bull or a cow, but there must be nothing wrong with the animal.
translation_verse: Nɛ esa ta kusɔbɔya nɛ e lara kɔnɔkoŋwule be sarga, a daga k baa la gbolu ŋko nache nɛ k maŋ kɔ ndulgi kikɛ kumo so nna, nɛ e keta kumo m ba Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be anishito.

english_verse: Lead it to the entrance of the sacred tent, lay your hand on its head, and have it killed there. A priest from Aaron's family will splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
translation_verse: Amodoŋwura beeŋ ta mbe enɔ n deŋi kusɔbɔya na be kumu so nseŋ mɔ kumo ashi wajɛbu na be kabuna ase. Kumo be kaman nɛ Ɛɛrɔn be mbinyɛnsobi nɛ b la bɔrɛmatapoana na e suse ŋklaŋ na ŋ ŋmenyaŋ bɔrɛsure na be mba ana na kikɛ so ŋ kulti,

english_verse: Offer all of the fat on the animal's insides,
translation_verse: nseŋ lara kusɔbɔya na be nfɔ nɛ a wɔ kumo be apuntosɔ so na kikɛ nɛ

english_verse: as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat.
translation_verse: kumo be achɛbi nɛ amo so be nfɔ kikɛ nseŋ ta kusɔbɔya na be kegberche be alela akpa n ti so n lara sarga n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.

english_verse: Some of the priests will lay these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke with a smell that pleases me, together with the sacrifice that is offered to please me.
translation_verse: Bɔrɛmatapoana na be beko beeŋ ta kusɔbɔya na be nfɔ na n ti ayu be sargajibi na so n chɔɔ bɔrɛsure na so nɛ k baa la sarga nɛ kumo be efɛa bee par Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nna.

english_verse: Instead of a bull or a cow, you may offer any sheep or goat that has nothing wrong with it.
translation_verse: Nɛ kusɔbɔya nɛ esa na ta nɛ e lara kɔnɔkoŋwule be sarga n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na la kubolpɔ ŋko kaboe nna, a daga k baa la kenyɛnso ŋko kecheso nɛ k maŋ kɔ ndulgi kikɛ kumo so.

english_verse: Lay your hand on its head and have it killed there. A priest will then splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
translation_verse: e beeŋ ta mbe enɔ n deŋi kumo be kumu so nseŋ mɔ kumo ashi wajɛbu na be kabuna ase nɛ bɔrɛmatapoana na e suse ŋklaŋ na ŋ ŋmenyaŋ bɔrɛsure na be mba ana na so ŋ kulti.

english_verse: as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat.
translation_verse: nɛ achɛbi anyɔ na nɛ amo so be nfɔ kikɛ nɛ kegberche na be alela akpa n sa

english_verse: One of the priests will lay these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke as a food offering for me.
translation_verse: bɔrɛmatapoana na be eko nɛ e chɔɔ amo kikɛ bɔrɛsure na so n lara ajibi be sarga n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.

english_verse: If you offer a goat, you must also present it to me
translation_verse: Nɛ fanɛ esa lara kaboe nna,

english_verse: at the entrance to the sacred tent. Lay your hand on its head and have it killed there. A priest will then splatter its blood against the four sides of the altar.
translation_verse: e beeŋ ta mbe enɔ n deŋi kumo be kumu so nseŋ mɔ kumo ashi wajɛbu na be anishito. Bɔrɛmatapoana na beeŋ suse ŋklaŋ na ŋ ŋmenyaŋ bɔrɛsure na be mba ana na kikɛ so ŋ kulti

english_verse: Offer all of the fat on the animal's insides,
translation_verse: nseŋ ta kaboe na be nfɔ nɛ a wɔ apuntosɔ na so na kikɛ

english_verse: as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat.
translation_verse: nɛ achɛbi anyɔ na nɛ amo so be nfɔ nɛ kegberche na be alela akpa na kikɛ n lara ajibi be sarga n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.

english_verse: One of the priests will put these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke as a food offering with a smell that pleases me. All fat belongs to me.
translation_verse: Bɔrɛmatapo na beeŋ chɔɔ amo kikɛ bɔrɛsure na so fanɛ ajibi be sarga nɛ k bee par Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na. Nfɔ na kikɛ la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na peya nna.

english_verse: So you and your descendants must never eat any fat or any blood, not even in the privacy of your own homes. This law will never change.
translation_verse: Israɛl be esa kikɛ maŋ daga e ka ji nfɔ ŋko ŋklaŋ. K la mbra nɛ k dese nna n sa Israɛl be basa kikɛ ashi kaplɛkama nɛ b wɔ nna hale mbaanaayɔ.

english_verse: dip a finger in the blood, and sprinkle some of it seven times toward the sacred chest behind the curtain.
translation_verse: n ya ta mbe keshilbi n nyɔ ŋklaŋ to ŋ ŋmenyaŋ patisa nɛ k bee kuŋ kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre be deka na ase ale ashunu ashi Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be anishito.

english_verse: This is a sacrifice for sin. So he will lay his hand on the animal's head, before having it killed in my presence at the north side of the bronze altar.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal k ka la kulubi be sarga so, e beeŋ ta mbe enɔ n deŋi kaboe na be kumu so nseŋ mɔ kumo ashi bɔrɛsure na be kelargato be esoso be kaba so be kakpa nɛ baa mɔ esarga chɔɔso be asɔbɔya na.

english_verse: Then a priest will dip a finger in the blood; he will smear some of it on each of the four corners of the altar and pour out the rest at the foot of the altar.
translation_verse: Bɔrɛmatapo na beeŋ ta mbe keshilbi n nyɔ kusɔbɔya na be ŋklaŋ to n wora amo ŋ gbiti bɔrɛsure na be mba ana na be nnɔso nseŋ chulgi amo nɛ a ka na n wurge kumo be kaseto.

english_verse: to say to the community of Israel: Offer a sacrifice to ask forgiveness when you sin by accidentally doing something I have told you not to do. When the High Priest Sins The Lord said:
translation_verse: “Kaŋɛ Israɛl be basa na fanɛ esa kikɛ nɛ e maŋ kute n wora kulubi n da Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be mbra so, kusɔ nɛ e beeŋ wora nde.

english_verse: When the high priest sins, he makes everyone else guilty too. And so, he must sacrifice a young bull that has nothing wrong with it.
translation_verse: Nɛ fanɛ Bɔrɛmatapo Nimuso e wora kulubi nɛ k suse basa na kikɛ, e beeŋ bar gbolu fɔlbi nɛ e maŋ kɔ ndulgi kikɛ kumo so m ba lara sarga n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ŋkpal mbe kulubi na so.

english_verse: The priest will lead the bull to the entrance of the sacred tent, lay his hand on its head, and kill it there.
translation_verse: E beeŋ bar gbolu na wajɛbu na be kabuna ase m ba ta mbe enɔ n deŋi kumo be kumu so nseŋ mɔ kumo ndoŋ ashi Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be anishito.

english_verse: He will take a bowl of the blood inside the tent,
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Bɔrɛmatapo Nimuso na e suse ŋklaŋ na be eko n luri wajɛbu na to

english_verse: Then, in my presence, he will smear some of the blood on each of the four corners of the incense altar, before pouring out the rest at the foot of the bronze altar near the entrance to the tent.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e wora ŋklaŋ na be ako ŋ gbiti bɔrɛsure nɛ baa chɔɔ duwu kumo so na be mba ana be nnɔso na be kekama so, ashi wajɛbu na to na nseŋ chulgi ŋklaŋ nɛ a ka na n wurge bɔrɛsure nɛ baa chɔɔ esarga kumo so na be kaseto ashi wajɛbu na be kabuna ase.

english_verse: The skin and flesh of the bull, together with its legs, insides, and the food still in its stomach, are to be taken outside the camp and burned on a wood fire near the ash heap. When the Whole Nation Sins The Lord said:
translation_verse: n lar keeyi na be ekarso n yɔ kakpa nɛ baa chulgi nsunɔ a lɛ na n ya chɔɔ amo ndibi so ndoŋ.

english_verse: Once you realize what has happened, you must sacrifice a young bull to ask my forgiveness. Lead the bull to the entrance of the sacred tent,
translation_verse: B baŋ pin kulubi na be asheŋ, a daga fanɛ b ta gbolu fɔlbi n lara kulubi be sarga. Baaŋ bar gbolu na wajɛbu na to ashi Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be anishito.

english_verse: where your tribal leaders will lay their hands on its head, before having it killed in my presence.
translation_verse: Efuli na be benimuana beeŋ ta bumo be enɔana n deŋi kusɔbɔya na be kumu so nseŋ mɔ kumo ndoŋ.

english_verse: The priest will take a bowl of the animal's blood inside the sacred tent,
translation_verse: Bɔrɛmatapo Nimuso na beeŋ suse gbolu na be ŋklaŋ na be ako n luri wajɛbu na to,

english_verse: dip a finger in the blood, and sprinkle some of it seven times toward the sacred chest behind the curtain.
translation_verse: n ya ta mbe keshilbi n nyɔ ŋklaŋ na to ŋ ŋmenyaŋ patisa nɛ k bee kuŋ kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre be deka na be anishito ale shunu.

english_verse: Then, in my presence, he must smear some of the blood on each of the four corners of the incense altar, before pouring out the rest at the foot of the bronze altar near the entrance to the tent.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e ta ŋklaŋ na be eko ŋ gbiti bɔrɛsure na be mba ana na be nnɔso pɔɛŋ nseŋ chulgi amo nɛ a ka na n wurge bɔrɛsure nɛ k wɔ wajɛbu na be kabuna ase nɛ baa chɔɔ esarga kumo so na be kaseto.

english_verse: After this, the priest will remove the fat from the bull and send it up in smoke on the altar. Finally, he will burn its remains outside the camp, just as he did with the other bull. By this sacrifice the sin of the whole nation will be forgiven. When a Tribal Leader Sins The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ e ta gbolu na n lar keeyi na be ekarso n ya chɔɔ fanɛ kananɛ e chɔɔ gbolu nɛ e ta n lara mo gbagba be kulubi be sarga na. Sarga nɛ k beeŋ lara efuli na kikɛ be basa be kulubi ashi bumo so nna na.

english_verse: As soon as the leader realizes what has happened, he must sacrifice a goat that has nothing wrong with it.
translation_verse: E baŋ pin kulubi na be asheŋ, e beeŋ ta kaboenyɛnso nɛ k maŋ kɔ ndulgi kikɛ n lara sarga.

english_verse: The priest will dip a finger in the blood, smear some of it on each of the four corners of the altar, and pour out the rest at the foot of the altar.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ bɔrɛmatapo na e suse ŋklaŋ na be eko n ta mbe keshilbi n nyɔ amo to ŋ gbiti bɔrɛsure na be mba ana na be nnɔso nseŋ chulgi amo nɛ a ka na n wurge bɔrɛsure na be kaseto.

english_verse: Then he must send all of the fat up in smoke, just as he does when a sacrifice is offered to ask my blessing. By this sacrifice the leader's sin will be forgiven. When Ordinary People Sin The Lord said:
translation_verse: E beeŋ chɔɔ kaboe na be nfɔ kikɛ fanɛ kananɛ e bee chɔɔ kɔnɔkoŋwule be sarga be kusɔbɔya be nfɔ na. Ekpa nɛ bɔrɛmatapo na beeŋ bɔla so n lara eyiri to be enimu be kulubi be sarga nɛ e nya ketampaŋ nna na.

english_verse: When any of you ordinary people disobey me without meaning to, you are still guilty.
translation_verse: Nɛ fanɛ efuli na so be esa ko e maŋ kute n wora n da Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be kusɔ nɛ e yili so gba e kraŋ wora kulubi nna.

english_verse: As soon as you realize what you have done, you must sacrifice a female goat that has nothing wrong with it.
translation_verse: Nɛ e baŋ pin kulubi nɛ e wora na be asheŋ, e beeŋ ta kaboeche nɛ k maŋ kɔ ndulgi kikɛ n lara kulubi nɛ e wora na be sarga.

english_verse: Lead the goat to the north side of the bronze altar and lay your hand on its head, before having it killed.
translation_verse: E beeŋ ta mbe enɔ n deŋi kaboe na be kumu so nseŋ mɔ kumo ashi bɔrɛsure na be kelargato be esoso be kaba so be kakpa nɛ baa mɔ esarga chɔɔso be asɔbɔya na.

english_verse: After this, the priest will remove all of the fat, just as he does when an animal is sacrificed to ask my blessing. The priest will then send the fat up in smoke with a smell that pleases me. This animal is sacrificed so that I will forgive you ordinary people when you sin.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e lara nfɔ na kikɛ fanɛ kananɛ baa lara kɔnɔkoŋwule be sarga be kusɔbɔya be nfɔ na n chɔɔ bɔrɛsure na so saŋɛ na so amo be efɛa beeŋ par Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na. Kananɛ bɔrɛmatapo na beeŋ lara esa be kulubi be sarga nɛ e nya ketampaŋ nna na.

english_verse: If you offer a lamb instead of a goat as a sacrifice for sin, it must be a female that has nothing wrong with it.
translation_verse: Nɛ fanɛ esa lara kubolpɔ nna fanɛ kulubi be sarga be kusɔbɔya, a daga k baa la kubolpɔche nɛ k maŋ kɔ ndulgi kikɛ.

english_verse: The priest will dip a finger in the blood, smear some of it on each of the four corners of the altar, and pour out the rest at the foot of the altar.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ bɔrɛmatapo na e suse kumo be ŋklaŋ na be ako n ta keshilbi n nyɔ amo to ŋ gbiti bɔrɛsure na be mba ana na be nnɔso so nseŋ chulgi amo nɛ a ka na n wurge kumo be kaseto.

english_verse: After this, all of the fat must be removed, just as when an animal is sacrificed to ask my blessing. Then the priest will send it up in smoke to me, together with a food offering, and your sin will be forgiven.
translation_verse: Kumo alɛ be kaman nɛ e lara kubolpɔ na be nfɔ kikɛ fanɛ kananɛ baa lara kusɔbɔya nɛ baa ta a lara kɔnɔkoŋwule be sarga be nfɔ na nseŋ ta amo n ti ajibi be sarga nɛ b bar m ba sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na so n chɔɔ bɔrɛsure na so. Kananɛ bɔrɛmatapo na beeŋ lara esa be kulubi be sarga nɛ e nya ketampaŋ nna na.”

english_verse: You are guilty and unfit to worship me, if you accidentally touch the dead body of any kind of unclean animal.
translation_verse: Nɛ esa maŋ kute m beta kusɔbɔya wuso ŋko kusɔ ko nɛ k maŋ walɛ so daŋkare be ekpa so gba, amodoŋwura wora eyurpi nseŋ wora n da so nna na.

english_verse: You are guilty if you find out that you have accidentally touched anything unclean that comes from a human body.
translation_verse: Nɛ esa maŋ kute m beta kusɔ kama nɛ k bee shin nɛ dimɛdi bee wora eyurpi daŋkare be ekpa so gba, nseŋ ba pin kumo be loŋ, e wora n da so nna na.

english_verse: You are guilty the moment you realize that you have made a hasty promise to do something good or bad.
translation_verse: Nɛ esa baaŋ bɔ ntaŋ alefasha so fanɛ e beeŋ wora kelela ŋko kulubi ko gba, nsaa maŋ wora loŋ, e wora n da so nna na.

english_verse: As soon as you discover that you have committed any of these sins, you must confess what you have done.
translation_verse: Esa kama nɛ e wora n da so ashi asheŋ ere be kekama to daga e tuba kulubi na to

english_verse: Then you must bring a female sheep or goat to me as the price for your sin. A priest will sacrifice the animal, and you will be forgiven.
translation_verse: nseŋ bar kubolpɔ cheso ŋko kaboeche Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be anishito m ba lara kulubi be sarga. Bɔrɛmatapo na e naaŋ yili esa na be katelamu to n lara sarga na.

english_verse: Give both birds to the priest, who will offer one as a sacrifice to ask my forgiveness. He will wring its neck without tearing off its head,
translation_verse: Esa na beeŋ bar mbuibi anyɔ na bɔrɛmatapo kutɔ nɛ e juŋkpar n ta ekoŋwule n lara kulubi be sarga na. E beeŋ kii kabuibi na be kubɔ to m bu ama e maaŋ chuge kumu bre.

english_verse: splatter some of its blood on one side of the bronze altar, and drain out the rest at the foot of the altar.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e wora ŋklaŋ na be ako ŋ ŋmenyaŋ danyaŋ be bɔrɛsure na be akel so nseŋ shin nɛ ŋklaŋ nɛ a ka na a chise n wurge bɔrɛsure na be kaseto. Ŋkpal manɛ so, k la kulubi be sarga nna.

english_verse: If you are so poor that you cannot afford doves or pigeons, you may bring one kilogram of your finest flour. This is a sacrifice to ask my forgiveness, so don't sprinkle olive oil or sweet-smelling incense on it.
translation_verse: Ama nɛ fanɛ esa na maŋ kɔ elepɔ anyɔ ŋko ali anyɔ na gba, e bar nyifu nɛ b kɔr nɛ e pe nɛnɛ be kurwa be bɔlɔ m ba lara kulubi be sarga na. E sa maŋ kaŋ ta ɔlif be ŋku m baga amo ŋko n ta duwu n ti amo so, ŋkpal manɛ so, k la kulubi be sarga nna.

english_verse: Give the flour to a priest, who will scoop up a handful and send it up in smoke together with the other offerings. This is a reminder that all of the flour belongs to me.
translation_verse: Esa na beeŋ bar nyifu na bɔrɛmatapo na kutɔ nɛ mo alɛ e jɔ amo be enɔ be bɔlɔ shɛda so a ŋini fanɛ amo kikɛ nɛ b ta n lara sarga n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na. Kumo be kaman nɛ e chɔɔ amo nɛ e jɔ na bɔrɛsure na so. Ŋkpal manɛ so, k la kulubi be sarga nna.

english_verse: By offering this sacrifice, the priest pays the price for any of these sins you may have committed. The priest gets to keep the rest of the flour, just as he does with grain sacrifices. Sacrifices To Make Things Right (Leviticus
translation_verse: Kananɛ bɔrɛmatapo na beeŋ lara esa na be kulubi be sarga nɛ e nya ketampaŋ nna na. Nyifu nɛ a beeŋ ka na la bɔrɛmatapo na peya nna fanɛ kananɛ ayu be sargajibi be nyifu la mo peya na.” Kewora n jija be sarga be asheŋ

english_verse: The Lord told Moses what the people must do to make things right when they find out they have cheated the Lord without meaning to: If this happens, you must either sacrifice a ram that has nothing wrong with it or else pay the price of a ram with the official money used by the priests.
translation_verse: “Nɛ esa maŋ ka asɔ cheembi nɛ a daga e ka n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ŋkpal e ka maŋ nyi so, e wora n da so nna na. Amodoŋwura beeŋ bar kpakpa nɛ k maŋ kɔ ndulgi kikɛ ŋko bɔrɛmatapo na beeŋ ku kukɔ n sa mo nɛ e ka nɛ b ta n tɔ kakpa na.

english_verse: The next morning you will dress in your priestly clothes, including your linen underwear. Then clean away the ashes left by the sacrifices and pile them beside the altar.
translation_verse: Bɔrɛmatapo na malɛ daga e ta mbe kabɔrɛmata be piŋi m buu ŋ deŋi mbe danshiki so m ba koli sarga chɔɔso na be nsunɔ na m muu n nase bɔrɛsure na be kekel to.

english_verse: and told him what sacrifices the priests must offer on the morning and evening of the day they are ordained: It is the same as the regular morning and evening sacrifices—half a kilogram of flour
translation_verse: “Kachɛ nɛ baaŋ ta kabɔrɛmata be kushuŋ n sa bumo na, le be sarga nɛ Ɛɛrɔn nɛ mbe mbinyɛnsobi beeŋ bar Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be anishito. Nyifu kurwa koŋwule be bɔlɔ fanɛ kananɛ ayu be sargajibi be nyifu nɛ baa sa na du na. Baaŋ bar bargato kachipurso nseŋ bar bargato kaaseso.

english_verse: This sacrifice is very holy, and only the priests may have any part of it.
translation_verse: Bɔrɛmatapo be kanaŋ to be kusɔnyɛn nawule e naaŋ tiŋ n ji loŋ be sarga na. K la sarga cheembi ga nna.

english_verse: If the meat was cooked in a clay pot, the pot must be destroyed, but if it was cooked in a bronze pot, the pot must be scrubbed and rinsed with water.
translation_verse: Kapuliya nɛ baaŋ daŋɛ eblaŋ na kumo to gba daga fanɛ b bure kumo nna. Nɛ fanɛ dadisani to nɛ b daŋɛ eblaŋ na, kumo ere b gbiti kumo to nɛnɛ nseŋ ta nchu n nyɛlpɔ kumo to.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to tell Aaron and his sons how to offer the daily sacrifices that are sent up in smoke to please the Lord: You must put the animal for the sacrifice on the altar in the evening and let it stay there all night. But make sure the fire keeps burning.
translation_verse: “Kaŋɛ Ɛɛrɔn nɛ mo mbinyɛnsobi fanɛ mbraana nɛ n yili a laŋɛ sarga chɔɔso be kaplɛa so nde: A daga fanɛ b baa chɔɔ esarga bɔrɛsure na so saŋkikɛ. A maŋ daga bɔrɛsure na so be edɛ ka duŋ kikɛ.

english_verse: Change into your everyday clothes, take the ashes outside the camp, and pile them in the special place.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e gbaŋ kabɔrɛmata be epiŋi na n nase nseŋ ta piŋi pɔtɛ m buu pɔɛŋ nseŋ muu nsunɔ na n lar keeyi na to n ya lɛ kakpa nɛ k daga.

english_verse: The fire must never go out, so put wood on it each morning. After this, you are to lay an animal on the altar next to the fat that you sacrifice to ask my blessing. Then send it all up in smoke to me.
translation_verse: Bɔrɛsure na so be edɛ na daga e baa suse jemanɛ kikɛ nna nsaa maa duŋ kikɛ. Amoso kachipurso kikɛ, a daga bɔrɛmatapo na ka wɔtɔ ndibi edɛ na to. Kumo be kaman nɛ e bela esarga chɔɔso na kikɛ n deŋi so n chɔɔ amo nɛ kusɔbɔya nɛ b kɔ a lara kɔnɔkoŋwule be sarga na be nfɔ na kikɛ bɔrɛsure na so.

english_verse: The altar fire must always be kept burning—it must never go out. Sacrifices To Give Thanks to the Lord The Lord said:
translation_verse: Bɔrɛsure na so be edɛ na daga e baa chɔɔ jemanɛ kikɛ nna, a maŋ daga b shin nɛ a duŋ kikɛ kuraa. Ayu be sargajibi be asheŋ

english_verse: When someone offers a sacrifice to give thanks to me, the priests from Aaron's family must bring it to the front of the bronze altar,
translation_verse: Ayu be sargajibi be mbraana nɛ a wɔtɔ nde. Bɔrɛmatapoana na e daga b ta ayu be sargajibi m ba Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kutɔ ashi bɔrɛsure na be anishito.

english_verse: where one of them will scoop up a handful of the flour and oil, together with all the incense on it. Then, to show that the whole offering belongs to me, he will lay all of this on the altar and send it up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ bɔrɛmatapo na e jɔ nyifu nɛ b ta ɔlif be ŋku m baga na enɔ be bɔlɔ nseŋ ta duwu n ti so n chɔɔ bɔrɛsure na so shɛda so a ŋini fanɛ amo kikɛ la sarga nɛ amo be efɛa bee par Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nna.

english_verse: The rest of it is to be baked without yeast and eaten by the priests in the sacred courtyard of the sacred tent. This bread is very holy, just like the sacrifices for sin or the sacrifices for making things right, and I have given this part to the priests from what is offered to me on the altar.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ bɔrɛmatapoana na e ta amo nɛ a ka na n wora bodobodo nɛ yiisi maŋ wɔ amo to n we ashi wajɛbu na be kelɔnɛ cheembi na so. Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e ta amo n sa bumo nɛ a baa la bumo be ayu be sargajibi to be kachige. Kananɛ kulubi nɛ kewora n jija be esarga du cheembi na nɛ bodobodo na gba du.

english_verse: Only the men in Aaron's family are allowed to eat this bread, and they must go through a ceremony to be made holy before touching it. This law will never change. When Priests Are Ordained
translation_verse: Ɛɛrɔn be kanaŋ to be benyɛn e naaŋ tiŋ n ji loŋ be ajibi na, ŋkpal manɛ so, a la bumo nɛ bumo be kenana be kachige nna ashi Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be ayu be sargajibi kama nɛ baa lara a sa mo to. Esa cheembi nawule e daga kebeta loŋ be ajibi na.”

english_verse: The Lord spoke to Moses
translation_verse: Ade be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na naŋ kaŋɛ Mosis:

english_verse: mixed with olive oil and cooked in a shallow pan. The bread must then be crumbled into small pieces and sent up in smoke with a smell that pleases me.
translation_verse: Baaŋ ta ɔlif be ŋku m baga nyifu n to mansaŋ. Kumo be kaman nɛ b pupur amo to n lara sarga fanɛ ayu be sargajibi nɛ amo be efɛa bee par Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.

english_verse: Each of Aaron's descendants who is ordained as a priest must perform this ceremony and make sure that the bread is completely burned on the altar. None of it may be eaten! Sacrifices for Sin (Leviticus
translation_verse: Sargajibi kama nɛ bɔrɛmatapo beeŋ lara daga kechɔɔ m mur nna. A maŋ daga b ka ji kumo be shɛŋ.” Kulubi be sarga be asheŋ

english_verse: how the priests from Aaron's family were to offer the sacrifice for sin: This sacrifice is very sacred, and the animal must be killed in my presence at the north side of the bronze altar.
translation_verse: “Kaŋɛ Ɛɛrɔn nɛ mbe mbinyɛnsobi fanɛ mbraana nɛ a wɔtɔ a yɔ kulubi be sarga be kaplɛa so nde: Kakpa nɛ baa mɔ sarga chɔɔso be kusɔbɔya na a daga b mɔ kulubi be sarga be kusɔbɔya gba. K la sarga cheembi ga nna.

english_verse: The priest who offers this sacrifice must eat it in the sacred courtyard of the sacred tent,
translation_verse: Bɔrɛmatapo nɛ e beeŋ lara kumo na beeŋ we kumo be eblaŋ na ashi wajɛbu na be kelɔnɛ nɛ k la kakpa cheembi na so.

english_verse: and anyone or anything that touches the meat will be holy. If any of the animal's blood is splattered on the clothes of the priest, they must be washed in a holy place.
translation_verse: Kusɔ kikɛ nɛ k beta eblaŋ na bee ki cheembi nna. Nɛ kumo be ŋklaŋ gba do piŋi so kakpa cheembi, a daga b fɔr kumo.

english_verse: None of the meat may be eaten from the sacrifices for sin that require blood to be brought into the sacred tent. These sacrifices must be completely burned.
translation_verse: Ama kulubi be sarga be kusɔbɔya kama nɛ b ta kumo be ŋklaŋ nɛ b ta n luri wajɛbu na to n ya kule ketampaŋ ashi kakpa cheembi na bre maŋ daga keji. A daga b chɔɔ kumo nna m mur.”

english_verse: One of the priests will lay these pieces on the altar and send them up in smoke to me.
translation_verse: Bɔrɛmatapo na beeŋ chɔɔ amo bɔrɛsure na so fanɛ sarga chɔɔso n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na, ŋkpal manɛ so, k la kewora n jija be sarga nna.

english_verse: Give me one loaf or wafer from each of these four kinds of bread, after which they will belong to the priest who splattered the blood against the bronze altar.
translation_verse: E beeŋ ta ajibi na be kekama n ti kusɔbɔya na so m ba sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na. Amo alɛ kikɛ la bɔrɛmatapo nɛ e beeŋ ta kɔnɔkoŋwule be sarga be kusɔbɔya na be ŋklaŋ ŋ ŋmenyaŋ bɔrɛsure na so na peya nna.

english_verse: Don't eat any of the meat that has touched something unclean. Instead, burn it. The rest of the meat may be eaten by anyone who is clean and acceptable to me.
translation_verse: Eblaŋ kama nɛ k beta daŋkare be ekpa so be keyurpisɔ kikɛ maŋ daga keji. K daga kechɔɔ nna. Ama eblaŋ nɛ a ka na bre, esa nɛ e maŋ wora eyurpi daŋkare be ekpa so beeŋ tiŋ n we amo.

english_verse: The animal must be killed in the same place where the sacrifice to please me is killed, and the animal's blood must be splattered against the four sides of the bronze altar.
translation_verse: Bɔrɛsure na be kelargato be esoso be kaba so na, kakpa nɛ baa mɔ esarga chɔɔso be asɔbɔya na, a daga b mɔ kewora n jija be sarga be kusɔbɔya na nseŋ ta kumo be ŋklaŋ ŋ ŋmenyaŋ bɔrɛsure na be mba ana na so ŋ kulti.

english_verse: Offer all of the animal's fat, including the fat on its tail and on its insides,
translation_verse: Baaŋ lara kusɔbɔya na be nfɔ kikɛ, amo nɛ a wɔ kpandu nɛ apuntosɔ na,

english_verse: as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat.
translation_verse: nɛ achɛbi na nɛ amo so be nfɔ kikɛ nɛ kegberche na be alela akpa n ti so n chɔɔ bɔrɛsure na so n lara sarga.

english_verse: This sacrifice for making things right is very holy. Only the priests may eat it, and they must eat it in a holy place.
translation_verse: Bɔrɛmatapo be kanaŋ to be kusɔnyɛn kikɛ beeŋ tiŋ n ji sarga na, ama a daga b ji kumo kakpa cheembi nna. Ŋkpal manɛ so, k la sarga cheembi nna.

english_verse: The ceremony for this sacrifice and the one for sin are the same, and the meat may be eaten only by the priest who performs this ceremony of forgiveness.
translation_verse: Mbra koŋwule e deŋ kulubi be sarga nɛ kewora n jija be sarga na kikɛ so. Kumo be eblaŋ la bɔrɛmatapoana nɛ baa yili basa be katelamu to a lara amo na peya nna.

english_verse: In fact, the priest who offers a sacrifice to please me may keep the skin of the animal,
translation_verse: Kusɔbɔya kama nɛ b yili esa be katelamu to n ta n lara sarga chɔɔso kikɛ be kawɔl la bɔrɛmatapo nɛ e lara sarga na peya nna.

english_verse: just as he may eat the bread from a sacrifice to give thanks to me.
translation_verse: Ayu be sargajibi kama fanɛ bodobodo ŋko mansaŋ gba la bɔrɛmatapo nɛ e lara kumo na peya nna.

english_verse: All other grain sacrifices—with or without olive oil in them—are to be divided equally among the priests of Aaron's family. Sacrifices To Ask the Lord's Blessing The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ayu be sargajibi kama nɛ b baga ŋku nɛ amo nɛ a maŋ baga kikɛ la bɔrɛmatapoana kikɛ peya nna nɛ a daga b barga amo to nɛ ekama e nya a sasa. Kɔnɔkoŋwule be sarga be asheŋ

english_verse: Here are the instructions for offering a sacrifice to ask my blessing:
translation_verse: Mbraana nɛ a dese a laŋɛ kɔnɔkoŋwule be sarga be kelara be kaplɛa so nde:

english_verse: If you offer it to give thanks, you must offer some bread together with it. Use the finest flour to make three kinds of bread without yeast—two in the form of loaves mixed with olive oil and one in the form of thin wafers brushed with oil.
translation_verse: Nɛ esa bee shin nɛ e lara kɔnɔkoŋwule be sarga fanɛ kapandi be sarga, a daga e ta bodobodo nɛ a maŋ kɔ yiisi ŋko ekrakashi nɛ a maŋ kɔ yiisi ŋko mansaŋ m b baga amo ŋku n ti kusɔbɔya na so n lara sarga na so n lara kumo.

english_verse: When you offer an animal to ask a blessing from me or to thank me, the meat belongs to you, but it must be eaten the same day.
translation_verse: Kusɔbɔya nɛ b ta n lara kɔnɔkoŋwule nɛ kapandi be sarga na daga b ka we kumo be eblaŋ kikɛ kachɛ nɛ b mɔ kumo na nna. Kare maa chɛ kumo be eblaŋ so.

english_verse: It is different with the sacrifices you offer when you make me a promise or voluntarily give me something. The meat from those sacrifices may be kept and eaten the next day,
translation_verse: Nɛ fanɛ sarga na la sarga nɛ esa lara a tia kɔnɔ nɛ e nase nna ŋko mbe keparso nɛ e lara kumo, a daga b we eblaŋ na kikɛ kachɛ nɛ e lara sarga na, ama baaŋ tiŋ n we kekama nɛ kare chɛ so na gba.

english_verse: but any that is left over must be destroyed. If you eat any of it after the second day, your sacrifice will be useless and unacceptable, and you will be both disgusting and guilty.
translation_verse: Nɛ eblaŋ na fo nchɛ asa nɛ b we kumo, Ebɔrɛ maaŋ sɔ esa na be sarga na. Esa nɛ e lara sarga na maaŋ nya kumo be nɛfa, kumo alɛ maaŋ baa la sarga cheembi. Kumo be kumu lubi malɛ beeŋ baa bɛ esa kikɛ nɛ e we kumo be eblaŋ na so.

english_verse: But don't eat any of this meat if you have become unclean by touching something unclean from a human or an animal or from any other creature. If you do, you will no longer belong to the community of Israel.
translation_verse: Nɛ esa beta dimɛdi ŋko kusɔbɔya nɛ k maŋ walɛ so daŋkare be ekpa so nseŋ ji kɔnɔkoŋwule be sarga nɛ k la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na peya, amodoŋwura maŋ naŋ ti Ebɔrɛ be basa so.

english_verse: to say to the people: Don't eat the fat of cattle, sheep, or goats.
translation_verse: fanɛ e kaŋɛ Israɛlebi na: “Men sa maŋ kaŋ ji kena ŋko kubolpɔ ŋko mboe be nfɔ kikɛ.

english_verse: If one of your animals dies or is killed by some wild animal, you may do anything with its fat except eat it.
translation_verse: Menyeeŋ tiŋ n ta kusɔbɔya wuso ŋko amo nɛ kusɔ pɛ be nfɔ n wora kusɔ pɔtɛ kikɛ, ama men sa maŋ kaŋ ji amo kikɛ.

english_verse: If you eat the fat of an animal that can be used as a sacrifice to me, you will no longer belong to the community of Israel.
translation_verse: Esa kama nɛ e beeŋ ji kusɔbɔya nɛ baaŋ ta n lara sarga n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be nfɔ maaŋ naaŋ ti Ebɔrɛ be basa so.

english_verse: And no matter where you live, you must not eat the blood of any bird or animal,
translation_verse: Kaplɛkama malɛ nɛ men wɔ, men sa maŋ kaŋ ji kabuibi ŋko kusɔbɔya kikɛ be ŋklaŋ.

english_verse: or you will no longer belong to the community of Israel.
translation_verse: Esa kama nɛ e beeŋ ji ŋklaŋ, maaŋ naa la Ebɔrɛ be basa to be eko.”

english_verse: to say to the people of Israel: If you want to offer a sacrifice to ask my blessing, you must bring the part to be burned and lay it on the bronze altar. But you must first lift up the choice ribs with their fat to show that the offering is dedicated to me.
translation_verse: Mo gbagba be enɔ to nɛ e beeŋ keta kumo m ba fanɛ ayu be sargajibi na. E beeŋ bar kusɔbɔya na be nfɔ nɛ kumo be kagbene fanɛ sargagboŋ m ba sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.

english_verse: A priest from Aaron's family will then send the fat up in smoke, but the ribs belong to the priests.
translation_verse: Bɔrɛmatapo na beeŋ chɔɔ nfɔ na bɔrɛsure na so, ama kagbene na bre la bɔrɛmatapo na peya nna.

english_verse: The upper joint of the right hind leg is for the priest who offers the blood and the fat of the animal.
translation_verse: bɔrɛmatapo nɛ e bee sɔ ŋklaŋ na nɛ nfɔ na a lara sarga na kutɔ nna.

english_verse: I have decided that the people of Israel must always give the choice ribs and the upper joint of the right hind leg to Aaron's descendants
translation_verse: Kusɔbɔya na be kagbene la kakɛgboŋ nna nɛ kumo be jisoso be kebɛaŋ na malɛ la kachige nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na bee sɔ Israɛlebi na kutɔ a sa bɔrɛmatapoana na.”

english_verse: These are the ceremonies for sacrifices to please the Lord, to give him thanks, and to ask for his blessing or his forgiveness, as well as the ceremonies for those sacrifices that demand a payment and for the sacrifices that are offered when priests are ordained.
translation_verse: Mbraana nɛ a dese a laŋɛ sarga chɔɔso nɛ ayu be sargajibi nɛ kulubi be sarga nɛ kewora n jija be sarga nɛ kelara n yili n sa Ebɔrɛ be sarga nɛ kɔnɔkoŋwule be sarga na nna na.

english_verse: While Moses and the people of Israel were in the desert at Mount Sinai, the Lord commanded them to start offering these sacrifices.
translation_verse: Sainai be kebee nɛ k wɔ keshishɛrsawule so na so nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ta amo n sa Mosis. Loŋ be kachɛ na nɛ e kaŋɛ Israɛlebi na fanɛ b baa lara esarga ere a sa mo ere Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.

english_verse: Moses lifted up the choice ribs of the ram to show that they were dedicated to the Lord. This was the part that the Lord had said Moses could have.
translation_verse: Ade be kaman nɛ Mosis maŋ kpakpa na be kagbene so a ŋini fanɛ k la kakɛgboŋ nna n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na. Kpakpa na be kagbene na daa la Mosis be kachige nna ashi sarga na to. Mosis daŋ wora kusɔ kama fanɛ kananɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ŋini mo na nna.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ Mosis:

english_verse: Send for Aaron and his sons, as well as their priestly clothes, the oil for ordination, the bull for the sin offering, the two rams, and a basket of bread made without yeast.
translation_verse: “Keta Ɛɛrɔn nɛ mbe mbinyɛnsobi m ba ma anishito ashi wajɛbu na be kabuna, nseŋ ta kabɔrɛmata be epiŋi na nɛ ŋku nɛfaso na m ba. Kumo be kaman nɛ fo ta kulubi be sarga be gbolu fɔlbi na nɛ ekpakpa anyɔ na nɛ bodobodo nɛ a maŋ kɔ yiisi na be kelantaŋɛ be bɔlɔ m ba.

english_verse: Then bring the whole community of Israel together at the entrance to the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ fo shin nɛ Israɛl be basa kikɛ e ba shɛr ndoŋ.”

english_verse: he said, “We are here to follow the Lord's instructions.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis kaŋɛ bumo, “Kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na yili nɛ mee sha kewora na.”

english_verse: After Moses told Aaron and his sons to step forward, he told them to wash themselves.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e shin nɛ Ɛɛrɔn nɛ mbe mbinyɛnsobi lar m ba yili anishito nɛ e shin nɛ b bɛr daŋkare be ekpa nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ŋini bumo na so.

english_verse: He put the priestly shirt and robe on Aaron and wrapped the sash around his waist. Then he put the sacred vest on Aaron and fastened it with the finely woven belt.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ e ta bɔrɛmatapo nimuso be asɔbuuso nɛ a la danshiki nɛ piŋi tenteŋ na nɛ kale nɛ k maŋ kɔ mbre nɛ baa tre ɛfɔd na m buu Ɛɛrɔn nseŋ ta kreso peŋgelembi ko ŋ kre mbe nteto.

english_verse: Next, he put on Aaron the sacred breastpiece that was used in finding out what the Lord wanted his people to do.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e ta demuji be kɔlgu na n di mo nseŋ ta ajembubi nɛ baa ta a to beri a pin Ebɔrɛ be nfɛra nɛ baa tre amo urim nɛ tumim na n wɔtɔ kɔlgu na to.

english_verse: He placed the turban on Aaron's head, and on the front of the turban was the narrow strip of thin gold as a sign of his dedication to the Lord.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ e ta neemu ŋ kre Ɛɛrɔn be kumu so nseŋ ta shuwa be kusɔ paŋgelambi na m mata neemu na be anishito fanɛ kananɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ Mosis na.

english_verse: Moses then dedicated the sacred tent and everything in it to the Lord by sprinkling them with some of the oil for ordination.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis naŋ wora ŋku nɛfaso na ŋ ŋmenyaŋ Enyɛnpe be wajɛbu na nɛ asɔ nɛ a wɔ kumo to na kikɛ so nɛ amo kikɛ ki cheembi.

english_verse: He sprinkled the bronze altar seven times, and he sprinkled its equipment, as well as the large bronze bowl and its base.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e naŋ wora ŋku nɛfaso na be ako ŋ ŋmenyaŋ bɔrɛsure na nɛ kumo be echeenshi nɛ danyaŋ be cheenshigboŋ na nɛ kumo be ketɔl kikɛ so ale shunu nɛ amo kikɛ ki cheembi.

english_verse: He also poured some of the oil on Aaron's head to dedicate him to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ade be kaman nɛ e wora ŋku nɛfaso na be ako n do Ɛɛrɔn be kumu so nɛ mo e ki Ebɔrɛ be esa laraso.

english_verse: Next, Moses dressed Aaron's sons in their shirts, then tied sashes around them and put special caps on them, just as the Lord had commanded.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Mosis shin nɛ Ɛɛrɔn be mbinyɛnsobi na ba anishito nɛ e ta edanshiki m buu bumo nseŋ ta ekreso paŋgelambiana ŋ kre bumo be nshɛr to nseŋ naŋ ta nwuro m buu bumo fanɛ kananɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ŋini na.

english_verse: Moses led out the bull that was to be sacrificed for sin, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.
translation_verse: Ade be kaman nɛ Mosis shin nɛ b bar gbolu fɔlbi nɛ baaŋ ta n lara kulubi be sarga na nɛ Ɛɛrɔn nɛ mbe mbinyɛnsobi na ta bumo be enɔana n deŋi kumo be kumu so.

english_verse: After it was killed, Moses dipped a finger in the blood and smeared some of it on each of the four corners of the bronze altar, before pouring out the rest at the foot of the altar. This purified the altar and made it a fit place for offering the sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Mosis mɔ kumo n suse ŋklaŋ na nseŋ ta mbe keshilbi n nyɔ amo to n do n do bɔrɛsure na be alambɛ ana na be nnɔso so nɛ k ki cheembi. Kumo be kaman nɛ e chulgi ŋklaŋ nɛ a ka na n wurge bɔrɛsure na be kaseto. Kananɛ e wora nɛ bɔrɛsure na ki cheembi nɛ b baa lara kulubi be esarga kumo so nna na.

english_verse: Moses then took the fat on the bull's insides, as well as the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat, and sent them up in smoke on the altar fire.
translation_verse: Nɛ Mosis naŋ lara gbolu fɔlbi na be apuntosɔ so be nfɔ nɛ kegberche na be alela akpa nɛ achɛbi anyɔ na nɛ amo so be nfɔ kikɛ n chɔɔ bɔrɛsure na so.

english_verse: Finally, he took the skin and the flesh of the bull, together with the food still in its stomach, and burned them outside the camp, just as the Lord had commanded.
translation_verse: Ade be kaman nɛ e ta gbolu fɔlbi na be eblaŋ na nɛ kawɔl na nɛ kepurfu na nɛ ebin nɛ a wɔ kumo to na n lar keeyi na to be ekarso n ya chɔɔ, fanɛ kananɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ŋini na.

english_verse: Moses led out the ram for the sacrifice to please the Lord. After Aaron and his sons had laid their hands on its head,
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ Mosis shin nɛ b bar kpakpa nɛ baaŋ ta n lara sarga chɔɔso na, nɛ Ɛɛrɔn nɛ mbe mbinyɛnsobi na ta bumo be enɔana n deŋi kumo alɛ gba be kumu so.

english_verse: Moses killed the ram and splattered its blood against the four sides of the altar.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Mosis mɔ kumo nseŋ suse ŋklaŋ na ŋ ŋmenyaŋ bɔrɛsure na be alambɛ ana na kikɛ so ŋ kulti.

english_verse: Moses had the animal cut up, and he washed its insides and hind legs. Then he laid the head, the fat, and the rest of the ram on the altar and sent them up in smoke with a smell that pleased the Lord. All this was done just as the Lord had commanded.
translation_verse: E ka loge, nɛ e shin nɛ b kuya kpakpa na to nɛ e ta nchu n fɔr apuntosɔ na nɛ kamanto be aya na so n ti kumu na nɛ eblaŋ na kikɛ so n chɔɔ bɔrɛsure na so fanɛ kananɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ŋini na. Sarga chɔɔso ere be efɛa bee par Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nna.

english_verse: Moses led out the ram for the ceremony of ordination. Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis shin nɛ b bar kpakpa nyɔsopo nɛ e beeŋ ta ŋ wora bɔrɛmatapoana be kebuu be kasheŋwora na, nɛ Ɛɛrɔn nɛ mbe mbinyɛnsobi na ta bumo be enɔana n deŋi kusɔbɔya na be kumu so.

english_verse: and it was killed. Moses smeared some of its blood on Aaron's right earlobe, some on his right thumb, and some on the big toe of his right foot.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Mosis mɔ kpakpa na n suse ŋklaŋ na nseŋ wora amo ŋ gbiti Ɛɛrɔn be jisoso be kusoe be kaseto nɛ mbe enɔjiso be keshilbinio nɛ mbe keya jiso be kenashilbinio na kikɛ so.

english_verse: He took the animal's fat tail, the fat on its insides, and the lower part of the liver and the two kidneys with their fat, and the right hind leg.
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ e ta nfɔ na nɛ kpandu na nɛ apuntosɔ be nfɔ nɛ kegberche na be alela ekpa nɛ achɛbi anyɔ na nɛ amo be nfɔ kikɛ nɛ jiso be kebɛaŋ na

english_verse: Then he took from a basket some of each of the three kinds of bread that had been made without yeast and had been dedicated to the Lord.
translation_verse: nseŋ lara ebodobodo nɛ a maŋ kɔ yiisi kelantaŋɛ nɛ b ta m bɔɔ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ enɔ na to be kukoŋwule nɛ bodobodo nɛ b ta ŋku n wea to n wora na be kukoŋwule nɛ krakashi koŋwule n deŋi nfɔ na nɛ kebɛaŋ na so

english_verse: Moses placed the bread on top of the meat and gave it all to Aaron and his sons, who lifted it up to show that it was dedicated to the Lord.
translation_verse: nseŋ ta amo kikɛ m bɔɔ Ɛɛrɔn nɛ mbe mbinyɛnsobi na enɔ, nɛ b maŋ amo so esoso a ŋini fanɛ b ta amo nna a bɔɔ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na enɔ.

english_verse: After this, Moses placed it on the fires of the altar and sent it up in smoke with a smell that pleased the Lord. This was part of the ordination ceremony.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Mosis naŋ sɔ amo bumo be enɔana to n ta n deŋi sarga chɔɔso na so n chɔɔ ashi bɔrɛsure na so a ŋini fanɛ k la keta esa ŋ ki bɔrɛmatapo n sa Ebɔrɛ na be sarga nna. Kede la sarga nɛ kumo be efɛa bee par Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nna.

english_verse: Finally, Moses sprinkled the priestly clothes of Aaron and his sons with some of the oil for ordination and with some of the blood from the altar. So Aaron and his sons, together with their priestly clothes, were dedicated to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ Mosis wora ŋku nɛfaso na nɛ bɔrɛsure na so be ŋklaŋ na be ako ŋ ŋmenyaŋ Ɛɛrɔn nɛ mbe mbinyɛnsobi na nɛ bumo be asɔbuuso so, nɛ bumo nɛ amo kikɛ ki cheembi Ebɔrɛ be anishito.

english_verse: Moses said to Aaron and his sons: The Lord told me that you must boil this meat at the entrance to the sacred tent and eat it there with the bread.
translation_verse: Mosis ka wora loŋ n loge nɛ e kaŋɛ Ɛɛrɔn nɛ mbe mbinyɛnsobi na le: “Men ta eblaŋ na n yɔ Enyɛnpe be wajɛbu na be kabuna ase n ya daŋɛ amo n ti ebodobodo nɛ a wɔ kelantaŋɛ na to so n we amo ndoŋ fanɛ kananɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ŋini na.

english_verse: We have obeyed the Lord in everything that has been done today, so that your sins may be forgiven.
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e yili kumo fanɛ an wora kusɔ nɛ k wora kabre ere saŋɛ na so, menyeeŋ nya alubi be ketampaŋ.

english_verse: The Lord has told me that you must stay near the entrance to the tent for seven days and nights, or else you will die.
translation_verse: A daga men baa wɔ wajɛbu na be kabuna to kapa nɛ kanyɛ kikɛ nsaa wora kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na yili na n ya fo nchɛ ashunu na. Nɛ men maŋ wora loŋ menyeeŋ wu.”

english_verse: Aaron and his sons obeyed everything that the Lord had told Moses they must do.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ɛɛrɔn nɛ mbe mbinyɛnsobi na nu nseŋ bɛ asɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na bɔla Mosis so n yili n sa bumo na kikɛ so.

english_verse: Then he said to Aaron: Find a young bull and a ram that have nothing wrong with them. Offer the bull to the Lord as a sacrifice for sin and the ram as a sacrifice to please him.
translation_verse: nɛ e kaŋɛ Ɛɛrɔn le: “Fin gbolu fɔlbi nɛ kpakpa nɛ a maŋ kɔ ndulgi nseŋ ta gbolu fɔlbi na n lara kulubi be sarga, n ta kpakpa na malɛ n lara sarga chɔɔso n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel that they must offer sacrifices as well. They must offer a goat as a sacrifice for sin, and a bull and a ram as a sacrifice to please the Lord. The bull and the ram must be a year old and have nothing wrong with them.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ fo kaŋɛ Israɛlebi na fanɛ b ta kaboenyɛn n lara kulubi be sarga nseŋ ta gbolu fɔlbi nɛ kpakpafɔlbi nɛ a ji nfɛ koko nsaa maa kɔ ndulgi kikɛ na n lara sarga chɔɔso n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na

english_verse: Then the people must offer a bull and a ram as a sacrifice to ask the Lord's blessing and also a grain sacrifice mixed with oil. Do this, because the Lord will appear to you today.
translation_verse: nseŋ naŋ ta gbolu nɛ kpakpa n lara kɔnɔkoŋwule be sarga. A daga b ta amo n ti ayu be sargajibi nɛ b ta ŋku m baga amo n lara kɔnɔkoŋwule be sarga n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na. A daga b ka wora loŋ, ŋkpal manɛ so, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na beeŋ lar bumo so kabre.”

english_verse: After the animals and the grain had been brought to the front of the sacred tent, and the people were standing there in the presence of the Lord,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ b bar asɔ nɛ Mosis kaŋɛ fanɛ b bar na kikɛ ashi wajɛbu na be anishito nɛ basa na kikɛ shɛr ndoŋ nɛ b bunyaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.

english_verse: Moses said: The Lord has ordered you to do this, so that he may appear to you in all of his glory.
translation_verse: Nɛ Mosis kaŋɛ: “Kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na yili fanɛ men wora nna na, saŋɛ na so mbe kemaŋkura beeŋ lar menyi so.”

english_verse: Aaron, step up to the altar and offer the sacrifice to please the Lord, then offer the sacrifices for the forgiveness of your sins and for the sins of the people, just as the Lord has commanded.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Mosis naŋ kaŋɛ Ɛɛrɔn le: “Yɔ bɔrɛsure na ase n ya lara fo kumu so be sarga chɔɔso pɔɛŋ nseŋ lara kulubi be esarga ŋ kule fo nɛ basa na kikɛ be alubi be ketampaŋ fanɛ kananɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na yili kumo na.”

english_verse: Aaron stepped up to the altar and killed the bull that was to be the sacrifice for his sins.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ɛɛrɔn yɔ bɔrɛsure na ase n ya mɔ gbolu fɔlbi na n lara mbe kumu so be kulubi be sarga.

english_verse: His sons brought him the blood. He dipped a finger in it, smeared some on the four corners of the bronze altar, and poured out the rest at its foot.
translation_verse: Nɛ mbe mbinyɛnsobi na suse kumo be ŋklaŋ m bar mo nɛ e ta keshilbi n nyɔ amo to ŋ gbiti bɔrɛsure na be alambɛ ana na be nnɔso nseŋ chulgi ŋklaŋ nɛ a ka na n wurge bɔrɛsure na be kaseto.

english_verse: But he sent up in smoke the fat, the kidneys, and the lower part of the liver, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ e ta kumo be nfɔ na nɛ achɛbi anyɔ na nɛ kegberche na be alela akpa n deŋi bɔrɛsure na so n chɔɔ fanɛ kananɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na yili n sa Mosis na.

english_verse: Then Aaron burned the skin and the flesh outside the camp.
translation_verse: Ama eblaŋ na nɛ kawɔl na bre, e ta amo nna n lar keeyi na be ekarso n ya chɔɔ.

english_verse: After Aaron had killed the ram that was sacrificed to please the Lord, Aaron's sons brought him the blood, and he splattered it against all four sides of the altar.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ e mɔ mbe sarga chɔɔso be kusɔbɔya na. Nɛ mbe mbinyɛnsobi na suse kumo be ŋklaŋ n sa mo nɛ e wora amo ŋ ŋmenyaŋ ŋ ŋmenyaŋ bɔrɛsure na be mba ana na kikɛ so.

english_verse: They brought him each piece of the animal, including the head, and he burned them all on the altar.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ b bela kusɔbɔya na be kumu nɛ eblaŋ kikɛ m bar mo nɛ e chɔɔ amo bɔrɛsure na so

english_verse: He washed the insides and the hind legs and also sent them up in smoke.
translation_verse: nseŋ ta nchu n fɔr kumo be apuntosɔ nɛ kaman be ayawɔrta so m bela amo n ti eblaŋ na so n chɔɔ bɔrɛsure na so.

english_verse: Next, Aaron sacrificed the goat for the sins of the people, as he had done with the sacrifice for his own sins.
translation_verse: Ɛɛrɔn ka wora loŋ n loge nɛ e bar basa na malɛ be esarga be asɔbɔya m ba mɔ kulubi be sarga be kaboe na n lara kulubi be sarga, fanɛ kananɛ e daŋ wora mo gba peya na.

english_verse: And so, he burned this sacrifice on the altar in the proper way.
translation_verse: E daŋ bar basa na be sarga chɔɔso be kusɔbɔya na nna m ba lara sarga fanɛ kananɛ mbra bee ŋini na.

english_verse: He also presented the grain sacrifice and burned a handful of the flour on the altar as part of the morning sacrifice.
translation_verse: E daŋ bar ayu be sargajibi gba nna nseŋ jɔ nyifu na enɔ be bɔlɔ n ti kachipurso be sarga chɔɔso na so n chɔɔ bɔrɛsure na so.

english_verse: Finally, he killed the bull and the ram as a sacrifice to ask the Lord's blessing on the people. Aaron's sons brought him the blood, and he splattered it against the four sides of the altar.
translation_verse: Kumo be lalaloge nɛ e mɔ gbolu nɛ kpakpa na n lara basa na be kɔnɔkoŋwule be sarga na. Nɛ mbe mbinyɛnsobi na suse ŋklaŋ na m ba sa mo nɛ e wora amo ŋ ŋmenyaŋ bɔrɛsure na be mba ana na so.

english_verse: His sons placed all the fat, as well as the kidneys and the lower part of the liver
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Ɛɛrɔn ta eblaŋ be nfɔ ekpa fanɛ kpandu na nɛ apuntosɔ nɛ achɛbi nɛ agbirche na be alela akpa kikɛ

english_verse: Then Aaron burned the fat on the altar and lifted up the ribs and the right hind leg to show that these were dedicated to the Lord. This was done just as the Lord had instructed Moses.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e ta ŋgbene na nɛ jiso be ebɛaŋ nɛ a la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be kakɛgboŋ nɛ k bee yɔ bɔrɛmatapoana na kutɔ fanɛ kananɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na yili n sa Mosis na.

english_verse: Aaron held out his hand and gave the people his blessing, before coming down from the bronze altar where he had offered the sacrifices.
translation_verse: Ɛɛrɔn ka lara esarga na kikɛ n loge nɛ e maŋ mbe enɔana so n shoŋi basa na nseŋ nɛfa bumo pɔɛŋ nseŋ shi bɔrɛsure na ase ŋ gbelge m ba.

english_verse: He and Moses went into the sacred tent, and when they came out, they gave the people their blessing. Then the Lord appeared to the people in all of his glory.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn luri wajɛbu na to. B ka lar m ba nɛ b nɛfa basa na nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be kemaŋkura fulto ndoŋ nɛ basa na kikɛ wu kumo.

english_verse: The Lord sent fiery flames that burned up everything on the altar, and when everyone saw this, they shouted and fell to their knees to worship the Lord.
translation_verse: Epul na to nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na shin nɛ edɛ ba buu sarga chɔɔso na nɛ nfɔ na kikɛ so bɔrɛsure na so n chɔɔ amo m mur. Basa na kikɛ ka wu loŋ nɛ b boŋ to kagbenefuliso n ta enɔana m buu bumo be anishi so nseŋ kur amu n yuu to.

english_verse: Nadab and Abihu were two of Aaron's sons, but they disobeyed the Lord by burning incense to him on a fire pan, when they were not supposed to.
translation_verse: Nadab nɛ Abihu kikɛ daa la Ɛɛrɔn be mbinyɛnsobi nna nɛ b daŋ wora n da Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na so ŋkpal b ka daŋ wora edɛ n wɔtɔ edɛtɔl to n chɔɔ duwu ekpa nɛ k maŋ daga so m ba Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be anishito so.

english_verse: Suddenly the Lord sent fiery flames and burned them to death.
translation_verse: Epul to nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na shin nɛ edɛ ba buu bumo so n chɔɔ bumo m mɔ.

english_verse: Then Moses told Aaron that this was exactly what the Lord had meant when he said: “I demand respect from my priests, and I will be praised by everyone!” Aaron was speechless.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis kaŋɛ Ɛɛrɔn: “Kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na daa de saŋɛ nɛ e daa malga fanɛ, bekama nɛ baa shuŋ mo daga b bɔla mbe kecheembiya so n sa mo bunyaŋ. Mo alɛ beeŋ shin nɛ mbe kemaŋkura a dii efuli ashi mbe basa to nɛ b bunyaŋ mo.” Ama Ɛɛrɔn daa maŋ kaŋɛ shɛŋ.

english_verse: Moses sent for Mishael and Elzaphan, the two sons of Aaron's uncle Uzziel. Then he told them, “Take these two dead relatives of yours outside the camp far from the entrance to the sacred tent.”
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Mosis tre Mishaal nɛ Ɛlzafan nɛ b la Ɛɛrɔn mo wɔpa, Uziɛl, be mbinyɛnsobi nseŋ kaŋɛ bumo le: “Men ba ta men kurgepoana ere be kebuni ashi wajɛbu na to n lar n yɔ keeyi na be ekarso n ya nase.”

english_verse: Then Moses told Aaron and his other two sons, Eleazar and Ithamar: Don't show your sorrow by messing up your hair and tearing your priestly clothes, or the Lord will get angry. He will kill the three of you and punish everyone else. It's all right for your relatives, the people of Israel, to mourn for those he destroyed by fire.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Mosis kaŋɛ Ɛɛrɔn nɛ mbe mbinyɛnsobi, Eliazaa nɛ Itama: “Men sa maŋ kaŋ jija menyi be anishiakpa ŋko ŋ kpɛa menyi be asɔbuuso to a ŋini fanɛ menyee shu keeli nna. Men baŋ wora loŋ menyeeŋ wu. Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na malɛ beeŋ nya agbo n wora kade na kikɛ. Ama men kurgepoana Israɛlebi na bre beeŋ tiŋ n shu ŋkpal bumo nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na shin nɛ edɛ chɔɔ m mɔ na so.

english_verse: The Lord said to Aaron:
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ Ɛɛrɔn le:

english_verse: When you or your sons enter the sacred tent, you must never drink beer or wine. If you do, you will die right there! This law will never change.
translation_verse: “Fo nɛ fo mbinyɛnsobi e sa maŋ kaŋ nuu yabra ŋko nsa booso be yiri kikɛ nseŋ ba luri wajɛbu na to kikɛ. Men baŋ wora loŋ menyeeŋ wu. Kede la mbra nna a dese n sa fo nɛ fo kaman to ebi kikɛ.

english_verse: You must also teach the people of Israel everything that I commanded Moses to say to them.
translation_verse: Menyi alɛ e ŋini Israɛlebi na mbraana nɛ m bɔla Mosis so n ta n sa menyi na kikɛ nyam.”

english_verse: Moses told Aaron and his two sons, Eleazar and Ithamar: The grain sacrifice that was offered to give thanks to the Lord is very holy. So make bread without yeast from the part that wasn't sent up in smoke and eat it beside the altar.
translation_verse: Nɛ Mosis kaŋɛ Ɛɛrɔn nɛ mbe mbinyɛnsobi anyɔ, Eliaza nɛ Itama, nɛ b ka na le: “Men ta ayu be sargajibi nɛ a ka ashi ajibi nɛ b ta n lara sarga n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na to na n wora ebodobodo nɛ a maŋ kɔ yiisi n chena bɔrɛsure na ase n we, ŋkpal manɛ so, k la sarga nɛ k du cheembi ga nna.

english_verse: The Lord has said that this belongs to you and your sons, and that it must be eaten in a holy place.
translation_verse: Men baa ji kumo kakpa cheembi, ŋkpal manɛ so, k la menyi nɛ men be mbinyɛnsobi be kachige nna ashi ayu be sargajibi nɛ baa lara a sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nna. Kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na yili n sa ma nna na.

english_verse: But the choice ribs and the hind leg that were lifted up may be eaten by your entire family, as long as you do so in an acceptable place. These parts are yours from the sacrifices that the people offer to ask the Lord's blessing. This is what the Lord has commanded, and it will never change.
translation_verse: Baaŋ ta kagbene na nɛ kebɛaŋ na n ti nfɔana na so m ba jemanɛ nɛ b kɔ amo a ba nɛ b ba lara sarga n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na. Le be ejikpaana ere la menyi nɛ men be mbia peya nna hale mbaanaayɔ, fanɛ kananɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na yili kumo na.”

english_verse: When Moses asked around and learned that the ram for the sin sacrifice had already been burned on the altar, he became angry with Eleazar and Ithamar and said,
translation_verse: Mosis ka bishi kaboe nɛ baaŋ ta n lara kulubi be sarga na be asheŋ nseŋ nu fanɛ b tiŋ n chɔɔ kumo nɛ e nya agbo n wora Eliaza nɛ Itama nseŋ bishi bumo:

english_verse: “Why didn't you eat the meat from this sacrifice in an acceptable place? It is very holy, and the Lord has given you this sacrifice to remove Israel's sin and guilt.
translation_verse: “Manɛ e ba nɛ men maŋ ji kulubi be sarga na ashi kakpa nɛ k du cheembi nseŋ daga? K la sarga cheembi ga nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ta n sa menyi nɛ e bɔla kumo so n lara kade na kikɛ be alubi bumo to.

english_verse: Whenever an animal's blood isn't brought into the sacred tent, I commanded you to eat its meat in an acceptable place, but you burned it instead.”
translation_verse: Men ka maŋ suse mo ŋklaŋ n luri kakpa cheembi na gba na, a daŋ daga men ka we eblaŋ na bre kakpa nɛ k daga, fanɛ kananɛ n yili menyi na.”

english_verse: Their father Aaron replied, “Today two of my sons offered the sacrifice for sin and the sacrifice to please the Lord, and look what has happened to me! Would the Lord have approved if I had eaten the sacrifice for sin?”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ɛɛrɔn kaŋɛ Mosis le: “Nɛ n daŋ ji kulubi be sarga na kabre, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na daa beeŋ shuli ma a? Kabre nɛ basa na lara bumo be kulubi be sarga nɛ sarga chɔɔso n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na, ama keni asheŋ tumase nɛ a tu ma.”

english_verse: Moses was satisfied with Aaron's reply.
translation_verse: Mosis ka nu Ɛɛrɔn be kamalga na nɛ mbe kagbene wushi mo.

english_verse: any animal that has divided hoofs and chews the cud.
translation_verse: Kusɔbɔya kama nɛ mbe alotobi barga to nɛ k bee gbu apla,

english_verse: The Lord told Moses and Aaron
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn

english_verse: But you must not eat animals such as camels, rock badgers, and rabbits that chew the cud but don't have divided hoofs. And you must not eat pigs—they have divided hoofs, but don't chew the cud. All of these animals are unclean, and you are forbidden even to touch their dead bodies.
translation_verse: A maŋ daga men ka ji le be asɔbɔya ere ŋko m beta amo be kuwuso gba. Ŋkpal manɛ so, a la asɔbɔya nɛ a maŋ walɛ nna.

english_verse: You may eat anything that lives in water and has fins and scales. But it would be disgusting for you to eat anything else that lives in water, and you must not even touch their dead bodies.
translation_verse: Men sa maŋ kaŋ ji nchu to be kusɔ keniso kama nɛ k maŋ kɔ afafaribi, ŋkpal manɛ so, a la ekishi nna n sa menyi.

english_verse: Eagles, vultures, buzzards, crows, ostriches, hawks, sea gulls, owls, pelicans, storks, herons, hoopoes, and bats are also disgusting, and you are forbidden to eat any of them.
translation_verse: Mbuibi nɛ a maŋ walɛso nsaa maŋ daga fanɛ men baa ji amo ŋkpal a ka la ekishi so nde: Kusore nɛ gbuŋgbula nɛ kɔl nɛ lambɛ nɛ kɔlfɔɔti nɛ margaati nɛ jita nɛ mɔmɔ nɛ nyiŋgbeŋ nɛ luku nɛ tɔkɔrkɔ nɛ kelɛkelɛ nɛ ebɔrɛ be kabuibi nɛ kɔŋkɔŋ.

english_verse: The only winged insects you may eat are locusts, grasshoppers, and crickets. All other winged insects that crawl are too disgusting for you to eat.
translation_verse: Ama asɔwurbi kama nɛ a kɔ atɛ nseŋ naa gbeye kasawule so maŋ walɛ, a la ekishi nna n sa menyi.

english_verse: Don't even touch the dead bodies of animals that have divided hoofs but don't chew the cud. And don't touch the dead bodies of animals that have paws. If you do, you must wash your clothes, but you are still unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Esa kama nɛ e beta asɔbɔya ere be kekama be kuwuso maaŋ baa walɛ so hale nɛ epeŋi e ya tɔr. Asɔbɔya na a la amo nɛ a kɔ alotobi nɛ a maŋ barga to nɛ amo alɛ maa gbu a pla nɛ asɔbɔya kikɛ nɛ a kɔ akuti. Esa kama nɛ e sulɔ asɔbɔya ere be kekama be kuwuso daga e fɔr mbe asɔbuuso, ama e kraa beeŋ baa wɔ eyurpi to n ya fo kaaseso.

english_verse: Anyone who touches their dead bodies or anything touched by their dead bodies becomes unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Esa kama nɛ e beeŋ beta amo be kekama be kekeniso ŋko kuwuso beeŋ baa wɔ eyurpi to hale nɛ epeŋi e ya tɔr.

english_verse: If something made of wood, cloth, or leather touches one of their dead bodies, it must be washed, but it is still unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Nɛ emo be kekama wu n tɔr kusɔ kikɛ so fanɛ kedibi ŋko wajɛ ŋko kawɔl ŋko bɔtɛ, k beeŋ wora eyurpi nseŋ daga kefɔr. Ama kumo alɛ kraa beeŋ baa wɔ eyurpi na to hale n ya fo kaaseso.

english_verse: If any of these animals is found dead in a clay pot, the pot must be broken to pieces, and everything in it becomes unclean.
translation_verse: Nɛ amo be kekama wu n tɔr kapuya to, kusɔ kikɛ nɛ k wɔ kumo to beeŋ wora eyurpi nseŋ daga fanɛ men bure kapuya na.

english_verse: If you pour water from this pot on any food, that food becomes unclean, and anything drinkable in the pot becomes unclean.
translation_verse: Nɛ kapuya na to be nchu do ajibi jiso to, ajibi na beeŋ wora eyurpi. Kusɔ nuuso kikɛ nɛ k shi kapuya na to ma alɛ gba wora eyurpi.

english_verse: If the dead body of one of these animals touches anything else, including ovens and stoves, that thing becomes unclean and must be destroyed.
translation_verse: Nɛ emo be kekama wu n tɔr kusɔ kama so k bee wora eyurpi nna. An ta fanɛ nɛ emo be kuko wu n tɔr asure nɛ b yuu ŋko bodobodo be ebu nɛ b pɔr so, k beeŋ wora eyurpi n daga fanɛ b bure kumo.

english_verse: A spring or a cistern where one of these dead animals is found is still clean, but anyone who touches the animal becomes unclean.
translation_verse: Ama nɛ kekama wu n tɔr ketirbu ŋko kakpa nɛ b pɔr a suse nchu a wɔtɔ to bre ketirbu na ŋko kusɔ suse, nchu na kraa walɛ nna, ama kusɔ kama nɛ k beeŋ beta kusɔ wuso na bre beeŋ wora eyurpi.

english_verse: But seeds that are soaking in water become unclean, if the dead animal is found in the water.
translation_verse: Ama nɛ asɔduu na pɔlɔ nchu to nna nɛ k wu n tɔr amo to, kumo ere asɔduu na wora eyurpi nna na.

english_verse: If an animal that may be eaten happens to die, and you touch it, you become unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Nɛ asɔbɔya nɛ menyeeŋ tiŋ n ji na gba be kekama wu kpi nɛ esa beta kumo, esa na beeŋ wora eyurpi hale nɛ kaase e ya fo.

english_verse: Don't eat any of those disgusting little creatures that crawl or walk close to the ground.
translation_verse: Amo e la amo nɛ a bee gbeye ŋko a nite aya ana ŋko aya damta so na.

english_verse: If you eat any of them, you will become just as disgusting and unclean as they are.
translation_verse: Men sa maŋ kaŋ we amo be kekama n ta eyurpi m pɛ menyi be amu.

english_verse: I am the Lord your God, and you must dedicate yourselves to me and be holy, just as I am holy. Don't become disgusting by eating any of these unclean creatures.
translation_verse: Ma e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ menyi be Ebɔrɛ na nɛ a daga men lara menyi be amu n yili a kɔr bekama to a ŋini fanɛ men la n nawule peya nna, ŋkpal manɛ so, n du cheembi nna.

english_verse: I brought you out of Egypt so that I could be your God. Now you must become holy, because I am holy!
translation_verse: Ma e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ n lara menyi ashi Ijipt be efuli so m ba nɛ m baa kaa la men be Ebɔrɛ, amoso men baa du cheembi, ŋkpal manɛ so, n du cheembi nna.

english_verse: I have given these laws so that you will know what animals, birds, and fish are clean and may be eaten, and which ones are unclean and may not be eaten.
translation_verse: Men baa da so nseŋ tiŋ m pin m barga asɔ nɛ a walɛ Ebɔrɛ be ekpa so ashi amo nɛ a maŋ walɛ so to, nseŋ tiŋ m barga asɔbɔya nɛ a daga keji ashi amo nɛ a maŋ daga keji to.”

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ Mosis fanɛ

english_verse: to say to the community of Israel: If a woman gives birth to a son, she is unclean for seven days, just as she is during her monthly period.
translation_verse: e kaŋɛ Israɛlebi na le: “Eche kama nɛ e di kedampo ŋ kurge ebinyɛn beeŋ wora eyurpi daŋkare be ekpa so nchɛnshunu fanɛ kananɛ e bee wora eyurpi jemanɛ nɛ e bee lar ntamaŋ na.

english_verse: Her son must be circumcised on the eighth day,
translation_verse: Kachɛ burwasopo na nɛ b ku kebia na kututu.

english_verse: When the mother has completed her time of cleansing, she must come to the front of the sacred tent and bring to the priest a year-old lamb as a sacrifice to please me and a dove or a pigeon as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: Nchɛ nɛ eche na beeŋ ta n nyalɛ so na kaŋ fo ekar, e beeŋ bar kpakpa nɛ k fo kafɛ koŋwule nɛ keli ŋko lepɔ m ba sa bɔrɛmatapo na ashi wajɛbu cheembi na be kabuna nɛ e ta kpakpa na n lara sarga chɔɔso nseŋ ta keli ŋko lepɔ na n lara kulubi be sarga.

english_verse: After the priest offers the sacrifices to me, the mother will become completely clean from her loss of blood, whether her child is a boy or a girl.
translation_verse: Bɔrɛmatapo na beeŋ bar eche na be sarga na Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kutɔ m ba lara kumo n fɔr mo so nɛ e naŋ nyalɛ so daŋkare be ekpa so. Kusɔ nɛ eche nɛ e kurge daga fanɛ e wora nna na.

english_verse: If she cannot afford a lamb, she can offer two doves or two pigeons, one as a sacrifice to please me and the other as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: Nɛ eche na maaŋ tiŋ n nya kpakpafɔlbi na, e beeŋ bar ali anyɔ ŋko elepɔ anyɔ, nɛ kukoŋwule e baa la sarga chɔɔso peya nɛ kenyɔsopo na e baa la kulubi be sarga peya. Nɛ bɔrɛmatapo na e ta amo n lara kenyalɛso be sarga nɛ eche na e nyalɛ so daŋkare be ekpa so.”

english_verse: The Lord told Moses and Aaron to say to the people:
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn fanɛ b kaŋɛ basa na le:

english_verse: If sores or boils or a skin rash should break out and start spreading on your body, you must be brought to Aaron or to one of the other priests.
translation_verse: “Nɛ achuu ŋko asɔtoso lar esa be eyur so nsaa beeŋ tiŋ m pete n suse basa, a daga b bar mo Bɔrɛmatapo Nimuso Ɛɛrɔn ŋko mbe mbinyɛnsobi nɛ b la bɔrɛmatapoana na be eko kutɔ.

english_verse: But if the infected area is white and only skin deep, and if the hair in it hasn't turned white, the priest will order you to stay away from everyone else for seven days.
translation_verse: Ama nɛ kuchuu na fuli to nna nsaa maŋ ji n luri eblaŋ to nɛ kumo to be afuibi na maŋ ki n fuli, kumo ere bɔrɛmatapo na beeŋ shin nɛ e barga basa n ya fo nchɛnshunu.

english_verse: If the disease hasn't spread by that time, he will order you to stay away from everyone else for another seven days.
translation_verse: Kachɛ shunusopo na, nɛ bɔrɛmatapo na e naŋ mige mbe kuchuu na to ŋ keni nɛnɛ. E kaŋ wu fanɛ k maŋ salga to e beeŋ naŋ shin nɛ e barga basa nchɛnshunu n ti so.

english_verse: Any of you with a skin disease must be brought to a priest.
translation_verse: Esa kama nɛ e nya eyur so be kulɔ lubi kikɛ daga b ka bar mo bɔrɛmatapo kutɔ nna,

english_verse: If he discovers that the sore spot is white with pus and that the hair around it has also turned white,
translation_verse: nɛ e mige mo to ŋ keni nɛnɛ. Nɛ k la kuchuu n fuli to nɛ kumo to be afuibi fuli nɛ k bee lar nchu nna,

english_verse: If you have a sore that either swells or turns reddish-white after it has healed, then you must show it to a priest.
translation_verse: kumo be kaman nɛ ndoŋ naŋ laŋɛ m puŋi n fuli to ŋko m pere to, esa na daga e yɔ bɔrɛmatapo na kutɔ n ya ta kakpa nɛ k puŋi na n ŋini mo.

english_verse: If he discovers that the hair in the infected area has turned white and that the infection seems more than skin deep, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
translation_verse: Bɔrɛmatapo na beeŋ mige mo to ŋ keni nɛnɛ, nɛ kakpa na wora fanɛ k ji n luri eblaŋ to nɛ kumo to be afuibi na ki n fuli, e beeŋ shin nɛ mo nɛ ekama e pin fanɛ e maŋ walɛ so. Kulɔ lubi e naa kar mo na.

english_verse: But if the white area is only on the surface of the skin and hasn't become any worse, and if the hair in it hasn't turned white, he will tell you to stay away from everyone else for seven days.
translation_verse: Ama nɛ bɔrɛmatapo na keni kumo nɛnɛ nseŋ wu fanɛ afuibi nɛ a wɔ kumo to na maŋ ki n fuli nɛ kumo alɛ maŋ ji n luri eblaŋ to nseŋ terge to bre, bɔrɛmatapo na beeŋ shin nɛ e barga basa nchɛnshunu.

english_verse: If the sore begins spreading during this time, the priest will say, “You are unclean because you have a disease.”
translation_verse: Nɛ kuchuu na bee nyɛrga bre, bɔrɛmatapo na beeŋ shin nɛ mo nɛ ekama e pin e ka maŋ walɛ so ŋkpal e ka bee lɔ kulɔ lubi so.

english_verse: But if it doesn't spread, and only a scar remains, he will say, “You are now clean.”
translation_verse: Ama nɛ k maa nyɛrga nsaa du kananɛ k du bre, bɔrɛmatapo na beeŋ shin nɛ mo nɛ ekama e pin fanɛ e walɛ so daŋkare be ekpa so.

english_verse: If you have a burn that gets infected and turns red or reddish-white,
translation_verse: Nɛ edɛ chɔɔ esa nɛ mbe eyur so be achuu na fuli ŋko m pere to,

english_verse: a priest must examine it. Then if he discovers that the hair in the infected area has turned white and that the infection seems more than skin deep, he will say, “The burn has turned into leprosy, and you are unclean.”
translation_verse: bɔrɛmatapo na beeŋ mige mo to ŋ keni nɛnɛ. Nɛ afuibi nɛ a wɔ mboŋ nɛ a chɔɔ na ki n fuli nseŋ ji n luri eblaŋ to, kumo ere kulɔ lubi e fara mboŋ nɛ a chɔɔ na. Bɔrɛmatapo na beeŋ shin nɛ mo nɛ ekama e pin fanɛ e maŋ walɛ so.

english_verse: But if the priest finds that the hair in the infected area hasn't turned white and that the sore is only skin deep and it is healing, he will tell you to stay away from everyone else for seven days.
translation_verse: Ama nɛ mboŋ nɛ a chɔɔ na maŋ ji n luri eblaŋ to nseŋ terge to nɛ afuibi na maŋ ki n fuli bre, bɔrɛmatapowura na beeŋ shin nɛ e barga basa nchɛnshunu.

english_verse: On the seventh day the priest will examine you again, and if the infection is spreading, he will say, “This is leprosy—you are unclean.”
translation_verse: Kachɛ shunusopo na nɛ bɔrɛmatapo na e naŋ mige mo to ŋ keni nɛnɛ. Nɛ kulɔ na bee salga eyur na so bɔrɛmatapo na beeŋ shin nɛ mo nɛ ekama e pin fanɛ e maŋ walɛ so, ŋkpal manɛ so, kulɔ suseso nɛ e bee lɔ na.

english_verse: However, if the infection hasn't spread and has begun to heal, and if only a scar remains, he will say, “Only a scar remains from the burn, and you are clean.”
translation_verse: Ama nɛ fanɛ kakpa na maŋ chɛrga nsaa maŋ salga to mbe eyur so nseŋ terge to, kumo ere k to kufɔr jiga nna nɛ bɔrɛmatapo na e shin nɛ mo nɛ ekama e pin fanɛ e walɛ so, ŋkpal manɛ so edɛ na a bɛlge mbe eyur.

english_verse: If you have a sore on your head or chin,

translation_verse: Bɔrɛmatapo na beeŋ mige mo to ŋ keni nɛnɛ, nɛ e kaŋ wu fanɛ kapɛ na pere to ŋko n fuli to,

english_verse: If you ever have leprosy, you must tear your clothes, leave your hair uncombed, cover the lower part of your face, and go around shouting, “I'm unclean! I'm unclean!”
translation_verse: Esa kama nɛ e bee lɔ kulɔ lubi daga e baa buu asɔfarbi nsaa maa mɔ mbe emin to nna. Mo alɛ e baa ta wajɛ a buu mbe kamuna so a gbelge mbe eyur so nsaa nite a ponte to a kaŋɛ, ‘M maŋ walɛ so, m maŋ walɛ so!’

translation_verse: Kachɛ shunusopo na e beeŋ naŋ mige kumo to ŋ keni nɛnɛ, nɛ kapuu na salga to kumo ere kusɔ na maŋ walɛ so nna na.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to say to the people:
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ Mosis,
