translation_verse: bɔrɛmatapo na beeŋ shin nɛ b ya bar mbuibi keniso anyɔ nɛ a daga keta n lara sarga nɛ kedibi nɛ baa tre sida na nɛ kechɛbi peper chɛŋchɛŋ nɛ keduuso nɛ baa tre hisɔp na be afantaŋ.

english_verse: The priest will order someone to kill one of the birds over a clay pot of spring water.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ bɔrɛmatapo na e shin nɛ b ta mbuibi anyɔ na to be ekoŋwule n chulgi kapuya nɛ k kɔ kechubu to be nchu so m mɔ kumo.

english_verse: Then he will dip the other bird, the cedar, the red yarn, and the hyssop in the blood of the dead bird.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ e ta kabuibi nyɔsopo na nɛ sida be kedibi na be keyabi nɛ kechɛbi peper chɛŋchɛŋ na nɛ hisɔp be afantaŋ na n nyɔ kabuibi nɛ b mɔ na be ŋklaŋ na to

english_verse: Next, he will sprinkle you seven times with the blood and say, “You are now clean.” Finally, he will release the bird and let it fly away.

english_verse: Then you must once again shave your head, face, and eyebrows, as well as the hair on the rest of your body. Finally, wash your clothes and take a bath, and you will be completely clean.
translation_verse: Kachɛ shunusopo na e beeŋ naŋ she mbe kumu nɛ katɔl nɛ anishi guŋgumbi nɛ mbe eyur so be afuibi kikɛ. Mo alɛ beeŋ naŋ fɔr mbe asɔbuuso nseŋ bɛr nchu pɔɛŋ nseŋ nyalɛ so.

english_verse: There he will offer one of the rams, together with the oil, as a sacrifice to make things right. He will also lift them up to show that they are dedicated to me.
translation_verse: nseŋ ya ta kpakpafɔlbi na be kuko n ti ŋku kɔlba koŋwule nɛ bargato na so n lara kewora n jija be sarga. Kumo be kaman nɛ e maŋ amo so a ŋini fanɛ k la sargagboŋ nna n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nɛ k bee yɔ bɔrɛmatapo na kutɔ.

english_verse: This sacrifice is very holy. It belongs to the priest and must be killed in the same place where animals are killed as sacrifices for sins and as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: Kakpa nɛ baa mɔ kulubi be esarga nɛ esarga chɔɔso be asɔbɔya na nɛ e beeŋ mɔ kpakpafɔlbi na. A daga e ka wora loŋ, ŋkpal manɛ so, k la kewora n jija be sarga nna fanɛ kananɛ kulubi be sarga la bɔrɛmatapoana na be kachige nsaa du cheembi ga na.

english_verse: The priest will smear some of the blood from this sacrifice on your right ear lobe, some on your right thumb, and some on the big toe of your right foot.
translation_verse: Bɔrɛmatapo na beeŋ suse ŋklaŋ na be eko n wora amo ŋ gbiti esa nɛ baa sha ekama ka pin fanɛ e ka nyalɛ so na be jisoso be kusoe to nɛ mbe enɔjiso be keshilbinio nɛ keya jiso be kenashilbinio.

english_verse: He will then pour some of the olive oil into the palm of his left hand,

translation_verse: nseŋ ta mbe enɔjiso be keshilbi n nyɔ ŋku na to ŋ ŋmenyaŋ ale ashunu ashi Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be anishito.

english_verse: Next, the priest will smear some of the oil on your right ear lobe, some on your right thumb, and some on the big toe of your right foot,
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e wora ŋku nɛ a wɔ mbe enɔ be epunto na nɛ kpakpafɔlbi na be ŋklaŋ na be ako ŋ gbiti esa nɛ baa sha ekama ka pin fanɛ e nyalɛ so na be jisoso be kusoe to nɛ mbe enɔjiso be keshilbinio nɛ mbe keya jiso be kenashilbinio.

english_verse: Depending on what you can afford, you must also offer either two doves or two pigeons, one as a sacrifice for sin and the other as a sacrifice to please me.

translation_verse: Mbe kenyalɛso be kesheŋ wora na be kachɛ burwasopo na nɛ e beeŋ bar amo bɔrɛmatapo na kutɔ ashi wajɛbu na be kabuna ase.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses and Aaron to say to the people:
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn le:

english_verse: After I have given you the land of Canaan as your permanent possession, here is what you must do, if I ever put mildew on the walls of any of your homes.
translation_verse: “Men kaŋ ya luri Keenan be kasawule nɛ mee sha keta n sa menyi ere to, nɛ ŋ kaŋ shin nɛ ndoŋ be laŋ ko be egbal puu,

translation_verse: bɔrɛmatapo na beeŋ naŋ yɔ n ya keni. Nɛ k ba fanɛ kapuu na salga to nna, kumo ere laŋ na maŋ walɛ so nna na.

english_verse: Then he will have the house torn down and every bit of wood, stone, and plaster hauled off to an unclean place outside the town.

translation_verse: Ama bɔrɛmatapo na ka naŋ ya keni laŋ na jemanɛ nɛ b lɔŋɛ kumo n la na, n wu fanɛ kapuu na maŋ naŋ lar egbal na so, e beeŋ shin nɛ ekama e pin fanɛ k walɛ so daŋkare be ekpa so, ŋkpal manɛ so, kapuu na maŋ naa wɔ laŋ na to.

english_verse: Then, to show that the house is now clean, he will get two birds, a stick of cedar wood, a piece of red yarn, and a branch from a hyssop plant and bring them to the house.
translation_verse: Mbuibi anyɔ nɛ kedibi nɛ baa tre sida na be keyabi nɛ kechɛbi peper chɛŋchɛŋ nɛ keduuso nɛ baa tre hisɔp na be afantaŋ nɛ bɔrɛmatapo na beeŋ ta n wora kenyalɛso be kesheŋ wora n shin nɛ laŋ na e naŋ nyalɛ so.

translation_verse: E beeŋ keta mbuibi na be eko n chulgi kapuya nɛ kechubu be nchu wɔ kumo to na so m mɔ kumo.

translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ta mbraana ere n sa Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn

english_verse: Any saddle or seat on which the man sits is unclean. And if you touch or carry either of these, you must wash your clothes and take a bath, but you still remain unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Esa kama nɛ e beta kusɔ kama nɛ e chena so beeŋ baa wɔ eyurpi to n ya fo kaaseso. Esa kama malɛ nɛ e sulɔ kusɔ kama nɛ e chena so daga fanɛ e fɔr mbe asɔbuuso nseŋ bɛr nchu, ama mo alɛ kraa beeŋ baa wɔ eyurpi to n ya fo kaaseso.
