translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Mosis shuŋi n tre Deetan nɛ Abiram. Ama le nɛ b daŋ kaŋɛ: “Anyi maaŋ ba!

english_verse: It's bad enough that you took us from our rich farmland in Egypt to let us die here in the desert. Now you also want to boss us around!
translation_verse: Men ka lara anyi ashi Ijipt be kasawule nɛ ajibi damta nɛ kedamaya wɔ na m ba lɛ keshishɛrsawule ere so nɛ men mɔ ere bre maŋ kukwe a? Nɛ men naa sha nɛ men ta anyi ŋ ki menyi be nyɛrbi a tɔrɔ a?

english_verse: Moses was very angry and said to the Lord, “Don't listen to these men! I haven't done anything wrong to them. I haven't taken as much as a donkey.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis nya agbo ga nseŋ kaŋɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ le: “Sa maŋ kaŋ sɔ sarga nɛ basa ere kɔ a bar fo ere. M maŋ wora bumo be ekama kulubi. Ma alɛ maŋ sɔ esa kama be kurma.”

english_verse: Then he said to Korah, “Tomorrow you and your followers must go with Aaron to the Lord's sacred tent.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Mosis kaŋɛ Koora malɛ le: “Echefo, fo nɛ fo braana na kikɛ nɛ Ɛɛrɔn e ba Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be wajɛbu na ase.

english_verse: Each of you take along your fire pan with incense in it and offer the incense to the Lord.”
translation_verse: Men be ekama e chulgi duwu n wɔtɔ mbe edɛtɔl to m ba chɔɔ n lara sarga n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.”

english_verse: The next day the men placed incense and coals in their fire pans and stood with Moses and Aaron at the entrance to the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Kumo be ŋklade nɛ b muu ajanwulɛ n wɔtɔ bumo be edɛtɔl to nseŋ chulgi duwu n wɔtɔ edɛ na to nɛ bumo nɛ Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn kikɛ ya yili Enyɛnpe be wajɛbu na be kabuna.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Korah had convinced the rest of the Israelites to rebel against their two leaders. When that happened, the Lord appeared in all his glory
translation_verse: Nɛ Koora shin nɛ Israɛlebi na kikɛ gbargbar abar m ba yili Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn be anishito ashi wajɛbu na be kabuna. Epul na to nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be kemaŋkura lar basa na kikɛ so,

english_verse: and said to Moses and Aaron,
translation_verse: nɛ e kaŋɛ Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn le:

english_verse: “Get away from the rest of the Israelites so I can kill them at once!”
translation_verse: “Men barga men be amu ashi basa na kutɔ saŋɛ na so, meeŋ mɔ bumo epul ere to.”

english_verse: But the two men bowed down and prayed, “Our God, you gave these people life. Why would you punish everyone here when only one man has sinned?”
translation_verse: Ama Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn bre daŋ gbir nna ŋ kurgi amu n yuu to nseŋ kaŋɛ le: “O Ebɔrɛ, fo e naa sa anyi ŋkpa. Feeŋ shuli n nya agbo n wɔtɔ basa ere kikɛ ŋkpal esa koŋwule be kulubi so a?”

english_verse: The Lord answered Moses,
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Mosis le:

english_verse: “Tell the people to stay away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.”
translation_verse: “Kaŋɛ basa na fanɛ b loŋi Koora nɛ Deetan nɛ Abiram be ewajɛbu na ase.”

english_verse: Moses walked over to Dathan and Abiram, and the other leaders of Israel followed.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis kpa n niŋi to nɛ Israɛl be bejuŋkparpoana na bɛ mo so n yɔ Deetan nɛ Abiram kutɔ.

english_verse: Then Moses warned the people, “Get away from the tents of these sinful men! Don't touch anything that belongs to them or you'll be wiped out.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Mosis kpele basa na kusoe ŋ kaŋɛ le: “Men loŋi basa lubi ere be ewajɛbu ase. Men sa maŋ beta bumo be kusɔ kama, nɛ manɛ aloŋ menyi nɛ bumo kikɛ beeŋ wu ŋkpal bumo be alubi so.”

english_verse: Moses said to the crowd, “The Lord has chosen me and told me to do these things—it wasn't my idea. And here's how you will know:
translation_verse: Nɛ Mosis kaŋɛ basa na le: “Kede e naaŋ shin nɛ men pin fanɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e shuŋi ma fanɛ n wora asɔ ere kikɛ, mannɛ fanɛ ŋ gbagba be keparso nɛ mee wora amo.

english_verse: If these men die a natural death, it means the Lord hasn't chosen me.
translation_verse: Nɛ Ebɔrɛ baŋ maŋ gberge basa ere kusoe n shin nɛ b wu, kumo ere mannɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e lara ma fanɛ ŋ ki men be ejuŋkparpo.

english_verse: But suppose the Lord does something that has never been done before. For example, what if a huge crack appears in the ground, and these men and their families fall into it and are buried alive, together with everything they own? Then you will know they have turned their backs on the Lord!”
translation_verse: Ama nɛ fanɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na wora kusɔ nɛ k maŋ naŋ wora kikɛ nseŋ shin nɛ kasawule baŋɛ to n ta basa ere nɛ bumo be beche nɛ mbia nɛ kusɔ kama nɛ b kɔ kikɛ m min, loŋ nɛ menyeeŋ pin fanɛ basa ere kini Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kashenteŋto.”

english_verse: As soon as Moses said this, the ground under the men opened up
translation_verse: Mosis ka baŋ malga n loge, nɛ kasawule baŋɛ to epul to

english_verse: and swallowed them alive, together with their families and everything they owned. Then the ground closed back up, and they were gone.
translation_verse: Kasawule na daŋ baŋɛ to nna nɛ bumo nɛ bumo be mpetɛ kikɛ tɔr to nɛ k daŋ buu bumo so nɛ b kra keni nɛ basa na maŋ naŋ wu bumo.

english_verse: The rest of the Israelites heard their screams, so they ran off, shouting, “We don't want that to happen to us!”
translation_verse: Israɛlebi nɛ b daa wɔ ndoŋ na ka nu bumo be kushu, nɛ b shile nsaa cha awɔr e kaŋɛ le: “Men baa shile! Nɛ manɛ aloŋ, kasawule na beeŋ ta anyi alɛ gba m min!”

english_verse: Then the Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ Mosis le:

english_verse: “Tell Aaron's son Eleazar to take the fire pans from the smoldering fire and scatter the coals. The pans are now sacred,
translation_verse: “Kaŋɛ bɔrɛmatapo Ɛɛrɔn pibinyɛn Eliaza fanɛ e lara danyaŋ be edɛtɔl na ashi kedɛmurmur na to nseŋ gbeŋi ajanwulɛ nɛ a wɔ amo to na n lɛ. Edɛtɔlana na ki asɔ cheembi nna,

english_verse: because they were used for offering incense to me. Have them hammered into a thin layer of bronze as a covering for the altar. Those men died because of their sin, and now their fire pans will become a warning for the rest of the community.”
translation_verse: ŋkpal b ka ta amo m ba Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be bɔrɛsure na ase so. Ta basa nɛ edɛ chɔ m mɔ ŋkpal bumo be alubi so ere be edɛtɔl m bɛl ebuuso a buu bɔrɛsure na so nɛ kumo be loŋ e baa la kefiɛso n sa Israɛlebi.”

english_verse: Eleazar collected the pans and had them hammered into a thin layer of bronze as a covering for the altar,
translation_verse: Amoso bɔrɛmatapo Eliaza e daŋ ta edɛtɔl na n sa nɛ b bɛl ebuuso a buu bɔrɛsure na so,

english_verse: just as the Lord had told Moses. The pans were a warning to the Israelites that only Aaron's descendants would be allowed to offer incense to the Lord. Anyone else who tried to would be punished like Korah and his followers. The Israelites Rebel and Are Punished
translation_verse: nɛ k baa la kanyiŋi n sa Israɛlebi na fanɛ esa kama nɛ e maŋ shi Ɛɛrɔn be kanaŋ to, maŋ daga e ka chɔɔ duwu n lara sarga bɔrɛsure na so n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na. Esa kama nɛ e wora loŋ beeŋ wu fanɛ kananɛ Koora nɛ mbe basa wu na. Ɛɛrɔn ka mɔlga Israɛlebi na be asheŋ

english_verse: The next day the people of Israel again complained against Moses and Aaron, “The two of you killed some of the Lord's people!”
translation_verse: Kumo be ŋklade nɛ Israɛlebi kikɛ naŋ fubel m bile asheŋ m malga ŋ gbiti Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn ŋ kaŋɛ le: “Men mɔ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be basa, ŋko!”

english_verse: As the people crowded around them, Moses and Aaron turned toward the sacred tent, and the Lord appeared in his glory in the cloud covering the tent.
translation_verse: B ka ba abar so nɛ b ba malga ŋ gbiti Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn na, nɛ b keni wajɛbu na be kaba so, nseŋ wu Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be kemaŋkura ka bɔla kuwɔlpa to m ba buu kumo so.

english_verse: So Moses and Aaron walked to the front of the tent,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn ya yili wajɛbu na be anishito,

english_verse: where the Lord said to them,
translation_verse: nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Mosis le:

english_verse: “Stand back! I am going to wipe out these Israelites once and for all.” They immediately bowed down and prayed.
translation_verse: “Men shile basa ere kutɔ nɛ m ba mɔ bumo epul ere to!” Epul na to nɛ Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn gbir ŋ kurgi amu n yuu to ŋ kule Ebɔrɛ,

english_verse: Then Moses told Aaron, “Grab your fire pan and fill it with hot coals from the altar. Put incense in it, then quickly take it to where the people are and offer it to the Lord, so they can be forgiven. The Lord is very angry, and people have already started dying!”
translation_verse: nɛ Mosis kaŋɛ Ɛɛrɔn le: “Ya chɔɔ bɔrɛsure na so be edɛ n wɔtɔ fo kedɛtɔl to nseŋ ta duwu n wɔtɔ amo to n wora manaŋ n yɔ basa na kutɔ n ya lara alubi be ketampaŋ be sarga n sa bumo. Ŋkpal manɛ so Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nya agbo nɛ aleblawu fara.”

english_verse: Aaron walked back and stood with Moses at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Aleblawu na ka ku nɛ Ɛɛrɔn yɔ Mosis kutɔ ashi wajɛbu na be kabuna to.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses:
translation_verse: Le nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ daŋ kaŋɛ Mosis:

english_verse: Place these sticks in the tent right in front of the sacred chest where I appear to you.
translation_verse: Nɛ fo ta akpabi na n ya yili ŋkre be deka na be anishito, ashi Enyɛnpe be wajɛbu na be kakpa nɛ mee kaa tu fo na.

english_verse: I will then choose a man to be my priest, and his stick will sprout. After that happens, I won't have to listen to any more complaints about you.
translation_verse: Ekama nɛ n lara fanɛ bɔrɛmatapo na be kekpabi beeŋ gbu kenishi. Loŋ e naaŋ shin nɛ Israɛlebi ere e yige kebaa fubel a bile asheŋ a malga a gbiti fo.”

english_verse: Moses told the people what the Lord had commanded, and they gave him the walking sticks from the twelve tribal leaders, including Aaron's from the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis kaŋɛ Israɛlebi na kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ na, nɛ bumo be nnaŋ kuduanyɔ na be kekama sa mo bumo be ejuŋkparpo be kekpabi n ta Ɛɛrɔn peya n ti so.

english_verse: Moses took them and placed them in the Lord's sacred tent.
translation_verse: Nɛ Mosis ta akpabi na kikɛ n nase Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be ŋkre be deka na be anishito ashi wajɛbu na to.

english_verse: Moses brought the twelve sticks out of the tent and showed them to the people. Each of the leaders found his own and took it.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis lara akpabi na kikɛ wajɛbu na to n m ba ŋini Israɛlebi na. B ka wu kusɔ nɛ k wora na, nɛ bejuŋkparpoana na be ekama ta mbe kekpabi.

english_verse: But the Lord told Moses, “Put Aaron's stick back! Let it stay near the sacred chest as a warning to anyone who might think of rebelling. If these people don't stop their grumbling about me, I will wipe them out.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Mosis le: “Bɛta Ɛɛrɔn bre be kekpabi na n ya nase ŋkre be deka na be anishito, nɛ k baa la kefiɛso n sa Israɛlebi nɛ baa fubel a bile asheŋ a malga a gbiti ma na. B baa maŋ yige bumo be nfubel na, bumo kikɛ beeŋ wu.”

english_verse: Moses did what he was told.
translation_verse: Nɛ Mosis wora kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ mo na kikɛ chap.

english_verse: The Israelites cried out to Moses, “We're done for
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Israɛlebi na kaŋɛ Mosis le: “Kumo ere, an wu nna na!

english_verse: and doomed if we even go near the sacred tent!”
translation_verse: Nɛ ekama nɛ e ba wajɛbu na ase beeŋ wu bre, kumo ere anyi kikɛ maŋ naa wɔtɔ nna na!”

english_verse: The Levites are your relatives and are here to help you in your service at the tent.
translation_verse: Fo kurgepoana Livaiebi na e naaŋ baa chɛ fo nɛ fo mbinyɛnsobi to a shuŋ wajɛbu na to.

english_verse: You must see that they perform their duties. But if they go near any of the sacred objects or the altar, all of you will die.
translation_verse: Shin nɛ b baa shuŋ kushuŋ kama nɛ feeŋ sa bumo ashi wajɛbu na to, ama b sa maŋ kaŋ beta asɔ cheembi nɛ a wɔ Enyɛnpe be wajɛbu na to na nɛ bɔrɛsure na bre, nɛ mannɛ aloŋ, fo nɛ bumo kikɛ beeŋ wu.

english_verse: No one else is allowed to take care of the sacred tent or do anything connected with it.
translation_verse: Bumo nawule e naaŋ baa tu menyi a shuŋ wajɛbu na to. A maŋ daga esa pɔtɛ ka wora loŋ.

english_verse: Follow these instructions, so I won't become angry and punish the Israelites ever again.
translation_verse: Fo nɛ fo mbinyɛnsobi nawule e daga kebaashuŋ Enyɛnpe be wajɛbu na to nɛ bɔrɛsure na so, loŋ nɛ ma agbo maaŋ naŋ ba Israɛlebi na so.

english_verse: I alone chose the Levites from all the other tribes to belong to me, and I have given them to you as your helpers.
translation_verse: Ŋ gbagba e lara fo kurgepoana Livaiebi na ashi Israɛlebi to fanɛ kakɛ nɛ b ta m bɔɔ ma enɔ n sa menyi, nɛ b baa chɛ to a shuŋ wajɛbu na to.

english_verse: But only you and your sons can serve as priests at the altar and in the most holy place. Your work as priests is a gift from me, and anyone else who tries to do that work must be put to death. The Priests' Share of Offerings Given to the Lord (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Fo nɛ fo mbinyɛnsobi nawule e naaŋ baa shuŋ kabɔrɛmata be kushuŋ na ashi bɔrɛsure na so nɛ acheembiana to be kakpa cheembi na to. Ŋkpal manɛ so ma e ta kabɔrɛmata be kushuŋ ere n sa menyi. Amoso esa kama nɛ e ta kpramɛ n shuŋ kumo, daga b ka mɔ mo.” Bɔrɛmatapoana be kachige be asheŋ

english_verse: You are allowed to eat the meat of those animals, just as you can eat the choice ribs and the right hind leg of the special sacrifices.
translation_verse: Amo be eblaŋ na bre kikɛ la menyeya nna fanɛ kananɛ sarga nɛ baa maŋ so a ŋini Ebɔrɛ na be ŋgbene na nɛ jiso be ebɛaŋana la menyeya na.

english_verse: The Lord said to Aaron: I have put you in charge of the sacred gifts and sacrifices that the Israelites bring to me. And from now on, you, your sons, and your descendants will receive part of the sacrifices for sin, as well as part of the grain sacrifices, and the sacrifices to make things right. Your share of these sacrifices will be the parts not burned on the altar.
translation_verse: Sarga cheembi kama nɛ b maa chɔɔ bɔrɛsure na so bre la menyeya nna, amo e la ayu be sargajibi nɛ kulubi be sarga nɛ abar be kelɔŋɛ be sarga. Kusɔ cheembi kama nɛ b ta m ba lara sarga n sa ma la fo nɛ fo mbinyɛnsobi peya nna.

english_verse: Since these things are sacred, they must be eaten near the sacred tent, but only men are allowed to eat them.
translation_verse: Le be asɔ ere la asɔ cheembi nna, amoso benyɛn nawule e chena kakpa cheembi n ji amo.

english_verse: You will also receive part of the special gifts and offerings that the Israelites bring to me. Any member of your family who is clean and acceptable for worship can eat these things.
translation_verse: Sarga pɔtɛ kama nɛ k naŋ ti ade so bre la menyeya nna mbaanaayɔ, nɛ fo nɛ fo mbinyɛnsobi nɛ becheso nɛ fo laŋ to ebi nɛ b walɛ so daŋkare be ekpa so, beeŋ tiŋ n ji amo.

english_verse: For example, when the Israelites bring me the first batches of oil, wine, and grain, you can have the best parts of those gifts.
translation_verse: N ta ɔlif be ŋku nɛ yabra belbelso nɛ ayu nɛ a la sososo be ajibi nɛ Israɛlebi bee lara kafɛ kafɛ kikɛ a sa ma na nna n sa menyi.

english_verse: And the first part of the crops from their fields and vineyards also belongs to you. The people will offer this to me, then anyone in your family who is clean may have some of it.
translation_verse: Amo kikɛ la menyeya nna nɛ men be laŋ to be esa kama nɛ e walɛ so daŋkare be ekpa so beeŋ tiŋ n ji amo.

english_verse: Everything in Israel that has been completely dedicated to me will now belong to you.
translation_verse: Kusɔ kama nɛ b lara n yili n sa ma ashi Israɛl be efuli so, la menyeya nna.

english_verse: The first-born son in every Israelite family, as well as the first-born males of their flocks and herds, belong to me. But every first-born son and first-born donkey must be bought back from me.
translation_verse: Dimɛdi ŋko kusɔbɔya be wurkoŋ kama nɛ Israɛlebi na baaŋ ta n sa ma, la menyeya nna. Ama a daga men ka shuli nɛ b ka wurkoŋ kama nɛ kusɔbɔya be wurkoŋ kama nɛ k maŋ walɛ so daŋkare be ekpa so be kukɔ.

english_verse: The price for a first-born son who is at least one month old will be five pieces of silver, weighed according to the official standards.
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe be wajɛbu to be kananɛ baa karga amansherbi na be gbiti be ndarbi anu e daga fanɛ b ka n tɔ mbia nɛ b ji afɔl koko.

english_verse: From now on, the sacred offerings that the Israelites give to me will belong to you, your sons, and your daughters. This is my promise to you and your descendants, and it will never change.
translation_verse: Baŋ yili kabre a yɔ, sarga cheembi kama nɛ Israɛlebi na lara n sa ma ki fo nɛ fo mbinyɛnsobi nɛ mbichesobi peya mbaanaayɔ. Kɔnɔ nɛ n sa fo nɛ fo kaman to ebi nna na, kumo alɛ maaŋ chɛrga kikɛ.”

english_verse: You will not receive any land in Israel as your own. I am the Lord, and I will give you whatever you need. What the Levites Receive The Lord said to Aaron:
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ naŋ kaŋɛ Ɛɛrɔn le: “Fo maaŋ nya kasawule be kachige nɛ k beeŋ baa la fo kapetɛ ashi Israɛl be kasawule so. Ma Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e naŋ baa la fo kapetɛ.” Livaiebi na be kushuŋ be asheŋ

english_verse: Ten percent of the Israelites' crops and one out of every ten of their newborn animals belong to me. But I am giving all this to the Levites as their pay for the work they do at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ naŋ kaŋɛ le: “N ta Israɛlebi na be kudukudusopo kikɛ nɛ baa bar ma nna a sa Livaiebi na. Amo e la Enyɛnpe be wajɛbu na to na be kushuŋ nɛ baa shuŋ be kakɔka.

english_verse: They are the only ones allowed to work at the tent, and they must not let anyone else come near it. Those who do come near must be put to death, and the Levites will also be punished. This law will never change. Since the Levites won't be given any land in Israel as their own,
translation_verse: Livaiebi na nawule e naa ba shuŋ wajɛbu na to nɛ kumo be kewora n da so be turju e ba bɛ bumo. Le be mbra ere dese nna n sa menyi nɛ men be kaman to ebi kikɛ mbaanaayɔ. Bumo alɛ maaŋ nya kapetɛ kikɛ ashi Israɛlebi na to,

english_verse: they will be given the crops and newborn animals that the Israelites offer to me. What the Levites Must Give
translation_verse: ŋkpal manɛ so, mee ta kudukudusopo nɛ Israɛlebi na bee ta a lara sarga a sa ma na nna a sa Livaiebi na fanɛ bumo be kapetɛ ashi Israɛl be kasawule so.” Livaiebi na be kudukudusopo be asheŋ

english_verse: to say to the Levites: When you receive from the people of Israel ten percent of their crops and newborn animals, you must offer a tenth of that to me.
translation_verse: e kaŋɛ Livaiebi na le: “Men baŋ sɔ Israɛlebi be kudukudusopo nɛ mee ta a sa menyi fanɛ men be kapetɛ na, menyi alɛ gba e lara amo be kudukudusopo n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ,

english_verse: as an offering to me. That amount must then be given to Aaron,
translation_verse: Le be ekpa so nɛ menyee baa bɔla a lara men be kudukudusopo. Bɔrɛmatapowura Ɛɛrɔn nɛ menyeeŋ ba ta amo a sa.

english_verse: so the best of what you receive will be mine.
translation_verse: Amo to be alela e daga fanɛ men ka lara n ya sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.

english_verse: After you have dedicated the best parts to me, you can eat the rest, just as the Israelites eat part of their grain and wine after offering them to me.
translation_verse: Men baŋ lara amo to be alela n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na, menyeeŋ tiŋ n ta amo nɛ a ka na fanɛ kananɛ edɔpo bee lara mbe adɔjibi be kudukudusopo nsaa ta amo nɛ a ka na.

english_verse: Your share may be eaten anywhere by anyone in your family, because it is your pay for working at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Menyi nɛ menyi be kanaŋ kikɛ beeŋ tiŋ n ji amo, ŋkpal manɛ so menyi be wajɛbu to be kushuŋ be kakɔka nna na.

english_verse: You won't be punished for eating it, as long as you have already offered the best parts to me. The gifts and sacrifices brought by the people must remain sacred, and if you eat any part of them before they are offered to me, you will be put to death.
translation_verse: Nɛ men baŋ lara amo to be alela n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na pɔɛŋ nseŋ ji amo nɛ a ka na, kumo ere men maŋ wora n da so. Menyi alɛ maŋ jija Israɛlebi na be esarga cheembi na. Menyi alɛ maaŋ wu.”

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following law: The people of Israel must bring Moses a reddish-brown cow that has nothing wrong with it and that has never been used for plowing.
translation_verse: fanɛ b ta mbra ere n sa Israɛlebi na fanɛ b bar kena peper nɛ b maŋ naŋ ta kumo n shuŋ kikɛ nɛ k maŋ kɔ ndulgi kumo so m ba sa Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn,

english_verse: Moses will give it to Eleazar the priest, then it will be led outside the camp and killed while Eleazar watches.
translation_verse: nɛ b ta kumo n sa bɔrɛmatapo Eliaza nseŋ keta kumo n lar keeyi na to n ya mɔ mbe anishito.

english_verse: He will dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times in the direction of the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Nɛ Eliaza e suse kumo be ŋklaŋ na be ako n ta keshilbi n nyɔ amo to ŋ ŋmenyaŋ wajɛbu na be kaba so ale ashunu.

translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ b chɔɔ kena na kikɛ nɛ kumo be kawɔl nɛ eblaŋ nɛ ŋklaŋ nɛ apuntosɔ bɔrɛmatapo na be anishito.

english_verse: A priest is to throw a stick of cedar wood, a hyssop branch, and a piece of red yarn into the fire.
translation_verse: Nɛ bɔrɛmatapo na e ta kedibi nɛ baa tre sida na nɛ kumo nɛ baa tre hisɔp na nɛ jese peper n lɛ edɛ na to.

english_verse: After the ceremony, the priest is to take a bath and wash his clothes. Only then can he go back into the camp, but he remains unclean and unfit for worship until evening.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ bɔrɛmatapo na e ya fɔr mbe epiŋi nseŋ bɛr pɔɛŋ m bɛta m ba keeyi na to. Ama e maaŋ baa walɛ so daŋkare be ekpa so hale n ya fo kaaseso.

english_verse: The man who burned the cow must also wash his clothes and take a bath, but he is also unclean until evening.

english_verse: A man who isn't unclean must collect the ashes of the burnt cow and store them outside the camp in a clean place. The people of Israel can mix these ashes with the water used in the ceremony to wash away sin.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ esa nɛ e walɛ so daŋkare be ekpa so e muu kena nɛ b chɔɔ na be nsunɔ n ya yili keeyi na to be ekarso be kakpa nɛ k walɛ daŋkare be ekpa so. Nɛ Israɛlebi na e baa ta nsunɔ na a wea nchu nɛ baa ta a fɔr basa be alubi a lɛ daŋkare be ekpa so na to.

english_verse: The man who collects the ashes must wash his clothes, but will remain unclean until evening. This law must always be obeyed by the people of Israel and the foreigners living among them. What Must Be Done after Touching a Dead Body The Lord said:

english_verse: But if you wash with the water mixed with the cow's ashes on the third day and again on the seventh day, you will be clean and acceptable for worship. You must wash yourself on those days; if you don't, you will remain unclean.

translation_verse: Esa kama nɛ e beta ebuni nseŋ kini kefɔr mbe kumu so daŋkare be ekpa so, wora eyurpi n jija Enyɛnpe be wajɛbu na nna nsaa maaŋ naŋ ti Ebɔrɛ be basa so.

english_verse: If someone dies in a tent while you are there, you will be unclean for seven days. And anyone who later enters the tent will also be unclean.
translation_verse: Nɛ fanɛ esa ko malɛ wu wajɛbu to, bekama nɛ b wɔ kumo to nɛ e wu na nɛ bekama nɛ e wu pɔɛŋ nɛ b luri kumo to na kikɛ wora eyurpi daŋkare be ekpa so nchɛnshunu.

english_verse: If you touch the body of someone who died or was killed, or if you touch a human bone or a grave, you will be unclean for seven days.
translation_verse: Ekama nɛ e beta esa nɛ b mɔ kowushina ŋko esa nɛ e wu kowushina be kebuni, ŋko dimɛdi be kuwibi ŋko nchaŋ gba wora eyurpi daŋkare be ekpa so nchɛnshunu.

english_verse: Before you can be made clean, someone who is clean must take some of the ashes from the burnt cow and stir them into a pot of spring water. translation_verse: Nɛ esa nɛ e walɛ so daŋkare be ekpa so, e ta kedibi nɛ baa tre hisɔp be keyabi n nyɔ nchu na to ŋ ŋmenyaŋ ŋ ŋmenyaŋ wajɛbu na nɛ kusɔ kama nɛ k wɔ kumo to na, nɛ basa nɛ b daa wɔ ndoŋ na kikɛ so. Loŋ koŋwule nɛ baaŋ wora esa kama nɛ e beta dimɛdi be kuwibi ŋko kebuni ŋko nchaŋ.

english_verse: If this is done on the third day and on the seventh day, you will be clean. Then after you take a bath and wash your clothes, you can worship that evening.

english_verse: If you are unclean and refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes, you will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean, and you will no longer belong to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Esa kama nɛ e wora eyurpi daŋkare be ekpa so nseŋ kini kefɔr mbe kumu so daŋkare be ekpa so wora eyurpi n jija Enyɛnpe be wajɛbu na nna nsaa maaŋ naŋ ti Ebɔrɛ be basa so.

english_verse: These laws will never change. The man who sprinkled the water and the ashes on you when you were unclean must also wash his clothes. And whoever touches this water is unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Mbra ere maaŋ chɛrga kikɛ. Ekama nɛ e bee ŋmenyaŋ nchu na a fɔr basa so daŋkare be ekpa so gba, daga e fɔr mbe epiŋi. Ekama nɛ e beta nchu na malɛ beeŋ wora eyurpi daŋkare be ekpa so n ya fo kaaseso.

english_verse: When you are unclean, everything you touch becomes unclean, and anyone who touches you will be unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Kusɔ kama nɛ esa nɛ e wora eyurpi daŋkare be ekpa so beta gba wora eyurpi. Esa kama nɛ mo alɛ beta kumo beeŋ wora eyurpi n ya fo kaaseso.

english_verse: The people of Israel arrived at the Zin Desert during the first month and set up camp near the town of Kadesh. It was there that Miriam died and was buried.

english_verse: and complained, “Moses, we'd be better off if we had died along with the others in front of the Lord's sacred tent.

translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn lar basa na kutɔ n ya gbir wajɛbu na be kabuna a kule Ebɔrɛ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be kemaŋkura lar bumo so.

translation_verse: “Ta kekpabi nɛ k wɔ ŋkre be deka na be anishito na, nɛ fo nɛ Ɛɛrɔn e tre basa na kikɛ n shɛr, nɛ fo yili bumo be anishito m malga n sa kefalta na nɛ nchu e shi kumo to n lar eleŋso nɛ basa na nɛ bumo be asɔbɔya kikɛ e nya nchu n nu.”

english_verse: Moses obeyed and took his stick from the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis bɛ kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ na so nseŋ ta mbe kekpabi na.

english_verse: He raised his stick in the air and struck the rock two times. At once, water gushed from the rock, and the people and their livestock had water to drink.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Mosis maŋ mbe kekpabi so ŋ ŋmɛa kefalta na ale anyɔ. Epul to nɛ nchu lar kefalta na to eleŋso a wurge nɛ basa na nɛ bumo be asɔbɔya kikɛ nuu.

english_verse: But the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you refused to believe in my power, these people did not respect me. And so, you will not be the ones to lead them into the land I have promised.”
translation_verse: Ama le nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ daŋ kaŋɛ Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn: “Ŋkpal men ka maŋ yirda ma nseŋ kini keshin nɛ Israɛlebi na pin ma eleŋ so, men maaŋ juŋkpar bumo n yɔ kasawule nɛ n nase kɔnɔ fanɛ meeŋ sa bumo na so.”

english_verse: The Israelites had complained against the Lord, and he had shown them his holy power by giving them water to drink. So they named the place Meribah, which means “Complaining.” Israel Isn't Allowed To Go through Edom
translation_verse: Israɛlebi na daŋ fubel m bile asheŋ nna m malga ŋ gbiti Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na, nɛ e ŋini bumo mbe kecheembiya be eleŋ nseŋ sa bumo nchu nɛ b nuu nseŋ nase kakpa na be ketre Mɛriba. Mɛriba be kifito e la kefubel m bile asheŋ.

english_verse: Moses sent messengers from Israel's camp near Kadesh with this message for the king of Edom: We are Israelites, your own relatives, and we're sure you have heard the terrible things that have happened to us.

english_verse: Our ancestors settled in Egypt and lived there a long time. But later the Egyptians were cruel to us,
translation_verse: nɛ kananɛ an nananyɛnana daŋ yɔ Ijipt be kasawule so nɛ kananɛ an chena ndoŋ n chɛr nɛ Ijiptebi na daŋ tɔrɔ anyi ga.

english_verse: and when we begged our Lord for help, he answered our prayer and brought us out of that land. Now we are camped at the border of your territory, near the town of Kadesh.
translation_verse: Nɛ an shu ŋ ŋini Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ e nu anyi be kushu nseŋ shuŋi malaika nɛ e ba lara anyi ashi Ijipt be kasawule so. Naniere an fo kade nɛ baa tre Kadɛsh nɛ k wɔ fo kasawule be egbaŋ be ekar na.

english_verse: Please let us go through your country. We won't go near your fields or vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. We will stay on the main road until we leave your territory.
translation_verse: Amoso jande, sa anyi ekpa nɛ an bɔla fo kasawule so n choŋ. Anyi maaŋ bɔla men be ndɔana ŋko men be asɔrso nɛ baa tre greep na be adɔ to. Anyi alɛ maaŋ nuu menyi be atirbu to be nchu. Anyeeŋ baŋ bɔla kegbembi so nna n nite a yɔ hale n ya baŋ menyi be kasawule so.”

english_verse: But the king of Edom answered, “No, I won't let you go through our country! And if you try, we will attack you.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Edɔm be ewura na kaŋɛ le: “M maaŋ shin nɛ men bɔla ma efuli so n choŋ! Men baŋ bɔla ndoŋ anyeeŋ lar ŋ kɔ menyi kena.”

english_verse: Moses sent back this message: “We promise to stay on the main road, and if any of us or our livestock drink your water, we will pay for it. We just want to pass through.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Israɛlebi na kaŋɛ le: “Anyeeŋ baa nite kegbembi so a yɔ. Nɛ anyi be ekama ŋko kusɔbɔya kaŋ nuu menyi be nchu, anyeeŋ ka kumo be kukɔ. An baa sha nɛ an bɔla ndoŋ nna n choŋ nawule.”

english_verse: But the king insisted, “You can't go through our land!” Then Edom sent out its strongest troops
translation_verse: Nɛ Edɔmebi na malɛ naŋ kaŋɛ le: “Anyi maaŋ shuli!” Kede be kaman nɛ b keta bumo be benapo lempo n lar nɛ b ya kɔ Israɛlebi na kena.

translation_verse: Nɛ Israɛlebi na kikɛ lar Kadɛsh n ya fo kebeegboŋ nɛ baa tre Hɔɔr

translation_verse: Israɛlebi na ka lar kebeegboŋ nɛ baa tre Hɔɔr na ase n sɔ Teku peper na be kaba so a kra Edɔm be efuli a yɔ nɛ b nyiti ŋ gben,

translation_verse: Nɛ basa na ba Mosis kutɔ m ba kaŋɛ le: “Ŋkpal an ka malga ŋ gbiti fo nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ so, an wora kulubi, amoso kule Ebɔrɛ nɛ e ju awɔ ere nfe naniere.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis kule Ebɔrɛ n sa bumo.

english_verse: Moses obeyed the Lord. And all of those who looked at the bronze snake lived, even though they had been bitten by the poisonous snakes. Israel's Journey to Moab
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mosis ta danyaŋ n lɔŋɛ kuwɔ n shiga kedibi tenteŋ so. Ekama malɛ nɛ kuwɔ baŋ duŋ nɛ e maŋ kumu so ŋ keni kumo, bee nya alenfia nna. Israɛlebi be keyɔ Mowab be asheŋ

english_verse: A song in The Book of the Lord's Battles mentions the town of Waheb with its creeks in the territory of Suphah. It also mentions the Arnon River,

translation_verse: nseŋ yili Bamɔf n yɔ Mowabebi be efuli so be kepla nɛ k gbelge to a yɔ kebeegboŋ nɛ baa tre Pisga nɛ k shoŋi keshishɛrsawule na. Israɛlebi ka kɔ m pɔɔ Ewura Sihɔn nɛ Ewura Ɔg so be asheŋ

english_verse: The Israelites sent this message to King Sihon of the Amorites:
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Israɛlebi shuŋi mbɔ Sihɔn nɛ e la Amɔriebi be ewura na kutɔ fanɛ b ya kaŋɛ mo le:

english_verse: Please let us pass through your territory. We promise to stay away from your fields and vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. As long as we're in your land, we'll stay on the main road.
translation_verse: “Men shin nɛ an bɔla men be kasawule ere so n choŋ. Anyi nɛ an be ana maaŋ yige ekpa n ya luri men be ndɔana nɛ men be asɔrso nɛ baa tre greep na be ndibi be adɔana to. Anyi alɛ maaŋ nuu menyi be atirbuana be nchu. Anyeeŋ baŋ bɔla kegbembi nna a yɔ hale nɛ an ya baŋ menyi be kasawule so.”

english_verse: But Sihon refused to let Israel travel through his land. Instead, he called together his entire army and marched into the desert to attack Israel near the town of Jahaz.
translation_verse: Ama Sihɔn daa maŋ shuli fanɛ Israɛlebi na e bɔla mbe kasawule so n choŋ. E daŋ chala mbe benapo kikɛ nna n yɔ kade nɛ baa tre Jahaaz nɛ k wɔ keshishɛrsawule so na n ya kɔ Israɛlebi na kena.

english_verse: Israel defeated them and took over the Amorite territory from the Arnon River gorge in the south to the Jabbok River gorge in the north. Beyond the Jabbok was the territory of the Ammonites, who were much stronger than Israel.
translation_verse: Israɛlebi na daŋ mɔ bumo doŋana na kena na to ga nseŋ sɔ bumo be kasawule nɛ k wɔ yili Aanɔn be Lɔr nɛ k wɔ kelargato be kaseto be kaba so na n ya fo Jabɔk be lɔr nɛ k wɔ kelargato be esoso. Jabɔk be lɔr na e daa la Amɔriebi nɛ Ammɔnebi na be nsawule be egbaŋ to. Ammɔnebi na bre daŋ pɔr egbal ŋ kulti bumo be nde nna.

english_verse: The Israelites settled in the Amorite towns, including the capital city of Heshbon with its surrounding villages.
translation_verse: Israɛlebi na daŋ sɔ Amɔriebi na be nde kikɛ nna n ta bumo be kadegboŋ nɛ baa tre Hishbɔn nɛ ndewurbi nɛ a kulti kumo na n ti so.

english_verse: That's why the Amorites had written this poem about Heshbon: Come and rebuild Heshbon, King Sihon's capital city!
translation_verse: Amoso nɛ beshɛbompo bee boŋ kashɛ fanɛ: “Men ba Hishbɔn nɛ k la Sihɔn be kadegboŋ na to! Anyee sha kelɔnɛ m pɔr kumo nna n yili nɛnɛ.

english_verse: We completely defeated Moab. The towns of Heshbon and Dibon, of Nophah and Medeba are ruined and gone.
translation_verse: An pɔɔ Mowabebi kikɛ so. An yili Hishbɔn m mur bumo be nde kikɛ n ya fo Dibɔn nseŋ yili Nashim m mur amo n ya fo Noofa nɛ k mata Mɛdiba na.”

english_verse: After the Israelites had settled in the Amorite territory,
translation_verse: Israɛlebi na ka sɔ Amɔriebi be kasawule n chena so na,

english_verse: Moses sent some men to explore the town of Jazer. Later, the Israelites captured the villages surrounding it and forced out the Amorites who lived there. Israel Defeats King Og of Bashan (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: nɛ Mosis shuŋi benyɛn ko fanɛ b ya keni kananɛ baaŋ wora ŋ kɔ kade nɛ baa tre Jeeza na kena. Kumo be kaman nɛ Israɛlebi na ya kɔ kade na kena n sɔ kumo nɛ ndewurbi nɛ a kulti kumo na, nseŋ ju Amɔriebi nɛ b wɔ ndoŋ na.

english_verse: The Israelites headed toward the region of Bashan, where King Og ruled, and he led his entire army to Edrei to meet Israel in battle.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Israɛlebi na naŋ kilgi n sɔ Bashan be kaba so, nɛ Bashan be ewura Ɔg keta mbe benapo nɛ e ya kɔ bumo kena ashi Edrei.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Don't be afraid of Og. I will help you defeat him and his army, just as you did King Sihon who ruled in Heshbon. Og's territory will be yours.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Mosis le: “Sa maa ŋana Ɔg nɛ mbe benapo. Meeŋ sa fo eleŋ nɛ fo kɔ m pɔɔ so bumo so fanɛ kananɛ fo wora Hishbɔn be ewura Sihɔn na. Ewura Ɔg be kasawule beeŋ ki menyeya.”

english_verse: So the Israelites wiped out Og, his family, and his entire army—there were no survivors. Then Israel took over the land of Bashan.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Israɛlebi na mɔ ewura Ɔg nɛ mbe mbinyɛnsobi nɛ mbe basa kikɛ nseŋ sɔ mbe kasawule na n chena so. Mbe esa kikɛ daa maŋ ji efute.

english_verse: Israel moved from there to the hills of Moab, where they camped across the Jordan River from the town of Jericho. King Balak of Moab Hires Balaam To Curse Israel
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Israɛlebi naŋ ya wora bumo be keeyi to Mowab be keplasawule so ashi Jɔɔdan be lɔr na be epeŋilarkpa be kaba so, nɛ Jɛriko be kadegboŋ na wɔ kumo be kaba ndoŋ.

english_verse: They said to the Midianite leaders, “That huge mob of Israelites will wipe out everything in sight, like a bull eating grass in a field.” So King Balak
translation_verse: Nɛ Mowabebi na kaŋɛ Midianebi be bejuŋkparpo na le: “Jimaŋ ere beeŋ ba mur anyi be kusɔ kama fanɛ kananɛ gbolu bee we afitiri adɛdɛ so ashi kupuŋ to na.” Amoso Ewura Balak

english_verse: sent a message to Balaam son of Beor who lived among his relatives in the town of Pethor near the Euphrates River. It said: I need your help. A large group of people has come here from Egypt and settled near my territory.
translation_verse: daŋ kpal loŋ so nna, n shuŋi mbɔ fanɛ b ta le be kubɔya n ya sa Biyɔɔ pibinyɛn Balaam nɛ e wɔ Pɛɛtɔ nɛ k mata lɔrgboŋ nɛ baa tre Yufreetes nɛ k wɔ Amawu be kasawule so na. “Mee sha nɛ fo pin fanɛ efuli lelemu be basa shi Ijipt be efuli so m ba. Bumo alɛ bee salga to nna a sɔ kaplɛkama nsaa sha kesɔ anyi be kasawule kikɛ.

english_verse: They are too powerful for us to defeat, so would you come and place a curse on them? Maybe then we can run them off. I know that anyone you bless will be successful, but anyone you curse will fail.
translation_verse: B kɔ eleŋ a chɔ anyi ga, amoso jande, ba sho bumo kɔnɔ n sa ma. Ashere loŋ e naaŋ shin nɛ an tiŋ m pɔɔ bumo so nseŋ ju bumo ashi anyi be kasawule ere so. M baa nyi geeŋ fanɛ fo baŋ nɛfa basa, baa nya nɛfa nna, fo naŋ sho basa kɔnɔ, kɔnɔsho bee pɛ bumo nna.”

english_verse: The leaders of Moab and Midian left and took along money to pay Balaam. When they got to his house, they gave him Balak's message.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mowabebi nɛ Midianebi be bejuŋkparpoana na ta amansherbi nɛ Ewura Balak be kubɔya na n yɔ nɛ b ya sa Balaam nɛ e ba shuŋ n sa bumo.

english_verse: “Spend the night here,” Balaam replied, “and tomorrow I will tell you the Lord's answer.” So the officials stayed at his house.
translation_verse: Nɛ Balaam kaŋɛ bumo le: “Men dese nɛ kare e chɛ nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ menyi kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ ma.” Amoso bejuŋkparpoana na daŋ dese Balaam kutɔ nna ŋklade.

english_verse: During the night, God asked Balaam, “Who are these people at your house?”
translation_verse: Loŋ be kanyɛ na nɛ Ebɔrɛ ba bishi Balaam le: “Basa mo malɛ e wɔ fo kutɔ ere?”

english_verse: “They are messengers from King Balak of Moab,” Balaam answered. “He sent them
translation_verse: Nɛ e kaŋɛ le: “Mowab be Ewura Balak e shuŋi bumo fanɛ b ba kaŋɛ ma

english_verse: to ask me to go to Moab and put a curse on the people who have come there from Egypt. They have settled everywhere around him, and he wants to run them off.”
translation_verse: fanɛ basa ko e shi Ijipt be kasawule so m ba sɔ bumo be kasawule so kikɛ n chena. Amoso e bee sha nna fanɛ m ba sho bumo kɔnɔ n sa mo nɛ e tiŋ ŋ kɔ m pɔɔ so bumo so n ju bumo n lar mbe kasawule so.”

english_verse: But God replied, “Don't go with Balak's messengers. I have blessed those people who have come from Egypt, so don't curse them.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Balaam le: “Sa maŋ kaŋ tu basa ere n yɔ, fo alɛ maŋ kraa sho Israɛlebi na kɔnɔ, ŋkpal manɛ so ma nɛfa wɔ bumo so nna.”

english_verse: The next morning, Balaam said to Balak's officials, “Go on back home. The Lord says I cannot go with you.”
translation_verse: Kare ka chɛ kachipurso, nɛ Balaam koso n ya kaŋɛ Ewura Balak be mbɔ le: “Men bɛta n yɔ epe, ŋkpal manɛ so, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ maŋ sa ma ekpa fanɛ n tu menyi n yɔ.”

english_verse: The officials left and told Balak that Balaam refused to come.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ mbɔ na bɛta n ya kaŋɛ Ewura Balak fanɛ Balaam kini kebɛ bumo so m ba.

english_verse: Then Balak sent a larger group of officials, who were even more important than the first ones.
translation_verse: Nɛ Ewura Balak naŋ shuŋi benimu nɛ b shi nsaa kɔ bunyaŋ a chɔ sososo be bumo nɛ e shuŋi na.

english_verse: They went to Balaam and told him that Balak had said, “Balaam, if you come to Moab,
translation_verse: Nɛ bumo alɛ ta Ewura Balak be kubɔya n ya kaŋɛ Balaam le: “Ewura Balak yɛ fo sa maŋ shin nɛ kusɔ kama e kuŋ fo keba anyi kutɔ akpa!

english_verse: I'll pay you very well and do whatever you ask. Just come and place a curse on these people.”
translation_verse: E yɛ e beeŋ ka fo kukɔ nseŋ naŋ sa fo kusɔ kama nɛ fee sha n ti so. Amoso jande, ba sho basa na kɔnɔ.”

english_verse: Balaam answered, “Even if Balak offered me a palace full of silver or gold, I wouldn't do anything to disobey the Lord my God.
translation_verse: Ama le nɛ Balaam daŋ kaŋɛ bumo: “Hale Ewura Balak ta ewurkpa be shuwa nɛ gbiti kikɛ gba n sa ma, maaŋ kini kenu n sa Enyɛnpe ma Ebɔrɛ na ekpa kama so.

english_verse: You are welcome to spend the night here, just as the others did. I will find out if the Lord has something else to say about this.”
translation_verse: Menyi alɛ gba beeŋ tiŋ n dese nfe kanyɛ ere fanɛ kananɛ bumo na wora na, nɛ ŋ keni ŋko Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kɔ kusɔ pɔtɛ ko nɛ e kaŋɛ a yɔ kumo be kaplɛa so a!”

english_verse: That night, God said, “Balaam, I'll let you go to Moab with Balak's messengers, but do only what I say.”
translation_verse: Kumo be kanyɛso nɛ Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Balaam le: “Meeŋ shin nɛ fo tu Ewura Balak be mbɔ na n yɔ Mowab, ama ya wora kusɔ kama nɛ meeŋ kaŋɛ fo.”

english_verse: So Balaam got up the next morning and saddled his donkey, then left with the Moabite officials. Balaam and His Donkey Meet an Angel
translation_verse: Kumo be ŋklade kachipurso, nɛ Balaam ta gaare n deŋi mbe kurma so nɛ mo nɛ benimuana na yɔ. Balaam be kurma be asheŋ

english_verse: Balaam was riding his donkey to Moab, and two of his servants were with him. But God was angry that Balaam had gone, so one of the Lord's angels stood in the road to stop him.
translation_verse: Balaam daŋ dii mbe kurma nna nɛ mbe nyɛrbi anyɔ ko tu mo a yɔ Mowab, nɛ Ebɔrɛ nya agbo ŋkpal Balaam ka daŋ tu basa na a yɔ so nseŋ shin nɛ mbe malaika ya kuŋ mo akpa.

english_verse: When Balaam's donkey saw the angel standing there with a sword, it walked off the road and into an open field. Balaam had to beat the donkey to get it back on the road.
translation_verse: Balaam be kurma na ka wu malaika ka keta tokobi a yil ekpa na to, nɛ k gbɛ n luri adɔ to. Nɛ Balaam bri kumo nɛ k bɛta m ba ekpa to.

english_verse: Then the angel stood between two vineyards, in a narrow path with a stone wall on each side.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ malaika na naaŋ ya yili ekpa mɔebi, nɛ k dese asɔrso nɛ baa tre greep na be adɔana anyɔ nɛ b pɔr ajembu be egbal ŋ kulti na be nferinto.

english_verse: When the donkey saw the angel, it walked so close to one of the walls that Balaam's foot scraped against the wall. Balaam beat the donkey again.
translation_verse: Kurma na ka wu malaika na, nɛ k gbɛ n ya mata egbal na nɛ Balaam be keyadra nyɛa egbal na. Ndoŋ nna nɛ Balaam naŋ bri kumo.

english_verse: The angel moved once more and stood in a spot so narrow that there was no room for the donkey to go around.
translation_verse: Nɛ malaika na naŋ firgi n yɔ anishito n ya yili ekpa na be kakpa mɔebi nɛ kurma na maaŋ nya kakpa ŋ gbɛ n choŋ.

english_verse: So it just lay down. Balaam lost his temper, then picked up a stick and whacked the donkey.
translation_verse: Kurma na ka naŋ wu malaika na nɛ k kilgi n dese. Nɛ agbo pɛ Balaam ga nɛ e ta mbe kekpabi a bri kumo.

english_verse: When that happened, the Lord told the donkey to speak, and it asked Balaam, “What have I done that made you beat me three times?”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ shin nɛ kurma na malga Balaam kutɔ ŋ kaŋɛ le: “Manɛ nɛ n wora fo nɛ fo bri ma ale asa kikɛ?”

english_verse: “You made me look stupid!” Balaam answered. “If I had a sword, I'd kill you here and now!”
translation_verse: Nɛ Balaam kaŋɛ: “Ŋkpal fo ka shin nɛ ŋ ki ewulpo na so, n daa kɔ tokobi gba nna, dafanɛ meeŋ mɔ fo.”

english_verse: “But you're my owner,” answered the donkey, “and you've ridden me many times. Have I ever done anything like this before?” “No,” Balaam admitted.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ kurma na kaŋɛ mo le: “Manɛ ma nɛ fee dii nfɛ damta ere kikɛ na a? Fo daŋ wu ŋ ka wora fo le kikɛ a?” Nɛ Balaam kaŋɛ: “M-m.”

english_verse: Just then, the Lord let Balaam see the angel standing in the road, holding a sword, and Balaam bowed down.
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ bugi Balaam be anishi nɛ e wu malaika na ka keta tokobi a yil ekpa na to. Ndoŋ nna nɛ Balaam kurgi kumu n yuu kasawule.

english_verse: The angel said, “You had no right to treat your donkey like that! I was the one who blocked your way, because I don't think you should go to Moab.
translation_verse: Nɛ malaika na kaŋɛ Balaam le: “Manɛ nna nɛ fo bri fo kurma ale asa kikɛ? M ba nna nɛ m ba kuŋ fo ekpa nɛ fo maaŋ yɔ fo enite ere to.

english_verse: If your donkey had not seen me and stopped those three times, I would have killed you and let the donkey live.”
translation_verse: Fo kurma na wu ma nna nseŋ gbɛ ma ale asa kikɛ. Kurma na daa maŋ gbɛ ma nna, dafanɛ m mɔ fo n yige kumo ere.”

english_verse: Balaam replied, “I was wrong. I didn't know you were trying to stop me. If you don't think I should go, I'll return home at once.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Balaam kaŋɛ le: “N wora kulubi. N daa maŋ nyi fanɛ fo yil ekpa na to nna a kuŋ ma akpa, ama nɛ fo wu fanɛ k maŋ daga ŋ ka yɔ ndoŋ bre, meeŋ bɛta n yɔ epe.”

english_verse: “It's all right for you to go,” the Lord's angel answered. “But you must say only what I tell you.” So Balaam went on with Balak's officials. King Balak Meets Balaam
translation_verse: Nɛ malaika na kaŋɛ: “Fo nɛ Ewura Balak be benimuana ere e baa yɔ, ama ya malga kusɔ nɛ meeŋ kaŋɛ fo na nawule.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ Balaam tu bumo n yɔ. Ewura Balak ka wora Balaam ansaŋ nɛ keba be asheŋ

english_verse: When Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went to meet him at the town of Ir on the Arnon River, which is the northern border of Moab.
translation_verse: Ewura Balak ka nu fanɛ Balaam bee ba, nɛ e yɔ nɛ e ya shɛr mo to ashi kade nɛ baa tre Ar nɛ k wɔ Aanɔn be lɔr be ekarso ashi Mowab be kasawule be ekarso na.

english_verse: Balak asked, “Why didn't you come when I invited you the first time? Did you think I wasn't going to pay you?”
translation_verse: Nseŋ kaŋɛ mo le: “Manɛ nna nɛ n shuŋi n tre fo sososo na nɛ fo kini keba? Ŋko fee fɛ fanɛ maaŋ tiŋ ŋ ka fo nɛnɛ nna a?”

english_verse: “I'm here now,” Balaam answered. “But I will say only what God tells me to say.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Balaam kaŋɛ le: “To m ba nna na! Ama maŋ kɔ eleŋ nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ kusɔ nɛ mee sha. Kusɔ nɛ Ebɔrɛ baŋ kaŋɛ nɛ mee malga.”

english_verse: They left and went to the town of Kiriath-Huzoth,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Balaam nɛ Ewura Balak kikɛ yɔ Kiriaf Huzɔɔf.

english_verse: where Balak sacrificed cattle and sheep and gave some of the meat to Balaam and the officials who were with him.
translation_verse: Nɛ Ewura Balak ya mɔ ana nɛ mbolpɔ nseŋ ta amo be eblaŋ na be ako n sa Balaam nɛ benimu nɛ b wɔ mo kutɔ na. Balaam be sososo be kewuŋkaŋɛ be asheŋ

english_verse: The next morning, Balak took Balaam to the town of Bamoth-Baal. From there, Balaam could see some of the Israelites.
translation_verse: Ŋklade kachipurso nɛ Ewura Balak keta Balaam n dii n yɔ Bamɔf Baal, kakpa nɛ Balaam beeŋ tiŋ n wu Israɛlebi na be beko.

english_verse: Balaam said to Balak, “Build seven altars here, then bring seven bulls and seven rams.”
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Balaam kaŋɛ Ewura Balak le: “Shin nɛ b pɔr ebɔrɛsure ashunu nfe n sa ma nseŋ bar ma egbolu ashunu nɛ ekpakpa ashunu.”

english_verse: After Balak had done this, they sacrificed a bull and a ram on each altar.
translation_verse: Nɛ Ewura Balak shin nɛ b wora loŋ nɛ mo nɛ Balaam ta gbolu koŋwule nɛ kpakpa koŋwule n lara sarga bɔrɛsure na be kekama so.

english_verse: Then Balaam said, “Wait here beside your offerings, and I'll go somewhere to be alone. Maybe the Lord will appear to me. If he does, I will tell you everything he says.” And he left.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Balaam kaŋɛ Ewura Balak le: “Baa yil fo sarga ere ase nɛ n yɔ anishito n ya keni, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ beeŋ ba ma kutɔ a? Saŋɛ na so meeŋ kaŋɛ fo kusɔ kama nɛ e lara ŋ ŋini ma, nseŋ dii n yɔ kebee na be kakpa nɛ ndibi nɛ afitiri maŋ wɔ na.”

english_verse: When God appeared to him, Balaam said, “I have built seven altars and have sacrificed a bull and a ram on each one.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nɛ Ebɔrɛ ba tu mo, nɛ Balaam kaŋɛ: “Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, m pɔr ebɔrɛsure ashunu nseŋ ta gbolu nɛ kpakpa n lara sarga amo be kekama so.”

english_verse: The Lord gave Balaam a message, then sent him back to tell Balak.
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ta kubɔya n sa Balaam fanɛ e ya sa Ewura Balak.

english_verse: When Balaam returned, he found Balak and his officials standing beside the offerings.
translation_verse: Nɛ Balaam bɛta n ya tu Ewura Balak nɛ mo nɛ Mowab be benimu yil mbe esarga na ase.

english_verse: Balaam said: “King Balak of Moab brought me from the hills of Syria to curse Israel and announce its doom.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Balaam kaŋɛ: “Mowab be ewura Balak e bar ma ashi Siriya nɛ k wɔ abee be efuli so na fanɛ m ba sho Israɛlebi kɔnɔ n shin nɛ b mur.

english_verse: But I can't go against God! He did not curse or condemn Israel. *
translation_verse: Ama nuso nɛ meeŋ tiŋ n sho basa nɛ Ebɔrɛ nɛfa kɔnɔ, ŋko n shin nɛ basa nɛ Ebɔrɛ maŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ b mur, e mur?

english_verse: “From the mountain peaks, I look down and see Israel, the obedient people of God.
translation_verse: N yili kebee be esoso n wu bumo. N wɔ kebee so a keni bumo. B la basa nɛ b kɔr bekama to nna. Basa nɛ Ebɔrɛ nɛfa.

english_verse: They are living alone in peace. And though they are many, they don't bother the other nations. “I hope to obey God for as long as I live and to die in such peace.”
translation_verse: Wanɛ e naŋ tiŋ ŋ karga Israɛlebi nɛ b shi m baŋ so ere? Shin nɛ ma lalaloge be nchɛ e baa du fanɛ Ebɔrɛ be basa peya. Shin nɛ n wu fanɛ esa niŋiso.”

english_verse: Balak said, “What are you doing? I asked you to come and place a curse on my enemies. But you have blessed them instead!”
translation_verse: Nɛ Ewura Balak kaŋɛ Balaam le: “Manɛ nɛ fee wora loŋ? M bar fo nna nɛ fo ba sho n doŋana kɔnɔ, nɛ fo ba kilgi a nɛfa bumo a!”

english_verse: Balaam answered, “I can say only what the Lord tells me.” Balaam's Second Message
translation_verse: Nɛ Balaam kaŋɛ: “Kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ fanɛ ŋ kaŋɛ nɛ meeŋ kaŋɛ.” Balaam be kubɔya nyɔsopo be asheŋ

english_verse: Balak said to Balaam, “Let's go somewhere else. Maybe if you see a smaller part of the Israelites, you will be able to curse them for me.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Ewura Balak kaŋɛ mo: “Shin nɛ an yɔ kaboŋ pɔtɛ nɛ fo ya wu Israɛlebi na be gbrɛbi nɛ b maŋ fo bumo nɛ fo wu na so, saŋɛ na so feeŋ sho bumo kɔnɔ n sa ma.”

english_verse: So he took Balaam to a field on top of Mount Pisgah where lookouts were stationed. Then he built seven altars there and sacrificed a bull and a ram on each one.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ e keta Balaam n yɔ Zɔfim be ndɔ to be kebeegboŋ nɛ baa tre Pisga na be esoso n ya pɔr ebɔrɛsure ashunu ndoŋ gba, nseŋ mɔ gbolu nɛ kpakpa amo be kekama so n lara sarga.

english_verse: “Wait here beside your offerings,” Balaam said. “The Lord will appear to me over there.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Balaam kaŋɛ Ewura Balak le: “Baa yil fo sarga ere be kakpa nɛ n yɔ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kutɔ m ba.”

translation_verse: Nɛ Balaam kaŋɛ le: “M maŋ kaŋɛ fo fanɛ kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ nɛ mee wora a?” Balaam be kewuŋkaŋɛ sasopo be asheŋ

english_verse: Balaam was sure that the Lord would tell him to bless Israel again. So he did not use any magic to find out what the Lord wanted him to do, as he had the first two times. Instead, he looked out toward the desert
translation_verse: Ŋkpal Balaam ka tea nyi fanɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ bee sha fanɛ e nɛfa Israɛlebi na so, e daa maŋ wora ŋkilgisheŋ kikɛ fanɛ kananɛ e chɛr a wora saŋko saŋko na. E daŋ kilgi mbe anishi nna n shoŋi keshishɛrsawule na be kaba so

english_verse: and saw the tribes of Israel camped below. Just then, God's Spirit took control of him,
translation_verse: nseŋ wu Israɛlebi na ka wora bumo be nyi to n chena eyiri yiri be ntuŋ so. Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be kiyoyu gbelge mo so,

translation_verse: Baaŋ nya mbɔrɛchu damta nseŋ duu bumo be adɔjibi kasawule nɛ k kɔ kayul nɛnɛ so. Bumo be ewura be kuwurji beeŋ baa chɔ Amalɛk be ewura Agag peya. Mbe kuwura beeŋ ji eleŋ ga nɛ mbe ketre e dii.

translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ e lara bumo ashi Ijipt be kasawule so. B kɔ eleŋ nna fanɛ kupuntona na, nsaa kɔ a pɔɔ bumo doŋana so. Baaŋ to bumo doŋana ata nɛ bumo be awibi kikɛ e buri to.

translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ewura Balak nya agbo alegaiso n wɔtɔ Balaam nseŋ a chicha ŋ kaŋɛ le: “N tre fo nna fanɛ fo ba sho n doŋana kɔnɔ, nɛ fo kini nseŋ nɛfa bumo ale asa kikɛ.

translation_verse: Lar nfe naniere kikɛ n yɔ epe! N daŋ nase kɔnɔ nna fanɛ meeŋ ka fo kukɔ nɛnɛ ama Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kuŋ kumo be loŋ be ekpa na.”

english_verse: that even if you offered me a palace full of silver or gold, I would still obey the Lord. And I explained that I would say only what he told me.
translation_verse: hale nɛ fo ta fo ewurkpa be shuwa nɛ gbiti kikɛ gba ŋ kɛ ma, m maaŋ kini kenu n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kikɛ. Kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ, nɛ meeŋ wora.” Balaam be lalaloge be kewuŋkaŋɛ be asheŋ

english_verse: So I'm going back home, but I'm leaving you with a warning about what the Israelites will someday do to your nation.” Balaam's Fourth Message
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Balaam kaŋɛ Ewura Balak le: “Naniere bre mee bɛta a yɔ epe nna na, ama kefiɛso nɛ ŋ kɔ a sa fo a laŋɛ kusɔ nɛ Israɛlebi beeŋ wora menyi kachako so nde.”

translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ e kaŋɛ le: “Biyɔɔ pibinyɛn Balaam be kubɔya nde, emo nɛ e bee wu nɛnɛ na be mmalga nde.

english_verse: My knowledge comes from God Most High, the Lord All-Powerful. I bowed down to him and saw a vision of Israel.
translation_verse: Mo e naa nu Ebɔrɛ be mmalga nsaa pin amo to; Mo e kɔ nfɛra nɛ k shi Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na kutɔ, nsaa nya kewuŋkaŋɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na kutɔ, nsaa tɔr kasawule a bunyaŋ mo na.

english_verse: “What I saw in my vision hasn't happened yet. But someday, a king of Israel will appear like a star. He will wipe out you Moabites and destroy those tribes who live in the desert.
translation_verse: N wu fanɛ kachako so, Ewura ko beeŋ lar Israɛl be efuli so a du fanɛ kechɛkpabi nɛ k fulto parr na. E beeŋ lar fanɛ kuwurkpabi ashi Israɛl. E beeŋ mur Mowabebi kikɛ, nseŋ mur Sɛt be kaman to ebi cheche.

english_verse: “And I saw this vision about the Amalekites: Their nation is now great, but it will someday disappear forever.
translation_verse: Balaam ka ku bɔrɛdare n wu Amalɛkebi na, nɛ e kaŋɛ le: “Amalɛk e daa la efuliana ere be kelempo, ama saŋko k beeŋ mur cheche.”

english_verse: Later, Moses and the people were at the sacred tent, crying, when one of the Israelite men brought a Midianite woman to meet his family.
translation_verse: Mosis nɛ Israɛlebi na kikɛ ka shɛr Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be wajɛbu na ase a shu na, nɛ Israɛlebi na be eko keta Midian be eche m bɔla bumo be anishito n yɔ mbe wajɛbu to.

translation_verse: Eliaza pibinyɛn Finihas nɛ e la bɔrɛmatapo Ɛɛrɔn mo nanabi na ka wu bumo, nɛ e lar nshɛr na to n ya ta mbe kekpa,

translation_verse: m bɛ Israɛl be kanyɛn na nɛ eche na so n yɔ mbe wajɛbu to n ya da mo nɛ eche na kikɛ m mata abar. Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ shin nɛ aleblawu nɛ k bee tɔrɔ Israɛlebi na kikɛ kuu.

translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Mosis le:

translation_verse: “Men karga Israɛlebi nɛ b fo nfɛ adunyɔ ŋko m baŋ so na kanaŋ kanaŋ so saŋɛ na so menyeeŋ pin bumo nɛ b fo kena to be keyɔ.”

translation_verse: Kachako nɛ mbe mbichesobi na ya yili Mosis nɛ bɔrɛmatapo Eliaza nɛ bejuŋkparpoana na nɛ kade na to ebi kikɛ be anishito ashi Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be wajɛbu na be kabuna to ŋ kaŋɛ le:

translation_verse: “An tuto daŋ wu keshishɛrsawule na so nna. Mo alɛ daŋ maŋ wu nna ŋkpal e ka bɛ Koora so nseŋ kini kebɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ so so. Mo gbagba be kulubi e daŋ mɔ mo. Mo alɛ daŋ maŋ kurge mbinyɛnsobi.
