english_verse: Saul killed two of his oxen, cut them up in pieces, and gave the pieces to the messengers. He told them to show the pieces to everyone in Israel and say, “Saul and Samuel are getting an army together. Come and join them. If you don't, this is what will happen to your oxen!” The Lord made the people of Israel terribly afraid. So all the men came together
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Sɔɔl mɔ ana dɔso na be anyɔ nseŋ kuya bumo to n ta eblaŋ na be eko n shuŋi mbɔ ŋ kaŋɛ bumo fanɛ b ta eblaŋ kuyatoso na n yɔ Israɛl be efuli so kikɛ n ya kpele bumo kusoe ŋ kaŋɛ le: “Esa kama nɛ e baa maŋ bɛ Sɔɔl nɛ Samuɛl so n yɔ kena to, le nɛ amodoŋwura gba be ana beeŋ ki na!” Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ shin nɛ kufu tɔr Israɛl be basa na so ga nɛ bumo kikɛ gbargbar abar so.

english_verse: Saul and his officers sent the messengers back to Jabesh with this promise: “We will rescue you tomorrow afternoon.” The messengers went back to the people at Jabesh and told them that they were going to be rescued. Everyone was encouraged!
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ b kaŋɛ mbɔ nɛ b shi Jabesh na le: “Men kaŋɛ menyi be basa fanɛ pɔɛŋ nɛ kapa e fo echefo anyeeŋ mɔlga bumo.” Jabesh be basa ka nu loŋ be baru na nɛ bumo be ŋgbene fuli bumo ga.

english_verse: So they told the Ammonites, “We will surrender to you tomorrow, and then you can do whatever you want to.”
translation_verse: Nɛ b kaŋɛ Nahaash le: “Echefo anyeeŋ shuli so n sa fo, saŋɛ na so feeŋ wora anyi kusɔ kama nɛ k par fo.”

english_verse: The next day, Saul divided his army into three groups and attacked before daylight. They started killing Ammonites and kept it up until afternoon. A few Ammonites managed to escape, but they were scattered far from each other.
translation_verse: Kumo be ŋklade nɛ Sɔɔl barga mbe basa na to ntuŋ asa nseŋ ta kena n ya tu bumo doŋana Ammɔnebi na ashi bumo be keeyi to kachipurdidi na. Israɛlebi na daŋ mɔ Ammɔnebi na nna hale n ya fo kapaso. Bumo be bumo nɛ b daa maŋ nya m mɔ na malɛ daŋ pesaŋ to nna nɛ bumo be basa anyɔ kama daŋ maŋ naa wɔ abar so.

english_verse: The Israelite soldiers went to Samuel and demanded, “Where are the men who said they didn't want Saul to be king? Bring them to us, and we will put them to death!”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Israɛl be basa na kaŋɛ Samuɛl le: “Nnɛ nɛ basa nɛ b kaŋɛ fanɛ Sɔɔl e sa maa la anyi be ewura na wɔ? Men bar bumo m ba sa anyi nɛ an mɔ!”

english_verse: “No you won't!” Saul told them. “The Lord rescued Israel today, and no one will be put to death.” Saul Is Accepted as King
translation_verse: Ama le nɛ Sɔɔl bre daŋ kaŋɛ: “B maaŋ mɔ esa kama kabre ŋkpal manɛ so le be kachɛ ere nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ta m mɔlga Israɛl be basa.”

english_verse: “Come on!” Samuel said. “Let's go to Gilgal and make an agreement that Saul will continue to be our king.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Samuɛl kaŋɛ bumo le: “Men shin nɛ an kikɛ e yɔ Gilgaal n naŋ ya lɔŋɛ ŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ Sɔɔl e la anyi be ewura.”

english_verse: Everyone went to the place of worship at Gilgal, where they agreed that Saul would be their king. Saul and the people sacrificed animals to ask for the Lord's blessing, and they had a big celebration.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ bumo kikɛ yɔ Gilgaal be kakpa nɛ baa bunyaŋ Ebɔrɛ na n ya yili kumo fanɛ Sɔɔl e la bumo be ewura. Kumo be kaman nɛ b lara kɔnɔkoŋwuleso be esarga ndoŋ nseŋ ji eyur ndoŋ ga.

english_verse: You have seen how I have led you ever since I was a young man. I'm already old. My hair is gray, and my own sons are grown. Now you must see how well your king will lead you.
translation_verse: Men gbagba ere wu kananɛ n juŋkpar menyi saŋɛ so nɛ n la kabrantiɛ na kikɛ. Naniere bre m bel nɛ ma emin malɛ gba fuli. Ma mbinyɛnsobi gba ki benimu. Naniere k daga men ka keni kananɛ menyi be ewura na beeŋ ba keni menyi so.

english_verse: Let me ask this. Have I ever taken anyone's ox or donkey or forced you to give me anything? Have I ever hurt anyone or taken a bribe to give an unfair decision? Answer me so the Lord and his chosen king can hear you. And if I have done any of these things, I will give it all back.
translation_verse: Ma e yili nfe na. Nɛ n wora kusɔ ko ŋ gbɛ to nna, kumo ere men kaŋɛ kulubi nɛ n wora na ashi Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ mbe ewura laraso na kikɛ be anishito. Wanɛ be kena ŋko kurma nɛ n daŋ suge? Wanɛ nɛ n daŋ puni ŋko m mɛaŋ? Wanɛ kutɔ nɛ n daŋ sɔ brɔbu? Nɛ fanɛ n wora asɔ ere be kekama nna, kumo ere meeŋ ka kumo be kukɔ.”

english_verse: Then Samuel told them: The Lord brought your ancestors out of Egypt and chose Moses and Aaron to be your leaders.
translation_verse: Nɛ Samuɛl kaŋɛ bumo le: “Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e lara Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn nseŋ lara men nananyɛnana ashi Ijipt be efuli so dra dra na.

english_verse: Now the Lord will be your judge. So stand here and listen, while I remind you how often the Lord has saved you and your ancestors from your enemies.
translation_verse: Naniere men yili nfe nɛ n nyiŋi menyi asheŋ tumase nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ wora nɛ kananɛ e mɔlga menyi nɛ men nananyɛnana na.

english_verse: After Jacob went to Egypt, your ancestors cried out to the Lord for help, and he sent Moses and Aaron. They brought your ancestors out of Egypt and led them here to settle this land.
translation_verse: Jeekɔb nɛ mbe laŋ to ebi ka daŋ yɔ Ijipt be kasawule so na, Ijiptebi na daa mɛaŋ bumo nna nɛ b shu ŋ ŋini Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ fanɛ e chɛ bumo to. Ndoŋ nna nɛ e shuŋi Mosis nɛ Ɛɛrɔn nɛ b ya lara bumo Ijipt be kasawule so m ba kasawule ere so.

english_verse: But your ancestors forgot the Lord, so he let them be defeated by the Philistines, the king of Moab, and Sisera, the commander of Hazor's army.
translation_verse: Ama ŋkpal Israɛlebi na ka daŋ kini kenu n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ so, E daŋ sa Filistiebi na nɛ Mowab be ewura nɛ Sisɛra nɛ e la Heezɔ be kade be benapo be enimu na ekpa nna nɛ b kɔ m pɔɔ bumo so.”

english_verse: Again your ancestors cried out to the Lord for help. They said, “We have sinned! We stopped worshiping you, our Lord, and started worshiping Baal and Astarte. But now, if you rescue us from our enemies, we will worship you.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ b naŋ shu n tre Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ŋ kaŋɛ le: “An wora kulubi ŋkpal an ka kini keshuŋ fo Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nsaa shuŋ agbir nɛ baa tre Baal nɛ kegbirche Ashtɔrɛf na so so. Mɔlga anyi ashi an doŋana kutɔ saŋɛ na so anyeeŋ shuŋ fo!”

english_verse: The Lord sent Gideon, Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel to rescue you from your enemies, and you didn't have to worry about being attacked.
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ shuŋi Gidiɔn nɛ Barak nɛ Jɛfta nɛ ma, nɛ an mɔlga menyi ashi men doŋana kutɔ nɛ men nya menyi be amu.

english_verse: Then you saw that King Nahash of Ammon was going to attack you. And even though the Lord your God is your king, you told me, “This time it's different. We want a king to rule us!”
translation_verse: Ama men ka wu Nahaash nɛ e la Ammɔn be ewura na ka bee ba nɛ e ba kɔ menyi na, nɛ men kini Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na fanɛ menyi be ewura nsaa fin menyi gbagba be ewura nɛ e beeŋ baa juŋkpar menyi.

english_verse: You asked for a king, and you chose one. Now he stands here where all of you can see him. But it was really the Lord who made him your king.
translation_verse: Ewura nɛ men lara na nde. “Menyi e kule fanɛ menyee sha ewura nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ lara mo n sa menyi.

english_verse: If you and your king want to be followers of the Lord, you must worship him and do what he says. Don't be stubborn!
translation_verse: Nɛ fanɛ menyi nɛ men be ewura bee bunyaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nna nsaa shuŋ mo a nu a sa mo nsaa bɛ mbe mmalga naseso so bre, asheŋ beeŋ nyalɛ n sa menyi.

english_verse: Just stand here and watch the Lord show his mighty power.
translation_verse: Amoso men baa yil to kakpa nseŋ keni kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be eleŋ beeŋ wora.

english_verse: Isn't this the dry season? I'm going to ask the Lord to send a thunderstorm. When you see it, you will realize how wrong you were to ask for a king.
translation_verse: Mannɛ ketarso nde a? Meeŋ kule Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ e shin nɛ bɔrɛ e ba nseŋ ponte eleŋso. Le be kesheŋ kaŋ wora na, nɛ menyeeŋ pin men ka wora kulubi gboŋgboŋi ŋ gbiti Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, ŋkpal men ka kule mo fanɛ e sa menyi ewura so.”

english_verse: Samuel prayed, and that same day the Lord sent a thunderstorm. Everyone was afraid of the Lord and of Samuel.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Samuɛl kule Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ e shin nɛ bɔrɛ ba nseŋ ponte eleŋso kumo be kamɔnchɛ na kikɛ. Nɛ basa na kikɛ fara a ŋana Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ Samuɛl.

english_verse: They told Samuel, “Please, pray to the Lord your God for us! We don't want to die. We have sinned many times in the past, and we were very wrong to ask for a king.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ b kaŋɛ Samuɛl le: “Jande kule Enyɛnpe fo Ebɔrɛ na n sa anyi, saŋɛ na so anyi maaŋ wu. Naniere an pin fanɛ anyi be alubi nɛ an wora na kikɛ be kaman, anyi be kekaŋɛ fanɛ anyee sha ewura na gba la kulubi nna.”

english_verse: Samuel answered: Even though what you did was wrong, you don't need to be afraid. But you must always follow the Lord and worship him with all your heart.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Samuɛl kaŋɛ le: “Men sa maa lɔ kufu. Kashenteŋ nna fanɛ men wora kulubi, ama amo na amo kikɛ, men sa maŋ lar Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaman ama men ta menyi be ŋgbene kikɛ a shuŋ mo.

english_verse: Don't worship idols! They don't have any power, and they can't help you or save you when you're in trouble.
translation_verse: Men sa maa shuŋ agbir, ŋkpal manɛ so, a maaŋ tiŋ n chɛ menyi to ŋko m mɔlga menyi. Agbir la asɔ fuloŋ nna.

english_verse: But the Lord has chosen you to be his own people. He will always take care of you so that everyone will know how great he is.
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ na e lara menyi fanɛ mo gbagba be basa. Ŋkpal mbe ketre ka shibi so, e maaŋ yige menyi kikɛ.

english_verse: I would be disobeying the Lord if I stopped praying for you! I will always teach you how to live right.
translation_verse: Nɛ m baŋ yige kebaakule Ebɔrɛ a sa menyi, kumo ere Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nɛ m maŋ wora kasonu na. Meeŋ ŋini menyi kusɔ nɛ k daga fanɛ men baa wora.

english_verse: You also must obey the Lord—you must worship him with all your heart and remember the great things he has done for you.
translation_verse: Men baa nu a sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nsaa ta menyi be ŋgbene kikɛ a shuŋ mo nsaa nyiŋi asheŋgboŋ damta nɛ e wora n sa menyi na.

english_verse: But if you and your king do evil, the Lord will wipe you out.
translation_verse: Ama nɛ fanɛ men kraŋ baa wɔtɔ a wora alubi bre, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na beeŋ mur menyi nɛ men be ewura kikɛ.”

english_verse: The messengers then said to the people of Israel, “Saul has destroyed the Philistine army camp at Geba. Now the Philistines really hate Israel, so every town and village must send men to join Saul's army at Gilgal.”
translation_verse: Nɛ mbɔ na kaŋɛ Israɛl be basa le: “Sɔɔl mɔ Filistiebi be benapo be enimu na ashi Gɛba nɛ Israɛlebi be asheŋ pɛ Filistiebi na agbo ga, amoso k daga fanɛ kade kikɛ ka lara benapo nɛ b ya ti Sɔɔl be benapo so ashi Gilgaal.”

english_verse: The Israelite army realized that they were outnumbered and were going to lose the battle. Some of the Israelite men hid in caves or in clumps of bushes, and some ran to places where they could hide among large rocks. Others hid in tombs or in deep dry pits.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nɛ b yili ŋ kre kena m ba kɔ Israɛlebi na n shin nɛ ebɔl lar bumo. Nɛ Israɛl be benapo ko shile n ya ŋana abeelaŋ to nɛ beko malɛ ya ŋana amaŋ to nɛ abee to nɛ ajanmaŋ to nɛ atirbu nɛ a maŋ kɔ nchu to;

english_verse: Still others went to Gad and Gilead on the other side of the Jordan River. Saul stayed at Gilgal. His soldiers were shaking with fear,
translation_verse: nɛ beko malɛ dii Jɔɔdan be Lɔr na n yɔ Gad nɛ Giliad be efuliana so. Sɔɔl bre daa wɔ Gilgaal nna, nɛ benapo nɛ mo nɛ bumo daa wɔ ndoŋ na daa chicha kufuso.

english_verse: and they were starting to run off and leave him. Saul waited there seven days, just as Samuel had ordered him to do, but Samuel did not come.
translation_verse: Nchɛnshunu nɛ Samuɛl kaŋɛ Sɔɔl fanɛ e jo nɛ e ba, ama Samuɛl malɛ daa maŋ nya manaŋ m ba Gilgaal, nɛ benapo na fara a shile Sɔɔl kutɔ.

english_verse: Finally, Saul commanded, “Bring me some animals, so we can offer sacrifices to please the Lord and ask for his help.” Saul killed one of the animals,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Sɔɔl kaŋɛ benapo na le: “Men ta asɔbɔya nɛ meeŋ ta n lara sarga chɔɔso nɛ amo nɛ meeŋ ta n lara kɔnɔkoŋwule be sarga na m bar ma.” Nɛ b ta amo m ba sa mo nɛ e lara sarga chɔɔso n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ.

english_verse: and just as he placed it on the altar, Samuel arrived. Saul went out to welcome him.
translation_verse: E baa lara sarga chɔɔso na nna a loge nɛ Samuɛl nde. Nɛ Sɔɔl shɛr mo to n wora mo ansaŋ nɛ keba.

english_verse: “What have you done?” Samuel asked. Saul answered, “My soldiers were leaving in all directions, and you didn't come when you were supposed to. The Philistines were gathering at Michmash,
translation_verse: Nɛ Samuɛl bishi mo le: “Manɛ nɛ fo wora ere?” Nɛ Sɔɔl kaŋɛ: “Ma benapo na bee pesaŋ to nna a yɔ, fo alɛ maŋ ba saŋɛ nɛ k daga fanɛ fo ba na. Kumo be kaman Filistiebi na bee gama abar nna ashi Mikmash.

english_verse: and I was worried that they would attack me here at Gilgal. I hadn't offered a sacrifice to ask for the Lord's help, so I forced myself to offer a sacrifice on the altar fire.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ n fɛ fanɛ Filistiebi na beeŋ ba kɔ ma kena ashi Gilgaal. Ma alɛ daa maŋ lara sarga kikɛ a fin kechɛto ashi Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kutɔ, amoso nɛ n fɛ fanɛ k daga fanɛ n lara sarga na.”

english_verse: “That was stupid!” Samuel said. “You didn't obey the Lord your God. If you had obeyed him, someone from your family would always have been king of Israel.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Samuɛl kaŋɛ mo le: “Fo wora kawulisheŋ ga. Fo maŋ bɛ kenishipere be mmalga nɛ Enyɛnpe fo Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ fo na so. Fo daŋ bɛ amo so nna e daa beeŋ shin nɛ fo nɛ fo kaman to ebi e baa ji Israɛl be kuwura mbaanaayɔ.

english_verse: But no, you disobeyed, and so the Lord won't choose anyone else from your family to be king. In fact, he has already chosen the one he wants to be the next leader of his people.”
translation_verse: Ama ŋkpal fo ka kini kenu n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ so nɛ e yɛ e maaŋ naŋ lara fo kanaŋ to be esa kikɛ nɛ e ki Israɛl be ewura na. E teŋ lara mo gbagba be kepar be esa nɛ e beeŋ baa la mbe basa be ewura.”

english_verse: Then Samuel left Gilgal. Part of Saul's army had not deserted him, and he led them to Gibeah in Benjamin to join his other troops. Then he counted them and found that he still had
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Samuɛl lar Gilgaal m pɛ mbe ekpa n choŋ. Ndoŋ nna nɛ basa na be beko bɛ Sɔɔl so n ya ti benapo nɛ b ka na so. Gilgaal nɛ b daŋ fara n nite hale n ya fo Gibia nɛ k wɔ Bɛnjamin be efuli so na. Sɔɔl ka karga benapo nɛ b ka na, b daa wɔ basa alfa ashe.

english_verse: Saul, Jonathan, and their army set up camp at Geba in Benjamin. Jonathan Attacks the Philistines The Philistine army was camped at Michmash.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl nɛ mo pibinyɛn Jonatan nɛ bumo be benapo daŋ yɔ bumo be keeyi to ashi Gɛba nɛ k wɔ Bɛnjamin be efuli so na nna. Ama Filisti be benapo na bre be keeyi to daa wɔ Mikmash nna.

english_verse: Each day they sent out patrols to attack and rob villages and then destroy them. One patrol would go north along the road to Ophrah in the region of Shual.
translation_verse: Filisti be benapo nɛ baa ta kena a purgi basa a suge bumo be asɔ na daŋ barga bumo amu to ntuŋ asa nna n lar bumo be keeyi to. Ntuŋ na be kuko daŋ bɔla Ɔfra ashi Shuwal be efuli so nna.

english_verse: Another patrol would go west along the road to Beth-Horon. A third patrol would go east toward the desert on the road to the ridge that overlooks Zeboim Valley.
translation_verse: Nɛ kuko bɔla Bɛf Hɔrɔn be kaba so nɛ katuŋ nɛ k ka na malɛ bɔla Zeboyim be ketaŋɛ na be kaba nɛ k dese n shoŋi keshishɛrsawule na be ekarso be kaba so na.

english_verse: The Philistines would not allow any Israelites to learn how to make iron tools. “If we allowed that,” they said, “those worthless Israelites would make swords and spears.”
translation_verse: Filisti be ebɔyɛpo na daa maa shin nɛ Israɛlebi na bee koya kananɛ baa bɛl etokobi nɛ akpa, saŋɛ na so Israɛlebi na maaŋ baa lɔŋɛ amo.

english_verse: Whenever the Israelites wanted to get an iron point put on a cattle prod, they had to go to the Philistines. Even if they wanted to sharpen plow-blades, picks, axes, sickles, and pitchforks they still had to go to them. And the Philistines charged high prices.
translation_verse: Filistiebi daa sɔ Israɛlebi amansherbi damta nna pɔɛŋ nsaa yee bumo be akpanfu nɛ ana dɔso be ntekpa nɛ ntɔkɔrɔ ŋko a lɔŋɛ anyembi nɛ baa ta a da ana dɔso a shin nɛ a bee nite na.

english_verse: So, whenever the Israelite soldiers had to go into battle, none of them had a sword or a spear except Saul and his son Jonathan.
translation_verse: Amoso Israɛl be benapo na be ekama daa maa keta tokobi ŋko kekpa a yɔ kena to, she Sɔɔl nɛ mo pibinyɛn Jonatan nawule.

english_verse: Jonathan decided to get to the Philistine camp by going through the pass that led between Shiny Cliff and Michmash to the north and Thornbush Cliff and Geba to the south.
translation_verse: Ajembu gboŋgboŋi na be kuko daa yil kebee na be kelargato be esoso be kaba so nna a shoŋi Mikmash, nɛ kuko malɛ wɔ kelargato be kaseto nsaa shoŋi Gɛba be kaba so.

english_verse: Jonathan and the soldier who carried his weapons talked as they went toward the Philistine camp. “It's just the two of us against all those godless men,” Jonathan said. “But the Lord can help a few soldiers win a battle just as easily as he can help a whole army. Maybe the Lord will help us win this battle.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Jonatan kaŋɛ kabrantiɛbia nɛ e bee sulɔ mbe akɔsɔ na le: “Ba nɛ an yɔ Filistiebi, nnyamase na, be keeyi to. Ashere Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na beeŋ chɛ anyi to. Nɛ e baŋ shuli fanɛ e beeŋ chɛ anyi to nɛ an kɔ m pɔɔ so bre, shɛŋ shɛŋ maaŋ tiŋ ŋ kuŋ mo ekpa. K maŋ tir fanɛ an shibi ŋko anyi maŋ shibi.”

english_verse: “Do whatever you want,” the soldier answered. “I'll be right there with you.”
translation_verse: Nɛ kabrantiɛbia na kaŋɛ le: “Wora kusɔ kama nɛ fee sha. M bɛ fo so nɛ ma kagbene kikɛ.”

english_verse: “This is what we will do,” Jonathan said. “We will go across and let them see us.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Jonatan malɛ kaŋɛ le: “Anyeeŋ dii n yɔ kakpa nɛ Filistiebi na beeŋ wu anyi.

english_verse: If they agree to come down the hill and fight where we are, then we won't climb up to their camp.
translation_verse: Nɛ b baŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ an yili kakpa nɛ an wɔ na a jo bumo bre, kumo ere anyeeŋ yili ndoŋ a jo bumo.

english_verse: But we will go if they tell us to come up the hill and fight. That will mean the Lord is going to help us win.”
translation_verse: Ama nɛ b baŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ an ba bumo kutɔ bre, anyeeŋ yɔ, ŋkpal manɛ so, kumo be loŋ e naaŋ ŋini fanɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na beeŋ shin nɛ an kɔ m pɔɔ bumo so.”

english_verse: Jonathan and the soldier stood at the bottom of the hill where the Philistines could see them. The Philistines said, “Look! Those worthless Israelites have crawled out of the holes where they've been hiding.” Then they yelled down to Jonathan and the soldier, “Come up here, and we will teach you a thing or two!” Jonathan turned to the soldier and said, “Follow me! The Lord is going to let us win.”
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Filistiebi ponte ŋ kaŋɛ Jonatan nɛ kabrantiɛbia na le: “Men dii a ba nfe nɛ an ŋini menyi fanɛ durnya ere wɔ anyɔ!” Nɛ Jonatan kaŋɛ kabrantiɛbia na le: “Bɛ ma so, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na beeŋ shin nɛ an kɔ m pɔɔ so.”

english_verse: Jonathan crawled up the hillside with the soldier right behind him. When they got to the top, Jonathan killed the Philistines who attacked from the front, and the soldier killed those who attacked from behind.
translation_verse: Jonatan daŋ gbeye mbe enɔana nɛ mbe amuli so nna n yɔ kebee na be esoso nɛ kabrantiɛbia na malɛ bɛ mo so. B ka dii n yɔ kebee na be esoso na, nɛ Jonatan mɔ Filistiebi be benapo nɛ b wɔ anishito a kɔ mo na, nɛ kabrantiɛbia na malɛ mɔ bumo nɛ b wɔ kaman a kɔ mo na.

english_verse: I wish you had eaten some of the food the Philistines left behind. We would have been able to kill a lot more of them.”
translation_verse: Nɛ fanɛ an be basa daŋ ji ajibi nɛ Filistiebi na yige n shile na nna bre, dafanɛ Filistiebi nɛ an daa beeŋ mɔ na daa beeŋ ba shi ga!”

english_verse: Saul quickly called his army together, then led them to the Philistine camp. By this time the Philistines were so confused that they were killing each other.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Sɔɔl nya manaŋ n tre mbe benapo m ba abar so nɛ b yɔ Filistiebi na be keeyi to nɛ b ya kɔ bumo kena, ama b ka yɔ nɛ kebagato tɔr Filistiebi na so nɛ bumo gbagba kilgi a mɔ abar.

english_verse: The whole Philistine army panicked—those in camp, those on guard duty, those in the fields, and those on raiding patrols. All of them were afraid and confused. Then God sent an earthquake, and the ground began to tremble. Israel Defeats the Philistines
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ kufu pɛ Filisti be benapo na ga. Bumo nɛ b wɔ keeyi na to na nɛ bumo nɛ b wɔ kade na be kupuŋ to na gba nɛ benapo nɛ baa ta kena a purgi basa na nɛ benapo nɛ b wɔ anishito a kuŋ keeyi na kikɛ daa chicha kufuso nna, nɛ Ebɔrɛ shin nɛ kasawule gbuŋgbuŋ nɛ keyeŋiyeŋi tɔr bumo so. Israɛlebi ka pɔɔ Filistiebi so be asheŋ

english_verse: Saul's lookouts at Geba saw that the Philistine army was running in every direction, like melted wax.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl be benapo nɛ b wɔ Gibia na k wɔ Bɛnjamin be kasawule so a dara bumo doŋana na, daŋ wu Filisti be benapo na ka bee shile a yɛla kenishi to kaplɛkama.

english_verse: Saul told his officers, “Call the roll and find out who left our camp.” When they had finished, they found out that Jonathan and the soldier who carried his weapons were missing.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Sɔɔl kaŋɛ mbe benapo na le: “Men karga benapo na ŋ keni bumo e maŋ wɔtɔ!” B ka karga bumo nɛ b wu fanɛ Jonatan nɛ kabrantiɛbia nɛ e bee sulɔ mbe akɔsɔ na e maŋ wɔtɔ.

english_verse: At that time, Ahijah was serving as priest for the army of Israel, and Saul told him, “Come over here! Let's ask God what we should do.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Sɔɔl kaŋɛ Ahija nɛ e daa la bɔrɛmatapo na le: “Ba nɛ an bishi Ebɔrɛ kusɔ nɛ e bee sha fanɛ an wora.”

english_verse: Just as Saul finished saying this, he could see that the Philistine army camp was getting more and more confused, and he said, “Ahijah, never mind!”
translation_verse: Saŋɛ nɛ Sɔɔl bee malga bɔrɛmatapo na kutɔ na nɛ kebagato nɛ k wɔ Filistiebi na be keeyi to na bee wora keshi a ti so. Ndoŋ nna nɛ Sɔɔl kaŋɛ le: “Yige, ŋkpal manɛ so saŋɛ maŋ naa wɔtɔ nɛ fo bishi Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kusɔ nɛ anyeeŋ wora.”

english_verse: There were also some hired soldiers in the Philistine camp, who now switched to Israel's side and fought for Saul and Jonathan.
translation_verse: Israɛlebi na be benapo ko nɛ Filistiebi na daŋ haya fanɛ b chɛ bumo to ŋ kɔ na gba daŋ naŋ kilgi nna n ya ti Sɔɔl nɛ Jonatan so a kɔ Filistiebi na.

english_verse: Many Israelites had been hiding in the hill country of Ephraim. And when they heard that the Philistines were running away, they came out of hiding and joined in chasing the Philistines.
translation_verse: Israɛlebi damta nɛ b daŋ ŋana abee nɛ a wɔ Efrayim be efuli so na ka nu fanɛ Filistiebi na bee shile na, nɛ b lar kakpa nɛ b ŋana na m ba chɛ to a ju Filistiebi na kenishipereso.

english_verse: So the Lord helped Israel win the battle that day. Saul's Curse on Anyone Who Eats Saul had earlier told his soldiers, “I want to get even with those Philistines by sunset. If any of you eat before then, you will be under a curse!” So he made them swear not to eat. By the time the fighting moved past Beth-Aven, the Israelite troops were weak from hunger.
translation_verse: Akoŋ daŋ mɔ Israɛlebi be benapo na nna nɛ b bɛlɛ ŋkpal Sɔɔl ka daŋ bɔ ntaŋ ŋ kaŋɛ le so: “Kɔnɔsho e baa wɔ ekama nɛ e beeŋ ji ajibi pɔɛŋ nɛ n wora ma doŋana n tal to so.” Ŋkpal loŋ so esa kama daa maŋ ji shɛŋ kumo be kamɔnchɛ.

english_verse: The army and the people who lived nearby had gone into a forest, and they came to a place where honey was dripping on the ground. But no one ate any of it, because they were afraid of being put under the curse.
translation_verse: Mushoŋ na daŋ baa chise ndibi so nna a do kasawule, ama ekama malɛ daa maŋ ji amo ŋkpal b ka daa ŋana fanɛ Sɔɔl be kɔnɔsho na beeŋ pɛ bumo so.

english_verse: Jonathan did not know about Saul's warning to the soldiers. So he dipped the end of his walking stick in the honey and ate some with his fingers. He felt stronger and more alert.
translation_verse: Jonatan bre daa maŋ wɔ ndoŋ n nu kananɛ mo tuto bɔ ntaŋ na, amoso e daŋ ta mbe kekpabi nɛ e daŋ keta na be kɔnɔso nna n nyɔ mushoŋ na to n ji. E ka baŋ wora loŋ nɛ mbe anishito saŋɛ mo.

english_verse: Then a soldier told him, “Your father swore that anyone who ate food today would be put under a curse, and we agreed not to eat. That's why we're so weak.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ benapo na be eko kaŋɛ mo le: “Akoŋ mɔ anyi kikɛ nna nɛ an bɛlɛ ŋkpal fo tuto ka kaŋɛ fanɛ, kɔnɔsho e baa wɔ ekama nɛ e beeŋ ji ajibi kabre so.”

english_verse: Jonathan said, “My father has caused you a lot of trouble. Look at me! I ate only a little of this honey, but already I feel strong and alert.
translation_verse: Nɛ Jonatan kaŋɛ le: “Nuso be asheŋ nɛ n tuto bar m ba sa anyi be basa le! Ma ere ka baŋ ji mushoŋ na gbrɛbi nɛ n naaŋ nya eleŋ!

english_verse: By evening the Israelite army was exhausted from killing Philistines all the way from Michmash to Aijalon.
translation_verse: Ta n ya ka fo kaaseso be jemanɛ nɛ Israɛl be benapo na kikɛ gben ga ŋkpal b ka fara Mikmash a mɔ Filistiebi na hale n ya fo Aijalɔn so.

english_verse: They grabbed the food they had captured from the Philistines and started eating. They even killed sheep and cows and calves right on the spot and ate the meat without draining the blood.
translation_verse: Amoso b daŋ shile nna n ya kaa mɔ mbolpɔ nɛ ana nɛ anabi nɛ b kɔ Filistiebi m pɔɔ so n suge na epul to ndoŋ a kuya amo to a we amo nɛ ŋklaŋ.

english_verse: Someone told Saul, “Look! The army is disobeying the Lord by eating meat before the blood drains out.” “You're right,” Saul answered. “They are being unfaithful to the Lord! Hurry! Roll a big rock over here.
translation_verse: Nɛ esa ko kaŋɛ Sɔɔl le: “Keni basa na bee wora alubi a gbiti Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nna ŋkpal b ka bee we eblaŋ nɛ a kɔ ŋklaŋ amo to so.” Nɛ Sɔɔl kaŋɛ kenishipereso le: “Kashenteŋ nɛ fo ji, b wora n da Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ so nna na. Men gbelti kejembu gboŋgboŋi m ba nfe manaŋ m ba sa ma.”

english_verse: Then tell everyone in camp to bring their cattle and lambs to me. They can kill the animals on this rock, then eat the meat. That way no one will disobey the Lord by eating meat with blood still in it.” That night the soldiers brought their cattle over to the big rock and killed them there.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Sɔɔl kaŋɛ le: “Ya kaŋɛ basa na kikɛ nɛ b ta bumo be ana nɛ mbolpɔ na m ba nfe.” K daga fanɛ b mɔ amo n we nfe a chɔ kebaawe amo nɛ ŋklaŋ nsaa wora alubi a gbiti Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ. Amoso bumo kikɛ daŋ bar bumo be ana kanyɛso na nna m ba mɔ amo ndoŋ.

english_verse: It was the first altar Saul had built for offering sacrifices to the Lord. The Army Rescues Jonathan
translation_verse: Nɛ Sɔɔl pɔr bɔrɛsure n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ndoŋ. Kumo e daa la bɔrɛsure sososo mo nɛ e pɔr.

english_verse: Saul said, “Let's attack the Philistines again while it's still dark. We can fight them all night. Let's kill them and take everything they own!” The people answered, “We will do whatever you want.” “Wait!” Ahijah the priest said. “Let's ask God what we should do.”
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Sɔɔl kaŋɛ le: “Men shin nɛ an ya kɔ Filistiebi na kanyɛ ere kikɛ hale n ya fo karechɛso m mɔ bumo kikɛ nseŋ muu bumo be asɔ kikɛ.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ b kaŋɛ le: “Anyeeŋ wora kusɔ kama nɛ fee sha.” Nɛ bɔrɛmatapo Ahija malɛ kaŋɛ le: “Men shin nɛ an bishi Ebɔrɛ kusɔ nɛ anyeeŋ wora.”

english_verse: Saul asked God, “Should I attack the Philistines? Will you help us win?” This time God did not answer.
translation_verse: Nɛ Sɔɔl bishi Ebɔrɛ le: “N naaŋ ya kɔ Filistiebi na kena a? Feeŋ shin nɛ an kɔ m pɔɔ bumo so a?” Ama kumo be kamɔnchɛ na Ebɔrɛ daŋ maŋ kaŋɛ bumo shɛŋ.

english_verse: Saul called his army officers together and said, “We have to find out what sin has kept God from answering.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Sɔɔl tre mbe benapo be benimu ŋ kaŋɛ bumo le: “Men shin nɛ an lege to n fin kulubi nɛ k wɔ anyi to kabre nɛ Ebɔrɛ kpal kumo so ŋ kini ketuge anyi ere.

english_verse: I swear by the living Lord that whoever sinned must die, even if it turns out to be my own son Jonathan.” No one said a word.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ e bee shin nɛ Israɛlebi bee kɔ a pɔɔ so na ka la ma shɛdajipo so, esa kama nɛ e wora kulubi daga luwu nna, hale nɛ k ba fanɛ m pibinyɛn Jonatan gba e wora kumo.” Ama esa kama daa maŋ kaŋɛ shɛŋ.

english_verse: Saul told his army, “You stand on that side of the priest, and Jonathan and I will stand on the other side.” Everyone agreed.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Sɔɔl kaŋɛ Israɛlebi be benapo na kikɛ le: “Men kikɛ e ya yili ndoŋ ere nɛ ma alɛ nɛ Jonatan e ya yili nfe ere.” Nɛ bumo kikɛ shuli so.

english_verse: Then Saul prayed, “Our Lord, God of Israel, why haven't you answered me today? Please show us who sinned. Was it my son Jonathan and I, or was it your people Israel?” The answer came back that Jonathan or Saul had sinned, not the army.
translation_verse: Nɛ Sɔɔl kule Enyɛnpe Israɛl be Ebɔrɛ na ŋ kaŋɛ le: “Enyɛnpe, manɛ nna nɛ fo maŋ tuge ma kabre? Jande ŋini anyi esa nɛ e wora kulubi. Nɛ ma nɛ m pibinyɛn Jonatan e wora kulubi ŋko fo basa Israɛlebi na e wora kulubi, fo kaŋɛ anyi.” Nɛ bɔrɛmatapo na bishi Ebɔrɛ nseŋ wu fanɛ kulubi na shi Jonatan ŋko Sɔɔl kutɔ nna.

english_verse: Saul told Ahijah, “Now ask the Lord to decide between Jonathan and me.” The answer came back that Jonathan had sinned.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Sɔɔl kaŋɛ bɔrɛmatapo na le: “Bishi Ebɔrɛ, ma nɛ m pibinyɛn Jonatan be emo nɛ e wora kulubi na.” Nɛ k tɔr Jonatan so.

english_verse: “Jonathan,” Saul exclaimed, “tell me what you did!” “I dipped the end of my walking stick in some honey and ate a little. Now you say I have to die!”
translation_verse: Nɛ Sɔɔl Kaŋɛ Jonatan le: “Kaŋɛ ma kusɔ nɛ fo wora.” Nɛ Jonatan yɛ: “N ta ma kekpabi nna n nyɔ mushoŋ to gbrɛbi n ji; nɛ kumo so nɛ k daga fanɛ n wu bre, kumo ere ma nde.”

english_verse: “Yes, Jonathan. I swear to God that you must die.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Sɔɔl kaŋɛ Jonatan le: “Nɛ fo baa maŋ wu bre, kumo ere Ebɔrɛ e mɔ ma.”

english_verse: “No!” the soldiers shouted. “God helped Jonathan win the battle for us. We won't let you kill him. We swear to the Lord that we won't let you kill him or even lay a hand on him!” So the army kept Saul from killing Jonathan.
translation_verse: Ama le nɛ basa na daŋ kaŋɛ Sɔɔl: “Jonatan nɛ e kɔ kena m pɔɔ so n sa Israɛl be efuli ere e daga luwu a? Loŋ maaŋ wora kikɛ, ŋkpal manɛ so, an teŋ nase kɔnɔ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ e la anyi be shɛdajipo na be anishito fanɛ Jonatan be kemin gba maaŋ tia, ŋkpal manɛ so, Ebɔrɛ e chɛ mo to nɛ e wora kusɔ nɛ e wora kabre ere.” Amoso basa na e daŋ mɔlga Jonatan nɛ e maŋ luri luwu to.

english_verse: When Saul became king, the Moabites, the Ammonites, the Edomites, the kings of Zobah, the Philistines, and the Amalekites had all been robbing the Israelites. Saul fought back against these enemies and stopped them from robbing Israel. He was a brave commander and always won his battles. Saul's Family
translation_verse: E daŋ kɔ kena kenyɛnso nna ga hale m pɔɔ Amalɛk be basa so. Mo e daŋ mɔlga Israɛl be basa ashi basa nɛ baa ta kena a purgi basa a suge bumo be asɔ na kutɔ.

english_verse: Saul was at war with the Philistines for as long as he lived. Whenever he found a good warrior or a brave man, Saul made him join his army.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ka daa wɔ ŋkpa to na, mo nɛ Filistiebi na daŋ kɔ ana kpakpaso damta nna. Mo alɛ daŋ baŋ wu enapo kama nɛ e kɔ eleŋ ŋko kenyɛn, e daa ta mo nna a ti mbe benapo so.

english_verse: One day, Samuel told Saul: The Lord told me to choose you to be king of his people, Israel. Now listen to this message from the Lord:
translation_verse: Kachako nɛ Samuɛl kaŋɛ Sɔɔl le: “Ma nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ shuŋi fanɛ m ba ta ŋku n do fo kumu so n lara fo ŋ ki mbe basa Israɛlebi be ewura. Amoso kaŋ kusoe naniere n nu kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpetale bee kaŋɛ.

english_verse: “When the Israelites were on their way out of Egypt, the nation of Amalek attacked them. I am the Lord All-Powerful, and now I am going to make Amalek pay!
translation_verse: E beeŋ gberge Amalɛk be basa kusoe ŋkpal bumo nananyɛnana ka daŋ ŋana ekpa to ŋ kɔ Israɛlebi kena saŋɛ nɛ b daŋ lar Ijipt be efuli so a ba na so.

english_verse: “Go and attack the Amalekites! Destroy them and all their possessions. Don't have any pity. Kill their men, women, children, and even their babies. Slaughter their cattle, sheep, camels, and donkeys.”
translation_verse: Men ya kɔ Amalɛkebi na nseŋ jija bumo be kusɔ kama nɛ b kɔ kikɛ kuraa. Men sa maŋ kaŋ yige shɛŋ shɛŋ. Men mɔ bumo be benyɛn nɛ beche nɛ mbia nɛ mbi popɔrbi kikɛ. Men mɔ bumo be ana nɛ mbolpɔ nɛ enyɔma nɛ ekurma gba.”

english_verse: Saul sent messengers who told every town and village to send men to join the army at Telaim. There were
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Sɔɔl tre mbe benapo m ba shɛr abar so ashi Tɛlɛm. Benapo ŋgboŋ alfa anyɔ e daŋ shi Israɛl be efuli so nɛ ŋgboŋ kudu malɛ shi Juda be efuli so.

english_verse: The Lord told Samuel,
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Samuɛl le:

english_verse: then led them to a valley near one of the towns in Amalek, where they got ready to make a surprise attack.
translation_verse: Nɛ Sɔɔl nɛ mbe benapo na ya ŋana ketaŋɛ ko nɛ k taga kade nɛ baa tre Amalɛk na to a jo nɛ b kɔ Amalɛkebi na kena.

english_verse: Some Kenites lived nearby, and Saul told them, “Your people were kind to our nation when we left Egypt, and I don't want you to get killed when I wipe out the Amalekites. So stay away from them.” The Kenites left,
translation_verse: Le nɛ Sɔɔl daŋ kaŋɛ Kenebi ko nɛ b daŋ chena m mata Amalɛkebi na: “Saŋɛ nɛ anyi be efuli ere so ebi daŋ lar Ijipt a ba na, menyi be basa daŋ wora bumo kelela ga. Amoso men lar Amalɛkebi ere to manaŋ nɛ an sa maŋ kaŋ mɔ menyi n ti bumo so saŋɛ nɛ anyee kɔ bumo kena na.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ Kenebi na lar Amalɛkebi na to.

english_verse: and Saul attacked the Amalekites from Havilah to Shur, which is just east of Egypt.
translation_verse: Nɛ Sɔɔl yili Havila kikɛ ŋ kɔ m pɔɔ Amalɛkebi na so hale n ya fo Shur nɛ k wɔ Ijipt be efuli so be epeŋilarkpa na.

english_verse: Every Amalekite was killed except King Agag.
translation_verse: E daŋ pɛ Amalɛk be ewura Agag nna nseŋ mɔ mbe basa kikɛ.

english_verse: Saul and his army let Agag live, and they also spared the best sheep and cattle. They didn't want to destroy anything of value, so they only killed the animals that were worthless or weak. The Lord Rejects Saul
translation_verse: Sɔɔl nɛ mbe benapo na daa maŋ mɔ Agag. B daa maŋ mɔ mbolpɔ lela nɛ bumo be bibi nɛ ana lela nɛ bumo be bibi ŋko n jija kusɔ kama nɛ k walɛ m par bumo na; kusɔ kama nɛ k daa maŋ kɔ tɔnɔ na nɛ b daŋ jija. Ebɔrɛ ka kini Sɔɔl fanɛ ewura be asheŋ

english_verse: “Saul has stopped obeying me, and I'm sorry that I made him king.” Samuel was angry, and he cried out in prayer to the Lord all night.
translation_verse: “K wora ma kagbenejija ga fanɛ ŋ ka ta Sɔɔl ŋ ki ewura; ŋkpal manɛ so e pal kaman n sa ma nseŋ kini ma mbra be keb so.” Kumo be loŋ daŋ pɛ Samuɛl agbo ga nɛ e kule Ebɔrɛ awɔrso hale nɛ kare ba chɛ.

english_verse: Early the next morning he went to talk with Saul. Someone told him, “Saul went to Carmel, where he had a monument built so everyone would remember his victory. Then he left for Gilgal.”
translation_verse: Kumo be ŋklade kachipurdidi Samuɛl koso nɛ e ya fin Sɔɔl, nseŋ nu fanɛ Sɔɔl yɔ Kamɛl be kade to. Ndoŋ nɛ e pɔr kapɔrduli tenteŋ n yili nɛ b baa kɔ kumo a nyiŋi mo. E ka loge nɛ e yɔ Gilgaal.

english_verse: Samuel finally caught up with Saul, and Saul told him, “I hope the Lord will bless you! I have done what the Lord told me.”
translation_verse: Samuɛl ka yɔ Sɔɔl kutɔ na nɛ Sɔɔl kaŋɛ mo le: “Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e nɛfa fo Samuɛl! N wora kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ ma na kikɛ.”

english_verse: “Then why,” Samuel asked, “do I hear sheep and cattle?”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Samuɛl bishi le: “Nɛ nuso be ana nɛ mbolpɔ e naa shu ere?”

english_verse: “The army took them from the Amalekites,” Saul explained. “They kept the best sheep and cattle, so they could sacrifice them to the Lord your God. But we destroyed everything else.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Sɔɔl kaŋɛ: “Ma benapo na e sɔ bumo ashi Amalɛkebi na kutɔ. B ta ana nɛ mbolpɔ duliduli na kikɛ nna nɛ b ya lara sarga n sa Eyɛnpe fo Ebɔrɛ na. Ama an mur amo nɛ a ka na bre kikɛ.”

english_verse: “Stop!” Samuel said. “Let me tell you what the Lord told me last night.” “All right,” Saul answered.
translation_verse: Nɛ Samuɛl kaŋɛ le: “Yili nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ fo kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ ma ndre kanyɛso.” Nɛ Sɔɔl yɛ: “Baa malga.”

english_verse: Samuel continued, “You may not think you're very important, but the Lord chose you to be king, and you are in charge of the tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: Nɛ Samuɛl yɛ: “Fo gbagba nyi fo ka daa maŋ la shɛŋ; ama naniere mannɛ fo e ba ki Israɛl be eyiri kikɛ be ejuŋkparpo ere a? Fo nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ lara fanɛ fo ki Israɛl be ewura naniere,

english_verse: When the Lord sent you on this mission, he told you to wipe out those worthless Amalekites.
translation_verse: nɛ e shuŋi fo fanɛ fo ya mur Amalɛkebi nɛ b la basa lubi na kikɛ. E yɛ: Men kɔ bumo kena m mur bumo kikɛ kuraa!

english_verse: Why didn't you listen to the Lord? Why did you keep the animals and make him angry?”
translation_verse: Manɛ nna nɛ fo maŋ wora kasonu n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ? Manɛ nna nɛ fo kuse n ya muu asɔ lela na kikɛ nseŋ shin nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nya agbo?”

english_verse: “But I did listen to the Lord!” Saul answered. “He sent me on a mission, and I went. I captured King Agag and destroyed his nation.
translation_verse: Nɛ Sɔɔl kaŋɛ le: “N wora kasonu n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, ŋkpal manɛ so n ya mɔ Amalɛkebi na kikɛ nna nseŋ pɛ bumo be ewura Agag.

english_verse: All the animals were going to be destroyed anyway. That's why the army brought the best sheep and cattle to Gilgal as sacrifices to the Lord your God.”
translation_verse: Ama ma benapo na daa maŋ mɔ bumo be mbolpɔ nɛ ana lela na bre. B ta bumo nna m ba Gilgaal nɛ b ba lara sarga n sa Enyɛnpe fo Ebɔrɛ na.”

english_verse: “Tell me,” Samuel said. “Does the Lord really want sacrifices and offerings? No! He doesn't want your sacrifices. He wants you to obey him.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Samuɛl kaŋɛ le: “Ade be kumo bre nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na bee sha ga? Kebaakɔ kasonu ŋko kebaalara esarga? Kebaakɔ kasonu bɔ fo kaa ta mbolpɔ duliduli a lara esarga e sa mo.

english_verse: Rebelling against God or disobeying him because you are proud is just as bad as worshiping idols or asking them for advice. You refused to do what God told you, so God has decided that you can no longer be king.”
translation_verse: Kekini kenu n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ du fanɛ kegbaya nna. Nɛ kamoowu malɛ du fanɛ kagbirshuŋ. Ŋkpal fo ka kini kenu n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na so, mo alɛ gba kini fo fanɛ ewura.”

english_verse: “I have sinned,” Saul admitted. “I disobeyed both you and the Lord. I was afraid of the army, and I listened to them instead.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Sɔɔl kaŋɛ Samuɛl le: “N shuli fanɛ n wora kulubi. Ŋ kini kenu n sa fo nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kikɛ. Benapo na nɛ n daa ŋana nseŋ nu n sa bumo.

english_verse: Please forgive me and come back with me so I can worship the Lord.”
translation_verse: Ama naniere bre mee kule fo nna nɛ fo ta ma alubi m paŋ ma nseŋ shin nɛ n tu fo n ya bunyaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ.”

english_verse: “No!” Samuel replied, “You disobeyed the Lord, and I won't go back with you. Now the Lord has said that you can't be king of Israel any longer.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Samuɛl yɛ: “M-m, Fo maaŋ naŋ bɛ ma so n yɔ. Ŋkpal fo ka kini Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be mbra na be kebɛso na so, mo alɛ gba kini fo fanɛ ewura.”

english_verse: As Samuel turned to go, Saul grabbed the edge of Samuel's robe. It tore!
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Samuɛl kilgi nɛ e yɔ nɛ Sɔɔl to m pɛ Samuɛl be piŋi tenteŋ nɛ e buu na be kɔnɔ so to nɛ k kpɛa.

english_verse: Samuel said, “The Lord has torn the kingdom of Israel away from you today, and he will give it to someone who is better than you.
translation_verse: Nɛ Samuɛl kaŋɛ mo le: “Kananɛ fo baŋ kpɛa ma piŋi ere be kɔnɔso ere, loŋ gbagba na chap nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ gboŋi fo Israɛl be kuwurji to kabre nseŋ ta kumo m buu fo echenashapo nɛ e bɔ fo.

english_verse: Besides, the eternal God of Israel isn't a human being. He doesn't tell lies or change his mind.”
translation_verse: Israɛl be Ebɔrɛ nɛ e kɔ kemaŋkura na maa ku efɛ ŋko a chɛrga mbe nfɛra, ŋkpal manɛ so, e maŋ la dimɛdi.”

english_verse: Saul said, “I did sin, but please honor me in front of the leaders of the army and the people of Israel. Come back with me, so I can worship the Lord your God.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Sɔɔl kaŋɛ le: “N wora kulubi ama mee kule fo nna nɛ fo ta bunyaŋ m buu ma so ashi benapo be benimu ere nɛ Israɛl be basa kikɛ be anishito n shin nɛ n tu fo n ya bunyaŋ Enyɛnpe fo Ebɔrɛ na.”

english_verse: Samuel followed Saul back, and Saul worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ mo nɛ Samuɛl bɛta n yɔ nɛ Sɔɔl ya bunyaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ.

english_verse: Then Samuel shouted, “Bring me King Agag of Amalek!” Agag came in chains, and he was saying to himself, “Surely they won't kill me now.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Samuɛl ponte ŋ kaŋɛ le: “Men ta Amalɛk be ewura Agag na m ba sa ma nfe.” Nɛ Agag ba yili Samuɛl kutɔ nsaa chicha kufuso a fɛ mbe kumu to le: “Naniere bre b maaŋ naŋ mɔ ma.”

english_verse: But Samuel said, “Agag, you have snatched children from their mothers' arms and killed them. Now your mother will be without children.” Then Samuel chopped Agag to pieces at the place of worship in Gilgal.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Samuɛl kaŋɛ Agag le: “Fo e naa suge mbiwurbi bumo nioana kutɔ a mɔ nɛ baa paŋ mbia na. Fo nio gba beeŋ paŋ ebi naniere kikɛ.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ Samuɛl mɔ Agag nseŋ ŋele mo to fanɛ mblaŋkul bɔrɛsure na ase ashi Gilgaal.

english_verse: Samuel went home to Ramah, and Saul returned to his home in Gibeah.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Samuɛl bɛta n yɔ Raama nɛ Sɔɔl malɛ bɛta n yɔ mbe kade to Gibia.

english_verse: Even though Samuel felt sad about Saul, Samuel never saw him again. The Lord Chooses David To Be King The Lord was sorry he had made Saul the king of Israel.
translation_verse: Baŋ yili kumo be saŋɛ na so kikɛ n ya fo saŋɛ so nɛ Samuɛl wu, e daa maŋ naŋ wu Sɔɔl kenishiso kikɛ. Ama Samuɛl be kagbene daŋ jija mo nna ga ŋkpal Sɔɔl so. K daŋ tɔrɔ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ malɛ nna ga ŋkpal e ka daŋ ta Sɔɔl ŋ ki Israɛl be ewura so.

english_verse: One day he said, “Samuel, I've rejected Saul, and I refuse to let him be king any longer. Stop feeling sad about him. Put some olive oil in a small container and go visit a man named Jesse, who lives in Bethlehem. I've chosen one of his sons to be my king.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Samuɛl le: “Nchɛ afanɛ nɛ fo shin nɛ fo chena kagbenejijaso a fɛ Sɔɔl be asheŋ? M maŋ naŋ shuli fanɛ e baa la Israɛl be ewura, amoso ta ɔlif be ŋku n yɔ kanyɛn nɛ baa tre Jɛsi nɛ e wɔ Bɛtlɛhɛm na pe. N lara mbe mbia na be eko nɛ e ki Israɛl be ewura.”

english_verse: Samuel answered, “If I do that, Saul will find out and have me killed.” “Take a calf with you,” the Lord replied. “Tell everyone that you've come to offer it as a sacrifice to me,
translation_verse: Nɛ Samuɛl kaŋɛ le: “M baŋ wora loŋ nɛ Sɔɔl nu, e beeŋ mɔ ma!” Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ mo: “Ta kenabi a yɔ n ya kaŋɛ fanɛ fo ba nna nɛ fo ba lara sarga n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ.

english_verse: then invite Jesse to the sacrifice. When I show you which one of his sons I have chosen, pour the olive oil on his head.”
translation_verse: Fo kaŋ baa lara sarga na fo tre Jɛsi nɛ e ba ndoŋ nɛ ŋ ŋini fo kusɔ nɛ feeŋ wora. Meeŋ ŋini fo esa nɛ feeŋ chulgi ŋku na n do mbe kumu so n lara ŋ ki ewura na.”

english_verse: Samuel did what the Lord told him and went to Bethlehem. The town leaders went to meet him, but they were terribly afraid and asked, “Is this a friendly visit?”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Samuɛl wora kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ fanɛ e wora na nseŋ yɔ Bɛtlɛhɛm, nɛ ndoŋ be benimuana na ba mo kutɔ m ba kaa chicha kufuso, nseŋ bishi le: “Kagbenewushi so nɛ fo ba ere a?”

english_verse: “Yes, it is!” Samuel answered. “I've come to offer a sacrifice to the Lord. Get yourselves ready to take part in the sacrifice and come with me.” Samuel also invited Jesse and his sons to come to the sacrifice, and he got them ready to take part.
translation_verse: Nɛ Samuɛl yɛ: “Mm. M ba nna nɛ m ba lara sarga n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, amoso men lara alubi ashi men be ŋgbene to pɔɛŋ nseŋ ba ŋ kutɔ.” Kumo be kaman nɛ e kaŋɛ Jɛsi nɛ mbe mbia fanɛ b lara kulubi ashi bumo be ŋgbene to pɔɛŋ nseŋ ba kakpa nɛ baa lara sarga na.

english_verse: When Jesse and his sons arrived, Samuel noticed Jesse's oldest son, Eliab. “He has to be the one the Lord has chosen,” Samuel said to himself.
translation_verse: B ka fo ndoŋ na, nɛ Samuɛl wu Jɛsi pibinyɛn Eliab nseŋ fɛ mbe kagbene to le: “Kashenteŋto kanyɛn ere e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be esa laraso na.”

english_verse: But the Lord told him, “Samuel, don't think Eliab is the one just because he's tall and handsome. He isn't the one I've chosen. People judge others by what they look like, but I judge people by what is in their hearts.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ naŋ kaŋɛ mo le: “Sa maŋ keni mbe nteŋ ŋko mbe kayɛrbi. Mannɛ mo nɛ n lara, ŋkpal manɛ so ma ere maa keni asheŋ fanɛ kananɛ dimɛdi bee kini asheŋ na. Dimɛdi bre bee keni eyur so nna ama ma ere bee keni kagbene to nna.”

english_verse: Jesse told his son Abinadab to go over to Samuel, but Samuel said, “No, the Lord hasn't chosen him.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Jɛsi naŋ tre mo pibinyɛn Abinadab m ba Samuɛl kutɔ, nɛ Samuɛl kaŋɛ le: “Manɛ ede gba nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na lara.”

english_verse: Next, Jesse sent his son Shammah to him, and Samuel said, “The Lord hasn't chosen him either.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Jɛsi naŋ keta Shamaa malɛ m ba. Nɛ Samuɛl kaŋɛ mo le: “Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ maŋ lara ede gba.”

english_verse: One by one, Jesse told all seven of his sons to go over to Samuel. Finally, Samuel said, “Jesse, the Lord hasn't chosen any of these young men.
translation_verse: Jɛsi daŋ keta mbia ashunu nna m ba Samuɛl kutɔ nɛ Samuɛl kaŋɛ mo le: “Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na maŋ lara bede be ekama.”

english_verse: Do you have any other sons?” “Yes,” Jesse answered. “My youngest son David is out taking care of the sheep.” “Send for him!” Samuel said. “We won't start the ceremony until he gets here.”
translation_verse: Nseŋ bishi mo le: “Fo kraa kɔ mbia ko a?” Nɛ Jɛsi yɛ: “Mm, m pibi kekarkarso Deevid e ka, ama mo alɛ wɔ kupuŋ to a kpa mbolpɔ.” Nɛ Samuɛl kaŋɛ mo le: “Shuŋi nɛ b ya tre mo m ba. Nɛ mannɛ loŋ, anyi maaŋ lara sarga ere ama an baaŋ wu mo nna.”

english_verse: Jesse sent for David. He was a healthy, good-looking boy with a sparkle in his eyes. As soon as David came, the Lord told Samuel, “He's the one! Get up and pour the olive oil on his head.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Jɛsi shuŋi nɛ b ya tre Deevid m ba. E daŋ baŋ yili enyɛn nna a walɛ kayɛrbi ga nsaa kɔ eleŋ. Kebia na ka ba nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Samuɛl le: “Mo gbagba nna na. Ta ŋku n do mbe kumu so n lara mo nɛ e ki ewura.”

english_verse: Samuel poured the oil on David's head while his brothers watched. At that moment, the Spirit of the Lord took control of David and stayed with him from then on. Samuel returned home to Ramah. David Plays the Harp for Saul
translation_verse: Nɛ Samuɛl duga ŋku na n do Deevid be kumu so nɛ mo daana yil a keni mo. Baŋ yili kumo be kamɔnchɛ na kikɛ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be kiyoyu ba luri m bɔlɔ Deevid to eleŋso nsaa wɔ mo to saŋkikɛ. Kumo be kamɔnchɛ na malɛ kikɛ nɛ Samuɛl bɛta n yɔ Raama. Deevid ka bee shuŋ Sɔɔl be asheŋ

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord had left Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord was terrifying him.
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be kiyoyu lar Sɔɔl to, nɛ kiyoyu lubi ba luri mo to a tɔrɔ mo ga.

english_verse: “It's an evil spirit from God that's frightening you,” Saul's officials told him.
translation_verse: Nɛ Sɔɔl be nyɛrbi kaŋɛ mo le: “An baa nyi fanɛ Ebɔrɛ e sa ekpa nɛ kiyoyu lubi ere bee tɔrɔ fo ga le na.

english_verse: “Your Majesty, let us go and look for someone who is good at playing the harp. He can play for you whenever the evil spirit from God bothers you, and you'll feel better.”
translation_verse: Amoso, sa anyi ekpa nɛ an ya fin esa nɛ e nyi jaŋjilaŋ be kelaŋ, saŋɛ na so saŋkama nɛ kiyoyu lubi na baŋ ba fo so, esa na beeŋ laŋ mbe jaŋjilaŋ nɛ fo eyur e wushi fo.”

english_verse: “All right,” Saul answered. “Find me someone who is good at playing the harp and bring him here.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Sɔɔl kaŋɛ bumo le: “Men fin esa nɛ e nyi jaŋjilaŋ be kelaŋ nɛnɛ m bar ma.”

english_verse: “A man named Jesse who lives in Bethlehem has a son who can play the harp,” one official said. “He's a brave warrior, he's good-looking, he can speak well, and the Lord is with him.”
translation_verse: Nɛ mbe nyɛrbi na be eko kaŋɛ: “Kanyɛn ko nɛ baa tre Jɛsi nɛ e wɔ Bɛtlɛhɛm na be kebia nyi jaŋjilaŋ be kelaŋ ga. E la enapo mo nɛ e kɔ kenyɛn nna ga nsaa walɛ kayɛrbi ga nɛ mbe mmalga gba wɔ ebel nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na wɔ mo kutɔ.”

english_verse: Saul sent a message to Jesse: “Tell your son David to leave your sheep and come here to me.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Sɔɔl shuŋi mbɔ fanɛ b ya kaŋɛ Jɛsi le: “Kaŋɛ fo pibinyɛn Deevid nɛ e bee kpa mbolpɔ na fanɛ e ba ŋ kutɔ.”

english_verse: Jesse loaded a donkey with bread and a goatskin full of wine, then he told David to take the donkey and a young goat to Saul.
translation_verse: Nɛ Jɛsi kre bodobodo n deŋi kurma so n ta kaboe fɔlbi nɛ nsa belbelso deŋkeŋ be bɔlɔ n ti so n shuŋi Deevid fanɛ e ya sa Sɔɔl.

english_verse: David went to Saul and started working for him. Saul liked him so much that he put David in charge of carrying his weapons.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Deevid yɔ Sɔɔl kutɔ n ya kaa shuŋ mo. Sɔɔl daa sha mbe asheŋ ga hale n lara mo fanɛ e baa sulɔ mbe kena to be akɔsɔ.

english_verse: Not long after this, Saul sent another message to Jesse: “I really like David. Please let him stay with me.”
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Sɔɔl ta ebɔl n shoŋi Jɛsi fanɛ e shin nɛ Deevid e ba wɔ mo kutɔ a shuŋ a sa mo, ŋkpal manɛ so mbe asheŋ bee par mo ga.

english_verse: Whenever the evil spirit from God bothered Saul, David would play his harp. Saul would relax and feel better, and the evil spirit would go away.
translation_verse: Baŋ yili loŋ be saŋɛ na nɛ Ebɔrɛ baŋ sa ekpa nɛ kiyoyu lubi na ba Sɔɔl so, Deevid bee ta mbe jaŋjilaŋ nna n laŋ, nɛ Sɔɔl be eyur e naa ŋ wushi mo.

english_verse: The Philistines got ready for war and brought their troops together to attack the town of Socoh in Judah. They set up camp at Ephes-Dammim, between Socoh and Azekah.
translation_verse: Kachako nɛ Filisti be basa ba abar so ashi Sukɔɔ nɛ k wɔ Juda be efuli so na nɛ b ba kɔ Israɛl be basa kena. B daŋ wora bumo be keeyi to ashi Efis Dammim nɛ k wɔ Sukɔɔ nɛ Azeka be kefɛato na nna.

english_verse: King Saul and the Israelite army set up camp on a hill overlooking Elah Valley, and they got ready to fight the Philistine army that was on a hill on the other side of the valley.
translation_verse: Filistiebi na daa wɔ kebee ko so nna nɛ Israɛlebi na malɛ wɔ kebee ko so, nɛ ketaŋɛ na dese bumo nɛ bumo be kefɛato.

english_verse: He wore a bronze helmet and had bronze armor to protect his chest and legs. The chest armor alone weighed about
translation_verse: E daa kɔ danyaŋ be asɔ nɛ e bee ta a wɔtɔ a kuŋ mbe aya gba nna, nseŋ ta danyaŋ be tokobi a di mbe kaman.

english_verse: When David came back from fighting Goliath, he was still carrying Goliath's head. Abner took David to Saul,
translation_verse: Deevid ka shi mo nɛ Goliɛf be kena na to m ba nɛ Abna keta mo n yɔ Sɔɔl kutɔ nɛ e kraŋ keta Goliɛf be kumu na.

english_verse: and his spear was so big that the iron spearhead alone weighed about seven kilograms. A soldier always walked in front of Goliath to carry his shield.
translation_verse: Mbe kekpa be kedibi be bumburuŋ daa sa fanɛ keyapuye, nɛ kumo be kumu be egbɛ malɛ sa fanɛ kilo ashunu. Enapo ko daa juŋkpar mo nna a keta mbe kebɛlso be kusɔ kuŋso na.

english_verse: Goliath went out and shouted to the army of Israel: Why are you lining up for battle? I'm the best soldier in our army, and all of you are in Saul's army. Choose your best soldier to come out and fight me!
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Goliɛf yili a ponte a kaŋɛ Israɛlebi na le: “Nuso be kena nɛ menyi alɛ gbare abar a ba nɛ men ba kɔ ere? Filisti be esa e la ma nɛ menyi alɛ la Sɔɔl be nyɛrbi! Amoso men lara menyi be enapo ko nɛ e gbelge m ba nɛ ma nɛ mo e kɔ.

english_verse: If he can kill me, our people will be your slaves. But if I kill him, your people will be our slaves.
translation_verse: Enapo na kaŋ tiŋ m pɔɔ ma so m mɔ ma, kumo ere, anyeeŋ ki menyi be anya, nɛ ma alɛ kaŋ pɔɔ mo so m mɔ mo, menyi alɛ beeŋ ki anyi be anya.

english_verse: Here and now I challenge Israel's whole army! Choose someone to fight me!
translation_verse: Menyi Israɛlebi be benapo fupo ere nɛ mee to emaŋ na. Men lara esa ko nɛ ma nɛ mo e kɔ abar!”

english_verse: Saul and his men heard what Goliath said, but they were so frightened of Goliath that they couldn't do a thing. David Decides To Challenge Goliath
translation_verse: Sɔɔl nɛ mbe basa ka nu kusɔ nɛ Goliɛf kaŋɛ na, nɛ kufu pɛ bumo ga nɛ bumo be aba pɔ bumo. Deevid ka yɔ Sɔɔl be keeyi to be asheŋ

english_verse: David's father Jesse was an old man, who belonged to the Ephrath clan and lived in Bethlehem in Judah. Jesse had eight sons:
translation_verse: Deevid mo tuto e daa la Jɛsi nɛ e la Efrat be kanaŋ to be esa nsaa shi Bɛtlɛhɛm nɛ k wɔ Juda be efuliso na. Jɛsi daa kɔ mbia aburwa nna, ama saŋɛ nɛ Sɔɔl daa la ewura na nɛ e teŋ bel ga.

english_verse: He took care of his father's sheep, and he went back and forth between Bethlehem and Saul's camp.
translation_verse: nsaa wɔ Sɔɔl pe a bɛta a yɔ Bɛtlɛhɛm saŋko saŋko n ya ka kpa mo tuto be mbolpɔ.

english_verse: Goliath came out and gave his challenge every morning and every evening for
translation_verse: Nchɛ adena kikɛ nɛ Goliɛf bee yili a to Israɛlebi na emaŋ kapa nɛ kanyɛ.

english_verse: and picked up his shepherd's stick. He went out to a stream and picked up five smooth rocks and put them in his leather bag. Then with his sling in his hand, he went straight toward Goliath. David Kills Goliath
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e ta kekpabi nɛ e kɔ a kpa mbolpɔ na nseŋ yɔ kabombi ko ase n ya tise ajembu mɔlmɔlbi anu n wɔtɔ mbe kɔlgu to nseŋ ta mbe ketababu a shɛr Goliɛf to. Deevid ka pɔɔ Goliɛf so be asheŋ

english_verse: One day, Jesse told David, “Hurry and take this sack of roasted grain and these ten loaves of bread to your brothers at the army camp.
translation_verse: Kachako nɛ Jɛsi kaŋɛ Deevid le: “Ta aboyu keeso be kilo kudu nɛ bodobodo kudu ere n shile n ya sa fo daana ashi bumo be keeyi to,

english_verse: And here are ten large chunks of cheese to take to their commanding officer. Find out how your brothers are doing and bring back something that shows that they're all right.
translation_verse: nseŋ ta wagashi kudu ere malɛ n ya sa fo daana be katuŋ na be enimu. Kumo be kaman nɛ fo keni kananɛ fo daana du ndoŋ nseŋ fin shɛdaso be kusɔ ko ndoŋ m ba ŋini fanɛ fo wu bumo nɛ b kɔ alenfia.

english_verse: David obeyed his father. He got up early the next morning and left someone else in charge of the sheep; then he loaded the supplies and started off. He reached the army camp just as the soldiers were taking their places and shouting the battle cry.
translation_verse: Kumo be ŋklade kachipurdidi nɛ Deevid koso nseŋ shin nɛ esa ko bee keni mbe mbolpɔ so nɛ e ta ajibi na n yɔ fanɛ kananɛ Jɛsi ŋini mo na gbagba chap. Saŋɛ so nɛ Israɛl be benapo na baŋ lar a boŋ kena to be nshɛ a yɔ kakpa nɛ baaŋ ya yili ŋ kɔ kena na, nɛ Deevid fo ndoŋ.

english_verse: David left his things with the man in charge of supplies and ran up to the battle line to ask his brothers if they were well.
translation_verse: Nɛ Deevid yige ajibi na n yili benapo be enimu nɛ e bee keni ajibi be asheŋ so na kutɔ nseŋ shile n yɔ mo daana kutɔ ashi kaboŋ nɛ b wɔ na n ya bishi bumo kananɛ asheŋ du.

english_verse: While David was talking with them, Goliath came out from the line of Philistines and started boasting as usual. David heard him.
translation_verse: Saŋɛ nɛ e bee malga mo daana kutɔ na, nɛ Goliɛf lar kakpa nɛ mbe basa wɔ na m ba ka to Israɛlebi na emaŋ a tege bumo fanɛ kananɛ e chɛr a wora na. Nɛ Deevid nu kumo.

english_verse: When the Israelite soldiers saw Goliath, they were scared and ran off.
translation_verse: Israɛl be benapo na ka wu Goliɛf, nɛ kufu pɛ bumo nɛ bumo kikɛ shile.

english_verse: They said to each other, “Look how he keeps coming out to insult us. The king is offering a big reward to the man who kills Goliath. That man will even get to marry the king's daughter, and no one in his family will ever have to pay taxes again.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ b kaŋɛ abar le: “Men keni, kananɛ kanyɛn ere bee ba kaa to anyi emaŋ nsaa tege anyi. Esa kama nɛ e tiŋ m mɔ mo, ewura na beeŋ sa mo kakɛ gboŋ. E beeŋ ta mo pibiche n sa mo nɛ e kil nɛ mbe kanaŋ malɛ kikɛ gba maaŋ naŋ ka lampo kikɛ ashi Israɛl be efuli so.”

english_verse: David asked some soldiers standing nearby, “What will a man get for killing this Philistine and stopping him from insulting our people? Who does that worthless Philistine think he is? He's making fun of the army of the living God!”
translation_verse: Nɛ Deevid bishi benapo nɛ b yili n taga mo to na le: “Manɛ nɛ baaŋ sa esa kama nɛ e beeŋ mɔ Filisti be esa ere nseŋ lara Israɛl ashi le be anishinyɔr ere to? Kanyamase jiga ere malɛ e la wanɛ nɛ e bee keni Ebɔrɛ nɛ e wɔ ŋkpa to na be benapo jiga?”

english_verse: The soldiers told David what the king would give the man who killed Goliath.
translation_verse: Nɛ b kaŋɛ mo kusɔ nɛ ewura na beeŋ wora n sa esa kama nɛ e mɔ Goliɛf.

english_verse: David's oldest brother Eliab heard him talking with the soldiers. Eliab was angry with him and said, “What are you doing here, anyway? Who's taking care of your little flock of sheep out in the desert? You spoiled brat! You came here just to watch the fighting, didn't you?”
translation_verse: Deevid mo da Eliab ka nu Deevid nɛ benapo na ka bee malga, nɛ agbo pɛ Eliab ga nɛ e kaŋɛ le: “Manɛ nɛ fee fin nfe? Wanɛ nɛ fo yige fo mbolpɔ kiyi na to n sa fanɛ e ba keni so? Fo kebia kpeŋso ere! Fo ba nfe nna nɛ fo baa keni kananɛ baa kɔ kena, ŋko?”

english_verse: “Now what have I done?” David answered. “Can't I even ask a question?”
translation_verse: Nɛ Deevid malɛ bishi le: “Manɛ nɛ n wora? Ama m maŋ kɔ ekpa nɛ m bishi shɛŋ a?”

english_verse: Then he turned and asked another soldier the same thing he had asked the others, and he got the same answer.
translation_verse: Nɛ e naŋ bishi enapo ko loŋ be kesheŋ koŋwule na. Saŋkama malɛ nɛ e baŋ bishi kesheŋ na, kusɔ koŋwule nɛ e nu na gbagba chap nɛ baa kaŋɛ mo.

english_verse: Some soldiers overheard David talking, so they told Saul what David had said. Saul sent for David, and David came.
translation_verse: Benapo na be beko ka nu kusɔ nɛ Deevid kaŋɛ na, nɛ b ya kaŋɛ Sɔɔl. Ndoŋ nna nɛ Sɔɔl shuŋi nɛ b ya tre Deevid.

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” he said, “this Philistine shouldn't turn us into cowards. I'll go out and fight him myself!”
translation_verse: Nɛ Deevid kaŋɛ Sɔɔl le: “Yiramu! Men sa maŋ shin nɛ Filisti be kanyɛn na e ta anyi ŋ ki befupo. Ma ere beeŋ ya tu mo ŋ kɔ.”

english_verse: “You don't have a chance against him,” Saul replied. “You're only a boy, and he's been a soldier all his life.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Sɔɔl kaŋɛ le: “M-m, fo maaŋ tiŋ n tu kanyɛn ere ŋ kɔ kikɛ, ŋkpal manɛ so kabrantiɛbia e kraa la fo, ama kanyɛn ere bre be kebia to kikɛ nɛ e kɔ kena hale m ba fo kabre!”

english_verse: But David told him: Your Majesty, I take care of my father's sheep. And when one of them is dragged off by a lion or a bear,
translation_verse: Nɛ Deevid kaŋɛ le: “Yiramu! Mee keni n tuto be mbolpɔ so nna. Saŋkama malɛ nɛ buluŋ ŋko shishiri baŋ pɛ mbolpɔ na be kekama,

english_verse: I go after it and beat the wild animal until it lets the sheep go. If the wild animal turns and attacks me, I grab it by the throat and kill it.
translation_verse: mee shile nna m bɛ kumo so n ya sɔ kubolpɔ na. Nɛ buluŋ na ŋko shishiri na baŋ kilgi n tu ma, mee pɛ kumo be kubɔ to nna n nyaŋ kumo m mɔ.

english_verse: Sir, I have killed lions and bears that way, and I can kill this worthless Philistine. He shouldn't have made fun of the army of the living God!
translation_verse: M mɔ ebuluŋ nɛ eshishiri kikɛ, amoso loŋ be ekpa koŋwule na so nɛ meeŋ bɔla so m mɔ Filisti be kanyamasenyɛn nɛ e bee keni Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ e wɔ ŋkpa to na be benapo jiga na.

english_verse: The Lord has rescued me from the claws of lions and bears, and he will keep me safe from the hands of this Philistine. “All right,” Saul answered, “go ahead and fight him. And I hope the Lord will help you.”
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ka baŋ mɔlga ma ashi ebuluŋ nɛ eshishiri to ere bre, e beeŋ mɔlga ma ashi Filisti be kanyɛn ere gba be enɔ to.” Nɛ Sɔɔl malɛ kaŋɛ mo le: “Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na beeŋ chɛ fo to, amoso baa yɔ n ya kɔ mo.”

english_verse: Saul had his own military clothes and armor put on David, and he gave David a bronze helmet to wear.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Sɔɔl ta mbe kenyɛnkale n sa Deevid fanɛ e buu. E daŋ ta mbe danyaŋ be kekpaŋwuro gba nna n sa mo fanɛ e buu.

english_verse: David strapped on a sword and tried to walk around, but he was not used to wearing those things. “I can't move with all this stuff on,” David said. “I'm just not used to it.” David took off the armor
translation_verse: Nɛ Deevid ta Sɔɔl be tokobi n di n deŋi akɔsɔ nɛ e buu na so, nseŋ wora ania nɛ e nite, ama e nite ŋ gben ŋkpal amo be kebuu ka maŋ deŋ mo so. Nɛ e kaŋɛ Sɔɔl le: “Ma ere maaŋ tiŋ m buu le be asɔ n yɔ kena to, ŋkpal manɛ so amo be kebuu maŋ deŋ ma.” Nseŋ gbaŋ asɔ na kikɛ.

english_verse: When Goliath saw that David was just a healthy, good-looking boy, he made fun of him.
translation_verse: keni n wu fanɛ e la kabrantiɛbia nna nsaa walɛ kayɛrbi, nɛ e wora mo eyurto

english_verse: “Do you think I'm a dog?” Goliath asked. “Is that why you've come after me with a stick?” He cursed David in the name of the Philistine gods
translation_verse: ŋ kaŋɛ Deevid le: “Jɔnɔ e la ma nɛ fee ta ndibi a ba ŋ kutɔ a?” Nɛ e melgi Deevid n sa Filistiebi na be agbir.

english_verse: and shouted, “Come on! When I'm finished with you, I'll feed you to the birds and wild animals!”
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e ponte ŋ kaŋɛ Deevid le: “Ba nfe, nɛ m mɔ fo, n ta fo eyur ere n sa mbuibi nɛ kupuŋ to be asɔbɔya nɛ b ji!”

english_verse: David answered: You've come out to fight me with a sword and a spear and a dagger. But I've come out to fight you in the name of the Lord All-Powerful. He is the God of Israel's army, and you have insulted him too!
translation_verse: Nɛ Deevid kaŋɛ mo le: “Fo ere ta tokobi nɛ kekpa nɛ chutre nna m ba nɛ fo ba kɔ ma, ama ma ere ba nna nɛ m ba kɔ fo ashi Enyɛnpetale nɛ e la Israɛl be benapo be Ebɔrɛ mo nɛ fee keni jiga na be ketre to.

english_verse: Today the Lord will help me defeat you. I'll knock you down and cut off your head, and I'll feed the bodies of the other Philistine soldiers to the birds and wild animals. Then the whole world will know that Israel has a real God.
translation_verse: Kabre be kachɛ ere, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ beeŋ ta fo m bɔɔ ma enɔ nɛ m pɔɔ fo so ŋ ku fo kumu ere, nseŋ ta Filisti be benapo be eyurana n sa mbuibi nɛ kupuŋ to be asɔbɔya nɛ b ji. Saŋɛ na so nɛ durnya kikɛ e pin fanɛ Ebɔrɛ wɔ Israɛlebi kutɔ.

english_verse: Everybody here will see that the Lord doesn't need swords or spears to save his people. The Lord always wins his battles, and he will help us defeat you.
translation_verse: Ekama malɛ nfe beeŋ pin fanɛ mannɛ etokobi ŋko akpa nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na bee ta a kɔ a mɔlga mbe basa. E la ekɔmpɔɔsopo kena kikɛ to nna. Mo alɛ beeŋ chɛ anyi to nɛ an kɔ m pɔɔ menyi so.”

english_verse: He put a rock in his sling and swung the sling around by its straps. When he let go of one strap, the rock flew out and hit Goliath on the forehead. It cracked his skull, and he fell facedown on the ground.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Deevid lara kejembu mbe kɔlgu na to n wɔtɔ mbe ketababu to n to Goliɛf nɛ k ŋmɛa mbe kasɔto m bure n luri nɛ e tɔr mbe epun so.

english_verse: David defeated Goliath with a sling and a rock. He killed him without even using a sword.
translation_verse: Ketababu nɛ kejembu nɛ Deevid daŋ ta m pɔɔ Goliɛf so. E daa maŋ ta tokobi.

english_verse: David ran over and pulled out Goliath's sword. Then he used it to cut off Goliath's head. When the Philistines saw what had happened to their hero, they started running away.
translation_verse: Deevid daŋ shile nna n ya pe Goliɛf be tokobi ashi kumo be efar to ŋ ku Goliɛf be kumu. Filistiebi na ka wu fanɛ bumo kikɛ to be elempo na wu, nɛ b lara keya n shile.

english_verse: But the soldiers of Israel and Judah let out a battle cry and went after them as far as Gath and Ekron. The bodies of the Philistines were scattered all along the road from Shaaraim to Gath and Ekron.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Israɛl nɛ Juda be benapo cha awɔr ga nseŋ shile n ju m buu Filistiebi na so hale n ya fo Filisti be nde nɛ baa tre Gaaf nɛ Ekrɔn be mbunagboŋ na. Nɛ Filistiebi wu n dese Shaaraim be ekpa na to hale n ya fo Gaaf nɛ Ekrɔn.

english_verse: When the Israelite army returned from chasing the Philistines, they took what they wanted from the enemy camp.
translation_verse: Israɛl be benapo na ka yige kebaaju Filistiebi na, nɛ b bɛta m ba bumo doŋana na be keeyi to m baa muu bumo be asɔ.

english_verse: David took Goliath's head to Jerusalem, but he kept Goliath's weapons in his own tent. David Becomes One of Saul's Officers
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Deevid ta Goliɛf be kumu na n yɔ Jerusalɛm, nseŋ ta mbe akɔsɔ na bre n nase mo ere Deevid be wajɛbu to. B ka bar Deevid m ba sa ewura Sɔɔl be asheŋ

english_verse: After King Saul had watched David go out to fight Goliath, Saul turned to the commander of his army and said, “Abner, who is that young man?” “Your Majesty,” Abner answered, “I swear by your life that I don't know.”
translation_verse: Saŋɛ nɛ Deevid daa yɔ nɛ e ya kɔ Goliɛf na, nɛ Sɔɔl bishi mbe benapo be enimu Abna le: “Abna, wanɛ pibinyɛn nde?” Nɛ Abna yɛ: “Yiramu, m maŋ nyi.”

english_verse: “Then find out!” Saul told him.
translation_verse: Nɛ Sɔɔl kaŋɛ le: “Kumo ere fo ya bishi to n nu.”

english_verse: and Saul asked, “Who are you?” “I am David the son of Jesse, a loyal Israelite from Bethlehem.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Sɔɔl bishi mo le: “Wanɛ pibinyɛn e la fo?” Nɛ Deevid yɛ: “Fo kayɛrbi Jɛsi nɛ e shi Bɛtlɛhɛm na pibinyɛn e la ma.”

english_verse: From that time on, Saul kept David in his service and would not let David go back to his own family.
translation_verse: Baŋ yili kumo be kachɛ na kikɛ Sɔɔl daŋ shin nna nɛ Deevid wɔ mo kutɔ. Mo alɛ daa maŋ sa mo ekpa nɛ e bɛta n yɔ mo tuto be laŋ to.

english_verse: Jonathan liked David so much that they promised to always be loyal friends.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal Jonatan malɛ ka bee sha Deevid ga so, e daŋ shin nna nɛ b nase keteri kpakpaso be kɔnɔ n sa abar.

english_verse: Jonathan took off the robe that he was wearing and gave it to David. He also gave him his military clothes, his sword, his bow and arrows, and his belt.
translation_verse: Nɛ Jonatan lara mbe piŋi nɛ e buu na n sa Deevid. E daŋ ta mbe kenyɛnkale gba nɛ mbe tokobi nɛ mbe keta nɛ amo be atanyembi nɛ mbe kreso n ti so nna n sa mo.

english_verse: David was a success in everything that Saul sent him to do, and Saul made him a high officer in his army. That pleased everyone, including Saul's other officers. Saul Becomes David's Enemy
translation_verse: Deevid daa ji kɔŋkɔŋ kusɔ kama nɛ Sɔɔl daa shuŋi mo fanɛ e ya wora to nna. Nɛ Sɔɔl ta mo ŋ ki mbe benapo be enimu gboŋ ko. Kumo be loŋ daŋ wora ekama nɛ Sɔɔl be benapo be benimu na kikɛ ebel ga. Sɔɔl ka bee kɔ Deevid kukɔrkɔ be asheŋ

english_verse: David had killed Goliath, the battle was over, and the Israelite army set out for home. As the army went along, women came out of each Israelite town to welcome King Saul. They were celebrating by singing songs and dancing to the music of tambourines and harps.
translation_verse: Deevid ka mɔ Goliɛf, nɛ benapo na bɛta a ba epe na, nɛ beche nɛ b shi Israɛl be nde karso na kikɛ lar a ba nɛ b ba chɔrɔ ewura Sɔɔl. B daa boŋ kagbenefuli be nshɛ nna nsaa laŋ echakachaka nɛ ejaŋjilaŋ a foŋ nlopi a cha.

english_verse: They sang: Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand!
translation_verse: Le be kashɛ nɛ beche na daa boŋ a cha: “Sɔɔl mɔ basa kagboŋ, ama Deevid bre mɔ basa ŋgboŋ kudu.”

english_verse: This song made Saul very angry, and he thought, “They are saying that David has killed ten times more enemies than I ever did. Next they will want to make him king.”
translation_verse: Nɛ bumo be kashɛ na shin nɛ Sɔɔl nya agbo ga n fɛ le: “B kaa bee kaŋɛ fanɛ Deevid mɔ basa ŋgboŋ kudu nɛ ma ere mɔ kagboŋ nawule ere, kusɔ nɛ k ka e la keta mo ŋ ki ewura.”

english_verse: The next day the Lord let an evil spirit take control of Saul, and he began acting like a crazy man inside his house. David came to play the harp for Saul as usual, but this time Saul had a spear in his hand.
translation_verse: Kumo be ŋklade nɛ Ebɔrɛ sa ekpa nɛ kiyoyu lubi ko ba luri Sɔɔl to eleŋso nɛ e fara a wora fanɛ ebompo ashi mbe laŋ to. Nɛ Deevid ba kaa laŋ jaŋjilaŋ a sa mo fanɛ kananɛ e chɛr a wora karechɛ kama na. Loŋ be saŋɛ na so nɛ Sɔɔl kɔ kekpa to.

english_verse: Saul thought, “I'll pin David to the wall.” He threw the spear at David twice, but David dodged and got away both times.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Sɔɔl fɛ fanɛ e beeŋ kpa kekpa na n da Deevid m mata egbal nseŋ kpa mo kumo ale anyɔ kikɛ nɛ Deevid gbar amo kikɛ.

english_verse: Saul was afraid of David, because the Lord was helping David and was no longer helping him.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Sɔɔl fara a ŋana Deevid ŋkpal Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ka daa chɛ Deevid to nseŋ kplaŋ mo ere Sɔɔl so so.

english_verse: The Lord helped David, and he and his soldiers always won their battles.
translation_verse: Saŋkama malɛ nɛ Deevid baŋ yɔ kena to, e daa kɔ nna a pɔɔ so ŋkpal Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ka daa wɔ mo kutɔ so.

english_verse: One day, Saul told David, “If you'll be brave and fight the Lord's battles for me, I'll let you marry my oldest daughter Merab.” But Saul was really thinking, “I don't want to kill David myself, so I'll let the Philistines do it for me.”
translation_verse: Kachako nɛ Sɔɔl kaŋɛ Deevid le: “Nɛ feeŋ nya kenyɛn a kɔ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be ana a sa ma bre, kumo ere ma alɛ beeŋ ta m pibiche nimuso Mɛrab n sa fo.” Sɔɔl be nfɛra e daa la fanɛ nɛ e wora loŋ, Filistiebi na beeŋ nya Deevid m mɔ, saŋɛ na so k maaŋ ba fanɛ mo e mɔ mo.

english_verse: But when the time came for David to marry Saul's daughter Merab, Saul told her to marry Adriel from the town of Meholah.
translation_verse: Ama k ka ba fo jemanɛ nɛ k daga fanɛ Mɛrab e kil Deevid na, nɛ Sɔɔl kaŋɛ fanɛ e ya kil kanyɛn nɛ baa tre Adriɛl nɛ e shi Mɛhola na.

english_verse: Saul had another daughter. Her name was Michal, and Saul found out that she was in love with David. This made Saul happy,
translation_verse: Sɔɔl daa kɔ ebiche ko gba nɛ baa tre mo Mikaal nɛ e daa sha Deevid ga. Sɔɔl ka nu loŋ, nɛ mbe kagbene fuli mo.

english_verse: and he thought, “I'll tell David he can marry Michal, but I'll set it up so that the Philistines will kill him.” He told David, “I'm going to give you a second chance to marry one of my daughters.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ e fɛ le: “Meeŋ kaŋɛ Deevid nɛ e ta Mikaal ŋ ki mbe eche, ama mee sha nna nɛ n wora loŋ saŋɛ na so Filistiebi na beeŋ mɔ mo.” Kede e ti so kela nyɔsopo Sɔɔl ka kaŋɛ fanɛ Deevid beeŋ ki mo sha.

english_verse: Saul ordered his officials to speak to David in private, so they went to David and said, “Look, the king likes you, and all of his officials are loyal to you. Why not ask the king if you can marry his daughter Michal?” “I'm not rich or famous enough to marry princess Michal!” David answered.
translation_verse: B ka kaŋɛ Deevid loŋ nɛ mo alɛ kaŋɛ le: “K beeŋ ba la bunyaŋ gboŋgboŋi nna n sa ma fanɛ m ba la ewura mo shanyɛn ama mannɛ etirpo nɛ ebɔlpo be asheŋ nna na.”

english_verse: The officials went back to Saul and told him exactly what David had said.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl be benimuana na ka kaŋɛ Sɔɔl kusɔ nɛ Deevid kaŋɛ na,

english_verse: Saul was hoping that the Philistines would kill David, and he told his officials to tell David, “The king doesn't want any silver or gold. He only wants to get even with his enemies. All you have to do is to bring back proof that you have killed
translation_verse: nɛ Sɔɔl kaŋɛ bumo fanɛ b ya kaŋɛ Deevid le: “Keshaji nɛ ewura baa fin fo kutɔ e la fanɛ fo mɔ Filistiebi na be basa kalfa nseŋ ba kaŋɛ ma fanɛ fo wora loŋ. Kumo be loŋ e naŋ ŋini fanɛ an kɔ an doŋana na n tal to.” Kananɛ Sɔɔl bre daŋ kre nna na, saŋɛ na so Filistiebi na beeŋ nya Deevid m mɔ.

english_verse: The officials told David, and David wanted to marry the princess. King Saul had set a time limit, and before it ran out,
translation_verse: Sɔɔl be benimuana na ka kaŋɛ Deevid kusɔ nɛ Sɔɔl kaŋɛ na, nɛ Deevid be kagbene fuli mo ŋkpal e ka bee fɛ fanɛ e beeŋ nya ewura na pibiche n ta so. Amoso pɔɛŋ nɛ kejafɔ achɛ na e fo na

english_verse: King Saul knew that she loved David, and he also realized that the Lord was helping David.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ka pin geeŋ fanɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ wɔ Deevid be kaman nɛ mo pibiche Mikaal malɛ bee sha Deevid ga na

english_verse: But knowing those things made Saul even more afraid of David, and he was David's enemy for the rest of his life.
translation_verse: nɛ e naa ŋana Deevid alegaiso nseŋ ta Deevid ŋ ki mo doŋ hale n ya fo mbe luwu be jemanɛ.

english_verse: The Philistine rulers kept coming to fight Israel, but whenever David fought them, he won. He was famous because he won more battles against the Philistines than any of Saul's other officers.
translation_verse: Saŋkama nɛ Filisti be bewura nɛ benapo nɛ Israɛlebi baa kɔ, Deevid e naa kaa kɔ a pɔɔ so a chɔ Sɔɔl be benapo be benimu na be ekama. Ŋkpal loŋ so, nɛ Deevid be ketre daŋ dii ga.

english_verse: One day, Saul told his son Jonathan and his officers to kill David. But Jonathan and David were best friends,
translation_verse: Sɔɔl daŋ kaŋɛ mo pibinyɛn Jonatan nɛ mbe benimuana fanɛ e bee kre kemɔ Deevid nna, ama Jonatan daa sha Deevid be asheŋ ga.

english_verse: and he warned David, “My father is trying to have you killed, so be very careful. Hide in a field tomorrow morning, and I'll bring him there. Then I'll talk to him about you, and if I find out anything, I'll let you know.”
translation_verse: Meeŋ keta n tuto m ba kakpa nɛ fo ŋana nna m ba malga fo asheŋ n sa mo, kumo be kaman, nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ fo kusɔ kama nɛ k wɔtɔ.”

english_verse: The next morning, Jonathan reminded Saul about the many good things David had done for him. Then he said, “Why do you want to kill David? He hasn't done anything to you. He has served in your army and has always done what's best for you. He even risked his life to kill Goliath. The Lord helped Israel win a great victory that day, and it made you happy.”
translation_verse: E ta mbe kumu gba nna ŋ kpa kelera saŋɛ nɛ e ya mɔ Goliɛf na. Kumo alɛ be loŋ e shin nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kɔ n sɔ Israɛl be basa na. Fo alɛ gba ka wu kumo be loŋ nɛ fo kagbene fuli fo. Nɛ manɛ e ba nɛ fee sha kewora esa nɛ e maŋ wora shɛŋ kulubi hale a fin Deevid nɛ fo mɔ kenyanyaŋɛso?”

english_verse: Saul agreed and promised, “I swear by the living Lord that I won't have David killed!”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Sɔɔl nu kusɔ nɛ Jonatan kaŋɛ na nseŋ nase kɔnɔ fanɛ ŋkpal Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ka la mbe shɛdajipo so, e maaŋ mɔ Deevid.

english_verse: Jonathan went to David and told him what Saul had said. Then he brought David to Saul, and David served in Saul's army just as he had done before.
translation_verse: Amoso Jonatan daŋ tre Deevid nna ŋ kaŋɛ mo kusɔ kama nɛ k wɔtɔ nseŋ keta mo n yɔ Sɔɔl kutɔ nɛ e ya ka shuŋ mo kananɛ e daa shuŋ mo na.

english_verse: The next time there was a war with the Philistines, David fought hard and forced them to retreat. Michal Helps David Escape
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ kena naŋ koso Israɛlebi nɛ Filistiebi na be kefɛato. Nɛ Deevid nɛ mbe benapo kɔ Filistiebi be benapo na eleŋso m pɔɔ bumo so nɛ b shile.

english_verse: One night, David was in Saul's home, playing the harp for him. Saul was sitting there, holding a spear, when an evil spirit from the Lord took control of him. Saul tried to pin David to the wall with the spear, but David dodged, and it stuck in the wall. David ran out of the house and escaped.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Sɔɔl kpa kekpa na nɛ e da Deevid m mata egbal nɛ Deevid gbar, nɛ kekpa na ya da egbal na m muni. Kumo be kanyɛso na kikɛ nɛ Deevid shile n lar Sɔɔl be laŋ to nɛ shɛŋ maŋ wora mo.

english_verse: Saul sent guards to watch David's house all night and then to kill him in the morning. Michal, David's wife, told him, “If you don't escape tonight, they'll kill you tomorrow!”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Sɔɔl shuŋi mbe basa fanɛ b ya kulti Deevid be laŋ n wɔtɔ, kare kaŋ chɛ kachipurso nɛ b mɔ mo. Nɛ Deevid be eche Mikaal kpele mo kusoe ŋ kaŋɛ le: “Fo baa maŋ shile kanyɛ ere, echefo baaŋ mɔ fo.”

english_verse: She helped David leave through a window and climb down to the ground. As David ran off,
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Mikaal chɛ Deevid to nɛ e bɔla tokuro to n lar n shile.

english_verse: Michal put a statue in his bed. She put goat hair on its head and dressed it in some of David's clothes.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mikaal ta kedibi ko nɛ b shɛl kumo fanɛ kegbir na n ya nase gedo so nseŋ ta kaboe be afuibi n deŋi kumo be kumu so nseŋ ta wajɛ m buu kumo be eyur so.

english_verse: The next morning, Saul sent guards to arrest David. But Michal told them, “David is sick.”
translation_verse: Sɔɔl be basa na ka ba nɛ b ba pɛ Deevid, nɛ Mikaal kaŋɛ bumo fanɛ Deevid bee lɔ nna.

english_verse: When the guards went in, all they found in the bed was the statue with the goat hair on its head.
translation_verse: Basa na ka luri Deevid be ebu to, kedibi nɛ b shɛl fanɛ kegbir na nɛ b ya wu mbe gedo so nɛ kaboe be afuibi deŋ kumo be kumu so.

english_verse: “Why have you tricked me this way?” Saul asked Michal. “You helped my enemy get away!” She answered, “He said he would kill me if I didn't help him escape!” Samuel Helps David Escape
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Sɔɔl tre Mikaal m bishi mo le: “Manɛ nna nɛ fo fule ma nɛ ma doŋ nya ekpa n shile?” Nɛ Mikaal kaŋɛ le: “E yɛ, nɛ m baa maŋ chɛ mo to nɛ e shile, e beeŋ mɔ ma.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, David went to Samuel at Ramah and told him what Saul had done. Then Samuel and David went to Prophets Village and stayed there.
