translation_verse: Deevid daŋ shile n yɔ Samuɛl kutɔ nna ashi Raama n ya kaŋɛ mo kusɔ nɛ Sɔɔl wora mo. Ndoŋ nna nɛ mo nɛ Samuɛl yɔ Nayɔf n ya ka wɔ ndoŋ.

english_verse: Someone told Saul, “David is at Prophets Village in Ramah.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Sɔɔl nu fanɛ Deevid wɔ Nayɔf nɛ k mata Raama na,

english_verse: Saul sent a few soldiers to bring David back. They went to Ramah and found Samuel in charge of a group of prophets who were all prophesying. Then the Spirit of God took control of the soldiers and they started prophesying too.
translation_verse: nseŋ shuŋi basa fanɛ b ya pɛ Deevid m ba. Basa na ka yɔ Raama nɛ b ya wu anebiana be katuŋ ko nɛ bumo nɛ Samuɛl nɛ e la bumo kikɛ be enimu na bee wu abɔrɛsheŋ a malga. Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ebɔrɛ be kiyoyu na ba luri Sɔɔl be basa na gba to nɛ bumo alɛ gba fara a wu asheŋ a malga.

english_verse: When Saul heard what had happened, he sent some more soldiers, but they prophesied just like the first group. He sent a third group of soldiers, but the same thing happened to them.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ka nu loŋ na nɛ e naŋ shuŋi mbɔ damta ko ndoŋ nɛ bumo alɛ gba fara a wu abɔrɛsheŋ a malga. Nɛ e naŋ shuŋi mbɔ be katuŋ sasopo, nɛ bumo alɛ gba ya wora loŋ koŋwule na.

english_verse: Finally, Saul left for Ramah himself. He went as far as the deep pit at the town of Secu, and he asked, “Where are Samuel and David?” “At Prophets Village in Ramah,” the people answered.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ mo gbagba koso a yɔ Raama. E ka ya fo ketirbu gboŋgboŋi ko ase ashi Seku nseŋ bishi Samuɛl nɛ Deevid be asheŋ, nɛ b kaŋɛ mo fanɛ b wɔ Nayɔf nɛ k mata Raama na.

english_verse: Saul left for Ramah. But as he walked along, the Spirit of God took control of him, and he started prophesying. Then, when he reached Prophets Village,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna, nɛ Ebɔrɛ be kiyoyu gbelge mo so nɛ mo alɛ gba fara a wu abɔrɛsheŋ a malga hale n ya fo Nayɔf.

english_verse: he stripped off his clothes and prophesied in front of Samuel. He dropped to the ground and lay there naked all that day and night. That's how the saying started, “Is Saul now a prophet?”
translation_verse: Sɔɔl daŋ yili Samuɛl gba be anishito n wu abɔrɛsheŋ ŋ kaŋɛ hale ŋ gbaŋ mbe epiŋi n le. Yili kachipurso kikɛ nɛ e daŋ baŋ delgeso n tɔr a dese Samuɛl be anishito hale n ya fo kanyɛso. Kananɛ k ji nna nɛ basa bee bishi le na: “Sɔɔl gba naŋ ki anebi nna a?”

english_verse: David escaped from Prophets Village. Then he ran to see Jonathan and asked, “Why does your father Saul want to kill me? What have I done wrong?”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Deevid shile n lar Nayɔf nɛ k wɔ Raama na n yɔ Jonatan kutɔ n ya bishi mo le: “Manɛ nɛ n wora fo tuto Sɔɔl nɛ e bee sha kemɔ ma? Manɛ be kulubi nɛ n wora?”

english_verse: “My father can't be trying to kill you! He never does anything without telling me about it. Why would he hide this from me? It can't be true!”
translation_verse: Nɛ Jonatan kaŋɛ le: “Ebɔrɛ maaŋ shuli gba nɛ n tuto e mɔ fo. E maa ta kusɔ kama a ŋana ma so. Kede bre nɛ e beeŋ ta ŋ ŋana ma so a? K maŋ la kashenteŋ!”

english_verse: “Jonathan, I swear it's true! But your father knows how much you like me, and he didn't want to break your heart. That's why he didn't tell you. I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I'm only one step ahead of death.”
translation_verse: Ama le nɛ Deevid daŋ kaŋɛ: “Fo tuto gba nyi kananɛ fee sha ma ga, amoso nɛ e yili kumo fanɛ e maaŋ kaŋɛ fo kusɔ nɛ e kre na, saŋɛ na so fo kagbene maaŋ jija fo ga. Fo nɛ Ebɔrɛ e la ma shɛdajipo fanɛ ma nɛ luwu maŋ naa wɔ kufɔ!”

english_verse: Then Jonathan said, “Tell me what to do, and I'll do it.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Jonatan kaŋɛ Deevid le: “Kusɔ kama nɛ fee sha, meeŋ wora kumo n sa fo.”

english_verse: David answered: Tomorrow is the New Moon Festival, and I'm supposed to eat dinner with your father. But instead, I'll hide in a field until the evening of the next day.
translation_verse: Nɛ Deevid kaŋɛ le: “Echefo e la kufɔl popɔr be kachɛ sososo be kejigboŋ na, nɛ k daga fanɛ ŋ ka ya tu fo tuto n ji, ama m maaŋ wora loŋ. Meeŋ yɔ kupuŋ to n ya fin kakpa ko ŋ ŋana n ya fo eklade be kaaseso.

english_verse: If Saul wonders where I am, tell him, “David asked me to let him go to his hometown of Bethlehem, so he could take part in a sacrifice his family makes there every year.”
translation_verse: Sɔɔl kaa fin ma, fo kaŋɛ mo fanɛ ŋ kule fo ekpa nna m bɛta n yɔ ma kade to Bɛtlɛhɛm nɛ n ya tu ma basa n lara kafɛ kikɛ be sarga nɛ baa lara ndoŋ na.

english_verse: If your father says it's all right, then I'm safe. But if he gets angry, you'll know he wants to harm me.
translation_verse: Nɛ e kaŋ maŋ kaŋɛ shɛŋ bre, kumo ere meeŋ nya ma kumu ama e kaŋ nya agbo bre kumo ere, e nya ma, e beeŋ tɔrɔ ma.

english_verse: Be kind to me. After all, it was your idea to promise the Lord that we would always be loyal friends. If I've done anything wrong, kill me yourself, but don't hand me over to your father.
translation_verse: Jande, wora ma kechɛto nseŋ bɛ kɔnɔ nɛ ma nɛ fo yili Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be ketre so n nase na so. Nɛ n wora kulubi nna, kumo ere fo gbagba mɔ ma bɔ fo ka ta ma n sa fo tuto nɛ e mɔ.”

english_verse: “Don't worry,” Jonathan said. “If I find out that my father wants to kill you, I'll certainly let you know.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Jonatan yɛ: “Kare gba! Nɛ n daa nyi fanɛ n tuto bee fin fo nna kashenteŋto nɛ e mɔ, dafanɛ maŋ kaŋɛ fo a?”

english_verse: “Let's go out to this field, and I'll tell you,” Jonathan answered. When they got there,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Jonatan kaŋɛ mo le: “Shin nɛ an yɔ kupuŋ to nɛ n ya kaŋɛ fo kusɔ ko.” B ka yɔ na,

english_verse: Jonathan said: I swear by the Lord God of Israel, that two days from now I'll know what my father is planning. Of course I'll let you know if he's friendly toward you.
translation_verse: nɛ Jonatan kaŋɛ le: “Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ e la Israɛl be Ebɔrɛ nsaa la ma shɛdajipo na be eleŋto, ta n ya ka fo eklade saŋɛ ere so nɛ m pin kusɔ nɛ n tuto bee fɛ. E kaa fɛ fo nfɛra lela, meeŋ kaŋɛ fo.

english_verse: But if he wants to harm you, I promise to tell you and help you escape. And I ask the Lord to punish me severely if I don't keep my promise. I pray that the Lord will bless you, just as he used to bless my father.
translation_verse: Nɛ fanɛ e bee sha ketɔrɔ fo malɛ nna, meeŋ kaŋɛ fo nseŋ chɛ fo to nɛ fo shile ŋ ŋana mo so. Nɛ ma alɛ kaa maŋ wora loŋ, kumo ere Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e gberge ma kusoe. Ma kabɔrɛkule e la fanɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e chɛ fo to fanɛ kananɛ e chɛ n tuto to na,

english_verse: Someday the Lord will wipe out all of your enemies. Then if I'm still alive, please be as kind to me as the Lord has been. But if I'm dead, be kind to my family.
translation_verse: kumo ere fo wora ma kanaŋ kelela. Hale nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ mur fo doŋana kikɛ gba, baa kraa wora ma kanaŋ kelela.

english_verse: Jonathan and David made an agreement that even David's descendants would have to keep. Then Jonathan said, “I pray that the Lord will take revenge on your descendants if they break our promise.”
translation_verse: Anyi be kɔnɔ nɛ an nase n sa abar na maaŋ jija kikɛ. Nɛ k baŋ jija malɛ, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e gberge fo kusoe.”

english_verse: Jonathan thought as much of David as he did of himself, so he asked David to promise once more that he would be a loyal friend.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal Jonatan ka daa sha Deevid fanɛ kananɛ e bee sha mo gbagba be kumu so e daŋ shin nɛ Deevid nase kɔnɔ kela nyɔsopo nna n sa mo fanɛ e beeŋ baa la mo teri kpakpaso.

english_verse: After this Jonathan said: Tomorrow is the New Moon Festival, and people will wonder where you are, because your place at the table will be empty.
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ Jonatan kaŋɛ le: Echefo e la kufɔl popɔr be kachɛ sososo be kejigboŋ na, fo alɛ baa maŋ yɔ ndoŋ, ekama nyam beeŋ pin fo ka maŋ wɔ ndoŋ.

english_verse: By the day after tomorrow, everyone will think you've been gone a long time. Then go to the place where you hid before and stay beside Going-Away Rock.
translation_verse: Eklade be kaaseso bre nɛ baaŋ pin ga fanɛ fo maŋ wɔtɔ, amoso naŋ yɔ kakpa nɛ fo daŋ ŋana saŋɛ so nɛ le be asheŋ ere kikɛ fara na, n ya ŋana ajembu nɛ a deŋ abar so kululu na ase.

english_verse: I'll shoot three arrows at a target off to the side of the rock,
translation_verse: Meeŋ to atanyembi asa n yɔ ajembu nɛ a deŋ abar so kululu na ase fanɛ ŋ ka bee to kusɔ ko na.

english_verse: and send my servant to find the arrows. You'll know if it's safe to come out by what I tell him. If it is safe, I swear by the living Lord that I'll say, “The arrows are on this side of you! Pick them up!”
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ n shuŋi ma kayɛrbi fanɛ e ya fin atanyembi na. Nɛ ŋ kaŋ baŋ kaŋɛ mo le: “Keni atanyembi na e dese fo anishito na, ta amo,” kumo ere shɛŋ maaŋ wora fo nna na, feeŋ tiŋ n lar a ba. Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e la ma shɛdajipo fanɛ shɛŋ maaŋ wora fo.

english_verse: But if it isn't safe, I'll say to the boy, “The arrows are farther away!” This will mean that the Lord wants you to leave, and you must go.
translation_verse: Ama nɛ m baŋ kaŋɛ mo fanɛ: “Keni atanyembi na e dese kufɔ ndoŋ ere nna, kumo ere Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na bee sha fanɛ fo baa yɔ nna na, nɛ fo baa yɔ.”

english_verse: But he will always watch us to make sure that we keep the promise we made to each other.
translation_verse: Anyi be kɔnɔ nɛ an nase n sa abar na bre, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na gbagba beeŋ chɛ anyi to nɛ an bɛ kumo so mbaanaayɔ.

english_verse: So David hid there in the field. During the New Moon Festival, Saul sat down to eat
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Deevid ya ŋana kupuŋ to. Kachɛ nɛ baa ji kufɔl popɔr be kachɛ sososo be kejigboŋ na nɛ Sɔɔl ba kejigboŋ na to

english_verse: by the wall, just as he always did. Jonathan sat across from him, and Abner sat next to him. But David's place was empty.
translation_verse: nseŋ ya chena kakpa nɛ e bee kaa chena na ŋ gbasa egbal nɛ Abna chena m bɛ mo so nɛ Jonatan malɛ chena ŋ kilgi anishito n shoŋi mo, ama esa kikɛ daa maŋ chena Deevid bre be kakpa na.

english_verse: Saul didn't say anything that day, because he was thinking, “Something must have happened to make David unfit to be at the Festival. Yes, something must have happened.”
translation_verse: Kumo be kamɔnchɛ na Sɔɔl daa maŋ kaŋɛ shɛŋ ŋkpal manɛ so e daa fɛ nna fanɛ, ashere Deevid wora n da daŋkare be ekishi ko so nna so nɛ e maŋ tiŋ n wea bumo to.

english_verse: The day after the New Moon Festival, when David's place was still empty, Saul asked Jonathan, “Why hasn't that son of Jesse come to eat with us? He wasn't here yesterday, and he still isn't here today!”
translation_verse: B ka ji kufɔl popɔr be kachɛ sososo be kejigboŋ na ŋklade nɛ esa kama kraa maŋ tase Deevid be kakpa na, nɛ Sɔɔl bishi Jonatan le: “Manɛ nna nɛ Deevid maŋ ba kejigboŋ na to ndre nɛ kabre kikɛ?”

english_verse: Jonathan answered, “The reason David hasn't come to eat with you is that he begged me to let him go to Bethlehem. He said, ‘Please let me go. My family is offering a sacrifice, and my brother told me I have to be there. Do me this favor and let me slip away to see my brothers.’ ”
translation_verse: E yɛ, ‘Jande, shin nɛ n yɔ Bɛtlɛhɛm, ŋkpal manɛ so ma kanaŋ bee lara sarga nna kabre, amoso nɛ mee sha fanɛ ma alɛ gba e ba wɔ ndoŋ. Nɛ fanɛ n la fo teri gbagba nna bre, kumo ere fo sa ma ekpa nɛ n ya wu ŋ kurgepoana.’ Amoso nɛ e maŋ wɔ fo ejikpa nfe na.”

english_verse: Saul was furious with Jonathan and yelled, “You're no son of mine, you traitor! I know you've chosen to be loyal to that son of Jesse. You should be ashamed of yourself! And your own mother should be ashamed that you were ever born.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Sɔɔl nya agbo ga n wɔtɔ Jonatan nseŋ kaŋɛ mo le: “Fo maŋ naa la m pibinyɛn ŋkpal manɛ so, fo ki edebɔrpo nna! Naniere nɛ m pin fanɛ fo nɛ Deevid e wɔ aya. Fo paŋ anishinyɔr ga. Fo nio kurge fo ŋ gben jiga.

english_verse: You'll never be safe, and your kingdom will be in danger as long as that son of Jesse is alive. Turn him over to me now! He deserves to die!”
translation_verse: Fo maŋ nyi fanɛ nɛ Deevid baa wɔ ŋkpa to, fo maaŋ ji efuli ere be kuwura kikɛ a? Men ya pɛ Deevid m bar ma nfe, ŋkpal manɛ so, e daga luwu!”

english_verse: “Why do you want to kill David?” Jonathan asked. “What has he done?”
translation_verse: Nɛ Jonatan bishi mo tuto le: “Manɛ nɛ Deevid wora nɛ fee sha kemɔ mo?”

english_verse: Saul threw his spear at Jonathan and tried to kill him. Then Jonathan was sure that his father really did want to kill David.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Sɔɔl ta mbe kekpa ŋ kpa Jonatan nɛ e mɔ mo. Ndoŋ nɛ Jonatan pin fanɛ mo tuto daa fin Deevid nna kenishipereso nɛ e mɔ.

english_verse: Jonathan was angry and hurt that his father had insulted David so terribly. He got up, left the table, and didn't eat anything all that day.
translation_verse: Jonatan daŋ nya agbo nna ga ŋkpal mo tuto ka daŋ tege Deevid so so, nseŋ koso ajibi na ase ŋ ka bumo. Mo alɛ daa maŋ naŋ ji shɛŋ kumo be kamɔnchɛ kikɛ.

english_verse: In the morning, Jonathan went out to the field to meet David. He took a servant boy along
translation_verse: Kumo be ŋklade be kachipurso nɛ Jonatan lar n yɔ kupuŋ na to n ya tu Deevid. E daŋ keta kabrantiɛ fɔlbi ko nna n ti mbe kumu so n yɔ.

english_verse: and told him, “When I shoot the arrows, you run and find them for me.” The boy started running, and Jonathan shot an arrow so that it would go beyond him.
translation_verse: B ka bee yɔ na, nɛ e kaŋɛ kebia na le: “M baŋ to atanyembi ere, fo shile manaŋ n ya fin amo m bar ma.” Kabrantiɛbia na ka fara a shile na, nɛ Jonatan to keta na nɛ ketanyembi na ya bɔla kebia na be kumu so n ya tɔr mbe anishito kufɔ.

english_verse: When the boy got near the place where the arrow had landed, Jonathan shouted, “Isn't the arrow on past you?”
translation_verse: Kebrantiɛ fɔlbi na ka ya fo kakpa nɛ ketanyembi na tɔr na, nɛ Jonatan ponte mo so ŋ kaŋɛ mo le: “Baa yɔ! Ketanyembi na kraa dese anishito!

english_verse: Jonathan shouted to him again, “Hurry up! Don't stop!” The boy picked up the arrows and brought them back to Jonathan,
translation_verse: Sa maŋ yili ndoŋ, wora manaŋ!” Ndoŋ nna nɛ kebia na ta ketanyembi na m ba sa mo nyɛnpe Jonatan.

english_verse: but he had no idea about what was going on. Only Jonathan and David knew.
translation_verse: Kebrantiɛ fɔlbi na bre daa maŋ nyi kesheŋ nɛ k wora na be kifito ama Jonatan nɛ Deevid nawule e nyi.

english_verse: Jonathan gave his weapons to the boy and told him, “Take these back into town.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Jonatan ta mbe akɔsɔ n sa kabrantiɛbia na fanɛ e ta amo m bɛta a yɔ kade to.

english_verse: After the boy had gone, David got up from beside the mound and bowed very low three times. Then he and Jonathan kissed each other and cried, but David cried louder.
translation_verse: Kabrantiɛbia na ka yɔ na be kaman, nɛ Deevid koso ashi ajembu nɛ a deŋ abar so kululu na ase n ya jɔŋɛ Jonatan ase ale asa. Nɛ b chɔrɔ abar kashaso nseŋ shu ga. Ama Deevid e daŋ shu ga.

english_verse: Jonathan said, “Take care of yourself. And remember, we each have asked the Lord to watch and make sure that we and our descendants keep our promise forever.” David left and Jonathan went back to town.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Jonatan kaŋɛ Deevid le: “Ebɔrɛ e yɛr fo nɛ alenfia, ama baa nyiŋi kananɛ ma nɛ fo nase kɔnɔ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be ketre to a yɔ anyi be keteri be kaplɛa so n sa abar na. Ebɔrɛ malɛ beeŋ shin nɛ ma kanaŋ nɛ fo kanaŋ e bɛ kɔnɔ naseso ere so hale mbaanaayɔ.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ Deevid choŋ, nɛ Jonatan malɛ bɛta n yɔ kade to.

english_verse: David went to see Ahimelech, a priest who lived in the town of Nob. Ahimelech was trembling with fear as he came out to meet David. “Why are you alone?” Ahimelech asked. “Why isn't anyone else with you?”
translation_verse: Nɛ Deevid yɔ bɔrɛmatapo Ahimɛlɛk kutɔ ashi kade nɛ baa tre Nɔb na. Nɛ Ahimɛlɛk chicha kufuso n lar m ba Deevid kutɔ m ba bishi mo le: “Manɛ nna nɛ fo nawule kpeŋ ba nfe?”

english_verse: “I'm on a mission for King Saul,” David answered. “He ordered me not to tell anyone what the mission is all about, so I ordered my soldiers to stay somewhere else.
translation_verse: Nɛ Deevid kaŋɛ mo le: “Ewura be kushuŋ so nɛ m ba. E kaŋɛ nna fanɛ n sa maŋ kaŋɛ esa kama kusɔ nɛ e shuŋi ma fanɛ m ba wora nfe. Ama ŋ ŋini mbraana na bre kaboŋ ko fanɛ b ba tu ma ndoŋ.

english_verse: Do you have any food you can give me? Could you spare five loaves of bread?”
translation_verse: Manɛ be ajibi nɛ fo kɔ nfe nɛ fo sa ma? Fo maŋ kɔ ebodobodo anu nɛ fo sa ma?”

english_verse: “The only bread I have is the sacred bread,” the priest told David. “You can have it if your soldiers didn't sleep with women last night.”
translation_verse: Nɛ bɔrɛmatapo na kaŋɛ mo le: “Bodobodo cheembi na nawule nɛ ŋ kɔ, ama nɛ fanɛ fo braana na nɛ beche maŋ di keche nɛ kenyɛn nchɛ nyɔ ere bre, feeŋ tiŋ n ta amo.”

english_verse: “Of course we didn't sleep with women,” David answered. “I never let my men do that when we're on a mission. They have to be acceptable to worship God even when we're on a regular mission, and today we're on a special mission.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Deevid yɛ: “Kashenteŋto, b maŋ di beche. Ŋkpal manɛ so hale nɛ anyee yɔ nɛ an ya shuŋ kushuŋ kama gba, b maa wora loŋ. Ama ewura be kushuŋ to bre nɛ baaŋ wora loŋ a?”

english_verse: The only bread the priest had was the sacred bread that he had taken from the place of worship after putting out the fresh loaves. So he gave it to David.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ bɔrɛmatapo na ta bodobodo cheembi nɛ b daŋ deŋi Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be teebɔl cheembi so na nseŋ ta apopɔr n deŋi so na, n sa Deevid ŋkpal manɛ so bodobodo kikɛ daŋ maŋ naa wɔtɔ.

english_verse: It so happened that one of Saul's officers was there, worshiping the Lord that day. His name was Doeg the Edomite, and he was the strongest of Saul's shepherds.
translation_verse: Duɛg nɛ e shi Edɔm be efuli so nsaa la Sɔɔl be mbolpɔkpapo nimuso na gba daŋ ba ndoŋ kumo be kamɔnchɛ nna, nɛ e ba bunyaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ.

english_verse: David asked Ahimelech, “Do you have a spear or a sword? I had to leave so quickly on this mission for the king that I didn't bring along my sword or any other weapons.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Deevid kaŋɛ Ahimɛlɛk le: “Fo kɔ kekpa ŋko tokobi nɛ fo sa ma a? Ewura na ka tre ma eleŋso na e shin nɛ ŋ kuse nseŋ teŋ ma tokobi nɛ ma akɔsɔ na be kekama so.”

english_verse: The priest answered, “The only sword here is the one that belonged to Goliath the Philistine. You were the one who killed him in Elah Valley, and so you can take his sword if you want to. It's wrapped in a cloth behind the statue.” “It's the best sword there is,” David said. “I'll take it!” David Tries To Find Safety in Gath
translation_verse: Nɛ Ahimɛlɛk malɛ kaŋɛ le: “Ŋ kɔ Goliɛf nɛ e la Filisti be esa nɛ fo mɔ ashi Ela be ketaŋɛ to na be tokobi ŋ kutɔ. B ta wajɛ m mɛa kumo so nɛ k wɔ kale lela nɛ baa tre Ɛfɔd na be kaman. Nɛ fee sha fo ta kumo ŋkpal manɛ so kumo nawule e la kekɔsɔ nfe.” Nɛ Deevid kaŋɛ: “Tokobi kama maŋ naa wɔtɔ n fo kumo so. Ta kumo n sa ma.”

english_verse: David kept on running from Saul that day until he came to Gath, where he met with King Achish.
translation_verse: Kumo be kamɔnchɛ na nɛ Deevid fara a shile a ŋana Sɔɔl so hale n yɔ ewura Akish kutɔ ashi Gaaf nɛ k wɔ Filisti be efuli so na.

english_verse: The officers of King Achish were also there, and they asked Achish, “Isn't David a king back in his own country? Don't the Israelites dance and sing, ‘Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand’?”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura na be benimuana na kaŋɛ Akish le: “Mannɛ Deevid ere e la mbe efuli so be ewura na a? Mannɛ mbe asheŋ nɛ beche bee boŋ kashɛ a cha a kaŋɛ fanɛ: ‘Sɔɔl mɔ basa kagboŋ ama Deevid bre mɔ basa ŋgboŋto kudu nna.’ ”

english_verse: David thought about what they were saying, and it made him afraid of Achish.
translation_verse: Bumo be mmalga na daŋ shin nna nɛ Deevid fara a ŋana ewura Akish ga.

english_verse: So right there in front of everyone, he pretended to be insane. He acted confused and started making scratches on the doors of the town gate, while drooling in his beard.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal loŋ so saŋkama nɛ basa baa wɔ mo kutɔ Deevid bee wora fanɛ eboŋ ka dii mo nna. B baŋ yɔ nɛ b ya pɛ mo malɛ e bee yɔ nna n ya ka chaŋ a chaŋ kade na be kabuna to be kukuloŋ gboŋ na so nsaa shin nɛ echɔl bee juye a wurge mbe katɔl so.

english_verse: “Look at him!” Achish said to his officers. “You can see he's crazy. Why did you bring him to me?
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Akish kaŋɛ mbe benimuana le: “Men keni! Kanyɛn na bee lɔ eboŋ nna na. Manɛ nna nɛ men bar mo ŋ kutɔ?

english_verse: I have enough crazy people without your bringing another one here. Keep him away from my palace!”
translation_verse: Bebompo damta tia wɔ kade ere to nɛ manɛ nna nɛ men naŋ keta ede m ba nɛ men ba ti so nɛ e baa wora kawulisheŋ? Men lara mo ma laŋ to!”

english_verse: When David escaped from the town of Gath, he went to Adullam Cave. His brothers and the rest of his family found out where he was, and they followed him there.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Deevid shile Gaaf be kade to n yɔ kebeelaŋ ko nɛ k mata kade nɛ baa tre Adulam na to. Mo daana nɛ mbe kanaŋ nɛ b ka na ka nu fanɛ e wɔ ndoŋ nɛ b yɔ ndoŋ n ya tu mo.

english_verse: A lot of other people joined him too. Some were in trouble, others were angry or in debt, and David was soon the leader of
translation_verse: Basa nɛ b daa ji awurfoŋ na nɛ bumo nɛ b ji akɔ nɛ bumo nɛ asheŋ maa bɔlɔ bumo kenishi na kikɛ daŋ shile nna n yɔ mo kutɔ. Loŋ be basa na daa sa fanɛ basa alfa ana, nɛ Deevid ki bumo be ejuŋkparpo.

english_verse: David left Adullam Cave and went to the town of Mizpeh in Moab, where he talked with the king of Moab. “Please,” David said, “let my father and mother stay with you until I find out what God will do with me.”
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Deevid lar kebeelaŋ nɛ k mata Adulam na to n yɔ Mizpa ashi Mowab be efuli so n ya kaŋɛ Mowab be ewura le: “Jande shin nɛ n tuto nɛ n nio e ba chena fo kutɔ n ya fo saŋɛ nɛ meeŋ wu kusɔ nɛ Ebɔrɛ beeŋ wora n sa ma.”

english_verse: So he brought his parents to the king of Moab, and they stayed with him while David was in hiding.
translation_verse: Nɛ Mowab be ewura na shuli nɛ Deevid shin nɛ mo tuto nɛ mo nio ya kaa wɔ ewura na kutɔ nɛ Deevid bre kraŋ ŋana.

english_verse: One day the prophet Gad told David, “Don't stay here! Go back to Judah.” David then left and went to Hereth Forest. Saul Kills the Priests of the Lord
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ anebi Gad kaŋɛ Deevid le: “Sa maŋ chena nfe. Bɛta n yɔ Juda be kasawule so manaŋ.” Nɛ Deevid lar n yɔ Hɛrɛf be kupo to.

english_verse: Saul was sitting under a small tree on top of the hill at Gibeah when he heard that David and his men had been located. Saul was holding his spear, and his officers were standing in front of him.
translation_verse: Kachako nɛ Sɔɔl tase kedibi fimbi ko nɛ baa tre tamariski na be kifito ashi Gibia be kebee na so nseŋ keta mbe kekpa nɛ mbe benapo be benimu kikɛ wɔ ndoŋ. Ndoŋ nna nɛ e nu fanɛ b wu Deevid nɛ mbe basa.

english_verse: He told them: Listen to me! You belong to the Benjamin tribe, so if that son of Jesse ever becomes king, he won't give you fields or vineyards. He won't make you officers in charge of thousands or hundreds as I have done.
translation_verse: Nɛ e kaŋɛ mbe benimuana na le: “Men nu nfe! Men la Bɛnjamin be kaman to ebi nna, amoso men baŋ shin nɛ Jɛsi pibinyɛn ere ki ewura, e maaŋ sa menyi kudɔsawule ŋko ndibi nɛ baa tre Greep na be adɔ. Mo alɛ maaŋ naŋ ta menyi ŋ ki mbe benapo ŋgboŋ ŋgboŋ nɛ kalfa kalfa be bejuŋkparpoana fanɛ kananɛ n ta menyi ŋ ki ere.

english_verse: But you're all plotting against me! Not one of you told me that my own son Jonathan had made an agreement with him. Not one of you cared enough to tell me that Jonathan had helped one of my officers rebel. Now that son of Jesse is trying to ambush me.
translation_verse: Ama menyi kikɛ maŋ yil ma kaman. Menyi alɛ be ekama malɛ maŋ kaŋɛ ma fanɛ m pibinyɛn Jonatan nɛ Deevid wora kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre nna. Ma asheŋ maŋ tir menyi, amoso esa kama maŋ kaŋɛ ma fanɛ Jonatan e naa leŋ Deevid to fanɛ e mɔ ma!”

english_verse: Doeg the Edomite was standing with the other officers and spoke up, “When I was in the town of Nob, I saw that son of Jesse. He was visiting the priest Ahimelech the son of Ahitub.
translation_verse: Duɛg nɛ e la Edɔm be esa na gba daa yil Sɔɔl be benimuana na kutɔ nna nseŋ kaŋɛ le: “N daŋ wu Deevid ka wɔ Ahitub pibinyɛn Ahimɛlɛk nɛ e la bɔrɛmatapo na kutɔ ashi Nɔb.

english_verse: Ahimelech talked to the Lord for him, then gave him food and the sword that had belonged to Goliath the Philistine.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Ahimɛlɛk bishi Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kusɔ nɛ k daga Deevid ka wora nseŋ sa Deevid ajibi. E ta Goliɛf nɛ e la Filisti be esa na be tokobi gba n ti so n sa mo.”

english_verse: Saul sent a message to Ahimelech and his whole family of priests at Nob, ordering them to come to him. When they came,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura Sɔɔl shuŋi n tre bɔrɛmatapo Ahimɛlɛk nɛ mbe kanaŋ, nɛ bumo kikɛ la bɔrɛmatapoana ashi Nɔb na, nɛ b ba mo kutɔ.

english_verse: Saul told them, “Listen to me, you son of Ahitub.” “Certainly, Your Majesty,” Ahimelech answered.
translation_verse: Nɛ Sɔɔl kaŋɛ Ahimɛlɛk: “Keni, nu nfe!” Nɛ Ahimɛlɛk yɛ: “Yiramu! Fo e wɔ ma.”

english_verse: Saul demanded, “Why did you plot against me with that son of Jesse? You helped him rebel against me by giving him food and a sword, and by talking with God for him. Now he's trying to ambush me!”
translation_verse: Nɛ Sɔɔl bishi mo le: “Manɛ nna nɛ fo nɛ Deevid bee fin ma kulubi? Manɛ nna nɛ fo sa mo ajibi nɛ tokobi nseŋ naŋ malga Ebɔrɛ kutɔ gba n sa mo? Naniere bre e nyaŋɛ to n wɔtɔ ma nsaa fin ma nɛ e mɔ.”

english_verse: “Your Majesty, none of your officers is more loyal than David!” Ahimelech replied. “He's your son-in-law and the captain of your bodyguard. Everyone in your family respects him.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ahimɛlɛk malɛ kaŋɛ le: “Fo benimuana ere be ekama maŋ wɔtɔ a ji kashenteŋ fanɛ Deevid. E la fo sha nna nseŋ naa la fo benapo nɛ baa kuŋ fo na be enimu nseŋ naa kɔ bunyaŋ gba ashi fo laŋ to ebi kikɛ kutɔ.

english_verse: This isn't the first time I've talked with God for David, and it's never made you angry before! Please don't accuse me or my family like this. I have no idea what's going on!”
translation_verse: Mannɛ kede e la ma sososo ŋ ka bee malga Ebɔrɛ kutɔ ŋkpal Deevid so. Kumo alɛ be loŋ maŋ naŋ dii fo agbo kikɛ. Nɛ manɛ be kulubi nɛ mee fin fo? Sa maŋ wu ma ŋko ma kanaŋ to be esa kikɛ kulubi ŋkpal le be asheŋ ere so!”

english_verse: “Ahimelech,” Saul said, “you and your whole family are going to die.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Sɔɔl kaŋɛ le: “Ahimɛlɛk, fo nɛ fo kanaŋ kikɛ daga luwu.”

english_verse: Saul shouted to his bodyguards, “These priests of the Lord helped David! They knew he was running away, but they didn't tell me. Kill them!” But the king's officers would not attack the priests of the Lord.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Sɔɔl ponte ŋ kaŋɛ bekumpo na le: “Men mɔ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be bɔrɛmatapoana na kikɛ, ŋkpal manɛ so, bumo nɛ Deevid e wora kɔnɔ ŋ kre asheŋ. B nyi Deevid ka daa shile nɛ b kini kekaŋɛ ma.” Ama bekumpo na be ekama maŋ teŋi keshilbi gba ŋ ŋini Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be bɔrɛmatapoana na.

english_verse: Then he attacked the town of Nob, where the priests had lived, and he killed everyone there—men, women, children, and babies. He even killed their cattle, donkeys, and sheep. Only Abiathar Escapes from Nob
translation_verse: Sɔɔl daŋ shin nna nɛ Duɛg yɔ Nɔb, nɛ k la bɔrɛmatapoana be kade to na, n ya mɔ ndoŋebi kikɛ. E daŋ mɔ benyɛn nɛ beche nɛ mbia nɛ mbi popɔrbiana nɛ ana nɛ ekurma nɛ mbolpɔ kikɛ nna.

english_verse: Ahimelech's son Abiathar was the only one who escaped. He ran to David
translation_verse: Ama Ahimɛlɛk pibinyɛn ko nɛ baa tre Abiata na bre daŋ ŋana nna n shile n ya tu Deevid.

english_verse: and told him, “Saul has murdered the Lord's priests at Nob!”
translation_verse: E daŋ ya kaŋɛ mo kananɛ Sɔɔl mɔ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be bɔrɛmatapoana nna.

english_verse: David answered, “That day when I saw Doeg, I knew he would tell Saul! Your family died because of me.
translation_verse: Nɛ Deevid yɛ: “Kachɛ nɛ n wu Duɛg na nɛ m pin kashenteŋto fanɛ e beeŋ ya kaŋɛ Sɔɔl. Ma ere so nɛ b kpal m mɔ fo kanaŋ na.

english_verse: Stay here. Isn't the same person trying to kill both of us? Don't worry! You'll be safe here with me.”
translation_verse: Amoso ba wɔ ŋ kutɔ. Sɔɔl bee fin ma nɛ fo kikɛ nna nɛ e mɔ, ama sa maa lɔ kufu, an kikɛ beeŋ lar.”

english_verse: One day some people told David, “The Philistines keep attacking the town of Keilah and stealing grain from the threshing place.”
translation_verse: Deevid ka nu fanɛ Filistiebi na bee kɔ Kiilaebi kena hale a yuri bumo be aboyu popɔr nɛ b buri n nase kugooro so,

english_verse: David asked the Lord, “Should I attack these Philistines?” “Yes,” the Lord answered. “Attack them and rescue Keilah.”
translation_verse: nɛ e bishi Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ le: “N ya kɔ Filistiebi na kena a?” Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ le: “Mm, ya kɔ bumo kena nseŋ mɔlga Kiilaebi.”

english_verse: But David's men said, “Look, even here in Judah we're afraid of the Philistines. We will be terrified if we try to fight them at Keilah!”
translation_verse: Ama le nɛ Deevid be basa na daŋ kaŋɛ mo: “Hale Juda nfe gba, anyee lɔ kufu nna; an kaŋ yɔ Kiila nɛ an ya kɔ Filistiebi ere bre, kufu na beeŋ naŋ wora kishi n ti so ga!”

english_verse: David asked the Lord about it again. “Leave at once,” the Lord answered. “I will give you victory over the Philistines at Keilah.”
translation_verse: Amoso Deevid daŋ naŋ laŋɛ nna fanɛ m bishi Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kumo be asheŋ to nɛnɛ, nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ mo le: “Ya kɔ Filistiebi na kena Kiila, ŋkpal manɛ so, meeŋ shin nɛ men kɔ m pɔɔ bumo so.”

english_verse: David and his men went there and fiercely attacked the Philistines. They killed many of them, then led away their cattle, and rescued the people of Keilah.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Deevid nɛ mbe basa yɔ Kiila n ya kɔ Filistiebi na kena m mɔ bumo be basa damta nseŋ ta bumo be asɔbɔya. Kananɛ Deevid wora m mɔlga Kiila be kade na nna na.

english_verse: David prayed, “Lord God of Israel, I was told that Saul is planning to come here. What should I do? Suppose he threatens to destroy the town because of me.
translation_verse: Nɛ Deevid kule Ebɔrɛ ŋ kaŋɛ le: “O Enyɛnpe, nɛ fo la Israɛl be Ebɔrɛ, n nu fanɛ Sɔɔl bee ba nɛ e ba mur Kiila be kade ebi ŋkpal fo kenya so.

english_verse: Would the leaders of Keilah turn me over to Saul? Or is he really coming? Please tell me, Lord.” “Yes, he will come,” the Lord answered.
translation_verse: Kiila be ndetobia na beeŋ ta ma n sa Sɔɔl a? Kashenteŋto nɛ Sɔɔl bee ba fanɛ kananɛ n nu ere a? Enyɛnpe nɛ fo la Israɛl be Ebɔrɛ, jande kaŋɛ ma kusɔ nɛ k la!” Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ le: “Mm Sɔɔl beeŋ ba.”

english_verse: David asked, “Would the leaders of Keilah hand me and my soldiers over to Saul?” “Yes, they would,” the Lord answered.
translation_verse: Nɛ Deevid naŋ bishi le: “Kiilaebi beeŋ ta ma nɛ ma basa m bɔɔ Sɔɔl enɔ a?” Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ yɛ: “Mm, baaŋ wora loŋ.”

english_verse: David stayed in hideouts in the hill country of Ziph Desert. Saul kept searching, but God never let Saul catch him.
translation_verse: Deevid daŋ ya ŋana abeelaŋ nɛ a wɔ keshishɛrsawule nɛ baa tre Ziif na to nna. Sɔɔl daŋ baa fin mo nna saŋkama, ama Ebɔrɛ daa maŋ ta Deevid m bɔɔ mo enɔ.

english_verse: One time, David was at Horesh in Ziph Desert. He was afraid because Saul had come to the area to kill him.
translation_verse: Jemanɛ ko Deevid ka wɔ Hɔrɛsh nɛ k wɔ keshishɛrsawule nɛ baa tre Ziif na; e daa lɔ kufu nna ŋkpal Sɔɔl ka daŋ ba ndoŋ nɛ e ba fin mo m mɔ so.

english_verse: But Jonathan went to see David, and God helped him encourage David.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Jonatan yɔ Deevid kutɔ n ya leŋ mo to ŋ kaŋɛ mo fanɛ Ebɔrɛ beeŋ kuŋ mo,

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Jonathan said. “My father Saul will never get his hands on you. In fact, you're going to be the next king of Israel, and I'll be your highest official. Even my father knows it's true.”
translation_verse: nseŋ naŋ kaŋɛ mo le: “N tuto Sɔɔl maaŋ tiŋ n wora fo shɛŋ, amoso sa maa lɔ kufu. E baa nyi geeŋ fanɛ fo e naa shin nɛ fo ba ki Israɛl be ewura nɛ ma alɛ e baa la enimu m bɛ so.”

english_verse: They both promised the Lord that they would always be loyal to each other. Then Jonathan went home, but David stayed at Horesh. David Escapes from Saul
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ bumo benyɔ kikɛ naŋ nase keteri kpakpaso be nnɔ ashi Ebɔrɛ be anishito n sa abar. Nɛ Deevid bre daŋ shir a wɔ Hɔrɛsh nɛ Jonatan malɛ yɔ epe.

english_verse: Some people from the town of Ziph went to Saul at Gibeah and said, “Your Majesty, David has a hideout not far from us! It's near Horesh, somewhere on Mount Hachilah south of Jeshimon.
translation_verse: Ade be kaman nɛ basa ko nɛ b shi Ziif be kade to yɔ Sɔɔl kutɔ ashi Gibia n ya kaŋɛ le: “Deevid maŋ wɔ kufɔ. E wɔ anyi be efuli so be kebeegboŋ nɛ baa tre Hakila nɛ k wɔ Jeshimɔn be kelargato be kaseto be kaba so m mata Hɔrɛsh na.

english_verse: Saul told them: You've done me a big favor, and I pray that the Lord will bless you.
translation_verse: Nɛ Sɔɔl kaŋɛ le: “Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e nɛfa menyi ŋkpal kusɔ nɛ men kaŋɛ ma ere so.

english_verse: Now please do just a little more for me. Find out exactly where David is, as well as where he goes, and who has seen him there. I've been told that he's very tricky.
translation_verse: N nu fanɛ e kɔ kanyiasheŋ ga, amoso men naŋ bɛta n ya fin mo m pin kakpa nɛ e wɔ gbagba nseŋ bishi to nɛnɛ ŋ keni esa ko gba wu mo ndoŋ n ti so a?

english_verse: Find out where all his hiding places are and come back when you're sure. Then I'll go with you. If he is still in the area, or anywhere among the clans of Judah, I'll find him.
translation_verse: Men lege to n fin mboŋ kama nɛ e bee kaa shile a ŋana na nseŋ ba kaŋɛ ma. Saŋɛ na so ma nɛ menyi beeŋ fin mo. E baa wɔ efuli ere so bre men nya mo. Hale nɛ meeŋ keni Juda be efuli so kikɛ gba n fin mo nna meeŋ wora loŋ.”

english_verse: The people from Ziph went back ahead of Saul, and they found out that David and his men were still south of Jeshimon in the Maon Desert.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ziif be basa na bɛta n juŋkpar Sɔɔl n yɔ Ziif. Ama Deevid nɛ mbe basa bre daa wɔ Mayɔn be kiyi to nna ashi Jeshimɔn be kelargato be kaseto be kaba so.

english_verse: Saul and his army set out to find David. But David heard that Saul was coming, and he went to a place called The Rock, one of his hideouts in Maon Desert. Saul found out where David was and started closing in on him.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Sɔɔl nɛ mbe benapo lar nɛ b ya fin Deevid, ama Deevid ka nu fanɛ Sɔɔl bee ba, nɛ e yɔ kefalta be kebee ko so ashi Mayɔn be kiyi to n ya kaa wɔ ndoŋ. Sɔɔl ka pin fanɛ Deevid wɔ ndoŋ na, nɛ e naŋ fara a ju a buu mo so.

english_verse: Saul was going around a hill on one side, and David and his men were on the other side, trying to get away. Saul and his soldiers were just about to capture David and his men,
translation_verse: Sɔɔl nɛ mbe basa daa wɔ kebee na be kaba ko nna nɛ Deevid malɛ nɛ mbe basa wɔ kaba ko a fin kananɛ baaŋ wora n nya ekpa n shile. A daŋ ka gbrɛbi nɛ Sɔɔl nɛ mbe basa e pɛ Deevid nɛ mbe basa.

english_verse: when a messenger came to Saul and said, “Come quickly! The Philistines are attacking Israel and taking everything.”
translation_verse: Nɛ kabɔ ko ba kaŋɛ Sɔɔl le: “Men ba manaŋ! Filistiebi na ta kena m ba purgi anyi be efuli ebi!”

english_verse: Saul stopped going after David and went back to fight the Philistines. That's why the place is called “Escape Rock.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Sɔɔl yige kebaa ju a buu Deevid so nseŋ yɔ nɛ e ya kɔ Filistiebi na. Amoso nɛ baa tre kebee na “Kefalta nɛ k barga basa to.”

english_verse: When Saul got back from fighting off the Philistines, he heard that David was in the desert around En-Gedi.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ka ya kɔ Filistiebi na kena n loge nseŋ bɛta m ba, nɛ b kaŋɛ mo fanɛ Deevid wɔ keshishɛrsawule nɛ k mata Engedi na ase.

english_verse: There were some sheep pens along the side of the road, and one of them was built around the entrance to a cave. Saul went into the cave to relieve himself. David and his men were hiding at the back of the cave.
translation_verse: E daŋ ba kebeelaŋ ko nɛ k mata mbolpɔ be aluu nɛ a mata ekpa na nna nseŋ luri ndoŋ nɛ e ya jɔŋɛ. Loŋ be saŋɛ na nɛ Deevid nɛ mbe basa malɛ ŋana loŋ be kebeelaŋ na be ŋkpar to.

english_verse: They whispered to David, “The Lord told you he was going to let you defeat your enemies and do whatever you want with them. This must be the day the Lord was talking about.” David sneaked over and cut off a small piece of Saul's robe, but Saul didn't notice a thing.
translation_verse: Nɛ Deevid be basa na kuli ŋ kaŋɛ mo le: “Ekpa bugi n sa fo alɛ gba naniere nna na! Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ fanɛ e beeŋ ta fo doŋ n wɔtɔ fo enɔ to nɛ fo wora mo kusɔ kama nɛ fee sha.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ Deevid pete n ya ku Sɔɔl be piŋi be keyɛlbi nɛ Sɔɔl maŋ nyi.

english_verse: Afterwards, David was sorry that he had even done that,
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Deevid be nfɛra fara a tɔrɔ mo ŋkpal e ka wora loŋ so.

english_verse: and he told his men, “Stop talking foolishly. We're not going to attack Saul. He's my king, and I pray that the Lord will keep me from doing anything to harm his chosen king.” Saul left the cave and started down the road.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Deevid kpele mbe basa kusoe fanɛ b sa maŋ kaŋ wora Sɔɔl shɛŋ. Nɛ Sɔɔl lar kebeelaŋ na to m pɛ ekpa a yɔ.

english_verse: Soon, David also got up and left the cave. “Your Majesty!” he shouted from a distance. Saul turned around to look. David bowed down very low
translation_verse: K maŋ chɛr ko nɛ Deevid malɛ gba lar kebeelaŋ na to nseŋ yili kufɔ m ponte ŋ tre: “Yiramu!” Sɔɔl ka gbɛ ŋ keni, nɛ Deevid jɔŋɛ bunyanso

english_verse: and said: Your Majesty, why do you listen to people who say that I'm trying to harm you?
translation_verse: nseŋ ŋ kaŋɛ le: “Manɛ nna nɛ fee nu kusɔ nɛ basa bee kaŋɛ fo, fanɛ mee sha kewora fo kulubi nna?

english_verse: You can see for yourself that the Lord gave me the chance to catch you in the cave today. Some of my men wanted to kill you, but I wouldn't let them do it. I told them, “I will not harm the Lord's chosen king!”
translation_verse: Fo gbagba wu fanɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ daŋ ta fo nna m bɔɔ ma enɔ ashi kebeelaŋ ere to kabre. Ma basa ko kaŋɛ ma fanɛ m mɔ fo, ama ma ere yige fo nseŋ kaŋɛ bumo fanɛ, k maŋ daga fanɛ n wora fo kulubi kikɛ, ŋkpal manɛ so, fo nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ lara fanɛ fo ba la ewura.

english_verse: Your Majesty, look at what I'm holding. You can see that it's a piece of your robe. If I could cut off a piece of your robe, I could have killed you. But I let you live, and that should prove I'm not trying to harm you or to rebel. I haven't done anything to you, and yet you keep trying to ambush and kill me.
translation_verse: Yiramu, keni kusɔ nɛ ŋ keta ere, fo gbagba be piŋi be keyɛlbi nna na. Baa nyi fanɛ kananɛ m baŋ nya ekpa ŋ ku fo piŋi be keyɛlbi ere, loŋ be ekpa nɛ n daa kɔ nɛ n tiŋ m mɔ fo gba, ama ma alɛ maŋ wora loŋ. Amoso le e daga fo alɛ gba ka pin fanɛ ma ere maŋ kɔ nfɛra lubi kikɛ n sa fo. Kashenteŋ nna fanɛ maŋ wora fo shɛŋ, ama fo alɛ pere kenishi a fin ma kemɔ.

english_verse: I'll let the Lord decide which one of us has done right. I pray that the Lord will punish you for what you're doing to me, but I won't do anything to you.
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nawule e naaŋ ji anyi kikɛ demu m pin emo nɛ e wora n foe ekpa. Mo alɛ beeŋ gberge fo kusoe ŋkpal kusɔ nɛ fo wora ma ere so. Ama ma ere maaŋ wora fo shɛŋ.

english_verse: An old proverb says, “Only evil people do evil things,” and so I won't harm you.
translation_verse: Dra kikɛ nɛ baa bɔ keŋasa a kaŋɛ fanɛ: ‘Basa lubi e naa wora kulubi.’ Amoso ma ere maaŋ wora fo kulubi kikɛ.

english_verse: Why should the king of Israel be out chasing me, anyway? I'm as worthless as a dead dog or a flea.
translation_verse: Wanɛ e la ma alɛ, kujɔnɔmu fuloŋ nɛ kejaŋjaŋkɔrso, nɛ Israɛl be ewura ju a buu ma so a fin ma nɛ e mɔ le ere?

english_verse: and said: David, you're a better person than I am. You treated me with kindness, even though I've been cruel to you.
translation_verse: nseŋ kaŋɛ Deevid le: “Fo kɔ kashenteŋ a chɔ ma. Fo wora ma kelela ga, ama kulubi nɛ ma ere ta a ka fo kukɔ!

english_verse: You've told me how you were kind enough not to kill me when the Lord gave you the chance.
translation_verse: Ama kabre, fo kaŋɛ ma kelela nɛ fo wora ma saŋɛ so nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ta ma m bɔɔ fo enɔ nɛ fo kini kemɔ ma na.

english_verse: If you really were my enemy, you wouldn't have let me leave here alive. I pray that the Lord will give you a big reward for what you did today.
translation_verse: Nɛ fo daa la ma doŋ nna kashenteŋto, dafanɛ fo daa maaŋ yige ma kemɔ. Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e nɛfa fo ŋkpal kusɔ nɛ fo wora ma ere so.

english_verse: I realize now that you will be the next king, and a powerful king at that.
translation_verse: Naniere nɛ m pin fanɛ, fo e naaŋ ba ki Israɛl be ewura nɛ fo kuwurji malɛ e ji eleŋ ga.

english_verse: Promise me with the Lord as your witness, that you won't wipe out my descendants. Let them live to keep my family name alive.
translation_verse: Ama nase kɔnɔ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be ketre to n sa ma fanɛ fo maaŋ mur ma kanaŋ. Saŋɛ na so, ma kanaŋ be ketre maaŋ mur.”

english_verse: So he sent ten men to Carmel with this message for Nabal: I hope that you and your family are healthy and that all is going well for you.
translation_verse: Le be kubɔya nɛ e daŋ ta n shuŋi bumo Nabaal kutɔ. E yɛ: “Fo teri Deevid e naa chɔrɔ fo na, nsaa bishi fo nɛ fo kanaŋ nɛ kusɔ kama nɛ fo kɔ be alenfia be asheŋ.

english_verse: I've heard that you are cutting the wool from your sheep. When your shepherds were with us in Carmel, we didn't harm them, and nothing was ever stolen from them.
translation_verse: E yɛ e nu fanɛ fee kuya fo mbolpɔ be afuibi nna amoso nɛ e bee sha fo ka pin fanɛ fo mbolpɔkpapoana wɔ anyi kutɔ nfe, anyi alɛ maŋ tɔrɔ bumo ekpa kikɛ so. Saŋkama malɛ nɛ bumo nɛ ma basa tu abar, ma basa maa sɔ bumo shɛŋ.

english_verse: Ask your shepherds, and they'll tell you the same thing. My servants are your servants, and you are like a father to me. This is a day for celebrating, so please be kind and share some of your food with us.
translation_verse: Fo bishi fo mbolpɔkpapoana na, bumo alɛ gba beeŋ kaŋɛ fo le be kesheŋ koŋwule ere. Kejigboŋ be kachɛ nɛ an ba na, amoso Deevid yɛ, fo keta anyi nɛnɛ. E yɛ kusɔ kama nɛ fo kɔ, fo ta kumo n chɛ fo teri Deevid nɛ fo nyɛrbi to.”

english_verse: David's men went to Nabal and gave him David's message, then they waited for Nabal's answer.
translation_verse: Le be kubɔya ere nɛ Deevid be basa na daŋ ta n ya sa Nabaal nsaa jo nɛ b nu kusɔ ko ashi mo kutɔ.

english_verse: This is what he said: Who does this David think he is? That son of Jesse is just one more slave on the run from his master, and there are too many of them these days.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Nabaal malɛ kaŋɛ le: “Wanɛ bre e la Jɛsi pibinyɛn Deevid ere? Naniere kananɛ nyɛrbi damta bee shile bumo nyɛnpeana nna na!

english_verse: What makes you think I would take my bread, my water, and the meat that I've had cooked for my own servants and give it to you? Besides, I'm not sure that David sent you!
translation_verse: Ashere bumo be eko e la mo alɛ gba na. M maaŋ ta ma ajibi nɛ nchu nɛ ma eblaŋ nɛ m bar nɛ m ba sa basa nɛ baa kuya mbolpɔ be afuibi na n sa basa nɛ m maŋ nyi!”

english_verse: The men returned to their camp and told David everything Nabal had said.
translation_verse: Nɛ Deevid be basa na bɛta n ya kaŋɛ mo kusɔ nɛ Nabaal kaŋɛ na kikɛ.

english_verse: “Everybody get your swords!” David ordered. They all strapped on their swords. Two hundred men stayed behind to guard the camp, but the other
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Deevid kaŋɛ bumo le: “Men ta men be etokobi!” Deevid nɛ mbe benapo, beeŋ wora fanɛ basa alfa ana, e ta bumo be etokobi nɛ b yɔ nseŋ yige basa alfa anyɔ malɛ bumo be keeyi to.

english_verse: He's a bully who won't listen to anyone. Isn't there something you can do? Please think of something! Or else our master and his family and everyone who works for him are all doomed.
translation_verse: Amoso jande, fɛ asheŋ ere be nfɛra nseŋ wora kusɔ ko a laŋɛ kumo be kaplɛa so, ŋkpal manɛ so, k beeŋ tiŋ m bar asheŋ m ba sa an nyɛnpe nɛ mbe kanaŋ kikɛ. Ŋkpal mo alɛ ka la kagbene kpakpasowura so, e maa nu a sa esa kama!”

english_verse: and told her servants, “Take this on ahead, and I'll catch up with you.” She didn't tell her husband Nabal what she was doing.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e kaŋɛ nyɛrbi na le: “Men ta asɔ ere a juŋkpar nɛ ma alɛ e wora a bɛ menyi so a ba.” Ama e daa maŋ kaŋɛ mo kul Nabaal kusɔ nɛ e daa wora.

english_verse: Abigail was riding her donkey on the path that led around the hillside, when suddenly she met David and his men heading straight at her.
translation_verse: Abigɛl ka dii mbe kurma m bɔla ekpa nɛ k bɔla abee na to na, nɛ e ba tu Deevid nɛ mbe basa nɛ b shi kebee na so a gbelge to a shɛr mo to.

english_verse: David had just been saying, “I surely wasted my time guarding Nabal's things in the desert and keeping them from being stolen! I was good to him, and now he pays me back with insults.
translation_verse: Deevid daa fɛ le be nfɛra nna: “M baŋ jija ma saŋɛ nna ŋ keni Nabaal be asɔ so ashi kiyi to nɛ b maŋ nya amo n yuri. Kelela nɛ n wora mo, ama kulubi nɛ mo ere ta a ka ma kukɔ.

english_verse: I swear that by morning, there won't be a man or boy left from his family or his servants' families. I pray that God will punish me if I don't do it!”
translation_verse: Ta a ba kachipurso nɛ mbe kanaŋ to be enyɛn kama kraa wɔ ŋkpa to, kumo ere Ebɔrɛ e mɔ ma!”

english_verse: Abigail quickly got off her donkey and bowed down in front of David.
translation_verse: Abigɛl ka baŋ wu Deevid, nɛ e gbelge mbe kurma so manaŋ, m ba gbir Deevid be anishito ŋ kurgi kumu n yuu to,

english_verse: Don't pay any attention to that good-for-nothing Nabal. His name means “fool,” and it really fits him! I didn't see the men you sent,
translation_verse: Jande sa maŋ kaŋ nu n sa Nabaal, esa jiga na. Mbe ketre na be kifito e la ewulpo! Nɛ mo alɛ be asheŋ woraso nɛ mbe ketre na duli abar. Ma ere daa maŋ wɔtɔ nna nɛ fo nyɛrbi na ba.

english_verse: Please forgive me if I say a little more. The Lord will always protect you and your family, because you fight for him. I pray that you won't ever do anything evil as long as you live.
translation_verse: Jande, nɛ n wora fo kulubi ko gba nna, fo ta m paŋ ma. Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na beeŋ shin nɛ fo ki ewura nɛ fo kanaŋ to ebi e baa ji kuwura ŋkpal fo ka bee kɔ a sa mo so. Ma kabɔrɛkule e la fanɛ fo maaŋ wora kulubi kikɛ hale nɛ fo ba lar durnya ere to.

english_verse: The Lord your God will keep you safe when your enemies try to kill you. But he will snatch away their lives quicker than you can throw a rock from a sling.
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na beeŋ kuŋ fo ashi bedoŋ kama nɛ baa fin fo nɛ b mɔ na be enɔ to. E beeŋ kuŋ fo fanɛ kananɛ esa bee kuŋ mbe kpanjawu na. Ama fo doŋana na bre Ebɔrɛ beeŋ kpa bumo n ya lɛ fanɛ kananɛ baa ta ajembu a wɔtɔ ketababu to a kpa a lɛ na.

english_verse: The Lord has promised to do many good things for you, even to make you the ruler of Israel. The Lord will keep his promises to you,
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ malɛ kaŋ wora alelasheŋ damta nɛ e nase kɔnɔ n sa fo na kikɛ nseŋ shin nɛ fo ki Israɛl be ewura,

english_verse: and now your conscience will be clear, because you won't be guilty of taking revenge and killing innocent people. When the Lord does all those good things for you, please remember me.
translation_verse: fo maaŋ wora n daa nyi ŋkpal fo ka wora n tal fo doŋana to so. Ama n nyɛnpe, jande, nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋ nɛfa fo, fo baa nyiŋi ma.”

english_verse: David told her: I praise the Lord God of Israel! He must have sent you to meet me today.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Deevid kaŋɛ Abigɛl le: “Kemaŋkura e baa la Enyɛnpe, Israɛl be Ebɔrɛ nɛ e shuŋi fo fanɛ fo ba shɛr ma to kabre ere peya!

english_verse: And you should also be praised. Your good sense kept me from taking revenge and killing innocent people.
translation_verse: Ama fo alɛ gba kɔ kechɔrɔ ŋkpal kanyiasheŋ be kasotoji nɛ fo sa ma kabre nɛ k kuŋ ma ashi kamɔ nɛ kewora n tal to be kulubi to so.

english_verse: If you hadn't come to meet me so quickly, every man and boy in Nabal's family and in his servants' families would have been killed by morning. I swear by the living Lord God of Israel who protected you that this is the truth.
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e shin nɛ m maŋ tɔrɔ fo na. Ama Enyɛnpe, Israɛl be Ebɔrɛ na be ketre to, nɛ fanɛ fo daa maŋ nya manaŋ m ba nna, ndafanɛ ta n ya ka fo kachipurso nɛ Nabaal nɛ mbe kanaŋ to be benyɛn kikɛ maŋ naa wɔ ŋkpa to.”

english_verse: David accepted the food Abigail had brought. “Don't worry,” he said. “You can go home now. I'll do what you asked.”
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Deevid sɔ asɔ nɛ Abigɛl ta m ba na, nseŋ kaŋɛ mo le: “Bɛta a yɔ epe nsaa maŋ shin nɛ kafɔŋ e baa kɔ fo. Kusɔ kama nɛ fee sha, meeŋ wora kumo n sa fo.”

english_verse: Abigail went back home and found Nabal throwing a party fit for a king. He was very drunk and feeling good, so she didn't tell him anything that night.
translation_verse: Abigɛl ka bɛta n yɔ nɛ mo kul Nabaal wɔ laŋ to a wora kejigboŋ fanɛ ewura ka wora kejigboŋ na. E daŋ boo nna le chil; ŋkpal loŋ so, Abigɛl daa maŋ kaŋɛ mo shɛŋ hale nɛ kare ya chɛ kachipurso.

english_verse: But when he sobered up the next morning, Abigail told him everything that had happened. Nabal had a heart attack, and he lay in bed as still as a stone.
translation_verse: Kare ka chɛ nɛ mbe kaboo na lar mo to na, nɛ Abigɛl kaŋɛ mo kusɔ kama nɛ k wora. Ndoŋ nna nɛ Nabaal kreŋ n dese fanɛ kejembu na.

english_verse: Ten days later, the Lord took his life.
translation_verse: Kumo be nchɛ kudu be kefɛato, nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na gberge Nabaal kusoe nɛ e wu.

english_verse: She bowed down and said, “I would willingly be David's slave and wash his servants' feet.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Abigɛl gbir ŋ kaŋɛ le: “N wora shiriya nɛ ŋ ki mbe kebita nsaa fɔr mbe nyɛrbi be aya so.”

english_verse: Abigail quickly got ready and went back with David's messengers. She rode on her donkey, while five of her servant women walked alongside. She and David were married as soon as she arrived.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ e koso epul na to n dii mbe kurma. Nɛ mo nɛ mbe mbita anu kikɛ tu Deevid be nyɛrbi na n yɔ nɛ Deevid ya ta mo ŋ ki mbe eche.

english_verse: David had earlier married Ahinoam from the town of Jezreel, so both she and Abigail were now David's wives.
translation_verse: Deevid daŋ chɛr a kɔ eche ko nɛ e shi Jizreel be kade to nɛ baa tre mo Ahinɔam pɔɛŋ nseŋ ta Abigɛl n ya ti mo so.

english_verse: Once again, some people from Ziph went to Gibeah to talk with Saul. “David has a hideout on Mount Hachilah near Jeshimon out in the desert,” they told him.
translation_verse: Basa ko daŋ shi Ziif nna m ba Sɔɔl kutɔ ashi Gibia m ba kaŋɛ mo fanɛ Deevid ŋana kebeegboŋ nɛ baa tre Hakila nɛ k mata Jeshimɔn na ase ashi Juda be efuli so be kiyi to be ekarso.

english_verse: Saul set up camp on Mount Hachilah, which is across the road from Jeshimon. But David was hiding out in the desert. When David heard that Saul was following him,
translation_verse: B daŋ ya wora bumo be keeyi to nna ashi ekpa nɛ k dese kebeegboŋ nɛ baa tre Hakila na ase. Loŋ be saŋɛ na nɛ Deevid kraa wɔ kiyi to, ama e ka nu fanɛ Sɔɔl bee fin mo na,

english_verse: he sent some spies to find out if it was true.
translation_verse: nɛ e shuŋi basa nɛ b ya ŋana n dara nseŋ wu fanɛ Sɔɔl wɔ ndoŋ kashenteŋto.

english_verse: Then he sneaked up to Saul's camp. He noticed that Saul and his army commander Abner the son of Ner were sleeping in the middle of the camp, with soldiers sleeping all around them.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Deevid koso epul na to n ya dara n wu kakpa nɛ Sɔɔl nɛ Neer pibinyɛn Abna nɛ e la Sɔɔl be benapo be enimu dese na. Sɔɔl daa dese keeyi na to nna a di nɛ mbe benapo malɛ dese ŋ kulti mo.

english_verse: That same night, David and Abishai crept into the camp. Saul was sleeping, and his spear was stuck in the ground not far from his head. Abner and the soldiers were sound asleep all around him.
translation_verse: Loŋ be kanyɛ na nɛ Deevid nɛ Abishai yɔ Sɔɔl be keeyi to n ya wu Sɔɔl nɛ e dese a di nɛ mbe kekpa yuu kasawule m mata mbe kumu ase. Abna nɛ benapo nɛ b ka na malɛ kikɛ daa dese ŋ kulti mo nna a di.

english_verse: Abishai whispered, “This time God has let you get your hands on your enemy! I'll pin him to the ground with one thrust of his own spear.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Abishai kuli ŋ kaŋɛ Deevid le: “Naniere bre Ebɔrɛ ta fo doŋ n wɔtɔ fo enɔ to nna na. Shin nɛ n ta mo gbagba be kekpa ere m baŋ da mo m mata kasawule kela koŋwule paati. M maaŋ da mo kumo ale anyɔ!”

english_verse: “Don't kill him!” David whispered back. “The Lord will punish anyone who kills his chosen king.
translation_verse: Ama le nɛ Deevid daŋ kaŋɛ mo: “Sa maŋ kaŋ mɔ mo! Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na beeŋ gberge esa kama nɛ e beeŋ mɔ mbe ewura laraso kusoe.

english_verse: As surely as the Lord lives, the Lord will kill Saul, or Saul will die a natural death or be killed in battle.
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ e la ma shɛdajipo ere be ketre to, n nyi fanɛ mo ere Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na gbagba beeŋ shin nɛ Sɔɔl e wu saŋɛ ŋko kachɛ nɛ e yili n sa mo ŋko n shin nɛ b mɔ mo kena to.

english_verse: But I pray that the Lord will keep me from harming his chosen king. Let's grab his spear and his water jar and get out of here!”
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e baa pete ma nɛ m mɔ esa nɛ mo ere Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ lara ŋ ki ewura. Men shin nɛ an ta mbe kekpa nɛ mbe kusɔjɔnchu a yɔ.”

english_verse: David took the spear and the water jar, then left the camp. None of Saul's soldiers knew what had happened or even woke up—the Lord had made all of them fall sound asleep.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Deevid ta Sɔɔl be kekpa nɛ mbe kusɔjɔnchu nɛ a yil m mata Sɔɔl be kumu ase nɛ mo nɛ Abishai lar keeyi na to n yɔ. Sɔɔl be benapo na malɛ be ekama maŋ tiŋ m pin kusɔ nɛ k wora ŋko n tiŋi edi to. Ŋkpal manɛ so Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e daŋ shin nɛ bumo kikɛ di m mel.

english_verse: David and Abishai crossed the valley and went to the top of the next hill, where they were at a safe distance.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Deevid nɛ Abishai dii ketaŋɛ na n yɔ kebee na be esoso be kakpa nɛ Sɔɔl be benapo na maaŋ nya bumo m mɔ na,

english_verse: “Abner!” David shouted toward Saul's army. “Can you hear me?” Abner shouted back. “Who dares disturb the king?”
translation_verse: nseŋ ponte n tre Sɔɔl be benapo na nɛ Abna ŋ kaŋɛ le: “Abna! Menyee nu anyi be ebɔl a?” Nɛ Abna malɛ bishi le: “Wanɛ bre e naa wora awɔr nɛ e tiŋi ewura ere?”

english_verse: “Abner, what kind of a man are you?” David replied. “Aren't you supposed to be the best soldier in Israel? Then why didn't you protect your king? Anyone who went into your camp could have killed him tonight.
translation_verse: Nɛ Deevid malɛ shuli so ŋ kaŋɛ le: “Mannɛ fo nɛ basa bee kaŋɛ Israɛl be efuli so kikɛ fanɛ fo e kɔ kenyɛn ga na a? Nɛ manɛ e ba nɛ fo maa kuŋ fo nyɛnpe nɛ fo ewura? Naniere nɛ esa ko yɔ menyi be keeyi to nɛ e ya mɔ fo nyɛnpe na.

english_verse: You're a complete failure! I swear by the living Lord that you and your men deserve to die for not protecting the Lord's chosen king. Look and see if you can find the king's spear and the water jar that were near his head.”
translation_verse: Abna! Fo maŋ shuŋ fo kushuŋ nɛnɛ. Ebɔrɛ nɛ e la ma shɛdajipo na be ketre to, menyi kikɛ daga luwu nna ŋkpal men ka maŋ kuŋ men nyɛnpe nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ lara mo n sa menyi fanɛ ewura na so. Men keni, ewura be kekpa nɛ mbe kusɔjɔnchu nɛ a yil mbe kumu ase na kraa wɔtɔ a?”

english_verse: Saul could tell it was David's voice, and he called out, “David, my son! Is that you?” “Yes it is, Your Majesty.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nɛ Sɔɔl pin Deevid be ebɔl nseŋ kaŋɛ le: “Fo nna a m pibinyɛn Deevid?” Nɛ Deevid malɛ shuli so ŋ kaŋɛ le: “Yiramu mm, ma nna.”

english_verse: Why are you hunting me down? Have I done something wrong, or have I committed a crime?
translation_verse: Nseŋ naŋ kaŋɛ le: “Manɛ nɛ fo kayɛrbi wora nɛ fo kraa ju a buu mo so loŋ? Manɛ be kulubi nɛ n wora fo?

english_verse: Please listen to what I have to say. If the Lord has turned you against me, maybe a sacrifice will make him change his mind. But if some people have turned you against me, I hope the Lord will punish them! They have forced me to leave the land that belongs to the Lord and have told me to worship foreign gods.
translation_verse: Yiramu, nu kusɔ nɛ mee sha nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ fo ere! Nɛ fanɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e shin nɛ fee kɔ ma, kumo ere meeŋ lara sarga n sa mo nɛ e chɛrga mbe nfɛra. Nɛ fanɛ dimɛdi malɛ e naa wora loŋ, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be kɔnɔsho na e pɛ amodoŋwura. Ŋkpal manɛ so, b ju ma ashi Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be kasawule so n ya lɛ nnyamase be efuli so, kakpa nɛ m maaŋ tiŋ n shuŋ Ebɔrɛ.

english_verse: Don't let me die in a land far away from the Lord. I'm no more important than a flea! Why should the king of Israel hunt me down as if I were a bird in the mountains?”
translation_verse: Sa maŋ kaŋ mɔ ma ashi nnyamase be kasawule so, ashi kakpa nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na maŋ taga to, ŋkpal manɛ so, m maŋ la shɛŋ. Kejaŋjaŋkɔrso gba chɔ ma! Nɛ manɛ e ba nɛ Israɛl be ewura bee fin ma alɛ le nɛ e mɔ fanɛ mbuibi ashi kebee so?”

english_verse: “David, you had the chance to kill me today. But you didn't. I was very wrong about you. It was a terrible mistake for me to try to kill you. I've acted like a fool, but I'll never try to harm you again. You're like a son to me, so please come back.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Sɔɔl malɛ kaŋɛ le: “M pibinyɛn Deevid n wora kulubi, amoso bɛta a ba! M maaŋ naŋ tɔrɔ fo kikɛ ŋkpal fo ka shin nɛ n ji efute kanyɛ ere so. N wora kawulisheŋ ga! M maŋ wora nɛnɛ!”

english_verse: “Your Majesty, here's your spear! Let one of your soldiers come and get it.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Deevid kaŋɛ le: “Fo kekpa na nde Yiramu. Shin nɛ fo basa ere be eko e ba sɔ kumo.

english_verse: The Lord put you in my power today, but you are his chosen king and I wouldn't harm you. The Lord rewards people who are faithful and live right.
translation_verse: Beshenteŋjipo nɛ basa cheembi nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ bee nɛfa. E ta fo nna m bɔɔ ma enɔ kabre, ama ma alɛ maŋ wora fo shɛŋ ŋkpal fo ka la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be ewura lara so so.

english_verse: I spared your life today, and I pray that the Lord will spare my life and keep me safe.”
translation_verse: Kananɛ m baŋ shin nɛ fo ji efute kabre le ere, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e baa kuŋ ma nsaa pete ma ashi etɔrɔsheŋ kikɛ to!”

english_verse: “David, my son, I pray that the Lord will bless you and make you successful!” David in Philistia Saul went back home. David also left,
translation_verse: Nɛ Sɔɔl kaŋɛ Deevid le: “M pibinyɛn Deevid, Ebɔrɛ e nɛfa fo n shin nɛ fo baa kɔ a pɔɔ so ashi kusɔ kama nɛ fee wora to!” Ndoŋ nna nɛ Deevid pɛ mbe ekpa n choŋ nɛ Sɔɔl malɛ bɛta n yɔ epe.

english_verse: but he thought to himself, “One of these days, Saul is going to kill me. The only way to escape from him is to go to Philistia. Then I'll be outside of Israel, and Saul will give up trying to catch me.”
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Deevid fɛ le: “Sɔɔl beeŋ tiŋ m mɔ ma nchɛ anyɔ ere to. Amoso kusɔ nɛ meeŋ wora e la fanɛ meeŋ shile n yɔ Filisti be efuli so n ya ŋana, saŋɛ na so e beeŋ fin ma Israɛl be efuli so ŋ gben nɛ n nya ma kumu.”

english_verse: When Saul found out that David had run off to Gath, he stopped trying to catch him.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ka nu fanɛ Deevid shile n yɔ Gaaf na, nɛ e yige kebaafin mo.

english_verse: One day, David was talking with Achish and said, “If you are happy with me, then let me live in one of the towns in the countryside. I'm not important enough to live here with you in the royal city.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Deevid kaŋɛ Akish le: “Nɛ fanɛ n la fo teri kashenteŋto nna, kumo ere fo sa ma kade ko nɛ k mata nfe nɛ n ya ka wɔ ndoŋ, ŋkpal manɛ so, k maŋ daga fanɛ ma nɛ fo kikɛ e baa wɔ kadegboŋ nɛ fo chena ere to.”

english_verse: Achish gave David the town of Ziklag that same day, and Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah ever since.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Akish ta kade nɛ baa tre Ziklag na n sa Deevid. Ŋkpal loŋ so nɛ Ziklag ki Juda be bewura be kade hale mbre na.

english_verse: David was in Philistia for a year and four months.
translation_verse: Kafɛ nɛ afɔl ana nɛ Deevid daŋ chena Filisti be kasawule so.

english_verse: Whenever David and his men attacked a town, they took the sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels, and the clothing, and killed everyone who lived there. After he returned from a raid, David always went to see Achish,
translation_verse: nsaa mɔ bumo be benyɛn nɛ beche kikɛ a pɛ bumo be mbolpɔ nɛ ana nɛ ekurma nɛ enyɔma nsaa ta bumo be epiŋi gba a ti so. Kumo be kaman nɛ e bɛta n yɔ Akish kutɔ,

english_verse: who would ask, “Where did you attack today?” David would answer, “Oh, we attacked some desert town that belonged to the Judah tribe.” Sometimes David would say, “Oh, we attacked a town in the desert where the Jerahmeel clan lives” or “We attacked a town in the desert where the Kenites live.”
translation_verse: nɛ Akish e bishi mo le: “Basa mo nɛ fo yaŋ kre kena n ya purgi kabre?” Nɛ Deevid malɛ e kaŋɛ mo fanɛ Juda be kelargato be kaseto be kaba so ŋko Jeramiil be kaman to ebi be kaba so ŋko Keenanebi na be kakpa nɛ b tase na be kaba so.

english_verse: That's why David killed everyone in the towns he attacked. He thought, “If I let any of them live, they might come to Gath and tell what I've really been doing.” David made these raids all the time he was in Philistia.
translation_verse: Deevid daa mɔ bumo be benyɛn nɛ beche kikɛ nna ŋkpal e ka daa maa sha esa kama ka yɔ Gaaf n ya kaŋɛ kusɔ nɛ mbe basa wora so.

english_verse: But Achish trusted David and thought, “David's people must be furious with him. From now on he will have to take orders from me.”
translation_verse: Akish daŋ yirda Deevid ga nsaa fɛ le: “Ŋkpal Deevid be basa, Israɛlebi, ka kishi mo ga so e beeŋ ki ma kayɛrbi mbaanaayɔ.”

english_verse: The Philistines went to Shunem and set up camp. Saul called the army of Israel together, and they set up their camp in Gilboa.
translation_verse: Kachako nɛ Filisti be benapo na ba abar so m ba wora bumo be keeyi to m mata Shunɛm; nɛ Sɔɔl malɛ shin nɛ Israɛlebi na ya wora bumo be keeyi to ashi kebeegboŋ nɛ baa tre Gilbɔa na ase.

english_verse: Saul took one look at the Philistine army and started shaking with fear.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ka wu Filisti be benapo na, nɛ kufu pɛ mo ga,

english_verse: So he asked the Lord what to do. But the Lord would not answer, either in a dream or by a priest or a prophet.
translation_verse: ndoŋ nna nɛ e bishi Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kusɔ nɛ k daga e ka wora. Ama Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ daa maŋ kaŋɛ mo shɛŋ. E daa maŋ bɔla edare so ŋko bɔrɛmatapo so ŋko anebi so m malga n sa mo.

english_verse: Then Saul told his officers, “Find me a woman who can talk to the spirits of the dead. I'll go to her and find out what's going to happen.” His servants told him, “There's a woman at Endor who can talk to spirits of the dead.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Sɔɔl ponte ŋ kaŋɛ mbe benimuana le: “Men fin lejipoche n sa ma nɛ n yɔ mo kutɔ n ya kpal.” Nɛ b yɛ: “Kache ko wɔ Endɔɔ a kpal.”

english_verse: The woman said, “Why are you trying to trick me and get me killed? You know King Saul has killed everyone who talks to the spirits of the dead!”
translation_verse: Nɛ kache na kaŋɛ le: “Manɛ nna nɛ menyee wora nambara nɛ men nya ma m mɔ? Men nyi kashenteŋto kusɔ nɛ Ewura Sɔɔl wora. Men nyi e ka ju bekpalpo nɛ belejipo ashi Israɛl be kasawule so.”

english_verse: Saul replied, “I swear by the living Lord that nothing will happen to you because of this.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Sɔɔl nase kɔnɔ ŋ kaŋɛ le: “Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ e la ma shɛdajipo na be ketre so, kasogberge kikɛ maaŋ ba fo so ŋkpal fo ka kpal ma so.”

english_verse: “Who do you want me to bring up?” she asked. “Bring up the ghost of Samuel,” he answered.
translation_verse: Nɛ kache na bishi mo le: “Wanɛ nɛ fee sha ŋ ka tre n sa fo?” Nɛ e yɛ “Tre Samuɛl n sa ma.”

english_verse: When the woman saw Samuel, she screamed. Then she turned to Saul and said, “You've tricked me! You're the king!”
translation_verse: Kache na ka wu Samuɛl be kebuni nɛ e boŋ to ga ŋ kaŋɛ Sɔɔl le: “Manɛ nna nɛ fee fule ma? Ewura Sɔɔl e la fo!”

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Saul replied. “Just tell me what you see.” She answered, “I see a spirit rising up out of the ground.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura na kaŋɛ mo le: “Sa maa lɔ kufu! Kaŋɛ ma kusɔ nɛ fo wu.” Nɛ e yɛ: “N wu kiyoyu ka lar kasawule to a ba.”

english_verse: “What does it look like?” “It looks like an old man wearing a robe.” Saul knew it was Samuel, so he bowed down low.
translation_verse: Nɛ e bishi mo le: “Manɛ nɛ k duli?” Nɛ kache na yɛ: “K duli kanyɛnnimubi ko ka buu piŋi tenteŋ nna nseŋ lar a ba.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ Sɔɔl pin fanɛ Samuɛl nna nseŋ jɔŋɛ kasawule n chɔrɔ mo.

english_verse: “Why are you bothering me by bringing me up like this?” Samuel asked. “I'm terribly worried,” Saul answered. “The Philistines are about to attack me. God has turned his back on me and won't answer any more by prophets or by dreams. What should I do?”
translation_verse: Nɛ Samuɛl kaŋɛ Sɔɔl le: “Manɛ nna nɛ fo tɔrɔ ma loŋ hale n shin nɛ n naŋ bɛta m ba?” Nɛ Sɔɔl yɛ: “N wɔ tɔrɔ damta to nna! Filisti be basa na bee kɔ ma kena nna nɛ Ebɔrɛ kplaŋ ma so. E maŋ naa bɔla edare ŋko anebiana so a malga a sa ma. Amoso nɛ n tre fo nɛ fo kaŋɛ ma kusɔ nɛ k daga ŋ ka wora.”

english_verse: Samuel said: If the Lord has turned away from you and is now your enemy, don't ask me what to do.
translation_verse: Nɛ Samuɛl kaŋɛ le: “Manɛ nna nɛ fee fin nfɛra ŋ kutɔ saŋɛ so nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ teŋ kplaŋ fo so nɛ fo ki mo doŋ.

english_verse: I've already told you: The Lord has sworn to take the kingdom from you and give it to David. And that's just what he's doing!
translation_verse: N chɛr ŋ kaŋɛ fo fanɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na teŋ yili kumo fanɛ e beeŋ sɔ fo kuwurji na n sa Deevid.

english_verse: When the Lord was angry with the Amalekites, he told you to destroy them, but you didn't do it. That's why the Lord is doing this to you.
translation_verse: Fo ka kini kenu n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nsaa maŋ mur Amalɛk be basa na nɛ kusɔ kama nɛ b kɔ kikɛ na so nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na bee wora fo loŋ na.

english_verse: Tomorrow the Lord will let the Philistines defeat Israel's army, then you and your sons will join me down here in the world of the dead.
translation_verse: Echefo, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ beeŋ shin nɛ Filisti be basa e pɔɔ Israɛl be benapo so, saŋɛ na so, fo nɛ fo mbia beeŋ wu m ba nfe m ba ti ma so.”

english_verse: At once, Saul collapsed and lay stretched out on the floor, terrified at what Samuel had said. He was weak because he had not eaten anything since the day before.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl ka nu kusɔ nɛ Samuɛl kaŋɛ na, nɛ kufu pɛ mo ga nɛ e tɔr epul na to n teŋi to a dese kasawule. E daa maŋ naa kɔ eleŋ ŋkpal e ka daa maŋ ji shɛŋ kachɛ lelemu kikɛ so.

english_verse: The woman came over to Saul, and when she saw that he was completely terrified, she said, “Your Majesty, I listened to you and risked my life to do what you asked.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ kache na firgi n taga mo to n wu fanɛ kufu pɛ mo alegaiso, nɛ e kaŋɛ mo le: “Yiramu, n ta ma kumu nna ŋ kpa kelera pɔɛŋ nseŋ wora kusɔ nɛ fo kaŋɛ ma fanɛ n wora ere na.

english_verse: Now please listen to me. Let me get you a little something to eat. It will give you strength for your walk back to camp.”
translation_verse: Amoso mee kule fo nna naniere bre, nɛ fo nu n sa ma. Shin nɛ n daŋɛ ajibi n sa fo nɛ fo ji saŋɛ na so feeŋ nya eleŋ a yɔ.”

english_verse: “No, I won't eat!” But his officers and the woman kept on urging Saul, until he finally agreed. He got up off the floor and sat on the bed.
translation_verse: Nɛ Sɔɔl kini fanɛ e maaŋ ji shɛŋ. Nɛ mbe benimu na leŋ mo to ga ŋ kaŋɛ mo fanɛ e ji, pɔɛŋ nɛ e shuli nseŋ koso kasawule n chena gedo so.

english_verse: At once the woman killed a calf that she had been fattening up. She cooked part of the meat and baked some thin bread.
translation_verse: Epul to nɛ kache na nya manaŋ m pɛ mbe kena fɔlbi duliduli ko nɛ e bee bela na m mɔ, nseŋ ta nyifu ŋ gbiti n wora bodobodo nɛ a maŋ kɔ yiisi amo to.

english_verse: Then she served the food to Saul and his officers, who ate and left before daylight.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e ta ajibi na n sa Sɔɔl nɛ mbe benimuana na nɛ b ji nseŋ lar kumo be kanyɛso na kikɛ n yɔ.

english_verse: The Philistine army commanders were angry and shouted: Send David back to the town you gave him. We won't have him going into the battle with us. He could turn and fight against us! Saul would take David back as an officer if David brought him the heads of our soldiers.
translation_verse: Ama Filisti be benapo be benimu na daŋ nya agbo nna n wɔtɔ Akish nseŋ kaŋɛ mo le: “Shin nɛ kanyɛn na e bɛta a yɔ kade nɛ fo sa mo na to. Sa maŋ shin nɛ e tu anyi n yɔ kena na to. Nɛ mannɛ aloŋ, e beeŋ naŋ kilgi a kɔ anyi nɛ Sɔɔl e kpal loŋ so n naŋ sɔ mo ŋ ki mbe benapo be enimu.

english_verse: Achish called David over and said: I swear by the living Lord that you've been honest with me, and I want you to fight by my side. I don't think you've done anything wrong from the day you joined me until this very moment. But the other Philistine rulers don't want you to come along.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Akish tre Deevid ŋ kaŋɛ mo le: “Israɛl be Ebɔrɛ nɛ e wɔ ŋkpa to na be ketre so, fee ji kashenteŋ a sa ma. N daa beeŋ ba sha fanɛ ma nɛ fo kikɛ ka ya kɔ kena ere. Baŋ yili kachɛ nɛ fo ba ŋ kutɔ na hale m ba fo kabre, ma ere maŋ wu kulubi kikɛ fo so. Ama bewura nɛ b ka na bre kikɛ maa sha fo ka yɔ kena na to.

english_verse: Go on back home and try not to upset them.
translation_verse: Amoso bɛta a yɔ epe nɛ kagbenewushi. Sa maŋ kaŋ wora kusɔ kama nɛ k beeŋ jija bumo be ŋgbene.”

english_verse: “But what have I done?” David asked. “Do you know of anything I've ever done that would keep me from fighting the enemies of my king?”
translation_verse: Nɛ Deevid kaŋɛ le: “N nyɛnpe, manɛ nɛ n wora? Fo nyi kusɔ ko nɛ n wora nɛ ŋkpal loŋ so m maaŋ tiŋ n tu n nyɛnpe nɛ ma ewura n ya kɔ mo doŋana a?”

english_verse: Achish said: I believe that you're as good as an angel of God, but our army commanders have decided that you can't fight in this battle.
translation_verse: Nɛ Akish yɛ: “Fo asheŋ bɔla ma kenishi ga fanɛ Ebɔrɛ be mbɔ na be eko. Ama bewura ana na e kaŋɛ fanɛ fo sa maŋ tu anyi n yɔ kena na to.

english_verse: You and your troops will have to go back to the town I gave you. Get up and leave tomorrow morning as soon as it's light. I'm pleased with you, so don't let any of this bother you.
translation_verse: Amoso Deevid, a daga fanɛ fo nɛ bekama nɛ men lar Sɔɔl kutɔ m ba ma kutɔ na ka wule ŋ koso echefo kachipurso n lar nfe pɔɛŋ nɛ kakpa e bugi to.”

english_verse: David and his men got up early in the morning and headed back toward Philistia, while the Philistines left for Jezreel.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Deevid nɛ mo braana na wule ŋ koso kachipurdidi m pɛ Ziklag be ekpa nɛ Filisti be benapo na malɛ lar n yɔ Jizreel nɛ b ya kɔ Israɛlebi na kena.

english_verse: It took David and his men three days to reach Ziklag. But while they had been away, the Amalekites had been raiding in the desert around there. They had attacked Ziklag, burned it to the ground,
translation_verse: Kachɛ sasopo na nɛ Deevid nɛ mbe basa luri Ziklag. Ama saŋɛ nɛ Deevid nɛ mbe basa daa maŋ wɔ ndoŋ na, Amalɛkebi na daŋ kre kena nna n ya purge Juda be kelargato be kaseto be kaba so ebi na hale ŋ kɔ Ziklag n chɔɔ kade na kikɛ

english_verse: When David and his men came to Ziklag, they saw the burned-out ruins and learned that their families had been taken captive.
translation_verse: Deevid nɛ mbe basa ka ba wu kananɛ b chɔɔ kade na nseŋ pɛ bumo be beche nɛ mbinyɛnsobi nɛ mbichesobi n choŋ

english_verse: They started crying and kept it up until they were too weak to cry any more.
translation_verse: nɛ b shu ga hale n ya chɛl pɔɛŋ nseŋ yige.

english_verse: David's two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail, had been taken captive with everyone else.
translation_verse: B daŋ pɛ Deevid be beche anyɔ, Ahinɔam nɛ Abigɛl, gba n ti so nna n yɔ.

english_verse: David was desperate. His soldiers were so upset over what had happened to their sons and daughters that they were thinking about stoning David to death. But he felt the Lord God giving him strength,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ kagbenejija tɔr Deevid so, nɛ mbe basa be ŋgbene kikɛ kaa bumo ŋkpal b ka paŋ bumo be mbia so. Nɛ baa kaŋɛ fanɛ baaŋ kpa Deevid ajembu m mɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ e la mbe Ebɔrɛ na leŋ mo to ga.

english_verse: and he said to the priest, “Abiathar, let's ask God what to do.” Abiathar brought everything he needed to get answers from God, and he went over to David.
translation_verse: Nɛ Deevid kaŋɛ Ahimɛlɛk pibinyɛn bɔrɛmatapo Abiata le: “Ta bɔrɛmatapo be kale nɛ baa tre Ɛfɔd na m bar ma.” Nɛ Abiata ta kumo n ya sa mo.

english_verse: Then David asked the Lord, “Should I go after the people who raided our town? Can I catch up with them?” “Go after them,” the Lord answered. “You will catch up with them, and you will rescue your families.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Deevid bishi Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ le: “N ju m buu basa nɛ baa kre kena a purgi basa ere so a? Meeŋ nya bumo m pɛ a?” Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ yɛ: “Nɛ fo ju m buu bumo so, feeŋ ya pɛ bumo n sɔ fo basa.”

english_verse: Some of David's men found an Egyptian out in a field and took him to David. They gave the Egyptian some bread, and he ate it. Then they gave him a drink of water,
translation_verse: Deevid be basa na be beko daŋ ya wu Ijipt be esa ko nna ashi kupuŋ to nseŋ bar mo Deevid kutɔ m ba sa mo ajibi nɛ nchu

english_verse: some dried figs, and two handfuls of raisins. This was the first time in three days he had tasted food or water. Now he felt much better.
translation_verse: nɛ figi be asɔrso wɔlso nɛ asɔrso jiso be asha anyɔ. E ka ji ajibi na nɛ e nya eleŋ, ŋkpal manɛ so, e daa maŋ ji shɛŋ ŋko n nuu nchu nchɛ asa kikɛ.

english_verse: “Who is your master?” David asked. “And where do you come from?” “I'm from Egypt,” the young man answered. “I'm the servant of an Amalekite, but he left me here three days ago because I was sick.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Deevid bishi mo le: “Fo nyɛnpe e la wanɛ? Nnɛ nɛ fo shi?” Nɛ e yɛ: “Ijipt nɛ n shi nsaa la Amalɛk be esa ko be kenya; ama ma nchɛ asa nna na e ka yige ma n lɛ nfe ŋkpal ŋ ka bee lɔ so.

english_verse: We had attacked some towns in the desert where the Cherethites live, in the area that belongs to Judah, and in the desert where the Caleb clan lives. And we burned down Ziklag.”
translation_verse: An ta kena nna n ya tu Chereti be basa nɛ b wɔ Juda be efuli so be kelargato be kaseto be kaba so na nɛ Kalɛb be kanaŋ to ebi be kaba so nseŋ chɔɔ Ziklag.”

english_verse: “Will you take me to those Amalekites?” David asked. “Yes, I will, if you promise with God as a witness that you won't kill me or hand me over to my master.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Deevid bishi mo le: “Feeŋ tiŋ n yɛr ma Amalɛkebi na kutɔ a?” Nɛ e yɛ: “Mm, nɛ feeŋ nase kɔnɔ Ebɔrɛ be ketre to fanɛ fo maaŋ mɔ ma ŋko n ta ma m bɔɔ n nyɛnpe enɔ bre, meeŋ yɛr fo bumo kutɔ.”

english_verse: David attacked just before sunrise the next day and fought until sunset. Four hundred Amalekites rode away on camels, but they were the only ones who escaped.
translation_verse: Kumo be ŋklade kachipurdidi nɛ Deevid nɛ mbe basa ya kɔ bumo kena hale n ya fo kaaseso. Ama Amalɛk be mbrantiɛfɔlbi alfa ana nawule e daŋ nya manaŋ n dii bumo be enyɔma n shile; nɛ b mɔ bumo nɛ b ka na kikɛ.

english_verse: David rescued his two wives and everyone else the Amalekites had taken from Ziklag.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nɛ Deevid sɔ mbe beche anyɔ na nɛ kusɔ kama nɛ Amalɛk be basa na daŋ ta na kikɛ.

english_verse: No one was missing—young or old, sons or daughters. David brought back everything that had been stolen,
translation_verse: Bumo be kusɔ kama daa maŋ foe ŋkpal manɛ so Deevid daŋ sɔ mbe basa na be mbinyɛnsobi nɛ mbichesobi nɛ asɔbɔya nɛ Amalɛkebi daŋ ta na kikɛ na m bɛta n yɔ.

english_verse: including their livestock. David also took the sheep and cattle that the Amalekites had with them, but he kept these separate from the others. Everyone agreed that these would be David's reward.
translation_verse: Ama Amalɛk be basa na be mbolpɔ nɛ ana nɛ b kɔ na bre, e daŋ shin nna nɛ b barga amo n ya yili ŋ kɔr. Nɛ ekama malɛ shuli so fanɛ loŋ be asɔbɔya na e baa la Deevid peya.

english_verse: Some of David's men were good-for-nothings, and they said, “Those men didn't go with us to the battle, so they don't get any of the things we took back from the Amalekites. Let them take their wives and children and go!”
translation_verse: Ama le nɛ Deevid be basa nɛ b daŋ yɔ kena na to nsaa la basa fuloŋ a kɔ amukpakpaso na bre daŋ kaŋɛ: “Ŋkpal basa ere ka maŋ tu anyi n yɔ kena ere to so, anyi nɛ bumo maaŋ barga asɔ nɛ an ya muu kena na to na n sa abar. Ama bumo be ekama beeŋ tiŋ ŋ keta mbe eche nɛ mbia bre a yɔ.”

english_verse: But David said: My friends, don't be so greedy with what the Lord has given us! The Lord protected us and gave us victory over the people who attacked.
translation_verse: Le nɛ Deevid malɛ daŋ kaŋɛ bumo: “Ŋkurgepoana, men sa maŋ kaŋ ta asɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ sa anyi n wora kejimuni. Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kuŋ anyi nseŋ shin nɛ an kɔ m pɔɔ basa nɛ baa ta kena a purgi basa a muu bumo be asɔ a shile na so.

english_verse: Who would pay attention to you, anyway? Soldiers who stay behind to guard the camp get as much as those who go into battle.
translation_verse: Wanɛ nɛ menyee fɛ fanɛ e beeŋ shuli m bɛ kusɔ nɛ men kaŋɛ ere so? Basa kama nɛ b ka keeyi to a keni anyi be asɔ so na nɛ bumo nɛ b yɔ kena na to na kikɛ beeŋ ji nna a sasa.”

english_verse: David made this a law for Israel, and it has been the same ever since.
translation_verse: Amoso Deevid daŋ yili kumo fanɛ mbra nna n sa Israɛlebi na, nɛ bumo alɛ bɛ kumo so hale m ba fo nɛ mbre.

english_verse: David went back to Ziklag with everything they had taken from the Amalekites. He sent some of these things as gifts to his friends who were leaders of Judah, and he told them, “We took these things from the Lord's enemies. Please accept them as a gift.”
translation_verse: Deevid ka bɛta n yɔ Ziklag nɛ e ta asɔ nɛ b ya muu kena to na be ako n ya sa mo teriana nɛ Juda be bejuŋkparpoana na nseŋ kaŋɛ bumo le be kubɔya ere: “Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ mo doŋana na kutɔ nɛ n suge asɔ ere nɛ m ba sa menyi fanɛ kakɛ na.”

english_verse: This is a list of the towns where David sent gifts: Bethel, Ramoth in the Southern Desert, Jattir, Aroer, Siphmoth, Eshtemoa, Racal, the towns belonging to the Jerahmeelites and the Kenites, Hormah, Bor-Ashan, Athach, and Hebron. He also sent gifts to the other towns where he and his men had traveled.
translation_verse: nɛ Hibrɔn be kade to ebi kikɛ nna, nseŋ ta mboŋ kama nɛ mo nɛ mbe basa daŋ kilgi to n yɔ na kikɛ n ti so.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Philistines were fighting Israel at Mount Gilboa. Israel's soldiers ran from the Philistines, and many of them were killed.
