translation_verse: Kebeegboŋ nɛ baa tre Gilbɔa na so nɛ Filistiebi na daŋ yili a kɔ Israɛlebi na kena. B daŋ mɔ Israɛlebi na be bedamta kena na to nna nɛ bumo nɛ b ka na nɛ ewura Sɔɔl nɛ mbe mbinyɛnsobi malɛ shile.

english_verse: The Philistines closed in on Saul and his sons, and they killed his sons Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua.
translation_verse: Ama Filistiebi na daŋ ju m buu bumo so nna nseŋ ya mɔ Sɔɔl be mbinyɛnsobi asa, Jonatan nɛ Abinadab nɛ Malkishuwa.

english_verse: The fighting was fierce around Saul, and he was badly wounded by enemy arrows.
translation_verse: Kena na be kenishipere be kakpa nɛ Sɔɔl daa wɔ, ŋkpal loŋ so, bedoŋ na be atanyembi daŋ da mo nna n doro mo alegaiso.

english_verse: Saul told the soldier who carried his weapons, “Kill me with your sword! I don't want these worthless Philistines to torture and make fun of me.” But the soldier was afraid to kill him. Saul then took out his own sword; he stuck the blade into his stomach, and fell on it.
translation_verse: Nɛ Sɔɔl kaŋɛ enapo nɛ e bee keta mbe akɔsɔ na le: “Ta fo tokobi m mɔ ma! Ŋkpal manɛ so, m maa sha Filistiebi, nnyamase ere ka mɛaŋ ma m mɔ.” Ama enapo na daŋ kini kewora loŋ nna ŋkpal kufu ka daŋ pɛ mo ga so. Ndoŋ nna nɛ Sɔɔl ta mo gbagba be tokobi be kumu ase n yuu kasawule nseŋ tɔr kumo so.

english_verse: When the soldier knew that Saul was dead, he killed himself in the same way.
translation_verse: Enapo nɛ e bee keta Sɔɔl be akɔsɔ na ka wu fanɛ Sɔɔl wu na, nɛ mo alɛ gba wora kananɛ Sɔɔl wora na gbagba n mɔ mbe kumu.

english_verse: Saul was dead, his three sons were dead, and the soldier who carried his weapons was dead. They and all his soldiers died on that same day.
translation_verse: Kananɛ Sɔɔl nɛ mbe mbinyɛnsobi asa na nɛ enapo nɛ e bee keta mbe akɔsɔ na daŋ wu nna na. Kachɛ koŋwule nɛ Sɔɔl nɛ mbe benapo kikɛ daŋ wu.

english_verse: The Israelites on the other side of Jezreel Valley and the other side of the Jordan learned that Saul and his sons were dead. They saw that the Israelite army had run away. So they ran away too, and the Philistines moved into the towns the Israelites had left behind.
translation_verse: Israɛlebi nɛ b wɔ Jizreel be ketaŋɛ be kaba ndoŋ, nɛ bumo nɛ bumo alɛ wɔ Jɔɔdan be lɔr na be epeŋilarkpa be kaba so na ka nu fanɛ Israɛl be benapo shile nɛ b mɔ Sɔɔl nɛ mbe mbinyɛnsobi, nɛ bumo alɛ gba shile n lar bumo be nde to nɛ Filistiebi na ba sɔ amo n chena.

english_verse: The day after the battle, when the Philistines returned to the battlefield to take the weapons of the dead Israelite soldiers, they found Saul and his three sons lying dead on Mount Gilboa.
translation_verse: B ka kɔ kena na ŋ klade, nɛ Filistiebi na yɔ nɛ b ya muu basa nɛ b wu na be asɔ nseŋ wu fanɛ Sɔɔl nɛ mbe mbinyɛnsobi asa na wu a dese kebeegboŋ nɛ baa tre Gilbɔa na so.

english_verse: The Philistines cut off Saul's head and pulled off his armor. Then they put his armor in the temple of the goddess Astarte, and they nailed his body to the city wall of Beth-Shan. They also sent messengers everywhere in Philistia to spread the good news in the temples of their idols and among their people.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ b ta mbe kena to be akɔsɔ na kikɛ n ya yili kegbirche Ashtɔrɛf be lambu to nseŋ gbir mo nɛ mbe mbia asa be eyurana malɛ m mata Bɛf Shan be kade to be egbal be kowushina.

english_verse: The people who lived in Jabesh in Gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul's body.
translation_verse: Jabesh be basa nɛ b wɔ Giliad na ka nu kusɔ nɛ Filistiebi na wora Sɔɔl na,

english_verse: So one night, some brave men from Jabesh went to Beth-Shan. They took down the bodies of Saul and his sons, then brought them back to Jabesh and burned them.
translation_verse: nɛ bumo be basa nɛ b kɔ kenyɛn ga na koso kanyɛso na kikɛ n nite n yɔ Bɛf Shan, n ya lara Sɔɔl nɛ mbe mbinyɛnsobi na be eyurana ashi egbal na so m bɛta amo n yɔ Jabesh n ya chɔɔ amo ndoŋ.

english_verse: They buried the bones under a small tree in Jabesh, and for seven days, they went without eating to show their sorrow.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ b ta bumo be awibi n ya puli kedibi fimbi nɛ baa tre tamariski na be kifito nseŋ kishi nchɛ ashunu kikɛ a ŋini kananɛ bumo be ŋgbene jija bumo.

english_verse: Saul was dead. Meanwhile, David had defeated the Amalekites and returned to Ziklag.
translation_verse: Israɛlebi be ewura Sɔɔl wu kena to nɛ Deevid kɔ m pɔɔ Amalɛkebi na so nseŋ bɛta m ba Ziklag.

english_verse: Three days later, a soldier came from Saul's army. His clothes were torn, and dirt was on his head. He went to David and knelt down in front of him.
translation_verse: Kumo be nchɛ asa be kaman nɛ kabrantiɛbia ko shi ewura Sɔɔl be keeyi to m ba. E daŋ kpɛa mbe asɔbuuso to nna nseŋ wora shishɛr n wurge mbe kumu so a ŋini kagbenejija nɛ k tɔr mo so. Kumo be kaman nɛ e yɔ Deevid kutɔ n ya jɔŋɛ m bunyaŋ mo.

english_verse: David asked, “Where did you come from?” The man answered, “From Israel's army. I barely escaped with my life.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Deevid bishi mo le: “Nnɛ nɛ fo shi?” Nɛ e kaŋɛ: “N shi Israɛlebi be keeyi to nna a shil a mɔlga ma kumu.”

english_verse: “Who won the battle?” David asked. The man said, “Our army turned and ran, but many were wounded and died. Even King Saul and his son Jonathan are dead.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Deevid kaŋɛ mo le: “Kumo ere kaŋɛ ma kusɔ nɛ k wora.” Nɛ e kaŋɛ: “Anyi be benapo e kilgi a shile nɛ b mɔ bumo be bedamta, hale ewura Sɔɔl nɛ mo pibinyɛn Jonatan gba wu.”

english_verse: David asked, “How do you know Saul and Jonathan are dead?”
translation_verse: Nɛ Deevid bishi mo: “Nuso nɛ fo wora m pin fanɛ Sɔɔl nɛ mo pibinyɛn Jonatan wu?”

english_verse: The young man replied: I was on Mount Gilboa and saw King Saul leaning on his spear. The enemy's war chariots and cavalry were closing in on him.
translation_verse: Nɛ kabrantiɛbia na kaŋɛ le: “N daŋ bɔla kebeegboŋ nɛ baa tre Gilbɔa na so a choŋ nna nseŋ wu ewura Sɔɔl nɛ e yirgi mbe kekpa so nɛ mo doŋana be egbaŋɛturko nɛ amo bediipoana bee chambɔ mo a wɔtɔ.

english_verse: When he turned around and saw me, he called me over. I went and asked what he wanted.
translation_verse: Nɛ e gbɛ ŋ keni n wu ma, nseŋ tre ma nɛ n shuliso,

english_verse: Saul asked me, “Who are you?” “An Amalekite,” I answered.
translation_verse: nɛ e bishi esa nɛ e la ma, nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ Amalɛk be esa e la ma.”

english_verse: Then he said, “Kill me! I'm dying, and I'm in terrible pain.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ e kaŋɛ ma le: “Ba m ba mɔ ma, ŋkpal manɛ so, n doro ga; ma alɛ bee wu nna na.”

english_verse: So I killed him. I knew he was too badly wounded to live much longer. Then I took his crown and his arm-band, and I brought them to you, Your Majesty. Here they are.
translation_verse: Nɛ n yɔ n ya mɔ mo, ŋkpal manɛ so, m baa nyi geeŋ fanɛ kananɛ e doro na so e beeŋ wu. Kumo be kaman nɛ n lara kuwurwuro na mbe kumu so nɛ mbe enɔ to be kepinibi nɛ m ba sa fo, n nyɛnpe!

english_verse: At once, David and his soldiers tore their clothes in sorrow.
translation_verse: Deevid ka nu loŋ nɛ mo nɛ basa nɛ b wɔ mo kutɔ na kikɛ kpɛa bumo be asɔbuuso to kagbenejijaso.

english_verse: They cried all day long and would not eat anything. Everyone was sad because Saul, his son Jonathan, and many of the Lord's people had been killed in the battle.
translation_verse: Nseŋ shu keeli ga ŋ kishi n ya fo kaaseso ŋkpal Ewura Sɔɔl nɛ mo pibi Jonatan nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be basa Israɛlebi na be bedamta ka wu kena na to so.

english_verse: David asked the young man, “Where is your home?” The man replied, “My father is an Amalekite, but we live in Israel.”
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Deevid bishi kabrantiɛbia nɛ e bar kubɔya na le: “Nnɛ ebi e la fo?” Nɛ e kaŋɛ: “N la Amalɛkebi be esa nna, nsaa wɔ fo efuli ere so.”

english_verse: David said to him, “Why weren't you afraid to kill the Lord's chosen king? And you even told what you did. It's your own fault that you're going to die!” Then David told one of his soldiers, “Come here and kill this man!” David Sings in Memory of Saul
translation_verse: Nɛ Deevid kaŋɛ Amalɛk be esa na le: “Fo e kil le be asheŋ n sa fo kumu na. Fo ka shuli so fanɛ fo e mɔ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be ewura laraso na so, nɛ le be luwu ere bee ba fo so na.” Kumo be kaman nɛ kabrantiɛbia na wu. Deevid ka shu Sɔɔl nɛ Jonatan be keeli

english_verse: David sang a song in memory of Saul and Jonathan,
translation_verse: Nɛ Deevid kpal Sɔɔl nɛ mo pibinyɛn Jonatan so n shu keeli ŋ karga awɔba.

english_verse: and he ordered his men to teach the song to everyone in Judah. He called it “The Song of the Bow,” and it can be found in The Book of Jashar. This is the song:
translation_verse: Nseŋ yili kumo fanɛ a daga Juda be esa kikɛ ka koya kumo. Ketre nɛ e daŋ sa kashɛ na e la Keta be kashɛ. Nɛ b sibɛ kumo n wɔtɔ Jashɛr be kawɔl to.

english_verse: Don't tell it in Gath or spread the news on the streets of Ashkelon. The godless Philistine women will be happy and jump for joy.
translation_verse: Sa maŋ ber kumo be kubomboŋ ashi Gaaf ŋko Ashkɛlɔn be abɔrbiana so. Nɛ mannɛ aloŋ, Filisti be nnyamaseche na be ŋgbene beeŋ fuli bumo nɛ b baa tɛto kagbenefuliso

english_verse: Don't let dew or rain fall on the hills of Gilboa. Don't let its fields grow offerings for God. There the warriors' shields were smeared with mud, and Saul's own shield was left unpolished.
translation_verse: Sa maŋ shin nɛ bɔrɛ ŋko bunyaŋ a ba Gilbɔa be abee so kikɛ. Sa maŋ shin nɛ kumo alɛ be ndɔana e naŋ wora ajibi. Benapo na be abɛlso kuŋso na kikɛ a dese kasawule a gbelti na. Nɛ Sɔɔl be kebɛlso kuŋso na gba ki kusɔ jiga.

english_verse: The arrows of Jonathan struck, and warriors died. The sword of Saul cut the enemy apart.
translation_verse: Jonatan be keta daa maa to a paŋ. Nɛ Sɔɔl malɛ be tokobi daa maa wu kuwɔr. Bedoŋ lempo nɛ k daa mɔ.

english_verse: It was easy to love Saul and Jonathan. Together in life, together in death, they were faster than eagles and stronger than lions.
translation_verse: Kemaŋkura nɛ kasha nɛ basa daa kɔ n sa Sɔɔl nɛ Jonatan na daa shi ga. Bumo alɛ be ŋkpa nɛ luwu kikɛ malɛ to, b maŋ yige abar. B daa du manaŋ manaŋ a chɔ kajɔnɔkoso, nsaa kɔ eleŋ malɛ a chɔ ebuluŋ.

english_verse: Women of Israel, cry for Saul. He brought you fine red cloth and jewelry made of gold.
translation_verse: “Israɛl be beche, men shu Sɔɔl be keeli! E sa menyi yawu kpakpaso be asɔbuuso nseŋ ta abitasɔ nɛ shuwa n ji menyi kebita.

english_verse: Our warriors have fallen in the heat of battle, and Jonathan lies dead on the hills of Gilboa.
translation_verse: Anyi be benapo lempo tɔr kena to. Kena to nɛ b wu n dese. Jonatan wu a dese Gilbɔa be abee ase.

english_verse: Jonathan, I miss you most! I loved you like a brother. You were truly loyal to me, more faithful than a wife to her husband.
translation_verse: N sipo Jonatan, fo shin nɛ kagbenejija gboŋgboŋi tɔr ma so; ŋkpal fo kasha nɛ fo kɔ n sa ma so; Fo daa sha ma a chɔ kananɛ eche bee sha mo kul.

english_verse: Our warriors have fallen, and their weapons are destroyed.
translation_verse: Anyi be benapo lempo wu, nɛ bumo be akɔsɔ kikɛ ki asɔ jiga.”

english_verse: Later, David asked the Lord, “Should I go back to one of the towns of Judah?” The Lord answered, “Yes.” David asked, “Which town should I go to?” “Go to Hebron,” the Lord replied.
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ Deevid bishi Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ le: “K daga fanɛ n yɔ Juda be ndeana ere be kuko to a?” Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ shuli so ŋ kaŋɛ: “Mm!” Nɛ Deevid naŋ bishi le: “Kade mo e daga ŋ ka yɔ?” Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ: “Yɔ Hibrɔn!”

english_verse: David went to Hebron with his two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail. Ahinoam was from Jezreel, and Abigail was the widow of Nabal from Carmel.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Deevid keta mbe beche anyɔ, Ahinɔam nɛ e shi Jizreel na nɛ ekulpoche Abigɛl nɛ e daa la Nabaal nɛ e shi kebeegboŋ nɛ baa tre Kaamɛl na be eche na n yɔ Hibrɔn.

english_verse: David also told his men and their families to come and live in the villages near Hebron.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e keta benyɛn nɛ b wɔ mo kutɔ na gba nɛ bumo be kanaŋ to ebi n ya chena Hibrɔn nɛ kumo be ndekarso.

english_verse: The people of Judah met with David at Hebron and poured olive oil on his head to show that he was their new king. Then they told David, “The people from Jabesh in Gilead buried Saul.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Juda be basa na ba Hibrɔn m ba duga ŋku n do Deevid be kumu so a ŋini fanɛ b buu mo Juda be kuwura. Deevid ka nu fanɛ Jabesh nɛ k wɔ Giliad na be basa e puli Sɔɔl,

english_verse: David sent messengers to tell them: The Lord bless you! You were kind enough to bury Saul your ruler,
translation_verse: nɛ e shuŋi benyɛn ko fanɛ b ta kubɔya ere n ya sa bumo: “Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e nɛfa menyi ŋkpal men ka wora menyi be ewura kelela nseŋ puli mo so.

english_verse: and I pray that the Lord will be kind and faithful to you. I will be your friend because of what you have done.
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be alelasheŋ nɛ mbe kagbene koŋwule so be asheŋ woraso e baa wɔ menyi so. Ma alɛ gba beeŋ keta menyi nɛnɛ ŋkpal kusɔ nɛ men wora ere so.

english_verse: Saul is dead, but the tribe of Judah has made me their king. So be strong and have courage. Ishbosheth Becomes King of Israel
translation_verse: Men baa kɔ eleŋ nsaa kɔ kenyɛn! Menyi be ewura Sɔɔl wu, nɛ Juda be basa ta ma ŋ ki bumo be ewura.” B ka buu Ishboshɛf Israɛl be kuwura be asheŋ

english_verse: Abner the son of Ner had been the general of Saul's army. He took Saul's son Ishbosheth across the Jordan River to Mahanaim
translation_verse: Neer pibi Abna nɛ e daa la Sɔɔl be benapo be enimu na daŋ ta Sɔɔl pibi Ishboshɛf nna n shile n dii Jɔɔdan be lɔr na n yɔ Mahanaim.

english_verse: and made him king of Israel, including the areas of Gilead, Asher, Jezreel, Ephraim, and Benjamin.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Abna shin nɛ Ishboshɛf ki Giliad nɛ Ashɛr nɛ Jizreel nɛ Efrayim nɛ Bɛnjamin nɛ Israɛl be efuli so kikɛ be ewura.

english_verse: and he ruled from Hebron for seven and a half years. The War between David and Ishbosheth
translation_verse: Hibrɔn to nɛ Deevid daŋ chena n ji Juda be efuli so be kuwura nfɛ ashunu nɛ bargato. Israɛl nɛ Juda be kena be asheŋ

english_verse: One day, Abner and the soldiers of Ishbosheth left Mahanaim and went to Gibeon.
translation_verse: Kachako nɛ Abna nɛ Ishboshɛf be benapo lar Mahanaim be kade to n yɔ Gibiɔn

english_verse: Meanwhile, Joab the son of Zeruiah was leading David's soldiers, and the two groups met at the pool in Gibeon. Abner and his men sat down on one side of the pool, while Joab and his men sat on the other side.
translation_verse: nɛ Jɔab nɛ mo nio la Zeruwa na malɛ keta Deevid be benapo nɛ bumo nɛ bumo ya tu abar ashi Gibiɔn be kepa na ase. Abna nɛ mbe basa daŋ yɔ kepa na be kaba ko so nna nɛ Jɔab malɛ nɛ mbe basa dii n yɔ kumo be kaba ko so.

english_verse: Abner yelled to Joab, “Let's get some of our best soldiers to stand up and fight each other!” Joab agreed,
translation_verse: Nɛ Abna ponte ŋ kaŋɛ Jɔab le: “Men shin nɛ an lara anyi be benapo ere be bumo nɛ b kɔ eleŋ ga nɛ b kɔ abar nɛ an keni.” Nɛ Jɔab shuli so ŋ kaŋɛ le: “K nyalɛ.”

english_verse: and twelve of Ishbosheth's men from the tribe of Benjamin got up to fight twelve of David's men.
translation_verse: Amoso benyɛn kuduanyɔ e daŋ yili n sa Ishboshɛf nɛ e la Sɔɔl pibinyɛn nsɛŋ shi Bɛnjamin be kanaŋ to, n tu Deevid be benyɛn kuduanyɔ na ŋ kɔ.

english_verse: They grabbed each other by the hair and stabbed each other in the side with their daggers. They all died right there! That's why the place in Gibeon is called “Field of Daggers.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ b to m pɛ abar be amu to n da abar nsaŋɛbi nɛ bumo basa adunyɔ nɛ ana na kikɛ wu. Ndoŋ nna nɛ b nase kaboŋ na ashi Gibiɔn fanɛ: “Etokobi be kasawule.”

english_verse: Then everyone started fighting. Both sides fought very hard, but David's soldiers defeated Abner and the soldiers of Israel.
translation_verse: Nɛ kolu gboŋgboŋi ko koso, nɛ Deevid be basa pɔɔ Abna nɛ mbe basa Israɛlebi na so.

english_verse: Zeruiah's three sons were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Asahel could run as fast as a deer in an open field,
translation_verse: Zeruwa gba be mbinyɛnbi asa daŋ ti bumo so. Bumo e daa la Jɔab nɛ Abishai nɛ Asahɛl. Ndoŋ nna nɛ Asahɛl nɛ e daa shile ga fanɛ chibir na,

english_verse: When Abner turned and saw him, he said, “Is that you, Asahel?” Asahel answered, “Yes it is.”
translation_verse: nɛ Abna gbɛ ŋ keni n wu mo nseŋ kaŋɛ le: “Asahɛl, fo nde a?” Nɛ e shuli so ŋ kaŋɛ: “Mm, ma nna.”

english_verse: Abner said, “There are soldiers all around. Stop chasing me and fight one of them! Kill him and take his clothes and weapons for yourself.” But Asahel refused to stop.
translation_verse: Nɛ Abna kaŋɛ mo le: “Yige kebaaju a bɛ ma so! Shile m bɛ benapo ere be eko so n ya pɛ mo n sɔ kusɔ nɛ e kɔ.” Amo kikɛ nɛ Asahɛl kraŋ kini a ju a buu mo so.

english_verse: Abner said, “If you don't turn back, I'll have to kill you! Then I could never face your brother Joab again.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Abna naŋ laŋɛ ŋ kaŋɛ mo le: “Fo baa maŋ bɛta ma so, k beeŋ ki tintiŋ nna n sa ma fanɛ m mɔ fo! Nɛ loŋ malɛ wora, m maaŋ naŋ tiŋ ŋ keni fo da Jɔab be anishito.”

english_verse: But Asahel would not turn back, so Abner struck him in the stomach with the back end of his spear. The spear went all the way through and came out of his back. Asahel fell down and died. Everyone who saw Asahel lying dead just stopped and stood still.
translation_verse: Ama Asahɛl maŋ pɔ aba, amoso Abna daŋ ta mbe kekpa be kedibi nna n da Asahɛl be epun hale nɛ k futi n lar mbe kaman. Ndoŋ nna nɛ Asahɛl tɔr kasawule n wu. Ekama malɛ nɛ e bee choŋ nseŋ wu mo bee yili nna ŋ keni mo kakpa nɛ e wu a dese na.

english_verse: But Joab and Abishai went after Abner. Finally, about sunset, they came to the hill of Ammah, not far from Giah on the road to Gibeon Desert.
translation_verse: Ama epeŋi ka bee tɔr nɛ Jɔab nɛ Abishai shile n ju Abna n ya fo Ammaa be kebee nɛ k wɔ Giya be epeŋilarkpa be kaba so a yɔ ekpa nɛ k dese a yɔ Gibiɔn be kiyi to na.

english_verse: Abner brought the men of Benjamin together in one group on top of a hill, and they got ready to fight.
translation_verse: Nɛ Bɛnjamin be kanaŋ to ebi be benyɛn ko ba kulti Abna ashi kebee na be esoso nɛ b kɔ mo kena.

english_verse: Abner shouted to Joab, “Aren't we ever going to stop killing each other? Don't you know that the longer we keep on doing this, the worse it's going to be when it's all over? When are you going to order your men to stop chasing their own relatives?”
translation_verse: Nɛ Abna ponte awɔrso ŋ kaŋɛ Jɔab le: “K daga fanɛ an baa wɔtɔ a kɔ abar mbaanaayɔ a? Fo maŋ nyi fanɛ kumo be lalaloge anyi maaŋ nya shɛŋ, ama kenyaŋɛto n wɔtɔ abar a? An la menyi be efuli so ebi nna, saŋɛ mo nɛ feeŋ kaŋɛ fo basa nɛ b yige kebaakɔ anyi?”

english_verse: Joab shouted back, “I swear by the living God, if you hadn't spoken, my men would have chased their relatives all night!”
translation_verse: Nɛ Jɔab kaŋɛ le: “Ebɔrɛ e la ma shɛdajipo. Nɛ fanɛ fo daa maŋ malga nna, dafanɛ ma basa ere kraa beeŋ ju m bɛ menyi so hale n ya fo echefo chipurso.”

english_verse: Joab took his trumpet and blew the signal for his soldiers to stop chasing the soldiers of Israel. At once, the fighting stopped.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Jɔab foŋ kabel nɛ mbe basa yige kebaaju a bɛ Israɛlebi na so. Ndoŋ nna nɛ kolu na ku.

english_verse: Abner and his troops marched through the Jordan River valley all that night. Then they crossed the river and marched all morning until they arrived back at Mahanaim.
translation_verse: Nɛ Abna nɛ mbe basa nite kanyɛso na kikɛ m bɔla Jɔɔdan be ketaŋɛ na to n ya dii Jɔɔdan be Lɔr na, nseŋ nite loŋ nɛ kare ya chɛ nɛ b ta n chuge so hale n ya Mahanaim.

english_verse: Joab and his troops carried Asahel's body to Bethlehem and buried him in the family burial place. Then they marched all night and reached Hebron before sunrise.
translation_verse: Jɔab nɛ mbe basa daŋ ta Asahɛl be kebuni nna n ya puli bumo kanaŋ to be kejembu laŋ be nchaŋ to ashi Bɛtlɛhɛm. Kumo be kaman nɛ b nite kumo be kanyɛso na kikɛ n ya fo Hibrɔn kachipurdidi.

english_verse: As the war went on between the families of David and Saul, Abner was gaining more power than ever in Saul's family.
translation_verse: Jemanɛ nɛ Deevid be kanaŋ to ebi nɛ Sɔɔl be kanaŋ to ebi bee kɔ kena na, Abna nawule ashi Sɔɔl be kanaŋ to ebi to be asheŋ woraso e daa bɔlɔ kenishi saŋkama.

english_verse: He had even slept with a wife of Saul by the name of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah. But Saul's son Ishbosheth told Abner, “You shouldn't have slept with one of my father's wives!”
translation_verse: Kachako nɛ Sɔɔl pibi Ishboshɛf ku Abna kɔnɔ fanɛ mo nɛ Sɔɔl mo jipo Rizpa nɛ e la Aiya pibiche na di keche nɛ kenyɛn.

english_verse: Abner was very angry because of what Ishbosheth had said, and he told Ishbosheth: Am I some kind of worthless dog from Judah? I've always been loyal to your father's family and to his relatives and friends. I haven't turned you over to David. And yet you talk to me as if I've committed a crime with this woman.
translation_verse: Nɛ Abna nya agbo ga ŋ kaŋɛ: “Fee fɛ fanɛ meeŋ debɔr Sɔɔl a, ŋko fee fɛ fanɛ n yili Judaebi be kaman nna? Sososo na kikɛ nɛ m bugi kagbene n shuŋ fo tuto Sɔɔl nɛ mo sipoana nɛ mo teriana. Ma alɛ e mɔlga fo ashi Deevid be enɔ to. Ama kabre ma e ki esa lubi fo kutɔ ŋkpal eche so na!

english_verse: God said that he wouldn't let anyone in Saul's family ever be king again and that David would be king instead. He also said that David would rule both Israel and Judah, all the way from Dan in the north to Beersheba in the south.
translation_verse: Nɛ m baa maŋ chɛ Deevid to nɛ e ji kuwura fanɛ kananɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nase kɔnɔ n sa mo fanɛ e beeŋ sɔ kuwurji na ashi Sɔɔl nɛ mbe kanaŋ kutɔ n sa mo nɛ e ki Israɛl nɛ Juda kikɛ be ewura, yili Dan be kasawule nɛ k wɔ kelargato be esoso na so n ya fo Bɛshiba nɛ k wɔ kelargato be kaseto be kaba so kikɛ na, kumo ere Ebɔrɛ e mɔ ma!”

english_verse: Ishbosheth was so afraid of Abner that he could not even answer.
translation_verse: Nɛ kufu pɛ Ishboshɛf ga hale nɛ e maŋ naŋ tiŋ m bugi kɔnɔ gba.

english_verse: Abner sent some of his men to David with this message: “You should be the ruler of the whole nation. If you make an agreement with me, I will persuade everyone in Israel to make you their king.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Abna shuŋi mbɔ Deevid kutɔ, fanɛ b ya kaŋɛ mo le: “Fo e naa shin nɛ fo ki kasawule ere kikɛ so be ewura, amoso shin nɛ ma nɛ fo e wora kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre nɛ n chɛ fo to nɛ fo sɔ Israɛl be efuli kikɛ ŋ ki feya.”

english_verse: David sent this message back: “Good! I'll make an agreement with you. But before I will even talk with you about it, you must get Saul's daughter Michal back for me.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Deevid yɛ: “Kenyalɛ! Kusɔ koŋwule nɛ meeŋ yili so nɛ ma nɛ fo e wora kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre n sa abar e la fanɛ, fo baa ba nɛ fo ba wu ma, fo keta Sɔɔl pibiche Mikaal m ba sa ma.”

english_verse: David sent a few of his officials to Ishbosheth to give him this message: “Give me back my wife Michal! I killed
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Deevid shuŋi mbɔ Ishboshɛf kutɔ fanɛ b ya kaŋɛ mo le: “Men shin nɛ ma eche Mikaal e laŋɛ m ba ŋ kutɔ, ŋkpal manɛ so, Filistiebi be basa kalfa nɛ m mɔ pɔɛŋ nseŋ nya mo n ta.”

english_verse: Ishbosheth sent some of his men to take Michal away from her new husband, Paltiel the son of Laish.
translation_verse: Nɛ Ishboshɛf sɔ Mikaal ashi mo kul Paltiɛl nɛ e la Laash pibinyɛn na kutɔ.

english_verse: Paltiel followed Michal and the men all the way to Bahurim, crying as he walked. But he went back home after Abner ordered him to leave.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Mikaal mo kul teŋi keeli m bɛ bumo so hale n ya fo Bahurim pɔɛŋ nɛ Abna kaŋɛ mo fanɛ e bɛta a yɔ epe. Nɛ e bɛta.

english_verse: Abner talked with the leaders of the tribes of Israel and told them, “You've wanted to make David your king for a long time now.
translation_verse: Nɛ Abna yɔ Israɛlebi be bejuŋkparpo na kutɔ n ya ber bare nseŋ kaŋɛ bumo le: “Men ka bee fin fanɛ Deevid e ki menyi be ewura na chɛr ga.

english_verse: So do it! After all, God said he would use his servant David to rescue his people Israel from their enemies, especially from the Philistines.”
translation_verse: Naniere bre men nya loŋ be ekpa. Men baa nyiŋi kusɔ nɛ Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ na.” E yɛ: “Meeŋ bɔla ma kayɛrbi Deevid so m mɔlga ma basa Israɛlebi ashi bumo doŋana kutɔ, fɔŋfɔŋ Filisti be basa na.”

english_verse: Finally, Abner talked with the tribe of Benjamin. Then he left for Hebron to tell David everything that the tribe of Benjamin and the rest of the people of Israel wanted to do.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Abna ya malga Bɛnjamin be kanaŋ to ebi kutɔ nseŋ yɔ Hibrɔn n ya kaŋɛ Deevid kusɔ nɛ Bɛnjamin be kanaŋ to ebi nɛ Israɛlebi na yili fanɛ baaŋ wora.

english_verse: soldiers with him, and when they got to Hebron, David gave a big feast for them.
translation_verse: Abna daŋ keta mbe benapo adunyɔ nna m ba Deevid kutɔ ashi Hibrɔn, nɛ Deevid wora kejigboŋ n sa bumo.

english_verse: After the feast, Abner said, “Your Majesty, let me leave now and bring Israel here to make an agreement with you. You'll be king of the whole nation, just as you've been wanting.” David told Abner he could leave, and he left without causing any trouble. Joab Kills Abner
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Abna kaŋɛ Deevid le: “Nɛ fo sa ma akpa, meeŋ shin nɛ Israɛlebi kikɛ e sɔ fo fanɛ bumo be ewura, nɛ fo nya kusɔ nɛ fee sha nsaa ji kuwura kasawule na kikɛ so.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ Deevid ta kɔnɔ lela ŋ kela mo nɛ e yɔ nɛ kayurwushi. B ka mɔ Abna be asheŋ

english_verse: Right after they arrived, someone told Joab, “Abner visited the king, and the king let him go. Abner even left without causing any trouble.”
translation_verse: Jɔab nɛ mbe basa ka ba, nɛ b kaŋɛ mo fanɛ Abna nɛ mbe basa ba ewura Deevid kutɔ nɛ e ta kɔnɔ lela ŋ kela bumo nɛ b bɛta.

english_verse: Joab went to David and said, “What have you done? Abner came to you, and you let him go. Now he's long gone!
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Jɔab yɔ ewura Deevid kutɔ n ya kaŋɛ mo le: “Manɛ nna nɛ fo wora loŋ? Manɛ nna nɛ fo shin nɛ Abna ba fo kutɔ nseŋ naŋ bɛta?

english_verse: You know Abner—he came to trick you. He wants to find out how strong your army is and to know everything you're doing.”
translation_verse: E ba nna nɛ e ba fule fo m pin kusɔ nɛ fee wora kikɛ nɛ kaplɛkama nɛ fee du fo aya. Ma alɛ baa nyi geeŋ fanɛ fo nyi kumo be loŋ!”

english_verse: Joab left David, then he sent some messengers to catch up with Abner. They brought him back from the well at Sirah, but David did not know anything about it.
translation_verse: Jɔab ka lar Deevid kutɔ na be kaman, nɛ e shuŋi mbɔ fanɛ b ya bar Abna, ndoŋ nna nɛ b yɔ Sira be ketirbu na ase n ya keta mo m ba; ama Deevid daa maŋ nyi mbe keba na be asheŋ.

english_verse: When Abner returned to Hebron, Joab pretended he wanted to talk privately with him. So he took Abner into one of the small rooms that were part of the town gate and stabbed him in the stomach. Joab killed him because Abner had killed Joab's brother Asahel. Abner's Funeral
translation_verse: Abna ka ba na nɛ Jɔab keta mo n lar kabunagboŋ na ekpa fanɛ e ka bee sha nɛ e kuli m malga mo kutɔ na, nseŋ ta kasaŋɛ n da mbe epun nɛ e wu. Ŋkpal Abna ka mɔ Jɔab mo sipo Asahɛl so nɛ Jɔab malɛ mɔ mo na.

english_verse: David heard how Joab had killed Abner, and he said, “I swear to the Lord that I am completely innocent of Abner's death!
translation_verse: Deevid ka nu Abna be luwu na be asheŋ nɛ e kaŋɛ le: “Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na gbagba nyi fanɛ ma nɛ ma beyaasepo maŋ nyi Abna be luwu ere be asheŋ.

english_verse: Joab and his family are the guilty ones. I pray that Joab's family will always be sick with sores and other skin diseases. May they all be cowards, and may they die in war or starve to death.”
translation_verse: Ama kumo be kasogberge beeŋ ba Jɔab nɛ mbe kanaŋ kikɛ so! Kumo e la fanɛ echefoso, bumo be kanaŋ mo nɛ k beeŋ koso be enyɛn ko beeŋ lɔ babaso be kulɔ ŋko keboti, ŋko e beeŋ baa la esa nɛ e maaŋ tiŋ n shuŋ benyɛn be kushuŋ ama beche peya ŋko e beeŋ baa la esa nɛ e beeŋ wu kena to, ŋko esa nɛ e maaŋ ji m moɛ kikɛ!”

english_verse: Joab and his brother Abishai killed Abner because he had killed their brother Asahel in the battle at Gibeon.
translation_verse: Jɔab nɛ mo sipo Abishai e daŋ wora kɔnɔ m mɔ Abna ŋkpal e ka mɔ bumo sipo Asahɛl ashi Gibiɔn be kena to so. B ka puli Abna be asheŋ

english_verse: David told Joab and everyone with him, “Show your sorrow by tearing your clothes and wearing sackcloth! Walk in front of Abner's body and cry!” David walked behind the stretcher on which Abner's body was being carried.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Deevid ponte ŋ kaŋɛ Jɔab nɛ mbe basa fanɛ b kpɛa bumo be asɔbuuso to, nseŋ ta kagbenejijaso be asɔbuuso m buu n shu Abna be keeli. Ewura Deevid gbagba e daŋ wora Abna be keeli.

english_verse: Abner was buried in Hebron, while David and everyone else stood at the tomb and cried loudly.
translation_verse: Hibrɔn nɛ b daŋ puli Abna, nɛ ewura Deevid shu ga ashi mbe nchaŋ ase. Basa nɛ b wɔ ndoŋ na gba kikɛ daŋ shu ga.

english_verse: Then the king sang a funeral song about Abner: Abner, why should you have died like an outlaw?
translation_verse: Le nɛ Deevid daŋ shu ŋ karga awɔba ashi Abna be keeli to. “Abna, manɛ nna nɛ fo wu fanɛ ewulpo loŋ?

english_verse: No one tied your hands or chained your feet, yet you died as a victim of murderers. Everyone started crying again.
translation_verse: B daa maŋ kre fo enɔana. Bumo alɛ daa maŋ kre fo aya gba. Ama fo wu fanɛ esa nɛ beyu mɔ.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ basa na naŋ pante kushu n lɛ to.

english_verse: Then they brought some food to David and told him he would feel better if he had something to eat. It was still daytime, and David said, “I swear to God that I won't take a bite of bread or anything else until sunset!”
translation_verse: Kamɔnchɛ na basa wora ania nɛ b sa Deevid kusɔ ko nɛ e ji, ama e daŋ bɔ ntaŋ nna fanɛ nɛ epeŋi baa maŋ tɔr pɔɛŋ nɛ n ji ajibi kumo ere Ebɔrɛ e mɔ mo!

english_verse: Everyone noticed what David did, and they liked it, just as they always liked what he did.
translation_verse: Kusɔ nɛ k wora na daŋ bɔlɔ basa na kikɛ kenishi. Kashenteŋto ewura Deevid be kusɔ nɛ e wora na daŋ bɔlɔ bumo kenishi ga.

english_verse: Now the people of Judah and Israel were certain that David had nothing to do with killing Abner.
translation_verse: Kumo be kamɔnchɛ na nɛ ewura Deevid be basa, nɛ Israɛlebi na yirda fanɛ ewura Deevid be enɔ maŋ wɔ Abna be luwu na be asheŋ to.

english_verse: David said to his officials, “Don't you realize that today one of Israel's great leaders has died?
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura na kaŋɛ mbe benimuana le: “Men maŋ nyi fanɛ esa gboŋ ko wu Israɛl to kabre a?

english_verse: I am the chosen king, but Joab and Abishai have more power than I do. So God will have to pay them back for the evil thing they did.”
translation_verse: Kashenteŋto nna fanɛ ma e la Ebɔrɛ be ewura laraso, ama kabre ma alɛ maŋ naa kɔ eleŋ. Zeruwa be mbinyɛnbi Jɔab nɛ Abishai bre bee ŋini ma nna fanɛ b kɔ eleŋ ga a chɔ ma. Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e ta kasogberge nɛ k daga n sa le be basa lubi ere!”

english_verse: Ishbosheth felt like giving up after he heard that Abner had died in Hebron. Everyone in Israel was terrified.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl pibinyɛn Ishboshɛf ka nu fanɛ b mɔ Abna ashi Hibrɔn, nɛ mbe aba pɔ mo nɛ keyeŋiyeŋi tɔr Israɛlebi na malɛ gba so.

english_verse: Ishbosheth had put the two brothers Baanah and Rechab in charge of the soldiers who raided enemy villages. Rimmon was their father, and they were from the town of Beeroth, which belonged to the tribe of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Ishboshɛf daŋ ta Baana nɛ Reekab nɛ bumo tuto e la Rimmɔn na nna ŋ ki benapo nɛ baa ta kena a purgi basa a pɛ bumo na be bejuŋkparpo. B shi Bɛɛrɔf nɛ k la Bɛnjamin be yiri to ebi be kasawule na be kaba ko nna.

english_verse: The people who used to live in Beeroth had run away to Gittaim, and they still live there.
translation_verse: Bɛɛrɔf be ndetobia gbagba daŋ shile nna n ya chena Gittaim. B kraa tase ndoŋ fanɛ befɔ hale kabre.

english_verse: Saul's son Jonathan had a son named Mephibosheth, who had not been able to walk since he was five years old. It happened when someone from Jezreel told his nurse that Saul and Jonathan had died. She hurried off with the boy in her arms, but he fell and injured his legs.
translation_verse: Sɔɔl mo nanabiana na be eko e daa la Jonatan pibinyɛn Mifiboshɛf. Saŋɛ nɛ kubɔya shi Jezreel m ba fanɛ b mɔ Sɔɔl nɛ Jonatan na nɛ eche nɛ e bee keta Mifiboshɛf na ta mo a shile. Ŋkpal e ka daa kuse so, nɛ kebia na suge mbe enɔ to n tɔr ŋ ki bobi. Loŋ be saŋɛ nɛ Mifiboshɛf la nfɛ anu.

english_verse: One day about noon, Rechab and Baanah went to Ishbosheth's house. It was a hot day, and he was resting
translation_verse: Kapiidi ko nɛ Ishboshɛf dese a wushi nɛ Reekab nɛ Baana yɔ mbe laŋ to.

english_verse: in his bedroom. The two brothers went into the house, pretending to get some flour. But once they were inside, they stabbed Ishbosheth in the stomach and killed him. Then they cut off his head and took it with them. Rechab and Baanah walked through the Jordan River valley all night long.
translation_verse: B ka luri Ishboshɛf be ebu to, nɛ b pe kasaŋɛ n da mbe epun m mɔ nseŋ ku mbe kumu n ta kumo m bɔla Jɔɔdan be ketaŋɛ na to n nite kanyɛso le hale nɛ kare ya chɛ.

english_verse: Finally they turned west and went to Hebron. They went in to see David and told him, “Your Majesty, here is the head of Ishbosheth, the son of your enemy Saul who tried to kill you! The Lord has let you get even with Saul and his family.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ b ta kumu na n ya sa ewura Deevid ashi Hibrɔn nseŋ kaŋɛ mo le: “Fo doŋ Sɔɔl nɛ e daa sha kemɔ fo na pibinyɛn Ishboshɛf be kumu nde. Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e shin nɛ fo kuwurji koso kabre a kɔ Sɔɔl nɛ mo nanabiana a tal to na.”

english_verse: David answered: I swear that only the Lord rescues me when I'm in trouble!
translation_verse: Nɛ Deevid shuli so ŋ kaŋɛ bumo le: “Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ e la ma shɛdajipo na nawule e mɔlga ma ashi tɔrɔ kikɛ to!

english_verse: When a man came to Ziklag and told me that Saul was dead, he thought he deserved a reward for bringing good news. But I grabbed him and killed him.
translation_verse: Kabɔ nɛ e ba Ziklag m ba kaŋɛ ma Sɔɔl be luwu be asheŋ na daŋ fɛ nna fanɛ baru lela nɛ e daa kɔ a bar ma. Ama n daŋ shin nna nɛ b mɔ mo. Mbe baru na be kebɔ be tɔnɔ nɛ e daŋ nya nna na.

english_verse: You evil men have done something much worse than he did. You've killed an innocent man in his own house and on his own bed. I'll make you pay for that. I'll wipe you from the face of the earth!
translation_verse: Shɛŋ shɛŋ maŋ naŋ lubi a chɔ fanɛ basa lubi ka beeŋ ya mɔ esa nɛ e maŋ wora kulubi kikɛ mbe laŋ to ashi mbe gedo so gba! Ma alɛ gba beeŋ wora menyi n tal to ŋkpal men ka mɔ kanyɛn ere so, menyi alɛ gba maaŋ naŋ ji efute durnya ere to.”

english_verse: Then David said to his troops, “Kill these two brothers! Cut off their hands and feet and hang their bodies by the pool in Hebron. But bury Ishbosheth's head in Abner's tomb near Hebron.” And they did.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Deevid ponte ŋ kaŋɛ mbe benapo na fanɛ b mɔ bumo, nɛ b mɔ Reekab nɛ Baana nseŋ ku bumo be enɔana nɛ bumo be aya nseŋ ya chɛ bumo eyurana efɔl n shiga ndibi so ashi Hibrɔn be kepa ase. Kumo be kaman nɛ b ta Ishboshɛf be kumu na n ya puli Abna be kebeelaŋ be nchaŋ to ashi Hibrɔn.

english_verse: King Hiram of Tyre sent some officials to David. Carpenters and stone workers came with them, and they brought cedar logs so they could build David a palace.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Taye be ewura Hiram shuŋi mbɔ ewura Deevid kutɔ nseŋ sa mo ndibi nɛ baa tre sida na n ta ekapɛnta nɛ basa nɛ baa ta ajembu a pɔr n ti so fanɛ b ya pɔr ewura be laŋ n sa Deevid.

english_verse: He lived in Hebron for the first seven and a half years and ruled only Judah. Then he moved to Jerusalem, where he ruled both Israel and Judah for
translation_verse: Nfɛ ashunu nɛ bargato nɛ e daŋ chena Hibrɔn ashi Juda be efuli so n ji kuwura, nseŋ naŋ chena Jerusalɛm malɛ n ji kuwura Israɛl nɛ Juda kikɛ be efuli so nfɛ adesa nɛ asa.

english_verse: David told his troops, “You will have to go up through the water tunnel to get those Jebusites. I hate people like them who can't walk or see.” That's why there is still a rule that says, “Only people who can walk and see are allowed in the temple.” David captured the fortress on Mount Zion, then he moved there and named it David's City. He had the city rebuilt, starting with the landfill to the east.
translation_verse: B ka sɔ kumɔlga be kakpa lempo na n loge, nɛ ewura Deevid chena ndoŋ nseŋ nase kumo “Deevid be kade.” Kumo be kaman nɛ e pɔr nwu m bɛ abar so n chambɔ kumo ashi kebee nɛ k wɔ ndoŋ be epeŋilarkpa be kaba so na.

english_verse: The Jebusites lived in Jerusalem, and David led his army there to attack them. The Jebusites did not think he could get in, so they told him, “You can't get in here! We could keep you out, even if we couldn't see or walk!”
translation_verse: Kachako nɛ ewura Deevid nɛ mbe basa yɔ nɛ b ya kɔ Jerusalɛmebi kena. Ama Jebusiebi nɛ b wɔ ndoŋ na bre daa fɛ nna fanɛ ewura Deevid maaŋ tiŋ m pɔɔ bumo so nseŋ kaŋɛ le: “Fo maaŋ tiŋ anyi kikɛ. Anyi to be etanpo nɛ ebobi gba beeŋ tiŋ ŋ kɔ m pɔɔ fo so.”

english_verse: David became a great and strong ruler, because the Lord All-Powerful was on his side.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ ka daa wɔ mo kutɔ so, e daa nya eleŋ nna a ti so saŋkama.

english_verse: David knew that the Lord had made him king of Israel and that he had made him a powerful ruler for the good of his people. David's Sons Born in Jerusalem (
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nɛ Deevid pin fanɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e yili kumo kashenteŋto fanɛ e ki Israɛl be ewura nsaa nɛfa mbe kuwurji ŋkpal Israɛlebi na so.

english_verse: After David left Hebron and moved to Jerusalem, he married many women from Jerusalem, and he had a lot of children.
translation_verse: Pɔɛŋ nɛ Deevid lar Hibrɔn m ba Jerusalɛm na, e daŋ ta bejipo nɛ beche nna n ti bumo nɛ e daa kɔ na so nseŋ kurge mbinyɛnbi nɛ mbichebi damta.

english_verse: Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia,
translation_verse: Ibhar nɛ Elishuwa nɛ Nefɛg nɛ Jefaya nɛ

english_verse: Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet. David Fights the Philistines (
translation_verse: Elishama nɛ Eliada nɛ Elifelɛt. Deevid ka kɔ m pɔɔ Filistiebi so be asheŋ

english_verse: The Philistines heard that David was now king of Israel, and they came into the hill country to try and capture him. But David found out and went into his fortress.
translation_verse: Filistiebi ka nu fanɛ Deevid ki Israɛl be ewura na nɛ bumo be benapo kikɛ ya ka fin mo nɛ b pɛ. Deevid malɛ ka nu loŋ nɛ e shile n yɔ kakpa nɛ e beeŋ nya kumɔlga.

english_verse: David asked the Lord, “Should I attack the Philistines? Will you let me win?” The Lord told David, “Attack! I will let you win.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Deevid bishi Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ le: “K daga ŋ ka ya kɔ Filistiebi ere kena a? Meeŋ tiŋ m pɔɔ bumo so a?” Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ shuli so ŋ kaŋɛ: “Mm, ya kɔ bumo! Meeŋ shin nɛ men kɔ m pɔɔ bumo so kashenteŋto!”

english_verse: David attacked the Philistines and defeated them. Then he said, “I watched the Lord break through my enemies like a mighty flood.” So he named the place “The Lord Broke Through.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Deevid nɛ mbe benapo ya kɔ m pɔɔ Filistiebi na so nseŋ kaŋɛ le: “Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ bure n luri ma doŋana na to fanɛ kananɛ nchu bee bɔlɔ a shile eleŋso na.” Kumo be kaman nɛ e nase kaboŋ na ketre: “Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ e bee bure e luri na.”

english_verse: David and his troops also carried away the idols that the Philistines had left behind.
translation_verse: Filistiebi be benapo na ka shile n yige bumo be agbir na nɛ Deevid nɛ mbe basa ta amo.

english_verse: Some time later, the Philistines came back into the hill country and camped in Rephaim Valley.
translation_verse: K maŋ chɛr ko nɛ Filistiebi be benapo na naaŋ bɛta n ya pesaŋ to n sɔ Refaebi be ketaŋɛ na to kikɛ.

english_verse: David asked the Lord what he should do, and the Lord answered: Don't attack them from the front. Circle around behind and attack from among the balsam trees.
translation_verse: Nɛ Deevid naaŋ bishi Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kusɔ nɛ e beeŋ wora, nɛ e kaŋɛ mo le: “Men sa maŋ kaŋ ta kena n tu bumo nfe, ama men bela ase n ya kuŋ bumo ndibi nɛ baa tre balsam na ase ŋ kɔ bumo ndoŋ.

english_verse: Wait until you hear a sound in the treetops like marching troops. Then attack quickly! That sound will mean I have marched out ahead of you to fight the Philistine army.
translation_verse: Men ka baŋ nu awɔr ka bee chɛ ndibi na to, kumo ere men fara a kɔ, ŋkpal manɛ so, meeŋ juŋkpar menyi n ya kɔ m pɔɔ Filistiebi be benapo na so.”

english_verse: David obeyed the Lord and defeated the Philistines. He even chased them all the way from Geba to the entrance to Gezer.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Deevid wora kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ na nseŋ ju Filisti be benapo na kikɛ ashi Gɛba n ya fo Gɛza.

english_verse: The people carrying the chest walked six steps, then David sacrificed an ox and a choice cow.
translation_verse: Basa nɛ b sulɔ deka na ka teŋi ateŋgreŋ ashe, nɛ e shin nɛ b yili; ndoŋ nna nɛ e lara gbolu nɛ kena fɔlbi duliduli ko n lara sarga n sa Ebɔrɛ.

english_verse: He was dancing for the Lord with all his might, but he wore only a linen cloth.
translation_verse: Deevid daŋ dela wajɛ fuful nawule mbe kashɛr to nna nseŋ ta mbe eleŋ kikɛ n cha m maŋkura Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ.

english_verse: He and everyone else were celebrating by shouting and blowing horns while the chest was being carried along.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ mo nɛ Israɛlebi na kikɛ ta ŋkre be deka na, a foŋ mbel a cha awɔr kagbenefuliso a yɔ Jerusalɛm.

english_verse: Saul's daughter Michal looked out her window and watched the chest being brought into David's City. But when she saw David jumping and dancing for the Lord, she was disgusted.
translation_verse: B ka ta ŋkre be deka na a luri kade to na, nɛ Sɔɔl pibiche Mikaal keni tokuro to n wu ewura Deevid ka bee cha a tɛto, nɛ mbe asheŋ nu mo agbo alegaiso nɛ e maŋ naa keni mo a bɔlɔ kenishi.

english_verse: They put the sacred chest on a new ox cart and started bringing it down the hill from Abinadab's house. Abinadab's sons Uzzah and Ahio were guiding the ox cart,
translation_verse: B daŋ lara kumo Abinadab be laŋ nɛ k yil kebee so na to nna nseŋ ta kumo n deŋi turko popɔr ko so a yɔ. Abinadab be mbinyɛnsobi Uzza nɛ Ahio e daa kɔ kumo a yɔ.

english_verse: led them to Baalah in Judah, which was also called Kiriath-Jearim. They were going there to get the sacred chest and bring it back to Jerusalem. The throne of the Lord All-Powerful is above the winged creatures on top of this chest, and he is worshiped there.
translation_verse: nseŋ juŋkpar bumo n yɔ Baala nɛ k wɔ Juda be efuli so na, nɛ b ya ta Enyɛnpe be ŋkre be deka nɛ mbe ketre Enyɛnpetale na deŋ kumo so ashi emalaika anyɔ na be nferinto na.

english_verse: with Ahio walking in front of it.
translation_verse: Ahio e daŋ juŋkpar.

english_verse: Some of the people of Israel were playing music on small harps and other stringed instruments, and on tambourines, castanets, and cymbals. David and the others were happy, and they danced for the Lord with all their might.
translation_verse: Deevid nɛ Israɛlebi na kikɛ daŋ ta bumo be eleŋ kikɛ nna a boŋ nshɛ a cha a maŋkura Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na. B daa laŋ ejaŋjilaŋ nɛ egoji nɛ ŋkure nɛ echakachaka nɛ ayawa nna.

english_verse: But when they came to Nacon's threshing-floor, the oxen stumbled, so Uzzah reached out and took hold of the sacred chest.
translation_verse: B ka fo Naakɔn be kugooro nɛ e b bri ayu kumo so na, nɛ egbolu na fiti nɛ ŋkre be deka na bee shin nɛ k tɔr nɛ Uzza teŋi enɔ nɛ e suse kumo to.

english_verse: The Lord God was very angry with Uzzah for doing this, and he killed Uzzah right there beside the chest.
translation_verse: Epul to nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nya agbo ga n wɔtɔ Uzza nseŋ mɔ mo, ŋkpal e ka maŋ sa mo bunyaŋ so. Uzza daŋ wu n dese ŋkre be deka na ase nna.

english_verse: David got angry with God for killing Uzzah. He named that place “Bursting Out Against Uzzah,” and that's what it's still called.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Deevid nya agbo ga ŋkpal Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ka gberge Uzza kusoe m mɔ so. Hale nɛ mbre Uzza be kasogberge nɛ b kraa tre kakpa na.

english_verse: David was afraid of the Lord and thought, “Should I really take the sacred chest to my city?”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Deevid fara a ŋana Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nseŋ kaŋɛ le: “Nuso nɛ meeŋ wora n ta ŋkre be deka ere a yɔ?”

english_verse: He decided not to take it there. Instead, he turned off the road and took it to the home of Obed Edom, who was from Gath.
translation_verse: E daŋ yili mbe nfɛra nna fanɛ e maaŋ naŋ yɛr kumo Jerusalɛm to, amoso e daŋ ta ŋkre be deka na nna ŋ gbɛ n ya yili Obɛd Edɔm nɛ e la Gaaf be kadetobia na be laŋ to.

english_verse: The chest stayed there for three months, and the Lord greatly blessed Obed Edom, his family, and everything he owned. Then someone told King David, “The Lord has done this because the sacred chest is in Obed Edom's house.” At once, David went to Obed Edom's house to get the chest and bring it to David's City. Everyone was celebrating.
translation_verse: Ewura Deevid ka nu fanɛ ŋkpal ŋkre be deka na ka wɔ Obɛd Edɔm be laŋ to so, nɛ mo nɛ mbe kanaŋ kikɛ nya nɛfa na nɛ e lara kumo laŋ na to n yɔ Jerusalɛm nɛ kagbenefuli.

english_verse: They put the chest inside a tent that David had set up for it. David worshiped the Lord by sacrificing animals and burning them on an altar,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ b ta deka na m ba yili wajɛbu nɛ Deevid lɔŋɛ na to. Nɛ e ta asɔbɔya n lara sarga nseŋ chɔɔ amo bɔrɛsure na so n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ.

english_verse: then he blessed the people in the name of the Lord All-Powerful.
translation_verse: E ka lara esarga na n loge nɛ e nɛfa basa na ashi Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na be ketre to.

english_verse: He gave all the men and women in the crowd a small loaf of bread, some meat, and a handful of raisins, then everyone went home. Michal Talks to David
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e chige bumo kikɛ ajibi. E daŋ sa benyɛn nɛ beche nɛ b wɔ Israɛl na kikɛ ebodobodo nɛ eblaŋ tɔso nɛ asɔrso jiso nɛ ekama ta n yɔ laŋ to.

english_verse: David went home so he could ask the Lord to bless his family. But Saul's daughter Michal went out and started yelling at him. “You were really great today!” she said. “You acted like a dirty old man, dancing around half-naked in front of your servants' slave-girls.”
translation_verse: B ka loge nɛ Deevid bee ba laŋ to nɛ e ba chɔrɔ mbe kanaŋ, nɛ Sɔɔl pibiche Mikaal shɛr Deevid to ŋ kaŋɛ mo le: “Kabre Israɛl malɛ be ewura nase ketande bre! Mbe beyaasepo be mbita be anishito nɛ e delgeso fanɛ ewulpo!”

english_verse: David told her, “The Lord didn't choose your father or anyone else in your family to be the leader of his people. The Lord chose me, and I was celebrating in honor of him.
translation_verse: Nɛ Deevid kaŋɛ le: “Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ maŋ lara esa kikɛ menyi be kanaŋ to fanɛ e ba sɔ fo tuto Sɔɔl so ŋ ki mbe basa be ejuŋkparpo. Ma nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na lara, amoso nɛ mee cha a maŋkura mo na.

english_verse: I'll show you just how great I can be! I'll even be disgusting to myself. But those slave-girls you talked about will still honor me!”
translation_verse: Hale nɛ n wora ma kumu yɛryɛrbi nseŋ ŋaba ma kumu fo ere kutɔ gba, mbita ere bre beeŋ sa ma bunyaŋ gboŋgboŋi!”

english_verse: But I will never put an end to my agreement with him, as I put an end to my agreement with Saul, who was king before you.
translation_verse: Ma alɛ maaŋ lar mo kaman fanɛ kananɛ n lar Sɔɔl nɛ n daŋ lara nɛ e ki ewura pɔɛŋ nɛ e ba chena so na kaman na.

english_verse: Then one day, as David was talking with Nathan the prophet, David said, “Look around! I live in a palace made of cedar, but the sacred chest has to stay in a tent.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura Deevid kaŋɛ anebi Neetan le: “Keni! Ndibi nɛ baa tre sida na nɛ b ta m pɔr ma laŋ ere, ama Ebɔrɛ be ŋkre be deka na bre wɔ wajɛbu to nna!”

english_verse: That night, the Lord told Nathan
translation_verse: Kumo be kanyɛso nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Neetan le:

english_verse: to go to David and give him this message: David, you are my servant, so listen to what I say. Why should you build a temple for me?
translation_verse: “Ya kaŋɛ ma kayɛrbi Deevid fanɛ ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e naa kaŋɛ mo na fanɛ mannɛ mo nɛ mee sha fanɛ e pɔr bɔrɛlambu n sa ma nɛ m baa wɔtɔ.

english_verse: I didn't live in a temple when I brought my people out of Egypt, and I don't live in one now. A tent has always been my home wherever I have gone with them.
translation_verse: Baŋ yili jemanɛ so nɛ n lara Israɛlebi ashi Ijiptebi na m ba fo kabre, m maŋ naŋ chena bɔrɛlambu to kikɛ, kaplɛkama nɛ ma alɛ yɔ, wajɛbu to nɛ mee luri.

english_verse: I chose leaders and told them to be like shepherds for my people Israel. But did I ever say anything to even one of them about building a cedar temple for me?
translation_verse: Enite damta nɛ ma nɛ Israɛlebi ere malɛ nite ere kikɛ, m maŋ naŋ bishi bumo be bejuŋkparpo nɛ n tre fanɛ b baa keni ma basa so fanɛ kananɛ mbolpɔkpapo bee keni mbe mbolpɔ so na be ekama kusɔ nɛ k ba nɛ b maŋ ta ndibi nɛ baa tre sida na m pɔr bɔrɛlambu n sa ma.

english_verse: David, this is what I, the Lord All-Powerful, say to you. I brought you in from the fields where you took care of sheep, and I made you the leader of my people.
translation_verse: Amoso kaŋɛ ma kayɛrbi Deevid fanɛ ma Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na e naa kaŋɛ mo ere, Deevid fanɛ n lara fo ashi mbolpɔkpapo be kushuŋ to nna nseŋ ta fo ŋ ki ma basa Israɛlebi be ejuŋkparpo.

english_verse: Wherever you went, I helped you and destroyed your enemies right in front of your eyes. I have made you one of the most famous people in the world.
translation_verse: Kaplɛkama nɛ e baŋ yɔ, ma nɛ mo nna. Nɛ ma alɛ bee pɔɔ mo doŋana kikɛ so a sa mo. Kananɛ basa ko be atre dii ga durnya ere to na, loŋ gbagba nɛ meeŋ shin nɛ mo alɛ gba be ketre e dii.

english_verse: I have given my people Israel a land of their own where they can live in peace, and they won't have to tremble with fear any more. Evil nations won't bother them, as they did
translation_verse: N sa ma basa Israɛlebi bumo gbagba be kakpa nɛ b chena, saŋɛ na so, shɛŋ shɛŋ maaŋ naŋ tɔrɔ bumo. Baŋ yili saŋɛ so nɛ b ba chena kasawule ere so kikɛ, basa lubi maŋ yige bumo ama loŋ maaŋ naŋ wora kikɛ.

english_verse: when I let judges rule my people. And I have kept your enemies from attacking you. Now I promise that you and your descendants will be kings.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal manɛ so, meeŋ kuŋ menyi ashi men doŋana kutɔ nseŋ naŋ shin nɛ menyi be kanaŋ to ebi e wora kishi ga n ti so.

english_verse: I'll choose one of your sons to be king when you reach the end of your life and are buried in the tomb of your ancestors. I'll make him a strong ruler,
translation_verse: E kaŋ wu nɛ b ta mo n ya nase mo nananyɛnana be edesekpa, meeŋ shin nɛ mbe mbinyɛnsobi ere be eko e ki ewura, nɛ n shin nɛ mbe kuwurji malɛ e ba kɔ eleŋ ga.

english_verse: and no one will be able to take his kingdom away from him. He will be the one to build a temple for me.
translation_verse: Mo e naŋ pɔr ma bɔrɛlambu n sa ma. Mo alɛ be kuwurji maaŋ loge kikɛ.

english_verse: I will be his father, and he will be my son. When he does wrong, I'll see that he is corrected, just as children are corrected by their parents.
translation_verse: Meeŋ ki mo tuto, nɛ mo alɛ e baa la m pibinyɛn. E baŋ wora n foe, meeŋ niŋi mo fanɛ kananɛ etuto bee niŋi mbe kebia na.

english_verse: After all, you really are Israel's God, the Lord All-Powerful. You've told me that you will let my descendants be kings. That's why I have the courage to pray to you like this, even though I am only your servant.
translation_verse: Enyɛnpetale, Israɛl be Ebɔrɛ, ŋkpal fo ka lara le be asheŋ ere kikɛ ŋ ŋini ma, fo kayɛrbi, nseŋ kaŋɛ ma fanɛ feeŋ shin nɛ n nanabiana e ba ki bewura kachako so na so nɛ n nya kagbene ŋ kule le be kabɔrɛkule ere na.

english_verse: David went into the tent he had set up for the sacred chest. Then he sat there and prayed: Lord All-Powerful, my family and I don't deserve what you have already done for us,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura Deevid yɔ wajɛbu na to ashi Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be anishito n ya kule Ebɔrɛ ŋ kaŋɛ le: “Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ, kusɔ nɛ fo wora n sa ma ere maŋ daga ma nɛ ma kanaŋ to ebi kuraa.

english_verse: I am your servant, and you know my thoughts, so there is nothing more that I need to say.
translation_verse: Manɛ bre nɛ n naa kɔ nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ fo! Fo nyi fo kayɛrbi be nfɛra.

english_verse: You have done this wonderful thing, and you have let me know about it, because you wanted to keep your promise.
translation_verse: Fo keparso nɛ fo wora le be kesheŋ tumase ere; fo alɛ wora loŋ nna nɛ fo ŋini ma

english_verse: Lord All-Powerful, you are greater than all others. No one is like you, and you alone are God. Everything we have heard about you is true.
translation_verse: kananɛ fo Enyɛnpetale be keshi du! Fo nawule e la Ebɔrɛ. Dra kikɛ nɛ an nyi fo ka la Ebɔrɛ.

english_verse: And there is no other nation on earth like Israel, the nation you rescued from slavery in Egypt to be your own. You became famous by using great and wonderful miracles to force other nations and their gods out of your land, so your people could live here.
translation_verse: Efuli pɔtɛana so ebi kikɛ malɛ maŋ naa wɔtɔ a du fanɛ Israɛl be efuli so ebi nɛ fo lara kenyaya to ashi Ijipt be efuli so nseŋ ta bumo ŋ ki fo gbagba be basa ere so. Fo asheŋ tumase damta nɛ fo wora nɛ fo ketre dii na so e shin nɛ efuli pɔtɛana kikɛ ta bumo agbirana n shile efuliana na so, saŋɛ na so, fo basa beeŋ sɔ ndoŋ n chena.

english_verse: You have chosen Israel to be your people forever, and you have become their God.
translation_verse: Fo lara Israɛlebi na fanɛ fo basa nna hale mbaanaayɔ, nɛ fo Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ malɛ ki bumo be Ebɔrɛ.

english_verse: And now, Lord God, please do what you have promised me and my descendants.
translation_verse: Naniere bre Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, shin nɛ fo kɔnɔ nɛ fo nase n sa ma nɛ n nanabiana na e bɔlɔ so.

english_verse: Then you will be famous forever, and everyone will say, “The Lord God All-Powerful rules Israel, and David's descendants are his chosen kings.”
translation_verse: Fo ketre beeŋ dii n sɔ kaplɛkama nɛ basa e baa kaŋɛ saŋkama fanɛ, fo e la Enyɛnpetale nɛ fo la Israɛl be Ebɔrɛ na. Ma alɛ be kanaŋ ere to nɛ feeŋ baa lara bewura saŋkama.

english_verse: Lord All-Powerful, you are God. You have promised me some very good things, and you can be trusted to do what you promise.

translation_verse: B ka wora keeli n loge, nɛ ewura Deevid shuŋi nɛ b ya keta mo m ba ewurkpa nɛ e ta mo ŋ ki mbe eche hale nɛ e kurge ebinyɛn n sa mo. Ama kusɔ nɛ Deevid wora na daa maŋ par Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ.

english_verse: The rich man owned a lot of sheep and cattle,
translation_verse: Damawura na daa kɔ ana nɛ mbolpɔ damta nna.

english_verse: One day someone came to visit the rich man, but the rich man didn't want to kill any of his own sheep or cattle and serve it to the visitor. So he stole the poor man's lamb and served it instead.
translation_verse: Kachako nɛ efɔ ko ba suge damawura na be laŋ to, ama e daa maŋ sha k ta mbe kusɔbɔya ŋ keta efɔ na kufɔ. E daŋ pɛ etirpo na be kubɔlpobi cheso na nna m mɔ ŋ keta mo kufɔ.”

english_verse: David was furious with the rich man and said to Nathan, “I swear by the living Lord that the man who did this deserves to die!
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ agbo ji ewura Deevid ga ŋkpal kusɔ nɛ damawura na wora na so nɛ e kaŋɛ le: “Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ e la ma shɛdajipo na so, kanyɛn ere daga luwu nna ŋkpal kusɔ nɛ e wora ere so.

english_verse: And because he didn't have pity on the poor man, he will have to pay four times what the lamb was worth.”
translation_verse: Ŋkpal le be kesheŋ lubi nɛ e wora n sa maŋ wu kuwɔr ere so a daga fanɛ e ka kusɔ nɛ e ta na be ntuŋ ana.”

english_verse: Then Nathan told David: You are that rich man! Now listen to what the Lord God of Israel says to you: “I chose you to be the king of Israel. I kept you safe from Saul
translation_verse: Nɛ Neetan kaŋɛ ewura Deevid le: “Fo e la loŋ be esa na. Kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe, Israɛl be Ebɔrɛ na malɛ bee kaŋɛ nde: ‘Ma e lara fo fanɛ Israɛl be ewura nseŋ mɔlga fo ashi Ewura Sɔɔl be enɔ to.

english_verse: and even gave you his house and his wives. I let you rule Israel and Judah, and if that had not been enough, I would have given you much more.
translation_verse: Mbe kuwura nɛ mbe beche kikɛ nɛ n ta n sa fo, nseŋ lara fo fanɛ Israɛl nɛ Juda kikɛ be ewura, nɛ a daa maŋ kukwe fo gba n daa beeŋ naŋ tiŋ n sa fo ako n ti so.

english_verse: Why did you disobey me and do such a horrible thing? You murdered Uriah the Hittite by letting the Ammonites kill him, so you could take his wife.
translation_verse: Nɛ manɛ e ba nɛ fo kini kenu n sa ma nseŋ ŋaba ma le ere? Fo e shin nɛ Ammɔnebi na mɔ Yuriya ashi kena to nɛ fo ta mbe eche ŋ ki feya.

english_verse: “Because you wouldn't obey me and took Uriah's wife for yourself, your family will never live in peace.
translation_verse: Amoso fo nanabiana nɛ baŋ koso kachako so na be beko beeŋ wu luwu nyaŋnyaŋso ŋkpal fo ka kini kenu n sa ma nseŋ wora le be kusɔ ŋ ŋaba ma so.

english_verse: Someone from your own family will cause you a lot of trouble, and I will take your wives and give them to another man before your very eyes. He will go to bed with them while everyone looks on.
translation_verse: Ma Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e naa kaŋɛ fo na fanɛ meeŋ shin nɛ esa ko nɛ e shi fo kanaŋ to e kil asheŋ m ba sa fo. Ma alɛ beeŋ sɔ fo beche fo kutɔ n ta bumo n sa fo kanaŋ to be esa ko nɛ mo bumo e di keche nɛ kenyɛn kowushina kapiidi basa be anishito.

english_verse: What you did was in secret, but I will do this in the open for everyone in Israel to see.”
translation_verse: Fo ere ŋana nna n wora kulubi ama ma ere beeŋ shin nɛ kusɔ nɛ meeŋ wora ere e dii efuli nɛ Israɛlebi kikɛ e wu kumo.’ ”

english_verse: David said, “I have disobeyed the Lord.” “Yes, you have!” Nathan answered. “You showed you didn't care what the Lord wanted. He has forgiven you, and you won't die. But your newborn son will.”
translation_verse: Ama ŋkpal fo ka maŋ keni Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ m bɔlɔ kenishi nseŋ shin nɛ mo doŋana keni mo jiga so, fo pibinyɛn nɛ eche na kurge na beeŋ wu.”

english_verse: Then Nathan went back home. David's Young Son Dies The Lord made David's young son very sick.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Neetan yɔ laŋ to. Deevid pibinyɛn ka wu be asheŋ Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ shin nɛ kulɔ kpakpaso pɛ kebia nɛ ewura Deevid nɛ Yuriya be eche kurge na.

english_verse: So David went without eating to show his sorrow, and he begged God to make the boy well. David would not sleep on his bed, but spent each night lying on the floor.
translation_verse: Nɛ ewura Deevid kule Ebɔrɛ a fin fanɛ kebia na e nya alenfia. E daa kishi nna a kule Ebɔrɛ nsaa dese kasawule kanyɛso kikɛ.

english_verse: His officials stood beside him and tried to talk him into getting up. But he would not get up or eat with them.
translation_verse: Mbe lambu to be benimuana na daa leŋ mo to nna fanɛ e baa niŋi to a chena, ama e daa maa shuli. Mo alɛ maaŋ naa tu bumo a ji shɛŋ gba.

english_verse: After the child had been sick for seven days, he died, but the officials were afraid to tell David. They said to each other, “Even when the boy was alive, David wouldn't listen to us. How can we tell him his son is dead? He might do something terrible!”
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ kebia na wu, ama ewura Deevid be basa daa lɔ kufu nɛ b kaŋɛ mo loŋ be baru na nna. Le nɛ b daŋ kaŋɛ: “Kebia ere ka daa wɔ mbe ŋkpa to gba, kusɔ kama nɛ an kaŋɛ ewura Deevid e maaŋ tuge anyi. Nɛ nuso bre nɛ anyeeŋ wora ŋ kaŋɛ mo kebia ere be keeli naniere? E beeŋ tiŋ ŋkpal loŋ so n wora mbe kumu kesheŋ lubi ko!”

english_verse: David noticed his servants whispering, and he knew the boy was dead. “Did my son die?” he asked his servants. “Yes, he did,” they answered.
translation_verse: Ewura Deevid ka nu kananɛ baa kuli abar kutɔ na, nɛ e pin fanɛ kebia na wu. Ndoŋ nna nɛ e bishi bumo le: “Kebia na wu nna a?” Nɛ b shuli so ŋ kaŋɛ: “Mm, e wu nna.”

english_verse: His officials said, “What are you doing? You went without eating and cried for your son while he was alive! But now that he's dead, you're up and eating.”
translation_verse: Nɛ mbe nyɛrbi na kaŋɛ mo le: “Anyi ere maŋ pin kesheŋ ere to ŋkpal manɛ so, kebia na ka wɔ ŋkpa to fo daa shu nna nsaa kishi a sa mo ama e ka baŋ wu bre, epul to nɛ fo fin ajibi n ji!”

english_verse: David answered: While he was still alive, I went without food and cried because there was still hope. I said to myself, “Who knows? Maybe the Lord will have pity on me and let the child live.”
translation_verse: Nɛ ewura Deevid shuli so ŋ kaŋɛ le: “Mm, e ka daa wɔ ŋkpa to, n daa kishi nna nsaa shu, ŋkpal manɛ so n daŋ fɛ nna fanɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ beeŋ wu ma kuwɔr nseŋ yige kebia na.

english_verse: But now that he's dead, why should I go without eating? I can't bring him back! Someday I will join him in death, but he can't return to me. Solomon Is Born
translation_verse: Nɛ e ka wu naniere, wanɛ bre so nɛ n naa kishi? Meeŋ tiŋ n sa kebia na ŋkpa a? Kachako, ma ere beeŋ ya tu mo kakpa nɛ e wɔ, ama mo ere maaŋ naŋ bɛta m ba ŋ kutɔ kikɛ.” B ka kurge Sɔlɔmɔn be asheŋ

english_verse: David comforted his wife Bathsheba and slept with her. Later on, she gave birth to another son and named him Solomon. The Lord loved Solomon
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura Deevid wushi mbe eche Bɛshiba kagbene nɛ mo nɛ mo di keche nɛ kenyɛn nɛ e kurge ebinyɛn nɛ ewura Deevid nase mbe ketre Sɔlɔmɔn. Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ daa sha Sɔlɔmɔn be asheŋ ga.

english_verse: and sent Nathan the prophet to tell David, “The Lord will call him Jedidiah.” The End of the War with Ammon (
translation_verse: Ŋkpal Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ka bee sha Sɔlɔmɔn ga so, e daŋ shin nna nɛ anebi Neetan ya nase mo ketre Jedidaya. Kumo be kifito e la fanɛ Ebɔrɛ bee sha mo. Deevid ka sɔ Raaba be asheŋ

english_verse: Meanwhile, Joab had been in the country of Ammon, attacking the city of Rabbah. He captured the royal fortress
translation_verse: Loŋ be saŋɛ na nɛ Jɔab daa kɔ Raaba nɛ k la Ammɔn be kadegboŋ na nsaa sha kesɔ kumo.

english_verse: and sent a messenger to tell David: I have attacked Rabbah and captured the fortress guarding the city water supply.
translation_verse: E daŋ shuŋi mbɔ Deevid kutɔ nna ŋ kaŋɛ mo le: “Ŋ kraa kɔ Raabaebi nna ama n sɔ bumo be mboŋ nɛ baa bɔla a sa basa nchu na kikɛ.

english_verse: Call the rest of the army together. Then surround the city, and capture it yourself. If you don't, everyone will remember that I captured the city.
translation_verse: Amoso naniere chala fo benapo nɛ b ka na kikɛ m ba kɔ n sɔ kade na fo gbagba, ŋkpal manɛ so, m maa sha kesɔ ketre n sa ma kumu.”

english_verse: David called the rest of the army together and attacked Rabbah. He captured the city
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura Deevid chala benapo nɛ b ka na n ya ti so ŋ kɔ n sɔ Raaba.

english_verse: David made the people of Rabbah tear down the city walls with iron picks and axes, and then he put them to work making bricks. He did the same thing with all the other Ammonite cities. David went back to Jerusalem, and the people of Israel returned to their homes.
translation_verse: E daŋ shin nna nɛ kumo be basa ta ekapɛnta be nsaŋɛgboŋ nɛ baa tre sɛrdaa na nɛ abɛlso be ntekpa nɛ akpanfu a tintiŋ bumo nɛ b baa shuŋ a ku ebirkesi. Loŋ koŋwule na nɛ e daŋ wora ndewurbi nɛ a wɔ Ammɔn be efuli so na kikɛ. Kumo be kaman nɛ mo nɛ mbe benapo bɛta n yɔ Jerusalɛm.

english_verse: David had a beautiful daughter named Tamar, who was the sister of Absalom. She was also the half sister of Amnon, who fell in love with her.
translation_verse: Deevid pibinyɛn Absalɔm daa kɔ mo sipoche lela kebita ko nɛ baa tre mo Tamaa. Deevid pibinyɛn ko malɛ nɛ baa tre Amnɔn na daa sha Tamaa na nna.

english_verse: But Tamar was a virgin, and Amnon could not think of a way to be alone with her. He was so upset about it that he made himself sick.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal Tamaa ka daa maŋ nyi enyɛn nɛ k daa du kpakpa n sa Amnɔn nɛ e nya mo n di keche nɛ kenyɛn na so k daŋ ki mo kulɔ nna.

english_verse: Amnon had a friend named Jonadab, who was the son of David's brother Shimeah. Jonadab always knew how to get what he wanted,
translation_verse: Deevid mo sipo Shamma pibinyɛn nɛ baa tre Jonadab na e daa la mo teri. Jonadab malɛ daa la enyiashempo nna nsaa kɔ kananɛ baa wora asheŋ manaŋ manaŋ be nfɛra ga.

english_verse: and he said to Amnon, “What's the matter? You're the king's son! You shouldn't have to go around feeling sorry for yourself every morning.” Amnon said, “I'm in love with Tamar, my brother Absalom's sister.”
translation_verse: Amoso le nɛ Jonadab daŋ kaŋɛ Amnɔn: “Ewura pibi e la fo, ama mee wu fo saŋkama fanɛ fo maŋ kɔ kagbenefuli. Manɛ e kɔ fo?” Nɛ Amnɔn kaŋɛ le: “N da Absalɔm mo sipoche Tamaa nɛ mee sha.”

english_verse: Jonadab told him, “Lie down on your bed and pretend to be sick. When your father comes to see you, ask him to send Tamar, so you can watch her cook something for you. Then she can serve you the food.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Jonadab kaŋɛ mo le: “Wora fanɛ fo ka bee lɔ na nseŋ ya dese fo gedo so. Fo tuto kaŋ ba nɛ fo kaŋɛ mo le: ‘Jande shin nɛ ma sipoche Tamaa a daŋɛ ajibi m bar ma. E ba ma kutɔ nɛ m baa keni mo nɛ e ba daŋɛ, saŋɛ na so e kaŋ daŋɛ n loge, e beeŋ baa ku amo a wɔtɔ ma kɔnɔ to.’ ”

english_verse: So Amnon went to bed and pretended to be sick. When the king came to see him, Amnon said, “Please, ask Tamar to come over. She can make some special bread while I watch, and then she can serve it to me.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Amnɔn wora fanɛ e ka bee lɔ na nseŋ ya dese mbe gedo so. Ewura Deevid ka yɔ nɛ e ya wu mo nɛ Amnɔn kaŋɛ mo le: “Jande shin nɛ Tamaa e ba daŋɛ ajibi lela ko n sa ma nfe nsaa ku amo a sa ma nɛ m baa ji.”

english_verse: When she got there, he was lying in bed. She mixed the dough, made the loaves, and baked them while he watched.
translation_verse: Tamaa ka yɔ, nɛ e ya wu Amnɔn nɛ e dese gedo so. Ndoŋ nna nɛ Tamaa ta nyifu n yili kakpa nɛ Amnɔn beeŋ baa wu mo na nseŋ gbiti bodobodo na n tɔ amo.

english_verse: Then she took the bread out of the pan and put it on his plate, but he refused to eat it. Amnon said, “Send the servants out of the house.” After they had gone,
translation_verse: E ka loge nɛ e ku ajibi na n wɔtɔ katishaŋ to n sa mo fanɛ e ji, nɛ e kini nseŋ kaŋɛ mo le: “Shin nɛ mbita na e lar kowu.” Nɛ bumo kikɛ lar.

english_verse: he said to Tamar, “Serve the food in my bedroom.” Tamar picked up the bread that she had made and brought it into Amnon's bedroom.
translation_verse: Nɛ e kaŋɛ Tamaa le: “Fo gbagba e ta bodobodo na m ba ma gedo ase m ba sa ma.” Nɛ e ta bodobodo na n ya ka sa mo.

english_verse: But as she was taking it over to him, he grabbed her and said, “Come to bed with me!”
translation_verse: E ka ta n sa mo n loge nɛ e to m pɛ mo to nseŋ kaŋɛ mo le: “Ba tu ma n dese!”

english_verse: She answered, “No! Please don't force me! This sort of thing isn't done in Israel. It's disgusting!
translation_verse: Nɛ Tamaa yɛ: “M-m, sa maŋ tintiŋ ma n wɔtɔ le be anishinyɔr ere to! Le be kesheŋ maŋ daga kewora Israɛl be efuli so!

english_verse: Think of me. I'll be disgraced forever! And think of yourself. Everyone in Israel will say you're nothing but trash! Just ask the king, and he will let you marry me.”
translation_verse: Nuso gba nɛ meeŋ naŋ wora n luri basa to? Anishinyɔr e naŋ mɔ fo alɛ ashi Israɛl to. Ama wora ania n ya malga n sa ewura, ma ere wora yirda fanɛ e beeŋ shin nɛ an ta abar.”

english_verse: But Amnon would not listen to what she said. He was stronger than she was, so he overpowered her and raped her.
translation_verse: Ama Amnɔn daŋ maŋ nu n sa kusɔ nɛ Tamaa bee kaŋɛ na nseŋ tintiŋ m pur mo.

english_verse: She said, “Don't send me away! That would be worse than what you have already done.” But Amnon would not listen.
translation_verse: Nɛ Tamaa ma alɛ yɛ: “M-m! M maaŋ yɔ. Kananɛ fee ju ma ere lubi gba a chɔ kusɔ nɛ fo wora ma na!” Ama Amnɔn daa maŋ tuge mo,

english_verse: He called in his servant and said, “Throw this woman out and lock the door!”
translation_verse: nseŋ kaŋɛ mbe kayɛrbi le: “Shin nɛ kebichebi ere a foe ma anishito! Gberge mo n lar kowu nseŋ ber kukuloŋ na so!”

english_verse: Tamar tore the robe she was wearing and put ashes on her head. Then she covered her face with her hands and cried loudly as she walked away. Absalom Kills Amnon
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Tamaa muu nsunɔ n wurge mbe kumu so, nseŋ kpɛa mbe kale to n ta mbe enɔana m buu mbe anishi so a shu a yɔ.

english_verse: Tamar's brother Absalom said to her, “How could Amnon have done such a terrible thing to you! But since he's your brother, don't tell anyone what happened. Just try not to think about it.” Tamar soon moved into Absalom's house, but she was always sad and lonely.
translation_verse: Mo da Absalɔm ka wu mo nɛ e bishi mo le: “Amnɔn pur fo nna a? Jande esipoche, sa maŋ shin nɛ kesheŋ ere e tɔrɔ fo, fo alɛ e sa maŋ kaŋɛ esa kama kumo, ŋkpal manɛ so, fo da nna.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ Tamaa ta kagbenejija nɛ kenawule a wɔ mo da Absalɔm be laŋ to.

english_verse: Absalom treated Amnon as though nothing had happened, but he hated Amnon for what he had done to his sister Tamar.
translation_verse: Absalɔm daa maŋ tuge Amnɔn shɛŋ ama e daŋ kishi mo nna, ŋkpal e ka pur mo sipoche Tamaa so so. Absalɔm ka mɔ Amnɔn be asheŋ

english_verse: Two years later, Absalom's servants were cutting wool from his sheep in Baal-Hazor near the town of Ephraim, and Absalom invited all of the king's sons to be there.
translation_verse: Kumo be nfɛ anyɔ nɛ Absalɔm yɛr mbe mbolpɔ Baal Hazɔɔ nɛ k mata Efrayim be kade to na nɛ e ya kuya bumo be afuibi so, nseŋ tre ewura be mbinyɛnbi na kikɛ nɛ b ba shɛr ndoŋ.

english_verse: Then he went to David and said, “My servants are cutting the wool from my sheep. Please come and join us!”
translation_verse: E daŋ yɔ ewura Deevid kutɔ nna n ya kaŋɛ mo le: “Yiramu, ma nyɛrbi bee she ma mbolpɔ be afuibi kabre nna! Fo nɛ fo benimu beeŋ tiŋ m ba ti anyi so a?”

english_verse: David answered, “No, my son, we won't go. It would be too expensive for you.” Absalom tried to get him to change his mind, but David did not want to go. He only said that he hoped they would have a good time.
translation_verse: Nɛ ewura Deevid kaŋɛ: “M-m, m pibi, nɛ an kikɛ baŋ yɔ ndoŋ, k beeŋ baa la tɔrɔ damta nna n sa fo.” Nɛ Absalɔm kini nseŋ kraa mata mo so, ama ewura Deevid kini keyɔ nseŋ kaŋɛ: “Baa yɔ Ebɔrɛ e chɛ fo to.”

english_verse: Absalom said, “If you won't go, at least let my brother Amnon come with us.” David asked, “Why should he go with you?”
translation_verse: Nɛ Absalɔm naŋ kaŋɛ le: “Nɛ fo ere maaŋ yɔ gba kumo ere, fo shin nɛ n sipo Amnɔn e ba tu ma n yɔ.” Nɛ Ewura kaŋɛ le: “Manɛ nna nɛ fee sha Amnɔn ka tu fo n yɔ?”

english_verse: But Absalom kept on insisting, and finally David let Amnon and all his other sons go with Absalom. Absalom prepared a banquet fit for a king.
translation_verse: Absalɔm daŋ mata so loŋ nna, nɛ ewura Deevid shin nɛ Amnɔn nɛ mo braana nɛ b ka na kikɛ tu Absalɔm n yɔ. B ka fo kakpa nɛ baa kuya mbolpɔ be afuibi so na nɛ Absalɔm wora kejigboŋ fanɛ ewura peya na n sa bumo.

english_verse: But he told his servants, “Keep an eye on Amnon. When he gets a little drunk from the wine and is feeling relaxed, I'll give the signal. Then kill him! I've commanded you to do it, so don't be afraid. Be strong and brave.”
translation_verse: B ka bee ji na nɛ Absalɔm kaŋɛ mbe nyɛrbi le: “Men shin nɛ men be lakal e ba wɔ Amnɔn so a keni saŋɛ so nɛ e beeŋ boo, a wora chilchil be asheŋ na. Loŋ be saŋɛ na nɛ men mɔ mo. Men sa maaŋ kaa lɔ kufu, ŋkpal manɛ so, meeŋ sɔ kumo be turju kikɛ n deŋi ma kumu so!”

english_verse: Absalom's servants killed Amnon, just as Absalom had told them. The rest of the king's sons quickly rode away on their mules to escape from Absalom.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ nyɛrbi na bɛ kusɔ nɛ Absalɔm kaŋɛ bumo na so nseŋ mɔ Amnɔn. Nɛ ewura na be mbinyɛnbi nɛ Absalɔm tre na kikɛ ta bumo be ekurma nɛ enyɔma n shile n choŋ ŋ ka mo ndoŋ.

english_verse: While they were on their way to Jerusalem, someone told David, “Absalom has killed all of your sons! Not even one is left.”
translation_verse: B kraa wɔ ekpa to nna a yɔ nɛ kubɔya ya tu ewura Deevid fanɛ Absalɔm mɔ mbe mbinyɛnsobi na kikɛ, hale ekoŋwule gba maŋ ka!

english_verse: David got up, and in his sorrow he tore his clothes and lay down on the ground. His servants remained standing, but they tore their clothes too.
translation_verse: Nɛ ewura Deevid kpa n niŋi to, nseŋ kpɛa mbe epiŋi to kagbenejijaso nseŋ dese kasawule. Mbe nyɛrbi nɛ b daa wɔ mo kutɔ na gba daŋ kpɛa bumo be epiŋi to nna.

english_verse: Then David's nephew Jonadab said, “Your Majesty, not all of your sons were killed! Only Amnon is dead. On the day that Amnon raped Tamar, Absalom decided to kill him.
translation_verse: Ama le nɛ ewura Deevid mo da Shamaa pibinyɛn Jonadab daŋ kaŋɛ mo: “Yiramu, fo mbinyɛnsobi na kikɛ maŋ wu, Amnɔn nawule e wu. Yili saŋɛ nɛ Amnɔn pur Tamaa na kikɛ nɛ feeŋ pin ŋkre nɛ Absalɔm kɔ a yɔ loŋ be asheŋ be kaplɛa so.

english_verse: Don't worry about the report that all your sons were killed. Only Amnon is dead,
translation_verse: Amoso sa maŋ kaŋ yirda fanɛ fo mbinyɛnsobi na kikɛ e wu, Amnɔn nawule e wu.”

english_verse: and Absalom has run away.” One of the guards noticed a lot of people coming along the hillside on the road to Horonaim. He went and told the king, “I saw some men coming along Horonaim Road.”
translation_verse: Le be saŋɛ malɛ nɛ Absalɔm shile. Epul to nɛ enapo ko nɛ e la bumo nɛ baa yili a keni kade so na b eko wu basa damta ko ka shi Horoneem be kubɔrbi so a gbelge kebee so a yɔ. Nɛ e ya kaŋɛ ewura Deevid kusɔ nɛ e wu.

english_verse: Jonadab said, “Your Majesty, look! Here come your sons now, just as I told you.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Jonadab kaŋɛ le: “Yiramu! M maŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ fo mbinyɛnsobi na kikɛ maŋ wu a? Keni! Bumo e naa ba na.”

english_verse: No sooner had he said it, than David's sons came in. They were weeping out loud, and David and all his officials cried just as loudly.
translation_verse: E maŋ naŋ malga n loge gba nɛ Deevid be mbinyɛnsobi na shu m ba luri laŋ to nɛ ewura Deevid nɛ mbe benimu shu ga.

english_verse: David was sad for a long time because Amnon was dead. David Lets Absalom Come Home Absalom had run away to Geshur, where he stayed for three years with King Talmai the son of Ammihud.
translation_verse: Absalɔm ka shile na nɛ e yɔ Amihuud pibinyɛn Talmai nɛ e la Gɛshur be ewura na kutɔ, n ya ji nfɛ asa ndoŋ. Nɛ ewura Deevid ta nchɛ damta n shu mo pibinyɛn Amnɔn be keeli.

english_verse: David still felt so sad over the loss of Amnon that he wanted to take his army there and capture Absalom.
translation_verse: E ka shu Amnɔn be keeli n loge, nɛ mo pibinyɛn Absalɔm malɛ be asheŋ fara e ba mo to ga.

english_verse: Joab knew that David couldn't stop thinking about Absalom,
translation_verse: Jɔab daa nyi fanɛ Absalɔm be asheŋ wɔ ewura Deevid to ga.

english_verse: The woman from Tekoa went to David. She bowed very low and said, “Your Majesty, please help me!”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ kache na yɔ ewura Deevid kutɔ n ya gbir kasawule bunyaŋ so nseŋ kaŋɛ mo le: “Yiramu! Chɛ ma to!”

english_verse: David asked, “What's the matter?” She replied: My husband is dead, and I'm a widow.
translation_verse: Nɛ ewura na malɛ bishi mo le: “Manɛ nɛ fee sha?” Nɛ kache na kaŋɛ le: “Ŋ kul wu ŋ ka ma nna.

english_verse: I had two sons, but they got into a fight out in a field where there was no one to pull them apart, and one of them killed the other.
translation_verse: Ma alɛ kɔ mbia anyɔ nɛ kachako nɛ kolu tɔr bumo so ashi kupuŋ to. Esa kama malɛ daa maŋ wɔtɔ nɛ e barga bumo to nɛ bumo eko mɔ mo barkasa.

english_verse: Now all of my relatives have come to me and said, “Hand over your son! We're going to put him to death for killing his brother.” But what they really want is to get rid of him, so they can take over our land. Please don't let them put out my only flame of hope! There won't be anyone left on this earth to carry on my husband's name.
translation_verse: Naniere ma kanaŋ to ebi kikɛ yuu ma kenishi nna nseŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ m bar ma kebia na nɛ b mɔ mo alɛ gba ŋkpal e ka mɔ mo sipo so. Nɛ b baaŋ wora loŋ, kumo ere ma ere maaŋ naa kɔ ebinyɛn kikɛ nna na. B baaŋ mɔ mo, kumo ere ma tama loge, ma kul malɛ be ketre beeŋ mur kuraa.”

english_verse: “Go on home,” David told her. “I'll take care of this matter for you.”
translation_verse: Nɛ ewura Deevid kaŋɛ mo le: “Bɛta a yɔ laŋ to, meeŋ wora ŋ keni kesheŋ na to.”

english_verse: The woman said, “I hope your decision doesn't cause any problems for you. But if it does, you can blame me.”
translation_verse: Nɛ kache na kaŋɛ le: “Yiramu, kusɔ kama nɛ fo kaŋ yili be turju e baa bɛ ma nɛ ma kanaŋ mannɛ fo.”

english_verse: He said, “If anyone gives you trouble, bring them to me, and it won't happen again!”
translation_verse: Nɛ ewura na kaŋɛ mo le: “Esa kama nɛ e kaŋ baa tɔrɔ fo, fo bar mo ŋ kutɔ nɛ n shin nɛ e maaŋ naŋ wora loŋ kikɛ.”

english_verse: “Please,” she replied, “swear by the Lord your God that no one will be allowed to kill my son!” He said, “I swear by the living Lord that no one will touch even a hair on his head!”
translation_verse: Nɛ kache na kaŋɛ le: “Yiramu, jande, kule Enyɛnpe nɛ fo Ebɔrɛ na saŋɛ na so ŋkurgepoana nɛ b sɔ ma pibinyɛn ere be luwu be asheŋ a shin nɛ b kɔ n tal to ere maaŋ mɔ ma pibinyɛn nɛ e ka ere malɛ n naaŋ bar asheŋ lubi ko n ti so.” Nɛ ewura Deevid kaŋɛ le: “Ŋkpal Ebɔrɛ ka la ma shɛdajipo so shɛŋ maaŋ tiŋ n tɔrɔ fo pibinyɛn ere kikɛ.”

english_verse: The woman said: Haven't you been hurting God's people? Your own son had to leave the country. And when you judged in my favor, it was the same as admitting that you should have let him come back.
translation_verse: Nɛ kache na kaŋɛ mo le: “Manɛ nna nɛ fo wora kulubi ŋ gbiti Ebɔrɛ be basa? Fo ju fo pibinyɛn gbagba ashi efuli ere so, ama ŋkpal fo ka ji n chɛ ma to ere so, fo alɛ gba e wora kusɔ ko a laŋɛ fo kebia na be kaplɛa so.

english_verse: Your Majesty, I came here to tell you about my problem, because I was afraid of what someone might do to me. I decided to come to you, because I thought you could help.
translation_verse: Yiramu, naniere kusɔ nɛ k ba nɛ m ba nɛ m ba kaŋɛ fo na a la fanɛ, basa na daa funti ma nna, kumo so nɛ n fɛ fanɛ meeŋ malga fo kutɔ ŋ keni feeŋ tiŋ n chɛ ma to a?

english_verse: In fact, I knew that you would listen and save my son and me from those who want to take the land that God gave us.
translation_verse: Ma alɛ naa fɛ nna fanɛ feeŋ nu n sa ma nseŋ mɔlga ma nɛ ma pibinyɛn ashi basa nɛ baa sha kemɔ anyi n sɔ kasawule nɛ Ebɔrɛ ta n sa anyi na be enɔ to.

english_verse: I can rest easy now that you have given your decision. You know the difference between right and wrong just like an angel of God, and I pray that the Lord your God will be with you.
translation_verse: Naniere bre ma kagbene dese ŋkpal fo ka pin alubi nɛ alela be mbarga nseŋ nase ma kɔnɔ lela so. Ma kabɔrɛkule e la fanɛ Enyɛnpe fo Ebɔrɛ na e baa wɔ fo kaman.”

english_verse: Then David said to the woman, “Now I'm going to ask you a question, and don't try to hide the truth!” The woman replied, “Please go ahead, Your Majesty.”
