translation_verse: Nɛ ewura na kaŋɛ le: “Shin nɛ m bishi fo kesheŋ bishiso ere nɛ fo kaŋɛ ma kumo be kashenteŋ.” Nɛ kache na kaŋɛ le: “Yiramu, bishi ma kusɔ kama nɛ fee sha.”

english_verse: David asked, “Did Joab put you up to this?” The woman answered, “Your Majesty, I swear by your life that no one can hide the truth from you. Yes, Joab did tell me what to say,
translation_verse: Nɛ ewura na bishi mo le: “Fee tama fanɛ Jɔab be kɔnɔ maa ji asheŋ ere to a?” Nɛ kache na yɛ: “Yiramu, fo kuwura be eleŋ so m maŋ kɔ ekpa kikɛ nɛ ŋ kini kesa fo mbishi ere be atuwebi. Fo kayɛrbi Jɔab gbagba e kaŋɛ ma kusɔ nɛ meeŋ wora nɛ kusɔ nɛ meeŋ kaŋɛ kikɛ.

english_verse: but only to show you the other side of this problem. You must be as wise as the angel of God to know everything that goes on in this country.”
translation_verse: Ama e wora loŋ nna nɛ e lɔŋɛ asheŋ ere kikɛ. Yiramu, fo nyi asheŋ nna fanɛ Ebɔrɛ be kabɔ. Fo nyi kusɔ kama malɛ nɛ k bee wora kikɛ.”

english_verse: David turned to Joab and said, “It seems that I have already given my decision. Go and bring Absalom back.”
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ ewura na kaŋɛ Jɔab le: “Naniere bre meeŋ wora kusɔ nɛ fee sha na. Ya keta Absalɔm m bar ma nfe.”

english_verse: Joab bowed very low and said, “Your Majesty, I thank you for giving your permission. It shows that you approve of me.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Jɔab dese ewura Deevid be anishito kasawule bunyanso n chɔrɔ mo ŋ kaŋɛ le: “Ebɔrɛ e nɛfa fo Yiramu! Naniere nɛ m pin fo kagbene ka fuli ma so ŋkpal fo ka wora kusɔ nɛ mee sha n sa ma so.”

english_verse: Joab went to Geshur to get Absalom. But when they came back to Jerusalem,
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Jɔab yɔ Geshur n ya keta Absalɔm m ba Jerusalɛm.

english_verse: David told Joab, “I don't want to see my son Absalom. Tell him to stay away from me.” So Absalom went to his own house without seeing his father. Absalom Was Handsome
translation_verse: Nɛ ewura na kaŋɛ fanɛ Absalɔm e sa maŋ kaŋ luri mbe laŋ to. E yɛ: “Maa sha kewu mo kenishiso.” Amoso Absalɔm daa wɔ mo gbagba be laŋ to nna, e maŋ ba ewura na kutɔ kikɛ. Absalɔm nɛ Deevid ka lɔŋɛ abar be asheŋ

english_verse: No one in all Israel was as handsome and well-built as Absalom.
translation_verse: Israɛl kikɛ, esa kama daa maŋ wɔtɔ nsaa walɛ keyɛrbi n fo Absalɔm so. Mbe kaplɛkama maŋ kɔ kulɔplɛ.

english_verse: His hair grew so thick and heavy that when he got it cut once a year, it weighed over two kilograms.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal e ka daa kɔ emin ga so kafɛ kikɛ nɛ emin na baŋ daŋ ga e bee she amo nna. Amo alɛ be egbɛ beeŋ ba du fanɛ kilo anyɔ.

english_verse: Absalom had three sons. He also had a daughter named Tamar, who grew up to be very beautiful. Absalom Finally Sees David
translation_verse: Absalɔm daa kɔ mbinyɛnsobi asa nɛ ebiche lela kebita koŋwule nɛ baa tre mo Tamaa.

english_verse: Absalom lived in Jerusalem for two years without seeing his father.
translation_verse: Absalɔm malɛ daŋ chena Jerusalɛm to nfɛnyɔ kikɛ nɛ mo nɛ ewura na be kenishi maŋ wu abar.

english_verse: He wanted Joab to talk to David for him. So one day he sent a message asking Joab to come over, but Joab refused. Absalom sent another message, but Joab still refused.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ e shuŋi n tre Jɔab nɛ e shuŋi mo nɛ e ya mata ewura na n sa mo, nɛ Jɔab kini keba. Nɛ Absalɔm naŋ lɔŋɛ n shuŋi kela nyɔsopo, nɛ Jɔab naŋ kini keba.

english_verse: Finally, Absalom told his servants, “Joab's barley field is right next to mine. Go set it on fire!” And they did.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Absalɔm kaŋɛ mbe nyɛrbi le: “Men keni, Jɔab be aboyu be kudɔ baŋ mata meya nna. Men ya wɔtɔ kumo edɛ.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ b ya wɔtɔ kudɔ na kikɛ edɛ.

english_verse: Joab went to Absalom's house and demanded, “Why did your servants set my field on fire?”
translation_verse: Nɛ Jɔab yɔ Absalɔm be laŋ to n ya bishi mo le: “Manɛ nna nɛ fo nyɛrbi ya wɔtɔ ma kudɔ edɛ?”

english_verse: Absalom answered, “You didn't pay any attention when I sent for you. I want you to ask my father why he told me to come back from Geshur. I was better off there. I want to see my father now! If I'm guilty, let him kill me.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Absalɔm kaŋɛ le: “N daa sha keshuŋi fo nna nɛ fo ya mata ewura n sa ma, ama ŋ ka shuŋi n tre fo, nɛ fo kini. Manɛ bre e lara ma Geshur m ba nfe? N daa wɔ ndoŋ gba nna k daa beeŋ baa bɔ ma so. Amoso wora ania n shin nɛ n wu ewura, nɛ k ba fanɛ ma e wora n jija, kumo ere fo shin nɛ ewura a mɔ ma.”

english_verse: Joab went to David and told him what Absalom had said. David sent for Absalom, and Absalom came. He bowed very low, and David leaned over and kissed him.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Jɔab yɔ ewura Deevid kutɔ n ya kaŋɛ mo kusɔ nɛ Absalɔm kaŋɛ kikɛ. Nɛ ewura shuŋi n tre Absalɔm nɛ e ba m ba jɔŋɛ mbe anishito, nɛ ewura na chɔrɔ mo kashaso.

english_verse: He would get up early each morning and wait by the side of the road that led to the city gate. Anyone who had a complaint to bring to King David would have to go that way, and Absalom would ask each of them, “Where are you from?” If they said, “I'm from a tribe in the north,”
translation_verse: Kachipurdidi kikɛ kade na be ekarso, kakpa nɛ benimu bee shɛr a to jina na be kubɔrbi so nɛ e daa lar n ya ka yili. Esa kama nɛ e baŋ nya kamalga nsaa yɔ ewura pe nɛ e ya lɔŋɛ kumo, Absalɔm bee tre mo nna m bishi mo kakpa nɛ e shi. Esa na baŋ kaŋɛ mo kakpa nɛ e shi nɛ yiri nɛ k la mo n loge,

english_verse: Absalom would say, “You deserve to win your case. It's too bad the king doesn't have anyone to hear complaints like yours.
translation_verse: nɛ Absalɔm e kaŋɛ mo le: “Keni, fo kamalga kɔ ekpa ama esa kama maŋ wɔtɔ nɛ e yili ewura be aya to n ji fo asheŋ n sa fo.”

english_verse: Whenever anyone came to Absalom and started bowing down, he would reach out and hug and kiss them.
translation_verse: Esa kama nɛ e baŋ ba Absalɔm kutɔ nɛ e ba bunyaŋ mo, Absalɔm bee daŋ keshɛr mo to nna nseŋ chɔrɔ mo kashaso.

english_verse: That's how he treated everyone from Israel who brought a complaint to the king. Soon everyone in Israel liked Absalom better than they liked David.
translation_verse: Loŋ nɛ Absalɔm daŋ wora Israɛl be basa kama nɛ b daa kɔ bumo be edemu a yɔ ewura kutɔ na. Ŋkpal loŋ so nɛ b daa sha Absalɔm nsaa bɛ mo so.

english_verse: Four years later, Absalom said to David, “Please, let me go to Hebron. I have to keep a promise that I made to the Lord,
translation_verse: Kumo be nfɛ ana be kaman nɛ Absalɔm kaŋɛ ewura Deevid le: “Mee sha keyɔ Hibrɔn n ya tia ma kɔnɔ nɛ n nase Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be anishito na.

english_verse: when I was living with the Arameans in Geshur. I promised that if the Lord would bring me back to live in Jerusalem, I would worship him in Hebron.”
translation_verse: Ŋkpal manɛ so saŋɛ so nɛ n daa wɔ Geshur ashi Siriya be efuli so na nɛ n nase kɔnɔ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be anishito fanɛ nɛ e baŋ shin nɛ n naŋ bɛta n yɔ Jerusalɛm, kumo ere ma alɛ beeŋ ya bunyaŋ mo ashi Hibrɔn.”

english_verse: David gave his permission, and Absalom went to Hebron.
translation_verse: Nɛ ewura na kaŋɛ mo le: “Ebɔrɛ e yɛr fo nɛ alenfia.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ Absalɔm yɔ Hibrɔn,

english_verse: David's officials were in Jerusalem with him, and he told them, “Let's get out of here! We'll have to leave soon, or none of us will escape from Absalom. Hurry! If he moves fast, he could catch us while we're still here. Then he will kill us and everyone else in the city.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Deevid kaŋɛ mbe benimu nɛ mo nɛ bumo wɔ Jerusalɛm to na le: “Nɛ an baa maa sha Absalɔm ka pɛ anyi bre, kumo ere an wora manaŋ n lar, nɛ manɛ a loŋ, e beeŋ tu anyi nfe naniere kikɛ ŋ kɔ m pɔɔ anyi so nseŋ mɔ basa nɛ b wɔ kade ere to gba kikɛ n ti so!”

english_verse: The officials said, “Your Majesty, we'll do whatever you say.”
translation_verse: Nɛ b shuli so ŋ kaŋɛ le: “Mm, Yiramu, kusɔ kama nɛ fo kaŋɛ, anyeeŋ wora”

english_verse: David left behind ten of his wives to take care of the palace, but the rest of his family and his officials and soldiers went with him. They stopped at the last house at the edge of the city.
translation_verse: Ewura na nɛ mbe basa ka lar a yɔ anishito gbrɛbi, nɛ b ya yili ekpa to kade na be lalaloge.

english_verse: David spoke to Ittai and said, “You're a foreigner from the town of Gath. You don't have to leave with us. Go back and join the new king!
translation_verse: Nɛ ewura na bishi benapo be enimu Ittai na le: “Manɛ nna nɛ men bɛ anyi so a ba? Men bɛta a yɔ menyi be ewura popɔr Absalɔm kutɔ. Men la befɔ nɛ men shile kena ashi menyi be kade to nna.

english_verse: You haven't been with me very long, so why should you have to follow me, when I don't even know where I'm going? Take your soldiers and go back. I pray that the Lord will be kind and faithful to you.”
translation_verse: Menyi maŋ ba nfe n chɛr, amoso m maŋ tiŋ n shin nɛ men baa bɛ ma so loŋ. M maŋ nyi kakpa nɛ mee yɔ gba. Men bɛta n ya tu men kurgepoana, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be kelela nɛ mbe kashenteŋ e baa kra wɔ menyi so.”

english_verse: Ittai answered, “Your Majesty, just as surely as you and the Lord live, I will go where you go, no matter if it costs me my life.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Ittai kaŋɛ ewura na le: “Yiramu, ŋkpal Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ e la ma shɛdajipo na so, kaplɛkama nɛ fee yɔ, hale nɛ k la luwu to nna gba, ma nɛ fo beeŋ yɔ.”

english_verse: “Then come on!” David said. So Ittai and all his men and their families walked on past David. David Sends the Sacred Chest Back to Jerusalem
translation_verse: Nɛ Deevid kaŋɛ le: “K nyalɛ. An baa yɔ!” Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ittai nɛ mbe basa nɛ mbe kanaŋ kikɛ tu Deevid n yɔ.

english_verse: The people of Jerusalem were crying and moaning as David and everyone with him passed by. He led them across Kidron Valley and along the road toward the desert.
translation_verse: Deevid nɛ mbe basa ka bee yɔ na nɛ Jerusalɛmebi na shu ga. Ewura na nɛ mbe basa daŋ ya dii ketaŋɛ nɛ baa tre Kidrɔn na nna n sɔ kiyitokpɛato a yɔ.

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar the priests were there along with several men from the tribe of Levi who were carrying the sacred chest. They set the chest down, and left it there until David and his followers had gone out of the city.
translation_verse: Bɔrɛmatapoana Zadɔk nɛ Abiata nɛ Livai be kanaŋ to be basa nɛ baa sulɔ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be ŋkre be deka cheembi na gba daŋ ti bumo so. B ka suge deka na n yili, b maŋ naŋ ta kumo kikɛ hale ewura Deevid nɛ mbe basa na kikɛ lar kade na to.

english_verse: Then David said: Zadok, take the sacred chest back to Jerusalem. If the Lord is pleased with me, he will bring me back and let me see it and his tent again.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura na kaŋɛ Zadɔk le: “Men bɛta ŋkre be deka na n yɔ Jerusalɛm be kade to. Nɛ Ebɔrɛ shuli, e beeŋ shin nɛ m bɛta m ba wu kakpa nɛ k wɔ kachako.

english_verse: But if he says he isn't pleased with me, then let him do what he knows is best.
translation_verse: Ama nɛ fanɛ e maŋ shuli bre, kumo ere e beeŋ tiŋ n wora ma kusɔ kama nɛ e bee sha.”

english_verse: Zadok, you are a good judge of things, so return to the city and don't cause any trouble. Take your son Ahimaaz with you. Abiathar and his son Jonathan will also go back.
translation_verse: Nɛ ewura na naŋ laŋɛ ŋ kaŋɛ bɔrɛmatapo Zadɔk le: “Keta fo pibinyɛn Ahimaaz nɛ Abiata pibinyɛn Jonatan n yɔ kade na to kagbenewushiso.

english_verse: I'll wait at the river crossing in the desert until I hear from you.
translation_verse: Ama meeŋ jo kiyi na to be kakpa nɛ baa bɔla a dii lɔr na n ya fo jemanɛ kama nɛ meeŋ nu kubɔya ashi menyi kutɔ.”

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar took the sacred chest back into Jerusalem and stayed there.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Zadɔk nɛ Abiata nɛ bumo be mbinyɛnsobi na ta ŋkre be deka na m bɛta n yɔ Jerusalɛm n ya ka wɔ ndoŋ.

english_verse: David went on up the slope of the Mount of Olives. He was barefoot and crying, and he covered his head to show his sorrow. Everyone with him was crying, and they covered their heads too.
translation_verse: Nɛ Deevid ta asɔ m buu mbe kumu so nsaa nite aya fuloŋ a shu n yɔ kebeegboŋ nɛ baa tre Ɔlifs na ase a ŋini kagbenejija nɛ k tɔr mo so. Basa nɛ b daa bɛ mo so na gba daŋ ta asɔ nna m buu bumo be amu so a shu a bɛ mo so.

english_verse: Someone told David, “Ahithophel is helping Absalom plot against you!” David said, “Please, Lord, keep Ahithophel's plans from working!” David Sends Hushai Back as a Spy
translation_verse: B ka kaŋɛ Deevid fanɛ Ahitofɛl gba ti Absalɔm so nna, nɛ e kule Ebɔrɛ le: “Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, jande shin nɛ Ahitofɛl be nfɛra nɛ e beeŋ sa Absalɔm na e ki nfɛra fuloŋ!”

english_verse: When David reached the top of the Mount of Olives, he met Hushai the Archite at a place of worship. Hushai's robe was torn, and dust was on his head.
translation_verse: Deevid ka dii n yɔ kebee na be esoso be kakpa nɛ baa bunyaŋ Ebɔrɛ na, nɛ e ya tu Hushai nɛ e la Aki be esa na ndoŋ nɛ e buu epiŋi kpɛatoso nseŋ ta shishɛr n wurge mbe kumu so.

english_verse: David told him: If you come with me, you might slow us down.
translation_verse: Nɛ Deevid kaŋɛ mo le: “Sa maŋ kaŋ ba n kutɔ ŋkpal manɛ so fo maaŋ baa kɔ kechɛto kikɛ n sa ma nfe.

english_verse: Go back into the city and tell Absalom, “Your Majesty, I am your servant. I will serve you now, just as I served your father in the past.” Hushai, if you do that, you can help me ruin Ahithophel's plans.
translation_verse: Kechɛ to nɛ feeŋ tiŋ n sa ma e la fanɛ, fo bɛta n yɔ kade to n ya kaŋɛ Absalɔm fanɛ kananɛ fo shuŋ mo tuto nɛnɛ na gbagba nɛ feeŋ shuŋ mo alɛ gba. Ama wora ania fanɛ feeŋ chɛrga nfɛra kama nɛ Ahitofɛl bee sa Absalɔm.

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar the priests will be there with you, and you can tell them everything you hear in the palace.
translation_verse: Bɔrɛmatapoana Zadɔk nɛ Abiata beeŋ baa wɔ ndoŋ, amoso wora ŋ kaŋɛ bumo kusɔ nɛ fo nu ashi ewura be lambu to na.

english_verse: Then they can send their sons Ahimaaz and Jonathan to tell me what you've heard.
translation_verse: Bumo be mbinyɛnbi Ahimaaz nɛ Jonatan kikɛ wɔ bumo kutɔ, fo alɛ beeŋ tiŋ ŋ kaŋɛ bumo baru kikɛ nɛ k wɔtɔ nɛ b ba kaŋɛ ma.”

english_verse: David's advisor Hushai slipped back into Jerusalem, at just about the same time Absalom was coming in.
translation_verse: Deevid mo teri Hushai ka bɛta n yɔ Jerusalɛm k maŋ chɛr ko nɛ Absalɔm gba fo ndoŋ.

english_verse: “What's all this?” David asked. Ziba said, “The donkeys are for your family to ride. The bread and fruit are for the people to eat, and the wine is for them to drink in the desert when they are tired out.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Deevid bishi mo le: “Manɛ nɛ fee sha nɛ fo wora asɔ ere kikɛ?” Nɛ Ziba yɛ: “Yiramu, ekurma ere bre la fo laŋ to ebi peya nna nɛ b baa dii. Ebodobodo ere nɛ asɔrso na malɛ la fo basa be kusɔ jiso nna. Nsa ere malɛ beeŋ chɛ bumo to saŋɛ nɛ b nite kiyi to ŋ gben na.”

english_verse: “And where is Mephibosheth?” David asked. Ziba answered, “He stayed in Jerusalem, because he thinks the people of Israel want him to rule the kingdom of his grandfather Saul.”
translation_verse: Nɛ ewura na bishi mo le: “Nnɛ nɛ fo nyɛnpe Sɔɔl mo nanabi Mifiboshɛf wɔ?” Nɛ Ziba yɛ: “E wɔ Jerusalɛm to, ŋkpal e ka bee fɛ fanɛ Israɛlebi na beeŋ laŋɛ mo nananyɛn Sɔɔl be kuwura n sa mo so.”

english_verse: David then told him, “Everything that used to belong to Mephibosheth is now yours.” Ziba said, “Your Majesty, I am your humble servant, and I hope you will be pleased with me.” Shimei Curses David
translation_verse: Nɛ ewura na kaŋɛ Ziba le: “Mifiboshɛf be kusɔ kama nɛ e kɔ na ki feya nna naniere.” Nɛ Ziba malɛ yɛ le: “Yiramu! Ebɔrɛ e shin nɛ m baa wora fo aparsheŋ saŋkama, ŋkpal manɛ so n la fo kayɛrbi nna.” Deevid nɛ Shimei be asheŋ

english_verse: David was near the town of Bahurim when a man came out and started cursing him. The man was Shimei the son of Gera, and he was one of Saul's distant relatives.
translation_verse: Ewura Deevid ka bee fo kade nɛ baa tre Bahurim na nɛ Sɔɔl mo kurgepo ko nɛ baa tre Shimei nɛ e la Gɛra pibinyɛn na bee shɛr mo to nsaa tege mo a sho mo kɔnɔ.

english_verse: He threw stones at David, at his soldiers, and at everyone else, including the bodyguards who walked on each side of David.
translation_verse: Deevid be bekumpo nɛ mbe benapo kikɛ daŋ kulti mo nna n wɔtɔ ama amo nɛ amo kikɛ Shimei daa kpa mo nɛ mbe benimuana nɛ mbe basa kikɛ ajembu nna.

english_verse: Shimei was yelling at David, “Get out of here, you murderer! You good-for-nothing,
translation_verse: Shimei daŋ sho mo kɔnɔ nna ŋ kaŋɛ le: “Fo emɔpo nɛ esa jiga ere! Baa yɔ ŋ ka anyi.

english_verse: the Lord is paying you back for killing so many in Saul's family. You stole his kingdom, but now the Lord has given it to your son Absalom. You're a murderer, and that's why you're in such big trouble!”
translation_verse: Sɔɔl be kuwura nɛ fo sɔ nseŋ mɔ mbe basa damta na so nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ bee gberge fo kusoe nseŋ ta fo kuwura n sa fo pibinyɛn Absalɔm nɛ fo asheŋ maŋ naa wu anishi na. Emɔpo e la fo.”

english_verse: Abishai said, “Your Majesty, this man is as useless as a dead dog! He shouldn't be allowed to curse you. Let me go over and chop off his head.”
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Zeruwa pibinyɛn Abishai kaŋɛ ewura na le: “Yiramu, manɛ nna nɛ fo shin nɛ esa fuloŋ fanɛ kujɔnɔmu ere bee sho fo kɔnɔ? Shin nɛ n yɔ n ya ku mbe kumu n lɛ!”

english_verse: David replied, “What will I ever do with you and your brother Joab? If Shimei is cursing me because the Lord has told him to, then who are you to tell him to stop?”
translation_verse: Nɛ ewura na kaŋɛ Abishai nɛ mo da Jɔab: “Nnɛ nɛ k nya menyi! Nɛ fanɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e kaŋɛ mo fanɛ e sho ma kɔnɔ, wanɛ malɛ e wɔtɔ nɛ e tiŋ m bishi kusɔ nɛ k ba nɛ e wora loŋ?”

english_verse: Then David said to Abishai and all his soldiers: My own son is trying to kill me! Why shouldn't this man from the tribe of Benjamin want me dead even more? Let him curse all he wants. Maybe the Lord did tell him to curse me.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Deevid kaŋɛ Abishai nɛ mbe benimuana na le: “M pibinyɛn gbagba e naa fin ma nɛ e mɔ na, amoso men sa maŋ shin nɛ kusɔ nɛ Bɛnjamin be esa ere wora ere gba a tir menyi. Nɛ kashenteŋ nna fanɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e kaŋɛ mo fanɛ e sho ma kɔnɔ, kumo ere fo yige mo nɛ e baa wora.

english_verse: But if the Lord hears these curses and sees the trouble I'm in, maybe he will have pity on me instead.
translation_verse: Ashere Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ beeŋ wu kagbenejija nɛ k tɔr ma so ere nseŋ shin nɛ kɔnɔsho ere e ki nɛfa n sa ma.”

english_verse: David and the others went on down the road. Shimei went along the hillside by the road, cursing and throwing rocks and dirt at them.
translation_verse: Deevid ka malga n loge nɛ mo nɛ mbe basa kilgi a yɔ, nɛ Shimei malɛ bɔ kebee na be kekil to a kuŋ bumo a sho bumo kɔnɔ a kpa bumo ajembu nsaa muu shishɛr a fari bumo.

english_verse: When David and those with him came to the Jordan River, they were tired out. But after they rested, they felt much better. Hushai Meets Absalom
translation_verse: Pɔɛŋ nɛ ewura na nɛ mbe basa e fo Jɔɔdan be Lɔr na ase nɛ bumo kikɛ chɛl, nseŋ chena n wushi n naŋ nya eleŋ. Absalɔm ka ba Jerusalɛm be asheŋ

english_verse: By this time, Absalom, Ahithophel, and the others had reached Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Le be jemanɛ ere nɛ Absalɔm nɛ mbe bebɛsopo, n ta Ahitofɛl gba n ti so ba Jerusalɛm to.

english_verse: David's friend Hushai came to Absalom and said, “Long live the king! Long live the king!”
translation_verse: Deevid mo teri kpakpaso Hushai ka tu Absalɔm nɛ e ponte ŋ kaŋɛ le: “Yiramu, Ebɔrɛ e sa fo ŋkpa tenteŋ!”

english_verse: But Absalom asked Hushai, “Is this how you show loyalty to your friend David? Why didn't you go with him?”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Absalɔm bishi Hushai le: “Le nɛ baa bugi kagbene a shuŋ eteri a? Nɛ manɛ e ba nɛ fo maŋ tu fo teri Deevid n yɔ?”

english_verse: Hushai answered, “The Lord and the people of Israel have chosen you to be king. I can't leave. I have to stay and serve the one they've chosen.
translation_verse: Nɛ Hushai kaŋɛ le: “M maaŋ tiŋ n yɔ, ŋkpal manɛ so, ekama nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ mbe basa Israɛlebi lara fanɛ ewura na nɛ malɛ gba bɛ so, nɛ m baa shuŋ mo.

english_verse: Besides, it seems right for me to serve you, just as I served your father.” Ahithophel's Advice
translation_verse: Wanɛ bre nɛ meeŋ naŋ shuŋ n naŋ baŋ n nyɛnpe Deevid pibinyɛn so? Kananɛ m baŋ shuŋ n sa fo tuto na, loŋ koŋwule na nɛ meeŋ shuŋ n sa fo alɛ gba.”

english_verse: Absalom turned to Ahithophel and said, “Give us your advice! What should we do?”
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Absalɔm kilgi m bishi Ahitofɛl le: “Manɛ be kasotoji nɛ fo kɔ nɛ fo sa anyi nfe naniere?”

english_verse: Ahithophel answered, “Some of your father's wives were left here to take care of the palace. You should have sex with them. Then everyone will find out that you have publicly disgraced your father. This will make you and your followers even more powerful.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Ahitofɛl malɛ kaŋɛ mo le: “Yɔ nɛ fo nɛ fo tuto mo jipoana nɛ e yige kaman fanɛ b baa keni mbe laŋ so na e ya di keche nɛ kenyɛn, saŋɛ na so ekama nɛ e wɔ Israɛl to beeŋ pin fanɛ naniere bre fo doŋ gbagba e la fo tuto nɛ keleŋ basa nɛ b bɛ fo so na kikɛ to ga.”

english_verse: Absalom had a tent set up on the flat roof of the palace, and everyone watched as he went into the tent with his father's wives.
translation_verse: Nɛ b yuu wajɛbu ewurkpa be kuchoŋi na be esoso nɛ basa nɛ b wɔ ndoŋ na wu Absalɔm ka luri kumo to nɛ e ya di mo tuto mo jipoana basa na kikɛ be anishito.

english_verse: Ahithophel gave such good advice in those days that both Absalom and David thought it came straight from God.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal Deevid nɛ Absalɔm kikɛ ka daa fɛ fanɛ kusɔ kama nɛ Ahitofɛl daŋ baŋ kaŋɛ shi Ebɔrɛ kutɔ na so, kasotoji kama nɛ e daŋ baŋ sa bumo baa nu nna a sa mo.

english_verse: and we will all go to fight David wherever he is. We will fall on him just as dew falls and covers the ground. He and all his soldiers will die!
translation_verse: Loŋ beeŋ shin nɛ an tɔr mo nɛ mbe basa so fanɛ kananɛ bunyaŋ bee tɔr kasawule so na m mur bumo kikɛ ashi kaplɛkama nɛ b wɔ.

english_verse: while he is tired and discouraged. He will panic, and everyone with him will run away. I won't kill anyone except David,
translation_verse: Saŋɛ so nɛ e gben nsaa maŋ naa kɔ eleŋ na nɛ meeŋ fara a kɔ mo. Keyeŋiyeŋi beeŋ tɔr mo so, nɛ mbe basa kikɛ e shile ŋ ka mo nɛ m mɔ mo nawule

english_verse: since he's the one you want to get rid of. Then I'll bring the whole nation back to you like a bride coming home to her husband. This way there won't be a civil war. Hushai Fools Absalom
translation_verse: nseŋ bɛta mbe basa na kikɛ m ba sa fo fanɛ kananɛ eche bee bɛta a ba mo kul pe na. Esa koŋwule nawule nɛ fee sha nɛ fo mɔ basa na kikɛ to nɛ bumo nɛ b ka na e nya bumo be amu.”

english_verse: Absalom and all the leaders of the tribes of Israel agreed that Ahithophel had a good plan.
translation_verse: Nɛ Absalɔm nɛ Israɛl be bejuŋkparpoana na wu fanɛ kesheŋ nɛ e kaŋɛ na duli kasotoji lela nna n sa bumo.

english_verse: Then Absalom said, “Bring in Hushai the Archite. Let's hear what he has to say.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Absalɔm yɛ: “Men tre Hushai naniere nɛ e ba kaŋɛ anyi kusɔ nɛ mo alɛ kɔ.”

english_verse: Hushai came in, and Absalom told him what Ahithophel had planned. Then Absalom said, “Should we do what he says? And if we shouldn't, can you come up with anything better?”
translation_verse: Hushai ka ba nɛ Absalɔm kaŋɛ mo kusɔ nɛ Ahitofɛl kaŋɛ na nseŋ bishi mo le: “An bɛ kumo so a, ŋko fo kɔ kusɔ ko nɛ fo kaŋɛ anyi?”

english_verse: Hushai said: This time Ahithophel's advice isn't so good.
translation_verse: Nɛ Hushai kaŋɛ le: “Ahitofɛl be kasotoji nɛ e sa fo naniere bre maŋ walɛ.

english_verse: You know that your father and his followers are real warriors. Now they are as fierce as a mother bear whose cubs have just been killed. Besides, your father has a lot of experience in fighting wars, and he won't be spending the night with the others.
translation_verse: Fo gbagba na nyi fo tuto Deevid nɛ mbe basa ka bee pere kenishi a kɔ kena ga, bumo alɛ nseŋ naŋ lubi a chɔ shishiri nɛ b mɔ kumo be mbia. Fo tuto nyi kena to nɛnɛ ga amoso e maaŋ tu mbe benapo n dese kakpa koŋwule kanyɛ ere.

english_verse: He has probably already found a hiding place in a cave or somewhere else. As soon as anyone hears that some of your soldiers have been killed, everyone will think your whole army has been destroyed.
translation_verse: Ashere e ŋana kebeelaŋ to ŋko kakpa ko naniere gba. Basa kama nɛ bumo alɛ baŋ nu fanɛ Deevid bee kɔ fo basa, beeŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ b pɔɔ fo basa so,

english_verse: Then even those who are as brave as a lion will lose their courage. All Israel knows what a great warrior your father is and what brave soldiers he has.
translation_verse: nɛ benapo kama nɛ b kɔ kenyɛn fanɛ ebuluŋ gba e fara a lɔ kufu, ŋkpal manɛ so Israɛl ebi kikɛ nyi fo tuto ka la enapogboŋ nɛ mbe basa malɛ bee kɔ kena ga.

english_verse: My advice is to gather all the fighting men of Israel from the town of Dan in the north down to the town of Beersheba in the south. You will have more soldiers than there are grains of sand on the seashore. Absalom, you should lead them yourself,
translation_verse: Ma kasotoji e la fanɛ fo yili Dan be kade to ashi kelargato be esoso be kaba so n chala Israɛl be benapo n ya fo Bɛshiba be kade to be kelargato be kaseto na saŋɛ na so feeŋ nya benapo, nɛ b baa shi fanɛ teku ase be leele na, nɛ fo Absalɔm gbagba e juŋkpar nɛ an ya kɔ Deevid kena.

english_verse: If they go into a walled town, we will put ropes around that town and drag it into the river. We won't leave even one small piece of a stone.
translation_verse: E kaŋ baŋ shile n yɔ kade nɛ k tase kebee so to, anyi be basa kikɛ beeŋ ta amamprɔŋ m ba chɛ kumo be egbal ŋ gberge kumo n ya lɛ ketaŋɛ to nɛ b maaŋ naŋ wu kumo be kejembu koŋwule gba ka dese.”

english_verse: Absalom and the others liked Hushai's plan better than Ahithophel's plan. This was because the Lord had decided to keep Ahithophel's plan from working and to cause trouble for Absalom. Jonathan and Ahimaaz Tell David the News
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Absalɔm nɛ mbe bebɛsopo na kaŋɛ le: “Hushai be kasotoji ere bɔ Ahitofɛl peya na, ŋkpal manɛ so, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e yili kumo fanɛ b sa maŋ bɛ Ahitofɛl be kasotoji na so, saŋɛ na so Absalɔm beeŋ luri asheŋ to. B ka fɛa Deevid so be asheŋ

english_verse: At once, Hushai went to Zadok and Abiathar. He told them what advice Ahithophel had given to Absalom and to the leaders of Israel. He also told them about the advice he had given.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Hushai kaŋɛ bɔrɛmatapoana Zadɔk nɛ Abiata kasotoji nɛ e sa Absalɔm nɛ Israɛlebi be bejuŋkparpoana na nɛ kumo nɛ Ahitofɛl malɛ gba sa bumo.

english_verse: Then he said, “Hurry! Send someone to warn David not to spend the night on this side of the Jordan. He must get across the river, so he and the others won't be wiped out!”
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e kaŋɛ bumo fanɛ b wora manaŋ n ya kaŋɛ Deevid fanɛ e sa maŋ kaŋ dese Jɔɔdan be lɔr na be kɔnɔ ase, ama e dii kumo manaŋ, saŋɛ na so b maaŋ nya mo nɛ mbe basa m mɔ.”

english_verse: Jonathan and Ahimaaz had been waiting at Rogel Spring because they did not want to be seen in Jerusalem. A servant girl went to the spring and gave them the message for David.
translation_verse: Abiata pibinyɛn Jonatan nɛ Zadɔk pibinyɛn Ahimaaz daa jo Ɛnrogɛl be kebuye na ase nna ashi Jerusalɛm be kade be ekarso ŋkpal manɛ so b daa maa sha b ka wu bumo nɛ baa luri kade na to. Kebichebi ko malɛ e naa kaa kaŋɛ bumo kusɔ nɛ k bee wora nɛ bumo alɛ e ta n ya kaŋɛ ewura Deevid.

english_verse: But a young man saw them and went to tell Absalom. So Jonathan and Ahimaaz left and hurried to the house of a man who lived in Bahurim. Then they climbed down into a well in the courtyard.
translation_verse: Kachako nɛ kebinyɛnbi ko wu bumo, nseŋ ya kaŋɛ Absalɔm. Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ahimaaz nɛ Jonatan nya manaŋ n ya ŋana ketirbu ko nɛ k mata Bahurim be kanyɛn ko be laŋ to,

english_verse: The man's wife put the cover on the well and poured grain on top of it, so the well could not be seen.
translation_verse: nɛ kanyɛn na be eche ta kusɔ ko m ba buu ketirbu na be kɔnɔ so nseŋ chulgi aboyu n fata kumo so, saŋɛ na so esa kama maaŋ pin kusɔ nɛ k wɔ kumo to.

english_verse: Absalom's soldiers came to the woman and demanded, “Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?” The woman answered, “They went across that stream.” The soldiers went off to look for the two men. But when they did not find the men, they went back to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Absalɔm be benapo ba laŋ na to m ba bishi kache na le: “Nnɛ nɛ Ahimaaz nɛ Jonatan wɔ?” Nɛ kache na kaŋɛ bumo le: “B dii Lɔr na n choŋ.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ basa na fin bumo ŋ gben nseŋ bɛta n yɔ Jerusalɛm.

english_verse: After the soldiers had gone, Jonathan and Ahimaaz climbed out of the well. They went to David and said, “Hurry! Get ready to cross the river!” Then they told him about Ahithophel's plan.
translation_verse: B ka choŋ na be kaman nɛ Ahimaaz nɛ Jonatan lar ketirbu na to n ya kaŋɛ ewura Deevid kusɔ nɛ Ahitofɛl kre kikɛ nseŋ kaŋɛ mo fanɛ e wora manaŋ n dii Lɔr na.

english_verse: David and the others got ready and started crossing the Jordan River. By sunrise all of them were on the other side. Ahithophel Kills Himself
translation_verse: Nɛ Deevid nɛ mbe basa fara e dii Jɔɔdan be Lɔr na, kare tea ya ka chɛ nɛ b dii n loge.

english_verse: When Ahithophel saw that Absalom and the leaders of Israel were not going to follow his advice, he saddled his donkey and rode back to his home in Gilo. He told his family and servants what to do. Then he hanged himself, and they buried him in his family's burial place. Absalom Puts Amasa in Charge of the Army
translation_verse: Ahitofɛl ka wu fanɛ b maŋ bɛ mbe kasotoji na so na, nɛ e dii n chena mbe kurma so n yɔ mbe kade to Gilo. E ka koli mbe laŋ to be kusɔ kama abar so n loge, nɛ e ya chɛ efɔl. Kakpa nɛ b puli mo nananyɛnana na nɛ b daŋ puli mo alɛ gba.

english_verse: David went to the town of Mahanaim, and Absalom crossed the Jordan River with the army of Israel.
translation_verse: Pɔɛŋ nɛ Absalɔm nɛ Israɛlebi be benapo na dii Jɔɔdan be Lɔr na n loge na nɛ Deevid bre tea wɔ Mahanaim.

english_verse: Absalom put Amasa in Joab's place as commander of the army. Amasa's father was Ithra from the family of Ishmael, and his mother was Abigal, the daughter of Nahash and the sister of Joab's mother Zeruiah.
translation_verse: Absalɔm daŋ ta Amasa nna n yili benapo na be enimu Jɔab be eyilikpa. Jɛta nɛ e la Ishmaɛl be kanaŋ to be esa na pibinyɛn e daa la Amasa. Nahaash be mbicheso e daa la Abigɛl, nɛ e la Amasa mo nio na nɛ Zeruwa nɛ mo alɛ la Jɔab mo nio na. Abigɛl mo sipo e daa la Zeruwa.

english_verse: The Israelites under Absalom's command set up camp in the region of Gilead. Friends Bring Supplies to David
translation_verse: Giliad be kasawule so nɛ Absalɔm nɛ mbe basa daŋ ya wora bumo be keeyi to n chena.

english_verse: After David came to the town of Mahanaim, Shobi the son of Nahash came from Rabbah in Ammon, Machir the son of Ammiel came from Lo-Debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite came from Rogelim.
translation_verse: Deevid ka ba Mahanaim na nɛ Nahaash pibinyɛn Shoobi e daŋ shi Raaba nɛ k wɔ Ammɔn na, nɛ Ammiɛl malɛ pibinyɛn Makiir nɛ e shi Lodiba na, nɛ Bazilai nɛ mo alɛ shi Rogeliim nɛ k wɔ Giliad be efuli so na m ba shɛr mo to.

english_verse: Here is a list of what they brought: sleeping mats, blankets, bowls, pottery jars, wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans, lentils, honey, yogurt, sheep, and cheese. They brought the food for David and the others because they knew that everyone would be hungry, tired, and thirsty from being out in the desert.
translation_verse: B daŋ bar ntishaŋ nɛ mpuliya nɛ b ta ebɔ m pɔr, nɛ asɔ deseso, nɛ ajibi nna m ba sa Deevid nɛ mbe basa. Ayu nɛ aboyu nɛ aboyutɔso nɛ chɛbɛ nɛ akuloŋku nɛ mushoŋ nɛ wagashi nɛ mbolpɔ gba daŋ ti so. Ŋkpal manɛ so b daa nyi geeŋ fanɛ akoŋ nɛ achukoŋ nɛ kegben beeŋ pɛ Deevid nɛ mbe basa ashi kiyi na to.

english_verse: He sent out one third of his army under the command of Joab, another third under the command of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, and the rest under the command of Ittai from Gath. He told the soldiers, “I'm going into battle with you.”
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e shin nɛ ntuŋ na kikɛ ba abar so nɛ e naŋ barga amo to ntuŋ asa nseŋ shin nɛ Jɔab bee keni katuŋ koŋwule so nɛ mo sipo Abishai malɛ bee keni katuŋ nyɔsopo so nɛ Ittai nɛ e shi Gaaf na malɛ bee keni katuŋ sasopo na so. Le nɛ ewura Deevid daŋ kaŋɛ mbe basa na: “Ma nɛ menyi e naŋ yɔ kena na to.”

english_verse: and one of them went and told Joab, “I saw Absalom hanging in a tree!”
translation_verse: Deevid be benapo na be ako ka wu mo nɛ e ya kaŋɛ Jɔab le: “N wu Absalɔm ka sha kedibi gboŋgboŋi ko so.”

english_verse: David said, “All right, if you think I should.” Then in a voice loud enough for everyone to hear, he said, “Joab! Abishai! Ittai! For my sake, be sure that Absalom comes back unharmed.” David stood beside the town gate as his army marched past in groups of
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Deevid be benapo na lar n yɔ kupo nɛ baa tre Efrayim na to n ya kɔ Absalɔm be benapo kena.

english_verse: Battles were being fought all over the forest, and David's soldiers were winning. Twenty thousand soldiers were killed that day, and more of them died from the dangers of the forest than from the fighting itself.
translation_verse: Kena na daŋ salga to nna n yɔ kade na be kupuŋ to nɛ kupo na to kikɛ nɛ benapo nɛ b wu ŋkpal kupo na to be awurfoŋ so daa shi a chɔ bumo nɛ b mɔ kena na gbagba to.

english_verse: Absalom was riding his mule under a huge tree when his head caught in the branches. The mule ran off and left Absalom hanging in midair. Some of David's soldiers happened by,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Absalɔm ba purgi Deevid be benapo ko. E daŋ dii kurma nna m bɔla kedibi gboŋgboŋi ko be kifito nɛ mbe kumu ya fɛga kumo be ayabi to nɛ kurma na shile ŋ ka mo n shiga kedibi na so.

english_verse: Joab said, “You saw Absalom? Why didn't you kill him? I would have given you ten pieces of silver and a special belt.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Jɔab malɛ kaŋɛ mo le: “Nɛ fo ka wu mo, manɛ nna nɛ fo maŋ mɔ mo epul to ndoŋ? N daa beeŋ sa fo gbiti be ndarbi kudu nɛ benapo be kreso.”

english_verse: He always finds out what's going on. I would have been risking my life to kill Absalom, because you would have let me take the blame.”
translation_verse: N daŋ kplaŋ ewura na be kɔnɔ so nseŋ mɔ Absalɔm, e daa beeŋ nu kumo, ŋkpal manɛ so asheŋ kikɛ maa wora a baŋ mo so. Fo alɛ daa maaŋ kuŋ ma.”

english_verse: Joab said, “I'm not going to waste any more time on you!” Absalom was still alive, so Joab took three spears and stuck them through Absalom's chest.
translation_verse: Nɛ Jɔab kaŋɛ le: “M maaŋ naŋ yili n jija saŋɛ.” Absalɔm ka sha kedibi gboŋ na so a maŋ naŋ wu na, nɛ Jɔab ta akpa asa m ber abar so n da Absalɔm be kagbene to.

english_verse: They threw Absalom's body into a deep pit in the forest and put a big pile of rocks over it. Meanwhile, the people of Israel had all run back to their own homes.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ b ta Absalɔm b kebuni n ya lɛ kupo na to be kejamaŋ chiŋgeliŋ ko to nseŋ muu ajembu gboŋgboŋi damta n deŋi mo so kululu. Loŋ be jemanɛ na so nɛ Absalɔm be bebɛsopo na kikɛ pɛ ekpa n shile n yɔ bumo peana.

english_verse: When Absalom was alive, he had set up a stone monument for himself in King's Valley. He explained, “I don't have any sons to keep my name alive.” He called it Absalom's Monument, and that is the name it still has today. Ahimaaz Wants To Tell David
translation_verse: Jemanɛ nɛ Absalɔm daa wɔ ŋkpa to na, nɛ e yuu ndulgi be kejembu bewura be ketaŋɛ na to ŋkpal manɛ so e daa maŋ kɔ ebinyɛn nɛ e beeŋ baa wɔtɔ kanyiŋiso n sa mo. Amoso mbe ketre nɛ e daŋ ta n nase kejembu na. Hale m ba fo kabre baa tre ndoŋ nna Absalɔm be kapɔrduli be kakpa. Deevid ka nu Absalɔm be luwu be asheŋ

english_verse: Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said, “Joab, let me run and tell King David that the Lord has rescued him from his enemies.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Zadɔk pibinyɛn Ahimaaz kaŋɛ Jɔab le: “Shin nɛ n shile n ya kaŋɛ ewura Deevid baru lela ere fanɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na mɔlga mo ashi mo doŋana be enɔ to.”

english_verse: Joab answered, “You're not the one to tell the king that his son is dead. You can take him a message some other time, but not today.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Jɔab kaŋɛ mo le: “Ayai! Ŋkpal ewura na pibinyɛn ka wu so, fo maaŋ yɛr baru kikɛ ndoŋ kabre. Ashere kachako nɛ feeŋ wora loŋ mannɛ kabre bre.”

english_verse: Someone from Ethiopia was standing there, and Joab told him, “Go and tell the king what you have seen.” The man knelt down in front of Joab, then got up and started running.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ e kaŋɛ mbe kenya nɛ e la Itiopia be esa na le: “Yɔ n ya kaŋɛ ewura Deevid kusɔ nɛ fo wu.” Nɛ kenya na jɔŋɛ m bunyaŋ mo nseŋ shile n yɔ.

english_verse: Ahimaaz spoke to Joab again, “No matter what happens, I still want to go. And besides, the Ethiopian has already left.” Joab said, “Why should you go? You won't get a reward for the news you have!”
translation_verse: Nɛ Ahimaaz kra marso a kaŋɛ le: “Kusɔ kama nɛ k beeŋ wora gba, ma ere b shɛŋ maŋ wɔtɔ, amoso jande, shin nɛ ma alɛ e ya bɔ baru na.” Nɛ Jɔab bishi mo le: “M pibi, manɛ nna nɛ fee sha kewora loŋ? Fo keya kaŋɛ mo ere maaŋ lar tɔnɔ kikɛ n sa fo.”

english_verse: “I'll run no matter what!” Ahimaaz insisted. “All right then, run!” Joab said. Ahimaaz took the road through the Jordan Valley and outran the Ethiopian.
translation_verse: Nɛ Ahimaaz naŋ kaŋɛ le: “Kusɔ kama nɛ k la gba ma ere beeŋ yɔ.” Nɛ Jɔab kaŋɛ mo le: “Kumo ere baa yɔ.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ahimaaz shile m bɔla Jɔɔdan be ketaŋɛ na be ekpa to n ya baŋ kenya na so n choŋ.

english_verse: Meanwhile, David was sitting between the inner and outer gates in the city wall. One of his soldiers was watching from the roof of the gate-tower. He saw a man running toward the town
translation_verse: Kade na be mbunagboŋ anyɔ nɛ kuko la kakpa nɛ baa bɔla a luri nɛ kakpa nɛ baa bɔla a lar na be kefɛato nɛ Deevid daa tase. Ndoŋ be ekenipo na ka dii kabunagboŋ na be egbal na be ketempreŋ jeŋgreŋ na, nɛ e wu kanyɛn ko nawule ka shil a ba.

english_verse: The soldier on the roof shouted, “The first one runs just like Ahimaaz the son of Zadok.” This time David said, “He's a good man. He must have some good news.”
translation_verse: Nɛ ekenipo na kaŋɛ le: “K du fanɛ sososo be esa nɛ e shile a ba na duli Zadɔk pibinyɛn Ahimaaz nna.” Nɛ ewura na kaŋɛ le: “Esa lela e la mo nɛ e kɔ baru lela a bar anyi.”

english_verse: Ahimaaz called out, “We won! We won!” Then he bowed low to David and said, “Your Majesty, praise the Lord your God! He has given you victory over your enemies.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ahimaaz ponte ŋ kaŋɛ le: “An kɔ m pɔɔ so! An kɔ m pɔɔ so! Kapandi e ba la Enyɛnpe fo Ebɔrɛ nɛ e shin nɛ fo kɔ m pɔɔ basa nɛ b nyaŋɛto a kɔ fo na peya, Yiramu.” Nseŋ ya jɔŋɛ mbe anishito bunyaŋ so.

english_verse: “Is my son Absalom all right?” David asked. Ahimaaz said, “When Joab sent your personal servant and me, I saw a noisy crowd. But I don't know what it was all about.”
translation_verse: Nɛ ewura na bishi le: “Absalɔm lar a?” Nɛ Ahimaaz yɛ: “Fo benapo be enimu Jɔab ka shuŋi ma na nɛ n nu kebagato be awɔr, ama ma alɛ maŋ pin kusɔ nɛ k la.”

english_verse: David told him, “Stand over there and wait.” Ahimaaz went over and stood there.
translation_verse: Nɛ ewura na kaŋɛ le: “Yɔ ndoŋ ere n ya yili.” Nɛ e yɔ ndoŋ n ya yili.

english_verse: “Is my son Absalom all right?” David asked. The Ethiopian replied, “I wish that all Your Majesty's enemies and everyone who tries to harm you would end up like him!” David Cries for Absalom
translation_verse: Nɛ ewura na bishi le: “Absalɔm lar a? E beeŋ pete a?” Nɛ kenya na yɛ: “Kusɔ nɛ k nya mo ere daŋ nya fo doŋana nɛ bekama nɛ b nyaŋɛto a kɔ fo na nna, n dafanɛ k daa beeŋ par ma ga.”

english_verse: David started trembling. Then he went up to the room above the city gate to cry. As he went, he kept saying, “My son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! I wish I could have died instead of you! Absalom, my son, my son!”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ kagbenejija tɔr ewura na so, nɛ e fara e chicha nseŋ dii n yɔ ebu nɛ k wɔ kabunagboŋ na be esoso na to n ya shu ga. Le nɛ e daa shu a kaŋɛ a yɔ: “O m pibinyɛn! M pibinyɛn Absalɔm! Absalɔm, m pibinyɛn! Nɛ k daa la fanɛ ma e wu gba, k daa bɔ fo ka wu ere.”

english_verse: Someone told Joab, “The king is crying because Absalom is dead.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ b kaŋɛ Jɔab fanɛ ewura Deevid bee shu Absalɔm be keeli.

english_verse: David's army found out he was crying because his son had died, and their day of victory suddenly turned into a day of sadness.
translation_verse: Benapo na ka nu fanɛ Deevid bee shu mo pibinyɛn be keeli na nɛ bumo be kekɔmpɔɔso be kagbenefuli na kilgi kagbenejija kumo be kamɔnchɛ.

english_verse: The troops were sneaking into Mahanaim, just as if they had run away from a battle and were ashamed.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ benapo na bɛta boeŋ n yɔ kade to fanɛ benapo nɛ b ta anishinyɔr a shile kena na.

english_verse: David covered his face with his hands and kept on crying loudly, “My son, Absalom! Absalom, my son, my son!”
translation_verse: Ewura Deevid daŋ buu mbe anishi so nna a shu awɔrso a kaŋɛ le: “O m pibinyɛn! Absalɔm! Absalɔm, m pibinyɛn!”

english_verse: Joab went to the house where David was staying and told him: You've made your soldiers ashamed! Not only did they save your life, they saved your sons and daughters and wives as well.
translation_verse: Nɛ Jɔab yɔ ewura na be laŋ to n ya kaŋɛ mo le: “Kabre fo ta anishinyɔr m pɛ fo benapo nɛ b mɔlga fo nɛ fo mbinyɛnbi nɛ mbichebi nɛ fo beche nɛ fo jipoana be ŋkpa na ga.

english_verse: You're more loyal to your enemies than to your friends. What you've done today has shown your officers and soldiers that they don't mean a thing to you. You would be happy if Absalom was still alive, even if the rest of us were dead.
translation_verse: Basa nɛ baa sha fo na nɛ fo kishi nsaa sha bumo nɛ b kishi fo na bre! Fo shin nɛ k dii efuli naniere fanɛ fo benapo nɛ bumo be benimuana na kikɛ maŋ la shɛŋ fo kutɔ. Nɛ Absalɔm daa wɔ ŋkpa to nɛ anyi ere kikɛ wu gba, fo kagbene daa beeŋ fuli fo.

english_verse: Now get up! Go out there and thank them for what they did. If you don't, I swear by the Lord that you won't even have one man left on your side tomorrow morning. You may have had a lot of troubles in the past, but this will be the worst thing that has ever happened to you!
translation_verse: Yɔ n ya leŋ fo basa na to naniere kikɛ. Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be ketre be eleŋto so, nɛ fo baa maŋ yɔ, ta a ba echefo chipurso saŋɛ ere esa koŋwule gba maŋ naŋ ka a bɛ fo so. Kumo alɛ be loŋ na beeŋ lubi a chɔ etɔrɔ kama nɛ a daŋ tu fo ŋ ku so na kikɛ.”

english_verse: David got up and went to the town gate and sat down. When the people heard that he was sitting there, they came to see him. Israel and Judah Want David Back After Israel's soldiers had all returned home,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura na koso n ya chena kade na be kabuna to. Mbe basa na ka nu fanɛ e wɔ ndoŋ nɛ bumo kikɛ yɔ mo kutɔ. Deevid ka bɛta m ba Jerusalɛm to be asheŋ Ama le be jemanɛ ere nɛ Absalɔm be bebɛsopo na bre shile n yɔ bumo peana.

english_verse: everyone in Israel started arguing. They were saying to each other, “King David rescued us from the Philistines and from our other enemies. But then we chose Absalom to be our new leader, and David had to leave the country to get away. Absalom died in battle, so why hasn't something been done to bring David back?”
translation_verse: Anyi e daŋ ta ŋku n wurge Absalɔm be kumu so fanɛ e ki anyi be ewura, ama e yɔ kena to n ya wu. Manɛ e ba nɛ anyi maaŋ naŋ ya keta Ewura Deevid m ba?”

english_verse: When David found out what they were saying, he sent a message to Zadok and Abiathar the priests. It said: Say to the leaders of Judah, “Why are you the last tribe to think about bringing King David back home?
translation_verse: Ewura Deevid ka nu asheŋ nɛ Israɛlebi na kaŋɛ na kikɛ nɛ e shuŋi n ya kaŋɛ bɔrɛmatapoana Zadɔk nɛ Abiata fanɛ b ya bishi Juda be bejuŋkparpoana na le: “Manɛ nna nɛ k ba fanɛ menyi e shir kaman n fɛ ewura be kelaŋɛ m ba mbe laŋ to be asheŋ?

english_verse: And tell Amasa, “You're my nephew, and with God as a witness, I swear I'll make you commander of my army instead of Joab.”
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ ewura Deevid naŋ kaŋɛ bumo fanɛ b kaŋɛ Amasa malɛ le: “Ŋkpal fo ka la ŋkurgepo so, yili kabre a yɔ, fo e naaŋ ki benapo nɛ Jɔab bee keniso na be enimu. Nɛ m baa maŋ wora loŋ, Ebɔrɛ e bishi ma!”

english_verse: Soon the tribe of Judah again became followers of David, and they sent him this message: “Come back, and bring your soldiers with you.” David Starts Back for Jerusalem
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Deevid be mmalga na shin nɛ Juda be basa na kikɛ be ŋgbene kilgi m bɛ mo so nɛ b shuŋi ŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ mo nɛ mbe benapo na kikɛ e bɛta m ba Jerusalɛm.

english_verse: Shimei the son of Gera was there with them. He had hurried from Bahurim to meet David. Shimei was from the tribe of Benjamin, and
translation_verse: Loŋ be saŋɛ na so gbagba nɛ Shemei nɛ e la Bɛnjamin be yiri to be esa nsaa la Gɛra nɛ e shi Bahurim na pibinyɛn nya manaŋ n ya tu Juda be basa na ashi Jɔɔdan be lɔr na to nɛ b ya shɛr ewura Deevid to.

english_verse: I know I was wrong. That's why I wanted to be the first one from the northern tribes to meet you.”
translation_verse: N nyi ŋ ka wora kulubi ŋ gbiti fo, amoso nɛ n juŋkpar ashi kelargato be esoso be kaba so be eyiri na kikɛ m ba nɛ m ba shɛr fo to kabre na Yiramu.”

english_verse: Then they brought David's family and servants back across the river, and they did everything he wanted them to do. Shimei Meets with David Shimei crossed the Jordan River and bowed down in front of David.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ b keta ewura na nɛ mbe laŋ to ebi m bɔla Lɔr na be kakpa nɛ k maŋ wɔ nchiŋ na n dii nseŋ wora mbe aparsheŋ kikɛ n sa mo. Deevid ka wora Shemei kelela be asheŋ Shemei ka dii lɔr na, nɛ e dese kasawule m bunyaŋ ewura Deevid

english_verse: He said, “Your Majesty, I beg you not to punish me! Please, forget what I did when you were leaving Jerusalem. Don't even think about it.
translation_verse: nseŋ kaŋɛ mo le: “Yiramu! Jande, ta alubi nɛ n wora fo kachɛ nɛ fee lar Jerusalɛm to na m paŋ ma. Jande ta m paŋ ma nsaa maŋ naa nyiŋi amo.

english_verse: David said, “Abishai, what will I ever do with you and your brother Joab? Is it your job to tell me who has done wrong? I've been made king of all Israel today, and no one will be put to death!”
translation_verse: Ama Deevid daŋ kaŋɛ Abishai nɛ mo da Jɔab nna le: “Menyi e naa ŋini ma kusɔ nɛ meeŋ wora a? Ŋko asheŋ nɛ menyee sha nɛ men fin n sa ma a? Naniere bre, ma e la Israɛl kikɛ be ewura, ma alɛ maa sha fanɛ b mɔ Israɛl be esa kikɛ kabre.”

english_verse: Then David promised Shimei that he would not be killed. Mephibosheth Meets with David
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura na nase kɔnɔ n sa Shemei fanɛ e maaŋ mɔ mo. Deevid ka wora Mifiboshɛf kelela be asheŋ

english_verse: Mephibosheth, the grandson of Saul, also came to meet David. He had missed David so much that he had not taken a bath or trimmed his beard or washed his clothes the whole time David was gone. David asked him, “Why didn't you go with me?”
translation_verse: Mifiboshɛf ka shi Jerusalɛm n fo ewura na kutɔ nɛ e bishi mo le: “Mifiboshɛf manɛ nna nɛ fo daa maŋ bɛ ma so n yɔ?”

english_verse: He answered, “Your Majesty, you know I can't walk. I told my servant to saddle a donkey for me so I could go with you. But my servant left without me, and
translation_verse: Nɛ e kaŋɛ le: “Yiramu, fo nyi ŋ ka la bobi. Ma alɛ ka kaŋɛ ma kayɛrbi fanɛ e mɛa ma kurma to nɛ n dii n tu fo n yɔ nɛ e kini nseŋ shile ŋ ka ma.

english_verse: then he lied about me. You're as wise as an angel of God, so do what you think is right.
translation_verse: E daŋ ya ku efɛ nna deŋi ma n sa fo. Yiramu, ama ŋkpal fo ka du fanɛ Ebɔrɛ be kabɔ so, fo wora kusɔ kama nɛ k par fo.

english_verse: After all, you could have killed my whole family and me. But instead, you let me eat at your own table. Your Majesty, what more could I ask?”
translation_verse: Fo Yiramu daŋ daga fo ka mɔ n tuto be kanaŋ to be basa kikɛ nna, ama fo wu ma ere kuwɔr hale nseŋ shin nɛ mee tu fo gba a ji. Amoso, a maŋ daga ŋ ka naŋ kule fo shɛŋ.”

english_verse: Mephibosheth replied, “He can have it all! I'm just glad you've come home safely.” Barzillai Returns Home
translation_verse: Nɛ Mifiboshɛf kaŋɛ le: “Shin nɛ Ziba e ta kapetɛ na kikɛ. Yiramu k wora ma ebel ga fo ka ba epe nɛ alenfia.” Deevid ka wora Bazilai kelela be asheŋ

english_verse: Barzillai came from Rogelim in Gilead to meet David at the Jordan River and go across with him.
translation_verse: Bazilai nɛ e la Giliad be esa na gba daŋ shi Rogelim nna m ba nɛ e ba tu ewura na n dii Jɔɔdan be Lɔr na.

english_verse: David said to him, “Cross the river and go to Jerusalem with me. I will take care of you.”
translation_verse: Nɛ ewura na kaŋɛ mo le: “Shin nɛ an dii n yɔ Jerusalɛm nɛ fo ya chena ŋ kutɔ nɛ m ba keni fo so.”

english_verse: Barzillai answered: Your Majesty, why should I go to Jerusalem? I don't have much longer to live.
translation_verse: Nɛ Bazilai malɛ kaŋɛ le: “Yiramu! Nchɛ afanɛ bre nɛ meeŋ naaŋ ji nseŋ ya kaa chena fo kutɔ ashi Jerusalɛm?

english_verse: I'll cross the river with you, but I'll only go a little way on the other side. You don't have to be so kind to me.
translation_verse: Le be kakɔka ere maŋ daga ma. Ama meeŋ shuŋi fo n ya dii Jɔɔdan be Lɔr na n yɔ anishito gbrɛbi.

english_verse: Just let me return to my hometown, where I can someday be buried near my father and mother. My servant Chimham can go with you, and you can treat him as your own.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ m bɛta n yɔ epe, saŋɛ na so ŋ kaŋ wu nɛ b ta ma n ya puli n tutoana be edesekpa. Ama ma kayɛrbi Chimham bre nde, n ta mo n sa fo. Ta mo a yɔ n ya wora mo kusɔ kama nɛ fee sha Yiramu!”

english_verse: David said, “I'll take Chimham with me, and whatever you ask me to do for him, I'll do. And if there's anything else you want, I'll also do that.”
translation_verse: Nɛ ewura Deevid kaŋɛ le: “Meeŋ ta mo a yɔ n ya wora kusɔ kama nɛ fee sha fanɛ n wora n sa mo. Kusɔ kama malɛ nɛ fo alɛ gba bee sha, meeŋ wora kumo n sa fo.”

english_verse: Chimham crossed the river with David. Israel and Judah Argue All of Judah's army and half of Israel's army were there to help David cross the river.
translation_verse: Juda be benapo kikɛ nɛ Israɛl be benapo be bargato ka keta ewura Deevid n dii Lɔr na n yɔ kaba ndoŋ na nɛ e yɔ Gilgaal nɛ Chimham gba bɛ mo so n yɔ.

english_verse: The soldiers from Israel came to him and said, “Why did our relatives from Judah secretly take you and your family and your soldiers across the Jordan?”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Israɛl be benapo na kikɛ yɔ ewura Deevid kutɔ n ya bishi mo le: “Yiramu, manɛ nna nɛ an niopibiana Juda be basa bee fɛ fanɛ bumo e kɔ ekpa nseŋ keta fo nɛ fo kanaŋ nɛ fo benapo kikɛ n dii Jɔɔdan be Lɔr na?”

english_verse: The people of Judah answered, “Why are you so angry? We are the king's relatives. He didn't give us any food, and we didn't take anything for ourselves!”
translation_verse: Nɛ Juda be basa na malɛ kaŋɛ le: “An wora loŋ nna ŋkpal manɛ so anyi nɛ ewura na la kukoŋwule nna. Manɛ nna nɛ men nya agbo ŋkpal le be kesheŋ ere so? E maŋ sa anyi ajibi, mo alɛ maŋ kɛ anyi shɛŋ malɛ gba.”

english_verse: Those from Israel said, “King David belongs to us ten times more than he belongs to you. Why didn't you think we were good enough to help you? After all, we were the first ones to think of bringing him back!” The people of Judah argued more strongly than the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Nɛ Israɛlebi na malɛ kaŋɛ le: “Hale nɛ menyi nɛ ewura Deevid la kukoŋwule gba, ŋkpal an ka la nnaŋ kudu so, an kɔ mo so eleŋ alɛ kudu a chɔ menyi. Amoso manɛ nna nɛ menyee keni anyi jiga? Men sa maŋ teŋ so fanɛ anyi e daŋ kenya nfɛra fanɛ anyeeŋ ya keta ewura na m ba!” Ama Juda be basa na daŋ nyaŋɛto na ga m malga m pɔɔ Israɛl be basa na so.

english_verse: A troublemaker from the tribe of Benjamin was there. His name was Sheba the son of Bichri, and he blew a trumpet to get everyone's attention. Then he said, “People of Israel, David the son of Jesse doesn't belong to us! Let's go home.”
translation_verse: Kanyɛn ko nɛ e daa ku asheŋ nɛ baa tre Shɛba nɛ e la Bikri pibinyɛn nseŋ shi Bɛnjamin be yiri to daa wɔ Gilgaal nna. E daŋ foŋ kabel nna m ber kubomboŋ ŋ kaŋɛ le: “Men sa maŋ bɛ Jɛsi pibinyɛn Deevid so! E maŋ la anyi to be eko! Israɛlebi men shin nɛ an yɔ epe!”

english_verse: So they stopped following David and went off with Sheba. But the people of Judah stayed close to David all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem. David's Ten Wives
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Israɛl be basa na shile ewura Deevid n ya bɛ Shɛba so, ama Juda be basa na bre daŋ bugi kagbene nna m bɛ Deevid so ashi Jɔɔdan be Lɔr na ase kikɛ hale n ya fo Jerusalɛm.

english_verse: David had left ten of his wives in Jerusalem to take care of his palace. But when he came back, he had them taken to another house, and he placed soldiers there to guard them. He gave them whatever they needed, but he never slept with any of them again. They had to live there for the rest of their lives as if they were widows. The Army Goes after Sheba
translation_verse: Ewura Deevid daŋ shin nna nɛ mo jipoana kudu na bee keni mbe laŋ so ashi Jerusalɛm. Ama e kaŋ naŋ bɛta m ba na nɛ e shin nɛ b yɛr bumo n ya wɔtɔ laŋ pɔtɛ to nseŋ shin nɛ bekumpo bee keni bumo so. E daa sa bumo kusɔ kama nɛ k tir bumo ama mo alɛ nɛ bumo daa maŋ di keche nɛ kenyɛn. Bumo alɛ daŋ baa wɔ laŋ na to nna fanɛ bekulpoche hale n ya fo bumo luwu be jemanɛ.

english_verse: David said to Amasa, “Three days from now I want you and all of Judah's army to be here!”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura Deevid kaŋɛ Amasa le: “Tre Juda be benapo na kikɛ nɛ fo nɛ bumo e ba nfe nchɛ asa be kefɛato.”

english_verse: Amasa started bringing the army together, but it was taking him more than three days.
translation_verse: Nɛ Amasa fara a tre benapo na nseŋ nya bumo m ba ewura kutɔ nchɛ asa be kefɛato na.

english_verse: So David said to Abishai, “Sheba will hurt us more than Absalom ever did. Take my best soldiers and go after him. We don't want him to take over any walled cities and get away from us.” Joab Kills Amasa
translation_verse: Nɛ ewura na kaŋɛ Abishai le: “Bikri pibinyɛn Shɛba beeŋ tɔrɔ anyi a chɔ Absalɔm. Amoso, ya keta ma benapo lempo na n ju m bɛ mo so, nɛ e maaŋ nya ekpa n luri kade nɛ b pɔr egbal ŋ kulti na to ŋ ŋana anyi so.”

english_verse: Abishai left Jerusalem to try and capture Sheba. He took along Joab and his soldiers, as well as David's bodyguard and best troops.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Abishai keta Jɔab nɛ benapo lempo na kikɛ, nɛ ewura be bekumpo n lar Jerusalɛm a fin Shɛba a yɔ.

english_verse: They had gone as far as the big rock at Gibeon when Amasa caught up with them. Joab had a dagger strapped around his waist over his military uniform, but it fell out as he started toward Amasa.
translation_verse: B ka bee yɔ n ya fo Gibiɔn be kefalta gboŋ na ase nɛ Amasa ba tu bumo ndoŋ. Jɔab malɛ daŋ buu mbe anasɔ nna nɛ mbe kasaŋɛbi wɔ kumo be efar to a chɛ mbe kashɛr to a chul. E ka bee ba Amasa kutɔ, nɛ mbe kasaŋɛbi na lar kumo be efar to n tɔr.

english_verse: Joab said, “Amasa, my cousin, how are you?” Then Joab took hold of Amasa's beard with his right hand, so that he could greet him with a kiss.
translation_verse: Nɛ Jɔab kaŋɛ Amasa le: “Ŋkurgepo, alenfia wɔtɔ a?” Nɛ e ta enɔ jisa m pɛ mbe katɔl to m ber mo to kashaso.

english_verse: Amasa did not see the dagger in Joab's other hand. Joab stuck it in Amasa's stomach, and his insides spilled out on the ground. Joab only struck him once, but Amasa was dying. Joab and his brother Abishai went off to chase Sheba.
translation_verse: Ama Amasa malɛ daa maŋ nyi Jɔab ka keta kasaŋɛbi na mbe enɔ ko to. Ndoŋ nna nɛ Jɔab ta kasaŋɛbi na n da Amasa be epun hale nɛ mbe apumbi lar n tɔr kasawule nɛ e wu epul na to ndoŋ. Jɔab maŋ da mo kasaŋɛbi na ale anyɔ. Kumo be kaman nɛ Jɔab nɛ mo sipo Abishai bee ju Shɛba.

english_verse: One of Joab's soldiers stood by Amasa and shouted, “If any of you are for Joab and David, then follow Joab!”
translation_verse: Nɛ Jɔab be basa na be eko ba yili Amasa be kebuni na ase ŋ kaŋɛ awɔrso le: “Ekama nɛ e nyi fanɛ Jɔab nɛ Deevid nɛ e bɛso, kumo ere e bɛ Jɔab so!”

english_verse: Amasa was still rolling in his own blood in the middle of the road. The soldier who had shouted noticed that everyone who passed by would stop, so he dragged Amasa off the road and covered him with a blanket.
translation_verse: Nɛ Amasa dese ŋklaŋ to ekpa na be nferinto. Jɔab be esa na ka wu fanɛ ekama nɛ e bee choŋ beeŋ yili ŋ keni mo, nɛ e gbeye kebuni na ekpa na to n ya nase kupuŋ to nseŋ ta keta m buu kumo so.

english_verse: After this, no one else stopped. They all walked straight past him on their way to help Joab capture Sheba. Sheba Hides Out in the Town of Abel
translation_verse: B ka lɔŋɛ kebuni na ekpa na to n nase na so, benapo na maŋ naŋ ba ka shir a yili. B daŋ baa bɛ Jɔab so nna a shile a ju Shɛba.

english_verse: Sheba had gone through all of the tribes of Israel when he came to the town of Abel Beth-Maacah. All of his best soldiers met him there and followed him into the town.
translation_verse: Shɛba daŋ bɔla Israɛl be nnaŋ na kikɛ be efuli so nna n yɔ Abel Bɛf Maaka. Ndoŋ nna nɛ Bikri be kanaŋ to ebi na malɛ ba abar so m bɛ mo so n luri kade to.

english_verse: Joab and his troops came and surrounded Abel, so that no one could go in or come out. They made a dirt ramp up to the town wall and then started to use a battering ram to knock the wall down. A Wise Woman Saves the Town
translation_verse: Jɔab be basa na ka nu fanɛ Shɛba wɔ kade na to na nɛ b yɔ n ya kulti kumo n wɔtɔ nseŋ gbare shishɛr n deŋi abar so egbal na be kaman nɛ benapo na e ba bɔla amoso a luri kade na to nseŋ fara n ta ndibi gbɛgbɛso a da egbal na nɛ b futi kumo n luri.

english_verse: A wise woman shouted from the top of the wall, “Listen to me! Listen to me! I have to talk to Joab! Tell him to come here!”
translation_verse: Kache nyiashempo ko malɛ daa wɔ kade na to nseŋ yili egbal na so a wora awɔr a kaŋɛ le: “Keni nfe; Kaŋɛ Jɔab nɛ e ba nfe, ŋkpal manɛ so mee sha k malga mo kutɔ nna.”

english_verse: When he came, the woman said, “Are you Joab?” “Yes, I am,” he answered. She said, “Please, listen to what I have to say.” “All right,” he said. “I'll listen.”
translation_verse: Jɔab ka yɔ nɛ kache na bishi mo le: “Fo e la Jɔab na a?” Nɛ Jɔab yɛ: “Mm, ma nna.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ kache na kaŋɛ mo le: “Nu kusɔ nɛ mee kaŋɛ fo ere!” Nɛ mo alɛ yɛ: “Mee nu.”

english_verse: She said, “Long ago people used to say, ‘If you want good advice, go to the town of Abel to get it.’ The answers they got here were all that was needed to settle any problem.
translation_verse: Nɛ kache na kaŋɛ le: “Dra na, b daa kaŋɛ nna fanɛ nɛ fee sha k wu fo asheŋ be anishi kumo ere fo yɔ Abel, loŋ malɛ gbagba na e naa wora na.

english_verse: We are Israelites, and we want peace! You can trust us. Why are you trying to destroy a town that's like a mother in Israel? Why do you want to wipe out the Lord's people?”
translation_verse: Kadegboŋ nɛ kagbenewushi be kade e la anyi be kade ere ashi Israɛl kikɛ nɛ feeŋ tiŋ n yirda kumo be basa. Amoso manɛ e ba nɛ menyee sha k jija kade nɛ k du fanɛ enio ashi Israɛl, ŋko menyee sha nna nɛ meeŋ mur kusɔ nɛ k la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ peya?”

english_verse: Joab answered, “No, no! I'm not trying to wipe you out or destroy your town!
translation_verse: Nɛ Jɔab kaŋɛ le: “Kaarɛ gba! Maa ba nɛ m bure ŋko m mur kade ere kikɛ!

english_verse: That's not it at all. There's a man in your town from the hill country of Ephraim. His name is Sheba, and he is the leader of a rebellion against King David. Turn him over to me, and we will leave your town alone.” The woman told Joab, “We will throw his head over the wall.”
translation_verse: Ŋkpal manɛ so, anyi ere maŋ kɔ loŋ be nfɛra. Bikri pibinyɛn Shɛba nɛ e shi kebee so be kade ko nɛ k wɔ Efrayim na e nyaŋɛto a kɔ ewura Deevid. Fo baŋ tiŋ n nya mo n sa ma bre, kumo ere ma alɛ maaŋ naŋ wora menyi be kade na shɛŋ.” Nɛ kache na yɛ: “Anyi beeŋ ta mbe kumu ŋ kpa egbal na be kaman n sa menyi.”

english_verse: She went to the people of the town and talked them into doing it. They cut off Sheba's head and threw it to Joab. Joab blew a signal on his trumpet, and the soldiers returned to their homes. Joab went back to David in Jerusalem. Another List of David's Officials
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ e yɔ kade na be basa kutɔ nɛ mo nɛ bumo kre ŋkre nɛ b ku Shɛba be kumu n ta kumo ŋ kpa egbal na be kaman n sa Jɔab. Nɛ Jɔab foŋ kabel a ŋini fanɛ mbe benapo na e lar kade na to. Benapo na ka lar n choŋ epe nɛ Jɔab malɛ bɛta n yɔ ewura Deevid kutɔ ashi Jerusalɛm. Deevid be benimu be asheŋ

english_verse: Joab was the commander of Israel's entire army. Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was in command of David's bodyguard.
translation_verse: Jɔab e daa la Israɛl be benapo na kikɛ be enimu nɛ Jehowada pibinyɛn Bɛnaya malɛ daa la basa nɛ baa kuŋ Deevid na be enimu,

english_verse: Adoram was in charge of the slave-labor force. Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept government records.
translation_verse: Adoniram e daa la anya nɛ baa tintiŋ nɛ baa shuŋ na be enimu; Nɛ Ahilud pibinyɛn Jehoshafat malɛ daa la esa nɛ e bee sibɛ asheŋ a nase kawɔl to.

english_verse: Sheva was the secretary. Zadok and Abiathar were the priests.
translation_verse: Shiiva malɛ e daa la bumo be demujikpa be esibɛpo, Zadɔk nɛ Abiata e daa la bɔrɛmatapoana.

english_verse: The Gibeonites were not Israelites; they were descendants of the Amorites. The people of Israel had promised not to kill them, but Saul had tried to kill them because he wanted Israel and Judah to control all the land. David had the Gibeonites come, and he talked with them.
translation_verse: Gibiɔnebi na daa maŋ la Israɛlebi, b daa la Amɔriebi be katuŋ fimbi ko nna nɛ Israɛlebi na daŋ nase kɔnɔ n sa bumo fanɛ baŋ baa kuŋ bumo. Ama Sɔɔl daŋ wora ania nɛ e mur bumo nna ŋkpal e ka daa sha fanɛ Israɛlebi nɛ Judaebi e sɔ bumo be efuli na kikɛ so.

english_verse: He said, “What can I do to make up for what Saul did, so that you'll ask the Lord to be kind to his people again?”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Deevid tre Gibiɔnebi na ŋ kaŋɛ bumo le: “Manɛ nɛ menyee sha ŋ ka wora nɛ k wushi menyi kagbene ŋkpal kusɔ nɛ Sɔɔl wora na so, saŋɛ na so menyeeŋ kule Ebɔrɛ nɛ e wu anyi mbe basa kuwɔr?”

english_verse: They replied, “Saul tried to kill all our people so that none of us would be left in the land of Israel.
translation_verse: Nɛ b yɛ: “Sɔɔl daa sha kemur anyi kikɛ nna, saŋɛ na so anyi be ekama maaŋ naa wɔ Israɛl be efuli so.

english_verse: Give us seven of his descendants. We will hang these men near the place where the Lord is worshiped in Gibeah, the hometown of Saul, the Lord's chosen king.” “I'll give them to you,” David said.
translation_verse: Amoso, lara mbe kanaŋ to be benyɛn ashunu n sa anyi nɛ an ya chɛ bumo efɔl n shiga ashi Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be ewura laraso Sɔɔl be kade nɛ baa tre Gibia na be kakpa nɛ baa bunyaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.” Nɛ Deevid yɛ: “Meeŋ ta bumo n sa menyi.”

english_verse: David had made a promise to Jonathan with the Lord as his witness, so he spared Jonathan's son Mephibosheth, the grandson of Saul.
translation_verse: Ama ŋkpal kashenteŋ be kɔnɔ naseso nɛ Deevid nɛ Jonatan nase n sa abar na so Deevid daŋ yige Sɔɔl mo nanabi Mifiboshɛf nɛ e la Jonatan pibi na bre nna.

english_verse: turned them over to the Gibeonites, who hanged all seven of them on the mountain near the place where the Lord was worshiped. This happened right at the beginning of the barley harvest. Rizpah Takes Care of the Bodies
translation_verse: Bumo nɛ Deevid daŋ ta n sa Gibiɔnebi na nɛ b ya chɛ efɔl ashi kebee so be kakpa nɛ baa bunyaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nɛ bumo basa ashunu na kikɛ wu kachɛ koŋwule, saŋɛ so nɛ b baŋ fara a buri akoŋboyu na.

english_verse: Rizpah spread out some sackcloth on a nearby rock. She wouldn't let the birds land on the bodies during the day, and she kept the wild animals away at night. She stayed there from the beginning of the harvest until it started to rain. The Burial of Saul and His Descendants
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Sɔɔl mo jipo Rizpa buu kagbenejijaso be asɔbuuso nseŋ wora kekpata ashi kefalta nɛ bubuni na dese na so n chena ndoŋ saŋɛ nɛ b fara a buri akoŋboyu na n ya fo dɔchubɔrɛ be saŋɛ so. E daa ju mbuibi kapaso nna nsaa ju kupuŋ to be asɔbɔya malɛ kanyɛso ashi bubuni na to.

english_verse: Earlier the Philistines had killed Saul and Jonathan on Mount Gilboa and had hung their bodies in the town square at Beth-Shan. The people of Jabesh in Gilead had secretly taken the bodies away, but David found out what Saul's wife Rizpah had done, and he went to the leaders of Jabesh to get the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan.
translation_verse: nɛ e ya sɔ Sɔɔl nɛ mo pibi Jonatan be kebuni be awibi ashi Jabesh Giliad be basa na kutɔ. Filistiebi e daŋ mɔ Sɔɔl nɛ Jonatan ashi Gilbɔa be kebeegboŋ na ase saŋɛ nɛ bumo nɛ Israɛlebi daa kɔ kena na nseŋ ta bumo be eyurana n ya chɛ n shiga egbal nɛ b pɔr ŋ kulti Bɛfshan na be kowushina nɛ Jabesh Giliad be basa ya yuri bumo be eyurana na n yɔ bumo pe n ya chɔɔ.

english_verse: David had their bones taken to the land of Benjamin and buried in a side room in Saul's family burial place. Then he gave orders for the bones of the men who had been hanged to be buried there. It was done, and God answered prayers to bless the land. The Descendants of the Rephaim (
translation_verse: Sɔɔl mo tuto Kish be nchaŋ to ashi Zɛla nɛ k wɔ Bɛnjamin be kasawule so na nɛ b daŋ puli Sɔɔl nɛ Jonatan be awibi fanɛ kananɛ ewura Deevid kaŋɛ bumo fanɛ b wora na. Ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ Ebɔrɛ nu bumo be kabɔrɛkule nseŋ nɛfa bumo be kasawule nɛ akoŋ nɛ k daŋ tɔr na loge. B ka kɔ Filistiebi kena be asheŋ

english_verse: There was another war, this time in Gath. One of the enemy soldiers was a descendant of the Rephaim. He was as big as a giant and had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ kena ko malɛ naŋ koso ashi Gaaf. Kanyɛn gboŋgboŋi ko nɛ mo alɛ gba shi Rafa be kanaŋ to nsaa sha kolu ga na daa wɔ ndoŋ. Ashilbi ashe she nɛ anashibi ashe she nɛ e daa kɔ.

english_verse: One of the Philistine warriors was Ishbibenob, who was a descendant of the Rephaim, and he tried to kill David. Ishbibenob was armed with a new sword, and his bronze spearhead alone weighed about three and a half kilograms.
translation_verse: Kanyɛn gboŋgboŋi ko nɛ baa tre Ishbibenɔb nɛ e shi Rafa be kanaŋ to a kɔ danyaŋ be kekpa nɛ kumo be egbɛ daa sa fanɛ kilo asa, nɛ tokobi popɔr to na fɛ fanɛ e beeŋ tiŋ m mɔ Deevid.

english_verse: But Abishai came to the rescue and killed the Philistine. David's soldiers told him, “We can't let you risk your life in battle anymore! You give light to our nation, and we want that flame to keep burning.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Zeruwa pibinyɛn Abishai daŋ ba mɔlga Deevid nseŋ mɔ kanyɛn gboŋgboŋi na. Kumo be kaman nɛ Deevid be basa na shin nɛ Deevid nase kɔnɔ fanɛ e maaŋ naa tu bumo a yɔ kena to. Nseŋ kaŋɛ mo le: “Anyi maa sha kepaŋ fo, ŋkpal manɛ so fo nɛ Israɛlebi kikɛ bee fute a yige so.”

english_verse: There was still another battle with the Philistines at Gob. A soldier named Elhanan killed Goliath from Gath, whose spear shaft was like a weaver's beam. Elhanan's father was Jari from Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Kena ko gba daŋ naŋ koso bumo nɛ Filistiebi na be kefɛato ashi Gɔɔb. Kena na to nɛ Jair pibinyɛn Elhanan nɛ e shi Bɛtlɛhɛm na daŋ mɔ Goliɛf mo sipo Lami nɛ e la Giti be esa nɛ mbe kekpa be kedibi be bumburuŋ daa du fanɛ esa be keyapuye na.

english_verse: But when he made fun of Israel, David's nephew Jonathan killed him. Jonathan was the son of David's brother Shimei.
translation_verse: E daa tege Israɛlebi na nna, nɛ ewura Deevid mo da Shamaa pibinyɛn Jonatan malɛ mɔ mo.

english_verse: David and his soldiers killed these four men who were descendants of the Rephaim from Gath.
translation_verse: Le be basa ana gboŋgboŋi ere kikɛ daŋ shi Rafa be kanaŋ to nna ashi Gaaf nɛ Deevid nɛ mbe benapo mɔ bumo kikɛ.

english_verse: David sang a song to the Lord after the Lord had rescued him from his enemies, especially Saul. These are the words to David's song:
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ka mɔlga ewura Deevid ashi mo doŋana nɛ ewura Sɔɔl be enɔ to na, nɛ e boŋ kashɛ ere m maŋkura mo.

english_verse: I will praise you, Lord, and I will honor you among the nations.
translation_verse: Amoso meeŋ di fo epaŋ nɛ efuli kikɛ e nu, nseŋ boŋ kashɛ m maŋkura fo ketre.

english_verse: Our Lord and our God, you are my mighty rock, my fortress, my protector.
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e la ma kefalta nɛ n yil so. Mo e la ma ekumpo gboŋ nɛ emɔlgapo.

english_verse: I praise you, our Lord! I prayed to you, and you rescued me from my enemies.
translation_verse: N kule Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nɛ e mɔlga ma ashi ma doŋana be enɔ to. Kemaŋkura e baa la mo peya!

english_verse: Death, like ocean waves, surrounded me, and I was almost swallowed by its flooding waters.
translation_verse: Luwu kulti ma n wɔtɔ fanɛ nchu ka kpa esa ekwi na nna a shin nɛ k mur ma.

english_verse: Ropes from the world of the dead had coiled around me, and death had set a trap in my path.
translation_verse: Luwu kre ma fanɛ efɔl nna, nɛ nchaŋ malɛ sho ma kejigbelɛ.

english_verse: I was in terrible trouble when I called out to you, but from your temple you heard me and answered my prayer.
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nɛ n shu e tre ma etɔrɔsheŋ kikɛ to nɛ ma kushu tɔr mbe asoe to ashi mbe kuwurputi so ebɔrɛso nɛ e nu ma kushu nseŋ chɛ ma to.

english_verse: Earth shook and shivered! The columns supporting the sky rocked back and forth. You were angry
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ kasawule chicha nseŋ gbuŋgbuŋ to. Nɛ awɔlpa malɛ gba fara a filito nsaa gbuŋgbuŋ to, ŋkpal Ebɔrɛ ka nya agbo so!

english_verse: and breathed out smoke. Scorching heat and fiery flames spewed from your mouth.
translation_verse: Edishi daa lar mbe kamuna to nna nɛ ajanwulɛbi be edɛ shi mbe kɔnɔ to a chɔ wuloŋwuloŋ.

english_verse: You opened the heavens like curtains, and you came down with storm clouds under your feet.
translation_verse: E lar awɔlpa to ŋ gbelge to a ba nɛ kuwɔlpa lembir ko wɔ mbe aya ase.

english_verse: You rode on the backs of flying creatures. You appeared with the wind as wings.
translation_verse: E dii nna n chena emalaika nɛ b du fanɛ asɔ firgiso so nɛ b kɔ mo a firgi afu to.

english_verse: Darkness was your tent! Thunderclouds filled the sky, hiding you from sight.
translation_verse: Tentembiri daŋ buu mo so nna nɛ abɔrɛwɔlpa kulti mo n wɔtɔ.

english_verse: Lord Most High, your voice thundered from the heavens.
translation_verse: Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na shi awɔlpa to m ponte fanɛ bɔrɛ ka gbri na. Nɛ b nu mbe ebɔl.

english_verse: You roared at the sea, and its deepest channels could be seen. You snorted, and the earth shook to its foundations.
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ka ponte n fiɛ mo doŋana so agboso na nɛ teku feeto ŋ ka kasawule, nɛ kumo be gbaltɔlase dii efuli.

english_verse: You reached down from heaven, and you lifted me from deep in the ocean.
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ yili esoso n teŋi enɔ m pɛ ma ŋ gberge n lara nchu chiŋgeliŋ na to.

english_verse: On the day disaster struck, they came and attacked, but you defended me.
translation_verse: Saŋɛ nɛ asheŋ tu ma na, nɛ baa kɔ ma, ama Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kuŋ ma.

english_verse: When I was fenced in, you freed and rescued me because you love me.
translation_verse: B kulti ma n shɛrto nɛ e mɔlga ma nseŋ sɔ ma n yige, ŋkpal ŋ kaa bee wora asheŋ nɛ a bee par mo so.

english_verse: You are good to me, Lord, because I do right, and you reward me because I am innocent.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal ŋ ka bee wora asheŋ niŋiso so nɛ fo Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be alelasheŋ shi ga n sa ma na. Fo nɛfa wɔ ma so nna ŋkpal ŋ ka maŋ wora kulubi so.

english_verse: I do what you want and never turn to do evil.
translation_verse: Kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ bee sha nɛ mee wora. Maa ba nɛ n shile ma Ebɔrɛ n ya wora kulubi kikɛ.

english_verse: I keep your laws in mind and never turn away from your teachings.
translation_verse: N ta mbe mbra kikɛ n wɔtɔ ma kagbene to nna. Ma alɛ maŋ kplaŋ mbe keŋini so kikɛ.

english_verse: I obey you completely and guard against sin.
translation_verse: E nyi ŋ ka maŋ kɔ amoso kikɛ, nsaa gelge alubisheŋ kikɛ malɛ.

english_verse: You have been good to me because I do right; you have rewarded me for being innocent by your standards.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal ma alɛ ka bee wora kusɔ nɛ k walɛ so, e bee nɛfa ma nna. Mo alɛ nyi fanɛ m maŋ wora kulubi mbe anishito.

english_verse: You are always loyal to your loyal people, and you are faithful to the faithful.
