translation_verse: Zimri ka wu fanɛ b kɔ m pɔɔ kade na so, nɛ e ya luri ewura be laŋ na to be kumɔlga be kakpa lempo na to nseŋ wɔtɔ laŋ na edɛ nɛ k suse so n chɔɔ mo m mɔ.

english_verse: Zimri had disobeyed the Lord by following the evil example of Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Asheŋ ere kikɛ daŋ ba mo so nna ŋkpal e ka daŋ wora kulubi ŋ gbiti Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ fanɛ kananɛ ewura Jeroboam gba wora kulubi nseŋ shin nɛ Israɛl kikɛ wora kulubi na.

english_verse: Everything else Zimri did while he was king, including his rebellion against Elah, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Omri of Israel
translation_verse: B sibɛ kusɔ kama nɛ ewura Zimri daŋ wora nɛ kananɛ e kre Ela kulubi be asheŋ nna n wɔtɔ Israɛl be bewura be adrasheŋ be nwɔl to. Israɛl be ewura Omri be asheŋ

english_verse: After Zimri died, some of the Israelites wanted Tibni son of Ginath to be king, but others wanted Omri.
translation_verse: Ewura Zimri ka wu be kaman, nɛ Israɛlebi na barga to. Bumo be beko daa sha Ginaaf pibinyɛn Tibni ka ki ewura nna nɛ beko malɛ daa sha Omri ka ki ewura.

english_verse: in the thirty-first year of Asa's rule in Judah. Omri ruled Israel for twelve years. The first six years he ruled from Tirzah,
translation_verse: Juda be ewura Asa ka ji kuwura be kafɛ adesa nɛ kakosopo to nɛ Omri malɛ gba ki Israɛl be ewura nseŋ ji kuwura nfɛ kuduanyɔ. E daŋ ji kuwura Tiiza be kade to nfɛ ashe,

english_verse: He acted just like Jeroboam and made the Lord God of Israel angry by causing the Israelites to sin and to worship idols.
translation_verse: Kulubi nɛ ewura Jeroboam daŋ wora hale n shin nɛ Israɛlebi bee shuŋ agbir, nɛ Enyɛnpe nɛ e la Israɛl be Ebɔrɛ na be agbo kaa na, gbagba nɛ mo alɛ gba daŋ wora.

english_verse: Everything else Omri did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: B sibɛ kusɔ kama nɛ ewura Omri daŋ wora be asheŋ nna n wɔtɔ Israɛl be bewura be adrasheŋ be nwɔl to.

english_verse: Omri died and was buried in Samaria, and his son Ahab became king. King Ahab of Israel
translation_verse: Ewura Omri ka wu Samɛria nɛ b puli mo nɛ mo pibinyɛn Ahab sɔ mo so n ji kuwura. Israɛl be ewura Ahab be asheŋ

english_verse: Ahab son of Omri became king of Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Asa's rule in Judah, and he ruled
translation_verse: Ewura Asa ka ji kuwura ashi Juda be efuli so be kafɛ adesa nɛ aburwasopo be jemanɛ so nɛ ewura Omri malɛ pibinyɛn Ahab ki Israɛl be efuli so be ewura nseŋ ji kuwura Samɛria to nfɛ adunyɔ nɛ anyɔ.

english_verse: Ahab did more things to disobey the Lord than any king before him.
translation_verse: Mo alɛ gba daŋ wora alubi ŋ gbiti Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na a chɔ bewura kama nɛ b juŋkpar mo na kikɛ.

english_verse: and set up a sacred pole for worshiping the goddess Asherah. Ahab did more to make the Lord God of Israel angry than any king of Israel before him.
translation_verse: E daŋ pɔr kegbirche Ashira gba nna n yili, nseŋ wora asheŋ lubi damta ga a chɔ Israɛl be bewura na kikɛ, nɛ Enyɛnpe nɛ e la Israɛl be Ebɔrɛ na be agbo kaa ga.

english_verse: While Ahab was king, a man from Bethel named Hiel rebuilt the town of Jericho. But while Hiel was laying the foundation for the town wall, his oldest son Abiram died. And while he was finishing the gates, his youngest son Segub died. This happened just as the Lord had told Joshua to say many years ago.
translation_verse: Jemanɛ nɛ Ahab daa ji kuwura na, nɛ Heil nɛ e shi Bɛtɛl na lɔŋɛ m pɔr Jɛriko be kade na. Saŋɛ so nɛ Heil daa pɔr kade na be egbal na be gbaltɔlase, nɛ mbe wurkoŋnyɛn Abiram wu. E ka pɔr kumo be mbunagboŋ a loge na malɛ nɛ mbe kowurnyɛn Segɔb malɛ wu. Le be kesheŋ ere daŋ wora nna nɛ kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ daŋ bɔla Nun pibi Joshuwa so ŋ kaŋɛ dra dra na e bɔlɔ so.

english_verse: Elijah was a prophet from Tishbe in Gilead. One day he went to King Ahab and said, “I'm a servant of the living Lord, the God of Israel. And I swear in his name that it won't rain until I say so. There won't even be any dew on the ground.”
translation_verse: Anebi Elaija nɛ e shi Tishbe nɛ k wɔ Giliad be kasawule so na daŋ yɔ ewura Ahab kutɔ kachako nna n ya kaŋɛ mo le: “Enyɛnpe nɛ e la Israɛl be Ebɔrɛ nsaa wɔ ŋkpa to saŋkikɛ nɛ mee shuŋ na be ketre to nɛ mee kaŋɛ na fanɛ bɔrɛ ŋko bunyaŋ maaŋ tɔr n ya fo nfɛnyɔ ŋko nfɛ asa ama ma e baŋ kaŋɛ k ba pɔɛŋ nɛ k ba.”

english_verse: Later, the Lord said to Elijah,
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Elaija le:

english_verse: “Leave and go across the Jordan River so you can hide near Cherith Creek.
translation_verse: “Lar nfe n yɔ epeŋilarkpa be kaba so be kabombi nɛ baa tre Cheriff nɛ k wɔ Jɔɔdan be lɔr na be epeŋilarkpa na n ya ŋana.

english_verse: You can drink water from the creek, and eat the food I've told the ravens to bring you.”
translation_verse: Ŋ kaŋɛ emɔmɔ fanɛ b baa sa fo ajibi ndoŋ nɛ fo baa nuu kabombi na to be nchu malɛ.”

english_verse: Elijah obeyed the Lord and went to live near Cherith Creek.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ anebi Elaija wora Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kasonu, nseŋ ya kaa wɔ Cheriff be kabombi na ase.

english_verse: Ravens brought him bread and meat twice a day, and he drank water from the creek.
translation_verse: Kabombi na be nchu nɛ e daa nuu, nɛ emɔmɔ bee bar mo ajibi nɛ eblaŋ kachipurso nɛ kaaseso kikɛ.

english_verse: But after a while, it dried up because there was no rain. Elijah Helps a Widow in Zarephath
translation_verse: K maŋ chɛr ko nɛ kabombi na wɔlto cheche ŋkpal bɔrɛ ka maŋ naa ba so. Elaija nɛ Zarefaat be ekulpoche na be asheŋ

english_verse: “Go to the town of Zarephath in Sidon and live there. I've told a widow in that town to give you food.”
translation_verse: “Yɔ kade nɛ baa tre Zarefaat nɛ k mata Sidɔn be kade na n ya ka wɔ ndoŋ ŋkpal manɛ so ŋ kaŋɛ ekulpoche ko nɛ e wɔ ndoŋ fanɛ e baa sa fo ajibi.”

english_verse: When Elijah came near the town gate of Zarephath, he saw a widow gathering sticks for a fire. “Would you please bring me a cup of water?” he asked.
translation_verse: Anebi Elaija ka bee yɔ Zarefaat, n ya ka taga to kade na be kabunagboŋ na, nɛ e wu ekulpoche ko ka bee kil ndibi nɛ e kaŋɛ mo le: “Jande, sa ma nchu nɛ n nuu.”

english_verse: As she left to get it, he asked, “Would you also please bring me a piece of bread?”
translation_verse: Kache na ka bee yɔ nɛ e ya jɔ nchu na m ba, nɛ e naŋ kaŋɛ mo le: “Jande wora n fin ajibi gba n ti so a bar ma.”

english_verse: The widow answered, “In the name of the living Lord your God, I swear that I don't have any bread. All I have is a handful of flour and a little olive oil. I'm on my way home now with these few sticks to cook what I have for my son and me. After that, we will starve to death.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ kache na kaŋɛ le: “Enyɛnpe fo Ebɔrɛ na be ketre to, m maŋ kɔ ajibi kikɛ ma laŋ to. Kusɔ nɛ m baa kɔ kikɛ e la nyifu enɔ be bɔlɔ nɛ a wɔ cheenshi to nɛ ɔlif be ŋku gbrɛ. M ba nfe nna nɛ m ba kil ndibi n ya daŋɛ kusɔ kama nɛ ŋ kɔ, nɛ ma nɛ ma kebia e ji. Kumo e naaŋ baa la anyi be lalaloge be ajibi nɛ anyeeŋ ji nseŋ wu.”

english_verse: Elijah said, “Everything will be fine. Do what you said. Go home and fix something for you and your son. But first, please make a small piece of bread and bring it to me.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ anebi Elaija kaŋɛ le: “Sa maa fɔŋ, fo ere e yɔ n ya daŋɛ fo ajibi ama, pɔɛŋ nɛ fo daŋɛ amo na, ya daŋɛ fo ajibi nɛ fo kɔ na be gbrɛbi m bar ma pɔɛŋ, kumo be kaman nɛ fo daŋɛ amo nɛ a ka na nɛ fo nɛ fo kebia na e ji.

english_verse: The Lord God of Israel has promised that your jar of flour won't run out and your bottle of oil won't dry up before he sends rain for the crops.”
translation_verse: Ŋkpal manɛ so, kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Israɛl be Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ nde: ‘Nyifu maaŋ loge katishaŋ na to kikɛ ŋku malɛ gba maaŋ loge kɔlba na to kikɛ hale n ya fo kachɛ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ beeŋ shin nɛ bɔrɛ e ba.’ ”

english_verse: The widow went home and did exactly what Elijah had told her. She and Elijah and her family had enough food for a long time.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ekulpoche na ya wora kusɔ nɛ anebi Elaija kaŋɛ mo na gbagba chap, amoso mo nɛ mbe kebia na nɛ Elaija nya ajibi yɛlyɛla so a ji nchɛ damta.

english_verse: The Lord kept the promise that his prophet Elijah had made, and she did not run out of flour or oil. Elijah Brings a Boy Back to Life
translation_verse: Ŋkpal kɔnɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ daŋ bɔla anebi Elaija so n nase na so, nyifu nɛ a wɔ katishaŋ na to na daa maŋ loge nɛ ŋku nɛ a daa wɔ kɔlba na to na gba daa maŋ loge.

english_verse: Several days later, the son of the woman who owned the house got sick, and he kept getting worse, until finally he died.
translation_verse: K maŋ chɛr nɛ kulɔ pɛ ekulpoche na be kebia na, nɛ e wu.

english_verse: The woman shouted at Elijah, “What have I done to you? I thought you were God's prophet. Did you come here to cause the death of my son as a reminder that I've sinned against God?”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ekulpoche na kaŋɛ anebi Elaija le: “Ebɔrɛ be esa, manɛ nna nɛ fo wora ma le? Fo ba nfe nna nɛ fo ba kaŋɛ Ebɔrɛ alubi nɛ n wora saŋɛ na so ma kebia beeŋ wu a?”

english_verse: “Bring me your son,” Elijah said. Then he took the boy from her arms and carried him upstairs to the room where he was staying. Elijah laid the boy on his bed
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ anebi Elaija kaŋɛ mo le: “Ta kebia na m bar ma.” Nɛ e ta kebia na m ba sa Elaija nɛ Elaija ta mo n dii n yɔ kuchoŋi be esoso be ebu nɛ e wɔtɔ na to, n ya nase kakpa nɛ e bee dese na,

english_verse: and prayed, “Lord God, why did you do such a terrible thing to this woman? She's letting me stay here, and now you've let her son die.”
translation_verse: nseŋ kule Ebɔrɛ awɔrso le: “O Enyɛnpe nɛ fo la ma Ebɔrɛ, manɛ nna nɛ fo shin nɛ le be kagbenejija be kesheŋ ere nya ekulpoche ere? Kelela damta nɛ e wora ma ere kikɛ be kaman nɛ fo mɔ mo pibi a?”

english_verse: Elijah stretched himself out over the boy three times, while praying, “Lord God, bring this boy back to life!”
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ anebi Elaija teŋi to n dese kebia na so ale asa nseŋ kule Ebɔrɛ ŋ kaŋɛ le: “O Enyɛnpe nɛ ma Ebɔrɛ, jande shin nɛ kebia ere e bɛta m ba ŋkpa to.”

english_verse: The Lord answered Elijah's prayer, and the boy started breathing again.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nu anebi Elaija be kabɔrɛkule na nseŋ shin nɛ kebia na naŋ fara a fute.

english_verse: Elijah picked him up and carried him downstairs. He gave the boy to his mother and said, “Look, your son is alive.”
translation_verse: Nɛ anebi Elaija ta kebia na ŋ gbelge to m ba kuchoŋi na be kaseto m ba sa mo nio nseŋ kaŋɛ mo le: “Fo kebia na naŋ nya ŋkpa!”

english_verse: “You are God's prophet!” the woman replied. “Now I know that you really do speak for the Lord.”
translation_verse: Nɛ kache na kaŋɛ le: “Naniere nɛ m pin fanɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be esa e la fo kashenteŋto nɛ e bee bɔla fo so a malga!”

english_verse: For three years no rain fell in Samaria, and there was almost nothing to eat anywhere. The Lord said to Elijah, “Go and meet with King Ahab. I will soon make it rain.” So Elijah went to see Ahab.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Elaija pɛ ekpa n yɔ nɛ e ya wu ewura Ahab. Kumo be jemanɛ so nɛ akoŋgboŋ tɔr Samɛria be kade to,

english_verse: At that time Obadiah was in charge of Ahab's palace, but he faithfully worshiped the Lord. In fact, when Jezebel was trying to kill the Lord's prophets, Obadiah hid
translation_verse: amoso Jɛzebel ka daa mɔ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be anebiana na, Obadaya e daŋ ta bumo be basa kalfa n ya ŋana abeelaŋ anyɔ to nsaa sa bumo ajibi nɛ nchu ndoŋ. E daŋ barga bumo to basa adununu nna n wɔtɔ kebeelaŋ kama to.

english_verse: and said, “We have to find something for our horses and mules to eat. If we don't, we will have to kill them. Let's look around every creek and spring in the country for some grass.
translation_verse: Obadaya ka ba nɛ ewura Ahab kaŋɛ mo le: “Shin nɛ an yɔ efuli ere be abuye nɛ kumo be ataŋɛ kikɛ to n ya keni anyeeŋ nya afitiri ndoŋ nɛnɛ nɛ anyi be egbaŋɛ nɛ ekurma e baa ji a? Saŋɛ na so an maaŋ mɔ amo be kekama ŋkpal akoŋ so.”

english_verse: You go one way, and I'll go the other.” Then they left in separate directions.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ b lara kaba mo so nɛ bumo be ekama beeŋ bɔla, nɛ Ahab sɔ kaba ko nɛ Obadaya malɛ sɔ kuko.

english_verse: As Obadiah was walking along, he met Elijah. Obadiah recognized him, bowed down, and asked, “Elijah, is it really you?”
translation_verse: Obadaya ka bee yɔ nɛ e ya tu anebi Elaija ekpa to m pin mo, nseŋ jɔŋɛ m bunyaŋ mo m bishi mo le: “N nyɛnpe Elaija, fo nde a?”

english_verse: Obadiah replied: King Ahab would kill me if I told him that. And I haven't even done anything wrong.
translation_verse: Nɛ Obadaya kaŋɛ le: “Manɛ nɛ n wora fo nɛ fee sha keta ma n wɔtɔ asheŋ to nɛ Ewura Ahab e mɔ ma?

english_verse: I swear to you in the name of the living Lord your God that the king has looked everywhere for you. He sent people to look in every country, and when they couldn't find you, he made the leader of each country swear that you were not in that country.
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe fo Ebɔrɛ na be ketre so nɛ mee kaŋɛ fo na fanɛ ewura Ahab nite durnya ere be kaplɛkama a fin fo. Efuli kama malɛ nɛ b fin fo n yɔ, nɛ kumo be ewura kaŋɛ fanɛ e maŋ wu fo mbe efuli so, ewura Ahab bee shin nɛ e bɔ nna fanɛ e maŋ wu fo kashenteŋto.

english_verse: Do you really want me to tell him you're here?
translation_verse: Kashenteŋto, fee sha fanɛ n ya kaŋɛ n nyɛnpe fanɛ anebi Elaija wɔ nfe a?

english_verse: What if the Lord's Spirit takes you away as soon as I leave? When Ahab comes to get you, he won't find you. Then he will surely kill me. I have worshiped the Lord since I was a boy.
translation_verse: Ŋ kaŋ lar fo kutɔ, m maŋ nyi kakpa nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be kiyoyu beeŋ ta fo n yɔ. Ŋ kaŋ ya kaŋɛ Ahab fanɛ fo wɔ nfe, nɛ e maŋ wu fo nfe, e beeŋ mɔ ma. Baa nyiŋi fanɛ n fara a bunyaŋ Ebɔrɛ saŋɛ so nɛ n la kebifɔlbi kikɛ nna.

english_verse: Elijah said, “I'm a servant of the living Lord All-Powerful, and I swear in his name that I will meet with Ahab today.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ anebi Elaija kaŋɛ le: “Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ nɛ mee shuŋ ere be ketre to, meeŋ yɔ n ya wu ewura Ahab kabre.”

english_verse: Obadiah left and told Ahab where to find Elijah. Ahab went to meet Elijah,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Obadaya ya kaŋɛ ewura Ahab nɛ Ahab yɔ nɛ e ya tu anebi Elaija.

english_verse: and when he saw him, Ahab shouted, “There you are, the biggest troublemaker in Israel!”
translation_verse: Ewura Ahab ka wu Elaija nɛ e kaŋɛ mo le: “Fo e la Israɛl kikɛ be asheŋwura na ŋko?”

english_verse: Elijah answered: You're the troublemaker—not me! You and your family have disobeyed the Lord's commands by worshiping Baal.
translation_verse: Nɛ anebi Elaija malɛ kaŋɛ le: “M maŋ la esa nɛ mee ku asheŋ. Fo nɛ fo tuto e naa ku asheŋ, nseŋ kini kebaanu a sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nsaa shuŋ Baal be kegbir na.

english_verse: Ahab got everyone together, then they went to meet Elijah on Mount Carmel.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura Ahab kaŋɛ Israɛlebi na nɛ Baal be agbirwuraana na fanɛ b shɛr kebeegboŋ nɛ baa tre Kamɛl na ase.

english_verse: Elijah stood in front of them and said, “How much longer will you try to have things both ways? If the Lord is God, worship him! But if Baal is God, worship him!” The people did not say a word.
translation_verse: Nɛ anebi Elaija yɔ basa na kutɔ n ya kaŋɛ bumo le: “Nchɛ afanɛ nɛ men yɛ men ta n yili men be kagbene kukoŋwule? Nɛ Enyɛnpe na e la Ebɔrɛ, men baa shuŋ mo! Nɛ Baal malɛ e la Ebɔrɛ kumo ere men baa shuŋ mo alɛ gba!” Ama basa na daa maŋ tuge shɛŋ.

english_verse: Bring us two bulls. Baal's prophets can take one of them, kill it, and cut it into pieces. Then they can put the meat on the wood without lighting the fire. I will do the same thing with the other bull, and I won't light a fire under it either.
translation_verse: Men ta egbolu anyɔ m ba, nseŋ shin nɛ Baal be agbirwuraana e ta kukoŋwule m mɔ ŋ kuya to n deŋi ndibi so; ama b sa maŋ wɔtɔ ndibi na edɛ. Ma alɛ gba beeŋ ta gbolu nɛ k ka na n wora loŋ.

english_verse: The prophets of Baal will pray to their god, and I will pray to the Lord. The one who answers by starting the fire is God. “That's a good idea,” everyone agreed.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ fo shin nɛ Baal be agbirwuraana na e kule bumo be kegbir nɛ ma alɛ e kule Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na. Bumo be emo nɛ e beeŋ nu kekule n shin nɛ edɛ e ba na e la Ebɔrɛ.” Nɛ basa na cha awɔr fanɛ b wora loŋ.

english_verse: Elijah said to Baal's prophets, “There are more of you, so you go first. Pick out a bull and get it ready, but don't light the fire. Then pray to your god.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ anebi Elaija kaŋɛ Baal be agbirwuraana na le: “Menyi ere ka shibi ere, men juŋkpar n ta gbolu ko n wora loŋ, nseŋ kule menyi be kegbir na, ama men sa maŋ kaŋ wɔtɔ ndibi na to edɛ.”

english_verse: They chose their bull, then they got it ready and prayed to Baal all morning, asking him to start the fire. They danced around the altar and shouted, “Answer us, Baal!” But there was no answer.
translation_verse: Nɛ b mɔ gbolu nɛ b sa bumo na n wora kananɛ b ŋini na nseŋ yili chipurso ŋ kule bumo be kegbir Baal na hale n ya fo kapaso. Le nɛ b daa cha awɔr a kaŋɛ: “Baal, nu anyi be kekule!” B daa boŋ nshɛ nna a cha awɔr a cha a kulti bɔrɛsure nɛ b pɔr na ama b daa maŋ nu shɛŋ.

english_verse: At noon, Elijah began making fun of them. “Pray louder!” he said. “Baal must be a god. Maybe he's daydreaming or using the toilet or traveling somewhere. Or maybe he's asleep, and you have to wake him up.”
translation_verse: Kapa ka fo nɛ anebi Elaija fara a wora bumo eyurto a kaŋɛ le: “Men baa kule men be kegbir na awɔrso. E ka la kegbir so, ashere e bee di nna nsaa ku edare, ŋko e yɔ nna nɛ e ya jɔŋɛ, ŋko e yɔ kade nna, ŋko e di nna m mel nseŋ daga fanɛ men tiŋi mo na!”

english_verse: The prophets kept shouting louder and louder, and they cut themselves with swords and knives until they were bleeding. This was the way they worshiped,
translation_verse: Amoso agbirwuraana na daa kule awɔrso nna nseŋ ta nsaŋɛbi nɛ etokobi a ku bumo be eyurana daŋkare be ekpa so nɛ ŋklaŋ bee lar.

english_verse: and they kept it up until time for the evening sacrifice. But there was no answer of any kind.
translation_verse: B daa cha awɔr nna nsaa malga kawuliso be mmalga hale n ya fo kaaseso ama amo nɛ amo kikɛ b daa maŋ nu shɛŋ.

english_verse: Then he used twelve stones to build an altar in honor of the Lord. Each stone stood for one of the tribes of Israel, which was the name the Lord had given to their ancestor Jacob. Elijah dug a ditch around the altar, large enough to hold about
translation_verse: Loŋ be ajembu na nɛ e ta n lɔŋɛ m pɔr Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be bɔrɛsure nɛ baaŋ ba lara sarga kumo so a bunyaŋ mo na. E daŋ kur kaman nɛ k beeŋ tiŋ n sɔ nchu egalɔn asa nna ŋ kulti bɔrɛsure na.

english_verse: He placed the wood on the altar, then they cut the bull into pieces and laid the meat on the wood. He told the people, “Fill four large jars with water and pour it over the meat and the wood.” After they did this,
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e ta ndibi n deŋi bɔrɛsure na so nseŋ mɔ gbolu na ŋ kuya to n deŋi ndibi na so nseŋ kaŋɛ basa na le: “Men jɔ nchu m bɔlɔ mpuya gboŋgboŋi ana n chulgi n wurge sarga na nɛ ndibi na so.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ b wora loŋ.

english_verse: he told them to do it two more times. They did exactly as he said
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e naŋ kaŋɛ le: “Men naŋ laŋɛ n wora loŋ.” Nɛ b wora. Nɛ e naŋ kaŋɛ: “Men naŋ wora loŋ kela sasopo.” Nɛ b wora.

english_verse: until finally, the water ran down the altar and filled the ditch.
translation_verse: Nɛ nchu na shile m bɔlɔ kaman nɛ b kur ŋ kulti bɔrɛsure na.

english_verse: When it was time for the evening sacrifice, Elijah prayed: Our Lord, you are the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel. Now, prove that you are the God of this nation, and that I, your servant, have done this at your command.
translation_verse: Kaaseso be saŋɛ nɛ baaŋ lara sarga na ka fo, nɛ anebi Elaija yɔ bɔrɛsure na ase n ya kule Ebɔrɛ ŋ kaŋɛ le: “O Enyɛnpe, Eebraham nɛ Aizek nɛ Jeekɔb be Ebɔrɛ, shin nɛ basa ere e pin fanɛ fo e la Israɛl be Ebɔrɛ nɛ ma alɛ la fo kayɛrbi nsaa bɛ fo kɔnɔ so a wora asheŋ ere kikɛ.

english_verse: Please answer me, so these people will know that you are the Lord God, and that you will turn their hearts back to you.
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe, nu ma kekule, saŋɛ na so basa ere beeŋ pin fanɛ fo Enyɛnpe na e la ma Ebɔrɛ, saŋɛ na so baaŋ kilgi bumo be ŋgbene m bɛ fo so.”

english_verse: The Lord immediately sent fire, and it burned up the sacrifice, the wood, and the stones. It scorched the ground everywhere around the altar and dried up every drop of water in the ditch.
translation_verse: Epul na to nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ shin nɛ edɛ ba chɔ sarga na nɛ ndibi na nɛ ajembu na nɛ shishɛr na, nɛ nchu nɛ a wɔ kemaŋ nɛ b kur ŋ kulti sarga na kikɛ feeto kuraa.

english_verse: When the crowd saw what had happened, they all bowed down and shouted, “The Lord is God! The Lord is God!”
translation_verse: Basa na kikɛ ka wu loŋ, nɛ b jɔŋɛ kasawule nseŋ boŋto ŋ kaŋɛ le: “Enyɛnpe na nawule e la Ebɔrɛ! Enyɛnpe nawule e la Ebɔrɛ!”

english_verse: Just then, Elijah said, “Grab the prophets of Baal! Don't let any of them get away.” So the people captured the prophets and took them to Kishon River, where Elijah killed every one of them. It Starts To Rain
translation_verse: Nɛ Elaija ponte ŋ kaŋɛ le: “Men pɛ Baal be agbirwuraana na. Men sa maŋ shin nɛ bumo be ekama e shile!” Nɛ basa na pɛ bumo kikɛ n yɔ Kishɔn be lɔr na to nɛ anebi Elaija shin nɛ b mɔ bumo kikɛ ndoŋ.

english_verse: Elijah told Ahab, “Get something to eat and drink. I hear a heavy rain coming.”
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ anebi Elaija kaŋɛ ewura Ahab le: “Ya fin kusɔ ko n ji naniere bre, ŋkpal manɛ so n nu bɔrɛ ka bee gbri a ba.”

english_verse: Ahab left, but Elijah climbed back to the top of Mount Carmel. Then he stooped down with his face almost to the ground
translation_verse: Ahab ka yɔ nɛ e ya ji, nɛ Elaija dii kebeegboŋ nɛ baa tre Kamɛl na be esoso n ya murgi n ta kumu n wɔtɔ aya to ŋ kule Ebɔrɛ.

english_verse: and said to his servant, “Look toward the sea.” The servant left. And when he came back, he said, “I looked, but I didn't see anything.” Elijah told him to look seven more times.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e kaŋɛ mbe kayɛrbi le: “Lar n ya keni Teku be kaba so.” Mbe kayɛrbi na ka ya keni, nɛ e bɛta m ba kaŋɛ anebi Elaija fanɛ mo ere maŋ wu shɛŋ. Ela ashunu kikɛ nɛ Elaija daŋ kaŋɛ mo fanɛ e ya keni.

english_verse: After the seventh time the servant replied, “I see a small cloud coming this way. But it's no bigger than a fist.” Elijah told him, “Tell Ahab to get his chariot ready and start home now. Otherwise, the rain will stop him.”
translation_verse: E ka ya keni kela shunusopo na nɛ e bɛta m ba m ba kaŋɛ le: “N wu kuwɔlpa ko fanɛ enɔ be epunto be mpar ka shi Teku na be kaba so a ba.” Nɛ Elaija ponte ŋ kaŋɛ mbe kayɛrbi le: “Ya kaŋɛ ewura Ahab nɛ e wora manaŋ n luri mbe gbaŋɛturko to n yɔ epe pɔɛŋ nɛ bɔrɛ ere e kuŋ mo akpa.”

english_verse: A few minutes later, it got very cloudy and windy, and rain started pouring down. So Elijah wrapped his coat around himself, and the Lord gave him strength to run all the way to Jezreel. Ahab followed in his chariot.
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be kiyoyu gbelge anebi Elaija so nɛ e lɔŋɛ mbe epiŋi ŋ kre to nseŋ shile n ya choŋ Ahab so n yɔ Jizreel be kade to.

english_verse: She sent a message to Elijah: “You killed my prophets. Now I'm going to kill you! I pray that the gods will punish me even more severely if I don't do it by this time tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Jɛzebel shuŋi fanɛ b ya kaŋɛ Elaija kubɔya ere. E yɛ: “Ta a ba echefo saŋɛ ere so nɛ ŋ ka maŋ wora fo kusɔ nɛ fo wora agbirwuraana ere gbagba n tal to, kumo ere agbir na e mɔ ma.”

english_verse: Elijah was afraid when he got her message, and he ran to the town of Beersheba in Judah. He left his servant there,
translation_verse: Anebi Elaija ka nu loŋ nɛ kufu pɛ mo nɛ e shile a mɔlga mbe kumu. E daŋ keta mbe kayɛrbi nna n yɔ Bɛshiba nɛ k wɔ Juda be efuli so be kelargato be kaseto na n ya yige mo ndoŋ.

english_verse: then walked another whole day into the desert. Finally, he came to a large bush and sat down in its shade. He begged the Lord, “I've had enough. Just let me die! I'm no better off than my ancestors.”
translation_verse: Anebi Elaija be kachɛ lelemu nɛ e na kiyi to. Ndoŋ nna nɛ e ba tu kedibi ko n chena kumo be kifito nseŋ fɛ fanɛ e daŋ wu gba k bɔ mo so. Kumo be kaman nɛ e kule Ebɔrɛ ŋ kaŋɛ le: “Enyɛnpe, asheŋ ere bre chɔ ma so. Lara ma ŋkpa, ŋkpal manɛ so n chɛr a beeŋ wu nna!”

english_verse: Then he lay down in the shade and fell asleep. Suddenly an angel woke him up and said, “Get up and eat.”
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e dese kedibi na be kifito a di. Epul to nɛ Ebɔrɛ be malaika ba tiŋi mo ŋ kaŋɛ le: “Koso n ji ajibi.”

english_verse: Elijah looked around, and by his head was a jar of water and some baked bread. He sat up, ate and drank, then lay down and went back to sleep.
translation_verse: E ka koso ŋ gbɛ ŋ keni nɛ e wu bodobodo nɛ nchu ka wɔ kusɔ to a yil mbe kumu ase, nɛ e ji amo nseŋ naŋ laŋɛ n dese.

english_verse: So Elijah sat up and ate and drank. The food and water made him strong enough to walk
translation_verse: Nɛ anebi Elaija koso n ji nseŋ nuu nchu nɛ ajibi na sa mo eleŋ nɛ e nite nchɛ adena kikɛ hale n yɔ kebee cheembi nɛ baa tre Sainai na.

english_verse: and he spent the night there in a cave. The Lord Appears to Elijah While Elijah was on Mount Sinai, the Lord asked, “Elijah, why are you here?”
translation_verse: Kumo be kanyɛso nɛ e yɔ kebeelaŋ to n ya dese a di. Ndoŋ nɛ e wɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na bishi mo le: “Elaija manɛ nɛ fee wora nfe?”

english_verse: He answered, “Lord God All-Powerful, I've always done my best to obey you. But your people have broken their solemn promise to you. They have torn down your altars and killed all your prophets, except me. And now they are even trying to kill me!”
translation_verse: Nɛ Elaija kaŋɛ le: “Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ, fo nawule nɛ mee shuŋ saŋkikɛ. Ama Israɛlebi na bre ku kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre nɛ fo nɛ bumo kɔ na to nna nseŋ da fo bɔrɛsureana n lɛ, m mɔ fo anebiana kikɛ. Naniere n nawule e ka nɛ baa sha kemɔ ma alɛ gba.”

english_verse: “Go out and stand on the mountain,” the Lord replied. “I want you to be there when I pass by.” All at once, a strong wind shook the mountain and shattered the rocks. But the Lord was not in the wind. Next, there was an earthquake, but the Lord was not in the earthquake.
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ mo le: “Lar n ya yili kebee na be esoso a jo ma, meeŋ ba choŋ.” Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ shin nɛ afu lempo ko ba ber kebee na nseŋ bu kumo n lɛ m bure afalta nɛ a wɔ ndoŋ na to, ama Enyɛnpe na daa maŋ wɔ afu na to. Afu na ka yige nɛ kasawule be kegbuŋgbuŋ malɛ bɛ so ama Enyɛnpe na daa maŋ wɔ kumo alɛ gba to.

english_verse: Then there was a fire, but the Lord was not in the fire. Finally, there was a gentle breeze,
translation_verse: Kasawule be kegbuŋgbuŋ na ka ba choŋ nɛ edɛ malɛ bɛ so ama Enyɛnpe na daa maŋ wɔ edɛ na gba to. Edɛ na ka ba choŋ, nɛ ebɔl fimbi ko kuli mmalga.

english_verse: and when Elijah heard it, he covered his face with his coat. He went out and stood at the entrance to the cave. A voice asked, “Elijah, why are you here?”
translation_verse: Anebi Elaija ka nu loŋ be ebɔl na nɛ e ta mbe piŋi m buu mbe anishi so nseŋ lar kebeelaŋ na to n ya yili kumo be kabuna to. Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ naŋ bishi mo le: “Elaija manɛ nɛ fee wora nfe?”

english_verse: Elijah answered, “Lord God All-Powerful, I've always done my best to obey you. But your people have broken their solemn promise to you. They have torn down your altars and killed all your prophets, except me. And now they are even trying to kill me!”
translation_verse: Nɛ Elaija naŋ kaŋɛ le: “Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ, fo nawule nɛ mee shuŋ saŋkikɛ. Ama Israɛlebi na bre ku kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre nɛ fo nɛ bumo kɔ na to nna nseŋ da fo ebɔrɛsureana n lɛ m mɔ fo anebiana kikɛ. Naniere n nawule e ka nɛ baa sha kemɔ ma alɛ gba.”

english_verse: The Lord said: Elijah, you can go back to the desert near Damascus. And when you get there, appoint Hazael to be king of Syria.
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ mo le, “Bɛta n yɔ kiyi nɛ k mata Damaskɔs be kade to na. Fo kaŋ fo ndoŋ nɛ fo ya fin kanyɛn ko nɛ baa tre Haziɛl na nseŋ chulgi ŋku n wurge mbe kumu so m buu mo Siriya be efuli so be kuwura.

english_verse: Elijah left and found Elisha plowing a field with a pair of oxen. There were eleven other men in front of him, and each one was also plowing with a pair of oxen. Elijah went over and put his own coat on Elisha.
translation_verse: Anebi Elaija ka lar a yɔ nɛ e ya tu Shafat pibinyɛn Elaisha nɛ e kɔ ana dɔso a dɔ: Ana dɔso nɛ b chɛ m mata abar benyɔnyɔ kudukako e daŋ juŋkpar mo a dɔ. Nɛ mo alɛ keta katuŋ kuduanyɔsopo na a bɛ so. Ndoŋ nna nɛ anebi Elaija lara mbe piŋi n deŋi Elaisha so.

english_verse: Elisha stopped plowing and ran after him. “Let me kiss my parents goodbye, then I'll go with you,” he said. “You can go,” Elijah said. “But remember what I've done for you.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Elaisha yige mbe ana dɔso na nseŋ shile m bɛ anebi Elaija so ŋ kaŋɛ mo le: “Shin nɛ n ya kela n tuto nɛ n nio pɔɛŋ nseŋ ba bɛ fo so.” Nɛ Elaija kaŋɛ mo le: “Baa yɔ, ama sa maŋ kaŋ teŋ so kusɔ nɛ n wora fo ere so.”

english_verse: Elisha left and took his oxen with him. He killed them and boiled them over a fire he had made with the wood from his plow. He gave the meat to the people who were with him, and they ate it. Then he left with Elijah and became his assistant.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Elaisha ya mɔ mbe ana dɔso na nseŋ ta amo be abɔto be ndibi na m puga edɛ n daŋɛ amo be eblaŋ na n ta n sa basa na nɛ b we. Kumo be kaman nɛ e ya bɛ anebi Elaija so a chɛ mo to.

english_verse: They dressed in sackcloth and put ropes on their heads, then they went to Ahab and said, “Your servant Benhadad asks you to let him live.” “Is he still alive?” Ahab asked. “Benhadad is like a brother to me.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ b ta kagbenejijaso be asɔbuuso n dela bumo be nshɛr to nseŋ ta efɔl n chɛ bumo be abɔto kagbenejijaso n yɔ ewura Ahab kutɔ n ya kaŋɛ mo le: “Fo kayɛrbi Bɛnhadad bee kule fo nna fanɛ fo sa maŋ mɔ mo.” Nɛ ewura Ahab malɛ kaŋɛ le: “Bɛnhadad kraa wɔ ŋkpa to a? Kashenteŋto e du fanɛ n niopibi nna!”

english_verse: But tomorrow at this time, I will send my officials into your city to search your palace and the houses of your officials. They will take everything else that you own.”
translation_verse: Echefo saŋɛ ere so meeŋ shuŋi ma benimu fo laŋ to nɛ fo benimuana be elaŋ to nɛ b ba keni n fin asɔ kama nɛ a walɛ na nseŋ ta amo kikɛ.”

english_verse: “Don't listen to him!” they answered. “You don't have to do what he says.”
translation_verse: Nɛ bejuŋkparpo na kikɛ kaŋɛ le: “Sa maŋ tuge mo.”

english_verse: So Ahab sent someone to tell Benhadad, “Your Majesty, I'll give you my silver and gold, and even my wives and children. But I won't let you have anything else.” When Benhadad got his answer,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ahab kaŋɛ mbɔ na fanɛ b ya kaŋɛ Bɛnhadad le: “Men ya kaŋɛ ewura na fanɛ n shuli sososo be kusɔ nɛ e kaŋɛ na ama kenyɔsopo ere bre, m maaŋ shuli kumo.” Mbɔ na ka yɔ nɛ ewura Bɛnhadad naŋ ta kubɔya popɔr n sa bumo.

english_verse: he replied, “I'll completely destroy Samaria! There won't even be enough of it left for my soldiers to carry back in their hands. If I don't do it, I pray that the gods will punish me terribly.”
translation_verse: E yɛ: “Meeŋ shin nɛ benapo e ba jija fo kade ere nɛ shɛŋ shɛŋ maaŋ naŋ ka ndoŋ. Nɛ ŋ kaa maŋ wora loŋ, kumo ere agbir nɛ mee shuŋ ere e mɔ ma!”

english_verse: Ahab then answered, “Benhadad, don't brag before the fighting even begins. Wait and see if you live through it.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura Ahab kaŋɛ le: “Men ya kaŋɛ ewura Bɛnhadad fanɛ enapo kashenteŋ bre bee ji njɔŋ saŋɛ so nɛ b kɔ kena n loge nna, mannɛ saŋɛ nɛ b kraa yɔ kena to.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, Benhadad and the other kings had been drinking in their tents. But when Ahab's reply came, he ordered his soldiers to prepare to attack Samaria, and they all got ready.
translation_verse: Saŋɛ so nɛ ewura Bɛnhadad nɛ bewura nɛ baa chɛ mo to na nɛ bejuŋkparpoana na wɔ bumo be ewajɛbu to a nuu bumo be nsa na be jemanɛ so nɛ ewura Ahab be kubɔya na tu mo. E daŋ kaŋɛ mbe benapo nna fanɛ b koso n ya kɔ kade na, nɛ bumo kikɛ wora shiriya nɛ b ya kɔ kumo.

english_verse: At that very moment, a prophet ran up to Ahab and said, “You can see that Benhadad's army is very strong. But the Lord has promised to help you defeat them today. Then you will know that the Lord is in control.”
translation_verse: Loŋ be jemanɛ nɛ anebi ko yɔ ewura Ahab kutɔ n ya kaŋɛ mo le: Enyɛnpe yɛ: “Men sa maa lɔ kufu ŋkpal benapo damta nɛ b kɔ ere so. Meeŋ shin nɛ men kɔ m pɔɔ bumo so, saŋɛ na so menyeeŋ pin fanɛ ma e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kashenteŋto!”

english_verse: “Who will fight the battle?” Ahab asked. The prophet answered, “The young bodyguards who serve the district officials.” “But who will lead them into battle?” Ahab asked. “You will!” the prophet replied.
translation_verse: Nɛ ewura Ahab bishi le: “Bumo e naaŋ kɔ n sa anyi?” Nɛ anebi na kaŋɛ le: “Enyɛnpe na yɛ mbrantiɛbia nɛ b la mbonfu mbonfu be egomena be benapo na e naaŋ wora loŋ.” Nɛ ewura Ahab naŋ bishi le: “Nɛ wanɛ e naaŋ juŋkpar bumo kena na to?” Nɛ anebi na kaŋɛ le: “Fo e naa shin nɛ fo juŋkpar bumo.”

english_verse: At noon, King Ahab and his Israelite army marched out of Samaria, with the young soldiers in front. King Benhadad of Syria and the
translation_verse: Benapo fɔlbi nɛ b shi mbonfu mbonfu na daŋ juŋkpar n lar. Ndoŋ nna Bɛnhadad be benapo nɛ baa ŋana a dara asheŋ na ba kaŋɛ mo fanɛ benapo be katuŋ ko shi Samɛria a ba nɛ b ba kɔ bumo kena.

translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ anebi na kaŋɛ mo le: “Ŋkpal fo ka kini kebɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be kɔnɔ so so, fo baŋ lar ŋ kutɔ nfe, buluŋ beeŋ mɔ fo.” E ka lar malɛ, epul na to nɛ buluŋ mɔ mo.

english_verse: The prophet found someone else and said, “Hit me!” So this man beat him up.
translation_verse: Nɛ loŋ be anebi koŋwule na naŋ ya tu esa ko nseŋ kaŋɛ mo le: “Ŋmɛa ma!” Nɛ kanyɛn na ŋmɛa mo ga hale nɛ e doro.

english_verse: The prophet left and put a bandage over his face to disguise himself. Then he went and stood beside the road, waiting for Ahab to pass by.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ anebi nɛ b ŋmɛa na ta kechɛbi m buu anishi so saŋɛ na so b maaŋ pin mo. Kumo be kaman nɛ e ya yili kubɔrbi so a jo Israɛl be ewura.

english_verse: When Ahab went by, the prophet shouted, “Your Majesty, right in the heat of battle, someone brought a prisoner to me and told me to guard him. He said if the prisoner got away, I would either be killed or forced to pay
translation_verse: Ewura na ka bee choŋ nɛ anebi na boŋ to n tre mo nseŋ kaŋɛ mo le: “Yiramu! Kena nɛ anyee kɔ nɛ enapo ko keta edompo ko ka shile kena m ba ŋ kutɔ m ba kaŋɛ le: ‘Baa keni kanyɛn ere so, nɛ fo baŋ yige nɛ e shile, feeŋ paŋ fo ŋkpa, ŋko ŋ ka gbiti be ndarbi ŋgboŋ asa.

english_verse: But I got busy doing other things, and the prisoner escaped.” Ahab answered, “You will be punished just as you have said.”
translation_verse: Ama ŋkpal ma kenishi ka daŋ pere ashuŋana ko so so, nɛ kanyɛn na daŋ nya ekpa n shile.’ ” Nɛ ewura Ahab na kaŋɛ le: “Fo ji fo gbagba be kumu demu nna na, feeŋ nya kumo be kasogberge.”

english_verse: The man quickly tore the bandage off his face, and Ahab saw that he was one of the prophets.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ anebi na bugi kechɛbi nɛ k buu mbe anishi so na, nɛ ewura na pin epul na to fanɛ anebiana na be eko e la mo.

english_verse: The prophet said, “The Lord told you to kill Benhadad, but you let him go. Now you will die in his place, and your people will die in place of his people.”
translation_verse: Nɛ anebi na kaŋɛ ewura na fanɛ Enyɛnpe na yɛ: “Ŋkpal ŋ ka kaŋɛ fo fanɛ fo mɔ ewura Bɛnhadad nɛ fo shin nɛ e shile so, fo alɛ gba beeŋ paŋ fo ŋkpa nɛ fo benapo malɛ kikɛ e wu ŋkpal bumo alɛ gba ka shin nɛ mbe basa shile ŋ ŋana so.”

english_verse: Ahab went back to Samaria, angry and depressed.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura Ahab ta agbo kagbenejija m bɛta n yɔ Samɛria.

english_verse: One day, Ahab said, “Naboth, your vineyard is near my palace. Give it to me so I can turn it into a vegetable garden. I'll give you a better vineyard or pay whatever you want for yours.”
translation_verse: Kachako nɛ ewura Ahab ya kaŋɛ Nabɔf le: “Ta fo asɔrso nɛ baa tre greep na be kudɔ nɛ k mata ma laŋ na n sa ma nɛ n dɔ epofantaŋ be kudɔ. Meeŋ sa fo asɔrso nɛ baa tre greep na be kudɔ lela n tal to. Nɛ fee sha malɛ, meeŋ ka fo kanaŋkama nɛ feeŋ fa kumo n sa ma.”

english_verse: Naboth answered, “This vineyard has always been in my family. I won't let you have it.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Nabɔf kaŋɛ ewura na le: “N nananyɛnana kutɔ nɛ n ji asɔrso be kudɔ ere be kapetɛ, amoso Ebɔrɛ e baa pete ma gba nɛ n ta kumo n sa fo!”

english_verse: So Ahab went home, angry and depressed because of what Naboth had told him. He lay on his bed, just staring at the wall and refusing to eat a thing.
translation_verse: Nɛ ewura Ahab nya agbo m bɛta n yɔ epe nɛ kagbenejija ŋkpal kusɔ nɛ Nabɔf kaŋɛ mo na so. E ka ba epe nɛ e ba dese ŋ kilgi mbe anishito n shoŋi egbal nseŋ kini keji ajibi.

english_verse: Jezebel his wife came in and asked, “What's wrong? Why won't you eat?”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ mbe eche Jɛzebel ya bishi mo le: “Manɛ nna nɛ fo kagbene jija fo loŋ hale nɛ fo kini keji ajibi?”

english_verse: “I asked Naboth to sell me his vineyard or to let me give him a better one,” Ahab replied. “And he told me I couldn't have it.”
translation_verse: Nɛ e yɛ: “Ŋkpal ŋ ka kaŋɛ Nabɔf fanɛ e fa mbe asɔrso be kudɔ n sa ma ŋko e shin nɛ n ta kuko n chɛr mo kumo, nɛ e kaŋɛ ma fanɛ e maaŋ sa ma kumo na so!”

english_verse: They told the people that it was a day to go without eating, and when they all came together, they seated Naboth at the front.
translation_verse: B daŋ lara kachɛ koŋwule nna m ber kebomboŋ n tre basa kikɛ n shɛr ŋ kishi, nseŋ shin nɛ Nabɔf chena kemaŋkura be echenakpa nshɛr na to.

english_verse: The two liars came in and sat across from Naboth. Then they accused him of cursing God and the king, so the people dragged Naboth outside and stoned him to death.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ befɛpo anyɔ ko lar n yili Nabɔf be anishito ŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ e sho Ebɔrɛ nɛ ewura na kɔnɔ. Ŋkpal loŋ so nɛ b gberge mo n lar kade na be ekarso n ya kpla mo ajembu m mɔ.

english_verse: The leaders of Jezreel sent a message back to Jezebel that said, “Naboth is dead.”
translation_verse: B ka mɔ mo n loge nɛ b ta le be kubɔya n ya sa Jɛzebel: “An kpla Nabɔf na ajembu m mɔ.”

english_verse: As soon as Jezebel got their message, she told Ahab, “Now you can have the vineyard Naboth refused to sell. He's dead.”
translation_verse: Jɛzebel ka baŋ nu loŋ, epul to nɛ e ya kaŋɛ ewura Ahab le: “Nabɔf wu, amoso naniere bre feeŋ tiŋ n ya ta mbe asɔrso nɛ baa tre greep be kudɔ nɛ e kini kefa n sa fo na ŋ ki feya.”

translation_verse: Ewura Ahab ka nu loŋ, epul to nɛ e koso n yɔ nɛ e ya sɔ kudɔ na.

english_verse: Ahab said, “So, my enemy, you found me at last.” Elijah answered: Yes, I did! Ahab, you have managed to do everything the Lord hates.
translation_verse: Ewura Ahab ka wu Elaija nɛ e kaŋɛ le: “Ma doŋ, fo wu ma a?” Nɛ anebi Elaija malɛ kaŋɛ le: “Mm, n wu fo. Fo kebaawɔtɔ to kikɛ fee wora alubi nna a gbiti Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.

english_verse: Now you will be punished. You and every man and boy in your family will die, whether slave or free.
translation_verse: Amoso Enyɛnpe na yɛ: ‘Meeŋ shin nɛ fo ji jɛrbi. Meeŋ mur fo nseŋ mur fo kanaŋ to be benimu nɛ mbia kama nɛ b la benyɛn na kikɛ.

english_verse: Your whole family will be wiped out, just like the families of King Jeroboam and King Baasha. You've made the Lord very angry by sinning and causing the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Kananɛ n wora Nebat pibinyɛn ewura Jeroboam nɛ Ahija pibinyɛn ewura Baasha na, nɛ mee shin nɛ n wora fo alɛ gba, ŋkpal fo ka wɔtɔ ma agbo to nseŋ shin nɛ ma basa Israɛlebi luri kulubi to so.’

english_verse: And as for Jezebel, dogs will eat her body there in Jezreel.
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na yɛ Jɛzebel bre, njɔnɔ e naaŋ ji mbe eyur ashi Jizreel be kade ere to.

english_verse: Dogs will also eat the bodies of your relatives who die in town, and vultures will eat the bodies of those who die in the country.
translation_verse: Njɔnɔ malɛ gba e naaŋ ji fo kurgepo kama nɛ e wu kade na to nɛ ejita malɛ e ji fo kurgepoana kama nɛ b wu kupuŋ to.”

english_verse: Ahab asked his officials, “Why haven't we tried to get Ramoth in Gilead back from the Syrians? It belongs to us.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ahab kaŋɛ mbe benimuana le: “Manɛ nna nɛ anyi maaŋ wora ania ŋ kɔ n sɔ Ramɔf nɛ k wɔ Giliad na ashi Siriya be ewura na be enɔ to? Efuli na la anyi peya nna!”

english_verse: Then he asked Jehoshaphat, “Would you go to Ramoth with me and attack the Syrians?” “Just tell me what to do,” Jehoshaphat answered. “My army and horses are at your command.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ ewura Ahab bishi ewura Jehoshafat le: “Feeŋ tu ma n ya kɔ Ramɔfebi kena a?” Nɛ ewura Jehoshafat kaŋɛ: “Saŋkama nɛ fo wora shiriya ma alɛ gba wora shiriya nɛ ma benapo nɛ benapo nɛ baa dii egbaŋɛ a kɔ na kikɛ gba wora shiriya. Anyeeŋ tu fo n yɔ.”

english_verse: But Jehoshaphat said, “Just to make sure, is there another of the Lord's prophets we can ask?”
translation_verse: Nɛ ewura Jehoshafat naŋ bishi: “Ama anebi kama maŋ naa wɔtɔ nɛ an ya sɔ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be nfɛra mo kutɔ n ti so a?”

english_verse: “We could ask Micaiah son of Imlah,” Ahab said. “But I hate Micaiah. He always has bad news for me.” “Don't say that!” Jehoshaphat replied.
translation_verse: Nɛ ewura Ahab kaŋɛ le: “Ekoŋwule ko kraa wɔtɔ nɛ anyeeŋ tiŋ n wu mo, mo e la Imla pibinyɛn Mikaya ama ŋ kishi mbe asheŋ ga ŋkpal manɛ so kusɔ kama nɛ e wu ŋ kaŋɛ ma maa walɛ.” Nɛ Jehoshafat kaŋɛ: “Sa maŋ kaŋ kaŋɛ loŋ!”

english_verse: All this time, Ahab and Jehoshaphat were dressed in their royal robes and were seated on their thrones at the threshing place near the gate of Samaria. They were listening to the prophets tell them what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Bewura anyɔ na daŋ buu bumo be ewurpiŋi nna a tase bumo be nwurputi so ashi kugooro bri asɔ nɛ k wɔ Samɛria be kabunagboŋ na be ekarso na so, nɛ anebiana na kikɛ yil bumo be anishito a kaŋɛ kusɔ nɛ Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ.

english_verse: Zedekiah son of Chenaanah was one of the prophets. He had made some horns out of iron and shouted, “Ahab, the Lord says you will attack the Syrians like a bull with iron horns and wipe them out!”
translation_verse: Chinana pibinyɛn Zɛdikaya nɛ e la anebiana be eko bre daŋ bɛl abɛlso be alambɛ nna nseŋ kaŋɛ ewura Ahab le: “Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ yɛ, le be kusɔ ere nɛ feeŋ ta ŋ kɔ Siriyaebi na kena m pɔɔ bumo so cheche.”

english_verse: All the prophets agreed that Ahab should attack the Syrians at Ramoth, and they promised that the Lord would help him defeat them.
translation_verse: Anebiana na kikɛ daŋ kaŋɛ le nna: “Men ya kɔ Ramɔfebi. Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na beeŋ shin nɛ men kɔ m pɔɔ so.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, the messenger who went to get Micaiah whispered, “Micaiah, all the prophets have good news for Ahab. Now go and say the same thing.”
translation_verse: Esa nɛ e daŋ yɔ Mikaya kutɔ na daŋ ya kaŋɛ mo nna le: “Anebiana na kikɛ daŋ wu ŋ kaŋɛ nna fanɛ ewura na beeŋ kɔ m pɔɔ so, amoso fo alɛ gba e ya kaŋɛ loŋ.”

english_verse: “I'll say whatever the living Lord tells me to say,” Micaiah replied.
translation_verse: Ama le nɛ anebi Mikaya daŋ kaŋɛ: “Kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ e wɔ ŋkpa to na kaŋɛ ma nɛ meeŋ kaŋɛ!”

english_verse: He answered, “In a vision I saw Israelite soldiers walking around in the hills like sheep without a shepherd to guide them. The Lord said, ‘This army has no leader. They should go home and not fight.’ ”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ anebi Mikaya naŋ kaŋɛ le: “N wu Israɛl be benapo na ka pesaŋ to n sɔ abee so fanɛ mbolpɔ nɛ b maŋ kɔ ekpapo na. Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ le: ‘Basa ere maŋ kɔ ejuŋkparpo, shin nɛ b ta kagbenewushi a yɔ epe.’ ”

english_verse: Micaiah replied: Listen to this! I also saw the Lord seated on his throne with every creature in heaven gathered around him.
translation_verse: Nɛ anebi Mikaya kraa malga nseŋ kaŋɛ le: “Nu! N wu Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ka chena mbe kuwurputi so nɛ mbe emalaika kikɛ kulti mo ashi Ebɔrɛso,

english_verse: This is exactly what has happened, Ahab. The Lord made all your prophets lie to you, and he knows you will soon be destroyed.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ anebi Mikaya malga mbe lalaloge be kamalga ŋ kaŋɛ le: “Kusɔ nɛ k wora e la fanɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e sa ekpa nɛ fo gbagba be anebiana kini keji fo kashenteŋ. Ama mo alɛ gbagba nyi fo ka beeŋ mur!”

english_verse: Zedekiah walked up to Micaiah and slapped him on the face. Then he asked, “Do you really think the Lord would speak to you and not to me?”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ anebi Zɛdikaya yɔ anebi Mikaya kutɔ n ya kpa mo etaŋ anishito nseŋ bishi mo le: “Saŋɛ mo nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ yige ma nseŋ ya malga fo kutɔ?”

translation_verse: Nɛ ewura Ahab ponte ŋ kaŋɛ le: “Men pɛ Mikaya n yɔ Ammɔn nɛ e la Samɛria be kade to be gomena na, nɛ ewurbi Jɔash kutɔ,

english_verse: However, during the fighting a soldier shot an arrow without even aiming, and it hit Ahab where two pieces of his armor joined. He shouted to his chariot driver, “I've been hit! Get me out of here!”

english_verse: So when they saw Jehoshaphat in his robe, they thought he was Ahab and started to attack him. But when Jehoshaphat shouted out to them,
translation_verse: Amoso Siriya be benapo na ka wu ewura Jehoshafat na, nɛ b fɛ fanɛ mo e la Israɛl be ewura na nsaa shin nɛ b kɔ mo kena. Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura Jehoshafat shu n tre Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nɛ Ebɔrɛ shin nɛ benapo na yige mo.

english_verse: they realized he wasn't Ahab, and they left him alone.
translation_verse: Amoso Siriya be benapo ka wu fanɛ mannɛ Israɛl be ewura Ahab nna nɛ b yige keyakɔ bumo kena.

english_verse: As the sun was going down, someone in Israel's army shouted to the others, “Retreat! Go back home!”
translation_verse: Epeŋi ka bee tɔr, nɛ Israɛl be benapo na be eko ponte awɔrso ŋ kaŋɛ mo braana le: “Ekama e yige kena na be kekɔ nseŋ bɛta a yɔ epe!”

english_verse: Ahab's body was taken to Samaria and buried there.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ b ta ewura Ahab n yɔ Samɛria n ya puli.

english_verse: Ahaziah disobeyed the Lord, just as his father, his mother, and Jeroboam had done. They all led Israel to sin.
translation_verse: E daŋ wora kulubi nna ŋ gbiti Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ŋkpal e ka daŋ bɛ mo tuto Ahab nɛ mo nio Jɛzebel nɛ ewura Jeroboam mo nɛ e shin nɛ Israɛlebi luri kulubi to so.

english_verse: Soon after King Ahab of Israel died, the country of Moab rebelled against his son King Ahaziah. One day, Ahaziah fell through the wooden slats around the porch on the flat roof of his palace in Samaria, and he was badly injured. So he sent some messengers to the town of Ekron with orders to ask the god Baalzebub if he would get well.

english_verse: About the same time, an angel from the Lord sent Elijah the prophet from Tishbe to say to the king's messengers, “Ahaziah has rejected Israel's own God by sending you to ask Baalzebub about his injury.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be malaika kaŋɛ anebi Elaija nɛ e shi Tishbe na fanɛ e ya shɛr Ewura Ahaziya be mbɔ na to nseŋ bishi bumo le: “Manɛ nna nɛ menyee yɔ Ekrɔn nɛ men ya wu kegbir nɛ baa tre Baalzebɔb na? Menyee fɛ nna fanɛ Ebɔrɛ kikɛ maŋ wɔ Israɛl be efuli so nɛ men ya wu mo a?

english_verse: When the messengers returned to Ahaziah, he asked, “Why are you back so soon?”
translation_verse: Ama mbɔ na ka bɛta m ba ewura na kutɔ le nɛ e daŋ bishi bumo: “Manɛ nna nɛ men bɛta m ba manaŋ loŋ?”

english_verse: “A man met us along the road with a message for you from the Lord,” they answered. “The Lord wants to know why you sent us to ask Baalzebub about your injury and why you don't believe there's a God in Israel. The man also told us that the Lord says you're going to die.”
translation_verse: Nɛ b yɛ: “Kanyɛn ko e ba tu anyi nseŋ kaŋɛ anyi fanɛ an bɛta m ba kaŋɛ fo le: ‘Manɛ nna nɛ fo lara mbɔ fanɛ b yɔ Baalzebɔb be kegbir nɛ k wɔ Ekrɔn na to n ya bishi so? Fee fɛ fanɛ Ebɔrɛ kikɛ maŋ wɔ Israɛl be kasawule so nna a? Fo maaŋ naŋ nya alenfia ashi fo doro ere to kikɛ: Feeŋ wu!’ ”
