english_verse: All of these soldiers voluntarily came to Hebron because they wanted David to become king of Israel. In fact, everyone in Israel wanted the same thing.
translation_verse: Benapo na kikɛ daŋ yɔ Hibrɔn nna nɛ b ya buu Deevid Israɛl be kuwura. Israɛlebi kikɛ gba daa sha kumo be loŋ nna.

english_verse: The soldiers stayed in Hebron three days, eating and drinking what their relatives had prepared for them.
translation_verse: Bumo nɛ Deevid kikɛ daŋ ji ndoŋ nchɛ asa nna nsaa ji ajibi a nuu asɔnuuso nɛ bumo kurgepoana bar bumo na.

english_verse: Then he led them to Baalah in Judah, which was also called Kiriath-Jearim. They went there to get the sacred chest and bring it to Jerusalem, because it belonged to the Lord God, whose throne is above the winged creatures on the lid of the chest.
translation_verse: Deevid nɛ mbe basa daŋ yɔ Baala nɛ baa tre kumo Kiriaf Jearim nɛ k wɔ Juda be efuli so na nna nɛ b ya ta Enyɛnpe be ŋkre be deka nɛ mbe ketre Enyɛnpetale deŋ mbe kuwurputi so ashi emalaika anyɔ na be nferinto kumo so na.

english_verse: David was afraid what the Lord might do to him, and he asked himself, “Should I really be the one to take care of the sacred chest?”
translation_verse: Nɛ Ebɔrɛ be asheŋ pɛ Deevid kufu ga nɛ e kaŋɛ le: “Nuso nɛ meeŋ wora n ta ŋkre be deka ere n yɔ naniere.”

english_verse: The sacred chest was still at Abinadab's house, and when David and the crowd arrived there, they brought the chest outside and placed it on a new ox cart. Abinadab's sons Uzzah and Ahio guided the cart,
translation_verse: B daŋ lara ŋkre be deka na Abinadab be laŋ to nna m ba deŋi turko popɔr ko so. Uzza nɛ Ahio e daa keni turko na so.

english_verse: while David and the crowd danced and sang praises to the Lord with all their might. They played music on small harps and other stringed instruments, and on tambourines, cymbals, and trumpets.
translation_verse: Nɛ Deevid nɛ Israɛlebi na ta bumo be eleŋ kikɛ a cha nsaa boŋ nshɛ a maŋkura Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ. B daa laŋ ejaŋjilaŋ nɛ ŋkure nɛ echakachaka nna nsaa foŋ mbel.

english_verse: But when they came to Chidon's threshing place, the oxen stumbled, and Uzzah reached out and took hold of the chest to stop it from falling.
translation_verse: B ka fo kakpa nɛ Kidɔn bee bri mbe ayu na nɛ egbolufɛlso na fiti nɛ ŋkre be Deka na bee shin nɛ k tɔr nɛ Uzza teŋi enɔ nɛ e suse kumo to.

english_verse: The Lord God was very angry with Uzzah for doing this, and he killed Uzzah right there beside the chest.
translation_verse: Epul na to nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nya agbo n wɔtɔ Uzza nseŋ mɔ mo ŋkpal e ka teŋi enɔ m beta deka na so. E daŋ tɔr Ebɔrɛ be anishito nna n wu.

english_verse: David then got angry with God for killing Uzzah. So he named that place “Attack on Uzzah,” and it's been called that ever since.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Deevid nya agbo ga ŋkpal Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ka nya agbo m mɔ Uzza so. Hale nɛ mbre Enyɛnpe nɛ mbe agbo mɔ Uzza na nɛ b kraa tre loŋ be kakpa na.

english_verse: So instead of taking it to Jerusalem, David decided to take it to the home of Obed-Edom, who lived in the town of Gath.
translation_verse: Amoso Deevid daa maŋ ta ŋkre be deka na n yɔ Jerusalɛm to. E daŋ yige kumo kanyɛn ko nɛ baa tre Obɛd Edɔm nɛ e la Gaaf be kadetobia na be laŋ to nna.

english_verse: The chest stayed there for three months, and the Lord blessed Obed-Edom, his family, and everything he owned.
translation_verse: Ŋkre be deka na daa wɔ ndoŋ nna n ya fo afɔl asa nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛfa Obɛd Edɔm nɛ mbe kanaŋ nɛ kusɔ kama nɛ e kɔ kikɛ.

english_verse: David and his army marched to Baal-Perazim, where they attacked and defeated the Philistines. He said, “I defeated my enemies because God broke through them like a mighty flood.” So he named the place “The Lord Broke Through.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Deevid nɛ mbe benapo yɔ Baal Pɛrazim n ya kɔ m pɔɔ Filistiebi na so, nseŋ kaŋɛ le: “Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ bure n luri ma doŋana na to fanɛ kananɛ nchu bee bɔlɔ a luri kakpa na. Ndoŋ nna nɛ e nase kaboŋ na Baal Perazim. Kumo be kifito e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ e bee bure e luri to na.”

english_verse: David obeyed God and he defeated the Philistines. He even chased them all the way from Gibeon to the entrance to Gezer.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Deevid wora kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ na nseŋ yili Gibiɔn n ju Filisti be benapo na kikɛ n ya fo Gɛza.

english_verse: King Hiram of Tyre sent some officials to David. They brought along carpenters and stone workers, and enough cedar logs to build David a palace.
translation_verse: Tai be ewura Hiram daŋ shuŋi mbɔ ewura Deevid kutɔ nna. E daŋ shuŋi ekapɛnta nɛ basa nɛ baa ta ajembu a pɔr nna nseŋ ta ndibi nɛ baa tre sida na n ti so fanɛ b ya pɔr ewura be laŋ n sa Deevid.

english_verse: After David moved to Jerusalem, he married more women and had more sons and daughters.
translation_verse: Deevid ka lar Hibrɔn m ba Jerusalɛm na, e daŋ ta beche damta nna ŋ kurge mbinyɛnsobi nɛ mbichesobi damta.

translation_verse: Amoso Deevid be ketre daŋ dii n yɔ kaplɛkama nna, nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ shin nɛ efuli kama so ebi bee ŋana mo.

english_verse: When the Philistines heard that David had become king of Israel, they came to capture him. But David heard about their plan and marched out to meet them in battle.
translation_verse: Filistiebi na ka nu fanɛ Deevid e ki Israɛl be efuli so kikɛ be ewura, nɛ bumo be benapo kikɛ ya ka fin mo nɛ b pɛ. Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura Deevid bela ase nɛ e ya n ya tu bumo.

translation_verse: Loŋ be jemanɛ na nɛ Filistiebi be benapo na ta kena n ya purgi Refaebi be ketaŋɛ to be ndeana nsaa muu bumo be asɔ.

english_verse: Then David ordered his troops to burn the idols that the Philistines had left behind.
translation_verse: Filistiebi be benapo na ka shile n yige bumo be agbir na nɛ Deevid kaŋɛ mbe benapo na fanɛ b ya chɔɔ amo.

english_verse: Some time later, the Philistines came back into the hill country and camped in Rephaim Valley.
translation_verse: K maŋ chɛr ko nɛ Filistiebi be benapo na naŋ bɛta n ta kena n ya purgi Refaebi be ketaŋɛ na to be nde kikɛ.

english_verse: David asked God what he should do, and God answered, “Don't attack them from the front. Circle around behind them where the balsam trees are.
translation_verse: Nɛ Deevid naŋ bishi Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kusɔ nɛ e beeŋ wora, nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ mo le: “Men sa maŋ kaŋ ta kena n tu bumo nfe, ama men wora shiriya a kulti bumo a yɔ ndibi nɛ baa tre balsam ere ase n ya kɔ bumo ndoŋ.

english_verse: Wait there until you hear the treetops making the sound of marching troops. That sound will mean I have marched out ahead of you to fight the Philistine army. So you must then attack quickly!”
translation_verse: Men ka baŋ nu awɔr ka shi ndibi na so a ba fanɛ benapo ka bɛ abar so a nite na, kumo ere men fara a kɔ bumo, ŋkpal manɛ so meeŋ juŋkpar menyi n ya kɔ m pɔɔ Filistiebi be benapo na so.”

english_verse: David had several buildings built in Jerusalem, and he had a tent set up where the sacred chest would be kept.
translation_verse: Ewura Deevid daŋ pɔr nwu damta nna ashi Jerusalɛm nseŋ shin nɛ b yuu wajɛbu nɛ b ta ŋkre be deka na bre n yili ndoŋ.

english_verse: Next, David invited everyone to come to Jerusalem and watch the sacred chest being carried to the place he had set up for it.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Deevid tre Israɛlebi na kikɛ m ba Jerusalɛm, nɛ b ya ta ŋkre be deka na m ba wajɛbu nɛ e yuu ŋkpal kumo so na to.

english_verse: He also sent for Aaron's descendants and for the Levites. The Levites that came were:

translation_verse: nɛ Jowɛl nɛ e bee juŋkpar basa kalfa nɛ adesa ashi Gɛshɔn be kabuna na,

translation_verse: nɛ Aminadab nɛ mo alɛ daa juŋkpar basa kalfa nɛ kuduanyɔ ashi Uziɛl be kabuna na.

english_verse: The first time we tried to bring the chest to Jerusalem, we didn't ask the Lord what he wanted us to do. He was angry with us, because you Levites weren't there to carry the chest.”

english_verse: The priests and the Levites made themselves clean. They were now ready to carry the sacred chest
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ bɔrɛmatapoana nɛ Livaiebi na lara alubi bumo be ŋgbene to nseŋ ki cheembi, saŋɛ na so baaŋ tiŋ n sulɔ Enyɛnpe Israɛl be Ebɔrɛ na be ŋkre be deka na.

english_verse: David then told the leaders to choose some Levites to sing and play music on small harps, other stringed instruments, and cymbals.

translation_verse: Ewura Deevid ka lara esarga chɔɔso na n loge nɛ e nɛfa basa na ashi Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be ketre to,

translation_verse: Kumo be jemanɛ na nɛ Ebɔrɛ be basa daa maŋ shi, nseŋ daa la befɔ ashi Keenan be kasawule so.

english_verse: We wandered from nation to nation, from one country to another.
translation_verse: B daŋ baa wɔtɔ nna a kilgi to efuliana nɛ nsawuleana so.

translation_verse: Ama Ebɔrɛ daa maŋ shuli nɛ ekama mɛaŋ bumo. E daŋ kpele ndoŋ be bewura kusoe nna saŋɛ na so b maaŋ wora bumo shɛŋ,

english_verse: and telling them, “Don't touch my chosen leaders or harm my prophets!”
translation_verse: nseŋ kaŋɛ bumo le: “Men sa maŋ kaŋ tɔrɔ ma basa laraso, ŋko n tɔrɔ ma anebiana.”

english_verse: Everyone on this earth, sing praises to the Lord. Day after day announce, “The Lord has saved us!”
translation_verse: Ekama nɛ e wɔ durnya ere to e boŋ kashɛ n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na! Men baa malga kananɛ e mɔlga menyi na be asheŋ karechɛ kikɛ.

english_verse: Tell every nation on earth, “The Lord is wonderful and does marvelous things!
translation_verse: Men malga kananɛ Ebɔrɛ be kemaŋkura du n sa efuliana kikɛ, nseŋ malga mbe asheŋgboŋ nɛ e bee wora ŋ ŋini basa kikɛ.

english_verse: The Lord is great and deserves our greatest praise! He is the only God worthy of our worship.
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kɔ eleŋ nseŋ daga kemaŋkura. Mo e daga bunyaŋ a chɔ agbir.

english_verse: Other nations worship idols, but the Lord created the heavens.
translation_verse: Agbir nɛ efuli pɔtɛana bre be basa bee shuŋ, ama Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e to esoso nɛ kasawule.

english_verse: Give honor and praise to the Lord, whose power and beauty fill his holy temple.”
translation_verse: Kemaŋkura nɛ kuwurji daga mo nna, nɛ eleŋ nɛ kagbenefuli kikɛ bɔlɔ mbe bɔrɛlambu to.

english_verse: Tell everyone of every nation, “Praise the glorious power of the Lord.
translation_verse: Ekama nɛ e wɔ durnya ere to e di Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ epaŋ, men ta mbe kemaŋkura nɛ mbe eleŋ n sa mo.

english_verse: He is wonderful! Praise him and bring an offering into his temple. Worship the Lord, majestic and holy.
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe be ketre daga bunyaŋ, amoso men shin nɛ an maŋkura mo. Men ta men be sarga m ba mbe lambu to. Enyɛnpe cheembi na kaŋ lar a ba, a daga fanɛ men bunyaŋ mo.

english_verse: Everyone on earth, now tremble!” The world stands firm, never to be shaken.
translation_verse: Esa kama nɛ e wɔ durnya ere to beeŋ chicha ashi mbe anishito! Durnya na yil kiŋkiŋ nna nsaa maa gbuŋgbuŋ.

english_verse: Tell the heavens and the earth to be glad and celebrate! And announce to the nations, “The Lord is King!”
translation_verse: Esoso nɛ kasawule so ebi, men shin nɛ men be ŋgbene e baa fuli! Men kaŋɛ efuliana na fanɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e la ewura.

english_verse: Command the ocean to roar with all of its creatures and the fields to rejoice with all of their crops.
translation_verse: Teku nɛ kusɔ kama nɛ k wɔ kumo to e baa cha awɔr; Ndɔana nɛ asɔ kama nɛ a wɔ amo to, men baa kɔ kagbenefuli!

english_verse: Then every tree in the forest will sing joyful songs to the Lord. He is coming to judge all people on earth.
translation_verse: Ndibi nɛ a wɔ kupo to beeŋ baa boŋ nshɛ kagbenefuli ŋkpal manɛ so Enyɛnpe na bee ba nɛ e ba ji durnya be basa demu.

english_verse: Praise the Lord because he is good to us, and his love never fails.
translation_verse: Men ta kechɔrɔ n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ŋkpal manɛ so, e walɛ, nɛ mbe kasha malɛ wɔtɔ mbaanaayɔ.

english_verse: Say to him, “Save us, Lord God! Bring us back from among the nations. Let us celebrate and shout in praise of your holy name.
translation_verse: Men kaŋɛ mo le: “Anyi be Ebɔrɛ nɛ anyi be emɔlgapo, mɔlga anyi. Gbegbar anyi abar so nseŋ mɔlga anyi ashi efuli pɔtɛ ana be enɔ to, saŋɛ na so anyeeŋ ta kechɔrɔ n sa fo, nseŋ di fo ketre cheembi ere epaŋ.”

english_verse: Lord God of Israel, you deserve to be praised forever and ever.” After David finished, the people shouted, “Amen! Praise the Lord!” David Appoints Worship Leaders at Jerusalem and Gibeon
translation_verse: Men di Enyɛnpe Israɛl be Ebɔrɛ na epaŋ! Men di mo epaŋ naniere hale mbaanaayɔ! Ndoŋ nna nɛ basa na kikɛ shuli so ŋ kaŋɛ le: “Amɛn” Nseŋ di Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ epaŋ. B ka bee shuŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ashi Jerusalɛm nɛ Gibiɔn be asheŋ

english_verse: David chose Asaph and the Levites in his clan to be in charge of the daily worship at the place where the sacred chest was kept.
translation_verse: Ewura Deevid daŋ lara Asaf nɛ Livaiebi nɛ b la kabuna koŋwule ebi na nna fanɛ b baa keni kakpa nɛ ŋkre be deka na yil na be kushuŋ so karechɛ kikɛ.

english_verse: David also chose Zadok the priest and his relatives who were priests to serve at the Lord's sacred tent at Gibeon.
translation_verse: Bɔrɛmatapowura Zadɔk nɛ mo braana bɔrɛmatapoana e daa keni Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be wajɛbu na so ashi Gibiɔn.

english_verse: They were to offer sacrifices on the altar every morning and evening, just as the Lord had commanded in the Law he gave Israel.
translation_verse: Kachipurso nɛ kaaseso kikɛ b daa lara sarga chɔɔso nna a deŋi bɔrɛsure na so fanɛ kananɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Israɛlebi na mbe mbra to na gbagba.

english_verse: Heman and Jeduthun were their assistants, as well as the other men who had been chosen to praise the Lord for his never-ending love.
translation_verse: Heman nɛ Jedutum e daa la bumo be bechɛtopo, n ta bumo nɛ b daŋ lara fanɛ b baa boŋ nshɛ a maŋkura Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ŋkpal mbe kasha ka maŋ kɔ ekarso na n ti so.

english_verse: Heman and Jeduthun were also responsible for blowing the trumpets, and for playing the cymbals and other instruments during worship at the tent. The Levites in Jeduthun's clan were the guards at Gibeon.
translation_verse: Heman nɛ Jedutum malɛ gba e daŋ naa foŋ mbel nsaa laŋ echakachaka nɛ alaŋsɔ nɛ baa laŋ nsaa boŋ nshɛ a di Ebɔrɛ epaŋ jemanɛ kikɛ. Basa nɛ b shi Jedutum be kabuna na e daa keni bumo be mbunaana so.

english_verse: After that, everyone went home, and David went home to his family.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ekama yɔ epe nɛ Deevid malɛ yɔ mbe kanaŋ kutɔ.

english_verse: Soon after David moved into his new palace, he said to Nathan the prophet, “Look around! I live in a palace made of cedar, but the sacred chest is kept in a tent.”
translation_verse: Ewura Deevid ka ya kaa wɔ mbe kuwura laŋ popɔr na to nɛ e tre anebi Neetan ŋ kaŋɛ mo le: “Keni! Ndibi nɛ baa tre sida na nɛ b ta m pɔr ewura be laŋ nɛ n wɔtɔ ere, ama Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be ŋkre be deka na bre wɔ wajɛbu to nna!”

english_verse: and yet you have promised to do even more for my descendants. You are treating me as if I am a very important person.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman, fo kraŋ nase kɔnɔ n sa ma kaman to ebi. Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, fee keni ma a bɔlɔ kenishi fanɛ esagboŋ ko nna.

english_verse: That night, the Lord told Nathan
translation_verse: Kumo be kanyɛso, nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Neetan le:

english_verse: to go to David and tell him: David, you are my servant, so listen carefully: You are not the one to build a temple for me.
translation_verse: “Ya kaŋɛ ma kayɛrbi Deevid fanɛ ma Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e naa kaŋɛ mo na fanɛ mannɛ mo nɛ mee sha fanɛ e pɔr bɔrɛlambu n sa ma nɛ m baa wɔtɔ.

english_verse: I didn't live in a temple when I brought my people out of Egypt, and I don't live in one now. A tent has always been my home wherever I have gone with them.
translation_verse: Yili jemanɛ so nɛ n lara Israɛlebi ashi Ijipt be efuli so dra dra na m ba fo kabre, m maŋ naŋ chena bɔrɛlambu to kikɛ. Kaplɛkama nɛ n yɔ malɛ, wajɛbu to nɛ mee luri.

english_verse: I chose special leaders and told them to be like shepherds for my people Israel. But did I ever say anything to even one of them about building a cedar temple for me?
translation_verse: Enite damta nɛ ma nɛ Israɛlebi nite ere kikɛ, m maŋ naŋ bishi bumo be bejuŋkparpo nɛ n tre fanɛ b baa keni ma basa so fanɛ kananɛ mbolpɔkpapo bee keni mbe mbolpɔ so na be ekama kusɔ nɛ k ba nɛ b maŋ ta ndibi nɛ baa tre sida na m pɔr bɔrɛlambu n sa ma.”

english_verse: Wherever you went, I helped you and destroyed your enemies right in front of your eyes. I have made you one of the most famous people in the world.
translation_verse: Kaplɛkama nɛ fo daŋ yɔ, ma nɛ fo nna. Nɛ ma alɛ bee pɔɔ fo doŋana kikɛ so a sa fo. Kananɛ basa ko be atre dii ga durnya ere to na, loŋ gbagba nɛ meeŋ shin nɛ fo alɛ gba be ketre e dii.

english_verse: I'll choose one of your sons to be king when you reach the end of your life and are buried beside your ancestors. I'll make him a strong ruler,
translation_verse: Fo kaŋ wu nɛ b ta fo n ya nase fo nananyɛnana be edesekpa, meeŋ shin nɛ fo mbinyɛnsobi ere be eko e ki ewura, nɛ n shin nɛ mbe kuwurji malɛ e baa kɔ eleŋ ga.

english_verse: and no one will be able to take his kingdom away from him. He will be the one to build a temple for me.
translation_verse: Mo e naŋ pɔr ma bɔrɛlambu n sa ma. Ma alɛ beeŋ shin nɛ mbe kuwurji e baa wɔtɔ mbaanaayɔ.

english_verse: I will be like a father to him, and he will be like a son to me. I will never put an end to my agreement with him, as I put an end to my agreement with Saul, who was king before you.
translation_verse: Meeŋ ki mo tuto, nɛ mo alɛ e baa la m pibinyɛn. M maaŋ yige kebaachɛ mo to fanɛ kananɛ n yige Ewura Sɔɔl mo nɛ n lara kuwurji to nseŋ ta fo n yuu to na.

english_verse: I will make sure that your son and his descendants will rule my people and my kingdom forever.
translation_verse: Meeŋ ta mo ŋ ki ma basa be ejuŋkparpo nɛ e baa keni ma efuli kikɛ so. Mbe mbia e naŋ ba ji kuwura a ka a sa abar so mbaanaayɔ.”

english_verse: Nathan told David exactly what the Lord had said. David Gives Thanks to the Lord (
translation_verse: Kusɔ nɛ Ebɔrɛ daŋ kaŋɛ Neetan na gbagba chap nɛ e kaŋɛ ewura Deevid. Ewura Deevid be kabɔrɛchɔrɔ be asheŋ (

english_verse: I am your servant, and you know my thoughts. What else can I say, except that you have honored me?
translation_verse: Manɛ nɛ n naa kɔ nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ? Fo nyi ma, fo kenya nɛnɛ. Ama fo kraŋ ta ma n yili kemaŋkura be eyilikpa.

english_verse: David went into the tent he had set up for the sacred chest. He sat there and prayed: Lord God, my family and I don't deserve what you have already done for us,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ewura Deevid ya luri Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be wajɛbu na to n ya chena ŋ kule Ebɔrɛ ŋ kaŋɛ le: “Ma nɛ ma kanaŋ maŋ daga kenya kusɔ nɛ fo wora n sa anyi ere.

english_verse: It was your choice to do these wonderful things for me and to make these promises.
translation_verse: Fo keparso nɛ fo wora asheŋ ere n sa ma nseŋ nase le be nnɔgboŋ ere n sa ma.

english_verse: No other god is like you, Lord—you alone are God. Everything we have heard about you is true.
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ kikɛ maŋ naa wɔtɔ fanɛ fo Enyɛnpe na. Fo nawule nɛ an nyi fo ka la Ebɔrɛ.

english_verse: And there is no other nation on earth like Israel, the nation you rescued from slavery in Egypt to be your own. You became famous by using great and wonderful miracles to force other nations and their gods out of your land, so that your people could live here.
translation_verse: Efuli kikɛ maŋ naa wɔ kasawule ere so fanɛ Israɛl be efuli nɛ fo lara ashi kenyaya to nseŋ shin nɛ b ki fo basa na. Mamachi be asɔ damta nɛ fo wora n sa bumo na e shin nɛ fo ketre dii durnya ere to. Fo mɔlga fo basa ashi Ijipt be kasawule so, m bar bumo nfe nseŋ ju efuli ere so ebi n shin nɛ fo basa chena bumo be nsawule so.

english_verse: You have chosen Israel to be your people forever, and you have become their God.
translation_verse: Dra dra na kikɛ nɛ fo ta Israɛlebi ŋ ki fo gbagba be basa mbaanaayɔ, nseŋ ki bumo be Ebɔrɛ.

english_verse: Then you will be famous forever, and everyone will say, “The Lord All-Powerful rules Israel and is their God.” My kingdom will be strong,
translation_verse: Saŋɛ na so fo ketre beeŋ dii nɛ ekama e baa kaŋɛ le: ‘Enyɛnpetale na e la Israɛl be Ebɔrɛ.’ Feeŋ yili ma kuwurji mbaanaayɔ.

english_verse: because you are my God, and you have promised that my descendants will be kings. That's why I have the courage to pray to you like this, even though I am only your servant.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal fo ka la ma Ebɔrɛ nseŋ nase kɔnɔ fanɛ ma kaman to ebi beeŋ baa la bewura na so nɛ fo kayɛrbi maa pɔ aba nɛ kebaakule fo na.

english_verse: You are the Lord God, and you have made this good promise to me.
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe, fo e la Ebɔrɛ nseŋ nase le be kɔnɔ fanɛ feeŋ wora asɔ lela ere n sa ma.

english_verse: Now please bless my descendants forever, and let them always be your chosen kings. You have already blessed my family, and I know you will bless us forever.
translation_verse: Enyɛnpetale nɛfa ma kaman to ebi, saŋɛ na so feeŋ baa lara fo bewura bumo to saŋkama. Fo Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e nase kɔnɔ fanɛ fo nɛfa beeŋ baa wɔ ma kaman to ebi so hale mbaanaayɔ.”

english_verse: Hadadezer's officers had carried gold shields, but David took these shields and brought them back to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ ewura Deevid ta Hadadeza be benimu be shuwa be asɔ kuŋso na n yɔ Jerusalɛm.

english_verse: Then David stationed some of his troops in Damascus, and the people there had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him. Everywhere David went, the Lord helped him win battles.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Deevid shin nɛ mbe benapo na be beko chena Damaskɔs n shin nɛ Siriyaebi na sɔ Deevid ŋ ki bumo be ewura a ka lampo a sa mo. Kaplɛkama nɛ ewura Deevid daŋ baŋ yɔ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ daa shin nɛ e bee kɔ a pɔɔ so nna.

english_verse: King Tou of Hamath and King Hadadezer had been enemies. So when Tou heard that David had defeated Hadadezer's whole army, he sent his son Hadoram to congratulate David on his victory. Hadoram also brought him gifts made of gold, silver, and bronze.
translation_verse: nɛ e shuŋi mo pibinyɛn Joram fanɛ e ya chɔrɔ ewura Deevid nseŋ sa mo ansaŋ nɛ kushuŋ ŋkpal e ka kɔ m pɔɔ Hadadeza nɛ mo ere Toi kɔ mo kena alɛ damta nsaa maŋ tiŋ m pɔɔ mo so so. Asɔ nɛ b ta shuwa nɛ gbiti nɛ danyaŋ n wora nɛ Joram daŋ ta m ba kɛ ewura Deevid.

english_verse: David gave these gifts to the Lord, just as he had done with the silver and gold he had captured from Edom, Moab, Ammon, Philistia, and Amalek.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura Deevid ta asɔ na n ti shuwa nɛ gbiti nɛ e kɔ Edɔm nɛ Mowab nɛ Ammɔn nɛ Filisti nɛ Amalɛk be efuliana n sɔ na so m bɔɔ Ebɔrɛ enɔ.

english_verse: Then he stationed troops in Edom, and the people there had to accept David as their ruler. Everywhere David went, the Lord gave him victory in war. A List of David's Officials (
translation_verse: E daŋ wora benapo be echenakpaana nna ashi Edɔm be efuli so kikɛ nna n shin nɛ basa nɛ b wɔ ndoŋ na kikɛ sɔ ewura Deevid ŋ ki bumo be ewura. Kaplɛkama malɛ nɛ ewura Deevid daŋ yɔ, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na daa shin nna nɛ e bee kɔ a pɔɔ so.

english_verse: Joab the son of Zeruiah was the commander in chief of the army. Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept the government records.
translation_verse: Zeruwa pibinyɛn Jɔab e daa la benapo na be enimu, nɛ Ahilud malɛ pibinyɛn Jehoshafat daa la esa nɛ e bee sibɛ asheŋ a nase kawɔl to.

english_verse: Zadok the son of Ahitub and Ahimelech the son of Abiathar were the priests. Shavsha was the secretary.
translation_verse: Ahitub pibinyɛn Zadɔk nɛ Abiata pibinyɛn Ahimɛlɛk e daa la bɔrɛmatapoana. Sɛraya malɛ e daa la ewura be esibɛpo.

english_verse: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was the commander of David's bodyguard. David's sons were his highest-ranking officials.
translation_verse: Jehowada pibinyɛn Bɛnaya e daa la benapo nɛ baa kuŋ ewura Deevid na be enimu, nɛ ewura Deevid malɛ be mbinyɛnsobi daa la mbe ekrachigboŋ.

english_verse: David said, “Nahash was kind to me, so I will be kind to his son.” He sent some officials to Ammon to tell Hanun how sorry he was that his father had died. But when David's officials arrived at Ammon,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura Deevid fɛ le: “A daga ŋ ka bugi kagbene n wora Hanuun kelela, fanɛ kananɛ, mo tuto Nahaash gba daŋ bugi mbe kagbene n wora ma kelela na.” Amoso Deevid daŋ shuŋi mbɔ nna fanɛ b ya wora Hanuun edaŋkena. B ka ya fo Ammɔn be kasawule so,

english_verse: Joab saw that the enemy troops were lined up on both sides of him. So he picked some of the best Israelite soldiers to fight the Syrians.
translation_verse: Jɔab ka wu fanɛ mo doŋana na wɔ mbe anishito nɛ kaman kikɛ na, nɛ e lara Israɛl be benapo lempo na fanɛ b ya kɔ Siriyaebi na,

english_verse: Some time later, King Nahash of Ammon died, and his son Hanun became king.
translation_verse: K maŋ chɛr ko nɛ Ammɔn be ewura Nahaash wu, nɛ mo pibinyɛn Hanuun ki ewura.

english_verse: When the kings who had been under Hadadezer's rule saw that Israel had defeated them, they made peace with David and accepted him as their new ruler. The Syrians never helped the Ammonites again.
translation_verse: Bewura mo nɛ b daa bɛ ewura Hadadeza so na ka pin fanɛ Israɛlebi na pɔɔ bumo so nɛ b fara a fin kagbenewushi ewura Deevid kutɔ, hale n shin nɛ e ki bumo be ewura. Kumo be kaman nɛ Siriyaebi na kini fanɛ b maaŋ naŋ chɛ Ammɔnebi na to kikɛ.

english_verse: the Ammonite leaders said to Hanun, “Do you really believe King David is honoring your father by sending these men to comfort you? He probably sent them to spy on our country, so he can come and destroy it.”
translation_verse: nɛ Ammɔn be bewurbi na kaŋɛ ewura na le: “Fee fɛ fanɛ fo tuto be bunyaŋ so nɛ ewura Deevid shuŋi basa ere fanɛ b ba wora fo edaŋkena ere a? Manɛ loŋ so nna! E shuŋi bumo nna nɛ b ba dara anyi be efuli ere saŋɛ na so e beeŋ ba kɔ m pɔɔ anyi so!”

english_verse: Hanun arrested David's officials and had their beards shaved off and their robes cut off just below the waist, and then he sent them away.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Hanuun shin nɛ b pɛ Deevid be mbɔ na n she bumo be ntɔl nseŋ ku bumo be epiŋi be aya ase n ya fo bumo be nshɛr to nseŋ yige bumo nɛ b choŋ.

english_verse: They were terribly ashamed. When David found out what had happened to his officials, he sent a message that told them, “Stay in Jericho until your beards grow back. Then you can come home.”
translation_verse: Nɛ mbɔ na fin kananɛ baaŋ naŋ bɛta n yɔ epe ŋ gben ŋkpal anishinyɔr so. Ewura Deevid ka nu kusɔ nɛ k wora na nɛ e shuŋi n ya kaŋɛ mbɔ na fanɛ b ya kaa wɔ Jɛriko n ya fo jemanɛ nɛ bumo be ntɔl na beeŋ kɔr pɔɛŋ nɛ b ba epe.

english_verse: David heard what was happening, and he sent out Joab with his army.
translation_verse: Ewura Deevid ka nu kusɔ nɛ k bee wora na, nɛ e shuŋi Jɔab nɛ mbe benapo kikɛ nɛ b ya tu bumo.

english_verse: The Ammonite troops marched to the entrance of the city and prepared for battle, while the Syrian troops took their positions in the open fields.
translation_verse: Nɛ Ammɔn be benapo kre kena n yili bumo be kade Raba be kabunagboŋ na ekpa nɛ Siriya be benapoana na malɛ kre n yili kade na be laŋgar.

english_verse: Then he put his brother Abishai in command of the rest of the army and told them to fight against the Ammonites.
translation_verse: nseŋ shin mo sipo Abishai malɛ juŋkpar benapo nɛ b ka na n ya kaa kɔ Ammɔnebi na.

english_verse: Joab told his brother, “If the Syrians are too much for me to handle, come and help me. And if the Ammonites are too strong for you, I'll come and help you.
translation_verse: Le nɛ Jɔab kaŋɛ Abishai: “Fo baŋ wu fanɛ Siriyaebi na bee pɔɔ ma so, fo wora ania m ba chɛ ma to, nɛ Ammɔnebi na kaa pɔɔ fo alɛ so, ma alɛ beeŋ ba chɛ fo to.

english_verse: Be brave and fight hard to protect our people and the towns of our Lord God. I pray he will do whatever pleases him.”
translation_verse: Baa kɔ eleŋ nsaa leŋ fo kumo to kpakpa! Men shin nɛ an pere kenishi ŋ kɔ n sa anyi be basa nɛ Ebɔrɛ be nde, nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be aparsheŋ e wora.”

english_verse: Joab and his soldiers attacked the Syrians, and the Syrians ran from them.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Jɔab nɛ mbe benapo yɔ nɛ b ya kɔ Siriyaebi na kena, nɛ b shile.

english_verse: When the Ammonite troops saw that the Syrians had run away, they ran from Abishai's soldiers and went back into their own city. Joab then returned to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Ammɔnebi na ka wu fanɛ Siriyaebi na bee shile, nɛ bumo alɛ gba lara keya fuful Abishai nɛ mbe benapo be anishito n shile n luri kade to. Ndoŋ nna nɛ Jɔab bɛta n yɔ Jerusalɛm.

english_verse: As soon as the Syrians realized they had been defeated, they sent for their troops that were stationed on the other side of the Euphrates River. Shophach, the commander of Hadadezer's army, led these troops to Ammon.

english_verse: The next spring, the time when kings go to war, Joab marched out in command of the Israelite army and destroyed towns all over the country of Ammon. He attacked the capital city of Rabbah and left it in ruins. But David stayed in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Dɔchubɔrɛ be saŋɛ nɛ bewura bee yɔ kena to na nɛ Jɔab juŋkpar Israɛl be benapo nɛ e ya kɔ n sɔ Ammɔn be kasawule. Ewura Deevid bre daŋ shir a wɔ Jerusalɛm nna. Benapo na daŋ pugi ŋ kulti kadegboŋ nɛ baa tre Raaba na nna n wɔtɔ ŋ kɔ m mur kumo.

english_verse: He forced the people of Rabbah to work with saws, iron picks, and axes. He also did the same thing with the people in all the other Ammonite towns. David then led Israel's army back to Jerusalem. The Descendants of the Rephaim (
translation_verse: Nseŋ tintiŋ kade na to be basa nɛ baa ta ekapɛnta be nsaŋɛgboŋ nɛ abɛlso be ntekpa nɛ akpanfu a shuŋ. Loŋ koŋwule na nɛ e daŋ wora nde nɛ a wɔ Ammɔn be efuli so na kikɛ. Kumo be kaman nɛ mo nɛ mbe benapo bɛta n yɔ Jerusalɛm.

english_verse: Some time later, Israel fought a battle against the Philistines at Gezer. During this battle, Sibbecai from Hushah killed Sippai, a descendant of the Rephaim, and the Philistines were defeated.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Israɛlebi na kɔ Filistiebi na kena ashi Gɛza. Loŋ be kena na to nɛ Sibikai nɛ e shi Husha na mɔ kanyɛn tenteŋ gboŋgboŋi ko nɛ baa tre Sipaya na nseŋ pɔɔ Filistiebi na so.

english_verse: In another battle against the Philistines, Elhanan the son of Jair killed Lahmi the brother of Goliath from Gath, whose spear shaft was like a weaver's beam.
translation_verse: Kena ko ka naŋ koso Israɛlebi na nɛ Filistiebi na be kefɛato nɛ Jair pibinyɛn Ɛlhanan mɔ Lami nɛ e la Goliɛf nɛ e shi Gaaf na mo da na. Mbe kekpa be kedibi be bumburuŋ daa du fanɛ keyapuye nna.

english_verse: Another one of the Philistine soldiers who was a descendant of the Rephaim was as big as a giant and had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot. During a battle at Gath,
translation_verse: Kena nyɔsopo ka naŋ koso ashi Gaaf, nɛ kanyɛn tenteŋ gboŋgboŋi ko nɛ e la Filisti be enapo nsaa kɔ ashilbi nɛ anashibi asheshe wɔ ndoŋ. E daa la dra na be basa tenteŋ gboŋgboŋiana nɛ baa tre Rafa na be kenana nna.

english_verse: he made fun of Israel, so David's nephew Jonathan killed him.
translation_verse: Mo e daŋ wora Israɛlebi na eyurto nɛ ewura Deevid mo da Shamaa pibinyɛn Jonatan mɔ mo na.

english_verse: David and his soldiers killed these three men from Gath who were descendants of the Rephaim.
translation_verse: Basa asa nɛ ewura Deevid nɛ mbe benapo mɔ ere kikɛ daa la Gaaf be basa tenteŋ gboŋgboŋi na be kenana nna.

english_verse: But David replied, “No! I want to pay you what they're worth. I can't just take something from you and then offer the Lord a sacrifice that cost me nothing.”
translation_verse: Nɛ ewura Deevid malɛ kaŋɛ mo le: “M-m, meeŋ ka amo be kukɔ n sa fo ŋkpal manɛ so m maa sha k lara sarga nɛ m maŋ bɔ kukɔ kumo so n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord said to Gad, one of David's prophets,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ anebi Gad le:

english_verse: Joab answered, “Your Majesty, even if the Lord made your kingdom a hundred times larger, you would still rule everyone in it. Why do you need to know how many soldiers there are? Don't you think that would make the whole nation angry?”
translation_verse: Nɛ Jɔab kaŋɛ ewura Deevid le: “Yiramu, hale nɛ Enyɛnpe fo Ebɔrɛ na shin nɛ Israɛl be benapo wora kishi n ti so fanɛ ntuŋ kalfa a chɔ kananɛ b du naniere gba bumo kikɛ kra la fo nyɛrbi nna. Manɛ e ba nɛ fee sha fanɛ fo wora le be kesheŋ nɛ k maŋ shi Ebɔrɛ kutɔ ere n shin nɛ nfɛra lubi ere e ba efuli ere so?”

english_verse: But David would not change his mind. And so Joab went everywhere in Israel and Judah and counted the people. He returned to Jerusalem
translation_verse: Ama ewura Deevid kini kechɛrga mbe nfɛra nseŋ shin nɛ Jɔab nu n sa mo nseŋ ya karga Israɛl be benapo na nseŋ bɛta m ba Jerusalɛm,

english_verse: Joab refused to include anyone from the tribes of Levi and Benjamin, because he still disagreed with David's orders. God Punishes Israel (
translation_verse: Ŋkpal ewura na be kusɔ nɛ e kaŋɛ na ka daŋ maŋ par Jɔab so, e daa maŋ karga Livai nɛ Bɛnjamin bre be eyiri na.

english_verse: “Tell David that I will punish him in one of three ways. But he will have to choose which one it will be.”
translation_verse: “Ya kaŋɛ Deevid fanɛ e lara asɔ asa nɛ mee sa mo ere to be kumo nɛ e bee sha fanɛ n ta ŋ gberge mo kusoe.”

english_verse: and David prayed, “It's my fault! I sinned by ordering the people to be counted. They have done nothing wrong—they are innocent sheep. Lord God, please punish me and my family. Don't let the disease wipe out your people.” David Buys Araunah's Threshing Place (
translation_verse: Nɛ Deevid kule Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ŋ kaŋɛ le: “Ma e wora n jija nseŋ wora kulubi ŋkpal ŋ ka shin nɛ baa karga basa na so. Nɛ manɛ nɛ bebɔlpo ere malɛ wora? N nyɛnpe nɛ ma Ebɔrɛ. Ma nɛ ma kanaŋ e daga fo ka gberge kusoe nseŋ yige basa ere bre.”

english_verse: David's order to count the people made God angry, and he punished Israel.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal ewura Deevid ka shin nɛ b karga benapo na so Ebɔrɛ daŋ nya agbo nna nseŋ gberge Israɛlebi kusoe.

english_verse: David prayed, “I am your servant. But what I did was stupid and terribly wrong. Please forgive me.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura Deevid kaŋɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ le: “Kusɔ nɛ n wora ere bee ŋini nna fanɛ n wora kulubi gboŋgboŋi. Amoso jande, ta m paŋ ma ŋkpal manɛ so n wora kawulisheŋ.”

english_verse: Gad went to David and told him: You must choose how the Lord will punish you:
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ anebi Gad yɔ ewura Deevid kutɔ n ya kaŋɛ mo kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ na. E yɛ: “Asɔ asa ere to be kumo nɛ feeŋ ba sha?

english_verse: Will there be three years when the land won't grow enough food for its people? Or will your enemies constantly defeat you for three months? Or will the Lord send a horrible disease to strike your land for three days? Think about it and decide, because I have to give your answer to God who sent me.
translation_verse: Akoŋgboŋ be ketɔr fo kasawule so nfɛ asa ŋko fo keshile fo doŋana afɔl asa ŋko kulɔ be aleblawu ko be keba fo kasawule so m ba mɔ basa nchɛnsa? Fɛ kumo be asheŋ nseŋ kaŋɛ ma kusɔ nɛ fee sha fanɛ ŋ kaŋɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ.”

english_verse: David was miserable and said, “It's a terrible choice to make! But the Lord is kind, and I'd rather be punished by him than by anyone else.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura Deevid kaŋɛ Gad le: “N wɔ kagbenejija be kebaawɔtɔ to nna ama maa sha dimɛdi ka gberge ma kusoe. Ŋkpal Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ka bee wu kuwɔr so, mo gbagba e gberge ma kusoe.”

english_verse: Then he sent an angel to destroy the city of Jerusalem. But just as the angel was about to do that, the Lord felt sorry for all the suffering he had caused the people, and he told the angel, “Stop! They have suffered enough.” This happened at the threshing place that belonged to Araunah the Jebusite.
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ka shuŋi malaika fanɛ e ya mur Jerusalɛm na, nɛ kuwɔr naŋ pɛ mo nɛ e chɛrga mbe nfɛra a yɔ basa na be kasogberge be kaplɛa so nseŋ kaŋɛ malaika nɛ e bee mɔ bumo na le: “K nyalɛ loŋ, Lara fo enɔ ashi bumo be asheŋ to!” Kumo be jemanɛ na nɛ Malaika na teŋ fo Aruna nɛ e shi Jerusalɛm na be kugooro na ase.

english_verse: David saw the Lord's angel in the air, holding a sword over Jerusalem. He and the leaders of Israel, who were all wearing sackcloth, bowed with their faces to the ground,
translation_verse: Deevid ka wu malaika na ka wɔ esoso ŋ keta mbe tokobi nɛ e mur Jerusalɛm na, nɛ mo nɛ Israɛl be bejuŋkparpoana nɛ b buu kagbenejijaso be asɔbuuso na tɔr epun so n dese kasawule.

english_verse: The Lord's angel told the prophet Gad to tell David that he must go to Araunah's threshing place and build an altar in honor of the Lord.
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be malaika na kaŋɛ Gad fanɛ e ya kaŋɛ ewura Deevid le: “Yɔ Aruna be kugooro nɛ baa bri asɔ na so n ya pɔr bɔrɛsure n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.”

english_verse: Araunah and his four sons were threshing wheat at the time, and when they saw the angel, the four sons ran to hide.
translation_verse: Aruna nɛ mbe mbinyɛnsobi ana ka wɔ kugooro na so a bri ayu nseŋ wu malaika na, nɛ mbe mbinyɛnsobi na shile n ya ŋana.

english_verse: Just then, David arrived, and when Araunah saw him, he stopped his work and bowed down.
translation_verse: Aruna ka wu ewura Deevid ka bee ba mo kutɔ na, nɛ e lar kugooro na so n ya gbir kasawule Deevid be anishito ŋ kur mbe kumu n yuu to.

english_verse: David said, “Would you sell me your threshing place, so I can build an altar on it to the Lord? Then this disease will stop killing the people. I'm willing to pay whatever you say it's worth.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura Deevid kaŋɛ mo le: “M ba nna nɛ m ba tɔ fo kugooro ere m pɔr bɔrɛsure n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, saŋɛ na so e beeŋ ju aleblawu ere ashi anyi so. Meeŋ tɔ kumo kanaŋkama nɛ feeŋ fa kumo.”

english_verse: Araunah answered, “Take it, Your Majesty, and do whatever you want with it. I'll even give you the oxen for the sacrifice and the wheat for the grain sacrifice. And you can use the threshing-boards for the fire. It's all yours!”
translation_verse: Nɛ Aruna kaŋɛ le: “Yiramu! Ta kumo n wora kusɔ kama nɛ kepar fo n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na. Ana gba nde! Feeŋ tiŋ n ta amo n lara sarga bɔrɛsure na so nseŋ ta ndibi nɛ b kɔ a bri ayu na malɛ m puga edɛ nseŋ ta ayu malɛ n lara ajibi be sarga. Amo kikɛ la feya nna.”

english_verse: David built an altar and offered sacrifices to please the Lord and sacrifices to ask his blessing. David prayed, and the Lord answered him by sending fire down on the altar.
translation_verse: E daŋ pɔr bɔrɛsure ndoŋ nna n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nseŋ lara esarga chɔɔso nɛ kɔnɔkoŋwuleso be esarga, nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ shin nɛ edɛ shi esoso m ba chɔɔ sarga na ashi bɔrɛsure na so.

english_verse: When David saw that the Lord had answered his prayer, he offered more sacrifices there at the threshing place,
translation_verse: Ewura Deevid ka wu malaika na ka wora loŋ a ŋini fanɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nu mbe kekule na, nɛ e naŋ lara esarga n ti so n sa Enyɛnpe na ashi Aruna be kugooro na so.

english_verse: because he was afraid of the angel's sword and did not want to go all the way to Gibeon. That's where the sacred tent that Moses had made in the desert was kept, as well as the altar where sacrifices were offered to the Lord.
translation_verse: ama ewura Deevid bre daa maŋ tiŋ n yɔ ndoŋ n ya bunyaŋ Ebɔrɛ ŋkpal e ka daa ŋana Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be malaika na be tokobi na so.

english_verse: David said, “The temple of the Lord God must be built right here at this threshing place. And the altar for offering sacrifices will also be here.” David Prepares To Build the Temple
translation_verse: Amoso le nɛ ewura Deevid daŋ kaŋɛ: “Kugooro ere so nfe ashi Jerusalɛm nɛ baaŋ pɔr Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be bɔrɛlambu na, nɛ bɔrɛsure nɛ Israɛlebi beeŋ baa lara esarga kumo so na gba e baa wɔ nfe.” B ka wora bɔrɛlambu na be kepɔr be shiriya be asheŋ

english_verse: David ordered the foreigners living in Israel to come to Jerusalem. Then he assigned some to cut blocks of stone for building the temple.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal loŋ so ewura Deevid daŋ shin nɛ befɔ nɛ b wɔ Israɛl na kikɛ daŋ ba shɛr Jerusalɛm nna, nɛ e shin nɛ bumo be beko bee kuya ajembu be ebirkesi nɛ a shishi nɛ b pɔr bɔrɛlambu na.

english_verse: He also brought an endless supply of cedar logs from the cities of Sidon and Tyre.
translation_verse: E daŋ ŋ kla nna n shoŋi Tayɛ nɛ Sidɔn be basa nɛ b bar mo sida be ndibi damta.

english_verse: He said, “The temple for the Lord must be great, so that everyone in the world will know about it. But since my son Solomon is young and has no experience, I will make sure that everything is ready for the temple to be built.” That's why David did all these things before he died. David Instructs Solomon To Build the Temple
translation_verse: Le nɛ ewura Deevid daŋ kaŋɛ: “Bɔrɛlambu nɛ m pibinyɛn Sɔlɔmɔn beeŋ pɔr na beeŋ baa walɛ m baŋ so nɛ durnya kikɛ e nu kumo be asheŋ.
