english_verse: That night the king could not sleep, and he had a servant read him the records of what had happened since he had been king.
translation_verse: Kanyɛ ka biri nɛ ewura na di ŋ gben, nseŋ shin nɛ b bar mbe efuli na so be asheŋ nɛ a wora mbe kuwurji be jemanɛ so nɛ b sibɛ amo n wɔtɔ nwɔl to na kikɛ, m baa kaa kraŋ a ŋini mo.

english_verse: the king asked, “What has been done to reward Mordecai for this?” “Nothing, Your Majesty!” the king's servants replied.
translation_verse: Nɛ ewura na bishi bumo le: “Mɔdikaya ka wora le ere bre, manɛ be kakɔka nɛ kemaŋkura bre nɛ an sa mo n tal to?” Nɛ mbe nyɛrbi na yɛ: “B maŋ wora shɛŋ n sa mo.”

english_verse: About this time, Haman came in to ask the king to have Mordecai hanged on the gallows he had built. The king saw him and asked, “Who is that man waiting in front of the throne room?”
translation_verse: Loŋ be jemanɛ so nɛ Heman baŋ ba luri ewurkpa nɛ e ba kule ewura ekpa n ya shin nɛ b chɛ Mɔdikaya efɔl n shiga kedibi nɛ e yuu na so. Nɛ ewura bishi le: “Wanɛ e wɔ lambu to ere?”

english_verse: The king's servants answered, “Your Majesty, it is Haman.” “Tell him to come in,” the king commanded.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ mbe nyɛrbi na kaŋɛ: “Heman nna.” Nɛ ewura na kaŋɛ: “Men shin nɛ e baa luri.”

english_verse: When Haman entered the room, the king asked him, “What should I do for a man I want to honor?” Haman was sure that he was the one the king wanted to honor.
translation_verse: Heman ka luri nɛ ewura na bishi mo le: “Manɛ e daga ŋ ka wora n sa esa nɛ mee sha keta n yili bunyaŋ be eyilikpa?” Nɛ Heman fɛ le: “M baa nyi geeŋ fanɛ ma nɛ ewura bee sha kewora le be kusɔ ere n sa na.”

english_verse: So he replied, “Your Majesty, if you wish to honor a man,

english_verse: The king replied, “Hurry and do just what you have said! Don't forget a thing. Get the robe and the horse for Mordecai the Jew, who serves as one of the king's officials!”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura na kaŋɛ Heman le: “Kumo ere wora manaŋ n ya fin piŋi na nɛ gbaŋɛ na m ba wora kusɔ nɛ fo kaŋɛ ere gbagba n sa Mɔdikaya nɛ e la Juw na. Mo e naa chena ewurkpa be kabunagboŋ na ase na. Nyiŋi n wora kusɔ kama nɛ fo kaŋɛ ere n sa mo nsaa maaŋ teŋ shɛŋ so.”

english_verse: Haman got the king's robe and put it on Mordecai. He led him through the city on the horse and shouted as he went, “This is how the king honors a man!”

translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ ewura Sɛgsis ta Heman nɛ e la Juwebi bumo doŋ na be kapetɛ kikɛ n sa ewurche Ɛsta kumo kamɔnchɛ kikɛ. Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ɛsta kaŋɛ ewura na kananɛ mo nɛ Mɔdikaya be kekurgeto lar kikɛ. Kumo be kamɔnchɛ nɛ ewura ta Mɔdikaya ŋ ki mbe ekrachi nimuso na be eko.

english_verse: They were written in the name of King Xerxes and sealed with his ring. Then they were taken by messengers who rode the king's finest and fastest horses.

translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Mɔdikaya ta kuwurpiŋi lela ko nɛ k la buru nɛ kefuful be weato m buu nseŋ ta ago be piŋi peper kunɔkunɔ m buu n deŋi kumo so, n ta shuwa be kuwurwuro nyɛkpɛso m buu nseŋ lar ewurkpa n yɔ. english_verse: In every province and city where the law was sent, the Jews had parties and celebrated. Many of the people in the provinces accepted the Jewish religion, because they were now afraid of the Jews.

english_verse: The first law that the king had made was to be followed on the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month. This was the very day that the enemies of the Jews had hoped to do away with them. But the Jews turned things around,

english_verse: Everyone in the provinces knew that the king had promoted him and had given him a lot of power.

english_verse: Later that day, someone told the king how many people had been killed in Susa.
translation_verse: Kumo be kamɔnchɛ gbagba nɛ b kaŋɛ ewura basa nɛ b mɔ ashi Susa be kade to.

english_verse: Then he told Esther, “Five hundred people, including Haman's ten sons, have been killed in Susa alone. If that many were killed here, what must have happened in the provinces? Is there anything else you want done? Just tell me, and it will be done.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura na kaŋɛ ewurche Ɛsta le: “Basa alfa anu nɛ Juwebi na mɔ ashi Susa be kade to gbagba. Heman be mbinyɛnbi kudu kikɛ daŋ ti bumo so. Kusɔ nɛ b naŋ wora ma efuli na be mba nɛ a ka na bre m maŋ nyi. Manɛ nɛ fo naa sha ŋ ka naŋ wora n sa fo? Kaŋɛ ma! Meeŋ wora kusɔ kama nɛ fee sha n sa fo.”

english_verse: Esther answered, “Your Majesty, please let the Jews in Susa fight to defend themselves tomorrow, just as they did today. And order the bodies of Haman's ten sons to be hanged in public.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Ɛsta kaŋɛ mo le: “Yiramu, nɛ k par fo bre, fo naŋ shin nɛ Juwebi na e wora kusɔ nɛ b wora kabre ashi Susa ere echefo gba, nseŋ shin nɛ b chɛ Heman be mbinyɛnsobi kudu na be kebuni efɔl n shiga ndibi nɛ b yuu na so.”

english_verse: On the thirteenth day of Adar, the Jews in the provinces had come together to defend themselves. They killed
translation_verse: Kufɔl nɛ baa tre Adar na be nchɛ kuduasa na nɛ loŋ daŋ wora. Kachɛ kuduanasopo na bre, b daa maŋ mɔ basa. B daŋ ta loŋ be kachɛ na nna ŋ ki kagbenefuli nɛ kejigboŋ be kachɛ.

english_verse: On the fifteenth day of the month the Jews in Susa held a holiday and celebrated, after killing their enemies on the thirteenth and the fourteenth.
translation_verse: Juwebi nɛ b wɔ Susa na bre daŋ ta kufɔl na be nchɛ kuduanu na nna ŋ ki kagbenefuli nɛ kejigboŋ nɛ kewushiachɛ ŋkpal manɛ so bumo ere daŋ mɔ bumo doŋana nchɛ kuduasa nɛ kuduana na nna.

english_verse: This is why the Jews in the villages now celebrate on the fourteenth day of the month. It is a joyful holiday that they celebrate by feasting and sending gifts of food to each other. The Festival of Purim
translation_verse: Amoso nɛ Juwebi nɛ b wɔ ndekarso na yili kufɔl nɛ baa tre Adar na be nchɛ kuduana na fanɛ kagbenefuli nɛ kejigboŋ be kewushiachɛ nɛ kachɛ nɛ baa chige abar ajibi na.

english_verse: Mordecai wrote down everything that had happened. Then he sent letters to the Jews everywhere in the provinces
translation_verse: Mɔdikaya daŋ sibɛ kusɔ kama nɛ k wora na kikɛ n wɔtɔ kawɔl to, nseŋ sa Juwebi nɛ b wɔ ewura Sɛgsis be efuli so na kikɛ nwɔl na,

english_verse: and told them: Each year you must celebrate on both the fourteenth and the fifteenth of Adar,
translation_verse: fanɛ kufɔl nɛ baa tre Adar na be nchɛ kuduana nɛ kuduanu na e baa la nchɛgboŋ kafɛ kikɛ to n sa bumo.

english_verse: the days when we Jews defeated our enemies. Remember this month as a time when our sorrow was turned to joy, and celebration took the place of crying. Celebrate by having parties and by giving to the poor and by sharing gifts of food with each other.
translation_verse: Le be nchɛ ere nɛ Juwebi na daŋ pɔɔ bumo doŋana so nɛ bumo kagbenejija ki kagbenefuli na. E daŋ kaŋɛ bumo nna fanɛ b ta loŋ be nchɛ na nna ŋ ki kejigboŋ nɛ ajibi be kedaŋɛ n chige abar nɛ betirpo.

english_verse: They followed Mordecai's instructions and set aside these two days every year as a time of celebration. The Reason for the Festival of Purim
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Juwebi na shuli n sɔ kusɔ kama nɛ Mɔdikaya sibɛ n sa bumo na, nseŋ ta loŋ be nchɛ na ŋ ki nchɛgboŋ kafɛ kikɛ to.

english_verse: Haman was the son of Hammedatha and a descendant of Agag. He hated the Jews so much that he planned to destroy them, but he wanted to find out the best time to do it. So he cast lots.
translation_verse: Hammedaata nɛ e shi Agag be kanaŋ to na pibinyɛn Heman nɛ e la Juwebi bumo doŋ na e daŋ to beri m fin kachɛ nɛ k daga b ka mɔ Juwebi na kikɛ.

english_verse: Esther went to King Xerxes and asked him to save her people. Then the king gave written orders for Haman and his sons to be punished in the same terrible way that Haman had in mind for the Jews. So they were hanged.
translation_verse: Nɛ Ɛsta yɔ ewura kutɔ nɛ ewura na shin nɛ b sibɛ mbra nɛ k shin nɛ kusɔ nɛ Heman kre fanɛ e beeŋ wora Juwebi na laŋɛ n ji mo. Nɛ b chɛ mo nɛ mbe mbinyɛnsobi kikɛ efɔl n shiga ndibi nɛ b yuu na so.

english_verse: Mordecai's letter had said that the Jews must celebrate for two days because of what had happened to them. This time of celebration is called Purim, which is the Hebrew word for the lots that were cast.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal kawɔl nɛ Mɔdikaya sibɛ na so, nɛ ŋkpal kusɔ nɛ k wora Juwebi na so, b daa tre nchɛgboŋ na Purim nna. Kumo be kifito e la keto beri.

english_verse: Now every year the Jews set aside these two days for having parties and celebrating, just as they were told to do.
translation_verse: Juwebi na yili kumo nna fanɛ bumo nɛ bumo nanabiana kikɛ nɛ esa kama nɛ e beeŋ ba ki Juw be esa kachako so, beeŋ baa ji loŋ be nchɛgboŋ anyɔ na fanɛ kananɛ Mɔdikaya kaŋɛ bumo na gbagba.

english_verse: Queen Esther, daughter of Abihail, wanted to give full authority to Mordecai's letter about the Festival of Purim, and with his help she wrote a letter about the feast.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewurche Ɛsta nɛ e la Abihail pibiche na nɛ Mɔdikaya cha abar n sibɛ kawɔl kpakpaso ko nɛ k kɔ ewurche na be eleŋ na ti kawɔl nɛ Mɔdikaya teŋ sibɛ a laŋɛ nchɛgboŋ nɛ baa tre Purim na so.

english_verse: You and your descendants must always remember to celebrate Purim at the time and in the way that we have said. You must also follow the instructions that we have given you about mourning and going without eating.
translation_verse: nsaa nyiŋi Juwebi na nɛ bumo nanabiana fanɛ b baa nyiŋi a ji nchɛgboŋ nɛ baa tre Purim na fanɛ kananɛ baa ji ekishi nɛ nli be nchɛgboŋ na. Mɔdikaya nɛ ewurche Ɛsta e daŋ yili le be kesheŋ ere n sa bumo.

english_verse: These laws about Purim are written by the authority of Queen Esther.
translation_verse: Ewurche Ɛsta be eleŋ so nɛ b wora nchɛgboŋ nɛ baa tre Purim na be mbra n nase kanyiŋi be nwɔl to.

english_verse: King Xerxes made everyone in his kingdom pay taxes, even those in lands across the sea.
translation_verse: Ewura Sɛgsis yili lampo nna n sa basa nɛ b tase teku ase nɛ bumo nɛ b maŋ tase teku ase ashi mbe efuli so kikɛ.

english_verse: All the great and famous things that King Xerxes did are written in the record books of the kings of Media and Persia. These records also tell about the honors that the king gave to Mordecai.
translation_verse: B sibɛ kananɛ e ji eleŋ mbe kuwura to nɛ kananɛ e maŋ Mɔdikaya so n yili eyilikpagboŋ kikɛ n wɔtɔ Pɛshiya nɛ Midia be efuliana so be bewura be adrasheŋ be nwɔl kikɛ to nna.

english_verse: Next to the king himself, Mordecai was the highest official in the kingdom. He was a popular leader of the Jews, because he helped them in many ways and would even speak to the king on their behalf.
translation_verse: Mɔdikaya e daa la enimu m bɛ ewura Sɛgsis so. E daa la esagboŋ nna Juwebi na kutɔ nɛ b daa sha mbe asheŋ ga ŋkpal e ka daŋ chɛ bumo to nsaa malga a sɔ bumo a yige so.

english_verse: Many years ago, a man named Job lived in the land of Uz. He was a truly good person, who respected God and refused to do evil.
translation_verse: Kanyɛn ko e daa wɔ Uz be kasawule so nɛ baa tre mo Job. Job daa la esa nɛ esa kikɛ maŋ tiŋ n wu mo kulubi nna. E daa la esa nɛ e bee bunyaŋ Ebɔrɛ nseŋ kishi kulubi be kewora nna.

english_verse: the Lord asked, “Satan, where have you been?” Satan replied, “I have been going all over the earth.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ bishi Setani le: “Nnɛ nɛ fo shi! Manɛ nɛ fo daa wora?” Nɛ Setani kaŋɛ: “N na a kulti durnya kikɛ to nna.”

english_verse: Job's sons took turns having feasts in their homes, and they always invited their three sisters to join in the eating and drinking.
translation_verse: Job be bibinyɛn ashunu na daa wora kejigboŋ bumo be elaŋana to kebɛso kebɛso nna nsaa tre bumo sipocheana besa na nɛ baa ba m ba kaa tu bumo a ji nsaa nuu.

english_verse: After each feast, Job would send for his children and perform a ceremony, as a way of asking God to forgive them of any wrongs they may have done. He would get up early the next morning and offer a sacrifice for each of them, just in case they had sinned or silently cursed God. Angels, the Lord, and Satan
translation_verse: Mbia na baŋ ji kejigboŋ ŋklade kachipurso kikɛ, Job beeŋ shuŋi n tre bumo m ba lara esarga chɔɔso n sa Ebɔrɛ ŋ kule alubi be ketampaŋ n sa mbia na, a fɛ fanɛ ashere b kaa bee ji nsaa nuu na b wora kulubi ko n da Ebɔrɛ so nɛ b maŋ nyi. Sososo be kewora ŋ keni nɛ k ba Job so be asheŋ

english_verse: One day, when the angels had gathered around the Lord, and Satan was there with them,
translation_verse: Kachako nɛ Ebɔrɛ be emalaika ba shɛr Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kutɔ ashi ebɔrɛso nɛ Setani gba ba ti bumo so ndoŋ.

english_verse: Then the Lord asked, “What do you think of my servant Job? No one on earth is like him—he is a truly good person, who respects me and refuses to do evil.”
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na naŋ bishi Setani le: “Manɛ nɛ fee fɛ a laŋɛ ma kayɛrbi Job be kaplɛa so? Durnya kikɛ to, esa kikɛ maŋ du fanɛ mo. Ŋkpal manɛ so, e la esa nɛ esa maaŋ tiŋ n wu mo kulubi nna. Mo alɛ bee bunyaŋ Ebɔrɛ nseŋ kishi kulubi be kewora nna.”

english_verse: “You are like a wall protecting not only him, but his entire family and all his property. You make him successful in whatever he does, and his flocks and herds are everywhere.
translation_verse: Jemanɛ kikɛ fee kuŋ mo nɛ mbe kanaŋ nɛ kusɔ kama nɛ e kɔ nna nseŋ naa shin nɛ kusɔ kama nɛ e bee wora bee nyalɛ a sa mo, hale nɛ mbe mbolpɔ nɛ ana salga to n sɔ kaplɛkama.

english_verse: Try taking away everything he owns, and he will curse you to your face.”
translation_verse: To, fo ere e mur mbe kusɔ nɛ e kɔ kikɛ ŋ keni a, e maaŋ yili fo gbagba be anishito n shoduu fo?”

english_verse: The Lord replied, “All right, Satan, do what you want with anything that belongs to him, but don't harm Job.” Then Satan left. Job Loses Everything
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ Setani le: “Yoo, n ta kusɔ kama nɛ e kɔ m bɔɔ fo enɔ, ama sa maŋ kaŋ doro Job gbagba bre.” Nɛ Setani lar Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kutɔ n choŋ. Job be kusɔ nɛ e kɔ kikɛ ka mur be asheŋ

english_verse: Job's sons and daughters were having a feast in the home of his oldest son,
translation_verse: Kachako nɛ Job be bibinyɛn ashunu nɛ bumo sipocheana besa na yaŋ wora kejigboŋ a ji nsaa nuu ashi Job be wurkoŋ be laŋ to.

english_verse: when someone rushed up to Job and said, “While your servants were plowing with your oxen, and your donkeys were nearby eating grass,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nɛ nna kabɔ ko ber to m ba Job kutɔ m ba kaŋɛ mo le: “An daa kɔ ana na nna a dɔ nɛ ekurma na malɛ wɔ kupuŋ to m mata anyi a ji.

english_verse: a gang of Sabeans attacked and stole the oxen and donkeys! Your other servants were killed, and I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: Epul na to nɛ Sabiaebi ko ba lar anyi so m mɔ beshumpo na nseŋ kpa ana nɛ ekurma na kikɛ n choŋ. N nawule e tiŋ n nya n shile m ba nɛ m ba kaŋɛ fo kusɔ nɛ k wora.”

english_verse: That servant was still speaking, when a second one came running and said, “God sent down a fire that killed your sheep and your servants. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: Kabɔ na kraa malga nna nɛ enyɔsopo shile m ba kaŋɛ le: “Bɔrɛ nyɛkpɛ nna m ponte mbolpɔ na nɛ mbolpɔkpapoana na m mɔ. N nawule e nya n shile m ba nɛ m ba kaŋɛ fo kusɔ nɛ k wora.”

english_verse: Before that servant finished speaking, a third one raced up and said, “Three gangs of Chaldeans attacked and stole your camels! All of your other servants were killed, and I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: Mo alɛ gba kraa malga nna nɛ kabɔ sasopo ba kaŋɛ Job le: “Beyu nɛ b kɔ akɔsɔ be ntuŋ asa shi Babilɔn be efuli so nɛ k wɔ kelargato be esoso be epeŋilarkpa na nna m ba kɔ n suge fo enyɔma na nseŋ kpa amo kikɛ n choŋ. N nawule e nya n shile m ba nɛ m ba kaŋɛ fo kusɔ nɛ k wora.”

english_verse: That servant was still speaking, when a fourth one dashed up and said, “Your children were having a feast and drinking wine at the home of your oldest son,
translation_verse: Loŋ be kabɔ na gba kraa malga nna nɛ enasopo shile m ba kaŋɛ le: “Fo mbia daŋ wora kejigboŋ nna a ji nsaa nuu ashi fo wurkoŋ be laŋ to

english_verse: when suddenly a windstorm from the desert blew the house down, crushing all of your children. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: nɛ bɔrɛfugboŋ ko ber n shi keshishɛrsawule so epul to m ba da kowu na n lɛ fo mbia na kikɛ so m mɔ. N nawule e nya n shile m ba nɛ ba kaŋɛ fo kusɔ nɛ k wora.”

english_verse: When Job heard this, he tore his clothes and shaved his head because of his great sorrow. He knelt on the ground, then worshiped God
translation_verse: Job ka nu le be asheŋ ere kikɛ, nɛ e pɛ mbe asɔbuuso ŋ kpɛa to nseŋ she mbe kumu so be emin kikɛ ŋkpal kagbenejija damta nɛ k tɔr mo so na so. Kumo be kaman nɛ e gbir m bunyaŋ Ebɔrɛ

english_verse: and said: “We bring nothing at birth; we take nothing with us at death. The Lord alone gives and takes. Praise the name of the Lord!”
translation_verse: nseŋ kaŋɛ le: “B ka kurge ma m ba durnya to, m maaŋ bar shɛŋ. Ŋ ka naŋ wu a lar durnya to, m maaŋ ta shɛŋ n lar. Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e sa, mo alɛ e sɔ; Kemaŋkura e baa la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ peya!”

english_verse: In spite of everything, Job did not sin or accuse God of doing wrong.
translation_verse: Asheŋ nɛ e wora ere kikɛ to, Job daa maŋ wora kulubi m malga ŋ gbiti Ebɔrɛ.

english_verse: When the angels gathered around the Lord again, Satan was there with them,
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ be emalaika ka naŋ ba shɛr Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be anishito ashi ebɔrɛso, nɛ Setani gba naŋ ba tu bumo n shɛr ndoŋ.

english_verse: and the Lord asked, “Satan, where have you been?” Satan replied, “I have been going all over the earth.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na bishi Setani le: “Nnɛ nɛ fo shi! Manɛ nɛ fo daa wora?” Nɛ Setani kaŋɛ: “N na a kulti durnya kikɛ to nna.”

english_verse: Then the Lord asked, “What do you think of my servant Job? No one on earth is like him—he is a truly good person, who respects me and refuses to do evil. And he hasn't changed, even though you persuaded me to destroy him for no reason.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na naŋ bishi mo: “Manɛ nɛ fee fɛ a laŋɛ ma kayɛrbi Job be kaplɛa so? Durnya kikɛ to esa kama maŋ du fanɛ mo. E la esa nɛ esa maaŋ tiŋ n wu mo kulubi nna nɛ mo alɛ bee bunyaŋ Ebɔrɛ nseŋ kishi kulubi be kewora. Fo ka kule ma ekpa n ya mur mbe asɔ kikɛ, nɛ e maŋ wora shɛŋ gba na, e kraa maŋ chɛrga mbe kebaawɔtɔ to.”

english_verse: Satan answered, “There's no pain like your own. People will do anything to stay alive.
translation_verse: Nɛ Setani kaŋɛ Ebɔrɛ le: “Esa shuli e ka paŋ asɔ nɛ e kɔ kikɛ nsaa kɔ mbe ŋkpa a wɔtɔ.

english_verse: Try striking Job's own body with pain, and he will curse you to your face.”
translation_verse: Fo ere e ta kayurnyaŋ n lɛ Job so ŋ keni, e beeŋ yili fo gbagba be anishito n shoduu fo.”

english_verse: “All right!” the Lord replied. “Make Job suffer as much as you want, but just don't kill him.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ malɛ naŋ kaŋɛ le: “To, n nu! Feeŋ tiŋ n shin nɛ kayurnyaŋ e tɔr Job so nɛ e ji awurfoŋ kananɛ fee sha, ama sa maŋ kaŋ mɔ mo bre!”

english_verse: Then Job sat on the ash-heap to show his sorrow. And while he was scraping his sores with a broken piece of pottery,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Job lar n ya chena kumuni so nseŋ ta kapɛlanfu a kuti mbe achuu na to.

english_verse: his wife asked, “Why do you still trust God? Why don't you curse him and die?”
translation_verse: Nɛ mbe eche ba kaŋɛ mo: “Manɛ nna nɛ fo kraŋ yirda Ebɔrɛ ashi awurfoŋ nɛ fee ji ere kikɛ to? Shoduu mo nseŋ wu nɛ k loge!”

english_verse: Job replied, “Don't talk like a fool! If we accept blessings from God, we must accept trouble as well.” In all that happened, Job never once said anything against God. Job's Three Friends
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Job kaŋɛ mbe eche le: “Sa maa malga fanɛ ewulpo! Nɛ anyeeŋ sɔ Ebɔrɛ be nɛfa nɛ enɔgboŋ anyɔ, manɛ nna nɛ anyi maaŋ sɔ etɔrɔ bre mo kutɔ?” Asheŋ ere kikɛ to, Job maŋ malga ŋ gbiti Ebɔrɛ fanɛ e maŋ wora n nyalɛ. Job mo teriana besa na be asheŋ

english_verse: When they came near enough to see Job, they could hardly recognize him. And in their great sorrow, they tore their clothes, then sprinkled dust on their heads and cried bitterly.
translation_verse: B kraa wɔ kufɔ kufɔ nna nseŋ wu Job, ama b daa maŋ pin mo. B ka ba pin fanɛ Job nna nɛ b fara a shu a boŋ to awɔrso nseŋ kpɛa bumo be asɔbuuso to nsaa wora eshishɛr a wurge bumo be amu so a ŋini fanɛ bumo be ŋgbene jija bumo.

english_verse: For seven days and nights, they sat silently on the ground beside him, because they realized what terrible pain he was in.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ b ya tu Job n chena kasawule nchɛ ashunu nɛ nnyɛ ashunu nɛ ekama maa bugi kɔnɔ a kaŋɛ shɛŋ, ŋkpal awurfoŋ gboŋgboŋi nɛ b wu e ka bee ji so.

english_verse: Finally, Job cursed the day of his birth
translation_verse: Kumo be lalaloge nɛ Job fara m malga n shoduu mbe kakurgeachɛ ŋ kaŋɛ Ebɔrɛ le:

english_verse: Blot out the day of my birth and the night when my parents created a son.
translation_verse: O Ebɔrɛ, sho kachɛ nɛ b kurge ma na kɔnɔ, nseŋ shoduu kanyɛ nɛ n nio sɔ ma kedampo na gba!

english_verse: Erase that night from the calendar and conceal it with darkness.
translation_verse: Lara loŋ be kanyɛ na ashi kafɛ be nchɛ to, nsaa maŋ naŋ shin nɛ b karga kumo n ti nchɛ so.

english_verse: because it let me be born into a world of trouble. Why Didn't I Die at Birth?
translation_verse: Sho kanyɛ nɛ b kurge ma na kɔnɔ ŋkpal k ka shin nɛ b kurge n wɔtɔ durnya nɛ etɔrɔ bɔlɔ kumo to ere so.

english_verse: Why was I accepted and allowed to nurse at my mother's breast?
translation_verse: Manɛ nna nɛ n nio ta ma n deŋi mbe aya so, nseŋ sa ma mbe kenyipo nɛ n nyipo?

english_verse: Now I would be at peace in the silent world below
translation_verse: N daŋ wu n laŋɛ nna, ndafanɛ n daa beeŋ ya tu

english_verse: with kings and their advisors whose palaces lie in ruins,
translation_verse: bewura nɛ benimuana nɛ b wu nseŋ ka bumo be ewurkpaana nɛ nwugboŋ nɛ a bure a dese na.

english_verse: I wish I had been born dead and then buried, never to see the light of day.
translation_verse: ŋko n ya dese nchaŋ to fanɛ kebia nɛ b kurge nɛ e laŋɛ nsaa maŋ wu kananɛ karechɛ du na.

english_verse: In the world of the dead, the wicked and the weary rest without a worry. *
translation_verse: Basa lubi maŋ naa tiŋ a wora asheŋ lubi nchaŋ to, basa nɛ b shuŋ ŋ gben malɛ bee nya a wushi ndoŋ nna.

english_verse: where captives and slaves are free at last. Why Does God Let Me Live?
translation_verse: Basa nɛ b kɔ atre nɛ bebɔlpo kikɛ wɔ ndoŋ nna. Anya gba nya bumo be amu ndoŋ.

english_verse: Why does God let me live when life is miserable and so bitter?
translation_verse: Manɛ nna nɛ Ebɔrɛ shin nɛ n wɔ ŋkpa to, saŋɛ nɛ kebaawɔtɔ du kekekra le ere?

english_verse: I keep longing for death more than I would seek a valuable treasure.
translation_verse: Ma ere bee sha luwu ga a chɔ keta kenishipere n fin yawu kpakpaso be asɔ, ama luwu malɛ maa ba.

english_verse: Nothing could make me happier than to be in the grave.
translation_verse: Shɛŋ shɛŋ maaŋ tiŋ n fuli ma kagbene a chɔ kewu n yɔ nchaŋ to.

english_verse: Why do I go on living when God has me surrounded, and I can't see the road?
translation_verse: Manɛ nna nɛ ŋ kraa wɔ ŋkpa to, jemanɛ nɛ Ebɔrɛ nawule nyi kananɛ ma kebaawɔtɔ beeŋ baa du echefoso?

english_verse: Moaning and groaning are my food and drink,
translation_verse: Ma keji nɛ kenuu e ki ebɔl to nɛ kagbene to be kushu na.

english_verse: and my worst fears have all come true.
translation_verse: Asheŋ nɛ mee ŋana ga na kikɛ e ki kashenteŋ na.

english_verse: I have no peace or rest— only troubles and worries.
translation_verse: M maŋ kɔ kagbenewushi ŋko ewushi kikɛ ma kebaawɔtɔ to, she etɔrɔ nɛ kagbenekuu damta nawule.

english_verse: Please be patient and listen to what I have to say. *
translation_verse: “Job, jande nya kanyiti n sa ma nseŋ nu kusɔ nɛ mee sha kekaŋɛ ere.

english_verse: In my experience, only those who plant seeds of evil harvest trouble,
translation_verse: Kusɔ nɛ ma ere nyi e la fanɛ basa nɛ baa du kulubi bumo be amu to nɛ k bee kɔr.

english_verse: and then they are swept away by the angry breath of God.
translation_verse: Kananɛ bɔrɛfu bee jija asɔ na, aloŋ nɛ Ebɔrɛ bee nya agbo a mur bumo.

english_verse: They may roar and growl like powerful lions. But when God breaks their teeth,
translation_verse: Kumu kpakpaso wuraana bee kaa ponte to fanɛ ebuluŋ nna, ama Ebɔrɛ e naa buri bumo be anyii nɛ bumo be nnɔ bee lo.

english_verse: A secret was told to me in a faint whisper—
translation_verse: Esa ko daŋ kuli ŋ kaŋɛ ma ashiri ko; e daa maŋ malga kumo awɔrso.

english_verse: I was overcome by sleep, but disturbed by dreams;
translation_verse: N daa maŋ tiŋ n di kamɔnchɛ be kanyɛso; ŋkpal edare bubɔrɔ nɛ n daa ku so.

english_verse: and my hair stood on end, as a wind blew past my face.
translation_verse: Kebuniyoyu ko e daŋ lar ma so nɛ kufu pɛ ma ga hale nɛ awo bibi dii ma.

english_verse: It stopped and stood still. Then a form appeared— a shapeless form. And from the silence, I heard a voice say,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ kebuniyoyu na pɛ afu n yili diim, a maŋ naa gbegber to nɛ m pɛshɛ kumo lee, ma alɛ maŋ pin kusɔ nɛ k la. Kumo be kaman nɛ n nu ebɔl ko ka kaŋɛ le:

english_verse: “No humans are innocent in the eyes of God their Creator.
translation_verse: ‘Edimɛdi kikɛ maŋ niŋi Ebɔrɛ nɛ e to bumo na be anishito.

english_verse: He finds fault with his servants and even with his angels.
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ maa yirda mbe emalaika nɛ baa shuŋ mo ebɔrɛso na gba.

english_verse: Humans are formed from clay and are fragile as moths, so what chance do you have?
translation_verse: Edimɛdi nɛ b maa chɛr nsaa wu fanɛ kananɛ kapuya maa chɛr nsaa bure na nɛ e beeŋ tiŋ n yirda a?

english_verse: Your tent pegs are pulled up, and you leave this life, having gained no wisdom.”
translation_verse: Dimɛdi be ŋkpa maa chɛr kelar mo to, Ebɔrɛ baŋ lara efute na, epul to nɛ e wu, nɛ k daa maŋ daga fanɛ e wu.’ ”

english_verse: Job, call out for help and see if an angel comes!
translation_verse: “Job, shu n fin kechɛto ŋ keni a, malaika ko beeŋ ba chɛ fo to a?

english_verse: Envy and jealousy will kill a stupid fool.
translation_verse: Kayurbesa nɛ kukɔrkɔ e naŋ mɔ ewulpo nɛ e maŋ nyi asheŋ.

english_verse: I have seen fools take root. But God sends a curse, suddenly uprooting them
translation_verse: N wu bewulpo ka yili to nɛnɛ kebaawɔtɔ to, ama kɔnɔsho ka ba bumo nɛ bumo be laŋ to ebi so nɛ asheŋ bri bumo.

english_verse: Then hungry and greedy people gobble up their crops and grab their wealth.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ kejimuni wuraana nɛ basa nɛ akoŋ kɔ ba fuu bumo be adɔjibi nseŋ gbare bumo be mpetɛsɔ ŋ ki bumo peya.

english_verse: Our suffering isn't caused by the failure of crops;
translation_verse: Awurfoŋ nɛ anyee ji maa shi anyi be adɔjibi ka maa wora to.

english_verse: Job, if I were you, I would ask God for help.
translation_verse: Job, nɛ ma e daa la fo, meeŋ ta ma asheŋ m bɔɔ Ebɔrɛ enɔ nɛ e chɛ ma to.

english_verse: His miracles are marvelous, more than we can count.
translation_verse: Anyi maaŋ tiŋ m pin asheŋ nɛ Ebɔrɛ bee wora to. Mo alɛ be emamachisheŋ maŋ kɔ ekar.

english_verse: God sends showers on earth and waters the fields.
translation_verse: Mo e naa shin nɛ bɔrɛ bee ba nɛ adɔsawule bee nya kayul.

english_verse: He protects the sorrowful and lifts up those who have been disgraced. *
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ e naa maŋ bebɔlpo so, nsaa sa basa nɛ baa shu nli kagbenewushi.

english_verse: Darkness is their only companion, hiding their path at noon.
translation_verse: Hale kapiidi gba baa nite nna a la a la a fin ekpa fanɛ b ka na tentembiri to na.

english_verse: God rescues the needy from the words of the wicked and the fist of the mighty.
translation_verse: Ama Ebɔrɛ e naa mɔlga basa nɛ asheŋ tir na ashi kumukpakpaso wuraana be nnɔ to be mmalga nɛ belempo be eleŋ to nɛ belempo be kɔrfɛ to.

english_verse: The poor are filled with hope, and injustice is silenced. Consider Yourself Fortunate
translation_verse: Mo e naa sa betirpo tama a shin nɛ kemaa ji asheŋ nɛ amo be ekpa so bee ba ekar.

english_verse: He may cause injury and pain, but he will bandage and heal your cuts and bruises.
translation_verse: E beeŋ tiŋ m bar doro nɛ ebesa fo so, ama mo alɛ beeŋ naŋ chɔɔ fo achuu nɛ alɔbi na kikɛ n chɛ amo.

english_verse: God will protect you from harm, no matter how often trouble may strike.
translation_verse: Saŋɛ kikɛ Ebɔrɛ beeŋ baa lara fo ashi etɔrɔ damta nɛ a bee bar fo kagbenejija ga ere kikɛ to.

english_verse: In times of war and famine, God will keep you safe.
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ e naŋ kuŋ fo ashi luwu to jemanɛ kikɛ; akoŋgboŋ nɛ kena be jemanɛ gba, fo maaŋ wu.

english_verse: You will be sheltered, without fear of hurtful words or any other weapon.
translation_verse: Mo e naŋ kuŋ fo ashi basa nɛ baa jija fo kutɔ, nseŋ mɔlga fo ashi kemur kama nɛ k bee ba fo so to.

english_verse: You will laugh at the threat of destruction and famine. And you won't be afraid of wild animals—
translation_verse: Kemur nɛ akoŋgboŋ be asheŋ maaŋ tir fo ere. Fo alɛ maaŋ naa ŋana kupuŋ to be asɔbɔya lubi.

english_verse: they will no longer be fierce, and your rocky fields will become friendly.
translation_verse: Fo kudɔsawule maaŋ baa kɔ ajembu nɛ afalta; kupuŋ to be asɔbɔya lubi malɛ maaŋ pɛ fo.

english_verse: Your home will be secure, and your sheep will be safe.
translation_verse: Feeŋ chena fo laŋ to nɛ kagbenewushi, nɛ shɛŋ maaŋ wora fo asɔ nɛ fo kɔ.

english_verse: You will have more descendants than there are blades of grass on the face of the earth.
translation_verse: Fo kamanebi beeŋ baa shi a chɔ afitiri nɛ e wɔ durnya kikɛ to.

english_verse: You will live a very long life, and your body will be strong until the day you die.
translation_verse: Fo ŋkpa beeŋ teŋi so nɛ fo chɛr, fo alɛ beeŋ baa kɔ eleŋ eyurto hale n ya fo kachɛ nɛ feeŋ wu.

english_verse: Our experience has proven these things to be true, so listen and learn.
translation_verse: Job, an dara asheŋ ere nna nseŋ koya amo n chɛr. A la kashenteŋ nna, amoso ta amo n shuŋ fo kebaawɔtɔ to.”

english_verse: They outweigh the sand along the beach, and that's why I have spoken without thinking first.
translation_verse: A shi a chɔ teku ase be shishɛr; amoso nɛ n daa maŋ fɛ nfɛra pɔɛŋ nseŋ malga na.

english_verse: The fearsome arrows of God All-Powerful have filled my soul with their poison.
translation_verse: K du fanɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na ka to atanyembi nna nɛ amo be kebɔr luri ma eyur to. Ebɔrɛ ta kufugboŋ nna n lɛ ma so.

english_verse: Do oxen and wild donkeys cry out in distress unless they are hungry?
translation_verse: Kurma baŋ nya afitiri a ji, kumo be kenishi bee bɔlɔ nna. Kena malɛ gba baŋ nya afitiri wɔlso a we, k maŋ naa shu.

english_verse: What is food without salt? What is more tasteless than the white of an egg?
translation_verse: Esa bee tiŋ n ji ajibi tataso nɛ nfɔl maŋ wɔ amo to a? Ŋko ebel mo e wɔ kefule be kefuful na to?

english_verse: That's how my food tastes, and my appetite is gone. *
translation_verse: Kananɛ ma ajibi du nna, e maŋ wɔ ebel. A maa yɛlga ma gba kuraa.

english_verse: I am not strong as stone or bronze,
translation_verse: M maŋ kɔ eleŋ fanɛ kejembu ŋko danyaŋ peper.

english_verse: and I have finally reached the end of my rope. My Friends, I Am Desperate
translation_verse: M maŋ naa kɔ eleŋ kikɛ nɛ m mɔlga ma kumu; kaplɛkama maŋ wɔtɔ nɛ n yɔ n ya nya kechɛto.

english_verse: My friends, I am desperate, and you should help me, even if I no longer respect God All-Powerful. *
translation_verse: Esa kama nɛ e wɔ le be awurfoŋ to, hale nɛ e maŋ naa kɔ kabɔrɛŋana n sa Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ gba; a daga mo nekpaana ka yili mbe kaman nna a leŋ mo to.

english_verse: like streams that swell with melting snow,
translation_verse: Eshishɛr bee ti loŋ be mbombi na nna nɛ amo be nchu maa shibi,

english_verse: thought they would find water. But they were disappointed,
translation_verse: ama mbombi wɔlso nɛ baa tu, nɛ bumo be tama a loge nɛ aba e pɔ bumo.

english_verse: just as I am with you. Only one look at my suffering, and you run away scared. What Have I Done Wrong?
translation_verse: Menyi alɛ gba du fanɛ loŋ be mbombi na nna na. Men ka ba wu awurfoŋ nɛ mee ji na, nɛ kufu pɛ menyi nɛ menyee fɛ keyige ma n lɛ.

english_verse: Have I ever asked any of you to give me a gift
translation_verse: M maŋ daŋ kule menyi be ekama fanɛ e sa ma kakɛ kikɛ

english_verse: What have I done wrong? Show me, and I will keep quiet.
translation_verse: To, men ŋini ma kulubi nɛ n wora. Meeŋ lo ma kɔnɔ to nseŋ nu menyi kutɔ.

english_verse: The truth is always painful, but your arguments prove nothing.
translation_verse: Kashenteŋ bee besa jemanɛ kikɛ nna, ama kusɔ nɛ menyee kaŋɛ ere maa ŋini shɛŋ.

english_verse: Here I am desperate, and you consider my words as worthless as wind.
translation_verse: Naniere ma kenishi pere nna na, ama menyee ta ma mmalga fanɛ afu fuloŋ nna.

english_verse: Why, you would sell an orphan or your own neighbor!
translation_verse: Menyi ere beeŋ tiŋ m barga amunibi to n sa abar ŋko n fa men nekpaana gba n nya amansherbi!

english_verse: Look me straight in the eye; I won't lie to you.
translation_verse: Men keni ma anishito nɛnɛ, m maaŋ fule ŋko ŋ ku efɛ n sa menyi.

english_verse: Stop accusing me falsely; my reputation is at stake.
translation_verse: Men yige kebaakuu ma kɔnɔ, nɛ manɛ aloŋ, ma ketre beeŋ jija.

english_verse: I know right from wrong, and I am not telling lies.
translation_verse: N nyi kulubi nɛ kelela be mbarga, m maa ku efɛ nna.”

english_verse: Why is life so hard? Why do we suffer?
translation_verse: Manɛ nna nɛ kebaawɔtɔ du kpakpa loŋ? Manɛ nna nɛ anyee ji awurfoŋ loŋ?

english_verse: We are slaves in search of shade; we are laborers longing for our wages.
translation_verse: An du fanɛ anya nɛ baa fin kiyoyul nɛ b chena to n wushi nna; An la beshumpo nɛ anyee jo anyi be kakɔka kenishipereso nna.

english_verse: God has made my days drag on and my nights miserable.
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ shin nɛ ma nchɛ maŋ naa kɔ tɔnɔ n sa ma nɛ kanyɛso bar ma keboltofinfiŋ damta.

english_verse: I pray for night to end, but it stretches out while I toss and turn.
translation_verse: M baŋ dese kanyɛso kikɛ, mee kilgi kelaŋ so nna a kule Ebɔrɛ fanɛ kare e chɛ manaŋ, ama kumo alɛ maa chɛ manaŋ.

english_verse: My parched skin is covered with worms, dirt, and sores,
translation_verse: Achuu nɛ e bee lar nchu nɛ ashushombi e sɔ ma eyur kikɛ so, abibi sɔ ma eyur kikɛ nna.

english_verse: and my days are running out quicker than the thread of a fast-moving needle. Don't Forget!
translation_verse: Ma nchɛ bee duga so manaŋ manaŋ a chɔ kɔrɛ be kekpaltobi be jese.

english_verse: I beg you, God, don't forget! My life is just a breath, and trouble lies ahead.
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ, mee kule fo nna; sa maŋ teŋ ma so! Ma ŋkpa baa du fanɛ afu nna, ma kagbenefuli teŋ fo ekar.

english_verse: I will vanish from sight, and no one, including you, will ever see me again.
translation_verse: Anishi nɛ a bee wu ma kabre ere maaŋ naŋ wu ma kikɛ; Menyeeŋ keni n fin ma, ama m maaŋ naa wɔtɔ.

english_verse: I will disappear in the grave or vanish from sight like a passing cloud.
translation_verse: Kananɛ abɔrɛwɔlpa bee deŋi nsaa choŋ na, a loŋ nɛ basa bee wu nsaa maŋ naa bɛta a ba.

english_verse: Never will I return home; soon I will be forgotten.
translation_verse: Ma alɛ gba maaŋ naŋ bɛta m ba epe, k maaŋ chɛr basa beeŋ teŋ ma so.

english_verse: And so, I cry out to you in agony and distress.
translation_verse: Amoso m maaŋ tiŋ n lo ma kɔnɔ. Kagbenejija nɛ ebesa damta to nɛ mee fubel a bile asheŋ na.

english_verse: Am I the sea or a sea monster? Is that why you imprison me?
translation_verse: M maŋ la teku ŋko kusɔ gbeyeso gboŋ nɛ k wɔ teku chiŋgeliŋ to nɛ fo ti ma n wɔtɔ a kuŋ ma.

english_verse: I go to bed, hoping for rest,
translation_verse: M baŋ yɔ kelaŋ so, nsaa tama fanɛ ma ebesa beeŋ ku

english_verse: but you torture me with terrible dreams. *
translation_verse: fee ta edare lubi nna a tɔrɔ ma nɛ kufu bee pɛ ma ga

english_verse: Won't you look away just long enough for me to swallow?
translation_verse: Ama fo maaŋ naŋ kpele fo anishi ma so nɛ n nya m min echɔl gba a?

english_verse: Why do you watch us so closely? What's it to you, if I sin? Why am I your target and such a heavy burden?
translation_verse: Hale nɛ n wora kulubi gba, kumo be nnɛ e nya fo? Manɛ nna nɛ fo lara kenishi n yuu ma loŋ? Ma asheŋ bee tɔrɔ fo nna a?

english_verse: How long will you talk and keep saying nothing?
translation_verse: “Jemanɛ mo nɛ feeŋ yige fo mmalga fuloŋ nɛ e maŋ kɔ kifi to ere be kebaamalga?

english_verse: Does God All-Powerful stand in the way of justice?
translation_verse: Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na maa ji esa durmu, mo alɛ maa wora kusɔ nɛ k maŋ daga.

english_verse: Your future will be brighter by far than your past. Our Ancestors Were Wise
translation_verse: E beeŋ shin nɛ fo echefoso be kebaawɔtɔ e baa bɔ fo kebaawɔtɔ dra na ga.

english_verse: Our ancestors were wise, so learn from them.
translation_verse: An nanaana daa nyi asheŋ ga, amoso koya asheŋ bumo kutɔ.

english_verse: Our own time has been short, like a fading shadow, and we know very little.
translation_verse: Anyi maŋ chɛr durnya to, anyi alɛ maŋ nyi shɛŋ. Anyi maa chɛr kasawule ere so nsaa choŋ fanɛ afu.

english_verse: But they will instruct you with great understanding.
translation_verse: Ama an nanaana na bre beeŋ ŋini fo kasheŋwora, nɛ fo pin amo to nɛnɛ.

english_verse: and if the water dries up, they die sooner than grass.
translation_verse: Nɛ fanɛ nchu na malɛ baŋ feeto ndoŋ, agasa na e naa daŋ afitiri kikɛ kewu.

english_verse: But once they are pulled up, they have no more place;
translation_verse: Ama nɛ esa baŋ gberge afitiri na n tia, b maaŋ naŋ pin fanɛ afitiri daŋ yili ndoŋ ŋ ku so gba.

english_verse: We know God doesn't reject an innocent person or help a sinner.
translation_verse: An nyi fanɛ Ebɔrɛ maa kini esa nɛ basa maa wu kulubi mo so a lɛ, mo alɛ maa chɛ alubiworapo to.

english_verse: And so, he will make you happy and give you something to smile about.
translation_verse: Amoso, e beeŋ naŋ shin nɛ fo kagbene e fuli nɛ fo mushe awɔrso nɛ basa e nu fo asheŋ.

english_verse: But your evil enemies will be put to shame and disappear forever.
translation_verse: Ama e beeŋ shin nɛ fo doŋana bre e ji anishinyɔr nseŋ mur gba kuraa nɛ esa maaŋ naŋ wu bumo kikɛ hale mbaanaayɔ.”

english_verse: What you say is true. No human is innocent in the sight of God.
translation_verse: “Kashenteŋ nɛ fo ji. Dimɛdi kikɛ maaŋ tiŋ n ji n lar Ebɔrɛ be anishito.

english_verse: Not once in a thousand times could we win our case if we took him to court.
translation_verse: Nɛ anyi nɛ Ebɔrɛ yɔ demujikpa ale kagboŋ gba, anyi maaŋ tiŋ n ya ji m bri mo.

english_verse: God is wise and powerful— who could possibly oppose him and win?
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ nyi asheŋ nsaa kɔ eleŋ ga, esa kikɛ maaŋ tiŋ n tu mo n ji emɔrɔ m pɔɔ so.

english_verse: When God becomes angry, he can move mountains before they even know it.
translation_verse: Nɛ Ebɔrɛ baŋ nya agbo, e beeŋ tiŋ m pulgi abee nseŋ melgi amo m buu, nɛ k purgi basa.

english_verse: God can shake the earth loose from its foundations
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ beeŋ tiŋ n shin nɛ kasawule nɛ kumo be gbaltɔlase kikɛ a gbuŋgbuŋ to.

english_verse: or command the sun and stars to hold back their light.
translation_verse: E beeŋ naŋ tiŋ n shin nɛ epeŋi nɛ achɛkpabi e biri to nɛ kakpa e fuli to ŋ gben.

english_verse: and set the stars in place— the Big Dipper and Orion, the Pleiades and the stars in the southern sky.
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ koŋwule na e to achɛkpabi be yiri yiri awɔlpa to, Mo e to achɛkpabi nɛ baa tre Shishirigboŋ na nɛ koshi nɛ mbe bibi nɛ achɛkpabi nɛ a wɔ awɔlpa to be kelargato be kaseto na kikɛ.

english_verse: Of all the miracles God works, we cannot understand a one.
translation_verse: Anyi maaŋ tiŋ m pin Ebɔrɛ be emamachisheŋ nɛ e bee wora na be kukoŋwule gba to kikɛ.

english_verse: God walks right past me, without making a sound.
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ baŋ bɔla ma ase a choŋ gba, m maaŋ wu mo ŋko m pin mbe asheŋ.

english_verse: And if he grabs something, who can stop him or raise a question?
translation_verse: E baŋ ta kusɔ, esa maaŋ tiŋ ŋ kuŋ mo akpa. Esa malɛ maaŋ tiŋ m bishi mo fanɛ manɛ nɛ fee wora ere?

english_verse: When God showed his anger, the servants of the sea monster fell at his feet.
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ be kagbene baŋ kaa, e bee mur mo doŋana nɛ baa chɛ kusɔkpaŋ gboŋgboŋi lubi nɛ k wɔ teku to nɛ baa tre Reehab na to na nna.

english_verse: How, then, could I possibly argue my case with God? Though I Am Innocent
translation_verse: Nɛ nuso nɛ ma alɛ le beeŋ tiŋ n ji Ebɔrɛ emɔrɔ ashi ma demu ere to?

english_verse: And if God came into court when I called him, he would not hear my case.
translation_verse: Hale nɛ e sa ma ekpa nɛ m malga gba a, m maŋ yirda fanɛ e beeŋ nu n sa ma.

english_verse: He would strike me with a storm and increase my injuries for no reason at all.
translation_verse: E beeŋ shin nɛ bɔrɛfugboŋ e doro ma n ti so, nɛ m maŋ wora shɛŋ.

english_verse: Before I could get my breath, my miseries would multiply.
translation_verse: Pɔɛŋ nɛ meeŋ nya n fute n wushi gba na, e beeŋ shin nɛ ma awurfoŋ e ti so.

english_verse: God is much stronger than I am, and who would call me into court to give me justice?
translation_verse: Nɛ kela fanɛ eleŋ nna, Ebɔrɛ kɔ eleŋ a chɔ ma! Nɛ kela asheŋ be keji malɛ gba nna, wanɛ e naŋ tiŋ n tre Ebɔrɛ demujikpa?

english_verse: Even if I were innocent, God would prove me wrong.
translation_verse: Nɛ fanɛ m maŋ wora n da so gba, ma kɔnɔ to be mmalga beeŋ ji m biri ma.

english_verse: I am not guilty, but I no longer care what happens to me.
translation_verse: Hale esa kikɛ maŋ wu kulubi ma so gba, ama kusɔ kama nɛ k beeŋ wora ma be asheŋ maŋ naa tir ma.

english_verse: What difference does it make? God destroys the innocent along with the guilty.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal manɛ so, Ebɔrɛ bee mur basa nɛ b wora n da so nɛ bumo nɛ b maŋ wora n da so kikɛ nna.

english_verse: When a good person dies a sudden death, God sits back and laughs.
translation_verse: Nɛ esa lela baŋ wu luwu purgiase gba, Ebɔrɛ bee chena nna a mushe.

english_verse: And who else but God blindfolds the judges, then lets the wicked take over the earth? My Life Is Speeding By
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ e sa basa lubi ekpa, nɛ b sɔ durnya m pugi so; nseŋ tan demujipoana malɛ. Nɛ mannɛ Ebɔrɛ e wora loŋ, wanɛ e wora loŋ?

english_verse: My life is speeding by, without a hope of happiness.
translation_verse: K du fanɛ ma nchɛ bee choŋ manaŋ manaŋ nna, nɛ m maŋ naa tama kagbenefuli kikɛ kuraa.

english_verse: Each day passes swifter than a sailing ship or an eagle swooping down.
translation_verse: Ma ŋkpa bee choŋ manaŋ manaŋ nna fanɛ afu na, k bee yɔ manaŋ manaŋ a chɔ kusore ka gbelge to n fuu kusɔ gba.

english_verse: Sometimes I try to be cheerful and to stop complaining,
translation_verse: Jemanɛ ko mee wora ania fanɛ meeŋ baa leŋ ma kumu to nseŋ yige kebaamuni to a fubel nna,

english_verse: but my sufferings frighten me, because I know that God still considers me guilty.
translation_verse: ama ma awurfoŋana na bee da ma kufu nna. Ŋkpal manɛ so, n nyi Ebɔrɛ ka kraa wu ma fanɛ esa nɛ e wora n da so nna.

english_verse: Even if I washed myself with the strongest soap,
translation_verse: Kɔya be yiri kikɛ maŋ wɔtɔ nɛ n tiŋ n ta n fɔr so n nyalɛ so.

english_verse: God would throw me into a pit of stinking slime, leaving me disgusting to my clothes.
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ ta ma n lɛ kemaŋ dufɛso to nna, hale ma asheŋ bee keta ma asɔbuuso gba nyɔmɔ.

english_verse: God isn't a mere human like me. I can't put him on trial.
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ maŋ la dimɛdi bomin fanɛ ma. M maaŋ tiŋ n tre mo nɛ e ba demujikpa nɛ an ji asheŋ.

english_verse: Who could possibly judge between the two of us?
translation_verse: Esa kikɛ maŋ wɔtɔ nɛ e tiŋ n ji ma nɛ Ebɔrɛ be kefɛato be asheŋ ere.

english_verse: Can someone snatch away the stick God carries to frighten me?
translation_verse: Esa ko maŋ wɔtɔ nɛ e tiŋ n sɔ kedibi nɛ Ebɔrɛ kɔ a funti ma ere mbe enɔ.

english_verse: I am sick of life! And from my deep despair, I complain to you, my God.
translation_verse: Kebaawɔtɔ lar ma ebɔl! O Ebɔrɛ, nya asoe n nu ma kenishipere be nfubel ere.

english_verse: Why do you take such delight in destroying those you created and in smiling on sinners?
translation_verse: Manɛ nna nɛ fo kekini ma n lɛ par fo, nɛ fo maa wora shɛŋ a laŋɛ basa lubi be ŋkre bre be kaplɛa so?

english_verse: Do you look at things the way we humans do?
translation_verse: Kananɛ anyi edimɛdi bee keni nsaa wora asheŋ na nɛ fo, Ebɔrɛ gba bee keni nsaa wora asheŋ a?

english_verse: Is your life as short as ours?
translation_verse: Fo alɛ gba be ŋkpa maŋ wɔ nteŋ fanɛ anyeya nna a?

english_verse: Is that why you are so quick to find fault with me?
translation_verse: Ama amoso nɛ fee nya manaŋ a mige to a fin kewu ma kulubi ere a?

english_verse: You know I am innocent, but who can defend me against you?
translation_verse: Fo nyi ŋ ka maŋ wora n jija, ama wanɛ e naaŋ tiŋ m malga ŋ kuŋ ma fo kutɔ?

english_verse: Remember that you molded me like a piece of clay. So don't turn me back into dust once again.
translation_verse: Baa nyiŋi fanɛ fo e pɔr ma fanɛ kananɛ baa ta ebɔ a pɔr asɔ na. Amoso sa maŋ naŋ kilgi ma eshishɛr a!

english_verse: As cheese is made from milk, you created my body from a tiny drop.
translation_verse: Fo e wɔtɔ n tuto eleŋ nɛ e tiŋ n di n nio kedampo, nseŋ shin nɛ n tiŋ n daŋ n nio be epun to.

english_verse: Then you tied my bones together with muscles and covered them with flesh and skin.
translation_verse: Fo e bela ma awibi n chuge abar so nseŋ wora eblaŋ nɛ kawɔl m buu awibi na so.

english_verse: You, the source of my life, showered me with kindness and watched over me. You Have Not Explained
translation_verse: Fo e sa ma ŋkpa nseŋ ŋini ma fo kasha nɛ k maa loge na. Fo e naa keni ma so nɛ n wɔ ŋkpa to na.

english_verse: Why did you let me be born? I would rather have died before birth
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ, manɛ nna nɛ fo shin nɛ b kurge ma bre? A daŋ daga ŋ ka laŋɛ kachɛ nɛ b kurge ma na nna.

english_verse: I have only a few days left. Why don't you leave me alone? Let me find some relief, *
translation_verse: Ma nchɛ maŋ naa shi durnya to. Yige ma nɛ n ji ma kumu gbrɛbi.

english_verse: Your words have silenced others and made them ashamed; now it is only right for you to be put to shame.
translation_verse: Job, fee fɛ fanɛ anyi maaŋ tiŋ n tuge fo mmalga ere to nna a? Esa wɔtɔ nɛ e fɛa fo so ŋkpal fo mmalga jiga ere so!

english_verse: You claim to be innocent and argue that your beliefs are acceptable to God.
translation_verse: Fee ta fo kumu fanɛ fo maŋ wora kulubi kikɛ nsaa ji emɔrɔ a kaŋɛ fanɛ fo ere be asheŋ woraso kikɛ bee par Ebɔrɛ nna.

english_verse: But I wish God would speak
translation_verse: Aloko Ebɔrɛ daa beeŋ tuge fo nna!

english_verse: Can you understand the mysteries surrounding God All-Powerful?
translation_verse: Feeŋ tiŋ m pin Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ be keshi nɛ mbe eleŋgboŋ to a?

english_verse: They are higher than the heavens and deeper than the grave. So what can you do when you know so little,
translation_verse: Mbe keshi nɛ mbe eleŋgboŋ awɔlpa so, nɛ fo maaŋ tiŋ n fo amo. Amo alɛ naa du chiŋgeliŋ a chɔ nchaŋ Mo alɛ naa nyi kusɔ nɛ k bee wora bubuni to nɛ fo maŋ nyi kumo kikɛ kuraa.

english_verse: and these mysteries outreach the earth and the ocean?
translation_verse: Mbe keshi nɛ eleŋgboŋ wɔ mpar a chɔ kasawule nɛ etekuana kikɛ.

english_verse: If God puts you in prison or drags you to court, what can you do?
translation_verse: Nɛ fanɛ Ebɔrɛ ti fo ebu ŋko n yɛr fo demujikpa, manɛ nɛ feeŋ tiŋ n wora mo?

english_verse: God has the wisdom to know when someone is worthless and sinful,
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ nyi basa nɛ b du jiga, mo alɛ nsaa wu bumo be asheŋ lubi kikɛ.

english_verse: but it's easier to tame a wild donkey than to make a fool wise. Surrender Your Heart to God
translation_verse: Keshin nɛ ewulpo e pin asheŋ du kpakpa a chɔ keshin nɛ kurma kpeŋso e nu n sa esa.

english_verse: Surrender your heart to God, turn to him in prayer,
translation_verse: Job, yili fo kagbene kukoŋwule n sa Ebɔrɛ, nseŋ bɛta n yɔ mo kutɔ kabɔrɛkule to.

english_verse: and give up your sins— even those you do in secret.
translation_verse: Tuba n lara kulubi ashi fo laŋ to, hale amo nɛ fo wora ashiri to na gba.

english_verse: Then you won't be ashamed; you will be confident and fearless.
translation_verse: Nɛ fo wora loŋ, fo maŋ naŋ ji anishinyɔr fo alɛ beeŋ nya kenyɛn a maaŋ naa wɔ kufu be kebaawɔtɔ to.

english_verse: and your darkest night will be brighter than noon.
translation_verse: Kebaawɔtɔ beeŋ fulto parr a chɔ kapiidi nɛ tentembiri malɛ e ki fanɛ kachipurso n sa fo.

english_verse: You will rest safe and secure, filled with hope and emptied of worry.
translation_verse: Sheŋ maa naa tɔrɔ fo ashi fo kebaawɔtɔ to, Ebɔrɛ beeŋ sa fo tama nɛ fo maŋ naa wɔ kafɔŋ to.

english_verse: You will sleep without fear and be greatly respected.
translation_verse: Fo maaŋ naa ŋana fo doŋana. Basa damta malɛ beeŋ baa fin kechɛto fo kutɔ.

english_verse: But those who are evil will go blind and lose their way. Their only escape is death!
translation_verse: Ama basa lubi bre beeŋ paŋ tama nseŋ fo akpa. Bumo be tama kikɛ beeŋ baa la luwu nna.”

english_verse: But I know as much as you do, and so does everyone else.
translation_verse: Ama kusɔ nɛ men nyi na nɛ ma alɛ gba nyi, kumo koŋwule na nɛ ekama gba nyi.

english_verse: I have always lived right, and God answered my prayers; now friends make fun of me.
translation_verse: Jemanɛ kikɛ kebaawɔtɔ niŋiso to nɛ n daa wɔ, nɛ Ebɔrɛ malɛ daa nu ma kabɔrɛkule. Ama naniere n nekpaana e naa wora ma eyur to na.

english_verse: It's easy to condemn those who are suffering, when you have no troubles.
translation_verse: Nɛ esa baa maŋ wɔ etɔrɔ kikɛ to, k maŋ du kpakpa n sa mo nɛ kemalga ŋ gbiti esa nɛ e bee ji awurfoŋ.

english_verse: Robbers and other godless people live safely at home and say, “God is in our hands!” If You Want To Learn
translation_verse: Beyu nɛ basa nɛ b maa ŋana Ebɔrɛ wɔ kayurwushi to nna, ama kusɔ koŋwule nɛ b yirda e la eleŋ nɛ b kɔ na.

english_verse: If you want to learn, then go and ask the wild animals and the birds,
translation_verse: Menyi beeŋ tiŋ ŋ koya asɔ damta ashi mbuibi nɛ asɔbɔya kutɔ.

english_verse: Any of them can tell you what the Lord has done.
translation_verse: Amo be kekama beeŋ tiŋ ŋ kaŋɛ menyi kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na wora.

english_verse: Every living creature is in the hands of God.
translation_verse: Kusɔ futeso kikɛ be ŋkpa bɔɔ Ebɔrɛ enɔ nna.

english_verse: No one can rebuild what he destroys, or release those he has imprisoned.
translation_verse: Esa kikɛ maaŋ tiŋ n lɔŋɛ kusɔ nɛ Ebɔrɛ jija, ŋko n lara basa nɛ e ti ebu ashi kabuti na to.

english_verse: puts mighty kings to shame, and takes away their power.
translation_verse: Mo e naa shin nɛ bewurgboŋ bee ji anishinyɔr, nsaa shin nɛ bumo be yuku bee ba ekar.

english_verse: God turns darkness to light;
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ e naa shin nɛ tentembiri bee ki kefulto.

english_verse: God strikes their rulers senseless, then leaves them to roam through barren deserts,
translation_verse: Mo e naa shin nɛ efuliana na bewuraana bee ki bewulpo, nsaa mel to a nite keshishɛrsawule nɛ akpaana maŋ wɔ so na.

english_verse: I know and understand every bit of this.
translation_verse: “N nyi asheŋ nɛ menyee malga ere kikɛ, ma alɛ pin amo be kekama to.

english_verse: None of you are smarter than I am; there's nothing you know that I don't.
translation_verse: Menyi be ekama maŋ kɔ kenyi a chɔ ma. Menyi alɛ maŋ nyi kusɔ ko nɛ m maŋ nyi kumo.

english_verse: But I prefer to argue my case with God All-Powerful—
translation_verse: Ama Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na nɛ mee sha nɛ n tu n ji kusɔ nɛ k tu ma ere, mannɛ menyi.

english_verse: you are merely useless doctors, who treat me with lies.
translation_verse: Efɛ nawule nɛ menyi ere bee ku a deŋi ma. Men du fanɛ bechɛpo nɛ b maŋ nyi shɛŋ nna.

english_verse: The wisest thing you can do is to keep quiet
translation_verse: Kanyiasheŋ be kusɔ nɛ menyeeŋ tiŋ n wora kikɛ e la kelo menyi be nnɔ to n chena.

english_verse: Are you telling lies for God
translation_verse: Mmalga nɛ menyee ta a wɔtɔ Ebɔrɛ be kɔnɔ to

english_verse: and not telling the whole truth when you argue his case?
translation_verse: jemanɛ nɛ men sɔ mo so a malga, nsaa maa ji kashenteŋ na.

english_verse: If he took you to court, could you fool him, just as you fool others?
translation_verse: Nɛ Ebɔrɛ mige menyi to ŋ keni asheŋ beeŋ nyalɛ n sa menyi a? Menyee tama fanɛ menyeeŋ tiŋ n fule Ebɔrɛ fanɛ kananɛ menyee fule basa na a?

english_verse: If you were secretly unfair, he would correct you,
translation_verse: Nɛ menyi maŋ ji kashenteŋ ashiri to gba, e beeŋ fɛa menyi so n niŋi menyi asheŋ,

english_verse: and his glorious splendor would make you terrified.
translation_verse: nɛ mbe eleŋgboŋ na e shin nɛ kufugboŋ e tɔr menyi so nɛ men baa chicha.

english_verse: Your wisdom and arguments will blow away like dust. Be Quiet While I Speak
translation_verse: Menyi be aŋasa nɛ menyee bɔ nɛ emɔrɔ nɛ menyee ji na kikɛ du fanɛ kalabɛr nɛ afu bee ber a yɔ nna.

english_verse: I will be responsible for what happens to me.
translation_verse: Kusɔ kama nɛ k nya ma shi ŋ gbagba be kumu to nna.

english_verse: God may kill me, but still I will trust him and offer my defense.
translation_verse: Hale nɛ Ebɔrɛ bee sha kemɔ ma gba, ŋ kraa beeŋ yirda mo.

english_verse: This may be what saves me, because no guilty person would come to his court.
translation_verse: Kusɔ nɛ k beeŋ mɔlga ma nna na, ŋkpal manɛ so, esa nɛ e wora n jija kikɛ maaŋ shuli m ba Ebɔrɛ be anishito nɛ e ji mo demu.

english_verse: Listen carefully to my words!
translation_verse: Men kaŋ asoe n nu ma mmalga nɛnɛ!

english_verse: I have prepared my case well, and I am certain to win.
translation_verse: M bela ma demu na ase nɛnɛ nna, ma alɛ baa nyi geeŋ fanɛ meeŋ ji n lar kumo to.

english_verse: If you can prove me guilty, I will give up and die. Job Prays I Ask Only Two Things
translation_verse: Nɛ fo, Ebɔrɛ beeŋ tiŋ ŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ n wora n jija, kumo ere meeŋ lo ma kɔnɔ nseŋ wu nɛ k loge.

english_verse: I ask only two things of you, my God, and I will no longer hide from you—
translation_verse: Ma Ebɔrɛ, asɔ anyɔ nɛ mee kule fo, amo be kaman, m maaŋ naaŋ shile ŋ ŋana fo so.

english_verse: Then speak, and I will reply; or else let me speak, and you reply.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ fo semaŋ ma, nɛ m ba malga n chɛ ma kɔnɔ. Ŋko fo shin nɛ m malga, nɛ fo ere e sa ma atuwebi.

english_verse: Please point out my sins, so I will know them.
translation_verse: Jande, ŋini ma alubi nɛ n wora, nɛ m pin amo kikɛ.

english_verse: Why have you turned your back and count me your enemy?
translation_verse: Manɛ nna nɛ fee ŋana ma so nsaa ta ma fanɛ fo doŋ?

english_verse: Why do you accuse me of horrible crimes and make me pay for sins I did in my youth?
translation_verse: Asheŋ lubi nɛ e maaŋ daga kuraa na, hale amo nɛ n wora ma kebia to kikɛ nɛ fo ta a deŋi ma so.

english_verse: I am rotting away like cloth eaten by worms.
translation_verse: Ma eyur baa bɛlge nna ayiyanto fanɛ kechɛbi nɛ e kaŋkaŋ muu na.”

english_verse: Life is short and sorrowful for every living soul.
translation_verse: “Dimɛdi be nchɛ maŋ shi durnya to, amo alɛ nɛ etɔrɔ damta nna.

english_verse: We are flowers that fade and shadows that vanish.
translation_verse: Dimɛdi du fanɛ ketoto ŋko kenyɔlɔ nna, k maa chɛr nɛ k bolo ŋko n wɔl n choŋ.

english_verse: There's no way a human can be completely pure.
translation_verse: Dimɛdi kikɛ maŋ wɔtɔ nɛ kulubi maŋ wɔ mo to.

english_verse: Our time on earth is brief; the number of our days is already decided by you.
translation_verse: Anyi edimɛdi be saŋɛ maŋ shi durnya to, Fo, Ebɔrɛ na, tea nyi nchɛ nɛ esa beeŋ ji durnya to.

english_verse: Why don't you leave us alone and let us find some happiness while we toil and labor? When a Tree Is Chopped Down
translation_verse: Manɛ nna nɛ fo maaŋ yige anyi nɛ an gbagba e fin kagbenefuli n sa anyi be amu, jemanɛ nɛ an wɔ kegben damta to ere?

english_verse: When a tree is chopped down, there is always the hope that it will sprout again.
translation_verse: Kedibi nɛ b ku n lɛ gba kraa kɔ tama fanɛ k beeŋ naŋ purge kachako.

english_verse: Its roots and stump may rot,
translation_verse: Kedibi beeŋ tiŋ n wu a yil,

english_verse: but at the touch of water, it sprouts once again.
translation_verse: ama k baŋ nya nchu nɛ k naŋ purge afantaŋ popɔr kaseto.

english_verse: Humans are different— we die, and that's the end.
translation_verse: Ama anyi edimɛdi kɔr ndibi to, an baŋ wu asheŋ loge.

english_verse: We are like streams and lakes after the water has gone;
translation_verse: An du fanɛ mbombi nɛ apaana nna, amo to be nchu baaŋ feeto a bee wɔlto nna.

english_verse: we fall into the sleep of death, never to rise again, until the sky disappears.
translation_verse: Anyi edimɛdi malɛ baaŋ wu, anyi maaŋ naŋ koso kikɛ, hale nɛ durnya e fo ekar.

english_verse: Please hide me, God, deep in the ground— and when you are angry no more, remember to rescue me. Will We Humans Live Again?
translation_verse: Jande, Ebɔrɛ, ta ma ŋ ŋana kasawule be kechimbi to. Fo agbo kaŋ wushi nɛ fo nyiŋi n sɔ ma n yige.

english_verse: Will we humans live again? I would gladly suffer and wait for my time.
translation_verse: Nɛ esa baŋ wu, e maaŋ naŋ tiŋ m ba ŋkpa to. Amoso awurfoŋ nɛ mee ji ere kikɛ mee jo ma saŋɛ nna.

english_verse: My Creator, you would want me; you would call out, and I would answer.
translation_verse: Feeŋ tre ma, nɛ n shuli, nɛ ma asheŋ a par fo, ma etopo.

english_verse: You would take care of me, but not count my sins—
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ fo baa keni aya nɛ meeŋ baa tia, ama fo maaŋ baa karga ma alubi a nase.

english_verse: you would put them in a bag, tie it tight, and toss them away.
translation_verse: Feeŋ ta ma alubi m paŋ ma nseŋ kplaŋ amo so. Fo alɛ beeŋ kpra ma asheŋ lubi kikɛ n lɛ.

english_verse: But in the real world, mountains tumble, and rocks crumble;
translation_verse: Kananɛ abee bee buri so a tɔr nɛ afalta bee bure to

english_verse: streams wear away stones and wash away soil. And you destroy our hopes!
translation_verse: nɛ nchu bee fɔr ajembu so nsaa sulɔ eshishɛr a yɔ na, aloŋ nɛ fee shin nɛ edimɛdi be tama bee mur!

english_verse: You change the way we look, then send us away, wiped out forever.
translation_verse: Fo, e naa shin nɛ anyee bel a chɛrga anishiakpa; kumo be kaman nɛ an wu n choŋ nsaa maaŋ naa wɔtɔ hale mbaanaayɔ.

english_verse: We never live to know if our children are praised or disgraced.
translation_verse: Anyi maa chena a chɛr a wu anyi be mbia ka nya kemaŋkura ŋko ka ji anishinyɔr ashi kebaawɔtɔ to.

english_verse: We feel no pain but our own, and when we mourn, it's only for ourselves.
translation_verse: Anyi maŋ naa nu ebesa kikɛ n naŋ ti an gbagba peya so; anyi alɛ maa shu esa kikɛ be keeli, ama an gbagba peya.”

english_verse: you would stop spreading all of this hot air.
translation_verse: “Job, nɛ fo daa nyi asheŋ nna, fo daa beeŋ yige mmalga fuloŋ nɛ fee malga ere.

english_verse: Your words are enough to make others turn from God and lead them to doubt.
translation_verse: Fo mmalga ere beeŋ tiŋ n shin nɛ basa pɔtɛ e lar Ebɔrɛ kaman nsaa maŋ naŋ yirda mo.

english_verse: And your sinful, scheming mind is the source of all you say.
translation_verse: Fo kɔnɔ to be mmalga e naa ŋini fo asheŋ lubi. Kamalganyi nɛ fee ta a kuŋ fo kumu bre de.

english_verse: I am not here as your judge; your own words are witnesses against you.
translation_verse: M maŋ wɔ nfe nna nɛ n ji fo demu; fo gbagba be mmalga e naa ji a bri fo.

english_verse: Were you the first human? Are you older than the hills?
translation_verse: Mannɛ fo e la dimɛdi juŋkparso durnya to. Fo alɛ maŋ chɛr a chɔ abee nɛ Ebɔrɛ to na.

english_verse: Have you ever been present when God's council meets? Do you alone have wisdom?
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ ka daa wora mbe ŋkre sososo na, fo daa wɔ ndoŋ a? Fo nawule e kɔ kanyiasheŋ a?

english_verse: Do you know and understand something we don't?
translation_verse: Kusɔ ko wɔtɔ nɛ fo nyi kumo nɛ anyi ere maŋ nyi kumo a?

english_verse: We have the benefit of wisdom older than your father.
translation_verse: Basa nɛ b bel a chɔ fo tuto gba kutɔ nɛ anyi ere koya kanyiasheŋ.

english_verse: Your emotions are out of control, making you look fierce;
translation_verse: Fo kagbene koso m baŋ so ga, n shin nɛ fo ki esa ŋana so.

english_verse: that's why you attack God with everything you say.
translation_verse: Amoso nɛ fo nya agbo n wɔtɔ Ebɔrɛ nsaa malga a gbiti mo na.

english_verse: and neither are angels— not in the sight of God. If God doesn't trust his angels,
translation_verse: Nɛ Ebɔrɛ maaŋ tiŋ n yirda emalaika nɛ baa shuŋ mo ebɔrɛso na gba,

english_verse: what chance do humans have? We are so terribly evil that we thirst for sin. Just Listen to What I Know
translation_verse: edimɛdi bre nɛ e beeŋ tiŋ n yirda a? Alubi la fanɛ nchu nna n sa anyi edimɛdi nɛ anyee nuu kapa nɛ kanyɛ.

english_verse: Just listen to what I know, and you will learn
translation_verse: Job, kaŋ kusoe n nu kusɔ nɛ n nyi, nseŋ koya kusɔ ko kumo to.

english_verse: But suffering is in store each day for those who sin.
translation_verse: Ama awurfoŋ wɔtɔ karechɛ kikɛ nna n sa basa nɛ b wɔ alubi be kebaawɔtɔ to.

english_verse: Darkness, despair, and death are their destiny.
translation_verse: Bumo be kelamba kikɛ e la tentembiri nɛ kepaŋ tama nɛ luwu.

english_verse: They scrounge around for food, all the while dreading the approaching darkness.
translation_verse: Baaŋ baa kulti a fin ajibi fanɛ ejita, bumo alɛ nsaa nyi fanɛ tentembiri be kachɛ na taga to.

english_verse: They are overcome with despair, like frightened soldiers facing a fearsome king in battle.
translation_verse: Kemurgboŋ, e du fanɛ ewura lempo ka bee shin nɛ e kɔ bumo kena, a jo nɛ k mur bumo cheche.

english_verse: but they will live in the ruins of deserted towns.
translation_verse: ama baaŋ baa ka wɔ nde bureso nɛ ekama shile ŋ ka to nna.

english_verse: They won't escape the darkness, and the blazing breath of God will set their future aflame. *
translation_verse: B maaŋ tiŋ ŋ gelge tentembiri kikɛ. Ebɔrɛ be agbo nɛ k bee suse wuloŋwuloŋ fanɛ edɛ na beeŋ mur bumo cheche.

english_verse: They have put their trust in something worthless; now they will become worthless
translation_verse: Nɛ b paŋ nfɛra nseŋ ta bumo be yirda n wɔtɔ asheŋ lubi to bre, kumo ere asheŋ lubi be kakɔka nɛ baaŋ nya.

english_verse: Yes, the godless and the greedy will have nothing but flames feasting on their homes,
translation_verse: Kashenteŋto, edɛ e naŋ ji bɔrɛkinipoana nɛ kejimuniwuraana be nwu nɛ bumo be kaman to ebi m mur.

english_verse: I have often heard this, and it offers no comfort.
translation_verse: “N daŋ kenu le be mmalga ere ŋ ku so, amo alɛ maa wushi ma kagbene kikɛ.

english_verse: If I speak, or if I don't, I hurt all the same. My torment continues.
translation_verse: Nɛ fanɛ m malga ŋko m maŋ malga gba, awurfoŋ to nɛ ŋ kraa wɔ a ji ebesa na.

english_verse: God has worn me down and destroyed my family;
translation_verse: O Ebɔrɛ, fo bar ma kaseto nseŋ mur ma laŋ to ebi kikɛ kuraa.

english_verse: God is my hateful enemy, glaring at me and attacking with his sharp teeth.
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ nya agbo nna a kɔrfɛ ma kenishipereso, nseŋ ta anishi n yuu ma so a we anyii to yurkishi so.

english_verse: And God is the one who handed me over to this merciless mob. Everything Was Going Well
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ malɛ e ta ma m bɔɔ basa lubi enɔ, nɛ jimaŋ nɛ k maa wu kuwɔr ere nya ma e wora loŋ.

english_verse: Everything was going well, until God grabbed my neck and shook me to pieces. God set me up as the target
translation_verse: Kusɔ kama daa nite nɛnɛ ma kebaawɔtɔ to nna pɔɛŋ nɛ Ebɔrɛ to m pɛ ma ebɔl to m buri ma to n lɛ. Ebɔrɛ lara ma n yili fanɛ kusɔ nɛ e beeŋ

english_verse: for his arrows, and without showing mercy, he slashed my stomach open, spilling out my insides.
translation_verse: ta mbe atanyembi n yuu so n to nna. Mo alɛ maŋ wu ma kuwɔr nseŋ futi ma epun n lara ma apuntosɔ n lɛ kasawule.

english_verse: and so, in my sorrow I dress in sackcloth and sit in the dust.
translation_verse: Amoso nɛ n ta bɔtɛ m ba piŋi m buu nseŋ chena eshishɛrpumpuŋ to a shu fanɛ ŋ ka bee shu keeli na.

english_verse: My face is red with tears, and dark shadows circle my eyes,
translation_verse: N shu nna nɛ ma anishi m pere, hale puŋi m buu so nɛ m maŋ naa wu nɛnɛ.

english_verse: though I am not violent, and my prayers are sincere.
translation_verse: Ama ma alɛ maŋ diewu n wora kulubi ko. Kebɔrkɔnshi kikɛ maŋ wɔ ma kabɔrɛkule to.

english_verse: If I should die, I beg the earth not to cover my cry for justice.
translation_verse: Nɛ fanɛ n wu gba, mee kule kasawule nna fanɛ k sa maŋ shin nɛ kushu nɛ mee shu a fin kashenteŋ ere e ŋana basa so kikɛ.

english_verse: Even now, God in heaven is both my witness and my protector.
translation_verse: Naniere gba, Ebɔrɛ nɛ e wɔ ebɔrɛso na e la ma shɛdajipo nɛ ma ekumpo.

english_verse: My friends have rejected me, but God is the one I beg
translation_verse: N nekpaana bre kini ma nna n lɛ, ama Ebɔrɛ nɛ mee shu a ŋini.

english_verse: to show that I am right, just as a friend should.
translation_verse: Kananɛ esa bee kule Ebɔrɛ a sa mo nekpa na nɛ mee fin esa nɛ e beeŋ kule Ebɔrɛ n sa ma.

english_verse: Because in only a few years, I will be dead and gone.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal manɛ so, m maaŋ naŋ ji nfɛ damta nseŋ wu n yɔ a maaŋ naŋ bɛta m ba.”

english_verse: My hopes have died, my time is up, and the grave is ready.
translation_verse: Ma tama loge nɛ ma jemanɛ malɛ fo n loge, nɛ ma nchaŋ malɛ kur a dese a jo ma.

english_verse: All I can see are angry crowds, making fun of me.
translation_verse: Kusɔ nɛ mee wu kikɛ e la jimaŋ nɛ b diewu a wora ma eyurto kenishipereso.

english_verse: If you, Lord, don't help, who will pay the price for my release?
translation_verse: Nɛ fo, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na maŋ chɛ ma to, wanɛ e naŋ ka kukɔ na n sɔ ma n yige?

english_verse: My friends won't really listen, all because of you, and so you must be the one to prove them wrong.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal fo so, n nekpaana kini kenu kusɔ nɛ mee kaŋɛ na. Amoso a daga fo shin nɛ b pin fanɛ b maŋ wora n nyalɛ.

english_verse: They have condemned me, just to benefit themselves; now blind their children.
translation_verse: B ji m bri ma nna ŋkpal kusɔ nɛ baaŋ nya so, amoso shin nɛ bumo be mbia be anishi e biri bumo.

english_verse: You, God, are the reason I am insulted and spit on.
translation_verse: Fo, Ebɔrɛ na so nɛ basa nya ma a tege nsaa tu echɔl a wɔtɔ ma anishito na.

english_verse: I am almost blind with grief; my body is a mere shadow.
translation_verse: A ka gbrɛ nɛ n tan, ŋkpal kushu nɛ kagbenejija damta so. Ma eyur ere malɛ maŋ naa du kananɛ k daa du na.

english_verse: People who are truly good would feel so alarmed, that they would become angry with my worthless friends.
translation_verse: Basa nɛ b la basa lela kashenteŋto baŋ wu ma bumo be nnɔ bee mɔ bumo nna nɛ baa nya agbo a wɔtɔ n nekpaana nɛ b maa sa Ebɔrɛ bunyaŋ ere.

english_verse: They would do the right thing and because they did, they would grow stronger.
translation_verse: Basa niŋiso beeŋ baa wora kusɔ nɛ k daga, ŋkpal loŋ so baaŋ baa nya eleŋ a ti so.

english_verse: But none of my friends show any sense.
translation_verse: Ama n nekpaana ere to be ekama maŋ kɔ kanyiasheŋ kikɛ mo to.

english_verse: My life is drawing to an end; hope has disappeared.
translation_verse: Ma nchɛ bee ba ekar nna na, ma ŋkre kikɛ jija. Ma alɛ be tama kikɛ loge.

english_verse: But all my friends can do is offer empty hopes.
translation_verse: Ama kusɔ nɛ n nekpaana na beeŋ tiŋ n wora e la kebaasa ma tama fuloŋ; b maa ji kashenteŋ.

english_verse: I could tell the world below to prepare me a bed.
translation_verse: Ma tama kikɛ e la keyɔ bubuni to, kakpa nɛ meeŋ ya dese tentembiri to.

english_verse: Then I could greet the grave as my father and say to the worms, “Hello, mother and sisters!”
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ n ta nchaŋ n tre n tuto, nseŋ ta ashushombi nɛ e beeŋ ji ma na n tre n nio nɛ n sipocheana.

english_verse: But what kind of hope is that?
translation_verse: Nɛ loŋ nna, ma tama wɔ nnɛ? Wanɛ e naŋ tiŋ n wu kumo?

english_verse: Will it keep me company in the world of the dead?
translation_verse: Tama maaŋ tu ma n yɔ luwu to, kumo alɛ maaŋ tu ma n yɔ bubuni to.

english_verse: How long will you talk? Be sensible! Let us speak.
translation_verse: “Job, saŋɛ mo nɛ feeŋ yige fo mmalga ere bre? Baa kɔ nfɛra nseŋ shin nɛ anyi ere e malga.

english_verse: Or do you think that we are dumb animals?
translation_verse: Fee fɛ nna fanɛ asɔbɔya nɛ a maŋ kɔ nfɛra e la anyi, ŋko nuso?

english_verse: You cut yourself in anger. Will that shake the earth or even move the rocks? *
translation_verse: Fo nya agbo nna a doro fo kumu kenyanyaŋɛso na. Fo kanya agbo na maaŋ tiŋ ŋ gbuŋgbuŋ durnya. Ebɔrɛ malɛ maaŋ kpal fo so m pulgi abee.

english_verse: Their powerful legs become weak, and they stumble on schemes of their own doing. *
translation_verse: Bumo be aya daa kɔ eleŋ nna ga, ama naniere e ki aya pɔso. Bumo gbagba be asheŋ woraso e shin nɛ b fiti n tɔr.

english_verse: Terror strikes and pursues from every side.
translation_verse: Kenishipere nɛ k bee keta kufu bɛ bumo so kaba kama so nna.

english_verse: then afterwards to be eaten alive by death itself.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ luwu gbagba e ba ji bumo m mur kuraa.

english_verse: Those sinners are dragged from the safety of their tents to die a gruesome death.
translation_verse: Baa gberge basa lubi na nna a lar bumo be elaŋana to nɛ b ya wu eluwu bumbuŋ nɛ e bee keta kufu.

english_verse: Then their tents and possessions are burned to ashes,
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ bumo be elaŋana nɛ asɔ kikɛ e chɔɔ m mur ŋ ki nsunɔ.

english_verse: and they are left like trees, dried up from the roots.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ b ki fanɛ ndibi nɛ amo be nliŋi nɛ ayabi kikɛ wu.

english_verse: They are gone and forgotten,
translation_verse: Bumo ere choŋ nɛ ekama teŋ bumo so nna na.

english_verse: Such is the fate of sinners and their families who don't know God.
translation_verse: Kelamba nɛ k jo basa lubi nɛ bumo be nnaŋ to ebi nɛ b maŋ nyi Ebɔrɛ nna na.”

english_verse: How long will you torture me with your words?
translation_verse: “Manɛ nna nɛ fee kɔrfɛ ma nɛ fo mmalga ere bre?

english_verse: Isn't ten times enough for you to accuse me? Aren't you ashamed?
translation_verse: Ale kudu nna na fo kaa bee malga a gbiti ma. Nyɔmɔ maŋ kɔ fo a?

english_verse: Even if I have sinned, you haven't been harmed.
translation_verse: Hale nɛ n wora kulubi gba, k nya fo nnɛ?

english_verse: You boast of your goodness, claiming I am suffering because I am guilty.
translation_verse: Fo alelasheŋ so nɛ fee puchi, a fɛ fanɛ n wora n jija na so nɛ mee ji awurfoŋ.

english_verse: But God is the one at fault for finding fault with me.
translation_verse: Ama Ebɔrɛ e maŋ wora n nyalɛ ŋkpal e kaa bee wu ma kulubi so.

english_verse: God rips me apart, uproots my hopes,
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ baŋ mur ma kikɛ nna nɛ m maŋ naa kɔ tama kikɛ kuraa.

english_verse: and attacks with fierce anger, as though I were his enemy.
translation_verse: Mbe agbo koso ma so alegaiso nna, nɛ e bee wora ma fanɛ mo doŋ gbagba na.

english_verse: and when I call my servants, they pay no attention.
translation_verse: M baŋ tre ma nyɛrbi gba, baa kini keba nna.

english_verse: Young children can't stand me, and when I come near, they make fun.
translation_verse: Mbiwurbi gba maa sha kebaamata ma, nɛ m baŋ taga bumo to baa mushe ma nna nsaa shile.

english_verse: My best friends and loved ones have turned from me.
translation_verse: M baa dufɛ nteri kpakpasoana be mmuna so nna, nɛ basa nɛ mee sha ga malɛ kilgi a kɔ ma.

english_verse: I am skin and bones— just barely alive.
translation_verse: N foe eyur to nna ŋ ki fanɛ awibi nawule. Gbrɛ a ka nɛ n wu.

english_verse: My friends, I beg you for pity! God has made me his target.
translation_verse: N teriana, men baa shu ma so. Ŋkpal manɛ so, Ebɔrɛ e ber ma n nase na.

english_verse: I wish that my words could be written down
translation_verse: B daŋ sibɛ ma mmalga ere n nase kawɔl to k daa beeŋ par ma ga.

english_verse: I know that my Protector lives, and at the end he will stand on this earth.
translation_verse: N nyi ma emɔlgapo Ebɔrɛ na ka wɔ ebɔrɛso, nɛ asheŋ ere kikɛ be lalaloge e beeŋ gbelge m ba durnya to m ba mɔlga ma.

english_verse: My flesh may be destroyed, yet from this body I will see God.
translation_verse: Hale pɔɛŋ nɛ ma eyur ere e mur gba, ŋ gbagba beeŋ wu Ebɔrɛ kenishiso.

english_verse: Yes, I will see him for myself, and I long for that moment.
translation_verse: Kashenteŋto, ŋ gbagba e naŋ wu mo, ma alɛ bee keni loŋ be kachɛ na ekpa nna.

english_verse: My friends, you think up ways to blame and torment me, saying I brought it on myself.
translation_verse: N teriana, menyi ere bee fɛ ekpa nɛ menyeeŋ bɔla so n wu ma kulubi nseŋ mɛaŋ ma nna, a kaŋɛ fanɛ ma e ta ma kumu n wɔtɔ asheŋ to.

english_verse: But watch out for the judgment, when God will punish you!
translation_verse: Ama men baa de demuji nɛ k bee ba menyi so jemanɛ nɛ Ebɔrɛ beeŋ gberge menyi kusoe na so.”

english_verse: You have accused and insulted me, and reason requires a reply.
translation_verse: Kusɔ nɛ fo malga na la katege nna, ama ma alɛ gba nyi kusɔ nɛ meeŋ kaŋɛ fo.

english_verse: that sinful people are happy for only a while.
translation_verse: basa lubi be kagbenefuli maa chɛr.

english_verse: Though their pride and power may reach to the sky,
translation_verse: Baaŋ tiŋ n nya eyilikpagboŋ n ji eleŋ ga, nɛ k wora fanɛ b kaa bee chute awɔlpa na,

english_verse: they will disappear like dust, and those who knew them will wonder what happened.
translation_verse: ama bumo alɛ beeŋ choŋ fanɛ afu ka ta kalabɛr na; nɛ basa nɛ b daa nyi bumo na e baa bishi abar fanɛ, nnɛ nɛ b yɔ?

english_verse: They will be forgotten like a dream
translation_verse: Basa beeŋ teŋ bumo so fanɛ kananɛ baa teŋ edareana so na.

english_verse: Their children will have to repay what the parents took from the poor.
translation_verse: Bumo be mbia e naŋ ba ka asɔ nɛ bumo kurgepoana suge betirpo kutɔ na be akɔ n sa bumo.

english_verse: Indeed, the wicked will die and go to their graves in the prime of life. Sinners Love the Taste of Sin
translation_verse: Basa lubi bee wu a yɔ nchaŋ to nna nɛ b kraa la mbifɔlbi.

english_verse: Then God will make them lose the wealth they gobbled up.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ebɔrɛ e shin nɛ b paŋ asɔ nɛ b suge beko kutɔ na kikɛ.

english_verse: They will die from the fangs of poisonous snakes
translation_verse: Baaŋ wu nɛ k wora fanɛ awɔ lubi ka duŋ bumo m mɔ na.

english_verse: Greedy people want everything and are never satisfied.
translation_verse: Kejimuni so, b maa nya asɔ, nɛ a bee kukwe bumo.

english_verse: But when nothing remains for them to grab, they will be nothing.
translation_verse: Jemanɛ nɛ shɛŋ maaŋ naa wɔtɔ nɛ b gbare n sa bumo be amu na, nɛ bumo be kanyɛ kikɛ beeŋ mur.

english_verse: While running from iron spears, they will be killed by arrows of bronze,
translation_verse: Jemanɛ nɛ baaŋ baa shile abɛlso akpa na, nɛ danyaŋ be atanyembi beeŋ da bumo m mɔ.

english_verse: whose shining tips go straight through their bodies. They will be trapped by terror,
translation_verse: B baŋ gberge atanyembi na m pee, amo be nnɔso beeŋ baa chise ŋklaŋ a do nɛ kufugboŋ e luri m bɔlɔ bumo be ŋgbene to.

english_verse: and what they treasure most will be lost in the dark. God will send flames to destroy them in their tents with all their property.
translation_verse: Asɔ kama nɛ b gbare n yili na beeŋ mur. Ebɔrɛ beeŋ shin nɛ edɛ wuloŋ wuloŋ e ba chɔɔ bumo nɛ bumo be asɔ kikɛ m mur ashi bumo be elaŋ to.

english_verse: The heavens and the earth will testify against them,
translation_verse: Esoso nɛ kasawule kikɛ beeŋ ji shɛda ŋ gbiti bumo be asheŋ lubi nɛ b wora na.

english_verse: and all their possessions will be dragged off when God becomes angry.
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ be agbo beeŋ ki fanɛ nchugboŋ m ba sulɔ bumo be asɔ kikɛ n yɔ.

english_verse: This is what God has decided for those who are evil.
translation_verse: Kusɔ nɛ Ebɔrɛ kre n yili n sa kumukpakpaso wuraana nna na.”

english_verse: If you want to offer comfort, then listen to me.
translation_verse: “Nɛ fanɛ fee sha kemalga n wushi ma kagbene nna, kumo ere nu ma kamalga ere.

english_verse: And when I have finished, you can start your insults all over again.
translation_verse: Ŋ kaŋ malga n loge, feeŋ naŋ tiŋ n fara a wora ma eyur to.

english_verse: Just looking at me is enough to make you sick,
translation_verse: Keni kananɛ ŋ ki. Ma asheŋ maa chinchiŋ fo nsaa mɔ fo kɔnɔ a?

english_verse: Why do evil people live so long and gain such power?
translation_verse: Manɛ nna nɛ Ebɔrɛ bee sa basa lubi ekpa nɛ baa chena chɛr ga nɛ asheŋ bee nite nɛnɛ a sa bumo?

english_verse: Why are they allowed to see their children grow up?
translation_verse: Manɛ nna nɛ bumo be mbia nɛ bumo nanabiana bee daŋ a tu bumo nɛ b kraa wɔ ŋkpa to?

english_verse: They have no worries at home, and God never punishes them.
translation_verse: Shɛŋ maŋ tir bumo ashi bumo be elaŋana to, Ebɔrɛ malɛ maa kaa gberge bumo kusoe.

english_verse: Their cattle have lots of calves without ever losing one;
translation_verse: Bumo be ana bee kurge nna ga, anabi na malɛ be ekoŋwule gba maa wu.

english_verse: These people sing and celebrate to the sound of tambourines, small harps, and flutes,
translation_verse: Baa ta echakachaka nɛ ejaŋjilaŋ nɛ nlopi a boŋ nshɛ a ji eyur nna.

english_verse: and they are successful, without a worry, until the day they die. Leave Us Alone!
translation_verse: Kebaawɔtɔ malɛ bee nite nɛnɛ nna a sa bumo, shɛŋ maa tɔrɔ bumo be nfɛra hale n ya fo kachɛ nɛ baaŋ wu.

english_verse: Those who are evil say to God All-Powerful, “Leave us alone! Don't bother us with your teachings.
translation_verse: Ama le nɛ basa lubi na bee kaŋɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na: ‘Yige anyi! Anyi maa sha kepin fo aparsheŋ.

english_verse: What do we gain from praying and worshiping you?
translation_verse: Anyi maa nya tɔnɔ kikɛ ashi kebaakule nɛ kebaabunyaŋ fo to.

english_verse: We succeeded all on our own.” And so, I keep away from them and their evil schemes.
translation_verse: Anyi gbagba be eleŋ so nɛ asheŋ bee nite nɛnɛ a sa anyi.’ Amoso nɛ ma, Job bre lara ma kumu ashi loŋ be basa, nɛ bumo be ŋkre lubiana to na.

english_verse: How often does God become angry and send disaster and darkness to punish sinners?
translation_verse: Ale afanɛ nɛ Ebɔrɛ daŋ nya agbo ŋ gberge alubiworapoana kusoe n shin nɛ b ji jɛrbi?

english_verse: How often does he strike them like a windstorm that scatters straw?
translation_verse: Ale afanɛ nɛ e daŋ farnyaŋ bumo to fanɛ kananɛ afugboŋ bee kpeta amimi a lɛ na?

english_verse: You say, “God will punish those sinners' children in place of those sinners.” But I say, “Let him punish those sinners themselves until they really feel it.
translation_verse: Menyi kaa kaŋɛ le: ‘Ebɔrɛ beeŋ gberge alubiworapoana be mbia kusoe ŋkpal bumo kurgepoana be asheŋ lubi so.’ Ama le nɛ ma ere kaŋɛ: ‘Ebɔrɛ e gberge alubiworapoana na gbagba kusoe nɛ b pin fanɛ bumo gbagba be alubi so nɛ e wora loŋ.’
