translation_verse: shin nɛ b ya lara ma kabuti to ashi ewurkpa m ba. Ahikam pibinyɛn, Gɛdaliya nɛ mo nana daa la Shafan na nɛ b daŋ shin nɛ e keni ma so nɛ n ya fo epe nɛ alenfia. B daŋ yige ma ŋ gbagba be basa to nna ashi Juda be efuli so. Tama nɛ k wɔtɔ n sa Ebedmɛlɛk na be asheŋ

english_verse: While I was a prisoner in the courtyard of the palace guard, the Lord told me to say
translation_verse: Jemanɛ nɛ n daa wɔ kabuti to ashi ewurkpa na, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na daŋ kaŋɛ ma nna fanɛ

english_verse: But because you trusted me, I will protect you from the officials of Judah, and when Judah is struck by disaster, I will rescue you and keep you alive. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Meeŋ mɔlga fo nɛ b sa maŋ mɔ fo. Feeŋ nya ekpa n shile m mɔlga fo kumu ŋkpal fo ka ta fo yirda n wɔtɔ ma to so. Ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e kaŋɛ na.”

english_verse: I was led away in chains along with the people of Judah and Jerusalem who were being taken to Babylonia. Nebuzaradan was the officer in charge of the guard, and while we were stopped at Ramah, the Lord caused him to set me free.
translation_verse: Nebuzaradan nɛ e la benapo nɛ baa kuŋ Babilɔn be ewura na be enimu na ka sɔ ma n yige ashi Rama na be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na malga ma kutɔ. B daŋ chɛ ma ŋgbɛlɛbi nna nseŋ daŋ keta ma nɛ Juda nɛ Jerusalɛm be basa nɛ b pɛ a yɔ Babilɔn be efuli so na nna n yɔ ndoŋ.

english_verse: Nebuzaradan said: Jeremiah, the Lord your God warned your people that he would bring disaster on this land.
translation_verse: Nebuzaradan daŋ keta ma nna n lar ekarso nseŋ ya kaŋɛ ma le: “Enyɛnpe fo Ebɔrɛ na daŋ kpele fo basa kusoe fanɛ e beeŋ mur kasawule ere,

english_verse: Today I am taking the chains off your wrists and setting you free! If you want to, you can come with me to Babylonia, and I will see that you are taken care of. Or if you decide to stay here, you can go wherever you wish.
translation_verse: To, kabre mee lara ŋgbɛlɛbi ere fo enɔana to nna nɛ fo nya fo kumu. Nɛ fee sha ketu ma n yɔ Babilɔn be efuli so, feeŋ tiŋ n yɔ nɛ m baa keni fo so. Nɛ fo maa sha keyɔ malɛ, feeŋ tiŋ ŋ kini keyɔ. Efuli ere kikɛ dese nna n sa fo nɛ fo lara kusɔ nɛ fee sha. Feeŋ tiŋ n yɔ kaplɛkama nɛ fee sha.”

english_verse: I decided to stay with the people of Judah, and I went to live near Gedaliah in Mizpah. The Harvest Is Brought In
translation_verse: Nɛ n yɔ Gɛmaliya kutɔ ashi kade nɛ baa tre Mizpa na nseŋ ya kaa wɔ basa nɛ b ka kasawule na so na to. B ka mɔ Gɛmaliya be asheŋ

english_verse: Gedaliah told them, “There's no need to be afraid of the Babylonians. Everything will be fine, if we live peacefully and obey King Nebuchadnezzar.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Gɛdaliya kaŋɛ bumo le: “Ma e kaŋɛ menyi na fanɛ a maŋ daga fanɛ men tɔr kapɔŋ n sa Babilɔnebi na. Menyeeŋ tiŋ n chena nfe nsaa shuŋ Babilɔn be ewura nɛ asheŋ e nite nɛnɛ n sa menyi.

english_verse: I will stay here at Mizpah and meet with the Babylonian officials on each of their visits. But you must go back to your towns and bring in the harvest, then store the wine, olive oil, and dried fruit.”
translation_verse: Ŋ gbagba beeŋ chena Mizpa nfe, saŋɛ na so Babilɔnebi na ya ba nfe meeŋ yili menyi be katelamu ashi bumo be anishito. Menyeeŋ tiŋ m bɛta n yɔ menyi be ndeana to n ya kaa chala eyabra nɛ asɔrsoana nɛ ɔlif be ŋkuana a yili.”

english_verse: Earlier, when the Babylonians had invaded Judah, many of the Jews escaped to Moab, Ammon, Edom, and several other countries. But these Jews heard that the king of Babylonia had appointed Gedaliah as ruler of Judah, and that only a few people were left there. So the Jews in these other countries came back to Judah and helped with the grape and fruit harvest, which was especially large that year. Gedaliah Is Murdered
translation_verse: nɛ b lar mboŋ nɛ b daŋ pesaŋ to n yɔ na m bɛta m ba Juda be efuli so. B daŋ ba Gɛdaliya kutɔ ashi Mizpa nna m ba chɛ to nɛ b chala eyabra nɛ asɔrso damta nɛ a chɔ nfɛ nɛ e choŋ na peya. B ka mɔ Gɛdaliya be asheŋ

english_verse: One day, Johanan got together with some of the other men who had been army officers, and they came to Mizpah and met with Gedaliah.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Johanan nɛ benapo nɛ b daŋ kini ketɔr kapɔŋ nsaa wɔ kupuŋ to na be benimuana na ba Gɛdaliya kutɔ ashi Mizpa

english_verse: They said, “Gedaliah, we came to warn you that King Baalis of Ammon hired Ishmael to murder you!” Gedaliah refused to believe them,
translation_verse: nseŋ ba kaŋɛ mo le: “Fo maŋ nyi fanɛ Ammɔn be ewura Baalis shuŋi Ishmaɛl nna fanɛ e ba mɔ fo a?” Ama Gɛdaliya daa maŋ yirda kumo.

english_verse: so Johanan went to Gedaliah privately and said, “Let me kill Ishmael. No one will find out who did it. There are only a few people left in Judah, but they are depending on you. And if you are murdered, they will be scattered or killed.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Johanan nawule yɔ Gɛdaliya kutɔ n ya kaŋɛ mo le: “Shin nɛ n ya mɔ Ishmaɛl nɛ esa kikɛ maaŋ pin esa nɛ e wora loŋ. Basa gbrɛbi ko e ka Juda be efuli so, ama fo nɛ bumo alɛ kikɛ baa keni na. Nɛ fo baŋ wu baaŋ pesaŋ to ŋko n wu gba.”

english_verse: But in the seventh month, Ishmael came to Mizpah with ten of his soldiers. He had been one of the king's officials and was a member of the royal family. Ishmael and his men were invited to eat with Gedaliah.
translation_verse: Kafɛ nɛ Johanan ya ji Gɛdaliya asoe to a laŋɛ kemɔ Ishmaɛl be kaplɛa so na be kufɔl shunusopo to nɛ Ishmaɛl nɛ e la Netaniya pibinyɛn nɛ Ɛlshama mo nanabi nseŋ shi kuwurji be kanaŋ to a la ewura be ekrachi na to be eko na yɔ Mizpa. Mo nɛ basa kudu ko e daŋ yɔ ndoŋ nɛ b ya wu Gɛdaliya nɛ e la gomena na. Jemanɛ nɛ bumo kikɛ daŋ chena a ji na

english_verse: During the meal, Ishmael and his soldiers killed Gedaliah, the man chosen as ruler of Judah by the king of Babylonia.
translation_verse: nɛ Ishmaɛl nɛ basa kudu nɛ b daa wɔ mo kutɔ na pee etokobi m mɔ Gɛdaliya.

english_verse: Then they killed the Jews who were with Gedaliah, and they also killed the Babylonian soldiers who were there.
translation_verse: Ishmaɛl daŋ mɔ Israɛlebi nɛ Babilɔnebi be benapo nɛ b daa wɔ Gɛdaliya kutɔ ashi Mizpa na nna n ti so.

english_verse: The next day, the murders had still not been discovered,
translation_verse: Kumo be ŋklade, pɔɛŋ nɛ esa kikɛ pin Gɛdaliya be kemɔ na be asheŋ,

english_verse: Ishmael went out the town gate to meet them. He pretended to be weeping, and he asked them to come into Mizpah to meet with Gedaliah, the ruler of Judah.
translation_verse: Ishmaɛl daŋ wora fanɛ e ka bee shu nna n lar Mizpa to n ya shɛr bumo to. E ka ba fo bumo nɛ e kaŋɛ bumo le: “Men jande, men luri m ba keni Gɛdaliya.”

english_verse: But after they were inside the town, Ishmael ordered his soldiers to kill them and throw their bodies into a well.
translation_verse: B ka baŋ ya ka luri kade na to, epul na to nɛ Ishmaɛl kaŋɛ mbe benapo fanɛ b mɔ bumo nseŋ ta bumo n lɛ ketirbu to.

english_verse: He let ten of the men live, because they offered to give him supplies of wheat, barley, olive oil, and honey they had hidden in a field.
translation_verse: Ama pɔɛŋ nɛ b mɔ bumo, basa na to be basa kudu ko daŋ kaŋɛ Ishmaɛl le nna: “Jande, sa maŋ mɔ anyi! An kɔ ayu be yiri yiri nɛ ɔlif be ŋku nɛ mushoŋ nɛ an ta ŋ ŋana kupuŋ to. Amoso e daa maŋ shin nɛ b mɔ bumo ere.

english_verse: The well that he filled with bodies had been dug by King Asa of Judah to store rainwater, because he was afraid that King Baasha of Israel might surround Mizpah and keep the people from getting to their water supply.
translation_verse: Ketirbu nɛ Ishmaɛl nɛ mbe benapo daŋ ta basa nɛ b daŋ mɔ n ti Gɛdaliya so n lɛ to na daa la ketirbu nɛ Juda be ewura Asa na daŋ kur a suse bɔrɛchu jemanɛ nɛ Israɛl be kuwurgboŋ nɛ k wɔ kelargato be esoso na be ewura Baasha na daa kɔ mo kena na nna. Ishmaɛl daŋ mɔ basa na nna m bɔlɔ ketirbu na.

english_verse: Nebuzaradan, King Nebuchadnezzar's officer in charge of the guard, had left King Zedekiah's daughters and many other people at Mizpah, and he had put Gedaliah in charge of them. But now Ishmael took them all prisoner and led them toward Ammon, on the other side of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman, nɛ e pɛ ewura Zɛdikaya be mbichesobi nɛ basa nɛ Nebuzaradan, nɛ e la benapo nɛ baa kuŋ Babilɔn be ewura na be enimu na, daŋ yige n sa Gɛdaliya fanɛ e baa keni so na ŋ keta bumo a yɔ Ammɔn be efuli so ashi Lɔr nɛ baa tre Jɔɔdan na be kaba ndoŋ.”

english_verse: Johanan and the other army officers heard what Ishmael had done.
translation_verse: Johanan nɛ benapo be benimuana nɛ b wɔ mo kutɔ na ka nu kushuŋ lubi nɛ Ishmaɛl shuŋ na be asheŋ

english_verse: So they and their troops chased Ishmael and caught up with him at the large pit at Gibeon.
translation_verse: nɛ b keta bumo be benapo n ju m buu bumo so n ya tu bumo ashi kepa nɛ k wɔ Gibiɔn na.

english_verse: and turned around and ran toward Johanan.
translation_verse: nɛ b kilgi a shile a yɔ Johanan kutɔ.

english_verse: But Ishmael and eight of his men escaped and went to Ammon. Johanan Decides To Take the People to Egypt
translation_verse: Ama Ishmaɛl nɛ mbe basa na be basa aburwa bre nya n shile n yɔ Ammɔn be kasawule so nɛ Johanan maŋ nya bumo m pɛ.

english_verse: Johanan and the officers had rescued the women, children, and royal officials that Ishmael had taken prisoner after killing Gedaliah. Johanan led the people from Gibeon
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Johanan nɛ benapo be benimuana mɔlga beche nɛ mbia nɛ ewurkpa be ekrachi nɛ Ishmaɛl daŋ mɔ Gɛdaliya ashi Mizpa nseŋ pɛ bumo a yɔ na. Nɛ Johanan juŋkpar basa na n shi Gibiɔn

english_verse: toward Egypt. They wanted to go there, because they were afraid of what the Babylonians would do when they found out that Ishmael had killed Gedaliah, the ruler appointed by King Nebuchadnezzar. The People Ask Jeremiah To Pray for Them On the way to Egypt, we stopped at the town of Geruth Chimham near Bethlehem.
translation_verse: a yɔ Ijipt be efuli so. B ka wɔ ekpa to a yɔ Ijipt na nɛ b ya chena kade nɛ baa tre Gɛrut Kimham nɛ k mata Bɛtlɛhɛm na n wushi.

english_verse: Johanan, Jezaniah, the other army officers, and everyone else in the group, came to me
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ benapo be benimuana na nɛ Kerii pibinyɛn, Johanan nɛ Hoshaya pibinyɛn, Azariya nɛ basagboŋ nɛ bebɔlpo kikɛ chala abar m ba ma, Jɛremaya kutɔ

english_verse: and said, “Please, Jeremiah, pray to the Lord your God for us. Judah used to have many people, but as you can see, only a few of us are left.
translation_verse: m ba kaŋɛ ma le: “Jande, wora kusɔ nɛ anyee kule fo ere n sa anyi. Kule Enyɛnpe, anyi be Ebɔrɛ na n sa anyi kikɛ nɛ an ji efute nsaa wɔ ŋkpa to ere. Jemanɛ nɛ k choŋ na an daa shi nna, ama fo gbagba beeŋ tiŋ n wu fanɛ naniere anyi basa gbrɛbi e ka.

english_verse: Ask the Lord to tell us where he wants us to go and what he wants us to do.”
translation_verse: Amoso kule Enyɛnpe, anyi be Ebɔrɛ na nɛ e ŋini anyi kakpa nɛ anyeeŋ yɔ nɛ kusɔ nɛ anyeeŋ wora.”

english_verse: Johanan, the officers, and the other people. So I called them together
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ n tre Johanan nɛ benapo be benimuana na nɛ basa pɔtɛ nɛ b ti so na kikɛ m ba abar so

english_verse: and told them that the Lord God of Israel had said: You asked Jeremiah to pray and find out what you should do.
translation_verse: nseŋ kaŋɛ bumo le: “Kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe, Israɛl be Ebɔrɛ nɛ men shuŋi ma mo kutɔ fanɛ n ya kule mo n sa menyi na kaŋɛ nde.

english_verse: I am sorry that I had to punish you, and so I now tell you to stay here in Judah, where I will plant you and build you up, instead of tearing you down and uprooting you.
translation_verse: E yɛ: ‘Nɛ menyee sha kechena kasawule ere so, kumo ere mee leŋ menyi to nna nɛ men chena kumo so nɛ m baa chɛ menyi to, saŋɛ na so men maaŋ naŋ lar kumo so. Kemur nɛ n shin nɛ k ba menyi so na sa ma kebɔltofinfin damta ga.

english_verse: Don't be afraid of the King of Babylonia. I will protect you from him,
translation_verse: Men sa maa ŋana Babilɔn be ewura na. Ma nɛ menyi e wɔtɔ. Ma alɛ beeŋ baa kuŋ menyi nseŋ mɔlga menyi ashi mbe eleŋgboŋ to.

english_verse: and I will even force him to have mercy on you and give back your farms.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal ŋ ka bee wu kuwɔr so, meeŋ shin nɛ e wu menyi kuwɔr nseŋ shin nɛ men bɛta n yɔ epe. Ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e kaŋɛ na.’

english_verse: You are afraid of war, starvation, and disease here in Judah, but they will follow you to Egypt and kill you there. None of you will survive the disasters I will send.
translation_verse: Basa kama nɛ b yili kumo fanɛ baaŋ yɔ Ijipt n ya chena na beeŋ wu kena to ŋko akoŋ ŋko kulɔ beeŋ mɔ bumo. Bumo to be ekama maaŋ ji efute, ekoŋwule gba maaŋ gelge jɛrbi nɛ meeŋ bar bumo so na.’

english_verse: I, the Lord, was angry with the people of Jerusalem and punished them. And if you go to Egypt, I will be angry and punish you the same way. You will never again see your homeland. People will be horrified at what I do to you, and they will use the name of your city as a curse word. Jeremiah Gives a Warning
translation_verse: Ade be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpetale, Israɛl be Ebɔrɛ na naŋ kaŋɛ le: ‘Nɛ men kaŋ kini n yɔ Ijipt, kananɛ n daŋ nya agbo ga n wɔtɔ Jerusalɛm be basa nseŋ gberge bumo kusoe na nɛ meeŋ nya agbo n wɔtɔ menyi alɛ gba nseŋ gberge menyi kusoe. Menyi be asheŋ beeŋ baa chinchiŋ basa nɛ b baa ta menyi kadegboŋ na be ketre a shoduu basa. Menyi alɛ maaŋ naŋ wu kakpa ere kenishiso kikɛ.’ ”

english_verse: I told the people: You escaped the disaster that struck Judah, but now the Lord warns you to stay away from Egypt.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ n naŋ kaŋɛ le: “Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na teŋ ŋ kaŋɛ menyi basa nɛ men ka a wɔ Juda be efuli so na fanɛ men sa maŋ yɔ Ijipt be efuli so. Ŋkpal loŋ so mee kpele menyi kusoe naniere nna

english_verse: You asked me to pray and find out what the Lord our God wants you to do, and you promised to obey him. But that was a terrible mistake,
translation_verse: fanɛ kewora n foe gboŋgboŋi nɛ menyee shin nɛ men wora na. Menyi e kaŋɛ ma fanɛ ŋ kule Enyɛnpe, anyi be Ebɔrɛ na n sa menyi nseŋ nase kɔnɔ fanɛ kusɔ kama nɛ e kaŋɛ menyeeŋ wora kumo.

english_verse: because now that I have given you the Lord's answer, you refuse to obey him.
translation_verse: Naniere ŋ kaŋɛ menyi kusɔ nɛ e kaŋɛ, ama menyi alɛ kini kewora kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe, menyi be Ebɔrɛ na shuŋi ma fanɛ m ba kaŋɛ menyi na kasonu.

english_verse: I told the people everything the Lord had told me.
translation_verse: Ŋ ka kaŋɛ basa na kusɔ kama nɛ Enyɛnpe, bumo be Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ na n loge,

english_verse: But Azariah, Johanan and some other arrogant men said to me, “You're lying! The Lord didn't tell you to say that we shouldn't go to Egypt.
translation_verse: nɛ Hoshaya pibinyɛn, Azariya nɛ Kerii pibinyɛn, Johanan nɛ basa kpeŋso na be beko kaŋɛ ma le: “Efɛ nɛ fee ku! Enyɛnpe, anyi be Ebɔrɛ na maŋ shuŋi fo fanɛ fo ba kaŋɛ anyi fanɛ an sa maŋ ya chena Ijipt be efuli so.

english_verse: Baruch son of Neriah must have told you to say that. He wants the Babylonians to capture us, so they can take us away to Babylonia or even kill us.”
translation_verse: Neriya pibinyɛn, Baruk e susu fo n wɔtɔ anyi, saŋɛ na so Babilɔnebi na beeŋ nya eleŋ anyi so nseŋ mɔ anyi ŋko ŋ keta anyi n yɔ Babilɔn be efuli so.”

english_verse: Johanan, the other army officers, and everyone else refused to stay in Judah in spite of the Lord's command.
translation_verse: Amoso Johanan nɛ benapo be benimuana na nɛ basa pɔtɛana na be ekama daa maŋ wora kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ na kasonu n chena Juda be kasawule so.

english_verse: So Johanan and the officers led us away toward Egypt. The group that left Judah included those who had been scattered in other countries and who had then come back to live in Judah.
translation_verse: Johanan nɛ benapo be benimuana na keta basa nɛ b daŋ pesaŋ to n shile n yɔ efuli pɔtɛana so nseŋ naŋ bɛta m ba Juda be kasawule so na nna n yɔ Ijipt be efuli so.

english_verse: Baruch and I and others in the group had been staying with Gedaliah, because Nebuzaradan, the Babylonian officer in charge of the guard, had ordered him to take care of the king's daughters and quite a few men, women, and children.
translation_verse: Bumo alɛ daŋ naŋ keta ma nɛ Baruk nɛ benyɛn nɛ beche nɛ mbia nɛ ewura Zɛdikaya be mbichesobi nɛ Nebuzaradan nɛ e daa la benapo nɛ baa kuŋ Babilɔn be ewura na be enimu na daŋ yige n sa Gɛdaliya fanɛ e baa keni so na gba nna n ti so n yɔ Ijipt be efuli so.

english_verse: The people disobeyed the Lord and went to Egypt. The group had settled in Tahpanhes,
translation_verse: B daa maŋ wora Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kasonu nseŋ daŋ yɔ Ijipt n ya chena kadegboŋ nɛ baa tre Taapanes na.

english_verse: when the Lord told me:
translation_verse: Ashi Taapanes ndoŋ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ ma le:

english_verse: Then tell them that I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, have sent for my servant, Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia. I will bring him here and have him set up his throne and his royal tent over these stones that I told you to bury.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ fo kaŋɛ bumo fanɛ ma, Enyɛnpetale, Israɛl be Ebɔrɛ na beeŋ shin nɛ ma kenya, Babilɔn be ewura Nebukadneeza e ba nfe m ba ta mbe kuwurputi n nase ajembu nɛ fo puli ere so nseŋ chena kumo so n ji kuwura bumo so.

english_verse: He will attack Egypt and kill many of its people; others will die of disease or be dragged away as prisoners.
translation_verse: Ewura Nebukadneeza beeŋ ba kɔ Ijipt be basa kena nseŋ mɔ bumo be basa damta. Alɔ beeŋ mɔ beko nɛ b pɛ beko malɛ ŋ gberge bumo n yɔ Babilɔn be efuli so.

english_verse: I will let him set Egypt's temples on fire, and he will either burn or carry off their idols. He will destroy the sacred monuments at the temple of the sun-god. Then Nebuchadnezzar will pick the land clean, just like a shepherd picking the lice off his clothes. And he will return safely home.
translation_verse: Babilɔn be ewura beeŋ mur kegbirlambu nɛ baa shuŋ epeŋi kumo to ashi kadegboŋ nɛ baa tre Hiliopolis ashi Ijipt be efuli so na nseŋ chɔɔ Ijipt be agbirana be elambuana kikɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord told me to speak with the Jews who were living in the towns of Migdol, Tahpanhes, and Memphis in northern Egypt, and also to those living in southern Egypt. He told me to tell them:
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na malga ma kutɔ a laŋɛ Israɛlebi nɛ b wɔ Ijipt be efuli so be ndegboŋana nɛ baa tre Migdɔl nɛ Taapanes nɛ Mɛmfis nɛ e wɔ efuli na be kelargato be esoso na nɛ bumo nɛ a wɔ efuli na be kelargato be kaseto be kaba so na be kaplɛa so.

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. You saw how I destroyed Jerusalem and the towns of Judah. They lie empty and in ruins today,
translation_verse: Kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpetale, Israɛl be Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ nde: “Menyi gbagba wu kemur nɛ n shin nɛ k ba Jerusalɛm nɛ Juda be efuli so be ndegboŋana na kikɛ so. Hale nɛ mbre a kraa dese fuloŋ nɛ esa kikɛ maŋ wɔ amo to,

english_verse: Time after time I sent my servants the prophets to tell the people of Judah how much I hated their disgusting sins. The prophets warned them to stop sinning,
translation_verse: Ma alɛ kraa shuŋi ma anya anebiana na menyi kutɔ nɛ baa kaŋɛ menyi fanɛ men sa maa wora asheŋ lubi nɛ ŋ kishi na.

english_verse: but they refused to listen and would not stop worshiping other gods.
translation_verse: Ama menyi maa nu ŋko n wɔtɔ lakal kusɔ nɛ baa kaŋɛ na to. Men kini keyige kebaalara esarga a sa agbirana na.

english_verse: You have made me angry by worshiping idols and burning incense to other gods after you came here to Egypt. You will die such a disgusting death, that other nations will use the name of Judah as a curse word.
translation_verse: Manɛ nna nɛ menyee bunyaŋ agbirana nsaa lara esarga a sa amo ashi Ijipt a wɔtɔ ma agbo to? Menyee wora le nna nɛ men mur menyi be amu, saŋɛ na so durnya to be efuli kama so be basa beeŋ baa keni menyi jiga nsaa ta menyi be ketre a sho basa kɔnɔ a?

english_verse: When you were living in Jerusalem and Judah, you followed the example of your ancestors in doing evil things, just like your kings and queens.
translation_verse: Menyi ka daa wɔ Jerusalɛm nɛ Juda be efuli so na, asheŋ lubi nɛ men nananyɛnana nɛ menyi be bewuraana nɛ bewurcheana daŋ wora na nɛ menyi alɛ gba daa kute to a wora.

english_verse: Even now, your pride keeps you from respecting me and obeying the laws and teachings I gave you and your ancestors.
translation_verse: Hale naniere gba, menyi be kamoowuso menyi maa sa ma bunyaŋ gba a bishi nɛ menyee wora ma mbraana nɛ keŋini nɛ n ta n sa men nananyɛnana na kasonu.

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, have decided to wipe you out with disasters.
translation_verse: Amoso ma, Enyɛnpetale, Israɛl be Ebɔrɛ na yili kumo fanɛ meeŋ shin nɛ men ji jɛrbi m mur.

english_verse: There were only a few of you left in Judah, and you decided to go to Egypt. But you will die such horrible deaths in war or from starvation, that people of other countries will use the name of Judah as a curse word.
translation_verse: Juda be basa nɛ b ka efuli na so ndoŋ nseŋ yili kumo bumo be ŋgbene to fanɛ baaŋ yɔ Ijipt be efuli so na bre, meeŋ shin nɛ bumo kikɛ e mur. Bumo to be benimu nɛ mbia kikɛ beeŋ wu ashi Ijipt ashi kena to ŋko akoŋ beeŋ mɔ bumo. Bumo be asheŋ beeŋ baa chinchiŋ basa nɛ b baa wora bumo eyurto nsaa ta bumo be ketre a sho basa kɔnɔ.

english_verse: I punished Jerusalem with war, hunger, and disease, and that's how I will punish you.
translation_verse: Kananɛ n ta kena nɛ akoŋ nɛ alɔ ŋ gberge Jerusalɛm to be basa kusoe na, aloŋ nɛ meeŋ gberge bumo nɛ b wɔ Ijipt na kusoe.

english_verse: None of you will survive. You may hope to return to Judah someday, but only a very few of you will escape death and be able to go back. The People Refuse To Worship the Lord
translation_verse: Basa nɛ b daŋ ka a wɔ Juda be efuli so nseŋ lar m ba kaa wɔ Ijipt na be ekama maaŋ nya n shile m mɔlga mbe kumu ŋko n ji efute. Bumo to be esa koŋwule gba maaŋ bɛta n yɔ Juda, kakpa nɛ b naa yɛlga kebɛta n yɔ na. Bumo to be basa gbrɛbi ko e naŋ nya m bɛta n yɔ.”

english_verse: A large number of Jews from both northern and southern Egypt listened to me as I told them what the Lord had said. Most of the men in the crowd knew that their wives often burned incense to other gods. So they and their wives shouted:
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ benyɛn nɛ b nyi bumo be beche ka bee lara esarga a sa agbirana nɛ beche nɛ b daa yil ndoŋ na, n ta Israɛlebi nɛ b daa wɔ Ijipt be kelargato be kaseto be kaba so na nɛ jimaŋ damta na kikɛ boŋ to awɔrso ŋ kaŋɛ ma le:

english_verse: Jeremiah, what do we care if you speak in the Lord's name? We refuse to listen!
translation_verse: “An kini kenu kusɔ nɛ fo kaŋɛ anyi ashi Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be ketre to nna.

english_verse: We have promised to worship the goddess Astarte, the Queen of Heaven, and that is exactly what we are going to do. We will burn incense and offer sacrifices of wine to her, just as we, our ancestors, our kings, and our leaders did when we lived in Jerusalem and the other towns of Judah. We had plenty of food back then. We were well off, and nothing bad ever happened to us.
translation_verse: Kusɔ kama nɛ an kaŋɛ fanɛ anyeeŋ wora na nɛ anyeeŋ wora. Anyeeŋ lara esarga n sa anyi be kegbirche nɛ e la ebɔrɛso be Ewurche na, nseŋ naŋ ta yabra n to nchu n sa mo, fanɛ kananɛ an nananyɛnana nɛ anyi be ewura nɛ bejuŋkparpoana na daŋ wora ashi Juda be ndeana to nɛ Jerusalɛm be agbembi so na. Kumo be kaman, an daa kɔ ajibi damta nseŋ daŋ dii dama nɛ etɔrɔbi kikɛ malɛ daa maŋ wɔ anyi to.

english_verse: Then the women said, “When we lived in Judah, we worshiped the Queen of Heaven and offered sacrifices of wine and special loaves of bread shaped like her. Our husbands knew what we were doing, and they approved of it.”
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ beche na naŋ kaŋɛ le: “Anyi ka daa wɔ Juda be efuli so na an daa bunyaŋ ebɔrɛso be Ewurche na nna nsaa ta yabra nɛ ebodobodo nɛ an lɔŋɛ fanɛ mbe kaduli a lara esarga a sa mo. An kulana malɛ daa nyi kusɔ nɛ an daa wora na nseŋ daa yil anyi be kaman ashi amo kikɛ to nna.”

english_verse: Then I told the crowd:
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ma alɛ kaŋɛ jimaŋ na le:

english_verse: Don't you think the Lord knew that you and your ancestors, your leaders and kings, and the rest of the people were burning incense to other gods in Jerusalem and everywhere else in Judah?
translation_verse: “Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na daa nyi esarga nɛ menyi nɛ men nananyɛnana nɛ menyi be bewuraana nɛ bejuŋkparpoana na nɛ kasawule na so be basa kikɛ daa lara ashi Juda be ndeana to nɛ Jerusalɛm be agbembi so na be asheŋ.

english_verse: This disaster happened because you worshiped other gods and rebelled against the Lord by refusing to obey him or follow his laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Jɛrbi nɛ men ji ere ba nna ŋkpal men ka lara esarga n sa agbirana nseŋ wora kulubi n da Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na so nsaa maŋ wora mbe mbraana nɛ keŋini kikɛ kasonu so.

english_verse: Keep these promises! But let me tell you what will happen. As surely as I am the Lord God, I swear that I will never again accept any promises you make in my name.
translation_verse: Ama naniere men kaŋ asoe n nu kɔnɔ nɛ ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na bee nase ashi ma ketregboŋ na to a sa menyi Israɛlebi kikɛ nɛ men wɔ Ijipt na. M maaŋ naŋ shin nɛ menyi be ekama e naŋ ta ma ketre n nase kɔnɔ a kaŋɛ le: ‘M bɔ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ nɛ e bee sa ŋkpa na!’

english_verse: Instead of watching over you, I will watch for chances to harm you. Some of you will die in war, and others will starve to death.
translation_verse: Meeŋ shin nɛ menyi maaŋ nyalɛ kikɛ! Menyeeŋ mur. Menyi be galeŋga beeŋ wu kena to ŋko alɔ beeŋ mɔ menyi n ya fo fanɛ menyi to be esa koŋwule gba maaŋ ka.

english_verse: Only a few will escape and return to Judah. Then everyone who went to live in Egypt will know that when I say something will happen, it will—no matter what you say.
translation_verse: Menyi to be gbrɛbi ko e naŋ nya ŋ gelge luwu nseŋ shi Ijipt m bɛta n yɔ Juda be efuli so. Aloŋ, bumo nɛ baaŋ ji efute na beeŋ pin ma nɛ menyi be mmalga be amo nɛ a la kashenteŋ.

english_verse: I will hand over King Hophra of Egypt to those who want to kill him, just as I handed Zedekiah over to Nebuchadnezzar, who wanted to kill him.
translation_verse: Meeŋ ta Ijipt be ewura Hofra m bɔɔ mo doŋana nɛ baa fin mo nɛ b mɔ na enɔ, fanɛ kananɛ n daŋ ta Juda be ewura Zɛdikaya m bɔɔ Babilɔn be ewura Nebukadneeza nɛ e daa la mo doŋ nseŋ daa fin mo nɛ e mɔ na enɔ na.”

english_verse: In the fourth year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, Baruch wrote down everything I had told him.
translation_verse: Jehowakim nɛ e la ewura Josaya pibinyɛn na ka ji Juda be kuwura be kafɛ nasopo to nɛ Baruk sibɛ kusɔ nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ mo na n nase. Kumo be kaman nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ mo

english_verse: Then later, the Lord God of Israel told me to say to Baruch:
translation_verse: kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe, Israɛl be Ebɔrɛ na bee kaŋɛ mo ere Baruk na gbagba.

english_verse: You are moaning and blaming me, the Lord, for your troubles and sorrow, and for being so tired that you can't even rest.
translation_verse: E yɛ: “Baruk, fee kaŋɛ le: ‘M maaŋ naŋ wora shɛŋ! Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na shin nɛ ma etɔrɔbi naŋ ti so nna. M baŋ shu nna n ya gben. M maaŋ naŋ tiŋ n shu gba!’

english_verse: But all over the earth I am tearing down what I built and pulling up what I planted.
translation_verse: Ama ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na bee bure kusɔ nɛ m pɔr na nna nsaa gberge kusɔ nɛ n duu a tia ashi durnya kikɛ to.

english_verse: I am bringing disaster everywhere, so don't even think about making any big plans for yourself. However, I promise that wherever you go, I will at least protect you from death. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Fo ere bee fin asheŋgboŋ nna a sa fo kumu a? Yige amo be kefin. Ŋkpal manɛ so, meeŋ shin nɛ edimɛdi kikɛ e ji jɛrbi, ama kaplɛkama nɛ fo ere yɔ, feeŋ nya n shile m mɔlga fo kumu n ji efute. Ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e kaŋɛ na.”

english_verse: The Lord often told me what to say about the different nations of the world. What the Lord Says about Egypt
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na daŋ malga ma kutɔ a laŋɛ efuliana na be kaplɛa so nna.

english_verse: In the fourth year that Jehoiakim was king of Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia defeated King Neco of Egypt in a battle at the city of Carchemish near the Euphrates River. And here is what the Lord told me to say about the Egyptian army:
translation_verse: Ijipt be asheŋ nɛ e daŋ juŋkpar m malga. Kusɔ nɛ e daŋ kaŋɛ a laŋɛ Ijipt be ewura Niko nɛ Babilɔn be ewura Nebukadneeza daŋ kɔ m pɔɔ so ashi kadegboŋ nɛ baa tre nɛ k mata Lɔrgboŋ nɛ baa tre Yufreetes na be benapo be kaplɛa so. Ewura Jehowakim ka ji Juda be kuwura be kafɛ nasopo to na nɛ loŋ wora. Kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na daŋ kaŋɛ ma nde:

english_verse: What nation is this, that rises like the Nile River overflowing its banks?
translation_verse: Efuli mo nde, nɛ k koso fanɛ kananɛ Nail be Lɔrgboŋ na bee bɔlɔ a dii kumo be agurɔŋgu so ashi Ijipt be efuli so?

english_verse: It is Egypt, rising with a roar like a raging river and saying, “I'll flood the earth, destroying cities, and killing everyone in them.”
translation_verse: Ijipt e koso fanɛ Nail na; k koso fanɛ lɔr ka bɔlɔ n dii kumo be agurɔŋgu so nna. Ijiptebi yɛ: ‘Anyeeŋ koso m buu durnya kikɛ so, anyeeŋ mur ndegboŋana nɛ amo to be basa.

english_verse: Go ahead, Egypt. Tell your chariots and cavalry to attack and fight hard. Order your troops to march out, with Ethiopians and Libyans carrying shields, and the Lydians armed with bows and arrows.
translation_verse: Kaŋɛ egbaŋɛ na kenishipereso fanɛ b baa shile a yɔ nɛ egbaŋɛturko na malɛ e baa shil a chɔ so! Kaŋɛ menyi be esoji na fanɛ b lar m bɛ abar so a yɔ, Itiopiaebi nɛ Libiyaebi na e keta abɛlso be asɔ kuŋamuso, Lidiya be basa na keta ata nɛ atanyembi nna.’ ”

english_verse: But the Lord All-Powerful will win this battle and take revenge on his enemies. His sword will eat them and drink their blood until it is full. They will be killed in the north near the Euphrates River, as a sacrifice to the Lord.
translation_verse: Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na be kachɛ nna na; e beeŋ wora n tal to kabre; kabre e beeŋ gberge mo doŋana kusoe. Mbe tokobi beeŋ mɔ bumo kumo be keparso, nɛ ŋklaŋ e gbiti kumo be kaplɛkama le gbetɛɛ. Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na beeŋ ta bumo n lara sarga ashi kelargato be esoso a mata Yufreetes be Lɔrgboŋ na.

english_verse: All nations have heard you weep; you are disgraced, and they know it. Your troops fall to the ground, stumbling over each other. A Warning for Egypt
translation_verse: Efuliana na nu men be ŋaba be asheŋ; esa kama malɛ nu men be kushu. Soja ko bee fiti mo barkasa nna nɛ bumo benyɔ na kikɛ e tɔr kasawule. Nebukadneeza be keba be asheŋ

english_verse: When King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia was on his way to attack Egypt, the Lord sent me with a warning for every Egyptian town, but especially for Migdol, Memphis, and Tahpanhes. He said to tell them: Prepare to defend yourselves! Everywhere in your nation, people are dying in war.
translation_verse: E yɛ: “Ber kebomboŋ ashi Ijipt be ndeana to; fɔŋfɔŋ ashi Migdɔl nɛ Mɛmfis nɛ Taapanes, ŋ kaŋɛ le: ‘Men wora shiriya ŋ kɔ n suge menyi be amu; asɔ kama nɛ men kɔ na kikɛ beeŋ mur kena to!

english_verse: I have struck down your mighty god Apis and chased him away.
translation_verse: Manɛ nna nɛ menyi be kegbirgboŋ Apis na tɔr? Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e ŋmɛa kumo n lɛ!’

english_verse: Your soldiers stumble over each other and say, “Get up! The enemy will kill us, unless we can escape to our own land.”
translation_verse: Menyi be esoji fiti abar nna n tɔr, nɛ eko kaŋɛ mo barkasa le: ‘Koso manaŋ nɛ an shile bedoŋ be tokobi m mɔlga anyi be amu nseŋ yɔ anyi be basa kutɔ epe!’ ”

english_verse: Egypt, I am the true king, the Lord All-Powerful, and as surely as I live, those enemies who attack will tower over you like Mount Tabor among the hills or Mount Carmel by the sea.
translation_verse: Ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e la ewura. Ma e la Ebɔrɛ nɛ e bee sa ŋkpa na. Kananɛ Tabɔɔ be kebee baa du jeŋgreŋ a chɔ abeeana, nɛ Kaamɛl be kebee malɛ dii awɔlto a chɔ teku na, aloŋ nɛ edoŋ nɛ e beeŋ ba kɔ fo na be eleŋ beeŋ baa chɔ feya.

english_verse: You will be led away captive, so pack a few things to bring with you. Your capital, Memphis, will lie empty and in ruins.
translation_verse: Ijipt be basa, men bela ase n wora shiriya; bedoŋ beeŋ ba pɛ menyi n yɔ kenyaya to. Menyi be kadegboŋ nɛ baa tre Mɛmfis na beeŋ bure a dese fuloŋ nɛ esa kikɛ maaŋ naa wɔ kumo to.

english_verse: An enemy from the north will attack you, beautiful Egypt, like a fly biting a cow.
translation_verse: Ijipt du fanɛ nache fɔlbi nɛ e walɛ kebita nɛ wuloŋ shi kelargato be esoso m ba duŋ mo nna.

english_verse: The enemy army will go forward like a swarm of locusts. Your troops will feel helpless, like a snake in a forest
translation_verse: Ijipt bee fɛɛto nna fanɛ kuwɔ a shile, saŋɛ nɛ bedoŋ be benapo bee ba eleŋ so na. Akpanfu nɛ b ta m ba kaa kɔ mo fanɛ kananɛ basa bee kuya ndibi

english_verse: when men with axes start chopping down trees. It can only hiss and try to escape.
translation_verse: kupo to be ndibi a mur ndibi nɛ a mel abar so na. Bumo be benapo shi ga nɛ esa maaŋ tiŋ ŋ karga bumo; b shi ga a chɔ gba.

english_verse: Your people will be disgraced and captured by the enemy from the north.
translation_verse: Ijipt be basa ji anishinyɔr; basa nɛ b shi kelargato be esoso na kɔ m pɔɔ bumo so.”

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel. Soon I will punish the god Amon of Thebes and the other Egyptian gods, the Egyptian kings, the people of Egypt, and everyone who trusts in the Egyptian power.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman, nɛ Enyɛnpetale, Israɛl be Ebɔrɛ na naŋ kaŋɛ le: “Meeŋ gberge Tebes be kegbir nɛ baa tre Ammɔn na nɛ Ijipt be agbirana nɛ kumo be basa nɛ bewuraana nɛ bekama nɛ b ta bumo be yirda n deŋi Ijipt be eleŋgboŋ so na kusoe.

english_verse: I will hand them over to King Nebuchadnezzar and his army. But I also promise that Egypt will someday have people living here again, just as it had before. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Will Bring Israel Home The Lord said:
translation_verse: Meeŋ ta bumo m bɔɔ ewura Nebukadneeza nɛ mbe benapo enɔ. Ama mee nase kɔnɔ nna fanɛ, kachako Ijipt beeŋ naŋ nya basa nɛ b chena nfe fanɛ kananɛ k daa du na. Ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e kaŋɛ na.” Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ka beeŋ mɔlga mbe basa be asheŋ

english_verse: Israel, don't be afraid. Someday I will bring you home from foreign lands. You and your descendants will live in peace and safety, with nothing to fear.
translation_verse: “Ma basa, men sa maa lɔ kufu. Israɛl be basa, men sa maa chicha kufuso. Kachako meeŋ lara menyi ashi efuli pɔtɛana so m bar menyi epe. Menyi nɛ menyi be kaman to ebi kikɛ beeŋ ba kaa wɔ kayurwushi to nɛ esa kikɛ maaŋ naŋ ta kufu n da menyi.

english_verse: So don't be afraid, even though now you deserve to be punished and have been scattered among other nations. But when I destroy them, I will protect you. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Meeŋ ba menyi kutɔ m ba mɔlga menyi. Ma alɛ beeŋ mur efuliana nɛ n daŋ pesaŋ menyi to n yɔ amo so na, ama m maaŋ mur menyi ere. M maaŋ shin nɛ men wora kulubi nɛ m maŋ gberge menyi kumo be kusoe; ama meeŋ gberge menyi kusoe na nɛ kumo be ekpa so nna. Ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e kaŋɛ na.”

english_verse: Before the king of Egypt attacked the town of Gaza, the Lord told me to say to the Philistines:
translation_verse: Pɔɛŋ nɛ Ijipt be ewura ya kɔ kade nɛ baa tre Gaaza na kena, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na daŋ kaŋɛ ma nna fanɛ ŋ kaŋɛ Filistiebi na le.

english_verse: You refugees from Crete, your time has now come, and I will destroy you. None of you will be left to help the cities of Tyre and Sidon.
translation_verse: Filistiebi be kemur be saŋɛ fo, saŋɛ fo nɛ bumo be ndegboŋ nɛ baa tre Tayɛ nɛ Sidɔn na e mur nɛ b maaŋ naŋ nya kechɛto. Ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e naaŋ mur Filistiebi nɛ b shi keplasawule nɛ baa tre Kriit na m ba na.

english_verse: You ask how long will I continue to attack you with my sword, then you tell me to put it away and leave you alone.
translation_verse: Menyee shu a kaŋɛ le: ‘Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be Tokobi! Saŋɛ mo nɛ feeŋ yige anyi be kemɔ? Bɛta n luri fo efar to n ya kaa wɔ kumo to a wushi!’

english_verse: But how can my sword rest, when I have commanded it to attack Ashkelon and the seacoast?
translation_verse: Ama nuso nɛ k beeŋ tiŋ n wushi, jemanɛ nɛ n sa kumo kushuŋ fanɛ k shuŋ? Ŋ kaŋɛ kumo kenishipereso fanɛ k kɔ Ashkɛlɔn nɛ basa nɛ b chena teku be ekarso na.”

english_verse: The Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, told me to say to the nation of Moab: The town of Nebo is doomed; Kiriathaim will be captured and disgraced, and even its fortress will be left in ruins.
translation_verse: Kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpetale, Israɛl be Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ a laŋɛ efuli nɛ baa tre Mowab na be kaplɛa so nde: “Asheŋ maaŋ nyalɛ n sa kade nɛ baa tre Nebo na; ŋkpal manɛ so, k beeŋ mur cheche. Bedoŋ beeŋ kɔ n suge Kiriataim, kumo be mboŋ lempoana beeŋ bure n tɔr nɛ kumo be basa e ji anishinyɔr.

english_verse: No one honors you, Moab. In Heshbon, enemies make plans to end your life. My sword will leave only silence in your town named “Quiet.”
translation_verse: Mowabebi, esa kikɛ maaŋ naaŋ maŋkura menyi. Bedoŋ bee kre keku menyi be ŋkpa so ashi men be kadegboŋ nɛ baa tre Hɛshbɔn na to. Kusɔ nɛ ma tokobi beeŋ wora e la keshin nɛ kakpa a wora shruum ashi kade nɛ baa tre Madmen na.

english_verse: The people of Horonaim will cry for help, as their town is attacked and destroyed.
translation_verse: Basa nɛ b wɔ Horoneem na beeŋ shu n fin kechɛto jemanɛ nɛ bedoŋ beeŋ kɔ bumo be kade m mur kumo na.

english_verse: Moab will be shattered! Your children will sob
translation_verse: Mowab be efuli na beeŋ mur! Kumo be mbia beeŋ shu;

english_verse: and cry on their way up to the town of Luhith; on the road to Horonaim they will tell of disasters.
translation_verse: baaŋ shu anishichubi m bɔla ekpa a yɔ kade nɛ baa tre Luhif nɛ k wɔ Horoneem be ekpa to na. Baaŋ baa kute ejɛrbi nɛ b ji na be asheŋ.

english_verse: Run for your lives! Head into the desert like a wild donkey.
translation_verse: Men shile manaŋ m mɔlga menyi be efute! Men ta kumu n shoŋi keshishɛrsawule so a yɔ fanɛ kurma nɛ e yeŋ na.

english_verse: You thought you could be saved by your power and wealth, but you will be captured along with your god Chemosh, his priests, and officials.
translation_verse: Mowabebi, men ta menyi be yirda nna n wɔtɔ menyi be eleŋ nɛ kedamaya to, ama naniere bedoŋ beeŋ kɔ m pɔɔ menyi so nseŋ yɛr menyi be kegbir nɛ baa tre Chemɔsh na nɛ kumo be agbirwuraana nɛ benimuana na efuli pɔtɛ wɔfɔ so.

english_verse: Not one of your towns will escape destruction. I have told your enemies, “Wipe out the valley and the flatlands of Moab.
translation_verse: Menyi be ndeana na be kukoŋwule gba maaŋ lar kemur na to. Menyi be apreŋsawule nɛ ataŋɛ kikɛ gba beeŋ mur. Ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e kaŋɛ na.

english_verse: I want you to kill the Moabites, and if you let them escape, I will put a curse on you.”
translation_verse: Mee sha fanɛ men mɔ Mowabebi na nna; men kaŋ shin nɛ b nya n shile m mɔlga bumo be amu meeŋ sho menyi kɔnɔ.”

english_verse: Then you will be ashamed, because your god Chemosh cannot save you, just as Bethel could not help the Israelites.
translation_verse: Saŋɛ na so Mowabebi na maaŋ naŋ yirda bumo be kegbir nɛ baa tre Chemɔsh na, fanɛ kananɛ Israɛlebi na maŋ naŋ yirda kade nɛ baa tre Bɛtɛl nɛ b daŋ ta yirda n wɔtɔ kumo to jemanɛ ko na.

english_verse: You claim that your soldiers are strong and brave.
translation_verse: Mowab be benyɛn bee kaŋɛ nna fanɛ bumo ere la benapo lempo nɛ b kɔ kenyɛn nna.

english_verse: But I am the Lord, the all-powerful King, and I promise that enemies will overpower your towns. Even your best warriors will die in the battle.
translation_verse: Ama ma e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ; Ewura nɛ e kɔ eleŋ ga na. Mee nase kɔnɔ nna fanɛ bedoŋ beeŋ ba kɔ kena m pɔ menyi be ndeana so. Menyi be benapo lempo gba beeŋ wu kena na to.

english_verse: It won't be long now— disaster will hit Moab!
translation_verse: K maaŋ chɛr ko nɛ Mowab be basa e ji jɛrbi;

english_verse: People in the town of Dibon, you will be honored no more, so have a seat in the dust. Your walls will be torn down when the enemies attack.
translation_verse: Menyi bumo nɛ men yɔ kade nɛ baa tre Dibɔn na e gbelge menyi be kemaŋkura so m ba chena kasawule eshishɛrpumpuŋ to; ŋkpal manɛ so, emo nɛ e beeŋ mur Mowab na ba nɛ e ba mur menyi be ndegboŋ lempoana na cheche.

english_verse: They will answer, “Moab has been defeated! Weep with us in shame. Tell everyone at the Arnon River that Moab is destroyed.”
translation_verse: Baaŋ kaŋɛ menyi le: “Mowabebi kɔ kena n tɔr nna! Men shu n sa bumo. B ji anishinyɔr. Men ber kumo be kebomboŋ ashi Aanɔn be Lɔr na be ekarso, fanɛ Mowab be efuli na mur!

english_verse: My decision is final— your army will be crushed, and your power broken.
translation_verse: Mowab be eleŋgboŋ nɛ yuku kikɛ mur; bumo be benapo maaŋ naŋ tiŋ n wora shɛŋ. Ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e kaŋɛ na.”

english_verse: You made fun of my people and treated them like criminals caught in the act.
translation_verse: Mowab be basa, men baa nyiŋi kananɛ men daŋ wora Israɛl be basa eyurto. Men daŋ wora bumo nna fanɛ b ka la beyu nɛ besugepo na.

english_verse: Now you must leave your towns and live like doves in the shelter of cliffs and canyons.
translation_verse: Menyi basa nɛ men wɔ Mowab be efuli so na e lar menyi be ndeana to nseŋ ya kaa wɔ abeelaŋ to fanɛ kananɛ elepɔ bee tɔ asha abeelaŋ to a di to na.

english_verse: But I also know bragging will never save you.
translation_verse: Ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nyi bumo be ŋkpensheŋ, ama bumo be mpuchi maaŋ tiŋ m mɔlga bumo.

english_verse: People of Sibmah, you were like a vineyard heavy with grapes, and with branches reaching north to the town of Jazer and west to the Dead Sea. But you have been destroyed, and so I will weep for you, as the people of Jazer weep for the vineyards.
translation_verse: Ma alɛ beeŋ shu n sa basa nɛ b wɔ kade nɛ baa tre Sibma nseŋ shu a chɔ loŋ n sa basa nɛ b wɔ kade nɛ baa tre Jaza na. Fo, kadegboŋ Sibma du fanɛ kefeelebi nɛ kumo be ayabi salga to n ya fo Teku Wuso na ashi epeŋitɔrkpa be kaba so hale n ya fo Jaza nna. Ama naniere fo asɔrso nɛ baa tre greeps nɛ fee sɔr kechali so na mur.

english_verse: Harvest celebrations are gone from the orchards and farms of Moab. I have silenced the shouts of people making wine.
translation_verse: Kagbenefuli nɛ kagbenewushi maŋ naa wɔ basa to ashi Mowab be adɔsawule nɛ ndibisɔrso be adɔana so ŋkpal b ka maŋ naa nya adɔjibi nɛ greeps, a wora yabra so.

english_verse: I will get rid of anyone who burns incense to the gods of Moab or offers sacrifices at their shrines. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Meeŋ shin nɛ Mowab be basa e yige kebaalara esarga nsaa chɔɔ eduwu ashi bumo be agbirase a sa bumo be agbirana. Ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e kaŋɛ na.

english_verse: In my heart I moan for Moab, like a funeral song played on a flute. I mourn for the people of the town of Kir-Heres, because their wealth is gone. *
translation_verse: “Mee shu ma kagbene to nna a sa Mowab nɛ Kir Hɛrɛs be basa, fanɛ kananɛ esa bee foŋ kalopi a boŋ keeli be kasha na, ŋkpal manɛ so, bumo ere be asɔ nɛ b kɔ kikɛ mur.

english_verse: The people of Moab mourn on the rooftops and in the streets. Men cut off their beards, people shave their heads; they make cuts on their hands and wear sackcloth. And it's all because I, the Lord, have shattered Moab like a jar that no one wants.
translation_verse: Bumo be achoŋi nɛ alɔnɛ kikɛ so, b baa shu nli nna, ŋkpal manɛ so, ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na farnyaŋ Mowab be basa to nna fanɛ kapuya nɛ esa kikɛ maa sha nɛ b ta n lɛ nɛ k bure na nna.

english_verse: Moab lies broken! Listen to its people cry as they turn away in shame. Other nations are horrified at what happened, but still they mock her.
translation_verse: Mowab be efuli bure cheche a dese nɛ kumo be basa ji anishinyɔr nɛ efuliana nɛ a kulti kumo na be basa kikɛ wu kumo nɛ k chinchiŋ bumo nɛ b wora bumo eyurto. Ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e kaŋɛ na.”

english_verse: Moab, an enemy swoops down like an eagle spreading its wings over your land.
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na daŋ nase kɔnɔ nna fanɛ efuli ko beeŋ ba parga kumo be atɛ to m buu Mowab so n fuu kumo fanɛ kusore na.

english_verse: Your cities and fortresses will be captured, and your warriors as fearful as women giving birth.
translation_verse: Baaŋ kɔ n suge ndeana na nɛ mboŋ lempoana na kikɛ. Loŋ be kachɛ na kufu beeŋ pɛ Mowab be benapo fanɛ kananɛ kufu bee pɛ eche nɛ kakurge ta mo na.

english_verse: You are finished as a nation, because you dared oppose me, the Lord.
translation_verse: Mowab be efuli na beeŋ mur nsaa maaŋ naa wɔtɔ, ŋkpal manɛ so, kumo be basa pal kaman nna n sa ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.

english_verse: If you are terrified and run, you will fall into a pit; and if you crawl out of the pit, you'll get caught in a trap. The time has come for you to be punished. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Esa kama nɛ e beeŋ nya n shile kenishipere gboŋgboŋi na to na beeŋ tɔr amaŋgboŋ na to. Ekama nɛ e beeŋ nya n dii n lar amaŋgboŋ na to malɛ beeŋ tɔr ajigbelɛ na to nɛ a pɛ mo, ŋkpal manɛ so, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ teŋ n yili jemanɛ nɛ Mowab be efuli na beeŋ nya kumo be kasogberge nna.

english_verse: Near the city of Heshbon, where Sihon once ruled, tired refugees stand in shadows cast by the flames of their burning city. Soon, the towns on other hilltops, where those warlike people live, will also go up in smoke.
translation_verse: Basa nɛ b shile kena na daŋ shile n yɔ Hɛshbɔn nna, kadegboŋ nɛ ewura Sihɔn daŋ chena ndoŋ n ji kuwura dra dra na. B daa shile nna a mɔlga bumo be amu, ama b ka yɔ nɛ kadegboŋ na bee ji edɛ. Mowab be basa bee sha anasheŋ nna ga, ama edɛ na teŋ n ji bumo be ndekarso nɛ abee so kikɛ m mur.

english_verse: People of Moab, you worshiped Chemosh, your god, but now you are done for, and your children are prisoners in a foreign country.
translation_verse: Asheŋ maaŋ nyalɛ n sa menyi, Mowab be basa! Men shuŋ menyi be kegbir Chemɔsh na, ama naniere menyi e mur nɛ b pɛ menyi be mbia malɛ katinso n yɔ efuli pɔtɛ wɔfɔ so na.

english_verse: Yet someday, I will bring your people back home. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ama kachako, ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na beeŋ naŋ bɛta Mowab be basa m ba nɛ b naŋ dii kedama. Ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e kaŋɛ na.

english_verse: The Lord has this to say about the nation of Ammon: The people of Israel have plenty of children to inherit their lands. So why have you worshipers of the god Milcom taken over towns and land belonging to the tribe of Gad?
translation_verse: Kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ a laŋɛ Ammɔn be efuli so be kaplɛa so nde: “Israɛl be basa kɔ mbi damta nɛ baaŋ ji kasawule na be kapetɛ. Nɛ manɛ nna nɛ b shin nɛ basa nɛ baa shuŋ kegbir nɛ baa tre Mɔlɛk na sɔ Gad be yiri to ebi be kebonfu be nsawule so n chena so?

english_verse: Someday I will send an army to attack you in Rabbah, your capital city. It will be left in ruins, and the surrounding villages will lie in ashes. You took some of Israel's land, but on that day Israel will take yours!
translation_verse: Kachako bee ba nɛ n shin nɛ benapo ko e ba kɔ basa nɛ b wɔ efuli na be kadegboŋ nɛ baa tre Rabba to na kena m mur kumo cheche nseŋ chɔɔ ndekarso na n lɛ. Kumo be kaman nɛ Israɛl be basa e naŋ sɔ bumo be kasawule ashi basa nɛ b daŋ suge kumo na kutɔ.

english_verse: Cry, people of Heshbon; your town will become a pile of rubble. You will turn here and there, but your path will be blocked. Put on sackcloth and mourn, you citizens of Rabbah, because the idol you worship will be taken to a foreign country, along with its priests and temple officials.
translation_verse: Menyi basa nɛ men wɔ Hɛshbɔn be kade to na beeŋ shu awɔrso. Kade nɛ baa tre Ai na beeŋ mur! Rabba be beche, menyeeŋ ta nli be asɔbuuso m buu a shu keeli! Ekama beeŋ wulto a shile a kulti kaplɛkama. Baaŋ ta menyi be kegbir, Mɔlɛk nseŋ pɛ agbirwuraana nɛ kegbir ase be benimuana na tintiŋ so n yɔ efuli pɔtɛ wɔfɔ so.

english_verse: You rebellious Ammonites trust your wealth and ask, “Who could attack us?” But I warn you not to boast when your strength is fading.
translation_verse: Manɛ so nɛ menyi, Ammɔnebi, nɛ menyee maa ji kashenteŋ ere bee puchi? Menyi be eleŋ bee duga so nna na nɛ manɛ nna nɛ men kraŋ yirda menyi be yuku nsaa kaŋɛ fanɛ esa kikɛ maaŋ tiŋ ŋ kɔ menyi kena?

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, will send neighboring nations to strike you with terror. You will be scattered, with no one to care for your refugees.
translation_verse: Meeŋ shin nɛ kenishipere gboŋgboŋi nɛ k bee keta kufu a shi kaba kama so m ba menyi so nɛ men shile m mɔlga menyi be amu. Esa kikɛ maaŋ naa wɔtɔ nɛ e naŋ gama menyi be benapo abar so.

english_verse: Yet someday, I will bring your people back home. I, the Lord, have spoken. What the Lord Says about Edom
translation_verse: Ama kachako meeŋ naŋ bɛta Ammɔn be basa m ba epe n shin nɛ b naŋ nya asɔ nɛ b paŋ na. Ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e kaŋɛ na.” Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ka beeŋ ji Edɔm be basa demu be asheŋ

english_verse: I will send disaster to punish you descendants of Esau, so anyone from Dedan had better turn around and run back home.
translation_verse: Menyi basa nɛ men wɔ kadegboŋ nɛ baa tre Dedan na e shile n ya ŋana! Meeŋ shin nɛ Isɔɔ be kaman to ebi e ji jɛrbi, ŋkpal manɛ so, jemanɛ fo nɛ ŋ gberge bumo kusoe.

english_verse: People who harvest grapes leave some for the poor. Thieves who break in at night take only what they want.
translation_verse: Basa nɛ baa teŋi ayu ŋko a chuge asɔrso bee teŋi ŋko a chuge nna nsaa ka ako nɛ betirpo malɛ e baa shishi amo. Beyu malɛ baa yɔ kayu to kanyɛso, asɔ nɛ baa sha nawule nɛ baa ta.

english_verse: But I will take everything that belongs to you, people of Edom, and I will uncover every place where you try to hide. Then you will die, and so will your children, relatives, and neighbors.
translation_verse: Ama ma ere beeŋ ta kusɔ kama nɛ k la menyi Isɔɔ be kaman to ebi peya nseŋ bugi menyi so n lɛ ashi kakpa nɛ menyeeŋ ŋana, saŋɛ na so menyi maaŋ naŋ tiŋ n ta menyi be amu ŋ ŋana. Edɔm be efuli so be basa kikɛ beeŋ mur nɛ ekoŋwule gba maaŋ ka.

english_verse: But I can be trusted to care for your orphans and widows.
translation_verse: Ama menyeeŋ tiŋ n yirda ma nseŋ yige menyi be amunibi nɛ bekulpoche n sa ma nɛ m baa keni bumo so.

english_verse: Even those nations that don't deserve to be punished will have to drink from the cup of my anger. So how can you possibly hope to escape?
translation_verse: Efuliana nɛ bumo be basa maŋ daga kasogberge gba ka beeŋ nuu ma agbo be kawiebi to, manɛ nna nɛ menyi ere maaŋ nya kasogberge? Menyi alɛ gba beeŋ nuu kawiebi na to.

english_verse: I, the Lord, swear in my own name that your city of Bozrah and all your towns will suffer a horrible fate. They will lie in ruins forever, and people will use the name “Bozrah” as a curse word.
translation_verse: Ŋ gbagba e bɔ ntaŋ fanɛ Bozra nɛ k la Edɔm be efuli so be kadegboŋ na beeŋ ki keshishɛrsawule nɛ basa e wu kumo nɛ k chinchiŋ bumo nseŋ keta bumo kufu. Basa beeŋ baa wora kumo eyurto nsaa ta kumo be ketre a shoduu basa. Ndekarso nɛ a kulti kumo na kikɛ beeŋ ki alambure a dese mbaanaayɔ. Ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e kaŋɛ na.”

english_verse: Your nation will be small, yet hated by other nations.
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na malɛ beeŋ shin nɛ men ki basa pɔso nɛ esa kama maaŋ naa sa menyi bunyaŋ.

english_verse: Pride tricks you into thinking that other nations look at you with fear. You live along the cliffs and high in the mountains like the eagles, but I am the Lord, and I will bring you down.
translation_verse: Menyi be kamoowuso nɛ menyee fɛ fanɛ efuliana na be basa bee ŋana menyi na. Menyi ka chena abee to nɛ abee be awɔlto so nɛ menyee fɛ loŋ, ama nɛ men wɔ awɔlto chilili fanɛ kusore gba, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na beeŋ tiŋ m bar menyi kaseto. Ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e kaŋɛ na.”

english_verse: I, the Lord, will attack you like a lion from the forest, attacking sheep in a meadow along the Jordan. In a moment the flock runs, and the land is empty. Who will I choose to attack you? I will do it myself! No one can force me to fight or chase me away.
translation_verse: Kananɛ buluŋ bee lar kupo nɛ k dese Jɔɔdan be Lɔrgboŋ na ase a ba asɔbɔya be ejikpa nɛ asɔbɔya na e baa shile na, nɛ ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na beeŋ ba nɛ Edɔmebi e shile epul to n lar bumo be kadegboŋ na to. Kumo be kaman nɛ ejuŋkparpo nɛ meeŋ lara na e ba chena n ji kuwura efuli na so. Wanɛ e naŋ tiŋ n ta mbe kumu m ber ma ŋko n to ma emaŋ? Ewurjipo kikɛ maŋ wɔtɔ nɛ e beeŋ tiŋ n tu ma ŋ kɔ.

english_verse: An enemy will swoop down to attack you, like an eagle spreading its wings and circling over Bozrah. Your warriors will be as fearful as women giving birth. What the Lord Says about Damascus
translation_verse: Bedoŋ na beeŋ ba kɔ Bozra be basa eleŋso fanɛ kusore ka ber atɛ to ŋ gbelge m ba kasawule so eleŋso na. Kachɛ na kaŋ fo, Edɔm be benapo be ŋgbene beeŋ jija bumo ga fanɛ eche nɛ kakurge ta mo na.” Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ka beeŋ ji Damaskɔs demu be asheŋ

english_verse: You people of Damascus have lost your courage, and in panic you turn to run, gripped by fear and pain.
translation_verse: Damaskɔs be basa na daŋ pɔ aba nna ga nseŋ daŋ ta kufu nɛ keyeŋi yeŋi n shile. Ebesa nɛ kagbenejija damta e daa wɔ bumo to fanɛ eche nɛ e bee kurge na.

english_verse: Once I was pleased with your famous city. But now I warn you, “Escape while you still can!”
translation_verse: Jemanɛ ko ma kagbene daŋ fuli menyi be kadegboŋ nɛ k kɔ ketre na so nna. Ama naniere mee kpele menyi kusoe nna fanɛ men lar kumo to n shile m mɔlga menyi be amu.

english_verse: Soon, even your best soldiers will lie dead in your streets. I, the Lord All-Powerful, have spoken.
translation_verse: Loŋ be kachɛ na kaŋ fo bedoŋ beeŋ mɔ mbrantiɛfɔlbi na agbembi so nseŋ mur bumo be benapo kikɛ.

english_verse: I will set fire to your city walls and burn down the fortresses King Benhadad built. Nebuchadnezzar and the People of the Desert
translation_verse: Meeŋ nya edɛ n wɔtɔ Damaskɔs be nwu to nseŋ chɔɔ ewura Bɛnhadad be ewurkpa lempoana n lɛ. Ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e kaŋɛ na.” Demuji nɛ k bee ba Kɛda be yiri nɛ Hazɔɔ be kadegboŋ so be asheŋ

english_verse: Here is what the Lord says about the Kedar tribe and the desert villages that were conquered by King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia: Listen, you people of Kedar and the other tribes of the eastern desert. I have told Nebuchadnezzar to attack and destroy you.
translation_verse: Kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ a laŋɛ Kɛda be yiri nɛ keshishɛrsawule so be ndekarso na be kaplɛa so nde: “Men nu nfe, Kɛda be basa nɛ eyiriana nɛ a wɔ keshishɛrsawule nɛ k wɔ a laŋɛ epeŋilarkpa be kaba so na. Ŋ kaŋɛ Babilɔn be Ewura Nebukadneeza fanɛ e ba kɔ menyi kena m mur menyi.

english_verse: You have no city walls and no neighbors to help, yet you think you're safe— so I told him to attack.
translation_verse: ‘Men shin nɛ an ya kɔ basa nɛ baa fɛ fanɛ shɛŋ maaŋ tiŋ n wora bumo na! Bumo be kadegboŋ na maŋ kɔ egbalana nɛ mbunagboŋana a kuŋ kumo.’

english_verse: Then your camels and large herds will be yours no longer. People of the Arabian Desert, disaster will strike you from every side, and you will be scattered everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Meeŋ suge bumo be enyɔma nɛ asɔbɔya kikɛ! Meeŋ pesaŋ basa nɛ baa kuya bumo be emin so na n sɔ kaplɛkama, nseŋ naŋ shin nɛ jɛrbi e shi kaba kama so m ba bumo so.

english_verse: Only jackals will live where your villages once stood. I, the Lord, have spoken. What the Lord Says about Elam
translation_verse: Hazɔɔ beeŋ ki keshishɛrsawule mbaanaayɔ nɛ ejiŋkaamu e baa wɔ kumo so. Esa kikɛ maaŋ naŋ chena kumo so kikɛ. Ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e kaŋɛ na.” Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ ka ji Elam demu be asheŋ

english_verse: Not long after Zedekiah became king of Judah, the Lord told me to say: People of Elam, I, the Lord All-Powerful, will kill the archers who make your army strong.
translation_verse: E yɛ: “Meeŋ shin nɛ b mɔ basa nɛ b ta ata ŋ kɔ n shin nɛ Elam be efuli na nya eleŋ ga na.

english_verse: Enemies will attack from all directions, and you will be led captive to every nation on earth.
translation_verse: Bedoŋ beeŋ shi kaba kama so m ba kɔ Elam be basa nseŋ pɛ bumo tintiŋso n yɔ durnya to be efuli kama so.

english_verse: Their armies will crush and kill you, and you will face the disaster that my anger brings.
translation_verse: Meeŋ shin nɛ Elam be basa bumo bedoŋana e mɔ bumo n jija bumo kuraa nseŋ naŋ shin nɛ b ji jɛrbi nɛ ma agbogboŋ beeŋ shin nɛ k ba bumo so na.

english_verse: Your king and his officials will die, and I will rule in their place. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Meeŋ mur bumo be bewura nɛ bejuŋkparpoana nseŋ nase ma kuwurputi ndoŋ n ji kuwura efuli na so.

english_verse: But I promise that someday I will bring your people back to their land.
translation_verse: Ama kachako meeŋ naŋ bɛta Elam be basa m ba bumo be kasawule so nɛ b naŋ dii kedama. Ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e kaŋɛ na.”

english_verse: The Lord told me to say: Announce what will happen and don't leave anything out.
translation_verse: Kubɔya nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na sa ma a laŋɛ Babilɔn be kadegboŋ nɛ kumo be basa be kaplɛa so nde:

english_verse: The attack on the Babylonians will come from the north; they and their animals will run, leaving the land empty. Israel and Judah Will Return to Their Land
translation_verse: Efuli ko beeŋ shi kelargato be esoso m ba kɔ Babilɔn be efuli na kena n shin nɛ k ki keshishɛrsawule a dese. Edimɛdi nɛ asɔbɔya kikɛ beeŋ shile nɛ esa kama maaŋ naa wɔ ndoŋ.” Israɛl be basa ka beeŋ naŋ bɛta n yɔ bumo be kasawule so be asheŋ

english_verse: The Lord said: People of Israel and Judah, when these things happen you will weep, and together you will return to your land and worship me, the Lord your God.
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ: “Jemanɛ na kaŋ fo, Israɛl nɛ Juda be basa kikɛ beeŋ cha abar n shu anishichubi. Kumo be kaman nɛ b bɛta m ba bumo be kasawule so m ba bunyaŋ ma.

english_verse: You will ask the way to Zion and then come and join with me in making an agreement you won't break or forget.
translation_verse: Baaŋ bishi n fin Jerusalɛm be ekpa nseŋ bɔla kumo so m bɛta m ba nɛ ma nɛ bumo e wora kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre nɛ k beeŋ baa wɔtɔ mbaanaayɔ. Bumo alɛ maaŋ naŋ wora n da kumo so ŋko n teŋ kumo so kikɛ.

english_verse: My people, you are lost sheep abandoned in the mountains by their shepherds. You don't even remember your resting place.
translation_verse: Ma basa du fanɛ mbolpɔ nɛ bumo be bekpapoana shin nɛ b foe abee so nna. B daa nite cham cham kebee ko so nna n ya kaa lar kuko so nseŋ daŋ teŋ kakpa nɛ bumo pe wɔ so.

english_verse: I am your true pastureland, the one who gave hope to your ancestors. But you abandoned me, so when your enemies found you, they felt no guilt as they gobbled you up.
translation_verse: Bekama nɛ b daŋ wu bumo daa kɔ bumo kena nna. Le nɛ bumo doŋana bee kaŋɛ: ‘B wora alubi nna n da Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ e sa bumo nananyɛnana tama na so. Amoso kusɔ nɛ an wora na maŋ lubi. Bumo nananyɛnana daŋ yirda Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nna, nɛ a daŋ daga fanɛ bumo alɛ gba ka ji kashenteŋ n sa mo.’

english_verse: Escape from Babylonia, my people. Get out of that country! Don't wait for anyone else.
translation_verse: Israɛl be basa, men shile n lar Babilɔn be efuli so. Men sa maŋ naŋ jo esa kama!

english_verse: In the north I am bringing great nations together. They will attack Babylon and capture it. The arrows they shoot are like the best soldiers, always finding their target.
translation_verse: N ya we n wɔtɔ efuli lempoana ko ashi kelargato be esoso be kaba so nna fanɛ b ba kɔ Babilɔn be efuli na kena. Baaŋ ber abar so nna m ba kɔ m pɔɔ kumo so. B la basa nɛ b nyi kekpaŋ to nɛnɛ nna nsaa to ata ga. B maa to a paŋ kikɛ.

english_verse: Babylonia will be conquered, and its enemies will carry off everything they want. Babylon Will Be Disgraced The Lord said:
translation_verse: Baaŋ ba fuu Babilɔn be asɔ kama nɛ baa sha na n yɔ. Ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e kaŋɛ na.” Babilɔn ka tɔr be asheŋ

english_verse: People of Babylonia, you were glad to rob my people. You had a good time, making more noise than horses and jumping around like calves threshing grain.
translation_verse: Ade be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na naŋ kaŋɛ le: “Babilɔn be basa, men daŋ suge ma basa be asɔ nna nɛ k par menyi ga nɛ menyee wora awɔr fanɛ mbrantiɛfɔlbi nɛ baa beri ayu ŋko gbaŋɛ ka bee shu na.

english_verse: My anger will destroy Babylon, and no one will live there. Everyone who passes by will be shocked to see what has happened.
translation_verse: Ma agbo beeŋ mur Babilɔn nɛ esa kama maaŋ naa wɔ kumo so. Kufu beeŋ pɛ esa kama nɛ e beeŋ bɔla ndoŋ a choŋ n wu kusɔ nɛ k wora na, nɛ e baa chicha.

english_verse: Attack from every side! Babylon surrenders! The enemy tears down its walls and towers. I am taking my revenge by doing to Babylon what it did to other cities.
translation_verse: Men kɔ bumo kaba kama so. Naniere Babilɔn shuli kapɔshi. Edoŋ na bure kumo be egbalana nɛ ebu jeŋgreŋana na n lɛ nɛ mee wora bumo kusɔ nɛ b ta n wora ndegboŋana ko na a bishi bumo kɔnɔ.

english_verse: There is no one in Babylonia to plant or harvest crops. Even foreigners who lived there have left for their homelands, afraid of the enemy armies.
translation_verse: Men sa maŋ naŋ shin nɛ b naŋ duu keduuso kikɛ n teŋi efuli na so. Befɔ kama nɛ b chena ndoŋ na beeŋ baa ŋana benapo nɛ baa kɔ na nseŋ kpal loŋ so m bɛta n yɔ epe.”

english_verse: Israel is a flock of sheep scattered by hungry lions. The king of Assyria first gobbled Israel up. Then Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylonia, crunched on Israel's bones.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ le: “Israɛl be basa na du fanɛ mbolpɔ nɛ ebuluŋ ju bumo nɛ b pesaŋ bumo to nna. Asiriya be Ewurgboŋ e juŋkpar m ba kɔ bumo kena, kumo be kaman nɛ Babilɔn be ewura Nebukadneeza malɛ ba we bumo be awibi m bure to.

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, punished the king of Assyria, and I will also punish the king of Babylonia.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal le so, ma, Enyɛnpetale, Israɛl be Ebɔrɛ na beeŋ gberge ewura Nebukadneeza nɛ mbe efuli so ebi kusoe fanɛ kananɛ ŋ gberge Asiriya be ewurgboŋ kusoe na.

english_verse: But I will bring Israel back to its own land. The people will be like sheep eating their fill on Mount Carmel and in Bashan, in the hill country of Ephraim and in Gilead.
translation_verse: Ama meeŋ naŋ bɛta Israɛl be basa na m ba bumo be kasawule so. Baaŋ dɔ adɔjibi kama nɛ baa sha ashi Kaamɛl be kebee nɛ k mata Mɛditerenia be Teku na nɛ Bashan be kebonfu nɛ k wɔ Jɔɔdan be lɔr na be epeŋilarkpa be kaba so na nɛ Efrayim nɛ Giliad be apreŋsawule so n ji kanaŋkama nɛ baa sha.

english_verse: I will rescue a few people from Israel and Judah. I will forgive them so completely that their sin and guilt will disappear, never to be found. The Lord's Commands to the Enemies of Babylonia
translation_verse: Loŋ be jemanɛ na kaŋ fo, kulubi kikɛ maaŋ naa wɔ Israɛl be efuli so, nɛ kumu kpakpaso kikɛ malɛ maaŋ naa wɔ Juda be efuli so. Ŋkpal manɛ so, meeŋ ta basa nɛ n yige bumo nɛ b ji efute na be alubi m paŋ bumo. Ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e kaŋɛ na.” Ebɔrɛ ka ji Babilɔn demu be asheŋ

english_verse: The Lord said: I have told the enemies of Babylonia, “Attack the people of Merathaim and Pekod. Kill them all! Destroy their possessions!”
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ Babilɔn mo doŋana le: “Men ya kɔ nde nɛ baa tre Merateem nɛ Pɛkɔd na be basa kena nseŋ mɔ bumo m mur. Men wora kusɔ kama nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ menyi kenishipereso na. Ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e kaŋɛ na.

english_verse: Sounds of war and the noise of destruction can be heard.
translation_verse: Kena nɛ kemur gboŋgboŋi be awɔr bee cha kasawule na so nna.

english_verse: Babylonia was a hammer pounding every country, but now it lies broken. What a shock to the nations of the world!
translation_verse: Babilɔn daa du fanɛ hama nna nseŋ daŋ bɛa durnya kikɛ to kpachɛrkpachɛrbi, ama loŋ be hama na gba e bɛa to kpachɛrkpachɛrbi na! Kusɔ nɛ k wora na daŋ chinchiŋ efuliana na be basa n shin nɛ bumo be nnɔ bumo.

english_verse: Babylonia challenged me, the Lord God All-Powerful, but that nation doesn't know it is caught in a trap that I set.
translation_verse: Babilɔn be efuli so be basa na daŋ to ma emaŋ nna a kɔ ma. Naniere kejigbelɛ nɛ n fe menyi na pɛ menyi nɛ menyi maŋ nyi gba.

english_verse: Kill the soldiers of Babylonia, because the time has come for them to be punished.
translation_verse: Men mɔ bumo be benapo kikɛ. Babilɔn be basa wu asheŋ pasaa! Ŋkpal manɛ so, bumo be kasogberge be jemanɛ fo!”

english_verse: The Babylonian army destroyed my temple, but soon I will take revenge. Then refugees from Babylon will tell about it in Zion.
translation_verse: Basa nɛ b nya n shile Babilɔn be kena na to na ba Jerusalɛm to m baa kaa kaŋɛ kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na wora ŋ ka Babilɔnebi kukɔ ŋkpal kusɔ nɛ b daŋ wora mbe bɔrɛlambu ashi Jerusalɛm so.

english_verse: People of Babylon, I, the Lord, promise that even your best soldiers will lie dead in the streets.
translation_verse: Amoso bumo be mbrantiɛfɔlbi beeŋ wu n dese kadegboŋ na be agbembi so nɛ bumo be benapo kikɛ e mur loŋ be kachɛ na. Ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e kaŋɛ na.”

english_verse: Babylon, you should be named, “The Proud One.” But the time has come when I, the Lord All-Powerful, will punish you.
translation_verse: “Kamoowu e baŋ bɔlɔ Babilɔn be efuli so be basa to, amoso, ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na maaŋ yige bumo kikɛ. Jemanɛ fo nɛ b nya bumo be kasogberge.

english_verse: You are proud, but you will stumble and fall, and no one will help you up. I will set your villages on fire, and everything around you will go up in flames.
translation_verse: Menyi be efuli nɛ kamoowu bɔlɔ kumo to na beeŋ fiti n tɔr nɛ esa kikɛ maaŋ chɛ to n niŋi kumo to n yili. Meeŋ shin nɛ menyi be ndegboŋana e ji edɛ nɛ asɔ kama nɛ a kulti menyi na kikɛ e mur.”

english_verse: This war will prove that your prophets are liars and fools. And it will frighten your warriors.
translation_verse: Luwu beeŋ ba bumo be anebiana nɛ b la bewulpo nsaa ku efɛ na so! Luwu beeŋ ba bumo be benapo so, nɛ kufugboŋ e tɔr bumo so!

english_verse: Then your chariot horses and the foreigners in your army will refuse to go into battle, and the enemy will carry away everything you treasure.
translation_verse: Bedoŋ beeŋ mur menyi be egbaŋɛ nɛ amo be eturko, nɛ benapo nɛ men ya haya m ba na kikɛ! Menyi be benapo na beeŋ pɔ fanɛ beche, nɛ bedoŋ e mur menyi be asɔ lela kikɛ, nseŋ muu amo nɛ baa sha n yɔ.

english_verse: Your rivers and canals will dry up. All of this will happen, because your land is full of idols, and they have made fools of you.
translation_verse: Ewule beeŋ tɔr menyi be kasawule so, nɛ elɔr nɛ mbombiana kikɛ e wɔl to. Ade kikɛ beeŋ wora, ŋkpal manɛ so, agbirana e bɔlɔ menyi be kasawule so n shin nɛ men ki bewulpo.

english_verse: I destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah and the nearby towns, and I will destroy Babylon just as completely. No one will live there again. Babylonia Is Invaded The Lord said:
translation_verse: Kusɔ nɛ k wora ndegboŋ nɛ b daa tre Sodɔm nɛ Gomɔra nɛ ndewurbi nɛ a kulti amo jemanɛ nɛ n daŋ mur amo na, koŋwule e naaŋ wora Babilɔn be efuli so gba. Esa kama maaŋ naŋ chena kumo so kikɛ. Ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e kaŋɛ na.

english_verse: Far to the north, a nation and its allies have been awakened. They are powerful and ready for war.
translation_verse: Basa ko bee shi efuli ko nɛ k wɔ kelargato be esoso a ba, k la efuligboŋ nɛ k kɔ bewura damta nna. B shi kufɔ n wora kena be shiriya nna a ba.

english_verse: Bows and arrows and swords are in their hands. The soldiers are cruel and show no pity. The hoofbeats of their horses echo like ocean waves crashing against the shore. The army has lined up for battle and is coming to attack you, people of Babylonia!
translation_verse: B teŋ ta bumo be ata nɛ etokobi ŋ keta; bumo be benapo maŋ kɔ kushuso, bumo alɛ maa wu kuwɔr. B baa dii egbaŋɛ a ba k bee gbri nna fanɛ teku be nchu ka bee wɔr na. B bela ase nna a ba nɛ b ba kɔ Babilɔn be efuli so be basa kena.

english_verse: Ever since your king heard about this army, he has been weak with fear; he twists and turns in pain like a woman giving birth.
translation_verse: Babilɔn be ewura ka nu baru na, nɛ kufu pɛ mo nɛ mbe eyur wu mo. Ndoŋ nna nɛ kagbenejija damta tɔr mo so nɛ e bee kii kɔnɔ to fanɛ kakurge ka ta eche na.

english_verse: Babylonia, I will attack you like a lion from the forest, attacking sheep in a meadow along the Jordan. In a moment the flock runs, and the land is empty. Who will I choose to attack you? I will do it myself! No one can force me to fight or chase me away.
translation_verse: Kananɛ buluŋ bee lar kupo nɛ k dese Jɔɔdan be Lɔrgboŋ na ase a ba asɔbɔya be ejikpa nɛ asɔbɔya na e baa shile na, nɛ ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na beeŋ ba nɛ Babilɔnebi e shile epul to n lar bumo be kadegboŋ na to. Kumo be kaman nɛ ejuŋkparpo nɛ meeŋ lara na e ba chena n ji kuwura efuli na so. Wanɛ e naŋ tiŋ n ta mbe kumu m ber ma ŋko n to ma emaŋ? Ewurjipo kikɛ maŋ wɔtɔ nɛ e beeŋ tiŋ n tu ma ŋ kɔ.

english_verse: The sounds of your destruction will be heard among the nations, and the earth will shake.
translation_verse: Jemanɛ nɛ Babilɔn beeŋ tɔr na, egbri nɛ k beeŋ gbri na beeŋ shin nɛ durnya kikɛ e gbuŋgbuŋ, nɛ efuli pɔtɛana so be basa e nu egbri na.”

english_verse: I, the Lord, am sending a wind to destroy the people of Babylonia and Babylon, its capital.
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na yɛ: “Meeŋ shin nɛ afu nɛ k bee jija asɔ e ba Babilɔn be efuli nɛ kumo be basa so.

english_verse: I will tell these soldiers, “Attack quickly, before the Babylonians can string their bows or put on their armor. Kill their best soldiers and destroy their army!”
translation_verse: Ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ beeŋ kaŋɛ befɔ na be benapo fanɛ b sa maŋ sa Babilɔn be benapo na ekpa nɛ b gberge bumo be ata to ŋko n ta bumo be abɛlso be asɔ kuŋamuso. Bumo alɛ e sa maŋ yige Babilɔn be mbrantiɛfɔlbi na, b mur benapo na kikɛ!

english_verse: Their troops will fall wounded in the streets of Babylon.
translation_verse: Babilɔn be benapo na beeŋ nya edoro n wu n tɔr bumo be ndegboŋana be agbembi so.

english_verse: Everyone in Israel and Judah is guilty. But I, the Lord All-Powerful, their holy God, have not abandoned them.
translation_verse: Israɛl nɛ Juda be basa kikɛ wora alubi n da ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na so, ama ma, Israɛl be Ebɔrɛ cheembi na, maŋ kini bumo n lɛ.

english_verse: Get out of Babylon! Run for your lives! If you stay, you will be killed when I take revenge on the city and punish it for its sins.
translation_verse: Men shile n lar Babilɔn be efuli so m mɔlga menyi be efute! Men sa maŋ shin nɛ b mɔ menyi ŋkpal Babilɔn be basa be alubi so. Bumo be kusɔ nɛ b wora na be kasogberge nɛ k daga bumo nɛ mee sa bumo a tal to na.

english_verse: Babylon was my golden cup, filled with the wine of my anger. The nations of the world got drunk on this wine and went insane.
translation_verse: Babilɔn daa du fanɛ shuwa be kawiebi nɛ ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be agbo daŋ bɔlɔ kumo nna, nɛ k shin nɛ durnya be efuli kikɛ so be basa nuu kawiebi na to m boo nseŋ daa wora asheŋ fanɛ b ka bee lɔ eboŋ na.

english_verse: But suddenly, Babylon will fall and be destroyed. I, the Lord, told the foreigners who lived there, “Weep for the city! Get medicine for its wounds; maybe they will heal.”
translation_verse: Ama Babilɔn gba beeŋ tɔr epul to m mur. Men shu n sa kumo be basa, nseŋ fin kudur n wɔtɔ bumo be achuu to, ashere baaŋ nya kechɛ.

english_verse: The foreigners answered, “We have already tried to treat Babylon's wounds, but they would not heal. Come on, let's all go home to our own countries. Nothing is left in Babylonia; everything is destroyed.”
translation_verse: Nɛ befɔ nɛ b wɔ ndoŋ na kaŋɛ abar le: ‘An wora ania fanɛ anyeeŋ chɛ Babilɔn be efuli na to, ama asheŋ teŋ n jija. Amoso men shin nɛ an bɛta epe. Ebɔrɛ be eleŋgboŋ na so nɛ e bɔla ŋ gberge Babilɔn kusoe nseŋ mur kumo cheche na.’ ”

english_verse: I, the Lord, want Babylon destroyed, because its army destroyed my temple. So, you kings of Media, sharpen your arrows and pick up your shields.
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na yɛ: “Ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na bee sha kemur Babilɔn be efuli nna, ŋkpal bumo be benapo ka mur ma bɔrɛlambu so. Amoso menyi Midia be efuli so be bewuraana e bɛl menyi be atanyembi nseŋ ta menyi be abɛlso be asɔ kuŋamuso ŋ keta.

english_verse: People of Babylon, you live along the Euphrates River and are surrounded by canals. You are rich, but now the time has come for you to die.
translation_verse: Efuli na so kɔ elɔr nɛ asɔ lela damta, ama kumo be saŋɛ fo nɛ kumo be kebaawɔtɔ a ku so.

english_verse: I, the Lord All-Powerful, swear by my own life that enemy soldiers will fill your streets like a swarm of locusts. They will shout and celebrate their victory. A Hymn of Praise (Jeremiah
translation_verse: Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na daŋ ta mbe ŋkpa nna m bɔ ntaŋ fanɛ e beeŋ bar bedoŋ be benapo damta fanɛ elotɔr nɛ b ba kɔ Babilɔn be efuli so be basa kena m pɔɔ bumo so. Kumo be kaman nɛ b boŋ kekɔmpɔɔso be nshɛ. Keboŋ kashɛ ŋ kpaŋ Ebɔrɛ be asheŋ

english_verse: The waters in the heavens roar at his command. He makes clouds appear; he sends the wind from his storehouse and makes lightning flash in the rain.
translation_verse: Mo e naa malga nɛ awɔlto be nchuana bee baga to a gbri, mo alɛ e naa shin nɛ awɔlpa bee deŋi durnya be kaplɛkama. Mo e naa shin nɛ bɔrɛ bee ba nsaa nyɛkpɛ nɛ afu bee shi kakpa nɛ e yili kumo na a ba.

english_verse: God used his wisdom and power to create the earth and spread out the heavens.
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e bɔla mbe eleŋgboŋ so n to durnya; mbe kanyiasheŋ so nɛ e bɔla n to esoso nɛ kasawule.

english_verse: But the Lord, Israel's God, is all-powerful. He created everything, and he chose Israel to be his very own. God's Hammer The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ama Ebɔrɛ nɛ an nananyɛn Jeekɔb daŋ shuŋ na bre maŋ du fanɛ agbirana na. Mo e to kusɔ kama nseŋ lara Israɛl be basa fanɛ b baa la mo gbagba be basa. Mbe ketre e la Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na. Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be guluŋgu be asheŋ

english_verse: Babylonia, you were my hammer; I used you to pound nations and break kingdoms,
translation_verse: Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na yɛ: “Babilɔn, fo e la ma kena to be guluŋgu. Fo nɛ mee ta a biri efuliana a pechɛto, nsaa ta fo a mur kuwurgboŋana.

english_verse: as well as men and women, young and old,
translation_verse: Fo nɛ mee ta a mɔ benyɛn nɛ beche, nɛ basakpar nɛ mbifɔlbi nɛ mbinyɛnsobi nɛ mbichesobi kikɛ.

english_verse: You destroyed the nations and seem strong as a mountain, but I am your enemy. I might even grab you and roll you off a cliff. When I am finished, you'll only be a pile of scorched bricks.
translation_verse: Babilɔn, fo du fanɛ kebee nna a kɔ eleŋ ga a mur durnya kikɛ, ama ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ki fo doŋ nna na. Meeŋ to m pɛ fo to ŋ gberge fo n lɛ kasawule nɛ fo bure to ŋ ki fanɛ ebirkesi ka bure to n deŋi abar so na.

english_verse: Your stone blocks won't be reused for cornerstones or foundations, and I promise that forever you will be a desert. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Nations Will Attack Babylon The Lord said:
translation_verse: Esa maaŋ naaŋ tiŋ n ta fo ajembu nɛ a bure to a dese na be kekama m pɔr kikɛ. Feeŋ ki keshishɛrsawule a dese fuloŋ mbaanaayɔ. Ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e kaŋɛ na.

english_verse: Tell the kings and governors, the leaders and the people of the kingdoms of the Medes to prepare for war!
translation_verse: Men kaŋɛ Midia be efuli so be bewura nɛ bumo be benimuana nɛ efuliana nɛ baa keniso na kikɛ be benapo nɛ b wora shiriya m ba kɔ Babilɔn kena.

english_verse: The earth twists and turns in torment, because I have decided to make Babylonia a desert where no one can live, and I won't change my mind.
translation_verse: Durnya bee kii to nsaa gbuŋgbuŋ to nna ŋkpal Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ka kre keshin nɛ Babilɔn be efuli na e ki keshishɛrsawule a dese fuloŋ nɛ esa maaŋ naa wɔ kumo so so.

english_verse: The Babylonian soldiers have lost their strength and courage. They stay in their fortresses, unable to fight, while the enemy breaks through the city gates, then sets their homes on fire.
translation_verse: Babilɔn be benapo na be eleŋ nɛ kenyɛn lar bumo to nɛ b ki fanɛ beche. Bumo kikɛ yige kena be kekɔ nna nseŋ shir a wɔ bumo be mboŋ lempoana. Bedoŋ bure kadegboŋ na be mbunagboŋ na n luri to a chɔɔ Babilɔnebi na be nwu.

english_verse: I am the Lord All-Powerful, the God of Israel, and I make this promise— “Soon Babylon will be leveled and packed down like a threshing place at harvest time.” Babylonia Will Pay!
translation_verse: K maaŋ chɛr nɛ bedoŋ na e pɔɔ bumo so nseŋ chichi bumo so m mata kasawule fanɛ kananɛ baa beri ayu kugooro so na. Ma, Enyɛnpetale, Israɛl be Ebɔrɛ na e kaŋɛ na.”

english_verse: The people of Jerusalem say, “King Nebuchadnezzar made us panic. That monster stuffed himself with us and our treasures, leaving us empty— he gobbled up what he wanted and spit out the rest.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Jerusalɛm be basa kaŋɛ le: “Babilɔn be ewura Nebukadneeza shin nɛ kufugboŋ tɔr anyi so. E suge anyi be kadegboŋ na to be asɔ lela kikɛ ŋ ki mo peya fanɛ kuwɔ ka min kusɔ na. Asɔ nɛ e bee sha nɛ e suge n ta, nseŋ ta amo nɛ a ka na n lɛ.

english_verse: The people of Babylonia harmed some of us and killed others. Now, Lord, make them pay!” The Lord Will Take Revenge on Babylon
translation_verse: Babilɔn be efuli so be basa piira anyi be beko nseŋ mɔ beko malɛ. Naniere, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ, shin nɛ b ka kumo be kukɔ!” Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ka beeŋ chɛ Israɛl to be asheŋ

english_verse: My people, I am on your side, and I will take revenge on Babylon. I will cut off its water supply, and its stream will dry up.
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ le: “N yil menyi be kaman nna, nɛ n sɔ menyi be kɔnɔ so ŋ ka Babilɔn be basa kukɔ. Meeŋ shin nɛ bumo be elɔr nɛ mbombi kikɛ e wɔl to nɛ b sa maŋ naa nya nchu.

english_verse: Babylon will be a pile of rubble where only jackals live, and everyone will be afraid to walk among the ruins.
translation_verse: Babilɔn be efuli na beeŋ bure a dese, nseŋ ki kupuŋ to be asɔbɔya fanɛ ejiŋkaamu be kakpa. Basa beeŋ baa mushe kumo. Ama bumo alɛ beeŋ baa ŋana kebɔla alambure na to n choŋ.

english_verse: The Babylonians roar and growl like young lions.
translation_verse: Babilɔnebi na kikɛ bee munto nna fanɛ ebuluŋ fɔlbi.

english_verse: And since they are hungry, I will give them a banquet. They will celebrate, get drunk, then fall asleep, never to wake up!
translation_verse: Akoŋ ka kɔ bumo ere bre, meeŋ wora kejigboŋ n sa bumo. Baaŋ ji bumo be amu nseŋ boo; kumo be kaman nɛ b dese n di, nsaa maaŋ naŋ koso kikɛ!

english_verse: I will lead them away to die, like sheep, lambs, and goats being led to the butcher.
translation_verse: Meeŋ gberge bumo n yɔ luwu to, fanɛ kananɛ baa gberge mbolpɔ ŋko mbolpɔfɔlbi nɛ mboe n ya kaa mɔ na.

english_verse: All nations now praise Babylon, but when it is captured, those same nations will be horrified.
translation_verse: Efuli pɔtɛana be basa bee kpaŋ Babilɔn naniere nna, ama bedoŋ kaŋ pɛ kumo be basa anya, kufu gboŋgboŋi beeŋ naŋ tɔr efuli pɔtɛana ere be basa so nɛ b baa chicha.

english_verse: Babylon's enemies will rise like ocean waves and flood the city.
translation_verse: Babilɔn mo doŋana beeŋ koso fanɛ ketili ka koso teku so na, m ba buu kadegboŋ na so.

english_verse: Horrible destruction will strike the nearby towns. The land will become a barren desert, where no one can live or even travel.
translation_verse: Kemur nɛ k bee keta kufu beeŋ ba ndeana nɛ e taga to kadegboŋ na so. Kasawule na beeŋ ki keshishɛrsawule fuloŋ, kakpa nɛ esa kama maaŋ tiŋ n chena ŋko m bɔla kumo so n choŋ gba.
