english_verse: The seed sprouted and grew into a grapevine that spread over the ground. It had lots of leaves and strong, deep roots, and its branches grew upward toward the eagle.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ keduuso na kɔr n daŋ ŋ ki kefeelebi a sɔr asɔrso nɛ baa tre greep na. Nɛ kumo be ayabi daŋ esoso a shoŋi kajɔnɔkoso na, nɛ kumo be nliŋi yɔ nchiŋ kasawule to. Nɛ kefeelebi na wora ayabi damta nseŋ purge afantaŋ.

english_verse: There was another eagle with strong wings and thick feathers. The roots and branches of the grapevine soon turned toward this eagle, hoping it would bring water for the soil.
translation_verse: Kajɔnɔkoso nyɔsopo ko malɛ gba daa wɔtɔ a kɔ aba lempo nɛ atɛ damta. Nɛ kefeelebi na be ayabi nɛ nliŋi salga to a yɔ kajɔnɔkoso nyɔsopo na kutɔ, a tama fanɛ k beeŋ nya nchu kumo kutɔ a chɔ kudɔbi nɛ k daa wɔ kumo to na.

english_verse: But the vine was already growing in fertile soil, where there was plenty of water to produce healthy leaves and large grapes.
translation_verse: Ama kasawule lela nɛ k kɔ nchu nɛnɛ so nɛ b daŋ duu kumo nɛ k tiŋ n daŋ nɛnɛ ŋ ki kefeelebi lela nseŋ tiŋ n sɔr nɛnɛ.

english_verse: Now tell me, Ezekiel, do you think this grapevine will live? Or will the first eagle pull it up by its roots and pluck off the grapes and let its new leaves die? The eagle could easily kill it without the help of a large and powerful army.
translation_verse: Naniere, Ezikɛl, kaŋɛ ma, fo tama fanɛ kefeelebi ere beeŋ pete a? Kajɔnɔkoso juŋkparso na maaŋ nya agbo n tia kumo nseŋ kuya kumo be ayabi to n lɛ nɛ a wɔl a? Kajɔnɔkoso na beeŋ tiŋ n tia kefeelebi na nɛ k maŋ fin benapo lempo damta be kechɛto gba.

english_verse: The grapevine is strong and healthy, but as soon as the scorching desert wind blows, it will quickly wither. The Lord Explains the Story
translation_verse: Kefeelebi na kɔ eleŋ nɛ alenfia nɛnɛ, ama nɛ fanɛ epeŋilarkpa be afu ber kumo so, k maaŋ chɛr nɛ k bolo.” Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ka bugi keŋasa na to be asheŋ

english_verse: Ezekiel, ask the rebellious people of Israel if they know what this story means. Tell them that the king of Babylonia came to Jerusalem, then he captured the king of Judah and his officials, and took them back to Babylon as prisoners.
translation_verse: “Bishi Israɛl be basa nɛ b pal kaman n sa ma ere fanɛ b pin keŋasa ere be kefito a? Kaŋɛ bumo fanɛ Babilɔn be efuli so be ewurgboŋ e ba Jerusalɛm to m ba pɛ Juda be ewura nɛ mbe benimuana m bɛta n yɔ Babilɔn be efuli so.

english_verse: He chose someone from the family of Judah's king and signed a treaty with him, then made him swear to be loyal. He also led away other important citizens,
translation_verse: Babilɔn be ewurgboŋ na daŋ ta Juda be ewura be kanaŋ to be esa ko nna n shin nɛ e bɔ ntaŋ fanɛ e beeŋ baa nu a sa mo, nseŋ shin nɛ mo nɛ mo wora kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre. Kumo be kaman nɛ e pɛ kade na be basa gboŋ n ti so n yɔ,

english_verse: so that the rest of the people of Judah would obey only him and never gain control of their own country again.
translation_verse: saŋɛ na so Juda be efuli so be basa nɛ b ka na beeŋ baa wɔ mbe kaseto a nu a sa mo nawule nsaa maaŋ naŋ tiŋ n nya eleŋ bumo gbagba be efuli na so kikɛ.

english_verse: But this new king of Judah later rebelled against Babylonia and sent officials to Egypt to get horses and troops. Will this king be successful in breaking the treaty with Babylonia? Or will he be punished for what he's done?
translation_verse: Ama ewura popɔr nɛ Babilɔn be ewurgboŋ lara na pal kaman n sa mo nseŋ shuŋi mbɔ Ijipt be efuli so a fin egbaŋɛ nɛ benapo damta. Fo tama fanɛ ewura ere beeŋ ji n lar kusɔ nɛ e bee wora ere to a? E maaŋ tiŋ n lar kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre na kaman nsaa maŋ nya kumo be kasogberge!”

english_verse: As surely as I am the living Lord God, I swear that the king of Judah will die in Babylon, because he broke the treaty with the king of Babylonia, who appointed him king.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ le: “Ŋ ka baa la Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ nɛ e bee sa ŋkpa ere bre, Juda be ewura ere beeŋ wu ashi Babilɔn be efuli so, ŋkpal e ka lar kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre nɛ mo nɛ Babilɔn be ewurgboŋ kre na kaman so nseŋ wora n da mo gbagba be ntaŋ nɛ e bɔ na so so.

english_verse: Even the king of Egypt and his powerful army will be useless to Judah when the Babylonians attack and build towers and dirt ramps to destroy the cities of Judah and its people.
translation_verse: Fɛɛro nɛ e la Ijipt be ewurgboŋ na nɛ mbe benapo lempo kikɛ maaŋ tiŋ n chɛ Juda be basa to ŋ kɔ jemanɛ nɛ Babilɔn be basa beeŋ ba gbare eshishɛr n deŋi abar so m mata Jerusalɛm be egbal na a fin keluri kade na to ŋ kɔ m mɔ basa na.

english_verse: The king of Judah broke his own promises and ignored the treaty with Babylonia. And so he will be punished!
translation_verse: Juda be ewura gbagba e wora n da mbe ntaŋ so nseŋ lar kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre nɛ mo nɛ Babilɔn be ewurgboŋ kre na kaman, ŋkpal loŋ so, e beeŋ nya kasogberge.

english_verse: He made a promise in my name and swore to honor the treaty. And now that he has broken that promise, my name is disgraced. He must pay for what he's done.
translation_verse: Amoso kusɔ nɛ ma Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ nɛ mee sa ŋkpa na kaŋɛ e la fanɛ meeŋ gberge Juda be ewura kusoe ŋkpal e ka wora n da mo gbagba be ntaŋ nɛ e bɔ so nseŋ lar kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre na kaman so so.

english_verse: I will spread out a net to trap him. Then I will drag him to Babylon and see that he is punished for his unfaithfulness to me.
translation_verse: Kewora fanɛ kashewu nɛ n ta m pɛ mo nseŋ yɛr mo Babilɔn be efuli so n ya ji mo demu ndoŋ ŋkpal e ka maŋ ji kashenteŋ n sa ma so.

english_verse: Someday, I, the Lord, will cut a tender twig from the top of a cedar tree, then plant it on the peak of Israel's tallest mountain,
translation_verse: Kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ nde: “Ŋ gbagba beeŋ ku kedibi nɛ baa tre sida na be keyabi n fɛa; keyabi popɔrbi nɛ meeŋ ku ashi kumo be awɔlto n ya fɛa kebee jeŋgreŋ so.

english_verse: where it will grow strong branches and produce large fruit. All kinds of birds will find shelter under the tree, and they will rest in the shade of its branches.
translation_verse: Israɛl be kebee nɛ k du jeŋgreŋ ga na be awɔlto nɛ meeŋ fɛa kumo. Nɛ k daŋ n wora ayabi nseŋ sɔr asɔrso nseŋ ki sida be kedibi lela. Nɛ mbuibi be yiri kikɛ e ba tɔ asha kumo so; nseŋ nya edikpa kumo be ayabi so.

english_verse: Every tree in the forest will know that I, the Lord, can bring down tall trees and help short ones grow. I dry up green trees and make dry ones green. I, the Lord, have spoken, and I will keep my word.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nɛ ndibi nɛ a wɔ kasawule na so beeŋ pin fanɛ ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e naa ku ndibi tenteŋ a lɛ nsaa shin nɛ ndibi shiimbi bee daŋ nteŋ. Mee naa shin nɛ ndibi bumbuŋ bee wɔl nsaa shin nɛ ndibi wɔlso bee purge. Ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e malga na; ma alɛ beeŋ wora kusɔ nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ na kikɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ ma:

english_verse: Ezekiel, I hear the people of Israel using the old saying, “Sour grapes eaten by parents leave a sour taste in the mouths of their children.”
translation_verse: “Ezikɛl, mee kaa nu Israɛl be basa ka bee bɔ keŋasa ere e kaŋɛ fanɛ; bekurgepo e ji anyinyembi nɛ a bee nyiri bumo be mbia be anyi.

english_verse: Now tell them that I am the Lord God, and as surely as I live, that saying will no longer be used in Israel.
translation_verse: Naniere kaŋɛ bumo fanɛ ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ nɛ e bee sa ŋkpa na e kaŋɛ na fanɛ b maaŋ naa bɔ loŋ be keŋasa na Israɛl be efuli so.

english_verse: The lives of all people belong to me—parents as well as children. However, only those who sin will be put to death.
translation_verse: Dimɛdi kikɛ be ŋkpa bɔɔ ma enɔ nna, bekurgepo nɛ bumo be mbia kikɛ. Amoso, esa nɛ e wora kulubi e naaŋ wu kumo be luwu.

english_verse: Suppose there is a truly good man who always does what is fair and right.
translation_verse: Nɛ fanɛ esa lela koso a ji kashenteŋ nsaa wora kusɔ nɛ k daga jemanɛ kikɛ.

english_verse: He refuses to eat meat sacrificed to foreign gods at local shrines or to worship Israel's idols. He doesn't have sex with someone else's wife or with a woman having her monthly period.
translation_verse: E maa ji agbirjibi ŋko a shuŋ Israɛl be basa be agbirana na. Mo alɛ maa sha mo barkasa be eche ŋko a di eche jemanɛ nɛ e bee lar ntamaŋ.

english_verse: He never cheats or robs anyone and always returns anything taken as security for a loan; he gives food and clothes to the poor
translation_verse: Amodoŋwura malɛ maa puni ŋko a suge esa, mo alɛ maa sɔ tarma pɔɛŋ nseŋ sa esa mpaŋ. Ade be kaman mo alɛ naa chɛ betirpo to a sa bumo ajibi nɛ asɔbuuso.

english_verse: and doesn't charge interest when lending money. He refuses to do anything evil; he is fair to everyone
translation_verse: Loŋ be esa na maa wɔtɔ amansherbi nɛ e ta m paŋ esa nchu, mo alɛ maa wora kulubi nseŋ naa ji asheŋ nɛ amo be ekpa so a sa ekama.

english_verse: But suppose this good man has an evil son who is violent and commits sins
translation_verse: Ama nɛ fanɛ esa lela ere kurge ebi nɛ e bee suge nsaa mɔ basa, nsaa wora

english_verse: his father never did. He eats meat at local shrines, has sex with someone else's wife,
translation_verse: asheŋ nɛ mo tuto bre maaŋ wora na. Ebi na bee ji agbirjibi nsaa di mo braana be beche.

english_verse: cheats the poor, and robs people. He keeps what is given to him as security for a loan. He worships idols, does disgusting things,
translation_verse: E bee puni betirpo nsaa suge basa. Nɛ esa ta kusɔ ko m ba yili tarma gba e maaŋ naŋ laŋɛ kumo n sa kumo wura. Mo alɛ bee shuŋ agbirana nsaa wora ekishisheŋ.

english_verse: and charges high interest when lending money. An evil man like that will certainly not live. He is the one who has done these horrible sins, so it's his own fault that he will be put to death.
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman, e bee wɔtɔ mpaŋ kama nɛ e sa esa nchu ga nna. Esa kikɛ nɛ e la esa lubi fanɛ mo maa ba nɛ e ji efute n chɛr. Mo gbagba e wora le be ekishisheŋ ere, amoso mo e daga amo be luwu. Mo luwu na be turju beeŋ baa bɛ mo gbagba nna.

english_verse: But suppose this evil man has a son who sees his father do these things and refuses to act like him.
translation_verse: Ama nɛ fanɛ esa lubi ere pibi wu asheŋ nɛ mo tuto bee wora na nseŋ kini kewora asheŋ fanɛ mo tuto,

english_verse: He doesn't eat meat at local shrines or worship Israel's idols, and he doesn't have sex with someone else's wife.
translation_verse: nsaa maa ji agbirjibi ŋko a shuŋ Israɛl be agbirana, mo alɛ maaŋ di mo barkasa be eche.

english_verse: He never cheats or robs anyone and doesn't even demand security for a loan. He gives food and clothes to the poor
translation_verse: E maaŋ suge ŋko m puni esa kikɛ, mo alɛ maaŋ sɔ tarma pɔɛŋ nseŋ sa esa mpaŋ. Mo alɛ bee sa betirpo ajibi nɛ asɔbuuso nna

english_verse: and refuses to do anything evil or to charge interest. And he obeys all my laws and teachings. Such a man will live. His own father sinned, but this good man will not be put to death for the sins of his father.
translation_verse: nsaa kini asheŋ lubi be kewora. Kusɔ nɛ e bee wora e la fanɛ e bee nu nna nsaa bɛ ma mbraana nɛ ma keŋini so. Le be esa beeŋ ji efute n chɛr. Mo tuto e wora alubi, nɛ le be esa lela ere maaŋ wu ŋkpal mo tuto be asheŋ lubi so.

english_verse: It is his father who will die for cheating and robbing and doing evil.
translation_verse: Mo tuto gbagba e naŋ wu ŋkpal mbe kapuni nɛ kasuge nɛ asheŋ lubi so.

english_verse: You may wonder why a son isn't punished for the sins of his father. It is because the son does what is right and obeys my laws.
translation_verse: Ashere menyeeŋ bishi fanɛ nɛ mannɛ e baa nɛ ebi maaŋ nya mo tuto be asheŋ lubi be kakɔka? Kusɔ nɛ k ba e la fanɛ ebi na wora kusɔ nɛ k daga nseŋ wora ma mbraana kasonu nna.

english_verse: Only those who sin will be put to death. Children won't suffer for the sins of their parents, and parents won't suffer for the sins of their children. Good people will be rewarded for what they do, and evil people will be punished for what they do.
translation_verse: Basa nɛ b wora alubi e naa wu alubi be luwu. Mbia maaŋ ji awurfoŋ ŋkpal bumo tutoana be alubi so nɛ bekurgepo gba maaŋ ji awurfoŋ ŋkpal bumo be mbia be alubi so. Basa lela beeŋ nya bumo be alelasheŋ be kakɔka nɛ basa lubi malɛ e nya kasogberge ŋkpal bumo be alubi so.

english_verse: Suppose wicked people stop sinning and start obeying my laws and doing right. They won't be put to death.
translation_verse: Nɛ fanɛ basa lubi yige asheŋ lubi be kewora nseŋ fara a wora ma mbraana kasonu nseŋ naa wora asheŋ nɛ a daga, b maaŋ wu manaŋ.

english_verse: All their sins will be forgiven, and they will live because they did right.
translation_verse: Baaŋ nya bumo be alubi kikɛ be ketampaŋ, ŋkpal b ka wora asheŋ nɛ a daga so.

english_verse: I, the Lord God, don't like to see wicked people die. I had much rather see them turn back from their sins and live.
translation_verse: Basa lubi be luwu maa par ma Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kikɛ. Kusɔ nɛ mee sha e la fanɛ b ka beeŋ tuba n lar bumo be alubi to nseŋ ji efute n chɛr.

english_verse: But when good people start sinning and doing disgusting things, will they live? No! All their good deeds will be forgotten, and they will be put to death because of their sins.
translation_verse: Ama nɛ fanɛ basa lela yige alela be kewora nseŋ fara a wora ekishisheŋ nɛ basa lubi bee wora na, a daga fanɛ b ji efute n chɛr a? Ayai! B maaŋ nyiŋi bumo alelasheŋ dra na. Baaŋ wu ŋkpal bumo be asheŋ lubi na so.

english_verse: If good people start doing evil, they must be put to death, because they have sinned.
translation_verse: Nɛ fanɛ basa lela fara asheŋ lubi be kewora, a daga fanɛ b wu ŋkpal bumo be alubi so.

english_verse: And if wicked people start doing right, they will save themselves from punishment.
translation_verse: Nɛ fanɛ basa lubi malɛ yige asheŋ lubi be kewora nsaa wora asheŋ lela, baaŋ mɔlga bumo be amu ashi kasogberge to.

english_verse: They will think about what they've done and stop sinning, and so they won't be put to death.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal b ka fɛ bumo be asheŋ wora so na be asheŋ nseŋ yige asheŋ lubi na be kewora so nɛ baaŋ ji efute.

english_verse: But you still say that I am unfair. You are the ones who have done wrong and are unfair!
translation_verse: Ama men kraa kaŋɛ fanɛ asɔ nɛ mee wora na maŋ walɛ. Menyi e wora n jija nsaa wora asɔ nɛ a maŋ walɛ.

english_verse: Give up your evil ways and start thinking pure thoughts. And be faithful to me! Do you really want to be put to death for your sins?
translation_verse: Men lar men be asheŋ lubi na to nseŋ fara a fɛ asheŋ lela be kewora be asheŋ menyi be ŋgbene to. Menyi alɛ e baa ji kashenteŋ a sa ma. Men sa maŋ shin nɛ menyi be alubi e mɔ menyi.

english_verse: I, the Lord God, don't want to see that happen to anyone. So stop sinning and live!
translation_verse: Ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na maa sha fanɛ men be ekama e wu. Amoso men tuba nseŋ ji efute n chɛr!”

english_verse: Your mother was a brave lioness who raised her cubs among lions.
translation_verse: “Men nio daa la fanɛ buluŋ cheso nɛ e daa kɔ kenyɛn nna nseŋ bela mbe bibi ashi ebuluŋ nyɛnso lempo to!

english_verse: She taught one of them to hunt, and he learned to eat people.
translation_verse: E bela mbe ebi ko nseŋ ŋini kumo kepɛ n ji, nɛ k koya edimɛdi be kepɛ n ji.

english_verse: When the nations heard of him, they trapped him in a pit, then they used hooks to drag him to Egypt.
translation_verse: Efuliana na ka nu mbe asheŋ, nɛ b fe mo kekpaala m pɛ mo, nseŋ ta edariwa ŋ gberge mo n yɔ Ijipt be efuli so.

english_verse: His mother waited for him to return. But soon she lost all hope and raised another cub, who also became fierce.
translation_verse: Kumo nio ka jo nseŋ wu fanɛ tama loge na, nɛ k naŋ ta kumo be bibi na be eko m bela kumo nɛ k ki buluŋ lempo.

english_verse: Nations plotted to kill him, and people came from all over to spread out a net and catch him in a trap.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ efuliana na kre kumo be kemɔ be nia, nɛ basa shi kaplɛkama m ba. Nɛ b sho kashewu m pɛ kumo

english_verse: They put him in a cage and took him to Babylonia. The lion was locked away, so that his mighty roar would never again be heard on Israel's hills.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ b ta kumo n wɔtɔ katurgegboŋ to nseŋ ta kumo n yɔ Babilɔn be ewura kutɔ. N ya ta mo n ti ebu nɛ ekama maŋ naŋ nu mbe kaponte ashi Israɛl be abee so kikɛ.

english_verse: Your mother was a vine like you, growing near a stream. There was plenty of water, so she was filled with branches and with lots of fruit.
translation_verse: Fo nio daa du fanɛ kedibi sɔrso nna nɛ k yil m mata kabombi; K daa sɔr nɛnɛ nna nsaa kɔ ayabi damta ŋkpal k ka daa nya nchu nɛnɛ so.

english_verse: Her strong branches became symbols of authority, and she was taller than all other trees— everyone could see how strong and healthy she was.
translation_verse: Kumo be ayabi daa kɔ eleŋ nna, nseŋ daa walɛ keku n wora kuwurkpabi. K daŋ daŋ n yɔ awɔlto a chɔ ndibi nɛ a ka na kikɛ nna. Ekama daŋ wu kumo be nteŋ nɛ ayabi damta.

english_verse: But in anger, I pulled her up by the roots and threw her to the ground, where the scorching desert wind dried out her fruit. Her strong branches wilted and burned up.
translation_verse: Ama agbo so nɛ n tia kumo n lɛ kasawule. Afu nɛ a shi epeŋilarkpa daŋ shin nɛ k bolo nɛ kumo be asɔrso gbaŋgbaŋ n tɔr; nɛ kumo be ayabi lempo na wɔl nɛ edɛ ji amo.

english_verse: Then she was planted in a hot, dry desert,
translation_verse: Naniere keshishɛrsawule so nɛ n duu kumo, kasawule wɔlso nɛ nchu maŋ wɔ kumo so.

english_verse: where her stem caught fire, and flames burned her branches and fruit. Not one strong branch is left; she is stripped bare. This funeral song must be sung with sorrow.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ kumo be keyabi gboŋgboŋi ko pɛ edɛ; nɛ edɛ na bɛ kumo so n chɔɔ kumo be ayabi nɛ asɔrso kikɛ. Keyabi lempo kikɛ daŋ maŋ naŋ ka kumo so nɛ b ku n wora kuwurkpabi. Kashɛ ere la kagbenejija be kashɛ nna n daga kebaaboŋ kagbenejijaso.”

english_verse: Seven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, some of Israel's leaders came to me on the tenth day of the fifth month. They sat down and asked for a message from the Lord.
translation_verse: B ka pɛ ewura Jehowachin nɛ anyi be beko n yɔ Babilɔn be efuli so na be kafɛ shunusopo to be kufɔl nusopo to be kachɛ kudusopo na nɛ Israɛl be benimuana ko ba chena ma anishi to a fin kenu kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kɔ nɛ e kaŋɛ bumo.

english_verse: Just then, the Lord God said:
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ ma

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, these leaders have come to find out what I want them to do. As surely as I live, I will not give them an answer of any kind.
translation_verse: fanɛ ŋ kaŋɛ Israɛl be benimuana na fanɛ kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ nde: “Men ba nna nɛ men ba pin kusɔ nɛ mee sha fanɛ men wora a? Ŋ ka baa la Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ nɛ e bee sa ŋkpa ere, m maaŋ shin nɛ men pin kusɔ nɛ mee sha fanɛ men wora.

english_verse: Are you willing to warn them, Ezekiel? Then remind them of the disgusting sins of their ancestors.
translation_verse: Dimɛdi pibi, fo wora shiriya nɛ fo kpele bumo kusoe a? Kumo ere nyiŋi bumo ekishisheŋ nɛ bumo tutoana daŋ wora na be asheŋ,

english_verse: Tell them that long ago I, the Lord God, chose Israel to be my own. I appeared to their ancestors in Egypt and made a solemn promise that I would be their God and the God of their descendants.
translation_verse: nseŋ naŋ kaŋɛ bumo fanɛ kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na bee kaŋɛ e la fanɛ kachɛ nɛ e lara menyi nɛ men baa la mbe basa na, e daŋ bɔ ntaŋ nna n nase kɔnɔ n sa Jeekɔb nɛ men tutoana nseŋ lara mbe kumu ŋ ŋini bumo ashi Ijipt be efuli so ŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ e beeŋ baa la menyi nɛ men be kaman to ebi be Ebɔrɛ.

english_verse: I swore that I would rescue them from Egypt and lead them to a land I had already chosen. This land was rich with milk and honey and was the most splendid land of all.
translation_verse: Loŋ be kachɛ na nɛ e nase kɔnɔ fanɛ e beeŋ lara bumo Ijipt be efuli so n yɔ kasawule nɛ k kɔ kanya alegaiso nsaa wora adɔjibi ga nseŋ naa la kasawule nɛ k walɛ a chɔ nsawule kikɛ nɛ mo gbagba fin n yili bumo na so.

english_verse: But that would have made me look like a liar, because I had already promised in front of everyone that I would lead them out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Ama n daa maŋ wora loŋ, ŋkpal ŋ ka daa maa sha fanɛ ma ketre e jija efuliana nɛ baaŋ wu kananɛ meeŋ lara ma kumu ŋ ŋini Israɛl be basa nseŋ juŋkpar bumo n lar Ijipt be efuli so na be anishito so.

english_verse: So I brought them out and led them into the desert.
translation_verse: Amoso nɛ n daŋ juŋkpar bumo n lar Ijipt be efuli so n yɔ keshishɛrsawule so na.

english_verse: I gave them my laws and teachings, so they would know how to live right.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nɛ n sa bumo ma mbraana nɛ ma keŋini, nɛ b wora amo kasonu nseŋ pin kananɛ baŋ baa keta bumo be amu.

english_verse: And I commanded them to respect the Sabbath as a way of showing that they were holy and belonged to me.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman, nɛ n yili ma Kewushiachɛ n sa bumo nɛ k baa la ashi tɔɔnɛ ma nɛ bumo be kefɛato, saŋɛ na so baaŋ pin fanɛ ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e shin nɛ b ki basa cheembi.

english_verse: But the Israelites rebelled against me in the desert. They refused to obey my laws and teachings, and they treated the Sabbath like any other day. Then in my anger, I decided to destroy the Israelites in the desert once and for all.
translation_verse: Ama Israɛl be basa na lar ma kaman keshishɛrsawule na so ndoŋ, nseŋ kini kebɛ ma mbraana nɛ keŋini nɛ a bee shin nɛ esa bee bii kebaawɔtɔ lela na so. Bumo alɛ nseŋ keni ma Kewushiachɛ na jiga. Amoso nɛ n daŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ meeŋ shin nɛ ma agbo e ba bumo so nɛ m mur bumo ashi keshishɛrsawule na so na.

english_verse: But that would have disgraced me, because many other nations had seen me bring the Israelites out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Ama n daa maŋ wora loŋ, ŋkpal ŋ ka daa maa sha fanɛ ma ketre e jija ashi efuliana nɛ b wu kananɛ n lara bumo ashi Ijipt be efuli so na be anishito so.

english_verse: Instead, I told them in the desert that I would not lead them into the beautiful, fertile land I had promised.
translation_verse: Amoso nɛ ma alɛ daŋ bɔ ntaŋ ŋ kaŋɛ bumo keshishɛrsawule na so fanɛ m maaŋ naŋ yɛr bumo kasawule lela nɛ k bee wora adɔjibi ga nɛ n daŋ sa bumo na so.

english_verse: I said this because they had not only ignored my laws and teachings, but had disgraced my Sabbath and worshiped idols.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal manɛ so, b kini kebɛ ma mbraana nɛ ma keŋini so nseŋ keni ma Kewushiachɛ na jiga, nɛ bumo be ŋgbene kikɛ malɛ daa wɔ bumo be agbirana na so a chɔ ma.

english_verse: Yet, I felt sorry for them and could not let them die in the desert.
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman, n daŋ wu bumo kuwɔr nna a maŋ mur bumo ŋko n shin nɛ b shir keshishɛrsawule na so ndoŋ.

english_verse: I reminded them that I was the Lord their God and that they should obey my laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Ma e la Enyɛnpe, menyi be Ebɔrɛ na; men be ma mbraana nɛ ma keŋini so.

english_verse: I told them to respect my Sabbath to show that they were my people and that I was the Lord their God.
translation_verse: Men ta ma Kewushiachɛ naŋ ki kachɛ cheembi, saŋɛ na so k beeŋ baa la tɔɔnɛ a ŋini fanɛ men la ma basa nna nɛ ma alɛ la Enyɛnpe menyi be Ebɔrɛ na.

english_verse: But the children also rebelled against me. They refused to obey my laws and teachings, and they treated the Sabbath as any other day. I became angry and decided to punish them in the desert.
translation_verse: Ama ashi keshishɛrsawule na so ndoŋ, mbia na gba lar ma kaman nseŋ kini kebɛ ma mbraana nɛ ma keŋini so. Bumo alɛ gba naŋ keni ma Kewushiachɛ na jiga nna. Amoso nɛn daŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ meeŋ shin nɛ ma agbo e ba bumo so ashi kiyi na to ndoŋ.

english_verse: But I did not. That would have disgraced me in front of the nations that had seen me bring the Israelites out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Ama n daa maŋ wora loŋ, ŋkpal ŋ ka daa maa sha fanɛ ma ketre e jija ashi efuliana nɛ b wu kananɛ n juŋkpar bumo n lar Ijipt be efuli so na be anishito so.

english_verse: So I solemnly swore that I would scatter the people of Israel across the nations,
translation_verse: Amoso nɛ n daŋ naŋ bɔ ntaŋ ŋ kaŋɛ bumo kiyi na to fanɛ meeŋ shin nɛ b pesaŋ to n sɔ efuliana pɔtɛana so na.

english_verse: because they had disobeyed my laws and ignored my teachings; they had disgraced my Sabbath and worshiped the idols their ancestors had made.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal manɛ so, b daŋ kini kebɛ ma mbraana nɛ atande so nsaa maŋ ta ma Kewushiachɛ na n tre sheŋ nna. Bumo tutoana be agbirana e daŋ bɔlɔ bumo kenishi ga nɛ b daa shuŋ amo.

english_verse: and I let them offer me unacceptable sacrifices, including their first-born sons. I did this to horrify them and to let them know that I, the Lord, was punishing them.
translation_verse: B daŋ naŋ bɔla bumo gbagba be esarga so n jija bumo be kebaawɔtɔ nna. B daa ta bumo be ewurkoŋ nna a lara esarga. N daŋ shin nɛ loŋ wora nna nɛ kufu e pɛ bumo nɛ b pin fanɛ ma e la Enyɛnpe na.

english_verse: Ezekiel, tell the people of Israel that their ancestors also rejected and insulted me
translation_verse: Amoso, dimɛdi pibi, Ezikɛl, kaŋɛ Israɛlebi na fanɛ, kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ e la fanɛ kananɛ bumo tutoana daŋ kini ma nseŋ tege ma nna na.

english_verse: I asked them where they went to worship those gods, and they answered, “At the local shrines.” And those places of worship are still called shrines.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ m bishi bumo fanɛ nuso be mboŋ nɛ menyee kaa yɔ na? Nɛ b kaŋɛ, ‘Agbir ase’ nɛ anyee yɔ. Hale nɛ mbre agbirshuŋkpa nɛ baa tre agbir ase.

english_verse: by worshiping idols and by sacrificing their own children as offerings. They commit these sins and still think they can ask me for a message. As surely as I am the living Lord God, I will give them no answer.
translation_verse: Jemanɛ nɛ menyee ta menyi be mbia a lara esarga a sa agbirana na hale nɛ mbre na, menyee jija menyi be amu nɛ menyi be kebaawɔtɔ nna na. O Israɛlebi, a daga ŋ ka naŋ sa menyi ekpa nɛ men bishi ma kusɔ ko a? Ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ e naa kaŋɛ menyi kashenteŋto na fanɛ m maaŋ sa menyi ekpa nɛ men bishi ma shɛŋ.

english_verse: They may think they can be like other nations and get away with worshiping idols made of wood and stone. But that will never happen! The Lord Promises To Restore Israel The Lord said to the people of Israel:
translation_verse: Menyee kaa kaŋɛ le nna: “Anyee sha fanɛ an baa du fanɛ efuliana nɛ amo be basa bee shuŋ ndibi nɛ ajembu na nna.” Ama kusɔ nɛ menyee fɛ na maaŋ tiŋ n wora kikɛ.

english_verse: As surely as I am the living Lord God, I will rule over you with my powerful arm. You will feel my fierce anger
translation_verse: Ma Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na e naa kaŋɛ menyi kashenteŋto na fanɛ meeŋ ta eleŋ n ji kuwura menyi so nɛ men pin kananɛ ma agbogboŋ du.

english_verse: and my power, when I gather you from the places where you are scattered
translation_verse: Eleŋ nɛ tintiŋ nɛ agbogboŋ nɛ meeŋ ta n lara menyi ashi efuliana nɛ men pesaŋ to n yɔ na, m ba gama abar so.

english_verse: and lead you into a desert surrounded by nations. I will meet you there face to face. Then I will pass judgment on you
translation_verse: Nseŋ bar menyi keshishɛrsawule nɛ efuliana na kulti kumo na so, nɛ ma nɛ menyi e tu abar ndoŋ nɛ n ji menyi demu nɛ men ji n tɔr.

english_verse: I will force each of you to obey the regulations of our solemn agreement.
translation_verse: “Meeŋ ta tintiŋ n shin nɛ men be ekama e wora kusɔ nɛ kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre na bee ŋini.

english_verse: I will separate the sinful rebels from the rest of you, and even though I will bring them from the nations where they live in exile, they won't be allowed to return to Israel. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Meeŋ lara ŋgbene kpakpaso wuraana nɛ baa lar ma kaman na ashi menyi to. Hale nɛ n lara bumo ashi efuliana nɛ b pesaŋ to n yɔ na gba m ba, b maaŋ nya m bɛta n yɔ Israɛl be kasawule so. Ndoŋ nɛ menyeeŋ pin fanɛ ma e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.

english_verse: Go ahead and worship your idols for now, you Israelites, because soon I will no longer let you dishonor me by offering gifts to them. You will have no choice but to obey me!
translation_verse: Kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ bee kaŋɛ menyi nde: Menyi Israɛlebi, be ekama nɛ e bee sha e ya kaa shuŋ mbe agbirana, ŋkpal manɛ so, ade kikɛ be kaman menyeeŋ ba nu n sa ma nseŋ yige kebaa lara esarga a sa menyi be agbirana a jija ma ketre.

english_verse: When that day comes, everyone in Israel will worship me on Mount Zion, my holy mountain in Jerusalem. I will once again call you my own, and I will accept your sacred offerings and sacrifices.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal manɛ so, kachɛ na kaŋ fo ekama ashi Israɛl be efuli so beeŋ shuŋ ma ashi kebee cheembi nɛ baa tre Zayɔn ashi Jerusalɛm to na so, nɛ ma alɛ e sɔ bumo esarga nɛ baaŋ lara n sa ma ndoŋ na. Menyi be asheŋ beeŋ baa par ma nɛ ma alɛ e baa keni menyi be esarga lela nɛ ŋkɛ cheembi na akpa.

english_verse: When I bring you home from the places where you are now scattered, I will be pleased with you, just as I am pleased with the smell of the smoke from your sacrifices. Every nation on earth will see that I am holy,
translation_verse: Jemanɛ nɛ meeŋ naŋ lara menyi efuliana nɛ men pesaŋ to n yɔ to m bɛta m ba gama abar so na, ma kagbene beeŋ naŋ fuli menyi so nɛ n sɔ menyi be esarga fanɛ duwu nɛ a bee dufɛ viim na. Ndoŋ nɛ efuliana na kikɛ beeŋ wu fanɛ n du cheembi nna.

english_verse: and you will know that I, the Lord, am the one who brought you back to Israel, the land I promised your ancestors.
translation_verse: Jemanɛ nɛ meeŋ bɛta menyi m ba Israɛl be efuli so, kasawule nɛ n nase kɔnɔ fanɛ meeŋ ta n sa men tutoana na, nɛ menyeeŋ pin fanɛ ma e la Enyɛnpe na.

english_verse: Then you will remember your wicked sins, and you will hate yourselves for doing such horrible things. They have made you unacceptable to me,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nɛ menyeeŋ nyiŋi menyi be asheŋ wora so nɛ a shin nɛ men jija menyi be kebaawɔtɔ na, nɛ a shin nɛ menyi be asheŋ e baa nu menyi gbagba agbo ŋkpal asheŋ lubi nɛ men wora so.

english_verse: so you deserve to be punished. But I will treat you in a way that will bring honor to my name, and you will know that I am the Lord God. Fire from the South
translation_verse: Jemanɛ nɛ meeŋ wora menyi, Israɛlebi, asheŋ nɛ a beeŋ bar ma ketre kemaŋkura nɛ mannɛ men be asheŋ lubi nɛ aworbi jiga so na nɛ menyeeŋ pin fanɛ ma e la Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na.”

english_verse: “Ezekiel, son of man, turn toward the south and warn the forests
translation_verse: E yɛ: “Dimɛdi pibi, kilgi a keni kelargato be kaseto nseŋ malga ŋ gbiti kupo nɛ k wɔ ndoŋ na.

english_verse: that I, the Lord God, will start a fire that will burn up every tree, whether green or dry. Nothing will be able to put out the blaze of that fire as it spreads to the north and burns everything in its path.
translation_verse: Kaŋɛ kupo na fanɛ k kaŋ kusoe n nu Enyɛnpe na be kubɔya. E yɛ: ‘Mee sha kenya edɛ n wɔtɔ fo to nɛ a chɔɔ fo ndibi bumbuŋ nɛ awɔlso kikɛ m mur nna na. Sheŋ maaŋ tiŋ n duŋ edɛ na saŋɛ nɛ a beeŋ yili kelargato be kaseto n chɔɔ a yɔ kelargato be esoso na. Kusɔkama malɛ nɛ edɛ na beeŋ tu amo be kebɔr so beeŋ ji edɛ m mur.

english_verse: Everyone will know that I started it, and that it cannot be stopped.”
translation_verse: Ekama beeŋ pin fanɛ ma Enyɛnpe na e nya edɛ na n wɔtɔ kupo na to nɛ ekama malɛ maaŋ tiŋ n duŋ amo.’ ”

english_verse: But I complained, “Lord God, I don't want to do that! People already say I confuse them with my messages.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ n fubel ŋ kaŋɛ: “Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ, sa maŋ shin nɛ n wora loŋ! Ekama bee malga a kaŋɛ fanɛ aŋasa nɛ mee bɔ nɛ a bee wul bumo to.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the places in Jerusalem where people worship. Warn everyone in Israel
translation_verse: “Dimɛdi pibi, Ezikɛl, kilgi fo anishi n shoŋi Jerusalɛm m malga ŋ gbiti kakpa nɛ basa na bee shuŋ be Ebɔrɛ na. Kpele Israɛl be basa kikɛ kusoe

english_verse: that I am about to punish them. I will pull out my sword and have it ready to kill everyone, whether good or evil.
translation_verse: nseŋ kaŋɛ bumo fanɛ ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na bee kaŋɛ fanɛ b ki ndoŋana nna. Amoso meeŋ pee ma tokobi kumo be efar to m mɔ bumo to be basa lela nɛ belubi kikɛ.

english_verse: Ezekiel, groan in sorrow and despair so that everyone can hear you.
translation_verse: Amoso, dimɛdi pibi, shin nɛ fo kagbene e jija fo nɛ fo baa shu ashi kakpa nɛ ekama beeŋ wu fo.

english_verse: When they ask why you are groaning, tell them you have terrifying news that will make them faint and tremble in fear and lose all courage. These things will happen soon. I, the Lord God, make this promise! A Sword Is Ready To Attack Israel
translation_verse: B kaŋ bishi fo kusɔ nɛ k ba nɛ fee shu fo kaŋɛ bumo le: ‘Baru nɛ k bee ba na so nɛ mee shu.’ Kumo jemanɛ kaŋ fo ekama be kagbene beeŋ jija mo nɛ kufu e tɔr ekama so nɛ bumo be aba e pɔ bumo nɛ b baa chicha a maaŋ naŋ tiŋ n wora shɛŋ. Kachɛ na bee ba! K maaŋ naŋ chɛr nseŋ ba. Ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na e kaŋɛ na.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Jerusalem: I have sharpened my sword to slaughter you; it is shiny and will flash like lightning! Don't celebrate— punishment is coming, because everyone has ignored my warnings.
translation_verse: N yee kumo nɛ n mɔ; n fifɛa kumo so nɛ k bee kpa edɛ fanɛ bɔrɛ ka nyɛkpɛ na! Kayurji maŋ naa wɔtɔ, ŋkpal manɛ so, ma basa kplaŋ ma kasokpele nɛ kasogberge kikɛ so nna.

english_verse: My sword has been polished; it's sharp and ready to kill.
translation_verse: Mee yee ma tokobi nna, a wora kumo shiriya a jo, esa nɛ e beeŋ ta kumo m mɔ na.

english_verse: Groan in sorrow, Ezekiel; the sword is drawn against my people and their leaders. They will die! So give up all hope.
translation_verse: Dimɛdi pibi, boŋ to awɔrso, ŋkpal manɛ so tokobi na bee ba ma basa nɛ Israɛl be benimuana so nna. Bumo kikɛ beeŋ wu, bumo nɛ basa nɛ b ka na kikɛ. Amoso, ta enɔ n deŋi kumu a shu!”

english_verse: I am testing my people, and they can do nothing to stop me. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na naŋ kaŋɛ le: “Mee wora ma basa a keni nna na, nɛ b kaŋ kini ketuba, kumo ere asheŋ ere kikɛ beeŋ ba bumo so.”

english_verse: It will slash right and left, wherever the blade is pointed.
translation_verse: K beeŋ baa ŋe bena nɛ jiso; kaplɛkama nɛ kumo be jisoso kilgi n shoŋi nɛ k beeŋ ŋe.

english_verse: Then I will stop being angry, and I will clap my hands in victory. I, the Lord, have spoken. The King of Babylonia and His Sword
translation_verse: Ma alɛ gba beeŋ ber enɔbelaŋ, nɛ ma agbo e yɔɔso. Ma, Enyɛnpe e kaŋɛ na.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, mark two roads for the king of Babylonia to follow when he comes with his sword. The roads will begin at the same place, but be sure to put up a signpost where the two roads separate and go in different directions.
translation_verse: E yɛ: “Dimɛdi pibi, ŋini ekpa anyɔ nɛ Babilɔn be efuli so be ewura beeŋ ta mbe tokobi na m bɔla so m ba. Ekpa anyɔ na daga fanɛ a fara efuli koŋwule so nna. Dulgi kakpa nɛ ekpa na barga to anyɔ na,

english_verse: Clearly mark where the two roads lead. One goes to Rabbah, the capital of Ammon, and the other goes to Jerusalem, the fortified capital of Judah.
translation_verse: a ŋini ekpa nɛ k bee yɔ Ammɔnebi be kadegboŋ nɛ baa tre Raba na, nɛ kumo nɛ kumo alɛ bee yɔ Juda be kadegboŋ nɛ baa tre Jerusalɛm nɛ b pɔr egbal ŋ kulti kumo na; nɛ Babilɔn be ewura na e bɔla so n yɛr mbe tokobi na.

english_verse: When the Babylonian king stands at that signpost, he will decide which way to go by shaking his arrows, by asking his idols, and by carefully looking at the liver of a sacrificed animal.
translation_verse: Babilɔn be ewura kaŋ baa fo ekpa anyɔ na be ŋkpancheri na, e beeŋ bɔla mbe atanyembi so nɛ mbe agbirana so nɛ kusɔbɔya nɛ b mɔ n lara sarga be kegbirche so m bishi so m pin kusɔ nɛ e beeŋ wora.

english_verse: His right hand will pull out the arrow marked “Jerusalem.” Then he will immediately give the signal to shout the battle cry, to build dirt ramps up to the top of the city walls, to break down its walls and gates with large wooden poles, and to kill the people.
translation_verse: Nɛ e baaŋ ta enɔjiso m pee ketanyembi nɛ b sibɛ ‘Jerusalɛm’ n deŋi kumo so a ŋini fanɛ b kɔ kumo kena, e beeŋ shin nɛ b foŋ kabel n sa benapo ekpa nɛ b ya kulti kadegboŋ na n wɔtɔ, nseŋ koli eshishɛr n deŋi abar so ŋ gbuŋ egbal nɛ k kulti kade na, saŋɛ na so baaŋ bɔla amo so n dii n luri kade na to ŋ kɔ basa na kena. Bumo alɛ beeŋ naaŋ ta ndibi gbɛgbɛso n da kade na be mbunagboŋ na m bugi n n luri to.

english_verse: Everyone in Jerusalem had promised to be loyal to Babylonia, and so none of them will believe that this could happen to them. But Babylonia's king will remind them of their sinful ways and warn them of their coming captivity.
translation_verse: Ekama nɛ e wɔ Jerusalɛm beeŋ baa fɛ fanɛ efɛ be kubɔya e la kumo, ŋkpal manɛ so, bumo nɛ Babilɔn be ewura nase nnɔ nna n sa abar. Ama e beeŋ nyiŋi bumo asheŋ lubi nɛ b wora na nseŋ yili amo so pɛ bumo ŋ ki anya.

english_verse: Ezekiel, tell the people of Jerusalem and their ruler that I, the Lord God, am saying: Everything you do is wicked and shows how sinful you are. You are guilty and will be taken away as prisoners.
translation_verse: Amoso kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ e la fanɛ, ŋkpal menyi, Jerusalɛm be basa, nɛ menyi be ewura be alubi ka dii efuli ashi kusɔ kama nɛ menyee wora to so, meeŋ shin nɛ b pɛ menyi ŋ ki anya.

english_verse: And now, you evil and wicked ruler of Israel, your day of final punishment is almost here.
translation_verse: Fo, Israɛl be ewura lubi nɛ kumu kpakpaso wura ere, fo kasogberge be kachɛ maaŋ naŋ chɛr nseŋ fo.

english_verse: I, the Lord God, command you to take off your royal turban and your crown, because everything will be different. Those who had no power will be put in charge, and those who now rule will become nobodies.
translation_verse: Ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e naa kaŋɛ fo na fanɛ fo shɛŋi fo kumu so be neemu na nseŋ lara kuwurwuro na. Ŋkpal manɛ so, asheŋ maaŋ naa du kananɛ a daa du na. Esa nɛ e daa maŋ kɔ eyilikpa beeŋ nya eyilikpa nɛ emo nɛ e daa kɔ eyilikpa e paŋ mbe eyilikpa.

english_verse: I will leave Jerusalem in complete ruins like no one has ever seen until my chosen one comes to punish this city. Judgment against Ammon
translation_verse: Meeŋ shin nɛ kadegboŋ na e mur! Kumo alɛ maaŋ naŋ ki kade kikɛ n ya fo fanɛ esa nɛ k la mo peya na ka beeŋ ba, nɛ n ta kumo n sa mo.

english_verse: The Lord God said: Ezekiel, son of man, the Ammonites have insulted Israel, so condemn them and tell them I am saying: A sword is drawn, ready to slaughter; it is polished and prepared to kill as fast as lightning.
translation_verse: Ama fo, dimɛdi pibi, kaŋɛ fanɛ kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na bee kaŋɛ a laŋɛ Ammɔn be basa nɛ baa tege Israɛl na be kaplɛa so e la fanɛ b gberge tokobi m pe, n wora shiriya nɛ b mɔ; b fifɛa kumo so nna m bela ase nɛ b ta kumo m mɔ. K bee kpa edɛ fanɛ bɔrɛ ka nyɛkpɛ nna!

english_verse: You wicked Ammonites see false visions and believe untrue messages. But your day of punishment is coming soon, and my sword will slaughter you!
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛdare nɛ menyee ku na la efɛ nna, nɛ asheŋ nɛ men kpal n wu na kikɛ la kafulesheŋ. Menyi amu kpakpasowuraana nɛ basa lubi ere, menyi be kasogberge be kachɛ bee ba; tokobi na beeŋ gbelge menyi be abɔ so.

english_verse: Your days to punish others are over, so put your swords away. You will be punished in the land of your birth.
translation_verse: Amoso men bɛta menyi be tokobi n wɔtɔ kumo be efar to. Ŋkpal manɛ so jemanɛ nɛ menyee gberge basa kusoe fo ekar. Meeŋ ji menyi demu kakpa nɛ b kurge menyi, ashi men nanaana be kasawule so na.

english_verse: My furious anger will scorch you like fire, and I will hand you over to cruel men who are experts in killing.

translation_verse: Ŋkpal ŋ ka nya agbo n wɔtɔ fo so, meeŋ shin nɛ benapo na e kaa kagbene n tɔrɔ fo ga. Benapo na beeŋ ku fo kamuna nɛ asoe nseŋ mɔ fo mbia. Kashenteŋto, baaŋ suge fo mbia n yɔ n ya chɔɔ bumo m mɔ.

translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ jimaŋ na e kpa bumo ajembu nseŋ ta etokobi ŋ kɔ bumo, m mɔ bumo be mbia nseŋ chɔɔ bumo be nwu n lɛ.

english_verse: I will get rid of sinful prostitution in this country, so that women everywhere will be warned not to act as you have.
translation_verse: Meeŋ lara kusɔjigaya be kebaawɔtɔ kasawule na kikɛ so nɛ k baa la kusoe kpele n sa eche kikɛ nɛ b sa maaŋ naŋ ji kubojua nɛ kesakalea fanɛ kananɛ Ohola nɛ Oholiba wora na.

english_verse: You will be punished for becoming prostitutes and for worshiping idols. Then you will know that I am the Lord God.
translation_verse: Ama meeŋ gberge menyi beche anyɔ nɛ men la kenio pibi ere kusoe kenishipereso, ŋkpal menyi be kusɔ jigaya be kebaawɔtɔ nɛ kagbirshuŋ be kulubi so. Aloŋ nɛ menyeeŋ pin fanɛ ma, e la Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na.”

english_verse: Nine years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the tenth day of the tenth month. He said:
translation_verse: B ka daŋ pɛ anyi be galeŋga nɛ ewura Jehowachin kenya n yɔ Babilɔn be efuli so na be kafɛ kpanusopo na to be kufɔl kudusopo na be kachɛ kudusopo na, nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ ma le:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, write down today's date, because the king of Babylonia has just begun attacking the city of Jerusalem.
translation_verse: “Dimɛdi pibi, Ezikɛl, sibɛ kabre be kachɛ ere n nase, ŋkpal manɛ so, k la kachɛ nɛ Babilɔn be ewura kre kena m ba kulti Jerusalɛm n wɔtɔ a kɔ nna.

english_verse: Throw in the legs and shoulders of your finest sheep and put in the juicy bones.
translation_verse: Nseŋ ta eblaŋ na be alela fanɛ ebɛaŋ nɛ aba n wɔtɔ to. Bela awibi lela na gba n wɔtɔ nɛ k bɔlɔ.

english_verse: These words mean that Jerusalem is doomed! The city is filled with murderers and is like an old, rusty pot. The meat is taken out piece by piece, and no one cares what happens to it.
translation_verse: Kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na bee kaŋɛ e la fanɛ asheŋ maaŋ nyalɛ n sa Jerusalɛm be kadegboŋ nɛ kumo to be basa bee mɔ basa ere! K du fanɛ kadaŋɛ kreŋ so nɛ b maŋ naŋ fɔr kumo na nna. Baa lara eblaŋ na kukoko to nna nɛ esa kikɛ be shɛŋ maŋ wɔ kusɔ nɛ k bee wora na to.

english_verse: The people of Jerusalem murdered innocent people in the city and didn't even try to cover up the blood that flowed out on the hard ground.
translation_verse: Jerusalɛm to be basa mɔ basa nɛ b maŋ wora shɛŋ ashi kadegboŋ na to, ama b maŋ wora ania nɛ b wora eshishɛr m buu bumo be ŋklaŋ nɛ a wurge kefalta so gba.

english_verse: But I have seen that blood, and it cries out for me to take revenge.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ma alɛ gba yige ŋklaŋ na kefalta na so, kakpa nɛ a maaŋ tiŋ ŋ ŋana. Nɛ amo alɛ bee fin fanɛ ŋ kɔ n sa amo.”

english_verse: so bring more wood and light it. Cook the meat and boil away the broth to let the bones scorch.
translation_verse: Amoso kil ndibi damta m ba nseŋ foŋ edɛ na to n wɔtɔ! Daŋɛ eblaŋ na nɛnɛ nseŋ shin nɛ amo be epochu na a feeto nɛ awibi na a chɔɔ!

english_verse: Then set the empty pot over the hot coals until it is red-hot. That will clean the pot and burn off the rust.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ fo ta danyaŋ be kadaŋɛ fuloŋ na m bɛ ajanwulɛ so hale nɛ k ya bel m pere, saŋɛ na so kumo be kananɛ k kreŋ so na beeŋ chɔɔ m mur nɛ k naŋ nyalɛ so.

english_verse: I've tried everything else. Now the rust must be burned away.
translation_verse: Ama edɛ wuloŋ wuloŋ na gba kra maaŋ tiŋ n shin nɛ kumo be kekreŋso na kikɛ e lar kumo so.

english_verse: Jerusalem is so full of sin and evil that I can't get it clean, even though I have tried. It will stay filthy until I let loose my fierce anger against it.
translation_verse: Naniere fo, Jerusalɛm, be kusɔ jigaya be kebaawɔtɔ e shin nɛ fo wora eyurpi. Ŋkpal ŋ ka wora ania nɛ n fɔr fo so nɛ fo nyalɛ so nɛ fo kraa kini nsaa wɔ fo eyurpi to so, fo maaŋ naŋ nyalɛ so kikɛ n ya fo fanɛ ma agbo gboŋ ka beeŋ ba fo so.

english_verse: That time will certainly come! And when it does, I won't show the people of Jerusalem any pity or change my mind. They must be punished for the evil they have done. I, the Lord God, have spoken. Ezekiel's Wife Dies
translation_verse: Ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na e kaŋɛ na fanɛ saŋɛ fo nɛ n wora kusɔ nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ meeŋ wora na. M maaŋ kplaŋ fo lubi so ŋko n wu fo kuwɔr ŋko n chɛrga ma nfɛra. Meeŋ gberge fo kusoe ŋkpal kusɔ nɛ fo wora so.” Ezikɛl be eche be luwu be asheŋ

english_verse: “Ezekiel, son of man, I will suddenly take the life of the person you love most. But I don't want you to complain or cry.
translation_verse: “Dimɛdi pibi, Ezikɛl, kachɛ koŋwule meeŋ sɔ esa nɛ fee sha ga na be ŋkpa. Ama fo alɛ e sa maŋ kaŋ fubel m bile asheŋ ŋko n shu ŋko n shin nɛ anishichubi a lar fo anishito gba kuraa.

english_verse: Mourn in silence and don't show that you are grieving. Don't remove your turban or take off your sandals; don't cover your face to show your sorrow, or eat the food that mourners eat.”
translation_verse: Fo alɛ e sa maŋ shin nɛ esa e nu fo ka bee shuto gba. Sa maŋ kaŋ shɛŋi fo neemu fo kumu so ŋko n lara fo asɛbta nsaa na aya fuloŋ a ŋini fanɛ fee shu keeli nna. Fo alɛ e sa maŋ buu fo anishiakpa so ŋko n ji daŋkare be ajibi nɛ basa nɛ baa shu nli bee ji na.”

english_verse: One morning, I was talking with the people as usual, and by sunset my wife was dead. The next day I did what the Lord had told me,
translation_verse: Kachipurso be jemanɛ nɛ n yaŋ ya ka malga basa na kutɔ fanɛ kananɛ n chɛr a wora na. Kumo be kaaseso nɛ ma eche wu. Kumo be ŋklade nɛ n wora kananɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ ma na.

english_verse: and when people saw me, they asked, “Why aren't you mourning for your wife?”
translation_verse: Basa na ka wu ma nɛ b bishi ma le: “Manɛ nna nɛ fo maa shu fo eche be keeli?”

english_verse: Then you will do the same things I have done. You will leave your face uncovered and refuse to eat the food that mourners usually eat.
translation_verse: Saŋɛ na so nɛ menyi alɛ gba e wora kananɛ n wora ere. Menyi maaŋ ta asɔ m buu menyi be anishiakpaana so ŋko n ji daŋkare jibi nɛ basa nɛ baa shu nli bee ji na.

english_verse: I am a warning sign—everything I have done, you will also do. And then you will know the Lord God has made these things happen.
translation_verse: Saŋɛ na so nɛ ma, Ezikɛl e baa la tɔɔnɛ n sa menyi. Nɛ menyi alɛ gba e wora asheŋ nɛ n wora na kikɛ. Ndoŋ nɛ menyeeŋ pin fanɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e shin nɛ asheŋ ere kikɛ wora.”

english_verse: The Lord said, “Ezekiel, I will soon destroy the temple that makes everyone feel proud and safe, and I will take away their children as well.
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman, nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na naŋ kaŋɛ le: “Dimɛdi pibi, Ezikɛl, meeŋ mur bɔrɛlambu nɛ basa na be ŋgbene bee fuli so nɛ baa puchi kumo so nsaa sha kumo to be kebaayɔ ga na. Ma alɛ beeŋ lara bumo be mbia ashi bumo to.

english_verse: On that same day, someone will escape from the city and come to tell you what has happened.
translation_verse: Kachɛ nɛ loŋ beeŋ wora na kaŋ fo, esa nɛ e beeŋ nya n shile kadegboŋ na to e naŋ ba kaŋɛ fo kusɔ nɛ k wora.

english_verse: Then you will be able to speak again, and the two of you will talk. You will be a warning sign to the people, and they will know that I am the Lord.”
translation_verse: Loŋ be kachɛ na gbagba nɛ fo kɔnɔ beeŋ bugi nɛ fo nɛ esa nɛ e bar kubɔya na e malga abar kutɔ. Amoso feeŋ baa la tɔɔnɛ n sa basa na, nɛ b pin fanɛ ma e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.”

english_verse: Now I am going to let you be conquered by tribes from the eastern desert. They will set up their camps in your land and eat your fruit and drink your milk.
translation_verse: Meeŋ shin nɛ eyiriana nɛ b wɔ keshishɛrsawule nɛ k wɔ epeŋilarkpa be kaba so na e ba kɔ m pɔɔ menyi so. Baaŋ ba yuu bumo be ewajɛbu n chena menyi be efuli so n ji kumo be asɔrso nseŋ nuu kumo be kenyipo nɛ a daga menyi na.

english_verse: Your capital city of Rabbah will be nothing but pastureland for camels, and the rest of the country will be pastures for sheep. Then you will know that I am the Lord God.
translation_verse: Ade be kaman, meeŋ naŋ shin nɛ menyi be kadegboŋ nɛ baa tre Rabba na a ki enyɔma be ejikpa nɛ Ammɔn be efuli so kikɛ malɛ a ki kakpa nɛ baŋ baa bela mbolpɔ. Loŋ nɛ menyeeŋ pin fanɛ ma e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.

english_verse: And so I will hand you over to enemies who will rob you. I will completely destroy you. There won't be enough of your people left to be a nation ever again, and you will know that I, the Lord, have done these things. Judgment on Moab
translation_verse: Amoso meeŋ ta menyi m bɔɔ efuli pɔtɛana be basa enɔ nɛ b suge menyi be asɔ nseŋ sesaŋ menyi to. Ma alɛ beeŋ mur menyi kuraa nɛ men maaŋ naa la efuli a kɔ menyi gbagba be kasawule a wɔtɔ. Ndoŋ nɛ menyeeŋ pin fanɛ ma, e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.” Mowab be kaplɛa so be kewuŋkaŋɛ be asheŋ

english_verse: So I will let Moab's fortress towns along its border be attacked, including Beth-Jeshimoth, Baal-Meon, and Kiriathaim.
translation_verse: Amoso meeŋ shin nɛ kena e ba ndegboŋ nɛ a bee kuŋ Mowab be efuli be egbaŋ na nɛ ndegboŋ lela fanɛ Bɛf Jeshimɔf nɛ Baal Mɛɔn nɛ Kiriyateem gba na so.

english_verse: Moab will be punished. Then the people there will know that I am the Lord.” Judgment on Edom
translation_verse: aloŋ nɛ meeŋ gberge Mowab be basa gba kusoe, nɛ b pin fanɛ ma, e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.” Edɔm be Kaplɛa so be kewuŋkaŋɛ be asheŋ

english_verse: The Lord God then said, “The people of Edom are guilty of taking revenge on Judah.
translation_verse: Ade be kaman, nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na naŋ kaŋɛ le: “Edɔm be efuli so be basa wora n jija ŋkpal b ka daŋ wora n tal Juda be basa to so.

english_verse: So I will punish Edom by killing all its people and livestock. It will be an empty wasteland all the way from Teman to Dedan.
translation_verse: Amoso meeŋ gberge Edɔm be basa kusoe nseŋ mɔ bumo be basa nɛ asɔbɔya kikɛ kena to nɛ kasawule nɛ k yili kadegboŋ nɛ baa tre Tɛman n dese n ya fo kumo nɛ baa tre Dedan na e dese jiga.

english_verse: I will send my own people to take revenge on the Edomites by making them feel my fierce anger. And when I punish them, they will know that I am the Lord God.” Judgment on Philistia
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ n shin nɛ ma basa Israɛlebi na e wora n tal Edɔm be basa to, nɛ b pin kananɛ kanya agbo gboŋ du. Ŋ kaŋ gberge Edɔm be basa kusoe na, nɛ baaŋ pin fanɛ ma, e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.” Filistiebi be Kaplɛa so be kewuŋkaŋɛ be asheŋ

english_verse: The Lord God said, “The cruel Philistines have taken revenge on their enemies over and over and have tried to destroy them.
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman, nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ le: “Filisti be efuli so be basa nyaŋnyaŋso na daŋ wora n tal bumo be dra dra be bedoŋana to nna a fin kemur bumo yurkishi so.

english_verse: Now it's my turn to treat the Philistines as my enemies and to kill everyone living in their towns along the seacoast.
translation_verse: Amoso meeŋ gberge Filisti be basa na kusoe m mɔ bumo. Ma alɛ beeŋ mur bumo be bekama nɛ b ka a wɔ teku ase be nde to na.

english_verse: In my fierce anger, I will take revenge on them. And when I punish them, they will know that I am the Lord.”
translation_verse: Meeŋ gberge bumo kusoe kenishipereso nseŋ wora n tal bumo to nɛ b pin kananɛ ma agbo gboŋ du nɛ b pin fanɛ ma, e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.”

english_verse: Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the month. He said:
translation_verse: B ka pɛ ewura Jehowachin nɛ anyi be galeŋga kenya n yɔ Babilɔn be efuli so na be kafɛ kudukakosopo na to be kufɔl na be kachɛ juŋkparso na nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ ma le:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, the people of the city of Tyre have celebrated Jerusalem's defeat by singing, “Jerusalem has fallen! It used to be powerful, a center of trade. Now the city is shattered, and we will take its place.”
translation_verse: “Dimɛdi pibi, Ezikɛl, kadegboŋ nɛ baa tre Tayɛ na be basa daŋ ji eyur nna nseŋ boŋ kashɛ ere ŋkpal Jerusalɛm ka daŋ kɔ n tɔr so: ‘Jerusalɛm bure n tɔr! Nɛ kumo be yawu be keji be eleŋ loge! Amoso k maaŋ naa kɔ anyi kukɔrkɔ ŋkpal yawu be keji so!’

english_verse: Because the people of Tyre have sung that song, I have the following warning for them: I am the Lord God, and I am now your enemy! I will send nations to attack you, like waves crashing against the shore.
translation_verse: Kusɔ nɛ ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na bee kaŋɛ e la fanɛ menyi Tayɛ be basa ki n doŋana nna na, nɛ meeŋ shin nɛ efuli damtaana e kre kena m ba kɔ menyi fanɛ kananɛ teku so bee ku atili a ba kaa gbuŋ teku be kɔnɔ na.

english_verse: They will tear down your city walls and defense towers. I will sweep away the ruins until all that's left of you is a bare rock,
translation_verse: Baaŋ bure egbalana nɛ men pɔr ŋ kulti menyi be kadegboŋ na nɛ menyi be ebu jeŋgreŋana nɛ menyee yili so a wu kufɔ na. Kumo be kaman nɛ ŋ gbare kumo be shishɛr na n lɛ nseŋ ka kefalta fuloŋ n nase.

english_verse: and that the people who live in your towns along the coast will be killed. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: nseŋ mɔ basa kama nɛ chena nde nɛ a wɔ teku ase na kikɛ. Ndoŋ nɛ Tayɛ be basa beeŋ pin fanɛ ma, e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.”

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia is the world's most powerful king, and I will send him to attack you. He will march from the north with a powerful army, including horses and chariots and cavalry troops.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman, nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na naŋ kaŋɛ: “Meeŋ shin nɛ Babilɔn be ewura Nebukadneeza, nɛ e la bewura to be ewura na, e shi kelargato be esoso be kaba so m ba kɔ Tayɛ be basa. E beeŋ keta benapo damta nɛ b kɔ egbaŋɛ nɛ egbaŋɛturko nɛ egbaŋɛ diipoana nna m ba.

english_verse: First, he will attack your towns along the coast and kill the people who live there. Then he will build dirt ramps up to the top of your city walls and set up rows of shields around you.
translation_verse: E beeŋ juŋkpar ŋ kɔ basa nɛ b chena teku ase na m mɔ bumo. Kumo be kaman nɛ e gbare eshishɛr n deŋi abar so nɛ a fo menyi be ndeana na be egbalana be esoso nɛ mbe benapo e keta bumo be abɛlso be asɔ kuŋamuso m bɛ abar so ŋ kulti menyi n wɔtɔ fanɛ egbal lempo na.

english_verse: He will command some of his troops to use large wooden poles to beat down your walls, while others use iron rods to knock down your watchtowers.
translation_verse: Ade be kaman nɛ mbe benapo na e ta ndibi gbɛgbɛso n da egbalana na n lɛ nseŋ ta akɔsɔ m bure m bure menyi be ebu jeŋgreŋana nɛ menyee yili so a keni a wu kufɔ na.

english_verse: He will have so many horses that the dust they stir up will seem like a thick fog. And as his chariots and cavalry approach, even the walls will shake, especially when he proudly enters your ruined city.
translation_verse: Mbe egbaŋɛ be keshi ga so amo be kalabɛr beeŋ buu menyi so fanɛ kunyɔlɔ na. Benapo na kaa luri menyi be ndeana to, bumo be egbaŋɛ nɛ egbaŋɛturko wurbi nɛ agboŋi kikɛ be egbri beeŋ shin nɛ menyi be ebuana be egbalana a gbuŋgbuŋ fɔŋfɔŋ saŋɛ nɛ b wɔ men be nde nɛ b bure na to na.

english_verse: His troops will ride through your streets, killing people left and right, and your strong columns will crumble to the ground.
translation_verse: Mbe benapo beeŋ dii bumo be egbaŋɛ n sɔ menyi be agbembi kikɛ so n ta etokobi a mɔ menyi be basa bena nɛ jiso, nɛ menyi be eshabɔrɛ lempo kikɛ a bure n tɔr kasawule.

english_verse: The troops will steal your valuable possessions; they will break down your walls, and crush your expensive houses. Then the stones and wood and all the remains will be dumped into the sea.
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman, baaŋ suge menyi be kedama nɛ menyi be asɔ faso. Bumo alɛ beeŋ bure menyi be egbalana nɛ menyi be nwu lela kikɛ nseŋ gbare ajembu na nɛ ndibi na nɛ eshishɛr na n ya lɛ teku to.

english_verse: because I will turn you into a bare rock where fishermen can dry their nets. And you will never rebuild your city. I, the Lord God, make this promise.
translation_verse: Ma alɛ beeŋ shin nɛ menyi be kasawule na a dese fanɛ kefalta fuloŋ nɛ ekɔrɔtɔ pɛpo e baa fata bumo be ashewu kumo so. Menyi maaŋ naŋ tiŋ n lɔŋɛ m pɔr menyi be kadegboŋ na kikɛ. Ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na e kaŋɛ na.”

english_verse: The people of the nations up and down the coast will shudder when they hear your screams and moans of death.
translation_verse: Kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na naŋ kaŋɛ Tayɛ be basa e la fanɛ basa nɛ b chena teku ase na kaŋ nu menyi be basa nɛ baa mɔ na be kushu kufu beeŋ pɛ bumo nɛ b baa chicha.

english_verse: The kings will step down from their thrones, then take off their royal robes and fancy clothes, and sit on the ground, trembling. They will be so shocked at the news of your defeat that they will shake in fear
translation_verse: Saŋɛ na so nɛ bekama nɛ baa ji kuwura efuliana nɛ a chena m mata teku ase na e gbelge bumo be nwurputi so. Kumo be kaman nɛ b gbaŋ bumo be bewura be epiŋiana nɛ bumo be asɔbuuso nɛ b jɔɔ amo na kikɛ nseŋ chena kasawule a chicha. Ŋkpal kusɔ nɛ k beeŋ tu menyi na so, kufu beeŋ pɛ bumo ga hale nɛ b maŋ tiŋ n yige kebaachicha.

english_verse: But now Tyre is in ruins, and the people on the coast stare at it in horror and tremble in fear.”
translation_verse: Kachɛ nɛ k tɔr na ka fo, basa nɛ b chena teku ase na bee chicha nna. Nɛ kumo be kemur na chinchiŋ bumo ga.

english_verse: and carry you down to the world of the dead, where you will join people of ancient times and towns ruined long ago. You will stay there and never again be a city filled with people.
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman, nɛ n shin nɛ men wu n yɔ bubuni to n ya tu bumo nɛ b juŋkpar n yɔ ndoŋ na nɛ nde nɛ a daŋ mur dra dra na kikɛ na. Menyeeŋ ya kaa wɔ bubuni to nɛ esa maaŋ naŋ sɔ menyi so n chena menyi be ndegboŋana to.

english_verse: You will die a horrible death! People will come looking for your city, but it will never be found. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Meeŋ shin nɛ men be kebaa maaŋ naa wɔtɔ na e baa la tɔɔnɛ nɛ k bee ta kufu a pɛ basa. Basa beeŋ fin menyi, ama b maŋ naŋ wu menyi.” Ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na e kaŋɛ na.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, sing a funeral song for Tyre,
translation_verse: “Dimɛdi pibi, Ezikɛl, boŋ keeli be kashɛ ere a laŋɛ Tayɛ nɛ k la

english_verse: the city that is built along the sea and that trades with nations along the coast. Tell the people of Tyre that the following message is from me: Tyre, you brag about your perfect beauty,
translation_verse: kadegboŋ nɛ k chena m mata teku ase nsaa tu basa nɛ b chena teku ase nɛ mboŋ damta a ji yawu na be kaplɛa so. Kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na bee kaŋɛ a laŋɛ Tayɛ be kaplɛa so e la fanɛ Tayɛ, fee puchi ŋkpal kananɛ fo walɛ kebita ga so nna.

english_verse: and your control of the sea. You are a ship built to perfection.
translation_verse: Teku kulti fo echenakpa nna n wɔtɔ. B pɔr fo, fanɛ nchu so be kuloŋ lela nna;

english_verse: Oak trees from Bashan were shaped into oars; pine trees from Cyprus were cut for your deck, which was then decorated with strips of ivory.
translation_verse: Kedibi gboŋgboŋi nɛ b ku ashi Bashan be efuli so n shɛl ebaŋɛ; Ndibi kpakpaso fanɛ chɛchɛdibi nɛ b ku ashi Saiprus be efuli so n wora fo kaseto Nseŋ baŋɛ ejebotenyi n fɛga n fɛga amo to nɛ a baa walɛ.

english_verse: Men from Sidon and Arvad did the rowing, and your own skilled workers were the captains.
translation_verse: Basa nɛ baa far fo na shi Sidɔn nɛ Aavad be ndegboŋ to nna. Fo basa nɛ b nyi nchu to e la bumo be benimu.

english_verse: Your guards came from Arvad and Cilicia, and men from Gamad stood watch in your towers. With their weapons hung on your walls, your beauty was complete.
translation_verse: Benapo nɛ b shi Aavad e daa kuŋ fo egbalana nɛ bumo nɛ b shi Gamad malɛ daa kuŋ fo ebu jeŋgreŋana na nsaa ta bumo be abɛlso be asɔ kuŋamuso a shiga egbalana so nɛ k shin nɛ fo nyalɛ kebita.

english_verse: You also did business with people from Rhodes, and people from nations along the coast gave you ivory and ebony in exchange for your goods.
translation_verse: Roodis be efuli so be basa gba daŋ tu fo n ji yawu nɛ basa nɛ b chena teku be ekarso be efuli damtaana ta ejebotenyi nɛ ndibi lembir lela ga n chɛr fo asɔ.

english_verse: Judah and Israel gave you their finest wheat, fancy figs, honey, olive oil, and spices in exchange for your merchandise.
translation_verse: Juda nɛ Israɛl be basa gba daŋ ta ayu nɛ mushoŋ nɛ ɔlif be ŋku nɛ eposɔ ŋ ka fo asɔ faso be kukɔ.

english_verse: The people of Damascus saw what you had to offer and brought you wine from Helbon and wool from Zahar.
translation_verse: Damaskɔs be basa daŋ wu asɔ damta be yiri yiri nɛ fee fa na, nɛ b shi Hɛlbɔn m bar yabra belbelso nseŋ naŋ shi Zaha m bar mbolpɔ be afuibi m ba tɔ amo.

english_verse: The people of Dedan supplied you with saddle blankets,
translation_verse: Dedan be basa gba daŋ ta ata nɛ baa ta a wora egaare na n tɔ fo asɔ.

english_verse: while people from Arabia and the rulers of Kedar traded lambs, sheep, and goats.
translation_verse: Nɛ Areebia be efuli so be basa nɛ Kɛda be efuli so be bewura gba ta mbolpɔfɔlbi nɛ mbolpɔ nɛ mboe m ba tɔ fo asɔ faso.

english_verse: Merchants from Sheba and Raamah gave you excellent spices, precious stones, and gold in exchange for your products.
translation_verse: Nɛ Shiba nɛ Raama be eyawujipo gba ta yawu kpakpaso be ajembu nɛ baa ta a wora abitasɔ nɛ shuwa nɛ asɔ dufɛso lela ga m ba tu fo n ji yawu.

english_verse: You also did business with merchants from the cities of Haran, Canneh, Eden, Sheba, Asshur, and Chilmad,
translation_verse: Ndegboŋ fanɛ Haran nɛ Kanne nɛ Iden nɛ Asshɔ nɛ Chilmad nɛ Shiba be efuli so be eyawujipo kikɛ daŋ ba tu fo n ji yawu.

english_verse: and sailing across the sea, but you were wrecked by strong eastern winds.
translation_verse: Jemanɛ nɛ fo befarpo far fo n lar teku so na, nɛ afugboŋ shi epeŋilarkpa m ba mur fo.

english_verse: The shouts of your drowning crew were heard on the shore.
translation_verse: nɛ basa nɛ baa ji nchu na boŋ to nɛ basa nɛ b wɔ kedeŋi so nu kumo.

english_verse: Every ship is deserted; rowers and sailors and captains all stand on shore,
translation_verse: Naniere bekama beeŋ shile ŋ ka ekuloŋ nawule, Nɛ efarpo kama e dii kedeŋi so.

english_verse: mourning for you. They show their sorrow by putting dust on their heads and rolling in ashes;
translation_verse: Bumo kikɛ beeŋ shu kagbenejijaso ŋkpal fo so, Baaŋ wora eshishɛr n wurge bumo be amu so nseŋ dese nsunɔ to a melti.

english_verse: In their grief they sing a funeral song for you: “Tyre, you were greater than all other cities. But now you lie in silence at the bottom of the sea.
translation_verse: Baaŋ boŋ awɔba n shu ŋ kaŋɛ le: ‘Wanɛ nɛ anyeeŋ ta ŋ keshɛr Tayɛ so, Tayɛ nɛ e dese teku to shruum le ere?

english_verse: “Nations that received your merchandise were always pleased; kings everywhere got rich from your costly goods.
translation_verse: Jemanɛ kama nɛ fo yɛr fo asɔ faso efuli pɔtɛ so, Efuli kama so ebi bee nya bumo be kepar nna. Bewura bɔla fo asɔ lela so N dii kedama.

english_verse: People living along the coast are shocked at the news. Their rulers are horrified, and terror is written across their faces.
translation_verse: Kusɔ nɛ k wora fo na be asheŋ mɔ ekama nɛ e chena teku ase na kɔnɔ. Hale kufu pɛ bumo be bewura gba nɛ baa chicha

english_verse: The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ ma le:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the king of Tyre that I am saying: You are so arrogant that you think you're a god and that the city of Tyre is your throne. You may claim to be a god, though you're nothing but a mere human.
translation_verse: Dimɛdi pibi, Ezikɛl, kaŋɛ Tayɛ be ewura kusɔ nɛ ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na bee kaŋɛ mo. Kamoowu shin nɛ fee fɛ fanɛ fo la kegbir nna nsaa kaŋɛ fanɛ fo ka la kegbir so nɛ fo chena kuwurputi so nɛ eteku kulti fo n wɔtɔ. Feeŋ tiŋ n ta fo kumu fanɛ kegbir e la fo, ama dimɛdi e la fo, mannɛ kegbir.

english_verse: Your wisdom has certainly made you rich, because you have storehouses filled with gold and silver.
translation_verse: Fo yɛ fo kanyiasheŋ nɛ kashennyi e shin nɛ fo dii kedama nseŋ nya shuwa nɛ gbiti m bɔlɔ ebu na.

english_verse: You compared yourself to a god, so now I, the Lord God,
translation_verse: “To, naniere kusɔ nɛ ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na bee kaŋɛ nde. Ŋkpal fo ka bee fɛ fanɛ fo nyi asheŋ fanɛ kegbir so,

english_verse: will make you the victim of cruel enemies. They will destroy all the possessions you've worked so hard to get.
translation_verse: meeŋ shin nɛ bedoŋ nɛ b maŋ kɔ kushuso e ba kɔ fo. Baaŋ mur asɔ lela nɛ fo bɔla kanyiasheŋ nɛ kashennyi so n nya na kikɛ kuraa.

english_verse: Your enemies will brutally kill you, and the sea will be your only grave.
translation_verse: Bumo alɛ beeŋ mɔ fo nseŋ ta fo n lɛ teku to nɛ k ki fo nchaŋ.

english_verse: When you face your enemies, will you still claim to be a god? They will attack, and you will suffer like any other human.
translation_verse: Jemanɛ nɛ baaŋ ba mɔ fo na, fo kraa beeŋ baa fɛ fanɛ kegbir e la fo a? Jemanɛ nɛ feeŋ yili fo bemɔpo be anishito na, dimɛdi e naaŋ baa la fo mannɛ kegbir.

english_verse: Foreigners will kill you, and you will die the death of those who don't worship me. I, the Lord, have spoken. A Funeral Song for the King of Tyre
translation_verse: Befɔ beeŋ mɔ fo, nɛ fo wu fanɛ bumo nɛ b maa shuŋ ma na. Ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na e kaŋɛ na.” Kananɛ Tayɛ be ewura loge to be asheŋ

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, sing a funeral song for the king of Tyre and tell him I am saying: At one time, you were perfect, intelligent, and good-looking.
translation_verse: “Dimɛdi pibi, boŋ awɔba n sa Tayɛ be ewura, nseŋ kaŋɛ mo kusɔ nɛ ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na bee kaŋɛ na fanɛ, jemanɛ ko fo kusɔ kama daa bɛ abar so dede nna nsaa la tɔɔnɛ. Fo alɛ daa nyi asheŋ ga nseŋ daa walɛ keyɛrbi nna.

english_verse: You lived in the garden of Eden and wore jewelry made of brightly colored gems and precious stones. They were all set in gold and were ready for you on the day you were born.
translation_verse: K daa du fanɛ Ebɔrɛ be kudɔbi nɛ baa tre Iden na to nɛ fo daa wɔ. Yawu kpakpaso be asɔ lela nyɛkpɛso be yiri yiri fanɛ shuwa be abitasɔ nɛ fo daa ta a mɛa to. Kachɛ nɛ b kurge fo na nɛ b bela amo kikɛ ase n sa fo.

english_verse: I appointed a winged creature to guard your home on my holy mountain, where you walked among gems that dazzled like fire.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ n shin nɛ malaika bee kuŋ fo kowu jemanɛ nɛ fo daa na ajembu nyɛkpɛso to ashi ma kebee cheembi na so na.

english_verse: You were truly good from the time of your birth, but later you started doing wicked things.
translation_verse: Yili kachɛ nɛ b kurge fo kikɛ, fo kasheŋwora daa walɛ nna ga n ya fo saŋɛ nɛ fo fara a asheŋ lubi be kewora.

english_verse: You traded with other nations and became more and more cruel and evil. So I forced you to leave my mountain, and the creature that had been your protector now chased you away from the jewels.
translation_verse: Fo daŋ pere kenishi nna n wɔtɔ yawu be keji to nɛ k shin nɛ fo luri keŋkenshi nɛ alubi be kebaawɔtɔ to. Amoso nɛ n tintiŋ fo nɛ fo lar ma kebee cheembi na so nɛ malaika nɛ e daa kuŋ fo na ju fo ashi ajembu nyɛkpɛso na so na.

english_verse: It was your good looks that made you arrogant, and you were so famous that you started acting like a fool. That's why I threw you to the ground and let other kings sneer at you.
translation_verse: Fo ka daa walɛ keyɛrbi so, fo daa wu fo kumu nna. Fo ketre ka dii so fo daa wora asheŋ nna fanɛ ewulpo. Amoso nɛ n lara fo n lɛ kasawule so nɛ bewura pɔtɛ e wu kusɔ nɛ n wora fo na nɛ k baa la kusoe kpele n sa bumo.

english_verse: You have cheated so many other merchants that your places of worship are corrupt. So I set your city on fire and burned it down. Now everyone sees only ashes where your city once stood,
translation_verse: Fo alɛ daŋ wora alubi nna ga ashi fo yawu be keji to hale nɛ fo kabɔrɛshuŋakpa ki asheŋ lubi be mboŋ. Amoso nɛ n shin nɛ edɛ chɔɔ fo kadegboŋ na m mur na. Naniere nsunɔ nawule nɛ ekama bee wu kakpa nɛ fo kadegboŋ na daa wɔ na.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the city of Sidon
translation_verse: “Dimɛdi pibi, kaŋɛ kadegboŋ nɛ baa tre Sidɔn na fanɛ k maŋ wora n nyalɛ.

english_verse: I will send deadly diseases to wipe you out, and I will send enemies to invade and surround you. Your people will be killed, and you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Meeŋ shin nɛ alɔ mɔso e ba menyi so nseŋ shin nɛ bedoŋ e ba kɔ menyi kaba kama so m mɔ menyi be basa. Ndoŋ nɛ menyeeŋ pin fanɛ ma e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.” Israɛl ka beeŋ nya nɛfa be asheŋ

english_verse: When that happens, the people of Israel will no longer have cruel neighbors that abuse them and make them feel as though they are in a field of thorns and briers. And the Israelites will know that I, the Lord God, have done these things. A Blessing for Israel
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman, nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na naŋ kaŋɛ le: “Efuliana nɛ a kulti Israɛl be basa n wɔtɔ a keni bumo jiga nsaa tege bumo na be kekama maaŋ naa la fanɛ ewi ŋko gɔŋnyaŋɛ a tɔrɔ Israɛl be basa. Ndoŋ nɛ baaŋ pin fanɛ ma, e la Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na.”

english_verse: The Lord God said: Someday I will gather the people of Israel from the nations where they are now scattered, and every nation will see that I am holy. The Israelites will once again live in the land I gave to my servant Jacob.
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na naŋ kaŋɛ le: “Meeŋ bɛta Israɛl be basa na n shi efuliana nɛ n daŋ pesaŋ bumo to n yɔ na m ba nɛ efuliana na kikɛ e pin fanɛ n du cheembi nna. Israɛl be basa na beeŋ naŋ ba chena bumo gbagba be kasawule so, kumo nɛ n ta n sa ma kayɛrbi Jeekɔb dra dra na.

english_verse: They will be safe and will build houses and plant vineyards. They will no longer be in danger, because I will punish their hateful neighbors. Israel will know that I am the Lord their God.
translation_verse: Baaŋ chena ndoŋ kayurwushi so m pɔr nwu nseŋ naŋ nase ndibisɔrso be adɔ. Ma alɛ beeŋ gberge bumo be bechenashapoana nɛ b keni bumo jiga na kusoe nɛ Israɛl be basa na e nya bumo be amu a wɔtɔ. Ndoŋ nɛ baaŋ pin fanɛ ma e la Enyɛnpe bumo be Ebɔrɛ na.”

english_verse: Ten years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the twelfth day of the tenth month. He said:
translation_verse: B ka pɛ anyi be beko nɛ ewura Jehowachin n yɔ kenyaya to ashi Babilɔn be efuli so na be kafɛ kudusopo na to be kufɔl kudusopo na be kachɛ kudu anyɔsopo na nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ ma le.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the king of Egypt. Tell him and his people
translation_verse: “Dimɛdi pibi, Ezikɛl, malga ŋ gbiti Ijipt be ewura, Fɛɛro, ŋ kaŋɛ mo kananɛ mo nɛ Ijipt be kasawule so be basa kikɛ beeŋ nya kasogberge be asheŋ.

english_verse: that I am saying: King of Egypt, you were like a giant crocodile lying in a river. You acted as though you owned the Nile and made it for yourself. But now I, the Lord God, am your enemy!
translation_verse: Kaŋɛ Ijipt be ewura fanɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na bee kaŋɛ fanɛ, fo ki n doŋ nna ŋkpal fo ka ta fo kumu fanɛ laŋchaŋ nɛ e kɔ eleŋ a wɔ lɔr to na so. Fo alɛ naŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ feeto lɔrgboŋ nɛ baa tre Nail na a ki feya.

english_verse: I will put a hook in your jaw and pull you out of the water, and all the fish in your river will stick to your scaly body.
translation_verse: Amoso meeŋ shin nɛ dariwa e kɔl fo ŋgbuŋ to nɛ ekɔrɔtɔ nɛ a wɔ lɔr na to e mata fo so nɛ ŋ gberge fo n lar Nail be lɔr na to.

english_verse: I'll throw you and the fish into the desert, and your body will fall on the hard ground. You will be left unburied, and wild animals and birds will eat your flesh.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ n ta fo nɛ ekɔrɔtɔ nɛ a mata fo so na kikɛ n lɛ keshishɛrsawule so nɛ fo ya dese ndoŋ a maaŋ nya kepuli. Meeŋ shin nɛ mbuibi nɛ asɔbɔya e ji fo.

english_verse: When they reached out to you for support, you broke in half, cutting their arms and making them fall.
translation_verse: B ka yirgi menyi so nɛ men bu n da bumo be aba to m bɔl n shin nɛ bumo be ketetowibi shege ŋko ŋ kpekpel.

english_verse: So I, the Lord God, will send troops to attack you, king of Egypt. They will kill your people and livestock,
translation_verse: Amoso, ma Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na e naa kaŋɛ menyi naniere na fanɛ meeŋ shin nɛ benapo e ba kɔ menyi kena nseŋ mɔ menyi be basa nɛ asɔbɔya kikɛ.

english_verse: until your land is a barren desert. Then you will know that I have done these things. You claimed that you made the Nile River and control it.
translation_verse: Nɛ Ijipt be efuli na a ki kasawule jiga nɛ shɛŋ maŋ naa wɔ kumo so a dese. Ndoŋ nɛ menyeeŋ pin fanɛ ma e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na. Ŋkpal fo ka kaŋɛ fanɛ feeto Nail be lɔr na a ki feya so,

english_verse: Now I am turning against you and your river. Your nation will be nothing but an empty wasteland all the way from the town of Migdol in the north to Aswan in the south, and as far as the border of Ethiopia.
translation_verse: fo nɛ Nail kikɛ ki n doŋ nna na. Amoso meeŋ shin nɛ Ijipt be efuli na a ki kasawule jiga nɛ shɛŋ maaŋ naa wɔ kumo so, yili kadegboŋ nɛ baa tre Migdɔl nɛ k wɔ kelargato be esoso na n ya fo kumo nɛ baa tre Aswan ashi kelargato be kaseto na, hale ŋ keta m ba choŋ menyi nɛ Kush be efuli so be egbaŋ to.

english_verse: No human or animal will even dare travel through Egypt, because no sign of life will be found there for
translation_verse: Dimɛdi ŋko kusɔbɔya kikɛ maaŋ naŋ bɔla kasawule na so n choŋ kikɛ. Nfɛ adena nɛ shɛŋ maŋ naa wɔ kumo so.

english_verse: They will once again live in their homeland in southern Egypt. But they will be a weak kingdom
translation_verse: chena Ijipt be kasawule so be kelargato be kaseto, nɛ k la bumo be echenakpa gbagba na. Ama bumo alɛ beeŋ baa la basa pɔso ndoŋ nna.

english_verse: My own people Israel will never again depend on your nation. In fact, when the Israelites remember what happened to you Egyptians, they will realize how wrong they were to turn to you for help. Then the Israelites will know that I, the Lord God, did these things. King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia Will Conquer Egypt
translation_verse: Israɛl be basa malɛ maaŋ naŋ ta bumo be amu n to Ijiptebi so a fin kechɛto. Kusɔ nɛ k beeŋ tu Ijipt be basa na beeŋ shin nɛ Israɛlebi na e nyiŋi fanɛ kedaa maŋ daga fanɛ b ta bumo be amu n to Ijipt so nseŋ pin fanɛ ma e la Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na.” Ewurgboŋ Nebukadneeza ka beeŋ pɔɔ Ijipt so be asheŋ

english_verse: Twenty-seven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the first month. He said:
translation_verse: B ka pɛ ewura Jehowachin nɛ anyi be beko n yɔ Babilɔn be efuli so kenyaya to na be kafɛ adunyɔ nɛ ashunusopo na to be kufɔl sososo na be kachɛ sososo na nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na naŋ kaŋɛ ma le:

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia has attacked the city of Tyre. He forced his soldiers to carry so many heavy loads that their heads were rubbed bald, and their shoulders were red and sore. Nebuchadnezzar and his army still could not capture the city.
translation_verse: “Dimɛdi pibi, Babilɔn be ewurgboŋ Nebukadneeza daŋ kre n ya kɔ Tayɛ be basa kena. Mo alɛ daŋ sulɔ mbe benapo esulɔ gbɛgbɛso nna hale nɛ bumo be amu kpra nɛ bumo be abatimu pɛge, ama ewura na nɛ mbe benapo kikɛ maŋ nya bumo be kegben be tɔnɔ ashi kena na to.

english_verse: So now I will hand over the nation of Egypt to him. He will take Egypt's valuable treasures and give them to his own troops.
translation_verse: Amoso kusɔ nɛ ma Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na bee kaŋɛ nde e la fanɛ: Meeŋ ta Ijipt be kasawule n sa ewurgboŋ Nebukadneeza nɛ e kɔ n suge bumo be asɔ nseŋ sulɔ Ijipt be efuli so be mpetɛsɔ lela n yɔ nɛ a ki mbe benapo be kakɔka.

english_verse: Egypt will be his reward, because he and his army have been following my orders. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal manɛ so, ewura na nɛ mbe benapo kikɛ daa shuŋ nna a sa ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na.

english_verse: Ezekiel, when Egypt is defeated, I will make the people of Israel strong, and I will give you the power to speak to them. Then they will know that I, the Lord, have done these things.
translation_verse: Nɛ kumo be loŋ kaŋ wora, meeŋ shin nɛ Israɛl be basa e nya eleŋ, nɛ fo, Ezikɛl, e yili kakpa nɛ ekama beeŋ nu fo ebɔl nseŋ malga, saŋɛ na so baaŋ pin fanɛ ma e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Egypt that I am saying: Cry out in despair,
translation_verse: “Dimɛdi pibi, Ezikɛl, kaŋɛ kusɔ nɛ ma Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na bee malga ere. A daga fanɛ fo kaŋɛ amo awɔrso fanɛ Kachɛ lubi lubi bee ba!

english_verse: because you will soon be punished! That will be a time of darkness and doom for all nations.
translation_verse: Kachɛ na taga to, kachɛ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na beeŋ gberge fo kusoe na fo nna na, K la kemur nɛ etɔrɔ be kachɛ nna n sa efuliana na.

english_verse: Your own nation of Egypt will be attacked, and Ethiopia will suffer. You will be killed in battle, and your land will be robbed and left in ruins.
translation_verse: Kena beeŋ ku Ijipt be efuli so; Nɛ kagbenejija damta e tɔr Itiopia be basa so. Basa damta beeŋ wu ashi Ijipt to; Nɛ b suge efuli na so be asɔ kikɛ Nseŋ ka kumo kelambure n nase.

english_verse: Soldiers hired from Ethiopia, Libya, Lydia, Arabia, Kub, as well as from Israel, will die in that battle.
translation_verse: Benapo nɛ b ya haya ashi Itiopia nɛ Libiya nɛ Lidiya n Areebia nɛ Kub be efuliana so na nɛ ma basa gbagba to be basa damta beeŋ wu kena na to.”

english_verse: Your nation of Egypt will be the most deserted place on earth, and its cities will lie in complete ruin.
translation_verse: Ijipt be efuli na beeŋ ki kakpa fuloŋ nɛ ekama kini ashi durnya kikɛ to nɛ kumo be ndegboŋ a ki nde bureso a dese.

english_verse: I will set fire to your land, and anyone who defended your nation will die. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Ŋ kaŋ shin nɛ edɛ ji Ijipt be efuli nɛ kumo be basa nɛ baa kɔ a kuŋ kumo na nɛ baaŋ pin fanɛ ma e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.

english_verse: On the same day I destroy Egypt, I will send messengers to the Ethiopians to announce their coming destruction. They think they are safe, but they will be terrified.
translation_verse: Kachɛ nɛ Ijipt beeŋ mur na, meeŋ shuŋi mbɔ nɛ b ta nchu so be ekuloŋgboŋ m ba bɔ Itiopia be basa nɛ b maa fɛ shɛŋ be asheŋ na kubɔya a laŋɛ kemur nɛ k bee ba bumo alɛ gba so be kaplɛa so nɛ kufu e pɛ bumo. Loŋ be kachɛ na malɛ bee ba!”

english_verse: Your Egyptian army is very strong, but I will send King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia to completely defeat that army.
translation_verse: Ade be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na naŋ kaŋɛ le: “Meeŋ bɔla Babilɔn be ewurgboŋ, Nebukadneeza so m mur Ijipt be efuli so be benapo damta kikɛ.

english_verse: He and his cruel troops will invade and destroy your land and leave your dead bodies piled everywhere.
translation_verse: Ewurgboŋ Nebukadneeza nɛ mbe benapo nɛ b maa wu kuwɔr beeŋ ba kɔ Ijipt be basa kena m mɔ basa m biti abar so kasawule na so be kaplɛkama.
