english_verse: I will dry up the Nile River, then sell the land to evil buyers. I will send foreigners to turn your entire nation into a barren desert. I, the Lord, have spoken. Egypt's Proud Cities Will Lie in Ruins The Lord said to the people of Egypt:
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ n shin nɛ lɔrgboŋ nɛ baa tre Nail na e wɔlto nseŋ naŋ shin nɛ basa lubi e ba ji Ijipt be efuli so eleŋ. Befɔ beeŋ ba jija kasawule na nɛ k maaŋ naa kɔ tɔnɔ. Ma Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e kaŋɛ.”

english_verse: All the idols and images you Egyptians worship in the city of Memphis will be smashed. No one will be left to rule your nation, and terror will fill the land.
translation_verse: Ade be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na naŋ kaŋɛ le: “Meeŋ mur agbirana nɛ mpɔrduliana nɛ Ijiptebi bee shuŋ ashi kadegboŋ nɛ baa tre Mɛmfis na. Esa kikɛ maaŋ naa wɔtɔ nɛ e ji Ijipt be efuli so kuwura, nɛ kufu a pɛ basa kikɛ efuli na so.

english_verse: I will set fire to your nation of Egypt! The city of Pelusium will be in anguish. Thebes will fall, and the people of Memphis will live in constant fear.
translation_verse: Meeŋ shin nɛ edɛ e ji Ijipt nɛ kagbenejija e tɔr basa nɛ b wɔ Pɛlusium na so. Egbal nɛ b pɔr ŋ kulti Tɛɛbis n wɔtɔ na beeŋ bure n tɔr nɛ nchu e ji kadegboŋ na; nɛ kufu a tɔr basa nɛ b wɔ Mɛmfis na so.

english_verse: The young soldiers in the cities of Heliopolis and Bubastis will die in battle, and the rest of the people will be taken prisoner.
translation_verse: Mbrantiɛfɔlbi nɛ b wɔ ndegboŋ nɛ baa tre Hiliopolis nɛ Bubastis na kikɛ beeŋ wu kena to nɛ b pɛ basa nɛ b ka na ŋ ki anya.

english_verse: You were so proud of your nation's power, but when I crush that power and kill that pride, darkness will fall over the city of Tahpanhes. A dark, gloomy cloud will cover the land as you are being led away into captivity.
translation_verse: Jemanɛ nɛ meeŋ jija Ijipt be eleŋ nɛ baa puchi so nseŋ shin nɛ k ba ekar na, tentembiri beeŋ tɔr kadegboŋ nɛ baa tre Taapanes na so. Kuwɔlpa beeŋ buu Ijipt be efuli na so nɛ b pɛ kumo be ndegboŋ to be basa ŋ ki anya.

english_verse: When I'm through punishing Egypt, you will know that I am the Lord. Egypt's King Is Powerless
translation_verse: Ŋ kaŋ gberge Ijiptebi le be kusoe ere n loge nɛ baaŋ pin fanɛ ma e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.” Ijipt be ewura be eleŋ ka yɔɔ be asheŋ

english_verse: Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the seventh day of the first month. He said:
translation_verse: B ka pɛ ewura Jehowachin nɛ anyi be beko n yɔ kenyaya to ashi Babilɔn be efuli so na be kafɛ kudukakosopo na to be sososo be kufɔl na to be kachɛ shunusopo na nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ ma le:

english_verse: So tell him that I am now his worst enemy. I will break both his arms—the good one and the broken one! His sword will drop from his hand forever,
translation_verse: Amoso, kusɔ nɛ ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ nde e la fanɛ: Ijipt be ewura la n doŋ nna nɛ mee sha kemur mo kuraa, saŋɛ na so, e maaŋ naŋ nya eleŋ ŋ koso n wora shɛŋ.

english_verse: and I will scatter the Egyptians all over the world.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman, meeŋ shin nɛ Ijiptebi na e pesaŋ to n yɔ durnya kikɛ to.

english_verse: I will strengthen the power of Babylonia's king and give him my sword to use against Egypt. I will also make the wounded king of Egypt powerless, and he will moan in pain and die in front of the Babylonian king. Then everyone on earth will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Kashenteŋto, meeŋ shin nɛ Ijipt be ewura, Fɛɛro, e ki esa pɔso nseŋ shin nɛ Babilɔn be ewura e nya eleŋ. Saŋɛ na so nɛ ŋ kaŋ ta ma tokobi m bɔɔ mo enɔ nɛ e ta kumo n shoŋi Ijipt, ekama beeŋ pin fanɛ ma e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.

english_verse: I will force the Egyptians to live as prisoners in foreign nations, and they will know that I, the Lord, have punished them.
translation_verse: Meeŋ shin nɛ Ijiptebi na e pesaŋ to n yɔ durnya kikɛ to. Saŋɛ na so nɛ b pin fanɛ ma e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.”

english_verse: Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the third month. He said:
translation_verse: B ka daŋ pɛ ewura Jehowachin nɛ anyi be galeŋga anya n yɔ Babilɔn be efuli so na be kafɛ kudukakosopo to be kufɔl sasopo na to be kachɛ sososo na nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ le:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the king of Egypt and his people that I am saying: You are more powerful than anyone on earth. Now listen to this.
translation_verse: “Dimɛdi pibi, kaŋɛ Ijipt be ewura, Fɛɛro nɛ mbe basa fanɛ Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ fanɛ; Fo kɔ eleŋ ga a chɔ ekama durnya to! Wanɛ nɛ meeŋ ta ŋ keshɛr fo?

english_verse: There was once a cedar tree in Lebanon with large, strong branches reaching to the sky.
translation_verse: Fo du fanɛ Lebanɔn be efuli so be kedibi nɛ baa tre sida; Nɛ k kɔ ayabi lela nɛ kiyoyul ga, nsaa wɔ nteŋ a sha kechute awɔlpa na nna.

english_verse: This tree had plenty of water to help it grow tall, and nearby streams watered the other trees in the forest.
translation_verse: Nchu e sa kumo kayul. Achubu nɛ a wɔ nchiŋ e shin nɛ k daŋ nteŋ; Nɛ eboŋana daa shile a kulti kumo be kaseto n shin nɛ kakpa nɛ k yil na bee wushi a sa kupuŋ to be ndibi kikɛ.

english_verse: But this tree towered over those other trees, and its branches grew long and thick.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal k ka daa nya kayul nɛnɛ so, nɛ k daŋ nteŋ a chɔ ndibi nɛ a ka na. Kumo be ayabi daŋ nɛnɛ nsaa wɔ nteŋ nna.

english_verse: Birds built nests in its branches, and animals were born beneath it. People from all nations lived in the shade of this strong tree.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ mbuibi be yiri kikɛ tɔl asha kumo be ayabi so; Nɛ kupuŋ to be asɔbɔya bee kurge amo be bibi kumo be kifito; Nɛ efuliana nɛ a wɔ durnya to be basa bee chena kumo be kiyoyul to a wushi.

english_verse: It had beautiful, long branches, and its roots found water deep in the soil.
translation_verse: Kedibi na daa walɛ ga. Kumo be ayabi daa wɔ nteŋ ga. Kumo be nliŋi daa fo kasawule to be nchu nna.

english_verse: I, the Lord, gave this tree its beauty, and I helped the branches grow strong. All other trees in Eden wanted to be just like it.
translation_verse: Mee to kumo nɛ k walɛ nsaa kɔ ayabi damta. Kedibi kama nɛ k wɔ Ebɔrɛ be kudɔbi nɛ baa tre Iden na to na daa sha kebaadu fanɛ kumo nna, ŋkpal loŋ so nsaa besa kumo eyur.

english_verse: King of Egypt, now listen to what I, the Lord God, am saying about that tree: The tree grew so tall that it reached the sky and became very proud and arrogant.
translation_verse: Amoso, naniere, kusɔ nɛ ma Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na bee kaŋɛ fanɛ k beeŋ wora kedibi nɛ k daŋ nteŋ hale n ya fo awɔlpa to na nde. K kaa daŋ nteŋ ga so nɛ k fara a wu kumo be kumu;

english_verse: So I, the Lord God, will reject the tree and hand it over to a foreign ruler, who will punish it for its wickedness.
translation_verse: ŋkpal loŋ so, ŋ kini kumo nna nsaa beeŋ shin nɛ efuli pɔtɛ ko be ewura e sɔ kumo nseŋ gberge kumo kusoe ŋkpal kumo be kumu kpakpaso so.

english_verse: Cruel foreigners will chop it down and leave it wherever it falls. Branches and broken limbs will be scattered over the mountains and in the valleys. The people living in the shade of those branches will go somewhere else.
translation_verse: Befɔ nɛ b maa wu kuwɔr beeŋ ku kumo nseŋ yige kumo n nase kakpa nɛ k beeŋ tɔr na. Kumo gbagba nɛ kumo be ayabi beeŋ tɔr kebee kama nɛ ketaŋɛ kama nɛ a wɔ efuli na so so. Saŋɛ na so efuliana nɛ a daa chena kumo be kiyoyul to na beeŋ yɔ mboŋ ko.

english_verse: Birds will then nest on the stump of the fallen tree, and wild animals will trample its branches.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ mbuibi e ba kaa jɔŋɛ kedibi nɛ k tɔr a dese na so nɛ kupuŋ to be asɔbɔya malɛ e baa chichi kumo be ayabi so.

english_verse: Never again will any tree dare to grow as tall as this tree, no matter how much water it has. Every tree must die, just as humans die and go down to the world of the dead.
translation_verse: Amoso yili le be jemanɛ a yɔ, kanaŋkamaso nɛ kedibi kikɛ nya nchu, k maaŋ tiŋ n daŋ nteŋ fanɛ kumo. Amo be kekama beeŋ wu fanɛ kananɛ edimɛdi bee wu a gbelge kasawule to a yɔ bubuni to na.”

english_verse: On the day this tree dies and goes to the world below, I, the Lord God, will command rivers and streams to mourn its death. Every underground spring of water and every river will stop flowing. The mountains in Lebanon will be covered with darkness as a sign of their sorrow, and all the trees in the forest will wither.
translation_verse: To, kusɔ nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ nde: “Kachɛ nɛ kedibi na beeŋ wu n yɔ bubuni to na, meeŋ shin nɛ elɔr nɛ mbombiana e bɔlɔ m buu kumo so a ŋini fanɛ a bee shu kumo be keeli nna. Meeŋ shin nɛ elɔr nɛ mbombiana kikɛ e sa maŋ naŋ shile. Kumo be kaman nɛ tentembiri e buu Lebanɔn be efuli so be abee so nɛ kiyi to be ndibi kikɛ e gbaŋgbaŋ amo be afantaŋ.

english_verse: This tree will crash to the ground, and I will send it to the world below. Then the nations of the earth will tremble. The trees from Eden and the choice trees from Lebanon are now in the world of the dead, and they will be comforted when this tree falls.
translation_verse: Jemanɛ nɛ meeŋ shin nɛ kedibi na e wu n yɔ bubuni to na, kumo be asheŋ beeŋ shin nɛ kufu e pɛ efuliana nɛ b baa chicha. Iden to be ndibi nɛ Lebanɔn be efuli so be ndibi nɛ a bee nya nchu nɛnɛ nɛ amo be nliŋi luri kasawule to kikɛ be ŋgbene beeŋ fuli amo ŋkpal k ka wu n tɔr so.

english_verse: Those people who found protection in its shade will also be sent to the world below, where they will join the dead.
translation_verse: Bekama nɛ b daa chena kumo be kiyoyul to na gba beeŋ tu kumo ŋ gbelge to n yɔ bubuni to kakpa nɛ bumo nɛ b daŋ kewu na yɔ na.

english_verse: King of Egypt, all these things will happen to you and your people! You were like this tree at one time—taller and stronger than anyone on earth. But now you will be chopped down, just as every tree in the garden of Eden must die. You will be sent down to the world of the dead, where you will join the godless and the other victims of violent death. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Kedibi na e la fo Ijipt be ewura nɛ mbe basa. Iden be kudɔbi na to be ndibi gba be kela daa maŋ fo feya so. Ama naniere, kananɛ Iden be ndibi wu ŋ gbelge to n yɔ bubuni to na nɛ fo alɛ gba beeŋ wu n ya tu basa nɛ b maa ŋana Ebɔrɛ nɛ bumo nɛ b wu kena to na. Ma Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e malga na.”

english_verse: Twelve years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the twelfth month. He said:
translation_verse: B ka pɛ ewura Jehowachin nɛ anyi be galeŋga anya n yɔ Babilɔn be efuli so na be kafɛ kudu anyɔsopo na be kufɔl kudu anyɔsopo na to be kachɛ sososo na, nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ ma le:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the king of Egypt and tell him I am saying: You act like a lion roaming the earth; but you are nothing more than a crocodile in a river, churning up muddy water with your feet.
translation_verse: “Dimɛdi pibi, Ezikɛl, kaŋɛ Ijipt be ewura, Fɛɛro, kenishipere be kasokpele be kubɔya ere fanɛ n yɛ: ‘Fee wora fanɛ buluŋ nna ashi efuliana na to, ama fo alɛ baa la fanɛ lɔr to be laŋchaŋ nɛ fee bri nchu to nna a jija amo.

english_verse: King of Egypt, listen to me. I, the Lord God, will catch you in my net and let a crowd of foreigners drag you to shore.
translation_verse: Efuli damtaana be basa kaŋ shɛr abar so, meeŋ to fo kashewu nseŋ shin nɛ b gberge fo nɛ kashewu na n dii kedeŋi so.’

english_verse: I will throw you into an open field, where birds and animals will come to feed on your flesh.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman, nɛ n lara fo n lɛ kasawule nseŋ bar durnya to be mbuibi nɛ asɔbɔya kikɛ nɛ a baa ji fo.

english_verse: I will spread your rotting flesh over the mountains and in the valleys,
translation_verse: Ma alɛ beeŋ shin nɛ fo eblaŋ bɛso e dese abee so nɛ ataŋɛ to kikɛ,

english_verse: and your blood will flow throughout the land and fill up the streams.
translation_verse: nɛ n chulgi fo ŋklaŋ m pɔ abee kikɛ hale nɛ a bɔlɔ eboŋana.

english_verse: I will cover the whole sky and every star with thick clouds, so that the sun and moon will stop shining.
translation_verse: Jemanɛ nɛ meeŋ mur fo na kaŋ fo, meeŋ shin nɛ kakpa e buu so nɛ epeŋi nɛ kufɔl nɛ achɛkpabi kikɛ e fulto ŋ gben.

english_verse: The heavens will become black, leaving your country in total darkness. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ma alɛ beeŋ shin nɛ esoso be kefulto kikɛ e ki tentembiri m buu fo efuli na kikɛ so. Ma Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ e kaŋɛ na.

english_verse: Foreign nations you have never heard of will be shocked when I tell them how I destroyed you.
translation_verse: Jemanɛ nɛ meeŋ shin nɛ fo kemur be asheŋ be baru e sɔ efuliana na so na, efuli damta so be basa nɛ fo maŋ naŋ nu bumo be asheŋ be ŋgbene beeŋ jija bumo ga.

english_verse: They will be horrified, and when I flash my sword in victory on the day of your death, their kings will tremble in the fear of what could happen to them.
translation_verse: Kusɔ nɛ meeŋ wora fo na beeŋ chinchiŋ basa damta. Kachɛ nɛ meeŋ pee ma tokobi m mɔ fo na, kufu beeŋ tɔr bewura so nɛ b baa chicha ŋkpal bumo gbagba be ŋkpa so.”

english_verse: The king of Babylonia is coming to attack you, king of Egypt!
translation_verse: Ade be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ Ijipt be ewura le: “Babilɔn be ewura beeŋ ba kɔ fo kena.

english_verse: Your soldiers will be killed by the cruelest army in the world, and everything you take pride in will be crushed.
translation_verse: Ma alɛ beeŋ shin nɛ efuliana nɛ amo be basa maa wu kuwɔr e ba mɔ fo basa kikɛ nseŋ mur asɔ kama nɛ fee puchi so na kikɛ.

english_verse: I will slaughter your cattle that graze by the river, and no people or livestock will be left to muddy its water.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ m mɔ menyi be ana nɛ b wɔ nchu ase kikɛ, saŋɛ na so edimɛdi ŋko ana maaŋ naa wɔtɔ a jija nchu na.

english_verse: The water will be clear, and streams will be calm. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Saŋɛ na so nɛ n shin nɛ menyi be nchuana e tɔr so a du keleŋkelembi nɛ menyi be eboŋana e baa shile boeŋ boeŋ. Ma Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ e kaŋɛ na.

english_verse: Egypt will become a barren wasteland, and no living thing will ever survive there. Then you and your people will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Ŋ kaŋ mur bekama nɛ b wɔ Ijipt be efuli so kikɛ nseŋ shin nɛ kasawule na dese fuloŋ na nɛ baaŋ pin fanɛ ma e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.

english_verse: This is your warning, and it will be used as a funeral song by foreign women to mourn the death of your people. I, the Lord God, have spoken. A Sad Ending for Egypt
translation_verse: Kasokpele ere beeŋ baa la awɔba nɛ efuli pɔtɛana so be beche e boŋ kumo n shu Ijipt nɛ kumo be basa kikɛ be keeli. Ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ e kaŋɛ na.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, mourn for the Egyptians and condemn them to the world of the dead, where they will be buried alongside the people of other powerful nations.
translation_verse: E yɛ: “Dimɛdi pibi, baa shu ŋkpal Ijipt be basa damta so nseŋ shin nɛ b pin fanɛ bubuni to e daga bumo. Ndoŋ e la kakpa nɛ baaŋ ta bumo nɛ efuli pɔtɛana nɛ a kɔ eleŋ ga na be basa n ya puli.”

english_verse: Say to them: You may be more beautiful than the people of other nations, but you will also die and join the godless in the world below.
translation_verse: Kaŋɛ bumo le: “Menyee tama fanɛ men walɛ nna ga a chɔ ekama a? Menyeeŋ yɔ bubuni to n ya tu basa nɛ b maa ŋana Ebɔrɛ na n dese ndoŋ.

english_verse: The graves of soldiers from Assyria are there. They once terrified people, but they were killed in battle and now lie deep in the world of the dead.
translation_verse: Bumo be nchaŋana dese efuli na kikɛ so nna. Ama bumo alɛ e daa funti basa jemanɛ ko na.

english_verse: The graves of soldiers from Elam are there. The very sight of those godless soldiers once terrified their enemies and made them panic. But now they are disgraced and ashamed as they lie in the world of the dead, alongside others who were killed in battle.
translation_verse: Elam e dese kakpa nɛ basa nɛ b mɔ kena to dese na nɛ kumo be benapo be nchaŋana kulti efuli na kikɛ so na. Bumo koŋwule na e daa funti basa na, ama naniere bumo e ji anishinyɔr n wu n tu basa nɛ b mɔ kena to a dese na.

english_verse: The graves of soldiers from Meshech and Tubal are there. These godless soldiers who terrified people were all killed in battle.
translation_verse: Meshɛk nɛ Tubal nɛ amo be benapo be nchaŋana kulti amo na gba wɔ ndoŋ. B la basa nɛ b maa ŋana Ebɔrɛ nna nɛ b mɔ bumo kikɛ kena to. Bumo e daa funti basa nɛ b wɔ ŋkpa to na.

english_verse: They were not given a proper burial like the heroes of long ago, who were buried with their swords under their heads and with their shields over their bodies. These were the heroes who made their enemies panic.
translation_verse: B daa maŋ puli bumo bunyaŋ so fanɛ kananɛ b daa puli dra na be basa nɛ b ji eleŋ ga nɛ b daa ta bumo nɛ bumo be akɔsɔ kikɛ a puli na. Jemanɛ ko le be benapo nɛ b ji eleŋ ga ere daa funti basa nɛ b wɔ ŋkpa to nna.

english_verse: You Egyptians will be cruelly defeated, and you will be buried alongside these other godless soldiers who died in battle.
translation_verse: Kananɛ Ijiptebi gba beeŋ wu m mur nseŋ dese basa nɛ b maa ŋana Ebɔrɛ nseŋ wu kena to na nna na.

english_verse: The graves of kings and leaders from Edom are there. They were powerful at one time. Now they are buried in the world of the dead with other godless soldiers killed in battle.
translation_verse: Edɔm nɛ mbe bewura nɛ bejuŋkparpo kikɛ gba wɔ ndoŋ. B daa la benapo lempo nna, ama naniere bumo nɛ basa nɛ b maa ŋana Ebɔrɛ nseŋ wu kena to na kikɛ e dese bubuni to na.

english_verse: The graves of the rulers of the north are there, as well as those of the Sidonians. Their powerful armies once terrified enemies. Now they lie buried in the world of the dead, where they are disgraced like other soldiers killed in battle.
translation_verse: Benimuana nɛ b shi kelargato be esoso na nɛ basa nɛ b daŋ shi Sidɔn be kadegboŋ to m ba na kikɛ gba wɔ ndoŋ. Bumo be eleŋ gboŋ daa funti basa nna, ama naniere bumo alɛ gba ta anishinyɔr nna n tu basa nɛ b wu kena to n yɔ bubuni to. Bumo kikɛ ji nyɔmɔ ashi bubuni to nna na.”

english_verse: The Lord God says: When your king of Egypt sees all of these graves, he and his soldiers will be glad they are not the only ones suffering.
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman, nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ le: “Ijipt be ewura nɛ mbe benapo kaŋ wu, bekama nɛ baa wu kena to na bumo be ŋgbene beeŋ wushi.

english_verse: I sent him to terrify people all over the earth. But he and his army will be killed and buried alongside other godless soldiers in the world of the dead. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal manɛ so, ma e shin nɛ Ijipt be ewura daa funti basa nɛ b wɔ ŋkpa to, ama baaŋ mɔ mo nɛ mbe benapo kikɛ nseŋ puli bumo kakpa nɛ b puli basa nɛ b maa ŋana ma nseŋ wu kena to na. Ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ e kaŋɛ na.”

english_verse: and to sound a warning signal when the enemy is seen coming.
translation_verse: Nɛ e baŋ wu edoŋ ka bee ba nɛ e foŋ kabel nɛ ekama e pin.

english_verse: Their past sins will be forgiven, and they will live because they have done right.
translation_verse: Meeŋ ta mbe alubi na m paŋ mo nɛ e ji efute, ŋkpal e ka wora asheŋ lela nɛ a daga na so.

english_verse: Twelve years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, a refugee who had escaped from Jerusalem came to me on the fifth day of the tenth month. He told me that the city had fallen.
translation_verse: Kafɛ nɛ b pɛ ewura Jehowachin nɛ anyi be galeŋga anya n yɔ Babilɔn be efuli so na be kafɛ kudu anyɔsopo na to be kufɔl kudusopo na be kachɛ nusopo na nɛ esa ko nya ekpa n shile Jerusalɛm to m ba kaŋɛ ma fanɛ Jerusalɛm bure n tɔr.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, warn your people by saying: Someday, I, the Lord, may send an enemy to invade a country. And suppose its people choose someone to stand watch
translation_verse: “Dimɛdi pibi, Ezikɛl, kaŋɛ fo basa fanɛ jemanɛ kama nɛ mee bar kena efuli so, loŋ be efuli na so be basa bee lara bumo to be eko nna nɛ e chena a keni ekpa to.

english_verse: If any of these people hear the signal and ignore it, they will be killed in battle. But it will be their own fault, because they could have escaped if they had paid attention.
translation_verse: Amodoŋwura gbagba e bar mbe luwu, ŋkpal manɛ so, e kplaŋ kefiɛso be kabel na be kushu so nna. Ashere nɛ e daŋ maŋ kplaŋ kumo so nna, e daŋ beeŋ gelge luwu na.

english_verse: But suppose the person watching fails to sound the warning signal. The enemy will attack and kill some of the sinful people in that country, and I, the Lord, will hold that person responsible for their death.
translation_verse: Ama nɛ fanɛ esa nɛ e chena a keni na wu edoŋ ka bee ba nsaa maŋ foŋ kabel na, edoŋ na beeŋ ba mɔ belubiworapoana na, ama meeŋ ta bumo be luwu na be turju m bɛ esa nɛ e chena a keni ekpa to na.

english_verse: Ezekiel, I have appointed you to stand watch for the people of Israel. So listen to what I say, then warn them for me.
translation_verse: Dimɛdi pibi, naniere mee lara fo nna nɛ fo baa la esa nɛ e beeŋ baa wu asheŋ nsaa kaŋɛ Israɛl be basa. A daga fanɛ fo shin nɛ b nu kefiɛso be kubɔya kama nɛ meeŋ sa fo fanɛ fo ta n sa bumo na.

english_verse: When I tell wicked people they will die because of their sins, you must warn them to turn from their sinful ways. But if you refuse to warn them, you are responsible for their death.
translation_verse: Nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ esa lubi ko beeŋ wu, nɛ fo maŋ fɛa mo so nɛ e chɛrga ashi mbe asheŋ na lubi to nseŋ mɔlga mbe kumu, kumo ere e beeŋ wu ashi mbe alubi na to ama mbe luwu be turju beeŋ baa bɛ fo.

english_verse: If you do warn them, and they keep sinning, they will die because of their sins, and you will be innocent. The Lord Is Always Fair (Ezekiel
translation_verse: Ama nɛ fanɛ fo fɛa esa lubi na so nɛ e maŋ yige alubi be kewora, nseŋ wu mbe alubi to, mannɛ fo e bar kumo.”

english_verse: If good people start doing evil, they will be put to death, because they have sinned.
translation_verse: Nɛ esa lela yige asheŋ lela be kewora nseŋ fara a wora asheŋ lubi, e beeŋ wu ŋkpal mbe alubi so.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, the people with you in Babylonia talk about you when they meet by the city walls or in the doorways of their houses. They say, “Let's ask Ezekiel what the Lord has said today.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na naŋ kaŋɛ le: “Dimɛdi pibi, basa nɛ fo nɛ bumo wɔ Babilɔn be efuli so nfe na baŋ shɛr kadegboŋ na be egbalana ase ŋko n chena bumo be ebuana be mbuna, fo asheŋ nɛ baa malga. Le nɛ baa kaŋɛ abar, ‘Men shin nɛ an ya bishi Ezikɛl n nu kubɔya nɛ k yaŋ shi Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kutɔ m ba kabre.’

english_verse: The Lord said: Ezekiel, son of man, the people of Israel are complaining that the punishment for their sins is more than they can stand. They have lost all hope for survival, and they blame me.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman, nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na naŋ kaŋɛ ma le: “Dimɛdi pibi, Israɛl be basa na bee bile asheŋ a fubel a kaŋɛ fanɛ bumo be alubi be kasogberge na chɔ bumo so. B maŋ naa kɔ tama kikɛ fanɛ baaŋ ji efute nseŋ kpal loŋ so a malga a gbiti ma.

english_verse: Tell them that as surely as I am the living Lord God, I don't like to see wicked people die. I enjoy seeing them turn from their sins and live. So if the Israelites want to live, they must stop sinning and turn back to me.
translation_verse: Kaŋɛ bumo fanɛ, ŋ ka la Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ nɛ e bee sa ŋkpa so, ma kagbene maa fuli alubiworapoana be luwu so. B ka yige bumo be alubi be kewora nseŋ ji efute e naa fuli ma kagbene. Amoso nɛ Israɛl be basa na bee sha keji efute, kumo ere b yige bumo be asheŋ lubi na nseŋ bɛta m ba ma kutɔ.

english_verse: Tell them that when good people start sinning, all the good they did in the past cannot save them from being punished. And remind them that when wicked people stop sinning, their past sins will be completely forgiven, and they won't be punished.
translation_verse: Dimɛdi pibi, kaŋɛ Israɛl be basa na fanɛ nɛ esa lela wora kulubi, kelela dra nɛ e wora na maaŋ tiŋ m mɔlga mo alubi na be kasogberge to. Nɛ fanɛ esa lubi yige alubi be kewora, e maaŋ naŋ nya kasogberge. Esa lela malɛ nɛ e yige alela be kewora nsaa wora asheŋ lubi maaŋ ji efute a wɔtɔ.

english_verse: Suppose I promise good people that they will live, then later they start sinning and believe they will be saved by the good they did in the past. These people will certainly be put to death because of their sins. Their good deeds will be forgotten.
translation_verse: Nɛ fanɛ n nase kɔnɔ n sa esa lela fanɛ e beeŋ ji efute, ama kumo be kaman nɛ e fara a fɛ fanɛ alelasheŋ nɛ e daŋ wora na so e beeŋ nya kumɔlga nseŋ fara a wora asheŋ lubi, m maaŋ naŋ nyiŋi alelasheŋ nɛ e daŋ wora na. E beeŋ wu ŋkpal mbe alubi na so.

english_verse: Suppose I warn wicked people that they will die because of their sins, and they stop sinning and start doing right.
translation_verse: Ama nɛ fanɛ ŋ fɛa esa lubi so fanɛ e beeŋ wu ŋkpal mbe alubi so, nɛ e yige asheŋ lubi be kewora nsaa wora asheŋ lela nɛ a daga

english_verse: For example, they need to return anything they have taken as security for a loan and anything they have stolen. Then if they stop doing evil and start obeying my Law, they will live.
translation_verse: fanɛ, e ka bɛta kusɔ nɛ e daŋ sɔ n yili tarma pɔɛŋ nseŋ sa esa ko mpaŋ na ŋko m bɛta kusɔ nɛ e yuri n ya sa kusɔwura na, kumo ere e maaŋ wu ama e beeŋ ji efute.

english_verse: Ezekiel, your people accuse me of being unfair. But they are the ones who are unfair.
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman, fo basa bee kaŋɛ fanɛ kusɔ nɛ mee wora na maŋ walɛ. Ama bumo ere be asheŋ nɛ baa wora na e maŋ niŋi.

english_verse: And if wicked people stop sinning and start doing right, they will save themselves from punishment.
translation_verse: Ama nɛ esa lubi yige asheŋ lubi be kewora nsaa wora asheŋ lela nɛ a daga, e mɔlga mbe kumu nna na.

english_verse: But the Israelites still think I am unfair. So warn them that they will be punished for what they have done. The News of Jerusalem's Fall
translation_verse: Ama menyi Israɛl be basa bee kaŋɛ fanɛ m maa wora asheŋ nɛ amo be ekpa so. Kusɔ nɛ menyee wora nɛ meeŋ yili so n ji menyi demu. Jerusalɛm ka bure n tɔr be baru be asheŋ

english_verse: The evening before this man arrived at my house, the Lord had taken control of me. So when the man came to me the next morning, I could once again speak. What Will Happen to Those Left in Israel?
translation_verse: Pɔɛŋ nɛ esa na ba ma kutɔ na be kaaseso, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be eleŋgboŋ daŋ gbelge ma so nna nɛ e shin nɛ ma kɔnɔ bugi nɛ n tiŋ m malga pɔɛŋ nɛ kanyɛn na ba ma kutɔ kumo be ŋklade kachipurso na. Basa nɛ b ka Israɛl na be alubi be asheŋ

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, the people living in the ruined cities of Israel are saying, “Abraham was just one man, and the Lord gave him this whole land of Israel. There are many of us, and so this land must be ours.”
translation_verse: Dimɛdi pibi, basa nɛ b kra wɔ Israɛl be efuli so be nde nɛ a bure na to na bee kaŋɛ nna fanɛ: ‘Eebraham daa la esa koŋwule nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ta kasawule na kikɛ n sa mo. Naniere an ka la basa damta ere, kasawule na ki anyeya nna a.’

english_verse: So, Ezekiel, tell them I am saying: How can you think the land is still yours? You eat meat with blood in it and worship idols. You commit murder
translation_verse: To, kaŋɛ bumo kusɔ nɛ ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na bee kaŋɛ. Menyee we eblaŋ nɛ ŋklaŋ kra wɔ amo to. Menyee shuŋ agbirana nsaa mɔ basa. Nɛ mannɛ so nɛ menyee fɛ fanɛ kasawule na ki menyeya nna?

english_verse: and spread violence throughout the land. Everything you do is wicked; you are even unfaithful in marriage. And you claim the land is yours!
translation_verse: Ade be kaman, men wɔtɔ nna a kɔ etokobi a mɔ abar nsaa wora ekishisheŋ. Ekama wɔtɔ nna a ji kubojua. Nɛ mannɛ so nɛ menyee fɛ fanɛ kasawule na ki menyeya nna?

english_verse: As surely as I am the living Lord God, you people in the ruined cities will be killed in battle. Those of you living in the countryside will be eaten by wild animals, and those hiding in caves and on rocky cliffs will die from deadly diseases.
translation_verse: Kaŋɛ bumo fanɛ ŋ ka la Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ nɛ e bee sa ŋkpa so, mee fɛa basa nɛ b kraa wɔ nde bureso na to na so nna nsaa kaŋɛ bumo fanɛ baaŋ wu kena to. Kumo be kaman nɛ kupuŋ to be asɔbɔya lubi e pɛ bumo nɛ b wɔ ndekarso na n we, nɛ kulɔ e mɔ bumo nɛ bumo alɛ ŋana a wɔ abee so nɛ abeelaŋ to na.

english_verse: I will make the whole country an empty wasteland and crush the power in which you take such pride. Even the mountains will be bare, and no one will try to cross them.
translation_verse: Meeŋ shin nɛ kasawule na e ki kasawule fuloŋ a dese, nɛ basa nɛ b daa kɔ eleŋgboŋ nsaa wu bumo amu kumo so na e ba ekar. Israɛl be abee beeŋ ki mboŋ lubi nɛ esa kama maaŋ naŋ tiŋ m bɔla amo ase n choŋ.

english_verse: I will punish you because of your sins, and I will turn your nation into a barren desert. Then you will know that I am the Lord. The People Listen, but Don't Change The Lord said:
translation_verse: Jemanɛ nɛ meeŋ gberge basa na kusoe ŋkpal bumo be alubi so nseŋ shin nɛ kasawule na e dese fuloŋ na, nɛ baaŋ pin fanɛ ma e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.” Kusɔ nɛ k wora Anebi Ezikɛl be kubɔya na be kaman be asheŋ

english_verse: So they all come and listen to you, but they refuse to do what you tell them. They claim to be faithful, but they are forever trying to cheat others out of their money.
translation_verse: Amoso ma basa bee chala nna m ba nu kusɔ nɛ fo kɔ a kaŋɛ, ama bumo alɛ maaŋ wora kusɔ nɛ fo kaŋɛ fanɛ b wora na. Kashaso nɛ baa malga a sa abar, ama kejimuni nɛ kapuni e bɔlɔ bumo be ŋgbene to.

english_verse: They treat you as though you were merely singing love songs or playing music. They listen, but don't do anything you say.
translation_verse: Kashenteŋto, bumo ere kutɔ fo la esa nɛ e kɔ ebɔl belbel so nna a laŋ jaŋjilaŋ nsaa boŋ kasha be nshɛ a deŋi bumo anishito. Baa nu asheŋ nɛ fee malga na kikɛ ama bumo alɛ maaŋ wora amo to be kukoŋwule gba.

english_verse: Soon they will be punished, just as you warned, and they will know that a prophet has been among them.
translation_verse: K maaŋ chɛr baaŋ nya kasogberge, fanɛ kananɛ fo kpele bumo kusoe na. Ndoŋ nɛ baaŋ pin fanɛ anebi ko ba bumo to.”

english_verse: The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ ma le:

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, Israel's leaders are like shepherds taking care of my sheep, the people of Israel. But I want you to condemn these leaders and tell them: I, the Lord God, say you shepherds of Israel are doomed! You take care of yourselves while ignoring my sheep.
translation_verse: “Dimɛdi pibi, Ezikɛl, Israɛl be bejuŋkparpoana na du fanɛ mbolpɔkpapo nɛ baa keni ma basa nɛ b du fanɛ mbolpɔ so nna. Ama mee sha fanɛ fo kaŋɛ Israɛl be bejuŋkparpo na fanɛ b maŋ wora n nyalɛ nɛ ekama e nu. Kaŋɛ bumo kusɔ nɛ ma Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ fanɛ: Asheŋ maaŋ nyalɛ n sa menyi, Israɛl be mbolpɔkpapo ere! Menyi be amu nɛ menyee keni so nseŋ kplaŋ ma mbolpɔ so.

english_verse: You drink their milk and use their wool to make your clothes. Then you butcher the best ones for food. But you don't take care of the flock!
translation_verse: Menyee nuu bumo be kenyipochu nna nsaa ta bumo be afuibi a lue asɔbuuso nseŋ naa mɔ bumo be belelabi a we, ama menyi alɛ maa keni bumo so nɛnɛ.

english_verse: You have never protected the weak ones or healed the sick ones or bandaged those that get hurt. You let them wander off and never look for those that get lost. You are cruel and mean to my sheep.
translation_verse: Menyee maa keni bumo be bumo nɛ b maŋ kɔ eleŋ na so, ŋko a chɛ bumo nɛ baa lɔ na ŋko a wɔtɔ bumo nɛ b doro na be achuu to adur a kre amo ŋko a kuŋ bumo nɛ baa lar a yɔ mboŋ ko na a ba ŋko a fin bumo nɛ foe na. Men du nyaŋnyaŋ nna a tɔrɔ bumo.

english_verse: They strayed in every direction, and because there was no shepherd to watch them, they were attacked and eaten by wild animals.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal mbolpɔ na ka maŋ kɔ ekpapo so, b pesaŋ to nna nɛ kupuŋ to be asɔbɔya lubi bee pɛ bumo a ji.

english_verse: So my sheep were scattered across the earth. They roamed on hills and mountains, without anyone even bothering to look for them.
translation_verse: Ma mbolpɔ ya kaa na abeegboŋ nɛ abeebi so nna. B daŋ pesaŋ to nna a wɔ durnya be kaplɛkama nɛ esa kikɛ malɛ daa maŋ keni n fin bumo.

english_verse: Now listen to what I, the living Lord God, am saying to you shepherds. My sheep have been attacked and eaten by wild animals, because you refused to watch them. You never went looking for the lost ones, and you fed yourselves without feeding my sheep.
translation_verse: Nɛ men nu n sa ma, asheŋ beeŋ baa bɔ menyi so ŋkpal manɛ so ma e la Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ nɛ e bee sa ŋkpa na. Kupuŋ to be asɔbɔya lubi pɛ ma mbolpɔ m mɔ n we ŋkpal esa kikɛ ka maa keni bumo so so. Ma mbolpɔkpapoana maŋ wora ania fanɛ baŋ fin mbolpɔ na. Bumo gbagba be amu so nɛ baa keni so, mannɛ ma mbolpɔ.

english_verse: So I, the Lord, will punish you! I will rescue my sheep from you and never let you be their shepherd again or butcher them for food. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Is the Good Shepherd
translation_verse: Ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na yɛ ma nɛ menyi maŋ naa kɔ shɛŋ. Ma alɛ beeŋ suge ma mbolpɔ menyi be enɔ to nɛ menyi maaŋ naa la bumo be ekpapo a nya bumo a mɔ a we. Mbolpɔkpapo lela na be asheŋ

english_verse: The Lord God then said: I will look for my sheep and take care of them myself,
translation_verse: Ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na e naa kaŋɛ menyi na fanɛ ŋ gbagba e naŋ fin ma mbolpɔ nsaa keni bumo so

english_verse: just as a shepherd looks for lost sheep. My sheep have been lost since that dark and miserable day when they were scattered throughout the nations. But I will rescue them
translation_verse: fanɛ kananɛ mbolpɔkpapoana bee keni bumo be mbolpɔ nɛ b daŋ pesaŋ to nɛ b naŋ ya bar bumo abar so na. Ma alɛ beeŋ bɛta bumo n shi mboŋ nɛ b pesaŋ to n yɔ kachɛ nɛ asheŋ daŋ maŋ nite nɛnɛ n sa bumo na kikɛ m ba.

english_verse: and bring them back from the foreign nations where they now live. I will be their shepherd and will let them graze on Israel's mountains and in the valleys and fertile fields.
translation_verse: Meeŋ lara bumo efuli pɔtɛana so m ba gama bumo abar so nseŋ shin nɛ b bɛta m ba bumo gbagba be kasawule so. Ma alɛ beeŋ baa la bumo be ekpapo nseŋ shin nɛ b nya n ji nɛnɛ ashi Israɛl be abee nɛ eboŋana ase.

english_verse: to look for those that are lost and bring back the ones that wander off, to bandage those that are hurt and protect the ones that are weak. I will also slaughter those that are fat and strong, because I always do right. Judgment on the Strong Sheep
translation_verse: Ma alɛ beeŋ fin bumo be bumo nɛ foe na nseŋ bɛta bumo nɛ yeŋ na m ba. Kumo be kaman nɛ ŋ kre bumo nɛ b doro na be achuu nseŋ chɛ bumo nɛ baa lɔ na. Ama bekama nɛ b ji n daŋ nsaa kɔ eleŋ na bre, meeŋ mur bumo, ŋkpal manɛ so, n la mbolpɔkpapo nɛ e bee wora kusɔ nɛ k daga nna.

english_verse: The Lord God said to his sheep, the people of Israel: I will carefully watch each one of you to decide which ones are the strong sheep and which ones are weak.
translation_verse: Naniere ma Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na bee kaŋɛ menyi nɛ men la ma mbolpɔ na nna fanɛ meeŋ keni menyi to m barga belela na ashi belubi na to nɛ mbolpɔ ashi mboe to.

english_verse: Some of you eat the greenest grass, then trample down what's left when you finish. Others drink clean water, then step in the water to make the rest of it muddy.
translation_verse: Menyi be beko ji ajibi lela nna ŋkukwe; nsaa chichi amo nɛ menyi maŋ ji so a wea shishɛr to! Menyeeŋ nuu nchu lela nna nseŋ gbar nchu nɛ menyi maaŋ nuu na to!

english_verse: but I will rescue them and no longer let them be mistreated. I will separate the good from the bad.
translation_verse: Ama ma alɛ beeŋ mɔlga ma mbolpɔ nɛ menyi maaŋ naa kɔrfɛ bumo. Meeŋ keni bumo so nseŋ barga belela na ashi belubi na to.

english_verse: After that, I will give you a shepherd from the family of my servant King David. All of you, both strong and weak, will have the same shepherd, and he will take good care of you.
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ n sa bumo ewura nɛ e beeŋ baa du fanɛ ma kayɛrbi ewura Deevid nɛ e baa kpa bumo nsaa keni bumo so nɛnɛ.

english_verse: He will be your leader, and I will be your God. I, the Lord, have spoken. A Bright Future for the Lord's Sheep The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Saŋɛ na so nɛ ma Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e baa la bumo be Ebɔrɛ, nɛ ewura nɛ e du fanɛ ma kayɛrbi ewura Deevid na e baa la bumo be ejuŋkparpo. Ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ e kaŋɛ na

english_verse: The people of Israel are my sheep, and I solemnly promise that they will live in peace. I will chase away every wild animal from the desert and the forest, so my sheep will not be afraid.
translation_verse: Ma nɛ bumo beeŋ wora kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre nɛ k beeŋ bar bumo kayurwushi. Ma alɛ beeŋ ju kupuŋ to be asɔbɔya lubi na kikɛ kasawule na so, saŋɛ na so ma mbolpɔ maaŋ naa ŋana kufu.

english_verse: They will live around my holy mountain, and I will bless them by sending more than enough rain
translation_verse: Ade be kaman, meeŋ nɛfa bumo nseŋ shin nɛ b baa wɔ ma kebee cheembi na ase nɛ n sa bumo bɔrɛchu lela jemanɛ nɛ k daga nsaa la nɛfa na.

english_verse: to make their trees produce fruit and their crops to grow. I will set them free from slavery and let them live safely in their own land. Then they will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Saŋɛ na so nɛ ndibi na e sɔr nɛnɛ nɛ nsawule na kikɛ malɛ e wora adɔjibi. Kumo be kaman nɛ ekama e chena mo gbagba be kasawule so nɛ kayurwushi. Ŋ kaŋ tuge ŋgbɛlɛbi nɛ a kre ma basa na, nseŋ shin nɛ b nya bumo be amu ashi basa nɛ b pɛ bumo anya na be enɔ na nɛ baaŋ pin fanɛ ma e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.

english_verse: Foreign nations will never again rob them, and wild animals will no longer kill and eat them. They will have nothing to fear.
translation_verse: Loŋ be jemanɛ so, efuli pɔtɛana maaŋ naŋ tiŋ m ba kɔ n suge bumo be asɔbɔya, nɛ kupuŋ to be asɔ lubi gba maaŋ naŋ pɛ bumo n ji. Baaŋ chena kayurwushi so nna nɛ esa kama maa naa funti bumo.

english_verse: I will make their fields produce large amounts of crops, so they will never again go hungry or be laughed at by foreigners.
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman, meeŋ sa bumo kasawule lela nɛ akoŋ maaŋ naa wɔ kumo so. Efuli pɔtɛana be basa maaŋ naaŋ mushe bumo kikɛ.

english_verse: Then everyone will know that I protect my people Israel. I, the Lord, make this promise.
translation_verse: Aloŋ nɛ ekama beeŋ pin fanɛ ma e naa kuŋ Israɛl be basa nɛ b la ma basa na. Ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ e kaŋɛ na.”

english_verse: They are my sheep; I am their God, and I take care of them.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ le: “Menyi, ma mbolpɔ, nɛ mee bela na, la ma basa nna nɛ ma alɛ la menyi be Ebɔrɛ.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the people of Edom
translation_verse: “Dimɛdi pibi, Ezikɛl, malga ŋ gbiti Edɔm be kebee nɛ k yili n sa kumo be basa na.

english_verse: and say to them: I, the Lord God, am now your enemy! And I will turn your nation into an empty wasteland,
translation_verse: Kaŋɛ Edɔmebi kusɔ nɛ ma Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na bee kaŋɛ. N yɛ ma nɛ menyi Edɔm be basa, maŋ naa kɔ shɛŋ! Meeŋ shin nɛ menyi be efuli e ki kasawule fuloŋ a dese, nɛ esa kikɛ maaŋ naa wɔ kumo so.

english_verse: leaving your towns in ruins. Your land will be a desert, and then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Ma alɛ beeŋ naŋ shin nɛ menyi be ndegboŋ e ki alambure a dese. Nɛ menyi be kasawule e ki kakpa nɛ ekama kini n lɛ. Aloŋ nɛ menyeeŋ pin fanɛ ma e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.

english_verse: People of Edom, not only have you been Israel's longtime enemy, you simply watched when disaster wiped out its people as punishment for their sins.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal manɛ so, dra dra kikɛ nɛ menyi Edɔm be basa ta Israɛl be basa ŋ ki men doŋana nseŋ kpal loŋ so n shin nɛ b wu ga jemanɛ nɛ b nya bumo be alubi be kasogberge na.

english_verse: And so, as surely as I am the living Lord God, you are guilty of murder and must be put to death.
translation_verse: Ŋ ka la Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ nɛ e bee sa ŋkpa so luwu nɛ men maaŋ tiŋ ŋ gbelge e naaŋ ba menyi so. Men wora n jija ŋkpal basa be kamɔ so, amoso menyi alɛ gba beeŋ wu.

english_verse: and your land will lie in ruins forever. No one will live in your towns ever again. You will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Saŋɛ na so nɛ menyi be efuli na e dese fuloŋ mbaanaayɔ, nɛ esa kikɛ maaŋ naa wɔ menyi be ndegboŋana to. Aloŋ e naaŋ shin nɛ men pin fanɛ ma e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.

english_verse: You thought the nations of Judah and Israel belonged to you, and that you could take over their territory. But I am their God,
translation_verse: Hale ma Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na ka daa la Juda nɛ Israɛl be Ebɔrɛ na gba, men daŋ kaŋɛ nna fanɛ bumo be efuliana be nsawule kikɛ la menyeya nna nseŋ daa sha keta amo ŋ ki menyeya.

english_verse: and as surely as I live, I will punish you for treating my people with anger and hatred. Then they will know that I, the Lord, am punishing you!
translation_verse: Amoso ma Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ ka baa wɔ ŋkpa to ere bre, meeŋ ka menyi kukɔ ŋkpal agbo nɛ kukɔrkɔ nɛ yurkishi nɛ men kɔ a laŋɛ ma basa be kaplɛa so so, saŋɛ na so baŋ pin fanɛ kusɔ nɛ men wora bumo na so nɛ mee gberge menyi kusoe na.

english_verse: And you will finally realize that I heard you laugh at their destruction and say their land was yours to take.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman, nɛ men pin fanɛ ma Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na daŋ nu men ka daa malga mmalga jiga a gbiti Israɛl be basa nsaa kaŋɛ fanɛ kasawule na dese jiga nna n sa menyi nɛ men ta ŋ ki menyeya.

english_verse: You even insulted me, but I heard it all.
translation_verse: Ma alɛ naŋ nu mpuchi be mmalga nɛ men malga ŋ gbiti ma na gba.”

english_verse: just as you celebrated when Israel was destroyed. Your nation of Edom will be nothing but a wasteland. Then everyone will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: fanɛ kananɛ men ji eyur jemanɛ nɛ ma basa Israɛlebi na daŋ mur na. Edɔm be efuli nɛ kumo be nsawule kikɛ beeŋ mur cheche, a maaŋ naa la shɛŋ. Kumo be kaman nɛ ekama e pin fanɛ ma e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.”

english_verse: that I, the Lord God, am saying: Your enemies sneered and said that you mountains belonged to them.
translation_verse: Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na kɔ n sa amo. Israɛl mo doŋana daŋ malga mmalga jiga ŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ, Naniere abee dra na ki bumo peya nna!

english_verse: So all you mountains and hills, streams and valleys, listen to what I will do. Your towns may now lie in ruins, and nations may laugh and insult you.
translation_verse: Amoso naniere kusɔ nɛ ma Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na bee kaŋɛ menyi abeegboŋ nɛ abeebi nɛ eboŋana nɛ ataŋɛ nɛ mboŋ nɛ a bure a dese nɛ ndegboŋ nɛ basa shile amo to nɛ efuliana nɛ a kulti menyi na ba muu amo to be asɔ n yɔ nseŋ wora menyi eyurto na kikɛ nde.

english_verse: But in my fierce anger, I will turn against those nations, and especially the Edomites, because they laughed at you the loudest and took over your pasturelands.
translation_verse: Ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na malga agbogboŋ so nna ŋ gbiti efuliana nɛ a kulti fo Israɛl be efuli na kikɛ, fɔŋfɔŋ Edɔm be efuli na. Ŋkpal manɛ so, bumo e daŋ ji eyur ga nseŋ daŋ sɔ ma kasawule nɛ kumo be asɔbɔya be ejikpa ŋ ki bumo peya.

english_verse: so I will now insult and disgrace them. That is my solemn promise.
translation_verse: Ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na bɔ ntaŋ fanɛ efuliana na beeŋ ji anishinyɔr.

english_verse: Trees will grow on you mountains of Israel and produce fruit for my people, because they will soon come home.
translation_verse: Ama ndibi nɛ a yil abee so ashi ma basa, Israɛlebi, be efuli so na beeŋ naŋ purge nseŋ sɔr asɔrso n sa bumo. K maaŋ chɛr baaŋ bɛta m ba epe.

english_verse: I will take care of you by plowing your soil and planting crops on your fertile slopes.
translation_verse: N nyi menyi Israɛlebi be asheŋ nɛ men be asheŋ tir n sa ma. Ma alɛ beeŋ shin nɛ men naaŋ dɔ menyi be adɔsawule so n duu adɔjibi.

english_verse: Children will be born, and animals will give birth to their young. You will no longer be deserted as you are now, but you will be covered with people and treated better than ever. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Ma alɛ beeŋ naŋ shin menyi be asɔbɔya kikɛ e salga n wora keshi nɛ men naaŋ chena kasawule na so fanɛ kananɛ men daŋ chena kumo so dra na. Menyeeŋ dii kedama ga a chɔ kananɛ men daa du na, saŋɛ na so nɛ menyeeŋ pin fanɛ ma e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.

english_verse: I will bring my people Israel home, and they will live on you mountains, because you belong to them, and your fertile slopes will never again let them starve.
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ n shin nɛ ma basa Israɛlebi na e naŋ bɛta m ba chena bumo be nsawule so. Nsawule na beeŋ baa la bumo gbagba peya nɛ akoŋ malɛ maaŋ naŋ mɔ bumo be mbia.

english_verse: It's true that you have been accused of not producing enough food and of letting your people starve.
translation_verse: Ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na yɛ: Kashenteŋ nɛ basa bee kaŋɛ fanɛ kasawule na maa wora ajibi nɛnɛ nsaa shin nɛ akoŋ bee mɔ kumo be basa.

english_verse: But I, the Lord, promise that you won't hear other nations laugh and sneer at you ever again. From now on, you will always produce plenty of food for your people. I, the Lord God, have spoken. The Lord Will Be Honored
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman, menyi maaŋ naŋ bugi asoe a nu mmalga jiga nɛ efuliana na bee malga a gbiti menyi. Meni alɛ maaŋ naŋ keni n wu basa ka bee wora menyi eyurto. Kasawule na maaŋ naŋ shin nɛ men paŋ menyi be mbia. Ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na, e kaŋɛ na.” Israɛl be basa be ŋkpa popɔr be asheŋ

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, when the people of Israel were living in their own country, they made the land unclean by the way they behaved, just as a woman's monthly period makes her unclean.
translation_verse: “Dimɛdi pibi, Israɛlebi na ka daa wɔ bumo be kasawule so na, b daŋ bɔla bumo be kebaawɔtɔ nɛ asheŋ woraso so nna n jija kumo. Kananɛ eche nɛ e bee lar ntamaŋ maŋ walɛ so daŋkare be ekpa so na, nɛ bumo be kebaawɔtɔ na daa du n sa ma.

english_verse: They committed murders and worshiped idols, which made the land even worse. So in my anger, I punished my people
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ n nya agbo n wɔtɔ bumo ŋkpal kabasamɔ nɛ kagbirshuŋ nɛ b ta n jija kasawule na so,

english_verse: Wherever they went, my name was disgraced, because foreigners insulted my people by saying I had forced them out of their own land.
translation_verse: Kaplɛkama malɛ nɛ b yɔ, b daa ŋaba ma ketre cheembi na nna; ŋkpal manɛ so, le nɛ efuli pɔtɛana be basa daa kaŋɛ: ‘Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be basa nna na. E tintiŋ bumo nna n lar bumo gbagba be kasawule so.’

english_verse: so tell the Israelites that I am saying: You have disgraced my holy name among the nations where you now live. So you don't deserve what I'm going to do for you. I will lead you home to bring honor to my name
translation_verse: Amoso kaŋɛ Israɛlebi na kubɔya nɛ ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na kɔ nɛ sa bumo: Mannɛ menyi Israɛlebi so nɛ meeŋ wora kusɔ nɛ mee sha kewora ere, ama ma ketre cheembi nɛ men ŋaba efuli pɔtɛ kama nɛ men yɔ kumo so na so.

english_verse: I will gather you from the foreign nations and bring you home.
translation_verse: Meeŋ lara menyi ashi efuli pɔtɛana kama to m ba epe menyi gbagba be kasawule so.

english_verse: I will sprinkle you with clean water, and you will be clean and acceptable to me. I will wash away everything that makes you unclean, and I will remove your disgusting idols.
translation_verse: Nɛ kebaadu fanɛ ŋ ka wora nchu lela ŋ ŋmenyaŋ menyi so nɛ men nyalɛ so ashi kagbirshuŋ nɛ kusɔ kama nɛ k shin nɛ men wora eyurpi na to.

english_verse: I will take away your stubborn heart and give you a new heart and a desire to be faithful. You will have only pure thoughts,
translation_verse: Ade be kaman, nɛ n lara menyi be ŋgbene kpakpaso fanɛ kejembu na nseŋ sa menyi ŋgbene popɔr nɛ a beeŋ shin nɛ men baa wora ma kasonu.

english_verse: because I will put my Spirit in you and make you eager to obey my laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Ma alɛ beeŋ ta ma kiyoyu n wɔtɔ menyi to nseŋ shin nɛ men bɛ ma mbraana nɛ keŋini kikɛ so kenishipereso.

english_verse: You will once again live in the land I gave your ancestors; you will be my people, and I will be your God.
translation_verse: Saŋɛ na so nɛ men chena kasawule nɛ n ta n sa men nananyɛnana na so nsaa la ma basa nɛ ma alɛ e baa la menyi be Ebɔrɛ.

english_verse: I will protect you from anything that makes you unclean. Your fields will overflow with grain, and no one will starve.
translation_verse: Meeŋ kuŋ menyi ashi kusɔ kama nɛ k bee shin nɛ menyee wora eyurpi na to nseŋ shin nɛ menyi be ayu e wora nɛnɛ, saŋɛ na so akoŋ maaŋ naa wɔtɔ.

english_verse: Your trees will be filled with fruit, and crops will grow in your fields, so that you will never again feel ashamed for not having enough food.
translation_verse: Ma alɛ beeŋ naŋ shin nɛ menyi be ndibi sɔrso nɛ adɔjibi e foo, saŋɛ na so menyi maaŋ naŋ ji anishinyɔr ashi efuliana na so ŋkpal akoŋ so.

english_verse: People of Israel, I'm not doing these things for your sake. You sinned against me, and you must suffer shame and disgrace for what you have done. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ le: Israɛlebi, mee sha nɛ men pin fanɛ mannɛ menyi so nɛ mee wora asheŋ ere, ama mee sha nna nɛ anishinyɔr nɛ nyɔmɔ e pɛ menyi ŋkpal asheŋ nɛ men wora na so.”

english_verse: After I have made you clean, I will let you rebuild your ruined towns and let you live in them.
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na naŋ kaŋɛ le: “Kachɛ nɛ meeŋ kpra menyi be alubi ashi menyi so na nɛ meeŋ naŋ shin nɛ men chena menyi be ndegboŋana to nseŋ lɔŋɛ alambure na m pɔr.

english_verse: Your land will be plowed again, and nobody will be able to see that it was once barren.
translation_verse: Ekama nɛ e daŋ bɔla menyi be adɔana ase a choŋ daa wu fanɛ e ki kupuŋ nna a dese, ama meeŋ naŋ shin nɛ men lɔŋɛ amo so n dɔ.

english_verse: Then the nearby nations that survive will know that I am the one who rebuilt the ruined places and replanted the barren fields. I, the Lord, make this promise.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ basa nɛ b wɔ efuliana nɛ a mata menyi nseŋ kraa wɔtɔ na e pin fanɛ ma Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e naa lɔŋɛ menyi be nde bureso a pɔr nsaa dɔ menyi be adɔpuŋ a du. Ma Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e nase kumo be kɔnɔ, ma alɛ beeŋ wora loŋ gbagba chap.”

english_verse: I will once again answer your prayers, and I will let your nation grow until you are like a large flock of sheep.
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman, nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na naŋ kaŋɛ le: “Meeŋ naŋ shin nɛ Israɛlebi na e kule ma kechɛto nɛ n shin nɛ b wora keshi n ti so fanɛ mbolpɔ na.

english_verse: The towns that now lie in ruins will be filled with people, just as Jerusalem was once filled with sheep to be offered as sacrifices during a festival. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Nɛ nde nɛ a bure a dese ere e naŋ bɔlɔ basa fanɛ kananɛ mbolpɔ daŋ bɔlɔ Jerusalɛm to nɛ b daa ta amo a lara esarga nchɛgboŋachɛ na. Ndoŋ nɛ baaŋ pin fanɛ ma e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.”

english_verse: Some time later, I felt the Lord's power take control of me, and his Spirit carried me to a valley full of bones.
translation_verse: Saŋko ka fo nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be eleŋgboŋ na gbelge ma so nɛ mbe Kiyoyu ta ma ŋ gbelge to n yɔ ketaŋɛ ko to nɛ awibi sɔ kaplɛkama a dese.

english_verse: The Lord showed me all around, and everywhere I looked I saw bones that were dried out.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na keta ma n nite ketaŋɛ na to nɛ n wu fanɛ awibi na daa shi nseŋ daŋ wɔl n fuli a dese.

english_verse: He said, “Ezekiel, son of man, can these bones come back to life?” I replied, “Lord God, only you can answer that.”
translation_verse: Nɛ e bishi ma: “Dimɛdi pibi, Ezikɛl, awibi ere beeŋ naŋ tiŋ m ba ŋkpa to a?” Nɛ ma alɛ kaŋɛ: “Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ, fo nawule e naŋ tiŋ m pin kumo be loŋ!”

english_verse: He then told me to say: Dry bones, listen to what the Lord is saying to you,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ e kaŋɛ: “Malga n sa awibi nɛ a wɔl n fuli na nseŋ kaŋɛ amo nɛ e nu Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be kamalga.

english_verse: “I, the Lord God, will put breath in you, and once again you will live.
translation_verse: Kaŋɛ amo fanɛ le nɛ ma Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ: Meeŋ shin nɛ efute e ba menyi to nɛ men naŋ nya ŋkpa.

english_verse: I will wrap you with muscles and skin and breathe life into you. Then you will know that I am the Lord.”
translation_verse: Ma alɛ beeŋ sa menyi achin nɛ eblaŋ, nseŋ shin nɛ kawɔl e ba buu menyi so. Kumo be kaman nɛ n sa menyi efute nɛ men nya ŋkpa. Ndoŋ nɛ menyeeŋ pin fanɛ ma e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.”

english_verse: I did what the Lord said, but before I finished speaking, I heard a rattling noise. The bones were coming together!
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ m malga n sa awibi na fanɛ kananɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ na. Ŋ kraa malga nna nseŋ nu egbri ko fanɛ basa ka bee kpla enɔ na nɛ awibi kɔŋkɔŋ na fara a chɛ abar so.

english_verse: I saw muscles and skin cover the bones, but they had no life in them.
translation_verse: Ŋ kraa yil a keni amo nna nɛ achin nɛ eblaŋ nɛ kawɔl ba buu amo so. Ama ŋkpa daa maŋ wɔ amo to.

english_verse: The Lord said: Ezekiel, now say to the wind, “The Lord God commands you to blow from every direction and to breathe life into these dead bodies, so they can live again.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ebɔrɛ naŋ kaŋɛ ma: “Dimɛdi pibi, malga n sa afu. Kaŋɛ afu na fanɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na yɛ k shi kaba kama so m ba luri eyurana nɛ a la bubuni a dese ere to nɛ e nya ŋkpa.”

english_verse: As soon as I said this, the wind blew among the bodies, and they came back to life! They all stood up, and there were enough to make a large army.
translation_verse: Ŋ ka baŋ kaŋɛ loŋ, nɛ afu ber m ba luri eyurana na to nɛ a nya ŋkpa ŋ koso n yili. B daa la benapo be katuŋ gboŋgboŋi ko nna.

english_verse: The Lord said: Ezekiel, the people of Israel are like dead bones. They complain that they are dried up and that they have no hope for the future.
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman, nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na naŋ kaŋɛ ma: “Dimɛdi pibi, Israɛl be basa du fanɛ awibi kɔŋkɔŋ ere nna. Baa fubel nna a kaŋɛ fanɛ b wɔlso nna nsaa maa kɔ echefoso be tama kikɛ kebaawɔtɔ to.

english_verse: So tell them, “I, the Lord God, promise to open your graves and set you free. I will bring you back to Israel,
translation_verse: Amoso kaŋɛ bumo fanɛ ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na bee sha kebugi bumo be nchaŋana nna nɛ b lar m bɛta m ba Israɛl be kasawule so.

english_verse: and when that happens, you will realize that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Ŋ kaŋ wora loŋ, baaŋ pin fanɛ ma e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na.

english_verse: My Spirit will give you breath, and you will live again. I will bring you home, and you will know that I have kept my promise. I, the Lord, have spoken.” Judah and Israel Together Again
translation_verse: Ma kiyoyu beeŋ sa bumo efute nɛ b nya ŋkpa m ba kaa wɔ bumo gbagba be kasawule so. Ndoŋ nɛ baaŋ pin fanɛ ma e la Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ nɛ n nase kɔnɔ fanɛ meeŋ wora loŋ na. Ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e kaŋɛ na.” Juda nɛ Israɛl ka naŋ ki kuwurji koŋwule be asheŋ

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, get a stick and write on it, “The kingdom of Judah.” Then get another stick and write on it, “The kingdom of Israel.”
translation_verse: E yɛ: “Dimɛdi pibi, fin kedibi nseŋ sibɛ le kumo so, ‘Juda be kuwurji be asheŋ.’ Kumo be kaman nɛ fo fin kedibi nyɔsopo nseŋ sibɛ le kumo alɛ gba so, ‘Israɛl be kuwurji be asheŋ.’

english_verse: And when your people ask you what this means,
translation_verse: Fo basa kaŋ bishi fo kusɔ nɛ k bee ŋini,

english_verse: tell them that I, the Lord, will join together the stick of Israel and the stick of Judah. I will hold them in my hand, and they will become one.
translation_verse: feeŋ tiŋ ŋ kaŋɛ bumo fanɛ ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na bee sha keta kedibi nɛ k yili n sa Israɛl nna n chuge kumo nɛ k yili n sa Juda na so nna, saŋɛ na so amo anyɔ na beeŋ ki kedibi koŋwule a wɔ ma enɔ to.

english_verse: Hold these two sticks where they can be seen by everyone
translation_verse: To, feeŋ keta ndibi anyɔ na fo enɔ to nɛ basa na e wu amo.

english_verse: and then say: I, the Lord God, will gather the people of Israel and bring them home from the foreign nations where they now live.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ fo kaŋɛ bumo fanɛ ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na bee sha kelara ma basa kikɛ ashi efuliana nɛ b pesaŋ to n yɔ to na n shin nɛ b ba abar so ashi bumo gbagba be kasawule so.

english_verse: I will make them into one nation and let them once again live in the land of Israel. Only one king will rule them, and they will never again be divided into two nations.
translation_verse: Ma alɛ beeŋ shin nɛ b baa la basa koŋwule ashi Israɛl be efuli so. Baaŋ baa kɔ ewura koŋwule nɛ e beeŋ baa ji bumo so kuwura a maaŋ naŋ barga to a wɔtɔ.

english_verse: They will no longer worship idols and do things that make them unacceptable to me. I will wash away their sin and make them clean, and I will protect them from everything that makes them unclean. They will be my people, and I will be their God.
translation_verse: Bumo alɛ maaŋ naŋ bɔla kagbirshuŋ so n jija bumo be amu ŋko n wora alubi ŋ gbiti bumo be amu. Ma alɛ beeŋ sɔ bumo n yige ashi ekpa kama so nɛ baa bɔla so a wora alubi a debɔr ma na, nseŋ fɔr bumo so, nɛ b baa la ma basa, nɛ ma alɛ e baa la bumo be Ebɔrɛ.

english_verse: Their king will always come from the family of my servant King David and will care for them like a shepherd. The people of Israel will faithfully obey my laws. They and their descendants will live in the land I gave my servant Jacob, just as their ancestors did.
translation_verse: Kasawule nɛ n ta n sa ma kayɛrbi Jeekɔb na so nɛ baaŋ chena, kakpa nɛ bumo nanaana daŋ chena na. Bumo nɛ bumo be mbia nɛ kaman to ebi kikɛ beeŋ chena kumo so hale mbaanaayɔ, nɛ ewura nɛ e du fanɛ ma kayɛrbi Deevid na e baa ji bumo so kuwura.

english_verse: I solemnly promise to bless the people of Israel with unending peace. I will protect them and let them become a powerful nation. My temple will stand in Israel for all time,
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman, ma nɛ bumo beeŋ luri kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre to a ŋini kayurwushi nɛ baaŋ baa wɔtɔ to hale mbaanaayɔ. Ma alɛ beeŋ shin nɛ b baa wɔtɔ nseŋ wora keshi n ti so nɛ ma bɔrɛlambu na e baa wɔ bumo to mbaanaayɔ.

english_verse: Every nation on earth will know that my temple is in Israel and that I have chosen the Israelites to be my people.
translation_verse: Jemanɛ nɛ meeŋ yili ma bɔrɛlambu bumo to mbaanaayɔ na, nɛ efuliana na beeŋ pin fanɛ ma Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na e lara Israɛlebi na ŋ ki ma basa.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn Gog, that wicked ruler of the kingdoms of Meshech and Tubal in the land of Magog. Tell him:

translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ kanyɛn na yili kowushina be kelɔnɛ na be kabuna to ŋ karga n ya fo epunto be kelɔnɛ na be kabuna to nɛ k koso fanɛ ayadra kalfa nɛ adeshe nɛ aburwa. Kelargato be esoso be kabunagboŋ na be asheŋ

translation_verse: Kabuna ko daa wɔ kelɔnɛ na be kelargato be esoso be kaba so nɛ baa bɔla kumo to a yɔ epunto be kelɔnɛ na so, fanɛ kananɛ kuko daa wɔ epeŋilarkpa be kaba so na. translation_verse: Ade be kaman, nɛ kanyɛn na naŋ ta ma n yɔ kelargato be kaseto na, nɛ n ya wu kabunagboŋ ko gba ndoŋ. Ndoŋ nna nɛ e karga kumo be epunto be egbalana na, nɛ kabuna to be ebu na, nɛ amo nɛ amo nɛ a wɔ mbunagboŋ anyɔ na ase na kikɛ sasa.

english_verse: Seven steps led up to the gate; the entrance room was at the far end of the passageway and faced the courtyard of the temple. Carvings of palm trees decorated the walls along the passageway.

english_verse: We then went into the inner courtyard, through the gate on the south side of the temple. The man measured the gate, and it was the same size as the gates in the outer wall.
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman, nɛ kanyɛn na naŋ keta ma m bɔla kelargato be kaseto be kabunagboŋ na to n luri epunto be kelɔnɛ na to nseŋ ya karga kabunagboŋ na. Kumo nɛ kowushina be kabunagboŋ na kikɛ sasa nna.

english_verse: The entrance room of this gate faced the outer courtyard, and carvings of palm trees decorated the walls of the passageway. Eight steps led up to this gate.
translation_verse: Ebu nɛ k wɔ kumo be kabuna to na daŋ kilgi anishito n shoŋi kowushina be kelɔnɛ na nna. Atemprembi aburwa nɛ baa dii a yɔ kabunagboŋ ere ase. Epeŋilarkpa be Kabunagboŋ na be asheŋ

english_verse: Next, we went through the east gate to the inner courtyard. The man measured this gate, and it was the same size as the others.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ kanyɛn na naŋ ta ma m bɔla epeŋilarkpa be kabunagboŋ na to n yɔ epunto be kelɔnɛ na so nseŋ ya karga kabuna to na. Kumo nɛ amo nɛ a ka na kikɛ sasa nna.

english_verse: The entrance room faced the outer courtyard, and the walls in the passageway were decorated with carvings of palm trees. Eight steps also led up to this gate.
translation_verse: Ebu nɛ k wɔ kumo be kabuna to na daŋ kilgi n shoŋi kowushina be kelɔnɛ na nna nɛ b wora abii be ndibi be nduli n deŋi kedɛdɛ na be egbalana so. Atempreŋ aburwa nɛ baa dii so a yɔ kabunagboŋ ere ase. Kelargato be esoso be kabunagboŋ na be asheŋ

english_verse: Then the man took me to the north gate. He measured it, and it was the same size as the others,
translation_verse: Kede be kaman, nɛ kanyɛn na naŋ keta ma n yɔ kelargato be esoso be kaba so be kabunagboŋ na ase nseŋ ya karga kumo. Kumo nɛ amo nɛ a ka na kikɛ daa sasa nna.

english_verse: and like the other inner gates, its entrance room faced the outer courtyard, and its walls were decorated with carvings of palm trees. Eight steps also led up to this gate. The Rooms for Sacrificing Animals
translation_verse: Ebu nɛ k wɔ kumo be kabuna to na daŋ kilgi n shoŋi kowushina be kelɔnɛ na nna, nɛ b wora abii be ndibi be nduli n deŋi kedɛdɛ na be egbalana na so. Atemprembi aburwa nɛ baa dii so a yɔ kabunagboŋ ere ase. Sarga be asɔbɔya be ebuana be asheŋ

english_verse: Inside the entrance room of the north gate, I saw four tables, two on each side of the room, where the animals to be sacrificed were killed. translation_verse: Eteebɔl ana e daa wɔ ebubi ere to. Amo be anyɔ daa yil kaba ko so nna nɛ anyɔ nɛ a ka malɛ daa yil kaba nyɔsopo so nɛ b daa mɔ esarga chɔɔso ŋko kulubi be sarga ŋko kewora n jija be sarga be asɔbɔya amo so.

translation_verse: B daŋ gbir ayir nɛ amo be nteŋ fo fanɛ enɔ be mparto egbalana na so nna ŋ kulti ebuana na to. Eteebɔl na malɛ so nɛ b daa ta esargablaŋ na a deŋi so. Bɔrɛmatapoana na be ebuana be asheŋ

translation_verse: Nɛ kanyɛn na kaŋɛ ma fanɛ ebu nɛ kumo be anishito bee shoŋi kelargato be kaseto be kaba so na la bɔrɛmatapoana nɛ baa shuŋ bɔrɛlambu na to na peya nna,

english_verse: and the building beside the south gate belongs to those who serve at the altar. All of them are descendants of Zadok and are the only Levites allowed to serve as the Lord's priests.” The Inner Courtyard and the Temple
translation_verse: nɛ kumo nɛ kumo alɛ be anishito be shoŋi kelargato be esoso be kaba so na malɛ la bɔrɛmatapoana nɛ baa shuŋ bɔrɛsure na ase na peya. english_verse: We walked to the porch of the temple, and the man measured the doorway of the porch: It was seven meters long, two and a half meters wide, and the distance from the doorway to the wall on either side was one and a half meters.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e naŋ keta ma n luri bɔrɛlambu na be kedɛdɛ na to nseŋ ya karga kumo be kabuna to na. Kumo be jeŋgreŋ daa sa fanɛ ayadra akpanu nna nɛ kumo be mparto malɛ daa sa fanɛ ayadra adunyɔ nɛ ana.

english_verse: Next we went into the main room of the temple. The man measured the doorway of this room: It was
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman, nɛ kanyɛn na naŋ keta ma n luri bɔrɛlambu na be ebu nɛ baa tre kakpa cheembi to. Nseŋ karga kumo be kedɛdɛ na, nɛ kumo be mparto daa sa fanɛ ayadra kudu,

english_verse: with carvings of winged creatures and had a carving of a palm tree between the creatures. These designs were carved into the paneling all the way around the two rooms.
translation_verse: B daa kɔ dimɛdi be anishito nna nɛ k bee keni abii be kedibi be nduli ko kaba ko so nseŋ naa kɔ buluŋ be anishito nɛ kumo alɛ bee keni abii be kedibi be nduli ko kaba pɔtɛ so. Aloŋ nɛ b daŋ yili kasawule n wora amo n ya fo akuloŋ na be awɔlto n deŋi egbalana na so ŋ kulti.

english_verse: Then the man walked to the far end of the temple's main room and said, “Beyond this doorway is the most holy place.” He first measured the doorway: It was one meter wide,
translation_verse: E ka loge, nɛ e karga ŋkpar to be ebu na gbagba; nɛ kumo be kaba kama so daa sa fanɛ ayadra adesa nɛ ana. Ebu ere daa wɔ nferinto be ebu na be anishito nna. Kumo be kaman nɛ e kaŋɛ ma: “Acheembiana to be kakpa cheembi nna na.” Ebuana nɛ baa ta asɔ a yili to na be asheŋ

english_verse: The walls of the temple were thicker at the bottom than at the top, which meant that the storage rooms on the top level were wider than those on the bottom level. Steps led from the bottom level, through the middle level, and into the top level.
translation_verse: Egbalana nɛ a kulti bɔrɛlambu na daa du pentren kaseto a chɔ esoso nna, a ŋini fanɛ esoso be ebuana na be epunto daŋ kpalga to a chɔ kaseto peya na. B daŋ pɔr atemprembi nna a dii so a yɔ nferinto nɛ awɔlto be asɔ be ebuana na to.

english_verse: The temple rested on a stone base three meters high, which also served as the foundation for the storage rooms.
translation_verse: Bɔrɛlambu na daa yil kejembu nɛ kumo be jeŋgreŋ daa sa fanɛ ayadra kudu nna. Kumo koŋwule na so nɛ ebuana na gba daa yil.

english_verse: The outside walls of the storage rooms were two and a half meters thick; there was nothing between these walls
translation_verse: Ebuana na be kaman to be egbalana na be pentren daŋ fo fanɛ ayadra aburwa. Efuli nɛ k daŋ dese egbalana ere

english_verse: One door led into the storage rooms on the north side of the temple, and another door led to those on the south side. The stone base extended two and a half meters beyond the outside wall of the storage rooms. The West Building and the Measurements of the Temple
translation_verse: Kabuna koŋwule daa bugi nna a yɔ asɔ be ebuana nɛ a wɔ a laŋɛ kelargato be esoso be kaba so nna nɛ kuko malɛ daa bugi a yɔ amo nɛ a wɔ a laŋɛ kelargato be kaseto be kaba so na. english_verse: The distance across the front of the temple, including the open space on either side, was also
translation_verse: E ka karga bɔrɛlambu na be anishito nɛ alɔnɛ nɛ a dese kumo be mba anyɔ na ase kikɛ nɛ kumo alɛ gba fo fanɛ ayadra kalfa nɛ adeshe nɛ aburwa.

english_verse: were paneled with wood all the way from the floor to the windows, while the doorways, the small windows, and the three side rooms were trimmed in wood.
translation_verse: kikɛ be epunto be egbalana na so hale n ya fo etokuro na. Ndibi na daa beeŋ tiŋ m buu etokuro na so gba kuraa.

english_verse: The doorframe to the temple's main room was in the shape of a rectangle. The Wooden Altar In front of the doorway to the most holy place was something that looked like
translation_verse: Kakpa cheembi be kukuloŋ na be jeŋgreŋ nɛ mparto kikɛ daa sasa nna. Ndibi be bɔrɛsure be asheŋ Kusɔ ko daa yil acheembiana to be kakpa cheembi na be kabuna to n duli

english_verse: a wooden altar. It was one and a half meters high and one meter square, and its corners, its base, and its sides were made of wood. The man said, “This is a reminder that the Lord is constantly watching over his temple.” The Doors in the Temple
translation_verse: bɔrɛsure nɛ b ta ndibi wora nna. Kumo be jeŋgreŋ daŋ fo fanɛ ayadra anu nɛ kumo be mparto malɛ daŋ fo fanɛ ayadra ana. Ndibi nɛ b ta n lɔŋɛ kumo be kaplɛkama.
