english_verse: Both the doorway to the main room of the temple and the doorway to the most holy place had two doors,
translation_verse: Kabuna ko daa wɔ kakpa nɛ baa bɔla a yɔ kakpa cheembi to nna nɛ kuko malɛ gba daa wɔ kakpa nɛ baa bɔla a yɔ acheembiana to be kakpa cheembi na to.

english_verse: and each door had two sections that could fold open.
translation_verse: Kabuna kama malɛ daa kɔ akuloŋ anyɔ nna.

english_verse: The doors to the main room were decorated with carvings of winged creatures and palm trees just like those on the walls, and there was a wooden covering over the porch just outside these doors.
translation_verse: B daŋ shɛl abii be ndibi nɛ asɔbɔya nɛ a kɔ aba fanɛ mbuibi na be nduli nna n deŋi kakpa cheembi be mbunaana na so fanɛ kananɛ b wora n deŋi egbalana na so na. Kumo be kaman nɛ b ta ndibi n ti kedɛdɛ na be kabuna ashi kowushina.

english_verse: The walls on each side of this porch had small windows and were also decorated with carvings of palm trees.
translation_verse: Kedɛdɛ na be akel to be egbalana na daa kɔ etokuro wurbi nna, nɛ b naŋ shɛl abii be ndibi be nduli n deŋi kumo alɛ gba be egbalana na so.

english_verse: After the man and I left the temple and walked back to the outer courtyard, he showed me a set of rooms on the north side of the west building. This set of rooms was
translation_verse: Kowu ere be nteŋ to daa sa fanɛ ayadra kalfa nɛ adeshe nɛ aburwa nna nɛ kumo be mparto malɛ daa sa fanɛ ayadra aduburwa nɛ ana.

english_verse: The rooms on the top level were narrower than those on the middle level, and the rooms on the middle level were narrower than those on the bottom level.
translation_verse: Ebuana nɛ a wɔ kowu ere be awɔlto gbagba na daa maŋ wɔ mpar n fo nferinto peya na so. Nferinto peya na malɛ daa maŋ naa wɔ mpar n fo kaseto peya na so.

english_verse: The rooms on the bottom level supported those on the two upper levels, and so these rooms did not have columns like other buildings in the courtyard.
translation_verse: Kowu na be ebuana nɛ a wɔ kaseto na e daa kɔ amo nɛ a wɔ esoso na to a yil, amoso esoso peya na daa maa kɔ eshabɔrɛ fanɛ nwu nɛ a ka a wɔ kelɔnɛ na so na.

english_verse: The door to these rooms was at the east end of the wall that stood in front of them.
translation_verse: Amo be akuloŋ daa shoŋi egbal nɛ k yil amo be anishito na be epeŋilarkpa be kaba so nna.

english_verse: The man then said to me: These rooms on the north and south sides of the temple are the sacred rooms where the Lord's priests will eat the most holy offerings. These offerings include the grain sacrifices, the sacrifices for sin, and the sacrifices to make things right.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ kanyɛn na kaŋɛ ma le: “Nwu anyɔ ere kikɛ la mboŋ cheembi nna. Amo to nɛ bɔrɛmatapoana nɛ baa luri a yɔ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be anishito na beeŋ baa chena a ji esargajibi cheembi na. Ebuana na ka du cheembi so, ndoŋ nɛ bɔrɛmatapoana na beeŋ baa ta ayu be esarga nɛ alubi be esarga nɛ kewora n jija be esarga cheembiana na a wɔtɔ.

english_verse: When the priests are ready to leave the temple, they must go through these rooms before they return to the outer courtyard. They must leave their sacred clothes in these rooms and put on regular clothes before going anywhere near other people. The Size of the Temple Area
translation_verse: Bɔrɛmatapoana na baa sha kelar bɔrɛlambu na to n yɔ kowushina be kelɔnɛ na so, a daga fanɛ b bɔla ebuana na ere to n lara bumo be asɔbuuso nɛ b buu n yɔ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be anishito na n nase ndoŋ pɔɛŋ nseŋ ta asɔbuuso pɔtɛ m buu n lar.” B ka karga bɔrɛlambu na be kowushina be asheŋ

english_verse: After the man had finished measuring the buildings inside the temple area, he took me back through the east gate and measured the wall around this area.
translation_verse: Kanyɛn na ka karga bɔrɛlambu na be epunto kikɛ n loge, nɛ e keta ma m bɔla kabunagboŋ nɛ k wɔ epeŋilarkpa be kaba so na to n lar nseŋ ya karga kumo be kowushina na kikɛ ŋ kulti.

english_verse: Then he measured the north side, the south side, and the west side of the wall, and they were each
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ e naŋ karga kumo be kelargato be esoso nɛ kaseto nɛ epeŋitɔrkpa be mbaana na kebɛso kebɛso. Kekama be nteŋ to daa sa fanɛ ayadra alfa aburwa nɛ ana nna,

english_verse: and so the temple area was a perfect square. The wall around this area separated what was sacred from what was ordinary.
translation_verse: a ŋini fanɛ bɔrɛlambu na be kakpa nɛ egbal na kulti na be kaba kama so daa sa fanɛ ayadra alfa aburwa nɛ adena nna. Egbal na daa barga mboŋ cheembi na nɛ amo nɛ a maŋ du cheembi na to nna.

english_verse: The man took me back to the east gate of the temple,
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ kanyɛn na keta ma n yɔ bɔrɛlambu na be kabunagboŋ nɛ k shoŋi epeŋilarkpa na ase.

english_verse: meters high, was the place where sacrifices were burned, and the four corners of the top section looked like the horns of a bull. The steps leading up to the altar were on the east side. The Dedication of the Altar
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nɛ n wu Israɛl be Ebɔrɛ na be kemaŋkura ka bee nyɛkpɛ pɛlpɛl n shi epeŋilarkpa a ba, nɛ Ebɔrɛ be ebɔl gbir fanɛ teku ka bee baga to na. Kusɔ kama nɛ k daa wɔ ndoŋ gba daŋ fulto nna a nyɛkpɛ.

english_verse: This vision was like the one I had seen when God came to destroy Jerusalem and like the one I had seen near the Chebar River. I immediately bowed with my face to the ground,
translation_verse: Bɔrɛdare nɛ n wu ere daa du fanɛ amo nɛ n daŋ wu jemanɛ nɛ Ebɔrɛ daŋ ba nɛ e ba mur kadegboŋ nɛ baa tre Jerusalɛm na nna nɛ jemanɛ nɛ n daa wɔ lɔr nɛ baa tre Kɛba na ase na nna. Ndoŋ nna nɛ n ta enɔ m buu anishi so nseŋ kurgi kumu n yuu to epul na to.

english_verse: The Lord's Spirit lifted me to my feet and carried me to the inner courtyard, where I saw that the Lord's glory had filled the temple.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman, nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be Kiyoyu keta ma n luri bɔrɛlambu na be laŋ be epunto be kelɔnɛ so nɛ n ya wu fanɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be kemaŋkura sɔ bɔrɛlambu na to kikɛ.

english_verse: But if the people and their kings stop worshiping other gods and tear down those memorials, I will live among them forever.
translation_verse: Naniere a daga fanɛ b yige kagbirshuŋ nseŋ lara bumo be bewuraana nɛ b wu na be kanyiŋi be asɔ nɛ b pɔr n yili na. Nɛ b wora loŋ, meeŋ ba ka wɔ bumo to mbaanaayɔ.”

english_verse: The temple area on my holy mountain must be kept sacred! This is the most important law about the temple. The Altar
translation_verse: Mbra nɛ k dese a laŋɛ bɔrɛlambu na be kaplɛa so e la fanɛ, kaboŋ nɛ k kulti kumo ashi kebee na be awɔlto na kikɛ la kakpa cheembi gbagba nna.” Bɔrɛsure na be asheŋ

english_verse: Each day for the next seven days, you must offer a goat and a bull and a ram as sacrifices for sin. These animals must have nothing wrong with them.
translation_verse: Karechɛ kama menyeeŋ baa ta kaboe nɛ gbolu nɛ kpakpa nɛ amo be kekama maŋ kɔ doro kikɛ amo so na a lara kulubi be sarga hale nɛ nchɛ ashunu e ya fo.

english_verse: The Lord God said: Ezekiel, son of man, after the altar is built, it must be dedicated by offering sacrifices on it and by splattering it with blood. Here is what you must do:
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na naŋ kaŋɛ ma le: “Dimɛdi pibi, nu kusɔ nɛ mee kaŋɛ fo ere. B kaŋ pɔr bɔrɛsure na n loge, menyeeŋ mɔ asɔbɔya n lara esarga kumo so, nseŋ ta ŋklaŋ na ŋ ŋmenyaŋ kumo so a ŋini fanɛ men ta kumo m bɔɔ Ebɔrɛ enɔ nna na.

english_verse: The priests of the Levi tribe from the family of Zadok the priest are the only ones who may serve in my temple—this is my law. So give them a young bull to slaughter as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: Bɔrɛmatapoana nɛ b shi Livai be yiri to nsaa la kanyɛn nɛ baa tre Zadɔk na be kanaŋ to be basa nawule e naŋ tiŋ m ba ma anishi to m ba shuŋ ma. Ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na be mbra nna na. Menyeeŋ sa bumo gbolu fɔlbi nɛ b ta n lara kulubi be sarga.

english_verse: Take some of the animal's blood and smear it on the four corners of the altar, some on the corners of the middle section, and some more on the rim around its edge. That will purify the altar and make it fit for offering sacrifices to me.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman, nɛ b suse kusɔbɔya na be ŋklaŋ ŋ gbiti bɔrɛsure na be akel to be nnɔso ana na so nɛ kumo be nferinto gba peya so nɛ kumo be ekarso kikɛ ŋ kulti. Kananɛ menyeeŋ wora nɛ k nyalɛ so nsaa la kusɔ nɛ menyeeŋ tiŋ a lara esarga kumo so a sa ma nna na.

english_verse: The next day, a goat that has nothing wrong with it must be offered as a sacrifice for sin. Purify the altar with its blood, just as you did with the blood of the bull.
translation_verse: Kumo be ŋklade nɛ men ta kaboenyɛnso nɛ doro kikɛ maŋ wɔ kumo so n lara kulubi be sarga. Menyeeŋ ta kumo be ŋklaŋ n lɔŋɛ bɔrɛsure na so fanɛ kananɛ men ta gbolu na be ŋklaŋ n wora na.

english_verse: Then choose a young bull and a young ram that have nothing wrong with them,
translation_verse: Men kaŋ wora loŋ n loge, nɛ men ta gbolu fɔlbi nɛ kpakpafɔlbi nɛ amo be kekama maŋ kɔ doro kikɛ kumo so

english_verse: and bring them to my temple. The priests will sprinkle salt on them and offer them as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: m ba sa ma. Bɔrɛmatapoana na beeŋ mɔ amo nseŋ wora nfɔl n fur amo so n chɔɔ amo n lara sarga n sa ma.

english_verse: The priests will purify the altar during those days, so that it will be acceptable to me and ready to use.
translation_verse: Nchɛ ashunu nɛ bɔrɛmatapoana na beeŋ ta n lɔŋɛ bɔrɛsure na so nɛ k nyalɛ so n sa ma.

english_verse: From then on, the priests will use this altar to offer sacrifices to please me and sacrifices to ask my blessing. Then I will be pleased with the people of Israel. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Nchɛ ashunu na kaŋ choŋ, bɔrɛmatapoana na beeŋ fara a lara esarga chɔɔso nɛ kɔnɔkoŋwule be esarga bɔrɛsure na so. Saŋɛ na so nɛ ma kagbene e fuli Israɛl be basa so. Kusɔ nɛ ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ nna na.”

english_verse: The man took me back to the outer courtyard, near the east gate of the temple area. I saw that the doors to this gate were closed.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ kanyɛn na naŋ keta ma n yɔ kowushina be kelɔnɛ na so a mata bɔrɛlambu na be kabunagboŋ nɛ k wɔ epeŋilarkpa be kaba so na. Nɛ n wu fanɛ kumo be akuloŋ na daŋ ti nna.

english_verse: The Lord said: I, the Lord God of Israel, came through this gate, so it must remain closed forever! No one must ever use it.
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ ma le: “Kabuna ere nɛ ma Enyɛnpe, Israɛl be Ebɔrɛ na bɔla to n luri bɔrɛlambu na to, amoso, a daga fanɛ k baŋ ti loŋ mbaanaayɔ! Esa kama e sa maŋ naŋ bɔla kumo to n luri kikɛ.

english_verse: The ruler of Israel may come here to eat a sacrificial meal that has been offered to me, but he must use only the entrance room of this gate. People Who Are Not Allowed in the Temple
translation_verse: Israɛl be ewura beeŋ tiŋ m ba nfe m ba ji ajibi nɛ b ta n lara sarga n sa ma, ama a daga fanɛ e bɔla kabunagboŋ ere be kedɛdɛ na to nna n luri ŋko n lar.” Basa nɛ b maŋ daga keluri bɔrɛlambu na to be asheŋ

english_verse: Then the man took me through the north gate to the front of the temple. I saw that the brightness of the Lord's glory had filled the temple, and I immediately bowed with my face to the ground.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ kanyɛn na keta ma m bɔla kelargato be esoso be kabuna na to n yɔ bɔrɛlambu na be anishito nɛ n to kenishi ŋ keni nseŋ wu fanɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ be kemaŋkura bɔlɔ bɔrɛlambu na to. Ndoŋ nna nɛ n ta ma enɔana m buu ma anishi so nseŋ kurgi kumu n yuu to.

english_verse: The Lord said: Ezekiel, son of man, I am going to give you the laws for my temple. So pay attention and listen carefully to what kind of people are allowed to come in the temple, and what kind are not.
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ ma le: “Dimɛdi pibi, Ezikɛl, shin nɛ fo lakal e baa wɔ kusɔ kama nɛ feeŋ wu nsaa nu ashi nfe so. Mbraana nɛ a wɔ bɔrɛlambu na to nɛ mee sha kekaŋɛ fo na. Baa de so nɛnɛ a nyi basa nɛ baaŋ tiŋ n luri nɛ bumo nɛ b maaŋ tiŋ n luri bɔrɛlambu na to.

english_verse: Tell those rebellious people of Israel: I, the Lord God, command you to stop your evil ways!
translation_verse: Kaŋɛ Israɛl be basa nɛ b kini ma nseŋ lar ma kaman na fanɛ ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na maŋ naa ba nɛ n sɔ ekishisheŋ nɛ baa wora na kikɛ.

english_verse: My temple has been disgraced, because you have let godless, stubborn foreigners come here when sacrifices are being offered to me. You have sinned and have broken our solemn agreement.
translation_verse: B wora eyurpisheŋ n jija ma bɔrɛlambu ŋkpal b ka shin nɛ befɔ nɛ b maa ŋana Ebɔrɛ luri kumo to jemanɛ nɛ baa lara esarga a sa ma na so. Amoso, ma basa wora kulubi nseŋ da ma nɛ bumo be kɔnɔkoŋwule be ŋkre na so.

english_verse: Instead of following the proper ways to worship me, you have put foreigners in charge of worship at my temple.
translation_verse: Bumo gbagba ka beeŋ baa wora asɔ nɛ a daga a laŋɛ esarga cheembi na kaplɛa so ashi bɔrɛlambu na to so na, befɔ nɛ b ta loŋ be kushuŋ nna n sa.

english_verse: And so I, the Lord God, say that no godless foreigner who disobeys me will be allowed in my temple. This includes any foreigner living in Israel. The Levites Are Punished The Lord said:
translation_verse: Amoso kusɔ nɛ ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na, bee kaŋɛ e la fanɛ efɔ kama nɛ e maa ŋana Ebɔrɛ nsaa maa nu a sa ma maŋ daga keluri ma bɔrɛlambu to, hale efɔ nɛ e chena Israɛl be basa na to gba maŋ daga keluri kumo to.” Livaiebi ko kaa nya kasogberge be asheŋ

english_verse: Some of the Levites turned their backs on me and joined the other people of Israel in worshiping idols. So these Levites must be punished!
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na naŋ kaŋɛ ma le: “Mee sha kegberge Livaiebi nɛ b tu Israɛl be basa na ŋ kini ma nseŋ ya shuŋ agbirana na kusoe nna na.

english_verse: They will still be allowed to serve me as temple workers by guarding the gates and by killing the animals to be sacrificed and by helping the worshipers.
translation_verse: B kraa beeŋ tiŋ a shuŋ bɔrɛlambu na to fanɛ basa nɛ baa keni mbunaana na so nseŋ naŋ tiŋ n chɛ basa na to m mɔ asɔbɔya nɛ b ta a lara esarga na.

english_verse: But because these Levites served the people of Israel when they worshiped idols, I, the Lord God, promise that the Levites will be punished. They did not stop the Israelites from sinning,
translation_verse: Ama ŋkpal Livaiebi ere ka chɛ Israɛl be basa na to jemanɛ nɛ b daa shuŋ agbirana na so, ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na bee nase kɔnɔ nna fanɛ Livaiebi na beeŋ nya kasogberge.

english_verse: and now I will no longer let the Levites serve as my priests or come near anything sacred to me. They must suffer shame and disgrace for their disgusting sins.
translation_verse: B maaŋ naŋ tiŋ n shuŋ ma fanɛ bɔrɛmatapoana ŋko n yɔ ma kusɔ cheembi kama ase ŋko n luri bɔrɛlambu na to be acheembiana to be kakpa cheembi na to. Ekishisheŋ nɛ b wora na be kasogberge nna na.

english_verse: They will be responsible for all the hard work that must be done in the temple. Rules for Priests The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ashuŋ kpakpaso nawule nɛ mee sa bumo ekpa fanɛ b baa shuŋ ashi bɔrɛlambu na to.” Mbraana nɛ a wɔtɔ n sa bɔrɛmatapoana be asheŋ

english_verse: The priests of the Levi tribe who are descendants of Zadok the priest were faithful to me, even when the rest of the Israelites turned away. And so, these priests will continue to serve as my priests and to offer the fat and the blood of sacrifices.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman, nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ le: “Livai be yiri to be bɔrɛmatapoana nɛ b shi kanyɛn nɛ baa tre Zadɔk na be kabuna na bre daŋ maŋ kini ma kushuŋ bɔrɛlambu na to nseŋ ya shuŋ agbirana jemanɛ nɛ Israɛl be basa na daŋ kini ma na. Amoso bumo e naŋ tiŋ m ba ma anishi to m ba shuŋ ma fanɛ bɔrɛmatapoana nseŋ ta asɔbɔya be nfɔ nɛ ŋklaŋ n lara esarga.

english_verse: They will come into my temple, where they will offer sacrifices at my altar and lead others in worship.
translation_verse: Zadɔk be kabuna ebi na nawule e naŋ tiŋ n luri bɔrɛlambu na to n shuŋ bɔrɛsure na ase nseŋ naŋ tiŋ n juŋkpar basa nɛ baa shuŋ ma na.

english_verse: When they come to the inner courtyard, they must wear their linen priestly clothes. My priests must never wear anything made of wool when they are on duty in this courtyard or in the temple.
translation_verse: A daga fanɛ b buu bɔrɛmatapoana be epiŋi lela na nna n luri bɔrɛlambu na be epun to be kelɔnɛ na so. A maŋ daga fanɛ b baa buu asɔbuuso nɛ b ta ateebi n lue jemanɛ nɛ b wɔ kushuŋ to ashi epun to be kelɔnɛ na so ŋko bɔrɛlambu na gbagba to.

english_verse: Even their turbans and underwear must be made of linen to keep my priests from sweating when they work.
translation_verse: A daga fanɛ b baa buu ago be kechɛbi be asɔbuuso nna nsaa chɛ ago be achɛbi be eneemu, saŋɛ na so b maaŋ baa pa kebleŋ jemanɛ nɛ baa shuŋ bumo be kabɔrɛmata be kushuŋ na.

english_verse: And before they leave to join the other people in the outer courtyard, they must take off their priestly clothes, then place them in the sacred rooms and put on their regular clothes. That way, no one will touch their sacred clothes and be harmed.
translation_verse: Pɔɛŋ nɛ b lar n yɔ kowushina be kelɔnɛ na so ashi kakpa nɛ basa wɔ na, a daga fanɛ b lara epiŋi nɛ b buu a shuŋ bɔrɛlambu na to na n nase ebu cheembiana na to nna. Kumo be kaman nɛ b ta asɔbuuso pɔtɛ m buu n lar, saŋɛ na so bumo be asɔbuuso cheembi na maaŋ bar tɔrɔ basa so.

english_verse: Priests must never shave their heads when they are mourning. But they must keep their hair properly trimmed and not let it grow too long.
translation_verse: Bɔrɛmatapoana maŋ daga fanɛ b she bumo be emin ŋko n shin nɛ e daŋ tenteŋ. A daga fanɛ b baa digi amo so nna.

english_verse: They must not drink wine before going to the inner courtyard.
translation_verse: Bɔrɛmatapoana maŋ daga fanɛ b nuu yabra pɔɛŋ nseŋ luri bɔrɛlambu na be epunto be kelɔnɛ na to.

english_verse: A priest must not marry a divorced woman; he can marry only a virgin from Israel or the widow of another priest.
translation_verse: Bɔrɛmatapowura kikɛ maŋ daga fanɛ e ta eche nɛ mo kul kini mo. A daga fanɛ e ta Israɛl to be eche nɛ e maŋ nyi enyɛn ŋko eche nɛ mo kul daa la bɔrɛmatapo nseŋ wu ŋ ka nawule nna.

english_verse: Touching a dead body will make a person unclean. So a priest must not go near a dead body, unless it is one of his parents or children, or his brother or unmarried sister.
translation_verse: Bɔrɛmatapowura maŋ daga fanɛ e beta kebuni kikɛ nseŋ wora eyurpi daŋkare be ekpa so, ama k baa la mo tuto ŋko mo nio ŋko mo pibi ŋko mo niopibi nyɛnso ŋko mo niopibi cheso nɛ e maa kil be kebuni nna.

english_verse: If a priest touches a dead body, he is unclean and must go through a ceremony to make himself clean. Then seven days later,
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e ka naŋ nyalɛ so daŋkare be ekpa so, a daga fanɛ e jo nchɛ ashunu pɔɛŋ

english_verse: he must go to the inner courtyard of the temple and offer a sacrifice for sin. After that, he may once again serve as my priest. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: nseŋ yɔ bɔrɛlambu na be epunto be kelɔnɛ na to n ya lara sarga nɛ k beeŋ shin nɛ e nyalɛ so, saŋɛ na so e beeŋ naŋ tiŋ a shuŋ bɔrɛlambu na to. Ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na, e kaŋɛ na.

english_verse: Instead, they will receive part of the grain sacrifices, as well as part of the sacrifices for sin and sacrifices to make things right. They will also be given everything in Israel that has been completely dedicated to me.
translation_verse: Ayu be esarga nɛ kulubi be esarga nɛ kewora n jija be esarga kikɛ beeŋ baa la bɔrɛmatapoana be asɔ jiso nna. Kumo be kaman, kusɔ kama nɛ b kɛ ma ashi Israɛl to kikɛ gba la bumo peya nna.

english_verse: The first part of every harvest will belong to the priests. They will also receive part of all special gifts and offerings the Israelites bring to me. And whenever any of my people bake bread, they will give their first loaf as an offering to the priests, and I will bless the homes of the people when they do this.
translation_verse: Adɔjibi kama nɛ b juŋkpar n teŋi nɛ kusɔ kama nɛ b ta n sa ma beeŋ baa la bɔrɛmatapoana na peya nna. Jemanɛ kikɛ nɛ basa na wora ebodobodo, a daga fanɛ b ta bodobodo nɛ b juŋkpar n wora na n sa bɔrɛmatapoana fanɛ kakɛ nɛ k bee yɔ Ebɔrɛ kutɔ, saŋɛ na so ma nɛfa beeŋ baa wɔ bumo be elaŋana so.

english_verse: Priests must not eat any bird or animal that dies a natural death or that has been killed by a wild animal.
translation_verse: Bɔrɛmatapoana maŋ daga fanɛ b ji kusɔbɔya ŋko kabuibi nɛ k wu kpi ŋko kumo nɛ kusɔbɔya pɔtɛ mɔ n ji ŋ ka be eblaŋ.”

english_verse: The Festival of Shelters will begin on the fifteenth day of the seventh month and will continue for seven days. On each day of this festival, the ruler will provide the same number of animals that he did each day during Passover, as well as the same amount of grain and olive oil for the sacrifices.
translation_verse: Abuu to be kebaawɔ be Kejigboŋ na bee fara kufɔl shunusopo na be kachɛ kuduanusopo na nseŋ keta loŋ n ya fo nchɛnshunu. Kananɛ ewura na baaŋ lara asɔbɔya nɛ ayu nɛ ɔlifs be ŋku karechɛ kikɛ jemanɛ nɛ b daa ji Kebansonchoŋ be Kejigboŋ na, aloŋ nɛ e beeŋ naŋ lara amo kede gba to.”

english_verse: kilometers wide. This will belong to the people of Israel and will include the city of Jerusalem. Land for Israel's Ruler The Lord said:
translation_verse: Men ku kakpa cheembi na be bargato, nɛ kumo be nteŋ to fo emayɛl ashunu nɛ kumo be mparto malɛ fo emayɛl asa m pɔr bɔrɛlambu na n yili so. Ndoŋ beeŋ baa la kakpa cheembi na kikɛ be acheembiakpa.

english_verse: The regions west and east of my sacred land and the city of Jerusalem will belong to the ruler of Israel. He will be given the region between the western edge of my land and the Mediterranean Sea, and between the eastern edge of my land and the Jordan River. This will mean that the length of his property will be the same as the sections of land given to the tribes. This property will belong to every ruler of Israel, so they will always be fair to my people and will let them live peacefully in the land given to their tribes. Israel's Rulers Must Be Honest
translation_verse: Kakpa nɛ esa nɛ e bee ji kuwura na beeŋ baa kɔ ashi Israɛl be kasawule so nna na, saŋɛ na so e maaŋ baa nyaŋ basa na, nseŋ shin nɛ efuli na be kasawule nɛ k ka na e baa la Israɛl be eyiriana na peya. Mbraana nɛ a wɔtɔ n sa ewura na be asheŋ

english_verse: The Lord God said: You leaders of Israel have cheated and abused my people long enough! I want you to stop sinning and start doing what is right and fair. You must never again force my people off their own land. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ade be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na naŋ kaŋɛ le: “Fo nɛ fee ji Israɛl so kuwura na wora alubi n chɛr pasaa! Yige fo kebagato nɛ kanyaŋ be asheŋ na nsaa wora kusɔ nɛ k daga nseŋ bɔla ekpa. A maŋ daga fanɛ fo naŋ ju ma basa n lar bumo be kasawule so kikɛ. Ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na e naa kaŋɛ fo le na.

english_verse: The ephah will be the standard dry measure, and the bath will be the standard liquid measure. Their size will be based on the homer, which will equal ten ephahs or ten baths.
translation_verse: Ekurwa nɛ ebɔtɛ nɛ ekɔlba nɛ egalɔn nɛ men kɔ a karga asɔ a fa na kikɛ maŋ daga fanɛ a baa la kapuni b kasɔkarga be asɔ. Amo kikɛ daga fanɛ a baa la asɔ nɛ ekama yirda fanɛ amo e la kashenteŋ be asɔ nɛ b kɔ a karga asɔ a fa nna.

english_verse: The same ceremony must also be done on the seventh day of the month, so that anyone who sins accidentally or without knowing it will be forgiven, and so that my temple will remain holy.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ men naŋ wora loŋ gbagba kufɔl na be kachɛ shunusopo na, saŋɛ na so nɛ esa ko nɛ e maŋ kute ŋko e maŋ nyi nseŋ wora kulubi beeŋ nya mbe alubi be ketampaŋ. Kananɛ menyeeŋ wora nɛ ma bɔrɛlambu e baa du cheembi nna na.

english_verse: Leaders of Israel, the people must bring you one sixtieth of their grain harvests as offerings to me.
translation_verse: A daga fanɛ men barga men be ayu nɛ menyeeŋ teŋi to ntunshe nna nseŋ ta katuŋ koŋwule m ba sa ma fanɛ kakɛ lela.

english_verse: They will also bring one percent of their olive oil. These things will be measured according to the bath, and ten baths is the same as one homer or one cor.
translation_verse: Menyeeŋ barga men be ɔlifs be ŋku to ntuŋ kalfa, nseŋ ta katuŋ koŋwule m ba sa ma. Menyeeŋ baa karga amo ekɔlba nɛ egalɔn to nna. Galɔn koŋwule malɛ la ekɔlba ashunu nna.

english_verse: But during New Moon Festivals, Sabbath celebrations, and other religious feasts, you leaders will be responsible for providing animals for the sacrifices, as well as the grain and wine. All these will be used for the sacrifices for sin, the grain sacrifices, the sacrifices to please me, and those to ask my blessing. I will be pleased and will forgive the sins of my people. The Festivals (Exodus
translation_verse: Mo e daga fanɛ e yili Israɛl be efuli na kikɛ be katelamu n lara asɔbɔya nɛ baaŋ ta n lara esarga chɔɔso nɛ baaŋ ta n lara ayu be esarga nɛ yabra belbelso be esarga na kikɛ jemanɛ nɛ baa ji Kufɔl Popɔr be Kachɛgboŋ nɛ Kewushiachɛ na nɛ nchɛgboŋ nɛ a ka na kikɛ na. Mo koŋwule na e daga fanɛ e lara asɔbɔya nɛ b ta n lara alubi nɛ ayu nɛ sarga chɔɔso nɛ kɔnɔkoŋwule be esarga nɛ e kpra Israɛl be basa be alubi.” Nchɛgboŋana na be asheŋ

english_verse: Each day of the festival he is to bring seven bulls and seven rams as sacrifices to please me, and he must bring a goat as a sacrifice for sin. These animals must have nothing wrong with them.
translation_verse: Karechɛ kama, ewura na beeŋ baa mɔ egbolu ashunu nɛ ekpakpa ashunu nɛ e maŋ kɔ doro kikɛ a lara sarga chɔɔso n ya fo nchɛ kachɛ shunusopo nɛ baaŋ ji kejigboŋ na n loge na. Mo alɛ beeŋ naa mɔ kaboenyɛn a lara alubi be sarga karechɛ kikɛ.

english_verse: The Lord God said: On the first day of the first month, a young bull that has nothing wrong with it must be offered as a sacrifice to purify the temple.
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman, nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na naŋ kaŋɛ le: “Menyeeŋ ta gbolu nɛ doro kikɛ maŋ wɔ kumo so n lara sarga n lɔŋɛ bɔrɛlambu na so kufɔl juŋkparso na be kachɛ sososo na.

english_verse: The priest will take some blood from this sacrifice and smear it on the doorposts of the temple, as well as on the four corners of the altar and on the doorposts of the gates that lead into the inner courtyard.
translation_verse: Bɔrɛmatapowura na beeŋ suse kulubi be sarga be kusɔbɔya na be ŋklaŋ na be ako ŋ gbiti bɔrɛlambu na be akuloŋ be ndibi na nɛ bɔrɛsure na be mba ana na nɛ epunto be kelɔnɛ be akuloŋ be ndibi na.

english_verse: Beginning on the fourteenth day of the first month, and continuing for seven days, everyone will celebrate Passover and eat bread made without yeast.
translation_verse: Kufɔl juŋkparso na be kachɛ kuduanasopo na nɛ menyeeŋ fara Kebansonchoŋ be Kejigboŋ na be kesheŋ wora. Nchɛnshunu nɛ ekama beeŋ ta n ji bodobodo nɛ a maŋ kɔ yisi.

english_verse: On the first day, the ruler will bring a bull to offer as a sacrifice for his sins and for the sins of the people.
translation_verse: Ewura na beeŋ mɔ gbolu n lara mo gbagba nɛ basa na kikɛ be alubi be sarga kejigboŋ na be kachɛ sososo na.

english_verse: He will also provide nine kilograms of grain and three liters of olive oil to be offered with each bull and each ram.
translation_verse: E beeŋ ta ayu cheenshigboŋ be bargato nɛ ɔlifs be ŋku galɔn koŋwule n ti gbolu kama nɛ kpakpa kama nɛ e beeŋ mɔ n lara sarga na so n lara sarga.

english_verse: The Lord said: The east gate of the inner courtyard must remain closed during the six working days of each week. But on the Sabbath and on the first day of the month, this gate will be opened.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na kaŋɛ le: “A daga fanɛ bɔrɛlambu na be epunto be kelɔnɛ na be kabuna nɛ k wɔ epeŋilarkpa be kaba so na ka ti so nna a yil nchɛnshe nɛ menyee shuŋ na kikɛ, ama men bugi kumo n yili Kewushiachɛ na nɛ Kufɔl popɔr be kachɛ juŋkparso na bre.

english_verse: Israel's ruler will go from the outer courtyard into the entrance room of this gate and stand in the doorway while the priest offers sacrifices to ask my blessing and sacrifices to please me. The ruler will bow with his face to the ground to show that he has worshiped me. Then he will leave, and the gate will remain open until evening.
translation_verse: Jemanɛ nɛ bɔrɛmatapo na malɛ bee lara ewura be sarga chɔɔso nɛ kɔnɔkoŋwule be esarga na Israɛl be ewura na beeŋ shi kowushina be kelɔnɛ na so m bɔla kabuna to be ebu na to n luri m ba yili m mata kabunagboŋ na be ndibi na; ŋ gbir m bunyaŋ ma nseŋ bɛta m bɔla kabunagboŋ na to n lar. Kabuna na beeŋ bugi n yili loŋ hale n ya fo kaaseso.

english_verse: Each Sabbath and on the first day of each month, the people of Israel must also come to the east gate and worship me.
translation_verse: Kewushiachɛ nɛ Kufɔl popɔr be kachɛ juŋkparso kikɛ, basa na kikɛ daga fanɛ b ba gbir m bunyaŋ ma ashi kabunagboŋ na ase.

english_verse: On the Sabbath, the ruler will bring six lambs and one ram to be offered as sacrifices to please me. There must be nothing wrong with any of these animals.
translation_verse: Ewura na beeŋ bar mbolpɔ fɔlbi ashe nɛ kpakpa nɛ e maŋ kɔ doro kikɛ m ba lara sarga chɔɔso kewushiachɛ na.

english_verse: With the ram, he is to offer nine kilograms of grain, and with each of the lambs, he can offer as much as he wants. He must also offer three liters of olive oil with every nine kilograms of grain.
translation_verse: E beeŋ ta ayu cheenshigboŋ be bargato n ti kpakpa kama so nseŋ ta kusɔ kama nɛ e bee sha n ti mbolpɔ fɔlbi na be kekama so nna m ba. Mo alɛ beeŋ naŋ ta ɔlifs be ŋku galɔn koŋwule n ti ayu cheenshigboŋ be bargato na so nna m ba.

english_verse: The ruler is to bring six lambs, a bull, and a ram to be offered as sacrifices at the New Moon Festival. There must be nothing wrong with any of these animals.
translation_verse: Kufɔl popɔr be kachɛgboŋachɛ na bre, ewura na beeŋ lara gbolu fɔlbi nɛ mbolpɔ fɔlbi ashe nɛ kpakpa nɛ e maŋ kɔ doro kikɛ nna.

english_verse: With the bull and the ram, he is to offer nine kilograms of grain, and with each of the lambs, he can offer as much as he wants. He must also offer three liters of olive oil with every nine kilograms of grain.
translation_verse: Ewura na beeŋ ta ayu cheenshigboŋ be bargato n ti gbolu nɛ kpakpa kama nɛ e lara na so nseŋ ta kusɔ kama nɛ e bee sha n ti mbolpɔ fɔlbi na be kekama malɛ so m ba. A daga fanɛ e ta ɔlifs be ŋku galɔn koŋwule n ti ayu cheenshigboŋ be bargato kama nɛ e beeŋ bar na so nna m ba.

english_verse: The ruler must come through the entrance room of the east gate and leave the same way.
translation_verse: Ekpa nɛ ewura na beeŋ bɔla n luri kabuna to be ebu nɛ k wɔ epeŋilarkpa be kabunagboŋ ase na to na so nɛ e beeŋ bɔla so n lar kumo to.

english_verse: When my people come to worship me during any festival, they must always leave by the opposite gate from which they came: Those who come in the north gate must leave by the south gate, and those who come in the south gate must leave by the north gate.
translation_verse: Ama jemanɛ kama nɛ basa na ba nɛ b ba bunyaŋ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na nchɛgboŋana na be kekama to, bekama nɛ baaŋ bɔla kelargato be esoso be kaba so be kabunagboŋ na to n luri na daga fanɛ b bɔla kelargato be kaseto be kaba so be kabunagboŋ na to nna n lar. Ekama e sa maŋ kaŋ naŋ bɔla kabuna nɛ e bɔla to n luri na to n lar, ama kabuna nɛ k wɔ kumo nɛ e bɔla to n luri na be kaba ndoŋ na.

english_verse: Their ruler will come in at the same time they do and leave at the same time they leave.
translation_verse: Jemanɛ nɛ basa na bee luri na a daga fanɛ ewura na gba e luri nseŋ na ŋ lar jemanɛ nɛ basa na naa lar na.

english_verse: At all other festivals and celebrations, nine kilograms of grain will be offered with a bull, and nine kilograms will be offered with a ram. The worshipers can offer as much grain as they want with each lamb. Three liters of olive oil must be offered with every nine kilograms of grain.
translation_verse: Kejigboŋachɛ nɛ nchɛgboŋachɛ kikɛ, ayu cheenshigboŋ be bargato nɛ esa bee ta a ti gbolu ŋko kpakpa kikɛ so a lara sarga, nsaa ta kusɔ kama nɛ e bee sha a ti mbolpɔ fɔlbi na be kekama malɛ so a lara sarga. Amo be kaman nɛ e ta ɔlifs be ŋku galɔn koŋwule n ti ayu cheenshigboŋ be bargato na so m ba.

english_verse: If the ruler voluntarily offers a sacrifice to please me or to ask my blessing, the east gate of the inner courtyard will be opened for him. He will offer his sacrifices just as he does on each Sabbath; then he will leave, and the gate will be closed.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ ewura na bee sha kelara mo gbagba be keparso be sarga chɔɔso ŋko kɔnɔkoŋwule be sarga n sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na baŋ bugi bɔrɛlambu na be epunto be kelɔnɛ na be kabunagboŋ nɛ k wɔ epeŋilarkpa be kaba so na n sa mo nɛ e luri. Kananɛ e baa lara Kewushiachɛ be esarga na nɛ e beeŋ lara kede gba. E kaŋ wora n loge nseŋ lar na nɛ b ti kabunagboŋ na.” Karechɛ kikɛ be esarga be asheŋ

english_verse: Along with it, two kilograms of fine flour mixed with a liter of olive oil must be offered as a grain sacrifice. This law will never change—
translation_verse: Menyi alɛ kraa beeŋ bar nyifu lela fanɛ kurwa anu nɛ ɔlifs be ŋku kɔlba nɛ barga kachipurso kikɛ m ba lara ajibi be sarga. Kebaa lara le be esarga ere a sa Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be mbraana ere baa wɔtɔ nna a yɔ, a maa chɛrga kikɛ.

english_verse: The Lord God said: If the ruler of Israel gives some of his land to one of his children, it will belong to the ruler's child as part of the family property.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na naŋ kaŋɛ le kenishipereso: “Nɛ fanɛ ewura na ku kasawule nɛ e kɔ na be kaba ŋ kɛ mbe mbia to be eko, k beeŋ baa la kebia na peya fanɛ mbe kanaŋ to be kapetɛsɔ.

english_verse: But if the ruler gives some of his land to one of his servants, the land will belong to the servant until the Year of Celebration, when it will be returned to the ruler. Only the ruler's children can keep what is given to them.
translation_verse: Ama nɛ fanɛ ewura na ku mbe kasawule ŋ kɛ esa kama nɛ e bee shuŋ mo, kumo ere k beeŋ naŋ bɛta ŋ ki ewura na peya kafɛ nɛ baa bɛta basa be mpetɛsɔ a sa bumo na to. Kasawule na la mbe kapetɛ nna. Mo nɛ mbe mbia nawule e naaŋ tiŋ a wɔ kumo mbaanaayɔ.

english_verse: The man who was showing me the temple then took me back to the inner courtyard. We walked to the south side of the courtyard and stopped at the door to the sacred rooms that belonged to the priests. He showed me more rooms at the western edge of the courtyard
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ kanyɛn nɛ e daŋ keta ma a ŋini bɔrɛlambu na, naŋ keta ma n yɔ ebuana nɛ a bee shoŋi kelargato be esoso be kaba so a mata kabunagboŋ nɛ k wɔ bɔrɛlambu na be epunto be kelɔnɛ na be kelargato be kaseto be kaba so na. Ebuana na daa la ebu cheembiana n sa bɔrɛmatapoana na nna. Ndoŋ nna nɛ e teŋi enɔ n ŋini kaboŋ ko ashi ebuana na be epeŋitɔrkpa be kaba so

english_verse: Around the inside of these smaller courtyards was a low wall of stones, and against the wall were places to build fires.
translation_verse: B daŋ ta ajembu m pɔr egbal ŋ kulti amo be kekama nna nseŋ yuu asure m mata egbal na.

english_verse: The man said, “These are the kitchens where the temple workers will boil the meat that worshipers offer as sacrifices.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ kanyɛn na naŋ kaŋɛ ma le: “Edaŋɛkpaana nɛ bɔrɛlambu na to be beshumpo bee daŋɛ esarga nɛ basa na bee lara na nna na.”

english_verse: The man took me back to the temple, where I saw a stream flowing from under the entrance. It began in the south part of the temple, where it ran past the altar and continued east through the courtyard.
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ kanyɛn na bɛta ma n yɔ bɔrɛlambu na to, ndoŋ nɛ n wu kabombi ko ka bee shile kabuna na be kaseto a yɔ epeŋitɔrkpa be kaba so. K fara bɔrɛlambu na be kelargato be esoso na nna a shile m ba bɔla bɔrɛsure na ase m baŋɛ kelɔnɛ na to a yɔ epeŋilarkpa be kaba so.

english_verse: We walked out of the temple area through the north gate and went around to the east gate. I saw the small stream of water flowing east from the south side of the gate.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ kanyɛn na naŋ keta ma m bɔla kelargato be esoso be kabunagboŋ na to n lar bɔrɛlambu na to nseŋ juŋkpar ma ŋ kulti n ya fo kabunagboŋ nɛ k bee shoŋi epeŋilarkpa na. Ndoŋ nɛ n wu kabombi ko ka bee shile kabunagboŋ na be kelargato be kaseto be kaba so na.

english_verse: The man said, “Ezekiel, son of man, pay attention to what you've seen.” We walked to the riverbank,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ kanyɛn na kaŋɛ ma le: “Dimɛdi pibi, Ezikɛl, baa de asheŋ ere kikɛ so nɛnɛ.” Kumo be kaman nɛ e keta ma n laŋɛ n yɔ kabombi na be ekarso,

english_verse: where I saw dozens of trees on each side.
translation_verse: nɛ n ya wu fanɛ ndibi damta daa yil kabombi na be mba anyɔ na kikɛ so nna.

english_verse: Wherever this water flows, there will be all kinds of animals and fish, because it will bring life and fresh water to the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Kaplɛkama nɛ nchu na beeŋ shile m bɔla, asɔbɔya nɛ ekɔrɔtɔ be yiri yiri beeŋ ba ndoŋ, ŋkpal manɛ so kabombi na beeŋ bar ŋkpa nɛ nchu nɛ e walɛ kenuu m ba wɔtɔ Teku Wuso na to.

english_verse: From En-Gedi to Eneglaim, people will fish in the sea and dry their nets along the coast. There will be as many kinds of fish in the Dead Sea as there are in the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Yili achubu nɛ baa tre Ɛngɛdi na hale n ya fo achubu nɛ baa tre Ɛneglem na, basa beeŋ baa pɛ ekɔrɔtɔ teku na to nsaa fata bumo be ashewu kumo be ekarso. Teku Wuso na beeŋ nya ekɔrɔtɔ be yiri yiri fanɛ kananɛ Mɛditerenia be Teku kɔ amo na.

english_verse: Fruit trees will grow all along this river and produce fresh fruit every month. The leaves will never dry out, because they will always have water from the stream that flows from the temple, and they will be used for healing people. The Borders of the Land
translation_verse: Ndibi be yiri yiri beeŋ kɔr a yil kabombi na be kaba kama so a sa kusɔ jiso. Amo be afantaŋ maa ba nɛ aba bolo, amo alɛ maaŋ yige kebaasɔr kikɛ. Kufɔl kikɛ a beeŋ baa kɔ asɔrso popɔr, ŋkpal manɛ so a bee nya nchu nɛ a bee shi bɔrɛlambu na to nna. Ndibi na be asɔrso beeŋ baa la ajibi nɛ amo be afantaŋ malɛ e baa chɛ basa alɔ.” Kasawule na be Egbaŋ ana be asheŋ

english_verse: The Lord God said to the people of Israel: When the land is divided among the twelve tribes of Israel, the Joseph tribe will receive two shares. Divide the land equally, because I promised your ancestors that this land would someday belong to their descendants. These are the borders of the land:
translation_verse: N daŋ bɔ ntaŋ n nase kɔnɔ n sa menyi nananyɛnana fanɛ meeŋ sa bumo kasawule ere nɛ k baa la bumo peya; amoso men barga kumo to dede n sa abar.

english_verse: Berothah, and Sibraim, which is on the border between the two kingdoms of Damascus and Hamath. The border will end at Hazer-Hatticon, which is on the border of Hauran.
translation_verse: Kumo alɛ beeŋ naŋ keta loŋ n ya fo ndegboŋ nɛ baa tre Bɛrota nɛ Sibreem nɛ a dese nwursawule anyɔ nɛ baa tre Damaskɔs nɛ Hamaf be nferinto na, hale n ya fo kadegboŋ nɛ baa tre Tikɔn nɛ k dese kebonfu nɛ baa tre Hawuran na be gbaŋ ase na.

english_verse: The eastern border will begin on the border between the two kingdoms of Hauran and Damascus. It will run south along the Jordan River, which separates the territories of Gilead and Israel, and it will end at the Dead Sea near the town of Tamar.
translation_verse: Epeŋilarkpa be gbaŋ na malɛ fara Damaskɔs nɛ Hawuran be abonfu anyɔ be nferinto nna ŋ keta n sɔ kelargato be kaseto, nɛ Jɔɔdan be Lɔr ki Israɛl be basa be kasawule ashi epeŋitɔrkpa be kaba so nɛ Giliad be kasawule ashi epeŋilarkpa be egbaŋ to, nseŋ keta loŋ n ya lar kade nɛ baa tre Tama nɛ k mata Teku Wuso na.

english_verse: The western border will run north along the Mediterranean Sea to a point just west of Lebo-Hamath.
translation_verse: Kumo be epeŋilarkpa be ekar malɛ beeŋ fara Mɛditerenia be Teku ase ŋ keta n sɔ kelargato be esoso n ya fo Lɛbo Hamaf be epeŋitɔrkpa be kaba so.

english_verse: That is the land to be divided among the tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: Kasawule nɛ menyeeŋ barga to n sa Israɛl be eyiriana na nna na.

english_verse: a share of the land given to the tribe where they live. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Yiri kama to nɛ efɔ chena, daga fanɛ b chige bumo kasawule na nɛ efɔ na gba e nya mbe kachige. Ma, Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na e kaŋɛ.”

english_verse: Each tribe will receive a section of land that runs from the eastern border of Israel west to the Mediterranean Sea. The northern border of Israel will run along the towns of Hethlon and Lebo-Hamath, and will end at Hazar-Enon, which is on the border between the kingdoms of Damascus and Hamath. The tribes will receive their share of land in the following order, from north to south: Dan, Asher, Naphtali, Manasseh, Ephraim, Reuben, and Judah. The Special Section of Land The Lord said:
translation_verse: Eyiriana na be kekama beeŋ nya kasawule na be kaba nɛ k beeŋ yili Israɛl be epeŋilarkpa be kaba so be gbaŋ nɛ k dese epeŋitɔrkpa be kaba so na n ya fo Mɛditerenia be Teku ase nna na. Israɛl be kelargato be esoso be kaba so be gbaŋ na beeŋ bɔla Hiflɔn nɛ Lɛbo Hamaf be ndeana to n ya fo kakpa nɛ baa tre Haza Ɛnɔn nɛ k dese m mata Damaskɔs nɛ Hamaf be egbaŋ to na. Kananɛ eyiriana na beeŋ nya bumo be nsawule be kachige nde. Dan be yiri e naŋ juŋkpar n nya nɛ Asha be yiri e bɛ so nɛ Naftali be yiri e bɛ so nɛ Manase be yiri e bɛ so nɛ Efrayim be yiri e bɛ so nɛ Ruben be yiri e bɛ so nseŋ ta Juda be yiri m bɛ so lalaloge. Kasawule na be nferinto be asheŋ

english_verse: South of Judah's territory will be a special section of land. Its length will be twelve and a half kilometers, and its width will run from the eastern border of Israel west to the Mediterranean Sea. My temple will be located in this section of land.
translation_verse: Kakpa nɛ menyeeŋ ku m bɛ Juda be yiri so a laŋɛ kelargato be kaseto na beeŋ baa la kasawule nɛ k beeŋ baa kɔr to nna. Kumo be mparto beeŋ yili kelargato be esoso m ba choŋ kelargato be kaseto nsaa la emayɛl ashunu nɛ kumo be nteŋ to malɛ nɛ kananɛ menyeeŋ ku n sa Israɛl be eyiriana na be nteŋ to e baa sasa. Kasawule ere so nɛ ma bɔrɛlambu beeŋ yili.

english_verse: An area in the center of this land will belong to me. It will be twelve and a half kilometers long and ten kilometers wide.
translation_verse: Kakpa ere be nferinto be kasawule na beeŋ baa la ma Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na peya. Kumo be nteŋ to beeŋ baa la emayɛl ashunu nɛ mparto malɛ e baa la emayɛl ashe.

english_verse: I, the Lord, will give half of my sacred land to the priests. Their share will be twelve and a half kilometers long and five kilometers wide, and my temple will be right in the middle.
translation_verse: Ma, Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na beeŋ ku ma kasawule cheembi na n sa bɔrɛmatapoana na. Kakpa nɛ meeŋ ku n sa bumo na be nteŋ beeŋ yili epeŋilarkpa n ya fo epeŋitɔrkpa nsaa la emayɛl ashunu, nɛ kumo be mpar malɛ e yili kelargato be esoso n ya fo kelargato be kaseto, nsaa la emayɛl asa. Saŋɛ na so baaŋ pɔr Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na be bɔrɛlambu n yili kumo be nferinto.

english_verse: Only priests who are descendants of Zadok will receive a share of this sacred land, because they remained faithful to me when the Levites and the rest of the Israelites started sinning.
translation_verse: Kakpa cheembi ere beeŋ baa la bɔrɛmatapoana nɛ b shi Zadɔk be kabuna na peya nna. Ŋkpal manɛ so, bumo e ta kashenteŋji a shuŋ ma nsaa maŋ tu Livaiebi nɛ Israɛl be basa nɛ b ka na a wora alubi.

english_verse: The land belonging to the priests will be the most sacred area and will lie south of the area that belongs to the Levites.
translation_verse: Amoso bumo e naŋ nya kakpa nɛ k daga m bɛ kasawule nɛ k la Livaiebi peya na so. Kumo alɛ e naŋ baa la nsawule na kikɛ to be kakpa cheembi ga.

english_verse: South of my sacred land will be a section twelve and a half kilometers long and three kilometers wide. It will not be sacred, but will belong to the people of Israel and will include the city of Jerusalem, together with its houses and pastureland.
translation_verse: Ma kakpa cheembi na be kaba nɛ k beeŋ ka n dese kelargato be kaseto nɛ kumo be nteŋ to la emayɛl ashunu nɛ mparto la emayɛl asa na maŋ naa du cheembi, ama k beeŋ baa la Israɛl be basa na kikɛ peya nna nɛ b tiŋ m pɔr nwu n chena so nsaa bela asɔbɔya. Baaŋ pɔr kadegboŋ nɛ baa tre Jerusalɛm na kumo be nferinto,

english_verse: The city will be a square: Each side will be two kilometers long,
translation_verse: nɛ kumo be nteŋ to nɛ mparto kikɛ e baa la ateŋgreŋ ŋgboŋ anyɔ nɛ alfa anu nɛ adunyɔ.

english_verse: People from the city will farm the land, no matter which tribe they belong to.
translation_verse: Yiri kama to be esa kama nɛ e chena kadegboŋ na to beeŋ tiŋ n dɔ kasawule na so n ji.

english_verse: And so the center of this special section of land will be for my sacred land, as well as for the city and its property. The land will be a square, twelve and a half kilometers on each side.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal loŋ so, kasawule nɛ menyeeŋ ku n nase nferinto n sa Ebɔrɛ na, n ta kaboŋ nɛ kadegboŋ na yil so na gba n ti so, kikɛ be kaba kama so beeŋ baa la emayɛl ashunu nna.

english_verse: South of this special section will be the land that belongs to the rest of Israel's tribes. Each tribe will receive a section of land that runs from the eastern border of Israel west to the Mediterranean Sea. The tribes will receive their share of land in the following order, from north to south: Benjamin, Simeon, Issachar, Zebulun, and Gad.
translation_verse: Kasawule nɛ k dese kumo nɛ b ku n nase ŋ kɔr na be kelargato be kaseto be kaba so na ka Israɛl be eyiriana nɛ a ka na peya nna. Eyiriana na be kekama beeŋ nya kasawule na be kaba nɛ k yili Israɛl be epeŋilarkpa be kaba so be gbaŋ nɛ k dese epeŋitɔrkpa be kaba so na n ya fo Mɛditerenia be Teku na ase nna. Kananɛ eyiriana na beeŋ nya bumo be nsawule be kachige nde na. Bɛnjamin be yiri e naŋ juŋkpar n nya nɛ Simiɔn be yiri e bɛ so nɛ Issaka be yiri e bɛ so nɛ Zɛbyulɔn be yiri e bɛ so nɛ Gad be yiri e bɛ so.

english_verse: Gad's southern border is also the southern border of Israel. It will begin at the town of Tamar, then run southwest to the springs near Meribath-Kadesh. It will continue along the Egyptian Gorge and end at the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Kaba nɛ baaŋ ku n sa Gad be yiri na be kelargato be kaseto be kaba so be ekar beeŋ fara Tama be kade nɛ k wɔ kelargato be kaseto be epeŋitɔrkpa na nna n ya fo Kadɛsh be achubu ase nna nseŋ naŋ keta m bɔla Ijipt be gbaŋ to loŋ n ya fo Mɛditerenia be Teku na ase.

english_verse: That's how the land of Israel will be divided among the twelve tribes. I, the Lord God, have spoken. The Gates of Jerusalem The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ade kikɛ be kaman nɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na naŋ kaŋɛ le: “Kananɛ a daga fanɛ b barga kasawule na to mba mba n sa Israɛl be eyiriana na nɛ bekama e baa kɔ bumo peya nna na.” Jerusalɛm be mbunagboŋ na be asheŋ

english_verse: The city of Jerusalem will have twelve gates, three on each of the four sides of the city wall. These gates will be named after the twelve tribes of Israel. The gates of Reuben, Judah, and Levi will be in the north; Joseph, Benjamin, and Dan will be in the east; Simeon, Issachar, and Zebulun will be in the south; Gad, Asher, and Naphtali will be in the west. Each side of the city wall will be two kilometers long,
translation_verse: Jerusalɛm be kadegboŋ na beeŋ baa kɔ mbunagboŋ kudu anyɔ nna. Egbalana nɛ a kulti kumo be mba ana na be kekama beeŋ baa kɔ mbunagboŋ asa nɛ b ta eyiriana na be atre n nase amo. Egbalana na be kekama beeŋ baa sa fanɛ ateŋgreŋ ŋgboŋ anyɔ nɛ alfa anu nɛ adunyɔ nna. Mbunagboŋ nɛ a beeŋ baa wɔ egbal nɛ k bee laŋɛ kelargato be esoso be kaba so na be atre e naŋ baa la Ruben nɛ Juda nɛ Livai. Amo nɛ a wɔ epeŋilarkpa be kaba so na malɛ e malɛ e la Josɛf nɛ Bɛnjamin nɛ Dan. Mbunagboŋ nɛ a wɔ kelargato be kaseto be kaba so na malɛ e la Simiɔn nɛ Issaka nɛ Zɛbyulɔn nɛ amo nɛ a wɔ epeŋitɔrkpa na malɛ la Gad nɛ Ashɛr nɛ Naftali.

english_verse: and so the total length of the wall will be ten kilometers. The new name of the city will be “The-Lord-Is-Here!”
translation_verse: Egbal nɛ k kulti kadegboŋ na n wɔtɔ na be nteŋ kikɛ n chambɔ beeŋ baa la fanɛ emayɛl adunyɔ nɛ ashe nna. Yili kabre a yɔ, kadegboŋ na be ketre e naŋ baa la “Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ na Wɔ Nfe!”

english_verse: The Lord let Nebuchadnezzar capture Jehoiakim and take away some of the things used in God's temple. And when the king returned to Babylonia, he put these things in the temple of his own god.
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe Ebɔrɛ shin nɛ ewura Nebukadneeza kɔ m pɔ ewura Jehowakim so m pɛ mo nɛ basa ko n ta bɔrɛlambu na to be asɔ na be ako n ti bumo so n yɔ Babilɔn be efuli so n ya ta asɔ na n yili mbe agbir be ebu to ashi Babilɔn.

english_verse: One day the king ordered Ashpenaz, his highest palace official, to choose some young men from the royal family of Judah and from other leading Jewish families.
translation_verse: Kachako nɛ Ewura Nebukadneeza kaŋɛ Ashpenaaz nɛ e la mbe lambu to be benimuana na kikɛ be ejuŋkparpo na fanɛ e fin Israɛlebi be mbrantiɛfɔlbi nɛ b pɛ kena to na be bumo nɛ b shi kuwurji nɛ benimuana be kanaŋ to na m ba ewurkpa.

english_verse: Four of the young Jews chosen were Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, all from the tribe of Judah.
translation_verse: Danɛl nɛ Hananiya nɛ Mishaal nɛ Azariya nɛ b shi Juda be yiri to na daŋ ti basa nɛ b daŋ lara na so nna.

english_verse: But the king's chief official gave them Babylonian names: Daniel became Belteshazzar, Hananiah became Shadrach, Mishael became Meshach, and Azariah became Abednego.
translation_verse: Ewura be lambu to be benimuana na be ejuŋkparpo na daŋ sa bumo atre popɔr nna. Danɛl e daa la Bɛlteshaaza nɛ Hananiya la Shaadrak nɛ Mishaal la Mɛshaak, nɛ Azariya malɛ la Abedneego.

english_verse: Daniel made up his mind to eat and drink only what God had approved for his people to eat. And he asked the king's chief official for permission not to eat the food and wine served in the royal palace.
translation_verse: Danɛl malɛ daŋ yili kumo mbe nfɛra to nna fanɛ, e maaŋ ji ewurkpa be ajibi na ŋko n nuu ndoŋ be nsa na n da bumo be daŋkare be ekishi so, amoso e daŋ kule Ashpenaaz nna fanɛ e chɛ mo to nɛ e sa maŋ da daŋkare be ekishi so.

english_verse: God had made the official friendly and kind to Daniel.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ebɔrɛ shin nɛ Danɛl be asheŋ pɛ Ashpenaaz kuwɔr.

english_verse: But the man still told him, “The king has decided what you must eat and drink. And I am afraid he will kill me, if you eat something else and end up looking worse than the other young men.”
translation_verse: Ama Ashpenaaz daa ŋana ewura na nna, amoso, le nɛ e daŋ kaŋɛ Danɛl: “Ewura na e yili kusɔ nɛ menyeeŋ baa ji nɛ kusɔ nɛ menyeeŋ baa nuu, nɛ men baa maŋ daŋ a walɛ eyurto fanɛ mbrantiɛfɔlbi nɛ b ka ere, e beeŋ mɔ ma.”

english_verse: The king's official had put a guard in charge of Daniel and his three friends. So Daniel said to the guard,
translation_verse: Amoso Danɛl daŋ yɔ ekumpo nɛ Ashpenaaz lara fanɛ e baa keni mo nɛ mo teriana besa na so na nna n ya kaŋɛ mo le:

english_verse: “For the next ten days, let us have only vegetables and water at mealtime.
translation_verse: “Jande ta nchɛ kudu n sa anyi epofantaŋ nɛ nchu nawule n wora anyi ŋ keni.

english_verse: When the ten days are up, compare how we look with the other young men, and decide what to do with us.”
translation_verse: Nchɛ kudu na be kaman nɛ fo ta anyi m ber mbrantiɛfɔlbi nɛ baa ji ewurkpa be ajibi na ŋ keni, nseŋ yili kananɛ anyeeŋ baa du so n wora anyi kusɔ nɛ fee sha.”

english_verse: The guard agreed to do what Daniel had asked.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ekumpo na shuli nseŋ shin nɛ b wora loŋ nchɛ kudu.

english_verse: Ten days later, Daniel and his friends looked healthier and better than the young men who had been served food from the royal palace.
translation_verse: Nchɛ kudu na ka fo nɛ b wu fanɛ Danɛl nɛ mo teriana na kɔ eyur be alenfia nɛ eleŋ nɛnɛ a chɔ bumo braana nɛ b daa ji ewurkpa be ajibi na.

english_verse: God made the four young men smart and wise. They read a lot of books and became well educated. Daniel could also tell the meaning of dreams and visions.
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ daŋ sa mbrantiɛfɔlbi ana na nwɔl be kenyi nɛ asheŋ be kepinto nna, nseŋ ta kebaa tiŋ a kute bɔrɛdare nɛ edare gbagba be afito be kenyi n ti Danɛl bre so.

english_verse: At the end of the three-year period set by King Nebuchadnezzar, his chief palace official brought all the young men to him.
translation_verse: Nfɛ asa nɛ ewura Nebukadneeza sa na ka fo ekar, nɛ Ashpenaaz keta mbrantiɛfɔlbi na kikɛ n yɔ mo kutɔ.

english_verse: The king interviewed them and discovered that none of the others were as outstanding as Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. So they were given positions in the royal court.
translation_verse: Ewura na ka malga bumo kikɛ kutɔ nɛ e wu fanɛ Danɛl nɛ Hananiya nɛ Mishaal nɛ Azariya be asheŋ e bɔlɔ mo kenishi ga a chɔ bumo nɛ b ka na kikɛ. Amoso bumo e daŋ ki ewurkpa be beshumpo.

english_verse: From then on, whenever the king asked for advice, he found their wisdom was ten times better than that of any of his other advisors and magicians.
translation_verse: Asheŋ kikɛ nɛ ewura na daŋ baŋ bishi, e daa wu nna fanɛ mbia ana na nyi asheŋ nsaa pin asheŋ to alɛ kudu a chɔ mbe belejipo nɛ ŋkilgiwuraana nɛ b wɔ mbe efuli so kikɛ.

english_verse: During the second year that Nebuchadnezzar was king, he had such horrible nightmares that he could not sleep.
translation_verse: Ewura Nebukadneeza ka ji kuwura be kafɛ nyɔsopo to nɛ e ku edare. Edare na daŋ tɔrɔ mo ga hale nɛ e maŋ tiŋ nɛ e di.

english_verse: and said, “I am disturbed by a dream that I don't understand, and I want you to explain it.”
translation_verse: nɛ e kaŋɛ bumo le: “Ŋ ku edare ko nna nɛ k sa ma kagbenejija nɛ mee sha fanɛ men kaŋɛ ma kumo be kifito.”

english_verse: They answered in Aramaic, “Your Majesty, we hope you live forever! We are your servants. Please tell us your dream, and we will explain what it means.”
translation_verse: Nɛ b malga Aramaik be ŋgbarto ŋ kaŋɛ ewura na le: “Yiramu! Ebɔrɛ e sa fo ŋkpa tenteŋ mbaanaayɔ. Kaŋɛ anyi fo edare na nɛ anyi alɛ e kaŋɛ fo kumo be kifito.”

english_verse: But the king replied, “No! I have made up my mind. If you don't tell me both the dream and its meaning, you will be chopped to pieces and your houses will be torn down.
translation_verse: Nɛ ewura na kaŋɛ bumo le: “Kusɔ nɛ n yili e la fanɛ, men pin ma edare nɛ ŋ ku na, nseŋ kaŋɛ ma kumo be kifito gba n ti so. Nɛ men baa maŋ tiŋ n wora loŋ, meeŋ shin nɛ b kuya menyi to fanɛ mblaŋkul nseŋ shin nɛ b bure menyi be elaŋana malɛ gba cheche.

english_verse: However, if you do tell me both the dream and its meaning, you will be greatly rewarded and highly honored. Now tell me the dream and explain what it means.”
translation_verse: Ama nɛ men baŋ tiŋ ŋ kaŋɛ ma edare na nɛ kumo be kifito bre, meeŋ sa menyi ŋkɛ damta nseŋ shin nɛ men nya kemaŋkuragboŋ. Amoso men kaŋɛ ma edare na nɛ kumo be kifito kikɛ.”

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” they said, “if you will only tell us your dream, we will interpret it for you.”
translation_verse: Nɛ b naŋ kaŋɛ: “Yiramu! Nɛ fo kaŋɛ anyi fo edare na bre, anyi alɛ beeŋ kaŋɛ fo kumo be kifito.”

english_verse: because you know what's going to happen if you don't come up with the answer. You've decided to make up a bunch of lies, hoping I might change my mind. Now tell me the dream, and that will prove that you can interpret it.”
translation_verse: fanɛ, nɛ men baa maŋ kaŋɛ ma edare nɛ ŋ ku na, meeŋ sa menyi kikɛ kasogberge koŋwule na so. Men wora kɔnɔkoŋwule nna a ku efɛ a fɛ fanɛ loŋ beeŋ shin nɛ asheŋ e chɛrga. Nɛ men baŋ kaŋɛ ma edare nɛ ŋ ku na, kumo ere m baa nyi fanɛ menyeeŋ tiŋ ŋ kaŋɛ ma kumo be kifito gba.”

english_verse: His advisors explained, “Your Majesty, you are demanding the impossible! No king, not even the most famous and powerful, has ever ordered his advisors, magicians, or wise men to do such a thing.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ mbe besoetojipoana na kaŋɛ le: “Yiramu, esa kikɛ maŋ wɔ durnya ere to nɛ e beeŋ tiŋ m pin ŋ kaŋɛ kusɔ nɛ fee sha ere. Ewura kama, nɛ e bee ji eleŋ kanaŋkama so, maŋ naŋ kaŋɛ mbe belejipo nɛ ŋkilgiwuraana nɛ benyiashempo fanɛ b wora le be kesheŋ kikɛ.

english_verse: It can't be done, except by the gods, and they don't live here on earth.”
translation_verse: Yiramu, kusɔ nɛ fee bishi ere du kpakpa ga, amoso esa kama maaŋ tiŋ n wora loŋ, she agbir. Amo alɛ maŋ la edimɛdi a wɔ anyi to.”

english_verse: This made the king so angry that he gave orders for every wise man in Babylonia to be put to death, including Daniel and his three friends. God Tells Nebuchadnezzar's Dream to Daniel
translation_verse: Nɛ b sibɛ mbra be kawɔl n sa fanɛ b mɔ benyiashempo na kikɛ, n ta Danɛl nɛ mo teriana gba n ti so. Ebɔrɛ ka ŋini Danɛl edare na be kifito be asheŋ

english_verse: Arioch was the king's official in charge of putting the wise men to death. He was on his way to have it done, when Daniel very wisely went to him
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Danɛl yɔ ewura na be basa nɛ baa kuŋ mo na be enimu nɛ baa tre Ariɔk na kutɔ. Ariɔk daa yɔ nna nɛ e ya mɔ benyiashempo na nɛ Danɛl ya tu mo nseŋ bɔla kanyiasheŋ nɛ kamubraseso,

english_verse: and asked, “Why did the king give such cruel orders?” After Arioch explained what had happened,
translation_verse: m bishi mo kusɔ nɛ k ba nɛ ewura na sa le be mbra kpakpaso ere. Ndoŋ nna nɛ Ariɔk kaŋɛ Danɛl kusɔ nɛ k ba.

english_verse: Daniel rushed off and said to the king, “If you will just give me some time, I'll explain your dream.”
translation_verse: Epul na to nɛ Danɛl ya kule ewura na fanɛ b sa bumo saŋɛ gbrɛbi, nɛ e kaŋɛ mo edare na be kifito.

english_verse: Then he said, “Pray that the God who rules from heaven will be merciful and explain this mystery, so that we and the others won't be put to death.”
translation_verse: Nseŋ kaŋɛ bumo fanɛ b kule Ebɔrɛ nɛ e wɔ ebɔrɛso na nɛ e wu bumo kuwɔr m bugi alemaŋkarsheŋ na to n sa bumo, saŋɛ na so b maaŋ mɔ bumo nɛ Babilɔn be besoetojipoana na.

english_verse: In a vision one night, Daniel was shown the dream and its meaning. Then he praised the God who rules from heaven:
translation_verse: Kumo be kanyɛso gbagba nɛ Ebɔrɛ bugi alemaŋkarsheŋ na be kifito n sa Danɛl ashi bɔrɛdare to, nɛ e di Ebɔrɛ nɛ e wɔ ebɔrɛso na epaŋ ga ŋ kaŋɛ le:

english_verse: “Our God, your name will be praised forever and forever. You are all-powerful, and you know everything.
translation_verse: “Kapandi e baa la fo Ebɔrɛ na peya mbaanaayɔ ŋkpal fo kanyiasheŋ nɛ eleŋ nɛ fo kɔ so.

english_verse: You control human events— you give rulers their power and take it away, and you are the source of wisdom and knowledge.
translation_verse: Fo e kɔ eleŋ a shin nɛ saŋɛ nɛ jemanɛ kikɛ bee chɛrga. Fo e naa buu nsaa gboŋi bewura. Fo koŋwule na e naa sa basa kanyiasheŋ nɛ asheŋ be kepinto.

english_verse: You are the God who was worshiped by my ancestors. Now I thank you and praise you for making me wise and telling me the king's dream, together with its meaning.” Daniel Interprets the Dream
translation_verse: N nananyɛnana be Ebɔrɛ, mee di fo epaŋ nsaa bunyaŋ fo. Fo e sa ma kanyiasheŋ nɛ eleŋ; fo alɛ nu ma kabɔrɛkule nseŋ ŋini ma ewura na be edare na be kifito.” Danɛl ka kaŋɛ ewura na edare na nɛ kumo be kifito be asheŋ

english_verse: Daniel went back to Arioch, the official in charge of executing the wise men. Daniel said, “Don't kill those men! Take me to the king, and I will explain the meaning of his dream.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Danɛl bɛta n yɔ Ariɔk nɛ ewura na kaŋɛ fanɛ e ya mɔ besoetojipoana na kutɔ n ya kaŋɛ mo le: “Sa maŋ kaŋ mɔ besoetojipoana na. Keta ma n yɔ ewura na kutɔ nɛ n ya kaŋɛ mo mbe edare na be kifito.”

english_verse: Arioch rushed Daniel to the king and announced, “Your Majesty, I have found out that one of the men brought here from Judah can explain your dream.”
translation_verse: Epul na to nɛ Ariɔk keta Danɛl n yɔ ewura Nebukadneeza kutɔ n ya kaŋɛ mo le: “Yiramu, n wu Juda b basa nɛ b pɛ kena to na be eko nɛ e beeŋ tiŋ ŋ kaŋɛ fo edare na be kifito.”

english_verse: Daniel answered: Your Majesty, not even the smartest person in all the world can do what you are demanding.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Danɛl kaŋɛ le: “Yiramu, lejipo nɛ ŋkilgiwura nɛ ekpalpo nɛ enyiashempo kikɛ maŋ wɔtɔ nɛ e beeŋ tiŋ m pin le be kesheŋ.

english_verse: But the God who rules from heaven can explain mysteries. And while you were sleeping, he showed you what will happen in the future.
translation_verse: Yiramu, fo ka daa di na, fo daŋ ku edare ko a yɔ kusɔ nɛ k beeŋ wora echefoso nna. Ebɔrɛ nɛ e bee bugi alemaŋkarsheŋ be wulo to na, e lara kusɔ nɛ k bee shin nɛ k wora na ŋ ŋini fo.

english_verse: However, you must realize that these mysteries weren't explained to me because I am smarter than everyone else. Instead, it was done so that you would understand what you have seen.
translation_verse: Yiramu, mannɛ ŋ ka nyi asheŋ a chɔ ekama so so nɛ le be alemaŋkar be wulo ere di efuli n sa ma, ama loŋ wora nna saŋɛ na so feeŋ pin fo edare nɛ fo ku na be kifito nseŋ pin nfɛra nɛ k ba fo to na malɛ gba to.

english_verse: Your Majesty, what you saw standing in front of you was a huge and terrifying statue, shining brightly.
translation_verse: Yiramu, kusɔ nɛ fo daŋ wu k ka yil fo anishito na e la kapɔrduli gboŋgboŋi ko, nɛ k fulto nsaa nyɛkpɛ nɛ kumo be kekeni gba kɔ kufu.

english_verse: Its head was made of gold, its chest and arms were silver, and from its waist down to its knees, it was bronze.
translation_verse: Shuwa lela nɛ b daŋ ta n lɔŋɛ kumo be kumu nseŋ ta gbiti malɛ n lɔŋɛ kumo be kagbene nɛ mbre; n ta danyaŋ n lɔŋɛ kumo be nteto n ya fo kumo be abembi to.

english_verse: From there to its ankles it was iron, and its feet were a mixture of iron and clay.
translation_verse: Kumo be aya malɛ daa la abɛlso nna, nɛ kumo be ayadra malɛ la abɛlso nɛ ebɔ be weato.

english_verse: As you watched, a stone was cut from a mountain—but not by human hands. The stone struck the feet, completely shattering the iron and clay.
translation_verse: Fo ka bee keni kumo na nɛ kejembu ko nɛ k maŋ shi dimɛdi be enɔ to shi esoso m ba ŋmɛa kapɔrduli na be kebɛlso nɛ ebɔ be weato be ayadra na m buri amo to kpachɛrkpachɛrbi.

english_verse: Then the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver, and the gold were crushed and blown away without a trace, like husks of wheat at threshing time. But the stone became a tremendous mountain that covered the entire earth.
translation_verse: Epul na to nɛ kebɛlso na nɛ ebɔ na, nɛ danyaŋ na, nɛ gbiti nɛ shuwa na kikɛ buri to kpachɛrkpachɛrbi ŋ ki fanɛ gbaŋgbaŋ to be kugooro so be shishɛr na. Nɛ afu ba ta amo kikɛ n choŋ nɛ amo kedodobi gba maŋ ka. Ama kejembu nɛ k ŋmɛa kumo m bure to na bre wora kishi nna hale ŋ ki kebeegboŋ m buu kasawule kikɛ so.

english_verse: That was the dream, and now I'll tell you what it means.
translation_verse: Edare nɛ fo ku na nna na, naniere a ka kumo be kifito nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ fo.

english_verse: Your Majesty, you are the greatest of kings, and God has highly honored you with power
translation_verse: Yiramu, fo e la bewura kikɛ to be ewurgboŋ. Ebɔrɛ nɛ e wɔ esoso na malɛ e ta fo ŋ ki ewurgboŋ nseŋ ta eleŋ nɛ bunyaŋ n sa fo.

english_verse: After you are gone, another kingdom will rule, but it won't be as strong. Then it will be followed by a kingdom of bronze that will rule the whole world.
translation_verse: Fo kuwura ere be kaman kuwurgboŋ ko nɛ k maŋ fo feya ere so beeŋ ba, kumo alɛ be kaman nɛ danyaŋ be kuwurgboŋ e bɛ so n ji durnya kikɛ so kuwura.

english_verse: This fourth kingdom will be divided—it will be both strong and brittle, just as you saw that the feet and toes were a mixture of iron and clay.
translation_verse: Kuwurgboŋ nasopo na beeŋ barga to nna nɛ kumo be kaba e baa kɔ eleŋ nɛ kaba malɛ e pɔshi fanɛ kananɛ fo wu kapɔrduli na be ayadra nɛ anashibi ka la ebɔ nɛ kebɛlso be weato na.

english_verse: During the time of those kings, the God who rules from heaven will set up an eternal kingdom that will never fall. It will be like the stone that was cut from the mountain, but not by human hands—the stone that crushed the iron, bronze, clay, silver, and gold. Your Majesty, in your dream the great God has told you what is going to happen, and you can trust this interpretation. Daniel Is Promoted
translation_verse: Fo wu kananɛ kejembu nɛ k maŋ shi dimɛdi be enɔ to shi esoso m ba ŋmɛa kapɔrduli nɛ b ta kebɛlso nɛ danyaŋ nɛ ebɔ nɛ gbiti nɛ shuwa n lɔŋɛ na. Yiramu, Ebɔrɛ lempo na bee kaŋɛ fo kusɔ nɛ k beeŋ wora kachako so nna na. Fo edare nɛ fo ku na nɛ kumo be kifito kikɛ nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ fo na.” Ewura na ka sa Danɛl kakɛ be asheŋ

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar bowed low to the ground and worshiped Daniel. Then he gave orders for incense to be burned and a sacrifice of grain to be offered in honor of Daniel.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura Nebukadneeza dese kasawule Danɛl be anishito bunyanso m ponte ŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ b lara sarga nseŋ chɔɔ duwu n sa Danɛl.

english_verse: The king said, “Now I know that your God is above all other gods and kings, because he gave you the power to explain this mystery.”
translation_verse: Nseŋ kaŋɛ Danɛl le: “Fo Ebɔrɛ na e kɔ eleŋ a chɔ agbirana kikɛ. Mo e la bewuraana kikɛ be Enyɛnpe, Mo alɛ e naa tiŋ a lara alemaŋkarsheŋ be wulo efuli. M pin le be kesheŋ ere nna ŋkpal fo ka tiŋ m bugi alemaŋkarsheŋ be wulo ere be kifito so.”

english_verse: The king then presented Daniel with a lot of gifts; he promoted him to governor of Babylon Province and put him in charge of the other wise men.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ ewura na sa Danɛl kenimu nɛ ŋkɛ lela damta nseŋ ta Babilɔn be kade nɛ nde nɛ a kulti kumo na kikɛ n sa mo fanɛ e baa keni so. Nseŋ naŋ shin nɛ e ki ewurkpa be besoetojipoana na kikɛ be enimu.

english_verse: At Daniel's request, the king appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to high positions in Babylon Province, and he let Daniel stay on as a palace official.
translation_verse: Nɛ Danɛl kule ewura na fanɛ e shin nɛ Shaadrak nɛ Mɛshaak nɛ Abedneego e ki kakpa nɛ e bee keni so na be ekrachigboŋ, nɛ mo alɛ Danɛl e baa wɔ ewurkpa nawule.

english_verse: and the king's high officials, governors, and advisors all crowded around them. The men were not burned, their hair wasn't scorched, and their clothes didn't even smell like smoke.
translation_verse: Nɛ ewura na be benimuana na nɛ gomena be benimuana na ba kulti mbrantiɛbia asa na n wɔtɔ, nseŋ wu fanɛ edɛ na daa maŋ wora bumo shɛŋ. Bumo be emin koŋwule gba daa maŋ chɔɔ. Bumo be epiŋi malɛ gba maŋ chɔɔ. Bumo be ekama malɛ daa maa dufɛ edishi gba.

english_verse: So all of them came and stood in front of it.
translation_verse: Basa na kikɛ ka gbargbar abar m ba yili kapɔrduli na be anishito na,

english_verse: and he commanded his governors, advisors, treasurers, judges, and his other officials to come from everywhere in his kingdom to the dedication of the statue.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ e kaŋɛ mbe gomena be benimuana, nɛ mbe besoetojipoana nɛ mbe amansherbi kenipoana nɛ demujipoana nɛ benimuana nɛ b ka na kikɛ fanɛ ekama e ba shɛr nɛ b kebugi kapɔrduli nɛ e pɔr na be kasheŋwora.

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar was furious. So he sent for the three young men and said,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ agbo dii ewura Nebukadneeza alegaiso nɛ e shuŋi fanɛ b ya pɛ mbrantiɛbia asa na m ba.

translation_verse: Men kaŋ baŋ nu mbel nɛ nlopi nɛ egoji nɛ ejirgo nɛ ejaŋjilaŋ nɛ alaŋsɔ be yiri kikɛ ka bee shu naniere, men jɔŋɛ m bunyaŋ kapɔrduli na. english_verse: The three men replied, “Your Majesty, we don't need to defend ourselves.
translation_verse: Nɛ Shaadrak nɛ Mɛshaak nɛ Abedneego kaŋɛ le: “Yiramu, anyi maa ba nɛ an malga ŋ kuŋ anyi be amu.

english_verse: Nebuchadnezzar's face twisted with anger at the three men. And he ordered the furnace to be heated seven times hotter than usual.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura Nebukadneeza nya agbo alegaiso n wɔtɔ Shaadrak nɛ Mɛshaak nɛ Abedneego, nseŋ shin nɛ b foŋ edɛ na to nɛ e bee tushi ale shunu so a chɔ kananɛ a daa du sososo na.

english_verse: Next, he commanded some of his strongest soldiers to tie up the men and throw them into the flaming furnace.
translation_verse: Nɛ e ponte ŋ kaŋɛ mbe benapo nɛ b kɔ eleŋ ga na fanɛ b kre mbrantiɛbia asa na, n ta bumo n ya lɛ edɛ na to.

english_verse: Suddenly the king jumped up and shouted, “Weren't only three men tied up and thrown into the fire?” “Yes, Your Majesty,” his officers answered.
translation_verse: Epul na to nɛ ewura Nebukadneeza kpa n niŋi to nseŋ bishi mbe benimuana le: “Mannɛ mbrantiɛbia asa nɛ an daŋ kre n ya lɛ edɛ wuloŋ wuloŋ na to na a?” Nɛ b kaŋɛ le: “Mm! Yiramu, loŋ gbagba nna.”

english_verse: “But I see four men walking around in the fire,” the king replied. “None of them is tied up or harmed, and the fourth one looks like a god.”
translation_verse: Nɛ ewura naŋ kaŋɛ le: “Nɛ manɛ nna nɛ mee wu benyɛn ana ka na edɛ na to nɛ shɛŋ shɛŋ maŋ naŋ kre bumo be eyur, nɛ bumo be eyur malɛ maŋ chɔɔ, nɛ esa nasopo na du fanɛ Ebɔrɛ be malaika?” B ka lara basa asa na nseŋ sa bumo kenimu be asheŋ

english_verse: Nebuchadnezzar went closer to the flaming furnace and said to the three young men, “You servants of the Most High God, come out at once!” They came out,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura Nebukadneeza firgi n taga edɛ wuloŋ wuloŋ na to m boŋ to n tre: “Shaadrak! Mɛshaak! Abedneego! Enyɛnpetale be nyɛrbi, men lar m ba!” Epul to nɛ b dii n lar edɛ be kemaŋ chiŋgeliŋ na to.

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar said: Praise their God for sending an angel to rescue his servants! They trusted their God and refused to obey my commands. Yes, they chose to die rather than to worship or serve any god except their own.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ewura Nebukadneeza kaŋɛ le: “Kemaŋkura e baa la Shaadrak nɛ Mɛshaak nɛ Abedneego be Ebɔrɛ na peya! Mo e shuŋi mbe malaika nɛ e ba mɔlga mbe nyɛrbi nɛ b yirda mo na. B kini k nu n sa ma nseŋ ta bumo be amu ŋ kpa kelara ŋ kini kejɔŋɛ m bunyaŋ kegbir kikɛ, she bumo be Ebɔrɛ na nawule.

english_verse: And I won't allow people of any nation or race to say anything against their God. Anyone who does will be chopped up and their houses will be torn down, because no other god has such great power to save.
translation_verse: Amoso n nase mbra nna na fanɛ efuli kama so ebi nɛ ŋgbar kama to ebi kaŋ pɛl m malga asheŋ kama ŋ gbiti Shaadrak nɛ Mɛshaak nɛ Abedneego be Ebɔrɛ na, b kuya bumo to fanɛ mblaŋkul nseŋ shin nɛ bumo be nwu e ki alambure, ŋkpal manɛ so kegbir kikɛ maŋ wɔtɔ a kɔ eleŋ nsaa beeŋ tiŋ n sa le be kumɔlga.”

english_verse: After this happened, the king appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego to even higher positions in Babylon Province.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ ewura na naŋ daŋɛ Shaadrak nɛ Mɛshaak nɛ Abedneego so kenimu ashi Babilɔn be kebonfu na to.

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar sent the following letter to the people of all nations and races on the earth: Greetings to all of you!
translation_verse: Ewura Nebukadneeza daŋ sa efuliana nɛ eyiriana nɛ ŋgbarana nɛ e wɔ durnya to kikɛ ebɔl nna ŋ kaŋɛ le: “Kagbenewushi e baa wɔ menyi kikɛ so.

english_verse: I am glad to tell about the wonderful miracles God Most High has done for me.
translation_verse: K wora ma ebel ga ŋ ka bee shin nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ menyi asheŋ tumase nɛ emamachisheŋ nɛ Enyɛnpetale wora n sa ma.

english_verse: His miracles are mighty and marvelous. He will rule forever, and his kingdom will never end.
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ be etumasesheŋ shibi ga nɛ mbe emamachisheŋ bee mɔ kɔnɔ. Mbe kuwurji wɔtɔ nna hale mbaanaayɔ.

english_verse: I was enjoying a time of peace and prosperity,
translation_verse: Ma, Nebukadneeza wɔ ma kuwurlaŋ to nna a kɔ asɔ damta nsaa ji ma eyur.

english_verse: Then I commanded every wise man in Babylonia to appear in my court, so they could explain the meaning of my dream.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ m ponte n tre Babilɔn be benyiashempo kikɛ fanɛ b ba kaŋɛ ma edare na be kifito.

english_verse: After they arrived, I told them my dream, but they were not able to say what it meant.
translation_verse: B ka ba shɛr nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ bumo ma edare na. Ama b daa maŋ tiŋ ŋ kaŋɛ ma kumo be kifito.

english_verse: Finally, a young man named Daniel came in, and I told him the dream. The holy gods had given him special powers, and I had renamed him Belteshazzar after my own god.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Danɛl malɛ ba nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ mo edare nɛ ŋ ku na. Agbir cheembi na be kiyoyu wɔ Danɛl to nna a chɛ mo to nɛ e bee tiŋ a pin edare be afito. N daŋ ta ma kegbir be ketre Bɛlteshaaza nna n nase Danɛl,

english_verse: I said, “Belteshazzar, not only are you the wisest of all advisors and counselors, but the holy gods have given you special powers to solve the most difficult mysteries. So listen to what I dreamed and tell me what it means:
translation_verse: nseŋ kaŋɛ le: Bɛlteshaaza nɛ fo la belejipoana na kikɛ be ewura, n nyi agbir cheembi na be kiyoyu ka wɔ fo to nɛ fee tiŋ a pin alemaŋkarsheŋ kikɛ be afito. Ma edare nde. Kaŋɛ ma kumo be kifito.

english_verse: In my sleep I saw a very tall tree in the center of the world.
translation_verse: Ŋ ka bee di nɛ ŋ ku bɔrɛdare n wu kedibi gboŋgboŋi ko ka yil durnya kikɛ be nferinto.

english_verse: It grew stronger and higher, until it reached to heaven and could be seen from anywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Kedibi na daŋ daŋ nna hale n ya chute awɔlpa nɛ durnya ere to be esa kikɛ bee wu kumo.

english_verse: It was covered with leaves and heavy with fruit— enough for all nations. Wild animals enjoyed its shade, birds nested in its branches, and all creatures on earth lived on its fruit.
translation_verse: Kumo be afantaŋ daa walɛ nna ga, nɛ k kɔ asɔrso damta nɛ durnya ere to be kepɔrso kikɛ beeŋ tiŋ n ji amo ŋ kukwe. Kupuŋ to be asɔbɔya bee dese kumo be kayul to nna a wushi nɛ mbuibi malɛ bee tɔ asha kumo be ayabi so nɛ kepɔrso kikɛ malɛ bee ji kumo be asɔrso.

english_verse: “While I was in bed, having this vision, a holy angel came down from heaven
translation_verse: Ŋ ka bee fɛ bɔrɛdare nɛ ŋ ku na be asheŋ, nɛ n wu malaika ko ka shi Ebɔrɛso ŋ gbelge to a ba,

english_verse: and shouted: ‘Chop down the tree and cut off its branches; strip off its leaves and scatter its fruit. Make the animals leave its shade and send the birds flying from its branches.
translation_verse: nseŋ boŋ to eleŋso ŋ kaŋɛ le: Men ku kedibi na n lɛ nseŋ kpele kumo be ayabi so. ‘Men nyia kumo be afantaŋ n lɛ nseŋ franyaŋ kumo be asɔrso to n lɛ. Men ju asɔbɔya ashi kumo be kifito nseŋ ju mbuibi nɛ b jɔŋ kumo be ayabi so na.

english_verse: But leave its stump and roots in the ground, surrounded by grass and held by chains of iron and bronze. ‘Make sure that this ruler lives like the animals out in the open fields, unprotected from the dew.
translation_verse: Ama men yige kumo be keyimu, nɛ b ta kebɛlso nɛ danyaŋ be ŋgbɛlɛbi ŋ kre na, nɛ kumo be nliŋi kasawule to ashi kupuŋ to. Kedibi ere du fanɛ dimɛdi nna. Amoso shin nɛ bunyaŋ e shi esoso m ba tɔr mo so, nseŋ shin nɛ mo nɛ asɔbɔya e baa wɔ kupuŋ to.

english_verse: Give him the mind of a wild animal for seven long years.
translation_verse: Shin nɛ e sa maa kɔ dimɛdi be nfɛra nfɛ lela ashunu, ama mbe nfɛra e baa du fanɛ kusɔbɔya peya.

english_verse: This punishment is given at the command of the holy angels. It will show to all who live that God Most High controls all kingdoms and chooses for their rulers persons of humble birth.’
translation_verse: Kusɔ nɛ Ebɔrɛ be emalaika cheembi na kaŋɛ nna na, saŋɛ na so dimɛdi kikɛ beeŋ pin fanɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na kɔ eleŋ dimɛdi be kuwurji so, nsaa kɔ ekpa nɛ e ta kumo n sa esa kama nɛ e bee sha, hale bebɔlpo gba.

english_verse: “Daniel, that was the dream that none of the wise men in my kingdom were able to understand. But I am sure that you will understand what it means, because the holy gods have given you some special powers.”
translation_verse: Edare nɛ ma ewura Nebukadneeza ku na nna na. Bɛlteshaaza, kaŋɛ ma kumo be kifito, ŋkpal manɛ so ma benyiashempo kikɛ maŋ tiŋ ŋ kaŋɛ ma kumo be kifito, ama n nyi fo ere ka beeŋ tiŋ. Ŋkpal manɛ so, agbir cheembi na be kiyoyu wɔ fo to.’ ” Danɛl ka kaŋɛ edare na be kifito be asheŋ

english_verse: For a while, Daniel was terribly confused and worried by what he was thinking. But I said, “Don't be bothered either by the dream or by what it means.” Daniel replied: Your Majesty, I wish the dream had been against your enemies.

english_verse: You saw a tree that grew so big and strong that it reached up to heaven and could be seen from anywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Fo wu Kedibi nɛ k danto a kɔ eleŋ nsaa wɔ nteŋ hale n ya ka chute awɔlpa nɛ durnya ere to be esa kikɛ bee wu kumo.

english_verse: Your Majesty, that tree is you. Your glorious reputation has reached heaven, and your kingdom covers the earth.
translation_verse: Yiramu, fo e la loŋ be kedibi tenteŋ lempo na. Fo eleŋ nɛ kemaŋkura wora kishi hale n ya fo awɔlpa so kikɛ, nseŋ salga to hale n ya fo durnya ere be kaplɛkama.

english_verse: Then you saw a holy angel come down from heaven and say, “Chop down the tree and destroy it! But leave its stump and roots in the ground, fastened there by a chain of iron and bronze. Let it stay for seven years out in the field with the wild animals, unprotected from the dew.”
translation_verse: Yiramu, fo ka wu malaika na ka shi esoso ŋ gbelge to a ba na, le nɛ e daŋ kaŋɛ: ‘Ku kedibi na n lɛ nseŋ kpele kumo to cheche ama ta kebɛlso nɛ danyaŋ be ŋgbɛlɛbi m mɛa kumo be keyimu so n yige kumo kasawule to nɛ k baa wɔ kupuŋ to. english_verse: Your Majesty, God Most High has sent you this message, and it means
translation_verse: Yiramu, edare na bee ŋini nna fanɛ Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ na e yili kumo fanɛ le be asheŋ beeŋ tu fo.

english_verse: that you will be forced to live with the wild animals, far away from humans. You will eat grass like a wild animal and live outdoors for seven years, until you learn that God Most High controls all earthly kingdoms and chooses their rulers.
translation_verse: Baaŋ ju fo n lar edimɛdi to nɛ fo ya ka wɔ kupuŋ to be asɔbɔya to. Nfɛ shunu nɛ fo wɔtɔ e ji afitiri fanɛ kena nseŋ naa dese kowu nɛ bunyaŋ e baa tɔr fo so. english_verse: But he gave orders not to disturb the stump and roots. This is to show that you will be king once again, after you learn that the God who rules from heaven is in control.
translation_verse: Ama malaika na shin nɛ b yige keyimu na kasawule to nna, a ŋini fanɛ feeŋ naŋ laŋɛ m ba ki ewura saŋɛ nɛ fo shuli so fanɛ Ebɔrɛ nawule e naa ji durnya ere so eleŋ na.

english_verse: Your Majesty, please be willing to do what I say. Turn from your sins and start living right; have mercy on those who are mistreated. Then all will go well with you for a long time. The Rest of Nebuchadnezzar's Letter about His Second Dream
translation_verse: Amoso Yiramu, nu n sa ma kasotoji ere. Yige alubi be kebaawora nsaa wora alela nɛ asheŋ niŋiso. Baa wu betirpo kuwɔr. Loŋ nɛ fo kanyɛ beeŋ baa ti so saŋkama.”

english_verse: About twelve months later, I was walking on the flat roof of my royal palace and admiring the beautiful city of Babylon, when these things started happening to me. translation_verse: nseŋ kaŋɛ le: “Keni kananɛ Babilɔn shibi loŋ! Ma eleŋ so nɛ m pɔr kumo nɛ kebaa la ma kadegboŋ a ŋini eleŋ nɛ kemaŋkura nɛ adelebigboŋ nɛ ŋ kɔ.”
