english_verse: One day on our way to the place of prayer, we were met by a slave girl. She had a spirit in her that gave her the power to tell the future. By doing this she made a lot of money for her owners.
translation_verse: Kachako an ka bee yɔ kabɔrɛkulekpa nɛ kebichebi ko nɛ kiyoyu lubi ko daa wɔ mo to a shin nɛ e daa wu asheŋ a kaŋɛ na tu anyi. Mbe kewu asheŋ ŋ kaŋɛ na daa shin nɛ e daa nya amansherbi damta ga nna a sa mo nyɛnpeana.

english_verse: The girl followed Paul and the rest of us, and she kept yelling, “These men are servants of the Most High God! They are telling you how to be saved.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ e bɛ anyi nɛ Pɔɔl so a ponte a kaŋɛ: “Basa ere la Enyɛnpetale Ebɔrɛ be anya nna. Baa kaŋɛ menyi kananɛ menyeeŋ tiŋ n nya kumɔlga nna.”

english_verse: This went on for several days. Finally, Paul got so upset that he turned and said to the spirit, “In the name of Jesus Christ, I order you to leave this girl alone!” At once the evil spirit left her.
translation_verse: E daŋ malga loŋ nchɛ damta nɛ kachako Pɔɔl be kagbene jija mo ga nɛ e gben ŋ kilgi ŋ kaŋɛ kiyoyu lubi na: “Yesu Kristo be ketre to nɛ mee kaŋɛ fo na: Lar kebichebi ere to!” Epul na gbagba to nɛ kiyoyu lubi na lar kebichebi na to.

english_verse: When the girl's owners realized they had lost all chances for making more money, they grabbed Paul and Silas and dragged them into court.
translation_verse: Kebichebi na mo nyɛnpeana ka pin fanɛ e maaŋ naŋ tiŋ n nya amansherbi n sa bumo nɛ b nyaŋ Pɔɔl nɛ Sailas ŋ gberge bumo n yɔ kelɔnɛ so, demujikpa n ya sa benimuana na.

english_verse: The crowd joined in the attack on Paul and Silas. Then the officials tore the clothes off the two men and ordered them to be beaten with a whip.
translation_verse: Nɛ jimaŋ na malɛ ta bumo be nnɔ n wɔtɔ a bri bumo, nɛ benimuana na kpɛa Pɔɔl nɛ Sailas be asɔbuuso to nseŋ shin nɛ b kuya bumo so.

english_verse: After they had been badly beaten, they were put in jail, and the jailer was told to guard them carefully.
translation_verse: B ka shin nɛ b bri bumo ga n loge nɛ b shin nɛ b ti bumo ebu nseŋ kaŋɛ kabutikenipo na fanɛ e ti bumo kpakpa n wɔtɔ.

english_verse: The jailer did as he was told. He put them deep inside the jail and chained their feet to heavy blocks of wood.
translation_verse: Kabutikenipo na ka nu loŋ nɛ e ta bumo n wɔtɔ lalaloge be ebu na to nseŋ kre bumo be ayaana m mata ŋgbuliŋ gbɛgbɛso ko.

english_verse: About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing praises to God, while the other prisoners listened.
translation_verse: Kumo be kamɔnchɛ be kiidiso Pɔɔl nɛ Sailas ka bee kule Ebɔrɛ nsaa boŋ nshɛ a di Ebɔrɛ epaŋ nɛ bumo braana nɛ b wɔ kabuti na to na bee nu.

english_verse: Suddenly a strong earthquake shook the jail to its foundations. The doors opened, and the chains fell from all the prisoners.
translation_verse: Nɛ kebembeŋgboŋ ko ba epul na to m ba gbuŋgbuŋ kasawule nɛ ebu na daa yil so na gba to nɛ mbuna na kikɛ bugi epul na to nɛ kabutipoana na be ŋgbɛlɛbiana lar bumo so n tɔr.

english_verse: When the jailer woke up and saw that the doors were open, he thought that the prisoners had escaped. He pulled out his sword and was about to kill himself.
translation_verse: Kabutikenipo na ka tiŋi n wu kananɛ mbuna na kikɛ bugi a yil na nɛ e pe tokobi nɛ e mɔ mbe kumu, ŋkpal manɛ so, e daa tama fanɛ basa na kikɛ lar nna.

english_verse: But Paul shouted, “Don't harm yourself! No one has escaped.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Pɔɔl boŋ to awɔrso ga ŋ kaŋɛ: “Sa maŋ doro fo kumu. Anyi kikɛ wɔtɔ.”

english_verse: The jailer asked for a torch and went into the jail. He was shaking all over as he knelt down in front of Paul and Silas.
translation_verse: Nɛ kabutikenipo na shin nɛ b sa mo fitila nɛ e jɔ to n luri ŋ gbir Pɔɔl nɛ Sailas be anishito a chicha.

english_verse: After he had led them out of the jail, he asked, “What must I do to be saved?”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ e keta bumo n lar n ya bishi bumo: “N nyɛnpeana, nuso nɛ meeŋ wora n tiŋ n nya kumɔlga?”

english_verse: They replied, “Have faith in the Lord Jesus and you will be saved! This is also true for everyone who lives in your home.”
translation_verse: Nɛ b kaŋɛ mo: “Yirda Enyɛnpe Yesu Kristo nɛ fo nɛ fo laŋ to ebi e nya kumɔlga.”

english_verse: Then Paul and Silas told him and everyone else in his house about the Lord.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ b bɔ Enyɛnpe na be kubɔya na n sa mo nɛ mbe kowu to ebi kikɛ.

english_verse: While it was still night, the jailer took them to a place where he could wash their cuts and bruises. Then he and everyone in his home were baptized.
translation_verse: Jemanɛ na malɛ kikɛ so nɛ kabutikenipo na fɔr bumo be achuuana na nɛ b bɛr mo nɛ mbe laŋ to ebi kabɔrɛbɛr epul na to.

english_verse: They were very glad they had put their faith in God. After this, the jailer took Paul and Silas to his home and gave them something to eat.
translation_verse: E daŋ yɛr Pɔɔl nɛ Sailas mo pe nna n ya sa bumo ajibi. Mo nɛ mbe eche nɛ bibi be ŋgbene daŋ fuli bumo ga ŋkpal b ka yirda Ebɔrɛ naniere so.

english_verse: The next morning the officials sent some police with orders for the jailer to let Paul and Silas go.
translation_verse: Kumo be ŋklade nɛ Romebi be ekrachigboŋana na ta le be kubɔya n shuŋi bepurshi ŋ kaŋɛ: “Men shin nɛ basa na e baa yɔ.”

english_verse: The jailer told Paul, “The officials have ordered me to set you free. Now you can leave in peace.”
translation_verse: Nɛ kabutikenipo na ta kumo ŋ kaŋɛ Pɔɔl: “Ekrachigboŋana na shuŋi n sa ekpa fanɛ b lara menyi kabuti to. Amoso, men koso kagbenewushiso a yɔ.”

english_verse: But Paul told the police, “We are Roman citizens, and the Roman officials had us beaten in public without giving us a trial. They threw us into jail. Now do they think they can secretly send us away? No, they cannot! They will have to come here themselves and let us out.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Pɔɔl kaŋɛ bepurshi na: “B maŋ ji anyi demu ŋ keni nseŋ shin nɛ b bri anyi basa to. Anyi alɛ la Rom be efuli so ebi nna. B ka bri anyi n loge nɛ b ta anyi n ti ebu nseŋ naa sha keŋana boeŋ n lara anyi a? Akai, loŋ maaŋ nya. A daga fanɛ bumo, Romebi be ekrachigboŋana na gbagba ka ba nfe m ba lara anyi.”

english_verse: So they came and apologized. They led them out of the jail and asked them to please leave town.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ b ya kule bumo fanɛ b ta m paŋ bumo. Kumo be kaman nɛ b lara bumo kabuti na to nseŋ kule bumo fanɛ b lar kade na to.

english_verse: But Paul and Silas went straight to the home of Lydia, where they saw the Lord's followers and encouraged them. Then they left.
translation_verse: Nɛ Pɔɔl nɛ Sailas lar kabuti na to n yɔ Libiya pe n ya tu bekurgepoana na ndoŋ n leŋ bumo to nseŋ lar kade na to.

english_verse: After Paul and his friends had traveled through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they went on to Thessalonica. A synagogue was in that city.
translation_verse: B ta loŋ m ba bɔla Amfipɔlis nɛ Apɔlonia m ba fo Tɛsalɔnika, kakpa nɛ Juwebi be nshɛrbu ko daa wɔ na.

english_verse: So as usual, Paul went there to worship, and on three Sabbaths he spoke to the people. He used the Scriptures
translation_verse: Nɛ Pɔɔl yaŋ yɔ nshɛrbu na to fanɛ kananɛ e chɛr a wora kade kama to na. Mbe kewushiachɛ asa nɛ e wɔ ndoŋ a kɔ abɔrɛsibɛ na a ji basa na emɔrɔ

english_verse: to show them that the Messiah had to suffer, but that he would rise from death. Paul also told them that Jesus is the Messiah he was preaching about.
translation_verse: a ta amo a bugi asheŋ to a ŋini bumo kananɛ a daga Kristo na ka beeŋ luri etɔrɔ to nɛ Ebɔrɛ e naŋ tiŋi mo luwu to ŋ kaŋɛ bumo: “Yesu nɛ mee malga mbe asheŋ ere e la Kristo na.”

english_verse: Some of them believed what Paul had said, and they became followers with Paul and Silas. Some Gentiles and many important women also believed the message.
translation_verse: Nɛ bumo be beko yirda Pɔɔl be kamalga na nɛ bumo nɛ Pɔɔl nɛ Sailas ba ki basa koŋwule a bɛ Yesu so. Loŋ koŋwule na nɛ Griikebi be bedamta ko nɛ b daa bunyaŋ Ebɔrɛ na nɛ bebunyampocheana na be bedamta malɛ gba daŋ wora.

english_verse: The Jewish leaders were jealous and got some troublemakers who hung around the marketplace to start a riot in the city. They wanted to drag Paul and Silas out to the mob, and so they went straight to Jason's home.
translation_verse: Ama kayurbesa daŋ pɛ Juwebi na ga nɛ b chala basa fuloŋ tɔlpo ko ashi kubɔrbi so nseŋ nya jimaŋ ko n ta kade na kikɛ to n wɔtɔ awɔrgboŋ ko to nseŋ ya mel Jeesɔn pe a fin kepɛ Pɔɔl nɛ Sailas m ba sa basa na.

english_verse: But when they did not find them there, they dragged out Jason and some of the Lord's followers. They took them to the city authorities and shouted, “Paul and Silas have been upsetting things everywhere. Now they have come here,
translation_verse: B ka fin Pɔɔl nɛ Sailas ŋ gben nɛ b gberge Jeesɔn nɛ bekurgepo ko n ya sa kade na to be benimuana m ponte ŋ kaŋɛ: “Basa ere na nde kama to nna a baga amo to nseŋ ba anyi alɛ be kade ere to.

english_verse: and Jason has welcomed them into his home. All of them break the laws of the Roman Emperor by claiming that someone named Jesus is king.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Jeesɔn ta bumo n wɔtɔ mo pe. Bumo kikɛ wɔtɔ nna a wora a da Romebi be ewurgboŋ na be mbraana na so a kaŋɛ basa fanɛ ewura ko malɛ gba naa wɔtɔ nɛ baa tre Yesu.”

english_verse: The officials and the people were upset when they heard this.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ jimaŋ na nɛ kade na to be benimuana na be kebagato sɔ kakpa kikɛ.

english_verse: So they made Jason and the other followers pay bail before letting them go. People in Berea Welcome the Message
translation_verse: Nɛ benimu na shin nɛ Jeesɔn nɛ mo braana na yili Pɔɔl nɛ Sailas be katelamu to ŋ ka kumo be loŋ be amansherbi pɔɛŋ nɛ b yige bumo. Pɔɔl nɛ Sailas ka ba Beriya be asheŋ

english_verse: That same night the Lord's followers sent Paul and Silas on to Berea, and after they arrived, they went to the synagogue.
translation_verse: Kanyɛ ka baŋ biri nɛ bekurgepoana na shin nɛ Pɔɔl nɛ Sailas yɔ Beriya. B ka fo ndoŋ nɛ b yɔ ndoŋ be nshɛrbu to.

english_verse: The people in Berea were much nicer than those in Thessalonica, and they gladly accepted the message. Day after day they studied the Scriptures to see if these things were true.
translation_verse: Ndoŋebi bre daŋ bugi bumo be asoe a sha kenu kubɔya na ga nsaa koya abɔrɛsibɛ na kachɛ kama a keni ŋko Pɔɔl be mmalga na bɔla ekpa a.

english_verse: Many of them put their faith in the Lord, including some important Greek women and several men.
translation_verse: Bumo be bedamta daŋ yirda nɛ Griikebi be bebunyampocheana be bedamta nɛ Egriiknyɛn be bedamta gba ba yirda.

english_verse: When the Jewish leaders in Thessalonica heard that Paul had been preaching God's message in Berea, they went there and caused trouble by turning the crowds against Paul.
translation_verse: Tɛsalɔnika be Juwebi na ka nu fanɛ Pɔɔl bɔ Ebɔrɛ be kubɔya na ashi Beriya gba nɛ b ba ndoŋ m ba fara a we a wɔtɔ basa na a yeŋ bumo to a wɔtɔ kebagato to.

english_verse: At once the followers sent Paul down to the coast, but Silas and Timothy stayed in Berea.
translation_verse: Epul na to nɛ bekurgepoana na nya manaŋ n shin nɛ Pɔɔl yɔ teku ase be nde to nseŋ ka Sailas nɛ Timoti Beriya to.

english_verse: Some men went with Paul as far as Athens, and then returned with instructions for Silas and Timothy to join him as soon as possible. Paul in Athens
translation_verse: Atens kikɛ nɛ bumo nɛ b daŋ shuŋi Pɔɔl a yɔ na daŋ ya yige mo nseŋ bɛta n ta Pɔɔl be ŋkela n yɔ Beriya fanɛ Sailas nɛ Timoti e ba manaŋ m ba tu mo. Pɔɔl ka malga ashi Atens be asheŋ

english_verse: While Paul was waiting in Athens, he was upset to see all the idols in the city.
translation_verse: Pɔɔl ka wɔ Atens a jo Sailas nɛ Timoti nseŋ wu kananɛ agbir bɔlɔ kade na to nɛ mbe kagbene jija mo ga.

english_verse: He went to the synagogue to speak to the Jews and to anyone who worshiped with them. Day after day he also spoke to everyone he met in the market.
translation_verse: Amoso, saŋkama e daa ji Juwebi nɛ nnyamase nɛ b daa bunyaŋ Ebɔrɛ na emɔrɔ nna ashi nshɛrbu na to nseŋ naa yɔ kelɔnɛ so gba kachɛ kama n ya kaa ji basa nɛ e daa tu ndoŋ emɔrɔ.

english_verse: Some of them were Epicureans and some were Stoics, and they started arguing with him. People were asking, “What is this know-it-all trying to say?” Some even said, “Paul must be preaching about foreign gods! That's what he means when he talks about Jesus and about people rising from death.”
translation_verse: Kanyiashenfinpoana be ntuŋ nɛ baa tre Epikyurisebi nɛ Stowikebi na malɛ gba be beko daŋ ba ji mo emɔrɔ nɛ beko bishi abar: “Manɛ nɛ kanyiashenfuloŋwura ere bee sha keŋini ere?” Nɛ beko kaŋɛ: “K du fanɛ e bee malga ebɔrɛ pɔtɛana ko be asheŋ nna.” Pɔɔl ka daa malga Yesu be ketiŋi luwu to na be asheŋ so nɛ b daŋ kaŋɛ loŋ na.

english_verse: They brought Paul before a council called the Areopagus, and said, “Tell us what your new teaching is all about.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ b keta Pɔɔl n yɔ nshɛrwuraana ko nɛ b daa shɛr Ariɔpages be kebee so na kutɔ n ya kaŋɛ mo:

english_verse: More than anything else the people of Athens and the foreigners living there loved to hear and to talk about anything new.
translation_verse: Atens be ndetoebi kikɛ nɛ befɔana na daa maa kɔ wale she kebaatase a nu ŋko a kaŋɛ abar ebaru popɔr nɛ b nu be asheŋ so so nɛ b daŋ kaŋɛ loŋ na.

english_verse: So Paul stood up in front of the council and said: People of Athens, I see that you are very religious.
translation_verse: Nɛ Pɔɔl niŋi to n yili Ariɔpages be nshɛr na to nseŋ kaŋɛ: “Atensebi, n wu kananɛ men ta menyi be yirda n wɔtɔ ebɔrɛ damtaana to.

english_verse: As I was going through your city and looking at the things you worship, I found an altar with the words, “To an Unknown God.” You worship this God, but you don't really know him. So I want to tell you about him.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal manɛ so, ŋ ka nite menyi be kade ere to nseŋ wu asɔ nɛ menyee bunyaŋ, n wu bɔrɛsure ko nɛ b sibɛ kumo so: ‘Ebɔrɛ nɛ b maŋ nyi peya.’ Kusɔ nɛ menyee bunyaŋ nsaa maa nyi na be asheŋ nɛ m baa kaŋɛ menyi naniere na.

english_verse: This God made the world and everything in it. He is Lord of heaven and earth, and he doesn't live in temples built by human hands.
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ nɛ e to durnya ere nɛ asɔ nɛ a wɔ kumo to kikɛ ere e la ebɔrɛso nɛ kasawule kikɛ be Enyɛnpe, mo alɛ maa chena nshɛrbu nɛ enyiŋgbasa pɔr nɛ b baa bunyaŋ mo to.

english_verse: He doesn't need help from anyone. He gives life, breath, and everything else to all people.
translation_verse: Mo alɛ maŋ naa sha kusɔ kama nɛ nyiŋgbasa ta enɔ a shuŋ a sa mo, ŋkpal manɛ so, mo e naa sa nyiŋgbasa ŋkpa nɛ efute nɛ kusɔ kama nyam.

english_verse: God has done all this, so that we will look for him and reach out and find him. He isn't far from any of us,
translation_verse: E daŋ wora loŋ nna nɛ b laa n fin mo kukoko to n ya nya mo ashi bumo be kafin na to. Ama anyi be ekama ere nyam nɛ Ebɔrɛ maŋ wɔ kufɔ,

english_verse: and he gives us the power to live, to move, and to be who we are. “We are his children,” just as some of your poets have said.
translation_verse: ŋkpal manɛ so: ‘Mo e naa shin nɛ an wɔtɔ a nite a kilgi to a du kananɛ an du ere na.’ Menyi be besibɛpo malɛ e naa kaŋɛ loŋ: ‘Anyi alɛ gba la mbe mbia nna.’

english_verse: Since we are God's children, we must not think that he is like an idol made out of gold or silver or stone. He isn't like anything that humans have thought up and made.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal anyi alɛ ka la mbe mbia so, an sa maa fɛ fanɛ Ebɔrɛ du fanɛ shuwa be kusɔ pɔrso ŋko gbiti be kusɔ pɔrso ŋko kejembu be kusɔ pɔrso ko nɛ nyiŋgbasa ta mo gbagba be kenyi be nfɛra n wora nna.

english_verse: In the past, God forgave all this because people did not know what they were doing. But now he says that everyone everywhere must turn to him.
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ kplaŋ saŋɛ nɛ basa daa maŋ nyi na so, ama naniere e bee kaŋɛ ekama kaplɛkama fanɛ e lar mbe alubi to.

english_verse: He has set a day when he will judge the world's people with fairness. And he has chosen the man Jesus to do the judging for him. God has given proof of this to all of us by raising Jesus from death.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal manɛ so, e lara kachako n yili a sha keshin nɛ esa ko nɛ e lara n yili na e ji durnya ere demu kumo be ekpa so. Mo alɛ ŋini ekama nyam kumo be loŋ n shin nɛ amodoŋwura tiŋi luwu to.”

english_verse: As soon as the people heard Paul say a man had been raised from death, some of them started laughing. Others said, “We will hear you talk about this some other time.”
translation_verse: B ka nu Pɔɔl ka malga ketiŋi luwu to be asheŋ na nɛ bumo be beko wora mo eyurto nɛ beko malɛ kaŋɛ: “Anyi ere kraa sha kenamba n nu fo kamalga na.”

english_verse: When Paul left the council meeting,
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Pɔɔl lar nshɛr na to n yɔ.

english_verse: some of the men put their faith in the Lord and went with Paul. One of them was a council member named Dionysius. A woman named Damaris and several others also put their faith in the Lord.
translation_verse: Nɛ basa ko yɔ mo kutɔ n ya ki bebɛsopo. Bumo to be beko e daa la Dayɔnaisias, Ariɔpages be katuŋ na to be esa, nɛ kache ko nɛ baa tre Damaris na n ta beko malɛ gba n ti so.

english_verse: Paul left Athens and went to Corinth,
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ Pɔɔl lar Atens n ta n yɔ Kɔrint.

english_verse: where he met Aquila, a Jewish man from Pontus. Not long before this, Aquila had come from Italy with his wife Priscilla, because Emperor Claudius had ordered the Jewish people to leave Rome. Paul went to see Aquila and Priscilla
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nɛ e ya tu Juwnyɛn ko nɛ b daŋ kurge mo ashi Pɔntes a tre mo Akwila na. Mo nɛ mbe eche Prisila ka daŋ shi Itali m ba ndoŋ ŋkpal Ewurgboŋ Klawdias ka daŋ ju Juwebi kikɛ ashi Rom na so, k daa maŋ chɛr.

english_verse: and found out they were tent makers. Paul was also a tent maker, so he stayed with them, and they worked together.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Pɔɔl ya chɔrɔ bumo nseŋ shir bumo pe a wɔtɔ a baa ewajɛbu a fa a nya amansherbi a tɔ mbe asɔ jiso fanɛ kananɛ bumo gbagba daa wora na.

english_verse: Every Sabbath, Paul went to the synagogue. He spoke to Jews and Gentiles and tried to win them over.
translation_verse: Kewushiachɛ kama e daa yɔ nshɛrbu na to nna n ya kaa bugi asheŋ to a kaŋɛ Juwebi nɛ Griikebi kikɛ a sha keshin nɛ b wu fanɛ mbe kamalga na e bɔla ekpa.

english_verse: But after Silas and Timothy came from Macedonia, he spent all his time preaching to the Jews about Jesus the Messiah.
translation_verse: Sailas nɛ Timoti ka shi Masɛdonia m ba nɛ Pɔɔl yige kusɔ kama nsaa wɔtɔ a bɔ kubɔya na a bugi kumo to nɛnɛ a kaŋɛ Juwebi na fanɛ Yesu e la Kristo na.

english_verse: Finally, they turned against him and insulted him. So he shook the dust from his clothes and told them, “Whatever happens to you will be your own fault! I am not to blame. From now on I am going to preach to the Gentiles.”
translation_verse: Nɛ b ji mo emɔrɔ kpakpaso nseŋ tege mo. Nɛ mo alɛ gbaŋgbaŋ mbe asɔbuuso to be shishɛr n lɛ bumo n wora bumo kusha ŋ kaŋɛ: “Menyi be ŋklaŋ e baa wɔ menyi gbagba be amu so, mannɛ ma e bar kumo. Yili kabre a yɔ nnyamase kutɔ nɛ meeŋ baa yɔ n ya kaa bɔ kubɔya na a sa bumo.”

english_verse: Paul then moved into the house of a man named Titius Justus, who worshiped God and lived next door to the synagogue.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e yige bumo nseŋ yɔ n ya kaa wɔ kanyɛn ko nɛ e daa bunyaŋ Ebɔrɛ na pe. Mbe ketre e daa la Titias Jɛstes. Mbe kowu daŋ mata ndoŋ be nshɛrbu nna.

english_verse: Crispus was the leader of the synagogue. He and everyone in his family put their faith in the Lord. Many others in Corinth also heard the message, and all the people who had faith in the Lord were baptized.
translation_verse: Nshɛrbu na be enimu nɛ b daa tre Krispes na nɛ mbe laŋ to ebi daŋ yirda Enyɛnpe na nɛ Kɔrintebi be basa damta gba nu kubɔya na n yirda nɛ b bɛr bumo kabɔrɛbɛr.

english_verse: One night, Paul had a vision, and in it the Lord said, “Don't be afraid to keep on preaching. Don't stop!
translation_verse: Kanyɛso ko Pɔɔl ku bɔrɛdare n nu Enyɛnpe ka bee kaŋɛ mo: “Sa maa lɔ kufu n yige, baa kraa malga, ŋkpal manɛ so, n wɔ fo kaman.

english_verse: I am with you, and you won't be harmed. Many people in this city belong to me.”
translation_verse: Esa kama maaŋ tiŋ n wora fo shɛŋ, ŋkpal manɛ so, kade ere to be basa damta la meya nna.”

english_verse: Paul stayed on in Corinth for a year and a half, teaching God's message to the people.
translation_verse: Kafɛ nɛ afɔl ashe nɛ Pɔɔl daŋ ji ndoŋ a ŋini kade na to ebi Ebɔrɛ be kubɔya na.

english_verse: While Gallio was governor of Achaia, some of the Jewish leaders got together and grabbed Paul. They brought him into court
translation_verse: Galio ka ba ki Romebi be gomena ashi Griis nɛ Juwebi na wora kɔnɔkoŋwule n nyaŋ Pɔɔl n ta mo n yɔ demujikpa n ya kaŋɛ gomena na:

english_verse: and said, “This man is trying to make our people worship God in a way that is against our Law!”
translation_verse: “Kanyɛn ere bee wora ania nna a sha fanɛ basa e nu n sa mo nseŋ bɔla ekpa nɛ anyi be mbra na maa ŋini so m bɛ Ebɔrɛ so.”

english_verse: Even before Paul could speak, Gallio said, “If you were charging this man with a crime or some other wrong, I would have to listen to you.
translation_verse: Pɔɔl ka bugi kɔnɔ nɛ e malga nɛ Galio ku mbe kɔnɔ so ŋ kaŋɛ Juwebi na: “Demu ere daa la kulubi ko ŋko dalubisheŋ ko be demu nna, a daŋ daga ŋ ka ji menyi Juwebi ere kanyiti.

english_verse: But since this concerns only words, names, and your own law, you will have to take care of it yourselves. I refuse to judge such matters.”
translation_verse: Ama k ka la mmalga nɛ atre nɛ menyi be mbraana be asheŋ ere bre, menyi gbagba e ji kumo kumo be ekpa so. M maaŋ ji loŋ be asheŋ be demu.”

english_verse: Then he sent them out of the court.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e shin nɛ b ju bumo n lar demujikpa na.

english_verse: The crowd grabbed Sosthenes, the Jewish leader, and beat him up in front of the court. But none of this mattered to Gallio. Paul Returns to Antioch in Syria
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ bumo kikɛ nyaŋ Sɔstenis nɛ e daa la nshɛrbu na to be enimu na m bri mo demujikpa na be kabuna to. Ama kumo alɛ daa maŋ tir Galio gbrɛbi gba kikɛ. Pɔɔl ka bɛta n yɔ Antiɔk be asheŋ

english_verse: After Paul had stayed for a while with the Lord's followers in Corinth, he told them goodbye and sailed on to Syria with Aquila and Priscilla. But before he left, he had his head shaved at Cenchreae because he had made a promise to God.
translation_verse: Pɔɔl ka chena bekurgepoana na kutɔ ashi Kɔrint n wora nchɛnnyɔ nɛ e kela bumo nɛ mo nɛ Prisila nɛ Akwila luri ekuloŋgboŋ ko to m bɔla nchu so n yɔ Siriya. E daŋ nase kɔnɔ ashi Kɛŋkriya nna n sa Ebɔrɛ n shin nɛ b she mbe kumu pɔɛŋ nɛ e luri ekuloŋgboŋ to n yɔ.

english_verse: The three of them arrived in Ephesus, where Paul left Priscilla and Aquila. He then went into the synagogue to talk with the people there.
translation_verse: B ka ba fo Ɛfeses nɛ Pɔɔl yige Prisila nɛ Akwila nseŋ yɔ ndoŋ be nshɛrbu to nɛ mo nɛ Juwebi na ya ji abɔrɛsheŋ na be emɔrɔ.

english_verse: They asked him to stay longer, but he refused.
translation_verse: Nɛ b kule mo fanɛ e chena bumo kutɔ kade na to n wora nchɛnnyɔ nɛ e kini.

english_verse: Paul sailed to Caesarea, where he greeted the church. Then he went on to Antioch.
translation_verse: E ka ta m ba fo Sizariya nɛ e yɔ Jerusalɛm n ya chɔrɔ ndoŋ be asɔriebi na nseŋ yɔ Antiɔk.

english_verse: After staying there for a while, he left and visited several places in Galatia and Phrygia. He helped the followers there to become stronger in their faith. Apollos in Ephesus
translation_verse: E ka ya wora nchɛnnyɔ ndoŋ nɛ e lar ndoŋ m bɔla Galeesha nɛ Frijia be efuliana so be egbaŋ to a leŋ beyirdapoana na kikɛ to. Apɔlɔs ka ba Ɛfeses nɛ Kɔrint be asheŋ

english_verse: A Jewish man named Apollos came to Ephesus. Apollos had been born in the city of Alexandria. He was a very good speaker and knew a lot about the Scriptures.
translation_verse: Juwnyɛn ko nɛ baa tre Apɔlɔs nɛ b daŋ kurge mo Alɛkzaandria na daŋ ba Ɛfeses. E daa nyi kamalga to ga nsaa nyi abɔrɛsibɛ na malɛ ga.

english_verse: He also knew much about the Lord's Way, and he spoke about it with great excitement. What he taught about Jesus was right, but all he knew was John's message about baptism.
translation_verse: B daŋ ŋini mo Enyɛnpe be ekpa na be asheŋ nna nɛ e daa wɔtɔ a yeŋi so a malga nsaa ŋini basa Yesu be asheŋ na kashenteŋto nɛ amo be ekpa so. Ama Jɔn be kabɔrɛbɛr na nawule be asheŋ nɛ e daa nyi.

english_verse: Apollos started speaking bravely in the synagogue. But when Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him to their home and helped him understand God's Way even better.
translation_verse: Prisila nɛ Akwila ka nu e ka malga nshɛrbu na to kenyɛnso n loge nɛ b keta mo n yɔ epe n ya bugi Ebɔrɛ be asheŋ na to ŋ ŋini mo nɛnɛ.

english_verse: Apollos decided to travel through Achaia. So the Lord's followers wrote letters, encouraging the followers there to welcome him. After Apollos arrived in Achaia, he was a great help to everyone who had put their faith in the Lord Jesus because of God's gift of undeserved grace.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Apɔlɔs yili kumo fanɛ e beeŋ yɔ Griis. Nɛ Ɛfeses be beyirdapoana na leŋ mo to nseŋ chɛ mo to n sibɛ nwɔl n sa bumo kurgepoana ashi Griis a kaŋɛ bumo fanɛ b sɔ mo nɛnɛ. E ka fo ndoŋ nɛ e chɛ bumo nɛ Ebɔrɛ ta mbe kuwɔr be kakɛ n shin nɛ b ki beyirdapo na to ga,

english_verse: He got into fierce arguments with the Jewish people, and in public he used the Scriptures to prove that Jesus is the Messiah.
translation_verse: ŋkpal manɛ so, e daŋ ta kamalganyi nna n ji m bri Juwebi na basa to a ta abɔrɛsibɛ na a bugi asheŋ a ŋini bumo nɛnɛ fanɛ Yesu e la Kristo na.

english_verse: While Apollos was in Corinth, Paul traveled across the hill country to Ephesus, where he met some of the Lord's followers.
translation_verse: Jemanɛ nɛ Apɔlɔs daa wɔ Kɔrint na nɛ Pɔɔl malɛ na kasawule na kikɛ so loŋ n ya fo Ɛfeses.

english_verse: He asked them, “When you put your faith in Jesus, were you given the Holy Spirit?” “No!” they answered. “We have never even heard of the Holy Spirit.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nɛ e ya tu beyirdapo ko m bishi bumo: “Men ka ki beyirdapo, Kiyoyu Cheeŋ na gbelge menyi so a?” Nɛ b kaŋɛ: “Anyi ere maŋ nu fanɛ Kiyoyu Cheeŋ ko malɛ wɔtɔ gba.”

english_verse: “Then why were you baptized?” Paul asked. They answered, “Because of what John taught.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Pɔɔl bishi bumo: “Nɛ nuso be kabɔrɛbɛr nɛ b bɛr menyi?” Nɛ b kaŋɛ: “Kabɔrɛbɛr nɛ Jɔn daŋ bɔ kumo be asheŋ na.”

english_verse: Paul replied, “John baptized people so they would turn to God. But he also told them someone else was coming, and they should put their faith in him. Jesus is the one that John was talking about.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Pɔɔl kaŋɛ: “Kabɔrɛbɛr nɛ Jɔn daa bɛr basa na daa ŋini fanɛ basa na yɛ b lar bumo be alubi to, ama e daa kaŋɛ ekama nna fanɛ a daga fanɛ e yirda esa nɛ e wɔ mo ere Jɔn be kaman a ba na, mo e la Yesu na.”

english_verse: After the people heard Paul say this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
translation_verse: Ɛfeses be beyirdapoana na ka nu loŋ nɛ b shin nɛ b bɛr bumo kabɔrɛbɛr Enyɛnpe Yesu be ketre to.

english_verse: Then Paul placed his hands on them. The Holy Spirit was given to them, and they spoke unknown languages and prophesied.
translation_verse: Nɛ Pɔɔl ta mbe enɔana n deŋi bumo so nɛ Kiyoyu Cheeŋ na gbelge bumo so nɛ b gbar ŋgbar nɛ bumo gbagba maa nu nseŋ naŋ wu abɔrɛsheŋ ŋ kaŋɛ.

english_verse: There were about twelve men in this group.
translation_verse: Bumo kikɛ daŋ fo fanɛ benyɛn kuduanyɔ.

english_verse: For three months Paul went to the synagogue and talked bravely with the people about God's kingdom. He tried to win them over,
translation_verse: Pɔɔl be afɔl asa nɛ e wɔtɔ a yɔ ndoŋ be nshɛrbu to n ya kaa malga basa na kutɔ kenyɛnso a ji bumo emɔrɔ a sha b ka yirda fanɛ Ebɔrɛ be kuwura na to be asheŋ nɛ e daa malga na la kashenteŋ nna.

english_verse: but some of them were stubborn and refused to believe. In front of everyone they said terrible things about God's Way. Paul left and took the followers with him to the lecture hall of Tyrannus. He spoke there every day
translation_verse: Ama bumo be beko daŋ ta amu kpakpaso ŋ kini kenu nseŋ malga mmalga lubi basa na kikɛ to ŋ gbiti ekpa nɛ Enyɛnpe bee ŋini na. Nɛ Pɔɔl yige bumo nseŋ keta beyirdapoana na nɛ b wɔtɔ a shɛr kachɛ kama a ber abɔrɛsheŋ na be bare ashi lambu nɛ Tiranes daa shɛr basa a malga a sa bumo na to.

english_verse: God gave Paul the power to work great miracles.
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ daa bɔla Pɔɔl so nna a wora emamachisheŋ popɔr damta ga.

english_verse: People even took handkerchiefs and aprons that had touched Paul's body, and they carried them to everyone who was sick. All of the sick people were healed, and the evil spirits went out.
translation_verse: B daa ta Pɔɔl be antikiana nɛ mbe kushuŋ to be asɔbuuso gba nna n ya kaa sa belɔpo nɛ a bee shin nɛ basa na be alɔ nɛ ayoyu lubiana malɛ gba bee lar bumo to.

english_verse: Some Jewish men started going around trying to force out evil spirits by using the name of the Lord Jesus. They said to the spirits, “Come out in the name of that same Jesus that Paul preaches about!”
translation_verse: Juwebi ko gba daa na a kilgi to a ju ayoyu lubi nseŋ wora ania nɛ b ta Enyɛnpe Yesu be ketre gba n wora loŋ ŋ kaŋɛ ayoyu lubi na: “Yesu nɛ Pɔɔl bee bɔ mbe kubɔya na be ketre to nɛ mee kaŋɛ menyi na, men lar esa ere to.”

english_verse: Seven sons of a high priest named Sceva were doing this,
translation_verse: Bɔrɛmatapo nimuso nɛ baa tre Skiva na be mbinyɛnbi ashunu e daa wora loŋ na.

english_verse: when an evil spirit said to them, “I know Jesus! And I have heard about Paul. But who are you?”
translation_verse: Nɛ kiyoyu lubi na kaŋɛ bumo: “N nyi Yesu nsaa nyi Pɔɔl be asheŋ nɛ basa mo malɛ e la menyi alɛ?”

english_verse: Then the man with the evil spirit jumped on them and beat them up. They ran out of the house, naked and bruised.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ kanyɛn nɛ kiyoyu lubi na wɔ mo to na nyaŋɛ to m buu bumo n doro bumo nseŋ kpɛa bumo be asɔbuuso to n lɛ nɛ b lar mbe kowu na to n delge so n shile n choŋ.

english_verse: When the Jews and Gentiles in Ephesus heard about this, they were so frightened that they praised the name of the Lord Jesus.
translation_verse: Juwebi nɛ nnyamase nɛ b daa wɔ Ɛfeses na kikɛ ka nu kumo nɛ kufu pɛ bumo kikɛ ga nɛ b sa Enyɛnpe Yesu be ketre kemaŋkura ga.

english_verse: Many who were followers now started telling everyone about the evil things they had been doing.
translation_verse: Nɛ beyirdapoana na be bedamta ba basa to m ba kaa bugi bumo gbagba be afito a kaŋɛ alubi nɛ b wora.

english_verse: After all this had happened, Paul decided to visit Macedonia and Achaia on his way to Jerusalem. Paul had said, “From there I will go on to Rome.”
translation_verse: Asheŋ nɛ a wora na be kaman nɛ Kiyoyu Cheeŋ na shin nɛ Pɔɔl yili kumo mbe kagbene to fanɛ e beeŋ bɔla Masɛdonia nɛ Griis to n ta n yɔ Jerusalɛm. Le nɛ e daŋ kaŋɛ: “A daga fanɛ, ŋ kaŋ yɔ ndoŋ, n fo Rom gba.”

english_verse: So he sent his two helpers, Timothy and Erastus, to Macedonia. But he stayed on in Asia for a while.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ e shuŋi mbe bechɛtopo anyɔ ko Masɛdonia nseŋ kraa wɔ Eeshia be kasawule so. Mbe bechɛtopo na e daa la Timoti nɛ Irastes.

english_verse: At that time there was serious trouble because of the Lord's Way.
translation_verse: Jemanɛ na so nɛ kenishipere be kayurnyaŋ koso Ɛfeses ŋkpal Enyɛnpe be ekpa na so.

english_verse: A silversmith named Demetrius had a business that made silver models of the temple of the goddess Artemis. Those who worked for him earned a lot of money.
translation_verse: Gbitibɔyɛponyɛn ko e daa wɔ Ɛfeses nɛ baa tre mo Demitrias. E daa ta egbiti nna a lɔŋɛ asɔ nɛ a du fanɛ kegbirche Aatemis be ebu. Mbe beshumpo daa nya tɔnɔ ga ashi kushuŋ na to.

english_verse: Demetrius brought together everyone who was in the same business and said: Friends, you know we make a good living at this.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ e tre mbe beshumpoana na nɛ bekama nɛ bumo alɛ gba daa shuŋ loŋ be kushuŋ na m ba shɛr ŋ kaŋɛ: “Men nyi fanɛ kushuŋ ere e naa nyalɛ anyi.

english_verse: But you have surely seen and heard how this man Paul is upsetting a lot of people, not only in Ephesus, but almost everywhere in Asia. He claims that the gods we humans make are not really gods at all.
translation_verse: Menyi alɛ gba bee wu nseŋ naa nu kusɔ nɛ kanyɛn nɛ baa tre Pɔɔl na wɔtɔ a wora. E wɔtɔ nna a kaŋɛ basa fanɛ agbirana nɛ baa lɔŋɛ na maŋ la ebɔrɛana kikɛ. Mo alɛ tiŋ n shin nɛ basa damta ashi Ɛfeses nfe nɛ Eeshia be kasawule ere so be basa damta shuli fanɛ mbe kamalga na la kashenteŋ nna.

english_verse: Everyone will start saying terrible things about our business. They will stop respecting the temple of the goddess Artemis, who is worshiped in Asia and all over the world. Our great goddess will be forgotten!
translation_verse: Nɛ an maŋ de so, basa beeŋ jija anyi be kushuŋ ere be ketre. Kumo alɛ be kaman, nɛ an maŋ de so, basa beeŋ ba kaa fɛl kegbirche Aatemis be ebu na nɛ mbe ketre maaŋ naŋ dii kikɛ. Men keni, kegbirche nɛ basa kikɛ bee bunyaŋ ashi Eeshia be efuli ere so na nɛ baa sha kewora loŋ na.”

english_verse: When the workers heard this, they got angry and started shouting, “Great is Artemis, the goddess of the Ephesians!”
translation_verse: Jimaŋ na ka nu asheŋ nɛ Demitrias malga na nɛ agbo pɛ bumo nɛ b fara a ponte a kaŋɛ: “Ɛfesesebi be kegbirche Aatemis e la elempo.”

english_verse: Soon the whole city was in a riot, and some men grabbed Gaius and Aristarchus, who had come from Macedonia with Paul. Then everyone in the crowd rushed to the place where the town meetings were held.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ kebagato na sɔ kade na to kikɛ nɛ jimaŋ yenso na nyaŋ Gayes nɛ Aristaakes, Masɛdonia be basa anyɔ ko nɛ bumo nɛ Pɔɔl daa na na ŋ gberge bumo n yɔ kade na be nshɛrkpa.

english_verse: Paul wanted to go out and speak to the people, but the Lord's followers would not let him.
translation_verse: Pɔɔl gbagba daa sha keyɔ jimaŋ na be anishito nna ashi nshɛr na to nɛ beyirdapoana na ju mo.

english_verse: A few of the local officials were friendly to Paul, and they sent someone to warn him not to go.
translation_verse: Nɛ efuli na so be benimuana nɛ b daa la Pɔɔl mo teriana na gba shuŋi ŋ kaŋɛ mo fanɛ e sa maŋ kaŋ ba nshɛrkpa na to.

english_verse: Some of the people in the meeting were shouting one thing, and others were shouting something else. Everyone was completely confused, and most of them did not even know why they were there.
translation_verse: Jemanɛ ere so kikɛ nɛ nshɛr na kikɛ bee baga to, nɛ ekama bee gbar a juge to, ŋkpal manɛ so, bumo be bedamta gba daa maŋ nyi kusɔ nɛ b shɛr ndoŋ nɛ b wora.

english_verse: Several of the Jewish leaders pushed a man named Alexander to the front of the crowd and started telling him what to say. He motioned with his hand and tried to explain what was going on.
translation_verse: Basa na be beko daa tama fanɛ Alɛkzaanda be asheŋ nna, ŋkpal Juwebi na ka daŋ shin nɛ e ya yili anishito na so. Ndoŋ nna nɛ Alɛkzaanda wora jimaŋ na enɔ a sha kemalga m mɔlga mbe kumu ashi jimaŋ na kutɔ.

english_verse: But when the crowd saw that he was Jewish, they all shouted for two hours, “Great is Artemis, the goddess of the Ephesians!”
translation_verse: B ka pin fanɛ e la Juw nna nɛ bumo kikɛ ponte awa anyɔ a kaŋɛ kusɔ koŋwule nɛ b daŋ fara ŋ kaŋɛ na: “Ɛfesesebi be kegbirche Aatemis e la elempo.”

english_verse: Finally, a town official made the crowd be quiet. Then he said: People of Ephesus, who in the world doesn't know that our city is the center for worshiping the great goddess Artemis? Who doesn't know that her image which fell from heaven is right here?
translation_verse: Jimaŋ na wora awɔr na loŋ nɛ kade na to be krachigboŋ na ya tiŋ n lɔlɔ bumo nɛ b lo to nɛ e kaŋɛ bumo: “Ɛfesesebi, ekama nyi fanɛ Ɛfeses e naa keni kegbirche Aatemis be ebu na nɛ kejembu cheembi nɛ k shi ebɔrɛso n tɔr na so.

english_verse: No one can deny this, and so you should calm down and not do anything foolish.
translation_verse: Esa kama maaŋ tiŋ n chɛ kumo be loŋ, amoso, men wushi eyur boeŋ n sa maŋ kuse n wora asheŋ brembreŋ.

english_verse: You have brought men in here who have not robbed temples or spoken against our goddess.
translation_verse: Basa nɛ men bar nfe ere maŋ yuri kegbirlambu na to be kusɔ kama, bumo alɛ maŋ malga kulubi ŋ gbiti anyi be kegbirche na.

english_verse: If Demetrius and his workers have a case against these men, we have courts and judges. Let them take their complaints there.
translation_verse: Nɛ Demitrias nɛ mbe beshumpo nɛ esa ko kɔ abar gba nna, baaŋ tiŋ n yɛr amodoŋwura benimuana na kutɔ nchɛ nɛ baa kaa lar a chena demujikpa na to na nɛ bumo nɛ amodoŋwura ya kaŋɛ kusɔ nɛ b wora abar.

english_verse: But if you want to do more than that, the matter will have to be brought before the city council.
translation_verse: Ama nɛ fanɛ men kraa sha kusɔ ko n ti so, kakpa nɛ baaŋ ji loŋ be demu e la ndetobia be nshɛr nɛ mbra na bee ŋini na to.

english_verse: We could easily be accused of starting a riot today. There is no excuse for it! We cannot even give a reason for this uproar.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal manɛ so, nɛ anyi maŋ de so, Romebi na beeŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ kusɔ nɛ k wora ere la kelantokɔ nna. Le be kebagato ere maŋ kɔ kifi. Anyi alɛ maaŋ tiŋ ŋ kaŋɛ bumo kusɔ nɛ k bar le be kebagato ere.”

english_verse: After saying this, he told the people to leave.
translation_verse: Krachi na ka malga n loge nɛ e shin nɛ basa na pesaŋ to n yɔ epe.

english_verse: When the riot was over, Paul sent for the followers and encouraged them. He then told them goodbye and left for Macedonia.
translation_verse: Basa na be kebagato na ka baŋ loge nɛ Pɔɔl tre beyirdapoana na n ta mmalga damta n leŋ bumo to ga nseŋ kela bumo nseŋ ta n yɔ Masɛdonia n ya yɔ ndoŋ be ndeana na to

english_verse: As he traveled from place to place, he encouraged the followers with many messages. Finally, he went to Greece
translation_verse: n ya kaa ta mmalga damta a leŋ beyirdapoana na to.

english_verse: and stayed there for three months. Paul was about to sail to Syria. But some of the Jewish leaders plotted against him, so he decided to return by way of Macedonia.
translation_verse: Ade be kaman nɛ e yili ndoŋ n yɔ Griis n ya ji afɔl asa ndoŋ. E daŋ naa bela ase nna nɛ e luri ekuloŋgboŋ ko to m bɔla nchu so n yɔ Siriya nseŋ nu Juwebi na ka bee sha kemɔ mo nɛ e naŋ bɛta m bɔla Masɛdonia.

english_verse: With him were Sopater, son of Pyrrhus from Berea, and Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica. Gaius from Derbe was also with him, and so were Timothy and the two Asians, Tychicus and Trophimus.
translation_verse: Mo nɛ Pires nɛ e shi Beriya na pibi Sopata nɛ Aristaakes nɛ Sɛkundes nɛ b shi Tɛsalɔnika na nɛ Gayes nɛ e shi Dɛbi na nɛ Timoti nɛ Eeshia be efuli so ebi Tikikes nɛ Trɔfimes na e daŋ yɔ.

english_verse: They went on ahead to Troas and waited for us there.
translation_verse: Bumo e daŋ juŋkpar n ya kaa jo anyi ashi Trowas.

english_verse: After the Festival of Thin Bread, we sailed from Philippi. Five days later we met them in Troas and stayed there for a week. Paul's Last Visit to Troas
translation_verse: Bodobodo nɛ a maŋ kɔ yiisi be Kejigboŋ na be jemanɛ ka choŋ nɛ an yili Filipai n luri ekuloŋgboŋ ko to m bɔla nchu so n ji nchɛ anu nseŋ ya tu bumo Trowas nɛ an kikɛ ji bɔkwe ndoŋ. Pɔɔl be lalaloge be kechɔrɔ Trowas be bebɛsopo be asheŋ

english_verse: On the first day of the week we met to break bread together. Paul spoke to the people until midnight because he was leaving the next morning.
translation_verse: Bɔkwe be kachɛ juŋkparso be kanyɛso ko an shɛr m bɔ enɔ n wɔtɔ kɔnɔkoŋwuleso be kawiejibi na to nɛ Pɔɔl kpal e ka beeŋ lar kade na to kumo be ŋklade na so m bɔ kubɔya na loŋ nɛ kiidiso ya fo.

english_verse: In the upstairs room where we were meeting, there were a lot of lamps.
translation_verse: Ndia damta ko malɛ e daa wɔ esoso be ebu nɛ an daŋ shɛr na to.

english_verse: A young man by the name of Eutychus was sitting on a window sill. While Paul was speaking, the young man got very sleepy. Finally, he went to sleep and fell three floors all the way down to the ground. When they picked him up, he was dead.
translation_verse: Kabrantiɛbia ko daa tase tokuro so nɛ baa tre mo Yutikes. Ŋkpal Pɔɔl ka malga n chɛr na so nɛ edi laa mo nɛ e fara a di hale n ya di n choŋ so n shi esoso be ebu sasopo na to m ba tɔr kasawule nɛ b ba nɛ b ba ta mo nɛ e wu.

english_verse: Paul went down and bent over Eutychus. He took him in his arms and said, “Don't worry! He's alive.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Pɔɔl gbelge n ya teŋi mbe kumu to n dese mo so nseŋ ta mbe enɔana m mea mo nseŋ kaŋɛ: “Men sa maa fɔŋ so, e kɔ ŋkpa.”

english_verse: After Paul had gone back upstairs, he broke bread, and ate with us. He then spoke until dawn and left.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Pɔɔl naŋ bɛta n dii n yɔ esoso be ebu na to n ya buri bodobodo to n we. Pɔɔl ka malga bumo kutɔ loŋ hale nɛ epeŋi ya pete nɛ e yige bumo nseŋ yɔ.

english_verse: Then the followers took the young man home alive and were very happy. The Voyage from Troas to Miletus
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ b keta kabrantiɛbia na ŋkpa to n yɔ epe. Bumo be ŋgbene daŋ fuli bumo ga ŋkpal loŋ so. Pɔɔl ka shi Trowas n yɔ Mailites be asheŋ

english_verse: Paul decided to travel by land to Assos. The rest of us went on ahead by ship, and we were to take him aboard there.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ an juŋkpar n yɔ ekuloŋgboŋ ko to m bɔla nchu so n ta n yɔ Asɔs, kakpa nɛ an daa yɔ nɛ an ya ta Pɔɔl na. E ka daŋ bɔla aya so n yɔ ndoŋ na so nɛ e daŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ an wora loŋ.

english_verse: When he met us in Assos, he came aboard, and we sailed on to Mitylene.
translation_verse: E ka tu anyi Asɔs nɛ an ta mo n wɔtɔ ekuloŋ na to n ta n yɔ Mitilini

english_verse: The next day we came to a place near Chios, and the following day we reached Samos. The day after that we sailed to Miletus.
translation_verse: n ya yili ndoŋ n luri ekuloŋgboŋ ko to n di ŋ klade m ba baŋ Kiyɔs so n choŋ. Kumo be ŋklade nɛ an ta n yɔ Samɔs n naŋ klade n yɔ Mailites.

english_verse: Paul had decided to sail on past Ephesus, because he did not want to spend too much time in Asia. He was in a hurry and wanted to be in Jerusalem in time for Pentecost. Paul Says Goodbye to the Church Leaders of Ephesus
translation_verse: Pɔɔl daa sha kekpar Ɛfeses so nna n yɔ, ŋkpal manɛ so, e daa maŋ naa sha kenaŋ n chɛr Eeshia be efuli so. E daa kuse nna nɛ e ya fo Jerusalɛm ta a ba Pɛntekɔst be kachɛgboŋ na, nɛ e beeŋ tiŋ nna na. Pɔɔl ka kela Ɛfeses be asɔri to be benimuana be asheŋ

english_verse: From Miletus, Paul sent a message for the church leaders at Ephesus to come and meet with him.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Pɔɔl yili Mailites n shuŋi kabɔ fanɛ e ya kaŋɛ ndoŋ be asɔriebi be benimuana fanɛ b shɛr mo to.

english_verse: When they got there, he said: You know everything I did during the time I was with you when I first came to Asia.
translation_verse: B ka ba nɛ e kaŋɛ bumo: “Men nyi kebaawɔtɔ nɛ n daa kɔ a wɔ menyi kutɔ na yili kachɛ nɛ n fara m ba Eeshia be efuli ere so na m ba fo kabre.

english_verse: Some of the Jews plotted against me and caused me a lot of sorrow and trouble. But I served the Lord and was humble.
translation_verse: N daa shuŋ ma kushuŋ nna fanɛ kebɔrɛnya nsaa yɔɔ ma kumu saŋkama a wɔtɔ a nya kagbenejija a shu nchɛ nchɛ to ŋkpal Juwebi be nia nɛ b daa kre ma na so.

english_verse: When I preached in public or taught in your homes, I didn't hold back from telling anything that would help you.
translation_verse: Men nyi fanɛ saŋɛ nɛ n daŋ bɔ kubɔya na n sa menyi nseŋ ŋini menyi asheŋ basa to nɛ menyi peana na, n daa maŋ ta kusɔ kama nɛ k beeŋ chɛ menyi to ŋ ŋana menyi so kikɛ.

english_verse: I told Jews and Gentiles to turn to God and have faith in our Lord Jesus.
translation_verse: Juwebi nɛ nnyamase kikɛ nɛ n daŋ fiɛ so kpakpa fanɛ b lar bumo be alubi to a bɛ Ebɔrɛ so nseŋ yirda an Nyɛnpe Yesu.

english_verse: I don't know what will happen to me in Jerusalem, but I must obey God's Spirit and go there.
translation_verse: Naniere malɛ, kenu n sa Kiyoyu Cheeŋ na so nɛ mee yɔ Jerusalɛm a maŋ nyi kusɔ nɛ k beeŋ ya wora ma ndoŋ na.

english_verse: In every city I visit, I am told by the Holy Spirit that I will be put in jail and will be in trouble in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Kusɔ nɛ m baa nyi e la fanɛ Kiyoyu Cheeŋ na bee fiɛ ma so kade kama to fanɛ kabuti nɛ etɔrɔ bee jo ma saŋko. Ama amo alɛ maŋ tir ma, ŋkpal manɛ so, m maa ta ŋ gbagba be ŋkpa ere fanɛ k la kusɔ ko ma kutɔ.

english_verse: But I don't care what happens to me, as long as I finish the work the Lord Jesus gave me to do. And this work is to tell the good news about God's gift of undeserved grace.
translation_verse: Kusɔ nɛ k tir ma e la kananɛ meeŋ tiŋ n loge Enyɛnpe Yesu be kushuŋ nɛ e sa ma na. Kumo alɛ e la kebɔ Ebɔrɛ be kuwɔr be kakɛ na be baru lela na.

english_verse: I have gone from place to place, preaching to you about God's kingdom, but now I know that none of you will ever see me again.
translation_verse: N yɔ menyi be ekama ere nyam kutɔ n ya bɔ Ebɔrɛ be kuwura na to be asheŋ n sa menyi, ama naniere n nyi fanɛ menyi be ekama maaŋ naŋ wu ma kikɛ.

english_verse: I tell you today I am no longer responsible for any of you!
translation_verse: Amoso, m baa bugi asheŋ to nna a kaŋɛ menyi kabre nna fanɛ: Nɛ menyi be ekama baŋ foe ekpa, mannɛ ma e bar kumo,

english_verse: I have told you everything God wants you to know.
translation_verse: ŋkpal manɛ so, m maŋ ta kusɔ nɛ Ebɔrɛ yili fanɛ e beeŋ wora na ŋ ŋana menyi so.

english_verse: Look after yourselves and everyone the Holy Spirit has placed in your care. Be like shepherds to God's church. It is the flock he bought with the blood of his own Son.
translation_verse: Men baa de men gbagba be amuana so nsaa de basa nɛ Kiyoyu Cheeŋ na ta m bɔɔ menyi enɔ na so. Men baa keni Ebɔrɛ be asɔriebi nɛ e ta ŋ ki mo peya ashi mo gbagba Pibinyɛn be luwu na so fanɛ kananɛ asɔbɔyakpapo bee keni mbe asɔbɔya so na.

english_verse: I know that after I am gone, others will come like fierce wolves to attack you.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal manɛ so, n nyi fanɛ ŋ kaŋ yɔ, befɛpo damta beeŋ ba menyi to m ba fin kemur asɔriebi na fanɛ kananɛ kuntuŋ bee luri mbolpɔ to a mur amo na.

english_verse: Some of your own people will tell lies to win over the Lord's followers.
translation_verse: Menyi to be beko malɛ gba beeŋ koso kachako ŋ ku efɛ n shin nɛ beyirdapoana na e bɛ bumo so.

english_verse: Be on your guard! Remember how day and night for three years I kept warning you with tears in my eyes.
translation_verse: Amoso, men baa da so a nyiŋi kananɛ n daŋ shu n fiɛ menyi so kenishipereso kapa nɛ kanyɛ nfɛ asa a ŋini menyi be ekama asheŋ na.

english_verse: I now place you in God's care. Remember the message about his gift of undeserved grace! This message can help you and give you what belongs to you as God's people.
translation_verse: Naniere, Ebɔrɛ be enɔ to nɛ mbe kuwɔr be kakɛ be kubɔya na be kebaawɔtɔ to nɛ mee ta menyi a wɔtɔ to na. Kubɔya na e naaŋ tiŋ n shin nɛ menyi be kenyi e wora keshi n ti so n naŋ shin nɛ men nya nɛfa nɛ Ebɔrɛ kɔ a jo nɛ e sa mbe basa cheembi na.

english_verse: I have never wanted anyone's money or clothes.
translation_verse: M maŋ yɛlga esa kama be gbiti ŋko shuwa ŋko asɔbuuso.

english_verse: You know how I have worked with my own hands to make a living for myself and my friends.
translation_verse: Menyi gbagba nyi fanɛ ma enɔana ere nɛ n daŋ ta n shuŋ n nya asɔ nɛ a daga fanɛ ma nɛ m braana na e nya.

english_verse: By everything I did, I showed how you should work to help everyone who is weak. Remember that our Lord Jesus said, “More blessings come from giving than from receiving.”
translation_verse: M bɔla kusɔ kama to ŋ ŋini menyi fanɛ kebaashuŋ le ere nɛ anyee chɛ bepɔshipo to nsaa nyiŋi Enyɛnpe Yesu gbagba be mmalga nɛ e kaŋɛ na: ‘Kakɛ kɔ kagbenefuli a chɔ kesɔ.’ ”

english_verse: After Paul had finished speaking, he knelt down with all of them and prayed.
translation_verse: Pɔɔl ka malga n loge nɛ mo nɛ bumo kikɛ gbir ŋ kule Ebɔrɛ.

english_verse: They were especially sad because Paul had told them, “You will never see me again.” Then they went with him to the ship.
translation_verse: Kusɔ nɛ k daŋ baa jija bumo be ŋgbene ga e daa la kananɛ e kaŋɛ fanɛ b maaŋ naŋ wu mo kikɛ na. Ade be kaman nɛ b shuŋi mo n lar ekpa n yɔ ekuloŋgboŋ nɛ e beeŋ luri na akpa.

english_verse: After saying goodbye, we sailed straight to Cos. The next day we reached Rhodes and from there sailed on to Patara.
translation_verse: An ka kela bumo n loge nɛ an luri ekuloŋgboŋ na to m bɔla nchu so n ta tinini loŋ n ya fo Kɔs ŋ klade n yɔ Rodes n ya shi ndoŋ n yɔ Patara.

english_verse: We found a ship going to Phoenicia, so we got on board and sailed off.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nɛ an ya nya ekuloŋgboŋ ko nɛ k bee shin nɛ k yɔ Fenisha nɛ an luri kumo to n yɔ.

english_verse: We came within sight of Cyprus and then sailed south of it on to the port of Tyre in Syria, where the ship was going to unload its cargo.
translation_verse: An ta loŋ m ba kaa wu Saipres nseŋ yige kumo anyi be bena so n lɛ nseŋ ta n yɔ Siriya n naŋ ta n ya yili Tayɛ, kakpa nɛ ekuloŋgboŋ na daa sha keyaa lara kumo be esulɔ.

english_verse: But when the week was over, we started on our way again. All the men, together with their wives and children, walked with us from the town to the seashore. We knelt on the beach and prayed.
translation_verse: Ama anyi be keyige bumo n yɔ be saŋɛ ka ba fo nɛ an lar bumo kutɔ ndoŋ. Bumo kikɛ nɛ bumo be beche nɛ mbia e daŋ shuŋi anyi n lar kadegboŋ na to nɛ an kikɛ ya gbir shishɛr so ashi teku na ase ŋ kule Ebɔrɛ.

english_verse: Then after saying goodbye to each other, we got into the ship, and they went back home.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ an kela abar ŋkeŋ shin nɛ an luri ekuloŋgboŋ na to nɛ bumo alɛ bɛta n yɔ epe.

english_verse: We sailed from Tyre to Ptolemais, where we greeted the followers and stayed with them for a day.
translation_verse: An ka naŋ fara anyi be enite na nɛ an lar Tayɛ n yɔ Petɔlemeeyis n ya ji kachɛ koŋwule ndoŋ n chɔrɔ bekurgepoana na.

english_verse: The next day we went to Caesarea and stayed with Philip, the preacher. He was one of the seven men who helped the apostles,
translation_verse: Kumo be ŋklade nɛ an lar ndoŋ n yɔ Sizariya n ya luri baru lela malgapo Filip pe. E daa la basa ashunu nɛ bebɛsopoana na daŋ lara Jerusalɛm na be eko nna.

english_verse: We had been in Caesarea for several days, when the prophet Agabus came to us from Judea.
translation_verse: An daŋ wora nchɛnnyɔ nɛ anebi ko nɛ baa tre Agabes na ya shi Judiya m ba.

english_verse: He took Paul's belt, and with it he tied up his own hands and feet. Then he told us, “The Holy Spirit says that some of the Jewish leaders in Jerusalem will tie up the man who owns this belt. They will also hand him over to the Gentiles.”
translation_verse: E ka ba anyi kutɔ nɛ e ba ta Pɔɔl be kreso ŋ kre mo gbagba be aya nɛ enɔana nseŋ kaŋɛ: “Le nɛ Kiyoyu Cheeŋ na kaŋɛ: ‘Le nɛ Jerusalɛm to be Juwebi na beeŋ kre kreso ere wura nseŋ ta mo m bɔɔ nnyamase enɔ.’ ”

english_verse: After Agabus said this, we and the followers living there begged Paul not to go to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: An ka nu loŋ nɛ anyi nɛ basa na kule Pɔɔl fanɛ e sa maŋ naŋ yɔ Jerusalɛm.

english_verse: But Paul answered, “Why are you crying and breaking my heart? I am not only willing to be put in jail for the Lord Jesus, but I am even willing to die for him in Jerusalem!”
translation_verse: Nɛ e bishi bumo: “Manɛ so nɛ menyee wora le ere nsaa shu le a jija ma kagbene? Ŋkpal Enyɛnpe Yesu so meeŋ shuli fanɛ b mɔ ma ashi Jerusalɛm to gba, a bishi kekre ma ndoŋ.”

english_verse: Since we could not get Paul to change his mind, we gave up and prayed, “Lord, please make us willing to do what you want.”
translation_verse: An daa maŋ tiŋ n shin nɛ e chɛrga mbe nfɛra, amoso, an daŋ yige mo nna nseŋ kaŋɛ: “Kusɔ kama nɛ Enyɛnpe yili e wora loŋ.”

english_verse: Then we got ready to go to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: An ka wora nchɛnnyɔ ndoŋ nɛ an bela ase n yɔ Jerusalɛm.

english_verse: Some of the followers from Caesarea went with us and took us to stay in the home of Mnason. He was from Cyprus and had been a follower from the beginning. Paul Visits James
translation_verse: Anyi nɛ Sizariya be bebɛsopo na be beko e daŋ yɔ nɛ b keta anyi n yɔ anyi be kowurnyɛn Meneesɔn pe. E daŋ shi Saipres nna a la ebɛsopo ashi mbe kebiato kikɛ. Pɔɔl ka ya chɔrɔ Jeems be asheŋ

english_verse: When we arrived in Jerusalem, the Lord's followers gladly welcomed us.
translation_verse: An ka ba Jerusalɛm nɛ bekurgepoana na bugi kagbene n sɔ anyi kagbenefuliso

english_verse: Paul went with us to see James the next day, and all the church leaders were present.
translation_verse: Kumo be ŋklade nɛ anyi nɛ Pɔɔl yɔ nɛ an ya chɔrɔ Jeems. Saŋɛ na so nɛ asɔriebi be benimuana na kikɛ wɔ ndoŋ.

english_verse: Paul greeted them and told how God had used him to help the Gentiles.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Pɔɔl chɔrɔ bumo nseŋ kaŋɛ bumo asɔ nɛ Ebɔrɛ bɔla mo so n wora nnyamase to kikɛ nyam.

english_verse: Everyone who heard this praised God and said to Paul: My friend, you can see how many tens of thousands of our people have become followers! And all of them are eager to obey the Law of Moses.
translation_verse: B ka nu mbe kamalga na nɛ bumo kikɛ di Ebɔrɛ epaŋ nseŋ kaŋɛ Pɔɔl: “Fo wu ai, ekurgepo, Jerusalɛm ere to be Juwebi damta gba ki beyirdapo naniere, ama bumo alɛ kraa mɔ bumo be amu nna a bɛ Mosis be mbra na so.

english_verse: But they have been told that you are teaching those who live among the Gentiles to disobey this Law. They claim that you are telling them not to circumcise their sons or to follow our customs.
translation_verse: Basa kaŋɛ bumo fanɛ fo wɔtɔ nna a ŋini Juwebi nɛ b wɔ nnyamase be efuliana so nna fanɛ b yige kebaabɛ Mosis be mbra na so. B yɛ fo yɛ, b sa maa ku bumo be mbia atutu, bumo alɛ e sa maa bɛ Juwebi be edaŋkare na so.

english_verse: What should we do now that our people have heard you are here?
translation_verse: Bumo be kenu fanɛ fo ba malɛ baŋ fuli nna, amoso, nuso nɛ anyeeŋ wora?

english_verse: Please do what we ask, because four of our men have made special promises to God.
translation_verse: Wora kusɔ nɛ anyeeŋ kaŋɛ fo ere. Benyɛn ana ko nase kɔnɔ n sa Ebɔrɛ a wɔ nfe.

english_verse: Join with them and prepare yourself for the ceremony that goes with the promises. Pay the cost for their heads to be shaved. Then everyone will learn that the reports about you are not true. They will know you do obey the Law of Moses.
translation_verse: Ya ti bumo so nɛ b fɔr fo nɛ bumo be eyurpi n lɛ nseŋ shin nɛ fo ka bumo be eyurpi be kefɔr n lɛ be kukɔ n sa bumo nɛ b tiŋ n shin nɛ b she bumo be amu. Loŋ nɛ ekama beeŋ pin fanɛ asɔ nɛ b nu na kikɛ la efɛ nna, ŋkpal fo gbagba ka bee bɛ Mosis be mbra na so so.

english_verse: Some while ago we told the Gentile followers what we think they should do. We instructed them not to eat anything offered to idols. They were told not to eat any meat with blood still in it or the meat of an animal that has been strangled. They were also told not to commit any terrible sexual sins.
translation_verse: To, nnyamase nɛ b ki bebɛsopo na malɛ, an sibɛ kawɔl n shuŋi bumo fanɛ b sa maŋ naa ji nlɔŋɛjibi ŋko ŋklaŋ ŋko a we kusɔbɔya kama nɛ b maŋ teŋ, nseŋ naŋ kaŋɛ bumo fanɛ b baa gelge kubojuaji gba.”

english_verse: The next day Paul took the four men with him and got himself ready at the same time they did. Then he went into the temple and told when the final ceremony would take place and when an offering would be made for each of them. Paul Is Arrested
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Pɔɔl shin nɛ mo nɛ basa na yɔ ŋ klade n ya wora bumo be kefɔr n lɛ be daŋkaresheŋ na nseŋ shin nɛ e yɔ bɔrɛlambu na to n ya kaŋɛ kachɛ nɛ baa loge eyurpi be kefɔr n lɛ be daŋkare na nseŋ lara basa na be ekama be sarga. B ka pɛ Pɔɔl ashi bɔrɛlambu na to be asheŋ

english_verse: When the period of seven days for the ceremony was almost over, some of the Jewish people from Asia saw Paul in the temple. They got a large crowd together and started attacking him.
translation_verse: Nchɛnshunu na ka taga to nɛ Eeshia be kasawule so be Juwebi ko wu Pɔɔl bɔrɛlambu na to nseŋ we n wɔtɔ jimaŋ na kikɛ nseŋ nyaŋ Pɔɔl

english_verse: They were shouting, “Friends, help us! This man goes around everywhere, saying bad things about our nation and about the Law of Moses and about this temple. He has even brought shame to this holy temple by bringing in Gentiles.”
translation_verse: m ponte ŋ kaŋɛ: “Israɛlebi, men ba chɛ to. Kanyɛn nɛ e na kaplɛkama a ŋini basa kikɛ asheŋ nɛ a bee da Israɛlebi nɛ Mosis be mbra na nɛ bɔrɛlambu na so e ba nfe hale m bar nnyamase bɔrɛlambu na to nɛ b ba jija kumo kananɛ k du cheembi na.”

english_verse: Some of them thought that Paul had brought Trophimus from Ephesus into the temple, because they had seen them together in the city.
translation_verse: B ka daŋ wu Trɔfimes nɛ e shi Ɛfeses nɛ Pɔɔl kade na to so nɛ b daŋ tama fanɛ Pɔɔl daŋ keta mo nna n luri bɔrɛlambu na to.

english_verse: The whole city was in an uproar, and the people turned into a mob. They grabbed Paul and dragged him out of the temple. Then suddenly the doors were shut.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ kadegboŋ na to ebi kikɛ luri kebagato to nɛ basa na kikɛ shile m ba abar so m ba nyaŋ Pɔɔl ŋ gberge mo n lar bɔrɛlambu na to nseŋ ti bɔrɛlambu na be mbuna epul na to.

english_verse: The people were about to kill Paul when the Roman army commander heard that all Jerusalem was starting to riot.
translation_verse: Jimaŋ yenso na daa sha kemɔ Pɔɔl nna nɛ esa ko ya kaŋɛ Romebi be benapo be enimu na fanɛ Jerusalɛmebi nyaŋɛ to.

english_verse: So he quickly took some soldiers and officers and ran to where the crowd had gathered. As soon as the mob saw the commander and soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.
translation_verse: Epul na to nɛ enimu na lara ekrachi ko nɛ benapo ko nɛ b bɛ mo so n nya manaŋ n yɔ jimaŋ na to. B ka baŋ wu mo nɛ benapo na nɛ b yige Pɔɔl be kebri.

english_verse: The army commander went over and arrested him and had him bound with two chains. Then he tried to find out who Paul was and what he had done.
translation_verse: Nɛ enimu na yɔ Pɔɔl kutɔ n ya shin nɛ b pɛ mo nseŋ shin nɛ b ta ŋgbɛlɛbi anyɔ ŋ kre mo. Kumo be kaman nɛ e bishi: “Nuso be esa e la kanyɛn ere, nɛ manɛ nɛ e wora?”

english_verse: Part of the crowd shouted one thing, and part of them shouted something else. But they were making so much noise that the commander could not find out a thing. Then he ordered Paul to be taken into the fortress.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ jimaŋ na gbar n juge to. Kebagato na be keshi na so benapo be enimu na daa maŋ tiŋ m pin kusɔ nɛ k baŋ wora, amoso, e daŋ shin nɛ mbe benapo keta Pɔɔl nna n yɔ kesɔnyige be ebu lempo na to.

english_verse: As they reached the steps, the crowd became so wild that the soldiers had to lift Paul up and carry him.
translation_verse: Ebu na be kabondiikpa nawule nɛ b daŋ fo nɛ benapo na maŋ mo so ŋkpal kananɛ jimaŋ yenso na nyaŋɛ to na so.

english_verse: The crowd followed and kept shouting, “Kill him! Kill him!” Paul Speaks to the Crowd
translation_verse: Bumo kikɛ daa shil nna a buu mo a ponte a kaŋɛ: “Men mɔ mo.” Kananɛ Pɔɔl malga ŋ kuŋ mbe kumu be asheŋ

english_verse: When Paul was about to be taken into the fortress, he asked the commander, “Can I say something to you?” “How do you know Greek?” the commander asked.
translation_verse: B ka daa shin nɛ b ta Pɔɔl n luri kesɔnyige be ebu lempo na to nɛ e malga benapo be enimu na kutɔ ŋ kaŋɛ: “Jande, shin nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ fo kusɔ ko.” Nɛ benapo be enimu na bishi mo: “Fee nu Griik to a?

english_verse: “No!” Paul replied. “I am a Jew from Tarsus, an important city in Cilicia. Please let me speak to the crowd.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Pɔɔl kaŋɛ: “N la Juw nna ashi Silisia be Taases nɛ k maŋ la kade fɔmbi na. Jande shin nɛ m malga n sa basa ere.”

english_verse: The commander told him he could speak, so Paul stood on the steps and motioned to the people. When they were quiet, he spoke to them in Aramaic:
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ benapo be enimu na sa Pɔɔl ekpa nɛ e yili ebu na be kabondiikpa nseŋ wora basa na enɔ nɛ b la to nɛ e malga Hibruw to ŋ kaŋɛ:

english_verse: “My friends and leaders of our nation, listen as I explain what happened!”
translation_verse: “M braana nɛ n tutoana, men lo to n nu ma kamalga nɛ mee sha kemalga ŋ kuŋ ma kumu ashi menyi kutɔ ere.”

english_verse: When the crowd heard Paul speak to them in Aramaic, they became even quieter. Then Paul said:
translation_verse: B ka nu e ka bee malga Hibruw to nɛ bumo kikɛ wora shruum a chɔ sososo b ka fara n lo to na nɛ Pɔɔl kaŋɛ:

english_verse: I am a Jew, born in the city of Tarsus in Cilicia. But I grew up here in Jerusalem where I was a student of Gamaliel and was taught to follow every single law of our ancestors. In fact, I was just as eager to obey God as any of you are today.
translation_verse: “N la Juw nna ashi Silisia be Taases, ama Jerusalɛm to nfe nɛ b bela ma nɛ Gameelial daa la ma eŋinipo. Kananɛ k daga fanɛ esa e bɛ an nanaana be mbra na so na nɛ b daŋ ŋini ma nɛ n ta ma kumu m bɔɔ Ebɔrɛ enɔ nɛ n shuŋ mbe kushuŋ fanɛ kananɛ menyi kikɛ nfe ere bee wora na.

english_verse: I made trouble for everyone who followed the Lord's Way, and I even had some of them killed. I had others arrested and put in jail. I didn't care if they were men or women.
translation_verse: N daŋ tɔrɔ basa nɛ b bɛ le be ekpa ere na so hale a sha kemɔ bumo kikɛ. Beche nɛ benyɛn kikɛ nɛ n daŋ pɛ n shin nɛ b ti ebu.

english_verse: The high priest and all the council members can tell you this is true. They even gave me letters to the Jewish leaders in Damascus, so that I could arrest people there and bring them to Jerusalem to be punished.
translation_verse: Bɔrɛmatapo nimuso nɛ nshɛrwuraana na kikɛ e la ma shɛdajipoana. Bumo kutɔ nɛ n daa sɔ nwɔl a yɔ bekurgepo Juwebi nɛ b wɔ Damaskɔs na kutɔ nɛ b sa ma ekpa nɛ m pɛ loŋ be basa na ŋ kre bumo ŋgbɛlɛbi m ba Jerusalɛm to nfe m ba kaa shin nɛ baa gberge bumo kusoe. Pɔɔl ka malga kananɛ e ba ki ebɛsopo be asheŋ

english_verse: One day about noon I was getting close to Damascus, when a bright light from heaven suddenly flashed around me.
translation_verse: Kachako ŋ ka wɔ loŋ be enite na to m ba kaa taga to Damaskɔs kapaso ko nɛ kefultogboŋ ko nyaŋɛ n shi ebɔrɛso m ba yuu ma so.

english_verse: I fell to the ground and heard a voice asking, “Saul, Saul, why are you so cruel to me?”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ n tɔr kasawule nseŋ nu ebɔl ka bee bishi ma: ‘Sɔɔl, Sɔɔl, manɛ e ba nɛ fee tɔrɔ ma?’

english_verse: “Who are you?” I answered. The Lord replied, “I am Jesus from Nazareth! I am the one you are so cruel to.”
translation_verse: Nɛ m bishi: ‘Fo wanɛ, Enyɛnpe?’ Nɛ e kaŋɛ: ‘Ma Nazarɛt be Yesu nɛ fee tɔrɔ na.’

english_verse: Those who were traveling with me saw the light, but did not hear the voice.
translation_verse: Ma nɛ basa nɛ b daa la na daŋ wu kefulto na, ama b daa maŋ nu esa nɛ e daŋ malga n sa ma na be ebɔl na.

english_verse: I asked, “Lord, what do you want me to do?” Then he told me, “Get up and go to Damascus. When you get there, you will be told what to do.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ m bishi: ‘Nɛ nuso nɛ meeŋ wora Enyɛnpe?’ Nɛ Enyɛnpe na kaŋɛ ma: ‘Niŋi to ŋ koso n luri Damaskɔs nɛ b kaŋɛ fo kusɔ kama nɛ Ebɔrɛ bee sha fanɛ fo wora.’

english_verse: The light had been so bright that I couldn't see. And the others had to lead me by the hand to Damascus.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal kefultogboŋ na so n daŋ tan nna, amoso, m braana na e daŋ pɛ ma enɔ to n luri Damaskɔs to.

english_verse: In that city there was a man named Ananias, who faithfully obeyed the Law of Moses and was well liked by all the Jewish people living there.
translation_verse: Kanyɛn ko daa wɔtɔ a la abɔrɛshenshapo a bɛ anyi be mbra na so nɛ baa tre mo Ananiyas. Damaskɔs to be Juwebi na kikɛ daa sa mo bunyaŋ nna.

english_verse: He came to me and said, “Saul, my friend, you can now see again!” At once I could see.
translation_verse: Mo e daŋ ba yili ma kutɔ ŋ kaŋɛ ma: ‘Ekurgepo Sɔɔl, naŋ bɛta a wu.’ Epul na malɛ to nɛ n naŋ nya ma anishi n wu mo.

english_verse: Then Ananias told me, “The God that our ancestors worshiped has chosen you to know what he wants done. He has chosen you to see the One Who Obeys God and to hear his voice.
translation_verse: Nɛ e kaŋɛ: ‘An nanaana be Ebɔrɛ na e lara fo fanɛ fo pin kusɔ nɛ e bee sha kewora nseŋ shin nɛ fo wu mbe Kenya cheembi na n naŋ shin nɛ fo nu mbe ebɔl na.

english_verse: What are you waiting for? Get up! Be baptized, and wash away your sins by praying to the Lord.”
translation_verse: Amoso, sa maŋ naŋ jo, koso n shin nɛ b bɛr fo kabɔrɛbɛr a ti Yesu be ketre na nɛ Ebɔrɛ e fɔr fo alubi n lɛ.’ B ka tre Pɔɔl nnyamase to be asheŋ

english_verse: After this I returned to Jerusalem and went to the temple to pray. There I had a vision
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ m bɛta m ba Jerusalɛm m ba kaa kule Ebɔrɛ bɔrɛlambu na to nseŋ ku bɔrɛdare n wu Enyɛnpe Yesu nɛ e kaŋɛ ma:

english_verse: of the Lord who said to me, “Hurry and leave Jerusalem! The people won't listen to what you say about me.”
translation_verse: ‘Nya manaŋ n lar Jerusalɛm, ŋkpal manɛ so, nfe be basa ere maaŋ yirda ma shɛda nɛ fee sha keji n sa bumo ere.’

english_verse: I replied, “Lord, they know that in many of our synagogues I arrested and beat people who had faith in you.
translation_verse: Nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ: ‘Enyɛnpe, b baa nyi geeŋ ŋ ka daŋ yɔ nshɛrbuana to n ya pɛ basa nɛ b yirda fo na nseŋ bri bumo.

english_verse: Stephen was killed because he spoke for you, and I stood there and cheered them on. I even guarded the clothes of the men who murdered him.”
translation_verse: Saŋɛ nɛ baa mɔ fo shɛdajipo Stiven na nɛ ma alɛ gba yil a keni mbe bemɔpo na be asɔbuuso so nsaa kaŋɛ fanɛ kashenteŋto e daga luwu.’

english_verse: But the Lord told me to go, and he promised to send me far away to the Gentiles.
translation_verse: Nɛ Enyɛnpe kaŋɛ ma: ‘Lar nɛ n shuŋi fo kufɔ kufɔ nnyamase kutɔ.’ ”

english_verse: The crowd listened until Paul said this. Then they started shouting, “Get rid of this man! He doesn't deserve to live.”
translation_verse: Pɔɔl ka bee malga asheŋ na kikɛ nɛ basa na bee nu. Ama e ka ba malga keyɔ nnyamase na kutɔ be asheŋ nɛ b fara a ponte ga a kaŋɛ: “Men lara mo durnya ere to. Men mɔ mo!”

english_verse: They kept shouting. They waved their clothes around and threw dust into the air. Paul and the Roman Army Commander
translation_verse: B daŋ baa ponte to nna a kpa bumo be nle a lɛ nsaa jɔ shishɛr a lɛ esoso.

english_verse: The Roman commander ordered Paul to be taken into the fortress and beaten with a whip. He did this to find out why the people were screaming at Paul.
translation_verse: Nɛ Romebi be benapo be enimu na shin nɛ mbe benapo ba keta Pɔɔl n yɔ kesɔnyige be ebu lempo na to nseŋ shin nɛ e kaŋɛ bumo fanɛ b kuya Pɔɔl so nɛ e kaŋɛ bumo kusɔ nɛ k ba nɛ Juwebi na bee boŋ to a malga a gbiti mo loŋ na.

english_verse: While the soldiers were tying Paul up to be beaten, he asked the officer standing there, “Is it legal to beat a Roman citizen before he has been tried in court?”
translation_verse: B ka kre mo nɛ b kuya mo so nɛ Pɔɔl bishi enapo nimusobi ko nɛ e daa yil ndoŋ na le: “Ekpa wɔtɔ fanɛ b kuya Rom be efuli so be esa so nɛ b maŋ ji mo demu ŋ keni a?”

english_verse: When the officer heard this, he went to the commander and said, “What are you doing? This man is a Roman citizen!”
translation_verse: Enapo nimusobi na ka nu loŋ na nɛ e yɔ benapo be enimu na kutɔ n ya bishi mo: “Manɛ nɛ fo yɛ fo wora ere? Kanyɛn na la Rom be esa nna.”

english_verse: The commander went to Paul and asked, “Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?” “Yes,” Paul answered.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ benapo be enimu na yɔ Pɔɔl kutɔ n ya bishi mo: “Kaŋɛ ma, Rom be esa e la fo a?” Nɛ Pɔɔl shuli so ŋ kaŋɛ: “Mm.”

english_verse: The commander then said, “I paid a lot of money to become a Roman citizen.” But Paul replied, “I was born a Roman citizen.”
translation_verse: Nɛ benapo be enimu na kaŋɛ: “Amansherbi damta nɛ ŋ ka n sa abane pɔɛŋ nseŋ ki Rom be esa.” Nɛ Pɔɔl kaŋɛ: “Ma ere, b kurge ma Rom be esa nna.”

english_verse: The men who were about to beat and question Paul quickly backed off. And the commander himself was frightened when he realized that he had put a Roman citizen in chains. Paul Is Tried by the Council
translation_verse: Epul na to nɛ basa nɛ b daa sha nɛ b bishi Pɔɔl asheŋ na bɛta kaman nɛ kufu pɛ benapo be enimu na gba ŋkpal e ka pin Pɔɔl ka la Rom be esa nɛ ŋkpal e ka shin nɛ b ta ŋgbɛlɛbi ŋ kre mo so so.

english_verse: The next day the commander wanted to know the real reason why the Jewish leaders had brought charges against Paul. So he had Paul's chains removed, and he ordered the chief priests and the whole council to meet. Then he had Paul led in and made him stand in front of them.
translation_verse: Benapo be enimu na daa sha kepin kusɔ nɛ k baŋ ba nɛ Juwebi na nɛ Pɔɔl daŋ baa kɔ abar loŋ nna. Amoso, kare ka chɛ nɛ e shin nɛ b saŋɛ Pɔɔl be ŋgbɛlɛbi na nseŋ shin nɛ bɔrɛmatapowuraana na nɛ nshɛrwuraana na kikɛ shɛr nɛ e shin nɛ Pɔɔl ba yili bumo be anishito.

english_verse: Paul looked straight at the council members and said, “My friends, to this day I have served God with a clear conscience!”
translation_verse: Nɛ Pɔɔl keni nshɛrwuraana na diimbi nseŋ kaŋɛ: “Ŋ kurgepoana, hale kabre ma kagbene to maa wora ma shikashika Ebɔrɛ be anishito fanɛ m maŋ kɔ kebaawɔtɔ cheembi.”

english_verse: Then Ananias the high priest ordered the men standing beside Paul to hit him on the mouth.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ bɔrɛmatapo nimuso Ananiyas shin nɛ basa nɛ b daŋ yili n taga to Pɔɔl na ŋmɛa Pɔɔl be kɔnɔ.

english_verse: Paul turned to the high priest and said, “You whitewashed wall! God will hit you. You sit there to judge me by the Law of Moses. But at the same time you order men to break the Law by hitting me.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Pɔɔl kaŋɛ mo: “Kebirkɔnshiwura ere! Ebɔrɛ beeŋ ŋmɛa fo kɔnɔ loŋ. Fo yɛ fo chena nfe nna nɛ fo bɔla ekpa nɛ mbra na bee ŋini na so n ji demu, ama ma nɛ fee shin nɛ baa ŋmɛa n naa wora a da mbra na so na.”

english_verse: The men standing beside Paul asked, “Don't you know you are insulting God's high priest?”
translation_verse: Nɛ basa nɛ b yili n taga to Pɔɔl na kaŋɛ mo: “Ebɔrɛ be bɔrɛmatapo nimuso nɛ fee tege ere a?”

english_verse: Paul replied, “Oh! I didn't know he was the high priest. The Scriptures do tell us not to speak evil about a leader of our people.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Pɔɔl kaŋɛ: “Ŋ kurgepoana, n daa maŋ nyi fanɛ e la bɔrɛmatapo nimuso nna, ŋkpal manɛ so, abɔrɛsibɛ na bee kaŋɛ fanɛ: ‘Sa maŋ kaŋ malga kamalga lubi ŋ gbiti fo basa be enimu.’ ”

english_verse: When Paul saw that some of the council members were Sadducees and others were Pharisees, he shouted, “My friends, I am a Pharisee and the son of a Pharisee. I am on trial simply because I believe that the dead will be raised to life.”
translation_verse: Pɔɔl ka wu fanɛ basa na be beko la Esadusiana nna nɛ beko malɛ la Efarisiana nɛ e malga awɔrso n sa nshɛrwuraana na ŋ kaŋɛ: “Ŋ kurgepoana, Farisinyɛn e kurge ma nɛ ma alɛ naa la Farisi. Baa ji ma demu nfe ere nna, ŋkpal ŋ ka kɔ tama kpakpaso fanɛ bumo nɛ b wu na ka beeŋ tiŋi luwu to so.”

english_verse: As soon as Paul said this, the Pharisees and the Sadducees got into a big argument, and the council members started taking sides.
translation_verse: E ka malga loŋ epul na to nɛ Efarisiana na nɛ Esadusiana na fara a bile nɛ basa na kikɛ barga to ntuŋ anyɔ so.

english_verse: The Sadducees do not believe in angels or spirits or that the dead will rise to life. But the Pharisees believe in all of these,
translation_verse: Ŋkpal manɛ so, Esadusiana bee kaŋɛ fanɛ basa maaŋ tiŋi luwu to nseŋ naa kaŋɛ fanɛ emalaika ŋko ayoyu maŋ wɔtɔ, ama Efarisiana daŋ yirda amo asa na kikɛ.

english_verse: and so there was a lot of shouting. Some of the teachers of the Law of Moses were Pharisees. Finally, they became angry and said, “We don't find anything wrong with this man. Maybe a spirit or an angel really did speak to him.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ bumo be kaponte na naŋ dii ga nɛ mbraŋinipoana nɛ b la Efarisiana na be beko niŋi to n yili m ponte eleŋso ŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ b maŋ shuli ŋ kaŋɛ: “Anyi ere maŋ wu kulubi kikɛ kanyɛn ere so. Ashere kiyoyu ko ŋko malaika e malga mo kutɔ kashenteŋto na.”

english_verse: The argument became fierce, and the commander was afraid that Paul would be pulled apart. So he ordered the soldiers to go in and rescue Paul. Then they took him back into the fortress.
translation_verse: Bumo be kolu na daŋ nyaŋɛ to ga hale basa na be kegberge Pɔɔl n tuge to be asheŋ pɛ benapo be enimu na kufu ga. Nɛ e shin nɛ mbe benapo luri basa na to ŋ keta Pɔɔl n lar bumo to n yɔ kesɔnyige be ebu lempo na to.

english_verse: That night the Lord stood beside Paul and said, “Don't worry! Just as you have told others about me in Jerusalem, you must also tell about me in Rome.” A Plot To Kill Paul
translation_verse: Kumo be kamɔnchɛ be kanyɛso nɛ Enyɛnpe ba yili Pɔɔl kutɔ nseŋ kaŋɛ mo: “Baa kɔ kenyɛn. Kananɛ fo ji ma shɛda ashi Jerusalɛm to ere nɛ fee naŋ yɔ Rom malɛ n ya wora.” Juwebi ka kre Pɔɔl be kemɔ be nia be asheŋ

english_verse: Then some of them went to the chief priests and the nation's leaders and said, “We have promised God that we would not eat a thing until we have killed Paul.
translation_verse: B ka sa kɔnɔ na n loge nɛ b yɔ bɔrɛmatapowuraana na nɛ benimuana na kutɔ n ya kaŋɛ bumo: “An ba abar so nna m ba sa kɔnɔ kpakpaso fanɛ an baa maŋ mɔ Pɔɔl, an maaŋ ji shɛŋ.

english_verse: You and everyone in the council must go to the commander and pretend that you want to find out more about the charges against Paul. Ask for him to be brought before your court. Meanwhile, we will be waiting to kill him before he gets there.”
translation_verse: Amoso, menyi nɛ nshɛrwuraana na e kute n shuŋi kabɔ nɛ e ya kaŋɛ Romebi be benapo be enimu na fanɛ e shin nɛ b bar Pɔɔl menyi kutɔ nɛ e ba malga nɛ men pin mbe demu na to nɛnɛ. Saŋɛ na so nɛ anyee jo mo ekpa to n nya mo m mɔ nɛ e maŋ fo nfe.”

english_verse: When Paul's nephew heard about the plot, he went to the fortress and told Paul about it.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Pɔɔl mo sipoche pibi nu bumo be nia na nseŋ ya luri kesɔnyige be ebu lempo na to n ya kaŋɛ Pɔɔl kesheŋ na.

english_verse: So Paul said to one of the army officers, “Take this young man to the commander. He has something to tell him.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Pɔɔl tre benapo be benimuwurbiana na be eko ŋ kaŋɛ mo: “Keta kabrantiɛbia ere n yɔ benapo be enimu na kutɔ. E bee sha kekaŋɛ mo kusɔ ko nna.”

english_verse: The officer took him to the commander and said, “The prisoner named Paul asked me to bring this young man to you, because he has something to tell you.”
translation_verse: Nɛ benapo be enimubi na juŋkpar ŋ keta mo n yɔ benapo be enimu na kutɔ n ya kaŋɛ mo: “Pɔɔl kabutipo na e tre ma ŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ ŋ keta kabrantiɛbia ere m ba fo kutɔ, ŋkpal manɛ so, e kɔ kusɔ ko nna nɛ e kaŋɛ fo.”

english_verse: The commander took the young man aside and asked him in private, “What do you want to tell me?”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ benapo be enimu na gbagba pɛ kabrantiɛbia na be enɔ to nseŋ keta mo n lar ekarso m bishi mo: “Manɛ nɛ fee sha kekaŋɛ ma?”

english_verse: He answered, “Some men are planning to ask you to bring Paul down to the Jewish council tomorrow. They will claim they want to find out more about him.
translation_verse: Nɛ e yɛ: “Juwebi na yili kumo fanɛ baaŋ kute ŋ kule fo echefo fanɛ fo keta Pɔɔl m ba nshɛrwuraana na kutɔ nɛ e malga nɛ b pin mbe demu na to nɛnɛ.

english_verse: The commander sent the young man away after saying to him, “Don't let anyone know you told me this.” Paul Is Sent to Felix the Governor
translation_verse: Nɛ benapo be enimu na kaŋɛ mo: “Sa maŋ kaŋɛ esa kikɛ fanɛ fo e kute le be kesheŋ ere n sa ma kikɛ.” Kumo be kaman nɛ e shin nɛ kabrantiɛbia na yɔ. B ka keta Pɔɔl n yɔ Gomena Filiks kutɔ be asheŋ

english_verse: Get a horse ready for Paul and make sure he gets safely through to Felix the governor.”
translation_verse: Men fin egbaŋɛ n sa Pɔɔl nɛ e dii nɛ men keni mo so nɛnɛ n yɛr mo nɛ alenfia n ya sa Gomena Filiks.”

english_verse: The commander wrote a letter that said:
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ benapo be enimu na sibɛ kawɔl ŋ kaŋɛ:

english_verse: Greetings from Claudius Lysias to the Honorable Governor Felix:
translation_verse: “Ma, Klawdias Lisias e naa sibɛ kawɔl ere a sa fo, ebunyampogboŋ Gomena Filiks na. Mee chɔrɔ fo.

english_verse: Some Jews grabbed this man and were about to kill him. But when I found out that he was a Roman citizen, I took some soldiers and rescued him.
translation_verse: Juwebi e daŋ nyaŋ kanyɛn ere a sha kemɔ mo nɛ n nu fanɛ e la Rom be esa nna nseŋ keta ma benapo n ya mɔlga mo bumo kutɔ.

english_verse: I wanted to find out what they had against him. So I brought him before their council
translation_verse: N daa sha kenu kusɔ nɛ e wora bumo nna,

english_verse: and learned that the charges concern only their religious laws. This man isn't guilty of anything for which he should die or even be put in jail.
translation_verse: ŋkpal loŋ so ŋ keta mo n yɔ nshɛrwuraana na kutɔ n ya wu fanɛ e maŋ wora kulubi kikɛ nɛ k daga mbe luwu ŋko kabuti. Bumo gbagba be mbraana be emɔrɔsheŋ nɛ b kɔ a wu mo kulubi.

english_verse: As soon as I learned that there was a plot against him, I sent him to you and told their leaders to bring charges against him in your court.
translation_verse: Ma alɛ nu fanɛ Juwebi na bee kre mbe kemɔ be nia nna, amoso nɛ n shin nɛ b kɔ mo a ba fo kutɔ na. Ŋ kaŋɛ basa nɛ bumo nɛ mo kɔ abar na fanɛ b ba kaŋɛ fo alubi nɛ e wora.”

english_verse: The soldiers obeyed the commander's orders, and that same night they took Paul to the city of Antipatris.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ benapo na wora asɔ nɛ benapo be enimu na kaŋɛ bumo na kikɛ ŋ keta Pɔɔl kanyɛso na kikɛ hale n ya fo Antipatris.

english_verse: The next day the foot soldiers returned to the fortress and let the soldiers on horseback take him the rest of the way.
translation_verse: Kumo be ŋklade nɛ aya so be benapo na yili Antipatris m bɛta n yɔ kesɔnyige be ebu lempo na to ŋ ka egbaŋɛdiipoana nɛ bumo nɛ Pɔɔl e baa yɔ.

english_verse: When they came to Caesarea, they gave the letter to the governor and handed Paul over to him.
translation_verse: B ka fo Sizariya nɛ b ta kawɔl na n sa gomena na nseŋ ta Pɔɔl m bɔɔ mo enɔ.

english_verse: The governor read the letter. Then he asked Paul and found out that he was from Cilicia.
translation_verse: Gomena na ka kraŋ kawɔl na nɛ e bishi Pɔɔl efuli na so be kaba mo nɛ e shi. E ka pin fanɛ Silisia nɛ e shi

english_verse: The governor said, “I will listen to your case as soon as the people come to bring their charges against you.” After saying this, he gave orders for Paul to be kept as a prisoner in Herod's palace.
translation_verse: nɛ e kaŋɛ: “Basa nɛ baa wu fo kulubi na kaŋ ba, meeŋ keni fo demu na to.” Kumo be kaman nɛ e shin nɛ benapo na ta Pɔɔl n yɔ kowu nɛ Hɛrɔd daŋ pɔr na to n ya kaa keni mo so.

english_verse: Five days later Ananias the high priest, together with some of their leaders and a lawyer named Tertullus, went to the governor to present their case against Paul.
