translation_verse: Kumo be nchɛ anu be kefɛato nɛ bɔrɛmatapo nimuso Ananiyas nɛ benimu ko nɛ mbraŋinipo nɛ baa tre Tetales yɔ Sizariya n ya kaŋɛ Gomena Filiks ashi demujikpa na kulubi nɛ Pɔɔl wora.

english_verse: So Paul was called in, and Tertullus stated the case against him: Honorable Felix, you have brought our people a long period of peace, and because of your concern our nation is much better off.
translation_verse: B ka tre Tetales, nɛ e ba fara le a kaŋɛ alubi nɛ Pɔɔl wora: “Ebunyampogboŋ, ŋkpal fo kanyiasheŋ so nɛ fo tiŋ n juŋkpar anyi n shin nɛ an nya kagbenewushi saŋɛ kikɛ m ba fo mbre nɛ asheŋ lela damta tiŋ n wora anyi be efuli ere so nɛ kumo be ketre dii na.

english_verse: All of us are always grateful for what you have done.
translation_verse: Saŋkama kumo be loŋ bee par anyi ga kaplɛkama. Anyee chɔrɔ fo ga ŋkpal loŋ so.

english_verse: I don't want to bother you, but please be patient with us and listen to me for just a few minutes.
translation_verse: M maa sha fanɛ m baa kɔ kechɛchɛrase nfe a wora fo, amoso, mee kule fo nna fanɛ fo wora ania n nu anyi be kamalga shiimbi ere.

english_verse: This man has been found to be a real pest and troublemaker for our people all over the world. He is also a leader of a group called Nazarenes.
translation_verse: An wu fanɛ kanyɛn ere la esa lubi nɛ kabɔlarwura nna. E wɔtɔ nna a yɔ kaplɛkama n ya kaa ta Juwebi a wɔtɔ kebagato to nseŋ naa la basa nɛ baa tre bumo be amu Nazarinebi be katuŋ na to be enimu.

english_verse: When he tried to disgrace the temple, we arrested him. If you question him, you will find out for yourself that our charges are true.
translation_verse: nseŋ yili demu na fanɛ basa nɛ bumo nɛ kanyɛn na kɔ abar e ba fo kutɔ.] Fo gbagba baŋ bishi kanyɛn na, feeŋ pin alubi nɛ e wora na kikɛ nyam.”

english_verse: The governor motioned for Paul to speak, and he began: I know that you have judged the people of our nation for many years, and I am glad to defend myself in your court.
translation_verse: Ade be kaman nɛ gomena na wora Pɔɔl enɔ fanɛ e malga nɛ Pɔɔl kaŋɛ: “Fo ka fara a ji efuli ere so ebi demu k chɛr ga kabre. Amoso, k par ma ga ŋ ka bee sha kemalga ŋ kuŋ ma kumu fo anishito ere.

english_verse: It was no more than twelve days ago that I went to worship in Jerusalem. You can find this out easily enough.
translation_verse: Yili kachɛ nɛ n yɔ Jerusalɛm nɛ n ya bunyaŋ Ebɔrɛ na m ba fo kabre maŋ naŋ fo nchɛ kuduanyɔ. Nɛ fee sha, fo bishi n nu.

english_verse: Never once did the Jews find me arguing with anyone in the temple. I didn't cause trouble in the synagogues or in the city itself.
translation_verse: Juwebi na maŋ wu ŋ ka bee ji esa kikɛ emɔrɔ ashi bɔrɛlambu na to, bumo alɛ maŋ wu ŋ ka bee we a wɔtɔ basa ashi bumo be nshɛrbuana to ŋko kadegboŋ na to be kaplɛkama.

english_verse: There is no way that they can prove these charges they are now bringing against me.
translation_verse: Bumo alɛ maŋ kɔ shɛŋ nɛ b ta ŋ ŋini fo fanɛ asheŋ nɛ baa malga ere la kashenteŋ nna.

english_verse: I admit that their leaders think the Lord's Way which I follow is based on wrong beliefs. But I still worship the same God that my ancestors worshiped. And I believe everything written in the Law of Moses and in the Prophets.
translation_verse: Kashenteŋto, an nanaana be Ebɔrɛ na nɛ mee bɔla ekpa nɛ b yɛ k la efɛ na so a bunyaŋ. N yirda asɔ nɛ a wɔ Mosis be mbra na to nɛ anebiana na be nwɔl na to kikɛ nyam.

english_verse: I am just as sure as these people are that God will raise from death everyone, good or evil.
translation_verse: Tama koŋwule nɛ basa ere kɔ Ebɔrɛ so na nɛ ma alɛ gba kɔ, kumo e la fanɛ basa lela nɛ belubi kikɛ nyam beeŋ ba tiŋi luwu to.

english_verse: And because I am sure, I try my best to have a clear conscience in whatever I do for God or for people.
translation_verse: Amoso, saŋkama mee wora ania nna nɛ m baa kɔ kagbene koŋwule nɛ k maa wora ma shikashika ashi ma nɛ Ebɔrɛ nɛ nyiŋgbasa be kebaawɔtɔ to.

english_verse: After being away for several years, I returned here to bring gifts for the poor people of my nation and to offer sacrifices.
translation_verse: Ŋ ka lar Jerusalɛm kumo be nfɛ damta nde kabre, nɛ n naŋ bɛta n ta amansherbi nɛ n ya kɛ ma basa nseŋ lara sarga.

english_verse: This is what I was doing when I was found going through a ceremony in the temple. I wasn't with a crowd, and there was no uproar.
translation_verse: Le be kesheŋ ere nɛ n daa wɔ bɔrɛlambu na to a wora nɛ b wu ma. Saŋɛ na so nɛ n wora kefɔr eyurpi n lɛ be daŋkare na be asheŋ n loge. Jimaŋ kikɛ daa maŋ wɔ ma kutɔ, kebagato malɛ kikɛ daa maŋ wɔtɔ.

english_verse: Some Jews from Asia were there at that time, and if they have anything to say against me, they should be here now.
translation_verse: Ama Eeshia be efuli so be Juwebi ko malɛ daa wɔtɔ, amoso, a daga fanɛ bumo alɛ gba ka ba nfe m ba kaŋɛ fo alubi nɛ b wu ma so nɛ fanɛ b wu alubi ma so nna na.

english_verse: Or ask the ones who are here. They can tell you that they didn't find me guilty of anything when I was tried by their own council.
translation_verse: Ŋko fo shin nɛ basa ere e kaŋɛ fo kulubi nɛ b wu ma so, saŋɛ nɛ n daŋ yili nshɛrwuraana na kutɔ na.

english_verse: The only charge they can bring against me is what I shouted out in court, when I said, “I am on trial today because I believe that the dead will be raised to life!”
translation_verse: Kusɔ koŋwule nɛ n daŋ ba n yili bumo to ndoŋ ŋ kaŋɛ e la: ‘Menyee ji ma demu kabre nna ŋkpal ŋ ka yirda fanɛ bumo nɛ b wu na kikɛ ka beeŋ tiŋi luwu to so.’ ”

english_verse: Felix knew a lot about the Lord's Way. But he brought the trial to an end and said, “I will make my decision after Lysias the commander arrives.”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Filiks nɛ e daŋ nu Enyɛnpe be ekpa na be asheŋ ga ŋ ku so na shin nɛ b yige demu na be kenu nseŋ shin nɛ e kaŋɛ basa na: “Benapo be enimu Lisias kaŋ ba, meeŋ keni menyi be demu na to.”

english_verse: He then ordered the army officer to keep Paul under guard, but not to lock him up or to stop his friends from helping him. Paul Is Kept under Guard
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ e shin nɛ benapo be enimubi nɛ e daa de Pɔɔl so na keta Pɔɔl n ya kaa de mo so. Ama e daŋ sa mo ekpa n shin nɛ mo teriana daa tiŋ a chɛ mo to kanaŋkamaso nɛ b daa sha. Pɔɔl ka malga n sa Filiks nɛ Drusila be asheŋ

english_verse: Several days later Felix and his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish, went to the place where Paul was kept under guard. They sent for Paul and listened while he spoke to them about having faith in Christ Jesus.
translation_verse: Kachako malɛ nɛ Filiks keta mbe eche Drusila nɛ e daa la Juw na m ba shin nɛ b ya bar Pɔɔl nɛ e ba malga keyirda Yesu Kristo be asheŋ nɛ e nu.

english_verse: But Felix was frightened when Paul started talking to them about doing right, about self-control, and about the coming judgment. So he said to Paul, “That's enough for now. You may go. But when I have time I will send for you.”
translation_verse: Ama Pɔɔl ka ba kaa malga alela be kebaawora nɛ kamootiŋ nɛ Ebɔrɛ be demujiachɛ be asheŋ nɛ kufu pɛ Filiks nɛ e kaŋɛ: “Feeŋ tiŋ a yɔ naniere. N naŋ nya kachena meeŋ naŋ tre fo.”

english_verse: After this, Felix often sent for Paul and talked with him, because he hoped that Paul would offer him a bribe.
translation_verse: Saŋkama e daa tama fanɛ Pɔɔl beeŋ sa mo amansherbi nna. Amoso, e daa sha kebaatre mo a malga mo kutɔ ga.

english_verse: Two years later Porcius Festus became governor in place of Felix. But since Felix wanted to do the Jewish leaders a favor, he kept Paul in jail.
translation_verse: B wɔtɔ loŋ nɛ nfɛ anyɔ ba choŋ nɛ Pɔkias Fɛstes ba sɔ mo so a la gomena. Ŋkpal kenya ketre Juwebi na kutɔ so, Filiks daŋ yige Pɔɔl kabuti na to nna nseŋ yɔ.

english_verse: Three days after Festus had become governor, he went from Caesarea to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Fɛstes ka ba kasawule na so mbe kachɛ sasopo nɛ e yili Sizariya n yɔ Jerusalɛm.

english_verse: There the chief priests and some Jewish leaders told him about their charges against Paul. They also asked Festus
translation_verse: Nɛ bɔrɛmatapowuraana na nɛ Juwebi be benimuana na ba kaa kaŋɛ mo alubi nɛ Pɔɔl wora.

english_verse: if he would be willing to bring Paul to Jerusalem. They begged him to do this because they were planning to attack and kill Paul on the way.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ b kule Fɛstes fanɛ e wora ania n chɛ bumo to n shin nɛ Pɔɔl e ba Jerusalɛm. B ka daŋ kre Pɔɔl be kemɔ ekpa to be nia so nɛ b daŋ kaŋɛ loŋ na.

english_verse: But Festus told them, “Paul will be kept in Caesarea, and I am soon going there myself.
translation_verse: Nɛ Fɛstes kaŋɛ: “Pɔɔl wɔ kabuti to ashi Sizariya, ma alɛ gbagba maaŋ chɛr nseŋ bɛta n yɔ Sizariya.

english_verse: If he has done anything wrong, let your leaders go with me and bring charges against him there.”
translation_verse: Amoso, men shin nɛ menyi be benimu e tu ma n yɔ Sizariya n ya kaŋɛ alubi nɛ e wora nɛ fanɛ e wora amo nna na.”

english_verse: Festus stayed in Jerusalem for eight or ten more days before going to Caesarea. Then the next day he took his place as judge and had Paul brought into court.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ Fɛstes naŋ ji fanɛ nchɛ burwa ŋko nchɛ kudu basa na be kade na to pɔɛŋ nseŋ naŋ bɛta n yɔ Sizariya. Kumo be ŋklade nɛ e ya chena mbe kakpa nɛ e ji demu n shin nɛ b ya bar Pɔɔl.

english_verse: As soon as Paul came in, the leaders from Jerusalem crowded around him and said he was guilty of many serious crimes. But they could not prove anything.
translation_verse: Pɔɔl ka ba nɛ Juwebi nɛ b shi Jerusalɛm m ba na yili ŋ kulti mo nseŋ malga kenishipereso be asheŋ lubi damta mo nɛ b kaŋɛ fanɛ e wora, ama bumo alɛ daa maŋ tiŋ ŋ ŋini fanɛ asheŋ nɛ b daa malga na la kashenteŋ.

english_verse: Then Paul spoke in his own defense, “I have not broken the Law of my people. And I have not done anything against either the temple or the Emperor.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Pɔɔl malga le ŋ kuŋ mbe kumu: “M maŋ wora shɛŋ n da Juwebi be mbra na ŋko bɔrɛlambu na ŋko Romebi be ewurgboŋ na so.”

english_verse: Festus wanted to please the leaders. So he asked Paul, “Are you willing to go to Jerusalem and be tried by me on these charges?”
translation_verse: Ŋkpal kenya ketre Juwebi na kutɔ so, Fɛstes daŋ bishi Pɔɔl nna: “Fee sha keyɔ Jerusalɛm nɛ n ya ji fo asheŋ nɛ b yɛ fo wora ere be demu ndoŋ a?”

english_verse: Paul replied, “I am on trial in the Emperor's court, and that's where I should be tried. You know very well I have not done anything to harm the Jewish nation.
translation_verse: Nɛ Pɔɔl kaŋɛ: “Romebi be ewurgboŋ na be demujikpa gbagba ere to nɛ m baa yil nɛ b ji ma demu na. Fo gbagba baa nyi fanɛ m maŋ wora Juwebi na shɛŋ.

english_verse: If I had done something deserving death, I would not ask to escape the death penalty. But I am not guilty of any of these crimes, and no one has the right to hand me over to these people. I now ask to be tried by the Emperor himself.”
translation_verse: Nɛ n daŋ wora kusɔ ko nna n da mbra na so nɛ k daga ma luwu, n daa maaŋ gelge kumo be loŋ. Ama nɛ kashenteŋ maŋ wɔ asheŋ nɛ baa kaŋɛ fanɛ n wora ere to, esa kikɛ maaŋ tiŋ n ta ma m bɔɔ bumo enɔ. Romebi be ewurgboŋ na nɛ mee kule fanɛ e keni ma demu na to.”

english_verse: After Festus had talked this over with members of his council, he told Paul, “You have asked to be tried by the Emperor, and to the Emperor you will go!” Paul Speaks to Agrippa and Bernice
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ Fɛstes bishi mbe beyaasepo kusɔ nɛ e beeŋ wora Pɔɔl pɔɛŋ nseŋ kaŋɛ Pɔɔl: “Fo yɛ Romebi be ewurgboŋ na e keni fo demu na to, amoso, mo kutɔ nɛ feeŋ yɔ!” Fɛstes ka kaŋɛ Ewura Agripa Pɔɔl be asheŋ

english_verse: A few days later King Agrippa and Bernice came to Caesarea to visit Festus.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman saŋko nɛ Ewura Agripa nɛ Benis ba Sizariya nɛ b ba chɔrɔ Fɛstes n wora mo ansaŋ nɛ keba.

english_verse: They had been there for several days, when Festus told the king about the charges against Paul. He said: Felix left a man here in jail,
translation_verse: B wora nchɛnnyɔ ndoŋ nɛ kachako nɛ Fɛstes kaŋɛ ewura na Pɔɔl be asheŋ fanɛ: “Filiks yige kabutipo ko nfe.

english_verse: and when I went to Jerusalem, the chief priests and the Jewish leaders came and asked me to find him guilty.
translation_verse: Ŋ ka yɔ Jerusalɛm nɛ Juwebi be bɔrɛmatapowuraana na nɛ benimuana na ba kaŋɛ ma asheŋ lubi nɛ b wu mo so nseŋ kaŋɛ ma fanɛ ŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ e wora n da so.

english_verse: I told them it isn't the Roman custom to hand a man over to people who are bringing charges against him. He must first have the chance to meet them face to face and to defend himself against their charges.
translation_verse: Ama ŋ kaŋɛ bumo fanɛ Romebi maa shin nɛ baa gberge esa kusoe ŋkpal kulubi kama so she mo nɛ basa nɛ b kɔ abar na ba yili nna geeŋ nɛ e malga n sɔ mbe kumu ashi kulubi nɛ b yɛ e wora na to.

english_verse: So when they came here with me, I wasted no time. On the very next day I took my place on the judge's bench and ordered him to be brought in.
translation_verse: Bumo kikɛ ka kpal loŋ so m ba nfe nɛ n nya manaŋ kumo be ŋklade n ya chena demujikpa n shin nɛ b bar amo be kanyɛn.

english_verse: But when the men stood up to make their charges against him, they did not accuse him of any of the crimes that I thought they would.
translation_verse: Ama basa nɛ bumo nɛ mo daa kɔ abar na daa maŋ tiŋ n wu mo kenishipereso be alubi nɛ n daa tama fanɛ baaŋ wu mo na be kekama.

english_verse: Instead, they argued with him about some of their beliefs and about a dead man named Jesus, who Paul said was alive.
translation_verse: Bumo gbagba be kabɔrɛshuŋ nɛ ebuninyɛn ko nɛ baa tre Yesu na be emɔrɔana nawule be asheŋ nɛ b daa kɔ. Pɔɔl bee kaŋɛ nna fanɛ amo be kanyɛn na wɔ ŋkpa to.

english_verse: Since I did not know how to find out the truth about all this, I asked Paul if he would be willing to go to Jerusalem and be put on trial there.
translation_verse: N daa maŋ nyi ekpa nɛ meeŋ bɔla so n naŋ nu kusɔ ko n ti so m pin bumo be demu na to nseŋ bishi Pɔɔl fanɛ e bee sha keyɔ Jerusalɛm nɛ b ya keni demu na to a.

english_verse: But Paul asked to be kept in jail until the Emperor could decide his case. So I ordered him to be kept here until I could send him to the Emperor.
translation_verse: Nɛ Pɔɔl kini nseŋ kule fanɛ benapo e baa keni mo so nfe nseŋ shin nɛ Romebi be ewurgboŋ na e keni mbe demu na to kacha ko. Ndoŋ nna nɛ n shin nɛ benapo bee de mo so nɛ kachako nɛ e yɔ Romebi be ewurgboŋ na kutɔ.”

english_verse: Then Agrippa said to Festus, “I would also like to hear what this man has to say.” Festus answered, “You can hear him tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Agripa kaŋɛ Fɛstes: “Ma alɛ gba bee sha fanɛ e malga mbe demu na nɛ n nu.” Nɛ Fɛstes shuli so ŋ kaŋɛ: “To, echefo feeŋ nu kumo ashi mbe kɔnɔ to.”

english_verse: The next day Agrippa and Bernice made a big show as they came into the meeting room. High ranking army officers and leading citizens of the town were also there. Festus then ordered Paul to be brought in
translation_verse: Kumo be ŋklade nɛ Agripa nɛ Benis ba luri nshɛrkpa na bunyanso nɛ basa sa bumo kemaŋkura ga. Bumo nɛ benapo be benimuana na nɛ kade na to be benimuana na e daŋ luri nshɛrkpa na. Ndoŋ nna nɛ Fɛstes shin nɛ b ya bar Pɔɔl.

english_verse: and said: King Agrippa and other guests, look at this man! Every Jew from Jerusalem and Caesarea has come to me, demanding for him to be put to death.
translation_verse: Nɛ e kaŋɛ: “Ewura Agripa nɛ menyi nɛ men wɔ nfe ere, men keni kanyɛn ere nɛ nfe be Juwebiana na nɛ Jerusalɛm to peyaana na kikɛ bee kaŋɛ ma fanɛ e wora alubi nsaa ponte a kaŋɛ fanɛ e maŋ naŋ daga kebaawɔtɔ na.

english_verse: I have not found him guilty of any crime deserving death. But because he has asked to be judged by the Emperor, I have decided to send him to Rome.
translation_verse: Ama ma alɛ maaŋ tiŋ n wu kusɔ nɛ e wora n daga luwu be kasogberge. Mo alɛ naŋ kule fanɛ n shin nɛ Romebi be ewurgboŋ na gbagba e keni mbe demu na to, amoso, meeŋ shin nɛ b yɛr mo ndoŋ.

english_verse: I have to write some facts about this man to the Emperor. So I have brought him before all of you, but especially before you, King Agrippa. After we have talked about his case, I will then have something to write.
translation_verse: Ama m maŋ kɔ shɛŋ nɛ n sibɛ ŋ kaŋɛ n nyɛnpe na mbe asheŋ. Amoso nɛ m bar mo menyi kutɔ nfe na, fɔnfɔŋ fo, Ewura Agripa kutɔ nɛ n tiŋ n nya kusɔ ko demu na be kaman n sibɛ.

english_verse: It makes no sense to send a prisoner to the Emperor without stating the charges against him.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal manɛ so, a maŋ daga fo ka shin nɛ kabutipo yɔ loŋ, a maŋ sibɛ shɛŋ a ŋini ekama kulubi nɛ e wora.”

english_verse: Agrippa told Paul, “You may now speak for yourself.” Paul stretched out his hand and said:
translation_verse: Nɛ Agripa kaŋɛ Pɔɔl: “N sa fo ekpa nɛ fo malga ŋ kuŋ fo kumu.” Nɛ Pɔɔl teŋi mbe enɔ to nseŋ fara a malga le a kuŋ mbe kumu:

english_verse: King Agrippa, I am glad for this chance to defend myself before you today on all these charges my own people have brought against me.
translation_verse: “Ewura Agripa, k la kumulela nna ga ŋ ka tiŋ n yili fo anishito nfe kabre nɛ m malga ŋ kuŋ ma kumu ashi asheŋ nɛ Juwebi na ku n deŋi ma kikɛ to.

english_verse: You know a lot about our religious customs and the beliefs that divide us. So I ask you to listen patiently to me.
translation_verse: Kumo alɛ baŋ kukwe nna ŋkpal kananɛ fo nyi Juwebi be edaŋkareana na nɛ asheŋ nɛ b kɔ a ji abar emɔrɔana na kikɛ nɛnɛ na so. Amoso, mee kule fo fanɛ fo ji kanyiti n nu ma demu ere.

english_verse: All the Jews have known me since I was a child. They know what kind of life I have lived in my own country and in Jerusalem. And if they were willing, they could tell you I was a Pharisee, a member of a group that is stricter than any other.
translation_verse: Nɛ baa sha keji kashenteŋ, baaŋ kaŋɛ fo fanɛ dra dra na kikɛ nɛ b pin ŋ ka wɔ katuŋ nɛ k bee bɛ anyi be mbraana na so nɛnɛ a chɔ ntuŋ nɛ a ka na kikɛ na, katuŋ nɛ baa tre Efarisiana be katuŋ na.

english_verse: Now I am on trial because I believe the promise God made to our people long ago.
translation_verse: Ama ma e yil nfe kabre nɛ baa ji ma demu ŋkpal ŋ ka kɔ kɔnɔ nɛ Ebɔrɛ nase n sa an nanaana na be tama so.

english_verse: Day and night our twelve tribes have earnestly served God, waiting for his promised blessings. King Agrippa, because of this hope, some of our leaders have brought charges against me.
translation_verse: Kɔnɔ naseso koŋwule nɛ anyi be basa be nnaŋ kuduanyɔ ebi na bee bunyaŋ Ebɔrɛ kapa nɛ kanyɛ nsaa tama kenya na gbagba chap na. Yiramu, le be tama ere malɛ so nɛ Juwebi na bee ku asheŋ a deŋi ma na.

english_verse: Why should any of you doubt that God raises the dead to life?
translation_verse: Manɛ e ba nɛ menyi Juwebi maaŋ tiŋ n yirda fanɛ Ebɔrɛ bee tiŋi basa luwu to?

english_verse: I once thought that I should do everything I could to oppose Jesus from Nazareth.
translation_verse: Ma alɛ gba daŋ yili kumo nna fanɛ meeŋ wora kusɔ kama n tiŋ n jija Nazarɛt be Yesu be ketre na.

english_verse: I did this first in Jerusalem, and with the authority of the chief priests I put many of God's people in jail. I even voted for them to be killed.
translation_verse: Loŋ malɛ nɛ n daŋ wora ashi Jerusalɛm. N daa sɔ a chɛ to nna a kaŋɛ fanɛ bumo be luwu na daga bumo.

english_verse: I often had them punished in our synagogues, and I tried to make them give up their faith. In fact, I was so angry with them, that I went looking for them in foreign cities.
translation_verse: N daa wɔtɔ nna a shin nɛ baa gberge bumo kusoe ashi nshɛrbuana na to nseŋ daa kɔ a fin kananɛ meeŋ wora nɛ b kaŋɛ fanɛ b maaŋ naŋ yirda Yesu na. Agbo daŋ pɛ ma ga ŋkpal bumo so nɛ n yɔ hale nde pɔtɛana to gba nɛ n ya tɔrɔ bumo.” Pɔɔl ka malga kananɛ e ki ebɛsopo be asheŋ

english_verse: King Agrippa, one day I was on my way to Damascus with the authority and permission of the chief priests.
translation_verse: Le be kesheŋ nɛ n daŋ kule ekpa ashi bɔrɛmatapowuraana na kutɔ a yɔ Damaskɔs nɛ n ya wora.

english_verse: About noon I saw a light brighter than the sun. It flashed from heaven on me and on everyone traveling with me.
translation_verse: Yiramu, kapaso ko e daa la nɛ n wu kefulto ko ka fuli to a chɔ epeŋi n nyaŋɛ ashi ebɔrɛso m ba yuu ma nɛ basa nɛ an daa na na so.

english_verse: We all fell to the ground. Then I heard a voice say to me in Aramaic, “Saul, Saul, why are you so cruel to me? It's foolish to fight against me!”
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ anyi kikɛ tɔr kasawule nɛ n nu ebɔl ko ka bee bishi ma Hibruw to: ‘Sɔɔl, Sɔɔl, manɛ e ba nɛ fee tɔrɔ ma? Fo gbagba be kumu nɛ fee doro fanɛ kananɛ kena bee to keya a sela mo nyɛnpe be kekpabi a doro mo gbagba be kumu na.’

english_verse: “Who are you?” I asked. Then the Lord answered, “I am Jesus! I am the one you are so cruel to.
translation_verse: Nɛ m bishi: ‘Fo wanɛ Enyɛnpe?’ Nɛ Enyɛnpe na kaŋɛ: ‘Ma Yesu nɛ fee tɔrɔ na.

english_verse: Now stand up. I have appeared to you, because I have chosen you to be my servant. You are to tell others what you have learned about me and what I will show you later.”
translation_verse: Ama niŋi to ŋ koso n yili. N lar fo so nna nɛ n shin nɛ fo ki ma eshumpo. A daga fanɛ fo ya kaŋɛ basa ma asheŋ nɛ fo wu kabre ere nɛ amo nɛ meeŋ ŋini fo kachako so ere be asheŋ.

english_verse: The Lord also said, “I will protect you from the Jews and from the Gentiles that I am sending you to.
translation_verse: Meeŋ mɔlga fo ashi Israɛl be basa nɛ nnyamase nɛ meeŋ shin nɛ fo yɔ bumo kutɔ ere kutɔ.

english_verse: I want you to open their eyes, so they will turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God. Then their sins will be forgiven, and by faith in me they will become part of God's holy people.”
translation_verse: Ya bugi bumo be anishi n shin nɛ b lar bumo be tentembiri na to m ba kefulto to. Shin nɛ b lar Setani be eleŋ to m ba Ebɔrɛ peya to n shin nɛ b yirda ma nɛ n ta bumo be alubi m paŋ bumo nɛ b nya bumo be kakpa ashi Ebɔrɛ be basa laraso na to.’ Pɔɔl ka malga a bɔ Yesu be kubɔya na be asheŋ

english_verse: First I preached to the people in Damascus, and then I went to Jerusalem and all over Judea. Finally, I went to the Gentiles and said, “Stop sinning and turn to God! Then prove what you have done by the way you live.”
translation_verse: Damaskɔs nɛ n fara m bɔ kubɔya na nseŋ yɔ Jerusalɛm nɛ Juwebi be efuli so kikɛ nɛ nnyamase to n ya kaa bɔ kubɔya na fanɛ b lar bumo be alubi to m ba Ebɔrɛ kutɔ m ba kaa wora asheŋ nɛ a beeŋ ŋini fanɛ b lar bumo be alubi to kashenteŋto.

english_verse: That is why some men grabbed me in the temple and tried to kill me.
translation_verse: Ŋ ka wora le ere so nɛ Juwebi na nyaŋ ma ashi bɔrɛlambu na to n fin kemɔ ma na.

english_verse: But all this time God has helped me, and I have preached both to the rich and to the poor. I have told them only what the prophets and Moses said would happen.
translation_verse: Ama Ebɔrɛ chɛ ma to hale m ba fo kabre nɛ n yili nfe a ji ma shɛda a sa ekama nyam, begboŋi nɛ bewurbi kikɛ na. Kusɔ nɛ mee malga e la kusɔ koŋwule chap nɛ anebiana nɛ Mosis gba kaŋɛ fanɛ k beeŋ wora na.

english_verse: I told them how the Messiah would suffer and be the first to be raised from death, so he could bring light to his own people and to the Gentiles.
translation_verse: Kumo e la fanɛ, a daga fanɛ Kristo na e ji awurfoŋ nseŋ wu n juŋkpar ekama n tiŋi luwu to ŋ ŋini Juwebi nɛ nnyamase fanɛ baaŋ tiŋ n nya kumɔlga, kumo alɛ e la kefulto bumo kutɔ.”

english_verse: Before Paul finished defending himself, Festus shouted, “Paul, you're crazy! Too much learning has driven you out of your mind.”
translation_verse: Pɔɔl ka yili a malga le a kuŋ mbe kumu na nɛ Fɛstes ponte mo so ŋ kaŋɛ: “Pɔɔl, keyeŋiyeŋi e kɔ fo na. Fo kawɔl be kenyi damta ere e naa shin nɛ keyeŋiyeŋi tɔr fo so na.”

english_verse: But Paul replied, “Honorable Festus, I am not crazy. What I am saying is true, and it makes sense.
translation_verse: Nɛ Pɔɔl kaŋɛ: “Yiramu, m maa lɔ nna. Ma nɛ ma nfɛra lela nɛ kashenteŋ be mmalga nɛ mee malga na.

english_verse: None of these things happened off in a corner somewhere. I am sure that King Agrippa knows what I am talking about. That's why I can speak so plainly to him.”
translation_verse: Ewura Agripa, n tiŋ n ta kenyɛn m malga fo kutɔ nna ŋkpal fo ka nyi asheŋ ere kikɛ so. Ma alɛ bee tama fanɛ fo ta asheŋ na be kekama n wɔtɔ fo kagbene to, ŋkpal manɛ so, asheŋ na daa maŋ wora ŋ ŋana.

english_verse: Then Paul said to Agrippa, “Do you believe what the prophets said? I know you do.”
translation_verse: Ewura Agripa, fo yirda anebiana na a? N nyi fo ka yirda bumo.”

english_verse: Agrippa asked Paul, “In such a short time do you think you can talk me into being a Christian?”
translation_verse: Nɛ Agripa bishi Pɔɔl: “Fo tama fanɛ feeŋ tiŋ n yili epul ere to n shin nɛ ŋ ki Kristo be ebɛsopo a?”

english_verse: Paul answered, “Whether it takes a short time or a long time, I wish you and everyone else who hears me today would become just like me! Except, of course, for these chains.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Pɔɔl kaŋɛ: “Nɛ fo ki Kristo be ebɛsopo epul ere to ŋko kachako so gba, kusɔ nɛ mee kule Ebɔrɛ e la fanɛ e shin nɛ fo nɛ bumo nɛ b yil nfe kabre a nu kamalga ere e ba ki kananɛ n du ere. Kusɔ nɛ m maa kule nɛ men nya e la kananɛ n wɔ ŋgbɛlɛbi to ere.”

english_verse: Then King Agrippa, Governor Festus, Bernice, and everyone who was with them got up.
translation_verse: Kumo be kaman nɛ ewura na nɛ gomena na nɛ Benis nɛ basa nɛ b ka na kikɛ koso a yɔ nsaa kaŋɛ abar:

english_verse: But before they left, they said, “This man isn't guilty of anything. He doesn't deserve to die or to be put in jail.”
translation_verse: “Kanyɛn ere maŋ wora kusɔ kama nɛ k daga mbe luwu ŋko kabuti.”

english_verse: Agrippa told Festus, “Paul could have been set free, if he had not asked to be tried by the Roman Emperor.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Agripa kaŋɛ Fɛstes: “Nɛ kanyɛn ere daa maŋ kule fanɛ Romebi be ewurgboŋ na e keni mbe demu ere to nna, an daa beeŋ shin nɛ e lar kabuti ere to.”

english_verse: When it was time for us to sail to Rome, Captain Julius from the Emperor's special troops was put in charge of Paul and the other prisoners.
translation_verse: B ka ba yili kumo fanɛ an luri ekuloŋgboŋ ko to m bɔla nchu so n yɔ Itali nɛ b ta Pɔɔl nɛ kabutipoana ko m bɔɔ Julias enɔ. E daa la Romebi be ewurgboŋ be benapo be katuŋ to be enimubi nna.

english_verse: We went aboard a ship from Adramyttium that was about to sail to some ports along the coast of Asia. Aristarchus from Thessalonica in Macedonia sailed on the ship with us.
translation_verse: Adramitiam nɛ an daŋ yili n luri ekuloŋgboŋ ko nɛ k daŋ bela ase a yil nɛ k yɔ Eeshia be efuli so be teku be nnɔ ase na to n yɔ. Anyi nɛ Masɛdonia be esa nɛ e shi Tɛsalɔnika nɛ baa tre mo Aristaakes na e daa la.

english_verse: The next day we came to shore at Sidon. Captain Julius was very kind to Paul. He even let him visit his friends, so they could give him whatever he needed.
translation_verse: Kumo be ŋklade nɛ an fo Saidɔn. Ndoŋ nɛ Julias wora Pɔɔl kelela n shin nɛ e lar n ya chɔrɔ mo teriana nɛ b sa mo asɔ nɛ a daga fanɛ e nya.

english_verse: When we left Sidon, the winds were blowing against us, and we sailed close to the island of Cyprus to be safe from the wind.
translation_verse: An ka naŋ lar ndoŋ nɛ an kpal afu ko ka daa ber a shɛr anyi to so m bɔla Saipres so be kakpa nɛ afu na daa maa ber eleŋso na.

english_verse: Then we sailed south of Cilicia and Pamphylia until we came to the port of Myra in Lycia.
translation_verse: An ta loŋ m ba bɔla teku na be mboŋ nɛ a taga to Silisia nɛ Pamfilia be efuliana so na, n naŋ ta ndoŋ m ba fo Maira nɛ k wɔ Lisia na.

english_verse: There the army captain found a ship from Alexandria that was going to Italy. So he ordered us to board that ship.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nɛ benapo be enimubi na ba nya Alɛkzaandria be ekuloŋgboŋ ko nɛ k daa sha keyɔ Itali nɛ e shin nɛ an luri kumo to.

english_verse: We sailed along slowly for several days and had a hard time reaching Cnidus. The wind would not let us go any farther in that direction, so we sailed past Cape Salmone, where the island of Crete would protect us from the wind.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal afu na so ekuloŋgboŋ na daŋ nite nchu na so nna boeŋ boeŋ loŋ nchɛ damta ko pɔɛŋ nɛ an ba kpar Kenaidas so n yɔ. Ŋkpal kananɛ afu na daa ber a shɛr anyi to na so an daa maŋ tiŋ m bɔla kakpa nɛ an daŋ bɔla so na n yɔ anishito, amoso, Kriit be kepla na so be kakpa nɛ k daŋ kuŋ anyi ashi afu na to nɛ an daŋ bɔla n ya mata Salmoni ŋ kpar so n yɔ.

english_verse: We went slowly along the coast and finally reached a place called Fair Havens, not far from the town of Lasea.
translation_verse: An daŋ baŋ kra teku na be kɔnɔ ase nna n ji awurfoŋ loŋ n ya fo kakpa ko nɛ baa tre Ekulonyilikpa Lela Nɛ Kafɔŋ Maŋ Wɔtɔ na. Ndoŋ nɛ Lasiya be kade to daa maŋ wɔ kufɔ.

english_verse: By now we had already lost a lot of time, and sailing was no longer safe. In fact, even the Great Day of Forgiveness was past.
translation_verse: An daŋ chɛr ndoŋ ga hale nɛ anyi be kenaŋ pɛ ekpa ya ki kpakpa, ŋkpal manɛ so, saŋɛ na so nɛ kachɛ nɛ baa nyiŋi alubi be keyigempaŋ be asheŋ be daŋkare na gba baŋ so.

english_verse: Then Paul spoke to the crew of the ship, “Men, listen to me! If we sail now, our ship and its cargo will be badly damaged, and many lives will be lost.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Pɔɔl fiɛ bumo so ŋ kaŋɛ: “M braana, n wu fanɛ yili nfe a yɔ, anyi be enite ere be ekpa ere to lubi ga. Ekuloŋgboŋ ere nɛ kumo be esulɔ ere be adamta beeŋ jija nɛ basa gba e mur.”

english_verse: But Julius listened to the captain of the ship and its owner, rather than to Paul.
translation_verse: Ama benapo be enimubi na daŋ kplaŋ Pɔɔl be kamalga na so nna nseŋ yirda kusɔ nɛ ekuloŋgboŋ na be befarpoana na be enimu nɛ ekuloŋ na wura na kaŋɛ nna.

english_verse: The harbor at Fair Havens wasn't a good place to spend the winter. Because of this, almost everyone agreed that we should at least try to sail along the coast of Crete as far as Phoenix. It had a harbor that opened toward the southwest and northwest, and we could spend the winter there. The Storm at Sea
translation_verse: Ndoŋ be ekulonyilikpa na ka daa maa la kakpa lela awo to so, basa na be bedamta daa sha keyige eyilikpa na nna nsaa wɔ ekuloŋgboŋ na to a bɛ teku na so a sha kewora ania n fo Finiks nɛ baaŋ tiŋ nna na. Ndoŋ daa la Kriit be ekulonyilikpa nna a kɔ nnɔ anyɔ, kukoŋwule daa wɔ epeŋitɔrkpa be jisoso be kaba so nna nɛ kukoŋwule malɛ daa wɔ epeŋitɔrkpa be bena so be kaba so. Ndoŋ nɛ b daa beeŋ tiŋ n shir a wɔ hale nɛ awo na be jemanɛ e ya choŋ. Afugboŋ ko ka ber teku na so be asheŋ

english_verse: The wind struck the ship, and we could not sail against it. So we let the wind carry the ship.
translation_verse: nɛ k shɛr afu na to kanaŋkamaso ŋ gben nseŋ shin nɛ afu na kɔ anyi be ekuloŋgboŋ na a yɔ.

english_verse: We went along the island of Cauda on the side that was protected from the wind. We had a hard time holding the lifeboat in place,
translation_verse: An ka bɔla Kawda be kepla na be epeŋitɔrkpa nɛ an luri kakpa ko nɛ k kuŋ anyi gbrɛ ashi afu na to. Ndoŋ nɛ an wora ania ga m ba tiŋ m mɔlga ekulombi nɛ kegboŋi na daa gberge na ashi kebure to.

english_verse: but finally we got it where it belonged. Then the sailors wrapped ropes around the ship to hold it together. They lowered the sail and let the ship drift along, because they were afraid it might hit the sandbanks in the gulf of Syrtis.
translation_verse: B daŋ gberge kumo nna n wɔtɔ kegboŋi na be epunto nseŋ ta efɔlana m bɔla kegboŋi koŋwule na be kaseto ŋ kre kumo kpakpa. Ŋkpal b ka daa lɔ kufu fanɛ baaŋ ya ber Libiya be teku be ekarso be keplagboŋ na to n nia so, b daŋ yɔɔ ekuloŋ na be wajɛ gbɛgbɛso nɛ afu bee ber a yɛr ekuloŋgboŋ na nna nseŋ shin nɛ afu na e baa kɔ ekuloŋ to na a yɔ loŋ.

english_verse: The storm was so fierce that the next day they threw some of the ship's cargo overboard.
translation_verse: Kare ka chɛ nɛ afugboŋ na kraa ber eleŋso nɛ b fara a lara kumo to be esulɔ na a lɛ nchu na to.

english_verse: For several days we could not see either the sun or the stars. A strong wind kept blowing, and we finally gave up all hope of being saved.
translation_verse: An daŋ ji nchɛ damta ekuloŋgboŋ na to a maa wu epeŋi nɛ achɛkpabi nɛ afu na malɛ kraŋ baa ber eleŋso, nɛ an ba gben n yige kebaatama anyi be kenaŋ pete be asheŋ.

english_verse: Since none of us had eaten anything for a long time, Paul stood up and told the men: You should have listened to me! If you had stayed on in Crete, you would not have had this damage and loss.
translation_verse: Basa na ka ta nchɛ damta loŋ a maa ji shɛŋ nɛ kachako nɛ Pɔɔl koso n yili bumo to ŋ kaŋɛ: “M braana, a daga men ka daŋ bɛ ma kɔnɔ so n daŋ shir Kriit to nɛ an daŋ tiŋ ŋ gelge le be awurfoŋ nɛ jɛrbi nɛ anyee ji ere.

english_verse: But now I beg you to cheer up, because you will be safe. Only the ship will be lost.
translation_verse: Ama mee kule menyi nna fanɛ men baa kɔ kenyɛn, ŋkpal manɛ so, menyi be ekama maaŋ paŋ mbe ŋkpa, ekuloŋgboŋ ere nawule e naaŋ mur.

english_verse: I belong to God, and I worship him. Last night he sent an angel
translation_verse: Ŋkpal manɛ so, ndre kanyɛso Ebɔrɛ nɛ e wɔ ma nɛ mee bunyaŋ mo na be malaika kaŋ ba ma kutɔ nna m ba kaŋɛ ma:

english_verse: to tell me, “Paul, don't be afraid! You will stand trial before the Emperor. And because of you, God will save the lives of everyone on the ship.”
translation_verse: ‘Pɔɔl, sa maa lɔ kufu. A daga fanɛ fo ya yili Romebi be ewurgboŋ na be anishito. Ŋkpal Ebɔrɛ malɛ nɛ mbe kelela so, basa nɛ fo nɛ bumo wɔ nchu so be enite ere to ere be ekama maaŋ mur.’

english_verse: Cheer up! I am sure that God will do exactly what he promised.
translation_verse: Amoso, men baa kɔ kenyɛn, ŋkpal manɛ so, n yirda Ebɔrɛ fanɛ kusɔ nɛ e kaŋɛ ma na maaŋ chɛrga kikɛ.

english_verse: But we will first be shipwrecked on some island.
translation_verse: Ama afu ere beeŋ ber anyi n ya lɛ kechɛɛ ko so bre.”

english_verse: They cut the anchors loose and let them sink into the sea. At the same time they untied the ropes that were holding the rudders. Next, they raised the sail at the front of the ship and let the wind carry the ship toward the beach.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ b ku abɛlso gbɛgbɛso ana na be efɔlana na to n shin nɛ abɛlsoana na ka nchu na to nseŋ saŋɛ ekuloŋ na be kamanto be ndibi paŋgelambi nɛ b kɔ a niŋi kumo na malɛ epul na to. Ade be kaman nɛ b maŋ ekuloŋgboŋ na be wajɛ gbɛgbɛso nɛ afu bee ber a yɛr kumo na so ashi ekuloŋgboŋ na be anishito nɛ afu na e ber ekuloŋgboŋ na n yɔ anishito kedeŋi so.

english_verse: The sailors wanted to escape from the ship. So they lowered the lifeboat into the water, pretending that they were letting down some anchors from the front of the ship.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ekuloŋgboŋ na be befarpo na wora ania nɛ b lar n shile nseŋ yɔɔ ekulombi na to n wɔtɔ nchu na to nsaa kute a wora fanɛ b ka bee sha keta abɛlso gbɛgbɛso na be ako n lɛ n wɔtɔ ekuloŋ na be anishito malɛ na.

english_verse: But Paul said to Captain Julius and the soldiers, “If the sailors don't stay on the ship, you won't have any chance to save your lives.”
translation_verse: Nɛ Pɔɔl kaŋɛ benapo na nɛ bumo be enimubi na: “Befarpo ere baŋ lar ekuloŋgboŋ ere to, men maaŋ lar kikɛ.”

english_verse: The soldiers then cut the ropes that held the lifeboat and let it fall into the sea.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ benapo na ku efɔlana nɛ a kre ekulombi na m mata kegboŋi na n shin nɛ k yɔ.

english_verse: I beg you to eat something. Your lives depend on it. Do this and not one of you will be hurt.”
translation_verse: Jande men ji ajibi n nya eleŋ m mɔlga menyi gbagba be amu. Menyi be ekama maaŋ paŋ mbe kemin koŋwule gba.”

english_verse: After Paul had said this, he took a piece of bread and gave thanks to God. Then in front of everyone, he broke the bread and ate some.
translation_verse: Pɔɔl ka malga le n loge nɛ e ta bodobodo n di Ebɔrɛ epaŋ bumo kikɛ be anishito nseŋ bu kumo to n fara a we.

english_verse: They all felt encouraged, and each of them ate something.
translation_verse: Nɛ basa na ji kenyɛn nɛ bumo be ekama malɛ ji ajibi.

english_verse: and after everyone had eaten, they threw the cargo of wheat into the sea to make the ship lighter. The Shipwreck
translation_verse: Ekama ka ji n kukwe nɛ b ta ayu nɛ a wɔ ekuloŋgboŋ na to na n lɛ teku na to nɛ ekuloŋgboŋ na e fuga so. Ekuloŋgboŋ na ka bure be asheŋ

english_verse: Morning came, and the ship's crew saw a coast they did not recognize. But they did see a cove with a beach. So they decided to try to run the ship aground on the beach.
translation_verse: Kare ka chɛ befarpo na maŋ tiŋ m pin teku na be kedeŋi nɛ b fo na. Ama b wu teku na ka ku kasawule n wɔtɔ nchu na be kakpa ko nseŋ naŋ wora kewawa nɛ b yili kumo bumo be ŋgbene to fanɛ b shin nɛ ekuloŋgboŋ na e ya fo kasawule na n yili nɛ baaŋ tiŋ nna na.

english_verse: But it ran aground on a sandbank. The front of the ship stuck firmly in the sand, and the rear was being smashed by the force of the waves.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ ekuloŋgboŋ na ya ber kechɛɛsawule ko to nchu na to nɛ kumo be anishito nia nɛ k tia ŋ gben nsaa yil nɛ atiligboŋ ko bee kpata ekuloŋgboŋ na be kamanto eleŋso a bure kumo.

english_verse: The soldiers decided to kill the prisoners to keep them from swimming away and escaping.
translation_verse: Nɛ benapo na kre kemɔ kabutipoana na kikɛ nɛ bumo be ekama e sa maŋ laa n dii n shile n yɔ.

english_verse: But Captain Julius wanted to save Paul's life, and he did not let the soldiers do what they had planned. Instead, he ordered everyone who could swim to jump into the water and head for shore.
translation_verse: Ama benapo be enimubi na ka daa maa sha nɛ Pɔɔl e wu so, e daŋ ju benapo na ashi loŋ be kesheŋ na to nna nseŋ kaŋɛ basa na be bumo nɛ b daa nyi kalaa na kikɛ fanɛ b fara n tɛ n luri nchu na to a laa a dii.

english_verse: Then he told the others to hold on to planks of wood or parts of the ship. At last, everyone safely reached shore.
translation_verse: Nɛ bumo nɛ b ka na malɛ pɛ ekuloŋgboŋ na be ndibi fɛtaso na to m bɛ kaman a ba. Loŋ nɛ ekama daŋ wora n dii nɛ alenfia.

english_verse: When we came ashore, we learned that the island was called Malta.
translation_verse: An ka dii kedeŋi so nɛ alenfia nɛ an nu fanɛ kepla na nɛ baa tre Malta.

english_verse: The local people were very friendly, and they welcomed us by building a fire, because it was rainy and cold.
translation_verse: Ndoŋebi daŋ chɛ anyi to ga. Bɔrɛ daŋ fara nna a ba nɛ awo ko ba nɛ b puga edɛ n sa anyi nɛ an wɔl.

english_verse: After Paul had gathered some wood and had put it on the fire, the heat caused a snake to crawl out, and it bit him on the hand.
translation_verse: Pɔɔl ka chala ndibi a wɔtɔ edɛ na to nɛ kuwɔ ko lar ndibi na to ŋkpal kuwuloŋ na so m mea mbe enɔ kpakpa.

english_verse: When the local people saw the snake hanging from Paul's hand, they said to each other, “This man must be a murderer! He didn't drown in the sea, but the goddess of justice will kill him anyway.”
translation_verse: Kepla na so be basa na ka wu kuwɔ na ka chul Pɔɔl be enɔ so nɛ b kaŋɛ abar: “Kanyɛn ere la emɔpo nna, k maŋ kɔ emɔrɔ. E tiŋ n lar nchu na to nɛ alenfia, ama kashenteŋ be ekpa so be ebɔrɛ na maaŋ yige mo nɛ e baa kraa wɔtɔ.”

english_verse: Paul shook the snake off into the fire and wasn't harmed.
translation_verse: Ama Pɔɔl tiŋ ŋ ŋmenyaŋ kuwɔ na n wɔtɔ edɛ na to nɛ k maŋ tiŋ n doro mo kikɛ.

english_verse: The people kept thinking that Paul would either swell up or suddenly drop dead. They watched him for a long time, and when nothing happened to him, they changed their minds and said, “This man is a god.”
translation_verse: B daa dara mo nna a keni kananɛ e beeŋ tiŋ to n tɔr epul na to n wu. Ama b ka jo loŋ n ya gben a maa wu kulubi kikɛ ka bee nya Pɔɔl nɛ b chɛrga bumo be nfɛra nseŋ kaŋɛ: “Ebɔrɛ ko e la mo.”

english_verse: The governor of the island was named Publius, and he owned some of the land around there. Publius was very friendly and welcomed us into his home for three days.
translation_verse: Kakpa nɛ kesheŋ ere daŋ wora Pɔɔl na nɛ kepla na so wura be adɔsawuleana so daa maŋ wɔ kufɔ. Ewura na be ketre e daa la Pablias. E daŋ sɔ anyi kasawule na so nseŋ keta anyi kufɔ nɛnɛ ga nchɛ nsa.

english_verse: His father was in bed, sick with fever and stomach trouble, and Paul went to visit him. Paul healed the man by praying and placing his hands on him.
translation_verse: Pablias mo tuto be eyur daŋ bel edɛ nna nɛ e dese ebu to a lɔ epun to nɛ Pɔɔl luri mbe ebu na to n ta mbe enɔana n deŋi mo so nseŋ kule Ebɔrɛ n sa mo nɛ e nya alenfia.

english_verse: After this happened, everyone on the island brought their sick people to Paul, and they were all healed.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ kechɛɛsawule na so be belɔpo kikɛ ba nɛ e chɛ bumo.

english_verse: Three months later we sailed in a ship that had been docked at Malta for the winter. The ship was from Alexandria in Egypt and was known as “The Twin Gods.”
translation_verse: Afɔl asa be kaman nɛ an luri Alɛkzaandria be ekuloŋgboŋ ko nɛ baa tre kumo Mborobi na to n yɔ. Kepla na so nɛ k daŋ ba kaa wɔ loŋ nɛ awo be jemanɛ ba choŋ.

english_verse: We arrived in Syracuse and stayed for three days.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ nna nɛ an ta n ya fo Sirakyus be kade to n ji nchɛ asa ndoŋ pɔɛŋ

english_verse: From there we sailed to Rhegium. The next day a south wind began to blow, and two days later we arrived in Puteoli.
translation_verse: nseŋ ta loŋ m ba fo kadegboŋ ko nɛ baa tre Rɛjiam. Kumo be ŋklade nɛ afu ko shi epeŋitɔrkpa be bena so m ber m ba. Kumo be kachɛ nyɔsopo nɛ an fo Putioli be ekulonyilikpa.

english_verse: There we found some of the Lord's followers, who begged us to stay with them. A week later we left for the city of Rome.
translation_verse: An ka ba wu bebɛsopo ko ndoŋ nɛ b shin nɛ an ji bɔkwe bumo kutɔ. Asheŋ nɛ a daŋ wora anyi anyi be enite na to pɔɛŋ nɛ an ya fo Rom nna na.

english_verse: Some of the followers in Rome heard about us and came to meet us at the Market of Appius and at the Three Inns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and was encouraged. Paul in Rome
translation_verse: Bekurgepo nɛ b wɔ Rom na ka nu anyi be asheŋ nɛ b lege anyi m ba hale Apias be Kebɛ nɛ kakpa nɛ baa tre Befɔ be Ewushikpa be Nwu Asa na. Pɔɔl ka wu bumo nɛ e nya kenyɛn chɔrɔ Ebɔrɛ ga. Kusɔ nɛ k wora Pɔɔl ashi Rom be asheŋ

english_verse: We arrived in Rome, and Paul was allowed to live in a house by himself with a soldier to guard him.
translation_verse: An ka ba Rom nɛ Romebi be abane be benimuana na shin nɛ Pɔɔl gbagba wɔtɔ a keni mbe kumu so nseŋ shin nɛ b lara enapo nɛ e baa de Pɔɔl so.

english_verse: Three days after we got there, Paul called together some of the Jewish leaders and said: My friends, I have never done anything to hurt our people, and I have never gone against the customs of our ancestors. But in Jerusalem I was handed over as a prisoner to the Romans.
translation_verse: Pɔɔl be kachɛ sasopo ashi Rom nɛ e tre ndoŋ be Juwebi be benimuana na m ba shɛr ŋ kaŋɛ bumo: “Ŋ kurgepoana, m maŋ wora shɛŋ n da anyi be basa ŋko edaŋkare nɛ an nanaana sa anyi na so nɛ m peebi ti ma ebu ashi Jerusalɛm nseŋ naŋ ta ma m bɔɔ Romebi enɔ.

english_verse: They looked into the charges against me and wanted to release me. They found that I had not done anything deserving death.
translation_verse: Romebi na ka bishi ma asheŋ a maŋ wu kulubi kikɛ nɛ n wora nɛ k daga luwu nɛ b daa shin nɛ b yige ma.

english_verse: The Jewish leaders disagreed, so I asked to be tried by the Emperor. But I don't have anything to say against my own nation.
translation_verse: Nɛ Juwebi na maŋ shuli kumo be loŋ nɛ ŋ gben ŋ kule fanɛ b shin nɛ Romebi be ewurgboŋ na gbagba e keni ma demu na to, mannɛ fanɛ ŋ kɔ kusɔ ko nna a sha keta n wu m peebi na kulubi.

english_verse: I am bound by these chains because of what we people of Israel hope for. This is why I have called you here to talk about this hope of ours.
translation_verse: Amoso nɛ n tre menyi nɛ ŋ kaŋɛ menyi amo na. Esa nɛ Israɛlebi na bee tama fanɛ e beeŋ ba na malɛ so nɛ ŋgbɛlɛbi ere wɔ ma enɔana to na.”

english_verse: The leaders replied, “No one from Judea has written us a letter about you. And not one of them has come here to report on you or to say anything against you.
translation_verse: Nɛ b kaŋɛ mo: “Esa kama maŋ sibɛ anyi nwɔl ashi Judiya ŋ kaŋɛ anyi fo asheŋ, an kurgepo kama malɛ maŋ shi ndoŋ m bar anyi fo baru lubi ŋko kulubi kama nɛ fo wora be asheŋ.

english_verse: But we would like to hear what you have to say. We understand that people everywhere are against this new group.”
translation_verse: Ama kaŋɛ anyi kusɔ nɛ k wɔ fo kumu to, kusɔ nɛ fee fɛ, ŋkpal manɛ so, an nyi basa ka bee malga kaplɛkama a gbiti katuŋ nɛ fo wɔ na to be basa.”

english_verse: They agreed on a time to meet with Paul, and many of them came to his house. From early morning until late in the afternoon, Paul talked to them about God's kingdom. He used the Law of Moses and the Books of the Prophets to try to win them over to Jesus.
translation_verse: Kede be kaman nɛ b sa Pɔɔl kachɛ nɛ baaŋ ba. Kachɛ na ka fo nɛ bumo be bedamta ba kakpa nɛ Pɔɔl daa wɔ na nɛ e baŋ yili chipurso m bɔ Ebɔrɛ be kuwura na to be asheŋ na ŋ ŋini bumo loŋ n ya fo kanyɛso. E daŋ bɛ Mosis be mbra na nɛ anebiana na be nsibɛ na so nna ŋ kɔ ga n fin keshin nɛ basa na yirda Yesu.

english_verse: Some of the leaders agreed with what Paul said, but others did not.
translation_verse: Beko daŋ yirda mbe kamalga na nɛ beko malɛ kini keyirda kumo.

english_verse: Since they could not agree among themselves, they started leaving. But Paul said, “The Holy Spirit said the right thing when he sent Isaiah the prophet
translation_verse: Pɔɔl ka malga kesheŋ koŋwule ere n loge nɛ b fara a ji abar emɔrɔ a yɔ. Le nɛ e daŋ kaŋɛ: “Kashenteŋ nɛ Kiyoyu Cheeŋ na daŋ shin nɛ anebi Aizaaya daŋ wu ŋ kaŋɛ men nanaana fanɛ e ya kaŋɛ basa na le:

english_verse: to tell our ancestors, ‘Go to these people and tell them: You will listen and listen, but never understand. You will look and look, but never see.
translation_verse: ‘Menyeeŋ nu hale n ya gben, ama men maaŋ pin to. Menyeeŋ keni hale n ya gben, ama men maaŋ wu shɛŋ.’

english_verse: All of you have stubborn hearts. Your ears are stopped up, and your eyes are covered. You cannot see or hear or understand. If you could, you would turn to me, and I would heal you.’ ”
translation_verse: ‘Ŋkpal basa ere be ŋgbene ka du kpakpa so b ti bumo be asoe nseŋ buu bumo be anishi so. Nɛ mannɛ aloŋ, bumo be anishi beeŋ bugi asheŋ be kewuto nɛ bumo be asoe e bugi asheŋ be kenuto nɛ bumo be ŋgbene e bugi asheŋ be kepinto. Ebɔrɛ yɛ: Loŋ na baaŋ ba ma kutɔ nɛ n lara bumo ashi bumo be kebaawɔtɔ dra to n sa bumo kebaawɔtɔ popɔr.’ ”

english_verse: Paul said, “You may be sure that God wants to save the Gentiles! And they will listen.”
translation_verse: Pɔɔl ka malga asheŋ ere n loge nɛ Juwebi na pesaŋ to a ji abar emɔrɔ kpakpaso a yɔ.

english_verse: He bravely preached about God's kingdom and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ, and no one tried to stop him.
translation_verse: Ndoŋ koŋwule na malɛ nɛ e daa wɔ a bɔ Ebɔrɛ be kuwura na to be kubɔya na a sa basa kenyɛnso a malga kayurwushiso a ŋini Enyɛnpe Yesu Kristo be asheŋ.

english_verse: From Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus. God chose me to be an apostle, and he appointed me to preach the good news
translation_verse: Kawɔl ere shi ma Pɔɔl nɛ n la Kristo Yesu be kenya na kutɔ nna. Ebɔrɛ e tre ma nseŋ lara ma ashi ma basa to n shin nɛ ŋ ki mbe eshuŋipo nɛ m ba kaa bɔ mbe baru lela na.

english_verse: that he promised long ago by what his prophets said in the holy Scriptures.
translation_verse: Dradra na kikɛ nɛ mo ere Ebɔrɛ na bɔla mbe anebiana so nɛ abɔrɛsibɛ cheembi na to n nase kɔnɔ

english_verse: This good news is about his Son, our Lord Jesus Christ! As a human, he was from the family of David. But the Holy Spirit proved that Jesus is the powerful Son of God, because he was raised from death.
translation_verse: Kebaawɔtɔ cheembi be Kiyoyu malɛ be kaplɛa so, Ebɔrɛ ta eleŋgboŋ ŋ ŋini e ka la mo Pibinyɛn saŋɛ nɛ e tiŋi mo luwu to na.

english_verse: Jesus was kind to me and chose me to be an apostle, so that people of all nations would obey and have faith.
translation_verse: Mo so nɛ Ebɔrɛ bɔla n wu ma kuwɔr n sa ma ekpa fanɛ m baa la eshuŋipo ŋkpal Yesu koŋwule na be ketre so nɛ efuli kama so ebi e ba yirda mo nseŋ fara a nu a sa mo.

english_verse: This letter is to all of you in Rome. God loves you and has chosen you to be his very own people. I pray that God our Father and our Lord Jesus Christ will be kind to you and will bless you with peace! A Prayer of Thanks
translation_verse: Amoso nɛ mee sibɛ kawɔl ere a sa menyi kikɛ nɛ men wɔ Rom be kade to nɛ Ebɔrɛ bee sha menyi nseŋ tre menyi fanɛ men ba kaa la mo gbagba be basa na. An Tuto Ebɔrɛ nɛ Enyɛnpe Yesu Kristo e sa menyi kuwɔr be kakɛ nɛ kagbenewushi. Pɔɔl ka bee di Ebɔrɛ epaŋ nsaa chɔrɔ mo be asheŋ

english_verse: First, I thank God in the name of Jesus Christ for all of you. I do this because people everywhere in the world are talking about your faith.
translation_verse: Men shin nɛ n fara m bɔla Yesu Kristo so n chɔrɔ ma Ebɔrɛ ŋkpal menyi kikɛ so. Ŋkpal manɛ so, durnya ere to ebi kikɛ baa ji kananɛ menyi be yirda du be asheŋ nna.

english_verse: God has seen how I never stop praying for you, while I serve him with all my heart and tell the good news about his Son.
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ nɛ n ta ma kagbene kikɛ nyam a bɔ mo Pibinyɛn be baru lela na gbagba e la ma shɛdajipo a nyi menyi be asheŋ ka baa wɔ ma kagbene to ashi ma kabɔrɛkule to saŋkikɛ.

english_verse: In all my prayers, I ask God to make it possible for me to visit you.
translation_verse: Ma alɛ bee kule Ebɔrɛ nna fanɛ naniere nɛ k par mo, e sa ma ekpa nɛ m ba bɔɔ menyi so.

english_verse: I want to see you and share with you the same blessings that God's Spirit has given me. Then you will grow stronger in your faith.
translation_verse: M baa sha kewu menyi gbrɛ nna n shin nɛ men nya abɔrɛsheŋ be nɛfa nɛ a bee bɔla Ebɔrɛ be Kiyoyu na so a ba anyi so na. Loŋ e naaŋ shin nɛ men nya eleŋ kebɛso na to n ti so.

english_verse: What I am saying is that we can encourage each other by the faith that is ours.
translation_verse: Kumo e la fanɛ nɛ n tiŋ m ba, menyi be yirda beeŋ leŋ ma to nɛ ma alɛ peya e leŋ menyi alɛ gba to.

english_verse: My friends, I want you to know that I have often planned to come for a visit. But something has always kept me from doing it. I want to win followers to Christ in Rome, as I have done in many other places.
translation_verse: Bekurgepoana, mee sha fanɛ men baa nyi fanɛ saŋɛ damta nɛ ŋ kre keba menyi kutɔ be nia nɛ m ba shin nɛ basa e yirda Yesu kananɛ n shin nɛ nnyamase ko gba wora ashi mboŋ ko na, ama m maŋ nya kumo be ekpa.

english_verse: It doesn't matter if people are civilized and educated, or if they are uncivilized and uneducated. I must tell the good news to everyone. That's why I am eager to visit all of you in Rome. The Power of the Good News
translation_verse: Amoso nɛ m baa sha kebɔ baru lela na n sa menyi nɛ men wɔ Rom be kade to gba na. Baru lela na be eleŋ be asheŋ

english_verse: The good news tells how God accepts everyone who has faith, but only those who have faith. It is just as the Scriptures say, “The people God accepts because of their faith will live.” Everyone Is Guilty
translation_verse: Ŋkpal manɛ so, baru lela na e naa ŋini kananɛ Ebɔrɛ bee nase kumo fanɛ basa e baa la belelapo mbe anishito. Kumo alɛ be sososo kikɛ la yirda nna hale n ya fo ekar. Loŋ gbagba malɛ nɛ abɔrɛsibɛ na bee kaŋɛ na fanɛ: “Esa kama nɛ Ebɔrɛ nase kɔnɔ fanɛ e la elelapo na beeŋ nya ŋkpa ŋkpal mbe yirda so.” Ebɔrɛ be agbo nɛ k bee ba basa so be asheŋ

english_verse: They know everything that can be known about God, because God has shown it all to them.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal manɛ so, asɔ nɛ basa beeŋ ta m pin Ebɔrɛ na baŋ dii efuli nna geeŋ a sa bumo, ŋkpal manɛ so, Ebɔrɛ gbagba e bugi amo to n sa bumo.

english_verse: They know about God, but they don't honor him or even thank him. Their thoughts are useless, and their stupid minds are in the dark.
translation_verse: B nyi Ebɔrɛ be asheŋ, ama bumo alɛ maa ta mo fanɛ Ebɔrɛ a bunyaŋ mo ŋko a chɔrɔ mo. Ama b shin nɛ bumo be nfɛra ki nfɛra fuloŋ nna nɛ bumo be kawuliso be ŋgbene malɛ ki m biri to.

english_verse: They claim to be wise, but they are fools.
translation_verse: B yɛ b nyi asheŋ, ama bumo alɛ ki bewulpo nna.

english_verse: They don't worship the glorious and eternal God. Instead, they worship idols that are made to look like humans who cannot live forever, and like birds, animals, and reptiles.
translation_verse: B ka beeŋ baa bunyaŋ Ebɔrɛ nɛ e wɔ ŋkpa to saŋkama na, b wɔtɔ nna a bunyaŋ asɔ nɛ enyiŋgbasa wora nna nɛ amo be ako duli basa nɛ ako duli mbuibi, ako malɛ duli asɔbɔya nɛ ade malɛ duli asɔ gbeyeso.

english_verse: So God let these people go their own way. They did what they wanted to do, and their filthy thoughts made them do shameful things with their bodies.
translation_verse: Amoso, Ebɔrɛ malɛ yige bumo be asheŋ nna n sa bumo nɛ b luri kesakalea be ayɛlgasɔ to a wɔtɔ a kɔ abar be eyurana a wora amɔmɔshiasheŋ.

english_verse: They gave up the truth about God for a lie, and they worshiped God's creation instead of God, who will be praised forever. Amen.
translation_verse: Kashenteŋ be mmalga nɛ a bee kute Ebɔrɛ be asheŋ na nɛ b kɔ a chɛr efɛ be mmalga a wɔtɔ a bunyaŋ nsaa shuŋ Ebɔrɛ be asɔtoso nsaa yige amo be Etopo na bre, emo nɛ e daga epaŋ be kedi hale mbaanaayɔ na. Amɛn.

english_verse: God let them follow their own evil desires. Women no longer wanted to have sex in a natural way, and they did things with each other that were not natural.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal le be asheŋ ere so Ebɔrɛ yige bumo nna n sa kesakalea be ayɛlgasɔ hale nɛ bumo be beche yige kedi benyɛn n lɛ nsaa kɔ bumo braana beche a di keche nɛ kenyɛn.

english_verse: Men behaved in the same way. They stopped wanting to have sex with women and had strong desires for sex with other men. They did shameful things with each other, and what has happened to them is punishment for their foolish deeds.
translation_verse: Loŋ koŋwule na nɛ benyɛn na gba bee yige kebaadi beche a lɛ nsaa shin nɛ bumo be ŋgbene bee kaa kesakalea so a wɔ bumo braana benyɛn be kasha to. Benyɛn wɔtɔ nna a kɔ abar kesakalea so a wora amɔmɔshiasheŋ nsaa nya amo be loŋ be tɔnɔ ashi bumo be eyurana to.

english_verse: Since these people refused even to think about God, he let their useless minds rule over them. That's why they do all sorts of indecent things.
translation_verse: Ade malɛ kikɛ be kaman Ebɔrɛ yige bumo be asheŋ nna n sa bumo ŋkpal b ka kini kenyiŋi kashenteŋ be abɔrɛsheŋ na so nɛ b baa wɔtɔ a wora asheŋ nɛ a maŋ daga kikɛ.

english_verse: They are evil, wicked, and greedy, as well as mean in every possible way. They want what others have, and they murder, argue, cheat, and are hard to get along with. They gossip,
translation_verse: Ŋkpal b ka kini Ebɔrɛ na so, eda lubi be yiri kikɛ nɛ alubisheŋ nɛ kejimuni nɛ abar be kebaawora alubi e bɔlɔ bumo to. Amo nɛ a bɔlɔ bumo to gba n ti so e la, kayurbesa nɛ kamɔ nɛ nlu nɛ efɛ nɛ kebaafɛ abar asheŋ lubi. Ade malɛ gba be buushi baa kuli bumo braana,

english_verse: say cruel things about others, and hate God. They are proud, conceited, and boastful, always thinking up new ways to do evil. These people don't respect their parents.
translation_verse: nsaa malga alubi a gbiti abar a kishi Ebɔrɛ be asheŋ a tege abar nsaa wu bumo be amu. B kɔ mpuchi a fin alubi be ekpa popɔrana a wora alubi nsaa kini kebaanu a sa bumo nioana nɛ bumo tutoana.

english_verse: They are stupid, unreliable, and don't have any love or pity for others.
translation_verse: B maŋ nyi asheŋ, bumo alɛ maŋ naa bɛ bumo be nnɔ so ŋko a wu kuwɔr nsaa maa la basa.

english_verse: They know God has said that anyone who acts this way deserves to die. But they keep on doing evil things, and they even encourage others to do them.
translation_verse: B nyi Ebɔrɛ be mbra na ka bee kaŋɛ fanɛ bekama nɛ b wɔ le be kebaawɔtɔ ere to daga luwu, ama b kraŋ pere kenishi nna a wora amo nsaa leŋ basa pɔtɛ gba to a wɔtɔ loŋ be asheŋ na be kewora to.

english_verse: Some of you accuse others of doing wrong. But there is no excuse for what you do. When you judge others, you condemn yourselves, because you are guilty of doing the very same things.
translation_verse: Amoso, manɛ be ekpa nɛ fo dimɛdi kɔ nsaa tiŋ a wu fo barkasa kulubi? Ŋkpal manɛ so, kanaŋkama nɛ fo du nseŋ wu fo barkasa kulubi, fee ji nna a bri fo gbagba be kumu nna na, ŋkpal manɛ so, asɔ koŋwule na nɛ fee wora.

english_verse: We know that God is right to judge everyone who behaves in this way.
translation_verse: Nɛ Ebɔrɛ bre bee ji basa nɛ baa wora asheŋ ere demu, an nyi e ka bee ji asheŋ kashenteŋ be ekpa so.

english_verse: Do you really think God won't punish you, when you behave exactly like the people you accuse?
translation_verse: Ama fo ere dimɛdi, asheŋ nɛ fo kɔ a wu basa kulubi ere gbagba nɛ fee wora, amoso, fee tama fanɛ feeŋ nya ŋ gelge Ebɔrɛ be demuji to a?

english_verse: You surely don't think much of God's wonderful goodness or of his patience and willingness to put up with you. Don't you know that the reason God is good to you is because he wants you to turn to him?
translation_verse: Ŋko fo kpal Ebɔrɛ be kelela ka shi mo to ga na so nna nɛ e ka maa nya manaŋ a gberge basa kusoe na nɛ mbe kanyiti na so so nna a fɛl mo a? Fo maŋ nyi fanɛ Ebɔrɛ be kelela wɔtɔ nna nɛ fo nya n lar fo alubi to a?

english_verse: But you are stubborn and refuse to turn to God. So you are making things even worse for yourselves on that day when he will show how angry he is and will judge the world with fairness.
translation_verse: Ama ŋkpal fo kagbene ka du kpakpa a maa sha kechɛrga na so, fo wɔ fo alubi na to nna a shin nɛ Ebɔrɛ be agbo bee kaa a ti so a jo kachɛ nɛ mbe agbo nɛ mbe demuji kashenteŋ be ekpa so na bee lar efuli na.

english_verse: God will reward each of us for what we have done.
translation_verse: Kusɔ kama nɛ esa wora, Ebɔrɛ beeŋ ka mo kumo be kukɔ.

english_verse: He will give eternal life to everyone who has patiently done what is good in the hope of receiving glory, honor, and life that lasts forever.
translation_verse: Bumo nɛ alelasheŋ be kewora maa gben bumo nɛ baa fin kemaŋkura nɛ bunyaŋ nɛ kebaawɔtɔ nɛ k maŋ kɔ luwu na, e beeŋ sa bumo ŋkpa nɛ k maŋ kɔ ekar na.

english_verse: But he will show how angry and furious he can be with every selfish person who rejects the truth and wants to do evil.
translation_verse: Ama bumo nɛ b wɔ bumo gbagba be aparsheŋ to a kini kashenteŋ na be kebɛso nsaa bɛ alubi so na, Ebɔrɛ be kagbene beeŋ kaa nɛ mbe agbo e ba bumo so.

english_verse: All who are wicked will be punished with trouble and suffering. It doesn't matter if they are Jews or Gentiles.
translation_verse: Tɔrɔ nɛ kayurnyaŋ beeŋ ba dimɛdi kama nɛ e bee wora alubi so, Juwebi e naaŋ juŋkpar n nya amo pɔɛŋ nɛ nnyamase e bɛ so.

english_verse: But all who do right will be rewarded with glory, honor, and peace, whether they are Jews or Gentiles.
translation_verse: Ama ekama nɛ e bee wora alelasheŋ, kemaŋkura nɛ bunyaŋ nɛ kagbenewushi beeŋ baa wɔ amodoŋwura so. Juwebi e naaŋ juŋkpar n nya amo pɔɛŋ nseŋ ta nnyamase m bɛ so.

english_verse: God doesn't have any favorites!
translation_verse: Ŋkpal manɛ so, Ebɔrɛ maa kpɛa basa to.

english_verse: Those people who don't know about God's Law will still be punished for what they do wrong. And the Law will be used to judge everyone who knows what it says.
translation_verse: Bekama nɛ b maŋ kɔ mbra na nseŋ wora alubi beeŋ lar mbra na be kaman n wu. Bekama malɛ nɛ b wɔ mbra na to nseŋ wora alubi, mbra na to nɛ Ebɔrɛ beeŋ bɔla n ji bumo demu.

english_verse: By reading the Scriptures you learn how God wants you to behave, and you discover what is right.
translation_verse: Mannɛ fo e naa kaŋɛ fanɛ fo nyi kusɔ nɛ Ebɔrɛ bee sha fanɛ esa e wora, fo alɛ naŋ koya ashi mbra na to a nyi kusɔ nɛ k daga esa ka lara na a?

english_verse: You are sure that you are a guide for the blind and a light for all who are in the dark.
translation_verse: Mannɛ fo koŋwule na e naa kaŋɛ fanɛ fo e baa la esa nɛ e bee keta betanpo kekpabi nsaa du fanɛ kefulto a sa bumo nɛ b wɔ tentembiri to na a?

english_verse: And since there is knowledge and truth in God's Law, you think you can instruct fools and teach young people.
translation_verse: Mannɛ fo koŋwule na e kraa kaŋɛ fanɛ fo e la basa balto be eŋinipo nɛ mbibi be eŋinipo, ŋkpal manɛ so, fo ere be kanyiasheŋ na nɛ kashenteŋ na bee shi mbra na to nna a?

english_verse: But how can you teach others when you refuse to learn? You preach it is wrong to steal. But do you steal?
translation_verse: To, fo nɛ fee ŋini basa pɔtɛ asheŋ, fo maa ŋini fo kumu loŋ be asheŋ na a? Fo e naa malga abɔrɛsheŋ a sa basa fanɛ b sa maa yuri, fo alɛ nsaa yuri a?

english_verse: You take pride in the Law, but you disobey the Law and bring shame to God.
translation_verse: Fo e wɔtɔ a kɔ mbra na a ji njɔŋ, fo alɛ nseŋ naa shin nɛ fo kemaa bɛ amo so bee bar Ebɔrɛ anishinyɔr.

english_verse: It is just as the Scriptures tell us, “You have made foreigners say insulting things about God.”
translation_verse: Loŋ koŋwule na malɛ nɛ abɔrɛsibɛ na bee kaŋɛ na fanɛ: “Menyi, Juwebi so nɛ nnyamase bee malga a ji Ebɔrɛ emɔrɔ.”

english_verse: Being circumcised is worthwhile, if you obey the Law. But if you don't obey the Law, you are no better off than people who are not circumcised.
translation_verse: Nɛ fee bɛ mbra na be kɔnɔ so nseŋ ku kututu, kumo ere fo keku na kɔ kifi, ama nɛ fo maa bɛ mbra na be kɔnɔ so nseŋ ku kututu, kenyanyaŋɛso nɛ fo ku na.

english_verse: In fact, if they obey the Law, they are as good as anyone who is circumcised.
translation_verse: Fo maŋ nyi fanɛ basa nɛ b maŋ ku atutu na baa wora asɔ nɛ mbra na bee ŋini, Ebɔrɛ bee sɔ bumo nna fanɛ bumo nɛ b ku atutu a?

english_verse: So everyone who obeys the Law, but has never been circumcised, will condemn you. Even though you are circumcised and have the Law, you still don't obey its teachings.
translation_verse: To, men baa nyi fanɛ basa nɛ b maŋ ku durnya ere to, bumo alɛ nsaa bɛ mbra na be kɔnɔ so na be kebaawɔtɔ so nɛ Ebɔrɛ beeŋ yili n ji menyi nɛ men ku nseŋ naa kɔ mbra na n ti so na demu.

english_verse: Just because you live like a Jew and are circumcised doesn't make you a real Jew.
translation_verse: Mannɛ kenishiso nɛ baa ta a pin Juw, mannɛ kuku kututu be nwɔl na n lɛ na malɛ e la kashenteŋ be katutuku na.

english_verse: To be a real Jew you must obey the Law. True circumcision is something that happens deep in your heart, not something done to your body. And besides, you should want praise from God and not from humans.
translation_verse: Kashenteŋto, dimɛdi be kebaawɔtɔ to e naa ŋini e ka la Juw nɛ kashenteŋ malɛ be keku na la kagbene to be kesheŋ, Ebɔrɛ be asheŋ nna, mannɛ kenishiso be asheŋ nna. Nɛ esa nɛ e ku loŋ na malɛ be kechɔrɔ bee shi Ebɔrɛ kutɔ nna, mannɛ nyiŋgbasa kutɔ.

english_verse: What good is it to be a Jew? What good is it to be circumcised?
translation_verse: To, nɛ nuso be kechɔ nɛ Juwebi chɔ basa pɔtɛ? Ŋko manɛ be tɔnɔ nɛ katutuku kɔ?

english_verse: It is good in a lot of ways! First of all, God's messages were spoken to the Jews.
translation_verse: Cha, Juwebi baa chɔ basa pɔtɛ ekpa kama so nna, ŋkpal manɛ so, kusɔ nɛ k juŋkpar e la fanɛ bumo nɛ Ebɔrɛ ta mbe mmalga m bɔɔ enɔ.

english_verse: It is true that some of them did not believe the message. But does this mean that God cannot be trusted, just because they did not have faith?
translation_verse: Ama nɛ bumo be beko malɛ kini kebugi epunto n sa Ebɔrɛ ai? Loŋ beeŋ tiŋ n shin nɛ Ebɔrɛ malɛ e ki kɔnɔleŋiwura a?

english_verse: No, indeed! God tells the truth, even if everyone else is a liar. The Scriptures say about God, “Your words will be proven true, and in court you will win your case.”
translation_verse: Kaarɛ fanɛ loŋ e tiŋ n wora. Nɛ nyiŋgbasa bre la efɛpo, Ebɔrɛ bre la kashenteŋjipo nna saŋkama fanɛ kananɛ abɔrɛsibɛ na bee kaŋɛ na. A yɛ: “Fo mmalga to e naa ŋini fo ka kɔ kashenteŋ, fo alɛ beeŋ baa ji a lar fo edemu to.”

english_verse: If our evil deeds show how right God is, then what can we say? Is it wrong for God to become angry and punish us? What a foolish thing to ask.
translation_verse: Kesheŋ bishiso ko malɛ nde fanɛ: “Nɛ fanɛ anyi be asheŋ lubi bee shin nɛ basa bee wu Ebɔrɛ be alelasheŋ, nuso nɛ an naa kaŋɛ ere? An kaŋɛ fanɛ nɛ Ebɔrɛ bar mbe agbo anyi so, e maŋ wora n nyalɛ ŋko?” Nyiŋgbasa be kamɔrɔji be kamalga nɛ mee malga na.

english_verse: But the answer is, “No.” Otherwise, how could God judge the world?
translation_verse: Kaarɛ, loŋ maŋ kɔ ekpa kuraa, ŋkpal manɛ so, nuso nɛ Ebɔrɛ daa tiŋ a ji durnya ere to ebi demu?

english_verse: Since your lies bring great honor to God by showing how truthful he is, you may ask why God still says you are a sinner.
translation_verse: Ama esa ko malɛ kraa beeŋ naŋ tiŋ n ji emɔrɔ m bishi le: “Nɛ fanɛ ŋkpal ma efɛsheŋ so Ebɔrɛ be kashenteŋ na bee lar efuli nɛnɛ a nya kemaŋkura a ti so, manɛ e naaŋ ba nɛ Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ fanɛ n wora n da so?”

english_verse: You might as well say, “Let's do something evil, so that something good will come of it!” Some people even claim that we are saying this. But God is fair and will judge them as well. No One Is Good
translation_verse: Le be kamalga koŋwule ere malɛ so nɛ basa ko bee yili so a ku anyi kɔnɔ a kaŋɛ fanɛ loŋ nɛ anyee kaŋɛ na. B yɛ: “Men shin nɛ an baa wora alubi nɛ a baa ki alela.” Loŋ be basa be kasogberge baŋ daga bumo nna. Dimɛdi ka maŋ du cheembi be asheŋ

english_verse: What does all this mean? Does it mean that we Jews are better off than the Gentiles? No, it doesn't! Jews, as well as Gentiles, are ruled by sin, just as I have said.
translation_verse: To, naniere, nuso nɛ anyeeŋ kaŋɛ fanɛ anyi chɔ basa pɔtɛ ŋko? Cha, anyi maaŋ tiŋ ŋ kaŋɛ loŋ kikɛ, ŋkpal manɛ so, an teŋ wu fanɛ dimɛdi kikɛ, Juwebi nɛ basa pɔtɛ kikɛ wɔ alubi to nna.

english_verse: Not one of them understands or even searches for God.
translation_verse: Esa kikɛ maŋ wɔtɔ a pin asheŋ to, ekama malɛ maŋ naa wɔtɔ a kɔ a fin Ebɔrɛ.

english_verse: They have all turned away and are worthless. There isn't one person who does right.
translation_verse: Ekama nyam kilgi m pal kaman n sa Ebɔrɛ n choŋ, ekama nyam ki jiga. Esa kikɛ maŋ wɔtɔ a wora kelela, hale esa koŋwule gba maŋ wɔtɔ.

english_verse: Their words are like an open pit, and their tongues are good only for telling lies. Each word is as deadly as the fangs of a snake,
translation_verse: Ekama be kɔnɔ du fanɛ b ka kur nchaŋ nna n nase. Efɛ nɛ bumo be nnɔana na bee ku mmalga nɛ a bee lar bumo be nnɔana to du fanɛ wasa ka duŋ esa n lara kɔrtɔ n wɔtɔ mo to na.

english_verse: and they say nothing but bitter curses.
translation_verse: Abar be kebaamelgi kpakpaso e bɔlɔ bumo be nnɔ to a wɔtɔ.

english_verse: Wherever they go, they leave ruin and destruction.
translation_verse: Kaplɛkama malɛ nɛ b yɔ, kasɔjija be tɔrɔ nɛ baa yige a lɛ basa so.

english_verse: They don't know how to live in peace.
translation_verse: B maŋ nyi kagbenewushi be ekpa.

english_verse: They don't even fear God.”
translation_verse: Bumo alɛ maŋ naa kɔ kabɔrɛŋana.”

english_verse: We know that everything in the Law was written for those who are under its power. The Law says these things to stop anyone from making excuses and to let God show that the whole world is guilty.
translation_verse: Ama an nyi fanɛ kusɔ kama nɛ mbra na bee kaŋɛ, basa nɛ b wɔ kumo to na to nɛ k de, saŋɛ na so esa kikɛ maaŋ nya kɔnɔ m bugi. Loŋ malɛ e naaŋ shin nɛ Ebɔrɛ e ji durnya kikɛ demu.

english_verse: God doesn't accept people simply because they obey the Law. No, indeed! All the Law does is to point out our sin. God's Way of Accepting People
translation_verse: Ŋkpal manɛ so, mannɛ esa nɛ e bee wora mbra be ashuŋ shunso e la esa nɛ Ebɔrɛ nase kumo fanɛ e la elelapo. Kusɔ nɛ mbra na baa ŋini e la kebaashin nɛ basa e baa pin kulubi be asheŋ. Kananɛ Ebɔrɛ bee shin nɛ mo nɛ basa bee nya kɔnɔkoŋwule be asheŋ

english_verse: Now we see how God does make us acceptable to him. The Law and the Prophets tell how we become acceptable, and it isn't by obeying the Law of Moses.
translation_verse: Ama naniere bre Ebɔrɛ ŋini kananɛ e nase kumo fanɛ basa e baa la belelapo mbe anishito, loŋ be ekpa na malɛ nɛ mbra na maŋ kɔ shɛŋ.

english_verse: All of us have sinned and fallen short of God's glory.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal manɛ so, ekama nyam wora kulubi a maŋ taga to Ebɔrɛ be kemaŋkura na.

english_verse: But God treats us much better than we deserve, and because of Christ Jesus, he freely accepts us and sets us free from our sins.
translation_verse: Ama ŋkpal Ebɔrɛ be kuwɔr be kakɛ nɛ esa maa wora shɛŋ nsaa nya na so, asheŋ naŋ nyalɛ n sa basa, ŋkpal kesɔnyige be ekpa nɛ b bɔla Yesu Kristo so m bugi na so.

english_verse: God sent Christ to be our sacrifice. Christ offered his life's blood, so by faith in him we could come to God. And God did this to show that in the past he was right to be patient and forgive sinners. This also shows that God is right when he accepts people who have faith in Jesus.
translation_verse: Ama naniere bre e maa kplaŋ dimɛdi be alubi so, a ŋini e ka bee ji asheŋ nɛ amo be ekpa so. Loŋ malɛ e naa ŋini mo gbagba ka la asheŋ be keji nɛ amo be ekpa so be Ebɔrɛ, mo alɛ nseŋ naa ta esa nɛ e yirda Yesu a ki elelapo mbe anishito.

english_verse: We see that people are acceptable to God because they have faith, and not because they obey the Law.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal manɛ so, kusɔ nɛ an baa kɔ to e la fanɛ yirda e naa shin nɛ esa bee ji a lar Ebɔrɛ be anishito, mannɛ kebaabɛ mbra na be asheŋ woraso so.

english_verse: Does God belong only to the Jews? Isn't he also the God of the Gentiles? Yes, he is!
translation_verse: Ŋko Ebɔrɛ la Juwebi nawule be Ebɔrɛ nna a? Mannɛ basa pɔtɛ gba be Ebɔrɛ e la mo a? Bumo alɛ gba be Ebɔrɛ nna walɛ.

english_verse: Do we destroy the Law by our faith? Not at all! We make it even more powerful.
translation_verse: Ama an ta le be yirda ere n ti mbra na ekpa ŋko? Ayai, an baa kraa kɔ kumo to a ti kumo so eleŋ.

english_verse: If he became acceptable to God because of what he did, then he would have something to brag about. But he would never be able to brag about it to God.
translation_verse: Nɛ fanɛ ashuŋ ko nɛ e daŋ wora nseŋ ji n lar Ebɔrɛ be anishito, kumo ere e daa beeŋ tiŋ ŋkpal amo so m puchi, ama e maaŋ tiŋ m puchi Ebɔrɛ bre be anishito.

english_verse: In the Scriptures David talks about the blessings that come to people who are acceptable to God, even though they don't do anything to deserve these blessings. David says,
translation_verse: Loŋ gbagba nɛ Ewura Deevid daa de saŋɛ nɛ e daŋ malga nɛfa nɛ k wɔ esa kama nɛ Ebɔrɛ bee lar amodoŋwura be ashuŋ shunso be kaman a ta mo a ki elelapo na be asheŋ na.

english_verse: “What a blessing when God forgives our sins and our evil deeds. What a blessing when the Lord erases our sins from his book.”
translation_verse: Nɛfa la esa nɛ Enyɛnpe na maa nyiŋi mbe alubi be asheŋ na peya nna.”

english_verse: But when did this happen? Was it before or after Abraham was circumcised? Of course, it was before.
translation_verse: Saŋɛ mo nɛ Ebɔrɛ daŋ wora loŋ Eebraham daŋ ku kututu nna pɔɛŋ nɛ Ebɔrɛ wora loŋ ŋko e daŋ wora loŋ nna pɔɛŋ nɛ Eebraham ku? E daŋ wora loŋ nna pɔɛŋ nɛ Eebraham ku.

english_verse: Abraham let himself be circumcised to show he had been accepted because of his faith even before he was circumcised. This makes Abraham the father of all who are acceptable to God because of their faith, even though they are not circumcised.
translation_verse: Mbe yirda na be kaman nɛ e daŋ ku kututu a ŋini fanɛ ŋkpal mbe yirda na so nɛ Ebɔrɛ nase kumo fanɛ e la elelapo pɔɛŋ nɛ e ku. Amoso, abɔrɛsheŋ be kaplɛa so, mo e la bumo nɛ b maŋ ku nseŋ yirda Ebɔrɛ na kikɛ bumo tuto, saŋɛ na so Ebɔrɛ beeŋ nase kumo fanɛ b la belelapo.

english_verse: This also makes Abraham the father of everyone who is circumcised and has faith in God, as Abraham did before he was circumcised. The Promise Is for All Who Have Faith
translation_verse: Mo ere Eebraham koŋwule na e la bumo nɛ b ku atutu na gba bumo tuto, ama mannɛ b ka baŋ ku na so, b ka wɔ yirda be kebaawɔtɔ koŋwule nɛ mo ere Eebraham daa wɔ to pɔɛŋ nseŋ ku kututu na gba so. Kananɛ yirda la Ebɔrɛ be kɔnɔ naseso be kumu be asheŋ

english_verse: God promised Abraham and his descendants that he would give them the world. This promise wasn't made because Abraham had obeyed a law, but because his faith in God made him acceptable.
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ daŋ nase kɔnɔ nna n sa Eebraham nɛ mbe kaman to ebi fanɛ baaŋ nya durnya ere. Mannɛ Eebraham ka daa bɛ mbra na so so nɛ Ebɔrɛ nase kɔnɔ na, e ka daŋ yirda Ebɔrɛ nɛ e nase kumo fanɛ e la elelapo na so nɛ e daŋ wora loŋ.

english_verse: If Abraham and his descendants were given this promise because they had obeyed a law, then faith would mean nothing, and the promise would be worthless.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal manɛ so, nɛ fanɛ Ebɔrɛ be kɔnɔ naseso na la bumo nɛ baa bɛ mbra na so na peya nna, kumo ere esa be yirda maŋ kɔ kifi nɛ Ebɔrɛ be kɔnɔ naseso na malɛ gba maŋ la shɛŋ.

english_verse: God becomes angry when his Law is broken. But where there isn't a law, it cannot be broken.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal manɛ so, mbra e naa shin nɛ Ebɔrɛ be agbo bee lar efuli. Kaplɛkama nɛ mbra maŋ wɔtɔ, kewora n da so malɛ gba maŋ wɔtɔ.

english_verse: Everything depends on having faith in God, so that God's promise is assured by his gift of undeserved grace. This promise isn't only for Abraham's descendants who have the Law. It is for all who are Abraham's descendants because they have faith, just as he did. Abraham is the ancestor of us all.
translation_verse: Amoso, yirda e la kɔnɔ naseso be kumu, saŋɛ na so, loŋ be kɔnɔ naseso na beeŋ baa la Ebɔrɛ be kakɛ be tɔɔnɛ a sa Eebraham be kaman to ebi kikɛ, mannɛ bumo nɛ baa bɛ mbra na so nawule na, ama bumo nɛ b yirda Ebɔrɛ fanɛ kananɛ Eebraham daŋ yirda na gba ti so. Ŋkpal manɛ so, Eebraham e la anyi kikɛ be etuto ashi abɔrɛsheŋ be kaplɛa so.

english_verse: The Scriptures say that Abraham would become the ancestor of many nations. This promise was made to Abraham because he had faith in God, who raises the dead to life and creates new things.
translation_verse: Loŋ nɛ abɔrɛsibɛ na bee kaŋɛ fanɛ Ebɔrɛ kaŋɛ Eebraham le na. E yɛ: “N ta fo ŋ ki efuli damtaana so ebi bumo tuto.” Amoso, Ebɔrɛ be anishito Eebraham nɛ e daŋ yirda mo ere Ebɔrɛ nɛ e bee sa basa wuso ŋkpa nsaa shin nɛ asɔ nɛ a maŋ wɔ durnya to bee fara kebaawɔtɔ na e la an tuto.

english_verse: God promised Abraham a lot of descendants. And when it all seemed hopeless, Abraham still had faith in God and became the ancestor of many nations.
translation_verse: Saŋɛ nɛ Eebraham daŋ yirda nseŋ tama na, e daa maŋ wu shɛŋ pɔɛŋ nna nseŋ tama. Amoso nɛ e ki efuli damta so ebi bumo tuto fanɛ kananɛ abɔrɛsibɛ na kaŋɛ mo le na: “Loŋ nɛ fo kaman to ebi beeŋ ba wora keshi a sa.”

english_verse: But Abraham never doubted or questioned God's promise. His faith made him strong, and he gave all the credit to God.
translation_verse: Mbe yirda daa maŋ gbuŋgbuŋ to n shin nɛ e fara a lar Ebɔrɛ be kɔnɔ naseso be kaman. E daŋ nya yirda be eleŋ nna n ti so nseŋ ta kemaŋkura n sa Ebɔrɛ.

english_verse: just as we read in the Scriptures. But these words were not written only for Abraham.
translation_verse: Kekaŋɛ fanɛ: “Ebɔrɛ nase kumo fanɛ e la elelapo na,” maŋ de mo nawule nna ashi abɔrɛsibɛ na to.

english_verse: They were written for us, since we will also be accepted because of our faith in God, who raised our Lord Jesus to life.
translation_verse: Anyi nɛ an yirda mo Ebɔrɛ nɛ e tiŋi Yesu an Nyɛnpe ashi luwu to ŋkaa beeŋ nase kumo fanɛ an la belelapo na gba ti so.

english_verse: God gave Jesus to die for our sins, and he raised him to life, so that we would be made acceptable to God.
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ shin nɛ b daŋ ta mo nna n sa nɛ e wu ŋkpal anyi be alubi so nseŋ naŋ shin nɛ e tiŋi luwu na to nɛ an baa la belelapo Ebɔrɛ be anishito.

english_verse: By faith we have been made acceptable to God. And now, thanks to our Lord Jesus Christ, we have peace with God.
translation_verse: Naniere Ebɔrɛ ka kpal anyi be yirda so n shin nɛ an ji n lar mbe anishito ere bre, an bɔla an Nyɛnpe Yesu Kristo so a kɔ kagbenewushi ashi Ebɔrɛ na be anishito.

english_verse: Christ has also introduced us to God's gift of undeserved grace on which we now take our stand. So we are happy, as we look forward to sharing in the glory of God.
translation_verse: Yesu kpal anyi be yirda so n shin nɛ an nya le be kuwɔr be kakɛ nɛ an wɔ ere to. Amoso, anyi be ŋgbene fuli anyi ŋkpal an ka kɔ tama fanɛ anyi alɛ gba beeŋ nya Ebɔrɛ be kemaŋkura nɛ e kɔ a jo anyi na so.

english_verse: And endurance builds character, which gives us a hope
translation_verse: nɛ kumo alɛ bee sa esa da lela, nɛ da lela malɛ bee sa esa tama.

english_verse: that will never disappoint us. All of this happens because God has given us the Holy Spirit, who fills our hearts with his love.
translation_verse: Ebɔrɛ bɔla Kiyoyu Cheeŋ nɛ e la Ebɔrɛ be kakɛ nɛ e kɔ a sa anyi na so nna n ta mbe kasha m bɔlɔ anyi be ŋgbene to.

english_verse: No one is really willing to die for an honest person, though someone might be willing to die for a truly good person.
translation_verse: Pɔɛŋ nɛ esa e wu n sa elelapo, k du kpakpa. Shere esa ko beeŋ shuli n wu n sa esa nɛ e la esa bre.

english_verse: But God showed how much he loved us by having Christ die for us, even though we were sinful.
translation_verse: Ama kananɛ Ebɔrɛ ŋini anyi mbe kasha nde fanɛ saŋɛ nɛ an daa la alubiworapoana na nɛ Yesu wu n sa anyi.

english_verse: But there is more! Now that God has accepted us because Christ sacrificed his life's blood, we will also be kept safe from God's anger.
translation_verse: Ŋkpal manɛ so, naniere Kristo wu n shin nɛ an ji n lar Ebɔrɛ be anishito, amoso, mbe kumɔlga anyi kachako ashi Ebɔrɛ be agbo na bre to nɛ e maaŋ wora a?

english_verse: Even when we were God's enemies, he made peace with us, because his Son died for us. Yet something even greater than friendship is ours. Now that we are at peace with God, we will be saved by the life of his Son.
translation_verse: An daa la Ebɔrɛ mo doŋana nna, ama e bɔla mo Pibinyɛn Kristo be luwu na so n shin nɛ anyi nɛ mo naŋ nyalɛ. To, nɛ naniere anyi nɛ mo ka nyalɛ ere bre nɛ e maaŋ bɔla Kristo be ŋkpa na so m mɔlga anyi kachako a?

english_verse: And in addition to everything else, we are happy because God sent our Lord Jesus Christ to make peace with us. Adam and Christ
translation_verse: Mannɛ aloŋ gba nawule so nna, ŋkpal manɛ so, an bɔla an Nyɛnpe Yesu Kristo nɛ e shin nɛ anyi nɛ Ebɔrɛ naŋ nyalɛ na so n nya kagbenefuli ŋkpal Ebɔrɛ so n ti so. Adam nɛ Kristo be asheŋ

english_verse: Adam sinned, and that sin brought death into the world. Now everyone has sinned, and so everyone must die.
translation_verse: To, naniere, men baa nyi fanɛ esa koŋwule so nɛ alubi bɔla m ba durnya to nɛ luwu malɛ ba ŋkpal alubi na so m ba sɔ durnya kikɛ to nyam, ŋkpal manɛ so, basa kikɛ wora alubi.

english_verse: Sin was in the world before the Law came. But no record of sin was kept, because there was no Law.
translation_verse: Alubi malɛ daa wɔ durnya to nna pɔɛŋ nɛ Ebɔrɛ sa mbra. Ama kakpa nɛ mbra maŋ wɔtɔ, Ebɔrɛ maa karga alubi.

english_verse: Yet death still had power over all who lived from the time of Adam to the time of Moses. This happened, though not everyone disobeyed a direct command from God, as Adam did. In some ways Adam is like Christ who came later.
